items.title: LUW rough-ground wall-model prototype design (design only; to be implemented only after the Lead's review)
items.text:
# LUW Ground Rough Wall Model Prototype Design (Design Only; To Be Implemented Only After Lead Review)

Time: 10-14 20:11 (US Eastern). Scope: Public LUW local read-only verification copy, verified HEAD `dd438c1c68664980a92460e4778f18f36be3f47c`. In this round, solver source code was neither copied nor modified, no new cases were run, and no CU was consumed. During implementation, a new source code copy will be created only in this directory; source code or modified version results will not be published.

## Basis and Applicable Boundaries

| Verified Facts | Usage / Limitations in This Design |
| --- | --- |
| The neutral ABL ground replaces no-slip with Monin–Obukhov wall stress; that paper uses cumulant-LBM and reconstructs the first-layer distribution, near-wall SGS may still be overly dissipative. | Using the neutral log law to compute wall stress has a sound basis, but distribution reconstruction and SGS modification methods cannot be directly copied to our code's BGK/FP16C. |
| WFB adjusts some diagonal distributions pointing toward the fluid interior; evidence is channel Reτ=640/2003. | Candidate momentum exchange scheme; do not extrapolate channel error improvements to urban near-ground wind speeds. |
| Under D3Q19/SRT/Smagorinsky, calculate τw from first-layer velocity and wall distance, subsequently modify boundary distributions and handle near-wall νt; Musker, Werner–Wengle, and Schmitt are selectable. | Numerical architecture closest to LUW; its smooth-wall Musker does not directly replace the known roughness length of Case E. |
| Comparison of channel wall functions and SGS; Smagorinsky may be limited at smaller y+, and the authors' overall preferred choice is not our code's BGK. | Near-wall SGS must be diagnosed separately; it cannot be claimed that switching the wall law will inevitably improve turbulence. |
| Official CFD ground is rough log law z0=0.024 m, buildings are smooth log law, domain approximately 500×500×300 m. | This prototype only takes ground z0=0.024 m; buildings retain the original LUW boundaries, which cannot be called an official full-boundary reproduction. |
| D3Q19/SRT, FP16C, SUBGRID, VOLUME_FORCE are currently compiled and enabled. `stream_collide` computes macroscopic fluid quantities after Esoteric-Pull `load_f`, Guo force is calculated before collision; `z==0` ground is enforced as TYPE_S, buildings are voxelized from STL. | Must correctly handle the even/odd timestep mapping of Esoteric-Pull; ground TYPE_S cannot be kept as no-slip while additionally superimposing wall drag in the same direction. |

The cards are excerpts, with listed page numbers following original printed pages indicated on each card; this is a targeted methodology check, not a comprehensive governance reading of all four PDFs. Paper conclusions and our prototype hypotheses are kept separate.

## Choices and Explicit Non-Choices

Choose "horizontal ground specular reflection (ensuring only non-penetration, no tangential no-slip constraint) + log-law tangential shear force within the first-layer fluid lattice" to **replace** the existing halfway no-slip bounce-back on flat horizontal ground, never superimposing resistance on top of it. Each incoming link at the bottom surface is specularly reflected according to `(c_x,c_y,c_z) → (c_x,c_y,−c_z)` (exact indices and even/odd step reads/writes must be verified link-by-link); this differs from the tangential momentum exchange of the original halfway bounce-back `(c_x,c_y,c_z) → (−c_x,−c_y,−c_z)`. Specular reflection only provides a non-penetration boundary, tangential drag caused by the original bounce-back should be reduced to numerical error, and the rough-wall stress given by the model is the specified ground resistance; buildings and non-planar bottom surfaces still use the old boundaries. Reasons: Asmuth card CFJREQTQ (article p. 3 §III, PDF p. 4) explicitly **replaces** no-slip with ground wall stress, and its p. 4 Eq. (19) uses distribution reconstruction; the "specular + first-layer Guo force" in this design is a prototype **hypothesis** adapted to the existing BGK/FP16C pathway, not the original algorithm of that paper, and must be verified using momentum budget. Haussmann card UAJ8VJH3 (print p. 3290 §2.5.1) provides a wall stress and distribution reconstruction reference for BGK+Smagorinsky, but its smooth wall law cannot directly replace the rough wall of Case E. Reasons: roughness and τw can be specified separately; the current Guo forcing/collision pathway already exists; it does not add a domain-wide GPU 3×float force field and can be calculated cell-by-cell inside the kernel; for FP16C, only the force in FP32 calculations is modified without directly writing compressed distributions. The link implementation of specular reflection requires greater caution than full distribution reconstruction in the first layer of BGK, hence it is listed as a unit test that must be passed first. Alternative: directional diagonal distribution momentum correction from Han FDR card S2IAE6TM (article p. 18 §5, PDF p. 19), but it requires deriving link-by-link coefficients for D3Q19, Esoteric-Pull, and rough-wall τw before use, and cannot be directly ported. Purely "retaining halfway bounce-back + negative body force" is not chosen: ground shear stress would be double-counted; the digital twin wind tunnel line has already observed in Silsoe/Urban Field that the first-layer stress approximation contribution is very small and bounce-back accounts for most of the ground resistance, so z0 did not actually control the profile (internal project experience, not literature proof). Haussmann's full distribution reconstruction and near-wall SGS linkage is a phase-two proposal and will not be introduced concurrently in this round.

## Lattice, Distance, and Physical Quantities

- Applied only to first-layer fluid cells whose immediate bottom neighbor is a `TYPE_S` **global** z=0 horizontal ground cell; global coordinates `z_global=z_local+Oz`, must not be erroneously applied at local z=1 of each GPU subdomain. Inlet/outlet `TYPE_Elbm.positionunits.si_x` conversion. Wall normal is vertical, and force has only x/y components.
- Let the distance of the first-layer fluid relative to the wall surface be y1>0, tangential velocity vector **u**t, air density ρ, κ=0.40 (commonly used constant, **hypothesis**; must be consistent with the inlet log law adopted in the future). Neutral roughness law, `τw = ρ u*²`, horizontal wall stress vector; first-layer volumetric force, where Δz is the actual thickness of the first-layer control volume. Zero-velocity safety branch F=0; z0 must be >0 and y1/z0 sufficiently large, input range validation, log≤0 not allowed. Convert SI physical quantities to lattice quantities first according to the existing `Units` relations of u, x, ρ, t, and then enter as Guo body forces into `fxn,fynFx_lb=−rho_lb*u*_lb²*(ux_lb/|ut_lb|)`, similarly for y. If the effective control volume thickness of the first layer is not 1 lattice unit, replace with the measured thickness. Compute using the currently updated macroscopic velocity, and must not use the initial profile field as a constant.
- Inlet comparison: Case E z0 comes from official tables; velocity normalization Uref fixes repository profile.dat at 15.9 m to 3.9286416 m/s (Round 10 records, lines 6 and 10); z0 is roughness length, not geometric STL ground elevation. Whether `profile.dat` is consistent with the neutral log law of this z0/κ has not been proven. There is no guarantee that "modifying the wall means the original profile must remain constant along the fetch": empty-domain tests must simultaneously record inlet momentum flux, outlet, bed stress, and development section; if non-equilibrium, report the inconsistency, and do not reverse-tune z0 or add arbitrary sustaining forces to fit. There are no verified values in this task for Case A's z0 and inlet scale; when using the same ground wall law, mark as **hypothesis**, keep consistent with Round 9 inlet, and do not claim that AIJ ground roughness has been verified.

## Two Numerical Details That Cannot Be Skipped

1. **Replace bottom tangential no-slip first, then add force; conservation check.** The implementation of `load_fstore_f` in `kernel.cpp` swaps addresses by even/odd steps (1338–1350); ordinary solid neighbor cells in the source code form halfway bounce-back. The prototype needs to establish a specular mapping `c_z -> -c_z, c_x,c_y` for bottom z-non-zero links (a total of ten directional velocities in D3Q19) (exact direction indices to be printed and checked against `c` item-by-item), taking effect only for "fluid ↔ marked ground" links; reflection position, even/odd timestep reads/writes must conform to Esoteric-Pull to avoid read-write races and floating-point distribution loss; building links retain original bounce-back. Note that this is not arbitrarily swapping two `fhn` items after `load_f`: this alters distributions originating from different fluid neighbor cells and is not necessarily conservative. Before implementation, conduct a zero-shear specular reflection test on a small grid to verify that link-by-link mass flux, normal momentum, and tangential momentum are zero; under non-zero shear, the total shear force should be consistent with the body force. If not passed, revert to design, do not proceed to urban cases.
2. **Near-wall Smagorinsky.** Existing `kernel.cpp` 1723–1737 adjusts `w` using non-equilibrium stress; wall force and this SGS effect may combine to cause excessive dissipation. The first version will keep the SUBGRID algorithm and constants unchanged for now, only diagnosing first-layer `nu_t` and recording profiles of ; "keeping unchanged" cannot be claimed as SGS having correct wall damping. If SGS is to be suppressed in the first layer, a switchable damping law must be set up separately and compared independently; it cannot be mixed into a single change together with the wall law. The numerical precision of FP16C also needs sample verification in the first layer; all stress/force calculations use float, recording stability at low speeds and high wind speed upper limits.

## File Modification Interfaces (Implementation Permission Not Yet Given; Estimation Only)

Implementation copy is expected to reside only in  (verify target does not exist first, never overwrite existing results):

| File / Function | Expected Changes | Estimated Added / Modified Lines |
| --- | --- | ---: |
|, `apply_profile_boundaries` for single profile cases and necessary flat ground label preparation | Boundary determination / unit conversion / reading and echoing configuration `ground_wall_model, ground_z0_si, ground_kappa`; default off, old cases point-by-point identical; label only ground plane without mislabeling buildings or DEM | 45–90 |
| `LBM_Domain` compile-time kernel parameters and `device_defines`; `lbm.hpp` when necessary | Pass switches, z0/κ, ground positions or labels as per-domain parameters to kernel; cross-GPU global z mapping | 20–50 |
| `load_fstream_collide` external force accumulation and diagnostics | Precise bottom specular reflection, roughness law local stress, protective branches, along existing `VOLUME_FORCE` Guo forcing pathway rather than an extra permanent F array; updated diagnostic pathways must not alter the model-free old pathway | 70–130 |
| (if enabling compile-time switch), minimal verification scripts / configs (only in wallmodel directory) | Comparison switches, tests, and outputs, without modifying published repository | 50–100 |

Total estimated solver code is about 135–270 lines, verification scripts counted separately; first complete small-grid conservation / multi-card indexing / equivalence tests of old cases with switch disabled, before starting computation. Existing `FORCE_FIELD` domain-wide F buffer should not be repurposed for step-accumulated ground force: allocated in source code `lbm.cpp` 293–302, it has independent function and double superposition must be avoided.

## Phased Verification (Not This Round's Execution Results)

0. Default off: Point-by-point / log comparison with HEAD on identical-grid small cases; when affected by floating-point scheduling, at least mass and velocity statistics must be consistent. Flat plate channel minimal grid: zero-shear specular reflection has zero tangential resistance, pure uniform flow has no penetration; when z0 is enabled, wall stress is opposite to flow velocity, and total momentum budget matches Guo force; boundary tests for z0>0, near-zero velocity, first-layer wall distance, corners, and cross-domain halos. If bottom normal is distorted or conservation fails, do not proceed to the next stage.
1. Empty domain: Along Case E flat ground 500 m, using identical profile.dat and wall settings, simultaneously measure **mean wind speed and turbulence intensity** at inlet, along the fetch, and outlet at 2, 5, 15.9 m (specify TI definition using three-component RMS / mean speed, retaining individual components and k), providing absolute values and ratios to inlet, fetch trends, and time-averaging windows respectively; require both to be interpretably maintained, rather than merely 2 m wind speed being close to input. Report that original model-free 2 m is about 41–52% (prior building domain diagnostics, cannot be taken as a strict empty-domain baseline), and run a true model-free empty domain separately. Additionally, perform an item-by-item **tangential momentum budget** on a section of flat ground control volume: inlet−outlet advective flux, top-bottom / lateral fluxes, pressure action, internal molecular and SGS fluxes, tangential momentum exchange of specular bottom links, first-layer Guo force integral, and momentum storage changes; quantify closure residuals and numerical errors. When wall force is disabled, tangential resistance of specular bottom links should be near numerical zero; when enabled, the integral of bottom model force should match expected `−∫τw dA`, and total ground resistance should be predominantly provided by model force rather than residual bounce-back. If independent contributions of bounce-back and model cannot be measured, or closure is not achieved, it cannot be claimed that z0 has controlled the profile; if empty domain does not meet standards, do not proceed to urban cases.
2. Case E R10a: Westerly wind, 1 m, identical time window / registration (+1,+1,0), inlet TI and original configuration, buildings unchanged; after modification, MAE/r/mean ratio of vector S and scalar approximation sqrt(S²+2k) across 80 points, as well as near-ground fetch; retain list of before and near-wall contaminated corner points, do not select parameters based on isolated MAE values.
3. Case A Round 9: Official z=4/40 m and center profiles, FAC2, q, r, NRMSE of mean velocity and k (according to established definitions and sensitivities); surface z0 source is unverified, do not default Case E's 0.024 m as the official Case A value.

The criteria are that profiles improve interpretably and Case E / Case A show no obvious side effects, without judging model correctness based on single MAE improvements. This prototype does not add any geometric roughness blocks; if roughness block experiments are established separately in the future, periodic layout acoustic tones and boundary reflections must be checked first: the digital twin wind tunnel line once observed a 1.317 Hz peak in its periodic layout case (internal experience, only a risk reminder, cannot be taken as the predicted frequency for this case). The above are merely proposed experiments, not verified results; only after design and actual verification are completed can they be handed over to the digital twin wind tunnel line root Lead for read-only reference.

# LUW Ground Wall Model r13 — Gate 0 Ruled Passed by Lead; Continuation 4 Empty Domain Failed

Time: From 10-14 21:15 (US Eastern). Internal prototype only, not published.

## Verified Inputs and Source Code

- The HEAD of read-only baseline  is `dd438c1c68664980a92460e4778f18f36be3f47c`.  Copied and created after confirming the target does not exist, intact, git working tree unmodified. No modification or overwriting of old results.
- In source code, `defines.hpp:17–24MOVING_BOUNDARIES` is currently disabled. `kernel.cpp:1338–1350` is Esoteric-Pull read/write; `1475–1516` computes macroscopic velocity after load; `1686–1747` handles Guo forcing and Smagorinsky. `setup.cpp:5948–5953` sets all z=0 to TYPE_S, with actual first-layer fluid cell at z=1; `lbm.cpp:612–697` uses def_Oz to represent global index for each subdomain.
- Parameter sources: Case E ground z0=0.024 m, AIJ PDF p. 2 Table 1; official Case A  has U and k by height (Inflow lines 34–59), without listing ground z0. Case A was checked in local `Tominaga_et_al_2008_JWEIAguide.pdf`, but its dedicated value was not found; ` pages` located Sim (2015) PDF p. 261, whose Table 28 recounts Case A z0=1.8×10⁻⁴ m, stated as a logarithmic fit to inlet velocity by Mochida et al. (2002). This is a secondary source and cannot yet be claimed as verified by official AIJ. If adopted in the next phase, it must be marked as hypothesis and sensitivity tests for 0.9×10⁻⁴ and 3.6×10⁻⁴ m must be conducted.
- κ=0.40 is the commonly used value hypothesis of the design; halfway wall position is at z=0.5 lattice, first-layer fluid z=1 has y1=0.5 dx: Case E dx=1 m, y1=0.5 m, ln((y1+z0)/z0)=3.083437854; Case A dx=2 m, y1=1 m, if using the aforementioned hypothesis z0=1.8×10⁻⁴ m, ln=8.622733691 (half and double z0 are 9.315790884 and 7.929766462, respectively). Actual physical height of fluid points and wall positions must be re-verified from run logs / VTK; paper values cannot replace numerical verification.

## Gate 0 Current Evidence

Checking item-by-item against source code D3Q19 directions and even/odd addresses of load_f/store_f, 4 static pre-checks ran and passed. It shows that two naive specular reflection formulations (only swapping fhn after load, only changing store direction at the current cell) are not equivalent to cross-cell specular flow for diagonal links; these are structural exclusions, not two conservation tests already performed on OpenCL. It cannot yet be asserted that the complete specular scheme failed, nor can it trigger the branch of "switching to moving wall if actual testing fails twice". The initial test assumption regarding Esoteric-Pull time parity did not hold, so that assertion was removed and re-run; static pre-checks are never counted as mass/momentum conservation verification.

Currently there is no solver diff, OpenCL build, or completed channel / empty-domain test, and none of the three gates have passed; the local CPU machine lacks a clinfo/OpenCL verification environment. Colab has not yet been requested, consuming 0 CU. It is prohibited to refer to this draft or existing old case results as modified wall model achievements.

## Incomplete Items and Conditions

Link-by-link mass, normal momentum, and tangential momentum verification of specular reflection must first be conducted on a real OpenCL small-grid mesh; if conservation actually fails twice, then only use the TYPE_S moving wall pathway as an alternative, and never superimpose Guo body force. Regardless of which path is chosen, it must be verified that default-off is point-by-point identical to HEAD, model drag and bounce-back are measured separately, and a 10% momentum closure of control volume pressure / advection / top-lateral fluxes / stresses / storage is achieved. In Gate 1, the mean velocity and TI at 2/5/15.9 m, 15.9 m change ≤10%, and 2 m improvement for true empty domain without/with model are unverified, therefore Case E/A must not be launched. If Gate 1 does not pass, halt at tier 1 according to the assignment and do not run urban cases.

## 10-14 21:42–21:46 Implementation Progress (US Eastern)

Using PyOpenCL on Colab A100-SXM4-40GB against  even/odd indices, a 24×12×10 D3Q19 SRT small channel kernel was written, periodic xy, z=0 and top solid; this is an **independent small kernel**, not the modified LUW kernel. In the initial launch version, top/bottom boundaries and timestep correspondence were incorrect, resulting in noticeable mass leakage; this was judged as a test fixture error, not counted as a failure of the specular scheme. After correcting to in-place Esoteric-Pull, initialize t=1 writing, first step t=0, and specular on both top and bottom, for 81 steps of zero-model-force uniform parallel flow: total fluid mass 2303.999756→2303.999756, total x-momentum 115.200020→115.200104, total z-momentum approximately 0; zero-shear check passed only for this simplified uniform flow.

However, after adding the Guo force of the inlet stress formula to the same small kernel, the bottom surface computed a resultant force of approximately −0.0121 to −0.0120 per step; total x-momentum 115.200020→114.917236, while the zero-force control remained 115.200104. This difference cannot be explained as approximately equal to the applied cumulative force: the current kernel function's Guo treatment, top/bottom reflections, and momentum definitions have not yet completed an item-by-item budget; code-internal  identities cannot be treated as real dynamic verification of <5%. In particular, it has not been verified on LUW's own OpenCL kernel, nor is there a verified control volume closure for empty domain without/with model. Therefore, **Gate 0 did not pass**, and urban cases should not yet be run; this is not a verified failure of two specular schemes, and does not trigger switching to moving wall. Complete hourly readings: , aforementioned small kernel: . The solver copy remains unmodified, with no solver diff. Colab was proactively stopped, and verified that no sessions remain for this task; total account balance 1395.09→1393.73 CU, but other people's sessions were billed during this period, so 1.36 CU cannot be attributed to this task.

Official Case A `CaseA(1_1_2).xls` Inflow table is actually on lines 3–26 of local sheet (the earlier 34–59 was not this sheet's line numbers); the first 3 heights z/b=0.0625, 0.125, 0.25, which correspond to z=2, 4, 8 m based on b=32 m, U=2.745, 2.935, 3.175 m/s. Performing least squares U=a·ln(z/z0) on these three points yields fitted z0=2.9466×10⁻⁴ m, slope a=0.31018 m/s; in the same order of magnitude as the secondary recounting of 1.8×10⁻⁴ m in Sim 2015. Fitting range is sensitive: expanding to 16/32/48 m yields z0 of 5.6055×10⁻⁴ / 1.6983×10⁻³ / 5.2107×10⁻³ m, respectively; it cannot be said that a single log law fits all heights. If used for Case A in the future, it should be marked as "fitted from official near-ground inlet profile, 2–8 m", with separate ×0.5/×2 runs. In this case, y1=0.5dx=1 m (dx=2 m), ln((y1+z0)/z0)=8.129998; κ=0.40 remains a design hypothesis. Case E y1=0.5 m, z0=0.024 m, by the same formula ln=3.083438. The above are merely paper fits / grid settings, not solver output verifications.

## 10-14 22:05–22:14 Continuation 2: Real Solver Gate 0 Failed (US Eastern)

Per Lead's instructions, only the Guo equilibrium velocity and force term velocity of the small kernel were changed to , without changing the original small kernel's boundary and streaming. A100 test : specular zero-force control in steps 0→80 had mass 2303.999756→2303.999756, Px 115.200020→115.200104; with wall force enabled, Px 115.200020→114.637985, deducting zero-force drift gives −0.562119. Sampled resultant force per step was −0.012117 to −0.011887, which over 80 steps is about −0.95 to −0.97; the actual value was only about 58%–59% of this value, and the **fixture still did not reach the <5% budget criterion**. These are sampled force range estimates, not step-by-step exact integrations; it cannot be blamed that the corrected Guo scheme is already wrong or the specular boundary is already correct.

Directly modified the default-off experimental compile switch in , `lbm.cpp::device_defines`, local specular of z_global=1 in `kernel.cpp::stream_collide` and its existing Guo pathway, and added an independent `WALL_GATE0` small channel driver (modified files see `solver_gate0_attempt2_final_r13.diff`). C++ `-fsyntax-only` and `git diff --check` both passed; the real FluidX3D OpenCL kernel generated using this copy on Colab, 24×12×10 channel, 81 steps, FP16C/SRT/SUBGRID, compiled and ran separately for both specular approaches as well as zero-force / with-force, all exiting with 0. However, exit code 0 does not equal passing numerical gates.

The first attempt was overwriting upward distributions from downward distributions of the same cell after `load_f`: at zero force, Px steps 0→80 went from 112.798279→53.648745 (a drop of 52.44%), and with force from 112.792221→53.291121; bottom zero-force tangential resistance was far from zero. The second attempt averaged upward and downward distributions with identical horizontal velocity and opposite-sign z in pairs to maintain conservation: zero-force Px 110.398316→11.706808 (a drop of 89.40%), with force Px 110.394109→11.702116; almost degenerating into the original halfway bounce-back (original pathway 110.398316→11.690552). Mass changed by a relative magnitude of about 1e-5 in both approaches, Pz was small, but **transverse drag criteria failed both times**. The second scheme was left in the working tree as an unusable failed prototype, not to be used for physical results. Records: , .  is the re-run fixture; its head_path is the model-off compilation branch of the same source code, not a separately cloned HEAD binary, so it cannot yet be claimed that "default-off is point-by-point identical to HEAD".

Pinpointed: the `ground_first_fluid` specular handling inserted after `load_f` in `kernel.cpp::stream_collide` still leaves strong zero-force bottom tangential resistance; suspected to be `store_ffxn/fyn` superimposing shear stress. This is a numerical gate failure of wall flow, rather than an OpenCL compilation or runtime abnormality. According to Lead's rule of "switching to alternative if actual testing fails twice", the next scheme can only be **TYPE_S moving wall velocity replacing force term**, neither retaining current specular plus Guo nor superimposing force on existing bounce-back. Before fluid collision, back-calculate tangential moving wall velocity for each ground solid cell from neighboring first-layer local velocity and specified τw, and update `u[ground]`/TYPE_MS step-by-step; otherwise, a domain-wide fixed moving wall will miscalculate local shear stress. This alternative has not yet been implemented or verified. **Gate 0 did not pass, and Gate 1 empty domain or Case E/A will not be conducted**; there are no empty-domain plots or new comparison metrics.

This independent Colab A100 session `luw-wall-r13-cont` was stopped and verified not in private/global sessions; two other non-task A100 sessions ran concurrently. Account balance 1387.80→1384.09 CU (change across entire account, cannot be attributed to this round; ~9 minutes for this task estimated at ~2.8 CU based on 18.84 CU/h displayed simultaneously, estimation only), not exceeding total budget of 15 CU. No HPC submission for this task. Source code, logs, and outputs are for internal testing only, not published.

## 10-14 22:26–22:44 Continuation 3: Pairwise Swapping, Re-Verification with Real Kernel (US Eastern)

In the working tree, according to the Esoteric-Pull local mapping pointed out by Lead, pairwise swapped 9↔16, 11↔18, keeping 5 unchanged; 1000 single-step checks with random asymmetric distributions passed on mass and x/y ground fluxes. Separately, a truly clean copy of HEAD dd438c1 (`LatticeUrbanWind_HEAD_gate`) was created via local git clone, without overwriting previous failed results.

In the first round of the real LUW kernel channel (24×12×10, FP16C), zero force still had large Px drift: 110.3983→54.4787 (81 steps). Diagnosis revealed that the fixture top z=9 was still no-slip solid, with only the bottom changed to specular; domain-wide Px decreased due to top drag, and this change cannot all be attributed to the bottom. Subsequently, the top surface was also set to specular in the WALL_GATE0 test branch; although the first compilation succeeded, test macros were not passed from C++ to device, reproducing identical results, which was fixed in `lbm.cpp::device_defines`. The following numbers come from kernels with two-sided specular actually enabled, not counting previous two invalid compilations as success.

FP32 diagnostics (only test build disabled FP16C, without changing production configuration) showed: specular zero-force channel mass remained 2304.00000000 throughout, total normal momentum ~10⁻⁶. In raw step 0→80 after initialization, Px was 110.400002→110.592226, drift +0.1741%, **failing to reach the <0.1% gate starting from step zero**. After the initial boundary transient passed, in step 39→119, Px was 110.600080→110.592118, drift −0.00720%; step 119→199 was only −0.0000146%. These are values achieved only after "pre-warming before taking 81 steps", and the raw 81 steps cannot be quietly claimed as meeting the standard. Logs: .

The same fixture injected a test-dedicated constant bottom force τ=5×10⁻⁵ lattice into the 24×12 bottom lattice cells via LUW's original Guo pathway. In step 39→119, Px difference against the zero-force baseline was −1.105647; the specified force integral over those 80 steps was −1.152, a difference of 4.024%, less than 5%; step 119→199 difference was 4.013%. This is a **constant force pathway check**, which has not yet integrated the true velocity-varying logarithmic stress step-by-step, nor is it a complete control volume budget. Logs: ); limited only to this channel, whole urban settings unverified.

Conclusion / Gates: Specular mapping demonstrated feasibility in channels with pre-warming, FP32, and two-sided slip; there is no need to switch to moving wall alternative solely based on the total Px loss in the initial one-sided fixture. The old conclusion in the preceding section that "the next scheme can only be moving wall" was corrected by pinpointing the top no-slip fixture and missing device macro propagation this time, and must not continue to be cited as final judgment. However, formal Gate 0 is still **not fully cleared**: raw 81 steps of FP16C, step-by-step stress integration of true log law, and independent momentum measurements of top/sidewalls are incomplete, and raw step 0→80 values also slightly exceeded <0.1%. One cannot use 4.0% of test constant force to pose as closure of the model itself; Gate 1 true model-free empty domain, fetch-wise mean velocity/TI, and ground momentum budget have not yet been run, Case E/A has not even been launched, and there are no empty-domain plots or urban metrics. Current verifiable source diff: `solver_gate0_swap_current_r13.diff`, model macros default-off; compatibility with production inlet has not yet been verified. Four new A100 sessions for this task `luw-wall-r13-swap`, `luw-wall-r13-fp32`, `luw-wall-r13-warm`, and `luw-wall-r13-parity` were all proactively stopped and verified that only others' sessions remained. Account balance dropped from 1381.84 to 1378.09 CU during this period, with concurrent billing from others, so the full amount cannot be attributed to this task; these four small-channel sessions for this task were each short-lived, nowhere near the cumulative 15 CU upper limit. No HPC submission, no external release.

## 10-14 23:12 Continuation 3 Wrap-Up: Real Model Force Integration + Gate 1 Empty Domain (US Eastern)

Addressing the deficiency in the preceding section that "logarithmic stress was not integrated step-by-step", a cell-by-cell `ground_force` diagnostic buffer was added to `stream_collide` in the test build branch; the initial version mistakenly read linear array slices of logical z=1, reading all zeros, and after verifying using test constant 1234 that the writing side indeed had 288 cells, changed to full-array summation (details see ). LUW OpenCL channel with FP32 true log-law wall force: after pre-warming, step-by-step wall force integral in step 39→119 was −0.865491, ΔPx relative to zero wall force pathway was −0.830785, closure error 4.010%; step 119→199 were −0.851018 and −0.817075, respectively, error 3.989%. Model-off was identical to separately cloned HEAD in the same test fixture, and zero wall force conserved mass. FP16C two-sided specular zero-force step 39→119 Px 110.586184→110.560364, drift −0.02335%; while from initialization step 0→80 it was still +0.14679%, failing the <0.1% without pre-warming. Raw force diagnostic logs , where `mirror_constforce` is a variant name carried over in scripts, and what was actually enabled by `GATE0_DYNAMIC=1` this time was **dynamic log law**, not constant force. Gate 0 satisfies numerical criteria only after explicitly pre-warming for 39 steps; initial transients did not pass and cannot be written as unconditionally passed. Formal production remains FP16C; FP32 is an auxiliary budget test.

Next, ran the **true empty domain**: retaining only 12 peripheral base triangle facets of repository STL, no buildings, westerly Case E `profile.dat`; domain 500×64×270 m, dx=1 m, 31000 steps, last 20000 steps averaged 500 times, model-off / on compiled separately with identical configuration. Both exited with 0, ~180 s each. First-round model-on results were virtually identical to model-off; inspecting actual VTK solid flags revealed physical z=0 was at global index 20, first-layer fluid at 21, whereas model criterion hardcoded `z_global==1`: this is the **specific error location** of `ground_first_fluid` in LUW kernel (`kernel.cpp::stream_collide` after load_f). That first-round "on" actually applied force to the wrong layer inside the base, cannot serve as wall model effect, and was preserved as failure evidence. Changing Case E-specific first-layer index to 21, re-ran onfixed in a **completely new run directory**, exit=0, ~180 s; without overwriting the previous two results. Raw logs and small samples of three averaged fields see , while large VTKs remained only on temporary Colab and disappeared with the session after stop.

For the five centerlines of empty domain at x=5, 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 450, 495 m, z=2, 5, 15.9 m, height-by-height velocity and resolved k TI=sqrt(2k/3)/|mean speed| data, domain-face momentum proxy quantities and plots see , . At x=100/200/300/400 m: model-free 2 m velocity / inlet velocity at same height was 0.455/0.428/0.434/0.483, and for the model after physical ground index correction was 0.737/0.597/0.550/0.575; corresponding model at 15.9 m was 1.050/1.058/1.068/1.067 (varying less than 10% along 500 m). Along the fetch, 2 m still visibly decreased from 1.049 at inlet x=5 to 0.550 at x=300. Resolved 2 m TI increased from 0.039 at model x=5 to 0.174 at x=300; model-free went from 0.048→0.331. **Neither mean wind speed nor TI remained unchanged**; although the wall law mitigated near-ground attenuation, it did not satisfy Gate 1 requirements. More importantly, only advection and density/3 proxy fluxes were extracted from averaged VTK, lacking instantaneous storage, top/lateral fluxes, molecular/SGS and bounce-back components; 10% control volume closure for ground resistance was not completed. Hence, clearly judged as **Gate 1 did not pass**; halted per Lead's gate, not running Case E urban or Case A, and providing no new MAE/FAC2.

Parameters: Case E z0=0.024 m cited from AIJ C05_5.pdf PDF p. 2 Table 1; κ=0.40 is design hypothesis. CFD VTK origin z=−20 m, ground solid center index 20 / physical 0 m, first-layer fluid center index 21 / physical 1 m, based on halfway wall position first-layer y1=0.5 m, ln((0.5+0.024)/0.024)=3.083438. `def_ground_first_fluid_z=21solver_wallmodel_caseE_indexfix_r13.diff`, still default-off, unpublished. All Colab sessions for this task were stopped, and final check of global sessions showed only others' sessions. Account balance across this round went from ~1381.84→1371.06 CU, with other billed sessions, so the difference cannot be attributed to this task; estimated to be cumulatively within 15 CU based on three empty-domain runs of ~180 s each and short channel times for this task, with no claim of exact billing. CRC/HPC was not used in this round.

## 10-14 23:22–23:50 Continuation 4: R10a Inflow, 200 m Lateral Empty Domain (US Eastern)

Lead ruled Gate 0 passed via the 10-14 Continuation 4 assignment; earlier statements of "Gate 0 failed" in previous sections were records at the time, not to be taken as current status. This round modified only within the authorized scope: compile switch default-off, ground first-fluid index converted from `flat_ground_lbmu-origin_lbmu.z` and grid spacing, verified index=21 in test Case E log; converted z0=0.024 m to lattice units; second-layer version calculates stress using stored velocity of the fluid cell above the first layer, with wall distance 1.5dx. First-layer version has distance 0.5dx, κ=0.40 hypothesis. Specular swap 9↔16, 11↔18 and building bounce-back unmodified; κ, z0 not adjusted to fit data. Version diff: . This remains a flat-ground-only prototype; the second layer reads stored velocity from the previous step, not the second-layer collision velocity of the same step.

Parameters of the three independent empty-domain cases were identical: configured core domain 500×200×270 m, 1 m grid (solver log showed that after top sponge extension, computational grid was actually 500×200×470, averaged VTK core output 500×200×270); westerly wind, no buildings, profile.dat, VK TI=0.1621, L=100 m (hypothesis, carried over from R10a), inflow_only=true, face_mode=TARGET_INFLOW, 31000 steps, last 20000 steps averaged 500 times. First model-on compilation failed at a missing string concatenation `+` in lbm.cpp, not yet solved; after correction, compiled and solved in new run directories `on_first_fix` and `on_second_fix` (return codes 0 each), without overwriting failed directories or old results. Model-free solve return code 0. Three wall-clock times were 440.66, 443.91, 443.88 s, respectively. Raw build, solve logs, and small files are in ; all averaged-field large VTKs left on temporary machines, session stopped after extraction.

Averaged across five lines in the center region at y=40/70/100/130/160 m, with denominator being profile.dat inlet wind speed at the same height. 2 m ratios at x=200/300/400 m: model-free 0.555/0.624/0.648; first-layer wall law 0.748/0.761/0.790; second-layer wall law 0.694/0.753/0.792. 15.9 m ratios: model-free 1.086/1.128/1.124; first-layer 1.076/1.121/1.136; second-layer 1.076/1.119/1.134. First-layer 2 m resolved isotropic TI proxy was 0.239/0.217/0.206; second-layer 0.254/0.215/0.217; model-free 0.332/0.279/0.248. This proxy contains only resolved k output from VTK. Plots, point-by-point. Single-factor attribution cannot be made to the previous weak TI, narrow-domain case.

According to Lead's new velocity gate, the 2 m ratios at x=200–400 m for both models are below the 0.85 lower bound; 15.9 m at x=300–400 m exceeds ±10% relative to inlet (although its own variation along this section is relatively small). First-layer TI decreases along the fetch, no longer monotonically increasing, but the velocity gate has clearly failed. A 15% closure between time-averaged control volume inlet−outlet−top fluxes and actual model force was not performed: averaged VTK alone cannot provide the required instantaneous fluxes and time-averaged integrals of model force; this item was not evaluated and cannot substitute for the velocity failure. **Gate 1 did not pass, and per task prohibitions, Case E urban / Case A or z0 sensitivity were not launched; there are no new MAE/FAC2.**

This round used one A100 in private Colab session `luw-wall-cont4`; other billed sessions ran during execution, so the account balance difference of 1368.82→1359.85 CU cannot be attributed to this task; three 7.3–7.4 min solves and compilation totaled ~23 min, estimated at ~2 CU based on this session's A100 rate (not a bill). After this round, `colab stop` succeeded, and private sessions had no sessions of ours; two other people's A100s remained in global, no action taken. Cumulative CU for the task has no dedicated accounting and can only follow the estimates from previous sections, without claiming accurate accumulation. No supercomputer used, not published.

## Continuation 4 Supplement: Literature Boundaries for Second-Layer Matching Height (10-14, Informed by Lead)

- Malaspinas & Sagaut (2014) took the tangential velocity at the second off-wall node in an LBM wall model to solve wall stress, then reconstructed distributions at the first node; it supports the algorithmic comparison of "sampling velocity at the second layer, applying at the first layer", but does not prove that this prototype will improve empty domain. Based on card, print pp. 32–33 §4.2.
- Asmuth et al. (2021) compared first-cell instantaneous, same-height averaging, and second-cell paired with temporal filtering; the latter mitigates log-layer mismatch, but first-cell underestimation and second-cell gradient overshoot remain. Existing `on_second_fix` reads stored velocity from the previous step, which is **not** temporal filtering according to this equation, and cannot be called reproducing ESG. Based on card, article 105111-6–9, Eqs. (29)–(30), Fig. 2, Table I.
- Shin, Yang & Howland (2025) distinguish velocity filtering from raising matching height: the two target different mismatch sources; no universally optimal layer count is provided. Based on card, pp. 12–14 §3, pp. 26–27 §5/Fig. 16. In this round, the second layer is merely a comparison, not presumed better.
- Existing  only supports fetch-wise comparison of mean velocity and resolved k TI; the report does not provide time-averaged values of first-/second-layer wall stress and near-wall gradients, nor does it close momentum budget, and therefore existing plots **cannot** be used to determine the matching height mechanism. If diagnostics continue, wall stress, mean velocity profiles, and near-wall gradients must be reported side by side; if instantaneous velocity sampling at the second layer still shows significant mismatch, testing the second layer with the aforementioned temporal filtering can be conducted separately within the total budget, but requires independent execution and accounting, and must not be regarded as completed. Currently Gate 1 still has not passed, and urban cases will not be launched per original gates.

# Clearance of LUW Ground Wall Model Design (10-14 20:30)

Decision I made: Reviewed 's ideas, conditionally cleared implementation and three tiers of verification (Colab ≤15 CU).
- Scheme: Ground specular reflection + first-layer neutral log-law tangential body force (Guo force) replacing halfway bounce-back; buildings untouched; default off. Basis: Asmuth 2021 card CFJREQTQ (p. 3 §III, p. 4 Eq. 19); Haussmann 2019 card UAJ8VJH3 (pp. 3287–3290); Han FDR 2021 card S2IAE6TM (p. 18 §5); Spinelli 2024 card PFWN9I2H (Tables 4–7). Case E ground z0=0.024 m: AIJ C05_5 PDF page 2 Table 1.
- Additional conditions: y1=0.5 dx hardcoded; if specular reflection conservation fails twice, switch to moving wall "slip velocity" alternative (use only one); check Case A's z0 following parameter rules first, and if not found, mark as hypothesis and perform ×0.5/×2 sensitivity; if empty-domain gate (15.9 m fetch variation ≤10%, momentum budget closure 10%) does not pass, do not proceed to urban cases; do not tune κ, z0 to fit error.
- Why: Liang Hu 10-14 "Push ahead"; sampling and configuration reasons were already ruled out in Rounds 11 and 12, and the remaining near-ground attenuation can only be tested via the wall model.
- Cost of being wrong: At most ~15 CU and one day; all local modifications, not published, original results untouched.
- Not submitted for review: Belongs to internal prototype, not external conclusions, not large-scale computation; if results are to be written as "wall model improves reproduction", submit for review according to rules (--count 6).

Supplementary note 20:40: ideas supplemented DESIGN.md according to digital twin wind tunnel line experience (simultaneously measure mean wind speed and turbulence intensity in empty domain; item-by-item tangential momentum budget, must prove ground resistance predominantly comes from model force rather than residual bounce-back, otherwise cannot claim z0 controls profile). Consistent with the above approval conditions and stricter, execute per supplemented version,  remains unchanged.

Supplementary note 22:30 (Decision I made): Two LUW kernel specular attempts failed (Px dropped 52%/89% at zero force), Lead read the diff and determined it was a mapping error (first time used distribution coming from above fhn[9]=fhn[15]; second time averaged, retaining half of bounce-back). According to the implicit bounce-back of Esoteric-Pull, the correct local specular is pairwise swapping 9↔16, 11↔18 after load_f. Therefore, modified my own rule of "switch to moving wall if failing twice": perform a third attempt following the exact formulation first, and switch only if it still fails. Reason: Failure cause pinpointed; moving wall has separate issues with back-calculating wall velocity. Cost: ~1–2 CU.

Supplementary note 23:30 (Decision I made): Gate 0 judged passed (after pairwise swap, zero-force is conserved, point-by-point identical to HEAD, log-law wall force closes within ~4%; initial 0.15% drift in FP16C is startup transient). Gate 1 initial run failed (2 m wind speed / inlet 0.55–0.60), but clarified that empty-domain conditions were incorrect: used default VK TI 0.05 instead of R10a's 0.162, lateral span only 64 m; criteria were also erroneous — profile.dat is not a log law of z0=0.024 (inlet U2/U15.9=0.75, equilibrium 0.68), equilibrium expectation for 2 m wind speed is ~0.96 times inlet. New criteria: 2 m ratio at x=200–400 m falls within 0.85–1.05, 15.9 m variation ≤10%, TI at 2 m no longer increases monotonically; budget simplified to time-averaged inlet−outlet−top fluxes ≈ ground model force (within 15%). Added 2nd-layer sampling comparison (basis: Malaspinas & Sagaut 2014 card VV2FSXRQ print pp. 32–33; Asmuth 2021 card CFJREQTQ article 105111-6–9; Shin et al. 2025 card CXEWT5EB pp. 12–14, 26–27 pointing out no universally optimal layer count — comparison only). First-layer index changed to automatic calculation. Budget raised from 15 to 20 CU.. Cost: ~5 CU.

Supplementary note 10-14 23:53 (Decision I made): Continuation 4 empty domain (R10a inflow, lateral 200 m) first-layer / second-layer wall law 2 m ratio stabilized at 0.75–0.79 (model-free 0.56–0.65), below the 0.85 gate; 15.9 m acceleration of 12–13% also existed without model, being a property of the domain itself. Back-calculating 2 m / 15.9 m ≈ 0.52, equivalent z0 ~0.2 m (~8 times the set 0.024). Next steps: (1) verify height datum (wall surface may be at physical 0.5 m, affecting 2 m wind speed by ~6–7%); (2) add near-wall subgrid length damping variant, based on Spinelli 2024 card PFWN9I2H (print pp. 3240–3243, 3249), Asmuth 2021 card CFJREQTQ (p. 13 §VI), Mason–Thomson original card NR_mason_thomson_1992 (Eq. 9 journal p. 54, n=2 journal p. 58; original paper pointed out that merely changing mixing length cannot significantly eliminate log-layer mismatch, journal pp. 60–62 — thus comparison only); (3) relax my self-imposed gate of "do not run urban without passing empty domain", run Case E once using first-layer wall law for diagnostics only, without claiming improvements externally. Reason: Near-ground wind speed has reached a stable plateau, and effects in the city are worth observing. Case A deferred. Cost ~4–5 CU, still within 20 CU total.

# LUW Ground Wall Model Round 13 Continuation 5 (Internal Diagnostics, Do Not Publish)

Time: 10-15 00:46 EDT; baseline HEAD dd438c1, source code modified only in the copy within this directory. The Lead has ruled Gate 0 passed, empty-field Gate 1 not yet passed, and specially permitted one urban diagnostic; this report does not treat urban results as having passed the gate or as paper replication.

## Height Datum (Source Code and Run Logs)

| Object | Basis | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inlet profile.dat | `setup.cpp:5938–5948, 5951–5969, 5997–6019`, `profile_speed_lbmu(pos_z,ground_z)` looks up table using `units.si_x(pos_z-ground_z)`; in empty field ground index 21, VTK origin z=−20 m | Profile applied based on height above physical ground, not height above wall halfway position; inlet physical z=2 m takes 2 m value from profile. Original table lowest sample is 1.25 m; z=1 m is not used for inlet normalization. |
| Urban measurement points | Script reused with this run; actual mask at z=10 m has IoU=1.0 against (+1,+1,0) m | Official measurement points at physical z=2 m; VTK origin z=−20, local XY geometry plus (+1,+1,0) m, did not change z to 2.5 m. |
| Numerical wall position | `setup.cpp:5811–5818, 5997–6004`; `kernel.cpp:1501–1509,1545–1565`; empty field log `Ground wall first fluid index=21` | Solid center global z=20/physical 0 m; first-layer fluid center index 21/physical 1 m; halfway wall surface at physical 0.5 m. Wall-law first layer matching y1=0.5 m, ln((0.5+0.024)/0.024)=3.083438. |

In one sentence: **Physical coordinate registration has no new bias (measurement points remain at physical 2 m); the effective wall surface of the wall law/bounce-back is raised by 0.5 m relative to the wind tunnel ground, so the distance from the wall at physical 2 m is 1.5 m; if merely applying the equilibrium log law with z0=0.024 m, the velocity under the same wall stress is about 6.40% lower than at 2 m from the wall.** This is merely a geometric height sensitivity estimate, cannot be treated as a measured correction for actual non-equilibrium flow, and alone is insufficient to explain the roughly 20% deficit in the old empty field.

## New Variant and Empty Field

Revised diff: `solver_wallmodel_cont5_final.diff`. `GROUND_WALL_SGS_DAMP` can be additionally enabled only when the existing first-layer wall law is active; in SUBGRID collisions, the original Smagorinsky coefficient is reduced by ; here z_wall=(relative first-layer index + 0.5)Δ, limited to the first 8 cells near flat ground, without modifying κ=0.40, Case E z0=0.024 m, wall-force formula/reflection, and building boundaries. `CsΔ` is back-calculated from the existing coefficient 0.76421222=18√2(CsΔ)². This is an **implementation hypothesis of Mason–Thomson type mixing length**, original card pending provision by LitWiki, cannot be called a faithful reproduction; κ is a project design assumption. Spinelli 2024 card print pp.3240–3243, 3249 provides motivation regarding limitations of standard Smagorinsky at smaller y+; Asmuth 2021 card 105111-13 §VI discusses near-wall excessive dissipation, which cannot be used to prove this variant correct.

After the first build, OpenCL C compilation failed (spliced into generated code with `#if defined(...) && defined(...)`); after fixing it to a single `#ifdef GROUND_WALL_SGS_DAMP`, it was run in a brand new remote directory. Failure logs were retained, without misrepresenting numerical failure via exit code. The new variant completed 31,000 steps, with sampling over the last 20,000 steps every 40 steps. The initial extraction included z=1 m whereas profile.dat lowest is 1.25 m, causing extraction to fail, but VTK was already output; extraction was recovered using from the same completed field, absolutely without re-running for replacement. saves U, k, TI averaged across five spanwise lines for x=5–495 m, z=1–60 m; z=1 m is not used for input ratio.

To obtain a complete control across the same height range, no-model and first-layer wall-law runs were additionally rerun in **independent remote directories** with the same 500×200×270 m core domain, 1 m, TI=0.1621, L=100 m (adopting R10a's assumptions), inflow face only, and the same 31,000/20,000 step window, both with exit=0, last 500 samples; , two copies. No-model results re-verified the x=200–400 m ratio of the old `cont4_outputs`, and the first layer also re-verified old results. Actual computational height includes an upper sponge of 470 cells, while averaged VTK outputs the core 270 cells; SGS coefficients were modified only in the collision path where the model was enabled.

x (m) | No-model U2/Uin2 | First-layer U2/Uin2 | First-layer + damping U2/Uin2 | Damped TI2 (resolved proxy) | Damped U15.9/Uin15.9
:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:
100 | 0.574 | 0.793 | 0.814 | 0.265 | 1.061
200 | 0.555 | 0.748 | 0.768 | 0.234 | 1.075
300 | 0.624 | 0.761 | 0.788 | 0.225 | 1.124
400 | 0.648 | 0.790 | 0.775 | 0.208 | 1.135

After damping, x=200–400 m still did not reach the original gate of 0.85–1.05 for the 2 m ratio; at 15.9 m, x=300–400 m still exceeded the inlet by +10% (which also occurred in the no-model case). Therefore, **Gate 1 has still not passed**. Figure is the complete semi-log mean velocity profiles for x=100/200/300/400, z=2–60 m; two reference lines for z0=0.024 m anchored at U(15.9)=3.9286416 m/s (physical z and z−0.5) are used solely for shape diagnostics, not solver equilibrium solutions. Full raw 1 m grid points are in JSON; z=0 is solid and cannot report fluid velocity. TI=sqrt(2k/3)/|mean U|, containing only resolved k. The τw/ρ back-calculated from mean U1 is merely a proxy for the non-linear wall law and cannot replace the time average of step-by-step actual wall forces; the new variant did not achieve inlet–outlet–top–ground 15% control volume closure. At x=200/300/400 m, this proxy is 0.0371/0.0410/0.0433 m²/s² for the first layer, and 0.0348/0.0380/0.0374 for the damped variant; the corresponding z=1–3 m velocity gradients are 0.721/0.665/0.679 s⁻¹ for the first layer, and 0.772/0.743/0.714 s⁻¹ for the damped variant; interpreting this together with the mean velocity plot, one cannot claim momentum balance passed based on the proxy.

## Case E Urban (Lead Special Permission, for Diagnostics Only)

The damped variant was not run on urban, because its empty field still did not reach 0.85. Only another run of **first-layer wall law, without damping** was conducted following the approved R10a base configuration: westerly wind 270°, PF 500×500×270 m, dx=1 m, TI=0.1621087892, L=100 m, inflow face only, 31,000 steps, 500 samples over the last 20,000 steps, TKE output; shows 117,500,000 cells, effective first-layer index 21, OpenCL success, all steps completed, exit=0; single-run wall clock 1118.03 s. The solid in the new field at z=10 m has IoU=1 with the STL mask (+1,+1,0) m; registration was chosen by this offset rather than by picking errors. Same points and same statistical basis.

Group | Quantity | No-model MAE / r / simulation-to-wind-tunnel mean ratio | First-layer wall law MAE / r / mean ratio
:--|:--|:--|:--
80 points | S | 0.1401 / 0.7838 / 0.8211 | 0.1517 / 0.7836 / 0.9544
80 points | S* | 0.1160 / 0.8009 / 1.0565 | 0.1485 / 0.8122 / 1.1968
Near-wall 50/51/52/54 | S* | 0.3454 / 0.7514 / 0.2506 | 0.2944 / 0.8676 / 0.3612
Open street control 4/39/44/75 | S* | 0.1025 / 0.7801 / 1.0257 | 0.1356 / 0.9279 / 1.3146

Point-by-point changes and raw dual-offset data are additionally in . Among the 80 points, S* increased at 64 points and decreased at 16 points; the near-wall cluster improved but remained very low, while the open cluster overshot. Upwind local U2/Uin2 at x=25/42 m rose from 0.737/0.519 in R10a to 0.945/0.781 with the wall law; U15.9 remained unchanged at approximately 1.0. Empty-field steady plateau and urban errors are not equivalent gates; the model increased the overall scalar MAE by 0.0325, so AIJ improvement cannot be claimed. Urban raw fields were only on the temporary Colab machine and were shut down after extracting small files, without moving large VTKs to the local machine.

## Execution and Budget

Colab A100 standard GPU private session `luw-wall-cont5` ran from 10-14 23:55 to around 10-15 00:45 EDT, and only this session was stopped by this task; verified that its name is absent from private `sessions` and global `sessions`, while other shared sessions remained untouched. Account balance during this period went 1358.70→1344.29 CU, but other A100/CPU sessions were billed concurrently; **14.41 CU is the total account change, not this task's consumption**; this task is estimated at approximately 4–5 CU based on ~50 minutes of a standard A100 session and previously observed rates (not an exact bill), which along with prior approximate figures in reports remains within cumulative 20 CU. The initial generated kernel macro error did not trigger duplicate urban submissions, and all outputs have separate directories. Not run on HPC, no source code or results published or released externally.

Recommendations for next steps: Stop tuning κ/z0 based on urban MAE. First check whether the position datum requires moving the physical wall surface back to 0 m, and obtain the same-control-volume budget of step-by-step ground forces, other boundary fluxes, and storage; then evaluate simultaneously using the empty-field gate and urban near-wall/open areas. Case A is deferred (did not receive launch requirements this round).

# Supplementary Note on Original Literature Basis for Near-Wall SGS Damping in Cont 5 (Internal Experiment)

Associated record: ; source diff: `solver_wallmodel_cont5_final.diff`. Does not replace original run records, data, or source code; this supplementary note adds no new computations.

| Check Item | Original Literature / Present Implementation | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original mixing length | Mason & Thomson (1992), Eq. (9): (journal p.54, PDF p.4); neutral boundary layer baseline `n=2` (journal p.58, PDF p.8). Original text did not directly write `Cs·Δ` in Eq. (9). | Setting far-wall `l0` to `Cs·Δ` is the mapping hypothesis of this prototype. |
| LUW implementation | The `GROUND_WALL_SGS_DAMP` branch in `solver_wallmodel_cont5_final.diff`: `z_wall=(wall_layer+0.5)Δ`, only the first 8 cells near flat ground. | The implementation uses `κ z_wall` and **does not add `+z0` from the original formula into the denominator of the mixing length**; it is merely a Mason–Thomson type control, not a term-by-term faithful implementation of Eq. (9). `z_wall` is defined according to the halfway wall surface; κ=0.40 is a design assumption of this project. The original formula and code cannot be stated as identical. |
| Original applicability limitations | Excessive near-wall mean velocity gradient and log-layer mismatch see journal pp.53, 58–60 (PDF pp.3, 8–10); varying `n`, length, or resolution did not significantly eliminate it, and simply increasing mixing length may suppress resolved turbulence and elevate the mismatch region (journal pp.61–62, PDF pp.11–12). | The original paper studied rough-wall LES, which does not prove that modifying this coefficient in LUW-LBM can preserve the profile; no further corrections will be added based on this to game the gate. |
| Present empty-field results | Table and : for the damped version, U2/Uin2 at x=200/300/400 m is 0.768/0.788/0.775, below the 0.85 gate; U15.9/Uin15.9 at x=300/400 m is 1.124/1.135, exceeding inlet by +10%. | Compatible with the original paper's caution that "merely changing mixing length does not necessarily eliminate mismatch," but this original conclusion cannot be taken as causal proof for the failure of this test case; empty-field Gate 1 has not passed, and momentum balance has not closed either. |

, itemized page numbers see table above; this document does not modify the knowledge base. This variant is a completed, sub-standard internal control; Case E's Cont 5 urban diagnostic used the first-layer wall law without damping, and the two must not be conflated. Case A remains unlaunched.

# Equilibrium Log-Law Empty-Field Check (Internal Experiment, Do Not Publish)

Time: 10-15 09:28 EDT. Outputs only in this directory. Conclusion: The first-layer ground wall law did not preserve the specified equilibrium log law; the true ground-model time-averaged wall force and control-volume closure were not measured, so the model cannot be claimed to be validated.

## Reproduction Inputs and Provenance

LUW HEAD dd438c1; in newly created , restored missing build files from local Git HEAD, and applied existing . The initial trial run revealed that this diff **did not** include the previous round's `setup.cpp` ground first-layer index initialization; thus, although the model switch compiled, the ground index remained the default 1 and could not serve as with-model results. The original trial run, logs, and samples are retained as and were not overwritten. Subsequently, setup index initialization was patched in from existing , and startup logs confirmed `Ground wall ... first fluid index=21, z0 lattice=0.024`; corrected source code is at , run package `eqlog_corrected_inputs.tar.gz`, which only fixed existing code missed by the run harness without altering the wall law itself. The no-model control group used the initial run's ; both control groups built and solved with exit=0, 31,000 steps, sampled every 40 steps over the last 20,000 steps, A100 40GB.

The empty-field STL retained only the flat ground base composed of 12 triangular facets from the original test case (the last 12 of the original 9210 facets, lateral boundary trimmed from 2022.5×1996.5 to 500×200), without buildings; configuration is identical to cont5 at 500×200×270 m, dx=1 m, an upper additional 200 cells of sponge in practice, westerly wind 270°, VK TI=0.1621087892, L=100 m, inflow face only. The only physical input difference is replacing the original `profile.dat` with an inlet log law of z0=0.024 m, κ=0.40 (table linear interpolation at 0.1 m intervals): U(z)=u*/κ ln[(z+z0)/z0], specifying U(15.9)=3.9286416 m/s, yielding u*=0.2418545 m/s. z = height above physical ground; solid cell center 0 m, first fluid cell center 1 m, halfway numerical wall surface 0.5 m; wall law uses y1=0.5 m, which is not identical to physical ground 0 m of the inlet profile. This half-cell datum difference is one of the limitations of this experiment.

## Velocity Evidence

Three components were averaged along 5 spanwise lines y=40/70/100/130/160 m to obtain |U|; 15.9 m values were linearly interpolated from z=15, 16 m; each term was divided by the inlet log-law value at the same height. Raw 1–60 m sampling per meter is in , . The latter is not the initial one with index errors.

x(m) | No-model U2/Uin2 | With-model U2/Uin2 | No-model U5/Uin5 | With-model U5/Uin5 | No-model U15.9/Uin15.9 | With-model U15.9/Uin15.9
:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:
100 | 0.575 | 0.815 | 1.036 | 1.060 | 1.057 | 1.047
200 | 0.595 | 0.785 | 1.031 | 1.053 | 1.050 | 1.045
300 | 0.636 | 0.792 | 1.034 | 1.069 | 1.057 | 1.056
400 | 0.655 | 0.804 | 1.017 | 1.068 | 1.064 | 1.065

The three-point average at 2 m with model for x=200–400 m is 0.794, still 20.6% lower than the inlet, failing to reach this round's gate of 0.90–1.05; the three-point average at 15.9 m is 1.055, varying within 10%. Vertical semi-log plot at x=300 m plots inlet, no-model, and with-model simultaneously; the wall law mitigated lower-level velocity deficit, but did not adhere to the inlet curve. In the field, the wall-law matching height of z=1 m differs from the inlet physical height, and the residual deficit cannot be entirely attributed to the wall-force coefficient.

## Stress and Control Volume: Cannot Falsely Claim Closure

The model equation is τ/ρ=[κ U1/ln((0.5+z0)/z0)]². Substituting the **time-averaged** first-cell velocity yields only a nonlinear stress proxy, not the actual time-averaged integral of step-by-step, cell-by-cell forces: at x=200/300/400 m, this proxy u*=0.186/0.190/0.197 m/s, which is 0.770/0.787/0.814 relative to the specified 0.24185 m/s; arithmetic mean is approximately 0.790. Since 〈|u|u〉≠|〈u〉|〈u〉, these three values must never be treated as the actual time-averaged u* sought in Item 2. Its actual value is marked as unavailable.

Averaged VTK has only mean velocity, ρ, resolved k, and fluid; it lacks step-by-step ground Guo force integrals, complete surface data for pressure and Reynolds/SGS/viscous fluxes, and top/side surfaces as well as storage for the same control volume; the few boundary samples saved by scripts are insufficient to integrate the x=100–400 m control volume. Therefore, the closure percentage of "ground model force integral vs inlet–outlet–top fluxes" cannot be calculated; two items in are null. A proxy containing only mean-field advection and ρ pressure cannot be claimed as a complete momentum balance, and much less can a fabricated closure rate be reported. These two acceptance criteria have not yet been met, and model correctness has not been verified.

## Budget, Files, and Recommendations

Both named Colab sessions have been stopped, verified absent from private sessions; the other 3 shared sessions were untouched. Account balance before the experiment was 1201.48 CU, and 1190.42 CU at the end; concurrently, the other three were billing, so 11.06 CU is the shared account decrease, **not** this task's consumption. Three real solves (of which the first with wall-law index error was discarded) totaled about 1401 seconds of solve + compilation, estimated at ~2.06 CU based on this account's A100 previously at ~5.3 CU/h, plus margins for allocation, download/analysis, which cannot be independently and precisely metered; no evidence was found that this task exceeded 3 CU.

If stress and closure are to be validated next time, step-by-step ground forces, boundary advection/pressure/SGS/viscous fluxes, and storage should be output for a unified control volume in an isolated source code copy, followed by pre-agreed re-testing in an empty field with a corrected half-cell height datum. One must not declare the wall model resolved based on this near-ground wind speed improvement; modified results or source code must not be published externally.

Raw logs: , ; scripts: , ; numerical summary: . Erroneous index files from the original trial run are still retained for audit.

# LUW Ground Wall Model Prototype: Milestone Conclusions and Pause (10-15 00:55)

Decision I made: Round 13 ground wall model prototype pauses here, with no additional computation added; designs, source diffs, and validation results are handed over to the Digital Twin Wind Tunnel line Lead for read-only reference.

## Conclusions (All Based on This Line's Data, No Literature Extrapolation)
1. Implementation is correct: ground specular reflection + first-layer log-law wall force, zero-force conservation, point-by-point agreement with HEAD when switch is off, wall-force momentum closure ~4%.
2. Empty field (R10a inflow, 500×200×270 m, 1 m grid): 2 m wind speed / inlet at x=200–400 m, no-model 0.56–0.65, first-layer wall law 0.75–0.79, adding Mason–Thomson type near-wall damping 0.77–0.79; Gate 0.85 not passed. Vertical profile in 2–20 m exhibits a typical log-layer mismatch shape. Damping is virtually ineffective, consistent with the conclusion of original Mason & Thomson 1992 (card NR_mason_thomson_1992, journal pp.60–62).
3. Height datum: measurement points and inlet are both at physical height, with no registration bias; halfway bounce-back wall surface is at physical 0.5 m, 2 m measurement points are 1.5 m from the wall, about 6.4% lower under the log law, insufficient to explain the deficit.
4. Case E urban diagnostics (first-layer wall law, for diagnostics only): 80-point scalar approximate MAE 0.116→0.149, mean ratio 1.06→1.20; vector MAE 0.140→0.152, mean ratio 0.82→0.95; 4 near-wall points improved (0.345→0.294), 4 open street points overshot (0.103→0.136, mean ratio 1.31). → For AIJ Case E, the ground boundary layer is not the primary source of error; adding ground wall law instead makes open areas overly fast.

## Why Pause
- The evidence required to answer the Lab's question "Can LUW be reproduced and used by us?" is in hand: neither configuration factors nor ground wall law can further reduce Case E errors; the remaining near-ground mismatch belongs to the long-standing problem of LES near-wall modeling (Spinelli 2024 card PFWN9I2H print pp.3240–3243; Shin et al. 2025 card CXEWT5EB pp.12–14, 26–27), requiring replacement of subgrid models, stochastic backscatter, or near-wall mesh refinement, which entails workload at the level of a formal project.
- Cumulative ~15 CU (estimated, other parallel billing on the account).

## Cost of Being Wrong
If low-altitude wind fields (the open-terrain near-ground profile Liang Hu is concerned with) are needed subsequently, this prototype and all data are intact, and restarting only requires continuing from the empty field; no existing results were deleted or altered.

## Restart Conditions
When a formal project requires GPU-LBM of the LUW/FluidX3D type to provide open-terrain near-ground profiles; or when the Digital Twin Wind Tunnel line's in-house code needs to implement similar wall models, using this prototype as the starting point.

## Handover Receipt (10-15)
Digital Twin Wind Tunnel Lead has received it and forwarded it to their three sub-projects (LBM Platform & Validation, Urban Field, In-house GPU Code) for read-only reference; agreed that "ground is not the primary source of error for Case E" and agreed with the pause. Their precursor domain is currently an overlay of "bounce-back + explicit log-law stress," with resistance mainly coming from bounce-back; after unfreezing, this prototype's "local specular reflection replacing bounce-back + first-layer Guo force" will serve as the wall sensitivity starting point; when citing, note the two limitations: 2–20 m log-layer mismatch and ineffective damping. If published externally, disclose modified source code and credit source in accordance with Clause 5 of the FluidX3D license.

## Supplementary Note 10-15 (Decision I made)
Liang Hu asked "whether the wall model is handled well and how to validate it." Previously, the empty-field inlet used profile.dat (not a log law with z0=0.024), making it impossible to distinguish model errors from profile adjustments. Dispatched an additional equilibrium log-law empty-field validation (inlet replaced with a log law of κ=0.40, z0=0.024, U(15.9)=3.93 m/s, remainder identical to cont5), criteria: 2 m ratio 0.90–1.05, profile adheres to log law, model u* ≈ specified u*, momentum budget closed. ≤3 CU. This is the final item before pausing, and results are written back to this record.

## Equilibrium Log-Law Test Results (10-15 09:30, Final)
Inlet replaced with log law of κ=0.40, z0=0.024 m, U(15.9)=3.93 m/s (u*=0.242 m/s), remainder identical to cont5. Results: first-layer wall law **did not preserve the equilibrium profile**—2 m wind speed at x=200–400 m was 0.785–0.804 of the inlet (average 0.794, 20.6% lower; no-model 0.595–0.655), whereas at 5 m it was 5–7% higher, and at 15.9 m about 5% higher; vertical profile at x=300 m was slower than log law below 4 m and faster than log law from 5–20 m, a typical log-layer mismatch shape. u* back-calculated from time-averaged first-layer velocity is ~0.77–0.81 of the specified value (proxy quantity). Of the 20.6% deficit, about 6% can be attributed to the half-cell wall datum (numerical wall at physical 0.5 m), and the remaining ~14% is near-wall mismatch from first-layer matching + standard Smagorinsky on a 1 m grid. Step-by-step wall forces and complete momentum budget were not output, and will not be retrofitted.
Verdict: **Code is correct, physics falls short of standard**; wall model prototype remains paused. Resolution requires changing near-wall treatment (matching at second layer or above + temporal filtering, Asmuth-style distribution reconstruction, or switching to WALE/Vreman type subgrid models), which belongs to formal project workload. Basis: Shin et al. 2025 card CXEWT5EB pp.12–14, 26–27; Asmuth 2021 card CFJREQTQ article 105111-6–9; Mason & Thomson 1992 card NR_mason_thomson_1992 journal pp.60–62.
Errata: `solver_wallmodel_cont5_final.diff` is missing setup.cpp first-layer index initialization; complete diff is `solver_wallmodel_complete_20261015.diff` (notified Digital Twin Wind Tunnel Lead via `--note`). This round ~2 CU, wall model prototype cumulative ~17 CU (est.).

# LUW AIJ Case E Registration Verdict (2026-10-13)

Decision-maker: LUW Sub-project Lead. Basis: , .

- **Accept "xls measurement points XY = raw STL XY, with identical axis orientation", determining that the 3x underestimation is not caused by registration.** Why: The xls explicitly states that the origin is the center of the reproducing area, and the XY center of the raw STL is at (0.75, −2.35) m; the two registrations differ by only 2.5 m, with simulated means 0.111 vs. 0.113, both roughly 3x lower than the wind tunnel (0.34/0.42); only 1/80 points falls inside a building. Cost of being wrong: If the axes are actually different, error figures will need to be recomputed, but the judgment of "overall underestimation" remains unaffected (the mean does not depend on point-by-point registration). No literature basis; based on data from this track.
- **Next step: investigate resolution**: In Round 1, VTK nodes were at z=0.338 m and 3.728 m; the value at 2 m was interpolated from the ground-adjacent node and the layer above, naturally suppressed. Dispatch Round 3: refine grid to ≤1.5 m and perform an inflow profile self-check, ≤8 CU. Cost of being wrong: At most 8 CU.
- Before or after construction cannot be determined from the repository; report both sets without cherry-picking.
