# Gemini 4 Argon Blind Test Scoring (10-14, Lead)

Subject: gpu-gemini (Argon High)'s blind test diagnosis  on "LUW AIJ Case E 2 m wind speed underpredicted" (submitted 10-13). Lead's own predictions were sealed in advance in .
Note: CRC job 1536823 originally intended to compare against predictions failed to launch twice (1536823, 1539640, both environmental issues, solver did not start), so two already completed cases were used for comparison instead: Round 5 (Westerly wind, 1 m, approx. 500 m domain, windward flat ground 49 m) and Round 6 (same as above, windward flat ground 509 m, identical windward length to 1536823).

## Item-by-Item Diagnosis
| Argon's Claim | Actual | Judgment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Near-surface incoming flow significantly decays before reaching buildings (npz verification) | Round 6 flat-ground section 2 m wind speed drops to only 33–53% of input, 15.9 m normal | **Correct** (Lead also discovered independently) |
| 2 m interpolation mixes in near-wall grid points, coarse grid suppresses readings | 3.39→1.86→1 m readings gradually recover | **Correct** (Lead also judged so) |
| setup.cpp 4083/4087 offsets output coordinates by +1 cell | Solid mask confirmed in x, y (IoU 1.000), z not offset | **Mostly correct, Lead did not think of this**; it claimed all three axes offset, z is wrong |
| Immersed boundary described in paper does not exist in public source code | Supplementary Material S5 detailed it, but none of the three solver directories have it | **Correct, Lead did not think of this** |
| Lines 253–254 have `pad_x_factor = 2.0` | No such variable in file | **Fabricated** |
| kernel.cpp lines 1344–1348 are Smagorinsky | Actually at lines 1723–1737 | Line numbers wrong |
| 1536823 is 2022×1996 full domain, 100k steps, dx=1996.5/1996 | Actually 1200×700 cropped domain, 30k steps, dx=1.000 | **Misread configuration**, the derived mechanism of "sampling jumps to layer 3 grid points" is invalid |
| Compliance: Read-only materials pack | No boundary violations in inventory | Compliant |

## Prediction Comparison (Using Round 6 as the case closest to 1536823)
| Item | Argon | Lead (Sealed) | Actual (Round 6) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| After Construction MAE | 0.145–0.185 (center 0.162) | 0.15–0.22 | 0.157 —— Both within interval, Argon center closer |
| Before Construction MAE | 0.115–0.145 | 0.13–0.19 | 0.196 —— Neither hit, Lead missed by less |
| Near-surface decay | Partially disappears | Partially alleviated, does not disappear, upstream 2 m is 50–80% of input | Did not disappear, flat-ground section 33–53% —— Both correct direction, both underestimated severity |
| Mean | 0.28–0.34 | — | 0.302 —— **Hit** |

## Overall Evaluation
- Got 4 major diagnoses right, among which 2 (coordinate offset, missing immersed boundary) were not thought of by Lead and carry practical value; coordinate offset has been confirmed by data and incorporated into formal metrics.
- Has 1 instance of fabrication (non-existent variable name and line numbers), 1 instance of misreading key configuration, and 1 instance of wrong line numbers. Fabrications were concentrated in "giving citations", while the overall direction of reading code was correct.
- Predictions: After Construction MAE and mean were hits, Before Construction was missed, near-surface decay underestimated. Roughly on par with Lead.
- Recommendation: Argon can be used for code/data diagnostics, **every citation with line numbers must be spot-checked**; its references must not directly enter decision records.

Scope: Official arXiv v2, journal public page and its directly linked supplementary PDF, and current public refs of GitHub hweifluids/LatticeUrbanWind. Did not contact authors, create issues, or download experimental data outside the repository. CRC 1536823 is still monitored separately per existing ; this report does not replace its post-processing.

| Item | Verified Content | Source (Natural Page / Exact Location) | Not Yet Found / Limitations |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S1 File | The journal's "Appendix A. Supplementary data" direct link provides MMC S1, downloaded 7,261,428 bytes, 15 PDF pages, SHA256 `[已隐去]_MMC_S1.pdf`, PDF pp. 1–15 (in-text numbering 53–67) | Page 53 of arXiv v2 only points to publisher's additional attached documents; official arXiv TeX source package (downloaded) has no supplementary text. |
| S1 Content | S1 is "Kriging boundaries constructed from lidar", time matching ±2 min, horizontal grid spacing 0.0005°, stratified target heights typically 50–750 m; not the AIJ Case E configuration. S4 gives LBM/LES, S5 gives immersed boundary. | `Han2026_MMC_S1.pdf` PDF pp.1–3 / in-text pp.53–55 (S1); PDF pp.6–10 / in-text pp.58–62 (S4–S5). | Paper Case E | Selects westerly wind, uniform 1 m, 80 2 m measurement points, normalized quantity U/Uref, MAE 0.143. The article only refers to Uref as "reference wind speed", without specifying the concrete height/value in this section; Fig. 1(b) shows inflow and geometry, exact domain boundaries cannot be inferred from the figure. | [arXiv v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.04516v2) natural PDF pp.11–12 / in-text pp.11–12, §2.3.1, Fig.1; local | Complete Case E x/y/z domain coordinates and exact Uref height are not found in this section of the article or the supplementary PDF, unable to prove that cropped domain r4crc is strictly the identical paper test case. |
| LUW-v2.8 | The paper's data statement claims release version used is LUW-v2.8, and states the repository has end-to-end files. The public LUW repo only shows `main` and `pre-[已隐去]-v2.8LatticeUrbanWind_repopre-release` corresponding to the paper's LUW-v2.8; current repository has a version provenance gap. Note that 's "v2.8" link points to ProjectPhysX/FluidX3D (2023), not LUW-v2.8. |
| Repository Case E Materials | Contains `CaseE(Niigata).xls`, , and `conf.luwpf`. The configured full domain is x=0..2022.500153 m, y=0..1996.500092 m, z=0..270 m, angles include 270, `cell_size` left blank, `gpu_memory=4000`; these are example default inputs, not the paper's 1 m westerly frozen deck. | [HEAD configuration](https://github.com/hweifluids/LatticeUrbanWind/blob/dd438c1c68664980a92460e4778f18f36be3f47c/examples/example_ProfileResearch_noDEM/conf.luwpf#L4-L29); local same path | No configuration labeled "paper Case E west 1 m", dedicated configuration for Case A validation, or paper Uref definition file was found. The xls Inflow/profile can define our normalization choice (existing report 15.9 m, 3.9286416 m/s), but does not equate to the paper explicitly specifying this height. |
| Near-wall and IBM | Paper Table 1 states impermeable no-slip for ground/buildings, stepwise reconstructed regularized IBM direct forcing; S5 describes three-point delta kernel and multiple direct forcing (Eqs. 33–38), S4 states building walls are implemented using S5's IBM. In the current HEAD FluidX3D setup, the bottom layer and some building/terrain voxels are marked as solid with `TYPE_S`, and code contains voxel no-slip and ground flags. | [arXiv v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.04516v2) p.10 Table 1; [Supplementary PDF](https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S2666165926002152-mmc1.pdf) PDF pp.9–10 / in-text pp.61–62; [HEAD setup.cpp](https://github.com/hweifluids/LatticeUrbanWind/blob/dd438c1c68664980a92460e4778f18f36be3f47c/core/cfd_core/FluidX3D/src/setup.cpp#L5170-L5212) | These static code evidences are insufficient to confirm the full wall operator of the branch run by 1536823, nor are they sufficient to treat TYPE_S and the paper's IBM as the same numerical boundary. Method matching can only be claimed after having its build macros, execution logs, and version lock. |

Summary: S1 has been obtained from the journal's official link, but mainly describes Guangzhou lidar → boundary Kriging, not providing the full Case E configuration; public LUW Git refs did not find the SHA corresponding to what the paper calls LUW-v2.8. Paper Case E can currently confirm westerly wind / 1 m / 80 points / 2 m / MAE, but domain, specific Uref measurement, and wall implementation are still insufficient to claim strict reproduction. When results from 1536823 are out, they can serve as a "cropped domain HEAD comparison under specified assumptions", but the results cannot be directly labeled as a reproduction of the paper's v2.8.

# Submission for Review Notes: LatticeUrbanWind Reproducing Han 2026 AIJ Case E Results (2026-10-14)

## Proposed Conclusions (Pending Review)
1. Using public code LatticeUrbanWind HEAD dd438c1 (termed LUW-v2.8 in the paper, public repository lacks this tag), following the paper's settings (Westerly wind, uniform 1 m), AIJ official-scale computational domain (approx. 500×500 m, windward flat ground 49 m), 80 2 m measurement points against "After Construction, Westerly wind" wind tunnel data yield MAE 0.1425, r 0.80, comparable to the paper's 0.143 (Han 2026 arXiv 2607.04516v2 p. 12)——**reproduced the paper's AIJ Case E results at the metrics level**.
2. The early three rounds being "simulated approx. 3 times lower" (MAE 0.17–0.31) primarily originated from conditions mismatched with the paper: Northerly wind, 3.39/1.86 m grids, LUW example 2 km domain.
3. LUW's flat ground (voxel bounce-back, no roughness/wall function) cannot maintain the inflow near-surface profile: on windward flat ground within approx. 50–150 m from inlet, 2 m wind speed drops to 33–53% of input, while 15.9 m maintains 99–104%. Extending windward flat ground from 49 m to 509 m shifts MAE from 0.1425 to 0.157 (Round 6).
4. Public code setup.cpp (lines 4083, 4087) offsets output VTK coordinates relative to STL by (+1,+1,0) cells, confirmed by solid mask IoU 1.000; z is not offset.

## Known Reservations
- Measurement quantity: Wind tunnel uses thermistor anemometer scalar average wind speed; simulation takes the magnitude of the time-averaged velocity vector (will be lower in wake regions).
- Computational domain position self-determined by centering based on "approx. 500 m" (assumption); official sources did not provide exact coordinates. Rounds 5 and 6 have different averaging periods (141 s vs. 256 s).
- Paper Table 1 and Supplementary Material S5 describe regularized delta kernel immersed boundary, but none of the three solver directories in the public code contain this implementation.
- Measurement point XY = raw STL XY, coaxial (assumption; xls writes the origin as reproduction area center, STL is centered).
- Uref=15.9 m inflow wind speed: Explicitly stated in official xls; Han Fig. 1(d) wind tunnel point 37≈1.18, point 16≈0.55 match xls After Construction Westerly wind column 1.169, 0.535 (Lead read figure).

## Upstream Inflow Profile Diagnostics

From 21 spanwise sampling points across x=750–1250 m, y=1990/1960/1900/1800/1600 m (upstream of building area) in the final time-averaged VTK, linearly interpolated vertically to z=2, 15.9 m. profile.dat specifies U(2)=2.964 m/s, U(15.9)=3.92864 m/s.

| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1990 | 3.197 | 4.009 | Near inflow boundary, 2m is ~8% higher than input; 15.9m is ~2% higher |
| 1960 | 2.357 | 3.997 | 2m has dropped to 80% of input |

The latter is not strictly a same-height 2 m comparison, used only to isolate the effect of wall-adjacent/solid interpolation. All 80 points have values; in the new z=2 m interpolation, 6 points have at least one horizontal corner suspected of being solid.

| Grid / Value | Vs. Wind Tunnel Before Construction: Simulated Mean / Observed Mean; MAE; r | Vs. Wind Tunnel After Construction: Simulated Mean / Observed Mean; MAE; r |

Scripts ,  can recompute small samples and metrics.

Judgment: Improvement is significant after refinement and extending averaging; near-ground interpolation/resolution is likely an important factor, but because the two parameters changed simultaneously, it cannot yet be attributed in isolation. Residual near-ground underestimation aligns with the rapid decay along the trajectory of upstream 2 m profile, most likely involving ground boundary / roughness or inflow maintenance settings rather than being explained solely by xls registration; building state mismatch is also not ruled out. Recommended to conduct low-cost empty-domain profile decay and same-grid fixed-window / same-window fixed-grid controls before judging solver accuracy; currently, wind tunnel replication cannot be claimed.

# LUW AIJ Case E Round 5: Official-Scale 500 m Domain Westerly Wind 1 m (10-13 19:41 EDT)

Status: Colab A100 40 GB single card completed 20,000 steps and 275 average samplings, exit code 0; session has stopped and sessions has no activity. At the final check of this round, CRC job 1536823 was still queued; once completed, its post-processing will take priority, and this run is not its replacement.

## Basis, Settings, and Limitations

- AIJ official Tominaga et al., "Cross Comparisons ... Part 2", PDF pp. 1–2 (Niigata section, Table 1): proposed A (60m), B/C (18m); wind tunnel thermistor anemometer measured scalar wind speed at full scale 2m; official CFD comparison domain approx. 500×500×300m, ground z0=0.024m log law, building smooth wall log law. Note that p. 2 of the paper has another definition for its CFD wind speed ratio using "inlet wind speed at the same height"; here, following the mandate, normalization uses the 15.9m inlet velocity explicitly stated in row 2 of repository xls `Results`, without arbitrarily changing to 2m inlet normalization. Han 2026 arXiv 2607.04516v2 p. 12: Westerly wind, 1m, 80 points MAE=0.143; it has not been verified whether public HEAD is LUW-v2.8, nor whether it is the same computational domain.
- Fresh repository clone commit `dd438c1c68664980a92460e4778f18f36be3f47c`, only modified new copy `conf.luwpf` and the last 12 triangles of the STL peripheral flat ground base; the first 9198 building triangles kept geometric uncut. Solver source code was not modified. PF clipping x=[760,1260], y=[750,1250]m, original STL corresponds to x=[-250.50008,249.49992], y=[-250.60004,249.39996]m (based on the **assumption** that PF=raw+(1010.50008,1000.60004,-0.10)m); windward edge to westernmost building is 49.0m, east, south, north edges to buildings are approx. 46.5, 48.6, 52.1m. Building range PF x=[809.00006,1213.5001], y=[798.60004,1197.9]m; 80 measurement points xls XY range x=[-133,125], y=[-94,112]m, all falling within the domain. Rectangular boundary and centering principle are **assumptions** given to realize the official "approx. 500m", not official exact coordinates; windward buffer is only 49m, so near-inlet building interference is possible.
- Kept original conf's si_z_cfd=[0,270]m, base_height=20, z_limit=250; actual solving grid is 500×500×470=117,500,000 cells (including extra 200 layers of upper region), not 75,000,000 cells. `angle=[270]` means Westerly wind (log Downstream BC +x), `n_gpu=[1,1,1]`, `mesh_control=cell_size`, `cell_size=1.0`. `run_nstep=20000, purge_avg=11000, purge_avg_stride=40`. Log 1s=78 steps, averaging time 11000/78=141.0s, flow-through time for 500m at Uref=3.9286416m/s is 127.3s; real near-surface windward speed is slower, so this is not a criterion to guarantee full dynamic convergence across the entire block.
- xls XY=raw STL XY, same orientation, continuing the **assumption** of the previous round. Primary focus is on After Construction data from official documents (STL maximum height 59.9m including proposed 60m building), with Before Construction reported simultaneously; `Uref=profile.dat|time-averaged velocity vector interpolated at 2m|/Uref`, whereas the thermistor measures average scalar velocity, which are not completely identical quantities in wakes, so it cannot be claimed to strictly reproduce the paper's MAE.

## Execution and Verification

Scripts: , . Build `make Linux -j2` returned 0, 27.06s; GPU A100-SXM4-40GB. Solving log effective settings angle=270, 1m, 20,000 steps, 11,000 steps averaging, 275 samples; average field VTK 1,350,000,360 bytes, retained in terminated temporary VM, therefore only small JSON of 80 points and solid fitting was downloaded, original VTK not retained. Final `solver_r5.exit`: `exit=0 wall_s=736.33 peak_gpu_memory_MiB=20027`; log estimated GPU core usage 9565MB, reported MLUPs approx. 5420 (actual step rate during statistics phase approx. 23 steps/s). Actual account balance 1489.68→1488.57, difference 1.11CU; initial usage showed no parallel allocation, ending with no activity. Spent less than 8CU.

Accidental manual trigger at startup  is a running snapshot,  is the final raw log (possibly missing the initial few seconds),  and  retained raw small files; local ,  are analysis results.

## Coordinate Offset (VTK Zero-Velocity Solid vs. STL z Cross-Section)

Using a grid of x=35..465, y=35..465m for cell-by-cell comparison, excluding the last 12 base faces of the STL. Zero velocity is only a solid proxy, not a direct voxel marker: at z=10m cross-section, when exactly adding 1 cell to each of x/y and adding nothing to z, actual zero velocity is 5996 cells, STL predicted 5996 cells, intersection 5996, IoU=1.000; at the same cross-section (+1,+1,+1) predicted 6443, intersection 5996, IoU=0.931. At z=2m, (+1,+1,0) IoU=0.99994 (54047/54050); at z=20m, both z options are 1.000 (the shape at this cross-section does not differentiate along height). Therefore, **data supports VTK offset (+1,+1,0)m relative to STL, and does not support uniformly adding 1m to z as well**. Simultaneously retained (0,0,0) and (+1,+1,+1)m columns requested by the mandate; the latter must not be mislabeled as geometric correction.

80 points, Westerly wind W, 2m; each column based on the same 80 points, MAE and Pearson r, mean ratio = simulated mean / wind tunnel mean:

| VTK offset relative to STL | After MAE | After r | After Mean Ratio | Before MAE | Before r | Before Mean Ratio | Points outside 8-corner all-fluid |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| (0,0,0)m | 0.147842 | 0.801441 | 0.786411 | 0.203152 | 0.238903 | 0.961413 | 2 |
| (+1,+1,+1)m (task requirement, but unsupported by z) | 0.131855 | 0.830884 | 0.946870 | 0.199658 | 0.279528 | 1.157580 | 1 |
| (+1,+1,0)m (supported by solid mask) | 0.142526 | 0.799003 | 0.806878 | 0.197999 | 0.209045 | 0.986435 | 5 |

Coordinate correction supported by mask yields After MAE≈0.143, close to Han 2026's value of 0.143; differences remain in geometric state, measurement quantity (scalar vs. vector), boundary/wall, domain, and code version, so **it is only numerically close and cannot be called a successful strict reproduction**. Across the 3 columns, wind tunnel After average is 0.432828; simulated means are 0.340381, 0.409832, and 0.349239, respectively. Measurement points include fluid-solid mixed interpolation, particularly under the supported offset where 5 points are not entirely fluid; one should not choose the seemingly better +z 1-cell column as the "corrected" result.

## Windward Zone Profile and Assessment

Upstream building-free zone local domain x=5, 15, 25, 35, 42m, spanwise y=100..400m/30m averaged over 11 points; x=42m is only 7m from the western edge of the buildings, possibly already influenced by the building pressure field, and cannot be called an infinite open field. Ratio of actual velocity at each height to input profile (2m input 2.964m/s; 15.9m input 3.9286416m/s):

| x distance from west boundary (m) | 2m | 15.9m |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5 | 1.050 | 1.024 |
| 15 | 0.851 | 1.020 |
| 25 | 0.680 | 1.021 |
| 35 | 0.528 | 1.020 |
| 42 | 0.434 | 1.019 |

After shortening the peripheral flat ground, the 2m incoming flow still dropped from 105% near the inlet to approx. 43% immediately before the buildings, whereas 15.9m remained at approx. 102%. The 42% reported in Round 3 came from a different Northerly wind and different upstream position; although values are similar, it cannot be considered a strict difference under identical conditions. **Windward near-surface decay did not noticeably disappear**; this run alone cannot judge the original 2km domain being too long as the main cause, and it is more worthwhile to check the LUW near-surface boundary / inlet maintenance mechanism. The official log-law ground differs from LUW voxel bounce-back. To attribute this to domain length, one should wait for CRC 1536823 with identical wind direction, grid, and averaging window to complete before comparing; the 49m buffer in this case itself makes boundary interference a risk.

Scientific conclusion: With this version and the official-scale small domain, the After metric values can come close to the paper's 0.143, but it is not a strict reproduction; near-surface profile decay remains significant. It is recommended that the Lead recheck the source and mask, and only use wording like "successful reproduction" with Liang Hu after review.

# LUW Case E Post-Round 6 Zero-Compute Cross-Check (10-14 00:55 EDT)

Basis: , and of repository HEAD dd438c1. Neither Colab nor CRC was started this time, and the original results were not modified.

Aligning id=1..80 of the two CSVs point by point, taking the identical coordinate correction (+1,+1,0)m supported by the geometric mask, the After W column, and the 15.9m inflow Uref. Among the 80 points, after extending the upwind domain, simulated values at 57 points decreased and at 23 points increased, with a mean difference r6b−r5 = −0.046969 (dimensionless) and a median difference −0.039050; r5/r6b MAE 0.142526/0.157099. After removing 5 points where any of the 8 interpolation corners in either run was not fully fluid, among the 75 points, 55 points decreased and 20 points increased, with the mean 0.369250→0.319029, and MAE 0.128079→0.143746. Hence, the overall decrease was not solely caused by these 5 fluid-solid mixed points; this remains an observational correlation between two different averaging windows and cannot be taken as a univariate causal effect of domain length.

For r5, at 5/15/25/35/42m inside the inlet, the ratios of 2m to the input are 1.050/0.851/0.680/0.528/0.434; at the same locations, 15.9m is around 1.02, and strong near-ground gradients appear right from the edge of the inlet. For r6b, at 50/150/250/350/400/502m inside the west boundary, the 2m ratios are 0.528/0.333/0.381/0.409/0.433/0.347 respectively; the 15.9m ratios are 1.035/1.041/1.031/1.012/0.993/0.914. The long-domain curve is non-monotonic, so an exponential decay rate cannot simply be fitted, nor can the value at x=502m (7m from the building) be treated as an open-terrain value.

Direct source code evidence: `setup.cpp:5901–5911` reads profiles by height above ground; `:5914–5934` initializes all-fluid velocities; `:5936–5995` fixes profiles on outer sides and top boundary, leaving the westerly downstream outlet open; `:5948–5954` marks the bottom layer z=0 as TYPE_S; `:6077–6078` calls initialization and boundary settings. Log `solver_r6b.log:87–89,126–129` shows no DEM, flat ground, profile ground z(SI)=20m, boundary mapping complete, and flux correction disabled. Thus, maintaining the profile at the inlet boundary does not mean 2m is maintained in the interior; flat ground without DEM and the bottom solid condition are credible targets for subsequent diagnostics. However, relying solely on these source lines cannot prove whether the decay is specifically caused by wall friction, building pressure, inlet corners, or averaging time, nor can the official log-law ground be treated as the same boundary as the solid bottom layer in this test case.

Suggested next minimal control: first run the same r5 short domain with identical source code/geometry/wind direction/1m configuration, keeping only `run_nstep=31000, purge_avg=20000` consistent with r6b, to recheck the 80-point differences and upstream profiles, isolating the averaging window confounder; a more direct ground mechanism experiment would be an empty flat terrain with the same profile / same two domain lengths, taking profiles along x at various heights (at least 2, 5, 10, 15.9m) sampled sufficiently far from boundaries/buildings, but this is a new scientific experiment design and requires prioritization by the Lead. Do not chase 0.143 by changing Uref or altering offsets.

Frontline assessment: lengthening the upstream domain is correlated with an exacerbated underestimation of 2m simulation and is not explained by the 5 mixed interpolation points; near-ground inlet preservation / ground boundary mechanisms have not yet been isolated, so it cannot yet be asserted which factor is the primary cause.

# LUW AIJ Case E Round 7: Scalar Velocity Metric (10-14 01:23 EDT)

## Inputs, Run, Budget
Using identical original repository HEAD `dd438c1c68664980a92460e4778f18f36be3f47c` as r5, westerly wind 270°, PF x=[760,1260], y=[750,1250] m for the 500×500 m outer base cropped domain, z=[0,270] m, 1 m mesh, single GPU A100 40GB. Script copied the original example and only modified conf and base STL (first 9,198 building triangular facets untouched); relative to r5's conf, only changed `output_tke_ti_tls=[]` to `[tke]`, `run_nstep=20000` to `31000`, `purge_avg=11000` to `20000`, with stride=40 unchanged. Build , exit flag `solver_r7.exit`.

Colab session `luw-aij-r7` already stopped; querying with independent config showed no active sessions for this task, with subsequent account usage at 0 activity. Global balance moved from 1482.60 to 1479.01, a difference of 3.59 CU; another A100 session was billed concurrently during execution at a global rate of 10.60 CU/h, so this difference cannot be entirely attributed to this round; wall-clock time of solving for this round × single A100 at approx. 5.3 CU/h corresponds to approx. 1.68 CU, plus approx. 1 minute of compilation/extraction, keeping the total within the 4 CU hard limit. No extra rerun.

## Quantities and Provenance
AIJ official 's APPENDIX (final page of main text of PDF) defines hot-wire anemometer readings as the temporal mean of instantaneous scalar velocity, standard CFD output as the magnitude of time-averaged velocity vector, and proposes the approximate conversion `S_exp = sqrt(S_CFD²+2k)`; this formula is not a strict identity between instantaneous scalar mean and second moments. Here, `S_CFD=|<u>|`, obtained at 2 m points by trilinearly interpolating the three components of average velocity first and then taking the magnitude; `k` is the trilinear interpolation of the TKE scalar from the averaged VTK; program `setup.cppS_exp<|u(t)|>`, so (c) **cannot be calculated directly**. The primary observation column is xls Results (After Construction) westerly W; Before W is for reference only. `xls XY=raw STL XY, same axial direction, PF=raw+(1010.50008,1000.60004,-0.10)m` remains an assumption, not an officially certified strict registration.

Comparing independent building cross-sections with the mean-field zero-velocity solid proxy (the `fluid` field of the averaged VTK is also used for measurement point corner identification): at z=10m, taking VTK relative to STL (+1,+1,0)m yields 5996/5996 exact overlap, IoU=1; if z also +1m, IoU=.93062; at z=2m, (+1,+1,0) IoU=.99994. The solid proxy supports offset (+1,+1,0) as the primary group; original coordinates (0,0,0) are presented in parallel. In the primary group, interpolation corners of 5/80 points fall partially within solid, and 4 out of the 13 low-speed points do so; numerical values in this portion require particular caution.

## 80-Point Metrics

The new solid mask has an IoU = .9375 at the rooftop z = 64 m for a (+2,+2,+2) m offset; none of the three sets of interpolation points contained mixed fluid-solid corners. The domain, geometry, profile.dat, 2 m grid, output, and averaging settings completely followed Round 8, with only four VK inflow configurations added in conf.luwpf; no solver source code modifications were made. Startup logs verified TI = .1468, L = 100m, inflow_only = true, and TARGET_INFLOW in effect only on west.

Parameter basis: The official Inflow table row z/b=2 (H=64m) gives U_H=4.491m/s, k=.652m²/s². Using the isotropic equivalent formula TI=sqrt(2k/3)/U_H yields .146803, hence setting `vk_inlet_ti = 0.1468030617`. Lines 3154–3164 of the source code read a single scalar for `vk_inlet_sigma` using `atof`; lines 962–966 multiply the point-by-point local mean velocity by a fixed TI when TI takes precedence, preventing inputting the official height-by-height sigma profile from conf; this round cannot claim to be identical to the official full turbulent inflow profile. `vk_inlet_inflow_only=true; vk_inlet_face_mode=TARGET_INFLOW`, verified by source lines 3232–3242 and the west face log. `vk_inlet_l=100.0 m` continues to use the Round 8 default value: the official Inflow table has no integral scale; checking the local AIJ guide yielded no Case A-specific scale, so 100 m is an assumption, testing only this single scale without providing a measured scale range. Other defaults—isotropy and 256 modes—remained untouched. Therefore, "modifying only inflow turbulence" simultaneously altered both amplitude and injection faces, making it impossible to separate the independent effects of the two.

Sampling: AIJ official z/b=.125, i.e., 4m; z/b=1.25, i.e., 40m; central vertical profile; Han Table 2 writes z/H, which is a clerical error per the Lead's verdict. U/U_H is the three-component mean vector magnitude (assumption); k/U_H² is the resolved-scale mean velocity fluctuation, excluding SGS; TKE FAC2 excludes observations with |k/U_H²|≤.05. FAC2 spans a factor of 0.5 to 2; the primary q column uses |simulation − observation|≤.25, NRMSE=RMSE/observed range, both being assumptions undefined in the paper; the JSON also includes relative 25% q and mean-normalized NRMSE. The order in each cell is FAC2/q/r/NRMSE/TKE FAC2/TKE r; q and NRMSE across the paper, this round, and Round 8 may not share the same basis.

| Measurement plane | Han Table 2 | Round 8 | Round 9 |

Relative to Round 8, the changes in TKE r are +.131, +.461, and +.570 respectively; FAC2 changes are +.346, +.276, and +.200. Mean wind speed did not degrade: velocity r improved by +.094/+.033/+.040, and FAC2 improved by +.033/+.100/+.136; however, this is merely a single-run result of simultaneously changing both TI and the inflow face, so it is inappropriate to conclude which one was effective. TKE correlation coefficients remain lower than the paper's .640/.880/.530, especially .447 at 40m. The upstream centerline x is 4–296m from the west inlet and 332–40m from the western building edge; resolved k/U_H²: z=4m goes from .0109 (x=4) to .0209 (x=296), non-monotonic; z=40m goes from .0265 to .0264, largely maintained; z=64m goes from .0334 to .0320, of the same order of magnitude as the official rooftop inlet .0323; z=128m drops from .0478 to .0417. The full series and plots are found in and . At x=296m, it is already 40m close to the building and may be influenced by flow around it, so it should not be regarded as pure inflow decay.

Execution and budget: Independent run directory, private Colab config; clone, commit verification, make Linux -j2 succeeded; launched in background with exclusive lock; short exec keep-alive and segmented log downloads; after `extract_caseA_turb.pycolab stop`, account-level `sessions` showed no activity, usage rate=0. Plots, point-by-point, metrics, raw , `solver_caseA_turb.exit`; all of the above are in this report directory. It must not be claimed as a strict reproduction of the paper's LUW-v2.8, because the version, turbulence profile, scales, etc., have not been verified.

One-line judgment: Modifying the rooftop equivalent TI and injecting only on the windward face significantly improves Case A turbulent kinetic energy and mean velocity metrics, but the TKE spatial correlation still does not reach that of the paper; this lightweight configuration experiment is worth archiving, but insufficient to declare a successful reproduction.

## Scope and Parameter Sources
The baseline is the Round 7 public repository HEAD `dd438c1c68664980a92460e4778f18f36be3f47c`, westerly wind 270°, 1 m mesh, PF x=[760,1260], y=[750,1250] m, original base clipped, z=[0,270] m, 31,000 steps, averaged every 40 steps over the last 20,000 steps, output `[tke]`. Round 7's and are itemized. The four runs only changed conf under the same cloned and compiled solver, with no modifications to source code or buildings. The VM came with a single NVIDIA L4 23 GB; after the initial A100 request returned 503, switched to L4; raw logs, all exit flags were 0, and the averaged VTKs were left on the stopped temporary VM after extracting 80 points. Round 10's newly added local scripts, configuration generators, point data, metrics, and plots are all in .

The official AIJ Inflow table lines 2–13 give , and table notes give ZR=250m, UR=7.8m/s. z=15.9m corresponds to z/ZR=0.0636, and neighboring rows 0.05 and 0.10 both have k/UR² of 0.010; hence k=0.6084 m²/s². Repository gives Uref=3.9286416m/s at 15.9m, rooftop reference height cannot be repurposed; TI=√(2k/3)/Uref=0.1621087892. Source `setup.cpp` lines 3154–3164 only parse scalar TI, sigma, and L, hence the full-height turbulence profile cannot be matched via conf alone; lines 962–966 multiply fixed TI by local mean velocity. R10a's `vk_inlet_ti=0.1621087892`, `vk_inlet_inflow_only=true`, `vk_inlet_face_mode=TARGET_INFLOW` (source lines 3220–3242); startup log lines 130–139 confirm west-side-only injection and TI=.1621. `vk_inlet_l=100m` is an assumed continuation of the default: AIJ Inflow table provides no integral scale, and checking the local AIJ guide yielded no verifiable Case E-specific value. This round is not a strict implementation of the official height-by-height turbulent inlet. R10a simultaneously changed TI and injection faces, making it impossible to separate their respective roles.

R10b only sets `flux_correction=true` on top of R10a; its log lines 129–134 report `S_in=S_out=19930.895, net_before=0, avg_dU=0`, hence this correction was a no-op. R10c only sets `si_z_cfd=[0,300]m,z_limit=280mz_limit` on top of R10a as companion parameters rather than an independent test. R10d only sets total steps to 51,000 on top of R10a, averaging over the last 40,000 steps; converted per the verified 78 steps/s, averaging took 512.82s, while R10a's last 20,000 steps were 256.41s, both exceeding twice the reference wind speed flow-through time of 500/3.92864=127.27s. For each case, stride=40, expected samplings are 500/500/500/1000 times respectively, verified by logs. Doubling the averaging window required extending the total duration to maintain the same starting point after the initial 11,000 steps.

Quantities and conventions: Observations are the official Results (After Construction) westerly W 80 points (primary); Before W is presented side by side. Uref uniformly adopts the inlet 15.9m velocity; `S` is the magnitude after trilinear interpolation of the three-component mean velocity at 2m; `S*=sqrt(S²+2k)` is the scalar wind speed approximation from AIJ `C05_5.pdf` Appendix; k comes from LUW-sampled resolved scales, excluding SGS. Coordinates adopt the prior assumption `xls XY=raw STL XY`, PF translated by (1010.50008,1000.60004,-0.10)m; each round is checked against STL cross-sections based on zero-velocity solid proxies at z=2, 10, 20m; at 10m, (+1,+1,0)m IoU=1, (+1,+1,+1)m IoU=.9306, hence the primary metric is (+1,+1,0)m; (0,0,0)m is shown side by side. Four solver exit=0: L4 wall-clock a/b/c/d were 2735.18/2735.04/2960.31/4628.57s respectively, peak GPU memory was 9756/9756/10364/9756MiB respectively; all passed `coordinator.doneluw-casee-r10-ideas` has been stopped, and global sessions check confirms they are no longer listed; remaining sessions do not belong to this task and were not touched. Raw logs, independent session configurations, and scripts for this round are retained in .

# Comparison of Mainstream LBM Software (10-14, Lead cross-check of Gemini and Grok online verifications)

Independently verified by two reviewers (commissioned: Reviewer E · Gemini, Reviewer F · Grok). Lead spot-check: FluidX3D has no wall function (line 454 of its DOCUMENTATION.md), XLB is Apache-2.0 (knowledge base card). The "Discrepancies" column lists points where the two sources disagree.

| Software | Developer | Type / License | GPU | Wall model | Atmospheric boundary layer / Urban wind | Discrepancies and notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PowerFLOW | Dassault SIMULIA | Commercial | Yes | Yes | Gemini: supports urban wind; Grok: product page only shows building HVAC applications, no ABL inflow model seen | Discrepancy in capabilities, vendor confirmation needed |
| XFlow | Dassault SIMULIA | Commercial | Yes | Yes | Same discrepancy as above | — |
| ultraFluidX | Altair (Altair is now part of Siemens) | Commercial | NVIDIA CUDA only | Yes (three types) | Official description states "building and environmental aerodynamics"; Grok considers this cannot be equated with ABL support | — |
| ProLB | CS Group et al. (France) | Commercial | In progress | Yes | **Most thoroughly validated in literature**: Feng et al. 2021 JAMES 13(3) e2020MS002107, includes temperature/humidity, buoyancy, Coriolis force, canopy, neutral/convective/stable/cloud-topped convective ABL benchmarks and Shinjuku, Paris urban cases (knowledge base card) | Product page does not mention ABL inflow (Grok); research version has it |
| M-Star CFD | M-Star (now part of Siemens) | Commercial | Yes | Yes (including roughness) | None, specializes in stirred tanks/reactors | Both agree |
| OMNIS/LB | Cadence | Commercial | — | — | — | Listed only in Japanese catalog, unverified if currently on sale (Grok) |
| **Ansys Fluent / Discovery** | Ansys | Commercial | Yes | — | — | **Both agree: No LBM**, GPU solver uses finite volume method |
| OpenLB | KIT et al. | Open source GPL-2.0 | NVIDIA + AMD | Yes | Gemini: has logarithmic wind profile function and urban digital twin test cases | Both recognize wall models |
| waLBerla (lbmpy) | FAU Erlangen | Open source GPL-3.0 | CUDA / HIP | Gemini: Yes (including Monin–Obukhov correction) | Gemini: has waLBerla-wind | Grok did not find ABL |
| Palabos | University of Geneva | Open source AGPL-3.0 | Pre-release | No turbulent wall function in mainline | — | — |
| XLB | Autodesk | Open source Apache-2.0 | Yes (JAX/Warp) | None in mainline | — | Used as benchmark in digital twin wind tunnel track |
| FluidX3D | M. Lehmann | Custom non-commercial license | OpenCL, cross-platform | **None** | None | Foundation of LUW |

Key takeaways: Ansys does not have LBM; FluidX3D/LUW that we use happens to lack wall models, whereas commercial LBMs oriented toward external flows as well as OpenLB/waLBerla all have them. If thermal (thunderstorm) problems are to be pursued, ProLB serves as a precedent already validated in literature. The digital twin wind tunnel track has determined that GPL/AGPL code is read-only and will not be ported.

# Case E Round 11: Local Geometry Verification for Fixed Discrepancy Points (10-14 EDT)

## Evidence and Methods

This round submitted no new solutions and used no Colab/CRC. Read-only on repository HEAD dd438c1's , stripped the last 12 peripheral base triangles, leaving 9,198 building triangles; the z=2m cross-section generated 5,540 deduplicated line segments. Code in ; point values taken from Round 7 (post-construction westerly wind, S*=sqrt(S_CFD²+2k)) in ; the established coordinate assumption is xls XY=raw STL XY, PF=raw+(1010.50008,1000.60004,-0.10)m, VTK solid relative to STL (+1,+1,0)m. Four control points were determined from non-target points according to |Round 7 scalar residual|<0.04, 8/8 fluid corner points, and mutual separation >45m: 44/75/4/39. This is the selection method for control samples, not a randomized group.

Locally for the z=2m STL polygon using and existing , z=2m) this (+1,+1,0)m predicted 54,047 solid cells versus actual 54,050, intersection 54,047, IoU=0.99994; at z=10m IoU=1. Source lines 2385–2445 adopt ray-intersection and inside-outside flipping. **Gray cells are not flags re-downloaded in this round; a small number of boundary cells and non-building zero-velocity cells may still differ.**

Wall distance: For STL, it is the minimum Euclidean distance from the original measurement point to the 2m cross-section line segments; for voxel, it is the distance from the sampling position rounded to the cell center to the **center** of the nearest solid cell, not equal to the wall surface distance. Channel width is the free span (STL) or number of contiguous fluid cells (voxel) between the nearest buildings on both sides along the crosswind direction y at the point's same x position; if a wall is missing on either side, it is recorded as undefined. Upstream inspection slices along the incoming westerly wind at every 1m across 30m west of the point at the same y, comparing only when walls exist on both sides of the STL and the original gap >0; voxel free width = 0 or ≤ half of STL is counted once as "blocked/narrowed". This is an operational definition, does not guarantee the 2D connectivity of that corridor, nor does it equate to causal attribution of wind speed errors. z=2m is located exactly at the existing VTK cell center; "interpolation corner points" in the table are counted per conventional bilinear 4 corners and legacy trilinear 8 corners, with zero-weight corners also included in the legacy count.

## Numerical Table

Residuals are Round 7 simulated scalar S* − After W (both normalized by Uref=15.9m inflow velocity). Width in m; "—" denotes point falls in STL solid or lacks paired boundaries. Actual decimals and upstream flagged x grid slots are in .

| Point | Group | Residual | Wall dist STL / Voxel center | Channel STL / Voxel | Blocked or narrowed ≥ half within 30m west | 2m 4-corner fluid / Legacy 3D 8-corner fluid |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| 50 | Underestimated | −.403 | .84 / 1.00 | 2.60 / 3 | Yes | 4/8 |
| 51 | Underestimated | −.368 | .00 / 1.00 | — / 46 | No* | 3/7 |
| 52 | Underestimated | −.338 | .22 / 1.00 | 27.36 / 27 | No | 3/7 |

| 17 | Overestimated | +.272 | 6.75 / 7.21 | 33.16 / 32 | No | 4/8 |

| 39 | Control | −.000 | 5.41 / 5.83 | 12.52 / 12 | No | 4/8 |

*Original coordinates of 51 happen to fall exactly on the STL cross-section edge: at the original coordinates it counts as "on solid/wall", and 1 of the 4 voxel corners is solid. Because the original STL gap was 0, the position of that point itself was filtered out in the 30m check, so "No" should not be interpreted as absence of wall proximity risk. Point 50 has 3 flagged grid slots upstream (x=178, 193, 203m); Control 4 also has 1 (x=160m); both are criteria on local cross-sections and cannot be taken directly to mean the complete 2D corridor is blocked. Among 50–54, all four points are within 1m of the STL wall, while the other four overestimated points and controls are none within 1m; underestimated points 51/52/54 have solid corners in 3D interpolation, whereas overestimated points have none. Control points were selected by small residuals; group-wise distance comparisons are diagnostic, not independent statistical tests. The original measurement point 50 has an STL narrowest cross-alley of only 2.60m, and the voxel still has 3 cells, **it is not blocked directly at its cross section**; the 0 versus 46 for 51 is a boundary ambiguity where the measurement point lies on the original STL edge line and sampling rounds into the cell center on the other side, and cannot be explained as "voxels creating a 46m boulevard".

## Position and Registration in Paper Fig. 1(c)

Han et al. 2026 arXiv 2607.04516v2 p. 11 Fig. 1(c) (local , enlarged from p. 11 of the official paper): In the figure, westerly wind blows from left to right; 50–54 cluster below the center of the central block, 17 and 23/25 lie above it, and 37 lies between the two zones; this qualitatively matches the relative distribution of current xls points (50–54 y=−45..−19.5m, 17/23/25 y=8..47m, 37 y=−23m). The figure has no coordinate scale/origin, and cannot independently prove the absolute translation/rotation of xls → STL. We did not re-register to reduce errors.

## Judgments and Limitations

These 8 fixed discrepancy points **are not the same type of geometric anomaly**: the four severely underestimated points are concentrated within 1m of the STL wall / in the narrowest alleys and involve 3D mixed fluid-solid sampling; the four overestimated points are 5.10–10.38m from walls, all fluid, with cross-alleys of 18–65m, resembling the controls more closely. Geometric/wall discretization is clearly suspect for the underestimated cluster, but one control point was also flagged by the upstream width criterion, and the overestimated cluster is not near walls; it cannot be asserted as the primary cause of all deviations across the eight points, nor can static footprints distinguish immersed boundaries, inflow, bed shear stress, or adjacent building airflow organization. Differences between the wall mechanism in paper S5 and the voxel bounce-back in public HEAD remain a hypothesis to be further verified; **this round did not isolate its effect experimentally**. It is recommended that if the Lead approves mechanism experiments for the next step, test post-processing sensitivity for 51/52/54 first with "only using all-fluid sampling or displacing ≤1m along the wall normal"; inspect velocity profiles/flow directions for 23/25/37/17 rather than immediately modifying source code.

Verification: Script ran locally with exit 0, generating 12 local plots, CSV, and JSON; raw averaged fields are not local, plots serve only as geometric diagnostics, 0 CUs. The newly produced file with the same name is `_r11_r11v2`. Known formulas and limitations are reproducible in the script.

Starting and ending global balance was 1419.61 → 1412.94 CUs, difference of 6.67, but multiple GPU/CPU sessions ran concurrently, which is not the cost of this task; single A100 at ~5.4 CU/h, 1127s solve estimated at ~1.69 CUs, including ~minute-level preparation and extraction remaining within the ≤3 CU budget, estimation rather than billing attribution.

Coordinates follow the established assumptions: xls XY=raw STL XY, PF=raw+(1010.50008,1000.60004,-0.10) m, VTK sampling horizontally offset by (+1,+1) m, z not offset. Domain-wide independent verification of geometric offsets is in R10a : z=2m IoU ≈ 0.99994, z=10m IoU=1; actual `fluid` flags in this round resulted in 7/8 fluid corners for the original sampling of 51/52/54 and 8/8 fluid corners for 50, item-by-item consistent with R10a point values (recomputed values of S and S* for the 8 points match R10a values, solution is reproducible). Therefore, it cannot be said that all four points suffer from the "containing solid corners" issue. STL z=2m cross-section finds the nearest pedal point using deduplicated line segments, moving along the normal toward the side of the measurement point to 1/2 m from the wall. Point 51 originally fell right on the edge line; flags were used to select the fluid-side normal without choosing sides based on error. The original interpolation applied trilinear weighting to all corner points; "fluid-cells-only" deletes solid corners and normalizes with the remaining non-zero weights; k follows the same rule, S=|<u>|/Uref, S*=sqrt(|<u>|²+2k)/Uref, Uref=3.9286416m/s at inlet 15.9m. S* is merely the official scalar velocity approximation, k excludes SGS. Control points are 5–10 m from walls; forcing them toward wall edges would exceed the ±5m window and alter their locational properties, so normal sensitivity for control points is shifting 1/2 m away from the wall from the original point, not "to 1/2 m from the wall"; these two positional operations cannot be conflated into the same intervention.

The table below shows After Construction W observations and S* (both Uref-normalized); complete S, S*, individual residuals, solid_weight, and coordinates are in . `solid_weight` represents non-zero weights of solid corners in the original interpolation; zero-weight corners are not treated as contamination.

| --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | -- |
| 50 | .4360 | .0122 | .0122 | .0121 | .0116 | 0 | Crosses into solid of opposing wall at 2m, cannot be used for all-fluid interpretation |
| 51 | .5153 | .1961 | .1961 | .2968 | .3830 | .000072 | Original point on STL edge, fluid side determined by flag |
| 52 | .3964 | .0929 | .1351 | .1733 | .2465 | .4499 | Significant fluid-solid interpolation weight |
| 54 | .4955 | .1607 | .1661 | .2072 | .3313 | .0500 | Still underestimated |
| 44 | .2577 | .2929 | .2929 | .2922 | .2909 | 0 | Control point, displacement is not distance to wall |
| 75 | .2577 | .3880 | .3880 | .4065 | .4152 | 0 | Control point |

| 39 | .5352 | .3522 | .3522 | .3326 | .2952 | 0 | Control point, not a small residual in this round |

S* MAE for the four near-wall points: original .3454; fluid-corners-only .3334 (decreased by .0119, ~3.5%); 1m from wall .2885; apparent value 2m from wall .2177, but point 50 at 2m has solid_weight=.208 with only 6/8 fluid corners, requiring separate classification as an invalid all-fluid control. Looking only at the three comparable points 51/52/54: original MAE .3192 → 1m .2433 → 2m .1488, still showing marked discrepancy after 2m. Point 50's original sampling was 8/8 fluid, S* ≈ .012; its narrow alley is enclosed by walls on both sides, and displacement did not recover wind speed. For the four control points, fluid-corners-only is completely unchanged; +1/+2m normal displacement increased S* MAE from .1025 to .1203/.1375; it cannot be claimed that control points remain stable after shifting, nor can error reduction after displacement be treated as a cost-free fix. The four control points were selected in Round 11 based on R7 small residuals, but R10a turbulent inlet altered S*, so points 39 and 75 in this round are not low-error points and should not be falsely claimed as matched controls. All values and formulas are reproducible via and the small ROI.

Judgment: Mixed fluid-solid interpolation itself explains only ~0.012 MAE across the four near-wall points, occurring primarily at point 52; position sensitivity relative to walls within ±1–2m is significant at 51/52/54, suggesting wall/street geometry and experimental measurement point localization are worth investigating, but causal effects of wall mechanisms cannot be inferred from post-processing displacement. Point 50 was originally all-fluid and nearly stagnant in an extremely narrow alley, especially failing to support that "modifying interpolation can fix the four points." This round introduced no new simulated wall scheme, nor did it alter original wind-tunnel measurement point locations.

results.text:
# LUW Ground Rough Wall Model Prototype Design (Design Only; To Be Implemented Only After Lead Review)

Time: 10-14 20:11 (US Eastern). Scope: Public LUW local read-only verification copy, verified HEAD `dd438c1c68664980a92460e4778f18f36be3f47c`. In this round, solver source code was neither copied nor modified, no new cases were run, and no CU was consumed. During implementation, a new source code copy will be created only in this directory; source code or modified version results will not be published.

## Basis and Applicable Boundaries

| Verified Facts | Usage / Limitations in This Design |
| --- | --- |
| The neutral ABL ground replaces no-slip with Monin–Obukhov wall stress; that paper uses cumulant-LBM and reconstructs the first-layer distribution, near-wall SGS may still be overly dissipative. | Using the neutral log law to compute wall stress has a sound basis, but distribution reconstruction and SGS modification methods cannot be directly copied to our code's BGK/FP16C. |
| WFB adjusts some diagonal distributions pointing toward the fluid interior; evidence is channel Reτ=640/2003. | Candidate momentum exchange scheme; do not extrapolate channel error improvements to urban near-ground wind speeds. |
| Under D3Q19/SRT/Smagorinsky, calculate τw from first-layer velocity and wall distance, subsequently modify boundary distributions and handle near-wall νt; Musker, Werner–Wengle, and Schmitt are selectable. | Numerical architecture closest to LUW; its smooth-wall Musker does not directly replace the known roughness length of Case E. |
| Comparison of channel wall functions and SGS; Smagorinsky may be limited at smaller y+, and the authors' overall preferred choice is not our code's BGK. | Near-wall SGS must be diagnosed separately; it cannot be claimed that switching the wall law will inevitably improve turbulence. |
| Official CFD ground is rough log law z0=0.024 m, buildings are smooth log law, domain approximately 500×500×300 m. | This prototype only takes ground z0=0.024 m; buildings retain the original LUW boundaries, which cannot be called an official full-boundary reproduction. |
| D3Q19/SRT, FP16C, SUBGRID, VOLUME_FORCE are currently compiled and enabled. `stream_collide` computes macroscopic fluid quantities after Esoteric-Pull `load_f`, Guo force is calculated before collision; `z==0` ground is enforced as TYPE_S, buildings are voxelized from STL. | Must correctly handle the even/odd timestep mapping of Esoteric-Pull; ground TYPE_S cannot be kept as no-slip while additionally superimposing wall drag in the same direction. |

The cards are excerpts, with listed page numbers following original printed pages indicated on each card; this is a targeted methodology check, not a comprehensive governance reading of all four PDFs. Paper conclusions and our prototype hypotheses are kept separate.

## Choices and Explicit Non-Choices

Choose "horizontal ground specular reflection (ensuring only non-penetration, no tangential no-slip constraint) + log-law tangential shear force within the first-layer fluid lattice" to **replace** the existing halfway no-slip bounce-back on flat horizontal ground, never superimposing resistance on top of it. Each incoming link at the bottom surface is specularly reflected according to `(c_x,c_y,c_z) → (c_x,c_y,−c_z)` (exact indices and even/odd step reads/writes must be verified link-by-link); this differs from the tangential momentum exchange of the original halfway bounce-back `(c_x,c_y,c_z) → (−c_x,−c_y,−c_z)`. Specular reflection only provides a non-penetration boundary, tangential drag caused by the original bounce-back should be reduced to numerical error, and the rough-wall stress given by the model is the specified ground resistance; buildings and non-planar bottom surfaces still use the old boundaries. Reasons: Asmuth card CFJREQTQ (article p. 3 §III, PDF p. 4) explicitly **replaces** no-slip with ground wall stress, and its p. 4 Eq. (19) uses distribution reconstruction; the "specular + first-layer Guo force" in this design is a prototype **hypothesis** adapted to the existing BGK/FP16C pathway, not the original algorithm of that paper, and must be verified using momentum budget. Haussmann card UAJ8VJH3 (print p. 3290 §2.5.1) provides a wall stress and distribution reconstruction reference for BGK+Smagorinsky, but its smooth wall law cannot directly replace the rough wall of Case E. Reasons: roughness and τw can be specified separately; the current Guo forcing/collision pathway already exists; it does not add a domain-wide GPU 3×float force field and can be calculated cell-by-cell inside the kernel; for FP16C, only the force in FP32 calculations is modified without directly writing compressed distributions. The link implementation of specular reflection requires greater caution than full distribution reconstruction in the first layer of BGK, hence it is listed as a unit test that must be passed first. Alternative: directional diagonal distribution momentum correction from Han FDR card S2IAE6TM (article p. 18 §5, PDF p. 19), but it requires deriving link-by-link coefficients for D3Q19, Esoteric-Pull, and rough-wall τw before use, and cannot be directly ported. Purely "retaining halfway bounce-back + negative body force" is not chosen: ground shear stress would be double-counted; the digital twin wind tunnel line has already observed in Silsoe/Urban Field that the first-layer stress approximation contribution is very small and bounce-back accounts for most of the ground resistance, so z0 did not actually control the profile (internal project experience, not literature proof). Haussmann's full distribution reconstruction and near-wall SGS linkage is a phase-two proposal and will not be introduced concurrently in this round.

## Lattice, Distance, and Physical Quantities

- Applied only to first-layer fluid cells whose immediate bottom neighbor is a `TYPE_S` **global** z=0 horizontal ground cell; global coordinates `z_global=z_local+Oz`, must not be erroneously applied at local z=1 of each GPU subdomain. Inlet/outlet `TYPE_Elbm.positionunits.si_x` conversion. Wall normal is vertical, and force has only x/y components.
- Let the distance of the first-layer fluid relative to the wall surface be y1>0, tangential velocity vector **u**t, air density ρ, κ=0.40 (commonly used constant, **hypothesis**; must be consistent with the inlet log law adopted in the future). Neutral roughness law, `τw = ρ u*²`, horizontal wall stress vector; first-layer volumetric force, where Δz is the actual thickness of the first-layer control volume. Zero-velocity safety branch F=0; z0 must be >0 and y1/z0 sufficiently large, input range validation, log≤0 not allowed. Convert SI physical quantities to lattice quantities first according to the existing `Units` relations of u, x, ρ, t, and then enter as Guo body forces into `fxn,fynFx_lb=−rho_lb*u*_lb²*(ux_lb/|ut_lb|)`, similarly for y. If the effective control volume thickness of the first layer is not 1 lattice unit, replace with the measured thickness. Compute using the currently updated macroscopic velocity, and must not use the initial profile field as a constant.
- Inlet comparison: Case E z0 comes from official tables; velocity normalization Uref fixes repository profile.dat at 15.9 m to 3.9286416 m/s (Round 10 records, lines 6 and 10); z0 is roughness length, not geometric STL ground elevation. Whether `profile.dat` is consistent with the neutral log law of this z0/κ has not been proven. There is no guarantee that "modifying the wall means the original profile must remain constant along the fetch": empty-domain tests must simultaneously record inlet momentum flux, outlet, bed stress, and development section; if non-equilibrium, report the inconsistency, and do not reverse-tune z0 or add arbitrary sustaining forces to fit. There are no verified values in this task for Case A's z0 and inlet scale; when using the same ground wall law, mark as **hypothesis**, keep consistent with Round 9 inlet, and do not claim that AIJ ground roughness has been verified.

## Two Numerical Details That Cannot Be Skipped

1. **Replace bottom tangential no-slip first, then add force; conservation check.** The implementation of `load_fstore_f` in `kernel.cpp` swaps addresses by even/odd steps (1338–1350); ordinary solid neighbor cells in the source code form halfway bounce-back. The prototype needs to establish a specular mapping `c_z -> -c_z, c_x,c_y` for bottom z-non-zero links (a total of ten directional velocities in D3Q19) (exact direction indices to be printed and checked against `c` item-by-item), taking effect only for "fluid ↔ marked ground" links; reflection position, even/odd timestep reads/writes must conform to Esoteric-Pull to avoid read-write races and floating-point distribution loss; building links retain original bounce-back. Note that this is not arbitrarily swapping two `fhn` items after `load_f`: this alters distributions originating from different fluid neighbor cells and is not necessarily conservative. Before implementation, conduct a zero-shear specular reflection test on a small grid to verify that link-by-link mass flux, normal momentum, and tangential momentum are zero; under non-zero shear, the total shear force should be consistent with the body force. If not passed, revert to design, do not proceed to urban cases.
2. **Near-wall Smagorinsky.** Existing `kernel.cpp` 1723–1737 adjusts `w` using non-equilibrium stress; wall force and this SGS effect may combine to cause excessive dissipation. The first version will keep the SUBGRID algorithm and constants unchanged for now, only diagnosing first-layer `nu_t` and recording profiles of ; "keeping unchanged" cannot be claimed as SGS having correct wall damping. If SGS is to be suppressed in the first layer, a switchable damping law must be set up separately and compared independently; it cannot be mixed into a single change together with the wall law. The numerical precision of FP16C also needs sample verification in the first layer; all stress/force calculations use float, recording stability at low speeds and high wind speed upper limits.

## File Modification Interfaces (Implementation Permission Not Yet Given; Estimation Only)

Implementation copy is expected to reside only in  (verify target does not exist first, never overwrite existing results):

| File / Function | Expected Changes | Estimated Added / Modified Lines |
| --- | --- | ---: |
|, `apply_profile_boundaries` for single profile cases and necessary flat ground label preparation | Boundary determination / unit conversion / reading and echoing configuration `ground_wall_model, ground_z0_si, ground_kappa`; default off, old cases point-by-point identical; label only ground plane without mislabeling buildings or DEM | 45–90 |
| `LBM_Domain` compile-time kernel parameters and `device_defines`; `lbm.hpp` when necessary | Pass switches, z0/κ, ground positions or labels as per-domain parameters to kernel; cross-GPU global z mapping | 20–50 |
| `load_fstream_collide` external force accumulation and diagnostics | Precise bottom specular reflection, roughness law local stress, protective branches, along existing `VOLUME_FORCE` Guo forcing pathway rather than an extra permanent F array; updated diagnostic pathways must not alter the model-free old pathway | 70–130 |
| (if enabling compile-time switch), minimal verification scripts / configs (only in wallmodel directory) | Comparison switches, tests, and outputs, without modifying published repository | 50–100 |

Total estimated solver code is about 135–270 lines, verification scripts counted separately; first complete small-grid conservation / multi-card indexing / equivalence tests of old cases with switch disabled, before starting computation. Existing `FORCE_FIELD` domain-wide F buffer should not be repurposed for step-accumulated ground force: allocated in source code `lbm.cpp` 293–302, it has independent function and double superposition must be avoided.

## Phased Verification (Not This Round's Execution Results)

0. Default off: Point-by-point / log comparison with HEAD on identical-grid small cases; when affected by floating-point scheduling, at least mass and velocity statistics must be consistent. Flat plate channel minimal grid: zero-shear specular reflection has zero tangential resistance, pure uniform flow has no penetration; when z0 is enabled, wall stress is opposite to flow velocity, and total momentum budget matches Guo force; boundary tests for z0>0, near-zero velocity, first-layer wall distance, corners, and cross-domain halos. If bottom normal is distorted or conservation fails, do not proceed to the next stage.
1. Empty domain: Along Case E flat ground 500 m, using identical profile.dat and wall settings, simultaneously measure **mean wind speed and turbulence intensity** at inlet, along the fetch, and outlet at 2, 5, 15.9 m (specify TI definition using three-component RMS / mean speed, retaining individual components and k), providing absolute values and ratios to inlet, fetch trends, and time-averaging windows respectively; require both to be interpretably maintained, rather than merely 2 m wind speed being close to input. Report that original model-free 2 m is about 41–52% (prior building domain diagnostics, cannot be taken as a strict empty-domain baseline), and run a true model-free empty domain separately. Additionally, perform an item-by-item **tangential momentum budget** on a section of flat ground control volume: inlet−outlet advective flux, top-bottom / lateral fluxes, pressure action, internal molecular and SGS fluxes, tangential momentum exchange of specular bottom links, first-layer Guo force integral, and momentum storage changes; quantify closure residuals and numerical errors. When wall force is disabled, tangential resistance of specular bottom links should be near numerical zero; when enabled, the integral of bottom model force should match expected `−∫τw dA`, and total ground resistance should be predominantly provided by model force rather than residual bounce-back. If independent contributions of bounce-back and model cannot be measured, or closure is not achieved, it cannot be claimed that z0 has controlled the profile; if empty domain does not meet standards, do not proceed to urban cases.
2. Case E R10a: Westerly wind, 1 m, identical time window / registration (+1,+1,0), inlet TI and original configuration, buildings unchanged; after modification, MAE/r/mean ratio of vector S and scalar approximation sqrt(S²+2k) across 80 points, as well as near-ground fetch; retain list of before and near-wall contaminated corner points, do not select parameters based on isolated MAE values.
3. Case A Round 9: Official z=4/40 m and center profiles, FAC2, q, r, NRMSE of mean velocity and k (according to established definitions and sensitivities); surface z0 source is unverified, do not default Case E's 0.024 m as the official Case A value.

The criteria are that profiles improve interpretably and Case E / Case A show no obvious side effects, without judging model correctness based on single MAE improvements. This prototype does not add any geometric roughness blocks; if roughness block experiments are established separately in the future, periodic layout acoustic tones and boundary reflections must be checked first: the digital twin wind tunnel line once observed a 1.317 Hz peak in its periodic layout case (internal experience, only a risk reminder, cannot be taken as the predicted frequency for this case). The above are merely proposed experiments, not verified results; only after design and actual verification are completed can they be handed over to the digital twin wind tunnel line root Lead for read-only reference.

results.text:
# LUW Ground Wall Model r13 — Gate 0 Ruled Passed by Lead; Continuation 4 Empty Domain Failed

Time: From 10-14 21:15 (US Eastern). Internal prototype only, not published.

## Verified Inputs and Source Code

- The HEAD of read-only baseline  is `dd438c1c68664980a92460e4778f18f36be3f47c`.  Copied and created after confirming the target does not exist, intact, git working tree unmodified. No modification or overwriting of old results.
- In source code, `defines.hpp:17–24MOVING_BOUNDARIES` is currently disabled. `kernel.cpp:1338–1350` is Esoteric-Pull read/write; `1475–1516` computes macroscopic velocity after load; `1686–1747` handles Guo forcing and Smagorinsky. `setup.cpp:5948–5953` sets all z=0 to TYPE_S, with actual first-layer fluid cell at z=1; `lbm.cpp:612–697` uses def_Oz to represent global index for each subdomain.
- Parameter sources: Case E ground z0=0.024 m, AIJ PDF p. 2 Table 1; official Case A  has U and k by height (Inflow lines 34–59), without listing ground z0. Case A was checked in local `Tominaga_et_al_2008_JWEIAguide.pdf`, but its dedicated value was not found; ` pages` located Sim (2015) PDF p. 261, whose Table 28 recounts Case A z0=1.8×10⁻⁴ m, stated as a logarithmic fit to inlet velocity by Mochida et al. (2002). This is a secondary source and cannot yet be claimed as verified by official AIJ. If adopted in the next phase, it must be marked as hypothesis and sensitivity tests for 0.9×10⁻⁴ and 3.6×10⁻⁴ m must be conducted.
- κ=0.40 is the commonly used value hypothesis of the design; halfway wall position is at z=0.5 lattice, first-layer fluid z=1 has y1=0.5 dx: Case E dx=1 m, y1=0.5 m, ln((y1+z0)/z0)=3.083437854; Case A dx=2 m, y1=1 m, if using the aforementioned hypothesis z0=1.8×10⁻⁴ m, ln=8.622733691 (half and double z0 are 9.315790884 and 7.929766462, respectively). Actual physical height of fluid points and wall positions must be re-verified from run logs / VTK; paper values cannot replace numerical verification.

## Gate 0 Current Evidence

Checking item-by-item against source code D3Q19 directions and even/odd addresses of load_f/store_f, 4 static pre-checks ran and passed. It shows that two naive specular reflection formulations (only swapping fhn after load, only changing store direction at the current cell) are not equivalent to cross-cell specular flow for diagonal links; these are structural exclusions, not two conservation tests already performed on OpenCL. It cannot yet be asserted that the complete specular scheme failed, nor can it trigger the branch of "switching to moving wall if actual testing fails twice". The initial test assumption regarding Esoteric-Pull time parity did not hold, so that assertion was removed and re-run; static pre-checks are never counted as mass/momentum conservation verification.

Currently there is no solver diff, OpenCL build, or completed channel / empty-domain test, and none of the three gates have passed; the local CPU machine lacks a clinfo/OpenCL verification environment. Colab has not yet been requested, consuming 0 CU. It is prohibited to refer to this draft or existing old case results as modified wall model achievements.

## Incomplete Items and Conditions

Link-by-link mass, normal momentum, and tangential momentum verification of specular reflection must first be conducted on a real OpenCL small-grid mesh; if conservation actually fails twice, then only use the TYPE_S moving wall pathway as an alternative, and never superimpose Guo body force. Regardless of which path is chosen, it must be verified that default-off is point-by-point identical to HEAD, model drag and bounce-back are measured separately, and a 10% momentum closure of control volume pressure / advection / top-lateral fluxes / stresses / storage is achieved. In Gate 1, the mean velocity and TI at 2/5/15.9 m, 15.9 m change ≤10%, and 2 m improvement for true empty domain without/with model are unverified, therefore Case E/A must not be launched. If Gate 1 does not pass, halt at tier 1 according to the assignment and do not run urban cases.

## 10-14 21:42–21:46 Implementation Progress (US Eastern)

Using PyOpenCL on Colab A100-SXM4-40GB against  even/odd indices, a 24×12×10 D3Q19 SRT small channel kernel was written, periodic xy, z=0 and top solid; this is an **independent small kernel**, not the modified LUW kernel. In the initial launch version, top/bottom boundaries and timestep correspondence were incorrect, resulting in noticeable mass leakage; this was judged as a test fixture error, not counted as a failure of the specular scheme. After correcting to in-place Esoteric-Pull, initialize t=1 writing, first step t=0, and specular on both top and bottom, for 81 steps of zero-model-force uniform parallel flow: total fluid mass 2303.999756→2303.999756, total x-momentum 115.200020→115.200104, total z-momentum approximately 0; zero-shear check passed only for this simplified uniform flow.

However, after adding the Guo force of the inlet stress formula to the same small kernel, the bottom surface computed a resultant force of approximately −0.0121 to −0.0120 per step; total x-momentum 115.200020→114.917236, while the zero-force control remained 115.200104. This difference cannot be explained as approximately equal to the applied cumulative force: the current kernel function's Guo treatment, top/bottom reflections, and momentum definitions have not yet completed an item-by-item budget; code-internal  identities cannot be treated as real dynamic verification of <5%. In particular, it has not been verified on LUW's own OpenCL kernel, nor is there a verified control volume closure for empty domain without/with model. Therefore, **Gate 0 did not pass**, and urban cases should not yet be run; this is not a verified failure of two specular schemes, and does not trigger switching to moving wall. Complete hourly readings: , aforementioned small kernel: . The solver copy remains unmodified, with no solver diff. Colab was proactively stopped, and verified that no sessions remain for this task; total account balance 1395.09→1393.73 CU, but other people's sessions were billed during this period, so 1.36 CU cannot be attributed to this task.

Official Case A `CaseA(1_1_2).xls` Inflow table is actually on lines 3–26 of local sheet (the earlier 34–59 was not this sheet's line numbers); the first 3 heights z/b=0.0625, 0.125, 0.25, which correspond to z=2, 4, 8 m based on b=32 m, U=2.745, 2.935, 3.175 m/s. Performing least squares U=a·ln(z/z0) on these three points yields fitted z0=2.9466×10⁻⁴ m, slope a=0.31018 m/s; in the same order of magnitude as the secondary recounting of 1.8×10⁻⁴ m in Sim 2015. Fitting range is sensitive: expanding to 16/32/48 m yields z0 of 5.6055×10⁻⁴ / 1.6983×10⁻³ / 5.2107×10⁻³ m, respectively; it cannot be said that a single log law fits all heights. If used for Case A in the future, it should be marked as "fitted from official near-ground inlet profile, 2–8 m", with separate ×0.5/×2 runs. In this case, y1=0.5dx=1 m (dx=2 m), ln((y1+z0)/z0)=8.129998; κ=0.40 remains a design hypothesis. Case E y1=0.5 m, z0=0.024 m, by the same formula ln=3.083438. The above are merely paper fits / grid settings, not solver output verifications.

## 10-14 22:05–22:14 Continuation 2: Real Solver Gate 0 Failed (US Eastern)

Per Lead's instructions, only the Guo equilibrium velocity and force term velocity of the small kernel were changed to , without changing the original small kernel's boundary and streaming. A100 test : specular zero-force control in steps 0→80 had mass 2303.999756→2303.999756, Px 115.200020→115.200104; with wall force enabled, Px 115.200020→114.637985, deducting zero-force drift gives −0.562119. Sampled resultant force per step was −0.012117 to −0.011887, which over 80 steps is about −0.95 to −0.97; the actual value was only about 58%–59% of this value, and the **fixture still did not reach the <5% budget criterion**. These are sampled force range estimates, not step-by-step exact integrations; it cannot be blamed that the corrected Guo scheme is already wrong or the specular boundary is already correct.

Directly modified the default-off experimental compile switch in , `lbm.cpp::device_defines`, local specular of z_global=1 in `kernel.cpp::stream_collide` and its existing Guo pathway, and added an independent `WALL_GATE0` small channel driver (modified files see `solver_gate0_attempt2_final_r13.diff`). C++ `-fsyntax-only` and `git diff --check` both passed; the real FluidX3D OpenCL kernel generated using this copy on Colab, 24×12×10 channel, 81 steps, FP16C/SRT/SUBGRID, compiled and ran separately for both specular approaches as well as zero-force / with-force, all exiting with 0. However, exit code 0 does not equal passing numerical gates.

The first attempt was overwriting upward distributions from downward distributions of the same cell after `load_f`: at zero force, Px steps 0→80 went from 112.798279→53.648745 (a drop of 52.44%), and with force from 112.792221→53.291121; bottom zero-force tangential resistance was far from zero. The second attempt averaged upward and downward distributions with identical horizontal velocity and opposite-sign z in pairs to maintain conservation: zero-force Px 110.398316→11.706808 (a drop of 89.40%), with force Px 110.394109→11.702116; almost degenerating into the original halfway bounce-back (original pathway 110.398316→11.690552). Mass changed by a relative magnitude of about 1e-5 in both approaches, Pz was small, but **transverse drag criteria failed both times**. The second scheme was left in the working tree as an unusable failed prototype, not to be used for physical results. Records: , .  is the re-run fixture; its head_path is the model-off compilation branch of the same source code, not a separately cloned HEAD binary, so it cannot yet be claimed that "default-off is point-by-point identical to HEAD".

Pinpointed: the `ground_first_fluid` specular handling inserted after `load_f` in `kernel.cpp::stream_collide` still leaves strong zero-force bottom tangential resistance; suspected to be `store_ffxn/fyn` superimposing shear stress. This is a numerical gate failure of wall flow, rather than an OpenCL compilation or runtime abnormality. According to Lead's rule of "switching to alternative if actual testing fails twice", the next scheme can only be **TYPE_S moving wall velocity replacing force term**, neither retaining current specular plus Guo nor superimposing force on existing bounce-back. Before fluid collision, back-calculate tangential moving wall velocity for each ground solid cell from neighboring first-layer local velocity and specified τw, and update `u[ground]`/TYPE_MS step-by-step; otherwise, a domain-wide fixed moving wall will miscalculate local shear stress. This alternative has not yet been implemented or verified. **Gate 0 did not pass, and Gate 1 empty domain or Case E/A will not be conducted**; there are no empty-domain plots or new comparison metrics.

This independent Colab A100 session `luw-wall-r13-cont` was stopped and verified not in private/global sessions; two other non-task A100 sessions ran concurrently.
