## 10-14 22:26–22:44 Continuation 3: Pairwise Swapping, Re-Verification with Real Kernel (US Eastern)

In the working tree, according to the Esoteric-Pull local mapping pointed out by Lead, pairwise swapped 9↔16, 11↔18, keeping 5 unchanged; 1000 single-step checks with random asymmetric distributions passed on mass and x/y ground fluxes. Separately, a truly clean copy of HEAD dd438c1 (`LatticeUrbanWind_HEAD_gate`) was created via local git clone, without overwriting previous failed results.

In the first round of the real LUW kernel channel (24×12×10, FP16C), zero force still had large Px drift: 110.3983→54.4787 (81 steps). Diagnosis revealed that the fixture top z=9 was still no-slip solid, with only the bottom changed to specular; domain-wide Px decreased due to top drag, and this change cannot all be attributed to the bottom. Subsequently, the top surface was also set to specular in the WALL_GATE0 test branch; although the first compilation succeeded, test macros were not passed from C++ to device, reproducing identical results, which was fixed in `lbm.cpp::device_defines`. The following numbers come from kernels with two-sided specular actually enabled, not counting previous two invalid compilations as success.

FP32 diagnostics (only test build disabled FP16C, without changing production configuration) showed: specular zero-force channel mass remained 2304.00000000 throughout, total normal momentum ~10⁻⁶. In raw step 0→80 after initialization, Px was 110.400002→110.592226, drift +0.1741%, **failing to reach the <0.1% gate starting from step zero**. After the initial boundary transient passed, in step 39→119, Px was 110.600080→110.592118, drift −0.00720%; step 119→199 was only −0.0000146%. These are values achieved only after "pre-warming before taking 81 steps", and the raw 81 steps cannot be quietly claimed as meeting the standard. Logs: .

The same fixture injected a test-dedicated constant bottom force τ=5×10⁻⁵ lattice into the 24×12 bottom lattice cells via LUW's original Guo pathway. In step 39→119, Px difference against the zero-force baseline was −1.105647; the specified force integral over those 80 steps was −1.152, a difference of 4.024%, less than 5%; step 119→199 difference was 4.013%. This is a **constant force pathway check**, which has not yet integrated the true velocity-varying logarithmic stress step-by-step, nor is it a complete control volume budget. Logs: ); limited only to this channel, whole urban settings unverified.

Conclusion / Gates: Specular mapping demonstrated feasibility in channels with pre-warming, FP32, and two-sided slip; there is no need to switch to moving wall alternative solely based on the total Px loss in the initial one-sided fixture. The old conclusion in the preceding section that "the next scheme can only be moving wall" was corrected by pinpointing the top no-slip fixture and missing device macro propagation this time, and must not continue to be cited as final judgment. However, formal Gate 0 is still **not fully cleared**: raw 81 steps of FP16C, step-by-step stress integration of true log law, and independent momentum measurements of top/sidewalls are incomplete, and raw step 0→80 values also slightly exceeded <0.1%. One cannot use 4.0% of test constant force to pose as closure of the model itself; Gate 1 true model-free empty domain, fetch-wise mean velocity/TI, and ground momentum budget have not yet been run, Case E/A has not even been launched, and there are no empty-domain plots or urban metrics. ## 10-14 23:12 Continuation 3 Wrap-Up: Real Model Force Integration + Gate 1 Empty Domain (US Eastern)

Addressing the deficiency in the preceding section that "logarithmic stress was not integrated step-by-step", a cell-by-cell `ground_force` diagnostic buffer was added to `stream_collide` in the test build branch; the initial version mistakenly read linear array slices of logical z=1, reading all zeros, and after verifying using test constant 1234 that the writing side indeed had 288 cells, changed to full-array summation (details see ). LUW OpenCL channel with FP32 true log-law wall force: after pre-warming, step-by-step wall force integral in step 39→119 was −0.865491, ΔPx relative to zero wall force pathway was −0.830785, closure error 4.010%; step 119→199 were −0.851018 and −0.817075, respectively, error 3.989%. Model-off was identical to separately cloned HEAD in the same test fixture, and zero wall force conserved mass. FP16C two-sided specular zero-force step 39→119 Px 110.586184→110.560364, drift −0.02335%; while from initialization step 0→80 it was still +0.14679%, failing the <0.1% without pre-warming. Raw force diagnostic logs , where `mirror_constforce` is a variant name carried over in scripts, and what was actually enabled by `GATE0_DYNAMIC=1` this time was **dynamic log law**, not constant force. Gate 0 satisfies numerical criteria only after explicitly pre-warming for 39 steps; initial transients did not pass and cannot be written as unconditionally passed. Formal production remains FP16C; FP32 is an auxiliary budget test.

Next, ran the **true empty domain**: retaining only 12 peripheral base triangle facets of repository STL, no buildings, westerly Case E `profile.dat`; domain 500×64×270 m, dx=1 m, 31000 steps, last 20000 steps averaged 500 times, model-off / on compiled separately with identical configuration. Both exited with 0, ~180 s each. First-round model-on results were virtually identical to model-off; inspecting actual VTK solid flags revealed physical z=0 was at global index 20, first-layer fluid at 21, whereas model criterion hardcoded `z_global==1`: this is the **specific error location** of `ground_first_fluid` in LUW kernel (`kernel.cpp::stream_collide` after load_f). That first-round "on" actually applied force to the wrong layer inside the base, cannot serve as wall model effect, and was preserved as failure evidence. Raw logs and small samples of three averaged fields see , while large VTKs remained only on temporary Colab and disappeared with the session after stop.

For the five centerlines of empty domain at x=5, 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 450, 495 m, z=2, 5, 15.9 m, height-by-height velocity and resolved k TI=sqrt(2k/3)/|mean speed| data, domain-face momentum proxy quantities and plots see , . At x=100/200/300/400 m: model-free 2 m velocity / inlet velocity at same height was 0.455/0.428/0.434/0.483, and for the model after physical ground index correction was 0.737/0.597/0.550/0.575; corresponding model at 15.9 m was 1.050/1.058/1.068/1.067 (varying less than 10% along 500 m). ## 10-14 23:22–23:50 Continuation 4: R10a Inflow, 200 m Lateral Empty Domain (US Eastern)

Lead ruled Gate 0 passed via the 10-14 Continuation 4 assignment; earlier statements of "Gate 0 failed" in previous sections were records at the time, not to be taken as current status. This round modified only within the authorized scope: compile switch default-off, ground first-fluid index converted from `flat_ground_lbmu-origin_lbmu.z` and grid spacing, verified index=21 in test Case E log; converted z0=0.024 m to lattice units; second-layer version calculates stress using stored velocity of the fluid cell above the first layer, with wall distance 1.5dx. First-layer version has distance 0.5dx, κ=0.40 hypothesis. Specular swap 9↔16, 11↔18 and building bounce-back unmodified; κ, z0 not adjusted to fit data. Version diff: . This remains a flat-ground-only prototype; the second layer reads stored velocity from the previous step, not the second-layer collision velocity of the same step.

Parameters of the three independent empty-domain cases were identical: configured core domain 500×200×270 m, 1 m grid (solver log showed that after top sponge extension, computational grid was actually 500×200×470, averaged VTK core output 500×200×270); westerly wind, no buildings, profile.dat, VK TI=0.1621, L=100 m (hypothesis, carried over from R10a), inflow_only=true, face_mode=TARGET_INFLOW, 31000 steps, last 20000 steps averaged 500 times. First model-on compilation failed at a missing string concatenation `+` in lbm.cpp, not yet solved; after correction, compiled and solved in new run directories `on_first_fix` and `on_second_fix` (return codes 0 each), without overwriting failed directories or old results. Model-free solve return code 0. Three wall-clock times were 440.66, 443.91, 443.88 s, respectively. Raw build, solve logs, and small files are in ; all averaged-field large VTKs left on temporary machines, session stopped after extraction.

Averaged across five lines in the center region at y=40/70/100/130/160 m, with denominator being profile.dat inlet wind speed at the same height. 2 m ratios at x=200/300/400 m: model-free 0.555/0.624/0.648; first-layer wall law 0.748/0.761/0.790; second-layer wall law 0.694/0.753/0.792. 15.9 m ratios: model-free 1.086/1.128/1.124; first-layer 1.076/1.121/1.136; second-layer 1.076/1.119/1.134. First-layer 2 m resolved isotropic TI proxy was 0.239/0.217/0.206; second-layer 0.254/0.215/0.217; model-free 0.332/0.279/0.248. This proxy contains only resolved k output from VTK. Plots, point-by-point. Single-factor attribution cannot be made to the previous weak TI, narrow-domain case.

According to Lead's new velocity gate, the 2 m ratios at x=200–400 m for both models are below the 0.85 lower bound; 15.9 m at x=300–400 m exceeds ±10% relative to inlet (although its own variation along this section is relatively small). First-layer TI decreases along the fetch, no longer monotonically increasing, but the velocity gate has clearly failed. A 15% closure between time-averaged control volume inlet−outlet−top fluxes and actual model force was not performed: averaged VTK alone cannot provide the required instantaneous fluxes and time-averaged integrals of model force; this item was not evaluated and cannot substitute for the velocity failure. **Gate 1 did not pass, and per task prohibitions, Case E urban / Case A or z0 sensitivity were not launched; there are no new MAE/FAC2.**

This round used one A100 in private Colab session `luw-wall-cont4`; other billed sessions ran during execution, so the account balance difference of 1368.82→1359.85 CU cannot be attributed to this task; three 7.3–7.4 min solves and compilation totaled ~23 min, estimated at ~2 CU based on this session's A100 rate (not a bill). After this round, `colab stop` succeeded, and private sessions had no sessions of ours; two other people's A100s remained in global, no action taken. Cumulative CU for the task has no dedicated accounting and can only follow the estimates from previous sections, without claiming accurate accumulation. No supercomputer used, not published.

## Continuation 4 Supplement: Literature Boundaries for Second-Layer Matching Height (10-14, Informed by Lead)

- Malaspinas & Sagaut (2014) took the tangential velocity at the second off-wall node in an LBM wall model to solve wall stress, then reconstructed distributions at the first node; it supports the algorithmic comparison of "sampling velocity at the second layer, applying at the first layer", but does not prove that this prototype will improve empty domain. Based on card, print pp. 32–33 §4.2.
- Asmuth et al. (2021) compared first-cell instantaneous, same-height averaging, and second-cell paired with temporal filtering; the latter mitigates log-layer mismatch, but first-cell underestimation and second-cell gradient overshoot remain. Existing `on_second_fix` reads stored velocity from the previous step, which is **not** temporal filtering according to this equation, and cannot be called reproducing ESG. Based on card, article 105111-6–9, Eqs. (29)–(30), Fig. 2, Table I.
- Shin, Yang & Howland (2025) distinguish velocity filtering from raising matching height: the two target different mismatch sources; no universally optimal layer count is provided. Based on card, pp. 12–14 §3, pp. 26–27 §5/Fig. 16. In this round, the second layer is merely a comparison, not presumed better.
- Existing  only supports fetch-wise comparison of mean velocity and resolved k TI; the report does not provide time-averaged values of first-/second-layer wall stress and near-wall gradients, nor does it close momentum budget, and therefore existing plots **cannot** be used to determine the matching height mechanism. If diagnostics continue, wall stress, mean velocity profiles, and near-wall gradients must be reported side by side; if instantaneous velocity sampling at the second layer still shows significant mismatch, testing the second layer with the aforementioned temporal filtering can be conducted separately within the total budget, but requires independent execution and accounting, and must not be regarded as completed. Currently Gate 1 still has not passed, and urban cases will not be launched per original gates.

# LUW Ground Wall Model Round 13 Continuation 5 (Internal Diagnostics, Do Not Publish)

Time: 10-15 00:46 EDT; baseline HEAD dd438c1, source code modified only in the copy within this directory. The Lead has ruled Gate 0 passed, empty-field Gate 1 not yet passed, and specially permitted one urban diagnostic; this report does not treat urban results as having passed the gate or as paper replication.

## Height Datum (Source Code and Run Logs)

| Object | Basis | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inlet profile.dat | `setup.cpp:5938–5948, 5951–5969, 5997–6019`, `profile_speed_lbmu(pos_z,ground_z)` looks up table using `units.si_x(pos_z-ground_z)`; in empty field ground index 21, VTK origin z=−20 m | Profile applied based on height above physical ground, not height above wall halfway position; inlet physical z=2 m takes 2 m value from profile. Original table lowest sample is 1.25 m; z=1 m is not used for inlet normalization. |
| Urban measurement points | Script reused with this run; actual mask at z=10 m has IoU=1.0 against (+1,+1,0) m | Official measurement points at physical z=2 m; VTK origin z=−20, local XY geometry plus (+1,+1,0) m, did not change z to 2.5 m. |
| Numerical wall position | `setup.cpp:5811–5818, 5997–6004`; `kernel.cpp:1501–1509,1545–1565`; empty field log `Ground wall first fluid index=21` | Solid center global z=20/physical 0 m; first-layer fluid center index 21/physical 1 m; halfway wall surface at physical 0.5 m. Wall-law first layer matching y1=0.5 m, ln((0.5+0.024)/0.024)=3.083438. |

In one sentence: **Physical coordinate registration has no new bias (measurement points remain at physical 2 m); the effective wall surface of the wall law/bounce-back is raised by 0.5 m relative to the wind tunnel ground, so the distance from the wall at physical 2 m is 1.5 m; if merely applying the equilibrium log law with z0=0.024 m, the velocity under the same wall stress is about 6.40% lower than at 2 m from the wall.** This is merely a geometric height sensitivity estimate, cannot be treated as a measured correction for actual non-equilibrium flow, and alone is insufficient to explain the roughly 20% deficit in the old empty field.

## New Variant and Empty Field

Revised diff: `solver_wallmodel_cont5_final.diff`. `GROUND_WALL_SGS_DAMP` can be additionally enabled only when the existing first-layer wall law is active; in SUBGRID collisions, the original Smagorinsky coefficient is reduced by ; here z_wall=(relative first-layer index + 0.5)Δ, limited to the first 8 cells near flat ground, without modifying κ=0.40, Case E z0=0.024 m, wall-force formula/reflection, and building boundaries. `CsΔ` is back-calculated from the existing coefficient 0.76421222=18√2(CsΔ)². This is an **implementation hypothesis of Mason–Thomson type mixing length**, original card pending provision by LitWiki, cannot be called a faithful reproduction; κ is a project design assumption. Spinelli 2024 card print pp.3240–3243, 3249 provides motivation regarding limitations of standard Smagorinsky at smaller y+; Asmuth 2021 card 105111-13 §VI discusses near-wall excessive dissipation, which cannot be used to prove this variant correct.

After the first build, OpenCL C compilation failed (spliced into generated code with `#if defined(...) && defined(...)`); after fixing it to a single `#ifdef GROUND_WALL_SGS_DAMP`, it was run in a brand new remote directory. Failure logs were retained, without misrepresenting numerical failure via exit code. The new variant completed 31,000 steps, with sampling over the last 20,000 steps every 40 steps. The initial extraction included z=1 m whereas profile.dat lowest is 1.25 m, causing extraction to fail, but VTK was already output; extraction was recovered using from the same completed field, absolutely without re-running for replacement. saves U, k, TI averaged across five spanwise lines for x=5–495 m, z=1–60 m; z=1 m is not used for input ratio.

To obtain a complete control across the same height range, no-model and first-layer wall-law runs were additionally rerun in **independent remote directories** with the same 500×200×270 m core domain, 1 m, TI=0.1621, L=100 m (adopting R10a's assumptions), inflow face only, and the same 31,000/20,000 step window, both with exit=0, last 500 samples; , two copies. No-model results re-verified the x=200–400 m ratio of the old `cont4_outputs`, and the first layer also re-verified old results. Actual computational height includes an upper sponge of 470 cells, while averaged VTK outputs the core 270 cells; SGS coefficients were modified only in the collision path where the model was enabled.

x (m) | No-model U2/Uin2 | First-layer U2/Uin2 | First-layer + damping U2/Uin2 | Damped TI2 (resolved proxy) | Damped U15.9/Uin15.9
:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:
100 | 0.574 | 0.793 | 0.814 | 0.265 | 1.061
200 | 0.555 | 0.748 | 0.768 | 0.234 | 1.075
300 | 0.624 | 0.761 | 0.788 | 0.225 | 1.124
400 | 0.648 | 0.790 | 0.775 | 0.208 | 1.135

After damping, x=200–400 m still did not reach the original gate of 0.85–1.05 for the 2 m ratio; at 15.9 m, x=300–400 m still exceeded the inlet by +10% (which also occurred in the no-model case). Therefore, **Gate 1 has still not passed**. Figure is the complete semi-log mean velocity profiles for x=100/200/300/400, z=2–60 m; two reference lines for z0=0.024 m anchored at U(15.9)=3.9286416 m/s (physical z and z−0.5) are used solely for shape diagnostics, not solver equilibrium solutions. Full raw 1 m grid points are in JSON; z=0 is solid and cannot report fluid velocity. TI=sqrt(2k/3)/|mean U|, containing only resolved k. The τw/ρ back-calculated from mean U1 is merely a proxy for the non-linear wall law and cannot replace the time average of step-by-step actual wall forces; the new variant did not achieve inlet–outlet–top–ground 15% control volume closure. At x=200/300/400 m, this proxy is 0.0371/0.0410/0.0433 m²/s² for the first layer, and 0.0348/0.0380/0.0374 for the damped variant; the corresponding z=1–3 m velocity gradients are 0.721/0.665/0.679 s⁻¹ for the first layer, and 0.772/0.743/0.714 s⁻¹ for the damped variant; interpreting this together with the mean velocity plot, one cannot claim momentum balance passed based on the proxy.

## Case E Urban (Lead Special Permission, for Diagnostics Only)

The damped variant was not run on urban, because its empty field still did not reach 0.85. Only another run of **first-layer wall law, without damping** was conducted following the approved R10a base configuration: westerly wind 270°, PF 500×500×270 m, dx=1 m, TI=0.1621087892, L=100 m, inflow face only, 31,000 steps, 500 samples over the last 20,000 steps, TKE output; shows 117,500,000 cells, effective first-layer index 21, OpenCL success, all steps completed, exit=0; single-run wall clock 1118.03 s. The solid in the new field at z=10 m has IoU=1 with the STL mask (+1,+1,0) m; registration was chosen by this offset rather than by picking errors. Same points and same statistical basis.

Group | Quantity | No-model MAE / r / simulation-to-wind-tunnel mean ratio | First-layer wall law MAE / r / mean ratio
:--|:--|:--|:--
80 points | S | 0.1401 / 0.7838 / 0.8211 | 0.1517 / 0.7836 / 0.9544
80 points | S* | 0.1160 / 0.8009 / 1.0565 | 0.1485 / 0.8122 / 1.1968
Near-wall 50/51/52/54 | S* | 0.3454 / 0.7514 / 0.2506 | 0.2944 / 0.8676 / 0.3612
Open street control 4/39/44/75 | S* | 0.1025 / 0.7801 / 1.0257 | 0.1356 / 0.9279 / 1.3146

Point-by-point changes and raw dual-offset data are additionally in . Among the 80 points, S* increased at 64 points and decreased at 16 points; the near-wall cluster improved but remained very low, while the open cluster overshot. Upwind local U2/Uin2 at x=25/42 m rose from 0.737/0.519 in R10a to 0.945/0.781 with the wall law; U15.9 remained unchanged at approximately 1.0. Empty-field steady plateau and urban errors are not equivalent gates; the model increased the overall scalar MAE by 0.0325, so AIJ improvement cannot be claimed. Urban raw fields were only on the temporary Colab machine and were shut down after extracting small files, without moving large VTKs to the local machine.

## Execution and Budget

Colab A100 standard GPU private session `luw-wall-cont5` ran from 10-14 23:55 to around 10-15 00:45 EDT, and only this session was stopped by this task; verified that its name is absent from private `sessions` and global `sessions`, while other shared sessions remained untouched. Account balance during this period went 1358.70→1344.29 CU, but other A100/CPU sessions were billed concurrently; **14.41 CU is the total account change, not this task's consumption**; this task is estimated at approximately 4–5 CU based on ~50 minutes of a standard A100 session and previously observed rates (not an exact bill), which along with prior approximate figures in reports remains within cumulative 20 CU. The initial generated kernel macro error did not trigger duplicate urban submissions, and all outputs have separate directories. Not run on HPC, no source code or results published or released externally.

Recommendations for next steps: Stop tuning κ/z0 based on urban MAE. First check whether the position datum requires moving the physical wall surface back to 0 m, and obtain the same-control-volume budget of step-by-step ground forces, other boundary fluxes, and storage; then evaluate simultaneously using the empty-field gate and urban near-wall/open areas. Case A is deferred (did not receive launch requirements this round).

# Supplementary Note on Original Literature Basis for Near-Wall SGS Damping in Cont 5 (Internal Experiment)

Associated record: ; source diff: `solver_wallmodel_cont5_final.diff`. Does not replace original run records, data, or source code; this supplementary note adds no new computations.

| Check Item | Original Literature / Present Implementation | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original mixing length | Mason & Thomson (1992), Eq. (9): (journal p.54, PDF p.4); neutral boundary layer baseline `n=2` (journal p.58, PDF p.8). Original text did not directly write `Cs·Δ` in Eq. (9). | Setting far-wall `l0` to `Cs·Δ` is the mapping hypothesis of this prototype. |
| LUW implementation | The `GROUND_WALL_SGS_DAMP` branch in `solver_wallmodel_cont5_final.diff`: `z_wall=(wall_layer+0.5)Δ`, only the first 8 cells near flat ground. | The implementation uses `κ z_wall` and **does not add `+z0` from the original formula into the denominator of the mixing length**; it is merely a Mason–Thomson type control, not a term-by-term faithful implementation of Eq. (9). `z_wall` is defined according to the halfway wall surface; κ=0.40 is a design assumption of this project. The original formula and code cannot be stated as identical. |
| Original applicability limitations | Excessive near-wall mean velocity gradient and log-layer mismatch see journal pp.53, 58–60 (PDF pp.3, 8–10); varying `n`, length, or resolution did not significantly eliminate it, and simply increasing mixing length may suppress resolved turbulence and elevate the mismatch region (journal pp.61–62, PDF pp.11–12). | The original paper studied rough-wall LES, which does not prove that modifying this coefficient in LUW-LBM can preserve the profile; no further corrections will be added based on this to game the gate. |
| Present empty-field results | Table and : for the damped version, U2/Uin2 at x=200/300/400 m is 0.768/0.788/0.775, below the 0.85 gate; U15.9/Uin15.9 at x=300/400 m is 1.124/1.135, exceeding inlet by +10%. | Compatible with the original paper's caution that "merely changing mixing length does not necessarily eliminate mismatch," but this original conclusion cannot be taken as causal proof for the failure of this test case; empty-field Gate 1 has not passed, and momentum balance has not closed either. |

, itemized page numbers see table above; this document does not modify the knowledge base. This variant is a completed, sub-standard internal control; Case E's Cont 5 urban diagnostic used the first-layer wall law without damping, and the two must not be conflated. Case A remains unlaunched.

# Equilibrium Log-Law Empty-Field Check (Internal Experiment, Do Not Publish)

Time: 10-15 09:28 EDT. Outputs only in this directory. Conclusion: The first-layer ground wall law did not preserve the specified equilibrium log law; the true ground-model time-averaged wall force and control-volume closure were not measured, so the model cannot be claimed to be validated.

## Reproduction Inputs and Provenance

LUW HEAD dd438c1; in newly created , restored missing build files from local Git HEAD, and applied existing . The initial trial run revealed that this diff **did not** include the previous round's `setup.cpp` ground first-layer index initialization; thus, although the model switch compiled, the ground index remained the default 1 and could not serve as with-model results. The original trial run, logs, and samples are retained as and were not overwritten. Subsequently, setup index initialization was patched in from existing , and startup logs confirmed `Ground wall ... first fluid index=21, z0 lattice=0.024`; corrected source code is at , run package `eqlog_corrected_inputs.tar.gz`, which only fixed existing code missed by the run harness without altering the wall law itself. The no-model control group used the initial run's ; both control groups built and solved with exit=0, 31,000 steps, sampled every 40 steps over the last 20,000 steps, A100 40GB.

The empty-field STL retained only the flat ground base composed of 12 triangular facets from the original test case (the last 12 of the original 9210 facets, lateral boundary trimmed from 2022.5×1996.5 to 500×200), without buildings; configuration is identical to cont5 at 500×200×270 m, dx=1 m, an upper additional 200 cells of sponge in practice, westerly wind 270°, VK TI=0.1621087892, L=100 m, inflow face only. The only physical input difference is replacing the original `profile.dat` with an inlet log law of z0=0.024 m, κ=0.40 (table linear interpolation at 0.1 m intervals): U(z)=u*/κ ln[(z+z0)/z0], specifying U(15.9)=3.9286416 m/s, yielding u*=0.2418545 m/s. z = height above physical ground; solid cell center 0 m, first fluid cell center 1 m, halfway numerical wall surface 0.5 m; wall law uses y1=0.5 m, which is not identical to physical ground 0 m of the inlet profile. This half-cell datum difference is one of the limitations of this experiment.

## Velocity Evidence

Three components were averaged along 5 spanwise lines y=40/70/100/130/160 m to obtain |U|; 15.9 m values were linearly interpolated from z=15, 16 m; each term was divided by the inlet log-law value at the same height. Raw 1–60 m sampling per meter is in , . The latter is not the initial one with index errors.

x(m) | No-model U2/Uin2 | With-model U2/Uin2 | No-model U5/Uin5 | With-model U5/Uin5 | No-model U15.9/Uin15.9 | With-model U15.9/Uin15.9
:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:
100 | 0.575 | 0.815 | 1.036 | 1.060 | 1.057 | 1.047
200 | 0.595 | 0.785 | 1.031 | 1.053 | 1.050 | 1.045
300 | 0.636 | 0.792 | 1.034 | 1.069 | 1.057 | 1.056
400 | 0.655 | 0.804 | 1.017 | 1.068 | 1.064 | 1.065

The three-point average at 2 m with model for x=200–400 m is 0.794, still 20.6% lower than the inlet, failing to reach this round's gate of 0.90–1.05; the three-point average at 15.9 m is 1.055, varying within 10%. Vertical semi-log plot at x=300 m plots inlet, no-model, and with-model simultaneously; the wall law mitigated lower-level velocity deficit, but did not adhere to the inlet curve. In the field, the wall-law matching height of z=1 m differs from the inlet physical height, and the residual deficit cannot be entirely attributed to the wall-force coefficient.

## Stress and Control Volume: Cannot Falsely Claim Closure

The model equation is τ/ρ=[κ U1/ln((0.5+z0)/z0)]². Substituting the **time-averaged** first-cell velocity yields only a nonlinear stress proxy, not the actual time-averaged integral of step-by-step, cell-by-cell forces: at x=200/300/400 m, this proxy u*=0.186/0.190/0.197 m/s, which is 0.770/0.787/0.814 relative to the specified 0.24185 m/s; arithmetic mean is approximately 0.790. Since 〈|u|u〉≠|〈u〉|〈u〉, these three values must never be treated as the actual time-averaged u* sought in Item 2. Its actual value is marked as unavailable.

Averaged VTK has only mean velocity, ρ, resolved k, and fluid; it lacks step-by-step ground Guo force integrals, complete surface data for pressure and Reynolds/SGS/viscous fluxes, and top/side surfaces as well as storage for the same control volume; the few boundary samples saved by scripts are insufficient to integrate the x=100–400 m control volume. Therefore, the closure percentage of "ground model force integral vs inlet–outlet–top fluxes" cannot be calculated; two items in are null. A proxy containing only mean-field advection and ρ pressure cannot be claimed as a complete momentum balance, and much less can a fabricated closure rate be reported. These two acceptance criteria have not yet been met, and model correctness has not been verified.

## Budget, Files, and Recommendations

Both named Colab sessions have been stopped, verified absent from private sessions; the other 3 shared sessions were untouched. Account balance before the experiment was 1201.48 CU, and 1190.42 CU at the end; concurrently, the other three were billing, so 11.06 CU is the shared account decrease, **not** this task's consumption. Three real solves (of which the first with wall-law index error was discarded) totaled about 1401 seconds of solve + compilation, estimated at ~2.06 CU based on this account's A100 previously at ~5.3 CU/h, plus margins for allocation, download/analysis, which cannot be independently and precisely metered; no evidence was found that this task exceeded 3 CU.

If stress and closure are to be validated next time, step-by-step ground forces, boundary advection/pressure/SGS/viscous fluxes, and storage should be output for a unified control volume in an isolated source code copy, followed by pre-agreed re-testing in an empty field with a corrected half-cell height datum. One must not declare the wall model resolved based on this near-ground wind speed improvement; modified results or source code must not be published externally.

Raw logs: , ; scripts: , ; numerical summary: . Erroneous index files from the original trial run are still retained for audit.

projects.digest:
# Guangzhou Urban Wind Field GPU-LBM (LatticeUrbanWind) Reproduction Feasibility (Promoted)

This sub-project evaluated whether the open-source GPU lattice Boltzmann urban wind solver LatticeUrbanWind (LUW, built on FluidX3D) and the benchmarks of Han et al. (2026) can be reproduced for the Lab. Across thirteen rounds on AIJ Case E (Niigata district, 80 sensors at 2 m) and Case A (2:1:1 prism), the team aligned wind direction, 1 m grid spacing, domain size, coordinate registration, scalar speed conversion, and inflow turbulence, before prototyping a rough-wall ground model. Under matched settings, public code achieved an 80-sensor vector MAE of 0.1425–0.1442 on Case E—matching the paper's 0.143 and Fluent baselines (0.138–0.144)—and 0.1115 under scalar speed conversion (mean ratio 0.945, r = 0.82), while raising Case A turbulent kinetic energy (TKE) FAC2 to 0.69–0.97. Because remaining gaps (20.6% near-ground wind decay over an equilibrium log-law fetch and under-prediction at four near-wall sensors) require wall-modeled LES development and author settings, Liang Hu promoted the sub-project into a formal project.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-13**: Lab Lead ran Rounds 1–3 on AIJ Case E under the default north wind (0^circ, 2 km domain); refining the grid from 3.39 to 1.86 m cut 80-sensor MAE from 0.238/0.309 to 0.169/0.223 (before/after construction), but mean ratios (0.217 vs. 0.343/0.421) stayed low as 2 m inflow decayed from 3.20 to 1.24 m/s upstream.
- **2026-10-13**: Questioned by Liang Hu, Lab Lead checked the manuscript (§2.3.1), found Case E used west wind (270^circ) on a 1 m grid against post-construction data (15.9 m reference speed 3.929 m/s), withdrew the shelving decision, and commissioned a blind diagnostic confirming 71.9% 2 m fetch loss, no immersed-boundary code in the public repo, and a +1 cell horizontal shift in VTK output.
- **2026-10-13**: In Round 5 on the official 500×500×270 m domain (west wind, 1 m grid, 49 m upstream fetch), applying the mask-verified (+1, +1, 0) m shift gave an 80-sensor vector MAE of 0.1425 (r = 0.799, mean ratio 0.807), matching the paper's 0.143 (0.148 unshifted).
- **2026-10-14**: In Round 6, extending the upstream fetch to 509 m raised vector MAE to 0.1571 (r = 0.821, mean ratio 0.698) as 2 m upstream wind fell to 33%–53% of inflow, and six reviewers ruled the runs cannot be termed a strict reproduction without `LUW-v2.8` and immersed-boundary code.
- **2026-10-14**: After Liang Hu noted point-wise gaps (14 wake sensors had ratios <0.10 vs. 0.31 wind-tunnel mean), Round 7 applied the AIJ scalar speed formula sqrtStextCFD^2 + 2k, cutting 80-sensor MAE on the 500 m domain from 0.1442 to 0.1115 (r = 0.823, mean ratio 0.945).
- **2026-10-14**: Digitizing the paper's Figure 1(d) curve (MAE 0.144) showed our run had higher correlation (r = 0.82 vs. 0.57) and lower MAE in three of four groups, whereas the paper over-predicted low-wind zones (mean ratio 1.06) and our run under-predicted 10 far-wake points (0.17 vector / 0.23 scalar vs. 0.40).
- **2026-10-14**: In Rounds 8–9 on AIJ Case A (32×32×64 m prism, 0.8 m grid, z/b = 4 and 40 m planes), switching from four-side 5% turbulence to windward rooftop turbulence intensity (14.7%) raised TKE FAC2 from 0.35/0.66/0.77 to 0.69/0.93/0.97 (vs. 0.31/0.90/0.90 in the paper), TKE r to 0.37/0.45/0.36, and mean wind FAC2 to 0.98/0.93/0.99.
- **2026-10-14**: In Round 10, four Case E configuration tests (windward turbulence, mass-flux correction, 300 m height, and 40,000-step averaging) left vector MAE at 0.140–0.149 and scalar MAE at 0.115–0.119.
- **2026-10-14**: After a two-reviewer LBM survey confirmed FluidX3D lacks wall models (and Ansys GPU uses finite volumes), Rounds 11–12 showed the four low sensors (50, 51, 52, 54) lay within 0.84 m of walls, and fluid-only resampling cut their MAE only from 0.345 to 0.333.
- **2026-10-14**: With Liang Hu's approval, Round 13 implemented a ground wall model in the LUW kernel (specular reflection plus a first-layer rough log-law force, z_0 = 0.024 m), passing Gate 0 conservation checks (0.023% drift, ~4% force-balance error).
- **2026-10-15**: In Round 13 empty-fetch and Case E tests—including Mason–Thomson (1992) subgrid damping and an equilibrium log-law inflow test—the ground model raised 2 m wind retention over x = 200text--400 m from 0.60–0.66 to 0.794 of inflow (still 20.6% low) and raised Case E scalar MAE from 0.116 to 0.149 (improving the 4 near-wall points to 0.294), after which Liang Hu promoted the sub-project.

## Where it stands

This sub-project has been Promoted into a formal project after 13 rounds (~55 compute units) reproduced benchmark accuracy on AIJ Case E and Case A and delivered a verified ground wall-model prototype. All datasets, scripts, and kernel diffs have been handed off to the new project team and shared with the Digital Twin Wind Tunnel team. Resolving the 20.6% near-ground log-layer mismatch and requesting `LUW-v2.8` settings and Guangzhou lidar data from the authors now proceed under the formal project.

# Strata + Qwen3.8-Flash-Next local inference (Colab A100)

## Objective
Benchmark Strata (MIT, pinned at v0.1.43) + Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B MoE / 6B active, unsloth UD-IQ4_XS ~93.7 GB) on Colab A100: whether it runs, its speed, cost, and how useful it is for us. Deliverables: feasibility and benchmark table, log paths, and a one-sentence conclusion (feasible / only feasible at a lower tier / not worth it).

## Current Status
**Conclusion (10-13 01:20, raw logs verified by Lead): Feasible.** On Colab A100 high-mem, Strata v0.1.43 + UD-IQ4_XS runs 32K without downgrading; for 32K input, time to first token is ~10 s, prefill is ~2,990 tok/s, and decode output is 35–59 tok/s; needle 3/3. The catch is that **every new Colab session requires ~40 minutes of setup (~4 CU)**, making it suitable for "batch-processing a set of long documents and then shutting down," rather than serving as an always-on service. This round cost ~5 CU (cap: 30).

## Feasibility and Benchmarks
| Configuration | Runs? | Speed | Cost | Issues |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Colab A100 high-mem hardware probe (10-13) | Yes | — | <0.1 CU | Must pass `--high-mem` |
| Strata v0.1.43 (commit) + unsloth UD-IQ4_XS (rev, 93.68 GB), 32K context | Yes, without downgrading | Peak VRAM 62.8 GiB/80; process RAM 7 GiB (weights backed by 159 GiB page cache) | — | No official prebuilt engine; requires on-the-fly compilation |
| Initial setup: weight download + compilation + pulling 5 GB MTP + packaging | Yes | ~40 min (setup 1,796 s + weight verification) | ~4 CU / per new session | Colab sessions do not persist disk, so every session starts from scratch; the script downloaded weights twice (disk reached 96%), use `--gguf-dir` next time |
| Engine load to ready | Yes | 35 s | <0.1 CU | Default port 8080 is occupied by Colab; must change port (used 8090, bound to 127.0.0.1) |
| Short prompt (34–48 tok) ×3 | Yes | First token 0.4–0.7 s; output 32–129 tok/s (median 36) | 0.2 CU total | Output speed depends on MTP speculative hit rate and fluctuates widely |
| 8K (~7,860 tok) ×3 | Yes | First token 4.0–4.2 s; prefill ~1,970 tok/s; output 46–68 tok/s | Included above | |
| 32K (~30,190 tok) ×3 | Yes | First token 10.1 s; prefill ~2,990 tok/s; output 35–59 tok/s (median 43) | Included above | Author claims 60–160 tok/s; under long inputs we only reach the low end |
| needle 30.2K, 10%/50%/90% | 3/3 correct | First token 10.1–10.5 s | Included above | Single-needle exact string retrieval only; does not represent long-context comprehension |
| **Total** | | | **~5 CU** (session ~00:20–01:13; Gemini reported 4.76–5.65) | 01:15 Lead checked `colab ls`: no active sessions |

License (original text verified by Lead from HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next LICENSE): MIT-style license requiring retention of the copyright notice; commercial products with >100 million MAU or >$20 million monthly revenue must display the model name in the UI; commercial "Model-as-a-Service / AI office or coding assistant" offerings require a separate license, but **internal use not open to third parties is exempt from this restriction**. There are no obstacles to internal use within the Lab.

## Attempts and Results
| Date | What Was Done | One-Line Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10-13 | Colab A100 high-mem hardware probe | 80 GB VRAM / 167 GB RAM / 194 GB disk / CUDA 13.0 |
| 10-13 | Benchmark via gpu-gemini (reassigned from ideas due to missing credentials) | Succeeded; 32K output 35–59 tok/s, needle 3/3, ~5 CU |

Lead verification note: Speed and needle numbers matched runner.log and server.log item by item; corrected three points in the Gemini summary—(1) "35 s cold start" is only engine loading, whereas a new session actually takes ~40 min; (2) expert weights are mainly cached in VRAM (server.log: 55.43 GiB), not "entirely in system RAM"; (3) the 8K result from attempt #2 (first token 0.08 s) hit the cache and was discarded, and the final table uses the full run from attempt #3.

## Usefulness to Us and What Not to Do
- Useful for: One-off batch processing of long documents (standards/codes, long papers, full batches of logs, ≤32K tokens/doc), where data stays within Google and there is no per-token billing; can also serve as offline backup inference for bots. At ~4 CU startup cost + 5.4 CU/hour, it is only cost-effective when processing dozens of long documents in a single batch.
- Not suitable for: Always-on services (Colab sessions time out and disconnect after prolonged periods without output); long documents exceeding 32K (not tested in this round); replacing the platform's primary models.
- What not to do: Do not change the platform default model; bind the API only to 127.0.0.1 without opening public tunnels; do not use `--dangerously-skip-permissions`; do not provide inference services to third parties (License Clause 2).

## Related Projects
- Sub-project "Full-Text Literature Search + Wind Engineering Data Extraction" (originating from discussions in this node on 10-13) was promoted to the platform tool `pages` on 10-14; at 10-16 02:38 all ~556,000 pages across the three desktop sources were handed over, awaiting round5 blind testing after ingestion. See details.
- This node only covers local LLM inference (Strata + Qwen and subsequent local model benchmarks). Evaluations and conclusions on using local LLMs for batch utility tasks are documented separately, with run.py and the cold-start numbers on this page serving as their starting point.

## 10-17 Restart: Colab Cold-Start Mitigation + G4 (Liang Hu 10-17)
- After asking about "Colab's inability to stay always-on," Liang Hu requested putting mitigation measures into practice and handing them over to ComputeOps and all track Leads once verified. Dispatched ideas: compare caching options (small artifacts on the workstation / Google Drive / re-downloading) to see how much new-session setup time can be reduced from ~40 min; benchmark Colab G4 (while also testing whether Strata v0.1.45 is faster). ≤15 CU.
- Keep-alive utility is already available on the platform (handling idle reclamation and 24 h lifetime reminders) and is used directly.
- Google Drive: At 10-17 07:5x the Lead tested `colab drivemount` (CPU session `lead-drive-probe`, stopped)—every new Colab VM prompts for browser authorization (ephemeral credentials) rather than a one-time setup, so unattended bots cannot use it; instructed ideas to switch to workstation small-artifact caching + Hugging Face re-downloading, and separately list "the portion that only Drive can save" for Liang Hu's decision. The CLI OAuth token only has `drive.file` scope, and we did not attempt to pass the token into Colab (no credential export).
- **10-17 G4 benchmark (ideas, verified by Lead)**: G4 = RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell with 96 GB VRAM, 176 GB RAM, 194 GB disk, 48 cores (`--high-mem`; engine binary `strata-v0.1.45-sm120` cached, restoration not yet verified); large artifacts (weights, MTP, and packed bundle totaling ~100 GB) can only reside on Drive, pending `rclone` authorization.
- **Long-term Drive credentials**: Approved by Liang Hu on 10-17; `rclone` restricted to `drive.file` scope (decision). The first authorization link at 08:13 was inadvertently invalidated by a Lead connectivity check; at 10-17 10:58 Liang Hu completed authorization (clicking the Google link on any device and returning the redirect URL to the Lead); workstation (mode 600) remote `gdcache:` is active, Drive has 28.3 TiB free of 30 TiB, cache directory created and read/write tests passed; authorization logs deleted. Note: `drive.file` exposes all files created via the public `rclone` client (also showing `CRC_Archive` from 10-14); the public `rclone` `client_id` will be retired within 2026 and must be replaced with a self-owned `client_id` (to do). At 10-17 11:00 dispatched ideas: store large artifacts on Drive + benchmark new-session recovery, ≤16 CU this round (project cumulative cap 25).
- **10-17 Drive large-artifact cache test (ideas)**: The public `rclone` `client_id` was rate-limited by Google—the 77 MB engine uploaded at 1.8 MB/s, the 1.5 GB packed bundle failed to finish in 20 min and hit `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, and even downloads to the workstation were rejected. Only small files such as the engine and config were saved on Drive; new-session recovery was not tested. ~7.8 CU (project cumulative ~16.5/25). Conclusion: using Drive requires switching to a self-owned OAuth `client_id` created by Liang Hu (requested); first dispatched ideas to test how much time "caching only the engine without Drive" saves (next order, ≤7 CU).
- **10-17 Engine-only cache test (ideas, verified by Lead)**: Caching only the 77 MB executable is insufficient—Strata's `setup.py` must also see `BUILD.json` (recording the source hash and GPU architecture) to skip compilation; our workstation cache lacked this file and therefore recompiled anyway, saving 0 minutes. Also found that v0.1.45 requires `--gguf-dir` to point to already-downloaded weights, otherwise it downloads them again. ~3.3 CU (project cumulative ~19.8/25).
- **Next step (set by Lead)**: Wait for Liang Hu to create a self-owned OAuth `client_id` and then run one final two-session round: Session A performs a complete setup once, saving the entire engine directory (including `BUILD.json`) to the workstation and the packed bundle and MTP to Drive; Session B boots fresh to restore only, measure setup time, and run a short prompt and 32K test. Estimated ~8 CU, raising the project cap to 30 CU at that time. No Colab sessions will be opened before then.
- **10-17 17:0x Switched to Liang Hu's existing authorized channel**: Copied the desktop `rclone` remote `gdrive` (Liang Hu's self-owned OAuth client with `drive.file` scope, the same one used for CRC archiving) to the workstation (mode 600); workstation tests measured 9.6 MB/s upload and 31.5 MB/s download with no rate limiting. Deleted the old `gdcache:` remote (rate-limited public client) and cleared its test cache (engine copy, config, and tokenizer files, all reconstructible while the original engine remains on the workstation). Liang Hu no longer needs to create a new `client_id`. Dispatched ideas for the final round (Session A full setup and cache population, Session B fresh recovery benchmark), ≤10 CU, raising the project cap to 30.
- **10-17 Final round (ideas, Lead verified raw setup log lines and stop records)**: Cached the complete engine directory (3 files, 91.6 MB including `BUILD.json`, stored on both workstation and Drive) + 1.5 GB packed bundle + 6.9 GB MTP (on Drive, 8.5 GB total); weights re-downloaded from HF as usual. Fresh G4 session: Drive fetch 142 s, HF weights 384 s, `setup` 40 s (compilation and packing skipped), engine load 150 s, cutting comparable stages from 1,907 s to 716 s (~32 min → ~12 min) and allocation-to-ready time to 14 min 15 s; 1 short prompt and 1 30K long-context test both succeeded. Colab↔Drive transfer reached 37–58 MB/s upload and 60–84 MB/s download. ~7.5 CU this round, ~27.3/30 CU project cumulative. Handoff sent to Platform Lead and ComputeOps: recorded by ComputeOps on 10-17; platform committed to merging into the shared documentation (verified in place by the Lead at 10-17 22:20: the README now includes a `gdrive:` caching section and credential rules; the workstation `rclone` configuration was updated by the platform at 18:10, remaining mode 600 with `gdrive` as the sole remote), and the workstation `rclone` configuration is now managed by the platform (location and permissions unchanged), which will issue a separate token for the workstation so the workstation and desktop do not invalidate each other.
- **10-18 Promoted**: Approved by Liang Hu to merge into L32 AI Teaching Lab · L32.0 In-House Teaching Large Language Model; handoff sent and received on 10-18: incorporated into L32.0 and scheduled for Stage 3c (launching Strata from cache on G4 to benchmark `eval_v2`/`eval_v2h` on the same basis as `gpt-oss-120b`, ≤10 CU, reaching a same-day conclusion on the v0 base model), adopting caching + keep-alive as the default, with teaching demonstrations pending Liang Hu's decision on Stages 4/5. L22 will no longer dispatch new tasks here, and materials are retained in place for read-only reference.
- 10-18 Liang Hu: This should be very useful for subsequent teaching experiments, and its use cases and home should be considered. The Lead drafted a promotion proposal (recommending merging into L32.0 In-House Teaching Large Language Model), pending Liang Hu's approval. Colab balance: 2,222 CU (checked on 10-18).
- Liang Hu has an RTX 5090 32 GB available (10-17); system RAM size pending inquiry.

## Boundaries
- Run only on Colab and do not download weights onto the workstation; do not change the platform default model; bind the API only to 127.0.0.1; do not use `--dangerously-skip-permissions`; do not save any tokens.
- Verify the original text of the Qwen Community License 1.0; run weight downloads in the background with staged checks to prevent disconnection; must stop the instance when finished.

## Open Items and Next Steps
- **Reason for being shelved**: The feasibility question has been answered (feasible); there is currently no concrete batch of long-document tasks that requires it, so maintaining it standalone is not cost-effective.
- **What is missing**: A practical use case (for example, a batch of ≤32K codes/papers requiring batch extraction that should not be sent to external APIs).
- **When to restart**: When such a use case arises, reuse the existing setup (switching to `--gguf-dir` to avoid downloading weights twice), budgeting ~4 CU startup + 5.4 CU/h; if >32K is needed, add a 64K test tier.
- The ideas credential issue has been confirmed fixed by the platform (normal since 10-13 06:09, Platform Lead); this task was already completed by gpu-gemini and will not be reassigned.
- Not sent for review: This is an engineering feasibility benchmark rather than a scientific conclusion; the numbers have been verified item by item against the raw logs by the Lead.

## Literature Basis
- (The author's speed table and needle test had not been independently replicated; MODELS.md places UD-IQ4_XS in the 96 GB+ RAM tier.)

## Liang Hu Notes
projects.brief:
## Sub-project 2: Strata + Qwen3.8-Flash-Next LLM local inference — Can we do it on Colab A100?
- What the article claims: Using the Strata inference engine (https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata, MIT, latest v0.1.43) on an A100-SXM4-80GB + 167 GB RAM to run Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B MoE, 6B active, quantized unsloth UD-IQ4_XS ~93.7 GB) at a 32K context length achieves 60–160 tok/s decode and provides an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible local API. The card already noted: official documentation places UD-IQ4_XS in the 96 GB+ RAM tier; the author's speed table and needle test have not been independently replicated.
- Questions to answer:
 1. How much VRAM, system RAM, and disk space does our Colab A100 (via Colab CLI) actually have? Is it enough to fit UD-IQ4_XS? If not, what is the largest quantization tier that will fit (check Strata first)?
 2. Pin the Strata version + model revision + quantization tier, install it, and run an actual benchmark: cold-start time, prefill/decode speeds on short prompts and 8K/32K long prompts, and one needle-in-a-haystack spot check. Record all raw logs.
 3. Cost: At ~5.4 compute units/hour for a Colab A100, estimate the total cost of downloading the weights + running one benchmark round; because prolonged periods without output cause disconnection, run weight downloads in the background and verify progress in stages.
 4. Conclusion: How this path is useful to us (e.g., providing controlled local inference for bots, processing long documents), and what we explicitly must not do (do not change the platform default model, do not expose the API beyond loopback, and do not use `--dangerously-skip-permissions` from the article).
- Deliverables: A "Feasibility and Benchmarks" table on the project page (Configuration / Runs? / Speed / Cost / Issues), log file paths, and a one-sentence conclusion: feasible / only feasible at a lower tier / not worth it.
- Boundaries: Run only on Colab and do not download weights to the workstation (C: drive space is tight); review the model license (Qwen Community License); do not save any tokens/passwords.

Both sub-projects are assigned to this track's bot `ideas` for execution, with gpu-gemini (` gpu`) available to assist on GPU-related tasks; the Lead is personally responsible for reading the results, writing the evaluation table, and updating the project page. Each reporting round should state only the conclusion and next steps.

Analysis of Original License Key Points (Qwen Community License 1.0) - **Original License URL**: - **4 Core Clause Key Points**: 1. **Academic & Internal Use**: The license explicitly grants royalty-free rights to any entity to access, use, modify, fine-tune, distribute, and deploy the model. Internal use within enterprises or academic institutions (without opening interfaces or services to third parties) is completely legal and requires no additional licensing. 2. **Commercial Threshold**: Free commercialization is permitted; only when the licensee's commercial product or service reaches **monthly active users (MAU) exceeding 100 million** or **monthly revenue exceeding 20 million USD** is it mandatory to prominently display the Qwen model name in the product user interface (UI). 3. **Attribution & Redistribution**: All copies of the software and its derivatives must retain in full the original author's copyright notice (Copyright (c) 2026 Qwen) and this license notice. 4. **MaaS & AI Work Assistant Restrictions**: If the licensee engages in commercial business of "Model as a Service (MaaS, providing model inference/fine-tuning APIs to third parties)" or "AI Work Assistant (standalone products primarily used for programming or office assistance)," a separate commercial license must first be requested from Qwen; however, this is limited to situations providing services to third parties, and building such tools for internal use within an organization does not require separate licensing. ## 8. Issues Identified in Testing and Boundary Recommendations 1. **Port conflict boundary**: Colab's default Node.js platform proxy listens on port `8080`; binding the Strata service to 8080 upon startup will cause exit (error code 2); one must explicitly specify `--port 8090` or other unoccupied ports. 2. **Context overflow protection**: The Strata server by default strictly validates requests with `prompt_tokens + max_tokens <= context`, returning 400 if exceeded (rejecting truncation). In 32,768 context testing, prompt length must be controlled within 32,700, or `"fit_max_tokens": true` should be added to the configuration to automatically compress output quota. 3. **MTP speculative decoding mechanism**: The MTP draft layer paired with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next can push short prompt decoding above 128 tok/s in routine Q&A; however, when the model generates highly complex academic/professional text, speculative acceptance rate decreases, and decode rate stabilizes at 35–68 tok/s. 4. **Hardware and memory pairing**: 80GB SXM4 VRAM is sufficient to accommodate 62.8 GB of resident tensors, and high-spec 167GB RAM ensures that all 55 GiB of expert parameters remain directly and fully resident, without SSD page swapping slowdown.

Cold Start and VRAM/RAM Peaks - **Weight Download and SHA-256 Check Time**: **627.1 s** (10.45 min, multi-connection average bandwidth ~150 MB/s) - **Engine Compilation and MTP/GGUF Packaging Time**: **1796.2 s** (29.94 min, A100 sm_80 C++/CUDA Ninja compilation + MTP range request fetch) - **Engine Cold Start Load to First Usable Request Time**: **35.02 s** (0.58 min, initial round populates 55.43 GiB weights into GPU cache and system RAM) - **GPU VRAM Peak**: **64,336 MiB** (62.83 GiB / 80 GiB, VRAM utilization 78.5%, highly consistent with 64,260 MiB reported in Lao Zhang's WeChat article) - **System RAM Peak**: **7,198 MiB** (7.03 GiB user-space memory, with an additional ~159 GiB as page cache hosting all weight shards) ## 6. Engine cold start loading** | 35.0 s | 0.58 min | 0.053 CU | Ready wait for first request | | **4. Full benchmark evaluation suite** | 119.0 s | 1.98 min | 0.179 CU | Includes short text, 8K, 32K, and 3 sets of Needle tests | | **Task itemized net total** | 2577.3 s | 42.96 min | **3.867 CU** | Effective duration of core compute and transmission | | **Platform actual session total settlement** | ~53 min (total session) | ~53.0 min | **5.650 CU** | Platform actual deduction (including port probing, session allocation, and shutdown settlement) | *Note: This project set a 30 CU overall ceiling and a 25 CU safety warning threshold; actual deduction of 5.65 CU is within budget safety margins.* ## 7. Analysis of Original License Key Points (Qwen Community License 1.0) - **Original License URL**: - **4 Core Clause Key Points**: 1. **Academic & Internal Use**: The license explicitly grants royalty-free rights to any entity to access, use, modify, fine-tune, distribute, and deploy the model. Internal use within enterprises or academic institutions (without opening interfaces or services to third parties) is completely legal and requires no additional licensing. 2. **Commercial Threshold**: Free commercialization is permitted; only when the licensee's commercial product or service reaches **monthly active users (MAU) exceeding 100 million** or **monthly revenue exceeding 20 million USD** is it mandatory to prominently display the Qwen model name in the product user interface (UI). 3. **Attribution & Redistribution**: All copies of the software and its derivatives must retain in full the original author's copyright notice (Copyright (c) 2026 Qwen) and this license notice. 4. **MaaS & AI Work Assistant Restrictions**: If the licensee engages in commercial business of "Model as a Service (MaaS, providing model inference/fine-tuning APIs to third parties)" or "AI Work Assistant (standalone products primarily used for programming or office assistance)," a separate commercial license must first be requested from Qwen; however, this is limited to situations providing services to third parties, and building such tools for internal use within an organization does not require separate licensing. ## 8. Issues Identified in Testing and Boundary Recommendations 1. **Port conflict boundary**: Colab's default Node.js platform proxy listens on port `8080`; binding the Strata service to 8080 upon startup will cause exit (error code 2); one must explicitly specify `--port 8090` or other unoccupied ports. 2. **Context overflow protection**: The Strata server by default strictly validates requests with `prompt_tokens + max_tokens <= context`, returning 400 if exceeded (rejecting truncation). In 32,768 context testing, prompt length must be controlled within 32,700, or `"fit_max_tokens": true` should be added to the configuration to automatically compress output quota. 3. **MTP speculative decoding mechanism**: The MTP draft layer paired with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next can push short prompt decoding above 128 tok/s in routine Q&A; however, when the model generates highly complex academic/professional text, speculative acceptance rate decreases, and decode rate stabilizes at 35–68 tok/s. 4. **Hardware and memory pairing**: 80GB SXM4 VRAM is sufficient to accommodate 62.8 GB of resident tensors, and high-spec 167GB RAM ensures that all 55 GiB of expert parameters remain directly and fully resident, without SSD page swapping slowdown.

# Strata + Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Local Inference (Colab A100) (Shelved)

This sub-project tested whether the 125B Mixture-of-Experts model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (6B active parameters per token, 93.68 GB in Unsloth dynamic 4-bit quantization) can run locally with the Strata v0.1.43 engine on a high-memory Colab A100-80GB instance up to 32K context. Benchmarks measured cold-start preparation, time-to-first-token (TTFT), prefill and decode throughput at short (<200 tokens), 8K, and 32K prompts, 32K needle-in-a-haystack retrieval, and license terms. The setup ran without quantization downgrade, reaching 43.0 tok/s median decode and 2,988.5 tok/s prefill at 32K context with 3/3 passkey accuracy. Because the Lab currently lacks a bulk local reading workload that offsets the ~40-minute session setup overhead, the sub-project is Shelved as a validated reserve.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-13**: Liang Hu approved opening the sub-project, and Lab Lead set the Colab A100-80GB high-memory (167 GB system RAM) test protocol with a 30 compute unit (CU) cap and 25 CU pause threshold.
- **2026-10-13**: Lab Lead assigned the benchmark to the research assistant and re-routed execution to the GPU worker when an initial dispatch credential failed.
- **2026-10-13**: Downloading the 93.68 GB weights took 10.45 minutes, while compiling Strata v0.1.43 and packing the multi-token prediction (MTP) draft weights took 29.94 minutes.
- **2026-10-13**: Engine loading took 35.0 seconds, with peak GPU VRAM reaching 62.83 GiB and system RAM holding near 19.6 GiB.
- **2026-10-13**: Short prompts (~39 tokens, 256 generated tokens) achieved 0.561 s median TTFT and 35.6 tok/s median decode (128.8 tok/s peak).
- **2026-10-13**: Medium prompts (7,860 tokens) achieved 4.018 s median TTFT, 1,967.7 tok/s prefill, and 66.8 tok/s median decode (82.0 tok/s peak).
- **2026-10-13**: Long prompts (30,190 tokens) achieved 10.144 s median TTFT, 2,988.5 tok/s prefill, and 43.0 tok/s median decode (59.3 tok/s peak).
- **2026-10-13**: In the 32K needle-in-a-haystack test (~30,206 tokens), 6-digit passkeys at 10%, 50%, and 90% depths were recovered with 3/3 (100%) accuracy.
- **2026-10-13**: The run finished in 52.85 minutes (4.76 CU total); Lab Lead skipped re-running on the research assistant channel to avoid duplicate expenditure.
- **2026-10-13**: Lab Lead audited the raw logs (clarifying that fresh Colab sessions still require ~40 minutes and ~4 CU for download and MTP packing, and that weights resided mainly in GPU VRAM), verified academic permission under Qwen Community License 1.0, and marked the sub-project Shelved.
- **2026-10-13**: Following discussion with Liang Hu on local LLMs (where local 32B scored 82% on abstract screening vs. 85.5% for Gemini 3.8 Flash and 92% vs. 96% on PDF value extraction), Liang Hu approved opening a page-level full-text literature search sub-project instead of training a domain LLM.

## Where it stands

This sub-project is Shelved with a verified script and benchmark baseline on Colab A100-80GB high-memory instances. It can be reactivated immediately if the Lab faces a single-session batch processing workload of hundreds of long documents or privacy-restricted texts that cannot use external APIs. For routine tasks, subscribed cloud flash models and the Promoted full-text search tool remain more economical.

projects.conclusion: 10-14 Promoted to the platform tool pages: all five acceptance groups passed, and Phase 2 non-first-page fact questions reached the target page on 22/27; Phase 3 blind test on 10-14: 21/30 reached the page (Chinese 9/10, Chinese-to-English 8/10, books 4/7, scanned books 0/3); books were weak, and after platform improvement 0062, round3 book page hits rose from 4/10 to 7/10 (meeting the target) while round4 remained 8/12; the desktop I drive is connected and inventoried: net new ~12.5k PDFs / 420k pages, with Phase 1 extracting 289k text-layer pages (1.8 GB on the workstation); desktop corpus 0069 went live (10-16), hitting the target page on 11/30 in the 台式机 blind test (vs. 24/30 for the two libraries), with improvement leads handed to the platform; 10-15 all tracks pushed forward: OCR of the remaining 105k pages completed at 10-16 02:38 (105,336 pages, handed to 0069), three-library metadata and work-level deduplication, 31,365 pages of djvu/pdg books handed to the platform (472 Chaoxing-format pages unresolved), and litwiki/knowledge trial results returned; ingestion awaits 0051 and C drive cleanup. 10-13 conclusion: retrieval only. Two libraries with 4,691 PDFs / 129k pages indexed locally by page; for non-first-page fact questions, top-5 results hit the exact page about half the time (English 8/14, Chinese originals 5/5, Chinese queries on English papers 3/5 after query translation, books 4/6), paper-level 1/27; platform integration underway (three phases, Phase 1 within the week), prototype frozen as baseline; `pages` Phase 1 is live (tested 10-13 22:40); OCR of 79 scanned documents / 5,422 pages handed to Phase 2. Profile extraction is Shelved (single-page text had 6/78 errors and 27/78 requiring qualification, with figure pages often mislocated); 0 CU; books on the other computer await information from Liang Hu
projects.goal: Answer "how to get the most out of Liang Hu's paper library and book library". No fine-tuning of large models; try (1) full-text search across the whole library with citable page numbers; (2) extracting one class of wind-engineering data from papers into a table. Brief.

# 文献库全文检索 + 风工程数据抽取

## 目标
回答"Liang Hu 的论文库/书籍库怎么用最值"。不微调大模型；试 (1) 全库全文检索、可引页码；(2) 从论文中抽一类风工程数据成表。任务书。

## 当前状态

projects.brief:
# Task Brief: Full-text search of the literature library + wind-engineering data extraction (New Lab Idea, Approved by Liang Hu on 10-13)

## Questions to Answer
How to get the most value out of the paper library accumulated by Liang Hu over the years (Zotero, 3,163 PDFs, 17.7 GB, of which 2,422 already have Zotero's built-in full-text cache `.zotero-ft-cache`) and the book library (location to be provided by Liang Hu). 10-13 assessment: **Do not use them to fine-tune an LLM** (the corpus is on the order of 10M–100M tokens, too small for continued pretraining; retrieval outperforms fine-tuning for knowledge injection; fine-tuning cannot provide source citations; copyright risks—per Review verdict Clause 4). Instead, test two things:
1. **Full-text search**: Chunk and index the entire library, connect it to the existing tool or build a command with identical usage, so Q&A can cite the exact paper and page number from the original text.
2. **Data extraction**: Pick one type of wind-engineering data (recommended: downburst vertical wind speed profiles, or high-rise building wind pressure coefficients / gust factors), extract it from dozens of papers into a table with sources and page numbers, spot-check against the original pages, and calculate accuracy and manual verification workload.

## No Local LLM Needed
Retrieval only requires a small text embedding model (runnable on CPU) or keyword search; extraction defaults to the Gemini 3.8 Flash batch pipeline, with 10% of each batch spot-checked by Claude (trial rule for this track as of 10-13). Local Qwen is considered only when encountering materials that should not be sent externally.

## Criteria (Pre-specified)
- Retrieval: Prepare ≥30 questions with ground-truth answers (known answer page numbers) and measure the proportion hitting the exact passage within the top 5 results; compare against the existing tool (which only covers literature with existing cards).
- Extraction: Value-by-value accuracy verified against the original pages; average manual verification time per paper; comparison against published datasets in the literature (if available).

## Boundaries
- Only ~51 GB remains on the C: drive: store indices and intermediate files on the local WSL disk (706 GB free) and do not write large files to the local Windows drive; write experimental artifacts (small files, scripts, result `.md` files) to the project directory.
- Keep the Zotero library read-only: do not modify `zotero.sqlite` or touch `storage`.
- Do not send full book texts to external services; when sending papers to Gemini for extraction, send only the relevant pages.
- Total cost ≤10 CU (if Colab is needed); do not modify the platform core—if integration is needed, write a proposal and submit it to the Platform Lead.
- Document any newly used external tools/models.

## Deliverables
An evaluation table on the project page (Stage / Feasible / Quality / Cost / Issues), retrieval hit rate, extraction accuracy and sample table, and a one-sentence conclusion: worth turning into a formal tool/dataset / do retrieval only / not worth it.

items.label: Result
items.title: Pre-registered criteria (frozen before the search run; do not modify)
items.text:
# Pre-registered Criteria (Frozen before retrieval run, do not modify)

Scope: Papers from local Zotero PDF attachments, excluding books and book chapters; read-only access to the original library. Extraction is performed physical page by physical page of the PDF, with page numbers starting from 1; indices and databases on disk contain only scripts and small evaluation results. Extraction failures and textless pages are tallied and disclosed, without treating text cache as page numbers.

A: At least 30 pre-frozen paraphrased questions, with answers independently verified against original PDF physical pages; covering downbursts, tall building wind pressure, wind spectra, CFD, and structural response, with at least 10 papers having cards in and at least 10 papers without cards. Questions and answers are written to questions.jsonl prior to the first retrieval, recording the question bank SHA-256; questions must not be created verbatim from the same source text. BM25, small CPU dense vector, and hybrid retrieval are all tested on the same questions; for the top-5 results per question (in units of unique paper-page), correct paper and page ±1 counts as a primary metric hit; correct paper only counts as a secondary metric. For , top-5 on the same questions are judged by paper; unverifiable page numbers are recorded as unjudgeable page numbers and do not count as hits. Report raw question-by-question results and grouped hit rates, without using an incomplete subset to pose as 30 questions. Feasibility-in-principle gate: hybrid retrieval primary metric ≥0.70, showing gain over BM25, and coverage ≥0.90; this is only prototype feasibility, not a publication-grade conclusion.

B: 30–40 papers actually containing profiles, including field measurements, wind tunnel, and CFD; send only the text of relevant PDF pages to Gemini 3.8 Flash, prompting to extract strictly based on visible content, leaving missing items blank, preserving page numbers, figure/table numbers, units, normalization, and r/D definitions. At least 60 atomic values are checked value-by-value against original PDF pages, reporting per-field accuracy (correct / checked non-empty values), omission rate (visible on original page but not extracted / fields that should have been extracted from original page), manual verification time per paper, and verifier; readings from figures must be labeled as figure readings, without inferring ambiguous numerical values. Metrics whose experimental measured values do not reach scale are marked 'unevaluated' and cannot be claimed as passed. Uploading full text, using local large models, modifying Zotero, running on supercomputers, or overwriting existing results is prohibited. Log the number of pages sent to external models and call volume. The final recommendation should be selected from 'formal tool/dataset', 'retrieval only', or 'not worthwhile'; if scale is not reached, it can only remain tentative.

items.label: Result
items.title: Error types in downburst profile extraction (single-page text experiment)
items.text:
# Downburst Profile Extraction Error Types (Single-Page Text Pilot)

1. Paper category and source confusion: Papers with both numerical/experimental in the title cannot have the source of the profile cited on this page determined based solely on the title. `kind` is a heuristic label, unverified paper by paper, and cannot be treated as field measurement / wind tunnel / CFD ground truth.
2. Mistaking cited paper values for this paper: "almost 80 m" on PDF physical page 2 of `SAI7PQLC` cites Hjelmfelt (1988) and cannot be attributed as the z_max of this paper (verification record already judged as error).
3. Treating normalized velocity as absolute maximum: Vr/Vjet≈1 on p.3 of `EFT4W6FE` cannot be treated as a unified U_max; velocity definitions across different r/D and heights must be separated (verification record already judged invalid).
4. z_max confusion: z_m and u_m on p.15 of `MBLWBMR6` are model symbols, not observed numerical values; Z/D≈0.06 on p.9 of `R5RKQGYZ` is non-dimensional height and must not be recorded as 0.06 m.
5. Distinction between figure reading and text: This round sent only one page of extractable text, with no images sent. Having curves in a figure caption does not mean reading the maximum value off the figure; figure reading precision cannot be reverse-inferred.
6. Misattributing figure numbers: When multiple figures are listed on a page at the same time, if the model only takes Fig. 9 without labeling the corresponding (a)–(d) and r/D, the radial position may be mismatched.
7. Omissions: 34 papers each had one page sent; many papers' relevant parameters are on other pages, and null values do not indicate that the full text has no data; a complete full-text omission rate cannot be computed in this round.
8. Optical character recognition / typesetting: PDF two-column interleaving, ¼/≈, ligatures, and captions blending into main text may lead to misjudgments of units, formula exponents, and page numbers. Journal print pages and PDF physical pages are recorded separately.

Verification principle: The appearance of numbers on the same page is merely literal co-occurrence, which does not prove that they belong to that model, figure/table, or data source; automatic numerical co-occurrence results in are not treated as scientific accuracy.

Round 2 adds non-first-page cross-page fact questions, book/Chinese questions, deduplicated top 5, extraction of ≥60 values verified + full-text ground truth omission rate + Gemini image figure reading.

# Supplementary Preregistered Criteria (EndNote and Books; Written Before Library Expansion and Supplementary Question Evaluation)
The original criteria.md is the frozen record of the previous round and will not be modified. Newly added all PDFs in EndNote Phd.Data/PDF and Zotero attachments such as book/bookSection/thesis; original libraries are read-only, indexed on DOI (only when metadata is trustworthy); otherwise normalize titles (Unicode NFKC, lowercase, removing punctuation and whitespace; overly short titles are not automatically merged), and identical titles with different editions/years must be flagged with risk. When EndNote has no structured metadata that can be parsed, derive titles and coarse types from filenames, reporting them as estimates without falsely claiming precision. The scanned proportion is approximated using extractable text pages or tests on PDF initial pages; image text is indistinguishable, and OCR is not performed.
The evaluation adds at least 5 questions with answers in books and at least 3 Chinese questions, with independent answers containing PDF physical pages and same-page verbatim source evidence; save the question bank first, then retrieve. The newly added questions are tested separately on the original BM25 and enhanced Chinese retrieval; top-5 hits for correct document and page ±1 and hits for document only are listed separately. Book questions should span beyond the first page as much as possible and be manually paraphrased, not using verbatim title sentences as questions. Chinese retrieval must not call external translation services; full text of books must not be sent externally. Results of the original 34 questions are retained; if retested after adding new corpus material, clearly state the base count and version, and do not conflate reports. Textless layers and failures are recorded as coverage discrepancies.

items.title: Correction to the inventory interpretation (the already generated corpus inventory.md is not changed)
items.text:
# Corrections to Inventory Interpretation (Without Modifying the Generated corpus_inventory.md)

The "lower bound of EndNote book markings" in corpus_inventory.md is invalid: the filename heuristic classified `Hill - 2010 - Climate and Tropical Cyclones.pdf` as a book, but the PDF cover page and table of contents show that it is a research degree document; 9 is the count of heuristic candidates, neither an exact value nor a lower bound. The vast majority of EndNote items (1517/1527) are unclassified, making it impossible to give a reliable, complete distribution by book / chapter / thesis / journal article. EndNote bibliographic metadata should first be decoded or manually annotated; 9 cannot be treated as the book count.

"no_text ~3.4% is the lower bound of OCR workload" is also not rigorous: textless files may be pure image scans, or may have extremely short content, corruption, or extractor anomalies; PDFs with text may still contain scanned pages. Therefore, 159/4691=3.39% is the proportion of attachments with entirely no indexable text, which is neither the proportion of scanned files across the full library nor a strict lower bound for OCR. In , 159 items total 10,553 physical pages; if all require OCR, approx. this many pages would need to be processed, but this is a conditional scale estimate, not a confirmed count of scanned pages. Another 31 items had extraction failures/timeouts and cannot be counted as scans. Follow-up work requires sampling PDF page images to re-estimate actual OCR workload.

Cross-library merging relies solely on Zotero DOIs and normalized filename titles, while EndNote lacks structured DOIs; the 3,845 in represents "candidate work clusters" rather than a verified count of unique documents. In particular, both false merges of different editions with the same title and missed merges due to truncated filenames may occur. The 87/32/60 user-provided Zotero itemTypes are entry counts; the corresponding visible PDF attachments in this round are 73/26/50, representing different counting targets.
