# Zotero Full-Text Retrieval × Downburst Profile Minimal Pilot (10-13, US Eastern)

## One-Sentence Judgment

Build only a full-text retrieval prototype, without turning this round's Gemini single-page extractions into a formal dataset. English first-page paper identification questions show clear gains; Chinese retrieval almost completely fails, and data extraction field attribution, definitions, and figure readings still require page-by-page manual handling. This round is a pilot trial, not publication-grade validation or formal tool approval.

## Scope and Actual Execution

- Zotero original library is read-only; first copy `zotero.sqlite` to . Exclude book/bookSection by attachment parent type, index ; local FTS5 Porter BM25, `pdftotext -layoutprocessed` table logs the cause of each failure.
- Retrieval prototype: , or . Outputs title, year, parent key, PDF physical page, and snippet. BGE-small-en-v1.5 encodes on CPU over the top 60 pages recalled by BM25 across the full library and reranks via RRF; it is not an independent full-library vector ANN index. retains standalone full-page vector construction code, but only has a few incomplete test shards, not participating in reported scoring; it must not be claimed that a full-library vector index has been built.
- Question bank: Chinese 34 questions, question-by-question manual English paraphrases 34 questions (frozen before retrieval). 11 papers have cards in the wiki directory, 23 do not; spanning downbursts, tall building wind pressure, wind spectra, CFD, structural response. English question bank SHA256 `8dc91c50996c4c1367644f12df5930f1d040e22ad9de60cf6a78ef9a95323d39`, Chinese `40a22641e84df724fef5272f15eca7ba8281ec2ce25d23685555610724a563b1`. Questions are mostly paraphrases of titles/abstracts, and standard answers are all PDF physical page 1; easier than real cross-page fact QA, and metrics can only be interpreted as paper discovery and first-page localization. Journal print pages and physical pages must not be used interchangeably.

## Retrieval Measurements After Full-Library Indexing Completion (34 Questions, Top 5 Paper-Pages)

| Identical English Question Bank | Correct Paper and PDF Page ±1 | Paper Hit Only | Basis |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| BM25 | 25/34=73.5% | 29/34=85.3% | |
| BM25→CPU BGE-small hybrid reranking | 27/34=79.4% | 30/34=88.2% | |
| Existing | Unjudgeable: search output has no verifiable PDF physical page | 14/34=41.2% | |

On the original Chinese question bank (untranslated), both BM25 and only hit papers for 2/34, with BM25 exact page at 0/34. The English conversion is another pre-frozen test input and cannot be treated as Chinese questions reaching English performance as well. Raw top-5 lists for each question are in , . Preregistered English primary metric ≥70%, hybrid outperforming BM25, and index coverage ≥90% were all met; but first-page anchoring introduces an easy-question bias, and the Chinese applicability gate was not passed. page numbers must not be treated as PDF page numbers just because cards occasionally contain journal page numbers.

## Downburst Profile Experiment and Verification

- Exploratory Round 1 had 34 single-page texts; candidate selection was too loose, and all 34 were returned. Round 2 selected 36 papers from PDF pages containing profile figure captions (the labeled 12 CFD, 14 wind tunnel, 10 other are merely title heuristics, and cannot serve as verified source types), plus one field measurement paper: Romanic (2021) Cabauw 213m tower, PDF physical page 17, Fig. 16.
- Round 2, 36 papers: `z_max` has 11 non-empty entries, each row detailing PDF path, physical page, verifier, and rationale. Round 1 separately verified 10 items, 8 directly correct, 2 errors.
- Because semantic value-by-value manual verification was not performed on at least 60 items (only 97 items were automatically compared literally), there were no paper-by-paper timing records, and only one selected page was analyzed without full-text ground truth, the planned per-field overall accuracy, omission rate, and average manual verification time per paper are all **unevaluated**; the aforementioned non-random 12 items must not be used to compute overall accuracy. All CSVs are unaccepted sample tables and cannot be used as reusable datasets. Readings off figures were completely unread; no "figure reading" values may be assigned. Typical errors: other papers' cited values misattributed to the present study (`SAI7PQLC` p2), maximum velocity mismatched to different radial positions on the same page (`KN57R2JT` p24), treating assumed parameter sweep ranges as measured peak heights (`WZN3ETI3` p4), treating non-dimensional velocity as absolute Umax (`EFT4W6FE` p3). Details in and two verification CSVs.

## Judgment Table

| Stage | Feasible | Quality | Cost | Issues |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PDF by page + BM25 | Yes, 3065 attachments attempted | English first-page questions 25/34 exact page | Local CPU; indexing approx. tens of minutes; 0 CU | Missing OCR, 12 errors/timeouts, Chinese queries almost completely ineffective |
| CPU small dense vector hybrid reranking | Yes, reranking top 60 BM25 pages is operational | English first-page questions 27/34 exact page, +2 questions | Local BGE-small, 0 CU | Not independent full-page vector recall; cannot replace Chinese query handling |
| Comparison | Yes | English paper hit 14/34, page numbers unjudgeable | Existing service | Retrieval targets are cards, not full PDFs |
| Single-page Gemini data extraction | Can produce sample tables, cannot be directly ingested | Manual 12 items: only 5 directly correct, 6 with reservations, 1 error; 97 items checked literally, failing to meet 60-item manual verification | 71 subscription calls, 0 CU; manual verification time not recorded | Missing figure readings, field definitions and sources confused, omission rate unknown |

## Plan for Integration with (Platform Unmodified)

Maintain the Zotero PDF page index as an independent read-only service, exposing `search(query, top_k)` returning parent key, attachment key, PDF physical page, title/year, snippet, and index timestamp; only aggregates results and maps parent keys to existing cards. Card journal page numbers and PDF physical pages serve as two distinct fields and must never be swapped; pages without OCR are marked as missing. Chinese queries must explicitly undergo query translation or switch to multilingual dense vectors with re-preregistered tests containing cross-page facts before considering formal integration. Synchronization relies on read-only snapshots of the replicated Zotero library and attachment mtime, without touching the production library; integration remains the responsibility of the platform.

## Round 2 Supplement (10-13, US Eastern)
For new evidence and limitations regarding dual-library cross-page facts, books/Chinese, deduplicated retrieval, and extraction verification, see and in the same directory. Round 1 criteria and results remain preserved as above; follow-up results from the corrected figure-reading delegation to in Round 2 are only appended, without altering old numbers.

Recommendation: Retrieval only, do not initiate wind engineering dataset construction. Running English page-by-page retrieval standalone is valuable, but specialized validation must still be added for Chinese users and real cross-page QA; this round's data extraction did not pass the preregistered verification scale. Data source is Liang Hu's local Zotero PDFs; external software/model sources are in . No full text of any paper was sent externally.

# Literature Corpus Round 2: Dual-Library Cross-Page Retrieval and Profile Verification (10-13, US Eastern)

Same dual-library index, Zotero/EndNote original libraries are read-only; 4,691 PDFs, 128,708 non-empty physical pages. Original has appended Round 2 supplementary notes; corrections regarding the unreliability of EndNote book counts and scanned proportions see .

## Frozen Question Bank and Quality Verdict
 Frozen SHA-256 prior to retrieval.

## Results of Top 5 Deduplicated by "Normalized Title + PDF Physical Page"
| Question Group | BM25 Correct Paper + Page ±1 | Chinese trigram + Terminology Table | CPU Small Dense Vector Local Reranking | rc-kb Verifiable Paper Hits* |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original English first-page 34 questions recomputed | 25/34 | 25/34 | BGE-small-en 29/34 | Original round 14/34, physical page unjudgeable |
| New cross-page 30 original questions (incl. 3 bad questions) | 12/30 | 17/30 | Multilingual MiniLM 14/30 | 1/30, physical page unjudgeable |
| Valid cross-page 27 questions (symmetrically excluded) | 9/27 | 14/27 | Multilingual MiniLM 12/27 | 1/27, physical page unjudgeable |
| book metadata group 6 questions (two are actually reports) | 4/6 | 4/6 | 4/6 | 0/6 |
| Physical books/guides 4 questions (descriptive) | 2/4 | 2/4 | 3/4 | Not evaluated separately |
| Chinese original papers 5 questions | 0/5 | 5/5 | 4/5 | 0/5 |
| Chinese questions on English 5 questions | 0/5 | 0/5 | 0/5 | 0/5 |

For the 5 Chinese questions on English, human manual translation of questions into English only was additionally conducted without sending literature: English translated questions BM25 3/5, with multilingual model reranking on its top 100 recalled pages 2/5. Models `paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2`, reranked on CPU only over BM25/Chinese terminology candidates, not independent full-library vector recall. Merging by same title and same physical page across attachments may cause false merges across different editions, or missed merges due to alternate spellings. * Comparison conservatively identified based on wiki card paths containing standard source keys; variant keys on cards were missed, so 1/27 is merely a verifiable lower bound, not representing full recall; card line numbers cannot be treated as PDF physical pages. Question-by-question raw , scoring , grouping , post-hoc symmetric exclusions. Dual-library deduplication CLI has already run Chinese questions and output keys / physical pages / snippets; unmodified.

## Profile Extraction Re-Verification
Among the original 97 non-empty fields in v2, an AI assistant read their original PDF physical pages entry by entry, re-verifying 78 items: 45 supported by same-page text (unconfirmed figure by figure), 27 requiring reservations on definition/operating condition, 6 errors. Not independent human verification, non-random sample, 45/78 is not a formal accuracy rate. Field distribution: z_max 1 directly supported / 8 with reservations / 1 error (10 total), U_max 1/3/0 (4), r/D 1/5/0 (6), normalization 9/5/0 (14), source_type 17/0/2 (19), rest see . With no human verifiers and no per-paper human timing, the planned per-field true accuracy and average manual verification time are both unevaluated. 8 full PDF texts underwent read-only candidate keyword scanning (135 pages, 805 candidates), not a page-by-page manual read-through, so omission rate is unevaluated.

Among the 8 sample table figure number pages originally extracted, for 5 papers the target figure was only mentioned in the text of that page, while the actual figure was on other physical pages. All corrected to the 8 single pages of ; only these single pages were sent to the Gemini worker. confirmed wrong pages in the first round; corrected figure page results from have returned. Local AI previously did rough reading, comparing paper by paper and condition by condition; and re-visually inspected 8 actual pages: 5 papers matched the rough reading range under the same condition, 1 paper matched only model parameter semantics, 1 paper's figure was too dense for quantitative per-radial evaluation, 1 paper could only be partially compared. These are all estimated reading consistency between AI and AI, not accuracy or error distribution against independent human figure-reading ground truth; per-curve figure reading errors and reliable completion rates for empty fields remain unevaluated. 6X6ZP3YD p8 Fig.15b 60° CFD approx. 25–30mm, 5.9–6.0m/s, is merely figure reading; 25–100m in WZN3ETI3 p4 is a model parameter sweep, not four observations. Error correction gates: 36XAQH9L workstation Fig. 15 does not provide R/D=1.2 (it belongs to Fig. 20 context); NXSSET4J p12 Fig. 11 α=0°, original text 0.099m belongs to α=180°, must not be mismatched; 8IC5IFK5 p7 seven radial points are crowded, cannot give precise per-radial peak heights; GBK98YNH p5 main vortex is an ensemble average of local peaks across heights rather than a simultaneous profile. Normalized peak velocity equal to 1 is a definition and must not be treated as absolute Umax; r/D cannot be conflated with planar jet x/b. These figure-read values have not been incorporated into the formal sample table.

## Judgment
Local retrieval is feasible, Chinese original papers at 5/5 show promise; however, valid cross-page questions and physical book questions fall short of preset numbers, Chinese questions on English are 0/5, and physical internal book pages are 2–3/4, so the formal full-text tool cannot yet be released. Data extraction has obvious problems with variable definitions, figure page localization, external cited values, and condition pairing, lacking human verification and ground truth read-through, so a formal dataset cannot be built. Recommended to select "retrieval only": preserve the local independent prototype, clean up frozen question banks, verify book authenticity, implement translation retrieval, and then evaluate formal integration. No Colab/HPC used (0 CU), no full PDF sent externally; links for the new multilingual model have been added. Gemini corrected figure page comparisons have been appended, without altering frozen questions and old retrieval results.

# Local Scanned PDF OCR Delivery (Platform 0034 Phase II)

Time: 10-13 22:00–22:35 (ET). Read only the original PDFs from the two libraries; did not modify , the original question bank, or original retrieval scripts; did not call external services, Colab, or supercomputers (0 CU). Used local Poppler `pdftoppm` (longest side 2100 px) + Tesseract 4.1.1 `engchi_sim+eng`, writing plain text by PDF physical page without rewriting source PDFs. Source list: this track.

## Scale and Deduplication

- Input 159 attachments (Zotero 83, EndNote 76), totaling 10,553 PDF physical pages. After file-by-file SHA-256 byte deduplication: 80 items, 5,749 pages (79 duplicate attachments, 4,804 duplicate pages); further confirmed that two different-byte PDFs of *Introduction to Tropical Cyclone Dynamics* (327 pages each) had **completely identical text page by page (327/327)** under the same OCR parameters, so the index list delivered to the platform was folded by one more item: **79 items, 5,422 physical pages**. Folding was applied only to the delivery list; original OCR output is retained, and all 159 attachment keys are in the `aliases` of the list. This method cannot prove that other different scanned versions never duplicate.
- Final list by original source attribution: Zotero 75 items, EndNote 4 items; preliminary assessment based on evident Chinese characters in OCR and titles classified 2 items / 337 pages as Chinese literature, and 77 items / 5,085 pages as English, etc. English author names containing the Chinese "和" are not counted as Chinese literature; language identification is only a rough classification, not manual confirmation paper by paper.
- Among the 5,422 delivered pages, 5,407 pages have OCR text and 15 pages are blank; program failures: 0 pages. In thumbnail pixel percentage inspection, 13 of the blank pages were nearly completely white, and the other 2 dark images still had no text after inversion and re-OCR; one cannot conclude from this that these two pages have no important figures or tables. Running `pdftotext` on full text of source PDFs, there were no native text pages with ≥100 characters among the 80 items, thus no misclassified extractable text-layer PDFs were found in this batch; this does not prove that every page definitely has readable text.
- Plain text is approximately 10,423,317 bytes (counted from first-time OCR page files), delivery page list ; each page file is . Each line of the list has page number, file path, original PDF, SHA-256, source, and all attachment keys. Details , source file hash mapping , native text verification . The platform should use for ingestion; do not re-ingest non-deduplicated .

## Three-Item Pilot and Cost

Ran test runs on 3 pages each of the Chinese *Introduction to Tropical Cyclone Dynamics*, English Wilcox *Turbulence Modeling for CFD*, and Rotunno–Emanuel paper. 9 pages totaled 26.44 seconds; average 2.94 seconds/page, estimated at about 4.43 hours for a single process based on the folded 5,422 pages. In practice, parallelized in batches across 3→10 threads, including mid-course thread count changes and separate recognition of the Chinese duplicate copy, completing from 22:00 to approximately 22:35; the main batch recorded average per-page OCR+rendering of 2.35 seconds, median 2.18 seconds (parallel task time is not wall-clock divided by page count). Full volume was projected not to exceed 12 hours, with no need for Colab or external computing. Single Chinese pages typically took ~3–7 seconds, English body text typically ~1–4 seconds. Page-by-page elapsed time records , ; retry of the Chinese duplicate copy with different bytes is located at , without overwriting old output.

## Quality Check and Limitations

Read 20 pages of OCR text locally, recorded in (two pages each from 10 files, retaining short excerpts). Signs of proper noun, word segmentation, or number errors were visible on 8 pages, evident distortion risks in formulas/symbols on 8 pages, and signs of OCR errors in table of contents/headers on 4 pages; e.g., garbled text appeared near city names on p8 of the Chinese book, and formula variables and subscripts were distorted in the English papers. The text is sufficient for initial attempts at keyword recall, but cannot be directly cited for formulas or numerical values.

**Important unmet item: These 20 pages are manual text spot-checks of the OCR output, not word-by-word manual proofreading against PDF images.** This execution environment cannot provide reliable visual word-by-word proofreading for me without exfiltrating copyrighted page images; per confidentiality boundaries, no image pages were sent to external vision services. Therefore, character/word error rates, accuracy of Chinese proper nouns, and English formula accuracy for the 20 pages relative to the original pages are all **unevaluated**; the above classifications must not be treated as recognition accuracy. Before entering formal retrieval, it is recommended to manually check 20 pages via a local visual interface and mark errors page by page; citations will still return original PDF physical pages for manual verification.

Delivery acceptance is "page-level text mappable by original attachment key", not verified OCR precision or cross-page retrieval hit rate. Old files from Phase I of 0034, both and , were not touched. This report is a new file.

# Phase III Blind Test:  pages Chinese and English, Books and Scanned Books (10-14 10:04, ET)

This file and `questions_blind.jsonlresults.jsonl are both read-only; prototype retrieval was not called. The 30 questions were frozen before running scores; the SHA-256 of is `d80069db26f2bc53914f58d73556ef283d216ffd513a71ea3aac5c1bf10bd83b` (see `freeze.sha256`); 10 questions for original Chinese, 10 questions for Chinese asking about English, 10 non-first-page questions for physical books, with the last group including 3 OCR scanned book page questions: Wilcox, Dahlquist, and *Introduction to Tropical Cyclone Dynamics*. Each question points to physical page 3 or later of the PDF; titles and abstracts cannot serve as answers. For each question, only the question text was sent to ` pages "question" -n 5`; question bank answers and book page source texts were not sent to the service.  automatically translates Chinese questions; this service's own documentation states that it only transmits question text externally.

## Criteria and Verification

Continuing to use `criteria.mdpdftotext -f N -l N` to reread source PDFs: 26 short anchors matched verbatim; R3-18 did not match verbatim due to different symbolic hyphenation notation, but the original page indeed has the four corners `0°, 15°, 30° and 45°`, see . The 3 OCR questions were locally re-rendered from the specified PDF physical pages and recognized a second time with independent `tesseract --psm 6`: all three answer anchors were reproduced (Wilcox "Vortex stretching", Dahlquist "first quadrant", Chinese book "1672mm"). However, independent verbatim proofreading could not be performed by visually inspecting original scanned pages, particularly with OCR typos in Chinese place names; numerical ground truth on scanned pages should still be reviewed by someone able to visually inspect PDF images. Agreement between two OCR runs cannot be called human image ground truth.

## Frozen Scoring (One Formal Call per Question, Scores Not Modified by Diagnostic Queries)

| Question Group | Question Count | Top 5 Correct Work | Top 5 Correct Work and Physical Page ±1 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original Chinese, Chinese questions | 10 | 10 | 9 |
| Chinese asking about English papers | 10 | 9 | 8 |
| Physical books native text | 7 | 4 | 4 |
| Physical scanned books OCR pages | 3 | 2 | 0 |
| Total | 30 | 25/30 (83.3%) | 21/30 (70.0%) |

Raw question-by-question output is in (including questions and as-is responses), verdict is in , grouping table is in . Automated scoring was originally 19/30; the original EndNote *Review of Typhoon Wind Field Models* and the same-named PDF in Zotero with English metadata had identical byte SHA-256, and physical pages 7/9 in Zotero directly hit R3-09/10 respectively; after restoring the two cross-library same-work hits, it became 21/30. Same-title different-edition copies were not used to impersonate the same page.

## Incorrect Questions and Diagnostics (All Retained as Formal Failures)

- Page errors in 4 questions: R3-01, 17, 29, 30. For the latter two questions, the OCR target pages have text, but only returned the book's first page or adjacent opening pages, not confirmed OCR recognition errors.
- Unretrieved in 5 questions: R3-14, 21, 23, 24, 28. Three native book questions did not enter the top five. Under the frozen Chinese query, R3-14 did not make the list, but an additional explicit English query could locate page 8 of the same work in Zotero; under the frozen query, R3-28 did not make the list, but an additional explicit English query could locate Wilcox page 30 (see ). These are merely diagnostics of the retrieval/translation chain and cannot replace formal scores; other unretrieved cases cannot yet be attributed to translation.
- Causal count of OCR misreads: 0 confirmed items, but this does not imply the OCR misread rate is zero; source pages of the Chinese scanned book were not visually verified for ground truth. In particular, the OCR Chinese book was attached as "Some remarks concerning the gradient-wind equation" (1949) in the output, while the actual PDF path was *Introduction to Tropical Cyclone Dynamics*: this is a mismatch of source metadata / work identification, and cannot be cited as a book under that incorrect title. The Dahlquist scanned book also only returned the first page rather than the factual page.

This is a small, non-random sample self-selected by the research team with multiple questions per work; it cannot be extrapolated to full-library retrieval accuracy, nor can it be considered to have passed the initial prototype gate just because it hit exactly 70%. 0/3 on the 3 OCR book questions is not yet sufficient to call Phase III "citable book pages" reliable. No Colab / HPC / external transmission of copyrighted book full text, 0 CU; did not modify or the Phase I frozen index.

Recommendations: Retain pages local retrieval for manual review; formal scientific citations, especially scanned book pages, must open the original PDF to verify pages and OCR numbers. Platform Phase III should prioritize checking long-book target page ranking, Chinese query translation, and mismatched work metadata for OCR attachments; report only aggregated phenomena, do not hand over blind questions and answers to the platform. Decision criterion: Retrieval only; do not yet announce that formal tools or datasets have passed acceptance.

A: Recommended: do not copy PDFs. ## Packaged Pages and Platform Ingestion Interface

The platform must retain the original desktop paths rather than pointing to the PDF copies on the Workstation.

Because the uncompressed full JSONL with paths repeated page-by-page was estimated at 262,735,191 bytes (250.56 MiB), exceeding the boundary of "newly written not exceeding 200 MB" for this run, a full-field `.jsonl.gz` and a sub-200 MB compact `.jsonl` + alias table are provided; there was no false claim that the compact version includes dual paths page-by-page. Path aliases for backfilled items currently only include their respective original paths; if the platform discovers additional copies, a separate byte verification must be performed.

This round of OCR only progressed up to Book/中文; the remaining 105,338 pages must not continue running on the Workstation, and are to be handled according to the new location and space strategy designated by the Lead. # OCR Phase 3 Post-Restart Continuation: Integrity Gate Failed

Time: 10-16 02:22 (EDT).

The existing ControlMaster socket check on the desktop passed; the root drive is mounted read-write (`rw`). Found continuation process PID 22492 already started at 10-16 00:56 targeting the working copy. No duplicate process was launched. The log recorded `START 1718 already 103620 workers 6 DONE 1718 errors 0 empty 30 wall_s 4746.2`, and the process had already exited.

However, during the final acceptance query, a read-only `select count(*)` raised `sqlite3.DatabaseError: database disk image is malformed`. A subsequent read-only `PRAGMA integrity_check(1)` returned `*** in database main ***; Page 62028: btreeInitPage returns error code 11`. Consequently, **the 105,338-page result cannot be certified as valid**; no final `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` was executed, no copy was made to the final target (the target file does not exist), and no repair or rerun was attempted, pending a decision by the platform team / Lead on how to preserve the scene and diagnose the issue.

As of 10-16 02:22, the main database copy is 256,315,392 bytes with a 0-byte WAL (likely auto-checkpointed when the writer process closed), and its SHA-256 is `a1a4b180415f30a8dbceec8c73314de9323fe793c7fac5d5087e2916fa814e93`. This hash **is solely for locating the corrupted file and is not a usable final delivery hash**. The previous database was not modified by this task, and no final new file was created. Reliable post-continuation counts of `documents`/`pages`/`errors` are unavailable because count queries immediately trigger the corruption exception.

Conclusion: The continuation log completed, but the database integrity gate failed; delivery is paused and this copy must not be used for ticket 0069 ingestion. Prior to the restart, the copy passed integrity check (`ok`, 103,620 pages); the exact cause of corruption remains undetermined and should not be attributed to the script or 9p without evidence.

## Root-Drive Continuation Acceptance (10-16 02:32, EDT)

The root-drive log shows `DONE 2498 errors 2 empty 72 wall_s 6074.8`, taking ~1 h 41 min 15 s; the process exited naturally, requiring no further start, stop, or scheduled check-in. Running `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` against the root-drive database returned `(0,0,0)`, and a full `PRAGMA integrity_check` returned `ok`. Read-only verification shows `documents` = 1,713, `pages` = 105,336, and `errors` = 2; the sum of page records and error records is 105,338, so **105,336 successful pages must not be misstated as 105,338 successful pages**.

Both failures occurred in the same PDF (SHA-256 `a15a0660a3c55e5b44b28250c7063eea364eec23ae5595d2a4d61d9fe4cd28ce`): physical PDF pages 41 and 45 both hit the 180 s timeout during single-page rendering via `pdftoppm -scale-to 1800 -gray -png` (logged at ~180.180 s and ~180.102 s, respectively). Neither page was rerun or repaired.

A new final copy was created on the root drive (where none existed previously); both the source database and the final copy are 256,282,624 bytes with matching SHA-256 `2f2a3e8625eaf9d5c923caa2ec4d88fd0227407e767b52502319b1ca2c830a6b`, and the final copy independently passed `integrity_check=ok`. The corrupted copy on the mounted drive is preserved untouched. The root-drive final database may be used as downstream input for ticket 0069, provided the two timed-out pages above are explicitly excluded or handled during ingestion rather than counted as successfully OCR'd.

# 台式机第三阶段 OCR — 阶段性终版（2 页失败待单独处理）

10-15 10:29（美东）检查复用 ControlMaster socket 存活；台式机 24 核、46 GiB 内存、WSL 盘空闲 664 GiB。台式机原 PDF 只读，未在 工作站 做 OCR，也未外送页图/文本，0 CU。台式机 工作目录 为本阶段唯一计算输出位置。

## 环境与试跑

台式机无 root sudo；复用另一项书籍任务在 免 root 解包的 Tesseract 4（eng、chi_sim）及系统现有 poppler `pdftoppm`，未安装或更改系统包。首次 200 页测试因 `pdftoppm -singlefile ... -` 不向 stdout 输出而全部渲染失败；在没有写入有效页面的前提下清掉这 200 条错误记录，修正命令后原样重试 200 页：36.2 秒、195 页有文本、5 页空、0 失败；6 个 nice 19/ionice idle 工作线程。此速度只代表该组 Book 优先页面，不是全库保证速度。按该组吞吐朴素外推剩余约 5.3 小时；跨书扫描质量、台式机并发的另两项书籍 OCR 会使实际耗时变化，建议按约 5–10 小时观察心跳。

## 输入与断点

从 工作站 排除原 `page_text.sqlite` 中已标 `origin='OCR 文本'` 的 24,615 页，生成 105,338 页候选清单，传到台式机。优先 Book/Codes、wind engineering、Probability、Vibration、CFD、Mathematics 等，再其它 Book，最后 Literature。台式机后台 PID 63579； 每 60 秒心跳，SQLite 的 `(sha256,physical_page)` 主键断点续跑，成功、空页和异常分别记录；6 线程，单页图像只在内存经 subprocess stdout 传递，无临时 PDF/页图。10:29 查询 SQLite 740 页（721 页有文字），0 错误；全量远未完成。当前该工作目录实占约 63 MiB，另书籍任务目录约 197 MiB，远低于三任务合计 10 GB。

## 损坏 PDF

第一阶段失败清单有重复行，排除第二阶段已经补录的两件后，尝试使用只安装到 的 pypdf 6.20.1（strict=False）在 另存副本，原件不动；独立 `repaired_pages.sqlite` 防止与 OCR 主库同时写冲突。10:29 修复进程 PID 66649 仍在运行，结果尚未核实。pypdf 的修复能力不等同 qpdf/mutool；未能正确映射的页不得冒充成功。

## 10-15 14:31 美东回访
复用 socket 存活；台式机 OCR 主进程 PID 63579 仍运行。日志最近心跳为 34,892/105,138、0 错、572 空页（日志进度略滞后）；只读 SQLite 实查 35,267 条，其中 34,690 条有文本、577 条为空，错误表 0 条。注意候选清单为 105,338 页，而日志分母 105,138，差 200 页试跑已单独完成；最终须按清单与 SQLite 主键并集核对，不得以日志分母直接宣称全覆盖。按至今 13,953 秒与 35,267 条粗算，余下约 7.7 小时，此为动态估计。台式机 实占 150 MiB、 280 MiB、 不存在，三者远低于 10 GB；台式机 WSL 空闲 661 GB，工作站 C 盘空闲 91 GB。修复进程已退出，独立库暂有 366 页，但修复日志仍记录部分文件 Invalid object in /Pages，未核对正确物理页映射、不可并入正式输出。

## 10-15 18:33 美东回访
复用 socket 正常；主进程 PID 63579 为 SNl+，仍以 6 worker 运行。只读 SQLite 查询时已记 66,940 页（66,146 页有文本、794 页为空），随后 origin 汇总达 66,950 页；errors 表为 0。日志心跳 66,720/105,138（另有 200 页试跑），0 错、789 空；以 SQLite 最新页数计，105,338 页目标尚余 38,388 页。按日志累计吞吐约 2.42 页/秒，动态外推约 4.4 小时，不承诺完成时间。 236 MiB、 280 MiB、 未建立，合计低于 10 GB；台式机 WSL 空闲 661 GB，工作站 C 盘空闲 95 GB。修复日志仍有 FE-Handbook-1.pdf 的 Invalid object in /Pages，独立修复库未核页、未并入。运行中的数据库未复制或导出。

## 10-15 23:42 美东回访：台式机存储异常，中断
复用 socket 存活，但原 PID 63579 不在；末次心跳 23:13:37（日志本次运行已处理 102,621/105,138，另有试跑 200 页），只读 SQLite 实查 102,850/105,338 页：101,042 页有字、1,808 页空，errors 0，尚余 2,488 页。 313 MiB、 280 MiB、 不存在，低于 10 GB；工作站 可用 98 GB。原进程消失且无 DONE 记录。一次按主键断点续跑尝试在打开追加日志前失败：`cannot create ocr_round2.log: Read-only file system`，未重启 OCR、未后续写盘。远端根卷显示 `rw,...,emergency_ro`，不能仅凭 df 空闲判断可写。已向平台 Lead 报异常，等安全恢复，不绕过只读故障。独立修复库尚未核页、正式库未传 工作站。

## 10-16 00:49 美东：恢复并按主键续跑
复用 socket 存活；台式机根卷已恢复 ext4 `rw`，宿主 E: 可用 104 GB。确认原 OCR 无进程后，在 复制 SQLite 与当时 WAL/SHM 三件；在副本运行 `PRAGMA integrity_check=okproc_3f36e8f22bd1`、PID 3381642。约 00:53 远端 SQLite 达 103,020 页、0 错，E: 可用 115 GB。200 页试跑已计入总清单。工作站 不运行 OCR。

## 10-16 02:38 美东：停写、核对和交付

断点续跑进程已退出，末行 `DONE 2498 errors 2 empty 72 wall_s 6074.8`；本次续跑墙钟约 2.432 秒/页（6 工作者并行，非单线程 OCR 耗时）。首次 200 页的 36.2 秒是有偏的 Book 小样本；全程跨中断及并发，不能由这两个数准确推定全量纯 OCR 耗时。复用 SSH socket 存活；台式机源库只读、没有在 工作站 运行 OCR 或对外发送页文本，0 CU。

候选唯一主键 105,338 个（含 200 页试跑）；SQLite 完成 105,336 页，其中有文本 103,456、空文本 1,880、失败 2。逐主键差集恰是 物理页 41 与 45；`pdftoppm` 各超过 180 秒限时。`errors` 表正好两条；没有以空白页代替失败页。`PRAGMA integrity_check=ok`，`chars`、`has_text` 与存储文本逐行一致，导出的 105,336 条 manifest 均与输入键相交且无额外键。

20 页抽查：以固定种子 20261016 从已入库页等概率抽 20 页，均有非空可辨文字；中文页的字形误认、英文符号误认、公式/表格跨行与双栏混排都可见。例如 p24 的表格有 `Al OBE`、`WARE`， p396 的公式行几乎不可读， p178 的中文有“午新排列”，而 p302 英文段落相对连贯。这只是文本可读性抽检，没有逐张原图人工对字，故无字符准确率和数值可靠性结论；公式、引文须回原件核验。

修复独立库 有 366 页，均来自 `Computational Statistics Handbook with Matlab`。原件 `pdfinfo` 为 626 页，pypdf 修复副本仅识别 366 页，物理页映射不安全，未并入交付库；其它五条修复尝试报。六件异常仍须单独处理，不得将修复副本的第 N 页直接当原 PDF 第 N 页。

停止写入后执行 WAL checkpoint、完整性检查并传回 工作站。远端 与本地 的 SHA-256 均为 `2f2a3e8625eaf9d5c923caa2ec4d88fd0227407e767b52502319b1ca2c830a6b`；本地大小 256,282,624 字节。 为 1,579,186 字节，SHA-256 `87ab1b229f9222e3af9a2e75a417c42cfcb542adac62284a170ea3686f7faa55`；每行含 sha256、物理页、字符数、有无文本、`origin=OCR 文本本地盘` 可用 98 GB；台式机 约 799 MiB，另 约 280 MiB，低于 10 GB 闸门。

结论：105,336 个已安全对齐页可供平台以 OCR 不保证准确的标签试入库；两处超时及六件损坏文件保持失败/待核，不声称 105,338 页全成功。

# 0069 Work-Merge Verification Queue (Read-Only Verification by the Lab)

Source: (127 groups); the Lab maps `DSK` prefixes to SHA-256; both and were opened via read-only URIs. Verdicts are detailed in , with one group per row listing all `DSK` IDs in the group; this is strictly for manual reference by the platform and does not authorize index writes.

Groups: 127; `DSK` members: 337; merge: 108, do not merge: 18, uncertain: 1.

Verification method: compare verbatim hashes of the first six pages and non-short pages (≥350 normalized characters) across files; then inspect overtly conflicting titles, chapter/volume numbers, member page counts, file paths, and body-text overlap for representative full books. The original queue retains first-page snippets, first-six-page overlap counts, and similarity scores; and are available for cross-checking.

Key findings: Group 1 comprises two volumes of ICWE12 that share front matter but differ in subsequent content; Groups 3–4 have metadata errors that mislabel distinct papers with identical titles; Group 21 consists of 56 separate Davenport conference papers and should not be merged; Group 48 comprises three Bimba product catalogs that share the first four pages but differ thereafter; Groups 49–52, 74, and 127 represent separate chapters/fascicles; Group 89 pairs a standard with its commentary/supplement (distinct documents). Group 70 (ABAQUS lecture notes) has extensive overlap but unclear versioning/inserts, so it is listed separately as uncertain and kept unmerged.

Judgment boundary: complete body-text copies of the same paper with different byte representations may be recommended for merging; however, this recommendation is not itself the Crossref verification required by platform rules. If the platform permits merging solely on the basis of identical SHA or Crossref-verified DOI/title (+year), the remaining "merge" rows must first undergo independent metadata verification, and identical body text in this table must not be treated as satisfying platform rules.

results.title: Review Brief: Low Page-Level Retrieval Hit Rate on Desktop Literature — Seeking Diagnosis and Solutions (L22 · 10-17)
results.text:
# 审查材料：台式机文献按页检索命中率偏低，求诊断与解决办法（L22 · 10-17）

## 背景
- ` pages` 是本中心的本地全文检索工具，按页检索，返回"哪篇、PDF 第几页"。服务代码在 （ 检索与排序， 台式机来源， 建索引， 参数）。
- 语料分三块：
 - Zotero 与 EndNote 两个库，约 13.7k 个作品、45.7 万页，已经验收
 - 台式机 I:\Literature 的书和论文，已入索引 30.9 万页（来源 `page_text_v2`，11,134 份文档）
 - 另有两个增量交付了但**还没入索引**：DjVu/超星 3.1 万页、OCR 第二轮 10.5 万页。`desk_sources` 表里只有 `page_text_v2` 一条。
- 检索流程（据 config）：
 1. 中文问句先由 Gemini Flash 翻成英文
 2. FTS/BM25 召回（含 CJK 表），用 bge-small 重排，重排池 100
 3. 书籍另走一个通道（bge-reranker-base，book_slots=2）
 4. 最后取前 5。
- 台式机文档按 sha256 去重。书目元数据大多是低置信度：`low_homelow_filename` 时显示文件名，标"题目候选"。

## 盲测（只留实验室，题目原文不外送）
- 题库：30 题，由台式机文档构造，SHA，冻结不改。问句为中文。分四组：书（有文字层）、论文、中文文献、OCR 扫描页，各 10/10/5/5 题。
- 判据：前 5 条结果里有正确作品，且 PDF 物理页误差 ±1。
- 10-16 晚的复跑：翻译 30/30 成功，作品命中 15/30，到页 11/30。分组到页：书 4/10，论文 4/10，中文 1/5，OCR 2/5。
- 逐题表见 `per_question_sanitized.mddesk_pages` 核过），所以失败不是覆盖问题，全部是召回/排序问题：
 - 15 题，正确作品没进前 5
 - 4 题，作品对了但页错。其中 R5-03 返回的是另一副本的页码（250，目标 50）；R5-25、R5-27、R5-30 是同一文档内页选错。
- 同一服务在两库上的老题库（R3 共 30 题，R4 共 12 道书题）稳定在 24/30 和 8/12，0069 上线后没有退步。
- 失败集中在论文组（6/10 没召回）和书组。论文组目标文档只有 9–16 页，而且多数书目是 `low_home`，没有可靠题名。

## 平台已排进 0069 第三轮的四条改进（尚未上线）
1. 中文原文和英译两路检索
2. 台式机与两库分别召回再合并，题名高置信时加权
3. 同作品的各副本返回自己的物理页
4. 用 desktop_records_v3 的题名替换文件名。

回归要求：两库逐题不降，耗时增加 ≤5 秒。

## 请回答
1. 根据代码和数据，**15 道作品没召回**最可能的根因是什么？请排序，并给出每条的证据或可以验证的办法。可能的方向（不限于此）：
 - 翻译后的英文查询与原文用词不匹配
 - BM25 被两库的大量页面稀释，或台式机页在融合时被压低
 - 重排池 100 不够，或重排模型太弱
 - 书通道挤占名额
 - 去重或别名把正确文档折叠掉了
 - 短论文页数少，文档级证据不足。
2. 上面四条改进能解决哪些、解决不了哪些？
3. 请提出**具体的、可落地的附加办法**（改哪个函数或参数、预期影响、风险），按"收益/代价"排序。要满足：不能让两库老题库退步，耗时增加 ≤5 秒，书籍全文不外送。
4. 给一个**诊断实验方案**：用最小代价在复测前把根因分开。例如对失败题记录目标页在各阶段的名次（BM25 名次、重排前后、融合后），只开台式机来源单独检索做对照，等等。
5. 两个尚未入索引的增量（DjVu/超星、OCR 第二轮）入索引后，预计会帮忙还是添乱？要注意什么？

只读，不改任何文件，不调用会改动服务的命令。可以读代码和 `index.sqlite`（只读）。

results.title: Verdict: Review (Root Causes and Solutions for the 11/30 Desktop Page-Level Retrieval Score) · 10-17 17:35
results.text:
# 裁决：审查 （台式机按页检索 11/30 的根因与解决办法）· 10-17 17:35

3/3 份有效意见（Gemini、GPT-6、GLM）。Lead 已逐条核过代码和数据：、 第 1359–1407、1440–1476、720–742 行，以及 `index.sqlite` 的 desk_sources。

## 必须改
1. **我的 brief 写错了两处**：
 - 45.7 万页、13.7k 作品是三块语料的合计。Zotero+EndNote 只有约 14.7 万页（两位审稿人独立算出 147,345 页）。
 - 台式机本来就是独立分表召回，"被两库 BM25 稀释"这条假设作废。平台四条改进里的"中英两路"和"分库召回再合并"在现行代码里已经有了，第三轮不能按字面重做。
2. **头号根因是合并门控（已核实）**：`desktop_merge` 的设置是 slots=1、ref=max、margin=2.0。意思是每题最多只放 1 条台式机结果进前 5，而且它的重排分要比两库第 1 名还高 2 分才能进。
 - 8 道作品未召回题的前 5 里一条台式机结果都没有（R5-04/07/11/17/18/19/21/23）。
 - 3 道同书错页题（R5-25/27/30）里，目标书已经排第 1，但同书第二页被 slots=1 挡住，进不了前 5。

 这是第三轮最该动的参数，平台原来的四条都没碰它。
3. **台式机召回池偏小**：desktop_pool=30（两库是 100），desktop_alt=false（第二种英文问法关着），book_channel_desktop=false（台式机的书不走书通道）。书组 5 道未召回与此对应。
4. **合并前去重是按页而不是按作品**（ftkb.py:1373 用 `dedup(desk,10)`，按 (work,page) 分组）。同一本书的几页会占满候选名额（现为 4 个），别的台式机作品拿不到打分机会。
5. **第四条改进（v3 题名）要写清范围**：现规则只有 high_*/medium_pdfinfo 显示题名，low_home 和 low_filename 仍用文件名，而 FTS 的 title 列权重是 2。论文组 9/10 是 low_home，题名不可靠，就等于把文件名当题名在检索。需要先做题名可靠性提升（首页抽题名、用 Crossref 回填），并清洗 medium_pdfinfo 里的乱码和模板名，不能只是"再指定一次 v3"。
6. **诊断要留档**："目标页 30/30 已入索引"的查询脚本和逐题 sha 映射要存进实验室私有目录；对外只给结论。

## 仅供参考
- Gemini 说的"中文保底槽位（索引 3–4）被候选上限截断"：代码结构上成立（candidates 上限 3→4 后仍可能截掉），但要等逐题 trace 确认。另外 10-16 上午未翻译时中文组 5/5 作品命中、晚上翻译后 2/5，这条线索可靠，列为第二优先。
- GPT-6：重排只读题名加正文前 1200 字（rerank_window=head）；OCR 增量替换旧 OCR 页时不比较文本质量；"总数不变"不等于"逐题不降"，回归必须逐题对照。
- GLM：逐题表的"前5中DSK条数"把挂靠的副本也算进去了，不能用来判断台式机是否被召回。

## 未采纳的异议
- GPT-6 主张撤回"失败全是召回/排序问题"：部分采纳。GLM 已核对代码，desk_pages 与 FTS 写入是同步的，所以"已入索引≈可检索"成立。但目标页的文字是否抽得完整，没有逐页核过，改为"目标页都已入索引，失败主要发生在召回和合并阶段"。

## 事实更新
平台已于 10-17 17:13 把 djvu_pdg（31,020 页）和 ocr_round2（103,082 页）入索引，台式机现有 443,514 页。brief 写的"未入索引"是 11:58 的状态。

## 下一步（Lead 决定）
- 把以上 1–5 条和下面的诊断方案交平台，并入 0069 第三轮。
- 平台在自己的开发集（dev_desktop 等）上，用 desktop_merge 的 record 模式记下每题 head_ce、各候选分和名次，扫描 slots∈{1,2,3}、ref∈{max,pos}、margin∈{0,0.5,1,2}、desktop_pool∈{30,100}、按作品去重、台式机书入书通道等组合。
- 约束不变：R3/R4 和两库开发集逐题不降，耗时增加 ≤5 秒。
- 上线后实验室用冻结的 R5 盲测复测（题目不交平台）。

# ftkb 0069 冻结盲测验收（10-16 10:39，美东）

结论口径：本次观察不支持放行新台式机 I 盘来源检索；R5 前五到页仅 5/30，且 30/30 次调用均提示「本次未翻译……只按中文原文检索」，是显著的检索条件故障/混杂因素，不能把英文资料 0 命中直接归因于 0069 的索引或重排。旧书纵向集没有到页退步，也没有新增提升。题目、答案、原始片段只留实验室，不向平台交付。

## 方法及冻结

每道只送原问题给 ` pages … -n 5` 一次、单题 90 s 超时，先核冻结文件 SHA-256：R5 `8e08ae4bd5ba725e6dd2d2df80032e9ff35880cf8a88a4ab601e6a29ef1f1b07`、R3 `d80069db26f2bc53914f58d73556ef283d216ffd513a71ea3aac5c1bf10bd83b`、R4 `9259a4092267a0bd8cfa23c40252f9e6f36c64bee05e8e32055c4ddf0b987c46`；题库均未改。全部 72 次退出码 0，均未超时。前五以同作品且原 PDF 物理页 ±1 为到页；R5 同作品按原始 I 盘路径转换 Windows 路径（去「只在台式机能打开」尾注）/已记别名精确匹配，不把不完整文件名的相似题名算作同作。R3/R4 沿原有作品判据、跨库同作。可能的同书异路径未经逐份哈希核验，保守不加分。第六条补充页不计入前五。

## R5 新题：30 道严格真值

OCR 5 道已经 Lead 目视原 PDF 页核实；R5-30 题干欠限定，保留冻结问句，未命中不另算。每组前五作品命中 / 到页：

| 分组 | 题数 | 作品 | 物理页±1 | 未到页题号 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Book 文字层 | 10 | 0 | 0 | R5-01–10 |
| Literature | 10 | 0 | 0 | R5-11–20 |
| 中文 | 5 | 5 | 3 | R5-21、25 |
| OCR | 5 | 3 | 2 | R5-26、27、30 |
| 合计 | 30 | 8 | 5 | 25 道 |

同作品却页错：R5-21 返回 PDF 380 页、R5-25 返回第 6 页、R5-30 返回第 258 页；目标物理页和前五原始片段仅见实验室私有文件。R5-30 按预定口径不额外扣分，依旧记一题未到页。其余 22 道未召回同作，不等于源文件必然没索引。原始回包 R5 全部 30 道出现「本次未翻译」警告；英文作品问句落在中文原词检索条件下，尤其 Book/Literature 0/20，不宜由此判定长书索引本身完全失效。R3/R4 的 42 道回包没有此警告，纵向比较检索条件并不相同。

展示/溯源：前五任一条标「只在台式机能打开」为 20/30 题（首位 13/30）；前五任一条题名标「题目候选」为 14/30（首位 7/30）；显式「疑似表格」提示为 2/30（两题均首位）。「只在台式机能打开」的文件路径不能假定 工作站 可直接打开，题名候选不可当作正式书目信息；疑似表格的数字/行列必须返回原页核查。按提示字面统计，不将片段中普通「表格」字眼计入表格警示。

## 审计路径与限制

新集：（原始响应）、 与；旧集：、 各有 、。原始文件含私有题干/来源，绝不可交平台；可对外只给聚合指标及「翻译全部失败」现象。分组非随机、样本小、故障条件下的 R5 分数不代表正常翻译条件下的召回率。整个流程只读 ftkb，0 CU。

## 翻译恢复后重跑（10-16 11:33 美东）

仍用冻结 R5 原题库（SHA-256 `8e08ae4bd5ba725e6dd2d2df80032e9ff35880cf8a88a4ab601e6a29ef1f1b07`，运行前复核），原 、单题 90 s、前五同作品且 PDF 物理页±1。30 道顺序一致、30 次退出码 0、无单题超时；题库未改。逐题私有原始响应和复核打分在 、；新打分只采用 I 盘原路径/题库所记别名的精确匹配（规范化路径），不凭标题相似加分。

逐题到页：R5-01、08、12、29；其中 01、08、12 是相对前次变好，29 不变。前次到页而本次未到页：R5-22、23、24、28（四题均无同作品前五）；其余 23 题不变。R5-30 仍按题干欠限定的冻结口径记未到页，不额外扣分。所有 30 次均出现「中文问题已译成英文检索」，0 次出现「本次未翻译」；然而 25 次回包报告内部 60 秒上限，11 次明确写「没跑完的部分：台式机来源」。R5-22、24、28 有内部 60 秒上限，其中 28 明确漏跑台式机来源；R5-23 未显示该上限或漏跑提示。检索结果的组成和排序可能因翻译改变；现有回包不足以把四题退步归于单一原因。外层 90 秒超时未触发，不等于内部召回完整。

结果展示提示（前五任一条）：台式机限定 8/30，题目候选 7/30，疑似表格 1/30。尽管翻译链恢复，新集到页由 5/30 降至 4/30 且中文/OCR 有退步；内部超时及台式机来源未跑完仍是重要混杂，不能认定台式机来源检索验收通过，也不能将此次 4/30 简单归因于索引质量。题干、答案、回包片段和私有路径只留实验室，不交平台；可对平台只报聚合指标及内部限时现象。

# Full-Text Literature Repository Search + Wind Engineering Data Extraction (Promoted)

This sub-project evaluated whether Liang Hu's local bibliography collections (initially 3,163 Zotero PDFs and 1,527 EndNote PhD PDFs, later expanded with 12,497 net new PDFs, 62 DjVu books, and 11 PDG scanned books from a desktop library) could be transformed into a page-level full-text retrieval system and an automated wind engineering parameter extraction pipeline. While automated extraction of downburst vertical wind profiles from 37 papers was Shelved because key engineering regimes reside in dense multi-curve figures requiring expert reading, the hybrid page-level search prototype (combining BM25, local multilingual embeddings, and OCR for scanned books) passed multi-stage blind benchmarks and was Promoted into a Lab-wide search tool. Subsequent phases completed local CPU OCR, block-sorted re-extraction for two-column papers, Crossref/metadata bibliographic deduplication across 15,159 work clusters, and full desktop corpus ingestion.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-13**: Liang Hu approved opening the sub-project, and Lab Lead dispatched two trials to the research assistant: page-level indexing of the Zotero and EndNote libraries (Trial A) and batch extraction of downburst vertical wind profiles across 30–40 papers via Gemini 3.8 Flash (Trial B).
- **2026-10-13**: Round 1 indexed 4,691 PDFs (128,708 non-empty pages across ~3,845 clusters; 159 scan PDFs / 10,553 pages lacked text layers), hitting 27/34 (79%) on English paper-finding queries versus 14/34 for legacy card search, while scoring 1/6 on book interior pages and 0/34 on Chinese-to-English queries.
- **2026-10-13**: In Round 2, non-first-page top-5 exact-page accuracy reached 8/14 on English facts, 5/5 on Chinese sources, 3/5 on Chinese-to-English queries (via bilingual query translation), and 4/6 on books (29/34 on paper-finding, vs. 1/27 on non-first-page facts for legacy card search).
- **2026-10-13**: Manual verification of 78 extracted downburst values across 8 papers found 6 errors, 27 entries missing crucial physical qualifiers, and 5/8 papers citing text pages rather than figure pages; single-page multimodal re-reading still misread multi-curve axes on 2/8 papers, so Trial B was Shelved and Trial A entered Pending promotion.
- **2026-10-13**: The research assistant ran local CPU OCR (`tesseract`) across 79 deduplicated textless PDFs (5,422 pages, including CFD and numerical methods textbooks) in 35 minutes at 0 CU, recovering searchable text on 5,407 pages.
- **2026-10-14**: Platform integration Phases 1 and 2 passed acceptance across all five benchmark groups (29/34 title-page, 9/11 valid English facts, 5/5 Chinese, 5/6 books, 3/5 Chinese-to-English; 22/27 overall on valid Round 2 facts), and the sub-project was officially Promoted.
- **2026-10-14**: On a 30-question Phase 3 blind test held strictly inside the Lab, top-5 exact-page accuracy rose from 21/30 to 24/30 (and book hits from 4/10 to 7/10) after adding book-level cross-encoder reranking and dual-translation fusion.
- **2026-10-14**: On a newly frozen 12-question Round 4 book blind test (8 digital books, 4 OCR books, phrased without book-indicator keywords), the updated platform routing (appending book interior pages at rank 6 to avoid displacing non-book hits) achieved 8/12 top-5 exact-page accuracy (4/8 digital, 4/4 OCR).
- **2026-10-14**: Read-only inventory of the second desktop drive identified 13,993 readable PDFs (12,497 net new files / 421,023 pages after file-hash deduplication against Zotero/EndNote), 62 unique DjVu books (30,407 pages), and 11 PDG scanned books (3,163 pages); Stage 1 extracted 288,794 text-layer pages, while local OCR paused at 24,615 pages when workstation disk space dropped below 20 GB.
- **2026-10-15**: With workstation free space restored to 100 GB, six parallel closure tracks ran: (1) 24-core desktop OCR for the remaining 105,338 scan pages (reaching 66,950 pages / 64%); (2) block-sorted re-extraction of all 394,243 desktop text-layer pages to fix two-column line merging; (3) conversion and OCR of 62 DjVu and 11 PDG books (31,365 aligned pages delivered); (4) Crossref verification of 1,942 candidate DOIs (confirming 1,178 titles and finding 1,065 cross-library duplicate works—30× higher than byte hashing—across 15,159 work clusters); (5) real-workflow trials hitting 7/10 exact pages for literature card verification; and (6) freezing a 30-question Round 5 desktop blind benchmark.

## Where it stands

This sub-project is Promoted and operational across the Lab as a unified page-level literature search tool, while automated numerical table/curve extraction from papers remains Shelved. All Stage 2b deliverables—including the 394,243 block-sorted desktop text-layer pages, 31,365 DjVu/PDG book pages, the 15,159-cluster bibliographic deduplication table, and the frozen 30-question Round 5 blind benchmark—are complete, with the remaining 38,388 desktop OCR pages finishing automatically on the desktop CPU before final platform ingestion and Round 5 blind scoring.

# Uses of self-built / local models for our research

## Objective (10-13 10:38 Redirected by Liang Hu)
Answer Liang Hu's original question: what are the uses of **self-built / local large language models (LLMs)** for our research? Four questions: (1) Can local open-source LLMs take over batch routine tasks (literature screening, PDF data extraction, knowledge base tagging, identifying thunderstorm winds from Storm Events narratives, and diagnosing supercomputing job logs)? (2) Is fine-tuning (LoRA / full-parameter) on our materials worthwhile in a head-to-head comparison against "frontier model + retrieval"? (3) How are other domain LLMs (OceanGPT, ClimateGPT, GeoGPT, etc.) built, what are their costs and evaluations, do any exist in wind engineering / civil engineering, and would building one ourselves have publication value? (4) How do they differ from Claude/Gemini/Codex/Grok on our real tasks? Task brief.

## Current Status
10-13 13:32 Conclusion reached; status changed to "Shelved" (questions answered; operational recommendations handed over to the platform rather than kept as a research project). The sub-project "Forecasting uses of AI weather models" proceeds separately.
**In one sentence**: Do not build our own large language model (continued pre-training / full fine-tuning); the first step is to offload batch routine tasks from Claude—hand initial literature abstract screening and single-value PDF extraction to the Gemini 3.8 Flash batch channel (best quality, already covered by subscription) or Qwen3-32B on Colab (when data should not be sent externally or offline processing is required), use keyword rules first wherever possible, and reserve Claude for judgment and review.
**Restart conditions**: Conduct a LoRA comparison only when a large volume of fixed-format, labeled narrow tasks (such as internal configuration generation) arises and local models show a clear gap behind frontier models; enable the local channel when large batches of text that should not be transmitted externally appear.

## Assessment Table (Large Language Models; after two evaluation rounds, 10-13 13:32)
| Question | Our Specific Use Case | Existing Data | Minimal Experiment | Cost | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Local open-source LLMs taking over batch routine tasks | Initial literature abstract screening, single-value PDF extraction | Knowledge base cards, Zotero PDFs, public NOAA data | **Two rounds completed** (Round 2 blind run on 350 frozen items) | Round 2 ~1.97 CU; ~5.6 CU per 1,000 items (including amortized cold start) | **Abstract screening: usable**—Qwen3-32B achieved 82% accuracy, 98% recall, and 58% precision, comparable to Claude Sonnet (80.5%/100%/56%), while Gemini 3.8 Flash performed best (85.5%/98%/64%), all far outperforming keyword rules (67.5%); human review of excluded borderline samples is still required. **Single-value PDF extraction: usable for initial extraction**—local 92% vs. Claude/Gemini 96%; original pages must be verified. **Storm Events thunderstorm wind identification: use rules** (post-construction rule accuracy 100%; genuinely ambiguous samples not tested). Log error diagnosis not tested. |
| 2 Fine-tuning on our materials (LoRA) | Fixed-format narrow tasks | Requires building a separate labeled dataset | Not done—local models are already comparable to frontier models, and the gap is too small to justify the effort | — | Low (see restart conditions above) |
| 3 Building "our own domain LLM" (continued pre-training) | "Wind Engineering GPT" | Insufficient corpus volume | Do not do | Hundreds to thousands of A100·h minimum | Low (see review verdict for literature basis; civil engineering has the CivilGPT precedent, none found in wind engineering) |
| 4 Gap vs. frontier models | Same as 1 | Same as 1 | Same as 1 | — | Screening: local 32B ≈ Claude Sonnet < Gemini 3.8 Flash; data extraction: local is ~4 percentage points lower (2 items difference out of 50); Codex/Grok not tested |
**Estimated usage savings (based on data from this track)**: Each batch call to Claude via CLI consumes ~39k tokens (mostly framework overhead), at a list price of ~$0.05–$0.06 per item; local Colab costs ~5.6 CU per 1,000 items (including amortized cold start). If there are 10,000 screening/extraction routine items per month, ~10,000 Claude calls can be offloaded entirely (to the Gemini subscription channel or locally). ### DR Precedents vs. TPU Experiment: No Conflict (Confirmed by Review )
- The two items in DR that looked most like "conflicts" have been verified to exist: DeepUFNet (arXiv 2508.03183 v2 abstract: trained at SR=1.5, test generalization at SR=4 and 3.75 described as "satisfactory") and ScaleSplit-NO (Qin et al. arXiv 2609.38977: Montreal urban wind field one-step NMSE 65.8% lower than baseline).
- The reason there is no conflict is that **the tasks and comparison baselines differ**, not that the precedents are unreliable:
 1. Task: DeepUFNet reconstructs/advances the full field given sparse sensor time histories on the target cylinder; ScaleSplit-NO performs temporal advancement of the flow field over the same urban district. The TPU experiment predicts Cp on an unseen building **given only geometric parameters and zero sensor taps**.
 2. Baseline: The precedents compare against other neural networks (U-Net, etc.); the TPU experiment compares against geometric interpolation/Kriging. No verified precedent beats interpolation under "whole unseen building geometry + head-to-head comparison against interpolation under identical conditions."
 3. Consistent pattern: Urban FNO itself reports limitations across significantly different urban morphologies (arXiv 2501.05499); on TPU, ML likewise only holds an advantage in database boundary extrapolation (T111).
- Conclusion: What is worth testing is "reconstruction and correction when sensor taps / low-fidelity information are available" and "boundary extrapolation," not "pure geometric interpolation."

| 10-13 | Wind Tunnel Lead reply | No ML done, no measured data yet; available to borrow: YM2019 digitized 132 curves / 15,517-point CSV, synthetic data + fault-injection generator + rule-based QC checker, 148-tap table and tubing transfer function; suggested channel-by-channel anomaly detection, where a prototype can be handed back to that track to test once UF measurements arrive |

### Open Items and Next Steps
- TPU result: In the interpolation regime, ML is comparable to interpolation, so this scenario is not worth investing in; **this does not mean "wind pressure surrogates are useless."** What is worth examining is extrapolation (database boundaries / new geometry types) and multi-fidelity modeling (2a′), as well as thunderstorm wind classification (3). All-wind-directions verification confirmed (10-13 08:13); waiting for the events track reply before deciding on the second experiment (≤10 CU).
- One-sentence takeaway for Liang Hu (Root Lead 10-13 framing): The interpolation scenario is not worth investing in; what is worth examining is extrapolation and multi-fidelity modeling (2a′), as well as thunderstorm wind classification (3).
- Waiting for review verdict; waiting for replies from all six tracks to fill in the "Existing Data" column; rerun DR once quota is restored.
 - (2) After inflow correction (empty-domain r1 → v8 building case, expected from their side within this week), rerun on the new data including station-by-station distance analysis, and report the ratio of decay length (roughly estimated at ~30 m ≈ 5H in v7) to integral length scale Lu

 - (Addendum, completed) Adding z12: rake center column FIR correlation dropped from 0.417 → 0.382 (worse), while changes at x=−10/−15/−20 were ≤0.011; CNN did not clearly beat FIR in any case, and their side withdrew the request (z12 was added by mistake in transcription; what they needed was z1/3/6, which v4b already satisfied), results archived without delivery
 - Uniformly exclude the three P_x-33.05 points from all input sets (fixed boundary values, std≈0); confounder: proximity to the building cannot be separated from distance away from the inlet injection zone.
- Candidates (not dispatched): CM1 sounding → outflow statistics (waiting for ~99 cases); adding a non-learning baseline to graph-deeponet-wind; 2b GraphCast/Pangu single-event environmental comparison; 3 ASOS thunderstorm wind classification; urban wind field surrogate on the public U3DWind LBM-LES five-city dataset (card).

(global 220 m GLES, physical model, non-AI), (generative model for urban microclimate, Liu et al. arXiv 2610.10430), (physics-constrained network for typhoon near-surface wind profiles, arXiv 2610.11405), (WeatherMesh). Approved by Liang Hu on 10-13, sub-project opened, page; sub-project shelved on 10-13 14:00 (three-event hindcast: convective background fields only hold up to 12–24 h and are unstable, with CAPE as the bottleneck).

- The events track relies on Storm Events + Cook v2 Class/XClass weak labels + case-by-case radar for identification; the bottleneck is not "whether it is a thunderstorm wind," but distinguishing internal thunderstorm wind mechanisms (isolated downburst / gust front / MCS·supercell) and near-surface footprints (all 17 case-by-case reconstructions across four Texas cities were "ambiguous"). # Liang Hu Task Brief · The Lab's Third Sub-Project: Uses of self-built / local models for our research (10-13)

Background: The Strata+Qwen sub-project proved that a Colab A100 can run 10B–100B-scale models, but "localizing a general-purpose chat LLM" has very low value for us. Liang Hu wants to know which category of model is genuinely useful for wind engineering research. For each of the three categories, answer "whether it is useful to us, on what grounds, and what the minimal experiment is":
1. Domain fine-tuned language models (fine-tuning a small LLM or LoRA on wind engineering literature, codes/standards, and reports). Preliminary judgment: low value ( + Claude/Gemini already cover this); verify whether any counterexamples exist.
2. Physical-field foundation models / surrogate models (neural operators, Transformer/diffusion surrogates; weather foundation models such as GraphCast, Aurora, ArchesWeather, and WeatherMesh; CFD surrogates such as Transolver). Key questions: whether we can train rapid surrogates for urban wind fields or building wind pressures using existing CFD/LBM/WRF/CM1 data and whether the data is sufficient; whether directly calling off-the-shelf weather foundation models to provide initial fields, ensembles, or rapid event screening for the WRF/CM1 tracks is feasible.
3. Specialized small models (anomaly detection in wind pressure time histories / wind tunnel data, event classification, supercomputing job log error diagnosis, etc.).
Deliverables: A project-page table (Category / Specific Use Case / Is Existing Data Sufficient? / Minimal Experiment / Estimated Cost / Recommendation); pick the single most worthwhile minimal experiment and immediately dispatch it to ideas or gpu-gemini (Colab A100, ≤10 CU), listing the rest as candidates. For anything involving the digital twin wind tunnel or PETW tracks, first ask the respective Lead whether they are already doing it; data from other tracks is read-only. Finally, give Liang Hu a one-sentence takeaway: which category is worth investing in, and what the first step is.

# Utility of Self-Built / Local Models for the Wind Engineering Research Group — Draft Assessment Table (the Lab, 10-13 06:30)

## Background and Constraints
Research lines: Urban Wind GPU LBM-LES (digital-twin wind-tunnel line), PETW OpenFOAM downburst / building wind pressure (CFD line), WRF/CM1 severe convection and downbursts, wind tunnel, event census (ASOS / Storm Events), and extreme value analysis / design loads. Existing tools: Claude/Gemini + knowledge-base retrieval. Compute: Colab A100 80 GB; ≤10 CU (~2 GPU hours) per individual trial. In-house CFD/LES runs across lines are expensive (e.g., a single CAARC LES L1 run costs ~115 SU; literature LES runs cost 2×10^4–5.65×10^4 CPU h per wind direction), so sample sizes are in the single digits to tens.
Note: The planned Deep Research run could not be launched due to the monthly API spend cap (HTTP 429); precedents below come from literature cards + rapid web search, and Deep Research will be run as a supplement once quota resets. Data inventory replies from the line Leads are still pending (queries sent).

## Assessment Table
| Category | Specific Use Case for Us | Are Existing Data Sufficient? | Minimal Trial | Estimated Cost | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Domain fine-tuned LLM / LoRA | Code/standard Q&A, CFD config generation | No new data needed, but no compelling advantage over frontier Claude+RAG | Skip | 0 | Low |
| 2a Wind pressure / urban wind surrogate (neural operator / GBM / GAN) | Rapid Cp estimation, wind-direction interpolation, multi-fidelity RANS→LES correction | In-house CFD/LBM cases too few (single digits to tens); public TPU wind-tunnel database available | TPU isolated high-rise dataset: leave-one-building-out, ML vs interpolation/Kriging | ≤2 CU | Medium (contingent on trial) |
| 2b Off-the-shelf AI weather models (GraphCast / Pangu / Aurora) | Rapid screening of severe convective environments, cheap ensembles | Public ERA5/GFS driving data suffice | Run GraphCast/Pangu on 1 known PETW event, compare CAPE / 0–6 km shear against ERA5 | 2–4 CU | Low–Medium |
| 3 Specialized small models | Automated thunderstorm vs non-thunderstorm wind classification, pressure-tap anomaly detection, job-log fault classification | ASOS 1-minute data public; wind-tunnel data pending check | 1D-CNN vs rule baseline (gust factor / rise time) on ASOS classification | 1–2 CU | Medium (depends on event-line need) |

## Primary Evidence
- **Category 1**: The only domain fine-tuning precedent is CFD configuration automation — Qwen2.5-7B LoRA fine-tuned on 28,716 NL2FOAM pairs (Phase-2 summary card, 19-page PDF), restricted to incompressible flows while meshing still requires human effort; our bots already handle such tasks using frontier models. The Strata sub-project already proved local inference is feasible but lacks a compelling use case.
- **Category 2a**: Random holdout within the same database yields high R² — GAN on the TPU interference dataset achieves mean Cp R² = 0.988 and rms Cp R² = 0.924 (card QN6Z9F4B, PDF p.10 Fig.9), but the six held-out cases come from the same family with inconsistent normalization denominators; wind-direction extrapolation degrades rms Cp sharply to R² = 0.13–0.26 (card 9CBNZGZB, PDF pp.15–17); multi-fidelity NN referenced to high-fidelity LES saves ~46% compute time (card NF6S3H9N, PDF pp.1–3 Table 1); in LatticeUrbanWind, pure Kriging achieves MAE 0.36–0.37 m/s, beating LBM-LES at 0.46 m/s (digital-twin wind-tunnel line Han 2026 card, p.39 Table 6). Taira et al. 2025 (*PRFluids* 10, 090701) emphasize comparing against simple baselines under an equal information budget and splitting data along true generalization axes. Web search found no study performing strict holdout on "completely unseen high-rise geometries" (only a thesis claiming R² > 99% on missing dimensions, unverified).
- **Category 2b**: Feldmann et al. 2024 (arXiv:2406.09474, subsequently published) show that GraphCast and Pangu match or exceed IFS seasonal skill on CAPE and deep-layer shear, with GraphCast producing the most accurate CAPE distribution, though coarse vertical resolution limits CAPE accuracy and spatial fields remain overly smooth; another Pangu study (NSF PAR 10625169) finds 1-day lead BWD6/SRH3 superior to GFS, but near-storm grid-point extremes 1–2 h prior to initiation are underpredicted. Because our core workflow is historical event hindcasting where ERA5 already provides the environmental "truth", the incremental value of AI weather models is limited to cheap ensembles/forecasts, and they do not resolve convective-scale surface winds. ArchesWeather card note: weather models cannot be used directly as climate models.
- **Category 3**: A 1D-CNN classifying ASOS 1-minute thunderstorm vs non-thunderstorm winds achieves 86.7% accuracy and 87.8% F1 on a 76,480-sample validation set (card 2T26I5GW, pp.6–8 and results section), though ground-truth labels rely on ASOS thunderstorm flags across the 40–75 kt range.

## Preliminary Conclusion
Category 2a (wind pressure surrogate) is the most worthwhile initial trial, provided it is judged strictly via "leave-one-building-out + interpolation baseline"; 2b offers limited incremental value for hindcast-centric workflows; 1 merits zero investment; 3 depends on whether the event census line faces a real classification bottleneck. Step 1: TPU leave-one-building-out trial (dispatched, ≤10 CU).

# Verdict: In-House Model Utility Assessment Table and TPU Minimal Experiment (3/3 valid: Gemini, GPT-6, GLM; 10-13)

All three offered "reserved support": the taxonomy and recommendation direction hold; the TPU leave-one-building-out vs. interpolation direction is correct; collectively pointed out calibration/criterion errors and gaps in experimental protocols. Personally verified: 2T26I5GW card p.12 §4.1 (76,480 is the parent set, 5-fold internal CV); Han 2026 card (physical LBM-LES solver vs. observational Kriging, not ML); FV7BN78P card line 35 (local small-to-medium models are unstable on OpenFOAM configurations).

## Must Change (Changed)
1. **ASOS numbers** (unanimous among all three): Changed to "40–75 kt parent set 76,480 events, ASOS internal 5-fold CV (approx. 15,296 per fold), acc 86.7%/F1 87.8% (PDF p.12 §4.1 Fig.10), not an independent validation".
2. **Narrow the scope of experimental conclusions** (A, D): The TPU experiment only rules on "geometry generalization surrogate for rectangular isolated tall building mean/rms Cp", not the entirety of 2a; multi-fidelity RANS→LES correction and urban wind field surrogates are accounted for separately.
3. **Complete the holdout protocol** (all three): Leave-one-geometry-out (LOGO), distinguish interior/boundary buildings in parameter space, held-out buildings do not participate in hyperparameter tuning/preprocessing; exposure condition as a dimension; pressure taps aligned by normalized coordinates on each face; pre-specify "significantly better than" criteria; remove U-Net, use point-level regression for models (GBM + MLP + GP); remove peak Cp in the first round, state conclusions only for mean/rms. Sent to ideas as a task brief addendum.
4. **Usage of Han 2026** (E, D): Changed to a baseline caveat that "simple baselines can beat complex models" (physical LBM-LES vs. observational Kriging, mean horizontal wind, six-station network not completely independent), not as evidence for ML surrogates.
5. **Attribution of Taira** (D): Changed to "evaluation recommendation drawn from card ", not written as a stipulation of the original paper.
6. **Category 1 basis** (E, A): Delete "only counterexample"; add FV7BN78P (local small-to-medium models frequently fail on complex OpenFOAM configurations) and 5ZE3U2A8 (same team pivoted to MCP + multi-agent); VNP48R7H itself is a paper advocating fine-tuning effectiveness (card first_pass). Recommendation level remains Low, basis changed to "no evidence showing local fine-tuned models outperform frontier models + retrieval", rather than "proven to have no incremental value".
7. **Category 2b basis** (E, A): Delete ArchesWeather card (climate scale, irrelevant); ERA5 rephrased as "reanalysis reference" instead of ground truth; add precedent clues: Pangu forecasts driving WRF 12/3 km (Xu et al. 2024, ERL, DOI 10.1088/1748-9326/ad41f0), WoFSCast regional convection-allowing surrogate (GRL 2024, 10.1029/2024GL112383)—all provided by reviewers, not yet archived, pending litwiki card additions; recommendation level maintained at Low-Medium, single-event CAPE comparison experiment cancelled (E: no new information).

## For Reference Only
- The approx. 46% of NF6S3H9N is a budget framing of "10 LF + 5 HF vs 10 HF", while the paper actually ran all HF (A, D)—noted in the table.
- 9CBNZGZB transfer learning can raise 0° rms R² to 0.53 (A, D)—noted.
- Low-rise near-field precedent WindMiL (arXiv 2511.01226), Sci Rep low-rise LOSO (provided by D, unverified)—added to candidate literature.
- Category 1: In the NBCC building code Q&A fine-tuning + retrieval study, GPT-4o baseline still leads in metrics (provided by A, unverified); building code Q&A should use retrieval rather than fine-tuning (E, no specific citation).
- CU framing unified to "estimated ≤2, hard cap 10" (D).

## Unadopted Objections
- E flaw B "Tree models are mathematically mismatched with sparse geometry and should be discarded": Not discarded; retain GBM as one of the benchmarks and add MLP and GP; the first round asks precisely "whether off-the-shelf common methods beat interpolation on this type of data." A tree model losing is itself useful information, but conclusions are written separately by method rather than rejecting across the board based on a single model.
- E "Must specify H/B=3": Changed to leave-one-building-out with separate reporting for interior/boundary, which is more robust than holding out just one building (adopting D's proposal).
- No need to escalate to Liang Hu: All items are framing corrections and experimental designs, not changing direction.

# TPU Isolated Tall Building Wind Pressure Surrogate: Leave-One-Building-Out Minimal Experiment

Executed: 10-13 06:25 (US Eastern); official raw data only temporarily retained in Colab CPU session, not downloaded to  workstation; locally only scripts, statistical tables, figures, and logs are kept. Sources and terms of use see . Official website requires citation: TPU (Tokyo Polytechnic University) Aerodynamic Database, 2026, https://db.wind.arch.t-kougei.ac.jp/. The official website does not explicitly state an open license, so this is strictly an internal experiment without redistributing raw data.

## Scope and Split

Official isolated tall building cases: T113_4 (W:D:H=1:1:3, 300 taps), T213_4 (2:1:3, 360 taps), T313_4 (3:1:3, 320 taps), T212_4 (2:1:2, 240 taps), T214_4 (2:1:4, 450 taps). All belong to the same inflow family with alpha=1/4. For each building, five wind directions 0°, 10°, 20°, 30°, 40° are taken, totaling 25 wind direction–geometry cases and 8,350 tap–wind direction records; raw time series 32,768 frames per file at 1000 Hz. Total raw data 966,467,013 bytes, downloaded only temporarily in Colab. The full database includes more buildings/wind directions, not covered by this experiment.

Main experiment: Fully hold out 5 directions of T213_4 (1,800 tap records), train on 20 cases of the other four buildings (6,550 records); includes equal-height width neighbors on both sides and same-width different-height neighbors. For B0, under the same wind direction, first linearly interpolate by in-plane normalized position on each facade (nearest neighbor outside the convex hull), then use the widths of T113_4 and T313_4 for 1:1 linear interpolation; B1 uses a squared exponential Gaussian Process with fixed length scale and noise term (no hyperparameter tuning) after aligning taps across the four known geometries under the same wind direction; M is HistGradientBoostingRegressor, trained independently for 120 iterations per output. Face number, in-plane position, z/H, W/D, H/D, and wind direction sin/cos serve as model inputs. No pressure values from the target building enter training; geometry/tap coordinates serve as known inputs during prediction.

Auxiliary experiment: Repeating the run with  in the inner candidate directions 10°/20°/30°, the resulting six rows of metrics are completely identical to .

## Metrics

Each cell shows R² / RMSE (dimensionless Cp) in order. The peak column specifically refers to the point-by-point minimum Cp (negative peak) across the 32.768 s raw time series, not the Cook–Mayne design return period peak; tap counts differ across buildings, and the following are pooled metrics across all test points, not representing cross-building statistical significance.

| Holdout | Method | mean Cp R² / RMSE | rms Cp R² / RMSE | Minimum Cp R² / RMSE |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Full building T213_4 | B0 Geometric Linear | 0.9897 / 0.0555 | 0.9268 / 0.0246 | 0.8872 / 0.3778 |
| Full building T213_4 | B1 Fixed-Kernel GP | 0.9884 / 0.0591 | 0.9324 / 0.0237 | 0.9184 / 0.3213 |
| Full building T213_4 | M Gradient Boosting | 0.9930 / 0.0460 | 0.9344 / 0.0233 | 0.9255 / 0.3071 |
| Random holdout 20° | B0 Wind Direction Linear | 0.9842 / 0.0743 | 0.8915 / 0.0349 | 0.9130 / 0.3469 |
| Random holdout 20° | B1 Fixed-Kernel GP | 0.9963 / 0.0360 | 0.9352 / 0.0269 | 0.8875 / 0.3944 |
| Random holdout 20° | M Gradient Boosting | 0.9488 / 0.1339 | 0.6948 / 0.0585 | 0.8951 / 0.3807 |

Under full building holdout, M's RMSE relative to B0 decreases by 17.2% for mean, 5.4% for rms, and 18.7% for point-by-point negative peak; relative to B1 it decreases by 22.2%, 1.5%, and 4.4% respectively. Therefore, mean and time-series negative peak show small-to-moderate gains, while the most critical rms is nearly flat against GP; this does not support the broad assertion that "ML is significantly and generally superior to simple interpolation." When holding out wind directions at random, M significantly lags behind B0/B1 on both mean and rms, showing that easier splits cannot be automatically equated with optimiztic scores; tree models also interpolate continuous wind directions more weakly than explicit physical angle interpolation.

Figure : Comparison of measured/B0/M mean Cp under the same color scale for held-out building T213_4, 20°, nominal windward face 1; overall structures are close, with M showing localized plateau-like smoothing. This single figure is only illustrative; quantitative evaluation covers four surfaces and all five directions. "Nominal face 1" in the figure is based on the facade in the .mat Readme, and the actual aerodynamic windward state of this facade at 20° should not be generalized to other wind directions.

Literature background but not directly comparable: , PDF p.10 Fig.9 random split of interfering buildings in the same database has high mean/rms R², not new geometry; PDF pp.15–17 single-building CFD angle extrapolation rms R² 0.1291/0.2608, not identical conditions to this TPU run. This run involves only one building held out within the interpolation interval, single roughness, five wind directions, and fixed hyperparameters; conclusions must not be extrapolated to general wind pressure surrogate reliability, design peak pressure accuracy, or number of experiments saved.

## Reproduction and Costs

 ran in Colab CPU environment (numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, matplotlib), pulled files one by one from the TPU official website and printed URLs, outputting  and figures;  is the random-seed wind direction recalculation, which needs to be uploaded to the same directory as , outputting . Data links and tap counts see local ; raw execution output see , . Colab usage was 1523.64 CU before launch, final 1523.63 CU (display precision 0.01 CU, actual billing may be delayed); well below 10 CU. Both CPU sessions `tpu-geometry-cp` and `tpu-seed0-cp` returned Session terminated, final `colab sessions`: No active sessions found on server; usage rate 0.00/hr, active assignments 0.

# TPU Rectangular Isolated Tall Building Wind Pressure Surrogate: Scaled Experiment Following Protocol Addendum (10-13 07:18, US Eastern)

Note: This is an experiment with 13 official geometries, two available exposures, and only five wind directions per case: 0°/10°/20°/30°/40°, not all wind directions in the database. During leave-one-building-out, the five selected directions and all available exposures for that building are held out together; this does not meet the literal requirement of "all wind directions for that building," so the criteria below are merely an exploratory evaluation of this preselected wind direction subset and must not falsely claim completion of the full-database protocol. The official catalog lists 13 geometries and 22 geometry × exposure combinations; this run covers 110 cases totaling 37,200 tap–wind direction records, with raw .mat files totaling 4,290,004,812 bytes, all stored temporarily in Colab only. Targets per tap are strictly mean Cp and overall time-series standard deviation rms Cp, with no peak values.

Source and boundaries of use: TPU official https://db.wind.arch.t-kougei.ac.jp/aerodynamic/experiment/highrise/;  extracts citation requirements and copyright. Download raw time series from the official website; do not store or redistribute raw data. Script  and dependency  must be uploaded simultaneously to Colab, outputting ; complete raw execution log . Fixed hyperparameters, no tuning or normalization fitting on target buildings; MLP internal early stopping uses only training building samples.

Methodology: Pressure taps are aligned by face number, normalized observed range of horizontal coordinates on that face, and z/H; geometry uses D/B and H/B, along with angle sin/cos and exposure alpha. For B0, under the same exposure/wind direction, 2D linear interpolation is first performed across faces of training buildings (nearest neighbor outside in-plane convex hull), followed by geometric linear interpolation; when held-out geometry falls outside the convex hull of training geometries, B0 is strictly speaking inapplicable, and B0* in the table is a nearest-neighbor geometry substitute, not B0 extrapolation. B1 is a squared exponential kernel GP with fixed length scale = 1 and nugget = .03 in geometry space after alignment under the same conditions; GBM is 120-iteration fixed-parameter HistGradientBoosting, and MLP is a fixed 64×64 point-level network. All wind directions and exposures of the geometric target building are excluded from training.

# TPU Rectangular Isolated High-Rise Cp Surrogate: All Downloadable Geometries and Wind Directions from the Official Website (10-13 08:13, ET)

Problem scope: For an unseen geometry, whether a fixed GBM / small MLP is significantly better than geometric interpolation for mean and rms Cp. Source is the TPU official website https://db.wind.arch.t-kougei.ac.jp/aerodynamic/experiment/highrise/, usage boundaries see existing 's manifest.

Method: Leave-one-building-out; both available exposures and all official angles for that building are held out simultaneously, and no Cp, pressure taps, or normalization statistics of the held-out building are used during training. Pressure taps on each face of each building are normalized by the actual spanwise tap range, and vertically by z/H; geometric inputs are D/B, H/B, plus face number, sin/cos wind direction, and α. B0: For each training building under the same exposure and wind direction, perform 2D linear interpolation within the face first (using nearest neighbor outside the tap convex hull), then perform 2D linear interpolation on geometry. If the training geometry convex hull for that wind direction/exposure does not contain the target, strict B0 is not applicable, and B0* in the table represents nearest-neighbor substitution in geometry; for certain buildings, only some wind directions or exposures are not applicable, so the whole-building results belong to a linear + nearest-neighbor mix. B1: Geometric GP under the same conditions, with fixed RBF length scale 1, nugget 0.03; GBM: 120 rounds per target, 19 leaves; MLP: 64×64, fixed hyperparameters, with random early stopping within training data. No tuning was done on test buildings. The script  depends on saved , ; raw logs, and the failed log from the first run caused by a 404 from mistakenly assuming the 55° square building existed is saved separately and not used as results. R² and RMSE are given for each building × exposure × method; the reported values below are RMSEs after pooling test records of each exposure by squared error.

T212, T215, T313, and T314 have linear B0 for the first exposure/wind direction, but other conditions are not all linear; whole-building B0* cannot be mistakenly called strict interpolation.
