According to predetermined criteria, the best ML method is selected post-hoc as MLP based on the mean across all buildings (not a model selection rule usable for the target building); relative to the baseline B0/B0* which has a better mean, mean RMSE increases by 13.2%, rms increases by 27.3%, and it outperforms that building's better baseline on only 2/13 buildings (even selecting per building post-hoc between GBM/MLP yields only 2/13), falling far short of "average reduction ≥20% and ≥2/3 buildings win". Strictly looking only at the 5 interior buildings where B0 is defined, MLP mean is 0.0618 vs B0 0.0412, rms is 0.0251 vs 0.0185, and ML is not superior on any of the 5 buildings. B0* in the boundary group is a nearest-neighbor surrogate, so it cannot be claimed that all 13 buildings represent a strict comparison of "ML vs B0 interpolation".

Random tap control: Randomly sample 20% taps in each geometry × exposure × angle case (seed 20261013; 25,248 test records), where B0 is in-plane interpolation B0_spatial for the same building, same angle, same exposure, rather than a cross-geometry baseline. mean R²/RMSE respectively: B0_spatial 0.9939/0.0428, GBM 0.9756/0.0854, MLP 0.9931/0.0455; rms respectively 0.9715/0.0156, 0.8650/0.0340, 0.9786/0.0135. With training taps already present in the same case, R² is optimiztic and cannot be equated with capability on new geometries.  is the comparison of measured/B0/GBM on the same color scale for T213, α=1/4, 20°, Face 1.

In the initial separate random wind direction hold-out (seed 0 sampled 20°, only five buildings and five directions), GBM significantly lost to interpolation: existing  records mean RMSE 0.1339 vs angle GP 0.0360, rms 0.0585 vs 0.0269. With taps of the same building at adjacent 10°/30° in the training set, continuous angle interpolation can exploit smoothness; tree models produce piecewise constant predictions on sin/cos encodings, making it difficult to smoothly interpolate unseen 20° in the same way, and training across five wind directions is very sparse. This is a plausible explanation of protocol/model inductive bias, not mechanistically ablated, and cannot prove overfitting; nor can it be extrapolated to the performance of leaving out all wind directions in this round.

Limitations: The TPU square building official website only provides 0–50°, asymmetrically covering angles; when test angles exceed 50°, there are no square buildings among training geometries under the same condition. Coordinates are normalized by the actual range of taps rather than the physical boundaries of the building. GP and ML hyperparameters are fixed, and MLP early stopping randomly splits training rows rather than grouping by training buildings; conclusions apply only to this set of fixed, lightweight point-level models and defined B0/B1, and do not represent all ML. Literature background card  PDF p.10 Fig.9 uses a different split;  PDF pp.15–17 is for wind direction extrapolation; neither can be directly compared horizontally with the values from this leave-one-building-out round.

Colab CPU session `tpu-all-angles-r2` has been stopped; after stopping, `colab sessions` only shows the `luw-aij` A100 session from another task, which is not this experiment, and the account balance change cannot be entirely attributed to this experiment. The CPU display rate is approximately 0.08 CU/h, actual script time was 2840.8 s, estimated at about 0.063 CU according to the rate; balance before launch was 1523.59, and 1523.11 CU after stopping, but another A100 session was running during that period, so the account difference of 0.48 CU cannot be attributed to this experiment. The estimate is well below the 10 CU cap.

Conclusion: Across all 13 geometries and all their downloadable wind directions listed on the official website, fixed GBM/MLP did not beat simple interpolation under the same conditions for mean/rms Cp on new geometries; interpolation won on all strictly interior five buildings. This conclusion applies only to these two statistics, this protocol, and models for rectangular isolated high-rise buildings.

# Deep Research Verification and Judgment Table Revision Proposal (the Lab, 10-13 08:39)

DR report: (approx. 22k words, **no DOIs whatsoever**, all 32 sources are Google redirect links; citations.md has no verifiable entries). Below is an item-by-item record of my verification of claims to be adopted / that would influence judgment (via online search of original abstract pages).

## I. Verification of Key Claims
| DR Claim | Verification Result | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DeepUFNet (Liu 2025) trained only on SR=1.5, successfully predicted surface wind pressure of unseen SR=4, 3.75 rectangular cylinders, proving cross-geometry extrapolation | arXiv 2508.03183 (later published in Physics of Fluids): Data is indeed wind tunnel pressure measurements for a 2D rectangular cylinder with SR=1.5 and 0° angle of attack; abstract mentions extrapolation, but the retrieved abstract shows no test on other side ratios. **Cross-side-ratio extrapolation could not be verified** | Do not adopt as cross-geometry evidence; list in original papers to read |
| ScaleSplit-NO (Rahman 2025/26): NMSE reduced by 65.8% compared to U-Net, VRAM 27.1→2.8 GiB, 370x speedup | Could not find the name "ScaleSplit-NO". Found the same group's FNO urban wind field series: arXiv 2308.03985 (Niigata, CityFFD), 2411.11348 (Montreal 2 km), 2501.05499 (cross-wind-direction, cross-city generalization); 370× (2.210 s→0.006 s, V100) comes from Building Simulation 10.1007/s12273-025-1392-x. 2501.05499 conclusion: **Generalizable across wind directions, limited across significantly different urban morphologies** | Do not adopt name and 65.8%/VRAM figures; adopt 370× and "limited across cities" (sources as on the left) |
| FoamGPT: 202 OpenFOAM cases LoRA fine-tuning, still requires RAG/Foam-Agent | NeurIPS 2025 page: 202-case dataset; GPT-4.1-mini fine-tuned success rate 17.27%→24.55% (AutoCFD 20.91%); Foam-Agent multi-agent (retrieval + error correction) 83.6% executable on 110 tasks | Adopt: Fine-tuning gain is small, retrieval + agent pipeline is far higher |
| BuildThemis / P4IR / EC-ARAG (code fine-tuning vs RAG comparison, 82.35%, 95.0%, etc.) | Sources are only redirect links, original text not verified | Do not adopt numbers; use only as clues |
| TPU interference database GAN 30% data predicts 70% (Chen 2020) | Namely arXiv 1908.07307 / card QN6Z9F4B (random hold-out within same database, PDF p.10 Fig.9) | Consistent with existing card; DR itself also points out it is essentially in-database interpolation |
| Aurora 0.1°, 10 m wind better than IFS-HRES, captured Storm Ciarán gusts | Did not verify original text (Aurora paper exists, specific numbers not verified) | Clue, do not adopt numbers |
| AI weather model output is overly smooth, cannot explicitly generate cold pool gust fronts | Consistent with Feldmann 2024 (arXiv 2406.09474) and Hua 2025 GRL (10.1029/2024GL109611, reviewer D has directly read) | Adopt (use the latter two as sources) |
| "No direct model evidence for automatic thunderstorm/non-thunderstorm wind classification" | **Contradicts knowledge base**: Card 2T26I5GW (Chen & Lombardo 2020, 1D-CNN, ASOS 5-fold internal CV acc 86.7%, PDF p.12 §4.1) | Do not adopt; missed by DR |
| SigLLM: LLM for wind turbine time-series anomaly detection has worse F1 than dedicated models like LSTM-DT and is slow | Did not verify original text (MIT project exists) | Clue, direction aligns with "dedicated small models are better than general-purpose LLMs" |
| 2a "absolute top choice", 2b "extremely high feasibility", 3 "immediate results" | Inference wording of DR, not precedent conclusions | Do not adopt |

## II. Relationship with TPU Experiments (Whether There Is a Conflict)
- TPU in-line data: Leave-one-building-out across 13 rectangular isolated high-rises × 2 exposures × all official wind directions; in interpolation scenarios, best ML has 13% (mean) / 27% (rms) higher RMSE than interpolation, winning on 2/13 buildings; database boundary extrapolation (T111) ML roughly halves the error.
- The only potentially conflicting claim from DR is that "FNO/DeepUFNet has strong cross-geometry extrapolation". After verification: DeepUFNet cross-side-ratio unverified; FNO urban wind field itself reports limitations across urban morphologies. **There is no verified precedent that beats interpolation under the condition of "whole-building geometry held out + compared with interpolation under the same budget"**, so there is **no conflict** with TPU conclusions. The difference between the two is: precedents tackle spatiotemporal fields / time-stepping or cross-wind directions in the same scenario, and their comparison baselines are other neural networks (U-Net/GNN) rather than interpolation.
- The truly usable directions suggested by DR align with root Lead's stance: extrapolation (new geometry categories), spatiotemporal/fluctuating field reconstruction, and multi-fidelity.

## III. Judgment Table Revision Proposal
| Category | Original Judgment | Proposal | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Domain fine-tuned LLM | Low (deferred) | **Low, maintain**; supplement FoamGPT: fine-tuning gain 17%→25%, retrieval + multi-agent 84% | FoamGPT NeurIPS 2025; cards FV7BN78P, 5ZE3U2A8 |
| 2a Wind pressure surrogate (interpolation: isolated rectangular, mean/rms) | Low | **Low, maintain** (no conflict with precedents) | TPU in-line data; QN6Z9F4B p.10; 9CBNZGZB pp.15–17 |
| 2a′ Extrapolation / spatiotemporal fluctuating field / multi-fidelity / urban wind field | TBD | **Medium**: The only direction with precedents and where we have compute; but precedents compare against other networks, need to build our own "vs interpolation/low-fidelity" baseline | NF6S3H9N pp.1–3; FNO urban wind field series (2501.05499 cross-city limitations); TPU T111 |
| 2b AI weather models | Low-Medium | **Low-Medium, maintain**: Environmental screening has techniques but is smooth; we focus mainly on hindcasting | Feldmann 2024; Hua 2025 GRL |
| 3 Dedicated small models | Medium | **Medium, maintain**: ASOS thunderstorm wind classification has direct precedent (missed by DR); wind tunnel anomaly detection has only synthetic data | 2T26I5GW p.12; wind tunnel track reply |
| One sentence for Liang Hu | — | Interpolation scenarios are not worth investing in; what is worth looking at are extrapolation and multi-fidelity (2a′), as well as thunderstorm wind classification (3) — unchanged after DR | — |

# 裁决：Deep Research 核对与判断表修订（3/3 有效：Gemini、GPT-6、GLM；GLM 曾排队等名额；10-13）

三位均"有保留地支持"："已核先例不推翻 TPU 结论"成立；1 低、2a 内插低、2b 低-中、3 中可维持；2a′ 统一升"中"不成立。亲核：arXiv 2508.03183 摘要页（v2 2025-12-07 摘要含 SR=4、3.75 泛化测试）；arXiv 2609.38977 摘要页（Qin, Zhao, Li, Wang, Xiao，2026-09-30；Montreal 500×150×500，一步 NMSE 比基线低 65.8%）；FoamGPT ML4PS 2025 PDF（Table 1：Qwen3-8B 0→26.36%，GPT-4.1-mini 35.45→39.09%，评估关闭自动纠错）； 分组表。

## 必须改（已改）
1. **DeepUFNet**（E、D；A 读的是 v1 正文）：撤回"未能核实"。v2 摘要含 SR=4、3.75 泛化测试。不作 TPU 冲突证据的理由改为：它是同类二维柱上**由稀疏测点时程重建/推进全场壁面风压**，基线是其他网络，不是无测点的参数化几何预测，也没和插值比。
2. **ScaleSplit-NO**（三位）：撤回"查无"。出处 Qin et al. arXiv 2609.38977（DR 把作者写成 Rahman）；采用"Montreal 城市风场一步 NMSE 比基线低 65.8%"。显存 27.1→2.8 GiB、基线为 U-Net、完整训练 9.7/25.5 h 来自审稿人 A 读的正文 §4.1、附录 B.8、D.4，本人只核到摘要，标"审稿人核，未亲核"。370× 仍单列为另一篇（Building Simulation 10.1007/s12273-025-1392-x，**推理**单帧，未亲核）。
3. **TPU 统计口径**（A）：13.2%/27.3%、2/13 是全部 13 栋（含最近邻替代）；严格内部 5 栋：MLP mean RMSE 0.0618 vs B0 0.0412、rms 0.0251 vs 0.0185，ML 0/5 获胜。几何×暴露为 22 个组合，不是 13×2。结论限"固定 GBM/MLP、本协议、本基线"。
4. **FoamGPT**（A、D）：数字改为 ML4PS 2025 版 Table 1（Qwen3-8B 0→26.36%，GPT-4.1-mini 35.45→39.09%）；17.27→24.55 来自会议页面，版本不明，不用。不再写"检索胜过微调"（底座与流程都不同）；Foam-Agent 83.6% 口径不一（D：arXiv 2505.04997 为 88.2%），不用。类别 1 仍低，依据是"没有证据显示本地微调比前沿模型 + 检索 + 纠错流水线更好"。
5. **FNO 跨风向**（A）：补条件——西风训练直接预测北风有困难，旋转对齐后改善（arXiv 2501.05499 §5.2，审稿人 A 核）；跨显著不同城市形态有局限。
6. **2a′ 评级**（E、A）：删"唯一有先例且我们有算力"。拆成两行：轻量方向（库边界外推、稀疏测点重建、多保真校正）=**附条件候选**（先例存在，本组数据/算力未核）；3D 高分辨率城市风场代理=**算力受限暂缓**（ScaleSplit-NO 完整训练 9.7–25.5 h，远超 ≤10 CU）。NF6S3H9N 改述：比较对象含 LF LES、Kriging 多保真、NN 多保真，低保真是粗网格 LES 不是 RANS，只做单楼跨风向（审稿人 A 读原 PDF pp.10–11）。T111 只证明参数边界外推，不证明新几何类别。
7. **2b 措辞**（A）：负面结论限定于所评估的 0.25° 全球模型（Feldmann 2024）与 Pangu 约一天提前量龙卷环境（Hua 2025 GRL 10.1029/2024GL109611），不概括所有 AI 天气模型。
8. **TPU GAN 作者**（A、D）：Hu et al. 2020（卡片 QN6Z9F4B），非 Chen；"30% 训练预测 70%"是作者推断，原文为随机留 6 例最终验证 + 子集内 80/20，分母 2558/2658 不一致。

## 仅供参考
- 2T26I5GW 卡片状态 not_approved / requires_pi_review（D）——引用时带"卡片待审"；"5 折"见原 PDF p.12（A 读原文确认）。
- 2b 后报增量有限（E）——维持低-中。

## 未采纳的异议
- E"2a′ 应维持'待定'"：部分采纳——3D 城市风场暂缓；轻量方向写"附条件候选"而非"待定"，因为已有可核先例（NF6S3H9N、DeepUFNet、TPU T111）且试验成本可控，需要一个可排期的标签。
- 无需升级 Liang Hu。

# Silsoe v7 Inflow–Windward Cp Time History Minimal Experiment

Same single LBM-LES inflow realization, normal windward, 11 windward pressure taps; here "measured time history" refers only to the LBM target time history, **not field pressure measurement validation**.
Data: , read-only; referencing taps and dynamic pressure definitions from its `analyze.py:87-103`.
30,001 samples, 42–642 s, 50 Hz; training 42–462 s, validation 462–522 s, testing 522–642 s, strictly sequential; initial 1.26 s used only as history window.
Cp=(ρ_tap − causal 2 s moving average of ρ_REF)/(3q), q=average 0.5ρ|u|² of REF point during training segment = 0.001279913 lattice units; quasi-steady U_ref = training mean uz = 0.05193638 lattice speed at center R_y0_z6 of 1h rack behind inlet.
Quasi-steady Cp_mean fitted on training segment only. Linear transfer function: 20 points × 3 components, ten causal lags at 0.1 s intervals over 0–0.9 s, fixed ridge penalty 100; TCN 1.28 s input, 4-layer causal dilated convolution, best epoch selected on validation segment. Normalization and selection never use the testing segment.
Persistence Cp(t+Δ)=Cp(t) is only suitable for lead-time Δ prediction; this experiment is a synchronous t inflow-to-pressure mapping, hence this baseline is not listed.

| Method | Windward 11-tap equal-weight RMSE Cp | Mean correlation coefficient | Mean fluctuating standard deviation ratio | Mean absolute error of min Cp | Mean absolute error of max Cp |

# Silsoe v7: Inflow → Windward Wind Pressure Experiment with Transport Time Lag Coverage

Single LBM-LES, single cube, normal windward, 11 windward pressure taps. Target is LBM time history, not field-measured Cp(t); only windward mean Cp is conditionally verified by field measurements.
Original CSV read-only, copied to local temporary directory to run; 42–642 s 50 Hz, training 42–462 s, validation 462–522 s, testing 522–642 s; non-random temporal split. Candidate training period 42–462 s, where 42–48 s only provides causal history, actual fitted points are 48–462 s (10 Hz, 4140 points); validation 462–522 s is 10 Hz (600 points), testing 522–642 s retains 50 Hz (6001 points); all input windows contain only current and past 0–6 s.

items.title: Uses of self-built models · first-round decision (10-13 06:40, sub-project)
items.text:
# In-House Model Uses · First-Round Decision (10-13 06:40, sub-project)

- What was done: Judgment table draft (1 Low / 2a Medium / 2b Low-Medium / 3 Medium); minimum viable experiment selected 2a: **whole-building holdout** on the TPU isolated tall building database, ML (GBM + small network) comparing interpolation and Kriging, dispatched to ideas, ≤10 CU; review  (3 members) underway, first dispatching revocable experiments.
- Why: 2a is the only category that could potentially change the research toolchain, but the literature only proves high accuracy for random holdouts within the same database (QN6Z9F4B p.10 Fig.9) and poor extrapolation rms (9CBNZGZB pp.15–17), and LatticeUrbanWind shows that interpolation can beat physics-based models; therefore, test first "whether changing geometry beats interpolation". Using public TPU data, independent of replies from other tracks. 1 has no counterexamples (VNP48R7H is only CFD configuration generation, and we already use frontier models); 2b offers small increments for hindcast-style work (Feldmann 2024 arXiv 2406.09474: environmental parameters have skill but are smooth, CAPE accuracy is limited by vertical levels, no literature card, based on quick web search).
- Cost of being wrong: ≤10 CU; if the review considers that the first step should be 3 or 2b, simply re-dispatch.
- Deep Research was not run due to the API 429 monthly limit and will be supplemented later; already reported to the platform.

## Postscript 10-13: Review  Verdict
- 3/3 qualified support. 7 revisions (ASOS parent set / internal CV, experiment conclusions limited to rectangular isolated tall building mean/rms Cp, leave-one-building-out and predetermined criteria, Han 2026 used only as a baseline warning, Taira attribution downgraded, Category 1 supplemented with FV7BN78P/5ZE3U2A8, Category 2b deleted climate card and added Pangu→WRF/WoFSCast precedent); canceled 2b single-event CAPE comparison.
- Protocol supplement sent to ideas via  (queued after ; if the original task has finished running under the old protocol, recalculate according to the supplement, cost ≤2 CU). Full verdict text.

## Postscript 10-13 07:30: TPU Wind Pressure Surrogate Conclusions
- 13 geometries × 2 exposures × 5 wind directions leave-one-building-out: ML is comparable to interpolation (mean −2.1%, rms +0.4%, each winning on 3/13 buildings), failing the predetermined criteria. 2a wind pressure surrogate recommendation level downgraded to Low; ML is significantly better only when extrapolating to boundary geometry (T111). Basis: our track data, no literature card; consistent with "high on random holdouts, degraded under shifted conditions" in 9CBNZGZB pp.15–17 and QN6Z9F4B p.10.
- All-wind-direction re-check  runs as usual (<1 CU), used only for confirmation.
- Cost of being wrong: If the all-wind-direction results flip, recommendation level changes back to Medium, with a loss of half a day.

## Postscript 10-13: Root Lead Framing Correction (Adopted)
- 2a "Low" is limited only to dense public databases, isolated rectangular tall buildings, mean/rms Cp, and geometric interpolation; peak Cp, interference effects, non-rectangular/complex geometries, and database boundary extrapolation (T111) have not been negated. The one-sentence summary to Liang Hu is revised to: Interpolation scenarios are not worth investing in; what is worth looking into is extrapolation and multi-fidelity (2a′), as well as thunderstorm wind classification (3). The second experiment to be decided after  and  return, ≤10 CU.

## Postscript 10-13 08:20: All-Wind-Direction Re-check
- : Under all wind directions, ML is worse in interpolation scenarios (mean +13%, rms +27%, 2/13 buildings), and the conclusion does not flip; the ML advantage in T111 extrapolation is retained. Second experiment candidates: extrapolation/multi-fidelity (2a′) or ASOS thunderstorm wind classification (3), waiting.

## Postscript 10-13: DR Supplementary Run and Review 
- DR (08:25–08:36, no DOI) was submitted for review after verification, 3/3 qualified support. Revisions: DeepUFNet and ScaleSplit-NO changed to verified but differing in task/baseline, not conflicting with TPU; TPU framing changed to strictly internal 5 buildings (ML 0/5); FoamGPT changed to ML4PS 2025 Table 1; 2a′ split into "Light: conditional candidate" and "Heavy: deferred due to 3D urban wind field computing power constraints". Verdict.
- The second experiment is still waiting for events track : If the events track has a classification bottleneck → ASOS thunderstorm wind classification; otherwise → TPU boundary extrapolation / sparse tap reconstruction (≤10 CU). Cost of being wrong: Choosing the wrong experiment of ≤3 CU.

## Postscript 10-13: Second Experiment Dispatched First with LBM Inflow → Wind Pressure Transfer Function
- Digital Twin Wind Tunnel Lead provided the preferred surrogate and readily available local data (approx. 120 MB CSV), belonging to the 2a′-Light "reconstruction with measurement taps / inflow information" direction, workable on workstation CPU. Dispatched first without waiting for the events track; if the events track has a classification bottleneck, ASOS classification will be queued later (each ≤3 CU).
- Criteria predetermined: Learned models have RMSE ≥20% lower than linear transfer functions and perform better on ≥2/3 windward taps. Conclusions are limited to a single cube, single wind direction, and single inflow; results delivered to Digital Twin Wind Tunnel "LBM Platform and Validation".
- Cost of being wrong: ≤3 CU and half a day.

## Postscript 10-13: LBM Inflow → Wind Pressure Experiment Conclusions
- The first round was invalidated because the input window was shorter than the ~4 s transport time lag (verified by Lead); after redoing, learned models do not beat linear transfer functions (upstream probe input FIR 0.207 vs CNN 0.220, 0/11 points). Our track data, no literature basis.
- The two minimum viable experiments share the same conclusion: On our existing data, learned models have not beaten appropriate classical baselines (interpolation / linear transfer functions). The next experiment leaves only Category 3 (ASOS thunderstorm wind classification or CAARC wind tunnel measured channel anomaly detection), waiting for the events track.
- Results delivered to their "LBM Platform and Validation" as requested by Digital Twin Wind Tunnel Lead.

## Postscript 10-13: Correction of LBM Experiment Input B
- Digital Twin Wind Tunnel track re-check: Input B (all P_x-*) includes x=0 (inside the cube), z12 (above the roof), and x=−5 (stagnation region) probes; correlation 0.66 cannot be treated as inflow predictive skill; the error lies in the Lead's task specification. The only valid conclusion remaining is the 1h mast rack group (FIR 0.269 ≈ CNN 0.271, correlation approx. 0.3). Rerun dispatched for x≤−10/−15 m. The conclusion that "learned models do not beat linear methods" still holds in the 1h mast rack group.
- Their other two reruns (v8 inflow, W3 member cross-prediction) await notification once their data is ready.

## Postscript 10-13: LBM Reruns (True Upstream Probes) Wrap-Up
- x≤−10 m: FIR 0.215 / CNN 0.212 (+1.3%); x≤−15 m: FIR 0.228 / CNN 0.229. Learned models do not significantly beat linear transfer functions; conclusions are consistent across all three inputs. Our track data, no literature basis. This experiment is wrapped up on the Lab side; v8 inflow and W3 cross-prediction await notification from the Digital Twin Wind Tunnel track.

items.text:
# Max Literature Review Verification (Lead, 10-13 10:58)
Report: (~34,000 words; only 2 DOIs, both found: OceanGPT ACL 2024, AstroMLab 2 SC24-W). Point-by-point verification of statements affecting judgment (arXiv abstract page / online search):

| Report Statement | Verification | Handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unsupervised fine-tuning struggles to learn new facts, RAG consistently outperforms (Ovadia et al.) | arXiv 2312.05934 abstract: RAG "consistently outperforms"; new facts require substantial paraphrased variants to potentially be learned. Report states EMNLP 2024; arXiv page does not indicate a conference | Adopt (cite source as arXiv 2312.05934) |
| Agriculture case: Fine-tuning +6 pp, stacking RAG adds another +5 pp, similarity 47%→72% (Balaguer et al.) | Matches arXiv 2401.08406 abstract word-for-word | Adopt |
| AstroLLaMA 7B performs worse than base model after continued pre-training; 70B improves after continued pre-training | Matches arXiv 2409.19750 (AstroMLab 2) abstract; "7–8 percentage points" "43.5% vs 51.3%" not verified in original tables | Adopt qualitative conclusion, mark numbers as unverified |
| ClimateGPT: 300B tokens trained from scratch for two 7B models; 4.2B domain tokens continued pre-training on Llama-2; 7B comparable to Llama-2-70B Chat | Matches arXiv 2401.09646 abstract; comparison only on authors' self-built climate benchmark | Adopt, note self-built benchmark |
| LLaMat (materials) information extraction "substantially outperforms Claude-3.5 and GPT-4o" | arXiv 2412.09560 abstract **does not** contain comparison with GPT-4o/Claude | Do not adopt this comparison |
| "OpenFOAMGPT (Feng et al., arXiv 2504.09602) Qwen2.5-7B fine-tuned on 28,716 NL2FOAM pairs, 88.7%" | **Author/name misattributed**: 28,716 NL2FOAM pairs, Qwen2.5-7B LoRA is Dong et al. (card, 88.7% claimed by source, card first_pass); OpenFOAMGPT (arXiv 2501.06327) is GPT-4o/o1 + RAG | Switch to VNP48R7H card; do not write "outperforms 72B" |
| Literature screening: Small open-source models have high recall, low precision | Online check: Compact models like Llama 3.1 8B have sensitivity up to 100%, precision <10% (Res Synth Methods 2025, PMC12873614); open-weight models across 12,360 runs average recall 83.6%, precision 18.5% (2026 study, DOI not obtained); local Llama 3.1 70B sensitivity 96.3%, specificity 89.1%, within 4% of GPT-4o (ISPOR Europe 2026 poster) | Adopt qualitative conclusion; numbers pending litwiki card creation |
| Qwen2.5-VL-72B OCRBench_v2 EN 61.5 / ZH 63.7, beats Gemini 1.5 Pro | Unverified | Lead |
| vLLM single-card A100 8B ~3,400 tok/s; 32B ~600–1,350 tok/s | Vendor/blog benchmark, unverified; our group's experiment will test empirically | Lead, subject to empirical testing |
| Darwin-27B-Opus (Qwen3.5-27B) GPQA 86.9%, "single-card 2-hour evolutionary merge" | Unverified, suspected to be mixed in from model community cards | Do not adopt |
| No dedicated LLM for wind engineering / structures / civil engineering; mainstream is general-purpose models + tools/RAG | Consistent with KB search (no hits) | Adopt as "none found", not "does not exist" |
| Log diagnostics: Local 8B insufficient, GPT-4o only 30% on AgentErrata | Unverified; furthermore it involves distributed agent faults, not HPC job logs | Do not adopt as evidence for our tasks |

## Judgment Directions Derived from This (Pending)
1. Offloading batch miscellaneous chores to local open-source LLMs: **Medium–High**, via "initial screening / extraction + frontier model verification"; throughput and quality must be empirically tested by our group.
2. Fine-tuning on our materials: **Low–Medium**—knowledge injection should prioritize retrieval (Ovadia; Balaguer); fine-tuning may only be useful for fixed-format outputs (configuration files, tag systems), and 7B continued pre-training carries risk of forgetting (AstroMLab 2).
3. Building "our own domain foundation model" (continued pre-training): **Low**—prior examples all require billions to hundreds of billions of tokens, evaluations are mostly on self-built benchmarks with few independent replications; no precedent seen in wind engineering (holds paper novelty, but high barrier to entry and weak evidence of value).
4. Gap with frontier models: Needs empirical testing on our group's benchmark set; literature only provides directions (low screening precision, weak complex reasoning).

## Second Report (Default File, ~24,000 words) Supplementary Verification (10:59)
| Report Statement | Verification | Handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "PE-Loop (Luo et al., arXiv 2610.08156)": LLM acting as judge caused 58.43% of designs to be misjudged as compliant | arXiv 2610.08156 is actually "Vibe Building", authors Jiang, Luo et al. (2026-10-06); Abstract: VB-Bench 3,577 physically adjudicated building instances, six code families; replacing physical verdict with LLM judge resulted in "58.43% non-compliant among accepted designs". Abstract does not mention OpenSees | Adopt (author corrected to Jiang et al.) |
| GPT + MCP(OpenSees) structural analysis error <1.5%, pure LLM error >230% | Online check found UTE data paper and Mendeley dataset: <1.5% is true, pure LLM deviation is **>400%**, not 230%; base shear not separated; single research group | Adopt qualitative conclusion, change number to >400% |
| OpenFOAM: Without retrieval 16.7% → With retrieval 100% success | Unverified | Lead |
| Open-source model recall for PDF long table extraction <14%; commercial model screening achieves both 100% recall and >88% precision | Unverified, and contradicts Max report's "Qwen2.5-VL matches GPT-4o" | Do not adopt, subject to empirical testing in our group's benchmark |
| Self-hosted vLLM 70B INT4 ~$0.55 per million tokens | Unverified, blog conversion | Lead |
Common points: Both agree that there is no dedicated LLM for wind engineering / civil engineering; the mainstream is frontier models + tools/retrieval; domain continued pre-training has high barriers and weak evidence.

items.label: Review verdict
items.title: Verdict: verification of the large-language-model review (3/3 valid: Gemini, GPT-6, GLM; 10-13)
items.text:
# Verdict: LLM Literature Review Verification (3/3 valid: Gemini, GPT-6, GLM; 10-13)

All three gave "reserved support": Continued pre-training "Low", local models for partial auxiliary tasks, gap requires empirical testing by our group—the direction holds; several verification records and overly broad statements must be revised. Personally verified: arXiv 2412.09560 v2 main text (§2.2, Figure 3: comparison of LLaMat with Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini-1.5-Pro, GPT-4o); PMC12657656 (Res Synth Methods 2025); CivilGPT (Journal of Tongji University 2025, 53(6):831–840, DOI 10.11908/j.issn.0253-374x.24358).

## Must Revise (Revised)
1. **LLaMat** (all three): Withdraw "Do not adopt". v2 §2.2 / Figure 3: For text extraction, LLaMat outperforms tested frontier models; for table extraction, it is only slightly superior, and commercial models are often comparable or even better, with advantages mainly in regex tables. Adopt as **author self-report on self-built materials benchmark**, model trained via 30B-token-level continued pre-training + instruction fine-tuning + downstream task fine-tuning; do not extrapolate to arbitrary PDF number extraction, do not treat as a fair comparison with "frontier models + retrieval". Journal version (NMI) not personally verified, do not cite.
2. **MCP Structural Analysis Numbers** (A, D): Withdraw "<1.5% is true, pure LLM >400%". Figures within source are inconsistent: Journal (Buildings 15(17):3190) abstract gives <1.5% and >400%, but its Tables 7–9 report 2.756%/2.834%, pure GPT across cases ranges from 235–267% to >400%; data paper (Data 10(11):169) gives 230–270%. Retain only qualitative statement: "Pure LLM structural calculations are unreliable, significantly improved after connecting to solver", both are self-reports by a single research group (verified by reviewers A and D, tables in main text not personally verified).
3. **NL2FOAM 72B Comparison** (A, D): Restore to source claims—Dong et al. (VNP48R7H, arXiv 2504.09602) reports 88.7% vs Qwen2.5-72B 31.4% on their benchmark; 88.7% is solution accuracy defined by L2 error, not success rate; meshing still requires human intervention.
4. **Delete "Fine-tuning only useful for fixed formats"** (A): Ovadia only compared unsupervised fine-tuning vs RAG; Balaguer had supervised fine-tuning +6 pp. Change to "Knowledge injection prioritizes retrieval; supervised fine-tuning can yield gains on narrow annotated tasks, whether it is worthwhile depends on our group's empirical testing".
5. **Add CivilGPT for Precedents in Civil Engineering** (A): Tongji CivilGPT uses staged pre-training + fine-tuning + engineering alignment, Civil-Bench 14,823 objective questions + 269 subjective questions, compared against 15 models (authors' self-evaluation). Withdraw "No dedicated LLM seen in civil engineering"; still none seen in wind engineering; change "holds paper novelty" to "insufficient evidence".
6. **PDF <14% is a Misplaced Metric** (E, A): Originates from page-level retrieval recall in OpenFOAM documentation, not table/numerical extraction; does not contradict OCRBench. Add SciAssess (NAACL Findings 2025, Table 3: table extraction recall for both Llama3.1 and GPT-4o is 0.441, verified by reviewer A, not personally verified).
7. **Rewrite Screening Evidence** (A, D): Add PMC12657656—Llama 3.3 70B sensitivity 0.88 / specificity 0.93, GPT-4o 0.85 / 0.97, Gemini 1.5 Pro 0.94 / 0.85, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 0.94 / 0.80 (personally verified). PMC12873614 low precision includes GPT-4o mini, not unique to open source; ISPOR 96.3%/89.1% belongs to the entire workflow, not a single model. **"Local initial screening + frontier verification" cannot guarantee recall**: Items excluded locally will not be recovered by verification—local model recall must be measured independently in the evaluation.
8. **Split Ratings** (A): Offloading chores to local models will no longer have a unified "Medium–High" rating, but will be rated separately by task, determined by our group's empirical testing.
9. **Change Status of Verified Numbers** (E, D): AstroMLab 2 Table I: LLaMA-2-7B 51.3% vs AstroLLaMA-2-7B 43.5% (answer token prediction metric); 70B full instruction Q&A 64.7% vs 70.7% actually decreased (A); CPT ~32 / 2000 A100·h (8B/70B). OpenFOAMGPT (Pandey et al., arXiv 2501.06327) 1/6 without retrieval, 6/6 with retrieval, N=6 tutorial cases.

## For Reference Only
- OceanGPT "used by ARPA" suspected to be fabricated (E)—do not adopt.
- Colab cold start ~40 min must be included in throughput/cost (E)—evaluation records wall clock including preparation.
- PDF extraction recommendation "layout parser (Docling/MinerU) + model extraction + physical constraint validation" (E)—incorporated into Group B as a variant.
- OPENXRD: LLaMat-2-chat accuracy actually dropped to 16.13% after adding expert materials (A, third-party negative evaluation)—recorded.
- Screening study DOI 10.1017/rsm.2026.10093 (A).

## Objections Not Adopted
- E "Strongly recommend for local miscellaneous chores (Medium–High)": Unified rating not adopted (see Must Revise 8).
- No need to escalate to Liang Hu.

items.text:
# Benchmark Label Sources (2026-10-13)

Fixed seed 20261013; 100 questions in total: A 40 (Yes 10, No 30), B 25, C 20, D 15. Generation scripts build_eval.py, build_pdf.py. All models only receive `prompt`, and must not receive `answer`, `sourcecfd_m4_downburst_cfd/paper_cards/`, negative examples come from and , with specific card paths and keys recorded for each question.

Group B is selected from Quantitative anchors of , cards contain page numbers, combined with original paper PDFs from Zotero; `pdftotext -layoutsource` carries PDF absolute path and physical page, `card` carries card path. Group B answer units in main text are standardized to the units requested within questions.

Group C uses NCEI Storm Events official details archive `StormEvents_details-ftp_v1.0_d2024_c20260728.csv.gz`, EVENT_TYPE as original label, EVENT_NARRATIVE as input; samples where category names directly appear in descriptions are removed, with sampling ratio Thunderstorm Wind 7, High Wind 5, Strong Wind 4, Other 4. Each question retains EVENT_ID and official source URL. Contains implicit weather semantics; does not guarantee descriptions can uniquely identify event categories.

Group D comes from audited candidate calculators of Design_Load : 8 existing ratios, 7 ratios determined by locked numerical values, source JSON pointers in each question's `sourcenot_for_design`, not used as code compliance determinations; this group actually tests low-difficulty numerical calculation and does not represent all ASCE 7-22 code tasks. Pre-fixed numerical relative error ≤1% judged correct; A recall ≥95% and precision ≥70% of frontier; C accuracy; for the rest, local best ≥90% of frontier and significantly outperforming simple baselines before being eligible for offloading. Keyword baselines do not apply to B/D. Small sample size; report single group scores without combining ratings.

# Local Open-Source LLMs and Claude: 100-Question Chores Benchmark (10-13)

## Scope of Conclusions and Protocol

Same 100-question benchmark set: A Literature screening 40 (positive 10 / negative 30), B Paper PDF single-page number extraction 25, C NOAA event description classification 20, D Candidate calculator regression ratios 15. Experimental figures are all internal track data, not scientific conclusions of papers/codes. The two local models used vLLM on Colab A100 40 GB, temperature=0, single-question JSON, batch of 10 questions; Claude Sonnet was invoked single-question via local `claude -p --model sonnet --tools ''` with concurrency 5. For B, all models were given identical `pdftotext -layout` raw PDF physical page text, with Docling Markdown page text additionally used as a local model variant (parser replaced only). Gemini CLI OAuth, literature does not substitute for this experiment.

The initial version of D13–15 did not provide locked-value files but required reciting numbers from memory; upon discovery, they were changed to ratio questions with complete given inputs (eval_set_v2); the initial version of C's example JSON placed the four options in a single string, which 30B copied verbatim leading to 0/20; upon discovery, options and single output were separated, and all participating models re-answered C (eval_set_v3). The initial version and responses are all retained; the table below only adopts retest results with identical v3 questions/prompts. Execution sequence also deviated: although the benchmark set had 100 questions generated and verified before the first round of calls, it was not reported back to the client separately before launching as required by the statement of work. Prompt changes occurred after seeing first-round outputs and cannot be regarded as a strict blind test; this simultaneously demonstrates format robustness issues. All positive example titles in A contain topical keywords, resulting in full marks for keyword rules; this is a low-difficulty benchmark that does not exert real recall pressure.

## Group Results

Quality scoring: A recall, precision; B numerical relative error ≤1% and equivalent units; C accuracy; D numerical relative error ≤1%. No cross-group overall rating. The token column reflects input + output reported by models; Claude CLI counts include large amounts of system/cache tokens, differing in accounting standard from vLLM single-question tokens. USD reflects only the list price from Claude CLI's `total_cost_usd`; local uses shared GPU CUs, which do not convert directly to subscription USD. Wall clock: Claude's initial-round single-group actual concurrency window is shown in the table; revised C/D required additional calls; for local models, because cold starts and downloads were shared across the entire run, only full-run empirical times are available (8B 163.53 s, 30B 260.71 s), without fabricating independent cold-start durations per group.

| Group | Method | Quality | A Recall/Precision | Input+Output Tokens | Claude USD | Claude Initial Round Group Wall Clock |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A | Title keywords | 40/40 | 100%/100% | 0 | 0 | — |
| A | Qwen3-8B | 40/40 | 100%/100% | 13,670 | — | — |
| A | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 | 39/40 | 100%/90.9% | 13,510 | — | — |
| A | Claude Sonnet | 40/40 | 100%/100% | 1,504,564 | 1.940 | 29.6 s |
| B | Qwen3-8B / pdftotext | 22/25 | — | 33,636 | — | — |
| B | Qwen3-30B / pdftotext | 24/25 | — | 33,530 | — | — |
| B | Claude Sonnet / pdftotext | 24/25 | — | 1,027,608 | 1.369 | 22.2 s |
| B | Qwen3-8B / Docling Markdown | 22/25 | — | 28,971 | — | — |
| B | Qwen3-30B / Docling Markdown | 23/25 | — | 28,873 | — | — |
| C | Keywords | 8/20 | — | 0 | 0 | — |
| C | Qwen3-8B | 11/20 | — | 3,220 | — | — |
| C | Qwen3-30B | 12/20 | — | 3,140 | — | — |
| C | Claude Sonnet | 15/20 | — | 791,649 | 0.973 | 18.7 s (initial round with old prompt; v3 retest counted separately) |
| D | Qwen3-8B | 11/15 | — | 1,962 | — | — |
| D | Qwen3-30B | 15/15 | — | 1,902 | — | — |
| D | Claude Sonnet | 14/15 | — | 566,707 | 0.728 | 24.4 s (initial round with old D13–15; corrections counted separately) |

Docling variant tokens: [已隐去] 28,652 input / 319 output, 30B 28,552 input / 321 output; already summed in the table above. The full Docling workflow for B required CPU installation and preprocessing, while the model batch generation itself took 2.24 s for 8B and 1.92 s for 30B; one cannot simply report generation time as the PDF pipeline wall clock. The list price for Claude's final 100 valid responses entered into the table totaled 5.010 USD; the experiment actually invoked the initial 100 items and two revisions totaling 23 items, with the CLI `total_cost_usd` summing to 6.203 USD. Per-thousand-question cost by group was A 48.50, B 54.77, C 48.65, D 48.50 USD, representing linear extrapolation group-by-group from final valid samples without amortizing revision trial-and-error (CLI has substantial cache/system overhead, affected by plan tier and concurrency). Local total duration was 3293 s, estimated at 4.848 CU, including preparation, post-failure repairs, and waiting; 296 local question inferences amortized to ~16.38 CU/thousand calls, which cannot serve as a steady-state model unit price. Account balance difference includes other sessions, see cu_record.md for details.

## Whether Each Group Is Eligible for Offloading

A: Both local models satisfy their own recall ≥95% and precision ≥70% of Claude's (8B 100/100, 30B 100/90.9). Formally, they are eligible for offloading initial screening on this small sample, but keyword rules also achieved 40/40 and positive titles directly reveal topics; practically, it is recommended to use rules first, and one cannot claim based on this that screening in real databases reaches ≥95% recall or leave records excluded by local models unreviewed.

B: 30B matches Claude at 24/25, reaching the 90% quality threshold of the frontier; 8B scored 22/25. The Docling variant did not improve 30B (23/25), while preprocessing increased complexity instead. It can be trialed as a candidate for "extracting a single number from a given page", but erroneous values/units still require verification against source pages and programmatic checks; since no simple baseline was established for B in this task, the strict condition of "significantly outperforming simple baselines" cannot be determined, and no unconditional offloading conclusion is given. For card quantitative anchor sources and PDF pages, see and `cardpage` in JSONL.

C: Best local 12/20=60%, Claude 15/20=75%, only 80% of Claude (below predefined 90%); although higher than keywords' 8/20, it still does not satisfy "eligible for offloading". Categories themselves may not be uniquely determinable from short narratives; label ambiguity must be resolved first, and automated independent classification is not recommended.

D: 30B 15/15, Claude 14/15, quality reaches the comparison threshold; but these are merely ratios of two given numbers, not the full ASCE 7-22 gust effect factor workflow, nor comprehensive Q&A for WRF/OpenFOAM configurations. Deterministic calculators should be a strong baseline on such tasks and avoid LLM arithmetic errors; lacking empirical simple baseline testing and real configuration questions, Group D as a whole cannot be officially judged "eligible for offloading". It is more reasonable to use local models for text localization and interpretation while leaving numbers to existing calculators.

## Limitations and Reproducibility

A title word leakage yielded full marks for rules; B's 25 questions concentrated on 7 published papers with relatively explicit numbers/units, and graphical numbers outside source pages were not tested; C's 20 single-year NOAA event descriptions and original EVENT_TYPE do not necessarily uniquely determine each other; D only had ratio arithmetic and did not cover real code calculations/configurations. Small-sample single-run temperature 0 has no confidence intervals. Docling CPU initial round suffered from incomplete installation and midway process `Cannot allocate memory`, and was later split into paper-by-paper conversion; failure logs and final successful files are all retained. vLLM first round had v0.13/Torch cu13 ABI mismatch, repaired to Torch 2.9.0+cu128 before running; all these preparation times were counted into CUs. No fine-tuning. Colab session has stopped; final sessions only showed others' sessions.

Reproduction: (original candidates), (original 100 questions), formed the final ; , . Raw responses are in , , and various revision files; is the scoring summary; is the raw CLI run history. Paper PDFs/Zotero, NCEI official archive, and design load regression JSONs are all read-only. No unpublished manuscripts copied or tokens saved.

# Gemini Supplementary Benchmark: Frozen v3 100-Question Set (In-Line Data)

Following delivery of the batch runner, we ran the supplementary benchmark on the `gemini-3.8-flash-high` subscription tier — **note that this is neither Gemini 2.5 Pro nor a bare API model without wrapper prompts**. Questions were drawn from the frozen v3 set, passing only the exact `id` and `prompt` fields without ground-truth answers, source metadata, or custom system prompts. After verifying the payload on Question 1 via `--dry-run`, the batch was executed at concurrency 3 with tools disabled and each question isolated. The first invocation hit the ~420 s client timeout after writing 94 responses to disk; rerunning the command resumed and completed only the remaining 6 items. All 100 unique IDs succeeded (`ok`) with a single attempt each. Raw outputs were saved and scored with the exact same per-question grading script used for the earlier models.

| Group | Gemini Score | Claude Sonnet | Best Local Model | Simple Rule | Gemini Input / Output Tokens | Sum of Per-Item Latencies |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A Literature Screening | 38/40; recall 90%, precision 90% | 40/40 | 8B: 40/40 | 40/40 | 479,665 / 20,748 | 207.84 s |
| B Numeric Extraction from PDF Page Text | 20/25 | 24/25 | 30B: 24/25 | Untested | 330,317 / 162,879 | 599.27 s |
| C NOAA Narrative Classification | 20/20 | 15/20 | 30B: 12/20 | 8/20 | 224,073 / 13,398 | 156.27 s |
| D Ratio of Given Numbers | 15/15 | 14/15 | 30B: 15/15 | Untested | 163,529 / 127,884 | 383.72 s |

In Group A, Gemini made one false negative (`A10`) and one false positive (`A13`), falling short of the pre-specified ≥95% screening recall threshold on its own; while the local 8B model formally hit 40/40, the simple keyword rule also scored 40/40, so true recall on harder borderline abstracts remains to be tested. In Group B, Gemini's five misses (`B08`, `B10`, `B11`, `B12`, `B14`) all extracted the exact right number but omitted units or violated the strict unit format rule (e.g., `B08` wrote `h` instead of `CPU h`); per the pre-specified "exact number + equivalent unit" rule, these are not re-graded. While the local 30B model matched Claude at 24/25 on B, no simple regex baseline was tested on B, so unconditional handover is not claimed. In Group C, Gemini scored 20/20 vs Claude's 15/20, whereas the best local model scored 12/20 (below the 90% frontier threshold) and cannot take over standalone classification; small sample size and inherent ambiguity between narrative descriptions and event types remain. In Group D, local 30B tied Gemini at 15/15, but the items only compute ratios of given numbers without testing a deterministic calculator baseline, which cannot be extrapolated to complex standard/configuration tasks. No cross-group composite score is computed.

Across the 100 subscription calls, reported token usage totaled 1,197,584 input tokens and 324,909 output tokens (including 324,047 thinking tokens), for 1,522,493 tokens total; roughly 12k input tokens per item come from fixed platform agent-wrapper overhead, so these figures must not be compared directly against bare vLLM inference tokens or Claude CLI tokens. Completion timestamps spanned 10-13 12:24:21 to 12:32:54 EDT (513 s); this is the span between first and last completion and **excludes pre-first-completion startup time, so it is not an exact end-to-end wall clock**. The sum of individual item latencies was 1,347.10 s (run at concurrency 3, not wall-clock time). Linearly scaling this batch gives ~15,224,930 tokens per 1,000 subscription calls as a rough capacity order of magnitude; because the subscription tier has no per-call USD billing, no fabricated dollar cost is entered, and 0 Colab CU was used. Given the distinct billing models across subscription, Claude CLI, and local inference, no strict cost-efficiency ranking is drawn. Group B passed the exact same `pdftotext -layout` plain text used for the other models rather than raw PDF binaries; the Docling variant was tested only on local models.

Comparison caveats: `v3` revised the C and D prompts after inspecting v1/v2 model outputs, so the benchmark as a whole is not a strictly blind test, and Gemini was added after that prompt revision. The Gemini batch runner injects a "do not call tools" agent-framework prompt, just as Claude CLI injects its own system prompt; we guarantee identical user-level prompts across models without claiming identical underlying system prompts. The original evaluation report is left unmodified, and this document serves as an appended supplementary record.

No questions modified or bad questions retested, nor any questions deleted.

Scoring script : A/C labels strictly equivalent; B numerical relative error ≤1% and units identical or equivalent (common word forms such as seconds↔s, pressure taps↔taps, CPU hours↔CPU h). Observed first from the same output that the scoring script initially missed equivalent units; after supplementing unit morphological mappings, all models were uniformly re-scored; raw outputs and questions remained unmodified. A2: Both local models achieved individual recall of 100% and 98%, with precision of 46.3% and 58.3%, both exceeding 70% of frontier-best Gemini's precision of 63.6% (44.5%), formally "eligible for offloading" based on predefined point estimates. In practice, prioritize 32B: offers an increment over keyword precision of 43.5%, but its recall of 49/50 has a Wilson lower bound of 89.5%, which cannot guarantee real-world recall ≥95%; manual review should be conducted when excluding papers. Obscuring neighbor titles in negative examples left keyword accuracy at only 67.5%, but labels represent this round's manual interpretation (not author ground truth), and boundary disputes may still persist for some papers mixing wind fields and loads. Has not reached the validation level where literature can be discarded without supervision.

B2: Local best 46/50=92%, which is 95.8% of the frontier's 48/50, satisfying the 90% quality line. The keyword numerical extraction baseline for B2 is non-definable/untested, and the condition of "significantly outperforming simple baselines" cannot be evaluated, so unconditional offloading cannot be declared under full criteria; it can only serve as a candidate for initial extraction on given pages, with programmatic/manual verification against original PDF pages. In the 22 table questions, two-column PDF text and units were error-prone; 25 historical questions from the first round were sampled again, resulting in weak independence this round and overly optimiztic confidence intervals. Did not validate automatic whole-paper page finding or OCR of figures.

C2: Local best 30B was 98/100, higher than Claude's 95/100 and reaching the 90% threshold of Gemini's 100/100; but pre-screening explicitly required positive examples to have convective keywords and negative examples to have non-convective keywords, and simple rules already achieved 100/100. Because it did not significantly outperform rules, the predefined "eligible for offloading" criterion does not hold; this group only demonstrates that rules suffice when explicit causal clues exist, and cannot be used to claim that local models strongly understand ambiguous events. Only narratives were given, with types following official EVENT_TYPE; archival discrepancies may exist between non-convective keywords and original labels.

Experimental scripts , ; raw answers , ; raw logs , . Literature evidence relies solely on per-question `card`, `page`, and original PDF pages, not to be used to draw scientific literature conclusions; all numbers in this experiment are internal track data.

# Second Round Frozen Labels and Sources (Pre-dataset Review)

Dataset: eval_set_r2.jsonl; SHA-256 `673e8e22fcab613e40ee14b39416126f6bac9897318a084b514f0fc008c8fecb`; A2=200 (positive 50 / negative 150), B2=50 (15 PDFs, of which 22 questions are tables), C2=100 (Thunderstorm Wind 50, High Wind 30, Strong Wind 20). Title, label, and source fields are not given to models; only prompt is sent. All models receive identical prompt text, with no question modifications after running; if problematic questions are found, they are only excluded while retaining raw outputs.

A2: Public paper Zotero metadata abstracts linked to Zotero keys in LitWiki cards; positive examples prioritize cfd_m4_downburst_cfd/paper_cards and windfield_step2/papers, negative examples are neighboring cards such as general CWE, WRF, EVA, accelerated wind tunnels, structural response, etc.; deduplicated by Zotero key (DOIs not verified paper-by-paper). Initial screening based on title and abstract keywords, manual inspection of candidate titles, sample inspection of abstracts, and explicit wind field research negative examples as well as load/response/review positive examples excluded; 200 abstracts were not independently manually verified paper-by-paper; after freezing, spot-checked 10 questions (A2_158, 108, 042, 142, 186, 115, 162, 036, 145, 023) comparing question prompt abstract with label, and no obvious conflicts were found, though this check is not an independent full annotation. For specific excluded keys, see build_eval_r2.py. Labels represent screening judgments for this round; neighboring abstracts may contain ambiguity (must not be taken as ground truth). A2 simple subject-keyword baseline: 135/200, 67.5%, failing to reach the 95% upper limit. Absolute path and key of source cards recorded for each question.

B2: Continued using the 25 verified PDF page numerical values from 7 papers in Round 1; added 25 values from 8 new papers, with values and page numbers clearly stated in card Quantitative anchor ledgers; script build_pdf_r2.py simultaneously verified that the values exist on corresponding physical pages in original Zotero PDFs, and checked that Table numbers for 22 new table questions were within the page. Each question records card / PDF path / physical page / unit / table number. Questions only provide `pdftotext -layout` page text; numbers in figures that cannot be recovered from text were not selected. The initial 25 questions are not newly independent questions this round (models might have seen them in Round 1), and scores must note the limitation of mixing historical questions. Predefined scoring: identical or equivalent units and numerical relative error ≤1%.

C2: NCEI Storm Events official d2019/d2021/d2023/d2024 detail CSVs, with archive URLs and EVENT_ID recorded per question; only Thunderstorm Wind, High Wind, Strong Wind, stratified by state and year, descriptions 140–1400 words. Excluded prior to model runs: event narratives directly containing full event type phrases; descriptions stating only damage without causal hints; narratives where convective/non-convective causes appear simultaneously. Positive examples require convective causal clues in narratives, negative examples require non-convective meteorological causal clues; these pre-screening rules may create lexical shortcuts. Broad keyword rule baseline: 100/100; if scoring full marks, this group cannot test semantic model gains over rules, and it should be clearly noted that offload eligibility cannot be determined based on this. Field names are not in model prompts; narrative content remains as-is without masking weather phenomena in text. Original EVENT_TYPE is an administrative archive label, not an independent meteorological reassessment.

Criteria fixed prior to model runs: A2 local model recall ≥95% and precision ≥70% of frontier best precision; B2/C2 local best ≥90% of frontier best score and significantly outperforming keyword baseline (B2 lacks an applicable keyword numerical extraction baseline, must note this condition is non-determinable). Each group evaluated independently, 95% CI uses Wilson binomial interval; throughput includes cold start/download. D canceled.

(4) Follow Liang Hu's step sequence: literature review → review → verdict table → evaluation set → experiment; evaluation set dispatched only after literature review returns.

## Postscript 10-13 11:14: Literature Review Review Verdict and Minimal Experiment
- Review has reached a verdict. Continued pre-training "Low", fine-tuning "Low-Medium", handling local routine tasks to be determined by empirical task tests.
- Decision I made: Dispatch ideas to run a 100-question four-group evaluation (A screening 40, B PDF number extraction 25, C Storm Events 20, D specification/configuration 15), local 8B/30B vs Claude/Gemini, criteria pre-defined, ≤50 CU. Log error classification excluded from Round 1 due to lack of samples with root cause labels. Cost of being wrong: ≤50 CU and one day.

## Postscript 10-13 12:24: Round 1 Evaluation and Round 2
- Round 1 results: Group B PDF single-value extraction local 30B = Claude (24/25); Group C local 60% < Claude 75%; Groups A and D questions too easy, inconclusive (Group A negative samples drawn from different topic databases, title leakage—Lead task brief design issue). ideas self-reported deviation: evaluation set not submitted before kickoff, some questions re-tested after corrections, not strictly blind testing—accepted, Round 2 requires writing to disk first, no question modification post-run.
- Decision I made: Dispatch Round 2 (A2 abstract-level hard negatives 200, B2 50, C2 100 binary classification, add Gemini 3.8 Flash, add a larger local model), ≤50 CU. Why: Existing evidence only suffices to support "PDF single-value extraction can be offloaded", insufficient to answer Liang Hu's "which ones can be offloaded, how much can be saved". Cost of being wrong: ≤50 CU and half a day.

## Postscript 10-13 13:32: Conclusion and Shelving
- Round 2 (blind run on 350 frozen questions, ~1.97 CU; two rounds total ~6.8 CU): Abstract preliminary screening local Qwen3-32B ≈ Claude Sonnet (82% vs 80.5%), Gemini 3.8 Flash best (85.5%); PDF single-value extraction local 92% vs frontier 96%; Storm Events 100% with keywords after construction. Track-internal data, no literature basis (see review verdict for literature background).
- Decision I made: (1) Do not build our own large language model (continued pre-training / full fine-tuning); hold off on LoRA for now (local is already close to frontier). (2) Recommend platform route bulk routine tasks to Gemini 3.8 Flash batch channel or Colab local Qwen3-32B, with Claude only doing judgment re-checks—sent as recommendation to Platform Lead, adoption to be decided by platform / Liang Hu. (3) Change project status to "Shelved", explicitly stating restart conditions. Cost of being wrong: If Liang Hu wants to pursue domain models as a paper direction, a new project needs to be initiated (counts as change of direction, to be decided by Liang Hu).

## Postscript 10-13: Platform Lead Reply
- Platform Lead approved recommendation: default to in-subscription `` (Gemini 3.8 Flash), local vLLM not default (costs CU, lowest accuracy); changing platform-wide bot default practices forwarded to Liang Hu for decision, recommended trying for one week on the Lab track and LitWiki first, sampling 10% for re-check.
- Decision I made: For subsequent batches of homogeneous screening/extraction routine tasks within this sub-project, require bot to use `` when dispatching, and sample 10% for re-check by Claude or manually; local Qwen3-32B only used for offline or non-shareable data. Why: Within the authority of the Lab track, do not alter other tracks. Cost of being wrong: Errors in certain task types by Gemini missed by spot check—10% re-check as fallback safety net.

# TPU Isolated Tall Building Database Parameters: Lead Self-Verification (10-13, platform test "check first" step 5; not included in judgment table)

Primary sources: Official website https://db.wind.arch.t-kougei.ac.jp/aerodynamic/experiment/highrise/; official .mat sample https://minio.wind.arch.t-kougei.ac.jp/web/media/case/T111_4/time_series_of_point_wind_pressure_0.mat (/tmp temporary, not retained after reading); wind profile PDF https://minio.wind.arch.t-kougei.ac.jp/web/media/type/highrise/condition_attaches/profile..pdf

| Parameter | Primary Source Observation | Excerpted Sentence from Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sampling frequency | 1000 Hz | .mat `Sample_frequency`=1000; Readme: "Wind_direction_angle,Sample_frequency and Sample_period are wind direction angle,sample frequency(hz)and sample period(second)" |
| Sampling duration / number of samples | 32.768 s / 32768 points (T111_4, 0°) | .mat `Sample_period`=32.768; `Wind_pressure_coefficients` size 32768×100; "All of the variables here are in model scale." |
| Top reference wind speed | 11.0017 m/s (T111_4, 0°; case-by-case field, other cases unverified) | .mat `Uh_AverageWindSpeed`='11.0017' |
| α | 1/4, 1/6 two categories | Official website: "Alpha parameter determining the exposure factor 1/4 1/6"; Wind profile PDF figure caption "Flow α=1/6", "Flow α=1/4" |
| Scale ratio | **Not stated** on official website, .mat Readme, or wind profile PDF | Model dimensions Building_breadth=0.1 m (T111, model scale); scale ratio source pending from E/F |

Our TPU script: uses only Cp (already non-dimensional), geometry D/B, H/B, and α=1/4, 1/6, independent of sampling frequency, duration, wind speed, and scale ratio; mean/rms uses full-length time series. α matches official website.

## Verification of E's (Gemini) Report (10-13)
- Scale ratio 1/400: Lead opened https://db.wind.arch.t-kougei.ac.jp/aerodynamic/case/T111_4/ and /T115_4/, original text "Model geometric parameters Breadth 100 Depth 100 Height 100 Model scale 1/400" (T115_4 has Height 500, also 1/400)——**Confirmed**.
- Uh for T115_4 0°: Lead downloaded official .mat, `Uh_AverageWindSpeed`='11.1438', 1000 Hz, 32.768 s, 32768×500——**Confirmed**.
- E's claim of "entire database 0° Uh range 10.6924–11.3737" not verified individually; 2:1 series only has α=1/4, consistent with what was observed in our experiment.
- Awaiting F's (Grok) report before merging table.

## E/F Merged Table (10-13, after Lead verification)
| Parameter | Value | Primary Source and Original Text | E | F | Adopted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Scale ratio | 1/400 | Official website case pages /aerodynamic/case/T111_4/, /T115_4/: "Model scale 1/400" | 1/400 | 1/400 | Adopted (Lead verified by opening page) |
| Sampling frequency | 1000 Hz | .mat `Sample_frequency`=1000; Readme "sample frequency(hz)" | 1000 | 1000 | Adopted |
| Duration / points | 32.768 s / 32768 (model scale) | .mat `Sample_period`=32.768, matrix 32768 rows; Readme "All of the variables here are in model scale." | Same | Same | Adopted |
| Top reference wind speed | Case-by-case field, ~10.7–11.4 (T111_4 0° 11.0017; T115_4 0° 11.1438) | .mat `Uh_AverageWindSpeed`; Readme defines neither unit nor location | Nominal 11 m/s, model top, range 10.69–11.37 | No single value; units and location not written in file, range 10.73–11.11 (6 files) | Adopt case-by-case values; "m/s, at building top height H" treated only as inference (field name Uh), not written as "stated in text" |
| α | 1/4, 1/6; 2:1 series only 1/4 | Official website "Alpha parameter determining the exposure factor 1/4 1/6"; wind profile PDF figure caption | Same | Same | Adopted |
Easily confused items (pointed out by both): non-conventional tall building database PRS_Unconfig (1/1000, 11.8 m/s, α 0.15/0.27); downstream papers converting to 1:478 based on target building. Disagreement lies only in the definition of "top wind speed": E claimed nominal value and location as certain, F was more rigorous——defer to F.
Comparison with TPU experiment script: script uses only Cp, geometric ratios, and α; α matches official website, independent of the rest, no discrepancies.

## Local Full-text Search Corroboration ( pages, 10-13 20:00 index)
- Ong et al. 2020 (Zotero WM3IXNTT, PDF p. 4): "performed on a scaled model with cube height equal to 0.1 m and assuming a scaling coefficient ... equal to 1/400 ... The reference velocity was equal to 11.0 m/s and the sampling rate was equal to 1000 Hz." (Description of TPU low-rise/cube database, same wind tunnel as tall building database, serves as corroboration)
- Building and Environment 2025, 113590 (Zotero ER29ZKGI, PDF p. 2): TPU isolated tall building D/B=1, H/D=5, "geometric scale of Γ = 1/400".

items.text:
# Lab Track Batch Routine Tasks Switched to Gemini Batch Channel (One-week trial, 10-13 to 10-20)

Decision maker: Lab Lead (Root). Basis: In-house large language model sub-project evaluation (: 200-question abstract preliminary screening Gemini 3.8 Flash 85.5% / Claude Sonnet 80.5% / local Qwen3-32B 82.0%; 50-question PDF single-value extraction 96/96/92%) and Platform Lead reply (default to in-subscription, local vLLM not default). No literature basis, based on track-internal data.

- **What to do**: In each sub-project of the Lab, for routine pure Q&A tasks with fixed question banks that can be batched (abstract preliminary screening, literature single-value extraction, table field extraction, preliminary label judgment), default to using ` Liang Hu decided.
- **Re-check**: Randomly sample 10% of each batch for re-check by Claude (Lead or ideas), recording the agreement rate; task types with an agreement rate <90% revert to the original method.
- **Not applicable**: Tasks requiring tools, reading repositories, running code, scientific judgment, or submission for review.
- **Why**: In the evaluation, Flash performed on par with Claude on these two types of tasks, and it uses the subscription without consuming Claude quota. **Cost of being wrong**: Any errors or omissions within the week are caught by the 10% re-check; worst case is a certain batch of routine tasks needs to be redone.
- 10-20 Retrospective: Agreement rate across sub-projects and saved workload to decide whether to continue or revoke.

## Postscript 10-13 Evening
- The batch run of 350 questions for lab-llm_eval-r2 on this track exhausted the Gemini pool's 5-hour quota, crowding out reviewer E. The platform has added yielding rules (automatically pause when 5-hour remaining <30%, stop the entire batch when weekly remaining <20%).
- Additional constraints for this track: single batch ≤100 questions; do not start batches while a review is running; do not use `--force` (if truly needed, to be decided by Root Lead with a written note). Cost of being wrong: batch routine tasks will be slightly slower.

## Mid-term Inspection 10-15 07:1x (Root Lead Safety Net Follow-up)
- During the trial period, the only one that actually used `` was I (Damage–Wind Speed Database): 5 batches of 100/100/100/40/70 = 410 questions, all gemini-3.8-flash-high, no `--force`, single batch ≤100; all status=ok.
- 10% independent re-check: Batch 1 severity 9/10; Batch 2 structural category and wind speed category each 9/10, remainder 10/10; Batch 3 structural category, severity, damage excerpt, and wind speed source each 9/10; Batch 4 (40 items) sampled 4 items: structural category 3/4=75% (<90%, according to rules, stop treating this field as passed, do not expand sample), remainder 4/4; hard samples 70 items manual gold standard: source 66/70=94.3%.
- Other sub-projects (ftkb, LUW, A1, etc.) had no fixed question bank routine tasks emerge, not used; the 350+100 questions of llm_eval were pre-trial evaluations on 10-13, not counted (the batch of 350 questions triggered the yielding rule).
- The three constraints added on the evening of 10-13 (single batch ≤100, do not start batches while a review is running, do not use --force): the first and last can be verified from the answer files, while "do not start batches while a review is running" has no logs to verify.
- Node I was migrated to AI Weather Models on 10-15; the Lab itself currently has no tasks using this channel. Continuation/removal on 10-20 to be decided according to this page; if retained, rules will be synchronized for reference.

reviews.label: Review verdict
reviews.title: Verdict: judgement table on uses of self-built models and the TPU minimal experiment (3/3 valid: Gemini, GPT-6, GLM; 10-13)
reviews.text:
# Verdict: In-House Model Utility Assessment Table and TPU Minimal Experiment (3/3 valid: Gemini, GPT-6, GLM; 10-13)

All three offered "reserved support": the taxonomy and recommendation direction hold; the TPU leave-one-building-out vs. interpolation direction is correct; collectively pointed out calibration/criterion errors and gaps in experimental protocols. Personally verified: 2T26I5GW card p.12 §4.1 (76,480 is the parent set, 5-fold internal CV); Han 2026 card (physical LBM-LES solver vs. observational Kriging, not ML); FV7BN78P card line 35 (local small-to-medium models are unstable on OpenFOAM configurations).

## Must Change (Changed)
1. **ASOS numbers** (unanimous among all three): Changed to "40–75 kt parent set 76,480 events, ASOS internal 5-fold CV (approx. 15,296 per fold), acc 86.7%/F1 87.8% (PDF p.12 §4.1 Fig.10), not an independent validation".
2. **Narrow the scope of experimental conclusions** (A, D): The TPU experiment only rules on "geometry generalization surrogate for rectangular isolated tall building mean/rms Cp", not the entirety of 2a; multi-fidelity RANS→LES correction and urban wind field surrogates are accounted for separately.
3. **Complete the holdout protocol** (all three): Leave-one-geometry-out (LOGO), distinguish interior/boundary buildings in parameter space, held-out buildings do not participate in hyperparameter tuning/preprocessing; exposure condition as a dimension; pressure taps aligned by normalized coordinates on each face; pre-specify "significantly better than" criteria; remove U-Net, use point-level regression for models (GBM + MLP + GP); remove peak Cp in the first round, state conclusions only for mean/rms. Sent to ideas as a task brief addendum.
4. **Usage of Han 2026** (E, D): Changed to a baseline caveat that "simple baselines can beat complex models" (physical LBM-LES vs. observational Kriging, mean horizontal wind, six-station network not completely independent), not as evidence for ML surrogates.
5. **Attribution of Taira** (D): Changed to "evaluation recommendation drawn from card ", not written as a stipulation of the original paper.
6. **Category 1 basis** (E, A): Delete "only counterexample"; add FV7BN78P (local small-to-medium models frequently fail on complex OpenFOAM configurations) and 5ZE3U2A8 (same team pivoted to MCP + multi-agent); VNP48R7H itself is a paper advocating fine-tuning effectiveness (card first_pass). Recommendation level remains Low, basis changed to "no evidence showing local fine-tuned models outperform frontier models + retrieval", rather than "proven to have no incremental value".
7. **Category 2b basis** (E, A): Delete ArchesWeather card (climate scale, irrelevant); ERA5 rephrased as "reanalysis reference" instead of ground truth; add precedent clues: Pangu forecasts driving WRF 12/3 km (Xu et al. 2024, ERL, DOI 10.1088/1748-9326/ad41f0), WoFSCast regional convection-allowing surrogate (GRL 2024, 10.1029/2024GL112383)—all provided by reviewers, not yet archived, pending litwiki card additions; recommendation level maintained at Low-Medium, single-event CAPE comparison experiment cancelled (E: no new information).

## For Reference Only
- The approx. 46% of NF6S3H9N is a budget framing of "10 LF + 5 HF vs 10 HF", while the paper actually ran all HF (A, D)—noted in the table.
- 9CBNZGZB transfer learning can raise 0° rms R² to 0.53 (A, D)—noted.
- Low-rise near-field precedent WindMiL (arXiv 2511.01226), Sci Rep low-rise LOSO (provided by D, unverified)—added to candidate literature.
- Category 1: In the NBCC building code Q&A fine-tuning + retrieval study, GPT-4o baseline still leads in metrics (provided by A, unverified); building code Q&A should use retrieval rather than fine-tuning (E, no specific citation).
- CU framing unified to "estimated ≤2, hard cap 10" (D).

## Unadopted Objections
- E flaw B "Tree models are mathematically mismatched with sparse geometry and should be discarded": Not discarded; retain GBM as one of the benchmarks and add MLP and GP; the first round asks precisely "whether off-the-shelf common methods beat interpolation on this type of data." A tree model losing is itself useful information, but conclusions are written separately by method rather than rejecting across the board based on a single model.
- E "Must specify H/B=3": Changed to leave-one-building-out with separate reporting for interior/boundary, which is more robust than holding out just one building (adopting D's proposal).
- No need to escalate to Liang Hu: All items are framing corrections and experimental designs, not changing direction.
