reviews.title: Verdict: Deep Research verification and judgement-table revision (3/3 valid: Gemini, GPT-6, GLM; GLM had queued for a slot; 10-13)
reviews.text:
# 裁决：Deep Research 核对与判断表修订（3/3 有效：Gemini、GPT-6、GLM；GLM 曾排队等名额；10-13）

三位均"有保留地支持"："已核先例不推翻 TPU 结论"成立；1 低、2a 内插低、2b 低-中、3 中可维持；2a′ 统一升"中"不成立。亲核：arXiv 2508.03183 摘要页（v2 2025-12-07 摘要含 SR=4、3.75 泛化测试）；arXiv 2609.38977 摘要页（Qin, Zhao, Li, Wang, Xiao，2026-09-30；Montreal 500×150×500，一步 NMSE 比基线低 65.8%）；FoamGPT ML4PS 2025 PDF（Table 1：Qwen3-8B 0→26.36%，GPT-4.1-mini 35.45→39.09%，评估关闭自动纠错）； 分组表。

## 必须改（已改）
1. **DeepUFNet**（E、D；A 读的是 v1 正文）：撤回"未能核实"。v2 摘要含 SR=4、3.75 泛化测试。不作 TPU 冲突证据的理由改为：它是同类二维柱上**由稀疏测点时程重建/推进全场壁面风压**，基线是其他网络，不是无测点的参数化几何预测，也没和插值比。
2. **ScaleSplit-NO**（三位）：撤回"查无"。出处 Qin et al. arXiv 2609.38977（DR 把作者写成 Rahman）；采用"Montreal 城市风场一步 NMSE 比基线低 65.8%"。显存 27.1→2.8 GiB、基线为 U-Net、完整训练 9.7/25.5 h 来自审稿人 A 读的正文 §4.1、附录 B.8、D.4，本人只核到摘要，标"审稿人核，未亲核"。370× 仍单列为另一篇（Building Simulation 10.1007/s12273-025-1392-x，**推理**单帧，未亲核）。
3. **TPU 统计口径**（A）：13.2%/27.3%、2/13 是全部 13 栋（含最近邻替代）；严格内部 5 栋：MLP mean RMSE 0.0618 vs B0 0.0412、rms 0.0251 vs 0.0185，ML 0/5 获胜。几何×暴露为 22 个组合，不是 13×2。结论限"固定 GBM/MLP、本协议、本基线"。
4. **FoamGPT**（A、D）：数字改为 ML4PS 2025 版 Table 1（Qwen3-8B 0→26.36%，GPT-4.1-mini 35.45→39.09%）；17.27→24.55 来自会议页面，版本不明，不用。不再写"检索胜过微调"（底座与流程都不同）；Foam-Agent 83.6% 口径不一（D：arXiv 2505.04997 为 88.2%），不用。类别 1 仍低，依据是"没有证据显示本地微调比前沿模型 + 检索 + 纠错流水线更好"。
5. **FNO 跨风向**（A）：补条件——西风训练直接预测北风有困难，旋转对齐后改善（arXiv 2501.05499 §5.2，审稿人 A 核）；跨显著不同城市形态有局限。
6. **2a′ 评级**（E、A）：删"唯一有先例且我们有算力"。拆成两行：轻量方向（库边界外推、稀疏测点重建、多保真校正）=**附条件候选**（先例存在，本组数据/算力未核）；3D 高分辨率城市风场代理=**算力受限暂缓**（ScaleSplit-NO 完整训练 9.7–25.5 h，远超 ≤10 CU）。NF6S3H9N 改述：比较对象含 LF LES、Kriging 多保真、NN 多保真，低保真是粗网格 LES 不是 RANS，只做单楼跨风向（审稿人 A 读原 PDF pp.10–11）。T111 只证明参数边界外推，不证明新几何类别。
7. **2b 措辞**（A）：负面结论限定于所评估的 0.25° 全球模型（Feldmann 2024）与 Pangu 约一天提前量龙卷环境（Hua 2025 GRL 10.1029/2024GL109611），不概括所有 AI 天气模型。
8. **TPU GAN 作者**（A、D）：Hu et al. 2020（卡片 QN6Z9F4B），非 Chen；"30% 训练预测 70%"是作者推断，原文为随机留 6 例最终验证 + 子集内 80/20，分母 2558/2658 不一致。

## 仅供参考
- 2T26I5GW 卡片状态 not_approved / requires_pi_review（D）——引用时带"卡片待审"；"5 折"见原 PDF p.12（A 读原文确认）。
- 2b 后报增量有限（E）——维持低-中。

## 未采纳的异议
- E"2a′ 应维持'待定'"：部分采纳——3D 城市风场暂缓；轻量方向写"附条件候选"而非"待定"，因为已有可核先例（NF6S3H9N、DeepUFNet、TPU T111）且试验成本可控，需要一个可排期的标签。
- 无需升级 Liang Hu。

reviews.label: Review verdict
reviews.title: Verdict: verification of the large-language-model review (3/3 valid: Gemini, GPT-6, GLM; 10-13)
reviews.text:
# Verdict: LLM Literature Review Verification (3/3 valid: Gemini, GPT-6, GLM; 10-13)

All three gave "reserved support": Continued pre-training "Low", local models for partial auxiliary tasks, gap requires empirical testing by our group—the direction holds; several verification records and overly broad statements must be revised. Personally verified: arXiv 2412.09560 v2 main text (§2.2, Figure 3: comparison of LLaMat with Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini-1.5-Pro, GPT-4o); PMC12657656 (Res Synth Methods 2025); CivilGPT (Journal of Tongji University 2025, 53(6):831–840, DOI 10.11908/j.issn.0253-374x.24358).

## Must Revise (Revised)
1. **LLaMat** (all three): Withdraw "Do not adopt". v2 §2.2 / Figure 3: For text extraction, LLaMat outperforms tested frontier models; for table extraction, it is only slightly superior, and commercial models are often comparable or even better, with advantages mainly in regex tables. Adopt as **author self-report on self-built materials benchmark**, model trained via 30B-token-level continued pre-training + instruction fine-tuning + downstream task fine-tuning; do not extrapolate to arbitrary PDF number extraction, do not treat as a fair comparison with "frontier models + retrieval". Journal version (NMI) not personally verified, do not cite.
2. **MCP Structural Analysis Numbers** (A, D): Withdraw "<1.5% is true, pure LLM >400%". Figures within source are inconsistent: Journal (Buildings 15(17):3190) abstract gives <1.5% and >400%, but its Tables 7–9 report 2.756%/2.834%, pure GPT across cases ranges from 235–267% to >400%; data paper (Data 10(11):169) gives 230–270%. Retain only qualitative statement: "Pure LLM structural calculations are unreliable, significantly improved after connecting to solver", both are self-reports by a single research group (verified by reviewers A and D, tables in main text not personally verified).
3. **NL2FOAM 72B Comparison** (A, D): Restore to source claims—Dong et al. (VNP48R7H, arXiv 2504.09602) reports 88.7% vs Qwen2.5-72B 31.4% on their benchmark; 88.7% is solution accuracy defined by L2 error, not success rate; meshing still requires human intervention.
4. **Delete "Fine-tuning only useful for fixed formats"** (A): Ovadia only compared unsupervised fine-tuning vs RAG; Balaguer had supervised fine-tuning +6 pp. Change to "Knowledge injection prioritizes retrieval; supervised fine-tuning can yield gains on narrow annotated tasks, whether it is worthwhile depends on our group's empirical testing".
5. **Add CivilGPT for Precedents in Civil Engineering** (A): Tongji CivilGPT uses staged pre-training + fine-tuning + engineering alignment, Civil-Bench 14,823 objective questions + 269 subjective questions, compared against 15 models (authors' self-evaluation). Withdraw "No dedicated LLM seen in civil engineering"; still none seen in wind engineering; change "holds paper novelty" to "insufficient evidence".
6. **PDF <14% is a Misplaced Metric** (E, A): Originates from page-level retrieval recall in OpenFOAM documentation, not table/numerical extraction; does not contradict OCRBench. Add SciAssess (NAACL Findings 2025, Table 3: table extraction recall for both Llama3.1 and GPT-4o is 0.441, verified by reviewer A, not personally verified).
7. **Rewrite Screening Evidence** (A, D): Add PMC12657656—Llama 3.3 70B sensitivity 0.88 / specificity 0.93, GPT-4o 0.85 / 0.97, Gemini 1.5 Pro 0.94 / 0.85, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 0.94 / 0.80 (personally verified). PMC12873614 low precision includes GPT-4o mini, not unique to open source; ISPOR 96.3%/89.1% belongs to the entire workflow, not a single model. **"Local initial screening + frontier verification" cannot guarantee recall**: Items excluded locally will not be recovered by verification—local model recall must be measured independently in the evaluation.
8. **Split Ratings** (A): Offloading chores to local models will no longer have a unified "Medium–High" rating, but will be rated separately by task, determined by our group's empirical testing.
9. **Change Status of Verified Numbers** (E, D): AstroMLab 2 Table I: LLaMA-2-7B 51.3% vs AstroLLaMA-2-7B 43.5% (answer token prediction metric); 70B full instruction Q&A 64.7% vs 70.7% actually decreased (A); CPT ~32 / 2000 A100·h (8B/70B). OpenFOAMGPT (Pandey et al., arXiv 2501.06327) 1/6 without retrieval, 6/6 with retrieval, N=6 tutorial cases.

## For Reference Only
- OceanGPT "used by ARPA" suspected to be fabricated (E)—do not adopt.
- Colab cold start ~40 min must be included in throughput/cost (E)—evaluation records wall clock including preparation.
- PDF extraction recommendation "layout parser (Docling/MinerU) + model extraction + physical constraint validation" (E)—incorporated into Group B as a variant.
- OPENXRD: LLaMat-2-chat accuracy actually dropped to 16.13% after adding expert materials (A, third-party negative evaluation)—recorded.
- Screening study DOI 10.1017/rsm.2026.10093 (A).

## Objections Not Adopted
- E "Strongly recommend for local miscellaneous chores (Medium–High)": Unified rating not adopted (see Must Revise 8).
- No need to escalate to Liang Hu.

results.title: TPU isolated high-rise wind-pressure surrogate: whole-building hold-out minimal experiment
results.text:
# TPU Isolated Tall Building Wind Pressure Surrogate: Leave-One-Building-Out Minimal Experiment

Executed: 10-13 06:25 (US Eastern); official raw data only temporarily retained in Colab CPU session, not downloaded to  workstation; locally only scripts, statistical tables, figures, and logs are kept. Sources and terms of use see . Official website requires citation: TPU (Tokyo Polytechnic University) Aerodynamic Database, 2026, https://db.wind.arch.t-kougei.ac.jp/. The official website does not explicitly state an open license, so this is strictly an internal experiment without redistributing raw data.

## Scope and Split

Official isolated tall building cases: T113_4 (W:D:H=1:1:3, 300 taps), T213_4 (2:1:3, 360 taps), T313_4 (3:1:3, 320 taps), T212_4 (2:1:2, 240 taps), T214_4 (2:1:4, 450 taps). All belong to the same inflow family with alpha=1/4. For each building, five wind directions 0°, 10°, 20°, 30°, 40° are taken, totaling 25 wind direction–geometry cases and 8,350 tap–wind direction records; raw time series 32,768 frames per file at 1000 Hz. Total raw data 966,467,013 bytes, downloaded only temporarily in Colab. The full database includes more buildings/wind directions, not covered by this experiment.

Main experiment: Fully hold out 5 directions of T213_4 (1,800 tap records), train on 20 cases of the other four buildings (6,550 records); includes equal-height width neighbors on both sides and same-width different-height neighbors. For B0, under the same wind direction, first linearly interpolate by in-plane normalized position on each facade (nearest neighbor outside the convex hull), then use the widths of T113_4 and T313_4 for 1:1 linear interpolation; B1 uses a squared exponential Gaussian Process with fixed length scale and noise term (no hyperparameter tuning) after aligning taps across the four known geometries under the same wind direction; M is HistGradientBoostingRegressor, trained independently for 120 iterations per output. Face number, in-plane position, z/H, W/D, H/D, and wind direction sin/cos serve as model inputs. No pressure values from the target building enter training; geometry/tap coordinates serve as known inputs during prediction.

Auxiliary experiment: Repeating the run with  in the inner candidate directions 10°/20°/30°, the resulting six rows of metrics are completely identical to .

## Metrics

Each cell shows R² / RMSE (dimensionless Cp) in order. The peak column specifically refers to the point-by-point minimum Cp (negative peak) across the 32.768 s raw time series, not the Cook–Mayne design return period peak; tap counts differ across buildings, and the following are pooled metrics across all test points, not representing cross-building statistical significance.

| Holdout | Method | mean Cp R² / RMSE | rms Cp R² / RMSE | Minimum Cp R² / RMSE |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Full building T213_4 | B0 Geometric Linear | 0.9897 / 0.0555 | 0.9268 / 0.0246 | 0.8872 / 0.3778 |
| Full building T213_4 | B1 Fixed-Kernel GP | 0.9884 / 0.0591 | 0.9324 / 0.0237 | 0.9184 / 0.3213 |
| Full building T213_4 | M Gradient Boosting | 0.9930 / 0.0460 | 0.9344 / 0.0233 | 0.9255 / 0.3071 |
| Random holdout 20° | B0 Wind Direction Linear | 0.9842 / 0.0743 | 0.8915 / 0.0349 | 0.9130 / 0.3469 |
| Random holdout 20° | B1 Fixed-Kernel GP | 0.9963 / 0.0360 | 0.9352 / 0.0269 | 0.8875 / 0.3944 |
| Random holdout 20° | M Gradient Boosting | 0.9488 / 0.1339 | 0.6948 / 0.0585 | 0.8951 / 0.3807 |

Under full building holdout, M's RMSE relative to B0 decreases by 17.2% for mean, 5.4% for rms, and 18.7% for point-by-point negative peak; relative to B1 it decreases by 22.2%, 1.5%, and 4.4% respectively. Therefore, mean and time-series negative peak show small-to-moderate gains, while the most critical rms is nearly flat against GP; this does not support the broad assertion that "ML is significantly and generally superior to simple interpolation." When holding out wind directions at random, M significantly lags behind B0/B1 on both mean and rms, showing that easier splits cannot be automatically equated with optimiztic scores; tree models also interpolate continuous wind directions more weakly than explicit physical angle interpolation.

Figure : Comparison of measured/B0/M mean Cp under the same color scale for held-out building T213_4, 20°, nominal windward face 1; overall structures are close, with M showing localized plateau-like smoothing. This single figure is only illustrative; quantitative evaluation covers four surfaces and all five directions. "Nominal face 1" in the figure is based on the facade in the .mat Readme, and the actual aerodynamic windward state of this facade at 20° should not be generalized to other wind directions.

Literature background but not directly comparable: , PDF p.10 Fig.9 random split of interfering buildings in the same database has high mean/rms R², not new geometry; PDF pp.15–17 single-building CFD angle extrapolation rms R² 0.1291/0.2608, not identical conditions to this TPU run. This run involves only one building held out within the interpolation interval, single roughness, five wind directions, and fixed hyperparameters; conclusions must not be extrapolated to general wind pressure surrogate reliability, design peak pressure accuracy, or number of experiments saved.

## Reproduction and Costs

 ran in Colab CPU environment (numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, matplotlib), pulled files one by one from the TPU official website and printed URLs, outputting  and figures;  is the random-seed wind direction recalculation, which needs to be uploaded to the same directory as , outputting . Data links and tap counts see local ; raw execution output see , . Colab usage was 1523.64 CU before launch, final 1523.63 CU (display precision 0.01 CU, actual billing may be delayed); well below 10 CU. Both CPU sessions `tpu-geometry-cp` and `tpu-seed0-cp` returned Session terminated, final `colab sessions`: No active sessions found on server; usage rate 0.00/hr, active assignments 0.

One-line verdict: Conditionally worthwhile to continue testing more leave-one-building-out cases, but on this single intermediate geometry, ML offers only a 1.5% RMSE gain for rms over GP, which is currently insufficient to establish "physical field surrogates" as a mature direction superior to interpolation.

# TPU Rectangular Isolated Tall Building Wind Pressure Surrogate: Scaled Experiment Following Protocol Addendum (10-13 07:18, US Eastern)

Note: This is an experiment with 13 official geometries, two available exposures, and only five wind directions per case: 0°/10°/20°/30°/40°, not all wind directions in the database. During leave-one-building-out, the five selected directions and all available exposures for that building are held out together; this does not meet the literal requirement of "all wind directions for that building," so the criteria below are merely an exploratory evaluation of this preselected wind direction subset and must not falsely claim completion of the full-database protocol. The official catalog lists 13 geometries and 22 geometry × exposure combinations; this run covers 110 cases totaling 37,200 tap–wind direction records, with raw .mat files totaling 4,290,004,812 bytes, all stored temporarily in Colab only. Targets per tap are strictly mean Cp and overall time-series standard deviation rms Cp, with no peak values.

Source and boundaries of use: TPU official https://db.wind.arch.t-kougei.ac.jp/aerodynamic/experiment/highrise/;  extracts citation requirements and copyright. Download raw time series from the official website; do not store or redistribute raw data. Script  and dependency  must be uploaded simultaneously to Colab, outputting ; complete raw execution log . Fixed hyperparameters, no tuning or normalization fitting on target buildings; MLP internal early stopping uses only training building samples.

Methodology: Pressure taps are aligned by face number, normalized observed range of horizontal coordinates on that face, and z/H; geometry uses D/B and H/B, along with angle sin/cos and exposure alpha. For B0, under the same exposure/wind direction, 2D linear interpolation is first performed across faces of training buildings (nearest neighbor outside in-plane convex hull), followed by geometric linear interpolation; when held-out geometry falls outside the convex hull of training geometries, B0 is strictly speaking inapplicable, and B0* in the table is a nearest-neighbor geometry substitute, not B0 extrapolation. B1 is a squared exponential kernel GP with fixed length scale = 1 and nugget = .03 in geometry space after alignment under the same conditions; GBM is 120-iteration fixed-parameter HistGradientBoosting, and MLP is a fixed 64×64 point-level network. All wind directions and exposures of the geometric target building are excluded from training.

results.text:
# TPU Rectangular Isolated High-Rise Cp Surrogate: All Downloadable Geometries and Wind Directions from the Official Website (10-13 08:13, ET)

Problem scope: For an unseen geometry, whether a fixed GBM / small MLP is significantly better than geometric interpolation for mean and rms Cp. Source is the TPU official website https://db.wind.arch.t-kougei.ac.jp/aerodynamic/experiment/highrise/, usage boundaries see existing 's manifest.

Method: Leave-one-building-out; both available exposures and all official angles for that building are held out simultaneously, and no Cp, pressure taps, or normalization statistics of the held-out building are used during training. Pressure taps on each face of each building are normalized by the actual spanwise tap range, and vertically by z/H; geometric inputs are D/B, H/B, plus face number, sin/cos wind direction, and α. B0: For each training building under the same exposure and wind direction, perform 2D linear interpolation within the face first (using nearest neighbor outside the tap convex hull), then perform 2D linear interpolation on geometry. If the training geometry convex hull for that wind direction/exposure does not contain the target, strict B0 is not applicable, and B0* in the table represents nearest-neighbor substitution in geometry; for certain buildings, only some wind directions or exposures are not applicable, so the whole-building results belong to a linear + nearest-neighbor mix. B1: Geometric GP under the same conditions, with fixed RBF length scale 1, nugget 0.03; GBM: 120 rounds per target, 19 leaves; MLP: 64×64, fixed hyperparameters, with random early stopping within training data. No tuning was done on test buildings. The script  depends on saved , ; raw logs, and the failed log from the first run caused by a 404 from mistakenly assuming the 55° square building existed is saved separately and not used as results. R² and RMSE are given for each building × exposure × method; the reported values below are RMSEs after pooling test records of each exposure by squared error.

Therefore, in this round there are 5 strictly interior buildings (T112, T113, T114, T213, T214), and 8 buildings where at least one condition requires nearest-neighbor substitution. T212, T215, T313, and T314 have linear B0 for the first exposure/wind direction, but other conditions are not all linear; whole-building B0* cannot be mistakenly called strict interpolation.

| Group, equal-weight per-building average RMSE | mean B0/B0* | B1 | GBM | MLP | rms B0/B0* | B1 | GBM | MLP |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5 Interior Buildings | 0.0412 | 0.0492 | 0.0794 | 0.0618 | 0.0185 | 0.0199 | 0.0373 | 0.0251 |
| 8 Boundary/Mixed Buildings | 0.1155 | 0.1152 | 0.1193 | 0.1214 | 0.0468 | 0.0475 | 0.0521 | 0.0585 |
| All 13 Buildings (B0* includes substitutions, not pure B0) | 0.0869 | 0.0898 | 0.1040 | 0.0984 | 0.0359 | 0.0369 | 0.0464 | 0.0457 |

According to predetermined criteria, the best ML method is selected post-hoc as MLP based on the mean across all buildings (not a model selection rule usable for the target building); relative to the baseline B0/B0* which has a better mean, mean RMSE increases by 13.2%, rms increases by 27.3%, and it outperforms that building's better baseline on only 2/13 buildings (even selecting per building post-hoc between GBM/MLP yields only 2/13), falling far short of "average reduction ≥20% and ≥2/3 buildings win". Strictly looking only at the 5 interior buildings where B0 is defined, MLP mean is 0.0618 vs B0 0.0412, rms is 0.0251 vs 0.0185, and ML is not superior on any of the 5 buildings. B0* in the boundary group is a nearest-neighbor surrogate, so it cannot be claimed that all 13 buildings represent a strict comparison of "ML vs B0 interpolation".

Random tap control: Randomly sample 20% taps in each geometry × exposure × angle case (seed 20261013; 25,248 test records), where B0 is in-plane interpolation B0_spatial for the same building, same angle, same exposure, rather than a cross-geometry baseline. mean R²/RMSE respectively: B0_spatial 0.9939/0.0428, GBM 0.9756/0.0854, MLP 0.9931/0.0455; rms respectively 0.9715/0.0156, 0.8650/0.0340, 0.9786/0.0135. With training taps already present in the same case, R² is optimiztic and cannot be equated with capability on new geometries.  is the comparison of measured/B0/GBM on the same color scale for T213, α=1/4, 20°, Face 1.

In the initial separate random wind direction hold-out (seed 0 sampled 20°, only five buildings and five directions), GBM significantly lost to interpolation: existing  records mean RMSE 0.1339 vs angle GP 0.0360, rms 0.0585 vs 0.0269. With taps of the same building at adjacent 10°/30° in the training set, continuous angle interpolation can exploit smoothness; tree models produce piecewise constant predictions on sin/cos encodings, making it difficult to smoothly interpolate unseen 20° in the same way, and training across five wind directions is very sparse. This is a plausible explanation of protocol/model inductive bias, not mechanistically ablated, and cannot prove overfitting; nor can it be extrapolated to the performance of leaving out all wind directions in this round.

Limitations: The TPU square building official website only provides 0–50°, asymmetrically covering angles; when test angles exceed 50°, there are no square buildings among training geometries under the same condition. Coordinates are normalized by the actual range of taps rather than the physical boundaries of the building. GP and ML hyperparameters are fixed, and MLP early stopping randomly splits training rows rather than grouping by training buildings; conclusions apply only to this set of fixed, lightweight point-level models and defined B0/B1, and do not represent all ML. Literature background card  PDF p.10 Fig.9 uses a different split;  PDF pp.15–17 is for wind direction extrapolation; neither can be directly compared horizontally with the values from this leave-one-building-out round.

Colab CPU session `tpu-all-angles-r2` has been stopped; after stopping, `colab sessions` only shows the `luw-aij` A100 session from another task, which is not this experiment, and the account balance change cannot be entirely attributed to this experiment. The CPU display rate is approximately 0.08 CU/h, actual script time was 2840.8 s, estimated at about 0.063 CU according to the rate; balance before launch was 1523.59, and 1523.11 CU after stopping, but another A100 session was running during that period, so the account difference of 0.48 CU cannot be attributed to this experiment. The estimate is well below the 10 CU cap.

Conclusion: Across all 13 geometries and all their downloadable wind directions listed on the official website, fixed GBM/MLP did not beat simple interpolation under the same conditions for mean/rms Cp on new geometries; interpolation won on all strictly interior five buildings. This conclusion applies only to these two statistics, this protocol, and models for rectangular isolated high-rise buildings.

# Local Open-Source LLMs and Claude: 100-Question Chores Benchmark (10-13)

## Scope of Conclusions and Protocol

Same 100-question benchmark set: A Literature screening 40 (positive 10 / negative 30), B Paper PDF single-page number extraction 25, C NOAA event description classification 20, D Candidate calculator regression ratios 15. Experimental figures are all internal track data, not scientific conclusions of papers/codes. The two local models used vLLM on Colab A100 40 GB, temperature=0, single-question JSON, batch of 10 questions; Claude Sonnet was invoked single-question via local `claude -p --model sonnet --tools ''` with concurrency 5. For B, all models were given identical `pdftotext -layout` raw PDF physical page text, with Docling Markdown page text additionally used as a local model variant (parser replaced only). Gemini CLI OAuth, literature does not substitute for this experiment.

The initial version of D13–15 did not provide locked-value files but required reciting numbers from memory; upon discovery, they were changed to ratio questions with complete given inputs (eval_set_v2); the initial version of C's example JSON placed the four options in a single string, which 30B copied verbatim leading to 0/20; upon discovery, options and single output were separated, and all participating models re-answered C (eval_set_v3). The initial version and responses are all retained; the table below only adopts retest results with identical v3 questions/prompts. Execution sequence also deviated: although the benchmark set had 100 questions generated and verified before the first round of calls, it was not reported back to the client separately before launching as required by the statement of work. Prompt changes occurred after seeing first-round outputs and cannot be regarded as a strict blind test; this simultaneously demonstrates format robustness issues. All positive example titles in A contain topical keywords, resulting in full marks for keyword rules; this is a low-difficulty benchmark that does not exert real recall pressure.

## Group Results

Quality scoring: A recall, precision; B numerical relative error ≤1% and equivalent units; C accuracy; D numerical relative error ≤1%. No cross-group overall rating. The token column reflects input + output reported by models; Claude CLI counts include large amounts of system/cache tokens, differing in accounting standard from vLLM single-question tokens. USD reflects only the list price from Claude CLI's `total_cost_usd`; local uses shared GPU CUs, which do not convert directly to subscription USD. Wall clock: Claude's initial-round single-group actual concurrency window is shown in the table; revised C/D required additional calls; for local models, because cold starts and downloads were shared across the entire run, only full-run empirical times are available (8B 163.53 s, 30B 260.71 s), without fabricating independent cold-start durations per group.

| Group | Method | Quality | A Recall/Precision | Input+Output Tokens | Claude USD | Claude Initial Round Group Wall Clock |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| B | Claude Sonnet / pdftotext | 24/25 | — | 1,027,608 | 1.369 | 22.2 s |

Docling variant tokens: [已隐去] 28,652 input / 319 output, 30B 28,552 input / 321 output; already summed in the table above. The full Docling workflow for B required CPU installation and preprocessing, while the model batch generation itself took 2.24 s for 8B and 1.92 s for 30B; one cannot simply report generation time as the PDF pipeline wall clock. The list price for Claude's final 100 valid responses entered into the table totaled 5.010 USD; the experiment actually invoked the initial 100 items and two revisions totaling 23 items, with the CLI `total_cost_usd` summing to 6.203 USD. Per-thousand-question cost by group was A 48.50, B 54.77, C 48.65, D 48.50 USD, representing linear extrapolation group-by-group from final valid samples without amortizing revision trial-and-error (CLI has substantial cache/system overhead, affected by plan tier and concurrency). Local total duration was 3293 s, estimated at 4.848 CU, including preparation, post-failure repairs, and waiting; 296 local question inferences amortized to ~16.38 CU/thousand calls, which cannot serve as a steady-state model unit price. Account balance difference includes other sessions, see cu_record.md for details.

## Whether Each Group Is Eligible for Offloading

A: Both local models satisfy their own recall ≥95% and precision ≥70% of Claude's (8B 100/100, 30B 100/90.9). Formally, they are eligible for offloading initial screening on this small sample, but keyword rules also achieved 40/40 and positive titles directly reveal topics; practically, it is recommended to use rules first, and one cannot claim based on this that screening in real databases reaches ≥95% recall or leave records excluded by local models unreviewed.

B: 30B matches Claude at 24/25, reaching the 90% quality threshold of the frontier; 8B scored 22/25. The Docling variant did not improve 30B (23/25), while preprocessing increased complexity instead. It can be trialed as a candidate for "extracting a single number from a given page", but erroneous values/units still require verification against source pages and programmatic checks; since no simple baseline was established for B in this task, the strict condition of "significantly outperforming simple baselines" cannot be determined, and no unconditional offloading conclusion is given. For card quantitative anchor sources and PDF pages, see and `cardpage` in JSONL.

C: Best local 12/20=60%, Claude 15/20=75%, only 80% of Claude (below predefined 90%); although higher than keywords' 8/20, it still does not satisfy "eligible for offloading". Categories themselves may not be uniquely determinable from short narratives; label ambiguity must be resolved first, and automated independent classification is not recommended.

D: 30B 15/15, Claude 14/15, quality reaches the comparison threshold; but these are merely ratios of two given numbers, not the full ASCE 7-22 gust effect factor workflow, nor comprehensive Q&A for WRF/OpenFOAM configurations. Deterministic calculators should be a strong baseline on such tasks and avoid LLM arithmetic errors; lacking empirical simple baseline testing and real configuration questions, Group D as a whole cannot be officially judged "eligible for offloading". It is more reasonable to use local models for text localization and interpretation while leaving numbers to existing calculators.

## Limitations and Reproducibility

A title word leakage yielded full marks for rules; B's 25 questions concentrated on 7 published papers with relatively explicit numbers/units, and graphical numbers outside source pages were not tested; C's 20 single-year NOAA event descriptions and original EVENT_TYPE do not necessarily uniquely determine each other; D only had ratio arithmetic and did not cover real code calculations/configurations. Small-sample single-run temperature 0 has no confidence intervals. Docling CPU initial round suffered from incomplete installation and midway process `Cannot allocate memory`, and was later split into paper-by-paper conversion; failure logs and final successful files are all retained. vLLM first round had v0.13/Torch cu13 ABI mismatch, repaired to Torch 2.9.0+cu128 before running; all these preparation times were counted into CUs. No fine-tuning. Colab session has stopped; final sessions only showed others' sessions.

Reproduction: (original candidates), (original 100 questions), formed the final ; , . Raw responses are in , , and various revision files; is the scoring summary; is the raw CLI run history. Paper PDFs/Zotero, NCEI official archive, and design load regression JSONs are all read-only. No unpublished manuscripts copied or tokens saved.

# Gemini Supplementary Benchmark: Frozen v3 100-Question Set (In-Line Data)

Following delivery of the batch runner, we ran the supplementary benchmark on the `gemini-3.8-flash-high` subscription tier — **note that this is neither Gemini 2.5 Pro nor a bare API model without wrapper prompts**. Questions were drawn from the frozen v3 set, passing only the exact `id` and `prompt` fields without ground-truth answers, source metadata, or custom system prompts. After verifying the payload on Question 1 via `--dry-run`, the batch was executed at concurrency 3 with tools disabled and each question isolated. The first invocation hit the ~420 s client timeout after writing 94 responses to disk; rerunning the command resumed and completed only the remaining 6 items. All 100 unique IDs succeeded (`ok`) with a single attempt each. Raw outputs were saved and scored with the exact same per-question grading script used for the earlier models.

| Group | Gemini Score | Claude Sonnet | Best Local Model | Simple Rule | Gemini Input / Output Tokens | Sum of Per-Item Latencies |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A Literature Screening | 38/40; recall 90%, precision 90% | 40/40 | 8B: 40/40 | 40/40 | 479,665 / 20,748 | 207.84 s |
| B Numeric Extraction from PDF Page Text | 20/25 | 24/25 | 30B: 24/25 | Untested | 330,317 / 162,879 | 599.27 s |
| C NOAA Narrative Classification | 20/20 | 15/20 | 30B: 12/20 | 8/20 | 224,073 / 13,398 | 156.27 s |
| D Ratio of Given Numbers | 15/15 | 14/15 | 30B: 15/15 | Untested | 163,529 / 127,884 | 383.72 s |

In Group A, Gemini made one false negative (`A10`) and one false positive (`A13`), falling short of the pre-specified ≥95% screening recall threshold on its own; while the local 8B model formally hit 40/40, the simple keyword rule also scored 40/40, so true recall on harder borderline abstracts remains to be tested. In Group B, Gemini's five misses (`B08`, `B10`, `B11`, `B12`, `B14`) all extracted the exact right number but omitted units or violated the strict unit format rule (e.g., `B08` wrote `h` instead of `CPU h`); per the pre-specified "exact number + equivalent unit" rule, these are not re-graded. While the local 30B model matched Claude at 24/25 on B, no simple regex baseline was tested on B, so unconditional handover is not claimed. In Group C, Gemini scored 20/20 vs Claude's 15/20, whereas the best local model scored 12/20 (below the 90% frontier threshold) and cannot take over standalone classification; small sample size and inherent ambiguity between narrative descriptions and event types remain. In Group D, local 30B tied Gemini at 15/15, but the items only compute ratios of given numbers without testing a deterministic calculator baseline, which cannot be extrapolated to complex standard/configuration tasks. No cross-group composite score is computed.

Across the 100 subscription calls, reported token usage totaled 1,197,584 input tokens and 324,909 output tokens (including 324,047 thinking tokens), for 1,522,493 tokens total; roughly 12k input tokens per item come from fixed platform agent-wrapper overhead, so these figures must not be compared directly against bare vLLM inference tokens or Claude CLI tokens. Completion timestamps spanned 10-13 12:24:21 to 12:32:54 EDT (513 s); this is the span between first and last completion and **excludes pre-first-completion startup time, so it is not an exact end-to-end wall clock**. The sum of individual item latencies was 1,347.10 s (run at concurrency 3, not wall-clock time). Linearly scaling this batch gives ~15,224,930 tokens per 1,000 subscription calls as a rough capacity order of magnitude; because the subscription tier has no per-call USD billing, no fabricated dollar cost is entered, and 0 Colab CU was used. Given the distinct billing models across subscription, Claude CLI, and local inference, no strict cost-efficiency ranking is drawn. Group B passed the exact same `pdftotext -layout` plain text used for the other models rather than raw PDF binaries; the Docling variant was tested only on local models.

Comparison caveats: `v3` revised the C and D prompts after inspecting v1/v2 model outputs, so the benchmark as a whole is not a strictly blind test, and Gemini was added after that prompt revision. The Gemini batch runner injects a "do not call tools" agent-framework prompt, just as Claude CLI injects its own system prompt; we guarantee identical user-level prompts across models without claiming identical underlying system prompts. The original evaluation report is left unmodified, and this document serves as an appended supplementary record.

A2: Both local models achieved individual recall of 100% and 98%, with precision of 46.3% and 58.3%, both exceeding 70% of frontier-best Gemini's precision of 63.6% (44.5%), formally "eligible for offloading" based on predefined point estimates. In practice, prioritize 32B: offers an increment over keyword precision of 43.5%, but its recall of 49/50 has a Wilson lower bound of 89.5%, which cannot guarantee real-world recall ≥95%; manual review should be conducted when excluding papers. Obscuring neighbor titles in negative examples left keyword accuracy at only 67.5%, but labels represent this round's manual interpretation (not author ground truth), and boundary disputes may still persist for some papers mixing wind fields and loads. Has not reached the validation level where literature can be discarded without supervision.

B2: Local best 46/50=92%, which is 95.8% of the frontier's 48/50, satisfying the 90% quality line. The keyword numerical extraction baseline for B2 is non-definable/untested, and the condition of "significantly outperforming simple baselines" cannot be evaluated, so unconditional offloading cannot be declared under full criteria; it can only serve as a candidate for initial extraction on given pages, with programmatic/manual verification against original PDF pages. In the 22 table questions, two-column PDF text and units were error-prone; 25 historical questions from the first round were sampled again, resulting in weak independence this round and overly optimiztic confidence intervals. Did not validate automatic whole-paper page finding or OCR of figures.

C2: Local best 30B was 98/100, higher than Claude's 95/100 and reaching the 90% threshold of Gemini's 100/100; but pre-screening explicitly required positive examples to have convective keywords and negative examples to have non-convective keywords, and simple rules already achieved 100/100. Because it did not significantly outperform rules, the predefined "eligible for offloading" criterion does not hold; this group only demonstrates that rules suffice when explicit causal clues exist, and cannot be used to claim that local models strongly understand ambiguous events. Only narratives were given, with types following official EVENT_TYPE; archival discrepancies may exist between non-convective keywords and original labels.

Experimental scripts , ; raw answers , ; raw logs , . Literature evidence relies solely on per-question `card`, `page`, and original PDF pages, not to be used to draw scientific literature conclusions; all numbers in this experiment are internal track data.

# Second Round Frozen Labels and Sources (Pre-dataset Review)

Dataset: eval_set_r2.jsonl; SHA-256 `673e8e22fcab613e40ee14b39416126f6bac9897318a084b514f0fc008c8fecb`; A2=200 (positive 50 / negative 150), B2=50 (15 PDFs, of which 22 questions are tables), C2=100 (Thunderstorm Wind 50, High Wind 30, Strong Wind 20). Title, label, and source fields are not given to models; only prompt is sent. All models receive identical prompt text, with no question modifications after running; if problematic questions are found, they are only excluded while retaining raw outputs.

A2: Public paper Zotero metadata abstracts linked to Zotero keys in LitWiki cards; positive examples prioritize cfd_m4_downburst_cfd/paper_cards and windfield_step2/papers, negative examples are neighboring cards such as general CWE, WRF, EVA, accelerated wind tunnels, structural response, etc.; deduplicated by Zotero key (DOIs not verified paper-by-paper). Initial screening based on title and abstract keywords, manual inspection of candidate titles, sample inspection of abstracts, and explicit wind field research negative examples as well as load/response/review positive examples excluded; 200 abstracts were not independently manually verified paper-by-paper; after freezing, spot-checked 10 questions (A2_158, 108, 042, 142, 186, 115, 162, 036, 145, 023) comparing question prompt abstract with label, and no obvious conflicts were found, though this check is not an independent full annotation. For specific excluded keys, see build_eval_r2.py. Labels represent screening judgments for this round; neighboring abstracts may contain ambiguity (must not be taken as ground truth). A2 simple subject-keyword baseline: 135/200, 67.5%, failing to reach the 95% upper limit. Absolute path and key of source cards recorded for each question.

B2: Continued using the 25 verified PDF page numerical values from 7 papers in Round 1; added 25 values from 8 new papers, with values and page numbers clearly stated in card Quantitative anchor ledgers; script build_pdf_r2.py simultaneously verified that the values exist on corresponding physical pages in original Zotero PDFs, and checked that Table numbers for 22 new table questions were within the page. Each question records card / PDF path / physical page / unit / table number. Questions only provide `pdftotext -layout` page text; numbers in figures that cannot be recovered from text were not selected. The initial 25 questions are not newly independent questions this round (models might have seen them in Round 1), and scores must note the limitation of mixing historical questions. Predefined scoring: identical or equivalent units and numerical relative error ≤1%.

C2: NCEI Storm Events official d2019/d2021/d2023/d2024 detail CSVs, with archive URLs and EVENT_ID recorded per question; only Thunderstorm Wind, High Wind, Strong Wind, stratified by state and year, descriptions 140–1400 words. Excluded prior to model runs: event narratives directly containing full event type phrases; descriptions stating only damage without causal hints; narratives where convective/non-convective causes appear simultaneously. Positive examples require convective causal clues in narratives, negative examples require non-convective meteorological causal clues; these pre-screening rules may create lexical shortcuts. Broad keyword rule baseline: 100/100; if scoring full marks, this group cannot test semantic model gains over rules, and it should be clearly noted that offload eligibility cannot be determined based on this. Field names are not in model prompts; narrative content remains as-is without masking weather phenomena in text. Original EVENT_TYPE is an administrative archive label, not an independent meteorological reassessment.

Criteria fixed prior to model runs: A2 local model recall ≥95% and precision ≥70% of frontier best precision; B2/C2 local best ≥90% of frontier best score and significantly outperforming keyword baseline (B2 lacks an applicable keyword numerical extraction baseline, must note this condition is non-determinable). Each group evaluated independently, 95% CI uses Wilson binomial interval; throughput includes cold start/download. D canceled.

# TPU Isolated Tall Building Database Parameters: Lead Self-Verification (10-13, platform test "check first" step 5; not included in judgment table)

Primary sources: Official website https://db.wind.arch.t-kougei.ac.jp/aerodynamic/experiment/highrise/; official .mat sample https://minio.wind.arch.t-kougei.ac.jp/web/media/case/T111_4/time_series_of_point_wind_pressure_0.mat (/tmp temporary, not retained after reading); wind profile PDF https://minio.wind.arch.t-kougei.ac.jp/web/media/type/highrise/condition_attaches/profile..pdf

| Parameter | Primary Source Observation | Excerpted Sentence from Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sampling frequency | 1000 Hz | .mat `Sample_frequency`=1000; Readme: "Wind_direction_angle,Sample_frequency and Sample_period are wind direction angle,sample frequency(hz)and sample period(second)" |
| Sampling duration / number of samples | 32.768 s / 32768 points (T111_4, 0°) | .mat `Sample_period`=32.768; `Wind_pressure_coefficients` size 32768×100; "All of the variables here are in model scale." |
| Top reference wind speed | 11.0017 m/s (T111_4, 0°; case-by-case field, other cases unverified) | .mat `Uh_AverageWindSpeed`='11.0017' |
| α | 1/4, 1/6 two categories | Official website: "Alpha parameter determining the exposure factor 1/4 1/6"; Wind profile PDF figure caption "Flow α=1/6", "Flow α=1/4" |
| Scale ratio | **Not stated** on official website, .mat Readme, or wind profile PDF | Model dimensions Building_breadth=0.1 m (T111, model scale); scale ratio source pending from E/F |

Our TPU script: uses only Cp (already non-dimensional), geometry D/B, H/B, and α=1/4, 1/6, independent of sampling frequency, duration, wind speed, and scale ratio; mean/rms uses full-length time series. α matches official website.

## Verification of E's (Gemini) Report (10-13)
- Scale ratio 1/400: Lead opened https://db.wind.arch.t-kougei.ac.jp/aerodynamic/case/T111_4/ and /T115_4/, original text "Model geometric parameters Breadth 100 Depth 100 Height 100 Model scale 1/400" (T115_4 has Height 500, also 1/400)——**Confirmed**.
- Uh for T115_4 0°: Lead downloaded official .mat, `Uh_AverageWindSpeed`='11.1438', 1000 Hz, 32.768 s, 32768×500——**Confirmed**.
- E's claim of "entire database 0° Uh range 10.6924–11.3737" not verified individually; 2:1 series only has α=1/4, consistent with what was observed in our experiment.
- Awaiting F's (Grok) report before merging table.

## E/F Merged Table (10-13, after Lead verification)
| Parameter | Value | Primary Source and Original Text | E | F | Adopted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Scale ratio | 1/400 | Official website case pages /aerodynamic/case/T111_4/, /T115_4/: "Model scale 1/400" | 1/400 | 1/400 | Adopted (Lead verified by opening page) |
| Sampling frequency | 1000 Hz | .mat `Sample_frequency`=1000; Readme "sample frequency(hz)" | 1000 | 1000 | Adopted |
| Duration / points | 32.768 s / 32768 (model scale) | .mat `Sample_period`=32.768, matrix 32768 rows; Readme "All of the variables here are in model scale." | Same | Same | Adopted |
| Top reference wind speed | Case-by-case field, ~10.7–11.4 (T111_4 0° 11.0017; T115_4 0° 11.1438) | .mat `Uh_AverageWindSpeed`; Readme defines neither unit nor location | Nominal 11 m/s, model top, range 10.69–11.37 | No single value; units and location not written in file, range 10.73–11.11 (6 files) | Adopt case-by-case values; "m/s, at building top height H" treated only as inference (field name Uh), not written as "stated in text" |
| α | 1/4, 1/6; 2:1 series only 1/4 | Official website "Alpha parameter determining the exposure factor 1/4 1/6"; wind profile PDF figure caption | Same | Same | Adopted |
Easily confused items (pointed out by both): non-conventional tall building database PRS_Unconfig (1/1000, 11.8 m/s, α 0.15/0.27); downstream papers converting to 1:478 based on target building. Disagreement lies only in the definition of "top wind speed": E claimed nominal value and location as certain, F was more rigorous——defer to F.
Comparison with TPU experiment script: script uses only Cp, geometric ratios, and α; α matches official website, independent of the rest, no discrepancies.

## Local Full-text Search Corroboration ( pages, 10-13 20:00 index)
- Ong et al. 2020 (Zotero WM3IXNTT, PDF p. 4): "performed on a scaled model with cube height equal to 0.1 m and assuming a scaling coefficient ... equal to 1/400 ... The reference velocity was equal to 11.0 m/s and the sampling rate was equal to 1000 Hz." (Description of TPU low-rise/cube database, same wind tunnel as tall building database, serves as corroboration)
- Building and Environment 2025, 113590 (Zotero ER29ZKGI, PDF p. 2): TPU isolated tall building D/B=1, H/D=5, "geometric scale of Γ = 1/400".

# Use Cases of In-House and Local Models for Our Research (Shelved)

This sub-project evaluated where self-trained or locally hosted models—spanning physical-field surrogates, local open-weight large language models (LLMs), and small embedding models—offer real value over classical baselines and frontier cloud APIs for wind engineering research. Through blind benchmarks and three-reviewer audits, the team established that machine learning surrogates fail to beat geometric interpolation on the TPU wind-tunnel database (winning 0/5 interior buildings) or linear transfer functions on Silsoe LBM inflow-to-pressure series, while domain-finetuned LLMs are unjustified because Gemini 3.8 Flash and local Qwen3-32B already reach 80.5–85.5% accuracy on abstract screening and 92–96% on PDF extraction. Before being Shelved, this conversation also incubated and spun off the standalone AI Weather and Climate Models for Wind Engineering project (12 sub-projects) and the Literature Figure Library and Sentence-Level Retrieval sub-project.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-13**: Sub-project launched by Lab Lead to evaluate four categories (domain-finetuned LLMs, physical-field surrogates, AI weather models coupled with WRF/CM1, and task-specific small models), querying six lines for data and dispatching a leave-one-building-out benchmark on the TPU high-rise database.
- **2026-10-13**: After a 3-reviewer audit (correcting the ASOS thunderstorm wind reference to 5-fold cross-validation on 76,480 records at 86.7% accuracy and setting a ge 20\% error-reduction gate across ge 2/3 of held-out buildings), full-direction tests on 13 TPU rectangular buildings showed ML had 13% higher mean-pressure error and 27% higher RMS error than interpolation, losing all 5 interior buildings (mean 0.062 vs. 0.041; RMS 0.025 vs. 0.019) and winning only on boundary extrapolation (T111 0.12 vs. 0.23).
- **2026-10-13**: A second 3-reviewer audit verified literature precedents (DeepUFNet partial-sensor reconstruction, ScaleSplit-NO urban flow stepping, and FoamGPT's 0% to 26% Qwen3-8B finetuning gain vs. 84% for retrieval-augmented pipelines), confirming no conflict with the TPU finding.
- **2026-10-13**: On the 642 s Silsoe cube LBM dataset (11 windward taps), after fixing a lag bug and excluding near-building probes, upstream probes at x le -10 m and -15 m gave linear FIR errors of 0.215 (r = 0.62) and 0.228 (r = 0.57), while temporal convolutional networks improved by le 1.3\% (<20% gate); correlation decayed from 0.67 at 7 m to 0.35 at 27 m (~30 m decay length), and adding z = 12 m probes gave no gain.
- **2026-10-13**: Surveying the CM1 line uncovered a legacy UrbanTALES pedestrian-wind surrogate directory (512 LES cases, >250 runs across 40 architectures reaching median R^2 approx 0.78text–0.79 vs. 0.72 for U-Net, without non-learning baselines); the physical surrogate branch was archived and Shelved as Liang Hu redirected the focus to LLMs and AI weather models.
- **2026-10-13**: After a 3-reviewer audit of two scientific LLM reviews, the research assistant ran a locked 350-question Round 2 benchmark (~2 compute units): on 200 hard abstract-screening items, local Qwen3-32B scored 82% (98% recall), Claude Sonnet 80.5% (100% recall), Gemini 3.8 Flash 85.5% (98% recall), and keyword rules 67.5%; on 50 PDF extractions, local scored 92% vs. 96% for Claude/Gemini; on 100 Storm Events wind labels, keyword rules and Gemini scored 100% vs. 95% for Claude and 91–98% for local.
- **2026-10-13**: Lab Lead ruled against building a custom LLM, routed batch screening/extraction to Gemini 3.8 Flash (with 10% Claude audit) while reserving local Qwen3-32B (~5.6 compute units per 1,000 items after a 40 min / 4-unit cold start) for confidential data, and opened an AI weather forecasting child sub-project.
- **2026-10-13**: The AI weather child sub-project tested Pangu-Weather and FuXi on three downburst events (Wister, Akron, ALTU) against ERA5 and persistence, finding wind shear and DCAPE beat persistence whereas CAPE errors limited joint skill to 12–24 h (failing all leads on ALTU), so direct global AI background forcing for hindcasts was Shelved.
- **2026-10-14**: Through a systematic review with Liang Hu across forecasting, climate, and CFD/data applications, Lab Lead formulated 12 sub-projects (A1–A3, B, C/G, E, F, H, I, J, K, and L/M), launched the first four (J, A1, L, C), and reorganized the tree under *AI Weather and Climate Models for Wind Engineering* (spun off on 2026-10-15).
- **2026-10-15**: Evaluating Jian Zhang's MiniLM retrieval materials (550,000 geoscience PDFs, 100 million sentences, and 3 million figures), Lab Lead showed the Lab's search already uses the same BGE/MiniLM architecture and the external package lacked layout or figure extraction code, then drafted frozen gates (ge 90\% figure–caption pairing on 50 samples and ge 14/20 top-5 hits) and spawned *Literature Figure Library and Sentence-Level Retrieval* across 17,167 PDFs.

## Where it stands

This sub-project remains Shelved after completing its evaluations of physical-field surrogates, local open-weight LLMs, and small embedding models. Routine batch screening and extraction now run on Gemini 3.8 Flash with 10% auditing (or local Qwen3-32B for confidential data), while the two major spin-offs—*AI Weather and Climate Models for Wind Engineering* and *Literature Figure Library and Sentence-Level Retrieval*—are actively advancing.

# Literature Figure Library and Sentence-Level Retrieval

## Objective
On top of the `ftkb` full-text library (Zotero 3,149 + EndNote 1,527 + Desktop 12,491 documents, ~600,000 pages), evaluate whether two capabilities are worth promoting into platform tools: (A) a figure library (extracting figures + captions across the entire corpus for caption-text and visual-semantic retrieval); and (B) whether sentence-level indexing + clustering is clearly superior to page-level retrieval. Deliver a one-sentence conclusion for each of A and B by 10-21. Task brief (approved by Liang Hu on 10-15).

## Current Status
10-17 13:0x: **A/B conclusions reached** (ahead of 10-21): A figure-caption retrieval is worth turning into a platform tool (96% pairing accuracy, English figure search 19/20; add a Chinese translation path and single-column crop fixes before productization); A2 image-to-image search will not be pursued (5/10); B sentence-level clustering will not be pursued (underperformed page-level retrieval on all three questions for structural reasons). B full-corpus encoding was stopped at 10-17 16:18 (172/469 shards; shards and logs retained). Handing A over to the platform for integration constitutes promotion, and Liang Hu has been asked. Conclusion.

## Settled Decisions
- 2026-10-15 Node established, gated on prerequisite platform update → 
- 2026-10-15 Restrict to preparation (scripts + trial run + frozen question bank) while prerequisite platform update is pending; figure-finding questions authored and frozen by Lead → 

## Settled Decisions (Continued)
- 2026-10-15 A1 v1 pairing accuracy below threshold; revise three rule categories and rerun → 

- 2026-10-15 Revised version passes pairing at 92%, fix 76% cropping completeness first, move both libraries to desktop processing → 

- 2026-10-15 Desktop read-only fault; pause A1 pending reboot → 

- 2026-10-15 Desktop not rebooted; detour by writing to the Windows drive → 

- 2026-10-16 Desktop rebooted and recovered with data intact; switch back to writing on root drive → 

- 2026-10-16 A1 preparation complete, waiting only on prerequisite platform update; ask Liang Hu whether to launch early → 

- 2026-10-16 Prerequisite platform update went live, A1 full run launched → 

- 2026-10-16 A1 decision: pairing 96% and English 19/20 passed, Chinese 12/20 failed; dispatched A2 → 

- 2026-10-17 A2 did not pass the bar; image-to-image search will not be pursued → 

- 2026-10-17 A/B conclusion: pursue A, do not pursue A2 or B → 

## Criteria (Pre-Specified in the Brief)
| Item | Criterion |
| --- | --- |
| A1 Caption Index | ≥90% pairing accuracy on 50 random figure–caption pairs; top-5 hit on ≥14/20 figure-finding questions |
| A2 Image Embeddings | Given 10 of our own simulation figures to find reference figures in the literature, top-5 contains a relevant figure on ≥6/10 queries (executed only if A1 passes) |
| B Sentence-Level + Clustering | Across 3 questions (climate-change wind-speed trend + 2 EVA questions), compare representative sentences + source tables per cluster against `pages` page-level results; Lead judges whether it is clearly better |

## Trials and Results
| Date | What Was Done | One-Line Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10-15 | EVA line provided 2 mixed-climate questions for B | Impact of separate vs. combined fitting on long-return-period design wind speeds; misclassification and missed-observation bias |
| 10-15 | A1 v1 trial run on 400 documents (`ideas`) + Lead judgment on 50 pairs | Pipeline works end-to-end; strict caption match 19/40, relaxed 35/40, 10 table titles, 7 false captions, 16 full-page crops; decoding failed on 120/400 |
| 10-17 | B sentence-level fast path on three questions (`ideas`) + Lead verdict | Clustering silhouette 0.07–0.11, representative sentences mostly reference entries; all three questions underperformed page-level top 10 |
| 10-17 | A2 image embeddings (`ideas`, CLIP ViT-B/32) + Lead verdict | 387k figures encoded in 2.3 h; top-5 across 10 queries: image-to-image 5/10, text-to-image 3/10, below the ≥6/10 bar |
| 10-16 | A1 full-scale evaluation (Lead) | 50-pair matching 48/50=96%, crop completeness 34/50; 20 queries top-5: English 19/20, Chinese 12/20 |
| 10-16 | A1 full-scale figure extraction (`ideas`, desktop 12 cores) | 17,167/17,167 items processed, 386,894 figures; 3,998 items had partial skipped figures, 0 whole-document failures; compact index 116 MB (<200 MB), thumbnails ~11 GB; caption vector encoding running |
| 10-16 | A1 post-reboot continuation (`ideas`) + Lead judgment on v3 20 pairs | All 4,676 PDFs staged; Zotero v3 rerun finished; 20-pair check scored 20/20 pairing and 18/20 (90%) cropping completeness |
| 10-15 | A1 pre-full-run preparation (`ideas`, v3) | v3 cropping rules implemented; Desktop 200 + EndNote 50 re-rendered; 2,314/4,676 PDFs staged across the two libraries; interrupted at 23:1x when desktop turned read-only |
| 10-15 | A1 revised rerun on 400 documents (`ideas`) + Lead judgment on new 50 pairs | Pairing 46/50=92% (passed); complete crop 38/50; 1 false caption, 0 table titles, 0 mid-run aborts across 400 documents; kind split: raster 36%/vector 22%/`page_region` 42% |
| 10-15 | Lead authored and froze 20 figure-finding questions | Covers downbursts, Cp, typhoon profiles, gust factors, spectra, bluff bodies, response control, extreme-value standards, etc. |

## Parameter Source Table
| Parameter | Value | Source or "Assumed" | Where Checked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Thumbnail size | Long edge ≤512 px JPEG | Assumed (sufficient to read plot types and axes while keeping storage manageable) | No literature basis |
| Caption block detection | Starts with Fig./Figure/Chinese "Tu" + number, not followed by predicate verbs like shows/gives, short block, adjacent to figure | Assumed (inductively refined from the 50-pair error analysis) | In-line trial runs |
| Full-corpus sentence count | ~15 million sentences | Task brief estimate (600,000 pages × ~25 sentences) | Pending empirical update from B |

## Open Items and Next Steps
- Prerequisite platform update go-live time → Lead follow-up check at 10-16 08:30; once live and desktop OCR is complete, notify `ideas` to launch full figure extraction (≤16 cores).

## Literature Basis
- Jian Zhang and Jia Shao, *Restructuring Higher Education Curricula, Textbooks, and Pedagogy with Small Language Models* (materials provided by Liang Hu): source of the sentence-level corpus + unsupervised clustering methodology and scripts; figure library retrieval originates from the accompanying slide deck (no code included in the package).

# Literature Figure Library and Sentence-Level Retrieval (Exploring)

This sub-project evaluates whether (A) a full-library figure and caption extraction and semantic retrieval system and (B) sentence-level indexing with clustering across the Lab's 17,167 wind engineering PDFs (~15 million sentences) outperform existing page-level search enough to be deployed as shared platform tools. Approved by Liang Hu on 2026-10-15, full-library extraction was staged behind ongoing desktop full-text ingestion and OCR tasks while the team froze blind evaluation benchmarks and executed a 400-PDF pilot. The initial pilot extracted 14,566 figure candidates (5,098 with captions) and demonstrated sub-second hybrid BM25 plus multilingual MiniLM search, but manual inspection of 50 random figure–caption pairs by Lab Lead yielded 47.5% strict and 87.5% lenient accuracy (below the 90% gate) due to rule-level caption and cropping errors. A revised 400-PDF pilot fixing these failure modes is currently underway before full-library extraction begins.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-15**: Lab Lead launched the sub-project following Liang Hu's approval to test two literature tools across all 17,167 PDFs (12,491 on the desktop library, 3,149 in Zotero, and 1,527 in EndNote): Part A (figure/caption extraction and semantic search) and Part B (sentence-level indexing and clustering vs. page-level search).
- **2026-10-15**: Lab Lead verified that the prerequisite full-text literature ingestion task was still running alongside 6-thread OCR on the desktop workstation, so full extraction was held back in favor of pipeline preparation and a 400-PDF pilot.
- **2026-10-15**: Lab Lead froze a blind benchmark of 20 figure-search queries covering downburst wind profiles, building pressure coefficient distributions, typhoon wind profiles, gust factors, wind turbulence spectra, bluff-body aerodynamics, structural control, and extreme value wind codes.
- **2026-10-15**: Lab Lead requested two mixed-climate extreme wind benchmark questions from the Extreme Value Analysis Lead to join a climate-change wind speed trend question for the Part B sentence-clustering evaluation.
- **2026-10-15**: Lab Lead dispatched the Part A1 400-PDF pilot to the research assistant—200 random PDFs from the desktop library (150 journal papers, 50 books) and 200 from Zotero/EndNote (150 and 50)—streaming thumbnail batches from the local workstation to desktop storage to avoid copying 4,676 raw PDFs.
- **2026-10-15**: The Extreme Value Analysis Lead delivered two mixed-climate benchmark questions—(B-2) separated versus pooled extreme value fitting of thunderstorm and non-thunderstorm winds for long-return-period design speeds, and (B-3) bias from mechanism misclassification or incomplete gust detection—which Lab Lead froze alongside (B-1) wind speed trends under climate change.
- **2026-10-15**: Lab Lead deferred dispatching Part B sentence encoding (~15 million sentences) until Part A1 full extraction starts and desktop OCR completes to avoid CPU contention.
- **2026-10-15**: The research assistant completed the first 400-PDF pilot (using PyMuPDF 1.28.2, Pillow 12.3.0, FastEmbed 0.9.0, ONNX Runtime 1.31.0, quantized multilingual MiniLM, and SQLite FTS5), extracting 14,566 thumbnails (36.415 figures/PDF); 5,098 (35.0%) had captions, while 2,488 captioned figures (48.8%) lacked embedded image bounding boxes (2,188 or 42.9% used vector or page-region fallback crops).
- **2026-10-15**: In the initial pilot, 120 of 400 PDFs stopped mid-document on pages with corrupted JPEGs or degenerate rectangles; extrapolating to all 17,167 PDFs projected ~17.63 single-process hours, ~19.34 GB of WebP thumbnails, and ~170.9 MB for the compact SQLite index (<200 MB limit).
- **2026-10-15**: The research assistant tested the `figsearch` prototype (FTS5 BM25 recall plus multilingual MiniLM reranking) on three self-created trial queries ("building wind pressure distribution", "downburst wind profile", "typhoon gust factor"); the first two returned relevant top hits, whereas the third ranked a typhoon fluctuation power-spectrum figure first.
- **2026-10-15**: Lab Lead manually audited all 50 random figure–caption pairs from the pilot: 19 clean pairs, 16 full-page crops containing the target figure plus other content, 12 mismatches (body sentences or list-of-figures entries treated as captions, or table captions paired with blank/text areas), and 3 table-caption-to-table pairs; excluding tables, strict accuracy was 47.5% and lenient accuracy was 87.5%, missing the 90% gate.
- **2026-10-15**: Lab Lead held back full extraction and dispatched a revised 400-PDF pilot to fix three rule-level errors (filtering body sentences like "Figure X shows…" and list-of-figures pages, excluding `kind=table` from figure search, and cropping the half-page above captions), skip corrupted pages without aborting documents, pre-compute MiniLM embeddings, and draw 50 new pairs (seed 20261016).

## Where it stands

This sub-project is Exploring. The Part A1 extraction and hybrid search prototype runs end-to-end and meets index size targets (~171 MB projected across 17,167 PDFs), but first-round figure–caption pairing accuracy (47.5% strict, 87.5% lenient) missed the 90% quality gate due to rule-level caption and cropping errors. A revised 400-PDF pilot is underway, and full-library extraction alongside Part B sentence indexing will proceed once desktop text ingestion and OCR finish and the new 50-pair audit reaches ge 90\% accuracy.

# L22.5 Kareem 教授论文收全与谈话纪要

# Redrawing the Graph-DeepONet Final Network Architecture Diagram with Scientific Plotting Skills

## Objective
Verify the repositories and licenses of 6 candidate Skills (AgentFigureGallery, Nature Skill, Academic Figure Skill, Origin Style Replot, figures4papers, K-Dense Scientific Visualization), select at most 2 (prioritizing those that output editable files) to test-draw the "final network architecture diagram" of the openclaw urban wind-field Graph-DeepONet project, and render a worth-using / drop verdict.

## How the Test Target Was Selected
Candidates: the 04-09 figure (UNet Speed Distillation Round 34, Global Best; boxes and connector lines overlap), checked against later final versions in the same directory: `UNet_7level_final.drawio` (04-15) and the project notes (recording the best model as HybridGraphCNN+FineGraph48+Fourier64, with no existing diagram). Which was chosen and why: both the round34 original figure (04-09) and `UNet_7level_final.drawio` (04-15) belong to a separate UNet reproduction track (`auto_v2`, Lu et al. 2025) and do not depict Graph-DeepONet. The optimal architecture of Graph-DeepONet exists only in text notes (04-02), where lines 35–36 specify a HybridGraphCNN + FineGraph48 + Fourier64 trunk; therefore a schematic was drawn from the text record, with any unrecorded layer counts or channel dimensions explicitly labeled "unrecorded" (original text verified by the Lead on 10-16). To test the specific question raised by Liang Hu—"can the overlaps in the original figure be fixed?"—a supplementary test was also run redrawing the round34 original figure.

## Current Status
10-16 03:20 Wrap-up: Worth using (with limitations), per the headline conclusion. Graph-DeepONet has no existing final architecture diagram, only text records; the schematic drawn from those records is labeled "not verified against code" and cannot be used as a final journal submission figure.

## Security Audit
See the audit report. Lead correction: `eval(parse(...))` at `compose.py:419` in Academic appears only inside a docstring usage example and is never executed anywhere in the repository (verified via `grep`), representing low risk and not grounds for disqualification.

## Trials and Results
| Date | Action Taken | One-Line Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10-16 | Supplementary test: redrew the round34 original figure with both Skills | Verified by Lead: title, subtitle, numbers across all 9 modules, 3 skip connections, and auxiliary head all match the original figure; all box-on-box overlaps and curve-through-box crossings in the original are eliminated; each SVG has 38 editable text elements and the PDFs have embedded fonts |
| 10-16 | Audited 6 repositories: 5 located, no matching repository found for Origin Style Replot; figures4papers is CC BY-NC | Selected Academic Figure Skill (Apache-2.0) and K-Dense `scientific-visualization` (MIT) |
| 10-16 | Drew Graph-DeepONet schematic from text records | Both figures are consistent in content, overlap-free, and have editable SVG text; the K-Dense version has excessive outer margins; all unrecorded parameters are explicitly labeled without fabricated numbers |

## Open Items and Next Steps
- Hand implementation recommendation to Platform Lead: equip the plotting bot (`figures`) only with the `scientific-visualization` subdirectory of K-Dense pinned to commit `a1043ef544`, without installing the full 177-skill repository; from Academic, take only the style reference documents under `references`. Delivery gate: item-by-item checklist against the original figure/notes + visual PNG inspection + editable SVG text.
- If a final submission figure for Graph-DeepONet is needed: first obtain the source code or configuration of the best model to verify the exact layer counts and channel dimensions.

items.text:
# Quick-Trial #12: Drawing a Recorded Graph-DeepONet Architecture Schematic with Two Scientific Plotting Skills

Time: 10-16 03:03 (ET). Data sources: local read-only record (2026-04-02) and candidate figure files; see repository links for external code sources. Public figures include only the abstract architecture and original record filenames/line numbers, omitting project paths, unpublished manuscript passages, or personal information. **This diagram is not a final network architecture verified against model code and is not intended as a final submission figure.**

## Verification of Six Repositories

GitHub REST API, repository metadata, and license endpoints were queried on 10-16; star counts reflect instantaneous values at query time. Mentioning a name in the source article does not equate to providing a direct repository link; the entries below represent verifiable identities, and repositories with identical or similar names must not be treated as the sole repository explicitly designated by the original post.

| Name in Article | Verifiable Repository / Status | Stars | Latest Commit (UTC) | Actual License / Usability |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| AgentFigureGallery | https://github.com/Dsadd4/AgentFigureGallery | 166 | 2026-09-05 02:17 | MIT; provides reference figure retrieval/installation wrappers, not specialized for network architecture diagramming |
| Nature Skill | https://github.com/Yuan1z0825/nature-skills | 48,590 | 2026-10-16 02:35 | Apache-2.0; multiple forks exist and must not be conflated |
| Academic Figure Skill | https://github.com/TingxiYu/academic-figure-skill | 505 | 2026-07-12 08:30 | Apache-2.0, verified against `LICENSE`; the MIT claim in README contradicts the actual LICENSE, so LICENSE prevails |
| Origin Style Replot | No public repository found matching this exact name that can be confirmed as the same project | — | — | Unknown; https://github.com/deliuou/originplot-skill is a similarly named but distinct MIT alternative and must not be passed off as this item; stars/commits/license are not attributed to the original project |
| figures4papers | https://github.com/ChenLiu-1996/figures4papers; source notes also mention https://github.com/mtdww/figures4papers (unverified whether identical) | 8,617 (former) | 2026-10-12 16:02 (former) | Former LICENSE is CC BY-NC 4.0 (API `NOASSERTION`), not a permissive commercial license; latter has no license on GitHub; neither was test-installed |
| K-Dense Scientific Visualization | https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills | 50,802 | Top-level repo latest 2026-10-12 09:43 | MIT ( / GitHub API); skill self-reports version 1.4, supporting editable SVG and explicit export checks |

Academic Figure Skill (commit `1df9940dd0`) and K-Dense Scientific Visualization (commit `a1043ef544`) were selected. The former provides semantic color palettes and typography/vector SVG output specifications; the latter provides an isolated style_context and non-overwriting export_figure for actual export. No online image-to-image generation was called, nor were repository Skills copied into the production profile. For this trial, architecture diagram scripts were manually authored, **genuinely utilizing** the former's rcParams/color palette/saving specifications and the latter's style_context/export_figure respectively; this was not a test of whether they could automatically infer a network from legacy figures without human supervision.

## Why the Target Diagram Is Not One of the Candidate Images

The candidate image has mtime 2026-04-09 16:03 (ET), with the original on-figure title `UNet Speed Distillation — Round 34 (Global Best)`, featuring a 4-level encoder-decoder, skip connections, and a coarse head—which is a UNet rather than a Graph-DeepONet. The 04-15 timestamps of `UNet_7level_final.drawioUNet_7level.drawioUNet_7level_v2.drawio_codex.drawio` are even earlier. A later file with mtime 2026-04-20 only turned up UNet and progress on other projects, not the basis for the final Graph-DeepONet architecture of this figure. The file in the openclaw workspace matches the imported copy identically in SHA256, with mtime 2026-04-02; lines 35–36 state verbatim "### Current Optimal Architecture / `HybridGraphCNN + FineGraph48 + Fourier64 trunk`", and line 28 states "Hybrid + FineGraph48 (current optimal branch)". Therefore, this **written record** was taken as the target architecture; no off-the-shelf editable architecture diagram for this combination was found. The default dual output `[u,v]` in the legacy zip is inconsistent with the speed-only single channel in the record, so it was not used to infer layer counts or channels for the optimal combination. FG64 at lines 115–116 of the record is another 40 ep variant and does not supersede the 160 ep FG48 combination already marked in the text as the current optimum.

## Item-by-Item Architectural Comparison (Identical Content Across Both Figure Versions)

| Item | Recorded Evidence (Filename and Line Numbers Only) | Treatment in Both Figures | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Target combination | `project_graph_deeponet.md:23–36` | HybridGraphCNN + FineGraph48 + Fourier64 trunk | Identical |
| Graph representation | Same file `:25–28` | FineGraph48; 48 is not guessed as node count or pixel dimension | Identical |
| Branch module | Same file `:27` | GAT + CNN dual path; fusion operator not drawn | Identical, details unrecorded |
| Trunk / position | Same file `:19–21,31–34` | Query coordinates → Fourier64 → position-aware trunk; explicitly noted that wiring details are unknown | Identical, specific graph-context wiring undetermined |
| Fourier parameters | Same file `:33` | m=64, σ=10.0 | Identical |
| Output basis / coupling | Same file `:40–44` | branch/trunk each p=64 → inner product + bias; only schematic broadcast multiplication is shown, without drawing unverified intermediate layers | Identical |
| Output channel | Same file `:50–52` (speed-only) and `:40–44` | Single-channel wind speed | Identical |
| GAT/CNN layer depth, conv channels, spatial resolution, fusion details, which node supplies graph context | No values in same file `:19–44` | Explicitly labeled "not in record / unknown"; values such as 64/128/256/512 or 640² from the UNet diagram are not borrowed | Unverified, cannot claim complete architecture |

Below the figure, an English note states the source and "schematic, not code-verified". The figure contains no RMSE values, data sample details, or unpublished manuscript text. Both figures rely solely on the written notes and are not "local touch-ups" of the old UNet diagram.

## Deliverables and Four Evaluation Criteria

| Skill | ① Content Consistency | ② Layout | ③ Editability | ④ Identity / License / Security | Conclusion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Academic Figure Skill | Pass (known information matched item by item; unrecorded parameters left blank) | Pass: v3 PNG visually inspected with no overlap or garbled text; right-side branch rerouted | Pass: `academic_figure_v3.svg` has 24 `<text><image>` elements, plus PDF | Pass with caveats: authentic repo, Apache-2.0; style snippets used read-only, synthesis scripts containing `eval` were not executed | Worth using as a scientific figure styling / vector export constraint after human verification; not promoted standalone as an automated skill for final architecture diagrams |
| K-Dense Scientific Visualization | Pass (same factual baseline) | Pass: v3 PNG visually inspected with no overlap or garbled text | Pass: `kdense_visualization_v3.svg` has 19 `<text><image>` elements, PDF Type42 + PNG + manifest | Pass with caveats: authentic repo, MIT; only local scripts of the selected sub-skill were audited/invoked, without certifying the entire 177-skill library as safe | Worth using as a provenance-backed static scientific plotting + non-overwriting export/manifest QA template; architecture must be human-verified |

Layout passing is not proof of journal acceptance; the current width is 11.5 inches and has not been sized against a target journal's current submission stage, so re-layout will be required prior to submission. The PDF contains embedded fonts, but SVG remains the preferred final editable format (with text preserved as `<text>`); rendering of PDF fonts and SVGs on other devices depends on local font availability. v1 produced warnings due to missing Chinese glyphs, v2 fixed the Chinese font issue, and v3 further corrected arrows crossing through trunk nodes; earlier versions are retained without overwriting and are not treated as final deliverables.

Files (all in the same directory as this report): , ; security check in . Both the PNGs and the tables derive from the same written record noted above. No supercomputer, Colab, or production profile modifications were made. External code and original sources require the Lead to add the public WeChat link to `PUBLIC_CITATIONS.md`; the K-Dense scientific skills paper should only be cited after verifying the original text.

## Recommended Adoption

Retain as a "human-reviewed vector architecture schematic workflow for the plotting-tool bot", enforcing pinned commits, item-by-item source cross-checking, omission of unverified parameters, independent UTF-8/font and collision checks, SVG `<text>` validation, and dual vector/PNG delivery. Do not install as a production skill without separate auditing; unrelated code paths in the former contain environment-variable evaluation and should be stripped out, while for the latter only the scientific-visualization subdirectory should be selected. If the goal is a submission-ready diagram showing the final complete layer/channel/resolution architecture, the configuration/weight source code corresponding to the best model and author-verified values must first be obtained; this quick trial does not meet that stronger requirement.
