# 快试 #12 静态安全检查（执行前）

审查范围：隔离目录克隆的 提交 `1df9940dd0` 和 提交 `a1043ef544` 中 子目录；手工阅读被调用入口、导出、样式代码，并在 Academic 仓库 Python 脚本做关键词搜索。不是全仓库/全部依赖安全认证。10-16 03:03 美东。只运行明确检查过的本地路径；未执行仓库安装命令、演示脚本、动态下载、PDF 上传或自带全库 evaluator。

| 检查类别 | Academic Figure Skill | K-Dense Scientific Visualization | 处置 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 网络外连 | README 的 npm 全局安装/技能复制仅为文档；所用 `SKILL.mdreferences` 的本地样式和导出无在线调用；没有按安装建议执行 | 所选 、 无请求/下载调用；SKILL 的 `uv run --with` 会触网，未执行 | 仓库本身通过 HTTPS 只克隆至隔离目录；运行时未把数据送出 |
| 读取凭据/环境变量 | 被用的样式不读取密钥；发现 在 R 片段里 `eval(parse(text=Sys.getenv("CNS_PNG_DEVICE")))`，环境变量被当代码执行，风险中/高（若让不可信环境变量参与，可能任意 R 代码执行） | 所选导出脚本没有读取密钥、SSH 或 token 的代码；不承诺其余 176 项 skill 无此类代码 | Academic 的 compose/eval_runner 不执行；清空真实密钥暴露，不把项目原始数据交给第三方 |
| 删改文件 | 会 `os.unlink(temp_r)`，仅跑 evaluator 的临时 R 脚本；未运行；此次自产图的常规写入限指定结果目录 | `figure_export.py:97–150` 临时文件 `unlink` 且目标默认 `overwrite=False`，通过 `checked_output_file` 阻止已有路径覆盖；会为输入指定目录创建自己的新文件 | 全部产物使用新名字；初版、v2 留存，v3 新建不覆盖 |
| 提权/执行外部命令 | README 指导的 npm 全局安装与复制生产 skill 路径不执行；`eval_runner.py工作目录` 的 venv 中调用；没有生产 profile 改动 |
| 混淆代码 | 所检查入口/脚本可读，未见 base64 解码后执行或加密载荷；但上面的 R `eval(parse)` 是动态执行风险 | 所选脚本可读、无混淆执行；Python 原生依赖 Matplotlib 从系统 site-packages 引入，仅用于本地图形渲染 | 不对未审阅的其他目录下安全性背书 |
| 许可 | 根目录 `LICENSE` 为 Apache-2.0；README 文本误称 MIT，按实际许可标注 | GitHub API 指向根目录，MIT，Skill 自身元数据亦 MIT | 对外使用保留许可证和仓库出处 |

隔离实现：仅在 克隆和建立 `.venv26_Quick_Trials/`。原图、项目笔记和 zip 只读。没有网络模型、API key、SSH、超算、Colab 作业。

剩余风险：Academic 的 compose 动态环境变量求值路径若未来被纳入自动技能则不满足“无高风险项”的扩展范围要求；本快试选用的有限样式代码路径无高风险执行项。克隆行为本身依赖 GitHub，未来部署需锁 commit 并重新静态；SVG 使用外部字体时跨机可能替代字形。

# Quick-Trial #12: Drawing a Graph-DeepONet Architecture Diagram from Project Notes Using Two Scientific Plotting Skills

Time: 10-16 03:03 (EDT). Data sources: local read-only project notes (dated `2026-04-02`) and candidate figure files; external code repositories are linked below. Public figures display only abstract network architecture and reference filename/line numbers, omitting any file paths, unpublished manuscript prose, or personal information. **This diagram has not been cross-verified against the underlying model source code and must not be used as a camera-ready journal figure.**

## Verification of Six Candidate Repositories

Queried via the GitHub REST API on 10-16; star counts reflect point-in-time values at query time. Because the source blog post did not provide direct repository URLs for every item, the table below records verified repository identities without assuming that identically or similarly named repositories are necessarily the exact ones intended by the post.

| Name in Post | Verified Repository / Status | Stars | Latest Commit (UTC) | Verified License / Usability |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| AgentFigureGallery | https://github.com/Dsadd4/AgentFigureGallery | 166 | 2026-09-05 02:17 | MIT; provides reference figure retrieval / installation wrapper rather than specialized neural-architecture diagramming |
| Nature Skill | https://github.com/Yuan1z0825/nature-skills | 48,590 | 2026-10-16 02:35 | Apache-2.0; multiple forks exist and must not be conflated |
| Academic Figure Skill | https://github.com/TingxiYu/academic-figure-skill | 505 | 2026-07-12 08:30 | Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE` verified directly; overrides the conflicting MIT mention in README) |
| Origin Style Replot | No public repository found matching this exact name and verifiable as the same project | — | — | Unknown; https://github.com/deliuou/originplot-skill is a similarly named MIT alternative that must not be conflated with the original item |
| figures4papers | https://github.com/ChenLiu-1996/figures4papers; source notes also mention https://github.com/mtdww/figures4papers (unconfirmed whether related) | 8,617 (former) | 2026-10-12 16:02 (former) | Former uses `CC BY-NC 4.0` (API reports `NOASSERTION`), which is non-commercial; latter has no license on GitHub; neither was installed |
| K-Dense Scientific Visualization | https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills | 50,802 | Top-level latest commit 2026-10-12 09:43 | MIT (verified via GitHub API); skill self-reports v1.4, supporting editable SVG output and explicit export checks |

We selected **Academic Figure Skill** (commit `1df9940dd0`) and **K-Dense Scientific Visualization** (commit `a1043ef544`). The former provides semantic color palettes and typography / vector SVG export guidelines; the latter provides an isolated `style_context` and an overwrite-safe `export_figure` utility. Neither online image-to-image generation nor production-profile skill installation was used. In this trial, we hand-authored the architecture diagram scripts while **genuinely applying** Academic's `rcParams`/palette/save specs and K-Dense's `style_context`/`export_figure`, respectively (rather than testing unsupervised neural architecture inference from an old raster image).

## Why the Target Diagram Follows the Text Notes Rather Than the Candidate Image

The candidate PNG (mtime `2026-04-09 16:03 EDT`) is titled `UNet Speed Distillation — Round 34 (Global Best)` and depicts a 4-level encoder–decoder with skip connections and a coarse head — i.e., a UNet rather than a Graph-DeepONet (and the `.drawio` files from `04-15` are likewise 7-level UNet diagrams, while a later file from `04-20` contains only general progress notes). Meanwhile, the imported copy of `project_graph_deeponet.md` (mtime `2026-04-02`, matching SHA256) states on lines 35–36: `"### Current Best Architecture / HybridGraphCNN + FineGraph48 + Fourier64 trunk"`, and on line 28: `"Hybrid + FineGraph48 (current best branch)"`. Because no editable diagram existed for this winning Graph-DeepONet combination, we drew the schematic strictly from this **written record** (without borrowing channel counts or layer depths from the older dual-output `[u,v]` archive or the 40-epoch `FG64` variant on lines 115–116).

## Item-by-Item Mapping Against Project Notes (Identical Across Both Skill Outputs)

| Element | Evidence in Notes (Filename & Line Numbers Only) | Representation in Both Diagrams | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Target architecture | `project_graph_deeponet.md:23–36` | `HybridGraphCNN + FineGraph48 + Fourier64 trunk` | Exact match |
| Graph representation | Same file `:25–28` | `FineGraph48` (without guessing whether `48` denotes node count or grid resolution) | Exact match |
| Branch module | Same file `:27` | Dual `GAT + CNN` paths; fusion operator left unspecifed | Exact match (fusion detail unrecorded) |
| Trunk / coordinates | Same file `:19–21, 31–34` | Query coordinates → `Fourier64` → position-aware trunk, noting that exact graph-context injection point is unspecified | Exact match |
| Fourier parameters | Same file `:33` | `m=64, σ=10.0` | Exact match |
| Basis width & inner product | Same file `:40–44` | Branch / trunk each output `p=64` → inner product + bias (schematically showing broadcast multiplication without inventing unverified intermediate layers) | Exact match |
| Output channel | Same file `:50–52` (`speed-only`) and `:40–44` | Single-channel wind speed | Exact match |
| GAT/CNN depth, conv channels, spatial resolution, fusion operator, graph-context source node | Unrecorded in `:19–44` | Explicitly labeled `"Not in record / Unknown"`; zero numbers (`64/128/256/512`, `640²`, etc.) borrowed from the UNet figure | Unverified; no claim of complete layer-level architecture |

A footer note in English on each figure states its provenance and labels it `"schematic, not code-verified"`. Neither RMSE figures, dataset sample details, nor unpublished manuscript sentences appear in the figures.

## Deliverables and Four-Criterion Evaluation

| Skill | ① Content Fidelity | ② Layout Quality | ③ Editability | ④ Identity / License / Security | Conclusion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Academic Figure Skill | Passed (matches all recorded facts; leaves unrecorded parameters blank) | Passed: `v3` PNG visually verified free of overlaps or garbled glyphs; right-hand branch rerouted cleanly | Passed: `academic_figure_v3.svg` has 24 `<text>` and 0 `<image>` elements, accompanied by PDF | **Did not pass full-repo security gate**: authentic Apache-2.0 repo, but an unused R helper contains `eval(parse(...))` on an environment variable (not triggered here) | **Do not install/adopt as a whole-repo skill**; static style rules may be referenced in isolation (see supplementary security note for subsequent docstring reassessment) |
| K-Dense Scientific Visualization | Passed (identical factual scope) | Passed: `v3` PNG visually verified free of overlaps or garbled glyphs | Passed: `kdense_visualization_v3.svg` has 19 `<text>` and 0 `<image>` elements, plus Type42 PDF + PNG + manifest | Passed with scoped boundary: authentic MIT repo; audited and invoked only the local scripts of the selected sub-skill without certifying all 177 skills in the monorepo | **Worth adopting** as a provenance-tracked static scientific diagramming + overwrite-safe export/manifest QA template (requires human verification of scientific topology) |

Layout cleanliness does not imply journal-ready sizing: the current canvas width is 11.5 inches and has not been tailored to a specific target journal's column width. While the PDF embeds TrueType fonts, SVG (`<text>` elements preserved) is the primary editable source format. Earlier iterations (`v1` had missing CJK glyph warnings; `v2` fixed CJK fonts; `v3` fixed an arrow crossing a trunk node) are preserved untouched without overwriting, and only `v3` serves as the formal deliverable. Zero cluster jobs, Colab sessions, or production profile modifications were made. The Lead should add the external repositories and source blog link to `PUBLIC_CITATIONS.md`.

Note: This file incorporates the post-security-audit revision of the initial report; the initial report is retained without overwriting.

## Deployment Recommendation

Adopt only the audited K-Dense `scientific-visualization` sub-skill as a "human-reviewed vector architecture schematic workflow for plotting tool bots": pin the exact commit, verify every block against written provenance, refuse to invent unrecorded layer parameters, enforce UTF-8/font and overlap checks, validate `<text>` elements in SVG, and deliver paired vector + PNG outputs. Do not install unreviewed whole-repository skills into production profiles. Producing a camera-ready submission diagram with full layer depths, channel counts, and spatial resolutions will require obtaining the exact model source code and configuration corresponding to the winning checkpoint.

items.text:
# Quick-Trial #12 Supplementary Test: Overlap-Free Vector Redraw of the Round 34 Original Figure

10-16 EDT. Reference input (read-only): a 2779×1580 PNG from the internal archive (file path recorded only in the internal log and omitted from all figures). Inspection confirms that this image is **UNet Speed Distillation Round 34** rather than Graph-DeepONet. While the two Graph-DeepONet schematic diagrams from the previous round are retained untouched, this supplementary test specifically addresses the box/label overlaps in the original figure noted by Liang Hu. All text strings in the original image were cross-checked via high-resolution visual inspection and `tesseract` OCR. We did not audit the underlying training code or config to verify whether the original figure's scientific labels are faithful to the code; "consistency" here means strictly faithful transcription of the original image.

## Item-by-Item Mapping from Original Figure to Redrawn Outputs

The "Redrawn Output" column below applies identically to both the Academic and K-Dense `_v2` deliverables; no unstated spatial resolutions or upsampling factors were extrapolated or added.

| Item in Original Figure | Readable Content / Connections in Original | Redrawn Output & Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Title | `UNet Speed Distillation — Round 34 (Global Best)` | Preserved verbatim |
| Subtitle / global metrics | `4-level encoder-decoder \| base=64 \| SE attention (r=1) \| 8.57M parameters \| EMA RMSE = 0.0586` | Preserved verbatim |
| Input block | `Input 3×64×64` | Preserved verbatim; this is the only block where the original specifies input spatial resolution |
| Encoder level E1 | `E1 64` | Preserved verbatim; did not guess whether `64` denotes channels or spatial size |
| Encoder level E2 | `E2 128` | Preserved verbatim |
| Encoder level E3 | `E3 256` | Preserved verbatim |
| Bottleneck E4 | `E4 512 (bottleneck)` | Preserved verbatim |
| Decoder level D3 | `D3 256` | Preserved verbatim |
| Decoder level D2 | `D2 128` | Preserved verbatim |
| Decoder level D1 | `D1 64` | Preserved verbatim |
| Output block | `Output 1×64×64` | Preserved verbatim |
| Auxiliary head | `Coarse Head 1×16×16` | Preserved verbatim |
| Auxiliary supervision | `Coarse Supervision` | Preserved verbatim, no numbers invented |
| Main path connections | `Input→E1→E2→E3→E4→D3→D2→D1→Output` | 8 main-path arrows laid out left-to-right in exact sequence |
| `Pool 2×` arrow labels | Four `Pool 2×` labels are readable near the first four adjacent main-path arrows in the original, though the original boxes overlap heavily and exact code semantics were not audited | Four `Pool 2×` labels placed on `Input→E1`, `E1→E2`, `E2→E3`, and `E3→E4`, reproducing the visual adjacency of the original without asserting that `Input→E1` performs pooling in code |
| `UpSample 2×` arrow label | Only a single `UpSample 2×` label appears in the original, near `E4→D3` | Single `UpSample 2×` label placed on `E4→D3`; no unprinted labels added on `D3→D2` or `D2→D1` |
| Skip connection x₃ | `Skip (x₃) + Cat`; `E3→D3` | Verbatim label and exact endpoints preserved |
| Skip connection x₂ | `Skip (x₂) + Cat`; `E2→D2` | Verbatim label and exact endpoints preserved |
| Skip connection x₁ | `Skip (x₁) + Cat`; `E1→D1` | Verbatim label and exact endpoints preserved |
| Auxiliary branch | `E4 → Coarse Head → Coarse Supervision` | Preserved as a two-segment branch |
| Legend | `Encoder (ConvBlock + SE)`, `Decoder (ConvBlock + SE)`, `Coarse Auxiliary Head`, `Skip Connection` | All four legend entries preserved verbatim |
| Per-layer spatial sizes, conv layer counts, channel semantics | Not printed in the original image (absent from the source, not merely illegible) | No inferred values added; boxes display only the exact strings printed in the original |

## Overlap Resolution Summary

| Visual Defect in Original | Fix Applied in Both `_v2` Redraws | Visual Check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Encoder boxes `E1/E2`, `E2/E3`, `E3/E4` collide; `Pool` text touches box borders | Aligned all 9 main-path boxes along a single horizontal baseline with positive gaps; placed `Pool 2×` labels cleanly in the open margin above each arrow | Fixed; zero text–border collisions |
| `E4/D3` collide; `UpSample` crowds the border | Separated `E4` and `D3`; moved `UpSample 2×` into the upper margin and routed the auxiliary branch cleanly upward | Fixed |
| Decoder boxes `D3/D2`, `D2/D1`, `D1/Output` collide | Separated into uniform-width boxes with dedicated inter-box gaps for arrows | Fixed |
| 3 purple skip curves cut right through crowded colored boxes | Routed as three orthogonal dashed channels at staggered heights underneath `E3/E2/E1` to the bottoms of `D3/D2/D1` | Fixed; zero box crossings or label occlusions |
| Two minor defects in our initial `_v1` redraw (not in original) | In `_v1`, arrow labels touched box edges and Arial lacked subscript glyphs (`₁₂₃`); preserved `_v1` untouched and generated `_v2` with increased label clearance and `DejaVu Sans` | `_v2` verified free of missing glyphs or border touches |

Note that rearranging the crowded layout clarifies reading order without auditing the underlying neural network code. Typography uses a clean hierarchy: 9.3 pt inside boxes, 8 pt for edge annotations, and 16 pt for the title. All PNGs were visually inspected; XML parsing of both SVGs confirmed 38 `<text>` elements and 0 `<image>` elements with all numbers and subscript skip labels intact; `pdffonts` confirmed embedded `DejaVu Sans` TrueType fonts (not outlined paths); and PNG dimensions are `3847×1977`. Both PDF and SVG deliverables remain fully text-editable and contain no private paths.

## Evaluation of the Two Skills

| Criterion | Academic Figure Skill (`1df9940dd0`) | K-Dense `scientific-visualization` (`a1043ef544`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ① Exact match on topology, numbers, titles, and links | Passed (see mapping table above; ambiguities inherent to the original image are not expanded into code-level claims) | Passed (identical transcription and mapping table) |
| ② Elimination of overlaps, clean fonts & alignment | Passed visual inspection | Passed visual inspection |
| ③ Editable SVG, PDF, and high-res PNG | Passed: 38 `<text>` / 0 `<image>` in SVG; embedded TrueType fonts in PDF | Passed: 38 `<text>` / 0 `<image>` in SVG; embedded TrueType fonts in PDF |
| ④ Security | Passed: restricted execution path is low-risk under Apache-2.0; corrected security table documented separately | Passed: selected sub-skill is low-risk under MIT (without endorsing the entire repo) |
| Verdict | **Worth adopting**: typography, palette, and vector export specs materially improve hand-scripted diagram delivery (note: it is a style/export specification, not an automated image-to-vector redrawing algorithm) | **Worth adopting**: local `style_context` and overwrite-safe multi-format `export_figure` are practical utilities (likewise not an automated image-understanding tool) |

Actual contribution of each skill: Academic provided typography, color-palette, and export specifications (`export-specs.md`); K-Dense provided `style_context`, `export_figure` (with non-overwrite guard, manifest generation, and 3-format export), and its palette. The layout coordinates and overlap removal were written in our Python rendering script inside an isolated venv — neither skill automatically parses or repairs raster input images.

## Final Deliverables (All Newly Created Without Overwriting Earlier Versions)

- Academic `_v2` SVG / PDF / PNG deliverables
- K-Dense `_v2` SVG / PDF / PNG deliverables
- Standalone Python generator script (executed inside an isolated venv; configured to refuse overwriting existing `_v2` outputs)
- Manifest and this report

Figure data provenance: read-only Round 34 reference figure; repository sources: Academic Figure Skill (https://github.com/TingxiYu/academic-figure-skill, Apache-2.0) and K-Dense (https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills, MIT). Source attributions are printed on the public figures, and the Lead should append both entries to `PUBLIC_CITATIONS.md`.

- Decision I made：开两页快试，判据、时限、资源上限开工前写定（见两页页头）；两单都派 bot quick（后者排队），写入范围分开，第三方代码只在 工作目录 一次性目录里试。
- 为什么：按本实验室规则（限时限资源、先静态安全检查、不进生产 bot）；同一个 bot 串行做，避免两单同时写共享文件。
- 错了的代价：最多浪费约 1.5 天 bot 时间，0 算力。
- 核对过：Graph-DeepONet（openclaw 工作区）不在 内（grep 无命中），不属保密项目；是 Liang Hu 自己定的试画对象。公开展示页上只放图与结论，不放稿件原文。
- 依据：无文献依据，属工具快试。

## 10-16 03:00 #15 svg-diagram 收口：值得用
- Decision I made：判"值得用"。bot 交的 v3 有拓扑错误（Router 画在 Lead 与模型之间；平台手册写的是 Router 在界面与 Lead/bot 之间），判据①不过；我直接改 SVG 文本出 v4，lint 0 错 0 警告，五条判据全过。判据没有改。
- 为什么：这次的错是作图者理解错了，不是工具的问题；改一处只用几分钟，正好也验证了判据③（可以直接改文本）。
- 错了的代价：低——技能只作为出图 bot 的可选项，交付前必须过 lint 和内容核对。

## 10-16 03:10 #12 补测 round34
- Decision I made：B 先不收口，追加补测——用两个 Skill 重画 round34 原图，检验能不能修好重叠、数字是否不变。同时更正 bot 对 Academic 的放弃理由：eval(parse) 只在 docstring 示例里，仓库里没有执行。
- 为什么：Liang Hu 指定的检验点是"原图有重叠，正好检验"；bot 改按文字记录画图，没有原图可对照，判据①、②都没真正测到。round34 本身是 UNet 线的图，这一点照实写清楚。
- 错了的代价：多花约半天 bot 时间，0 算力。

## 10-16 03:20 #12 收口：值得用（有限）
- Decision I made：首选 K-Dense scientific-visualization（MIT；导出不覆盖、三格式、清单），Academic Figure Skill（Apache-2.0）只作样式参考；两个都不装整库。round34 重画我逐项核过：数字与原图一致，重叠全部消除。
- 为什么：两张图几乎一样，说明出图质量主要来自 bot 手写的排版脚本，Skill 提供的是样式和导出规范；K-Dense 的许可更宽，导出检查更实在。
- 错了的代价：低——技能只作可选项，交付仍要人工逐项对照。
- 留给 Liang Hu 知道：Graph-DeepONet 没有现成的最终结构图（round34 原图属于 UNet 线），据文字记录画的示意图不能当投稿终稿。

results.text:
# Quick-Trial #12: Drawing a Recorded Graph-DeepONet Architecture Schematic with Two Scientific Plotting Skills

Time: 10-16 03:03 (ET). Data sources: local read-only record (2026-04-02) and candidate figure files; see repository links for external code sources. Public figures include only the abstract architecture and original record filenames/line numbers, omitting project paths, unpublished manuscript passages, or personal information. **This diagram is not a final network architecture verified against model code and is not intended as a final submission figure.**

## Verification of Six Repositories

GitHub REST API, repository metadata, and license endpoints were queried on 10-16; star counts reflect instantaneous values at query time. Mentioning a name in the source article does not equate to providing a direct repository link; the entries below represent verifiable identities, and repositories with identical or similar names must not be treated as the sole repository explicitly designated by the original post.

| Name in Article | Verifiable Repository / Status | Stars | Latest Commit (UTC) | Actual License / Usability |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| AgentFigureGallery | https://github.com/Dsadd4/AgentFigureGallery | 166 | 2026-09-05 02:17 | MIT; provides reference figure retrieval/installation wrappers, not specialized for network architecture diagramming |
| Nature Skill | https://github.com/Yuan1z0825/nature-skills | 48,590 | 2026-10-16 02:35 | Apache-2.0; multiple forks exist and must not be conflated |
| Academic Figure Skill | https://github.com/TingxiYu/academic-figure-skill | 505 | 2026-07-12 08:30 | Apache-2.0, verified against `LICENSE`; the MIT claim in README contradicts the actual LICENSE, so LICENSE prevails |
| Origin Style Replot | No public repository found matching this exact name that can be confirmed as the same project | — | — | Unknown; https://github.com/deliuou/originplot-skill is a similarly named but distinct MIT alternative and must not be passed off as this item; stars/commits/license are not attributed to the original project |
| figures4papers | https://github.com/ChenLiu-1996/figures4papers; source notes also mention https://github.com/mtdww/figures4papers (unverified whether identical) | 8,617 (former) | 2026-10-12 16:02 (former) | Former LICENSE is CC BY-NC 4.0 (API `NOASSERTION`), not a permissive commercial license; latter has no license on GitHub; neither was test-installed |
| K-Dense Scientific Visualization | https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills | 50,802 | Top-level repo latest 2026-10-12 09:43 | MIT ( / GitHub API); skill self-reports version 1.4, supporting editable SVG and explicit export checks |

Academic Figure Skill (commit `1df9940dd0`) and K-Dense Scientific Visualization (commit `a1043ef544`) were selected. The former provides semantic color palettes and typography/vector SVG output specifications; the latter provides an isolated style_context and non-overwriting export_figure for actual export. No online image-to-image generation was called, nor were repository Skills copied into the production profile. For this trial, architecture diagram scripts were manually authored, **genuinely utilizing** the former's rcParams/color palette/saving specifications and the latter's style_context/export_figure respectively; this was not a test of whether they could automatically infer a network from legacy figures without human supervision.

## Why the Target Diagram Is Not One of the Candidate Images

The candidate image has mtime 2026-04-09 16:03 (ET), with the original on-figure title `UNet Speed Distillation — Round 34 (Global Best)`, featuring a 4-level encoder-decoder, skip connections, and a coarse head—which is a UNet rather than a Graph-DeepONet. The 04-15 timestamps of `UNet_7level_final.drawioUNet_7level.drawioUNet_7level_v2.drawio_codex.drawio` are even earlier. A later file with mtime 2026-04-20 only turned up UNet and progress on other projects, not the basis for the final Graph-DeepONet architecture of this figure. The file in the openclaw workspace matches the imported copy identically in SHA256, with mtime 2026-04-02; lines 35–36 state verbatim "### Current Optimal Architecture / `HybridGraphCNN + FineGraph48 + Fourier64 trunk`", and line 28 states "Hybrid + FineGraph48 (current optimal branch)". Therefore, this **written record** was taken as the target architecture; no off-the-shelf editable architecture diagram for this combination was found. The default dual output `[u,v]` in the legacy zip is inconsistent with the speed-only single channel in the record, so it was not used to infer layer counts or channels for the optimal combination. FG64 at lines 115–116 of the record is another 40 ep variant and does not supersede the 160 ep FG48 combination already marked in the text as the current optimum.

## Item-by-Item Architectural Comparison (Identical Content Across Both Figure Versions)

| Item | Recorded Evidence (Filename and Line Numbers Only) | Treatment in Both Figures | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Target combination | `project_graph_deeponet.md:23–36` | HybridGraphCNN + FineGraph48 + Fourier64 trunk | Identical |
| Graph representation | Same file `:25–28` | FineGraph48; 48 is not guessed as node count or pixel dimension | Identical |
| Branch module | Same file `:27` | GAT + CNN dual path; fusion operator not drawn | Identical, details unrecorded |
| Trunk / position | Same file `:19–21,31–34` | Query coordinates → Fourier64 → position-aware trunk; explicitly noted that wiring details are unknown | Identical, specific graph-context wiring undetermined |
| Fourier parameters | Same file `:33` | m=64, σ=10.0 | Identical |
| Output basis / coupling | Same file `:40–44` | branch/trunk each p=64 → inner product + bias; only schematic broadcast multiplication is shown, without drawing unverified intermediate layers | Identical |
| Output channel | Same file `:50–52` (speed-only) and `:40–44` | Single-channel wind speed | Identical |
| GAT/CNN layer depth, conv channels, spatial resolution, fusion details, which node supplies graph context | No values in same file `:19–44` | Explicitly labeled "not in record / unknown"; values such as 64/128/256/512 or 640² from the UNet diagram are not borrowed | Unverified, cannot claim complete architecture |

Below the figure, an English note states the source and "schematic, not code-verified". The figure contains no RMSE values, data sample details, or unpublished manuscript text. Both figures rely solely on the written notes and are not "local touch-ups" of the old UNet diagram.

## Deliverables and Four Evaluation Criteria

| Skill | ① Content Consistency | ② Layout | ③ Editability | ④ Identity / License / Security | Conclusion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Academic Figure Skill | Pass (known information matched item by item; unrecorded parameters left blank) | Pass: v3 PNG visually inspected with no overlap or garbled text; right-side branch rerouted | Pass: `academic_figure_v3.svg` has 24 `<text><image>` elements, plus PDF | Pass with caveats: authentic repo, Apache-2.0; style snippets used read-only, synthesis scripts containing `eval` were not executed | Worth using as a scientific figure styling / vector export constraint after human verification; not promoted standalone as an automated skill for final architecture diagrams |
| K-Dense Scientific Visualization | Pass (same factual baseline) | Pass: v3 PNG visually inspected with no overlap or garbled text | Pass: `kdense_visualization_v3.svg` has 19 `<text><image>` elements, PDF Type42 + PNG + manifest | Pass with caveats: authentic repo, MIT; only local scripts of the selected sub-skill were audited/invoked, without certifying the entire 177-skill library as safe | Worth using as a provenance-backed static scientific plotting + non-overwriting export/manifest QA template; architecture must be human-verified |

Layout passing is not proof of journal acceptance; the current width is 11.5 inches and has not been sized against a target journal's current submission stage, so re-layout will be required prior to submission. The PDF contains embedded fonts, but SVG remains the preferred final editable format (with text preserved as `<text>`); rendering of PDF fonts and SVGs on other devices depends on local font availability. v1 produced warnings due to missing Chinese glyphs, v2 fixed the Chinese font issue, and v3 further corrected arrows crossing through trunk nodes; earlier versions are retained without overwriting and are not treated as final deliverables.

Files (all in the same directory as this report): , ; security check in . Both the PNGs and the tables derive from the same written record noted above. No supercomputer, Colab, or production profile modifications were made. External code and original sources require the Lead to add the public WeChat link to `PUBLIC_CITATIONS.md`; the K-Dense scientific skills paper should only be cited after verifying the original text.

## Recommended Adoption

Retain as a "human-reviewed vector architecture schematic workflow for the plotting-tool bot", enforcing pinned commits, item-by-item source cross-checking, omission of unverified parameters, independent UTF-8/font and collision checks, SVG `<text>` validation, and dual vector/PNG delivery. Do not install as a production skill without separate auditing; unrelated code paths in the former contain environment-variable evaluation and should be stripped out, while for the latter only the scientific-visualization subdirectory should be selected. If the goal is a submission-ready diagram showing the final complete layer/channel/resolution architecture, the configuration/weight source code corresponding to the best model and author-verified values must first be obtained; this quick trial does not meet that stronger requirement.

# Quick-Trial #12: Drawing a Graph-DeepONet Architecture Diagram from Project Notes Using Two Scientific Plotting Skills

Time: 10-16 03:03 (EDT). Data sources: local read-only project notes (dated `2026-04-02`) and candidate figure files; external code repositories are linked below. Public figures display only abstract network architecture and reference filename/line numbers, omitting any file paths, unpublished manuscript prose, or personal information. **This diagram has not been cross-verified against the underlying model source code and must not be used as a camera-ready journal figure.**

## Verification of Six Candidate Repositories

Queried via the GitHub REST API on 10-16; star counts reflect point-in-time values at query time. Because the source blog post did not provide direct repository URLs for every item, the table below records verified repository identities without assuming that identically or similarly named repositories are necessarily the exact ones intended by the post.

| Name in Post | Verified Repository / Status | Stars | Latest Commit (UTC) | Verified License / Usability |

| AgentFigureGallery | https://github.com/Dsadd4/AgentFigureGallery | 166 | 2026-09-05 02:17 | MIT; provides reference figure retrieval / installation wrapper rather than specialized neural-architecture diagramming |
| Nature Skill | https://github.com/Yuan1z0825/nature-skills | 48,590 | 2026-10-16 02:35 | Apache-2.0; multiple forks exist and must not be conflated |
| Academic Figure Skill | https://github.com/TingxiYu/academic-figure-skill | 505 | 2026-07-12 08:30 | Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE` verified directly; overrides the conflicting MIT mention in README) |
| Origin Style Replot | No public repository found matching this exact name and verifiable as the same project | — | — | Unknown; https://github.com/deliuou/originplot-skill is a similarly named MIT alternative that must not be conflated with the original item |
| figures4papers | https://github.com/ChenLiu-1996/figures4papers; source notes also mention https://github.com/mtdww/figures4papers (unconfirmed whether related) | 8,617 (former) | 2026-10-12 16:02 (former) | Former uses `CC BY-NC 4.0` (API reports `NOASSERTION`), which is non-commercial; latter has no license on GitHub; neither was installed |
| K-Dense Scientific Visualization | https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills | 50,802 | Top-level latest commit 2026-10-12 09:43 | MIT (verified via GitHub API); skill self-reports v1.4, supporting editable SVG output and explicit export checks |

We selected **Academic Figure Skill** (commit `1df9940dd0`) and **K-Dense Scientific Visualization** (commit `a1043ef544`). The former provides semantic color palettes and typography / vector SVG export guidelines; the latter provides an isolated `style_context` and an overwrite-safe `export_figure` utility. Neither online image-to-image generation nor production-profile skill installation was used. In this trial, we hand-authored the architecture diagram scripts while **genuinely applying** Academic's `rcParams`/palette/save specs and K-Dense's `style_context`/`export_figure`, respectively (rather than testing unsupervised neural architecture inference from an old raster image).

## Why the Target Diagram Follows the Text Notes Rather Than the Candidate Image

The candidate PNG (mtime `2026-04-09 16:03 EDT`) is titled `UNet Speed Distillation — Round 34 (Global Best)` and depicts a 4-level encoder–decoder with skip connections and a coarse head — i.e., a UNet rather than a Graph-DeepONet (and the `.drawio` files from `04-15` are likewise 7-level UNet diagrams, while a later file from `04-20` contains only general progress notes). Meanwhile, the imported copy of `project_graph_deeponet.md` (mtime `2026-04-02`, matching SHA256) states on lines 35–36: `"### Current Best Architecture / HybridGraphCNN + FineGraph48 + Fourier64 trunk"`, and on line 28: `"Hybrid + FineGraph48 (current best branch)"`. Because no editable diagram existed for this winning Graph-DeepONet combination, we drew the schematic strictly from this **written record** (without borrowing channel counts or layer depths from the older dual-output `[u,v]` archive or the 40-epoch `FG64` variant on lines 115–116).

## Item-by-Item Mapping Against Project Notes (Identical Across Both Skill Outputs)

| Element | Evidence in Notes (Filename & Line Numbers Only) | Representation in Both Diagrams | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Target architecture | `project_graph_deeponet.md:23–36` | `HybridGraphCNN + FineGraph48 + Fourier64 trunk` | Exact match |
| Graph representation | Same file `:25–28` | `FineGraph48` (without guessing whether `48` denotes node count or grid resolution) | Exact match |
| Branch module | Same file `:27` | Dual `GAT + CNN` paths; fusion operator left unspecifed | Exact match (fusion detail unrecorded) |
| Trunk / coordinates | Same file `:19–21, 31–34` | Query coordinates → `Fourier64` → position-aware trunk, noting that exact graph-context injection point is unspecified | Exact match |
| Fourier parameters | Same file `:33` | `m=64, σ=10.0` | Exact match |
| Basis width & inner product | Same file `:40–44` | Branch / trunk each output `p=64` → inner product + bias (schematically showing broadcast multiplication without inventing unverified intermediate layers) | Exact match |
| Output channel | Same file `:50–52` (`speed-only`) and `:40–44` | Single-channel wind speed | Exact match |
| GAT/CNN depth, conv channels, spatial resolution, fusion operator, graph-context source node | Unrecorded in `:19–44` | Explicitly labeled `"Not in record / Unknown"`; zero numbers (`64/128/256/512`, `640²`, etc.) borrowed from the UNet figure | Unverified; no claim of complete layer-level architecture |

A footer note in English on each figure states its provenance and labels it `"schematic, not code-verified"`. Neither RMSE figures, dataset sample details, nor unpublished manuscript sentences appear in the figures.

## Deliverables and Four-Criterion Evaluation

| Skill | ① Content Fidelity | ② Layout Quality | ③ Editability | ④ Identity / License / Security | Conclusion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Academic Figure Skill | Passed (matches all recorded facts; leaves unrecorded parameters blank) | Passed: `v3` PNG visually verified free of overlaps or garbled glyphs; right-hand branch rerouted cleanly | Passed: `academic_figure_v3.svg` has 24 `<text>` and 0 `<image>` elements, accompanied by PDF | **Did not pass full-repo security gate**: authentic Apache-2.0 repo, but an unused R helper contains `eval(parse(...))` on an environment variable (not triggered here) | **Do not install/adopt as a whole-repo skill**; static style rules may be referenced in isolation (see supplementary security note for subsequent docstring reassessment) |
| K-Dense Scientific Visualization | Passed (identical factual scope) | Passed: `v3` PNG visually verified free of overlaps or garbled glyphs | Passed: `kdense_visualization_v3.svg` has 19 `<text>` and 0 `<image>` elements, plus Type42 PDF + PNG + manifest | Passed with scoped boundary: authentic MIT repo; audited and invoked only the local scripts of the selected sub-skill without certifying all 177 skills in the monorepo | **Worth adopting** as a provenance-tracked static scientific diagramming + overwrite-safe export/manifest QA template (requires human verification of scientific topology) |

Layout cleanliness does not imply journal-ready sizing: the current canvas width is 11.5 inches and has not been tailored to a specific target journal's column width. While the PDF embeds TrueType fonts, SVG (`<text>` elements preserved) is the primary editable source format. Earlier iterations (`v1` had missing CJK glyph warnings; `v2` fixed CJK fonts; `v3` fixed an arrow crossing a trunk node) are preserved untouched without overwriting, and only `v3` serves as the formal deliverable. Zero cluster jobs, Colab sessions, or production profile modifications were made. The Lead should add the external repositories and source blog link to `PUBLIC_CITATIONS.md`.

Note: This file incorporates the post-security-audit revision of the initial report; the initial report is retained without overwriting.

## Deployment Recommendation

Adopt only the audited K-Dense `scientific-visualization` sub-skill as a "human-reviewed vector architecture schematic workflow for plotting tool bots": pin the exact commit, verify every block against written provenance, refuse to invent unrecorded layer parameters, enforce UTF-8/font and overlap checks, validate `<text>` elements in SVG, and deliver paired vector + PNG outputs. Do not install unreviewed whole-repository skills into production profiles. Producing a camera-ready submission diagram with full layer depths, channel counts, and spatial resolutions will require obtaining the exact model source code and configuration corresponding to the winning checkpoint.

Scope: Isolated clones of Academic Figure Skill (`1df9940dd0`) and the `scientific-visualization` subdirectory of K-Dense (`a1043ef544`). No reading of real secrets found along the used code paths | No secret/token reads found in the used export scripts | Withdraw the earlier conclusion that this docstring example renders the entire Academic repository high-risk; if a user copies that example into R code in the future, it must be reviewed separately |

# Quick-Trial #12 Supplementary Test: Overlap-Free Vector Redraw of the Round 34 Original Figure

10-16 EDT. Reference input (read-only): a 2779×1580 PNG from the internal archive (file path recorded only in the internal log and omitted from all figures). Inspection confirms that this image is **UNet Speed Distillation Round 34** rather than Graph-DeepONet. While the two Graph-DeepONet schematic diagrams from the previous round are retained untouched, this supplementary test specifically addresses the box/label overlaps in the original figure noted by Liang Hu. All text strings in the original image were cross-checked via high-resolution visual inspection and `tesseract` OCR. We did not audit the underlying training code or config to verify whether the original figure's scientific labels are faithful to the code; "consistency" here means strictly faithful transcription of the original image.

## Item-by-Item Mapping from Original Figure to Redrawn Outputs

The "Redrawn Output" column below applies identically to both the Academic and K-Dense `_v2` deliverables; no unstated spatial resolutions or upsampling factors were extrapolated or added.

| Item in Original Figure | Readable Content / Connections in Original | Redrawn Output & Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Title | `UNet Speed Distillation — Round 34 (Global Best)` | Preserved verbatim |
| Subtitle / global metrics | `4-level encoder-decoder \| base=64 \| SE attention (r=1) \| 8.57M parameters \| EMA RMSE = 0.0586` | Preserved verbatim |
| Input block | `Input 3×64×64` | Preserved verbatim; this is the only block where the original specifies input spatial resolution |
| Encoder level E1 | `E1 64` | Preserved verbatim; did not guess whether `64` denotes channels or spatial size |
| Encoder level E2 | `E2 128` | Preserved verbatim |
| Encoder level E3 | `E3 256` | Preserved verbatim |
| Bottleneck E4 | `E4 512 (bottleneck)` | Preserved verbatim |
| Decoder level D3 | `D3 256` | Preserved verbatim |
| Decoder level D2 | `D2 128` | Preserved verbatim |
| Decoder level D1 | `D1 64` | Preserved verbatim |
| Output block | `Output 1×64×64` | Preserved verbatim |
| Auxiliary head | `Coarse Head 1×16×16` | Preserved verbatim |
| Auxiliary supervision | `Coarse Supervision` | Preserved verbatim, no numbers invented |
| Main path connections | `Input→E1→E2→E3→E4→D3→D2→D1→Output` | 8 main-path arrows laid out left-to-right in exact sequence |
| `Pool 2×` arrow labels | Four `Pool 2×` labels are readable near the first four adjacent main-path arrows in the original, though the original boxes overlap heavily and exact code semantics were not audited | Four `Pool 2×` labels placed on `Input→E1`, `E1→E2`, `E2→E3`, and `E3→E4`, reproducing the visual adjacency of the original without asserting that `Input→E1` performs pooling in code |
| `UpSample 2×` arrow label | Only a single `UpSample 2×` label appears in the original, near `E4→D3` | Single `UpSample 2×` label placed on `E4→D3`; no unprinted labels added on `D3→D2` or `D2→D1` |
| Skip connection x₃ | `Skip (x₃) + Cat`; `E3→D3` | Verbatim label and exact endpoints preserved |
| Skip connection x₂ | `Skip (x₂) + Cat`; `E2→D2` | Verbatim label and exact endpoints preserved |
| Skip connection x₁ | `Skip (x₁) + Cat`; `E1→D1` | Verbatim label and exact endpoints preserved |
| Auxiliary branch | `E4 → Coarse Head → Coarse Supervision` | Preserved as a two-segment branch |
| Legend | `Encoder (ConvBlock + SE)`, `Decoder (ConvBlock + SE)`, `Coarse Auxiliary Head`, `Skip Connection` | All four legend entries preserved verbatim |
| Per-layer spatial sizes, conv layer counts, channel semantics | Not printed in the original image (absent from the source, not merely illegible) | No inferred values added; boxes display only the exact strings printed in the original |

## Overlap Resolution Summary

| Visual Defect in Original | Fix Applied in Both `_v2` Redraws | Visual Check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Encoder boxes `E1/E2`, `E2/E3`, `E3/E4` collide; `Pool` text touches box borders | Aligned all 9 main-path boxes along a single horizontal baseline with positive gaps; placed `Pool 2×` labels cleanly in the open margin above each arrow | Fixed; zero text–border collisions |
| `E4/D3` collide; `UpSample` crowds the border | Separated `E4` and `D3`; moved `UpSample 2×` into the upper margin and routed the auxiliary branch cleanly upward | Fixed |
| Decoder boxes `D3/D2`, `D2/D1`, `D1/Output` collide | Separated into uniform-width boxes with dedicated inter-box gaps for arrows | Fixed |
| 3 purple skip curves cut right through crowded colored boxes | Routed as three orthogonal dashed channels at staggered heights underneath `E3/E2/E1` to the bottoms of `D3/D2/D1` | Fixed; zero box crossings or label occlusions |
| Two minor defects in our initial `_v1` redraw (not in original) | In `_v1`, arrow labels touched box edges and Arial lacked subscript glyphs (`₁₂₃`); preserved `_v1` untouched and generated `_v2` with increased label clearance and `DejaVu Sans` | `_v2` verified free of missing glyphs or border touches |

Note that rearranging the crowded layout clarifies reading order without auditing the underlying neural network code. Typography uses a clean hierarchy: 9.3 pt inside boxes, 8 pt for edge annotations, and 16 pt for the title. All PNGs were visually inspected; XML parsing of both SVGs confirmed 38 `<text>` elements and 0 `<image>` elements with all numbers and subscript skip labels intact; `pdffonts` confirmed embedded `DejaVu Sans` TrueType fonts (not outlined paths); and PNG dimensions are `3847×1977`. Both PDF and SVG deliverables remain fully text-editable and contain no private paths.

## Evaluation of the Two Skills

| Criterion | Academic Figure Skill (`1df9940dd0`) | K-Dense `scientific-visualization` (`a1043ef544`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ① Exact match on topology, numbers, titles, and links | Passed (see mapping table above; ambiguities inherent to the original image are not expanded into code-level claims) | Passed (identical transcription and mapping table) |
| ② Elimination of overlaps, clean fonts & alignment | Passed visual inspection | Passed visual inspection |
| ③ Editable SVG, PDF, and high-res PNG | Passed: 38 `<text>` / 0 `<image>` in SVG; embedded TrueType fonts in PDF | Passed: 38 `<text>` / 0 `<image>` in SVG; embedded TrueType fonts in PDF |
| ④ Security | Passed: restricted execution path is low-risk under Apache-2.0; corrected security table documented separately | Passed: selected sub-skill is low-risk under MIT (without endorsing the entire repo) |
| Verdict | **Worth adopting**: typography, palette, and vector export specs materially improve hand-scripted diagram delivery (note: it is a style/export specification, not an automated image-to-vector redrawing algorithm) | **Worth adopting**: local `style_context` and overwrite-safe multi-format `export_figure` are practical utilities (likewise not an automated image-understanding tool) |

Actual contribution of each skill: Academic provided typography, color-palette, and export specifications (`export-specs.md`); K-Dense provided `style_context`, `export_figure` (with non-overwrite guard, manifest generation, and 3-format export), and its palette. The layout coordinates and overlap removal were written in our Python rendering script inside an isolated venv — neither skill automatically parses or repairs raster input images.

## Final Deliverables (All Newly Created Without Overwriting Earlier Versions)

- Academic `_v2` SVG / PDF / PNG deliverables
- K-Dense `_v2` SVG / PDF / PNG deliverables
- Standalone Python generator script (executed inside an isolated venv; configured to refuse overwriting existing `_v2` outputs)

# E2 Close Reading of Two Papers: Recommended Exit X2 for Both (10-15 23:2x, Pending Approval by Liang Hu via Platform)

Close-reading cards: (wx). Lead spot-checked the original PDF text layers: for 003, 7,524 QC profiles, R² 0.948/0.963, and Lee case MAE 1.774 / RMSE 1.936 m/s; for 004, 1 million columns in Fortran at 54546.96 ms vs. JAX at 152.64 ms, and the authors' exact statement "focusing on numerical correctness and GPU performance rather than differentiability" (PDF page 2)—all consistent with the cards.

- (arXiv 2610.11405, Ma et al.): Recommend X2. Useful takeaways include 10 m hard anchoring + 10–300 m continuous profile + soft physical constraints; however, it requires trustworthy 10 m wind and RMW as inputs, whereas the 35–38% low bias in chains B1+B4 stems precisely from input assumptions, which this method cannot correct; moreover, it was trained and validated only on marine dropsondes and not validated over US landfall terrain. Code is not public; QC profile data are on Zenodo 21868265 (CC BY 4.0).
- (arXiv 2610.12662, Linck et al., NCAR LAFT): Recommend X2. Useful takeaways include the migration verification workflow of "cross-compiler envelope as per-variable tolerance + interface bridge unit tests + re-verification after GPU profiling"; however, it only validated a single Kessler call without differentiability, gradients, or coupling, offering no direct utility for current K/L/C issues. Code is public (github.com/NCAR/LAFT, Apache-2.0).
- Decision I made: Recommend X2 for both papers rather than X3/X4 — Why: neither is directly applicable to the current bottlenecks on this track (B is bottlenecked on inputs, while K/L/C are not doing physics migration) — Cost if wrong: if hybrid physics models or marine inflow are pursued later, they can be retrieved from the method cards when needed at minimal cost.
- Basis: The close-reading cards above (physical PDF pages marked); no other literature basis.

items.title: Close-Reading Card | Ma et al., arXiv:2610.11405v1 [Approved X2, Liang Hu 10-16]
items.text:
# Close-Reading Card | Ma et al., arXiv:2610.11405v1 [Approved X2, Liang Hu 10-16]

One-sentence verdict: The paper's "hard-anchored observed 10 m wind + learned 10–300 m profile shape" approach is worth cataloging as a hindcast / marine vertical-profile reconstruction method, but it cannot directly replace the landfalling station wind-field forecasts in `B1+B4` — nor can it fix the 35–38% low bias caused by operational pressure-deficit extrapolation and frozen-RMW assumptions; recommended outlet is **X2 (method card into knowledge base)** without model integration. [1]

Source and scope: Jian Ma et al., *A Physics-Constrained Implicit Profile Network for Continuous Reconstruction of Tropical Cyclone Near-Surface Wind Profiles*, 35-page PDF, downloaded copy SHA-256 `7743adf1c79e47313f289d9833e6dad32f35176f76c5c8aa570e1fc6f8ca3cd4`. All page numbers on this card refer to physical PDF pages, as the preprint has no journal pagination. [1]

## Methodology and Validation

- **Inputs**: Single-location 10 m radial and tangential wind components, storm maximum wind speed (`Vmax`), radius of maximum wind (`RMW`), normalized radius (`r/RMW`), sine and cosine of storm-relative azimuth, magnitude and sign of the Coriolis parameter, and storm center latitude/longitude, plus normalized target height `z`. As listed in Table 2 (PDF p. 8), environmental wind shear, storm translation speed, surface roughness, land-cover type, sea state, and radar VAD are **not** inputs to this model. The network predicts radial and tangential wind components continuously across `z ∈ [10, 300] m` (not the full boundary layer or free atmosphere) within roughly `10 × RMW` of the storm center (PDF p. 13). [1]
- **Architecture**: Continuous height encoding (`Fourier + RBF`), conditioning branch, `FiLM` residual blocks, and dual radial/tangential heads, hard-anchoring both 10 m wind components via `V(z) = V10 + ΔV(z) − ΔV(10 m)` (PDF pp. 9–11, Eqs. 12–17). Training minimizes a weighted Huber loss combined with six soft physical constraints: second-order vertical curvature penalty, hemisphere-consistent tangential wind sign, monotonic inflow-angle variation with height, `10–40 m` logarithmic profile adherence, `FiLM`/coupling regularization, and first-order vertical gradient bounds (PDF pp. 11–13, Eqs. 18–27). Note that the log-law term is a soft penalty rather than a full momentum-equation solve. [1]
- **Training and validation data**: 13,058 raw NOAA HRD dropsonde profiles across 93 tropical cyclones (`2001–2022`), reduced to 7,524 profiles after quality control (requiring at least one observation within `10 m ± 20 m` and ≥3 valid points in each of `10–100 m`, `100–200 m`, and `200–300 m`). For the 10 m anchor value: 4,951 profiles have a lowest measurement below 10 m, whereas the remaining 2,573 profiles have their lowest point between `10 m` and `30 m` and assign the nearest measurement as the nominal 10 m wind — meaning the "exact hard anchor" anchors to the assigned input value rather than guaranteeing zero physical error at true 10 m height (PDF pp. 3–5, Fig. 1). Data are split `8:1:1` grouped by storm and stratified by intensity, with normalization statistics computed strictly on the training split (PDF p. 13). [1]
- **Quantitative metrics**: On the held-out test set, overall `R²` is `0.948` (radial), `0.963` (tangential), and `0.963` (wind speed magnitude) (PDF pp. 13–14, Fig. 5); in the `Cat4+` regime, radial MAE/RMSE is `1.961 / 3.277 m/s` and tangential MAE/RMSE is `1.924 / 3.193 m/s` (PDF pp. 18–19, Tables 3–4) — note that point-by-point profile errors over open water must not be equated with peak wind errors at landfalling surface stations. In a case study on Hurricane Lee (2023) feeding SAR 10 m winds to reconstruct `100/200/300 m` fields, only 4 valid dropsondes fell within `±1 h`, yielding a 4-profile mean wind speed MAE/RMSE of `1.774 / 1.936 m/s` (PDF pp. 22–24, Figs. 14–15, Table 5). The Lee reconstruction covers only a narrow SAR swath over the ocean rather than full-storm validation, and per the NHC Tropical Cyclone Report, Lee made landfall in Nova Scotia as an extratropical cyclone — so this case study does not validate overland applicability for US hurricane landfalls. [1][15]
- **Internal critical reading**: In Table 7 (PDF p. 25), the curvature-violation rate of the `no_curv` ablation remains `0`, whereas `fit_only` is positive; thus the prose claim on p. 26 calling curvature regularization the "sole mechanism" is not supported by the single-term ablation table. Moreover, Tables 7 and 8 report internal physical-consistency proxy metrics rather than accuracy gains over traditional boundary-layer models. Figures 7–9 (PDF pp. 15–17) show individual case profiles that qualitatively track vertical trends, from which aggregate error statistics cannot be read directly. [1]

## Applicability to Track B

As recorded on our project page (lines 23–38) and execution report (lines 27–35, 67–82), both the 48 h Pangu and `OFCL` chains underpredict station winds by ~`35–38%`, driven primarily by operational pressure-deficit extrapolation, frozen `RMW`, and intensity input assumptions, leading `B1+B4` to be Shelved; furthermore, CLIMADA `H08` predicts 10 m winds with terrestrial exposure and gust averaging conventions that differ from this paper's dropsonde framework. Because Ma et al.'s network requires a reliable 10 m wind vector (plus `RMW` and `Vmax`) as a hard anchor, feeding it a 35–38% low-biased 10 m forecast wind will not self-correct the low bias; fundamentally, the model performs observation-conditioned marine profile reconstruction rather than standalone track/intensity-driven overland wind forecasting. Its potential utility is restricted to reconstructing `10–300 m` engineering inflow profiles in marine/coastal hindcasts where reliable 10 m observations exist — and even there, US events, coastal roughness transitions, extreme tails, vector wind direction, and 10 m input error propagation would have to be independently validated first (with no extrapolation above 300 m). [1]

## Availability of US Landfalling Hurricane Observations (By Instrument Category; Does Not Imply Complete Co-Located Profiles Per Event)

| Instrument | Public Archive, Temporal Coverage & Access | Relationship / Limitations Relative to This Method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dropsondes | NOAA HRD storm/flight archive pages provide direct downloads of `.avp.tar.gz` raw files, and high-resolution `.frd` aircraft files are available from 2002 onward. The paper trained on `2001–2022` and published its 7,524 QC'd profiles on Zenodo v2 (`profiles_json.zip`, 14.4 MB, CC BY 4.0, verified online), suitable for initial format inspection; matching raw dropsondes to specific landfall events requires storm-by-storm screening. [1][3][4][5] | Raw AVAPS files are un-QC'd and real-time messages have coarse vertical resolution; HRD's research-grade post-processed sonde archive requires contacting the data manager and is not directly downloadable in bulk, so the paper's QC'd JSON bundle must not be equated with HRD's full post-processed archive. Opportunistic marine/eyewall sampling, not continuous fixed-site overland monitoring. [5] |
| Radar VAD | NCEI NEXRAD Level-II archive spans 1991–present (radial velocities can be downloaded by station/time for custom VAD retrieval), and Level-III `NVW/48` VAD wind profiles can be queried by station/year. HRD P-3 airborne radar pages list storms from the 1990s–2021 with partial gridded wind fields/plots, without guaranteeing VAD files for every storm or altitude. [6][7] | VAD was not used as a training input in this paper; operational Level-III VAD reports wind barbs at ~1,000 ft increments, which generally cannot provide continuous fine resolution across `10–300 m`. Requires accounting for radar beam height, range, rainband coverage, QC, and spatiotemporal co-location; low-level gate availability is unverified. [6] |
| Buoys / C-MAN | NDBC / NCEI coastal and marine station archives cover Feb 1970–present; historical standard meteorological and continuous-wind records are downloadable by station-year via NDBC and NCEI HTTPS/THREDDS, filtered by landfall location and time. [8] | Single anemometer height per station, serving as a candidate near-10 m vector anchor rather than a `10–300 m` vertical profile; sensor elevation, averaging period, storm dropouts, and high-wind QC must be verified station by station. [8] |
| Portable wind towers (FCMP) | Legacy FCMP deployments (e.g., Katrina) previously had public tower location/summary indexes used in `2004–2008` landfall papers, but accessing FCMP's `collected-data-index` returned `"archived or suspended"`, so direct public bulk download cannot be guaranteed. [9] | Legacy FCMP towers measured primarily at `5/10 m` overland, which is insufficient to validate a `10–300 m` profile; listed only as a historical reference rather than an actionable dataset. |
| ASOS (single-level supplement) | NCEI ASOS/AWOS archives provide hourly, local climatological, and 1/5-minute surface wind records by station and year; Project B already maintains a curated station pool. [14] | Provides near-10 m surface anchors / independent single-level verification only, not multi-level vertical profiles; subject to landfall power/comms dropouts, anemometer height, and averaging-time issues documented on the Project B page. [14] |

## Public Code and Parameter Provenance

Page 30 of the PDF provides only HRD and Zenodo data availability links with no code repository URL; querying GitHub for `Smartyphoon-BL3D` and `Smartyphoon BL3D` returned zero public code repositories. The Zenodo record (https://zenodo.org/records/21868265, v2 published/modified `2026-08-10`) contains only the QC'd dropsonde profile dataset (`profiles_json.zip`), not model weights or training/inference code. [1][3]

Missing parameters and reproducibility boundaries: while the main text gives the loss equations and initial loss weights (Table 6, PDF p. 25), the exact network width and depth, number of Fourier frequencies, RBF width hyperparameters, optimizer settings and learning-rate schedule, storm-by-storm train/val/test split lists, random seeds, software package versions, estimation formulas for surface roughness and friction velocity, and exact SAR retrieval product IDs were **not found** in the main text, figures, tables, references, or Zenodo record, and must not be guessed. Also note that "sparse" in this paper refers to spatial sparsity across the storm rather than ultra-sparse vertical sampling of only 1–2 heights: the QC filter explicitly requires ≥3 valid points per 100 m vertical bin (PDF p. 5). [1][3]

Recommended outlet: **X2 (method into knowledge base)** — the 10 m hard-anchoring formulation, soft physical constraints, storm-grouped split against data leakage, and SAR-to-profile reconstruction workflow merit a method card, whereas **X3** (missing code/hyperparameters, unvalidated overland, and unable to fix Track B's low-biased 10 m anchor) and **X4** (Track B shelving conditions remain in effect) are not recommended. Recommendation only; no deployment actions taken.

Page-reading audit: read the text layer across all physical pages 1–35 of the PDF; additionally rendered and visually inspected p. 16 (Figs. 7–9) and p. 22 (Fig. 14, Hurricane Lee). For Figs. 1, 3, 5, 6, 10–13, and 15, read captions and main-text discussion without digitizing individual axis ticks (unprinted fine-grained numbers are treated as `"not in text"`); read the reference list on pp. 33–35. External data archives were queried independently during this review. [1]

## Sources

[1] https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.11405
[3] https://zenodo.org/records/21868265
[4] https://www.aoml.noaa.gov/hrd/data_sub/dropsonde.html
[5] https://aoml.noaa.gov/hrd/Storm_pages/sondeformat.html
[6] https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/radar/next-generation-weather-radar
[7] https://www.aoml.noaa.gov/hrd/data_sub/radar.html
[8] https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/archive/accession/NDBC-CMANWx
[9] https://fcmp.ce.ufl.edu/collected-data-index
[14] https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/land-based-station/automated-surface-weather-observing-systems
[15] https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/AL132023_Lee.pdf

items.title: Close-Reading Card | Linck et al., arXiv:2610.12662v1 [Approved X2, Liang Hu 10-16]
items.text:
# Close-Reading Card | Linck et al., arXiv:2610.12662v1 [Approved X2, Liang Hu 10-16]

One-sentence conclusion: What can be borrowed from LAFT is the migration workflow of "variable-by-variable comparison against Fortran within a compiler envelope + interface-bridge unit testing + re-verification after GPU profiling", rather than an off-the-shelf differentiable WRF/ACE2 weather physics module; recommended disposition is X2 (method archiving), as a recommendation only without immediate implementation. [2]

Source and scope: Iris Linck et al., Evaluating LLMs for Translating Legacy Fortran Atmospheric Physics to GPU-Accelerated JAX, 21-page PDF, SHA-256 `3c79ea5ba95e2dcc9a0f758486a3f36c15a8cfd15a81216088a0738ffdc20b2e`. Page numbers in this card refer to physical PDF pages. [2]

## Methodology, Itemized Verification, and Diagnosing Discrepancies

- LAFT uses Tree-sitter on Fortran to extract procedures, signatures, dimensions, and module dependencies (translating dependencies first); rule-based generation builds a Fortran index-order (ncol,nz) ↔ JAX (nz,ncol) bridge, transposing rank≥2 arrays inside JIT and returning outputs; the model translates only the physics core. Unit tests for the bridge's round-trip shape/layout/state are separated from physical numerical consistency. The current bridge converts all non-character arrays uniformly to float64 without preserving integer/logical array types (not used by the Kessler interface), so it cannot yet be called a general-purpose Fortran bridge (PDF pp. 5–7, Fig. 1). [2]
- Four passes per procedure: draft → JIT safety → vectorization/control flow → final review; scalar initialization is translated only to plain Python. The verification ladder proceeds from lint (forbidding in-kernel NumPy/I/O/redundant layout transforms) → dummy-input wrapper/core JIT execution and finite-value checks → running the full JAX driver on fixed-seed shared inputs → variable-by-variable comparison against Fortran on identical inputs, checking shapes on both sides, physically reasonable ranges for potential temperature, and non-negativity of water vapor / cloud water / rain water / precipitation / humidity. Each stage reads fresh results, exception tracebacks, and error reports; failure logs record the failed stage, summary, and modified files, allowing up to 5 repair attempts, each rerunning from lint; after performance repairs, the entire numerical ladder is likewise rerun (PDF pp. 8–11). [2]
- "Tolerance" is not an arbitrary relative-error percentage: running the same Kessler Fortran code on the same input across 22 builds—spanning GNU/Intel/NVIDIA/Cray compilers, optimization levels / floating-point settings / CPU and OpenACC A100—yields 15 distinct outputs, defining a per-variable maximum absolute difference envelope εv across all compiler combinations; JAX's maximum absolute difference Ev against the baseline is accepted only if `Ev≤εv` holds for every variable alongside structural and physical checks (PDF pp. 9–10, Eqs. 1–2). MAE and relative RMSE are also reported, but the gate is the maximum absolute difference. This envelope applies only to a single call, this specific input set, and these machines, and does not prove consistency across rare branches or long integrations (an explicit limitation noted by the authors on PDF p. 10). [2]
- Locating performance discrepancies: jax.profiler.trace counts dispatches/synchronizations/copies, while optimized HLO counts fusion/scatter/gather/while operations; running 1000 vs. 250 columns with 56 levels distinguishes column-serial execution from batched execution; column-by-column loops are flagged as critical, scatter as high, and unfused gather as advisory only. The Qwen version used Qwen to generate the draft and Claude Code to perform repairs; its sequential column loop remained unresolved after 5 performance repair attempts, passing numerical checks but failing the production GPU performance gate (PDF pp. 7–8, 11, 13–14, Tables 1–2). [2]

## Key Figures and Comparability Baselines

| Item | Original Figures and Page Numbers | Limitations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Numerical accuracy | Single call with 128 columns × 56 levels, 6 outputs; Table 3 (PDF p. 16) worst-case across 4 translations vs. Fortran envelope: potential temperature 5.7e−14/1.1e−13 K, water vapor 6.2e−17/7.1e−17 kg/kg, cloud water 2.9e−17/5.7e−17, rain water 2.1e−17/3.3e−17, precipitation 1.1e−19/1.4e−19, RH 4.1e−13/9.8e−13%; ratios 0.42–0.87. | Cannot claim equivalence for long-range weather forecasts or microphysical trajectories. |
| Execution structure | 1000 columns, 56 levels: Claude/GPT 292 XLA ops / 1 while entry, Gemini 138/1, Qwen 190546/1000 (PDF p. 14, Tables 1–2). | Identical numerical correctness does not mean identical GPU efficiency; Fig. 2 axes verified as logarithmic. |
| GPU/CPU | Single A100 40 GB, JAX 0.6.2, CPU baseline gfortran -O2 single core; at 1M columns, serial Fortran is 54546.96 ms, Gemini JAX 152.64 ms (357×), Claude 632.06, GPT 619.74; at 10k columns, Gemini is 3.05 ms, CPU 496.194 ms, Qwen 6271.75 ms (PDF pp. 12, 15–16, Fig. 2). | Median of 5 warm runs after 1 JIT warm-up; synchronizes only the first output; excludes initial compilation and input/output PCIe transfers; not "357× speedup for full WRF". |
| GPU/GPU | 50 columns OpenACC 0.218 vs. Gemini JAX 0.74 ms; 10k columns 2.96 vs. 3.05; 100k columns 54.38 vs. 16.30; 1M columns 751.16 vs. 152.64 (PDF pp. 17–18, Fig. 3). | OpenACC is faster at small scales, JAX is faster at large scales; hardware- and implementation-dependent. |
| Interface overhead | At 1M columns, stage-summed bridge cost for C-contiguous input is 1036.640 ms (H2D 319.061, D2H 706.927); for true Fortran-order memory input, 1468.771 ms (PDF pp. 16–17, Table 4). | Stage-wise estimate, not an end-to-end production call measurement; uses a different timing baseline than the 152.64 ms kernel, so 357× cannot be directly claimed as an end-to-end gain. |

## Specific Applicability and Non-Applicability to Our Tracks

- K "AI-Forecast-Driven WRF": Lines 13–16 and 27–34 of the current project involve paired simulations driving the same WRF with Pangu/GFS, where the bottlenecks lie in driving-field alignment, real boundary conditions, and thunderstorm location / wind gust verification—not microphysics translation. The staged verification methodology can be borrowed if we replace an individual WRF physics kernel in the future: first conducting identical-initial-state Fortran↔JAX variable-by-variable single-step comparisons, bridge isomorphism tests, cross-compiler envelope checks, and special-branch tests before moving to multi-step/coupled verification; this paper does not couple Kessler JAX into WRF and does not alter current Track K criteria or tasks. [2]
- L "Convection-Allowing AI": Lines 13–25 and 44–52 on StormCast gust hit rates vs. HRRR are forecast-physics evaluation tasks; LAFT neither produces 3 km gust weights nor improves hit rates. Only if a separate AI↔physics coupling is built could one first benchmark column physics processes as device-resident vectorized kernels and then test whether moist-process outputs/gradients remain stable; this is a proposed verification sequence, not a coupled experiment completed by the paper. [2]
- C "ACE2 Climate Emulator": Lines 13–20 and 58–64 currently test ACE2-ERA5 cold-season 10 m wind tails / GEV / POT. LAFT offers a reference for verifying single-step equivalence and long-term statistics separately in idealized differentiable physics modules, but single-call Kessler numerical equivalence cannot be transplanted into ACE2 extreme-value reliability, 50-year return wind speed corrections, or coupling gains; there is no need to replace ACE2 results already run. [2]
- Differentiability audit: The authors explicitly state on PDF p. 2 that "this paper focuses on numerical correctness and GPU performance rather than differentiability"; no gradient checks, backpropagation costs, long-integration adjoint stability, or AI parameter assimilation results are provided. That JAX supports automatic differentiation does not mean this Kessler code—containing booleans, thresholds, and substepping control—is "gradient-usable" in a scientific sense. Thus, for K/L/C, one can only borrow the design principle of "if building a hybrid model later, validate inputs/outputs and gradients independently first", and cannot list it as a validated capability. [2]

## Open-Source Status and Unknown Parameters

Open Research on PDF p. 19 provides a Zenodo concept DOI; opening it redirects to version v1.0.0, with a 4.2 MB software ZIP under Apache-2.0 linked on the Zenodo page. The GitHub repository is public under Apache-2.0, with the latest default-branch commit via API dated 2026-10-09 21:03:56 UTC, SHA `ae95165562f4beb6669e2fba7cf947a16035d20d` (recording only the source platform's original timestamp here, not as a log timestamp for our track); "Zenodo modified 2026-10-15" does not equate to a new code commit. Source code and reproduction packages are public, though they were not executed in this round. [11][12] The latest repository commit date was verified via the GitHub commits API. [13]

The paper specifies test scales, hardware, seeds, compiler envelopes, and the Kessler environment (PDF pp. 10–13); numerical tolerances for rare-branch input sets, specific convective events, and larger physics schemes are not provided and should be recorded as "not found in text", without extrapolating from the existing single-step tolerance assumptions. On p. 18, the authors state that P3/Droplet work is still ongoing and EAMxx integration is only preliminary, so an end-to-end WRF implementation cannot be claimed. [2]

Recommended disposition: X2 (method archiving). Distinction from X3: although code is available, the paper covers only a single small warm-rain process verified on a single call, lacking coupling and gradient evidence applicable to K/L/C. Distinction from X4: Liang Hu's brief here only asks for an assessment of methodological reference value, and current K/L/C problems are not Fortran migrations; there is no need to spin up a new quick trial based on the 357× figure.

Page-reading audit: Physical PDF pages 1–21 were read sequentially through the text layer; Fig. 2 on p. 15 was additionally rendered from the same PDF to verify axes and curves, while Fig. 1 and Fig. 3 were cross-checked against figure captions, tables, and main text without independently reading indistinct pixel-level numbers. The authors' code repository and Zenodo page were verified separately and are not counted as paper pages. [2]

[11] https://zenodo.org/records/22696826
[12] https://github.com/NCAR/LAFT
[13] https://api.github.com/repos/NCAR/LAFT/commits?per_page=1
