| Observation averaging window | 1 h mean centered on forecast valid time (WSPD); gust takes maximum WMAX in the same window | Convention (AI output is instantaneous / 6 h step, requiring a unified definition) | Mesonet definition card |
| 10 m representing 30–120 m flight altitude | Proxy only | **Assumption**, limitation written into conclusions | To be checked |

## Open Items and Next Steps
- Compute location (tightened by Liang Hu on 10-14, communicated by Node A on 10-15): the workstation does not run computations or store compute data; solvers, training, batch cases, and large downloads must all run and be stored on Colab or CRC/TACC; the workstation only holds scripts, small individual results <200 MB, figures, and reports; if >1 GB must be temporarily placed on the workstation, report to Node A first. CRC group storage is at ~95%, so new large datasets should prioritize TACC /work or /scratch; CRC defaults to a single node via resource request +, separating pre-check and submission into two commands. Every task brief must explicitly state which machine runs the computation and where results are stored.
- Colab policy (communicated by parent project on 10-15, aligned with Liang Hu's "use Colab heavily at this stage, no CU cap"): no single-experiment cap is set, voiding previous task brief limits of "≤20 CU", "≤10 CU", and "≤5 CU"; if a single experiment is expected to exceed >100 CU, stop first and report to Node A via `--report`; must run `colab stop` when finished; dispatch to only one executor per round. Supercomputer single-job limit of ≤50 SU remains unchanged.
- Hierarchy (Root Lead 10-14): this node is Tier 2 and does not open Tier 3 sub-projects; task dispatching goes at most two hops (bot → tool), and task briefs must not allow tool bots to delegate further.
- **Digital Twin Wind Tunnel boundary established (10-14)**: the counterpart has no forecast-driven cases and does not perform Mesonet/ASOS verification, so Step 1 has no duplication. Step 2 demonstration is conditionally feasible: time-varying inflow intensity requires development first, earliest around early November (counterpart's estimate); wind direction cannot vary continuously within a single run and can only be split into sectors, each using its own geometry; neutral stratification only, unable to represent low wind speeds under stable stratification. Forcing format: CSV, UTC, 10 min resolution, 100 m wind speed/direction (meteorological convention), preferably accompanied by 10–300 m profiles and stability (Obukhov length or Ri); select several near-neutral hours with wind direction steady within a single sector. Formally propose after Step 1 conclusions are out, for the counterpart to evaluate scheduling.
- C2 virtual observation network (741 points, 50/100/150 m above ground/rooftop, no 30 m, 1 s three-component) can be cited read-only at the 50 and 100 m levels to compute urban-to-open-terrain speed-up/slow-down ratios; must note: rooftop point heights are measured from the rooftop, development-case inflow has not passed equilibrium acceptance, and same-model twin has not been validated against observations. Candidate next step (after Step 1 passes its gate): use it to derive conversion ratios from "open-station forecast → various urban locations".
- Review verdict rendered: withdraw the claim of "no precedent" for urban areas and narrow the US station gap; revise Step 1 to 2022 training / 2023 verification, 10-year climatology, pre-selecting the AI source in the training year, evaluating gusts only at 1-minute stations, reporting observation definitions separately, and adding logistic-regression probabilistic forecasts. Revisions sent to ideas.

## Literature Basis
- Bremnes, Nipen & Seierstad 2024, NPG 31:247–257, doi 10.5194/npg-31-247-2024, abstract (PDF p. 1): across 183 stations in Norway, Pangu 10 m wind is slightly worse than HRES, and post-processing improves global models more — supporting "apply unified bias correction before comparing".

# Task Brief: A1 Step 1 — Multi-Station Multi-Month Verification of AI Near-Surface Wind Forecasts around OKC (2026-10-14)

## Objective
Answer one question: do off-the-shelf global AI weather forecasts (after applying the same simple bias correction) forecast 10 m winds and "no-fly" exceedance events at stations around OKC no worse than GFS, and substantially better than persistence and climatology? This serves as the prerequisite gate for whether the "AI forecast → urban low-altitude wind → fly/no-fly" chain is worth extending into urban downscaling.

## Deliverables (Write to )
1. : One-sentence conclusion + pass/fail status for each criterion + main table (each forecast source × lead times 6/12/24/36/48/72 h: pre- and post-correction wind speed MAE, bias, wind direction error; hit rate, false alarm ratio, CSI, and Brier score across threshold bins) + limitations.
2. , hourly station sample CSVs (small files, station time series only, do not store gridded fields), and two figures (MAE vs. lead time; 8 m/s bin CSI vs. lead time) with data sources noted in the figure corner annotations.
3. Batch-ready scripts: take "station list + time period + forecast source list" as input so switching cities/years requires no code changes; log data-fetching time, data volume, and CUs per "station-year".
4. : URL, version, download timestamp, and excerpted terms of use for each data source; items requiring citation must also be appended to (author, year, venue, link/DOI).

## Configuration (Fixed, do not alter; if anything is genuinely infeasible, document the reason, adopt the closest feasible alternative, and note it in results.md)
- Forecast sources: models in the AWS AIWP archive (NOAA/CIRA, Radford 2025 BAMS 10.1175/BAMS-D-24-0057.1) that include 10 m u/v — at least GraphCast, Pangu, and FourCastNet v2 (use all available), initialized at 00/12 UTC; benchmarked against operational GFS forecasts (AWS noaa-gfs-bdp-pds, 0.25°, 10 m u/v). Do not run AI models yourself.
- Time period: ≥12 consecutive months in a year covered by both AIWP and GFS (e.g., full year 2023).
- Observations: ≥8 Oklahoma Mesonet stations within 60 km of downtown OKC (including OKCE, OKCN, OKCW, SPEN, NRMN; select the rest yourself and document coordinates and surface exposure), using WSPD/WDIR/WMAX (10 m) from 5-min files; ASOS may be used optionally as a supplement. Verify and excerpt Mesonet data terms of use first.
- Pairing: bilinear interpolation from grid points to stations; observations use 1 h mean centered on valid time (list vector-averaged wind speed/direction separately), and gusts use the maximum WMAX within the same window.
- Baselines: persistence (observation at initialization time), station-month-hour climatology, and GFS.
- Correction: apply the same linear correction across all forecast sources (per station and per lead time, wind speed a+b·U, and gusts regressed from WMAX against corrected wind speed); train on the first 8 months and verify on the last 4 months (or rolling monthly leave-one-out; choose one and state clearly), with the verification period strictly excluded from any fitting.
- Threshold bins: sustained wind 6/8/10/12 m/s, gust 10/13/15 m/s — these are **assumed bins** (literature verification of UAV operational limits is conducted separately); report all bins.
- Criteria (pre-registered, do not modify after running): post-correction best AI source has 24 h and 48 h wind speed MAE no more than 5% worse than post-correction GFS, and ≥15% better than both persistence and climatology; 8 m/s bin 24 h CSI is no lower than GFS. Passing all three = "AI upstream is sufficient"; attach a bootstrap 95% confidence interval (resampled by day) to every difference.

## Boundaries
- Compute: Colab (either CPU or A100 is fine; Liang Hu places no CU cap at this stage; must run `colab stop` when finished and finally `colab ls` to confirm no active sessions remain). Process large files only on Colab, and transfer only small files such as station time series (<200 MB total) back to the workstation; do not use supercomputers.
- Do not download data from unknown sources; do not store any tokens or passwords.
- For parameters not given in papers, search first; if not found, make an assumption and label it "assumed".
- Reply only with the conclusion, criterion pass/fail status, and file paths; no need to ask for approval midway

# A1 Step 1: OKC AI Near-Surface Wind Forecast Verification—Incomplete, Data Gate (10-14 14:30 ET)

One-sentence conclusion: Currently cannot judge that “upstream AI is sufficient”; redistribution permission for observational data for the annual comparison has not yet been confirmed, and OKCN/OKCW specified in the task brief were already decommissioned in the years archived by AIWP GraphCast. **This is not evidence that AI is inferior to GFS, but rather that verification has not yet been conducted.**

Pre-defined criteria item by item: Post-correction AI 24/48 h MAE not worse than GFS by more than 5% = Unevaluated; advantage over persistence and climatology both ≥15% = Unevaluated; 8 m/s tier 24 h CSI not lower than GFS = Unevaluated. Daily bootstrap 95% CI = No data, uncalculated; do not record “unevaluated” as failed.

Main table (all missing values indicate uncalculated in this round, not 0):

| Forecast Source | Lead Time h | Pre-/Post-Correction MAE, Bias, Wind Direction Error | Sustained Wind 6/8/10/12 m/s and Gust 10/13/15 m/s: Hit Rate, False Alarm Rate, CSI, Brier |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GraphCast, Pangu, FourCastNet v2, GFS, Persistence, Climatology | 6/12/24/36/48/72 | Unevaluated | Unevaluated |

Empirical data retrieval verification: Official AWS directory confirms the three designated AIWP 2023 files and GFS 2023-01-01 f024 GRIB2 can be located; an official 2023 Mesonet MDF lists stations such as OKCE/SPEN/NRMN, but does not include OKCN/OKCW. Mesonet retired sites page explicitly states OKCW ended on 2015-06-09 and OKCN on 2018-05-07; GraphCast archives start from 2022, so a continuous year containing both these stations and GraphCast does not exist. See and https://mesonet.org/about/mesonet-sites/retired-sites , https://registry.opendata.aws/aiwp/. The task brief allows “closest feasible approach”: still-operating OKCE/SPEN/NRMN and other stations within radius after verifying coordinates and station history should be substituted for OKCN/OKCW; currently the official geography metadata CSV is empty, so we cannot claim to have assembled 8 valid stations within 60 km.

Terms of use gate: Official sources state that Mesonet data is copyrighted and non-media redistribution is prohibited; the result md/png/station CSV in this directory will be automatically displayed publicly, so station CSV containing hourly observations cannot be directly delivered according to the task brief. Research licensing and the scope of publicly releasable derived data must first be confirmed by rights holders (https://mesonet.org/about/data-access-and-pricing). This round did not create a Mesonet account, did not use credentials, did not pull observations or grid fields in bulk, and did not launch Colab; CU attributed to this task is 0. Two empirical performance figures cannot be plotted without valid data; is a machine-readable unevaluated state, containing no fabricated values.

Code progress: is a correction/statistics **prototype** that accepts paired station CSVs with lawful licensing (input source list, 8/4 month split, 6 lead times, threshold statistics); executed in isolated scratch using clearly labeled synthetic 8-station full-year data, command ran successfully and produced 36 summary records. This only proves prototype execution, not meteorological performance. Data retrieval, bilinear interpolation, 1 h observation window, co-located sample screening, daily bootstrap, formal figures / station CSVs, and per-station-year CU accounting have not yet been implemented; the prototype must not replace the full deliverables specified in the task brief.

Limitations: Official pages only describe representative station sites and cannot be used to judge underlying surfaces for specific stations; sustained wind and gust thresholds are assumptions pre-set by the task brief, not flight licensing standards. Note also that persistence at the 00/12 UTC initialization time requires zero-lead observations; the prototype can only back-query from paired target times, and formal retrieval must separately supplement initialization observations.

Next step gate: Confirm permissions for Mesonet scientific research use and hourly observation/chart display; finalize replacement list after verifying geographical locations and surface conditions of valid 2023 stations, then handle only remote slicing in Colab; do not touch existing results or publish unauthorized observations. If lawful authorization is unavailable, openly licensed ASOS can be used as an independent alternative experiment, but cannot be passed off as satisfying Mesonet criteria.

## Ratio Distribution of 100 m Forecast Wind to 10 m Observation (10-14 Supplement)

Both NOAA/CIRA AIWP official README and AWS data directory state that FourCastNet v2-small contains 100 m u/v, belonging to the `FOUR_v200_GFS` archive alongside 10 m u/v (see ). This round did not download this variable, has no station time series, and has not obtained publicly shareable paired Mesonet 10 m observations; therefore, ratio distributions, quantiles, and sample sizes are all “uncalculated”, not zero. Corrections and three criteria of the original task remain unchanged; 100 m is not part of the criteria. Once approved in the future, first bilinearly interpolate 100 m u/v to stations, dividing the magnitude by the 1 h average wind speed of the 10 m observation at the same valid time; invalid or zero denominators must be explicitly eliminated and quantities reported. The ratio describes paired differences across heights and across forecast/observation sources, and cannot be directly used as an urban 30–120 m wind profile conversion factor.

Literature comparison: Bremnes, Nipen, Seierstad (2024), *Nonlinear Processes in Geophysics* 31:247–257, DOI https://doi.org/10.5194/npg-31-247-2024, Abstract and Section 2: 183 Norwegian SYNOP stations; raw Pangu 10 m wind speed was slightly inferior to ECMWF global model, post-processing yielded greater improvement for coarse-resolution global models. This supports the design of pairing stations and applying corrections to each source, but the Norwegian Pangu/HRES ranking cannot infer the AIWP/GFS ranking in OKC.

# A1 Deep Research Verification and Preliminary Assessment (2026-10-14)
Report: (Over 32 sources are all Google redirect links; citation check: 1/5 DOIs searchable, the remaining 4 are formatting errors or dataset DOIs).
Supporting: Grok quick check verification.

## Itemized Verification
| DR Claim | Verification | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| South Asian Monsoon 458 stations: AI model errors against observations are 15–45% larger than against reanalysis; AIFS is the most consistent, followed by GraphCast and GenCast | Verified against arXiv 2509.01879 abstract ("forecast errors up to 15-45% larger than those relative to reanalysis"; AIFS most consistent); abstract does not mention MAE, does not mention ERA5, and contains no breakdown figures for wind; DR's variable-specific ranking (zonal wind GraphCast/FCN best, meridional wind AIFS best) unverified | Adopt qualitative conclusion (abstract only); do not adopt variable-specific ranking |
| WeatherNext 3: 10 m/100 m wind 0.1° output; ML6 report states 100 m wind MAE is 29% lower than IFS, 6 months in Benelux, trading imbalance cost reduced by €465,000 | Sources are Google blogs and consulting firm industry reports, not peer-reviewed; WN3 does not open-source weights | Lead, do not adopt figures |
| CorrDiff Abu Dhabi 200 m (driven by FourCastNet), slightly outperforms GEFS within 36–48 h, but worse at 5–7 days | Source is UNDP/Neuralio report, original text not opened | Lead |
| SpLIIF is 10–20% better than CorrDiff and interpolation | Abstract level only, source unclear | Do not adopt |
| Verification of AI global models against US Mesonet/ASOS/urban stations: Not found; Quantification of gap before and after post-processing: Not found | Consistent with Grok; but for post-processing, DR missed Bremnes 2024 NPG (we have verified) | Adopt "US station verification is a blank"; do not adopt "no quantification of post-processing" |
| Forecast-driven 30–150 m urban microscale (LES/LBM) simulation: No successful precedents found | Consistent with the digital twin wind tunnel track (they haven't done it either); WindAware mentioned by Grok (Chrit 2024, WRF-LES 100 m + LSTM, Chicago, validated against ASOS/soundings) is an approximate precedent, which DR missed | Adopt "blank" but note WindAware as an approximate precedent (content unverified) |
| EU 2021/664: U-space meteorological information service is a mandatory service, wind speed in m/s, wind direction relative to true north; Member States may set thresholds, USSP verifies against authorization; no specific values for resolution and update frequency | Regulation exists, Article 12 being meteorological information services is known; unable to open original text in this round | Adopt qualitative (pending verification against original text) |
| FAA UTM wind/turbulence stratified at 3000 ft, surface SPECI threshold | Unverified | Lead |
| Industry wind limits: Consumer grade 8–12, professional grade 12–15, fixed-wing 15–20 m/s, operators apply 75% discount | Source is commercial blog | Do not adopt; thresholds remain "assumptions", but bins 6–15 m/s fall within this range |
| ASTM vertical rate grading, F3389 | Irrelevant to wind limits | Do not adopt |
| CROCUS Chicago data on ESS-DIVE; NYS Mesonet 17-station LiDAR; JU2003 has no public download | CROCUS and NYS Mesonet are consistent with the known list of the digital twin wind tunnel track; DOI format error unverified | Adopt as data lead |
| Conclusions "WN3 + cost-loss proves economic closed loop", "Recommend directly performing generative downscaling to 30–150 m" | Report's own inferences, based on industry reports | Do not adopt |

## Preliminary Assessment of A1 (Pending)
1. **Upstream Tier**: Literature consistently shows that AI global models against station observations perform comparably to or slightly worse than ECMWF operational models, with a smaller advantage than against reanalysis; statistical correction yields large gains. There is no published verification against US stations (including OKC)—Step 1 (AIWP vs. ASOS, comparing against GFS after unified correction) serves as both a threshold and a blank, and the design holds up.
2. **Urban Tier**: There are no published successful precedents for forecast-driven urban 30–150 m microscale simulations (the closest are WindAware and CorrDiff 200 m, both with unverified content); this is A1's potential novelty, but the digital twin wind tunnel line's workflow currently only reaches neutral stratification and sector division, with a demonstration at the earliest in early November.
3. **Decision-making Tier**: Regulations (FAA Part 107, EASA Open Category, EU 2021/664) do not provide numerical values for wind speed limits; thresholds can only be set according to aircraft model/operator, and A1's use of multi-tiered thresholds + probability/exceedance scoring is a reasonable approach.
4. **Recommendation Level**: Maintain "High" (followed by Liang Hu); keep Step 1 unchanged; Step 2 to be decided after Step 1 passes the gate.

items.title: Verdict: A1 literature conclusions and step 1 design (2026-10-14)
items.text:
# Verdict: A1 Literature Conclusions and Step 1 Design (2026-10-14)
Reviewers: E · Gemini, A · GPT-6, D · GLM, 3/3 valid, all "supported with reservations". Lead personally verified: local cards Onodera 2021, Kiseleva 2024, Resler 2024, Stromberg 2026, Zhang 2025 all present; running script in ideas, lines 13–16, 28, 62, 76–79; WeatherReal arXiv 2409.09371 abstract (station observations verifying AI and numerical models, no US/GFS details mentioned).

## Required Changes
1. **Withdraw "No precedent for forecast-driven urban 30–150 m microscale simulations"** (unanimous among all three). Precedents for NWP-driven urban LES/LBM already exist: Onodera 2021 WRF→CityLBM (OKC), Kiseleva 2024 COSMO→PALM (Stuttgart 100 m LiDAR), Resler 2024 ICON-D2 forecast→PALM (Prague), Zhang 2025 WRF→GPU-LBM (local card); Muñoz-Esparza 2025 Urban Climate 60:102334 WRF→FastEddy 5 m (cited by Reviewer A, not personally verified). The blank is narrowed down to: **AI global forecast-driven urban building-resolving microscale simulations, as well as the verification of 30–150 m against simple baselines and fly/no-fly decisions under multi-day continuous forecasts**. In addition: CorrDiff 200 m and WindAware 100 m are horizontal grids, not flight altitudes.
2. **Narrow down "blank in US station verification"**: WeatherReal (arXiv 2409.09371), Aurora, etc., already have overall verifications including US stations; Brewer et al. 2025 WAF GraphCast→WRF against MADIS wind (cited by Reviewer A); CastCheck and NCAR BEACON are non-peer-reviewed examples (cited by Reviewer D). Change to: No published verifications found for multi-model AIWP vs. GFS on OKC with unified station-level correction, scored against fly/no-fly thresholds (search is non-exhaustive).
3. **Revise Step 1 temporal split and climatology baseline**: Training on the first 8 months of 2023 and verifying on the last 4 months fragments seasonality; the script uses the single year of 2022 for month-by-month and hour-by-hour climatology, resulting in a baseline that is too noisy and weak. Change to: **Full-year 2022 training for correction (GraphCast archives available from 2022-01), full-year 2023 verification; climatology uses 10-year ASOS observations from 2013–2022**.
4. **Predefine the "best AI source"**: Select one source in the training year 2022 based on post-corrected 24 h MAE (including both GFS/IFS initializations, with all sources still reported), and evaluate the gate criteria only on this source in 2023; the same source must simultaneously satisfy both 24 h and 48 h MAE conditions as well as the CSI condition; when the 95% interval crosses the boundary, report "point estimate passed, statistically uncertain", which does not count as passing. Change "24–48 h" on the project page to "24 h and 48 h".
5. **Gust truncation bias** (script verified: fit uses only rows with gusts, event drops NaN): METAR only reports gust when a gust occurs; gust correction and the 10/13/15 m/s bins are only evaluated at stations with 1-minute data; METAR station gusts are not scored.
6. **Report observation criteria separately**: Sustained winds are split into two groups—all stations use METAR 2-minute values (homogeneous), and 1-minute stations additionally report 1 h averages; do not mix them. Record anemometer type (different gust averaging periods of 3 s / 5 s) and height for each station.
7. **Brier**: The current 0/1 Brier is merely misclassification rate; rename and report as is; add an additional set of probabilistic forecasts (fit logistic regression in the training year to provide exceedance probabilities), report true Brier and reliability diagrams—"probabilistic skill" should only be claimed based on this.
8. **Revise regulatory phrasing**: The four mandatory services under EU 2021/664 Article 3(2) do not include weather, while Article 3(3) allows Member States to add Article 12 weather services; AMC imposes a 30 s / 5 min time limit on forwarding observations/forecasts; Member States may set maximum/minimum wind values. Revise to "there is no uniform wind speed value applicable to all drones". (Reviewer A, original text not personally verified, wording revised based on reviewer's citation.)
9. **Corrections to the literature verification table**: arXiv 2509.01879 full text is readable (MAE against 458 stations is 15–45% higher than against ERA5, "up to"; variable-specific wind component ranking see Figure 2, which is for the Indian monsoon region and wind components, not to be extrapolated); arXiv 2609.10564 is for 10 m wind, the difference between GraphCast and HRES is not significant, and for high winds ≥10.8 m/s, FCN3 is best while HRES underestimates most severely (Reviewer E read full text); Bremnes 2024 uses quantile neural network probabilistic post-processing, not linear MOS; AIWP GraphCast from 2022-01, FCNv2/Pangu from 2020-10; manufacturer specifications are verifiable (DJI Mini 4 Pro 10.7 m/s, Mavic 3 Pro 12 m/s), but operational limits have no numerical source citation.

## For Reference Only
- Literature comparison baselines are mostly HRES/IFS, which does not foreshadow whether AI wins or loses against GFS (D).
- AIFS applying IMPROVER operational post-processing (arXiv 2504.12672, cited by D) can be added as literature evidence, unverified.
- Bae 2025 ERL (addc84) is an emulator of CFD, not an observational wind validation at 30–150 m (A).

## Unadopted Objections
- None. The "High" recommendation level is a project trade-off (followed by Liang Hu); none of the three objected, so it is maintained.

## Assessment of A1 (Revised)
Upstream Tier: Step 1 remains a threshold, and still holds after narrowing the blank (OKC, multiple AIWP sources, unified correction, fly/no-fly scoring). Urban Tier: NWP-driven urban LES/LBM is already mature; A1's incremental value is "AI forecast-driven + multi-day continuous + scoring against simple baselines and decisions". Decision-making Tier: No uniform wind speed limit; use multi-tiered thresholds + probabilistic scoring. Evaluate the gate after re-running Step 1 according to items 3–7 above.

# A1 ASOS 2023 Execution Audit (10-14 15:20 ET)

This round was processed in an independent directory; the original  etc. were not overwritten. The Colab CPU session `ideas-a1-asos-2023` ran from approximately 14:35–15:20 ET; `colab stop` has been run, and `colab sessions` confirmed that the session has disappeared (the remaining two GPU sessions belong to other tasks and were not touched).

Downloads completed: AIWP/GFS station sampling files 2,918/2,920; FOUR and PANG are each missing one official object at 2023-10-18 12 UTC (S3 404), which were excluded based on common timestamps across the four sources. First 8 months for training, last 4 months for independent verification. 2022 ASOS was used for by-station by-month UTC hour climatology for Sep–Dec, because the first 8 months of 2023 do not contain the validation months. Complete station series 2023 and 2022 observations, along with two figures and statistics, have been retrieved; this directory totals 118.65 MB, excluding original gridded fields.  each object URL, initialization time, and retrieval seconds; ,  monthly response bytes and elapsed time;  summarizes station-year rows, CSV bytes, and allocated retrieval time. The `object_size` in the AIWP manifest is the total size of the original object, by no means the actual HTTP Range downloaded bytes; actual network received bytes were not instrumented per request, and the total object size must not be passed off as transfer volume.

The shared Colab account balance went from 1470.07 CU to 1460.64 CU, a reduction of 9.43 CU; during this period there were concurrently two to three other GPU sessions, so this was not an exclusive consumption of this CPU session, and the station-year CU field is marked null (cannot be reliably attributed). This CPU session has ended, and there are currently no remaining expenses. In this round, at least 12 stations have full-year archives for 2023, but the actual effective paired row count varies by station; RQO/SRE are sparse, see station_year_ledger for details.

Code execution evidence: HDF5 HTTP range slicing and GRIB2 `.idx` range requests for all four sources at 2023-01-01 00 UTC were all successful; subsequently, six shards completed the full-year data retrieval, and the statistics script returned `METRICS_DONE GRAP_v100_GFS True 60 62424` on real data, generating a 60-row main table and 62,424 source × station × init × lead records for the verification period. Daily bootstrap resampling 1,000 times. The above  explicitly list "unverified"; this experiment must not be referred to as an exact uniform 10 m or urban low-altitude flight clearance validation.

# A1 Review Revision Execution Status (2026-10-14 15:52 US Eastern)

Conclusion: The revised annual verification is incomplete; all three criteria (5% non-inferiority to GFS and 15% improvement over persistence/ten-year climatology for 24 h and 48 h MAE, and 24 h 8 m/s CSI against GFS) are "Not evaluated", and the previous version's "Passed" must not be retained. 95% intervals were not calculated.

## Actual Completion
- Retained the old-design results of the four sources for 2023 in the original , without overwriting. It uses an 8/4-month split for 2023, single-year climatology, and a mixed observational standard, and can only be called preliminary, not the result of this revision.
- Colab CPU actually acquired 132 months and 12 stations of IEM METAR from 2013–2023, totaling 1,001,568 station-hour observation rows; the NCEI 1-minute window series already acquired for 2022/23 and the 2023 four-source station series were reused intact. Historical METAR monthly files and the partial forecast station series from this run are archived in `partial_station_data.tar.gz` (station-level series and metadata only, no gridded data stored).
- A total of 7,300 objects are required for the six AIWP models × initial condition sources and GFS for 2022, and the forecasts of three IFS initial condition sources for 2023; 87 were sampled as a trial (84 for 2022, 3 for 2023), with zero object errors. See archives and for details; the single lead-time chunk of AIWP HDF5 u/v is global 721×1440, and remote slicing still transfers the full-globe compressed chunk. The median time for actual object fetching was around tens to over a hundred seconds, and annual acquisition far exceeds this bounded session; therefore, no primary source was selected, and there is no one-year independent verification or confidence interval.
- A pipeline smoke test was conducted on an incomplete sample, which once output nominal numerical values, but the sample consists only of the first few timesteps of 2022 and the initial timestep of 2023, and is strictly not provided as results. The script has added a hard gate of ≥95% archive coverage per source per month, and the current partial data will reject annual conclusions.
- Data fetching methods: HDF5 HTTP Range for official AIWP AWS objects; byte ranges via official GFS .idx; public IEM METAR API. Colab session `ideas-a1-review93-cpu` has stopped and is no longer listed in `colab sessions`; the other 3 sessions belong to other work and were untouched. The account balance observed this time dropped from 1458.87 to 1457.40 CU, but there were other concurrent sessions during this period and it cannot be attributed to this task or individual station-years; CU is recorded as null per station. The 2022 single-year climatology of the 2023 legacy data was not treated as a ten-year climatology.

## Criteria Status
| Condition | Point Estimate | Daily Bootstrap 95% Interval | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2023 24 h MAE for the same AI source preselected in 2022, relative to corrected GFS ≤+5%, persistence/climatology ≤−15% | Not calculated | Not calculated | Not evaluated |
| The above three MAE metrics at 48 h for the same AI source | Not calculated | Not calculated | Not evaluated |
| 24 h 8 m/s CSI for the same AI source ≥GFS | Not calculated | Not calculated | Not evaluated |

## Subsequent Reusable Artifacts and Limitations
 and are both in this directory. The primary verification should standardize on METAR 2 min wind; 1 min stations separately report 1 h mean / within-window maximum 5 s gust, with METAR gusts not counted; 2022 fits corrections and logistic regressions, while 2023 is verification only; 2013–2022 METAR climatology by station × month × UTC hour; preselect a single AI source using the training year 24 h MAE. 100 m FCNv2 / 1 min 10 m wind ratio remains descriptive only and does not participate in the criteria. The script has not been verified on full-year data; do not treat the smoke test as a scientific research deliverable.

The contemporaneous actual anemometer heights and instrument/gust averaging periods for each station in 2023 have not received station-by-station original configuration proof; the station table remains unverified, and it cannot be claimed that airport observations are all precisely 10 m. Bremnes et al. (2024, NPG 31:247–257, DOI 10.5194/npg-31-247-2024) serves as a design precedent; its probabilistic post-processing uses quantile neural networks rather than this linear correction, and specific accuracy is not extrapolated. See for data sources and licensing.

items.text:
# A1 Step 1.5: Station Forecast × C2 Virtual Urban Ratio (Development Diagnosis)

One-line conclusion: In the southerly wind scenario, the number of hours with wind speed exceeding thresholds at 50–100 m is sensitive to both height conversion and local position, warranting an independently verified urban layer; however, current choice of conversion source can shift the 8 m/s, 24 h exceedance proportion from ~10–30% to 35–62%, and the hours here cannot be taken as real urban flight risk predictions.

## Inputs, Specifications, and Reproducibility

Read-only inputs: (2023 ASOS pairs); (C2 741 virtual points, development test case); background note. Outputs are and ; prior internal test plots for this round are retained in the directory root and revision2, not for final citation. Input files were not modified.

Using the mean U=6.793 m/s of the 100 m point for KOKC/KPWA (`OKCPWAopen` in CSV) as the uniform reference, each point's U is divided by this value as the spatial multiplier; at 50/100 m, there are 222 open, 13 wake, and 12 rooftop points, respectively. Each station-initialization combination is equally weighted, and each virtual point of the same category is equally weighted to compute the proportion of exceedance combinations; this does not cover all hours of the year in OKC, nor is it urban measured hours. There are 662 valid southerly station-initialization combinations for 24 h, and 664 for 48 h; the two stations are pooled, and the two lead times are not mixed. The 5th/25th/50th/75th/95th percentiles of raw FCNv2 100/10 ratio are 1.462/1.674/1.821/1.968/2.252.

Local gust proxy is defined as U·(1+g Iu), where g=3 is an **assumption**, with 2.5/3.5 additionally calculated; `Iu` is C2 longitudinal turbulence intensity. Hayakawa (2023, PDF p. 2) explains that the peak factor depends on averaging period, gust duration, and turbulence spectrum, and g=3 cannot be directly assigned from that paper to the 3-second gust in this C2; here it is an exploratory parameter, not a calibrated drone gust. All "gust ratios" below use U·(1+g·mean Iu) of C2 open 100 m as reference; mean Iu=0.1812 for open 100 m. Fixed thresholds of 6/8/10/12 m/s are hypothetical bins for A1, not operational limits. [1]

## C2 Multipliers Relative to open 100 m

| Location | Number of Points | Mean Wind Ratio 50 m | Mean+Gust Ratio 50 m (g=2.5/3/3.5) | Mean Wind Ratio 100 m | Mean+Gust Ratio 100 m (g=2.5/3/3.5) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| open | 222 | 0.848 | 0.884 / 0.889 / 0.893 | 1.000 | 0.993 / 0.993 / 0.992 |
| wake | 13 | 0.726 | 0.817 / 0.829 / 0.839 | 0.916 | 0.963 / 0.969 / 0.975 |
| rooftop | 12 | 0.804 | 0.872 / 0.881 / 0.889 | 0.974 | 0.995 / 0.998 / 1.000 |

Ratios are first calculated point by point, then averaged by category; the gust ratio for open 100 m is not strictly equal to 1, because the point-by-point correlation between U and Iu differs from the product of their means. Wake has lower mean wind but higher Iu (0.290 at 50 m), and rooftop 50 m has even higher Iu (0.361); local position distributions are wide, and category means cannot represent every single point.

## Exceedance Proportions Under 24 h Southerly Winds (Percentages, Not Measured Risk)

On the same sample, the station-corrected 10 m reference across 6/8/10/12 bins is 33.7/8.8/2.0/0.0%; the converted open 100 m mean reference is 81.4/64.2/42.1/27.2%. The table below shows the equally weighted exceedance hour proportions for each urban point category; values in parentheses are structural alternative results using raw FCNv2 100 m wind to directly drive the same C2 ratio, not 95% intervals. The gust column shows proxy exceedance proportions for g=3.

| AGL | Category | 6 m/s Mean/Gust | 8 m/s Mean/Gust (Direct FCNv2 Alternative Mean) | 10 m/s Mean/Gust | 12 m/s Mean/Gust |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 50 m | open | 70.1/89.9 | 48.0/81.0 (15.2) | 28.5/69.1 | 13.9/55.1 |
| 50 m | wake | 54.8/86.4 | 35.3/74.2 (10.4) | 19.7/60.8 | 9.3/46.4 |
| 50 m | rooftop | 64.6/86.9 | 46.1/77.3 (15.6) | 28.9/66.5 | 14.5/54.5 |
| 100 m | open | 79.5/92.6 | 62.3/85.4 (29.8) | 42.6/76.1 | 26.6/64.8 |
| 100 m | wake | 72.6/92.3 | 52.6/84.7 (22.0) | 34.4/74.7 | 20.1/62.5 |
| 100 m | rooftop | 75.4/92.6 | 60.4/84.7 (30.6) | 41.4/75.2 | 27.3/64.4 |

Relative to the station 10 m value of 8.8%, the 8 m/s bin increases by 26.5–53.5 percentage points; but compared with 64.2% for open 100 m, the mean wind proportions at various locations are actually ~1.9–28.9 percentage points lower. Thus most of the "amplification" stems from the 10→100 m conversion; C2 local position differences are mostly sheltering deceleration, and one cannot mistakenly claim that all urban positions are higher than open points at the same height. Although the gust proxy exceeds thresholds more frequently, it has a different averaging duration from the station 2-minute sustained wind, and the gust column must not be validated against station proportions under the same specification.

## Uncertainty and Sensitivity

Resampling across 2023 valid days 1,500 times as a whole (retaining all stations, cycles, and virtual points for that day), the 24 h, 8 m/s urban mean wind exceedance proportions and conditional sampling 95% intervals are as follows: 50 m open 48.0% [43.1, 53.0], wake 35.3% [31.4, 39.3], rooftop 46.1% [41.5, 50.7]; 100 m open 62.3% [57.3, 67.3], wake 52.6% [48.2, 57.2], rooftop 60.4% [55.7, 65.0]. The corresponding point estimates for 48 h are 47.1/35.0/45.0% and 62.0/52.0/60.1%, respectively; see JSON for all four bins and intervals. The intervals only quantify variation across sampled days, and do **not** cover C2 model/inflow, station forecast error, systematic error in FCNv2 ratio, or peak factor uncertainty, and cannot be called "true urban forecast confidence intervals".

Spatial heterogeneity: at 24 h, 8 m/s, the 10th–90th percentiles of exceedance proportions for individual C2 points are 34.9–64.5% for 50 m open, 0.6–59.3% for wake, and 5.9–59.7% for rooftop; 49.0–73.1% for 100 m open, 24.7–70.2% for wake, and 56.6–69.5% for rooftop. When g=2.5/3/3.5, the 24 h, 8 m/s gust proxy proportions for 50 m wake are 70.4/74.2/78.1%, and 82.0/84.7/86.8% for 100 m rooftop; see JSON for other sensitivities. The structural alternative "direct drive by raw FCNv2 100 m" yields only 10.4–30.6% (24 h, 8 m/s), highlighting that the main chain's GraphCast corrected 10 m × raw FCNv2 vertical multiplier may cause excessive amplification; previously in A1, the median ratio of FCNv2 100 m / ASOS 1 h 10 m was 1.342, which is also not a directly substitutable vertical correction coefficient. Original logistic regression probabilities were not multiplied: probabilities cannot be multiplied by deterministic wind speed multipliers, and urban event probabilities require separate calibration; this table uses only corrected wind speeds and does not misrepresent probabilities as validated urban probabilities.

![24 h, 8 m/s urban mean wind and gust proxy exceedance proportions; blue 50 m, orange 100 m, error bars are conditional intervals from daily resampling; footnote cites A1 ASOS/AIWP and C2 virtual point sources.](revision3/urban_exceedance8.png)

## Limitations of Use and Next-Step Judgments

C2 is a **development test case**; its 8b inflow **has not passed equilibrium acceptance**; same-model digital twins **have not been verified by independent observations**. The height of C2 rooftop points is measured from the **local rooftop**, not on the same elevation plane, and cannot be treated as the same absolute height as 50/100 m in streets. There is only this single scenario of **southerly wind neutral stratification**, which cannot represent year-round wind directions, thermal stability, or severe weather; open/wake/rooftop are geometric proxy labels, not observational identified real wakes. C2 open 100 m is not a co-located field measurement anchor for airport ASOS 10 m. Instrument heights for some stations and vertical profile calibrations for the two models have also not been verified. The next step should first be to calibrate 10→100 m at independent urban observation points, check C2 inflow and equilibrium as well as multiple wind directions in real street blocks, and only then evaluate flight altitude increments; verdict here: **has exploratory value, quantitative risk is unclear**.

Runs: , . Data sources are the aforementioned A1 pairs and C2 development virtual points; literature is used only for peak concepts, with no external data replacing C2.

## Sources

[1] https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jwe/48/3/48_1/_pdf/-char/en — Hayakawa 2023 peak-factor and averaging-time conversions

# A1 Step 2: Paris Lidar Feasibility Gate (10-14 18:47, US Eastern)

Conclusion: According to the project brief's "first complete 12 months for training, subsequent testing, and using station × month × UTC climatology during the training period as baseline", this Paris dataset cannot support the preset criteria for city-center 100 m AGL; following the boundary of "stop first if the dataset cannot support it", no forecasts were downloaded, no fitting or scoring was performed, and none of the three criteria were evaluated. This is not a failure of AI forecasting.

| Verification Item | Data Evidence | Impact on Original Design |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Timeline and first complete 12 months | Zenodo L3 v1.42 covers 2022-06-10 to 2024-03-05; the first complete calendar twelve months is 2022-07 to 2023-06. Actually scanning monthly records of 600 s files from 2022-06 to 2023-05, city-center PALUPD 100 m/150 m are both zero, and only suburban PASIRT 150 m has values; PALUPD only appears in 2023-06 (monthly records in scan log). | The first complete 12 months only has partial urban observations in the final month, making it impossible to perform year-round city-center 100 m training or establish same-month climatology for each month in the subsequent verification period. |
| Urban primary station | PALUPD: NetCDF station height 26 m, elevation 65 m, closest gates for target 100/150 m AGL are 111/161 m AGL, respectively; 2023-06 aggregates 422 hours each with centered hour and ≥4 valid 10 min scans, 2023-07 has 723 hours each; closest gate to 50 m at 61 m has no valid values. For 2023-09 3600 s files, 100/150 m have 719 hours each, and 139 hours each in 2024-02 (the latter two are sample checks of monthly hourly files, not QC statistics for full seasons). | 100/150 m have short-term observations, 50 m is not reportable; however, the urban primary station lacks a full year, making it impossible to provide any same-month training estimate for "station × month × UTC climatology during the training period" in subsequent different calendar months. Switching to an annual pooled climatology would change the criteria and cannot be done covertly. |
| Other stations | PAJUSS is an 88 m rooftop instrument with an instrument blind zone for the first ~150 m; sample 50/100/150 m are all 0 in 2023-06 and 2024-02. PASIRT only has stable values at 150 m (699 hours in 2023-06); suburban PAARBO has 50/100/150 m in 2024-02, PACHEM has 100/150 m; airport PAROIS is zero during the same period. | PASIRT cannot masquerade as the city-center 100 m primary station; PAJUSS's elevation grid must not be mistaken for usable AGL wind. |

Method verification: L3 `altitude` is a 25 m grid relative to sea level, ground elevation is calculated using `station_altitude−station_height`, and actual AGL is `altitude−station_altitude+station_height`. 600 s). NetCDF's `station_height` is 0 m for PASIRT, whereas Table 2 of the paper lists ~4.5 m; this metadata discrepancy was not treated as an exact measured height.

Alternative recommendations (preset criteria were not changed based on this): prioritize finding urban 100 m AGL profiles with at least two consecutive years where every verification month also has same-month observations in the training period; first check station by station the actual gates at 100 m AGL, temporal coverage, and licenses for CROCUS Chicago (open but raw records un-QC'd) and Prague TURBAN/TURDATA (CC BY 4.0), before deciding whether to establish a separate design. NYS Mesonet profile nominal minimum is 100 m and requires data request; it is not directly substitutable open data. Only if the Lead explicitly permits changing the Paris task into a short-term exploration for summer 2023 and changing climatology to a non-monthly-split baseline can PALUPD be used for a new design; it cannot be packaged as a pass/fail of the currently predetermined criteria.

Execution and resources: only public Zenodo monthly archive verification was performed; no AIWP/GFS was retrieved, and no formal station pairs, MAE/AUC/intervals, or plots were generated. The only Colab CPU session belonging to this task, `ideas-a1-paris-lidar-1014`, has stopped; `colab sessions` no longer lists it, and the remaining four sessions in the list do not belong to this task. Account balance went from 1436.03 to 1430.95 CU; the difference of 5.08 CU had other concurrent sessions and cannot be attributed as usage of this task; the 15 CU pause line was not reached. A duplicate process was mistakenly started once in the scan log and the second process was terminated; duplicate months in the log are not treated as duplicate observations.

Auditable materials: (preprocessing script), (actual monthly archive log); data Zenodo https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17710093 (Morrison et al., 2025; CC BY 4.0), paper https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-17-6507-2025. No need to download grid fields. Limitations: later months were only spot-checked with hourly files; if the design is modified in the future, complete 600 s QC, station instrument configurations, and diurnal matching checks will still be required.

# A1 Paris Short-Term Experiment: Data Provenance and Reproduction Specifications

Access date: 2026-10-14 (US Eastern). This directory only outputs station-level series and does not duplicate global grid archives.

1. Urban wind observations: Morrison, W. et al. (2025), *Earth System Science Data* 17, 6507–6529, DOI https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-17-6507-2025; data Zenodo record https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17710093, monthly `paris_dwl_L3V1.600s.tar.gz` of L3 v1.42. Zenodo API `metadata.license.id` verified as `cc-by-4.0`; attribution must be retained for station series. `altitude` is sea level elevation, AGL = altitude - (station_altitude - station_height); closest gates for PALUPD 100/150 m are 111/161 m AGL. Using QC'd finite u/v, at least four 10 min periods per centered hour, vector averaging first then calculating speed. Monthly compressed archives were discarded after processing, without copying raw large files to workstation.
2. NOAA/CIRA/NOAA-GSL AIWP reforecasts: Radford et al. (2025), *BAMS*, DOI https://doi.org/10.1175/BAMS-D-24-0057.1; directory and fields https://registry.opendata.aws/aiwp/, public bucket `noaa-oar-mlwp-data`, GFS initializations FOUR_v200_GFS, GRAP_v100_GFS, PANG_v100_GFS. Open directory terms of use verbatim: "Open Data. There are no restrictions on the use of this data." Remote HDF5 small-window slicing by lead time, 100 m u/v exists only in FOUR.
3. NOAA/NCEP operational GFS 0.25°, `noaa-gfs-bdp-pds.idx` boundary read-only for UGRD/VGRD at 10/100 m AGL; terms: "NOAA data disseminated through NODD are open to the public and can be used as desired." NOAA requests source attribution and prohibits claiming NOAA endorsement for derivative works. Downstream interpolation and correction are all processed for this experiment, not as-is NOAA products.
4. Height conversion: neutral logarithmic law for the primary comparison, where z0=0.03 m is an assumption not determined station-by-station (with 0.3 m sensitivity additionally calculated); power law, alpha=0.2 is likewise an assumption (with 0.14, 0.3 sensitivities additionally calculated). None of these coefficients are measured PALUPD values given in literature. The above simplifications at urban 10 m may lie within the roughness sublayer and do not represent the local actual profile; independent sensitivities need to be made explicit in results. Theoretical reference: WMO (2023), *Guide to Instruments and Methods of Observation*, Vol III, Ch.9, https://amc.namem.gov.mn/wp-content/uploads/WMO/1.%208_III-2023_en.pdf; this citation does not equate to WMO providing parameters for this station.

# A1 Paris Lidar Short-Term Verification (2023-06—2024-03)

One-line conclusion: In the selection period, GFS direct 100 m wind was selected based on the preset 24 h MAE, rather than AI; this GFS method passed all three numerical thresholds in leave-one-month verification, but this cannot be used to claim that "AI urban flight altitude forecasts are usable". The gap between AI and GFS in this sample is small; raw errors of height conversion are sensitive, while fixed-multiplier conversions are indistinguishable from each other after linear MOS.

## Preset Criteria (PALUPD 111 m AGL, Selected GFS/direct100; Verification is Leave-One-Month Cross-Validation)

| Condition | Point Estimate | Bootstrap 95% Interval by Verification Day | Preset Boundary | Determination |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 24 h MAE improvement relative to persistence | 53.6% | 48.0%—58.5% | ≥15% | Passed; n=317 |

Formally, both 24 h and 48 h baseline comparisons and AUC passed, with intervals not crossing the boundaries; however, this "preselected primary method" is GFS, not AI, so the scientific objective "AI is usable" remains unproven by these criteria. The summer selection set was only used to preselect source × conversion; for the evaluation set 2023-09—2024-03, each fold used only the remaining months to fit station/gate/lead-time linear corrections, statistical ratios, probabilities, and climatologies; left-out months did not enter in-fold training. During preselection, in order to comply with the given design, fitting was done on the same summer set and ranked by MAE on the same set (optimiztic bias); the primary method selection result cannot be inversely reselected using the evaluation set.

## Primary Table: PALUPD (All Times are Identical Four-Source Available Times for Each Source and Lead Time, 111 m, n=317/lead time)

| Source | Conversion | 24 h Raw MAE | 24 h MOS MAE | 48 h Raw MAE | 48 h MOS MAE | 24 h AUC8 |

Lowest corrected MAE among the top four primary candidates in the 24 h selection set: GFS/direct100 1.264 m/s; GraphCast 10 m conversion 1.296, Pangu 1.320, FCNv2 1.370 m/s; thus GFS was selected as the primary method. In the leave-one-month verification period, GraphCast/log_z0_0p03 and GFS/direct100 for 24/48 h are 1.167/1.267 and 1.186/1.324 m/s, respectively, with differences of −0.019/−0.057 m/s (descriptive only; GraphCast cannot be reselected in the verification period and deemed compliant).

## Height Conversion, 161 m, and Suburban Comparisons

At PALUPD 111 m, GFS 24 h raw MAE is: 100 m direct 1.804, 10 m × logarithmic law (z0=0.03 m) 1.268, power law (alpha=0.2) 1.462, and training-month statistical ratio 1.303 m/s. Raw MAE for hypothetical sensitivities z0=0.3 and alpha=0.14/0.3 are 1.585, 1.269, and 2.549 m/s, respectively. After MOS, the MAE for all "10 m × fixed per-station constant" is ~1.182 m/s, because the free intercept and slope absorb the fixed multiplier; only the independent input of direct 100 m shows a difference (1.186). Therefore, this linear MOS setup cannot determine which of logarithmic law / power law / statistical ratio is superior, nor can the small post-correction gap negate the uncertainty of raw conversions.
PALUPD 161 m has n=316 valid pairs per source/lead time; GFS direct 100 m wind (not extrapolated to 161 m, with nominal height mismatch) has post-MOS 24/48 h MAE=1.113/1.286 m/s, descriptive only and not part of the criteria. Per-station comparisons for PAARBO (50/100/150 m), PACHEM (100/150 m), and PASIRT (150 m only) are found in metrics.json `records`; different stations have differing missing-data periods and available gates, and cannot be merged into tables to replace the PALUPD criteria.

## Valid Hours and Sources

| PALUPD Gate | 2023-06 | 07 | 08 | 09 | 10 | 11 | 12 | 2024-01 | 02 | 03 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 111 m | 422 | 723 | 741 | 715 | 742 | 720 | 744 | 742 | 139 | 0 |
| 161 m | 422 | 723 | 744 | 716 | 742 | 720 | 737 | 742 | 139 | 0 |

The evaluation period for the primary station actually contains only six months with data from 2023-09 to 2024-02, with only 139 observation hours in 2024-02 and zero hours in 2024-03; thus it is not seven months of independent verification. Scoring is performed only when 00/12 UTC initializations, 24/48 h valid times, all four sources, and initialization observations are simultaneously available, with n=317 for each of the two lead times at 111 m across 159 verification days. `altitude` in Zenodo L3 QC is sea level elevation, subtracting station ground elevation to obtain 111/161 m AGL; 10 min u/v requires at least four points vector-averaged per centered hour. The primary station has no valid gate at 50 m, and PAJUSS was not used due to an instrument blind zone.

AIWP expected 556 initialization objects per source, with actual counts being FCNv2 555, GraphCast 556, Pangu 555, GFS 556; FCNv2/Pangu were missing for 2023-10-18 12 UTC and were uniformly removed from common pairs. Total read and process wall-clock time was 4,716 s; global HDF5 only underwent remote slicing without saving grid points locally. Total response bytes for GFS .idx request ranges are seen in audit.json; raw source object sizes in AIWP JSON are not actual transferred bytes and are not commingled.

Figures: methods_mae.png (24 h MOS MAE for 111 m each source × conversion), monthly_mae.png (primary method by leave-out month); figure footnotes all cite Morrison et al. Zenodo 17710093, NOAA/CIRA AIWP, and NOAA/NCEP GFS AWS. Station-level CSV: paired_station.csv.gz. Scripts and sources are run_observations.py, run_forecasts.py, run_verify.py, provenance.md, respectively.

## Limitations and Verdict

A single urban primary station, a single city, ~6 months of valid evaluation (with incomplete inter-monthly climatology), 2 cycles/day sampling, lidar vertical gate mismatch, and a complex urban roughness sublayer cannot be extrapolated to the full year, all street blocks, or drone operations. The 8 m/s threshold is a hypothetical risk bin, not a regulatory limit. Probabilistic AUC measures only discrimination (ranking) and does not guarantee probability calibration or decision value. Taking training-month statistical ratios and simple neutral profiles for sensitivity, z0 and alpha lack contemporaneous independent measurements at PALUPD; direct 100 m fields at 111 m inherently have an 11 m nominal difference.

Strict point estimates and intervals for this round: numerical criteria for the selected GFS method all passed; AI was not preselected, and GFS's pass must not be portrayed as a pass for AI; differences between AI and GFS in the verification period serve only as exploratory comparisons. Conclusion: the urban layer warrants continued measurement and calibration, while which height conversion is most reliable and whether AI is genuinely usable remain unclear.

items.text:
# A1 Paris Upper-Air Observation Point Transfer Experiment (111 m AGL, Exploratory)

One-line conclusion: Across the six valid months and 159 verification days of PALUPD, when pre-applying LFPO surface METAR correction + assumed neutral logarithmic profile (S1), GFS 24 h MAE is 4.09% higher than local upper-air MOS (S0) (resampled 95% interval across verification days: −1.14% to 9.83%); according to the preset point-estimate interpretation, this qualifies as a "small gap" (<10%), but the interval approaches 10% and altering profile assumptions degrades performance markedly, so one cannot claim that urban downscaling is unnecessary. PAARBO transfer requiring no local upper-air data is also only 4.46% higher, but event CSI drops from 0.481 to 0.357.

## Primary Table for Identical Sample

PALUPD 111 m, leave-one-month from 2023-09 to 2024-02; n=317 per lead time (no valid data for 2024-03). S0 is the leave-one-month local MOS prediction fixed from the previous round, not refitted in left-out months. Relative to S0 column reports MAE percentage increase and paired bootstrap 95% interval across 159 valid dates; 8 m/s is a hypothetical bin, CSI = hits / (hits + misses + false alarms).

| Source | Lead Time | Scheme | MAE m/s | Bias m/s | AUC8 | CSI8 | MAE Increase Relative to S0 (95% CI) |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| GFS | 24 | S0 Local MOS | 1.186 | +0.001 | 0.921 | 0.481 | Reference |

| GraphCast | 48 | S1 | 1.296 | −0.069 | 0.928 | 0.553 | +2.34% (−1.12%, +5.92%) |
| GraphCast | 48 | S2 PAARBO | 1.312 | −0.540 | 0.930 | 0.441 | +3.58% (−2.28%, +9.65%) |
| GraphCast | 48 | S3 | 1.305 | −0.001 | 0.930 | 0.552 | +3.00% (−1.20%, +7.25%) |

According to the pre-fixed interpretation, taking the best scheme S1 without local upper-air observations for GFS 24 h as the benchmark, the point estimate 4.09% <10%: "small gap". However, this judgment applies only to the current definition and neutral profile, and cannot be taken as non-inferiority proof for all urban situations; although the upper end of the interval is below 10%, it is close to the boundary. S1 48 h differs by 2.82%. S3 24 h at 52.09% indicates that uncorrected direct 100 m forecasts have significant systematic positive bias. GraphCast S3 already uses an assumed logarithmic conversion and cannot be treated as an equivalent "unconverted" input as raw GFS 100 m.

## Conversions and Diagnostics

S1 first fits in-fold a+bU between model 10 m wind at the PALUPD grid location and LFPO surface METAR wind, then multiplies by U111/U10=ln(111/z0)/ln(10/z0), assuming z0=0.03 m. Note that this is not strict collocated correction on the airport grid point: reused grid point series only include lidar stations, while LFPO METAR is separated from the PALUPD grid point with different underlying surfaces. PALUPD 111 m observations were not used to fit S1. Per-station training-period statistical height ratios are unidentifiable in S1 without local upper-air observations, and were not misrepresented as deployable methods.

Profile sensitivity of S1 for GFS (24/48 h MAE, m/s): z0=0.03 is 1.235/1.361; z0=0.3 is 1.640/1.658; power law alpha=0.14 is 1.230/1.362, alpha=0.2 is 1.493/1.534, alpha=0.3 is 2.723/2.703. These parameters are all assumptions, not measured roughness for the station or literature-specified parameters. Thus, the "small gap" can be reversed by profile assumptions.

S2 fits a+bU using training-month observations at the PAARBO 102 m gate with corresponding model inputs at that station, applying coefficients directly to PALUPD as is; PALUPD observations were not used to recalibrate the intercept. The PACHEM 104 m gate has a mean wind speed of only ~0.46 m/s in this data batch, compared to ~5.34 m/s for PAARBO, and regression transfer yields virtually zero wind (failed results are retained in table); PACHEM cannot be treated as transferable 100 m ground truth without on-site QC. PASIRT has only a 146 m gate, so same-height 100 m coefficient transfer was not performed. AUC is ranking discrimination, not probability calibration: S1 logistic function was trained using airport wind event threshold 8/conversion coefficient, S2 was trained using suburban events; S3 has no externally fitted probability, and AUC was calculated directly on raw velocity scores. Absolute probability values across different sites cannot be compared directly.

Figure: , GFS/GraphCast schemes for same-sample two-lead-time MAE. Footnote sources are Morrison et al. (2025) Zenodo 17710093 (CC BY 4.0), NOAA/NCEP GFS, NOAA/CIRA AIWP, and LFPO METAR archived by Iowa Environmental Mesonet.

Limitations: a single station, single city, six months, two initialization cycles per day at 00/12 UTC, not covering the full year / all street blocks; lidar 111 m gate is not exactly 100 m; METAR 2 min and lidar 1 h centered average averaging times are not identical; airport and urban surfaces/wind fields are not interchangeable. It estimates a simple statistical transfer gap, not verified gains from LBM/CFD, and non-flyable thresholds must not be treated as regulatory limits. Inputs come from existing small files; local computation on workstation, no Colab/CU, no supercomputing.

# A1 Step 4: Building Morphological Height Conversion (Paris PALUPD, Exploratory)

One-sentence conclusion: On the same 317 validation samples/lead times, Macdonald morphological z₀/d calculated using only public building footprints and heights failed to replace local upper-air MOS: GFS 24 h MAE was 3.008 m/s, which is 153.59% higher than S0's 1.186 m/s (bootstrap 95% confidence interval across validation days: +128.42% to +181.46%). According to the predefined ≥25% rule, this qualifies as "still a large gap"; however, this failure cannot be directly interpreted as LBM/CFD already being capable of closing this gap, because the airport reference profile and cross-site MOS themselves have not undergone co-located verification.

## Predefined Interpretation and Scoring

Consistent with Step 3 leave-one-month-out folds, the same PALUPD 111 m lidar station, 317 pairs/lead times from 2023-09 to 2024-02, and 159 validation days. S0 is the leave-fold local upper-air observation MOS; morphological method M only reuses in-fold LFPO METAR surface wind corrections, replacing the fixed z₀=0.03 m urban ratio with per-30° building morphological ratios; held-out month PALUPD upper-air winds are not used for M. The hypothesized threshold is 8 m/s; AUC uses wind speed as the ranking score, and CSI is deterministic threshold exceedance; S0 AUC here uses its wind speed ranking and thus may differ slightly from the logistic regression probability AUC of the previous round.

Sector 330° has a noticeably high H; target observations were not used to prune this sector. Itemized building counts, sector errors, and machine-readable denominators for all sectors see , . Directions originate from the forecast 10 m u/v (FROM) at the PALUPD interpolated grid point; binned by forecast direction, without using held-out month observed wind directions. "Building count" here allows the same building spanning multiple sectors to be counted once in each sector.

## Formulas, Provenance, and Non-negligible Limitations

Adopting Macdonald, Griffiths & Hall (1998) print p.1861, PDF page 5 Eqs. 22–23: d/H = 1 + A^(−λp)(λp−1), z₀/H=(1−d/H) exp{−[0.5 C_D (1−d/H) λf / κ²]^(−1/2)}; A=4.43 (staggered arrays), κ=0.40, C_D=1.2. A and C_D are model assumptions applying idealized array parameters to irregular cities, without measuring local site drag; subsequent β corrections were not introduced (same card print pp.1862–1863). H is the footprint-area-weighted mean of buildings with positive heights within the source area; λp is the footprint area of these buildings / source area; λf sums the projected frontal width of building polygons perpendicular to the incoming wind direction × their height / source area. Polygons are clipped at sector boundaries first. Grimmond & Oke (1999) print pp.1275–1276, 1283, PDF pages 14–15, 22 note that urban morphological methods exhibit large scatter and roughness elements should include trees; only buildings are considered here, and estimated z₀/d are not referred to as measured values. Corresponding knowledge cards are , and .

According to the specified formula U111/Uref = ln((111−d)/z₀) / ln((10−d_ref)/z₀_ref); on the LFPO end, d_ref=0, z₀_ref=0.03 m, and anemometer z_ref=10 m are all assumptions not yet verified locally, rather than computed from LFPO buildings. The airport 2 min observations and lidar centered hourly averages have unequal durations; earlier S1 MOS used PALUPD grid 10 m forecasts to fit LFPO observations, not the LFPO co-located grid. Step 4 retains the existing pipeline, so the failure cannot be uniquely attributed to building roughness. Using the 2026 building map to infer 2023–24 wind conditions introduces a temporal mismatch; 1,122 out of 19,712 original objects have missing/non-positive heights and are excluded from λp, λf, and H; trees, complex terrain, winds below the displacement height, atmospheric stability, and the roughness sublayer are unmodeled. While the ratio of 100 m to morphological H can be calculated, the aforementioned issues do not automatically disappear.

 is an Apur script trial run covering only Paris city limits; southern/eastern sectors were blank on the map, leading to incomplete morphological estimates; original files are preserved and not used for this conclusion. This v2, completed with the full ring from French official IGN BD TOPO, is the delivery version and does not overwrite or move v1. Conclusions are limited to a six-month single-station exploration; it cannot be claimed that CFD has achieved independent validation, nor can the 8 m/s hypothetical threshold be treated as a regulatory limit. Run locally on  workstation, without Colab/supercomputing. Determination: this simple neutral logarithmic chain based on building morphology is not worth deploying directly; if continuing in the next step, one should first verify LFPO co-located grid points, reference height/roughness, and more physically meaningful airport → urban profiles before benchmarking against independent upper-air observations.

# A1 Paris Two-Segment Morphological Conversion v3 Provenance

No new gridded data, buildings, or observations were downloaded in this round. Only read  .gz, sectors.csv; their object-level IGN BD TOPO V3 (queried in 2026, License Ouverte 2.0), PALUPD Zenodo 17710093 (CC BY 4.0), LFPO IEM METAR, NOAA GFS/CIRA GraphCast provenance, processing, licensing, and acquisition times see . This round only writes v3 derived files; the original 317 pairs/lead times and 2023-09 to 2024-02 leave-month folds remain unchanged. Using 2026 building maps for 2023–24 observations entails an epochal mismatch.

Literature check: The quote "wind speed conversion using the blending height of 60 m" attributed in the task description to Blocken, Stathopoulos & van Beeck (2016), *Building and Environment* 100:50–81, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.buildenv.2016.02.004 (allegedly PDF page 25 / journal p. 74) was not found in the searchable full text of that paper; one must not falsely claim it has been verified on that page. Exact wording search was found in Blocken (2018), *Building Simulation* 11:821–870, https://doi.org/10.1007/s12273-018-0459-3, where the original text in the pedestrian wind application section states: "The terrain-related contribution is obtained by combining the expression of the vertical mean wind speed profile by the logarithmic law and the wind speed conversion using the blending height of 60 m (Verkaik 2006)." That paper attributes this to Verkaik 2006; the original Verkaik text and page numbers were not checked. Therefore, 60 m is an example mentioned in literature, not a measured blending height in Paris; this experiment takes it as a hypothesis, and additionally computes 100/200 m. Blocken (2016) PDF link: https://pure.tue.nl/ws/files/16601170/BlockenPedestrian2016.pdf; Blocken (2018) original paper link: https://pure.tue.nl/ws/portalfiles/portal/106812211/2018_BuildSim_Blocken_Position_Paper.pdf. Publisher PDFs are not copied.

Morphological parameters continue to use v2 estimates from Macdonald et al. (1998) print p. 1861 Eqs. 22–23, see ; they are not local site measurements. z0_ref=0.03 m, d_ref=0, LFPO anemometer height 10 m, cross-site 10 m MOS, and the neutral two-segment matching are all assumptions; 0.01/0.1 m and 100/200 m are sensitivities, with no parameter tuning performed on PALUPD held-out months. The 60 m mentioned in the literature does not guarantee that true profiles from both locations strictly match at this height, particularly as the building roughness sublayer, stability, and internal boundary layers are not represented.

items.text:
# A1 Step 4 Correction v3: Airport → Urban Two-Segment Blending Height

One-sentence conclusion: After correcting the cross-roughness formula, the GFS 24 h MAE for the primary setting z_b=60 m, z0_ref=0.03 m is 1.455 m/s, which is 22.71% higher than local upper-air correction S0's 1.186 m/s (paired bootstrap 95% confidence interval across validation days: +13.09% to +32.96%), qualifying as a "moderate gap" under the pre-fixed interpretation, and building data cannot be judged capable of replacing observation points; however, sensitivity results for z_b=100/200 m show only about +5%, and the conclusion is dominated by the blending height assumption.

## Predefined Determination

PALUPD 111 m gate, identical to v2 with 317 pairs per source/lead time and 159 valid validation days; S0 and LFPO surface MOS predictions are reused as is, without using PALUPD held-out month winds to fit M. The primary criterion is GFS 24 h, z_b=60 m, z0_ref=0.03 m: only when relative to S0 <10% and the upper bound of the interval <15% is it termed "building data can replace"; ≥25% is a "large gap"; in between is "moderate". This round yielded +22.71%, with an upper bound of +32.96%: moderate, failing to reach the replacement threshold. The interval simultaneously encompasses 25%, so the statistical distinction between moderate/large gaps is unstable; the primary criterion is not revised post hoc simply because z_b=100/200 performed better.

## Blending Height Comparison (Same Sample; MAE in m/s, Parentheses Show Increment Relative to Same-Source S0 and by-Day Bootstrap 95% Confidence Interval)

| Source | Lead Time | S0 MAE | z_b=60 m | z_b=100 m | z_b=200 m |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| GFS | 24 h | 1.186 | 1.455；+22.71% [13.09,32.96] | 1.250；+5.37% [−0.21,11.47] | 1.253；+5.65% [−0.15,11.98] |
| GFS | 48 h | 1.324 | 1.510；+14.06% [5.55,22.63] | 1.363；+2.98% [−1.62,8.00] | 1.407；+6.26% [0.89,12.05] |
| GraphCast | 24 h | 1.167 | 1.423；+21.91% [12.90,31.61] | 1.216；+4.25% [0.10,8.57] | 1.202；+3.01% [−2.15,8.06] |
| GraphCast | 48 h | 1.267 | 1.496；+18.08% [9.71,27.24] | 1.311；+3.52% [−0.21,7.37] | 1.299；+2.60% [−2.25,7.50] |

Primary setting GFS 24 h bias +0.658 m/s, 48 h +0.661 m/s; changed to z_b=100 m, they are approximately +0.036/+0.037 m/s, respectively. z0_ref sensitivity under GFS 24 h, z_b=60 m: 0.01 m gives MAE 1.363, +14.89% [6.97,23.33]; 0.1 m gives MAE 1.654, +39.47% [26.84,53.13]. Comparing to assumed single terrain z0=0.03,d=0 MAE 1.235, +4.09%, and z0=0.3,d=0 1.640, +38.29%; v2's erroneous cross-terrain single-segment is 3.008, +153.59%, which serves only as an error diagnostic and under no circumstances as a physical baseline.

![Two-segment and comparison errors](morph_v3_mae.png)
Figure 1: PALUPD 111 m MAE on the same sample; building morphology from IGN BD TOPO V3, observations from Morrison et al. (2025) Zenodo 17710093, forecasts from NOAA GFS/CIRA AIWP, airport winds from IEM LFPO METAR; two-segment example refers to Blocken (2018) citing Verkaik (2006), not a blending height measured at this site.

## Methods, Sectors, and Limitations

U(z_b)=U_LFPO10 ln(z_b/z0_ref)/ln(10/z0_ref); U111=U(z_b) ln((111−d)/z0)/ln((z_b−d)/z0). For 30° forecast incoming wind sectors, 0.5–2 km annular ring, z0 calculated from IGN buildings ranges from 1.175–3.307 m, d from 5.18–17.59 m (for all sectors itemized see ); sectors with z_b−d≤2z0 should be skipped, but across all three values of 60/100/200 m in this round, no sector met this condition, so n remains unchanged. GFS 24 h z_b=60 m sector-wise MAE is approximately 0.78–1.97 m/s; itemized sector n, MAE, bias, and S0 comparisons see metrics.json; with only 8 to 70-odd samples per sector, strong conclusions are not drawn individually. z_b=200 m is higher than the 111 m target, representing a sensitivity of first extrapolating up to 200 m then converting downward, not a physically validated true blending layer height.

Literature citation correction: The 60 m sentence listed in the task description on Blocken et al. (2016) PDF page 25 / journal p. 74 was not verified in its searchable full text; verifiable wording comes from Blocken (2018) pedestrian wind application section and is attributed to Verkaik (2006); that original text was not verified, so 60 m remains an assumption. See provenance.md for details. Other limitations: LFPO anemometer 10 m and z0_ref assumptions were not verified on-site; airport MOS used PALUPD grid 10 m forecasts to fit LFPO winds (not airport co-located grid points); lidar hourly averages differ from METAR 2 min; neutral profiles ignore atmospheric stability, roughness sublayer, and urban internal boundary layer; 2026 building footprints back-cast to 2023–24; single-station six-month sample cannot be extrapolated to full year or prove CFD/LBM can bridge the gap. Recalculated locally on  workstation, 0 CU, no Colab/supercomputing.

# A1 Multi-site Data Minimum Coverage Verification

Conclusion: Under the counting criterion of "at least four profiles with valid values per center hour", Paris PALUPD and Prague PVK roof each have at least six consecutive months of candidate gates in the 30–150 m range; however, qualifying months for the two sites do not overlap, and Prague processed profiles have no verifiable gate-by-gate QC flags, exhibit anomalous peaks, and have time zone / roof height ambiguities, so they can only be listed as **conditional two-city candidates**, and cannot yet be claimed to have "assembled a QC-verified multi-city validation sample." [1][2][3]

Paris L3v1.42: Monthly 600 s tar containing daily NetCDF, finite u/v, actual AGL = altitude−(station_altitude−station_height). Consistent with earlier scripts, recording timestamps were shifted back by five minutes and then binned to the nearest hour, deduplicated across days by month, and counted as valid only if the same center hour has ≥4 distinct 10 min records; wind speed mean was calculated by first averaging u/v and then taking the magnitude. The numbers in the monthly table are the **number of valid hours** for that gate, not the joint forecast paired count, nor monthly coverage. 2022-03 is an incomplete month and was not included in the six consecutive months; 2022-04—09 has six consecutive months of 101.4 m with 629–744 "format-valid hours" per month, plus another 608 in October. Starting from 2022-11, the HPL interval is ~33 minutes (verified via RAW headers and filename samples), with at most ~2 per hour, thus strictly zero under the ≥4 **10 min** criterion; 0 does not imply no observations for the entire month. The file interval in 2022-04/09 can be ~8–11 minutes, not strictly at equal 10 min intervals. Sample processed values show 49.3 m exceeding 50 m/s and isolated 147.8 m exceeding 70 m/s, which obviously cannot treat "format valid" directly as scientific QC; complete gate-by-gate physical review and original SNR verification remain to be done. ## Determination and Next Steps

Under the relaxed threshold of "having finite processed values, ≥4 records/hour, and six consecutive months": PALUPD 111 m (recommending 2023-07—2024-01, seven full months) and Prague PVK 101.4 m (recommending 2022-04—09, six months) can form a two-city, two-site **candidate**. Under the strict threshold of "credible QC and the same calendar-month period", they cannot be assembled: these two periods of observation from the two locations **have no shared time period**, precluding concurrent cross-city pairing; however, both lie after GraphCast 2022-01, allowing independent forecast verification for each city across different periods without conflating seasonal and urban effects. The anomalous high wind values in Prague processed data, timestamp discrepancies between nominal 33 min and actual earlier 8–11 min, roof AGL definition, and time zone must be clarified first; if this fails, CROCUS should be verified with priority, and generalization cannot be declared established based on the current table.
