Note: This version adopts a single-segment cross-roughness conversion, which is physically inapplicable to airport → urban; values are retained for auditing and not used for final determination, see .

# A1 Step 4: Building Morphological Height Conversion (Paris PALUPD, Exploratory)

One-sentence conclusion: On the same 317 validation samples/lead times, Macdonald morphological z₀/d calculated using only public building footprints and heights failed to replace local upper-air MOS: GFS 24 h MAE was 3.008 m/s, which is 153.59% higher than S0's 1.186 m/s (bootstrap 95% confidence interval across validation days: +128.42% to +181.46%). According to the predefined ≥25% rule, this qualifies as "still a large gap"; however, this failure cannot be directly interpreted as LBM/CFD already being capable of closing this gap, because the airport reference profile and cross-site MOS themselves have not undergone co-located verification.

## Predefined Interpretation and Scoring

Consistent with Step 3 leave-one-month-out folds, the same PALUPD 111 m lidar station, 317 pairs/lead times from 2023-09 to 2024-02, and 159 validation days. S0 is the leave-fold local upper-air observation MOS; morphological method M only reuses in-fold LFPO METAR surface wind corrections, replacing the fixed z₀=0.03 m urban ratio with per-30° building morphological ratios; held-out month PALUPD upper-air winds are not used for M. The hypothesized threshold is 8 m/s; AUC uses wind speed as the ranking score, and CSI is deterministic threshold exceedance; S0 AUC here uses its wind speed ranking and thus may differ slightly from the logistic regression probability AUC of the previous round.

Directions originate from the forecast 10 m u/v (FROM) at the PALUPD interpolated grid point; binned by forecast direction, without using held-out month observed wind directions. "Building count" here allows the same building spanning multiple sectors to be counted once in each sector.

## Formulas, Provenance, and Non-negligible Limitations

Adopting Macdonald, Griffiths & Hall (1998) print p.1861, PDF page 5 Eqs. 22–23: d/H = 1 + A^(−λp)(λp−1), z₀/H=(1−d/H) exp{−[0.5 C_D (1−d/H) λf / κ²]^(−1/2)}; A=4.43 (staggered arrays), κ=0.40, C_D=1.2. A and C_D are model assumptions applying idealized array parameters to irregular cities, without measuring local site drag; subsequent β corrections were not introduced (same card print pp.1862–1863). H is the footprint-area-weighted mean of buildings with positive heights within the source area; λp is the footprint area of these buildings / source area; λf sums the projected frontal width of building polygons perpendicular to the incoming wind direction × their height / source area. Polygons are clipped at sector boundaries first. Grimmond & Oke (1999) print pp.1275–1276, 1283, PDF pages 14–15, 22 note that urban morphological methods exhibit large scatter and roughness elements should include trees; only buildings are considered here, and estimated z₀/d are not referred to as measured values. Corresponding knowledge cards are , and .

According to the specified formula U111/Uref = ln((111−d)/z₀) / ln((10−d_ref)/z₀_ref); on the LFPO end, d_ref=0, z₀_ref=0.03 m, and anemometer z_ref=10 m are all assumptions not yet verified locally, rather than computed from LFPO buildings. The airport 2 min observations and lidar centered hourly averages have unequal durations; earlier S1 MOS used PALUPD grid 10 m forecasts to fit LFPO observations, not the LFPO co-located grid. Step 4 retains the existing pipeline, so the failure cannot be uniquely attributed to building roughness. Using the 2026 building map to infer 2023–24 wind conditions introduces a temporal mismatch; 1,122 out of 19,712 original objects have missing/non-positive heights and are excluded from λp, λf, and H; trees, complex terrain, winds below the displacement height, atmospheric stability, and the roughness sublayer are unmodeled. While the ratio of 100 m to morphological H can be calculated, the aforementioned issues do not automatically disappear.

 is an Apur script trial run covering only Paris city limits; southern/eastern sectors were blank on the map, leading to incomplete morphological estimates; original files are preserved and not used for this conclusion. This v2, completed with the full ring from French official IGN BD TOPO, is the delivery version and does not overwrite or move v1. Conclusions are limited to a six-month single-station exploration; it cannot be claimed that CFD has achieved independent validation, nor can the 8 m/s hypothetical threshold be treated as a regulatory limit. Run locally on  workstation, without Colab/supercomputing. Determination: this simple neutral logarithmic chain based on building morphology is not worth deploying directly; if continuing in the next step, one should first verify LFPO co-located grid points, reference height/roughness, and more physically meaningful airport → urban profiles before benchmarking against independent upper-air observations.

This round only writes v3 derived files; the original 317 pairs/lead times and 2023-09 to 2024-02 leave-month folds remain unchanged. Using 2026 building maps for 2023–24 observations entails an epochal mismatch.

Literature check: The quote "wind speed conversion using the blending height of 60 m" attributed in the task description to Blocken, Stathopoulos & van Beeck (2016), *Building and Environment* 100:50–81, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.buildenv.2016.02.004 (allegedly PDF page 25 / journal p. 74) was not found in the searchable full text of that paper; one must not falsely claim it has been verified on that page. Exact wording search was found in Blocken (2018), *Building Simulation* 11:821–870, https://doi.org/10.1007/s12273-018-0459-3, where the original text in the pedestrian wind application section states: "The terrain-related contribution is obtained by combining the expression of the vertical mean wind speed profile by the logarithmic law and the wind speed conversion using the blending height of 60 m (Verkaik 2006)." That paper attributes this to Verkaik 2006; the original Verkaik text and page numbers were not checked. Therefore, 60 m is an example mentioned in literature, not a measured blending height in Paris; this experiment takes it as a hypothesis, and additionally computes 100/200 m. Blocken (2016) PDF link: https://pure.tue.nl/ws/files/16601170/BlockenPedestrian2016.pdf; Blocken (2018) original paper link: https://pure.tue.nl/ws/portalfiles/portal/106812211/2018_BuildSim_Blocken_Position_Paper.pdf. Publisher PDFs are not copied.

Morphological parameters continue to use v2 estimates from Macdonald et al. (1998) print p. 1861 Eqs. 22–23, see ; they are not local site measurements. z0_ref=0.03 m, d_ref=0, LFPO anemometer height 10 m, cross-site 10 m MOS, and the neutral two-segment matching are all assumptions; 0.01/0.1 m and 100/200 m are sensitivities, with no parameter tuning performed on PALUPD held-out months. The 60 m mentioned in the literature does not guarantee that true profiles from both locations strictly match at this height, particularly as the building roughness sublayer, stability, and internal boundary layers are not represented.

results.label: Result
results.title: A1 step 4 correction v3: airport→city two-stage blending height
results.text:
# A1 Step 4 Correction v3: Airport → Urban Two-Segment Blending Height

One-sentence conclusion: After correcting the cross-roughness formula, the GFS 24 h MAE for the primary setting z_b=60 m, z0_ref=0.03 m is 1.455 m/s, which is 22.71% higher than local upper-air correction S0's 1.186 m/s (paired bootstrap 95% confidence interval across validation days: +13.09% to +32.96%), qualifying as a "moderate gap" under the pre-fixed interpretation, and building data cannot be judged capable of replacing observation points; however, sensitivity results for z_b=100/200 m show only about +5%, and the conclusion is dominated by the blending height assumption.

## Predefined Determination

PALUPD 111 m gate, identical to v2 with 317 pairs per source/lead time and 159 valid validation days; S0 and LFPO surface MOS predictions are reused as is, without using PALUPD held-out month winds to fit M. The primary criterion is GFS 24 h, z_b=60 m, z0_ref=0.03 m: only when relative to S0 <10% and the upper bound of the interval <15% is it termed "building data can replace"; ≥25% is a "large gap"; in between is "moderate". This round yielded +22.71%, with an upper bound of +32.96%: moderate, failing to reach the replacement threshold. The interval simultaneously encompasses 25%, so the statistical distinction between moderate/large gaps is unstable; the primary criterion is not revised post hoc simply because z_b=100/200 performed better.

## Blending Height Comparison (Same Sample; MAE in m/s, Parentheses Show Increment Relative to Same-Source S0 and by-Day Bootstrap 95% Confidence Interval)

| Source | Lead Time | S0 MAE | z_b=60 m | z_b=100 m | z_b=200 m |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| GFS | 24 h | 1.186 | 1.455；+22.71% [13.09,32.96] | 1.250；+5.37% [−0.21,11.47] | 1.253；+5.65% [−0.15,11.98] |
| GFS | 48 h | 1.324 | 1.510；+14.06% [5.55,22.63] | 1.363；+2.98% [−1.62,8.00] | 1.407；+6.26% [0.89,12.05] |
| GraphCast | 24 h | 1.167 | 1.423；+21.91% [12.90,31.61] | 1.216；+4.25% [0.10,8.57] | 1.202；+3.01% [−2.15,8.06] |
| GraphCast | 48 h | 1.267 | 1.496；+18.08% [9.71,27.24] | 1.311；+3.52% [−0.21,7.37] | 1.299；+2.60% [−2.25,7.50] |

Primary setting GFS 24 h bias +0.658 m/s, 48 h +0.661 m/s; changed to z_b=100 m, they are approximately +0.036/+0.037 m/s, respectively. z0_ref sensitivity under GFS 24 h, z_b=60 m: 0.01 m gives MAE 1.363, +14.89% [6.97,23.33]; 0.1 m gives MAE 1.654, +39.47% [26.84,53.13]. Comparing to assumed single terrain z0=0.03,d=0 MAE 1.235, +4.09%, and z0=0.3,d=0 1.640, +38.29%; v2's erroneous cross-terrain single-segment is 3.008, +153.59%, which serves only as an error diagnostic and under no circumstances as a physical baseline.

![Two-segment and comparison errors](morph_v3_mae.png)
Figure 1: PALUPD 111 m MAE on the same sample; building morphology from IGN BD TOPO V3, observations from Morrison et al. (2025) Zenodo 17710093, forecasts from NOAA GFS/CIRA AIWP, airport winds from IEM LFPO METAR; two-segment example refers to Blocken (2018) citing Verkaik (2006), not a blending height measured at this site.

## Methods, Sectors, and Limitations

U(z_b)=U_LFPO10 ln(z_b/z0_ref)/ln(10/z0_ref); U111=U(z_b) ln((111−d)/z0)/ln((z_b−d)/z0). For 30° forecast incoming wind sectors, 0.5–2 km annular ring, z0 calculated from IGN buildings ranges from 1.175–3.307 m, d from 5.18–17.59 m (for all sectors itemized see ); sectors with z_b−d≤2z0 should be skipped, but across all three values of 60/100/200 m in this round, no sector met this condition, so n remains unchanged. GFS 24 h z_b=60 m sector-wise MAE is approximately 0.78–1.97 m/s; itemized sector n, MAE, bias, and S0 comparisons see metrics.json; with only 8 to 70-odd samples per sector, strong conclusions are not drawn individually. z_b=200 m is higher than the 111 m target, representing a sensitivity of first extrapolating up to 200 m then converting downward, not a physically validated true blending layer height.

Literature citation correction: The 60 m sentence listed in the task description on Blocken et al. (2016) PDF page 25 / journal p. 74 was not verified in its searchable full text; verifiable wording comes from Blocken (2018) pedestrian wind application section and is attributed to Verkaik (2006); that original text was not verified, so 60 m remains an assumption. See provenance.md for details. Other limitations: LFPO anemometer 10 m and z0_ref assumptions were not verified on-site; airport MOS used PALUPD grid 10 m forecasts to fit LFPO winds (not airport co-located grid points); lidar hourly averages differ from METAR 2 min; neutral profiles ignore atmospheric stability, roughness sublayer, and urban internal boundary layer; 2026 building footprints back-cast to 2023–24; single-station six-month sample cannot be extrapolated to full year or prove CFD/LBM can bridge the gap. Recalculated locally on  workstation, 0 CU, no Colab/supercomputing.

# A1 Multi-site Data Minimum Coverage Verification

Conclusion: Under the counting criterion of "at least four profiles with valid values per center hour", Paris PALUPD and Prague PVK roof each have at least six consecutive months of candidate gates in the 30–150 m range; however, qualifying months for the two sites do not overlap, and Prague processed profiles have no verifiable gate-by-gate QC flags, exhibit anomalous peaks, and have time zone / roof height ambiguities, so they can only be listed as **conditional two-city candidates**, and cannot yet be claimed to have "assembled a QC-verified multi-city validation sample." [1][2][3]

Paris L3v1.42: Monthly 600 s tar containing daily NetCDF, finite u/v, actual AGL = altitude−(station_altitude−station_height). Consistent with earlier scripts, recording timestamps were shifted back by five minutes and then binned to the nearest hour, deduplicated across days by month, and counted as valid only if the same center hour has ≥4 distinct 10 min records; wind speed mean was calculated by first averaging u/v and then taking the magnitude. The numbers in the monthly table are the **number of valid hours** for that gate, not the joint forecast paired count, nor monthly coverage. The script read all monthly packages from 2022-06 to 2024-03; month-end boundary timestamps were counted according to the UTC month in which the hour falls. [2]

PAARBO 102 m is zero in 2023-10; 2023-08—2024-02 is **not valid for seven consecutive months**. PALUPD 111 m has valid values in 2023-06—2024-02, with only 139 hours in 2024-02; PASIRT 146 m is available over the long term for 2022-06—2024-02, but is a suburban station and does not replace city center stations. Finite values in PARIS L3 have already undergone L3 processing; this verification did not independently review SNR / daily retrieval flags. [2]

Prague TURDATA: [Zenodo 10655033](https://zenodo.org/records/10655033) is CC BY 4.0. Remotely read in the ZIP, the metadata workbook and processed HPL headers, without downloading the full archive. **Profiles feature only one lidar at the PVK roof** (LDR, 50.072588°N, 14.428428°E, ground 235 m ASL, instrument mounting height 4.5 m; metadata states Urban), not one lidar each at Legerova and Karlov. Karlov has a surface station and a microwave radiometer, and cannot serve as a second profile site. [1][3]

The README states that the three columns of processed HPL are height / wind direction / wind speed, with a measurement range starting at 8.7 m and a gate spacing of ~2.9 m; sampled files contain 49.3/101.4/147.8 m. The README refers to them as AGL, but the instrument is on a 4.5 m roof, and whether the instrument mounting height has been added is not substantiated by file headers: if relative to the instrument, the corresponding ground AGL would be ~53.8/105.9/152.3 m; the 100 m gate is unaffected in eligibility, while the 147.8 m gate is not classified under strict ≤150 m. The processed files show no gate-by-gate SNR/QC fields; RAW HPL contains intensity/SNR, but no SNR re-examination was performed. From 2022-04 to 10, binned by filename timestamps (the file and RAW header share the same timestamp; actual time zone unconfirmed) to hours around the hour with "time − 5 min", with ≥4 finite, non-negative processed profiles with directions in 0–360° per hour counted as "format valid"; this **is not equivalent to passing independent QC**. 2022-03 is an incomplete month and was not included in the six consecutive months; 2022-04—09 has six consecutive months of 101.4 m with 629–744 "format-valid hours" per month, plus another 608 in October. Starting from 2022-11, the HPL interval is ~33 minutes (verified via RAW headers and filename samples), with at most ~2 per hour, thus strictly zero under the ≥4 **10 min** criterion; 0 does not imply no observations for the entire month. The file interval in 2022-04/09 can be ~8–11 minutes, not strictly at equal 10 min intervals. Sample processed values show 49.3 m exceeding 50 m/s and isolated 147.8 m exceeding 70 m/s, which obviously cannot treat "format valid" directly as scientific QC; complete gate-by-gate physical review and original SNR verification remain to be done. [3]

## Determination and Next Steps

Under the relaxed threshold of "having finite processed values, ≥4 records/hour, and six consecutive months": PALUPD 111 m (recommending 2023-07—2024-01, seven full months) and Prague PVK 101.4 m (recommending 2022-04—09, six months) can form a two-city, two-site **candidate**. Under the strict threshold of "credible QC and the same calendar-month period", they cannot be assembled: these two periods of observation from the two locations **have no shared time period**, precluding concurrent cross-city pairing; however, both lie after GraphCast 2022-01, allowing independent forecast verification for each city across different periods without conflating seasonal and urban effects. The anomalous high wind values in Prague processed data, timestamp discrepancies between nominal 33 min and actual earlier 8–11 min, roof AGL definition, and time zone must be clarified first; if this fails, CROCUS should be verified with priority, and generalization cannot be declared established based on the current table. [1][2][3]

Data and execution: HTTP Range was used only on the workstation to retrieve the TURDATA ZIP central directory and required processed profile segments; Prague accumulated 363.0 MB in range requests (including central directory); Paris monthly packages were streamed in memory for 469.9 MB, without saving monthly raw packages on the workstation. No Colab or HPC was used this time, 0 CU. Original summaries can be verified: , ; scripts , .

# A1 Prague QC preflight provenance

Verification period 10-14 to 10-15 (US Eastern), local workstation; no Colab/HPC (0 CU).

- TURDATA / Bauerová et al., Zenodo record 10655033, https://zenodo.org/records/10655033, DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10655033. Original package ~1.963 GB; no full local ZIP was retained in the end. This document does not publish raw observations.
- Päschke, E., Leinweber, R., Lehmann, V. (2015), *Atmospheric Measurement Techniques* 8:2251–2266, https://doi.org/10.5194/amt-8-2251-2015, §2.2.1 intensity is SNR+1, recommending a 1.015 threshold. This is a **radial velocity** threshold, and cannot prove the full quality of the six-ray processed wind components. 1.010 and 1.020 are sensitivity values; the upper limit of 0–40 m/s for processed wind speed is a hypothesis for this round, not specified by that paper.
- Existing coverage verification counted only finite values of processed HPL, without accounting for intensity. For Paris figures, see , all being existing results of this line; Paris regression parameters were not transferred to Prague.

Data citations have been added. The internal clock time zone and instrument gate height relative reference in RAW have not yet received explicit written confirmation; another TURBAN product states its illustrated time is UTC, which does not automatically prove the RAW HPL filename is UTC. # A1 Step 5 Prague Independent Replication: QC Gate Abort Note (10-15, US Eastern)

One-sentence conclusion: It has not yet been possible to confirm that the TURDATA PVK roof lidar passed gate-by-gate RAW signal quality verification for at least four consecutive months in 2022-04—09, and the file time zone remains unconfirmed; adhering to "QC first, score later", AIWP/GFS were not fetched, and Paris-style S0/S1/S3 scores were not calculated. The Prague replication result is "unclear" and cannot serve as an independent validation or refutation of the Paris conclusion.

## Actual Checks

- Sourced from the public CC BY 4.0 ZIP in [TURDATA Zenodo 10655033](https://zenodo.org/records/10655033). Previously, counts were based only on finite values in processed HPL: for the 101.4 m gate, 2022-04—09 had 719/743/629/640/744/720 hours each month (≥4 records per hour), which are not hours passing RAW SNR/QC; see lines 34–57. Earlier file intervals were ~11 min, but the published README stated "about 33 min"; judgment must be based on actual timestamps rather than nominal frequency.
- In this round, the scanning pattern was verified from RAW HPL headers as `Wind profile - overlapping`, 6 rays, gate length 18 m, overlapping spacing ~3 m, 75° elevation angle; RAW column `Intensity (SNR+1)`. The processed HPL 101.4 m is a **candidate interpretation of instrument-relative gate height**; the metadata sheet clearly specifies LDR on PVK roof, ground elevation 235 m ASL, `Height (m AGL)=4.5`. RAW geometry is consistent with the 101.4 m instrument gate, so relative to ground AGL it could be ~105.9 m; the README simultaneously refers to range as AGL, and the original files have no field explicitly stating "4.5 m added". The exact height reference still requires verification; 101.4 m cannot be asserted as ground AGL.
- Päschke et al. (2015, *AMT* 8:2251–2266, §2.2.1) recommended radial velocity SNR 0.015 for Halo StreamLine, i.e., RAW intensity ≥1.015, while also discussing lower thresholds. An exploratory conservative screening was attempted: at least 4 of the 6 radial rays at the RAW ~101 m gate reach 1.015, processed wind speed is finite and 0–40 m/s (40 is this round's **hypothesized** outlier cutoff), with ≥4 qualified processed profiles per center hour; sensitivity was also tested for 1.010/1.020. Testing only a sample on 2022-04-15: 133 RAW/processed pairs yielded 24/23/19 qualified hours under thresholds 1.010/1.015/1.020, respectively; see for details. This is merely a **single-day screening**, not proof of validity for four months; per-ray intensity gating did not replace VAD retrieval R²/condition numbers or cross-site QC with adjacent stations.
- RAW header `Start time: 20220415 00:02:06.51` and filename `..._20220415_000156` only prove that both use similar device clocks, not that the clock is UTC. Other measurements on Zenodo have UTC explanations, but no file-by-file evidence explicitly marking this stretch of HPL original device clock as UTC was found; if CEST were mistakenly taken as UTC, forecast pairing would shift by two hours.
- The preflight target was all 25,934 RAW HPL objects for 2022-04—09. Remote ZIP byte-range sequential reading was too slow; switching to 12 threads resulted in Zenodo returning HTTP 429; falling back, an attempt was made to download ~1.963 GB (below the single-request 5 GB cap) to WSL temporary space, but only ~66 MB was transferred before the tool timed out, and the incomplete temporary file has been deleted. It is impossible to claim four-month QC passage or fewer than four months based on this. Script retains reviewable rules; its concurrency must be reduced in a 429 environment, and failures cannot be treated as missing observations. Neither the entire database nor grid fields were saved.

## Original Criteria / Paris Comparison

| Item | Paris Reported | Prague Current Round |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Local station corrected 24 h MAE | PALUPD 111 m ~1.19 m/s | Not evaluated; QC gate not passed |
| Local station corrected 48 h MAE, persistence/climatology improvement | See | Not evaluated |
| ≥8 m/s AUC ≥0.85 | Paris selected GFS ~0.92 | Not evaluated |
| No local upper-air site S1 relative to S0, mixed height sensitivity | Paris see | Not evaluated |

No valid Prague site hourly series, forecast matching metrics, or plots. According to the prerequisites of the task statement, no MAE/AUC plots that would imply completed results are produced, and no fabricated intervals are filled in. 0 CU, neither Colab nor HPC was launched, nor were Paris materials modified. The next minimum step is to obtain HPL time zone and instrument height explanations, and complete RAW ray and retrieval quality checks for four or more months when server rate limits permit; forecast scoring must not be replicated without passing the gate.

# A1 Prague PVK Roof Lidar: Independent Replication after RAW QC (10-15 01:53, US Eastern)

One-sentence conclusion: The 101.4 m gate passed the preset RAW intensity screening for six consecutive months, making Prague scorable; for GraphCast preselected in 2022-04—05, in the leave-one-month-out evaluation for 2022-06—09, the 24 h wind speed MAE baseline gate passed, but the 48 h improvement over climatology had an interval straddling the threshold, and the 8 m/s AUC did not reach 0.85, so the preset "predictability" overall **did not pass**; the two-step conversion of airport surface MOS + building morphometry at preset z_b=60 m had an error ~48–53% higher than local station MOS, indicating a large gap, and the moderate-gap judgment from Paris cannot be copied directly. This is an exploratory result from a short-term single site with few high-wind events, not proof of a general failure of AI urban forecasting.

## Prerequisite QC and Time/Height

The official 1.963 GB ZIP for TURDATA PVK roof was kept entirely on Colab CPU, pairing RAW/processed HPL one by one. Primary screening: at least four of the six radial rays for gate 32 have intensity ≥ 1.015 (Päschke et al. 2015, §2.2.1, journal pp. 2253–2254; this is a radial SNR threshold); processed 101.4 m wind speed is finite and 0–40 m/s (upper limit **assumption**); at least four qualified profiles per center hour based on file clock. 1.010/1.020 are threshold sensitivities. This workflow does **not** test VAD retrieval R²/condition number; "passing QC" refers only to this preset screening, not an instrument product certification.

| 2022 Month | intensity≥1.010 hours | ≥1.015 hours | ≥1.020 hours | Primary screening monthly mean wind m/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 04 | 706 | 660 | 607 | 4.88 |
| 05 | 742 | 730 | 693 | 4.18 |
| 06 | 617 | 613 | 585 | 3.98 |
| 07 | 626 | 619 | 581 | 3.94 |
| 08 | 744 | 734 | 705 | 3.38 |
| 09 | 693 | 638 | 584 | 3.66 |

All six months have a large number of qualified hours; this count is not the joint paired forecast count for 00/12 UTC. The TURBAN report (Bauerová et al. 2024 preprint, p. 13 §2.3) explicitly states that data use UTC; for LKPR UTC METAR, cross-correlation between HPL file clock and airport hourly wind at lags of −2/0/+2 hours is 0.768/0.847/0.711 (jointly ~3992–3994 hours), with 0 lag being the best; however, based only on diurnal mean correlation, −2 hours is higher, so zero lag is a combined judgment based on synoptic weather phase and the paper, not an independent calibration of individual RAW device clocks. The README terms HPL gate height as AGL, and this round primarily uses 101.4 m AGL; metadata places the lidar on a roof with instrument 4.5 m AGL; if HPL is counted from the instrument, the true gate height is ~105.9 m. HPL does not explicitly state whether roof height is already added, leaving ~4.5 m ambiguity in absolute height; both interpretations fall under the ~100 m gate category.

## Pre-specified S0 Primary Method Criteria

All four sources (GraphCast, Pangu, FCNv2 with GFS initial conditions, and operational GFS) initialized at 00/12 daily for 2022-04—09, at 24/48 h, 366 initializations × 4 sources = 1464 objects, were all obtained; only the PVK small window was extracted and site series retained. Preselection on 2022-04—05 for 24 h MAE chose `GRAP_v100_GFS` 10 m wind × z0=0.03 m log law (this z0 follows the Paris assumption); 2022-06—09 leave-one-month-out cross-fitting was applied to local station linear MOS, logistic regression, and non-monthly UTC cycle climatology, with persistence using same-gate observations at initialization time. Evaluation months were not used for source/method preselection. Fixed-multiplier methods are mathematically approximately equivalent after linear intercept-slope MOS; preselected labels do not prove physical correctness of z0=0.03 m.

| 111/101 m Urban Gate Comparison | Prague PVK 101.4 m, GraphCast Primary Method | Paris PALUPD 111 m, Original Experiment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 24 h corrected MAE | 1.106 m/s (196 pairs shared across four sources) | GFS primary method ~1.19 m/s |
| 48 h corrected MAE | 1.200 m/s (196 pairs) | See |
| 24 h improvement over persistence ≥15% | 35.9%, daily bootstrap 95% CI 26.1%–44.7%, passed (full baseline n=175) | ~53.6%, passed |
| 24 h improvement over climatology ≥15% | 26.2%, CI 18.3%–34.0%, passed (n=175) | ~47.1%, passed |
| 48 h improvement over persistence ≥15% | 34.6%, CI 23.7%–42.8%, passed (n=176) | ~51.5%, passed |
| 48 h improvement over climatology ≥15% | 17.9%, CI 9.5%–25.6%, point estimate passed, interval straddles 15%, **not considered passed** (n=176) | ~41.0%, passed |
| 24 h ≥8 m/s probability AUC≥0.85 | 0.686, CI 0.390–0.955, **not passed** (n=175, only 5 events) | ~0.921, passed |

Per-source 24 h corrected MAE (same 196 pairs): GraphCast 10 m conversion 1.106, Pangu 1.147, GFS direct 100 m 1.151, FCNv2 direct 100 m 1.287 m/s; GraphCast vs. GFS shows only a 0.045 m/s difference in point estimate, without independent statistical criteria established for this source difference. High-wind events were extremely scarce, yielding very wide AUC CIs; point estimate differences should not be attributed to AI architectures.

## Without Local Upper-Air Station: S0/S1/S3 (Same Source, Same Fold, Same 196 Pairs/Lead Time)

For S1, LKPR METAR 10 m wind was used to fit per-fold airport MOS against the 10 m forecast of the same PVK grid point, followed by a two-step conversion to 101.4 m at assumed blending height z_b=60 m using airport open terrain z0_ref=0.03 m and z0/d derived from OSM building morphometry over 0.5–2 km, 30° upwind sectors. Story ×3 m and 15 m imputation for buildings without height are both assumptions; among 10,776 building footprints, only 122 have explicit heights, 7,719 have stories, and 2,935 have neither. Across sectors, d=3.21–9.18 m, z0=0.71–2.05 m; all satisfy z_b−d>2z0. As in Paris Step 3, airport observations were fitted against the PVK grid point 10 m forecast, not a collocated MOS of airport grid points. S3 is direct 100 m without upper-air correction (GFS) or 10 m × assumed log law (GraphCast). S0 is local upper-air MOS.

| Source/Lead time | S0 MAE | S3 MAE (relative to S0) | S1 z_b=60 m MAE (relative to S0; 95% CI) | S1 z_b=100 m | S1 z_b=200 m |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GFS 24 h | 1.151 | 1.389 (+20.6%) | 1.701 (+47.8%; +30.9%～+66.1%) | 1.492 (+29.6%) | 1.336 (+16.1%) |
| GFS 48 h | 1.247 | 1.570 (+25.8%) | 1.786 (+43.1%; +28.0%～+59.3%) | 1.575 (+26.3%) | 1.428 (+14.5%) |
| GraphCast 24 h | 1.106 | 1.200 (+8.5%) | 1.696 (+53.3%; +36.2%～+72.2%) | 1.458 (+31.9%) | 1.278 (+15.6%) |
| GraphCast 48 h | 1.200 | 1.309 (+9.1%) | 1.757 (+46.4%; +31.4%～+62.1%) | 1.514 (+26.2%) | 1.342 (+11.9%) |

According to the pre-agreed interpretation in the original task, S1 being ≥25% higher than S0 under z_b=60 m is judged as a "large gap"; point estimates shrink markedly under z_b=100/200 m, indicating that unconstrained blending height remains dominant. Under the GFS 24 h S0/S1 primary setup, deterministic CSI for ≥8 m/s is 0/0.077; events were rare, and one cannot claim S1 is superior to S0 based on this. For all sensitivities and bias/AUC/CSI for airport z0_ref=0.01/0.1 m, see . The post-hoc better z_b=200 m was not adopted as the primary scheme.

The time periods of this city and Paris do not overlap, and observational sites, nearby roughness, and missingness in open building heights all differ; no causal attribution to urban effects is made. The original in the directory is an incomplete historical explanatory note from the prior round, not overwritten; this document along with , are follow-up reports after full data retrieval this round. Two plots and . The original 1.963 GB ZIP and full OSM geometries were not saved to the workstation.

Main limitations: only one Prague rooftop station and four evaluation months; only five 8 m/s events (full baseline sample), rendering ROC impossible to generalize stably; RAW intensity proxy is not equal to complete VAD QC; HPL height may have ~4.5 m ambiguity; OSM 2026 map retroactively applied to 2022, with widespread floor-based extrapolation/missing-value imputation; morphometry, airport roughness, and z_b were not verified on site; airport MOS is cross-location. The current "failure to pass preset gates" must not be phrased as global forecasts being impossible to use in urban areas.

For sources and definitions, see ; for monthly `MONTH_DONE` records, see , ; monthly raw QC JSONs were not successfully saved to the delivery directory, so summaries can only be reviewed from the retained site paired series, execution logs, and scripts; per-ray RAW cannot be redone on the workstation. Metrics and scripts can be reviewed in the same directory. Colab CPU throughout, session for this task has been terminated; the shared billing includes other sessions, and account balance changes cannot be counted as CU for this task.

# Low-Altitude UAV Wind Forecast (Exploring)

This sub-project investigated whether global AI weather forecast models (`GraphCast`, `Pangu-Weather`, and `FourCastNet v2GFS` within 0.02–0.06 m/s. Calibrating with local urban lidar via linear Model Output Statistics (MOS) reduced 24h MAE to 1.11–1.19 m/s, whereas uninstrumented sites using building-morphometric profile conversions faced a +5% to +48% MAE penalty dominated by unconstrained blending heights.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead launched the sub-project under Liang Hu's guidance on low-to-moderate UAV wind thresholds, coordinating with Digital Twin Wind Tunnel Lead to reuse OKC GPU-LBM fields and dispatching Step 1 (12-month OKC verification of `GraphCast`, `Pangu-Weather`, and `FourCastNet v2` vs. `GFS`) plus literature surveys.
- **2026-10-14**: After Oklahoma Mesonet rules and retired stations (`OKCN` 2018, `OKCWGraphCastGFS` within +2.57% (24h) and +1.17% (48 h) MAE, with `FourCastNet v2` 100 m to ASOS 10 m ratios averaging 1.483.
- **2026-10-14**: Three reviewers audited the literature review and Step 1 protocol (3/3 conditional support), citing global station benchmarks (`WeatherReal`, >18,000 stations) and NWP-coupled urban LES/LBM studies, while requiring pre-registered 2022 model selection, a 10-year (2013–2022) climatology baseline, logistic exceedance probabilities, and METAR gust-truncation notes.
- **2026-10-14**: Under the adjudicated Step 1 protocol (selecting `GraphCast` on 2022 data and testing on full-year 2023), `GraphCast` passed the 24h (+0.01% vs. `GFS`; -39.4% vs. persistence; -28.0% vs. climatology) and 48 h (-0.59% vs. `GFSGFS` by -0.0080 (95% CI -0.0616 to +0.0408, tied).
- **2026-10-14**: In Step 1.5 (0 CU), coupling 2023 OKC southerly forecasts with 741 virtual probes (50/100/150 m AGL) from the OKC LBM dataset showed 24h 8 m/s exceedance hours jumping from 8.8% at 10 m airport stations to 52.6%–62.3% at 100 m when scaled from 10 m winds, versus 10.4%–30.6% with `FourCastNet v2` 100 m winds.
- **2026-10-14**: In Step 2 using open 2022–2024 Paris Doppler lidar data at central urban site `PALUPDGraphCast` vs. `GFS` within 0.02–0.06 m/s.
- **2026-10-14**: Step 3 (0 CU) tested `PALUPDPAARBOLFPO`) 10 m METAR MOS plus log-law extrapolation ranged from +4.1% (z_0=0.03 m) to +38% (z_0=0.3 m) and >100% under a 0.3 power law.
- **2026-10-14**: In Step 4 (0 CU), deriving directional roughness (z_0=1.2text--3.3 m, d=5text--18 m) from 3D Paris buildings via Macdonald (1998) gave +153.6% MAE (3.008 m/s) under a single-layer formula; under a corrected two-layer blending-height conversion, z_b=60 m yielded a +22.7% MAE gap (1.455 m/s, 95% CI +13.1% to +33.0%), shrinking to +5.4%–+5.7% at z_b=100text--200 m.
- **2026-10-14**: A survey of 8 urban networks (0 CU) identified Prague (`TURDATA` rooftop lidar at 101 m AGL, April–September 2022) as the only open multi-month urban dataset overlapping the AIWP archive outside Paris.
- **2026-10-15**: In Step 5 (Prague 101 m AGL, 613–734 hours/month), local lidar MOS achieved 1.11 m/s 24h MAE (-36% vs. persistence, -26% vs. climatology; AI vs. `GFS` within 0.045 m/s), missing full gate passage only on the 48 h climatology CI and rare 8 m/s events (5 samples, 0.69 AUC), while uncalibrated two-layer morphometric scaling left a +48% MAE gap at z_b=60 m (+30% at 100 m, +16% at 200 m); AI Weather Models Lead submitted the Stage 1 assessment with Options A (LBM profile conversion) and B (shelve).

## Where it stands

Stage 1 exploration across Oklahoma City, Paris, and Prague is complete, showing that open AI weather models match operational `GFS` (~1.1–1.2 m/s 24h MAE with local lidar calibration) and isolating uncalibrated urban profile transfer (+5% to +48% MAE gap) as the main bottleneck. The sub-project awaits Liang Hu's decision between LBM-assisted profile parameterization and shelving.

# A2 High-wind forecasting and active control for buildings

## Objective
Across three control layers — forecast-driven (hours–days) control mode switching, second–minute feedforward, and real-time feedback — determine which layer AI weather forecasts can serve; control encompasses active mass dampers (AMDs) and active aerodynamic shaping, with wind as the unified input.

## Current Status
Node opened on 10-14. 14:38 Step 1: Grok quick search dispatched and returned (14:39, report, abstract-level only); 14:5x Step 2 Deep Research (--gemini) dispatched (brief), borrowing the feedforward conclusions from A3 Grok report cb8bff without re-searching (its Section 6 numbers were later judged unverified by A3 review and discarded, replaced by citations verified in A3). Original plan: (brief), read A3's Grok report after our report returns (borrowing the feedforward portion), then draft the second Deep Research (--gemini) brief, and send conclusions to 

Deep Research returned at 15:0x; after Lead verified citations, sent to review **** (3 reviewers, dispatched at 15:1x, awaiting results). Review packet.

Review (E with reservations, A does not support, D with reservations) rendered verdict →. Original minimal experiment (AI forecast → TPU → threshold exceedance) cancelled. New minimal experiment dispatched to ideas **** (queued): in-house Silsoe LBM lead-time τ prediction + stroke-limited active mass damper preview feedforward, workstation CPU, 0 CU, task brief.

### Three-Layer Table (Finalized after Review)
| Time Scale | Control Action | Required Lead Time and Accuracy | Precedents (Citation & Page) | Can AI Forecasts Supply It? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hours–Days | Slow actions only: mass-block recentering and mechanical unlocking/locking, hydraulic/backup power preparation and manual check, slow mechanical aerodynamic shaping or TLD water filling/draining, full-storm stroke budgeting | Literature does not specify execution duration or latest decision time; "requires hour-scale lead time" is an assumption | No written operating procedures for "switching based on weather forecasts" (none found across three independent searches; not claiming non-existence); commissioned devices trigger in real time via acceleration/stroke thresholds (PAFC: Zhou & Li 2022 Eng Struct 269:114840 abstract, "accurately triggered according to operation principles", damping ratio 0.6%→2–7%, no threshold values given) | Yes, but marginal value is small: slow actions are already covered by official typhoon/hurricane warnings; global AI models lack skill for hurricane intensity (DeMaria 2025 card, event_step0, line 14) → **deferred** |
| Seconds–Minutes | Near-field preview feedforward / preview MPC; gain reduction, semi-active gear shifting (millisecond–second scale, real-time sensing suffices) | Preview seconds: no verified source (numbers in Section 6 of A3 Grok report discarded after A3 review); wind-turbine lidar feedforward is effective under stationary turbulence: Guo 2023 WES 8:149 §5.2 tower-base fore-aft bending moment DEL up to −16.7%, Bossanyi 2014, Schlipf 2018 (verified by A3) | No full-scale engineering validation; research/concept level: Abdelaziz & Hobeck 2022 SPIE 12046 (10.1117/12.2630805, surrounding-building pressure taps + GRU prediction window + aerodynamic corner flaps, 1:400 wind tunnel, RMS torsional acceleration up to −75%, title verified, content cited via reviewer D); US5592791A (1997 patent, corner outrigger boom upstream wind measurement feedforward, original text verified by Lead); Klein 1972, Soong & Skinner 1981, Abdel-Rohman 1983 synchronous wind-sensing aerodynamic appendages (cited via Korkmaz 2011 journal p. 2130); theoretical Marzbanrad 2004 Eng Struct pp.1463–1471 | No — requires on-site near-field wind measurements; **narrowed focus of this node**; in-house LBM τ=0 correlation 0.67 at 7 m → 0.35 at 27 m (in-house data) |
| Real-time | Acceleration/displacement feedback | None | Standard practice | Not needed |

**Existing preview statistics results**: near-field velocity provides second-scale preview of windward Cp (correlation half-decay lead time 2.6–6.5 s, in-house data). Control Round 2 ideas (dispatched 10-14 16:1x) first performs a control-model self-check: without saturation, perfect preview must reduce acceleration RMS by ≥30%, before measuring the ratio of predicted-preview gain to perfect-preview gain; task brief, deliverables.

**One-sentence conclusion (finalized 10-14)**: Shelved. AI weather forecasts can only serve hour-scale slow actions with small marginal value; second-scale near-field preview offers large theoretical gains (perfect preview reduces acceleration by 68–80%), but prediction from sparse upstream probes captures only 0–17% of that gain, with the bottleneck in inflow prediction skill. For causes, missing conditions, and restart criteria, see .

(Earlier provisional note) Driving building control with AI weather forecasts has low value, so that layer is shelved; what is worth pursuing is second-scale near-field preview feedforward (research-level precedents exist, no full-scale engineering validation), first using in-house data to quantify usable lead time and gain for stroke-limited dampers before deciding whether to promote or merge into A3's downburst preview experimental framework.

## Established Decisions
- 2026-10-14 Literature conclusion verdict and scope narrowing → 

## Experiments Conducted and Results
| Date | What Was Done | One-Sentence Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10-14 | Grok quick search | Almost no precedents for building/bridge wind-induced vibration control driven by "upstream inflow preview" or "numerical weather prediction"; existing "prediction" studies mostly involve MPC state extrapolation / disturbance estimation; operational ATMDs start up and lock based on acceleration thresholds (fragmentary numbers only, unverified). Three issues: 2004 preview control DOI actually points to another paper (Xie 2004 interference effects); Taipei 101 TAO DOI not found; "~0.75–1.5 s effective preview" was back-calculated by Grok from our in-house 30 m figure and does not count as literature evidence |
| 10-14 | Minimal experiment Round 2 v3 (ideas, workstation CPU 20.5 s, 0 CU) | With corrected feedforward, perfect 8 s preview reduces acceleration RMS by 68% (near spectral peak) / 80% (off-resonance); velocity-probe predicted preview captures only 0–17% of the perfect gain, with only 4 of 360 combinations (near spectral peak with tight stroke limit, 10.3–12.6% reduction) passing the gate, showing weak discriminative power; best off-resonance gain is 0.8% → bottleneck lies in inflow prediction skill |
| 10-14 | Minimal experiment v2 (ideas, workstation CPU 14.5 s, 0 CU) | Preview statistics: lead time at which windward 11-point Cp correlation drops by half is 2.6 s (7 m upstream) → 6.5 s (27 m), unchanged after notch filtering (2.7–6.6 s), single realization from in-house data. Control: no predicted-preview combination passed the gate, but **even perfect 8 s preview reduced RMS by only 0.4–0.9%**, and the loose stroke tier still hit saturation — control model lacked discriminative power, invalidating the control conclusion; Round 2 dispatched |
| 10-14 | Deep Research (--gemini) | Confirmed that real inflow preview for buildings/bridges is essentially a blank slate; identified genuine preview-control paper Marzbanrad 2004; compiled operating-logic table for Citicorp, Kyobashi Seiwa, Yokohama Landmark, Canton Tower, and PAFC (original texts unverified); found no forecast-switched operating procedures. Excluded: deriving 1–2 s from in-house 30 m (violates task brief), vehicle/passenger-boarding-bridge cases, and unreferenced "manual pre-warming several hours before a typhoon" |
| 10-14 | Lead original-text verification of Abdelaziz 2021 | Verified (PDF p. 1 abstract): predictor ANN looks up flap angles from current wind conditions, steady 2D FSI, "preliminary results" show amplitude reduction up to 94%; this is "wind-condition scheduling", not inflow preview |

## Parameter Source Table
| Parameter | Value | Source or "Assumed" | Places Checked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PAFC ATMD startup/lockout threshold | Not found in public literature | Grok snippet 0.01 m/s² / 2.2 m not adopted | Grok, DR, Crossref/OpenAlex abstracts (not accessible) |
| Citicorp TMD wake-up threshold | 0.003 g for two cycles | Secondary citation via DR (vibrationdata/buffalo webpage), original text unverified | No hits in pages |
| Kyobashi Seiwa AMD stroke/force | ±25 cm / 1 tf | Secondary citation via DR, unverified | — |
| Minimal experiment TPU scale / α | 1/400, α=1/4, 1/6 | TPU official case page (verified 10-13) | |

## Open Items and Next Steps
- Correlation–τ–distance table has been copied to the Digital Twin Wind Tunnel Root Lead, who archived it with no objections to the interpretation. After A2 was shelved, they will no longer specially export empty-domain building-location inflow dynamic pressure (job 1542028); if needed upon restart, request it directly from the Digital Twin Wind Tunnel Lead, who can provide it anytime.
- Hierarchy constraint (Root Lead 10-14): this is a Tier-2 node and will not open Tier-3 sub-projects; use tasks for subdivision; task briefs must not allow tool bots to delegate further.
- Grok report returns → read A3 Grok report → Deep Research brief (--gemini) → 3-reviewer review → define minimal GPU experiment candidates.
- In-house data reference: Silsoe LBM inflow → windward Cp correlation decays monotonically with upstream distance (0.67 at 7 m → 0.35 at 27 m), (in-house data, not literature).

## Literature Basis
- Knowledge base (10-14 search): no cards on forecast/preview-driven structural control. Local full texts (pages) contain readable leads without cards yet: Abdelaziz et al. 2021 JWEIA 212:104601 smart facade control (Zotero U8L4S2VK, PDF p. 1); Korkmaz 2011 active structural control review (T8ADPIGM, PDF p. 18 = journal p. 2130, citing Abdel-Rohman 1983 aerodynamic appendages and Nissen 2004 bridge active aerodynamic stabilization); Kareem 1978 (2F6RHVB9, PDF p. 55 = journal p. 32). Cards to be created and verified.

items.text:
# A2 Review Package: Forecast-Driven and Inflow Preview for Active Wind Vibration Control of Buildings/Bridges—Literature Conclusions (10-14)

## Evidence Sources
- Grok Quick Check: (Grok_quick_check) (self-stated as abstract-level only)
- Google Deep Research: ((citations are redirect links, no DOI)
- A3 Grok (wind turbine LiDAR feedforward, borrowed): *
- Our track data (non-literature): —— Silsoe cube LBM, single-station upstream probe → windward 11-point Cp(t) linear FIR average correlation: surface distance 7 m 0.67, 12 m 0.62, 17 m 0.55, 22 m 0.45, 27 m 0.35. Note: this is a low-rise cube, same-instant prediction (not lead-time prediction), which cannot be directly converted into "preview seconds" for tall buildings.

## Verified by Lead
- Abdelaziz et al. 2021 JWEIA 212:104601 (local PDF page 1 abstract): predictor ANN provides facade panel angle combinations based on current wind conditions, steady-state 2D FSI, "preliminary results" amplitude reduced by up to 94%. Categorized as scheduling based on wind conditions, not inflow preview.
- Marzbanrad, Ahmadi, Jha 2004 "Optimal preview active control of structures during earthquakes", Engineering Structures, pp.1463–1471, DOI 10.1016/j.engstruct.2004.05.010 (existence confirmed via Crossref; content only reviewed via DR paraphrase). The 10.1016/j.engstruct.2004.03.007 provided by Grok is actually Xie 2004 on interference effects, incorrect.
- Laks, Simley, Pao 2013 ACC "A spectral model for evaluating the effect of wind evolution on wind turbine preview control", DOI 10.1109/acc.2013.6580400 (exists on Crossref).
- Zhou & Li 2022 Eng Struct 269:114840 (Ping An Finance Center ATMD, multiple tropical storms) exists; abstract not retrieved.

## Lead Determined Not to Adopt
- Grok's "PAFC 0.01 m/s² sustained for two cycles to start, stroke >2.2 m locked": no original text, DR called it a confusion (DR's own explanation that "2.2 m comes from medical literature" cannot be verified either). Neither is adopted; PAFC operating thresholds are recorded as "not found in public literature".
- Both reports extrapolated an "effective preview of approximately 1–2 s" using 30 m from our track: the project charter explicitly ordered not to treat this as literature evidence, and our track data is a same-instant prediction, so the conversion does not hold. Not adopted.
- In the DR table, "Xiao 2025 active rear wing + road preview 92.73%" is vehicle suspension, conflated with bridge flap literature; "passenger boarding bridge 3D LiDAR MPC 73.5% (Yoo 2026)" is a non-wind-load contact problem. Neither is taken as a precedent for building wind vibration.
- DR's "property management conducts human-in-the-loop review, hydraulic pre-loading, and UPS cut-in hours before typhoon landfall according to meteorological bureau warnings": no citation, not adopted, listed as pending verification.
- The open-source MACS ARB recommended by DR (Tomizuka/Chen adaptive vibration control benchmark): targets narrowband disturbances, not building wind vibration, for reference only.

## Proposed Conclusions (for Review)
1. In active wind vibration control of buildings/bridges, precedents of using upstream inflow measurements or numerical weather prediction as control inputs are virtually nonexistent in public literature; existing "predictive control" is mostly estimation and extrapolation of structural states or disturbances (Miyamoto 2025 JWEIA 261:106049; Zimmer 2022 SCHM 10.1002/stc.3034, abstract level). The theory of preview control originates from earthquakes (Marzbanrad 2004) and wind turbine LiDAR feedforward (A3).
2. The startup and protection logic of operational AMD/ATMD/HMD is governed by structural acceleration and stroke thresholds (Citicorp 0.003 g two-cycle wake-up, Kyobashi Seiwa ±25 cm/1 tf bounded force, PAFC two-stage damping, all paraphrased by DR and without checking original texts); **no** written operating procedures or lead-time/accuracy requirements for "switching modes several hours in advance based on weather forecasts" were found in public literature.
3. Three-tier assessment:
 - Hour–day (mode switching: activation, gain reduction/two-stage, locking, semi-active gear shift, aerodynamic shape presetting): physically justified need (stroke/output saturation), literature gap; matched with time scales of AI/numerical weather prediction, this is the only tier that AI forecasting can directly supply.
 - Second–minute (preview feedforward): wind turbine LiDAR feedforward is effective under steady turbulence (Guo 2023 WES 8:149 §5.2, Bossanyi 2014, Schlipf 2018, verified in A3), specific preview seconds have no verified sources (10-14 addendum: A3 Grok Section 6 numbers rejected upon review); no empirical evidence for buildings/bridges; AI forecast time scales do not match, requiring on-site wind measurement; our track LBM data indicates near-field inflow predictability drops relatively rapidly with distance.
 - Real-time feedback: no forecast needed.
4. Conclusion: Worth continuing, but only at the "hour–day forecast-driven mode switching" tier; the first step is not to design a controller, but to test "how many hours in advance AI forecasts can reliably determine that structural response exceeds thresholds" (a decision skill issue).
5. Minimal GPU/computation experiment candidate: Select 3–5 hurricanes making landfall on US coastal cities (same batch as Node B), use AI global models (A1 existing AIWP data retrieval: GraphCast/Pangu/FCN v2) to backcalculate roof-height hourly mean wind at 6–72 h lead times, convert the response obtained via the TPU isolated tall building library (1/400, α=1/4, already used in our track) into top peak acceleration, determine "threshold-exceeding periods" according to comfort/device protection thresholds, and compare hit rate/false alarm rate variations with lead time against results similarly converted from ASOS observed wind. Estimated ≤5 Colab CU or CPU.
## Reviewers Please Answer
- Are there counterexamples to Conclusions 1–3 (specifically: is there any literature/operational report where a building/bridge actually used upstream wind measurements or weather forecasts for control or mode switching)?
- Does the judgment of "worth continuing, only at the hour–day tier" hold? Can the minimal experiment design answer this question, and are there any fatal flaws?
- Are there any unmarked speculative parameters?

items.title: Verdict: A2 literature conclusions on forecast/preview-driven control of wind-induced vibration of buildings/bridges (2026-10-14)
items.text:
# Verdict: Literature Conclusions on Forecast/Preview Driving for A2 Building/Bridge Wind Vibration Control (2026-10-14)

Reviewers: E (Gemini) support with reservations; A (GPT-6) do not support; D (GLM) support with reservations. 3/3 valid, no alternates. Lead personally verified: US5592791A original patent text (Google Patents, "upstream sensor array consisting of wind sensors ... located on poles off the corners of an upper floor"), Abdelaziz & Hobeck 2022 SPIE 12046 (DOI 10.1117/12.2630805, exists on Crossref), DeMaria 2025 card (line 14: AI global models have no intensity skill, MAE ~40 kt after 72 h and almost entirely biased weak), A1 provenance line 7 (AIWP file f000_f240_06, 6 h step).

## Mandatory Revisions (All Adopted)
1. **Add search boundaries to Conclusion 1 and incorporate counterexamples** (D, A, E). Revised to: In wind vibration control of buildings/bridges, **there are no full-scale/operational precedents driven by upstream preview or weather forecasts**; there are at least three categories of research-grade and conceptual-grade precedents—Abdelaziz & Hobeck 2022 (surrounding building pressure measurement network + GRU prediction window + aerodynamic corner plates, 1:400 wind tunnel, RMS rotational acceleration reduced by up to 75%, based on D's citation of the NSF PAR full-text abstract, Lead only verified that the title exists); US5592791A (1997 patent, upstream wind sensing on poles extending from upper-floor four corners → feedforward-driven mass, conceptual grade, no operational evidence, Lead verified original text); early "synchronous wind measurement at building top driving active aerodynamic appendages" Klein 1972, Soong & Skinner 1981, Abdel-Rohman 1983 (cited via Korkmaz 2011, local PDF page 18 = journal page 2130, original text unverified). Search scope: Grok (abstract level), Deep Research (redirect links), local full text, three reviewers.
2. **Correct Citicorp to passive TMD** (E): The 0.003 g two-cycle wake-up is for the hydraulic oil-film bearings, not active force application; the first AMD building is 1989 Kyobashi Seiwa (E cited Soong & Dargush 98-MN01, Lead has not verified original text). **Delete "PAFC two-stage damping"** (E, A): The source is the Zhang & Li 2019 multi-stage PTMD design, not the operational logic of PAFC's operational ATMD; the PAFC 2022 abstract (CityU institutional repository, verified by both E and D) only states "damping ratio 0.6% → 2–7% across 7 storms" and "precisely triggered according to operating principles", without thresholds. Kyobashi Seiwa ±25 cm/1 tf comes from 11WCEE 1547, which is seismic bounded force control (E), and cannot serve as the basis for wind-protection switching.
3. **Retain only slow actions for the hour–day tier** (E, A): Gain reduction and semi-active gear shifting are millisecond-to-second electronic operations that can be performed in real time by on-site accelerometers/anemometers without needing weather forecasts. The only actions genuinely requiring hour-level lead time are: mass recentering and mechanical locking, hydraulic pressure/backup power preparation and human-in-the-loop review, slow mechanical shaping or TLD water filling/draining, and stroke budget for the entire storm. The execution duration and latest decision time for these actions **are not provided in the literature** (A), so "requiring hour–day forecasts" is downgraded to an assumption.
4. **Revoke original minimal experiment** (E identified four fatal flaws, concurred by A and D): AI global models have no intensity skill for hurricanes (DeMaria 2025), AIWP has 6 h per frame; the same batch of ASOS had missing reports during peak periods (Node B chain_a_results); forecasts and observations share the same deterministic conversion, the TPU step is mathematically equivalent to thresholding wind speed, and lacks device dynamics and switching consequences; "A1 already has AIWP data retrieval" is untrue (only verified the directory); a sample of 3–5 storms cannot support "reliable".
5. **Unmarked parameters** (E, D, A): The original design implicitly included building geometry/frequency/damping/peak factor, thresholds, profiles, and averaging interval conversions, none of which had cited sources, and are revoked together with the experiment; the new experiment task specification must provide a parameter source table.

## For Reference Only
- Division of labor in Abdelaziz 2021: The one querying the table to provide panel angles is the optimizer ANN, while the predictor ANN is a dynamics surrogate (E, Lead verified original text and agreed); to be corrected on the project page.
- "30 m" must not be used as a physical coherence length: In results_v4b, the 30.05 m station is a fixed boundary value, correlation is undefined (A, D); our track only uses the five stations from 7–27 m with correlations 0.67 → 0.35.
- Gu & Peng 2002 used sinusoidal reference signals, not inflow preview (A). Zimmer 2022 and Miyamoto 2025 are state/disturbance estimations (A verified full text/abstract).
- No operating procedures for "switching based on forecasts": All three parties reported "not found"; retain the wording "not found", do not claim nonexistent (D, A).

## Objections Not Adopted
- A: "Worth continuing" cannot be packaged as a literature conclusion. **Adopted its qualification**, but did not adopt "overall not supported": Lead will no longer claim that literature proves the value of the hour–day tier; on the contrary, following the verdict, Lead's judgment is that **the value of this tier driven by AI weather forecasts is low** (slow actions are already covered by official typhoon/hurricane warnings, and execution durations lack literature), whereas the narrow opening worth continuing at this node shifts to **second-level near-field preview** (research-grade precedents exist, but no engineering empirical evidence). This is Lead's project trade-off based on the review, without literature backing, based on the review and our track data.

## Results
- Finalized three-tier table is available on the project page. Hour–day tier: AI forecasts can supply this but marginal gain is small (relative to official warnings), not pursued for now; second-level tier: AI forecasts cannot supply this, research-grade precedents exist but engineering gap remains, serving as the narrow opening for this node; real-time tier: no forecasts needed.
- New minimal experiment: Use our track's Silsoe v7 LBM data to change "same-instant prediction" to "lead-time τ prediction", measure the variation of usable preview duration with probe distance, and then connect a single-degree-of-freedom + active mass damper model with stroke limitations to compare "preview feedforward + feedback" versus "pure feedback". Workstation CPU, 0 CU.

# A2 Parameter Sources and Assumptions

| Parameter | Value | Source/Nature | Basis and Verification Scope |

| Time step, split, and Cp | 0.02 s, 42–642 s; q=0.00127991343 | Our track | Retain original protocol; test reporting <634 s, lead time ≤8 s |
| Probes and surface distances | −30/−25/−20/−15/−10 m, mast −27.1 m; windward surface −3 m | Our track | −33.05 fixed boundary excluded, x≥−5 and z12 excluded |
| Cp REF pressure and dynamic pressure | Causal 100 frames REF ρ; training window constant q | Our track | 16.8 Hz pressure oscillation, smoothed with causal 2 s pressure; empty domain same-window q is missing, not fabricated |
| Acoustic mode filtering | 0.27/.52/.95 Hz, iirnotch Q20 bidirectional | Frequencies from project charter; Q20 and offline method are assumptions | Two sets of sensitivities for raw/notched targets; bidirectional filtering is for offline diagnostics only |
| Surface pressure area weights | C(y,z)=V(z)+H(y)−V(3.01), Voronoi representative width; 36 m² normalized | Coordinates from ; interpolation is an assumption | Do not treat 11 points as a complete 2D pressure field; windward proxy only |
| Mass and scale | M=1, m=.05; F=ΣwCp minus training mean | Assumption | No real building scale; m/M=.05, not scanned individually, conclusions limited to this assumption |
| Frequency | 0.08545 / 1.400 Hz | Spectral peaks based on Welch of training load, far-resonance selection is an assumption | Near/far two levels of sensitivity; the former is below acoustic band, used only for proxy |
| Structural damping ratio | .02 | Assumption | Lightly damped prototype; not scanned, not a real building value |
| Stroke limits | ±.12 / ±.025 | Assumption | Loose/tight two levels of sensitivity; dimensionless displacement |
| LQR weights and saturation | Q=diag(ω²,1,20ω²,.2), R=.08; u_max=2σ_F | Assumption | Fixed to same feedback/feedforward/perfect signal comparison; not a verified physical actuator |
| End-stop | Position clipping, outward relative velocity inelastically zeroed, primary structure receives momentum | Assumption | Impulse accounted for in acceleration; real end-stop material and contact duration not modeled |
| Control discrete step | .1 s | Assumption, follows input history spacing | Control applied once every five frames on 50 Hz Cp; discrete step size not scanned |

Mass, stiffness, limits, controller, and force scales lacking literature basis are all explicitly stated as assumptions; the two levels of frequency and stroke mentioned above represent the minimum sensitivity required by the task, and robust performance cannot be claimed.

# A2: Near-Field Preview and Stroke-Constrained AMD Minimal Experiment

Pre-fixed criterion: preview feedforward is counted as "useful" only if structural acceleration RMS decreases by ≥10% relative to the same pure feedback and the damper peak stroke does not increase; results do not alter this gate.

## Data, Timing, and Boundaries
Single Silsoe v7 LBM simulation run data (non-measured); 42–642 s, 50 Hz. train 48–462 s, validation 462–522 s, test dispatch 522–634 s, with test targets for τ≤8 s still before 642 s. Each station z=1/3/6 m × three-component velocity; P_x−33.05 fixed inlet excluded; rack R_y0 as an independent station. FIR uses current and past 0–6 s (0.1 s interval), training PCA up to nine dimensions; ridge penalty 100/1000/10000 selected only on validation set. Training and validation at 10 Hz, testing at 50 Hz. Original CSV is read-only and hash matches , copied to WSL scratch; does not cross seg1/seg2 splice points.

Cp=(ρtap − past/current 100-frame causal 2 s REF ρ mean)/(3q), q=training window average ½ρ_REF|u_REF|²=0.00127991343 lattice units; constant denominator across the whole window (not step-by-step REF q). Pressure is not used as prediction input, only velocity. The attached acoustic_notch target undergoes 0.27/0.52/0.95 Hz, Q=20 offline bidirectional notch filtering; for diagnosis only, not online filtering, with possible slight preview leakage near boundaries. Both specifications' τ curves and half-correlation times are listed. For v7 with the same inflow, the complete q at the empty-field building location has no ready-made time history in the same window; this secondary specification cannot be calculated this time, and empty field from other inflow v8 cannot be substituted. See .

## Control Model and Full Combination Metrics
Cube 6×6 m windward face proxy: V2–V6 height profiles and H1–H6 spanwise profiles adopt Voronoi representative widths, with separable additive interpolation C(y,z)=V(z)+H(y)−V(3.01 m); V(3.01) is linearly interpolated between V3/V4. The 11 coefficients and station coordinates are in , original . F=Σ(w_i Cp_i) is the dimensionless proxy for the average windward Cp (equivalent to ∫Cp dA/36 m²), with the training period mean removed; not full-building force, and does not hard-convert lattice density/velocity into real-building physical force. Area interpolation coefficients may be negative (correcting intersection points), not point-by-point measured areas.

Mass M=1, AMD m=.05, damping ratio .02, frequencies near spectral peak 0.0854 Hz and off-resonance 1.4000 Hz; stroke limits ±.12/±.025 (dimensionless displacement), u_max=2 · test wind force standard deviation (this is a force scaling assumption, identical across all schemes). 0.1 s ZOH mass-spring-damper + relative stroke r; identical state LQR feedback, Q=diag(ω²,1,20ω²,.2), R=.08 (see also params.md). Feedforward is a convolution of known disturbances given by the discrete LQR closed-loop Bellman equation, taking the 0..τ predictions at each dispatch, where predictions for each discrete τ are trained independently and linearly interpolated within intervals; τ=0 has contemporaneous prediction. Pure feedback sets feedforward to zero; truth-8s uses the real future force under the same control law, serving as a "perfect signal control", which is not an upper bound of optimal control under fixed control laws and saturation/hard stops. Force saturates; after reaching limits, position is clipped, relative outward velocity is inelastically zeroed, and impulse is transferred to the primary structure, with the impulse counted into discrete acceleration; this is a simplified stop, not representative of physical details.

## Limitations and One-Sentence Verdict
The preview lead time of this experiment is given by a single LBM realization of the same run; the notch results are close to the raw specification, but the test period and acoustic filtering method have not undergone independent implementation/leak-free audit; not equivalent to a field-deployable forecast. Farther stations may show τ>0 slightly better than τ=0, reflecting advective time lag rather than unconditional distance gain. Small sample, assumed control parameters, proxy surface loads, simplified hard stops, excluding wind directions/multiple events; cannot be generalized to physical buildings. Scientific judgment has no literature basis and is based on data from this line; literature is only used for geometric coordinates, see source references in the task specification, and simulation is not referred to as measured.

Verdict: Statistical preview of near-field velocity for windward Cp is on the order of seconds, but under the current stroke-constrained AMD assumptions, it does not pass the pre-fixed joint gate of 10% acceleration reduction and no stroke increase; as a lead for further controlled benchmark experiments, it currently does not support conversion into an engineering benefit conclusion.

Run on local  workstation CPU, 0 Colab CU, no supercomputing; elapsed time 14.5 s. The root directory metrics.json/figures are preliminary diagnostic versions, not deliverable results; all formal numbers use only  and .

# A2 v3 Parameters and Sources

Data, constant q, velocity inputs, 11-point surface weights, offline notch filter: inherited from v2 params.md and run_a2.py; original CSV SHA256 verified against this line.

Assumptions: M=1, m=.05, ζ=.02, frequencies near training spectral peak and 1.4 Hz, control step size 0.1 s; units are surrogate dimensionless, not the actual building.

New control assumptions: per-step a²+ηr²+εu², Q=CᵀC+diag(1e−5,1e−5,η,1e−5), N=CᵀD, R=DᵀD+ε, a=Cx+Du+F, C=[−k,−c,0,0], D=−1. Bellman linear disturbance term includes the same-step DᵀF; solve for P using discrete DARE, H=R+BᵀPB, K=H⁻¹(BᵀPA+Nᵀ), g=Cᵀ−KᵀDᵀ+(A−BK)ᵀPE, kernel h₀=H⁻¹(BᵀPE+Dᵀ), hⱼ=H⁻¹Bᵀ[(A−BK)ᵀ]ʲ⁻¹g. Formulas originate from the quadratic Bellman derivation in this script, without literature endorsement; previously v2's state weights and feedforward omitted the same-step acceleration term, so their numerical values cannot be directly compared.

η/ε grids are (0.0001,.01,1.) / (.0001,.01,.1), respectively; from those reaching 30% in the validation window, select the combination with the minimum force RMS; not retuned for testing. Force upper limit = 20 × training wind force standard deviation; unlimited self-check uses ∞; three strokes are ∞, unconstrained FB peak × 1.5, × .75. All stroke-limit schemes share the same feedback/feedforward gains; inelastic end-stop momentum transfer and impulse acceleration are inherited from v2, representing simplified assumptions. Discount = max(0, validation Pearson r)², interpolated across lead times; compare raw targets against offline acoustic notch filter targets (no claim of online feasibility). See metrics.json for individual candidates, peak values, clipping ratios, and validation skill.

# A2 v3 Review and Explanation (Without Modifying Existing Results)

Reviewing  's 360 combinations (two frequencies × three strokes × six stations × five τ × raw / offline notch filter): raw target under near spectral peak / tight stroke had 4/30 passing the preset dual gates; notch diagnostic target had another 3/30; the remaining 10 frequency-stroke-target strata were all 0/30. Stroke, collisions, and force limiting for each combination are preserved item by item in metrics.json.

Raw target passes: 22 m from surface, τ=5 s, 10.28% reduction, accounting for 13.72% of ground truth gain; 17 m, τ=3 s, 11.22% reduction, accounting for 14.98%; 17 m, τ=5 s, 12.63% reduction, accounting for 16.87%; 24.1 m mast, τ=5 s, 12.38% reduction, accounting for 16.53%. Only these four groups; not a robust result across frequencies/strokes.

Control parameters selected in the validation segment: for near spectral peak η=0.0001, ε=0.1, perfect 8s preview reduced by 70.24% relative to feedback; for off-resonance η=1, ε=0.1, reduced by 82.20%. On the test segment, they reduced by 67.89% and 80.34%, respectively (unlimited stroke). Here, "perfect preview" is a fixed-law ground-truth signal, not an optimal upper bound. For explicit reproducibility: original control v2 omitted the direct DᵀF term in the instantaneous acceleration objective and targeted states rather than acceleration; v3 incorporates all instantaneous disturbances and future closed-loop adjoint terms.

Strict limitations: near spectral peak unlimited-stroke pure feedback peak reached 32.50 (dimensionless), while ground-truth preview was 17.65; "loose" 48.75 and "tight" 24.37 are both defined relative to this very large unconstrained feedback peak, not engineered realizable strokes. In the tight setting, pure feedback hit the end-stop for 4.11% of steps, and raw best prediction hit it for 2.59% of steps; both peaks were clipped to 24.37 by the same hard limit, so "peak does not increase" has weak discriminative power in end-stop collision combinations; it is still executed literally according to the original gate, without equating its passage with engineering practicality. The feedback deterioration caused by end-stop impulses this time is also part of the reason for the 10% reduction in the tight setting; it lacks basis for real AMD design. The best prediction for off-resonance was only about 0.1% (unlimited/loose) or 0.8% (tight), even though the ground-truth control could achieve about 80% reduction.

Discount is obtained by squaring the positive part of Pearson r for the surrogate resultant force on the validation segment and linearly interpolating across time domains, with no parameter tuning on the test segment; this was an approach permitted by the preliminary task, and does not represent an optimal discount. Frequency, mass, control cost, and impulse contact are all experimental assumptions without literature source; see params.md for details. A single simulation, surrogate loads, and no field data mean that usable control benefits for real buildings cannot be claimed. The vertical axis of result plot control.png is predicted gain / fixed ground-truth 8s gain of the same setting, colors indicate station distance, and statistical confidence intervals are not shown.

The platform repeatedly reminded that ,  belong to the reference field/budget of "Non-convective extreme wind design wind speed: AI climate simulator", which differs from the inputs, run roots, and work goals of this A2 LBM-AMD v3; those run roots were not rebuilt, Colab was neither submitted nor recomputed, and no duplicate tasks were dispatched for those two items. In this round, only the CPU completed one formal run in a2_preview/v3, with no writes to v2.

items.text:
# A2 High-Wind-Speed Forecasting and Active Control for Buildings: Shelved (2026-10-14)

## What Was Done
- Two-step literature review (Grok df4bc2, Deep Research 86bfec) + review  (3 people) verdict rendered: there is no operational engineering precedent for preview or weather-forecast-driven control in buildings/bridges; at the research/conceptual level, there are at least three categories (Abdelaziz & Hobeck 2022 SPIE; US5592791A; Klein 1972 et al., cited via Korkmaz 2011 journal page 2130). AI weather forecasting can only provide hour-to-day slow dynamics with small incremental value (already covered by official warnings; AI global models have no hurricane intensity skill, DeMaria 2025 stuck at event_step0 line 14) → Not doing.
- Minimal experiment (ideas and second round, workstation CPU, 0 CU, single Silsoe v7 LBM realization on this line):
 - Preview statistics: lead time for windward 11-point Cp correlation halving goes from 2.6 s (7 m from surface) → 6.5 s (27 m), unchanged after notch filtering; Digital Twin Wind Tunnel Lead had no objection to this interpretation (≈ advection time + 1.5–2 s).
 - Control: After correcting the feedforward formula, **perfect 8 s preview** reduced acceleration RMS by 68% (near spectral peak) / 80% (off-resonance) relative to pure feedback, showing the control model has discriminative power. **Preview predicted using upstream velocity probes** only captured 0–17% of the perfect preview gain: out of 360 combinations, only 4 groups under near spectral peak tight stroke passed the gate (10.3–12.6% reduction), and in this setting feedback hit the end-stop, making "stroke does not increase" poorly discriminative; off-resonance was at best 0.8%.
## Assessment
Preview has great value in principle, but the bottleneck lies in "inflow prediction skill" rather than the controller: the skill of sparse near-field probes in predicting loads several seconds ahead is too low to yield substantial gains. Data on this line (single LBM, cube windward surface surrogate load, dimensionless AMD, structural/control parameters all assumed) does not support further investment. Without literature basis, based on data on this line.
## Decision
A2 status changed to "Shelved".
- Why it doesn't work: Incremental value at the AI forecasting level is small; gains at the second-level are blocked by inflow prediction skill, and this line lacks better prediction methods and real building parameters.
- Missing conditions: High-skill short-term load predictions provided by multi-point/scanning near-field wind measurements (lidar arrays or surrounding building pressure networks, referencing Abdelaziz & Hobeck 2022); real high-rise building dynamics and AMD parameters; wind tunnel or field-measured data (not a single LBM).
- Under what conditions to restart: (1) A3 downburst preview feedforward experiments show prediction skill can be raised to ≥50% of perfect preview gain, and the method is transferable to buildings; (2) A collaborator provides high-rise AMD field measurements or aeroelastic wind tunnel data with upstream wind measurements; (3) Liang Hu requests hour-level forecast-driven locking/stroke budgeting (following the Node B "AI track + official intensity + parametric wind field" chain and adding a damper stroke model).
## Cost of Being Wrong
May miss a research angle on "multi-point wind measurement + preview control"; restarting requires only the v3 script (20 s CPU) plus new data.
