# A3: Post-Reading Assessment of Segment A2, Transition to Segment B (2026-10-14 21:3x)
Data (data on this line, deterministic Nguyen 2012 analytical field; card JS2NGXLR_Nguyen_2012_thesis.md Table 4.4 PDF p. 114, shutdown rules PDF p. 112–113): , metrics_A2.json (Case III raw values read by Lead), metrics_A2_screened.json.

## Lead Correction of an Assessment in ideas (Error in My Task Brief)
Case III was judged as "yaw ineffective, loads not reported": yaw was already engaged (NacYaw peaked at 41.7°), lagging the inflow by 78° is a physical result under the 0.3°/s rate limit—Nguyen 2012 original text explicitly pointed out that the wind direction rate of change of 0.6–1.2°/s far exceeds 0.3°/s (reviewer E cited PDF p. 129–133). My task brief demanding "fixing it to follow the inflow" is physically impossible. Case III loads are valid under the "rate-limited yaw" operating condition, which is precisely the difficult operating condition this node seeks.

## Results
- Pitch feedforward: For both trajectories, perfect preview changes tower base resultant extreme value by ≤1% (I −0.9%; III +4.6%), and realistic preview actually increases. **Pitch feedforward provides no gain during downburst slow ramp-up, not entering Segment B.** (Consistent with Guo 2023 where gains are mainly in turbulent fluctuations: card NR_Guo_2023_lidar_turbulence.md journal p. 168)
- Shutdown: Canceling the 50 s wait itself (instantaneous threshold shutdown, no preview) reduces tower base resultant extreme by 15% (I) / 37% (III)—this is not a preview gain.
- Net gain of preview (relative to instantaneous shutdown): Case I tower base resultant ≤3.4%, T=40 actually increases by 12%; Case III tower base resultant ≤3% (T=40 reduces by 12%), but tower top yaw moment decreases by 19%/36%/67% (perfect T=5/10/20), and blade root out-of-plane negative peak amplitude decreases by 16%/29%/41%; realistic 1D (actual lead time 4.7 s) yaw moment decreases by 16%, blade root negative peak decreases by 17%.
- Ratio given to A2 (Case III, relative to instantaneous shutdown): tower top yaw moment realistic 1D / perfect T5 = 0.83; blade root negative peak 1.05; tower base resultant "not applicable" (perfect gain ~1%).

Decision I made: Segment B will only do shutdown groups (instantaneous threshold, realistic 1D/2D, perfect T=5/10/20/40), two trajectories × 6 turbulence seeds, criteria predetermined (see task brief); pitch feedforward group exits. The "② vs ①" item in the review  criteria is replaced by the deterministic results of Segment A/A2 (≤1%), which constitutes narrowing my scope without changing the remaining criteria.
Why: Deterministic results have shown that gains can only lie in "using preview to shut down early under wind direction rotation to reduce yaw / blade root loads"; whether it is robust under turbulence is the question to be answered.
Cost of being wrong: If turbulent fluctuations make pitch feedforward beneficial at the downburst front, this node will miss it—but this area belongs to mechanisms already covered in steady-state LAC literature, not a gap for this node.

## Postscript (10-14 22:1x): Pitch Feedforward Group Added Back
Guo law rerun (near-center, data on this line): realistic 1D/2D feedforward reduces tower base resultant by 12%/24%, while perfect (effective lead time about 2–3 s) reduces it by only 1.6%. Assessment: gains come from longer lead time (raising pitch early before the storm front arrives, similar to protective derating in Haizmann 2018, card NR_Haizmann_2018_protective_derating.md PDF p. 4), not more accurate preview information. The previous statement "pitch feedforward exits" is retracted; Segment B adds G5–G8 to decouple the two using "perfect information + same lead time". Cost: Segment B adds about 48 runs.

reviews.title: Verdict: A2 literature conclusions on forecast/preview-driven control of wind-induced vibration of buildings/bridges (2026-10-14)
reviews.text:
# Verdict: Literature Conclusions on Forecast/Preview Driving for A2 Building/Bridge Wind Vibration Control (2026-10-14)

Reviewers: E (Gemini) support with reservations; A (GPT-6) do not support; D (GLM) support with reservations. 3/3 valid, no alternates. Lead personally verified: US5592791A original patent text (Google Patents, "upstream sensor array consisting of wind sensors ... located on poles off the corners of an upper floor"), Abdelaziz & Hobeck 2022 SPIE 12046 (DOI 10.1117/12.2630805, exists on Crossref), DeMaria 2025 card (line 14: AI global models have no intensity skill, MAE ~40 kt after 72 h and almost entirely biased weak), A1 provenance line 7 (AIWP file f000_f240_06, 6 h step).

## Mandatory Revisions (All Adopted)
1. **Add search boundaries to Conclusion 1 and incorporate counterexamples** (D, A, E). Revised to: In wind vibration control of buildings/bridges, **there are no full-scale/operational precedents driven by upstream preview or weather forecasts**; there are at least three categories of research-grade and conceptual-grade precedents—Abdelaziz & Hobeck 2022 (surrounding building pressure measurement network + GRU prediction window + aerodynamic corner plates, 1:400 wind tunnel, RMS rotational acceleration reduced by up to 75%, based on D's citation of the NSF PAR full-text abstract, Lead only verified that the title exists); US5592791A (1997 patent, upstream wind sensing on poles extending from upper-floor four corners → feedforward-driven mass, conceptual grade, no operational evidence, Lead verified original text); early "synchronous wind measurement at building top driving active aerodynamic appendages" Klein 1972, Soong & Skinner 1981, Abdel-Rohman 1983 (cited via Korkmaz 2011, local PDF page 18 = journal page 2130, original text unverified). Search scope: Grok (abstract level), Deep Research (redirect links), local full text, three reviewers.
2. **Correct Citicorp to passive TMD** (E): The 0.003 g two-cycle wake-up is for the hydraulic oil-film bearings, not active force application; the first AMD building is 1989 Kyobashi Seiwa (E cited Soong & Dargush 98-MN01, Lead has not verified original text). **Delete "PAFC two-stage damping"** (E, A): The source is the Zhang & Li 2019 multi-stage PTMD design, not the operational logic of PAFC's operational ATMD; the PAFC 2022 abstract (CityU institutional repository, verified by both E and D) only states "damping ratio 0.6% → 2–7% across 7 storms" and "precisely triggered according to operating principles", without thresholds. Kyobashi Seiwa ±25 cm/1 tf comes from 11WCEE 1547, which is seismic bounded force control (E), and cannot serve as the basis for wind-protection switching.
3. **Retain only slow actions for the hour–day tier** (E, A): Gain reduction and semi-active gear shifting are millisecond-to-second electronic operations that can be performed in real time by on-site accelerometers/anemometers without needing weather forecasts. The only actions genuinely requiring hour-level lead time are: mass recentering and mechanical locking, hydraulic pressure/backup power preparation and human-in-the-loop review, slow mechanical shaping or TLD water filling/draining, and stroke budget for the entire storm. The execution duration and latest decision time for these actions **are not provided in the literature** (A), so "requiring hour–day forecasts" is downgraded to an assumption.
4. **Revoke original minimal experiment** (E identified four fatal flaws, concurred by A and D): AI global models have no intensity skill for hurricanes (DeMaria 2025), AIWP has 6 h per frame; the same batch of ASOS had missing reports during peak periods (Node B chain_a_results); forecasts and observations share the same deterministic conversion, the TPU step is mathematically equivalent to thresholding wind speed, and lacks device dynamics and switching consequences; "A1 already has AIWP data retrieval" is untrue (only verified the directory); a sample of 3–5 storms cannot support "reliable".
5. **Unmarked parameters** (E, D, A): The original design implicitly included building geometry/frequency/damping/peak factor, thresholds, profiles, and averaging interval conversions, none of which had cited sources, and are revoked together with the experiment; the new experiment task specification must provide a parameter source table.

## For Reference Only
- Division of labor in Abdelaziz 2021: The one querying the table to provide panel angles is the optimizer ANN, while the predictor ANN is a dynamics surrogate (E, Lead verified original text and agreed); to be corrected on the project page.
- "30 m" must not be used as a physical coherence length: In results_v4b, the 30.05 m station is a fixed boundary value, correlation is undefined (A, D); our track only uses the five stations from 7–27 m with correlations 0.67 → 0.35.
- Gu & Peng 2002 used sinusoidal reference signals, not inflow preview (A). Zimmer 2022 and Miyamoto 2025 are state/disturbance estimations (A verified full text/abstract).
- No operating procedures for "switching based on forecasts": All three parties reported "not found"; retain the wording "not found", do not claim nonexistent (D, A).

## Objections Not Adopted
- A: "Worth continuing" cannot be packaged as a literature conclusion. **Adopted its qualification**, but did not adopt "overall not supported": Lead will no longer claim that literature proves the value of the hour–day tier; on the contrary, following the verdict, Lead's judgment is that **the value of this tier driven by AI weather forecasts is low** (slow actions are already covered by official typhoon/hurricane warnings, and execution durations lack literature), whereas the narrow opening worth continuing at this node shifts to **second-level near-field preview** (research-grade precedents exist, but no engineering empirical evidence). This is Lead's project trade-off based on the review, without literature backing, based on the review and our track data.

## Results
- Finalized three-tier table is available on the project page. Hour–day tier: AI forecasts can supply this but marginal gain is small (relative to official warnings), not pursued for now; second-level tier: AI forecasts cannot supply this, research-grade precedents exist but engineering gap remains, serving as the narrow opening for this node; real-time tier: no forecasts needed.
- New minimal experiment: Use our track's Silsoe v7 LBM data to change "same-instant prediction" to "lead-time τ prediction", measure the variation of usable preview duration with probe distance, and then connect a single-degree-of-freedom + active mass damper model with stroke limitations to compare "preview feedforward + feedback" versus "pure feedback". Workstation CPU, 0 CU.

results.title: A2 review package: forecast-driven and inflow-preview active control of wind-induced vibration of buildings/bridges — literature conclusions (10-14)
results.text:
# A2 Review Package: Forecast-Driven and Inflow Preview for Active Wind Vibration Control of Buildings/Bridges—Literature Conclusions (10-14)

## Evidence Sources
- Grok Quick Check: (Grok_quick_check) (self-stated as abstract-level only)
- Google Deep Research: ((citations are redirect links, no DOI)
- A3 Grok (wind turbine LiDAR feedforward, borrowed): *
- Our track data (non-literature): —— Silsoe cube LBM, single-station upstream probe → windward 11-point Cp(t) linear FIR average correlation: surface distance 7 m 0.67, 12 m 0.62, 17 m 0.55, 22 m 0.45, 27 m 0.35. Note: this is a low-rise cube, same-instant prediction (not lead-time prediction), which cannot be directly converted into "preview seconds" for tall buildings.

## Verified by Lead
- Abdelaziz et al. 2021 JWEIA 212:104601 (local PDF page 1 abstract): predictor ANN provides facade panel angle combinations based on current wind conditions, steady-state 2D FSI, "preliminary results" amplitude reduced by up to 94%. Categorized as scheduling based on wind conditions, not inflow preview.
- Marzbanrad, Ahmadi, Jha 2004 "Optimal preview active control of structures during earthquakes", Engineering Structures, pp.1463–1471, DOI 10.1016/j.engstruct.2004.05.010 (existence confirmed via Crossref; content only reviewed via DR paraphrase). The 10.1016/j.engstruct.2004.03.007 provided by Grok is actually Xie 2004 on interference effects, incorrect.
- Laks, Simley, Pao 2013 ACC "A spectral model for evaluating the effect of wind evolution on wind turbine preview control", DOI 10.1109/acc.2013.6580400 (exists on Crossref).
- Zhou & Li 2022 Eng Struct 269:114840 (Ping An Finance Center ATMD, multiple tropical storms) exists; abstract not retrieved.

## Lead Determined Not to Adopt
- Grok's "PAFC 0.01 m/s² sustained for two cycles to start, stroke >2.2 m locked": no original text, DR called it a confusion (DR's own explanation that "2.2 m comes from medical literature" cannot be verified either). Neither is adopted; PAFC operating thresholds are recorded as "not found in public literature".
- Both reports extrapolated an "effective preview of approximately 1–2 s" using 30 m from our track: the project charter explicitly ordered not to treat this as literature evidence, and our track data is a same-instant prediction, so the conversion does not hold. Not adopted.
- In the DR table, "Xiao 2025 active rear wing + road preview 92.73%" is vehicle suspension, conflated with bridge flap literature; "passenger boarding bridge 3D LiDAR MPC 73.5% (Yoo 2026)" is a non-wind-load contact problem. Neither is taken as a precedent for building wind vibration.
- DR's "property management conducts human-in-the-loop review, hydraulic pre-loading, and UPS cut-in hours before typhoon landfall according to meteorological bureau warnings": no citation, not adopted, listed as pending verification.
- The open-source MACS ARB recommended by DR (Tomizuka/Chen adaptive vibration control benchmark): targets narrowband disturbances, not building wind vibration, for reference only.

## Proposed Conclusions (for Review)
1. In active wind vibration control of buildings/bridges, precedents of using upstream inflow measurements or numerical weather prediction as control inputs are virtually nonexistent in public literature; existing "predictive control" is mostly estimation and extrapolation of structural states or disturbances (Miyamoto 2025 JWEIA 261:106049; Zimmer 2022 SCHM 10.1002/stc.3034, abstract level). The theory of preview control originates from earthquakes (Marzbanrad 2004) and wind turbine LiDAR feedforward (A3).
2. The startup and protection logic of operational AMD/ATMD/HMD is governed by structural acceleration and stroke thresholds (Citicorp 0.003 g two-cycle wake-up, Kyobashi Seiwa ±25 cm/1 tf bounded force, PAFC two-stage damping, all paraphrased by DR and without checking original texts); **no** written operating procedures or lead-time/accuracy requirements for "switching modes several hours in advance based on weather forecasts" were found in public literature.
3. Three-tier assessment:
 - Hour–day (mode switching: activation, gain reduction/two-stage, locking, semi-active gear shift, aerodynamic shape presetting): physically justified need (stroke/output saturation), literature gap; matched with time scales of AI/numerical weather prediction, this is the only tier that AI forecasting can directly supply.
 - Second–minute (preview feedforward): wind turbine LiDAR feedforward is effective under steady turbulence (Guo 2023 WES 8:149 §5.2, Bossanyi 2014, Schlipf 2018, verified in A3), specific preview seconds have no verified sources (10-14 addendum: A3 Grok Section 6 numbers rejected upon review); no empirical evidence for buildings/bridges; AI forecast time scales do not match, requiring on-site wind measurement; our track LBM data indicates near-field inflow predictability drops relatively rapidly with distance.
 - Real-time feedback: no forecast needed.
4. Conclusion: Worth continuing, but only at the "hour–day forecast-driven mode switching" tier; the first step is not to design a controller, but to test "how many hours in advance AI forecasts can reliably determine that structural response exceeds thresholds" (a decision skill issue).
5. Minimal GPU/computation experiment candidate: Select 3–5 hurricanes making landfall on US coastal cities (same batch as Node B), use AI global models (A1 existing AIWP data retrieval: GraphCast/Pangu/FCN v2) to backcalculate roof-height hourly mean wind at 6–72 h lead times, convert the response obtained via the TPU isolated tall building library (1/400, α=1/4, already used in our track) into top peak acceleration, determine "threshold-exceeding periods" according to comfort/device protection thresholds, and compare hit rate/false alarm rate variations with lead time against results similarly converted from ASOS observed wind. Estimated ≤5 Colab CU or CPU.
## Reviewers Please Answer
- Are there counterexamples to Conclusions 1–3 (specifically: is there any literature/operational report where a building/bridge actually used upstream wind measurements or weather forecasts for control or mode switching)?
- Does the judgment of "worth continuing, only at the hour–day tier" hold? Can the minimal experiment design answer this question, and are there any fatal flaws?
- Are there any unmarked speculative parameters?

# A2: Near-Field Preview and Stroke-Constrained AMD Minimal Experiment

Pre-fixed criterion: preview feedforward is counted as "useful" only if structural acceleration RMS decreases by ≥10% relative to the same pure feedback and the damper peak stroke does not increase; results do not alter this gate.

## Data, Timing, and Boundaries
Single Silsoe v7 LBM simulation run data (non-measured); 42–642 s, 50 Hz. train 48–462 s, validation 462–522 s, test dispatch 522–634 s, with test targets for τ≤8 s still before 642 s. Each station z=1/3/6 m × three-component velocity; P_x−33.05 fixed inlet excluded; rack R_y0 as an independent station. FIR uses current and past 0–6 s (0.1 s interval), training PCA up to nine dimensions; ridge penalty 100/1000/10000 selected only on validation set. Training and validation at 10 Hz, testing at 50 Hz. Original CSV is read-only and hash matches , copied to WSL scratch; does not cross seg1/seg2 splice points.

Cp=(ρtap − past/current 100-frame causal 2 s REF ρ mean)/(3q), q=training window average ½ρ_REF|u_REF|²=0.00127991343 lattice units; constant denominator across the whole window (not step-by-step REF q). Pressure is not used as prediction input, only velocity. The attached acoustic_notch target undergoes 0.27/0.52/0.95 Hz, Q=20 offline bidirectional notch filtering; for diagnosis only, not online filtering, with possible slight preview leakage near boundaries. Both specifications' τ curves and half-correlation times are listed. For v7 with the same inflow, the complete q at the empty-field building location has no ready-made time history in the same window; this secondary specification cannot be calculated this time, and empty field from other inflow v8 cannot be substituted. ## Control Model and Full Combination Metrics
Cube 6×6 m windward face proxy: V2–V6 height profiles and H1–H6 spanwise profiles adopt Voronoi representative widths, with separable additive interpolation C(y,z)=V(z)+H(y)−V(3.01 m); V(3.01) is linearly interpolated between V3/V4. The 11 coefficients and station coordinates are in , original . F=Σ(w_i Cp_i) is the dimensionless proxy for the average windward Cp (equivalent to ∫Cp dA/36 m²), with the training period mean removed; not full-building force, and does not hard-convert lattice density/velocity into real-building physical force. Area interpolation coefficients may be negative (correcting intersection points), not point-by-point measured areas.

Mass M=1, AMD m=.05, damping ratio .02, frequencies near spectral peak 0.0854 Hz and off-resonance 1.4000 Hz; stroke limits ±.12/±.025 (dimensionless displacement), u_max=2 · test wind force standard deviation (this is a force scaling assumption, identical across all schemes). 0.1 s ZOH mass-spring-damper + relative stroke r; identical state LQR feedback, Q=diag(ω²,1,20ω²,.2), R=.08 (see also params.md). Feedforward is a convolution of known disturbances given by the discrete LQR closed-loop Bellman equation, taking the 0..τ predictions at each dispatch, where predictions for each discrete τ are trained independently and linearly interpolated within intervals; τ=0 has contemporaneous prediction. Pure feedback sets feedforward to zero; truth-8s uses the real future force under the same control law, serving as a "perfect signal control", which is not an upper bound of optimal control under fixed control laws and saturation/hard stops. Force saturates; after reaching limits, position is clipped, relative outward velocity is inelastically zeroed, and impulse is transferred to the primary structure, with the impulse counted into discrete acceleration; this is a simplified stop, not representative of physical details.

## Limitations and One-Sentence Verdict
The preview lead time of this experiment is given by a single LBM realization of the same run; the notch results are close to the raw specification, but the test period and acoustic filtering method have not undergone independent implementation/leak-free audit; not equivalent to a field-deployable forecast. Farther stations may show τ>0 slightly better than τ=0, reflecting advective time lag rather than unconditional distance gain. Small sample, assumed control parameters, proxy surface loads, simplified hard stops, excluding wind directions/multiple events; cannot be generalized to physical buildings. Scientific judgment has no literature basis and is based on data from this line; literature is only used for geometric coordinates, see source references in the task specification, and simulation is not referred to as measured.

Verdict: Statistical preview of near-field velocity for windward Cp is on the order of seconds, but under the current stroke-constrained AMD assumptions, it does not pass the pre-fixed joint gate of 10% acceleration reduction and no stroke increase; as a lead for further controlled benchmark experiments, it currently does not support conversion into an engineering benefit conclusion.

# A2 v3 Parameters and Sources

Data, constant q, velocity inputs, 11-point surface weights, offline notch filter: inherited from v2 params.md and run_a2.py; original CSV SHA256 verified against this line.

Assumptions: M=1, m=.05, ζ=.02, frequencies near training spectral peak and 1.4 Hz, control step size 0.1 s; units are surrogate dimensionless, not the actual building.

New control assumptions: per-step a²+ηr²+εu², Q=CᵀC+diag(1e−5,1e−5,η,1e−5), N=CᵀD, R=DᵀD+ε, a=Cx+Du+F, C=[−k,−c,0,0], D=−1. Bellman linear disturbance term includes the same-step DᵀF; solve for P using discrete DARE, H=R+BᵀPB, K=H⁻¹(BᵀPA+Nᵀ), g=Cᵀ−KᵀDᵀ+(A−BK)ᵀPE, kernel h₀=H⁻¹(BᵀPE+Dᵀ), hⱼ=H⁻¹Bᵀ[(A−BK)ᵀ]ʲ⁻¹g. Formulas originate from the quadratic Bellman derivation in this script, without literature endorsement; previously v2's state weights and feedforward omitted the same-step acceleration term, so their numerical values cannot be directly compared.

η/ε grids are (0.0001,.01,1.) / (.0001,.01,.1), respectively; from those reaching 30% in the validation window, select the combination with the minimum force RMS; not retuned for testing. Force upper limit = 20 × training wind force standard deviation; unlimited self-check uses ∞; three strokes are ∞, unconstrained FB peak × 1.5, × .75. All stroke-limit schemes share the same feedback/feedforward gains; inelastic end-stop momentum transfer and impulse acceleration are inherited from v2, representing simplified assumptions. Discount = max(0, validation Pearson r)², interpolated across lead times; compare raw targets against offline acoustic notch filter targets (no claim of online feasibility). See metrics.json for individual candidates, peak values, clipping ratios, and validation skill.

results.text:
# A2 v3 Review and Explanation (Without Modifying Existing Results)

Reviewing  's 360 combinations (two frequencies × three strokes × six stations × five τ × raw / offline notch filter): raw target under near spectral peak / tight stroke had 4/30 passing the preset dual gates; notch diagnostic target had another 3/30; the remaining 10 frequency-stroke-target strata were all 0/30. Stroke, collisions, and force limiting for each combination are preserved item by item in metrics.json.

Raw target passes: 22 m from surface, τ=5 s, 10.28% reduction, accounting for 13.72% of ground truth gain; 17 m, τ=3 s, 11.22% reduction, accounting for 14.98%; 17 m, τ=5 s, 12.63% reduction, accounting for 16.87%; 24.1 m mast, τ=5 s, 12.38% reduction, accounting for 16.53%. Only these four groups; not a robust result across frequencies/strokes.

Control parameters selected in the validation segment: for near spectral peak η=0.0001, ε=0.1, perfect 8s preview reduced by 70.24% relative to feedback; for off-resonance η=1, ε=0.1, reduced by 82.20%. On the test segment, they reduced by 67.89% and 80.34%, respectively (unlimited stroke). Here, "perfect preview" is a fixed-law ground-truth signal, not an optimal upper bound. For explicit reproducibility: original control v2 omitted the direct DᵀF term in the instantaneous acceleration objective and targeted states rather than acceleration; v3 incorporates all instantaneous disturbances and future closed-loop adjoint terms.

Strict limitations: near spectral peak unlimited-stroke pure feedback peak reached 32.50 (dimensionless), while ground-truth preview was 17.65; "loose" 48.75 and "tight" 24.37 are both defined relative to this very large unconstrained feedback peak, not engineered realizable strokes. In the tight setting, pure feedback hit the end-stop for 4.11% of steps, and raw best prediction hit it for 2.59% of steps; both peaks were clipped to 24.37 by the same hard limit, so "peak does not increase" has weak discriminative power in end-stop collision combinations; it is still executed literally according to the original gate, without equating its passage with engineering practicality. The feedback deterioration caused by end-stop impulses this time is also part of the reason for the 10% reduction in the tight setting; it lacks basis for real AMD design. The best prediction for off-resonance was only about 0.1% (unlimited/loose) or 0.8% (tight), even though the ground-truth control could achieve about 80% reduction.

Discount is obtained by squaring the positive part of Pearson r for the surrogate resultant force on the validation segment and linearly interpolating across time domains, with no parameter tuning on the test segment; this was an approach permitted by the preliminary task, and does not represent an optimal discount. Frequency, mass, control cost, and impulse contact are all experimental assumptions without literature source; see params.md for details. A single simulation, surrogate loads, and no field data mean that usable control benefits for real buildings cannot be claimed. The vertical axis of result plot control.png is predicted gain / fixed ground-truth 8s gain of the same setting, colors indicate station distance, and statistical confidence intervals are not shown.

The platform repeatedly reminded that ,  belong to the reference field/budget of "Non-convective extreme wind design wind speed: AI climate simulator", which differs from the inputs, run roots, and work goals of this A2 LBM-AMD v3; those run roots were not rebuilt, Colab was neither submitted nor recomputed, and no duplicate tasks were dispatched for those two items. In this round, only the CPU completed one formal run in a2_preview/v3, with no writes to v2.

projects.digest:
# Building High-Wind Forecast and Active Control (Shelved)

This sub-project investigated whether weather forecasts (at hour-to-day lead times) or upstream near-field wind measurements (at second-to-minute lead times) can drive mode switching or preview feedforward control for high-rise building active mass dampers (AMDs) and aerodynamic appendages. A two-stage literature review and a three-reviewer audit separated building control across three timescales, showing that hour-scale preparations are already covered by official tropical cyclone warnings while global 0.25° AI weather models lack hurricane core intensity skill. Pivoting to second-scale near-field preview control using the Lab's 600-second Silsoe cube GPU-LBM dataset, two rounds of single-degree-of-freedom AMD simulations showed that while ideal 8-second preview reduced building RMS acceleration by 68%–80% over pure feedback, upstream velocity-probe predictions captured only 0%–17% of that ideal gain and failed under realistic stroke limits, leading the sub-project to be Shelved.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead launched the sub-project under Liang Hu's directive to evaluate weather forecasts and inflow preview as unified inputs for structural (AMD/ATMD/semi-active) and aerodynamic building control across three timescales: hour-to-day mode switching, second-to-minute preview feedforward, and real-time feedback.
- **2026-10-14**: Literature surveys and checks of local papers (Abdelaziz et al. 2021 on smart facades reducing 2D FSI amplitude by up to 94%; Marzbanrad et al. 2004 on seismic preview control) found no operational precedents for forecast-driven damper switching, while AI Weather Models Lead proposed a trial coupling 6–72 hour AI forecasts with the Tokyo Polytechnic University (TPU) aerodynamic database across 3–5 hurricanes.
- **2026-10-14**: Following Lab Lead's cross-check on a sibling wind-energy sub-project, AI Weather Models Lead replaced unverified preview lead-time numbers with verified wind-turbine lidar control citations (Guo et al. 2023 showing up to 16.7% tower-base fatigue reduction; Bossanyi 2014; Schlipf 2018).
- **2026-10-14**: Three reviewers audited the literature synthesis and trial design (two giving conditional support and one opposing): reviewers identified prior precedents for inflow-driven building control (Abdelaziz & Hobeck 2022 wind-tunnel GRU preview network on surrounding buildings reducing rotational RMS acceleration by up to 75%; 1997 patent US5592791A on boom-anemometer feedforward; Klein 1972 and Soong & Skinner 1981 on roof-wind appendages), corrected Citicorp Center's device to a passive TMD with a 0.003 g hydraulic wake-up threshold, and removed an unverified Ping An Finance Center two-stage damping claim.
- **2026-10-14**: Reviewers also showed that electronic gain and semi-active adjustments execute in milliseconds to seconds via on-site sensors (leaving only mechanical lock-out, hydraulic warm-up, backup power, and storm stroke budgeting at the hour-to-day scale), and identified four flaws in the hurricane/TPU trial (0.25° AI models underpredict hurricane winds by ~40 kt, ASOS stations drop out in peak winds, monotonic TPU scaling reduces to a wind threshold test, and rigid-model C_p data lack damper stroke dynamics).
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead adjudicated the review, dropped the hour-to-day forecast switching trial, and pivoted the minimum experiment to second-scale near-field preview feedforward using the Lab's Silsoe v7 GPU-LBM dataset on local CPU (0 CU) with a pre-registered pass gate (10% RMS acceleration reduction over pure feedback without increasing peak stroke).
- **2026-10-14**: Digital Twin Wind Tunnel Lead confirmed no overlap with its same-time inflow-to-C_p transfer function work and provided five Silsoe v7 data quality rules (constant 600 s reference dynamic pressure to avoid a 23% drift, 2 s smoothing for 16.8 Hz oscillations, velocity-only probe inputs plus notch filtering at 0.27/0.52/0.95 Hz acoustic modes, 11-point windward load integration, and splice removal).
- **2026-10-14**: In Round 1 (0 CU), upstream velocity probes at 7–27 m predicted windward C_p with correlation half-life lead times of 2.6–6.5 s (2.7–6.6 s after acoustic notch filtering, matching advection time plus 1.5–2 s), which Digital Twin Wind Tunnel Lead archived; however, even ideal 8-second true-load preview reduced RMS acceleration by only 0.4%–0.9%, revealing a defective feedforward law.
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead rejected the Round 1 negative control result and dispatched Round 2 requiring a 30% ideal-preview self-check before testing predicted preview across 360 combinations.
- **2026-10-14**: In Round 2 (0 CU), fixing the feedforward law enabled ideal 8-second preview to reduce validation RMS acceleration by 70.24% (near spectral peak) and 82.20% (off-peak) over pure feedback (67.89% and 80.34% on unconstrained tests); however, velocity-probe predicted preview passed the gate in only 4/360 test combinations (up to 12.63% reduction, or 16.87% of ideal gain, only when both controllers clipped against tight stroke stops, and le 0.8\% off-peak), so AI Weather Models Lead Shelved the sub-project.

## Where it stands

This sub-project is Shelved at zero compute-unit cost with verified literature tables, the Silsoe v7 correlation-versus-lead-time benchmark (2.6–6.5 s correlation half-life across 7–27 m upstream probes), and the validated preview-control solver archived. It can be reactivated if multi-probe spatial inflow reconstruction achieves >50\% of ideal preview gain, or if aeroelastic wind-tunnel or full-scale tall-building AMD datasets with upstream wind sensors become available.

# A3 High-wind forecasting and regulation for wind turbines

## Objective
Survey existing work and gaps in forecasting and active regulation of wind turbines under high wind speeds (pitch/yaw/derating, lidar feedforward, tower/blade vibration control), and determine whether there is a viable entry point (upper bounds of feedforward and vibration reduction under extreme/non-stationary inflow).

## Current Status
**Shelved (10-15 07:5x)**, per .
- One-sentence conclusion: In simulations combining an analytical downburst + synthetic turbulence + offline triggering, using nacelle lidar to trigger shutdown ~7 s early reduces tower-top yaw moment by ~25% and blade-root negative peak moment by ~15% on an off-center path where rapid wind-direction rotation outpaces yaw tracking; however, on a near-center path it worsens the tower-base reverse bending moment by ~14%, failing the pre-specified rule. The pitch feedforward component was already shelved earlier because the toolchain failed the steady-turbulence literature gate.
- **Why shelved**: (1) Negative-load worsening on the near-center path exceeds the pre-specified 10% limit; (2) the "pass" on the off-center path carries an unexplained actual yaw overspeed (0.44–0.46°/s vs. 0.3°/s setting) and a LOS turbulence approximation; (3) the physical mechanism is simply "shutting down earlier", whose value depends on identifying downbursts in advance, which is a detection/forecasting problem.
- **What is missing**: Realistic downburst inflow (CM1/LES), online triggering, verification of yaw dynamics, gentler shutdown feathering strategies, and a working OpenFAST 5.x lidar feedforward implementation.
- **Conditions for restart**: (a) Off-center path gains remain after fixing yaw overspeed, and a shutdown strategy is found that does not worsen tower-base reverse bending moment; (b) the CM1 track or Digital Twin Wind Tunnel track can provide realistic downburst wind fields; (c) a lidar feedforward implementation validated on OpenFAST 5.x becomes available (to restart the pitch feedforward component); (d) there is a concrete wind-farm demand for downburst shutdown.
- Migration: Starting 10-15, this node is managed under the "AI Weather Models" project; experimental records remain in place; old run roots on the workstation have been archived to TACC.

## Boundaries (10-14 18:3x parent project correction)
- Working directory cleanup: Root Lead cleaned up the workstation as authorized by Liang Hu (lines 15–16, 26); OpenFAST outputs, pilots, logs, and `run_nrel5mw_*` across Segments A/A2/B totaling 8,188 files and 11.39 GB have been moved to TACC (deleted locally after verifying file counts and byte sizes one by one); `env`, `src`, third-party source code, and build artifacts have been deleted (reconstructible). # A3 Wind Turbine High-Wind-Speed Forecasting and Regulation: Literature Assessment v1 (Lead, 10-14 15:0x)
Basis: Grok quick search report  (citations 8/8 DOIs exist); Lead personally verified (following "Verified" section); Deep Research second step **not done** (30-day quota 30/30 exhausted).

## Sources Verified by Lead
1. Guo, Schlipf & Cheng 2023, WES 8:149, DOI 10.5194/wes-8-149-2023 — Abstract original: LAC mainly reduces rotor speed variations (up to 40%), tower base fore-aft bending moments (up to 16.7%), power fluctuations (up to 20%), OpenFAST; "Taylor's frozen hypothesis does not take into account the coherence decay"; gains depend on turbulence models, turbulence parameters, and mean wind speed. [Abstract verified]
2. Schlipf & Raach 2016, JPCS 753:052011 — Abstract: Under turbulent fitted EOG, LAC "still able to significantly reduce the ultimate loads on the tower base" (no percentage). [Abstract verified]
3. Nguyen 2012 dissertation (UT Austin, local Zotero FI6QJ5T3, PDF p. 133 / journal p. 116) original: when both wind direction and wind speed change rates are very high, "pitch and yaw control even together are insufficient to reduce turbine load range"; shutdown "can minimize loads effectively as soon as it is implemented; however, it is likely that the turbine might already have been subjected to very high loads before the shutdown sequence starts". [Original verified] → This is precisely where "lead time / preview" may have value.
4. Lu, Hawbecker, Basu & Manuel 2019, Energies 12:2773 (local KW4WFENX, PDF pp. 1, 16): LES idealized downburst, three stability conditions, 5 MW onshore wind turbine, studying the effects of pitch/yaw control and ultimate/fatigue loads. [Original first page and page 16 verified]
5. Pratapa, Nguyen & Manuel 2023, DOI 10.1115/1.4055076 (card): Non-turbulent axisymmetric CFD downburst → 5 MW loads, loads depend on yaw/pitch states.
6. Gap search: Lead performed two online searches ("lidar-assisted feedforward ... downburst thunderstorm outflow"; "preview control gust front/downburst nacelle lidar OpenFAST") and neither found papers applying lidar feedforward/preview to downbursts or gust fronts; the closest is Stuttgart's extreme gust detection for power derating (EOG / turbulent EOG). Grok likewise reported "not found". — Classified as "not found", which does not equal "nonexistent".

## Grok Claims Not Adopted
- The "1–2 building heights", "10–15 s lead time", and "15–40% load reduction under realistic conditions" in Section 6 "Borrowable for buildings" provided no specific citations; they are Grok generalizations and not treated as literature evidence.
- A2's Grok report restated the 30 m decay length on this line and extrapolated "0.75–1.5 s preview"—a restatement of data on this line, not treated as literature evidence.
- "Goldwind thousands of LAC units", "typhoon yaw optimization reduces load by 1–9%", "floating TMD reduces pitch by 9.5%", etc.: unverified, not used for now.

## Existing Work and Gaps (v1)
| Direction | Representative Work and Citation | Maturity | Can We Enter | Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lidar feedforward under steady turbulence (collective pitch) | Bossanyi 2014 JPCS 555:012011; Guo 2023 WES 8:149 (Abstract: tower base fore-aft bending moment up to −16.7%); Schlipf 2018 IEA Task 32 certification | Mature → early commercial | No (home turf of wind energy community) | — |
| Feedforward under IEC extreme operating gust (EOG / turbulent EOG) | Schlipf & Raach 2016 JPCS 753:052011 (Abstract: significantly reduces tower base ultimate loads); Stuttgart extreme gust detection for power derating | Developing | Weak (already being done) | — |
| Wind turbine loads and control under downbursts / gust fronts (feedback/shutdown only) | Nguyen 2012 (PDF p. 133: pitch + yaw insufficient, shutdown too late); Lu 2019 Energies 12:2773; Pratapa 2023 | Developing (mainly load assessment) | Yes (our group's downburst wind field, CM1/LES resources) | Downburst inflow time series (literature parameters or CM1 line read-only output), OpenFAST+ROSCO |
| Preview feedforward, early shutdown / soft cutout under downbursts / gust fronts | Not found (Grok, Lead two searches) | Gap (pending DR confirmation) | Yes—most promising entry point | Same as above + lidar simulation (OpenFAST built-in LidarSim or ViConDAR), quantification of Taylor's frozen hypothesis breakdown |
| Forecast-driven wind-farm-level shutdown / derating (hours–minutes) | Jia 2023 Electronics (DOI 10.3390/electronics12214443, ramp forecasting and control under extreme storms, unverified); Typhoon review Li 2022 Atmosphere 13:451 (unverified) | Basic shutdown mature, optimization strategies developing | Medium (leaning grid/operations, not our group's forte) | Forecast skill data (retrieved from A1) |
| Tower/blade vibration mitigation (TMD/TLCD/IPC/flaps) | Fakhry 2026 review JLFNVAC DOI 10.1177/14613484261437475 (unverified) | TMD/IPC mature, active developing; upper limits under non-stationary transients unquantified | Medium (sharable with A2 active dampers) | Add TMD module to the same simulation chain |

## One-Sentence Summary (Tentative, Pending Review)
Worth pursuing, but only in a narrow aperture: **under non-stationary inflows such as downbursts / gust fronts, how much more ultimate loads can preview (lidar feedforward or early shutdown) reduce compared to pure feedback, and how much lead time is needed**; do not touch steady-state LAC or IEC gusts.

## Minimal Experiment Candidates
OpenFAST + ROSCO (NREL 5 MW onshore), workstation  local CPU, 0 CU: using the same set of downburst inflows (analytical downburst model superimposed with turbulence, parameters taken from Lu 2019 / Pratapa 2023, checking before assuming), compare ① pure feedback ROSCO, ② perfect preview collective pitch feedforward, ③ "realistic preview" advected according to Taylor's frozen hypothesis with coherence decay, ④ triggering shutdown / soft cutout T seconds in advance (T sweep), observing tower base fore-aft bending moment extremes, blade root bending moments, and overspeed. Criteria (predetermined): if ② reduces tower base extreme by <10% relative to ①, it indicates feedforward has no payoff in downbursts, Shelved; if ≥10% and ③ retains more than half, then discuss the next step.

## Verification of OpenFAST Lidar / ROSCO Feedforward Interfaces (Distinguishing Module from Controller)

In OpenFAST v3.5.0, new fields such as `SensorTypeNumBeam` and `MeasurementInterval` were added to InflowWind input, indicating lidar simulation has been incorporated; v5.0.0 source includes [](https://github.com/OpenFAST/openfast/blob/v5.0.0/modules/inflowwind/src/Lidar.f90). [v3.5 Input Changes Table](https://openfast.readthedocs.io/en/v3.5.3/source/user/api_change.html#openfast-v3-4-0-to-openfast-v3-5-0) indicates the source; [InflowWind driver documentation](https://openfast.readthedocs.io/en/dev/source/user/inflowwind/driver.html) explicitly names it the LidarSim module. FAST.Farm/TurbSim are in the same OpenFAST repository, but no lidar/wind field test cases were run this time. Note that the baseline case currently has `SensorType=0`, which does not mean lidar was activated in this simulation.

The OpenFAST [Extended Bladed Interface table](https://openfast.readthedocs.io/en/dev/source/user/servodyn/ExtendedBladedInterface.html) specifies that `Ext_Interface=1` in `avrSWAPDISCON.IN` uses the OpenFAST 3.5+ extended `avrSWAP`; this merely indicates extended channel compatibility and **does not equal** native implementation of lidar feedforward control in ROSCO. In ROSCO v2.10.6, [`ReadSetParameters.f90avrSWAP(27)` hub wind speed (`HorWindV`) without reading the lidar section 2001–2500; `Lidarfeedforward` was not detected in the controller source code. The wind speed index for `OL_ModeOL_BP_Mode=1` uses internal estimate `WE_VwavrSWAP(27)` current hub wind speed or wind speed estimator as a feedforward preview interface.

A research-implemented integration path indeed exists: the IEA Task 52 / MSCA-LIKE [project README](https://github.com/IEAWindTask52/LidarAssistedControl) specifies a Bladed-style `WRAPPER.dll` calling `LDP.dll` (LOS → rotor equivalent wind speed) → `FFP.dllLidarWindSpeedFF_Mode` parameter. This time, only standard ROSCO ran successfully, without claiming preview signal integration.

## Local Run Positioning

The 60 s steady wind NREL 5MW onshore configuration originates from [ROSCO v2.10.6 Official Test_Cases/NREL-5MW](https://github.com/NatLabRockies/ROSCO/tree/v2.10.6/Examples/Test_Cases/NREL-5MW); the original case was already `TMax=60 s`, `WindType=1`, `Ext_Interface=1`. Only ServoDyn's `DLL_FileName="DISCON_LIB_PATH"` was changed to `libdiscon.soHWindSpeedsmoke/` inside the conda environment; specific termination status and elapsed time are subject to logs. No turbulence, no IEC EOG, no downbursts, nor lidar feedforward. GitHub figures and interface verification are current as of this query. Non-official GitHub QBlade source code and unverified small repositories without licenses must not be treated as verified, reproducible code.

# A3 Downburst Feedforward Experiment: Incomplete, Stopped at Machine-Time Budget Gate

Time: 10-14 15:34 (EDT); workstation  WSL CPU only; first checked  available 50G. This document is not a conclusion on the four load sets. The existing 60 s OpenFAST/ROSCO 2.10.6 smoke test has passed (see ), and this round additionally verified/compiled/actually ran the research controller chain. No Colab/HPC.

## Actual Execution and Results

1. Linux compilation of WRAPPER → LDP_v1 → FFP_v1 → modified ROSCO 2.6.0 in repository snapshot `45992f08c3c3`: WRAPPER original code referenced Windows `IFWINTYkernel32`, and ROSCO's CMake used incorrect casing `Filters.f90`; after changing to  and `filters.f90` in the WSL source copy, all four libraries compiled successfully. Changes seen in `linux_port.patch`, compilation logs . Upstream repository README lines 14–20 define this chain and its feedforward rate interface; actual Fortran source  lines 174–205 filter, buffer, apply static pitch curve, and take time derivatives;  lines 57–62, 414–416 retrieve this feedforward rate from extended avrSWAP and set `FlagLAC`;  lines 61–64 enable/disable feedforward PI. License: README states MIT, but the repository lacks a standard LICENSE file, legitimate reuse requires separate verification.
2. Copied the existing NREL 5MW onshore test case to a brand new WSL run root; used upstream ROSCO v2.6.0 / performance table (commit `51629665d22f`), inserted `FlagLAC=1` specifically needed by the research controller; OpenFAST InflowWind `SensorType=1, NumBeam=1`, WRAPPER chaining three Linux . The first two independent test runs failed due to incorrect library paths and omitting the FlagLAC line; their original logs are preserved in WSL ( and ), not treated as evidence of success.  is the preparation script for the final chain test run, which refuses to overwrite the run root.
3.  and  are inflow geometric diagnostics, not wind turbine load results: hub height in near-center Case I first reaches 25 m/s at approximately 317.46 s, with threshold lead times at 1D/2D positions of approximately 8.56/17.10 s; hub height in eccentric Case III is approximately 480.68 s, with lead times of approximately 8.65/17.30 s. These are merely geometric thresholds of turbulence-free analytical fields, not achievable lidar effective feedforward times or shutdown gains. Sources of data/equations are noted in the figures.

## Unmet Acceptance Items (Blank Metrics Must Not Impersonate Zero Gain)

Veers-correlated turbulence of Nguyen §3.4 has not yet been generated and modulated by ε κ Um; the complete 4D wind has not been input to the OpenFAST rotor (currently `WindType=1metrics.jsonnull`, lacking two or three load plots; the preset 10% criterion must not be applied, nor can feedforward gain be claimed to be small or large.

Machine-time gate: According to the conservative combinatorial accounting for independent runs across full scenarios (two trajectories × six seeds × [①–③ × two protection rules 6 + ④ five settings × two protection rules × perfect/realistic 20 + upstream 1D/2D two settings 2]) = 336 runs. The actual chain test run of 10 s took 3.27 s; if retaining the full time series of approximately 800 s from touchdown to post-storm for both storms, even with linear extrapolation and zero failure / zero I/O, it would be approximately 24.42 h, already exceeding the authorized single total machine time of 6 h. This is an extrapolation, not spent machine time; batch runs have not been initiated. Investigating checkpoint reuse at the same state or compliant event window cropping is possible, but it is necessary to first verify that initialization / controller memory and extreme value windows do not alter scientific criteria; one must not prematurely replace the full storm with a 120 s window to report conclusions.

# A3: Downburst Preview Feedforward Minimum Experiment Split into Two Segments (2026-10-14 16:5x)
Decision I made: Stop at the 6 h gate (extrapolating the full matrix of 336 runs × 800 s gives ~24 h). Switch to Segment A: non-turbulent analytical field, 2 paths × (①②③1D③2D + ④ T-scan 5 levels × perfect/realistic) ≈ 28 runs, ≤3 h, reporting only numbers and "whether to proceed with Segment B"; Segment B will then follow the review's criterion of ≥6 seeds, running only the cases with differences in Segment A. Truncate the simulation window to "60 s before impact arrival to 60 s after subsiding". Preview signal bypasses the InflowWind lidar and feeds the precomputed time series directly to FFP.
Why: Use the cheapest deterministic cases first to see if there is any difference; if there is no difference, turbulence statistics are unnecessary.
Cost of being wrong: Deterministic fields lack fast-varying turbulence, which might underestimate feedforward benefits (as reviewer D pointed out)—therefore, Segment A will not issue a Shelved verdict, but only make the decision on how Segment B is run.
Licensing: LidarAssistedControl README declares MIT (GitHub did not recognize a LICENSE file); for internal use, patches will not be released externally.

# A3 Supplementary Test of License-Compliant Feedforward Chain (Interface Smoke Test Only, Not Downburst Benefit Experiment)

10-14 15:40 ET, workstation WSL Linux CPU. This supplementary test continues from the parent directory `RESULTS.mddf -h 本地盘` with 50 GB available; using the existing ROSCO 2.10.6 release source code, with no new large downloads. No Colab/HPC.

Implementation choices: In an **isolated local copy** of Apache-2.0 ROSCO v2.10.6, only modified , with modifications relative to the original source code shown in `rosco210_ff.patch`. The same compiled controller library (SHA-256 `ec12bb61bb17f97a301fd9d403e6d0f7c7f4b592ce7a4648c36328e6eb7b016d`) was shared by both test runs. `ROSCO_FF_FILE` points to time series in ascending order of time; `ROSCO_FF_GAIN_DEG_PER_MS` was set to 0 (feedback) or 1 (positive test for artificial pulse interface). The code linearly interpolates preview signals that have reached the rotor, taking the current ROSCO `LocalVar%HorWindV` as a reference, applying a collective pitch offset `gain × (U_preview−U_hub)` [deg], added after the PI command and before the original pitch angle limits and rate limits. This implementation is **merely a feedforward signal injection interface**, not a lidar control law that has undergone physical fitting, filtering/delay, line-of-sight averaging, and verification; a gain of 1 is an interface testing assumption, not a value from Nguyen or NREL. Both tests changed PC_MaxRat/PC_MinRat from the original example to ±0.13962634 rad/s, i.e., approximately ±8°/s, while retaining the amplitude from the original ROSCO example of 0–1.57 rad; the rest remained the same as the example (yaw mode 0, which does not equal the target 0.3°/s four-case comparable configuration).

Validation: OpenFAST 5.0.0 NREL-5MW onshore case, rotor input was constant 14 m/s in both runs; additionally in , . Sources and non-downburst nature are noted inside the figures.

Original task unmet: Rotor wind and 1D/2D upstream preview sequences have not yet been generated from independent Nguyen 4D turbulence fields; advection prediction, spatial averaging, filtering delays, identification of real feedforward gains, comparable yaw/protection for two storm paths, six seeds, shutdown T-scans, and designated resultant/blade-root extremes have not yet been added. The benefits in the previous version remain null. Previously, a full-field matrix of 336 cases was calculated according to the task combinations; linear extrapolation from the 10.67 s of actual execution for the current 30 s run to the full 800 s storm gives approximately 26.56 h (estimate only, excluding wind field generation/failures/I/O), far exceeding the total single-run machine time limit of 6 h; therefore, full batch runs were not launched, nor was the statistical window arbitrarily shortened. The preset 10% criterion cannot be applied.

Software licenses: OpenFAST 5.0.0 Apache-2.0; ROSCO 2.10.6 Apache-2.0; Python data plotting NumPy 2.4.6 BSD-3-Clause, matplotlib 3.11.2 PSF-2.0. Using existing NREL 5MW cases and Apache-2.0 ROSCO source code, without introducing unlicensed controllers. Here, the parameter `gain=1` and artificial pulses are explicitly stated as ABI test assumptions, with no claims of literature provenance; complete Nguyen parameter sources and unverified items can still be found in .

In a nutshell: The license-compliant collective pitch feedforward entry point has been compiled on Linux and validated via feedback/feedforward test runs using the same binary, but the 4D downburst and required full matrix comparisons have not yet been completed; no conclusions on benefits can be drawn at present.

items.title: Verdict: A3 literature judgement v1 (3/3 valid: Gemini E, GPT-6 A, GLM D; 2026-10-14 15:5x)
items.text:
# Verdict: A3 Literature Assessment v1 (3/3 Valid: Gemini E, GPT-6 A, GLM D; 2026-10-14 15:5x)
Dispatch notes: In sequence Gemini, Codex slot filled by GPT-6, GLM dispatched after queueing; all 3 valid, no vacancies. All three gave "qualified support". Only one round of review.

## Lab Lead Personally Verified
- Guo 2023 WES 8:149 main text §5.2: 16.7% is the tower fore-aft bending moment **DEL** ("reductions of the tower fore–aft bending moment DEL", 22 m/s, unstable stratification); extreme values are not evaluated in the paper. ✔ Confirmed by E and A.
- Ahmed/El Damatty group downburst wind turbine: Page 3 of our repository records "1.5-MW HAWT, parked, β = 90°, warning assumed before downburst". ✔ Confirmed by E.
- Pratapa 2023 PDF pp. 7–8 §4.4 explicitly superimposes turbulence (ε·κ·Um, frequency-domain method); Figs. 13–14 include turbulence. ✔ Confirmed by A; card Z454567N in our repository has an inaccurate self-limiting phrasing "Non-turbulent", handed over to litwiki for correction.
- Nguyen 2012 PDF pp. 112–113 (thesis pp. 95–96; corrected by litwiki on 10-14): shutdown rule "wind speeds above cut-out are permitted for only up to 10 revolutions or 50 seconds". ✔ Confirmed by E.
- IEAWindTask52/LidarAssistedControl repository exists (GitHub API: latest push 2026-09-03, 14 stars, no license declared). ✔ Confirmed by A and D.
- Zhang et al. 2026 Energy (DOI 10.1016/j.energy.2025.139730, Crossref title "Optimization control model for wind farms considering the spatiotemporal dynamics of gusts") exists; full text 403 unread, content treated only as "nearest neighbor" based on A's abstract-level description.

## Mandatory Changes
1. Mark 16.7% as DEL (fatigue), and no longer juxtapose it with extreme value criteria. (E1, A8)
2. Redefine the gap: Load analyses for "shutdown under downburst / feathering shutdown after early warning" already exist (the 50 s over-limit shutdown sequence in Nguyen 2012 / Nguyen & Manuel 2014 DOI 10.3390/en7106527; Ahmed et al. 2022/2023 assuming shutdown after warning); wind-farm-level lidar preview observation + early yaw/IPC related to gust fronts already exist (Zhang 2026 Energy, full text unread); IEC gust-scale extreme gust detection derating already exists (Hagemann 2017 DOI 10.18419/opus-9333; Haizmann 2018 DOI 10.1088/1742-6596/1037/3/032025, unverified). **What is genuinely not found**: Nacelle lidar preview feedforward pitch control for a single turbine under downburst (time-varying mean + wind direction rotation) inflow, and quantification of benefits from "second-to-minute preview signals determining the shutdown/soft cut-out trigger time T". Still categorized as "not found", do not refer to it as "nonexistent", pending DR supplementary runs. (E2, A1, D note)
3. Inflow: Parameters and equations are taken from Nguyen 2012 Chapters 3–4 (analytical downburst + storm translation + amplitude-modulated turbulence); Lu 2019 is LES cold pool and Pratapa is CFD paused snapshot + frequency-domain turbulence—do not mix parameter names. Preview signals must be independently sampled upstream in the 4D field, and cannot use the constant-speed Taylor translation of the InflowWind single-plane wind box (otherwise ② and ③ degenerate from a shared source). (E3, A2, A4, D1)
4. Controller: All four groups share the same IEAWindTask52/LidarAssistedControl toolchain (modified ROSCO 2.6.0), with ① taking feedforward gain 0; explicitly document actuator rate limits, amplitude limits, and filtering delays. (E4, A3, D3)
5. Wind direction / yaw: Two storm paths (near-center small wind direction change, eccentric large wind direction change, referring to Nguyen 2012 Case I/III), with consistent yaw control across the four groups (rate limit 0.3°/s); add tower-top yaw moment, tower-base resultant moment, blade-root out-of-plane moment extremes in both positive and negative directions, and overspeed to the metrics. (E5, A5, D2)
6. Group ④ definition: Benchmark against T=0 reactive shutdown (both Nguyen 50 s rule and instantaneous threshold), with ①–③ sharing the same protection logic; T is defined relative to "hub wind speed exceeding 25 m/s", with information split into two tiers: perfect and realistic. (E5, A6, D note)
7. Criteria: Fix turbulence seeds (≥6) × 2 paths before results are generated, taking the median; 10% serves only as an internal screening threshold for this implementation, with conclusion wording restricted to "this inflow + this control law", without extrapolating to "feedforward has no merit in downbursts". (A7, D4)

## For Reference Only
- In the maturity column, write only the technical status; "whether to enter" is separately listed as this group's judgment. (A Note 1)
- Other generalized numbers from the Grok report (20–60%, 5–50+%, "standard shutdown is safest") are likewise not used. (A Note 2)
- Lu 2019 consists of five stability cases and three categories. (A Note 3) Corrected.
- Add Lu et al. 2021 Energies 14:5407, Motes 2025 Sandia DOI 10.2172/2997331. (D Note)
- Downburst mean ramp is on the order of minutes, slower than feedback bandwidth; the ②−① difference primarily comes from the fast front and turbulence; inflow needs to retain the fast front. (D Note)`
- OpenFAST InflowWind includes lidar parameters starting from v2.5 (D Note), but it will still not be used to generate previews (see Mandatory Change 3).

## Unadopted Objections
- A: "Current evidence does not support any 'gap' determination" — Partially adopted: Broad "preview control under gust fronts" will no longer be called a gap; the narrow scope (single-turbine downburst nacelle lidar feedforward + preview-determined shutdown time) was not found in 7 total searches by the three reviewers and Lab Lead, retained as "not found, pending DR" as a working hypothesis, not claimed as a gap externally.
- E: "Early feathering in the post-cut-out stage of a downburst may amplify negative upwind bending moments" — Included in metrics as a phenomenon to be tested (in both positive and negative directions), without pre-judging conclusions.

## Conclusion
The direction is worth continuing (narrow scope as above); do not tell Liang Hu it is a "gap", only call it "no precedent found". Rewrite the task specification for the minimum experiment according to Mandatory Changes 3–7, to be dispatched after the ideas smoke test results return.

items.text:
# A3 Segment A: Partial Results for Deterministic Downburst After Protection Logic Revision

10-14 19:30 ET. Workstation WSL local CPU; no Colab/HPC used. Previous OpenFAST/ROSCO smoke tests passed. This report is not a complete 28-run acceptance: valid protection-enabled configuration `SD_Mode=1 and .

## Verification and Errata (Read First)

, are exploratory files generated from the earlier round of 28 test runs in `segment_a_v9`, and **cannot be used for Segment A load or shutdown conclusions**: although `SD_EnableTime=1` was set in every DISCON input, the master switch was missed and three `_v10c_` plots. The `_v10b_` plots lack Chinese glyphs and will not be delivered. Additionally, corrected the earlier Case III of .

## Design and Validation

Non-turbulent 4D vector field `(x,y,z,t)` from Nguyen 2012 §3.3 Eqs. 3.2–3.11, 3.21–3.24 / Table 4.4; Case I near-center, Case III eccentric. A 9-point average is taken at rotor plane x=0, then projected to the uniform wind time series of OpenFAST InflowWind WindType 2 (horizontal speed and direction, vertical speed, fixed power-law shear 0.2); this is not a full planar (y,z) non-uniform field. An independent upstream 9-point spatial average at x=−126/−252 m undergoes idealized line-of-sight reconstruction along the upstream local direction, 2 s first-order filtering, and 2 s processing delay; 1D advection arrival time is estimated from the wind speed measured upstream at that time. Preview is not sampled from the InflowWind frozen wind box, nor does it use rotor direction information. Perfect preview is the rotor-equivalent wind speed shifted forward by 2 s into the future, used only as an upper-bound comparison.

The same ROSCO 2.10.6 Apache-2.0 control library binary, ① gain zero, ②/③ gain one (**assumed, unoptimized**); additive collective pitch offset placed before original ROSCO limits/rate limits. Static pitch curve taken from NREL5MW bundled ROSCO `Cp_Ct_Cq.NREL5MW.txtbuild_segment_a_curve.pyPC_MaxRat/MinRat=±8°/sSD_Mode=1`, `SD_EnableTime=1`, shutdown pitch rate 8°/s, torque derate 2000 Nm/s (ROSCO example settings). T=0 is shutdown after rotor-equivalent wind speed first reaches 25 m/s and sustains exceedance for 50 s; both analytical time series sustained exceedance for >50 s, so first threshold crossing + 50 s is consistent with continuous exceedance. Perfect T>0 triggers T seconds before the true threshold; realistic 1D can only act after the threshold is detected upstream, and larger requested T values are all truncated to the detection time due to insufficient information, and cannot be treated as actual 40 s advances. Both qualities of T=0 use the same protection settings, and the two output extreme values for Case III are completely identical.

Important physical limitation: The scheduled 0.3°/s yaw command has entered ROSCO debug output (Case III `YawRateComNacYaw` was measured only within approximately ±0.12°, not truly following large directional rotations; likely an issue with baseline ServoDyn yaw mechanism / channel wiring, not yet pinpointed. Therefore, eccentric path loads **are not qualified 0.3°/s tracking yaw cases**; no generalizable conclusions should be drawn from this. Output derivatives exceeding 0.3°/s during abrupt changes also cannot be used to claim compliance with actual actuator rate limits.

Case I simulation raw storm timestamp 220.5–528.75 s (the initial ~60 s is warm-up close to 12 m/s, first equivalent wind speed of 13 m/s at ~280.7 s); Case III 399.25–638.75 s, 13 m/s at ~459 s. Both statistical windows run from simulation t≥60 s to the end (ending ~60 s after the last >25 m/s). Numerical startup transients in the initial few seconds are excluded; loads remain during the near-steady-state warm-up portion (certain extremes for Case I occur at t≈64 s); if event peaks need to be compared independently from background peaks, an event sub-window must be explicitly reported separately in the next stage. Source fields: `TwrBsMxt` side-to-side, `TwrBsMyt` fore-aft, `YawBrMzp` tower-top yaw, `RootMyb1` blade 1 out-of-plane root bending moment, `RotSpeed` rotational speed; resultant is `hypot(TwrBsMxt,TwrBsMyt)`. All metrics, both positive and negative directions, and actual trigger times for each run are in the JSON; the wind turbine is not a field measurement.

## Results (24 Valid Runs, Decisive Subset)

| Case | Tower-base resultant extreme kN·m | Reduction relative to respective baseline | Actual advance relative to first 25 m/s exceedance |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ① Feedback, 50 s protection | 72018 | Baseline | Protection at 50 s post-exceedance |
| ② Perfect feedforward | 71370 | 0.90% | Same protection |
| ③ Realistic 1D / 2D | 75035 / 74819 | −4.19% / −3.89% | Same protection |
| ④ Perfect T=5 / 20 / 40 | 60344 / 60833 / 68674 | 16.21% / 15.53% / 4.64% | 5 / 20 / 40 s |
| ④ Realistic 1D requested T=5 / 40 | 59066 / 59066 | 17.98% / 17.98% | Both only 4.61 s |
| ① Feedback, 50 s protection | 134682 | Baseline | Protection at 50 s post-exceedance |
| ② Perfect feedforward | 130481 | 3.12% | Same protection |
| ③ Realistic 1D / 2D | 147439 / 123803 | −9.47% / 8.08% | Same protection |
| ④ Perfect T=5 / 10 / 20 / 40 | 65236 / 62783 / 64174 / 62104 | 51.56% / 53.38% / 52.35% / 53.89% | 5 / 10 / 20 / 40 s |
| ④ Realistic 1D requested T=5–40 | 67628 (identical across levels) | 49.79% | All only 4.73 s |

Case I still lacks independent runs for ④ Perfect T=10, Realistic T=0/10/20, explicitly noted in the JSON; for example, Case III feedback blade-root out-of-plane positive/negative extremes and rotational speed overshoots are listed run by run in the JSON, and one cannot look at the tower base alone. The large reduction in Case III was accompanied by the aforementioned yaw malfunction, and values under true yaw may be completely different.

## Parameter Sources and Gaps

| Parameter | Current Round Value | Source / Checked / Nature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Analytical radial/vertical profile | α=2, c1=0.22, c2=2.75, f/g/p/q | Nguyen 2012 PDF physical p. 66, §3.3 Eqs. 3.2–3.7; verified in local Zotero text, Lu/Pratapa parameters not adopted |
| Case I | Urm=47, Utrans=12, zm0=90, kzm=0, rm0=1000, krm=1, t0=360, t1=720, x0=−6000, y0=−100 (SI) | Nguyen 2012 PDF physical ~p. 114 Table 4.4; verified against main text p. 96 printed page |
| Case III | 47, 14, 70, **0.05**, 610, 0.05, 540, 600, −7570, −610 (SI) | Same Table 4.4; checked complete local PDF extracted text, correcting previous round kzm=0 error |
| Ambient wind / shear | 90 m 12 m/s, exponent 0.2 | Nguyen 2012 PDF pp. 79/83, Eq. 3.24 and §4.2; actual warm-up at surface may deviate slightly from 12 |
| Pitch rate limit / range | ±8°/s, 0–90° | Jonkman et al. 2009, NREL/TP-500-38060 §7.3 original text has 8°/s and 0–90°; retrieved from official PDF web page this round, but physical PDF page number not verified, hence following task specification without falsely claiming verified page number; local DISCON.IN and |
| Rated parameters / Cp | 5 MW, 12.1 rpm, R=63m, air density 1.225, efficiency 0.944 | NREL5MW local lines 4–38; curves generated programmatically, not independently verified via steady-state OpenFAST operating point scans |
| >34.5m/s FFP extrapolation, gain | +0.95°/(m/s), gain=1 | **Assumption**; checked the performance table above (insufficient TSR support range) and original ROSCO control inputs, no literature calibration; sensitivity check recommended, must not be treated as optimal control law |
| 1D/2D, sampling and delay | D=126 m; 9-point planar average, 0.25s, 2s filter + 2s delay; lookahead horizon perfect +2s | D see Jonkman 2009 turbine definition; 1D/2D task specification, the rest are all **assumptions**, checked Nguyen 2012 and ROSCO examples, no directly transferable lidar error calibration for this turbine; sensitivity analysis pending |
| Shutdown / yaw | >25m/s sustained for 50s; requested advance 0/5/10/20/40s; commanded yaw 0.3°/s | Nguyen 2012 PDF physical ~pp. 113–114, §4.4 (rules on printed pp. 95, 109), task specification; ROSCO `SD_Mode`, `SD_EnableTime`, `SD_MaxPitchRate`, `Y_Rate`; current actual yaw did not reach target |
| Shutdown torque derate | 2000 Nm/s | Local ROSCO NREL5MW `DISCON.IN` original default line 182; this is not a parameter given by Nguyen; borrowed example setting, must be swept if affecting conclusions |

Software: OpenFAST 5.0.0 Apache-2.0; ROSCO 2.10.6 Apache-2.0 (only local self-authored patches); NumPy 2.4.6 BSD-3-Clause, matplotlib 3.11.2 PSF-2.0. Artifact scripts , ; valid raw logs are in respective WSL run directories, with inputs and provenance.json co-located. External data/papers from Nguyen 2012, Jonkman et al. 2009, and NREL/ROSCO bundled NREL5MW Cp table; no modifications made to knowledge base or Zotero originals.

In a nutshell: Early protection in deterministic fields may significantly reduce extreme values, but yaw currently failed to track in practice and four runs are missing from the matrix, so Segment A is **not accepted**; do not use these percentages directly to launch the six-seed Segment B for now; first fix yaw actuation and high wind speed pitch curves and re-check the remaining four cases, and v9 unprotected test runs must not be treated as official results.

Sources: Nguyen (2012), local Zotero thesis, §3.3, §4.4, Table 4.4; Jonkman et al. (2009), [NREL/TP-500-38060](https://docs.nlr.gov/docs/fy09osti/38060.pdf) §7.3; local OpenFAST/ROSCO versions and source file paths above.

# A3: Post-Reading Assessment of Segment A (v10, 24/28) (2026-10-14 19:5x)
Data: , metrics_A_v10_partial.json (this pipeline's data, non-turbulent deterministic inflow, Nguyen 2012 analytical field, card Table 4.4 PDF p. 114).
- Pitch feedforward: Perfect preview reduced tower-base resultant extreme by only 0.9% (Case I) / 3.1% (Case III), while realistic 1D increased by 4.2% / 9.5% instead. Under deterministic slow ramps, pitch feedforward yields basically no benefit—consistent with Guo 2023 (card NR_Guo_2023_lidar_turbulence.md, journal p. 168) that "benefits lie mainly in turbulent fluctuations"; no final conclusion drawn (no turbulence, gain unoptimized).
- All numbers for Case III invalidated: NacYaw ±0.12°, inflow turned 111°, large negative value of −119.5 MN·m in tower-base fore-aft originates from yaw failure.
- Shutdown: Realistic 1D only advanced by 4.7 s yet achieved reductions comparable to perfect T=5–40 → benefits stem primarily from canceling Nguyen's 50 s waiting rule (PDF pp. 112–113), not preview. Need to add an "instantaneous threshold reactive shutdown" benchmark.
Decision I made: Do not proceed to Segment B; dispatch Segment A2 (fix yaw + instantaneous reactive shutdown benchmark + event sub-window, ≈20 runs, ≤2 h).
Why: Current percentages are contaminated by yaw failure and a weak benchmark; proceeding to six-seed statistics is meaningless.
Cost of being wrong: 2 h more of local CPU; if yaw cannot be fixed, Case III will be dropped from comparison, leaving conclusions solely on the near-center path.
A2 additional metrics (benefit ratio): Perfect benefit of pitch feedforward <1–3%, ratio is "not applicable"; shutdown ratio recalculated under the new benchmark, old values will not be handed over.

# A3 Execution Status of Supplementary Directives for Segment A (10-14 19:38 ET)

Status: Paused according to the cumulative ≤3 h solver machine time gate; previous results were not passed off as new control law results. Existing , , and plots are retained as-is, none of which may serve as final Segment A conclusions for this supplementary requirement.

## Verified Cumulative Machine Time

Aggregating all actually completed solves from WSL (excluding preparation, build, failed/interrupted solves): 10505.357 s, i.e., 175.089 min, only 4.911 min away from the 180 min upper limit. By version: v1 3.2 s; v3 159.7 s; v4 385.5 s; v6 790.5 s; v7 832.2 s; v9 4731.9 s; v10 3421.1 s; v11 181.4 s. A single recent Case I solve takes ~181 s. Interrupted solves are not yet counted, so the remaining margin is an upper bound rather than a conservative allocatable budget; completing 28 new control law combinations within the quota is impossible. No new OpenFAST solves or background tasks were launched.

## Control Law Gaps and Available Bases

The current 24/28 runs with valid protection used a binary compiled from the same local Apache-2.0 ROSCO 2.10.6 source copy, not LidarAssistedControl. However, the feedforward term in remains `gain × [θss(U_preview) − θss(U_hub)]NacYaw` without tracking, see line 15 of .

Directly verified against the open PDF of Guo, Schlipf & Cheng (2023), Wind Energy Science 8:149–171, DOI 10.5194/wes-8-149-2023: journal p. 159 §3.4/Fig. 5 defines the cutoff frequency as the −3 dB point of the lidar-rotor transfer gain, scheduled with mean wind speed, rather than assigning a fixed 2 s time constant for this scenario; journal pp. 160–161 §4.4 Eqs. (39), (41), (42) provide `θFF=θss(uLLf)`, first-order filter , . In the paper, `Tpitch=0.22 s`, `Twindow=1 s` belong to their device/scanning setup; transferring them to this 9-point preview field is an assumption that needs explanation; they cannot be directly claimed as measured parameters for Nguyen downbursts. The original paper places the feedforward pitch rate before the PI integrator; the current self-authored patch adds a pitch offset before original ROSCO amplitude/rate limits, and the two are also not equivalent.

After obtaining a new budget next time, all 28 runs with protection enabled must be completed using the same binary (feedback gain 0) compiled in a fresh WSL source/run root; first verify the new replacement file for ; the 10% criterion of Segment B is not used for deterministic Segment A.

This status note does not alter or retract the raw numbers run previously, but only clarifies that they do not meet the new control law acceptance conditions. Software versions still follow previous logs: OpenFAST 5.0.0, ROSCO 2.10.6; this round is read-only verification only, with no new software installation, build, or runs.

# A3 Segment A: Supplementary Realistic/Perfect Preview Benefit Ratios (Exploratory Results with Valid Protection in v10 Only)

This file is read-only post-processing; the original is erroneous exploratory output from v9 without protection enabled, and will under no circumstances be computed upon or overwritten. This supplementary table does not change the unaccepted status of .

Definition: For the same path and same metric, (feedback extreme − realistic extreme) / (feedback extreme − perfect extreme). For ④, taking T=0 (shutdown after exceeding 25 m/s sustained for 50 s) on the same path as baseline, calculated separately for each requested T. Take magnitude first for negative peaks; positive peaks and rotational speed overshoot follow originally recorded values. If the denominator is non-positive or the perfect reduction is ≤ 1% of the baseline magnitude, record as "Not applicable", without forcing division; negative ratios can be obtained when reality worsens, and values greater than 1 are not truncated. The threshold is merely a numerical stability rule for ratios this time, not the 10% test criterion for A/B.
