items.title: A3 segment A2: fixing yaw enabling and the immediate-threshold reactive shutdown
items.text:
# A3 Segment A2: Fixing Yaw Enablement and Instant-Threshold Reactive Shutdown

10-14 21:13 ET. Workstation local CPU, 0 CU/0 SU. 20/20 planned cases finished normally; successful solve wall-clock totaled 1747.025 s (approx. 29.1 min), plus one partial solve interrupted by tool timeout, well under 2 h combined with preparation/analysis; this interrupted root was retained and not counted as a success. Original A/v9/v10 results were not overwritten. Large outputs are located in , each successful root has , inputs, and `NREL-5MW.out`; the interrupted root was not analyzed, and the successful retry exists independently in .

## Priority Review: Yaw Gate and Data Validity

ElastoDyn `YawDOF=True`, ServoDyn `YCMode=5`; the old v10's `TYCOn=9999.9 s` disabled active yaw across the entire window. This round only changed it to `0.0 s`, and the four groups continue to use the same `YawNeut=0°`, ROSCO. The for Case III feedback separately provides directional and NacYaw time-history evidence; the previously auto-generated contains unfiltered loads and is not delivered. The unfiltered is the raw diagnostic generated first, which can only be used to cross-check solutions, **cannot be used for reporting load conclusions**; the only one used for conclusions is the newly added , in which Case III loads and benefits have been masked, and the original is retained per the no-overwrite rule.

Case I directional variation is small, and NacYaw tracks effectively; the 1 s difference is about 0.31°, influenced by text output rounding/structural degrees of freedom, "≤0.3°/s" still cannot be understood as an actual hard limit verified at every instant; the controller's command rate limit is 0.3°/s. The following exploratory results are reported for Case I, while strict acceptance of yaw rate still awaits dedicated testing.

## Design and Statistical Criteria

Following the analytical 4D field of Nguyen (2012) §3.3 Eqs. 3.2–3.11/3.21–3.24 and Table 4.4, WindType 2 uniform projection after nine-point rotor disk sampling, independent upstream nine-point 1D/2D preview, 2 s filtering / 2 s processing lag and the pitch offset `θss(U_preview)−θss(U_hub)` of the old ROSCO 2.10.6 patch, feedback gain=0, other feedforward gains=1; control library is the same binary. **The filter cutoff frequency / buffering law of Guo et al. (2023) required by the previous supplementary task has not yet been satisfied**, so this round cannot be accepted as the new feedforward control law. The four groups' master protection switch is `SD_Mode=1SD_Time`, acting only at that moment in simulation without reading future wind speed; it reproduces the instant-threshold action time, but **is not an online sensor real-time trigger**, and its anti-measurement-noise performance cannot be extrapolated.

Case I absolute window is 220.5–528.75 s, Case III is 399.25–638.75 s; full-window statistics are for simulation t≥60 s to the end. The event window is from when rotor effective wind speed first exceeds >13 m/s to 60 s after the last time >25 m/s. For both windows, tower base resultant peaks across all successful cases happen to be identical; other metrics for both windows exist item-by-item in the filtered JSON, and it should not be asserted from this that windows are generally equivalent. Blade root is blade 1, and rotor speed overshoot is relative to the rated 12.1 rpm.

## Case I: Valid Exploratory Numerical Values (Event Window; Tower Base Peak Identical Across Full Window)

| Group | Tower Base Resultant Peak kN·m | Change Relative to Instant-Threshold Baseline | Actual Lead Relative to First >25 m/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ① Feedback + 50 s | 72018 | Not used as shutdown net benefit baseline | 50 s after exceedance |
| ① Instant threshold (no preview) | 61161 | 0% | 0 s |
| ② Perfect pitch feedforward + same protection | 71370 | Shutdown net benefit not compared | 50 s after exceedance |
| ③ Realistic 1D / 2D feedforward + same protection | 75035 / 74819 | Shutdown net benefit not compared | 50 s after exceedance |
| ④ Perfect T=5/10/20/40 s | 60344 / 59407 / 60833 / 68674 | Down 1.34% / 2.87% / 0.54% / Up 12.28% | Respective requested lead times |
| ④ Realistic 1D, practically reachable | 59066 | Down 3.43% | 4.61 s |

The tower base resultant peak of the instant reactive case decreases by 15.07% relative to waiting 50 s, which cannot be credited to preview. Perfect pitch feedforward drops by only 0.90% relative to feedback under the same protection, while realistic 1D/2D increase by 4.19%/3.89% respectively; the Segment B six-seed 10% criterion is not applied. Tower base fore-aft, side-side, tower top yaw, blade root out-of-plane positive/negative extrema, and rotor speed overshoot are all in the of ; for example, Case I feedback/instant/realistic shutdown tower top yaw absolute peaks are 12080/6416/5723 kN·m, respectively. Positive and negative directions are reported independently; negative peak benefit calculation is based on absolute magnitude, and making a negative number larger cannot be treated as an improvement.

Additional benefit ratio : pitch is broken down into realistic 1D/2D against the ① feedback baseline; shutdown is benchmarked against instant threshold ①, pairing realistic 1D with each level of perfect T respectively. Non-positive denominators or perfect benefits ≤ 1% of baseline absolute value are all recorded as . For Case I tower base resultant, both pitch tiers are not applicable; shutdown relative to perfect T=5/10 ratios are 2.563/1.194, and T=20/40 is not applicable. This ratio can exceed 1 (actual trigger times are not completely identical, and each group's peak may occur at different instants), and should not be treated as "signal fidelity". Ratios across all metrics and full windows are in JSON `benefit_ratios`.

## Parameter Sources and Limitations (Carried Over from Segment A, Updated Items Listed Explicitly)

| Parameter | Value / Source and Checked | Nature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Field shape function, two paths | Nguyen 2012 local Zotero dissertation PDF physical p. 66 §3.3; Table 4.4 PDF approx. p. 114: Case I Urm=47, Utrans=12, zm0=90, kzm=0, rm0=1000, krm=1, t0=360, t1=720, x0=−6000, y0=−100; Case III 47,14,70,0.05,610,0.05,540,600,−7570,−610 (SI); local script lines 52–67 | Literature / discrete projection is an approximation of this experiment |
| Ambient, shear | Nguyen 2012 PDF physical pp. 79/83, 90 m 12 m/s, power law 0.2 | Literature |
| NREL5MW, pitch curve | Local NREL5MW lines 4–38, extrapolated +0.95°/(m/s) above 34.5 m/s | Curve back-calculation / extrapolation is an assumption; checked NREL Cp table, no original high wind speed table |
| Feedforward gain / filtering / delay | 1, 2 s first-order filter, 2 s processing delay, lines 75–95; checked Guo, Schlipf & Cheng (2023), WES 8:149–171 pp. 159–161 (their method is −3 dB cutoff frequency scheduling / buffering) | Old-law assumption for this round, not equivalent to Guo's law |
| Pitch rate limit / amplitude | ±8°/s, 0–90°; Jonkman et al. (2009) NREL/TP-500-38060 §7.3, physical page numbers not yet checked, specified per task brief | Command limit; measured rate requires independent verification |
| Yaw enablement | `YawDOF=True` local source ElastoDyn line 15; `YCMode=5, TYCOn=0` this time; old model `TYCOn=9999.9` ServoDyn lines 61–65; `YawSprYawDamp` carried over from that model | Wiring fix; Case III tracking failed |
| Shutdown threshold and comparison | Nguyen 2012 §4.4 PDF approx. pp. 113–114 >25m/s lasting 50s; instant threshold / lead time T per this round's task brief; `SD_Time` input | Instant scheme is a deterministic time replay assumption, not an online algorithm |
| Torque derating / preview spatial averaging | NREL5MW ROSCO local DISCON.IN line 182 2000 Nm/s; nine-point and 1D/2D see Segment A script | Example default / task specification and assumption, sensitivity not performed |

Software OpenFAST 5.0.0 (Apache-2.0), ROSCO 2.10.6 local patch (Apache-2.0), NumPy 2.4.6 (BSD-3-Clause), matplotlib 3.11.2 (PSF-2.0). Figures , , and all contain eccentric path loads that did not pass the gate.

In one sentence: Fixed the wiring where "yaw does not act at all", and Case I shows that the instant threshold itself explains the main apparent benefit of early shutdown, while the additional benefit of realistic preview is small; however, Case III did not pass the tracking/rate gate and the feedforward law is still the old version, so this segment cannot enter random-seed Segment B based on this.

items.title: A3 segment A2 supplementary control law: Case I near-center deterministic experiment
items.text:
# A3 Segment A2 Supplementary Control Law: Case I Near-Center Deterministic Test

10-14 21:53 ET. Workstation CPU only; Case III yaw gate did not pass, so following "if it cannot be fixed, only run the near-center path", eccentric path loads are neither reported nor rerun. The previous A2 is the gate evidence: old input `TYCOn=9999.9 s` disabled active yaw; after changing to 0, although NacYaw moved, when inflow reached 111.15°, the nacelle was only at 33.02° (difference of 78.13°), and second-by-second actual changes had readings exceeding 0.3°, which cannot be called qualified yaw tracking. Near-center path direction variation is relatively small, but the strict actual instantaneous rate of ≤0.3°/s has also not been independently verified. Original A2/v10 files were not overwritten.

## Control Chain and Scope

In the isolated copy of ROSCO 2.10.6 (Apache-2.0), the same was used for all 10 near-center main cases, with feedforward gain 0 for feedback and shutdown groups, and gain 1 for feedforward groups. LidarAssistedControl code was not used. NREL 5 MW onshore / OpenFAST 5.0.0; Nguyen (2012) §3.3, Table 4.4 analytical non-turbulent 4D field, sampled at nine rotor points and projected into WindType 2 time-varying uniform wind (including wind direction, vertical component, 0.2 shear). Upstream 1D/2D were sampled independently from nine points of the original 4D field, rather than forging preview from an InflowWind single-plane frozen wind box. Total simulation absolute window 220.5–528.75 s; full window t≥60 s, event window absolute 280.659–528.75 s (from first >13 m/s to 60 s after last >25 m/s). Numerical values are given according to the event window; see for detailed comparison of all metrics against the full window.

Guo, Schlipf & Cheng (2023), WES 8:149–171, DOI 10.5194/wes-8-149-2023, journal p. 159 §3.4, pp. 160–161 Eqs. 39/41/42: θFF=θss(u through first-order low-pass), transfer function 2πfc/(s+2πfc); buffering Tlead−Tfilter−Tpitch−Twindow/2. Main test fc=0.10 Hz (assumption), Tfilter≈1/(2πfc); estimate Tlead=distance/wind speed using upstream measured nine-point wind speed, buffering not allowed to be less than 0; Tpitch=0.22 s, Twindow=1 s (borrowed from Guo device, applying to this turbine is an assumption). Corrected perfect input is also filtered with the same fc, using real future rotor wind so that after filtering it reads t+Tfilter+Tpitch+Twindow/2; this group of files and run roots are back-calculated curve; above 34.5 m/s +0.95°/(m/s) is an assumption. All cases have the same protection switch, same maximum pitch command rate 8°/s, maximum yaw command rate 0.3°/s.

## Results (Case I; Unit kN·m)

| Group | Tower Base Resultant Moment Peak | Description |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Feedback + >25 m/s lasting 50 s | 72017.75 | Feedforward off |
| Instant-threshold reactive shutdown | 61161.42 | Down 15.07% relative to waiting 50 s; timing replayed offline from pre-determined threshold, not an online noisy sensor |
| Perfect preview pitch feedforward, filtered v3 | 70881.89 | Down 1.58% relative to feedback with same protection |
| Realistic 1D / 2D pitch feedforward, fc=0.10 Hz | 63343.61 / 54453.09 | Down 12.04% / 24.39% relative to feedback with same protection |
| Perfect T=5/10/20/40 s shutdown | 60343.88 / 59406.57 / 60832.73 / 68673.57 | Down 1.34% / 2.87% / 0.54% / Up 12.28% relative to instant threshold |
| Realistic 1D shutdown (actual lead 4.61 s) | 59066.38 | Down 3.43% relative to instant threshold |

Realistic / perfect benefit ratio per : For tower base resultant metrics, pitch feedforward 1D=7.637, 2D=15.464; shutdown corresponds to T=5 at 2.563, T=10 at 1.194; T=20/40 perfect benefit ≤ 1% of baseline, marked "not applicable". Values exceeding 1 are a **red flag**, not a reliable physical conclusion that "realistic preview outperforms the ideal": peaks of each scheme may occur at different moments, and absolute pitch offset, timing, and nine-point uniform projection will affect the extrema. All metrics (tower base fore-aft / side-side, tower top yaw, blade root out-of-plane positive / negative directions, rotor speed overshoot) and full / event dual windows are retained entry-by-entry in the JSON; benefit ratios for negative extrema first take absolute magnitude. The main plot overlays wind speed, wind direction, actual yaw, pitch, tower base resultant; is a sweep relative to instant shutdown. Nguyen 2012 field, OpenFAST/ROSCO sources are noted on the plot.

Cutoff frequency sensitivity (assumed 0.05/0.10/0.20 Hz, not given in literature; only realistic feedforward was recalculated, comparison with other gain 0 or perfect baselines requires caution): Realistic 1D tower base peaks are 62711.73/63343.61/62939.44 in order; realistic 2D is 53863.22/54453.09/54728.45 kN·m. The interrupted 0.20 Hz 2D original root was not overwritten; successful results come from the independent `_attempt2`. Original time-series inputs, logs, and `.out` are in WSL, with only small files written back to this directory.

## Parameter Sources and Assumption Updates

| Parameter | Value and Source / Checked Location | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Field shape function, path, ambient wind, shear | Nguyen 2012 PDF physical p. 66 §3.3; Table 4.4 PDF approx. p. 114; ambient p. 79/83; old parameter table detailed, unchanged | Original text; nine-point uniform projection is an approximation for this experiment |
| Static pitch curve | Local; lines 4–38 back-calculated; +0.95°/(m/s) above 34.5 m/s | Post-segment extrapolation assumption |
| Cutoff frequency, filtering/buffering | Guo 2023 journal pp. 159–161 §3.4/Eqs. 39,41,42; fc=0.05/0.10/0.20 Hz; Tfilter approximated with 1/(2πfc) | fc, fixed group delay, and negative buffer clamped to zero are assumptions; −3 dB point cannot be identified from this nine-point field |
| Tp, window | 0.22 s, 1 s; Guo 2023 journal pp. 160–161, not intrinsic values of NREL5MW | Borrowed assumptions |
| Control injection | line 112; local script | Not equivalent to Guo's pre-integrator pitch rate method |
| Pitch/yaw upper limit | 8°/s (specified in task brief, Jonkman 2009 §7.3 physical page not yet checked), 0.3°/s command | Command constraints, strict actual yaw rate limit not verified |
| Protection | >25m/s 50s from Nguyen 2012 §4.4 PDF approx. pp. 113–114; instant threshold and lead T are task settings | Offline replay of time; online triggering unverified |

Solve machine time ledger: Standalone A2 previously had 20 runs of 1747.025 s; this round main 10 runs 1202.272 s, fc=.05 two runs 226.347 s, fc=.20 two runs 222.773 s, filtered perfect correction one run 93.788 s; successful solves totaled 3492.205 s (58.20 min). Another incomplete solve of 0.20 Hz 2D due to tool timeout was not counted; combined with its incomplete time, it is also well below 2 h; 175 min of Segment A is not counted in this segment. Software: OpenFAST 5.0.0 Apache-2.0, ROSCO 2.10.6 Apache-2.0, NumPy 2.4.6 BSD-3-Clause, matplotlib 3.11.2 PSF-2.0.

In one sentence: Yaw tracking on the eccentric path failed, so only the near-center deterministic revised law was completed; near-center instant shutdown explains the main early shutdown benefit, and although the peak reduction of realistic feedforward is significant, it is much larger than "perfect", indicating implementation/definition still requires verification, which is insufficient to make a decision to enter six-seed Segment B; the 10% criterion is not applied in this phase.

# A3 Segment B: Partial Records at Pause, Not a Six-Seed Acceptance

# A3 Segment B: Colab Resume Run Abortion Record (10-14 23:48 ET)

Status: Incomplete, six-seed criteria cannot be applied. Per the task brief "if G6≫G7, indicating implementation issues, stop and report back", this Colab session was stopped after the first paired seed showed a red flag; OpenFAST was not started on Workstation, `segment_b_run.py.HOLD_cdisk_20261014` was not released, and the original 26 runs' results were not overwritten.

## Runs Performed and Cross-Validation

Colab session `ideas-a3-b-colab-cpu-1014` was CPU Standard (2 cores); uploaded the Workstation-verified OpenFAST 5.0.0 Linux binary and the same binary of ROSCO 2.10.6 Apache-2.0 isolated patch. 12 fields were regenerated on Colab using the same random seeds and spectral synthesis program as the original . Performed a recalculation on the Case I, seed 112, G1 case already run on Workstation: tower base resultant peaks on both ends were 84587.583013 kN·m, difference 0.000%, passing the preset <0.5% validation; this recalculation is not counted redundantly.

The planned matrix is 2 paths × 6 seeds × (4 T levels of original 8 groups G0–G4 + 4 new groups G5–G8) = 144 runs, not approx. 156 runs estimated in the task brief. Original Workstation had 26 successful runs, this round newly succeeded in 4 runs of G5–G8 for Case I, seed 112, totaling 30/144; 114 are still missing. The two timeouts of original Workstation are not counted as successes. The four new runs took 303.356, 305.861, 303.354, 302.920 seconds; validation recalculation took approx. 162.224 seconds. The rest of the generated stochastic fields are not OpenFAST solves.

| Case I, Seed 112 | Tower Base Resultant Extremum (kN·m) | Change Relative to G0 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| G0 feedback+50s, Workstation old result | 84587.583 | Baseline |
| G5 realistic 1D pitch feedforward | 83714.244 | Down 1.03% |
| G6 realistic 2D pitch feedforward | 73463.300 | Down 13.15% |
| G7 perfect info + G6 measured lead time | 91332.693 | Up 7.97% |
| G8 perfect info + G5 measured lead time | 112868.355 | Up 33.43% |

G6 is significantly better than G7 (same measured Tlead), triggering the task brief stop condition. The current formulation of G7 is `rotor(t+Tlead(t))`, first applying a 0.10 Hz first-order low-pass filter to this variable time-shifted sequence, and then buffering according to G6's `max(0,Tlead−Tfilter−0.22−0.5)`; whereas G6 first filters and then buffers upstream measurements. Although both use the same Tlead sequence, the operator order of variable time shifting, filtering, and buffering does not commute, potentially producing non-causal or excessive advance, and has not proven to achieve a fair comparison with information quality as the sole variable. This is an implementation issue awaiting diagnosis; the single-seed 13.15% of G6 cannot be regarded as a robust scientific benefit. Absolute pitch offset injection is also not equivalent to the pre-integrator pitch rate injection of Guo 2023. Data sources for time-history diagnostic plots are written in the figures.

 explicitly indicates `STOPPED_IMPLEMENTATION_RED_FLAG`, retaining 30 successful records and a missing list of 114 items; both preset six-seed gates are null, and cannot be used to determine "robust benefit" or "no robust benefit". Complete six-seed tables and seed scatter plots for G2/G3/G4 were not generated, and old partial plots cannot masquerade as complete plots.

## Resources, Reproduction, and Boundaries

Session logs record creation at 23:25:47 and termination at 23:48:19 (ET; original logs were 03:25:47–03:48:19 UTC). `colab stop -s ideas-a3-b-colab-cpu-1014` returned `Session terminated`; thereafter `colab sessions` only listed three other existing non-test GPU sessions, with this test's CPU session not in the list. `colab ls` is a remote file listing command, not a session list; one cannot claim that the entire account has no sessions. At creation, `colab usage` balance was 1367.69 CU, and after termination 1359.85 CU, total account change was 7.84 CU, but during this time the other three GPU sessions were still billed at approx. 18.84 CU/h, so the account change cannot be misreported as the actual CU of this test. Observing that after CPU joined, the account rate went from 18.84 to 18.92 CU/h, approx. 0.08 CU/h; based on this, this CPU session was approx. 0.03 CU (estimated, CLI has no single-session actual settlement figure), far below the 100 CU pause line. Data downloads of JSON, compressed time series, and plots totaled far less than 50 MB; large raw results only exist in the terminated temporary Colab runtime, with no guarantee of being readable again. C drive has approx. 21 GB available, Workstation HOLD remains in effect.

Parameters and sources follow `RESULTS_B_partial_20261014.mdexp(−3 f Δx/12)`, 7×7/3×3 grid points, 3 s threshold are all assumptions of this test / task specifications, not values given in original text; feedforward 0.10 Hz is an assumption, 0.22 s pitch and 1 s window are borrowed from Guo, Schlipf & Cheng (2023), WES 8:149–171, pp. 160–161 Eqs. 39/41/42, whose transfer to this turbine is still an assumption. Versions: OpenFAST 5.0.0, ROSCO 2.10.6, both Apache-2.0; Python array libraries this round were Colab NumPy 2.1.3, SciPy 1.16.3, Matplotlib 3.10.0.

The next resumption cannot directly reopen the matrix: First perform causal path verification on the phase, clock, and buffering of G6/G7 input signals at the storm front, and only after passing single-seed comparison can batch runs be re-approved. This recommendation is not a six-seed test conclusion.

# A3: Feedforward Injection Changed to Pitch Rate into PI Integrator, Adding Steady Turbulence Literature Gate (2026-10-14 23:5x)
Basis: (Colab single seed 112, this line's data)—G6 realistic 2D reduces tower base resultant by 13%, G7 perfect + same lead time increases by 8%, G8 perfect + 1D lead time increases by 33%.
Diagnosis (Lead): Feedforward is added as absolute θss(u) after the PI output, duplicating the steady-state pitch already provided by the PI; the more accurate the information, the more excessive the feathering; A2_guo_v3's "realistic 12–24% outperforming perfect 1.6%" shares the same root cause as the Segment B single-seed results, **neither serves as evidence of benefit**. The previous interpretation of "suspected early derating effect" is withdrawn, pending re-evaluation after correction.
Decision I made: Change to feedforward pitch rate into the PI integrator per Guo 2023 (card NR_Guo_2023_lidar_turbulence.md, journal pp. 160–161 Eqs. 39/41/42); first reproduce Guo's order of magnitude in IEC normal turbulence (rotor speed standard deviation reduction, journal p. 168 §6 tower DEL reduction 3.0–16.7%) as a gate, and run downburst G5–G8 only after passing; shutdown groups G0–G4 are unaffected and retained. All on Colab, Workstation does not compute.
Why: When the control law itself has an error, any comparison separating "lead time vs. information" is meaningless; the literature gate can test the implementation against known answers.
Cost if wrong: If double counting is not the primary cause, the gate will pass but G6≫G7 will remain, requiring another check on timing and spending another round of Colab (approx. a few CUs).

## Control Law and Testing

In ROSCO 2.10.6 Apache-2.0 independent source directory `rosco210_ff_src_rate_B2`, created new `libdiscon.so` (Colab GNU Fortran 13.3; compilation succeeded). Changed `θss(u_preview,filtered,buffered)DT*(ki*error+ff_rate)c9a598bf20ddaa8fa2717c5fe05fd09b7e0ccdda3e0087d3b6cb19ad588f93ff`; did not overwrite the old controller. Referenced Guo, Schlipf & Cheng (2023), WES 8:149–171, §4.4 pp. 160–161 Eqs. 39/41/42 (task-given literature); integrator location was also read-only benchmarked against the MIT implementation; new code was written independently within the original Apache-2.0 ROSCO isolated copy.

IEC normal turbulence gate: TurbSim/OpenFAST v5.0.0, IECKAI, IEC 61400-1 NTM A, Uref=16 m/s, NREL 5 MW onshore, 7×7, 0.5 s, three seeds 112/203/317; each group simulated to 600 s, output window for calculating standard deviation is 100–600 s. FB and FF use the same wind box for the same seed; preview is the same BTS rotor disk grid mean future 6 s, first filtered by fc=0.10 Hz first-order filter, then buffered by s. This is an approximate stand-in for ideal information, not strict REWS directly output from the OpenFAST rotor-weighted estimator; 7×7, 6 s, fc, pitch and window times remain test assumptions. Official TurbSim template source: https://github.com/OpenFAST/openfast/blob/main/docs/source/user/turbsim/examples/TurbSim.inp. New controller compiled successfully on Colab; all six OpenFAST runs finished normally. The phased parsing compatibility issue with BTS new version ID=8 was fixed, and the first two failed attempts were not included in the metrics.

DEL was not calculated this time.

## Limitations and Resources

The current failure cannot yet distinguish between: discrepancy between constructed "perfect" preview and OpenFAST actual effective wind, clock registration of BTS starting 7 s padding frames, controller feedforward rate sign/filtering coupling with integrator, steady-state pitch curve adaptation, etc. One cannot infer from this gate that feedforward is physically ineffective, nor declare benefit based on local moment changes of any single seed. This time, successful solves totaled 993.08 s; there was also overhead from TurbSim/compilation and two pre-check failures. # A3: Feedforward Steady Turbulence Gate Not Passed, Diagnostic Routes (2026-10-15 00:5x)
Basis: (IEC NTM 16 m/s, 3 seeds, perfect feedforward rotor speed standard deviation +14% to +18%, this line's data). Literature expectation is a reduction (Guo 2023, card NR_Guo_2023_lidar_turbulence.md, abstract up to −40%, journal p. 168 §6).
Decision I made: Parallelize two diagnostic routes—(1) Time-shift sweep of −6 to +6 s for the self-written controller feedforward (focusing on checking the BTS approx. +7 s time index offset recorded in Segment B); (2) Run the authors' reference implementation LidarAssistedControl (README declares MIT, internal use) on the same gate. If the reference chain passes the gate, move the downburst test onto the reference chain (replacing LDP with our preview input). If neither passes, stop and report back.
Why: Using the authors' validated implementation as a benchmark is the fastest way to determine whether the issue lies in our implementation or in the setup; continuing to debug on our own carries a higher cost.
Cost if wrong: One round of Colab (estimated <5 CU); if the reference chain has hidden issues in the Linux port, it will also fail the gate, at which point the conclusion will be "the toolchain of this test facility is insufficient to reliably evaluate feedforward", and the feedforward part is Shelved, retaining only the shutdown groups.

# A3-B3 Feedforward Literature Gate Diagnostics (10-15 01:32 ET)

Status: Both diagnostics have been executed; none of the three seeds in the reference chain passed the gate. Execution has been stopped according to the task specification, without running downburst or continuing segment B. Workstation is not running OpenFAST/TurbSim; `segment_b_run.py.HOLD_cdisk_20261014` remains untouched. All solves were performed in a single Colab CPU high-memory session `ideas-a3-b3-cpu-1015`; `colab stop` has been executed, and neither private nor global `colab sessions` list this session anymore (the other three sessions do not belong to this task).

## Common Definitions

NREL 5 MW onshore; TurbSim 5.0.0 `IECKAIRotSpeedFlagLAC` 0/1, pitch rate upper limits both changed to 8°/s.

## 1. Timing Sweep of the In-House Chain

The existing B2 same-seed FB `RotSpeed` standard deviation is 0.251289 rpm. Δ is the overall displacement relative to the B2 preview time history; a positive sign makes the preview time history appear earlier; filtering (fc=0.10 Hz), buffer (~3.69 s), and steady-state curve are kept consistent with B2. All sweep results terminated normally:

| Δ (s) | Gain | Standard deviation rpm | Reduction relative to FB |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| −6 | 1 | 0.245562 | +2.28% |
| −4 | 1 | 0.277358 | −10.37% |
| −2 | 1 | 0.271720 | −8.13% |
| 0 | 1 | 0.294044 | −17.01% |
| +2 | 1 | 0.289730 | −15.30% |
| +4 | 1 | 0.264881 | −5.41% |
| +6 | 1 | 0.269589 | −7.28% |
| 0 | 0.5 | 0.266902 | −6.21% |

−6 s is the minimum within this discrete grid, but it is only 2.28% lower than FB, not the "significant decrease" required by the task, and with only a single seed, the time-shift fix cannot be deemed to have passed the gate based on this. Independently verified the BTS time origin: cross-registering the seed 112 raw BTS center pixel u(t) with OpenFAST output `Wind1VelX(t)` over 100–580 s, the optimal `Wind1VelX(t)≈BTS center u(t−7.0 s)`; Pearson r=0.9999994, RMSE=0.00286 m/s, whereas assuming zero offset yields r=0.5029. That is, the original timeline of the B2 preview file indeed has a 7 s physical mismatch, and −6 s shifts it in the correct direction; however, the preview target itself also contains filter group delay, buffering, and required control lead time, so "correcting clock by −7 s" cannot simply be equated with optimal control Δ. Preview is an ideal proxy for the grid average over the BTS rotor disk, not the aerodynamic REWS true value.

Timing curves; numerical values , clock registration.

## 2. Same Three Seeds on Author's Reference Chain

The four author libraries compiled on Linux were first verified on a 20 s NREL 5 MW test case. During the initial "normal termination", ROSCO dbg's REWS and feedforward pitch rate were actually both 0: the legacy LDP treated `avrSWAP(63)` as the starting point for lidar channels, whereas OpenFAST 5.0's lidar data resides at 2001–2500. Therefore, the unadapted run cannot be called an author chain gate. A separate copy of the MIT WRAPPER source code was created, bridging only the single-beam measured x-wind speed from OpenFAST 5.0 extended channel 2005 to 2103 of the legacy chain prior to entering LDP, and setting pointers 63→2100 for legacy LDP/FFP/ROSCO; LDP, FFP, and the modified ROSCO algorithm libraries were not modified. The 20 s short test terminated normally, with ROSCO dbg REWS at 11.44–20.46 m/s and feedforward pitch rate at −0.04696 to +0.05581 rad/s, confirming non-zero signals. This is a compatibility adaptation, not proof that the author repository supports OpenFAST 5.0 unmodified.

FFP uses the NREL 5 MW local steady-state pitch curve (106 points downsampled to 23 points to prevent its fixed-length input parser from truncating; this downsampling is an implementation assumption of this test), first-order low-pass filter 2π×0.10 rad/s, buffer 3.7 s; InflowWind single-beam lidar is located 96 m upstream, URefLid=16 m/s, sampling 0.5 s, radial projection disabled to return the x-component. This is a fixed single-point preview, **not equivalent to the full multi-point/multi-scale measurement setup of Guo 2023**. Paired results across the three seeds:

| Seed | FB standard deviation rpm | FF standard deviation rpm | FF relative to FB |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 112 | 0.248095 | 0.337578 | Increase 36.07% |
| 203 | 0.214690 | 0.349073 | Increase 62.59% |
| 317 | 0.223771 | 0.361990 | Increase 61.77% |

All six OpenFAST return codes were 0; the pitch rate dbg for all three FF runs was non-zero, ruling out the false negative of "FF not connected". The author chain reversed across all three seeds under **this adapted NREL 5 MW configuration**; this does not mean the published conclusions of Guo 2023 are refuted, nor can this bridged configuration be regarded as a literature replication. Reference figure `reference_gate_line_B3.svg` (seed curves) and  (bar chart), data source: this Colab run.

## Resources, Evidence, and Destinations

New scripts: , . Repository source: https://github.com/IEAWindTask52/LidarAssistedControl; extended interface source: https://openfast.readthedocs.io/en/dev/source/user/servodyn/ExtendedBladedInterface.html.

A total of 177,020 bytes of metrics, figures, and log summaries were retrieved this time, without copying large outputs. Single session ~00:55–01:30 on 10-15; CLI does not provide per-session actual CU billing. With other concurrent sessions, the total account balance went from 1343.13 to 1333.89 CU (difference of 9.24 CU, **cannot be attributed to this task**); before this session stopped, the account burn rate decreased by ~0.26 CU/h, estimating ~0.15 CU for this session over ~35 min, which is not an independent bill. After stopping, neither private nor global `colab sessions` contain `ideas-a3-b3-cpu-1015`. The 26 successful operating cases of segment B and all legacy files on the workstation remain untouched.

Conclusion: There is direct measurement evidence for the BTS clock mismatch, but the discrete time-shift sweep did not noticeably outperform FB; the author's reference chain across three seeds also failed the gate that "rotational speed standard deviation should decrease". Stopped at the literature gate per the task specification, without executing the seed 112 downburst benchmark or the subsequent six-seed matrix; robust benefit criteria were not evaluated. If continuing in the next round, one should first check the measurement phase of lidar channels against the static pitch curve and controller gains/signs in the author chain, and re-pass the gate under independent IEC conditions, rather than directly continuing segment B.

# A3: After Reading Segment C, Send to Six Reviewers (2026-10-15)
Basis: , metrics_C.json (data from this track). Lowering thresholds to 22/20/18 m/s across both trajectories cannot achieve ≥80% yaw reduction with a false shutdown rate ≤ preview (false shutdowns 17–18/18 vs. preview 10/18, 25 m/s baseline 9/18) → according to predetermined criteria, "preview has unique value".
Lead's reservations after reading: (a) The 3 s >25 m/s rule itself falsely shuts down 9/18 in 20–22 m/s regular turbulence; actual wind turbines mostly use longer averaging and hysteresis, so the false shutdown rate lacks operational significance; (b) Lowering threshold results are non-monotonic (e.g., offset 20 m/s reduces by 4%, 18 m/s reduces by 30%), 6 seeds have large noise; (c) Triggers are replayed offline; (d) Inflow is an analytical field.
Decision I made: Draft a promotion proposal, send conclusions together with the proposal, per Liang Hu's 10-11 rule: "conclusion holds" type conclusions submitted to Liang Hu require review by six reviewers); after the verdict, ask Liang Hu via node A whether to promote.
Cost of being wrong: If the review points out fatal flaws, the proposal will be returned and A3 may be Shelved—only the time spent writing the proposal is lost.

items.title: Verdict: A3 conclusion on preview-based early shutdown and the promotion proposal (6/6 valid: Gemini E, GPT-6 A, GLM D, DeepSeek C, Kimi B, Grok F; 2026-10-15)
items.text:
# Verdict: A3 Preview Early Shutdown Conclusions and Promotion Proposal (6/6 Valid: Gemini E, GPT-6 A, GLM D, DeepSeek C, Kimi B, Grok F; 2026-10-15)
Dispatch note: All 6 copies valid, no vacancies to backfill. E/A/D/C/B support with reservations, F does not support. Only one round of review.

## Lead Personal Verification (metrics_B_stop.json recomputation, scripts, Nguyen 2012 original text)
- Yaw moment G2 vs G1 seed-by-seed: near-center [18.0, −3.2, 28.0, 21.9, 2.0, 13.1]%, offset [−3.1, 43.0, 26.0, −3.1, 27.0, 22.3]%—medians of 15.5/24.2% are true, but 1/6 and 2/6 seeds increased reversely. ✔
- Blade root out-of-plane negative peak amplitude: near-center seeds 112/203 deteriorated by 128%/158%. ✔ (E, A, D, F)
- Tower base fore-aft **negative** bending moment amplitude: near-center paired median deteriorated by 23.7%; offset deteriorated across 6/6 seeds (median 3.95%, maximum 28.8%). ✔ (E)—"tower base and blade root basically unchanged" is untrue.
- Turbulence isotropy: segment_b_run line 121 multiplies u, v, w by 0.1·speed simultaneously. ✔ (E) Nguyen 2012 PDF page 113 (thesis page 96) body text states turbulence intensity should "scale with the storm's translation speed", whereas this test scaled by instantaneous total wind speed, differing from the original text. ✔ (E, F)
- Case III kzm: PDF page 113 body text kzm=0.05 m/s is consistent with the script; F claimed Table 4.4 is 0, but table text extraction cannot verify cell-by-cell—listed as "pending verification".
- Nguyen 2012 PDF page 131: downburst Case I–III inflows "might arguably be outside the range of validity for aerodynamic loads computation in FAST", and large yaw errors likewise. ✔ (F)
- Upstream signal is a fixed-coordinate 3×3 horizontal wind vector magnitude, not following nacelle yaw, with no line-of-sight projection. ✔ (E, A, script lines 115–140)

## Must Change
1. Do not promote; do not report to Liang Hu that the "conclusion holds". External phrasing narrowed to: under this analytical inflow, offline trigger replay, idealized upstream sampling, and 3 s >25 m/s rule, paired median yaw moment across 6 seeds decreased by 15.5%/24.2%, with individual seeds increasing reversely; simultaneously, tower base fore-aft negative bending moment and some seeds' blade root negative peaks deteriorated; do not claim "robust", "lidar", "unique value", or "optimal distance". (All)
2. Simple radar-free alternatives not ruled out: yaw error trigger, wind direction rate-of-change trigger, longer averaging windows, symmetric-filtered rotor signals. The distinguishing feature of a downburst is precisely wind direction rotation; such triggers might achieve near-zero false shutdowns in false shutdown tests. (All)
3. Modify turbulence according to Nguyen's original text: component intensity ratios and scaling by translation speed; use actual mean wind speed for spectral/coherence reference wind speed in steady-state false shutdown wind fields. (E, A)
4. Add "no deterioration" conditions to criteria: tower base fore-aft negative peaks and blade root negative peaks (all blades) must not deteriorate by median >10%. (E, A, D, F)
5. Change upstream signal to line-of-sight measurement following nacelle yaw (at least single-beam LOS projection), and verify actual yaw rate seed-by-seed for offset cases. (E, A, C, B)
6. Increase seed count to 12, report seed-by-seed ranges and paired tests. (E, D)
7. Risks must be stated: legacy 26 cases have only process-level traceability; Case III yaw error reaches 78°, and Nguyen 2012 PDF p.131 notes this may exceed the aerodynamic validity range of FAST; false shutdowns are 600 s window counts, not operational probabilities. (A, D, C, B, F)

## For Reference Only
- Lowering threshold benchmark is fair within the "same 3 s rule family", and criteria were not changed post-hoc (D, B); but G2 has 1 s more filtering, and spatial averaging differs (E, D).
- Resource estimates should follow actual measurements (B ~3–4 CU, C ~0.1 CU). (D)
- Offline replay is not future information leakage (A).
- 2D results lack a false shutdown arm and cannot answer the optimal distance question. (F)

## Unadopted Objections
- F "overall does not support": Partially adopted—do not promote, do not report conclusions; but do not shelve, because the median direction is consistent, keeping one robust (D), and untested simple alternatives do not mean already replaced; one additional round is sufficient to judge.

## Conclusion
Proposal returned. Dispatch segment D (task specification), with criteria pre-fixed; if D shows that simple radar-free triggers can achieve equivalent load reduction without more false shutdowns, or that preview shutdown causes negative loads to deteriorate beyond limits → A3 Shelved entirely; otherwise rewrite proposal according to narrowed phrasing and submit to Liang Hu via Node A (as exploratory evidence, without claiming conclusion holds).

items.text:
# A3 Segment D: Shutdown Rules and False-Shutdown Trade-offs (10-15 07:34 EDT Follow-up Analysis)

Source: of Colab `ideas-a3-d-1015` was detected by keepalive at 07:25:59, last checkpoint `D_checkpoint.tar_1015_072559.gz` (SHA-256 `3a28ec9cbc9c83a01fb4e7da15de17b7abcfa1641aa65287d35938c656cc8206`), local adapted version of analysis code `analyze_d_checkpoint_20261015.pycolab --auth oauth2 sessions` does not include this session, and other listed sessions belong to other tasks. The session ran approximately from 03:22 to 07:26 (about 4.1 hours); the shared account had other sessions running in parallel, and the CLI lacks separate CU billing and allocation rates for this session, so actual CUs cannot be reliably attributed; the shared balance difference was not counted as consumption for this task.

## Ledger and Predetermined Criteria

12 seeds × 3 inflows (Case I, Case III kzm=0.05, Case III kzm=0) × 10 rules, totaling 360/360 successful solves; the 324/324 in checkpoint storm_status are only the nine groups other than G1, plus 36 for G1. Steady-state 18/20/22 m/s, each 12 seeds × 600 s, 36/36 NoStop solves and trigger interpretations completed. Event window is from the first time the rotor 3-second average exceeds 13 m/s to 60 s after the last time it exceeds 25 m/s. Metrics, seed-by-seed values, paired reductions, and two-sided Wilcoxon p-values are all in ; in Figures and , points represent each seed, and diamonds/horizontal lines represent paired medians, all sourced from the above synthetic fields and OpenFAST/ROSCO.

Criteria (a) G2L paired median reduction in yaw moment of at least 10%; (b) deterioration in fore-aft negative peak at tower base and out-of-plane negative peak at three blade roots both do not exceed 10%; (c) for every simple trigger whose yaw reduction reaches 80% of G2L, the number of steady-state false-shutdown windows is greater than G2L. Negative reduction indicates deterioration. The table below is calculated according to fixed criteria; the yaw rate limit anomaly below still needs to be verified, and physical acceptance cannot be declared based on this.

| G2L Yaw Peak Reduction | Tower Base Fore-Aft Negative Peak Reduction | Three Blade Roots Out-of-Plane Negative Peak Reduction | (a,b,c) | Rule Calculation |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| 20.95% (p=0.0122) | −14.40% (p=0.00146) | +2.23% | Yes/No/Yes | Failed: Negative tower base load exceeds 10% |
| 24.95% (p=0.000488) | +2.77% | +15.27% | Yes/Yes/Yes | Rule Passed |
| 24.25% (p=0.000977) | +0.96% | +14.39% | Yes/Yes/Yes | Rule Passed |

Paired median reduction in yaw moment / triggers out of 36 steady-state windows: G1 0%/15; G2L above table/16; ideal fixed sampling G2 is 13.02%/17, 31.89%/17, 29.44%/17 (corresponding to three trajectories respectively); S1 is −9.42%/15, −0.63%/15, −11.28%/15; S2_23 is 0%/24, −2.08%/24, −3.09%/24; S2_24 is −8.23%/18, −9.50%/18, −10.79%/18; S3_30 is −85.32%/0, −49.24%/0, −83.20%/0; S3_20 is −85.32%/0, −20.20%/0, −21.41%/0; S4_05 is 38.42%/36, 40.72%/36, 57.73%/36; S4_1 is −85.32%/36, 39.94%/36, 51.84%/36. S4_05 (three trajectories) and S4_1 (Case III) reach 80% of G2L reduction, but both are 36/36 false shutdowns, so (c) holds across all trajectories. G2L's 16/36 is also not a low false-shutdown rate. Trigger counts by mean wind speed, per-seed dispersion, and other loads/rotor speeds are in JSON.

## Key Limitations Not Passed by Gates

`colab_d_run_20261015.py:101–105` calculates actual maximum rate from ASCII NacYaw using 1-second differencing. The checkpoint shows that for Case III kzm=.05 all groups have a maximum of 0.44°/s, and kzm=0 has a maximum of 0.46°/s, exceeding the required 0.3°/s (0.01° output rounding is insufficient to explain the 0.14–0.16°/s difference); G1 for both Case III settings has 12/12 seeds exceeding 0.31°/s. Case I has a maximum of 0.813°/s. The controller's 0.3°/s command limit does not equal the actual nacelle rate limit; ServoDyn/ElastoDyn dynamics and raw time series should be read back to locate the exceeding segments. Before this point is clarified, the "Rule Passed" for Case III can only be called a computational result, not considered as validation passed under yaw-limited conditions; the entire Segment D cannot be declared as preview having unique value.

The single-beam LOS analytical mean in `colab_d_run_20261015.py:134–147` moves with the baseline nacelle yaw, but its turbulence residual inherits from fixed 3×3 upstream sample points rather than being independently generated at moving measurement points and maintaining longitudinal cross-spectra; therefore, it is a moving mean + fixed residual approximation, not a physical single-beam measurement fully rotating with nacelle yaw. Trigger times were calculated offline and replayed, which is not equivalent to an online detector. The paired median reduction in tower base resultant moment is zero in most combinations; yaw benefits cannot be generalized to overall load benefits. Wilcoxon p-values are uncorrected exploratory p-values for multiple metrics and do not replace predetermined thresholds.

## Parameter Sources and Assumptions

| Parameter | Value Used | Source / Nature | Verification Location |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Storm analytical field and translation scaling | Nguyen 2012 §3–4; turbulence σ as 0.1 × storm translation velocity | Source PDF p. 113 main text; actual code `colab_d_run_20261015.py:40–64` | Local Nguyen 2012 card; PDF p. 113 |
| u/v/w intensity ratio | 1 / 0.7373885 / 0.3337688 | Discrete engineering choice integrated over 0–1 Hz based on three-component Kaimal spectrum in Nguyen PDF pp. 74–75; not three constants directly listed in the paper | Code lines 12, 47–51; independent verification should be performed for integral normalization |
| Case III kzm | 0.05 and 0 | Conflict between original PDF p. 113 main text and Table 4.4 PDF p. 114; both retained | Code lines 37–38 |
| IEC approximate normal turbulence wind field | 18, 20, 22 m/s; σ=0.14(0.75U+5.6), spectrum/coherence reference wind speed actual U of each window | Borrowed from IEC-B turbulence intensity format; wind field is custom approximation rather than original TurbSim | Code lines 184–203 |
| G1/G2L/G2 | 25 m/s, 3 s average; G2L upstream 1D, LOS, 1 s filter + 1 s delay | Specified by task description / LOS geometry and delay are assumptions; G2 fixed 3×3 sample points control | Code lines 134–159, 219–232 |
| S1–S4 thresholds | 25; 10 s >23/24; yaw error >30/20° lasting 3 s and wind speed >15; wind direction rate >0.5/1°/s and wind speed >15 | Assumptions, predetermined simple alternative controls | Task description lines 14–15; code lines 149–155, 227–232 |
| Yaw command and actual yaw | Command 0.3°/s; measured exceedance see above | Command specified in task description, actual output is saved metric (with 0.01° ASCII quantization) | `yaw_rate_max_deg_s` of |

Newly generated local small files total less than 1 MB; old A/B/C files were not overwritten, and Colab raw large outputs were not moved back to workstation.

In a nutshell: The computational criteria for the three trajectories are "Failed, Passed, Passed", respectively, but the actual yaw rate exceedance and moving LOS turbulence approximation in Case III have not yet been ruled out, so Segment D is not yet sufficient to confirm that lidar preview has unique value.

items.text:
# A3 Wind Turbine High Wind Speed Forecast and Control: Read Segment D, Shelved According to Predetermined Rules (2026-10-15 07:5x)
Basis: , (internal line data: Nguyen 2012 analytical downburst + modified turbulence, NREL 5 MW, OpenFAST 5 + ROSCO 2.10.6, 12 seeds × 3 inflows × 10 rules = 360 + steady-state 36 windows, Colab, triggers replayed offline). Lead checked metrics_D.json gates.
- Near-center trajectory: Nacelle line-of-sight (LOS) 1D preview shutdown G2L relative to instantaneous threshold shutdown reduces paired median yaw moment by 20.9% (p=0.012), but tower base fore-aft negative bending moment deteriorates by 14.4% (p=0.0015) > 10% → criterion (b) not passed.
- Off-center trajectories (kzm=0.05 / 0): Yaw moment reduced by 25.0% / 24.3%, blade root negative peak improved by 15.3% / 14.4%, tower base negative peak does not deteriorate → computationally passes all of (a)(b)(c). However, actual nacelle yaw rate reached a maximum of 0.44–0.46°/s (near-center 0.81°/s), exceeding the 0.3°/s setting, with causes unascertained; LOS turbulence residual still takes fixed sample points, which is an approximation.
- Simple radar-free triggers: Wind direction change rate trigger (S4) can achieve equivalent load reduction, but has 36/36 false shutdowns in steady state; yaw error trigger (S3) has no false shutdowns but deteriorates yaw moment by 20–85%; long average window (S2) yields no gain. Preview G2L steady-state false shutdowns are 16/36, close to the 25 m/s baseline of 15/36.
Decision I made: According to the rule pre-written in the review verdict ("Preview shutdown causes negative load deterioration exceeding limit → A3 overall Shelved"), the near-center trajectory has triggered this, and A3 is changed to **Shelved**; the draft promotion proposal is voided. No supplementary review will be conducted for the "passing" of the off-center trajectories—it carries unexplained yaw overspeed and LOS approximations, insufficient to independently support promotion.
Why: Predetermined rules cannot be relaxed after the fact; benefits only appear in "off-center trajectories where yaw cannot keep up", while near-center trajectories come at the cost of reverse bending moment at the tower base; the mechanism itself is "shutting down early", and its value depends on whether downbursts can be identified in advance, which is a detection/forecasting problem, not a control problem.
Cost of being wrong: If off-center trajectory gains remain after yaw overspeed is corrected, and near-center reverse bending moments can be mitigated by gentler feathering, an engineered, practically useful rule of "early shutdown during rapid wind direction shifts" would be missed. See project page for restart conditions.
Literature: Nguyen 2012 (card, PDF p. 113 turbulence scaling, p. 131 FAST aerodynamic validity warning); remainder is internal line data.

The existing six-seed criteria values remain unchanged and require no correction; they remain limited to synthetic fields and offline shutdown replay, and do not equate to online verification.

Reproduction environment: OpenFAST 5.0.0, modified ROSCO 2.10.6 (feedforward gain 0), single Colab CPU high-memory session; input a3_b_colab_bundle_1014.tar.gz, execution script colab_recompute_v4c_20261015.py. Original large outputs are not transferred back to the workstation.

reviews.title: Verdict: A3 literature judgement v1 (3/3 valid: Gemini E, GPT-6 A, GLM D; 2026-10-14 15:5x)
reviews.text:
# Verdict: A3 Literature Assessment v1 (3/3 Valid: Gemini E, GPT-6 A, GLM D; 2026-10-14 15:5x)
Dispatch notes: In sequence Gemini, Codex slot filled by GPT-6, GLM dispatched after queueing; all 3 valid, no vacancies. All three gave "qualified support". Only one round of review.

## Lab Lead Personally Verified
- Guo 2023 WES 8:149 main text §5.2: 16.7% is the tower fore-aft bending moment **DEL** ("reductions of the tower fore–aft bending moment DEL", 22 m/s, unstable stratification); extreme values are not evaluated in the paper. ✔ Confirmed by E and A.
- Ahmed/El Damatty group downburst wind turbine: Page 3 of our repository records "1.5-MW HAWT, parked, β = 90°, warning assumed before downburst". ✔ Confirmed by E.
- Pratapa 2023 PDF pp. 7–8 §4.4 explicitly superimposes turbulence (ε·κ·Um, frequency-domain method); Figs. 13–14 include turbulence. ✔ Confirmed by A; card Z454567N in our repository has an inaccurate self-limiting phrasing "Non-turbulent", handed over to litwiki for correction.
- Nguyen 2012 PDF pp. 112–113 (thesis pp. 95–96; corrected by litwiki on 10-14): shutdown rule "wind speeds above cut-out are permitted for only up to 10 revolutions or 50 seconds". ✔ Confirmed by E.
- IEAWindTask52/LidarAssistedControl repository exists (GitHub API: latest push 2026-09-03, 14 stars, no license declared). ✔ Confirmed by A and D.
- Zhang et al. 2026 Energy (DOI 10.1016/j.energy.2025.139730, Crossref title "Optimization control model for wind farms considering the spatiotemporal dynamics of gusts") exists; full text 403 unread, content treated only as "nearest neighbor" based on A's abstract-level description.

## Mandatory Changes
1. Mark 16.7% as DEL (fatigue), and no longer juxtapose it with extreme value criteria. (E1, A8)
2. Redefine the gap: Load analyses for "shutdown under downburst / feathering shutdown after early warning" already exist (the 50 s over-limit shutdown sequence in Nguyen 2012 / Nguyen & Manuel 2014 DOI 10.3390/en7106527; Ahmed et al. 2022/2023 assuming shutdown after warning); wind-farm-level lidar preview observation + early yaw/IPC related to gust fronts already exist (Zhang 2026 Energy, full text unread); IEC gust-scale extreme gust detection derating already exists (Hagemann 2017 DOI 10.18419/opus-9333; Haizmann 2018 DOI 10.1088/1742-6596/1037/3/032025, unverified). **What is genuinely not found**: Nacelle lidar preview feedforward pitch control for a single turbine under downburst (time-varying mean + wind direction rotation) inflow, and quantification of benefits from "second-to-minute preview signals determining the shutdown/soft cut-out trigger time T". Still categorized as "not found", do not refer to it as "nonexistent", pending DR supplementary runs. (E2, A1, D note)
3. Inflow: Parameters and equations are taken from Nguyen 2012 Chapters 3–4 (analytical downburst + storm translation + amplitude-modulated turbulence); Lu 2019 is LES cold pool and Pratapa is CFD paused snapshot + frequency-domain turbulence—do not mix parameter names. Preview signals must be independently sampled upstream in the 4D field, and cannot use the constant-speed Taylor translation of the InflowWind single-plane wind box (otherwise ② and ③ degenerate from a shared source). (E3, A2, A4, D1)
4. Controller: All four groups share the same IEAWindTask52/LidarAssistedControl toolchain (modified ROSCO 2.6.0), with ① taking feedforward gain 0; explicitly document actuator rate limits, amplitude limits, and filtering delays. (E4, A3, D3)
5. Wind direction / yaw: Two storm paths (near-center small wind direction change, eccentric large wind direction change, referring to Nguyen 2012 Case I/III), with consistent yaw control across the four groups (rate limit 0.3°/s); add tower-top yaw moment, tower-base resultant moment, blade-root out-of-plane moment extremes in both positive and negative directions, and overspeed to the metrics. (E5, A5, D2)
6. Group ④ definition: Benchmark against T=0 reactive shutdown (both Nguyen 50 s rule and instantaneous threshold), with ①–③ sharing the same protection logic; T is defined relative to "hub wind speed exceeding 25 m/s", with information split into two tiers: perfect and realistic. (E5, A6, D note)
7. Criteria: Fix turbulence seeds (≥6) × 2 paths before results are generated, taking the median; 10% serves only as an internal screening threshold for this implementation, with conclusion wording restricted to "this inflow + this control law", without extrapolating to "feedforward has no merit in downbursts". (A7, D4)

## For Reference Only
- In the maturity column, write only the technical status; "whether to enter" is separately listed as this group's judgment. (A Note 1)
- Other generalized numbers from the Grok report (20–60%, 5–50+%, "standard shutdown is safest") are likewise not used. (A Note 2)
- Lu 2019 consists of five stability cases and three categories. (A Note 3) Corrected.
- Add Lu et al. 2021 Energies 14:5407, Motes 2025 Sandia DOI 10.2172/2997331. (D Note)
- Downburst mean ramp is on the order of minutes, slower than feedback bandwidth; the ②−① difference primarily comes from the fast front and turbulence; inflow needs to retain the fast front. (D Note)`
- OpenFAST InflowWind includes lidar parameters starting from v2.5 (D Note), but it will still not be used to generate previews (see Mandatory Change 3).

## Unadopted Objections
- A: "Current evidence does not support any 'gap' determination" — Partially adopted: Broad "preview control under gust fronts" will no longer be called a gap; the narrow scope (single-turbine downburst nacelle lidar feedforward + preview-determined shutdown time) was not found in 7 total searches by the three reviewers and Lab Lead, retained as "not found, pending DR" as a working hypothesis, not claimed as a gap externally.
- E: "Early feathering in the post-cut-out stage of a downburst may amplify negative upwind bending moments" — Included in metrics as a phenomenon to be tested (in both positive and negative directions), without pre-judging conclusions.

## Conclusion
The direction is worth continuing (narrow scope as above); do not tell Liang Hu it is a "gap", only call it "no precedent found". Rewrite the task specification for the minimum experiment according to Mandatory Changes 3–7, to be dispatched after the ideas smoke test results return.

reviews.title: Verdict: A3 conclusion on preview-based early shutdown and the promotion proposal (6/6 valid: Gemini E, GPT-6 A, GLM D, DeepSeek C, Kimi B, Grok F; 2026-10-15)
reviews.text:
# Verdict: A3 Preview Early Shutdown Conclusions and Promotion Proposal (6/6 Valid: Gemini E, GPT-6 A, GLM D, DeepSeek C, Kimi B, Grok F; 2026-10-15)
Dispatch note: All 6 copies valid, no vacancies to backfill. E/A/D/C/B support with reservations, F does not support. Only one round of review.

## Lead Personal Verification (metrics_B_stop.json recomputation, scripts, Nguyen 2012 original text)
- Yaw moment G2 vs G1 seed-by-seed: near-center [18.0, −3.2, 28.0, 21.9, 2.0, 13.1]%, offset [−3.1, 43.0, 26.0, −3.1, 27.0, 22.3]%—medians of 15.5/24.2% are true, but 1/6 and 2/6 seeds increased reversely. ✔
- Blade root out-of-plane negative peak amplitude: near-center seeds 112/203 deteriorated by 128%/158%. ✔ (E, A, D, F)
- Tower base fore-aft **negative** bending moment amplitude: near-center paired median deteriorated by 23.7%; offset deteriorated across 6/6 seeds (median 3.95%, maximum 28.8%). ✔ (E)—"tower base and blade root basically unchanged" is untrue.
- Turbulence isotropy: segment_b_run line 121 multiplies u, v, w by 0.1·speed simultaneously. ✔ (E) Nguyen 2012 PDF page 113 (thesis page 96) body text states turbulence intensity should "scale with the storm's translation speed", whereas this test scaled by instantaneous total wind speed, differing from the original text. ✔ (E, F)
- Case III kzm: PDF page 113 body text kzm=0.05 m/s is consistent with the script; F claimed Table 4.4 is 0, but table text extraction cannot verify cell-by-cell—listed as "pending verification".
- Nguyen 2012 PDF page 131: downburst Case I–III inflows "might arguably be outside the range of validity for aerodynamic loads computation in FAST", and large yaw errors likewise. ✔ (F)
- Upstream signal is a fixed-coordinate 3×3 horizontal wind vector magnitude, not following nacelle yaw, with no line-of-sight projection. ✔ (E, A, script lines 115–140)

## Must Change
1. Do not promote; do not report to Liang Hu that the "conclusion holds". External phrasing narrowed to: under this analytical inflow, offline trigger replay, idealized upstream sampling, and 3 s >25 m/s rule, paired median yaw moment across 6 seeds decreased by 15.5%/24.2%, with individual seeds increasing reversely; simultaneously, tower base fore-aft negative bending moment and some seeds' blade root negative peaks deteriorated; do not claim "robust", "lidar", "unique value", or "optimal distance". (All)
2. Simple radar-free alternatives not ruled out: yaw error trigger, wind direction rate-of-change trigger, longer averaging windows, symmetric-filtered rotor signals. The distinguishing feature of a downburst is precisely wind direction rotation; such triggers might achieve near-zero false shutdowns in false shutdown tests. (All)
3. Modify turbulence according to Nguyen's original text: component intensity ratios and scaling by translation speed; use actual mean wind speed for spectral/coherence reference wind speed in steady-state false shutdown wind fields. (E, A)
4. Add "no deterioration" conditions to criteria: tower base fore-aft negative peaks and blade root negative peaks (all blades) must not deteriorate by median >10%. (E, A, D, F)
5. Change upstream signal to line-of-sight measurement following nacelle yaw (at least single-beam LOS projection), and verify actual yaw rate seed-by-seed for offset cases. (E, A, C, B)
6. Increase seed count to 12, report seed-by-seed ranges and paired tests. (E, D)
7. Risks must be stated: legacy 26 cases have only process-level traceability; Case III yaw error reaches 78°, and Nguyen 2012 PDF p.131 notes this may exceed the aerodynamic validity range of FAST; false shutdowns are 600 s window counts, not operational probabilities. (A, D, C, B, F)

## For Reference Only
- Lowering threshold benchmark is fair within the "same 3 s rule family", and criteria were not changed post-hoc (D, B); but G2 has 1 s more filtering, and spatial averaging differs (E, D).
- Resource estimates should follow actual measurements (B ~3–4 CU, C ~0.1 CU). (D)
- Offline replay is not future information leakage (A).
- 2D results lack a false shutdown arm and cannot answer the optimal distance question. (F)

## Unadopted Objections
- F "overall does not support": Partially adopted—do not promote, do not report conclusions; but do not shelve, because the median direction is consistent, keeping one robust (D), and untested simple alternatives do not mean already replaced; one additional round is sufficient to judge.

## Conclusion
Proposal returned. Dispatch segment D (task specification), with criteria pre-fixed; if D shows that simple radar-free triggers can achieve equivalent load reduction without more false shutdowns, or that preview shutdown causes negative loads to deteriorate beyond limits → A3 Shelved entirely; otherwise rewrite proposal according to narrowed phrasing and submit to Liang Hu via Node A (as exploratory evidence, without claiming conclusion holds).

results.title: A3 high-wind forecasting and regulation for wind turbines: literature judgement v1 (Lead, 10-14 15:0x)
results.text:
# A3 Wind Turbine High-Wind-Speed Forecasting and Regulation: Literature Assessment v1 (Lead, 10-14 15:0x)
Basis: Grok quick search report  (citations 8/8 DOIs exist); Lead personally verified (following "Verified" section); Deep Research second step **not done** (30-day quota 30/30 exhausted).

## Sources Verified by Lead
1. Guo, Schlipf & Cheng 2023, WES 8:149, DOI 10.5194/wes-8-149-2023 — Abstract original: LAC mainly reduces rotor speed variations (up to 40%), tower base fore-aft bending moments (up to 16.7%), power fluctuations (up to 20%), OpenFAST; "Taylor's frozen hypothesis does not take into account the coherence decay"; gains depend on turbulence models, turbulence parameters, and mean wind speed. [Abstract verified]
2. Schlipf & Raach 2016, JPCS 753:052011 — Abstract: Under turbulent fitted EOG, LAC "still able to significantly reduce the ultimate loads on the tower base" (no percentage). [Abstract verified]
3. Nguyen 2012 dissertation (UT Austin, local Zotero FI6QJ5T3, PDF p. 133 / journal p. 116) original: when both wind direction and wind speed change rates are very high, "pitch and yaw control even together are insufficient to reduce turbine load range"; shutdown "can minimize loads effectively as soon as it is implemented; however, it is likely that the turbine might already have been subjected to very high loads before the shutdown sequence starts". [Original verified] → This is precisely where "lead time / preview" may have value.
4. Lu, Hawbecker, Basu & Manuel 2019, Energies 12:2773 (local KW4WFENX, PDF pp. 1, 16): LES idealized downburst, three stability conditions, 5 MW onshore wind turbine, studying the effects of pitch/yaw control and ultimate/fatigue loads. [Original first page and page 16 verified]
5. Pratapa, Nguyen & Manuel 2023, DOI 10.1115/1.4055076 (card): Non-turbulent axisymmetric CFD downburst → 5 MW loads, loads depend on yaw/pitch states.
6. Gap search: Lead performed two online searches ("lidar-assisted feedforward ... downburst thunderstorm outflow"; "preview control gust front/downburst nacelle lidar OpenFAST") and neither found papers applying lidar feedforward/preview to downbursts or gust fronts; the closest is Stuttgart's extreme gust detection for power derating (EOG / turbulent EOG). Grok likewise reported "not found". — Classified as "not found", which does not equal "nonexistent".

## Grok Claims Not Adopted
- The "1–2 building heights", "10–15 s lead time", and "15–40% load reduction under realistic conditions" in Section 6 "Borrowable for buildings" provided no specific citations; they are Grok generalizations and not treated as literature evidence.
- A2's Grok report restated the 30 m decay length on this line and extrapolated "0.75–1.5 s preview"—a restatement of data on this line, not treated as literature evidence.
- "Goldwind thousands of LAC units", "typhoon yaw optimization reduces load by 1–9%", "floating TMD reduces pitch by 9.5%", etc.: unverified, not used for now.

## Existing Work and Gaps (v1)
| Direction | Representative Work and Citation | Maturity | Can We Enter | Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lidar feedforward under steady turbulence (collective pitch) | Bossanyi 2014 JPCS 555:012011; Guo 2023 WES 8:149 (Abstract: tower base fore-aft bending moment up to −16.7%); Schlipf 2018 IEA Task 32 certification | Mature → early commercial | No (home turf of wind energy community) | — |
| Feedforward under IEC extreme operating gust (EOG / turbulent EOG) | Schlipf & Raach 2016 JPCS 753:052011 (Abstract: significantly reduces tower base ultimate loads); Stuttgart extreme gust detection for power derating | Developing | Weak (already being done) | — |
| Wind turbine loads and control under downbursts / gust fronts (feedback/shutdown only) | Nguyen 2012 (PDF p. 133: pitch + yaw insufficient, shutdown too late); Lu 2019 Energies 12:2773; Pratapa 2023 | Developing (mainly load assessment) | Yes (our group's downburst wind field, CM1/LES resources) | Downburst inflow time series (literature parameters or CM1 line read-only output), OpenFAST+ROSCO |
| Preview feedforward, early shutdown / soft cutout under downbursts / gust fronts | Not found (Grok, Lead two searches) | Gap (pending DR confirmation) | Yes—most promising entry point | Same as above + lidar simulation (OpenFAST built-in LidarSim or ViConDAR), quantification of Taylor's frozen hypothesis breakdown |
| Forecast-driven wind-farm-level shutdown / derating (hours–minutes) | Jia 2023 Electronics (DOI 10.3390/electronics12214443, ramp forecasting and control under extreme storms, unverified); Typhoon review Li 2022 Atmosphere 13:451 (unverified) | Basic shutdown mature, optimization strategies developing | Medium (leaning grid/operations, not our group's forte) | Forecast skill data (retrieved from A1) |
| Tower/blade vibration mitigation (TMD/TLCD/IPC/flaps) | Fakhry 2026 review JLFNVAC DOI 10.1177/14613484261437475 (unverified) | TMD/IPC mature, active developing; upper limits under non-stationary transients unquantified | Medium (sharable with A2 active dampers) | Add TMD module to the same simulation chain |

## One-Sentence Summary (Tentative, Pending Review)
Worth pursuing, but only in a narrow aperture: **under non-stationary inflows such as downbursts / gust fronts, how much more ultimate loads can preview (lidar feedforward or early shutdown) reduce compared to pure feedback, and how much lead time is needed**; do not touch steady-state LAC or IEC gusts.

## Minimal Experiment Candidates
OpenFAST + ROSCO (NREL 5 MW onshore), workstation  local CPU, 0 CU: using the same set of downburst inflows (analytical downburst model superimposed with turbulence, parameters taken from Lu 2019 / Pratapa 2023, checking before assuming), compare ① pure feedback ROSCO, ② perfect preview collective pitch feedforward, ③ "realistic preview" advected according to Taylor's frozen hypothesis with coherence decay, ④ triggering shutdown / soft cutout T seconds in advance (T sweep), observing tower base fore-aft bending moment extremes, blade root bending moments, and overspeed. Criteria (predetermined): if ② reduces tower base extreme by <10% relative to ①, it indicates feedforward has no payoff in downbursts, Shelved; if ≥10% and ③ retains more than half, then discuss the next step.

## Verification of OpenFAST Lidar / ROSCO Feedforward Interfaces (Distinguishing Module from Controller)

In OpenFAST v3.5.0, new fields such as `SensorTypeNumBeam` and `MeasurementInterval` were added to InflowWind input, indicating lidar simulation has been incorporated; v5.0.0 source includes [](https://github.com/OpenFAST/openfast/blob/v5.0.0/modules/inflowwind/src/Lidar.f90). [v3.5 Input Changes Table](https://openfast.readthedocs.io/en/v3.5.3/source/user/api_change.html#openfast-v3-4-0-to-openfast-v3-5-0) indicates the source; [InflowWind driver documentation](https://openfast.readthedocs.io/en/dev/source/user/inflowwind/driver.html) explicitly names it the LidarSim module. FAST.Farm/TurbSim are in the same OpenFAST repository, but no lidar/wind field test cases were run this time. Note that the baseline case currently has `SensorType=0`, which does not mean lidar was activated in this simulation.

The OpenFAST [Extended Bladed Interface table](https://openfast.readthedocs.io/en/dev/source/user/servodyn/ExtendedBladedInterface.html) specifies that `Ext_Interface=1` in `avrSWAPDISCON.IN` uses the OpenFAST 3.5+ extended `avrSWAP`; this merely indicates extended channel compatibility and **does not equal** native implementation of lidar feedforward control in ROSCO. In ROSCO v2.10.6, [`ReadSetParameters.f90avrSWAP(27)` hub wind speed (`HorWindV`) without reading the lidar section 2001–2500; `Lidarfeedforward` was not detected in the controller source code. The wind speed index for `OL_ModeOL_BP_Mode=1` uses internal estimate `WE_VwavrSWAP(27)` current hub wind speed or wind speed estimator as a feedforward preview interface.

A research-implemented integration path indeed exists: the IEA Task 52 / MSCA-LIKE [project README](https://github.com/IEAWindTask52/LidarAssistedControl) specifies a Bladed-style `WRAPPER.dll` calling `LDP.dll` (LOS → rotor equivalent wind speed) → `FFP.dllLidarWindSpeedFF_Mode` parameter. This time, only standard ROSCO ran successfully, without claiming preview signal integration.

## Local Run Positioning

The 60 s steady wind NREL 5MW onshore configuration originates from [ROSCO v2.10.6 Official Test_Cases/NREL-5MW](https://github.com/NatLabRockies/ROSCO/tree/v2.10.6/Examples/Test_Cases/NREL-5MW); the original case was already `TMax=60 s`, `WindType=1`, `Ext_Interface=1`. Only ServoDyn's `DLL_FileName="DISCON_LIB_PATH"` was changed to `libdiscon.soHWindSpeedsmoke/` inside the conda environment; specific termination status and elapsed time are subject to logs. No turbulence, no IEC EOG, no downbursts, nor lidar feedforward. GitHub figures and interface verification are current as of this query. Non-official GitHub QBlade source code and unverified small repositories without licenses must not be treated as verified, reproducible code.

10-14 19:30 ET. Workstation WSL local CPU; no Colab/HPC used. Previous OpenFAST/ROSCO smoke tests passed. This report is not a complete 28-run acceptance: valid protection-enabled configuration `SD_Mode=1 and .

## Verification and Errata (Read First)

, are exploratory files generated from the earlier round of 28 test runs in `segment_a_v9`, and **cannot be used for Segment A load or shutdown conclusions**: although `SD_EnableTime=1` was set in every DISCON input, the master switch was missed and three `_v10c_` plots. The `_v10b_` plots lack Chinese glyphs and will not be delivered. Additionally, corrected the earlier Case III of .

## Design and Validation

Non-turbulent 4D vector field `(x,y,z,t)` from Nguyen 2012 §3.3 Eqs. 3.2–3.11, 3.21–3.24 / Table 4.4; Case I near-center, Case III eccentric. A 9-point average is taken at rotor plane x=0, then projected to the uniform wind time series of OpenFAST InflowWind WindType 2 (horizontal speed and direction, vertical speed, fixed power-law shear 0.2); this is not a full planar (y,z) non-uniform field. An independent upstream 9-point spatial average at x=−126/−252 m undergoes idealized line-of-sight reconstruction along the upstream local direction, 2 s first-order filtering, and 2 s processing delay; 1D advection arrival time is estimated from the wind speed measured upstream at that time. Preview is not sampled from the InflowWind frozen wind box, nor does it use rotor direction information. Perfect preview is the rotor-equivalent wind speed shifted forward by 2 s into the future, used only as an upper-bound comparison.

The same ROSCO 2.10.6 Apache-2.0 control library binary, ① gain zero, ②/③ gain one (**assumed, unoptimized**); additive collective pitch offset placed before original ROSCO limits/rate limits. Static pitch curve taken from NREL5MW bundled ROSCO `Cp_Ct_Cq.NREL5MW.txtbuild_segment_a_curve.pyPC_MaxRat/MinRat=±8°/sSD_Mode=1`, `SD_EnableTime=1`, shutdown pitch rate 8°/s, torque derate 2000 Nm/s (ROSCO example settings). T=0 is shutdown after rotor-equivalent wind speed first reaches 25 m/s and sustains exceedance for 50 s; both analytical time series sustained exceedance for >50 s, so first threshold crossing + 50 s is consistent with continuous exceedance. Perfect T>0 triggers T seconds before the true threshold; realistic 1D can only act after the threshold is detected upstream, and larger requested T values are all truncated to the detection time due to insufficient information, and cannot be treated as actual 40 s advances. Both qualities of T=0 use the same protection settings, and the two output extreme values for Case III are completely identical.

Important physical limitation: The scheduled 0.3°/s yaw command has entered ROSCO debug output (Case III `YawRateComNacYaw` was measured only within approximately ±0.12°, not truly following large directional rotations; likely an issue with baseline ServoDyn yaw mechanism / channel wiring, not yet pinpointed. Therefore, eccentric path loads **are not qualified 0.3°/s tracking yaw cases**; no generalizable conclusions should be drawn from this. Output derivatives exceeding 0.3°/s during abrupt changes also cannot be used to claim compliance with actual actuator rate limits.

Case I simulation raw storm timestamp 220.5–528.75 s (the initial ~60 s is warm-up close to 12 m/s, first equivalent wind speed of 13 m/s at ~280.7 s); Case III 399.25–638.75 s, 13 m/s at ~459 s. Both statistical windows run from simulation t≥60 s to the end (ending ~60 s after the last >25 m/s). Numerical startup transients in the initial few seconds are excluded; loads remain during the near-steady-state warm-up portion (certain extremes for Case I occur at t≈64 s); if event peaks need to be compared independently from background peaks, an event sub-window must be explicitly reported separately in the next stage. Source fields: `TwrBsMxt` side-to-side, `TwrBsMyt` fore-aft, `YawBrMzp` tower-top yaw, `RootMyb1` blade 1 out-of-plane root bending moment, `RotSpeed` rotational speed; resultant is `hypot(TwrBsMxt,TwrBsMyt)`. All metrics, both positive and negative directions, and actual trigger times for each run are in the JSON; the wind turbine is not a field measurement.

## Control Law Gaps and Available Bases

The current 24/28 runs with valid protection used a binary compiled from the same local Apache-2.0 ROSCO 2.10.6 source copy, not LidarAssistedControl. However, the feedforward term in remains `gain × [θss(U_preview) − θss(U_hub)]NacYaw` without tracking, see line 15 of .

(39), (41), (42) provide `θFF=θss(uLLf)`, first-order filter , . In the paper, `Tpitch=0.22 s`, `Twindow=1 s` belong to their device/scanning setup; transferring them to this 9-point preview field is an assumption that needs explanation; they cannot be directly claimed as measured parameters for Nguyen downbursts. The original paper places the feedforward pitch rate before the PI integrator; the current self-authored patch adds a pitch offset before original ROSCO amplitude/rate limits, and the two are also not equivalent.
