# F Wind-sensitive operations and structural warnings

## Objective
Ensemble / multi-source forecasts provide exceedance probabilities → warning decisions for wind-sensitive operations and structures such as crane lifting, bridge closures, and construction; assess how much economic value this pipeline adds over deterministic forecasts and persistence.

## Current Status
**10-14 20:0x Shelved** (3/3 conditional support; verdict).
- Failed frozen primary criterion: for sustained wind 10 m/s, 24 h lead time, and C/L 0.05–0.5 (assumed), the four-source mean probability achieved relative economic value V = 0.266 vs. 0.156 for the best deterministic forecast—a difference of 0.111, with a 95% CI of [−0.006, 0.179].
- The advantage of probabilistic decision rules over deterministic thresholds stems primarily from the probabilistic formulation itself: at low C/L, single-source GFS probability performs just as well as the four-source mean (0.598 vs. 0.599 at 10 m/s); across C/L 0.05–0.5, the four-source mean exceeds the best single source (Pangu) by only 0.024, and at the 12 m/s threshold it underperforms single-source GraphCast. No stable incremental gain unique to AI multi-source blending was found.
- Precedents: HS2 Align (2021–23) already used global NWP + local LSTM bias correction to support viaduct lifting decisions; the Severn Bridge closes based on forecast gusts. The only aspects not found in prior work are "directly driven by AI global models" and "empirically measured C/L."
- By-products: threshold and wind-speed definition table (below); finding that deterministic linear bias correction dampens strong winds and underperforms raw GFS at low C/L (a cautionary note for A1 bias-correction design).
- **Restart conditions**: an operational partner provides downtime cost/loss data or specific operational requirements; or A1 adds daytime operational verification hours (e.g., 18 UTC); or Node B produces a true ensemble (used only as a re-evaluation trigger). Re-evaluation takes ~10 minutes and 0 CU using existing scripts.

## Operation Type / Criteria & Sources / Current Warning Practices / What We Can Add
| Operation Type | Criteria & Sources | Current Warning Practices | What We Can Add |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Crane lifting | 3 s gust at boom tip: tower crane design limit 20 m/s, UK practical shutdown at 16.5–17 m/s; mobile crane mean 9–11 m/s; crawler crane 12–16 m/s; personnel basket 7 m/s (CPA CIG/TCIG 2507, PDF pp. 13, 20, 23, 47, citing BS EN 13001-2 and BS 7121). Converted to 10 m mean wind, this corresponds to roughly 5–10 m/s (assumption; see verification log). Chinese national standards (GB) / OSHA clauses pending verification by reviewers E/F | Real-time on-site anemometer monitoring + manufacturer manual thresholds; HS2 Align used NWP + local LSTM correction to support lifting decisions (HS2 Learning Legacy, verified); advance planning by multiplying surface forecasts by height-dependent gust factors (CPA PDF pp. 21–22); no probabilistic exceedance warning products found (Grok; not found ≠ nonexistent) | Hindcast replay: probabilistic decision rules outperform deterministic thresholds, but the gain comes from the probabilistic formulation rather than AI multi-source blending (primary criterion failed) |
| Bridge traffic restrictions / closures | Severn M48: tiered by forecast gusts at 30/35/40/70 kn, full bridge closure at 40 kn (National Highways official website); Mackinac: tiered by sustained winds at 20/35/50/65 mph (official website FAQ, explicitly sustained wind rather than gust); verified | Severn already decides bridge closures based on **forecast gusts**—precedent exists for forecast-driven closures | Probabilistic formulation + cost/loss economic value evaluation; no internal hindcast replay (lacking bridge-site observations) |
| Work at height / construction | OSHA 1926.1431(k)(8)(i): >20 mph at personnel platform requires judgment by a competent person (verified); Chinese standards (secondary sources, primary text unverified): GB 55034 "suspend work at height when workplace wind reaches Beaufort scale 5 or above"; JGJ 80 "Beaufort scale 6 or above" | Primarily on-site judgment | TBD |

## Boundaries
- No per-experiment cap on Colab (updated by parent project at 10-14 18:3x; previous ≤20 CU cap is void); report to Node A via `--report` first if a single experiment is projected to exceed 100 CU; must run `colab stop` immediately after use; dispatch only one executor per round. Supercomputer single-job limit of ≤50 SU remains unchanged.

## Finalized Decisions
- 10-14: Selected crane lifting as the initial operation type; replaced "ensemble" with an equal-weighted average of four-source probabilities (GraphCast/Pangu/FCNv2/GFS) while explicitly noting it is a proxy; froze hindcast replay criteria (see task brief). Decision.

## Trials and Results
| Date | Action | One-Sentence Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10-14 | Hindcast replay: OKC 12 stations in 2023, four-source mean probability vs. deterministic vs. persistence, cost/loss relative economic value V (ideas, 0 CU) | **Failed frozen primary criterion**: for sustained wind 10 m/s at 24 h lead time across C/L 0.05–0.5, V = 0.266 vs. 0.156 for best deterministic, difference 0.111, daily-block bootstrap 95% CI [−0.006, 0.179] crosses 0 (135 events). Supporting evidence is consistently positive: point estimates for multi-source probability exceed best deterministic across all 12 threshold × lead-time combinations (+0.08–0.22), with CIs not crossing 0 for 8 m/s sustained wind and 10 m/s gust; multi-source probability beats single-source GFS probability by 0.108 [0.036, 0.226]; persistence V is negative across the board. Lead independently recomputed both primary V values with identical results. Supplemental report for 6 m/s (roughly corresponding to mobile crane shutdown, report only): 24 h V = 0.492 vs. 0.320, difference 0.171 [0.119, 0.214]; 48 h difference 0.175 [0.122, 0.214] (Lead recomputation matched; if deterministic candidates also include bias-corrected Pangu/FCNv2, the best deterministic at 6 m/s is Pangu at 0.329 with a difference of ~0.163, whereas at the 10 m/s primary criterion the best deterministic remains GFS at 0.156, unchanged) |

## Parameter Source Table
| Parameter | Value | Source or "Assumption" | Sources Checked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Crane lifting shutdown wind speed (3 s gust at boom tip) | Tower crane 16.5–17 m/s (design 20); mobile crane 9–11; crawler crane 12–16; personnel basket 7 | CPA CIG/TCIG 2507 (2025) PDF pp. 13/20/23/47 | , pages (none); Grok; original CPA text |
| 10 m mean wind → boom-tip gust factor | 1.65 (50 m)–1.86 (150 m); gust → gust 1.18–1.33 | CPA PDF pp. 21–22 (Liebherr table, rural roughness) | Same as above |
| Hindcast threshold tiers | Sustained wind 8/10/12 m/s, gust 10/13/15 m/s | Assumption: inherited from A1 tiers, roughly corresponding to tower/mobile crane shutdown per the conversion factors above | — |
| Cost/loss ratio C/L | 0.05–0.5 (frozen criterion); sensitivity 0.01–0.10 | Assumption. Reviewer E reported a typical offshore operations value of 0.1 (Carrasco 2013, cited via SECLI-FIRM 2021 slides), link 404 unverified; E roughly estimated 0.01–0.10 from daily downtime cost / accident loss without multiplying L by accident probability, biasing it low. Reviewer F found no published figures | , Grok, reviewers E/F |
| Chinese domestic lifting thresholds | >9.0 m/s at highest point during erection/dismantling (GB 55034 §3.4.7); ≥12 m/s for tower crane operation (JGJ 196 §4.0.9, clause does not specify averaging period or height; reviewer A reported verifying the primary text); Beaufort scale "6 or above" for lifting (JGJ 276 §3.0.14; "10 m, 10 min mean" is extrapolated from the meteorological wind-scale definition rather than stated in the standard itself) | Consistent between reviewers E and F, but both from secondary sources (JGJ 33 §§4.1.14/4.1.15, JGJ 196 §4.0.9, GB 55034 §3.4.7), primary text unverified | E/F |
| Relative economic value V definition | Static cost/loss model, V={min(o,r)−(h+f)r−m}/{min(o,r)−o·r}, r=C/L, climatology=0, perfect forecast=1 | Zhu et al. 2002 BAMS journal p. 75 (PDF p. 3) Eqs. 5–7, card; hindcast implementation (unavoidable loss = 0) matches this formulation, verified by Lead | Card created by litwiki |
| Daily event definition | Exceedance at either 00 or 12 UTC on a given day | Assumption (sensitivity analysis only) | — |

## Open Items and Next Steps
- Grok response received and checked against primary sources. Waiting for reviewers E/F to return: verify primary texts, populate operational thresholds and C/L values, finalize the assessment table, and submit literature conclusions.
- Currently shelved, with no running tasks. Once Deep Research quota recovers, a supplemental check for precedents on "AI global models used for operational shutdown decisions" can be run (low priority).
- Pending verification (for reference only): Glasgow S2S crane-hire cost–loss study (eprints.gla.ac.uk/320158); primary texts of JGJ/GB clauses. Final "worth pursuing / shelved" determination awaits E/F clause checks so literature conclusions and hindcast interpretation can be submitted together; Lead inclination: make no claim of economic value, treat as shelved, and document restart conditions (empirical C/L, operational daytime verification hours, true ensemble).
- Limitations noted upfront: A1's 24/48 h verification times only cover 00/12 UTC (local morning/evening); 10 m wind ≠ boom-tip wind.

## Literature Basis
- CPA CIG/TCIG 2507 (2025) guidance on wind speeds for crane lifting, original PDF archived.
- Browell et al. 2016 ESREL: cost/loss + logistic probabilistic decision-making (offshore wind O&M), methodological precedent.
- Relative economic value V: Zhu et al. 2002 BAMS (journal p. 75, Eqs. 5–7); Richardson 2000 QJRMS (author preprint PDF p. 4 Eq. 3, journal page unverified); Murphy 1977 MWR (journal p. 808 Eq. 11). Card index.

# Task Brief: F Hindcast Pilot — Economic Value of Exceedance Probability Warnings vs. Deterministic GFS vs. Persistence (Frozen 10-14 18:40)

Workstation local CPU, 0 CU, do not run on Colab or supercomputers.

## Inputs (Read-Only, Do Not Recompute Forecasts)
- (2022) and `paired_station_test.csv.gz` (2023).
- Columns: source∈{GRAP_v100_GFS, PANG_v100_GFS, FOUR_v200_GFS, GFS}, lead_h∈{24,48} with `corrected` and `prob_wind_{6,8,10,12}`, `prob_gust_{10,13,15}` (gusts available at only three stations: GOK/OKC/PWA); observations `metar_speed` (2 min sustained wind) and `minute_gust`; baselines `persistence` and `climatology`.
- Reference scripts. Python environment to use.

## Tasks
1. Warning schemes (compute once for each threshold × lead time combination):
 - P_multi: equal-weighted average of four-source probabilities (multi-source proxy for an ensemble; explicitly state that this is a proxy rather than a true ensemble)
 - P_stack: four-source logistic stacking fitted exclusively on 2022 data (optional, if 2022 sample size suffices)
 - Individual single-source probabilities
 - Deterministic: GFS raw, GFS corrected, GraphCast corrected (suspend operations whenever forecast ≥ threshold)
 - Persistence (suspend operations whenever prior observation ≥ threshold); climatological frequency as reference (baseline defining V=0).
2. Thresholds: sustained wind 6, 8, 10, 12 m/s; gust 10, 13, 15 m/s. (18:30 addendum: converted per the CPA crane lifting guidance, sustained winds of 6–8 m/s roughly correspond to mobile crane shutdown and 8–10 m/s to tower crane shutdown, see reference; the 6 m/s tier is for reporting only, while the primary criterion remains unchanged.)
3. Economic value: standard static cost/loss model (relative economic value V per Richardson 2000 QJRMS 126:649, scaled with climatology = 0 and perfect forecast = 1). Compute full curves across C/L from 0.01 to 0.99; for each C/L, probabilistic schemes trigger shutdown whenever p≥C/L (do not tune optimal probability thresholds on 2023 data).
4. Statistics: block bootstrap by verification date (1,000 resamples) to obtain 95% confidence intervals for V; report event counts for each threshold.
5. In addition to the "station-timestep" evaluation, provide a daily-scale version: exceedance at either of the two daily verification times counts as a "daily event," with the shutdown decision based on the maximum daily probability (for sensitivity analysis only).

## Frozen Criteria (No Changes Prior to Results)
Within C/L ∈ [0.05, 0.5] (assumed interval, literature source pending verification; final evaluation will read the curve at the verified range):
- Primary criterion: sustained wind 10 m/s, 24 h lead time: mean V of P_multi exceeds that of the "best deterministic scheme" by ≥0.05, and the bootstrap confidence interval does not cross 0
- Guardrail: within the same interval, V of P_multi is not lower than single-source GFS probability by more than 0.02 (tests whether AI multi-source blending adds incremental value over single-source GFS probability; reported separately, not a primary criterion)
- Gust 13 m/s is reported only (three stations, small sample size).

## Deliverables (Write To)
(One-sentence conclusion on the first line, main table, item-by-item criterion evaluation, limitations), .

## Boundaries
- Check literature before assuming unspecified parameters: the C/L range and "daily event" definition are both assumptions and must be explicitly labeled as "Assumption" in `results.md`.
- Limitations must be stated explicitly: verification times are only 00/12 UTC (local morning/evening, not midday working hours); ASOS anemometer heights have not been verified station by station; 10 m wind does not equal boom-tip wind.
- Do not delegate to other bots; only this single executor.

# Node F: Grok Quick Search Report Verification (10-14 18:25)

Report: . Original PDF stored at . Page numbers are all PDF physical pages (CPA document footer "Page N of 57" = PDF page − 1).

## Personally Verified in Original Text and Adopted
| Conclusion | Source | Original Quote |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tower crane design in-use wind speed upper limit 20 m/s, defined as 3 s mean gust | CPA CIG/TCIG 2507, PDF page 20 (citing BS EN 13001-2:2021 Table 1) | "specifies a maximum wind speed of 20 m/s (45 mph / 72 km/h)"; "gust wind velocity averaged over a period of 3 seconds." |
| UK tower cranes actually winded-off at 16.5–17 m/s | Ibid. PDF page 13 (citing BS 7121-5:2019 §14.1), page 20 | "usually winded-off at 16.5m/s (38mph)"; "typically taken out of service at 17 m/s (38 mph)" |
| Wind-off speed varies by model: tower cranes 12–17 m/s, traditional mobile cranes average 9–11 m/s, crawler cranes 12–16 m/s | Ibid. PDF page 23 | "a traditional mobile crane winds-off on average at around 9-11 m/s" |
| Man basket carrying personnel 7 m/s | Ibid. PDF page 47 (citing BS 7121) | "BS 7121 limits this activity to 7 m/s" |
| Thresholds refer to gusts at jib level; ground forecasts must use height/gust factors for conversion: when gusts are provided, 50/100/150 m are 1.181/1.272/1.329; when 10 min averages are provided, they are 1.653/1.78/1.861 (Liebherr table, rural roughness) | Ibid. PDF pages 21–22 | "If the average wind speeds however are being supplied, then the relevant factors increase significantly: 1.653 at 50m AGL…" |
| In high winds, gusts rarely exceed 1.5 times the mean | Ibid. PDF page 22 | "very rarely will the gust be more than 1.5 times its mean average" |
| Cost/loss decision rule + logistic probabilistic forecast used for offshore wind O&M transit decisions (closest methodological precedent), C is fuel and labor for going to sea, L is lost power generation | Browell et al. 2016 ESREL, PDF pages 1–2 | "We propose a simple cost-loss decision rule … Probability of success is predicted using a logistic model" |

## Not Adopted / To Be Verified
- Grok claims EN 13000 mobile cranes "upper limit approx. 14 m/s", China GB 6067.1 "halt operations at Force 6 wind", OSHA 1926.1431 "20 mph" — all are secondary retellings, waiting for reviewer E/F parameter lookup to verify specific clauses.
- "weather window yields 47–57% more operational time" (Gintautas 2017 JMSE) — only read abstract, not adopted.
- "AI models are weak on wind extremes" (Olivetti 2024 GMD) — original text not verified, not adopted.
- DOI 10.1016/j.ress.2021.107xxx could not be found, discarded.
- Report states "no actual values found for C/L in crane/construction stoppage" — consistent with our expectation, but falls under "not found", not evidence; C/L interval temporarily maintained as assumption.
- Report states "no precedents found for AI global models used in lifting/bridge/construction stoppage decisions" — same as above, treated as a clue, to be backfilled after Deep Research quota recovers.

## Implications for Replay Demonstration (No literature basis, based on internal track data + above table conversions, classified as assumptions)
Lifting thresholds are 3 s gusts at the jib. According to the factors on CPA PDF page 22, 10 min average wind at 10 m ≈ jib gust / 1.65–1.86. Therefore, mobile crane 9–11 m/s gust ≈ 10 m average wind 5–7 m/s; tower crane 17 m/s gust ≈ 10 m average wind 9–10 m/s. A1's existing 8/10 m/s sustained wind bins roughly correspond to "tower crane stoppage", and 6–8 m/s bins correspond to "mobile crane stoppage". ASOS 2 min sustained wind differs from 10 min average, and conversion factors remain approximations.

## Reviewer F (Grok) Parameter Lookup Results Verification (10-14 19:0x)
Personally opened original text to verify:
| Conclusion | Source | Original Quote |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OSHA personnel hoisting: when sustained wind or gusts at personnel platform >20 mph, a qualified person must determine whether to halt | 29 CFR 1926.1431(k)(8)(i) (eCFR) | "When wind speed (sustained or gusts) exceeds 20 mph at the personnel platform, a qualified person must determine if … it is not safe to lift personnel." |
| Severn M48 categorized by **expected** gusts: 30 kn speed limit, 35 kn close leeward lane, 40 kn close bridge, 70 kn close both bridges | National Highways Severn Bridges page | "When we expect gusts above 40 knots (46mph), we close the M48 Severn Bridge"; "30 knots – 40mph speed limits … 40 knots – bridge closed 70 knots both bridges closed" |
| Mackinac categorized by **sustained wind** (not gusts): 20–35 mph advisory, 35–50 escorts … | Mackinac Bridge Authority FAQ | "These speeds are not for gusts; they are sustained winds from any direction … 20-35 mph: High wind advisory … 35-50 mph: Escorts required." |
Unverified (provided by F, full text could not be scraped from original sites, awaiting cross-validation by reviewer E): JGJ 196-2010 Clause 4.0.9 tower crane operations halt at 12 m/s; GB 55034-2022 Clause 3.4.7 erection and dismantling halt at >9.0 m/s, work at height halts at Force 5 or above; GB 5144-2006 erection and dismantling 13 m/s; "halt all hoisting at Force 6" cannot be found in GB 6067.1; EN 13000's 20 m/s is 3 s gust at 10 m (= 14.3 m/s 10 min average × 1.4); Forth closed to high-sided vehicles at 50 mph gusts; Tsing Ma / Ting Kau 10 min average 60/75 km/h.
C/L: F also could not find C/L for crane/construction stoppage; the only close one, "additional cost of closing Forth bridge for one day > £600k", is secondary, not adopted. C/L interval maintained as an assumption.
Implications: Bridge traffic restrictions already have public precedents of making decisions based on "expected gusts" (Severn), indicating that "forecast-driven closure" itself is not new; all we can add is the probabilistic form and economic value assessment.

items.title: review question
items.text:
Node F (the Lab testbed) plans to conclude, please review:
Draft conclusions:
1. Current practices: Lifting stoppage thresholds vary widely by machine type / load / height, defined as 3 s gusts at the jib (CPA 2025 guidelines, EN 13001-2, BS 7121); domestic standards specify 9/12 m/s measured or "Force 6 or above" (10 m, 10 min average); bridge traffic restrictions already close bridges based on "expected gusts" (Severn). No measured C/L values found for crane/construction stoppage, nor precedents found for AI global models used in such stoppage decisions ("not found" ≠ does not exist).
2. Replay (OKC 12 stations 2023, A1 sequence, four-source GFS initial condition AI/GFS equal-weighted probability average): Frozen primary criterion (10 m/s, 24 h, C/L 0.05–0.5, multi-source probability V is ≥0.05 higher than the best deterministic scheme and CI does not cross 0) did not pass (difference 0.111, CI [−0.006, 0.179]); however, point estimates for all thresholds are positive, and bins with more events (6/8 m/s, gust 10 m/s) have CIs not crossing 0; multi-source is 0.108 [0.036, 0.226] higher than single GFS probability; under low C/L (0.01–0.10, unverified source), advantages are large and significant.
3. Proposed verdict: F Shelved — "probabilistic early warning has more economic value than deterministic thresholds" is a known property of the cost-loss framework; this replay does not show incremental value unique to AI multi-source that can be translated into operational benefits; lacks real C/L, operational-period verification valid times, jib-height wind, and true ensembles. Restart conditions: obtain partner stoppage/loss data, or Node B true ensembles, or specific operator needs.
Please focus review on: (a) whether literature conclusions are supported by evidence and whether any precedents were missed; (b) whether the replay interpretation is reasonable — particularly whether "primary criterion not passed but collateral evidence consistently positive" should be decided as Shelved or to continue, and whether "multi-source vs single GFS probability +0.108" is sufficient to demonstrate that AI multi-source has incremental value (all four sources share GFS initial conditions, and equal-weight averaging has smoothing effects); (c) whether there are any unmarked speculative parameters.

items.title: F wind-sensitive operations and structural warnings: review verdict and shelving (10-14 20:0x)
items.text:
# F Wind-Sensitive Operations and Structural Early Warning: Review Verdict and Shelved (10-14 20:0x)

, 3/3 valid (E Gemini, A GPT-6, D GLM), all three "support Shelved with reservations". Only one round of review. Lead has personally verified the following key bases (recalculation script see the end of this text).

## Must Change (Changed)
1. **Low C/L sensitivity was written in the wrong direction** (E). Lead recalculation verified: the deterministic pool in the task statement included GFS raw; my sensitivity analysis excluded it, yet wrote "more favorable to deterministic". Under low C/L, GFS raw (uncorrected, high bias) is far better than corrected values: 10 m/s, C/L 0.01–0.10, GFS raw V=0.389, GFS corrected 0.199. After inclusion, multi-source − best deterministic = 0.21 (originally written as 0.40), and 0.44 for 8 m/s (originally 0.79). More critically: in this interval, P_multi 0.599 vs single GFS probability 0.598, **no difference**. Changed.
2. **"+0.108" cannot be interpreted as AI multi-source increment** (E, D; A added "nor can it be asserted as smoothing"). Lead verified: C/L 0.05–0.5, 10 m/s, 24 h, P_multi 0.266, best single-source probability Pangu 0.242, only 0.024 higher; at the 12 m/s tier, P_multi 0.085 is lower than GraphCast single-source 0.160. +0.108 is mainly because single-source GFS probability has a large high-tail bias at C/L>0.2 (E's piecewise analysis, Lead did not recalculate segment by segment). Wording changed to: relative to single GFS probability, there is a conditional positive difference in this hypothetical interval, but relative to the best single source it is only about +0.02, negative for high threshold tiers, and zero under low C/L; the mechanism (calibration differences or averaging smoothing) is unidentified.
3. **Delete the generalization that "probability is superior to deterministic is a known property"** (A). The cost/loss framework only provides a method and does not guarantee that any probabilistic forecast is superior (reliable calibration is required). Changed to the empirical interpretation of this replay: the advantage mainly stems from the "probabilistic form", because pure GFS single-source probability is as good as multi-source under low C/L; it is not brought by AI sources.
4. **Downgrade domestic codes and distinguish operating conditions** (E, A, D). Changed to: secondary search, original texts unverified—installation and dismantling at highest point >9.0 m/s stop (GB 55034-2022 §3.4.7); tower crane operation ≥12 m/s stop (JGJ 196-2010 §4.0.9, reviewer A claimed to have verified on page 20 of the original PDF from Shanghai Municipal Housing and Urban-Rural Development Commission, Lead has not personally verified; this clause does not define averaging duration and height); hoisting stops at "force 6 or above" (JGJ 276-2012 §3.0.14), "10 m, 10 min average" is an extrapolation from wind scale definitions, not the original clause wording. A stated that JGJ 33 §4.1.14 has been announced repealed by GB 55034 (unverified). The 20 m/s in EN 13001-2 is the design wind speed upper limit, not a work-stoppage value (D).
5. **Add construction precedent HS2 Align** (A). Lead opened the original HS2 Learning Legacy text to verify: Align JV, in precast segment hoisting for the Colne Valley Viaduct (November 2021 to May 2023 innovation project), used global NWP + LSTM correction trained on local weather stations for site wind forecasting to support hoisting decisions; GraphCast was only mentioned in the background and was not adopted. Therefore, there is already precedent for "AI used in construction hoisting decisions"; what was not found is merely "direct driving by AI global models" and "measured C/L".
6. **Gust persistence criterion definition** (A). Verified lines 34–37 of run_value.py: renamed the maximum gust within a 1 h window centered on the verification time as the observation at initialization time, which contains data about 30 min after initialization. A correction note has been added at the top of results.md; this only affects the persistence baseline for gust tiers, and the primary evaluation for sustained wind is unaffected.

## For Reference Only (Record)
- "Corroborating evidence consistently positive" is an interval average difference with shared observations and nested thresholds, not independent multiple verifications; the point-by-point C/L guardrail did not pass (minimum −0.0225) (A, D).
- Low C/L sensitivity is another hypothesis, not a reproduction of the primary evaluation; Lead used 300 bootstrap iterations, official used 1000 iterations (A, D).
- Model idealization conditions: loss after stoppage is 0, cost per stoppage is fixed; daily scale "maximum probability of two forecast times" ≠ probability of at least one threshold exceedance on that day (A).
- The definitions of C and L in Browell 2016 are on page 3 §2.2 of the PDF, where p is the "access to sea" probability, opposite in direction to this replay (E).
- D reported the University of Glasgow cost-loss study on S2S forecasts for wind turbine maintenance crane leasing (eprints.gla.ac.uk/320158, hoisting wind speed limit interview 5–8 m/s), which could supplement methodological precedent, unverified.
- E reported commercial probabilistic hoisting wind forecasting platforms (EHAB WeatherWise, Windcrane); unverified.
- "Node B true ensemble" is only a trigger condition for re-evaluation, insufficient to claim operational benefits (A).

## Unaccepted Objections
No substantive disagreement: all three support Shelved. A considered that "smoothing effect explains increment" is likewise insufficiently evidenced—adopted, wording changed to "unidentified mechanism", without taking sides.

## Conclusion and decision
Decision I made: F Shelved.
- Why: The frozen primary evaluation did not pass (10 m/s, 24 h, C/L 0.05–0.5, difference 0.111, CI [−0.006, 0.179]). In the replay, the advantage of probabilistic rules relative to deterministic thresholds mainly stems from the probabilistic form itself; pure GFS probability is as good as the four-source average under low C/L, and no unique, stable increment from AI multi-source was observed. The use of AI-corrected forecasts for construction hoisting already has HS2 precedent. Real C/L, operational window verification, and boom-height wind are all missing.
- Valuable by-products: bridge/hoisting threshold and wind speed definition table (including sources), cost/loss replay scripts, the finding that "deterministic linear correction flattens strong winds and under low C/L is actually worse than raw GFS" (serves as a cautionary reminder for A1's correction design).
- Conditions for resumption: an operator provides work-stoppage cost and loss data or specific requirements; or Node B true ensemble (only as a trigger for re-evaluation); or A1 provides additional verification times during operational periods (such as 18 UTC).
- Cost of being wrong: low. Scripts and data are all present; changing C/L, threshold, or forecast source to re-read takes about 10 minutes, 0 CU.

Basis cards: Relative economic value formulas Zhu et al. 2002 BAMS journal p. 75 (Eqs. 5–7), card ; hoisting thresholds CPA CIG/TCIG 2507 PDF pp. 13/20–23/47 (original archived); remaining replay conclusions have no literature basis and are based on this line's data.

> **Correction (10-14 20:0x, Review Must Change Item 1)**: The original statement in this text that "including Pangu and FCNv2 beyond the task statement is more favorable to deterministic" was incorrect—I excluded GFS raw from the task statement's deterministic pool, whereas under low C/L, GFS raw is far better than corrected values (10 m/s: 0.389 vs 0.199). After including GFS raw, multi-source − best deterministic in C/L 0.01–0.10 is: 6 m/s 1.64, 8 m/s 0.44, 10 m/s 0.21 (2.14/0.79/0.40 in the table below are invalidated). Moreover, in this interval, P_multi and single GFS probability are almost identical (10 m/s 0.599 vs 0.598; 8 m/s 0.645 vs 0.613), meaning that the advantage at low C/L comes from the probabilistic form, not from AI multi-source.

# Lead Sensitivity: Low C/L Interval (10-14 19:2x, Lead Independent Recalculation Using A1 Test Set, Non-Frozen Criterion)

Why do this: reviewer E reported "typical C/L=0.1 for offshore operations (Carrasco 2013, cited via SECLI-FIRM 2021 slides)", and roughly estimated hoisting C/L∈[0.01,0.10] using downtime daily cost / accident loss. Opening that slide link at 10-14 19:2x resulted in 404, **unverified**; E's rough estimate took "loss per accident" as L without multiplying by the "probability of accident when exceeding threshold and not stopping work", so L was overestimated and C/L was underestimated. Therefore, C/L remains a hypothesis, the frozen criterion (C/L 0.05–0.5) is **not changed**, and only sensitivity is reported here.

Method: Same as the V definition in ideas run_value.py (Richardson 2000), 24 h, per station-forecast time; best deterministic = maximum V among the four corrected sources (GFS/GraphCast/Pangu/FCNv2) (including Pangu and FCNv2 beyond the task statement, more favorable to deterministic); 300 cluster bootstrap iterations by verification day.

| Sustained wind 6 m/s | 0.01–0.10 | 0.366 | 2.14 | [1.69, 2.60] |

Interpretation: When C/L is far lower than the event climatological frequency, deterministic "stop work only when forecast ≥ threshold" carries a heavy cost for missed detections, and V is substantially negative (difference can be >1); the advantage of probabilistic rules is a standard property of the cost/loss model, not unique to AI. For the 10 m/s, 0.05–0.5 row, the lower bound of Lead's recalculation interval is 0.009, while the official ideas run (1000 iterations, task statement definition) is −0.006—at the critical boundary; the primary evaluation is recorded as "failed" according to the official ideas result.

> **Lead Correction (10-14 20:0x)**: The statement below that "persistence gust uses the same-station gust available at initialization time" is inaccurate—lines 34–37 of run_value.py used the maximum gust in a 1 h window centered on that time, containing observations about 30 min after initialization, so the persistence baseline for gust tiers takes a slight advantage; the sustained wind primary evaluation is unaffected. For interpretation, see .

One-sentence conclusion: In the OKC 2023 paired replay, the primary evaluation of multi-source probabilistic economic value for sustained wind 10 m/s / 24 h failed; this is only a decision replay for ASOS candidate thresholds, not an empirical proof of hoisting work-stoppage benefits.

# F: Cost-Loss Replay of Exceedance Probability Early Warning

A1 original paired tables with 2022 training / 2023 testing, replay decisions only on workstation CPU without recomputing forecasts. For each threshold/lead time/scale, the identical set of observations and forecasts available to all methods was used; probability thresholds were not tuned for 2023.
P_multi is the equal-weighted average of probabilities from four sources (GraphCast, Pangu, FourCastNet v2, GFS); all four sources are initialized from GFS with correlated shared errors, so surrogate ensembles are not truly independent ensembles. P_stack is a logistic stacking of four probabilities fitted using 2022 data only; tiers with fewer than 30 positives/negatives in 2022 are not fitted, marked in metrics.json. Individual single-source probabilities are listed separately.
Static C/L: C is the cost of stopping work and taking protection, L is the loss when work is not stopped and an event occurs, with loss normalized to 1; E_clim=min(C/L, 2023 event frequency of the same sample), E_perfect=(C/L)×event frequency, V=(E_clim−E_forecast)/(E_clim−E_perfect). The 2023 climatological frequency is used only for score normalization and not for training decisions; V can be negative. For probability, use p≥C/L; for deterministic, use forecast quantity ≥ candidate threshold; for persistence, use initialization observation ≥ threshold. Full curve C/L=0.01..0.99 at intervals of 0.01; [0.05,0.50] is the hypothetical interval of the frozen criterion, not measured construction costs.

Primary evaluation: Multi-source mean V − best deterministic GFS_corrected = 0.1105, 1000 cluster bootstrap iterations by verification day, 95% CI [-0.0063, 0.1789]; requires point estimate ≥0.05 and interval not straddling 0: Failed. Best deterministic refers to taking the maximum of the three means on 2023, with the maximum re-selected in each bootstrap iteration, and cannot be understood as an optimal scheme locked in advance.
Guardrail: Multi-source − GFS single-source probability, interval mean difference 0.1084, 95% CI [0.0364, 0.2263]; mean difference not lower than −0.02: Passed; minimum difference across C/L points -0.0225, point-by-point criterion Failed. Guardrail is reported separately and not used as the primary evaluation.
Gust 13 m/s reported only: 24 h 1771 pairs, 102 events (GOK/OKC/PWA); not entered into the primary evaluation.

## Hypothesis: Daily-Scale Sensitivity

Each station per day requires both 00/12 UTC verification times to be complete; an event is defined as exceeding the threshold at either time. Probabilistic warning takes the maximum probability of the two times of the day; deterministic and persistence judge after taking the maximum wind speed. This daily definition and operational windows are both hypotheses, not prescribed by literature; clustered resampling by each verification UTC day, stations/forecast times are not treated as independent bootstrap units.

## Figures and Limitations

Figures: value_curves_wind_24h_instant.png, value_curves_wind_24h_daily.png, value_curves_wind_48h_instant.png, value_curves_wind_48h_daily.png, value_curves_gust_24h_instant.png, value_curves_gust_24h_daily.png, value_curves_gust_48h_instant.png, value_curves_gust_48h_daily.png. Full 99 points, V of all schemes and point-by-point bootstrap 95% intervals are in metrics.json.
Sustained wind observations are ASOS METAR 2 min; gusts are the maximum gust in a 1 h window centered on the verification time constructed from 3-station IEM 1 min data; persistence gust uses the same-station gust available at initialization time, and pairs are excluded if missing. GFS raw has no corresponding product for gusts; this replay compares raw_speed (sustained wind) with gust thresholds merely as a crude proxy; corrected GFS and GraphCast gusts use A1's pred_gust.
Verification times are only at 00/12 UTC (local morning and evening), without verifying operational window noon, all-day continuous exceedance, or whether stopping work in advance is operable. ASOS measurement heights have not been verified station by station; station surface wind does not equal crane boom tip wind, and thresholds are candidate tiers rather than verified specific crane operation thresholds. The cost/loss interval and taking the maximum of two daily times are both assumptions; actual work-stoppage and loss surveys are required before converting into monetary benefits.
A1 2022 was trained only around 00/12 UTC for the first 15 days of each month, with probabilities regressed per station/lead time; extreme threshold training and 2023 events are scarce. No spatial extrapolation / operational update verification; homologous GFS initial values and post-processing are correlated, and cannot be regarded as four independent members.

Source: A1 run_verify_revised.py and paired_station_{train,test}.csv.gz in the same directory; NOAA NCEI ASOS via IEM, NOAA/CIRA GraphCast/Pangu/FourCastNet v2 via AWS AIWP, NOAA GFS AWS. Method: Richardson (2000), QJRMS 126(563), 649–667, https://doi.org/10.1002/qj.49712656313; REV formula verified against https://scores.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorials/Relative_Economic_Value_Score.html.

Same-source 2022 training / 2023 testing paired series and method as the original replay, with 1000 cluster bootstrap iterations by verification day; for independent incremental results see , generation script ; original , script, and figures remain unchanged. Full 99 C/L points' individual single-source probability, deterministic, and persistence V curves and point-by-point intervals are in incremental JSON; figure is ); ASOS 2 min wind does not equal the 10 min mean wind in the guidelines, nor is it the 3 s gust at the crane boom, and stoppage benefits cannot be claimed on this basis. The C/L interval and the definition of station-days where either of the two verification times exceeds the threshold remain hypotheses. The 10 m/s, 24 h frozen primary evaluation still failed.

4. **Downgrade domestic codes and distinguish operating conditions** (E, A, D). Changed to: secondary search, original texts unverified—installation and dismantling at highest point >9.0 m/s stop (GB 55034-2022 §3.4.7); tower crane operation ≥12 m/s stop (JGJ 196-2010 §4.0.9, reviewer A claimed to have verified on page 20 of the original PDF from Shanghai Municipal Housing and Urban-Rural Development Commission, Lead has not personally verified; this clause does not define averaging duration and height); hoisting stops at "force 6 or above" (JGJ 276-2012 §3.0.14), "10 m, 10 min average" is an extrapolation from wind scale definitions, not the original clause wording. A stated that JGJ 33 §4.1.14 has been announced repealed by GB 55034 (unverified). The 20 m/s in EN 13001-2 is the design wind speed upper limit, not a work-stoppage value (D).
5. **Add construction precedent HS2 Align** (A). Lead opened the original HS2 Learning Legacy text to verify: Align JV, in precast segment hoisting for the Colne Valley Viaduct (November 2021 to May 2023 innovation project), used global NWP + LSTM correction trained on local weather stations for site wind forecasting to support hoisting decisions; GraphCast was only mentioned in the background and was not adopted. Therefore, there is already precedent for "AI used in construction hoisting decisions"; what was not found is merely "direct driving by AI global models" and "measured C/L".
6. **Gust persistence criterion definition** (A). Verified lines 34–37 of run_value.py: renamed the maximum gust within a 1 h window centered on the verification time as the observation at initialization time, which contains data about 30 min after initialization. A correction note has been added at the top of results.md; this only affects the persistence baseline for gust tiers, and the primary evaluation for sustained wind is unaffected.

## For Reference Only (Record)
- "Corroborating evidence consistently positive" is an interval average difference with shared observations and nested thresholds, not independent multiple verifications; the point-by-point C/L guardrail did not pass (minimum −0.0225) (A, D).
- Low C/L sensitivity is another hypothesis, not a reproduction of the primary evaluation; Lead used 300 bootstrap iterations, official used 1000 iterations (A, D).
- Model idealization conditions: loss after stoppage is 0, cost per stoppage is fixed; daily scale "maximum probability of two forecast times" ≠ probability of at least one threshold exceedance on that day (A).
- The definitions of C and L in Browell 2016 are on page 3 §2.2 of the PDF, where p is the "access to sea" probability, opposite in direction to this replay (E).
- D reported the University of Glasgow cost-loss study on S2S forecasts for wind turbine maintenance crane leasing (eprints.gla.ac.uk/320158, hoisting wind speed limit interview 5–8 m/s), which could supplement methodological precedent, unverified.
- E reported commercial probabilistic hoisting wind forecasting platforms (EHAB WeatherWise, Windcrane); unverified.
- "Node B true ensemble" is only a trigger condition for re-evaluation, insufficient to claim operational benefits (A).

## Unaccepted Objections
No substantive disagreement: all three support Shelved. A considered that "smoothing effect explains increment" is likewise insufficiently evidenced—adopted, wording changed to "unidentified mechanism", without taking sides.

## Conclusion and decision
Decision I made: F Shelved.
- Why: The frozen primary evaluation did not pass (10 m/s, 24 h, C/L 0.05–0.5, difference 0.111, CI [−0.006, 0.179]). In the replay, the advantage of probabilistic rules relative to deterministic thresholds mainly stems from the probabilistic form itself; pure GFS probability is as good as the four-source average under low C/L, and no unique, stable increment from AI multi-source was observed. The use of AI-corrected forecasts for construction hoisting already has HS2 precedent. Real C/L, operational window verification, and boom-height wind are all missing.
- Valuable by-products: bridge/hoisting threshold and wind speed definition table (including sources), cost/loss replay scripts, the finding that "deterministic linear correction flattens strong winds and under low C/L is actually worse than raw GFS" (serves as a cautionary reminder for A1's correction design).
- Conditions for resumption: an operator provides work-stoppage cost and loss data or specific requirements; or Node B true ensemble (only as a trigger for re-evaluation); or A1 provides additional verification times during operational periods (such as 18 UTC).
- Cost of being wrong: low. Scripts and data are all present; changing C/L, threshold, or forecast source to re-read takes about 10 minutes, 0 CU.

Basis cards: Relative economic value formulas Zhu et al. 2002 BAMS journal p. 75 (Eqs. 5–7), card ; hoisting thresholds CPA CIG/TCIG 2507 PDF pp. 13/20–23/47 (original archived); remaining replay conclusions have no literature basis and are based on this line's data.

# Node F: Grok Quick Search Report Verification (10-14 18:25)

Report: . Original PDF stored at . Page numbers are all PDF physical pages (CPA document footer "Page N of 57" = PDF page − 1).

## Personally Verified in Original Text and Adopted
| Conclusion | Source | Original Quote |

| UK tower cranes actually winded-off at 16.5–17 m/s | Ibid. PDF page 13 (citing BS 7121-5:2019 §14.1), page 20 | "usually winded-off at 16.5m/s (38mph)"; "typically taken out of service at 17 m/s (38 mph)" |
| Wind-off speed varies by model: tower cranes 12–17 m/s, traditional mobile cranes average 9–11 m/s, crawler cranes 12–16 m/s | Ibid. PDF page 23 | "a traditional mobile crane winds-off on average at around 9-11 m/s" |
| Man basket carrying personnel 7 m/s | Ibid. PDF page 47 (citing BS 7121) | "BS 7121 limits this activity to 7 m/s" |
| Thresholds refer to gusts at jib level; ground forecasts must use height/gust factors for conversion: when gusts are provided, 50/100/150 m are 1.181/1.272/1.329; when 10 min averages are provided, they are 1.653/1.78/1.861 (Liebherr table, rural roughness) | Ibid. PDF pages 21–22 | "If the average wind speeds however are being supplied, then the relevant factors increase significantly: 1.653 at 50m AGL…" |
| In high winds, gusts rarely exceed 1.5 times the mean | Ibid. PDF page 22 | "very rarely will the gust be more than 1.5 times its mean average" |
| Cost/loss decision rule + logistic probabilistic forecast used for offshore wind O&M transit decisions (closest methodological precedent), C is fuel and labor for going to sea, L is lost power generation | Browell et al. 2016 ESREL, PDF pages 1–2 | "We propose a simple cost-loss decision rule … Probability of success is predicted using a logistic model" |

## Not Adopted / To Be Verified
- Grok claims EN 13000 mobile cranes "upper limit approx. 14 m/s", China GB 6067.1 "halt operations at Force 6 wind", OSHA 1926.1431 "20 mph" — all are secondary retellings, waiting for reviewer E/F parameter lookup to verify specific clauses.
- "weather window yields 47–57% more operational time" (Gintautas 2017 JMSE) — only read abstract, not adopted.
- "AI models are weak on wind extremes" (Olivetti 2024 GMD) — original text not verified, not adopted.
- DOI 10.1016/j.ress.2021.107xxx could not be found, discarded.
- Report states "no actual values found for C/L in crane/construction stoppage" — consistent with our expectation, but falls under "not found", not evidence; C/L interval temporarily maintained as assumption.
- Report states "no precedents found for AI global models used in lifting/bridge/construction stoppage decisions" — same as above, treated as a clue, to be backfilled after Deep Research quota recovers.

## Implications for Replay Demonstration (No literature basis, based on internal track data + above table conversions, classified as assumptions)
Lifting thresholds are 3 s gusts at the jib. According to the factors on CPA PDF page 22, 10 min average wind at 10 m ≈ jib gust / 1.65–1.86. Therefore, mobile crane 9–11 m/s gust ≈ 10 m average wind 5–7 m/s; tower crane 17 m/s gust ≈ 10 m average wind 9–10 m/s. A1's existing 8/10 m/s sustained wind bins roughly correspond to "tower crane stoppage", and 6–8 m/s bins correspond to "mobile crane stoppage". ASOS 2 min sustained wind differs from 10 min average, and conversion factors remain approximations.

## Reviewer F (Grok) Parameter Lookup Results Verification (10-14 19:0x)
Personally opened original text to verify:
| Conclusion | Source | Original Quote |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OSHA personnel hoisting: when sustained wind or gusts at personnel platform >20 mph, a qualified person must determine whether to halt | 29 CFR 1926.1431(k)(8)(i) (eCFR) | "When wind speed (sustained or gusts) exceeds 20 mph at the personnel platform, a qualified person must determine if … it is not safe to lift personnel." |
| Severn M48 categorized by **expected** gusts: 30 kn speed limit, 35 kn close leeward lane, 40 kn close bridge, 70 kn close both bridges | National Highways Severn Bridges page | "When we expect gusts above 40 knots (46mph), we close the M48 Severn Bridge"; "30 knots – 40mph speed limits … 40 knots – bridge closed 70 knots both bridges closed" |
| Mackinac categorized by **sustained wind** (not gusts): 20–35 mph advisory, 35–50 escorts … | Mackinac Bridge Authority FAQ | "These speeds are not for gusts; they are sustained winds from any direction … 20-35 mph: High wind advisory … 35-50 mph: Escorts required." |
Unverified (provided by F, full text could not be scraped from original sites, awaiting cross-validation by reviewer E): JGJ 196-2010 Clause 4.0.9 tower crane operations halt at 12 m/s; GB 55034-2022 Clause 3.4.7 erection and dismantling halt at >9.0 m/s, work at height halts at Force 5 or above; GB 5144-2006 erection and dismantling 13 m/s; "halt all hoisting at Force 6" cannot be found in GB 6067.1; EN 13000's 20 m/s is 3 s gust at 10 m (= 14.3 m/s 10 min average × 1.4); Forth closed to high-sided vehicles at 50 mph gusts; Tsing Ma / Ting Kau 10 min average 60/75 km/h.
C/L: F also could not find C/L for crane/construction stoppage; the only close one, "additional cost of closing Forth bridge for one day > £600k", is secondary, not adopted. C/L interval maintained as an assumption.
Implications: Bridge traffic restrictions already have public precedents of making decisions based on "expected gusts" (Severn), indicating that "forecast-driven closure" itself is not new; all we can add is the probabilistic form and economic value assessment.

results.label: Result
results.title: review question
results.text:
Node F (the Lab testbed) plans to conclude, please review:
Draft conclusions:
1. Current practices: Lifting stoppage thresholds vary widely by machine type / load / height, defined as 3 s gusts at the jib (CPA 2025 guidelines, EN 13001-2, BS 7121); domestic standards specify 9/12 m/s measured or "Force 6 or above" (10 m, 10 min average); bridge traffic restrictions already close bridges based on "expected gusts" (Severn). No measured C/L values found for crane/construction stoppage, nor precedents found for AI global models used in such stoppage decisions ("not found" ≠ does not exist).
2. Replay (OKC 12 stations 2023, A1 sequence, four-source GFS initial condition AI/GFS equal-weighted probability average): Frozen primary criterion (10 m/s, 24 h, C/L 0.05–0.5, multi-source probability V is ≥0.05 higher than the best deterministic scheme and CI does not cross 0) did not pass (difference 0.111, CI [−0.006, 0.179]); however, point estimates for all thresholds are positive, and bins with more events (6/8 m/s, gust 10 m/s) have CIs not crossing 0; multi-source is 0.108 [0.036, 0.226] higher than single GFS probability; under low C/L (0.01–0.10, unverified source), advantages are large and significant.
3. Proposed verdict: F Shelved — "probabilistic early warning has more economic value than deterministic thresholds" is a known property of the cost-loss framework; this replay does not show incremental value unique to AI multi-source that can be translated into operational benefits; lacks real C/L, operational-period verification valid times, jib-height wind, and true ensembles. Restart conditions: obtain partner stoppage/loss data, or Node B true ensembles, or specific operator needs.
Please focus review on: (a) whether literature conclusions are supported by evidence and whether any precedents were missed; (b) whether the replay interpretation is reasonable — particularly whether "primary criterion not passed but collateral evidence consistently positive" should be decided as Shelved or to continue, and whether "multi-source vs single GFS probability +0.108" is sufficient to demonstrate that AI multi-source has incremental value (all four sources share GFS initial conditions, and equal-weight averaging has smoothing effects); (c) whether there are any unmarked speculative parameters.

# Lead Sensitivity: Low C/L Interval (10-14 19:2x, Lead Independent Recalculation Using A1 Test Set, Non-Frozen Criterion)

Why do this: reviewer E reported "typical C/L=0.1 for offshore operations (Carrasco 2013, cited via SECLI-FIRM 2021 slides)", and roughly estimated hoisting C/L∈[0.01,0.10] using downtime daily cost / accident loss. Opening that slide link at 10-14 19:2x resulted in 404, **unverified**; E's rough estimate took "loss per accident" as L without multiplying by the "probability of accident when exceeding threshold and not stopping work", so L was overestimated and C/L was underestimated. Therefore, C/L remains a hypothesis, the frozen criterion (C/L 0.05–0.5) is **not changed**, and only sensitivity is reported here.

Method: Same as the V definition in ideas run_value.py (Richardson 2000), 24 h, per station-forecast time; best deterministic = maximum V among the four corrected sources (GFS/GraphCast/Pangu/FCNv2) (including Pangu and FCNv2 beyond the task statement, more favorable to deterministic); 300 cluster bootstrap iterations by verification day.

For interpretation, see .

One-sentence conclusion: In the OKC 2023 paired replay, the primary evaluation of multi-source probabilistic economic value for sustained wind 10 m/s / 24 h failed; this is only a decision replay for ASOS candidate thresholds, not an empirical proof of hoisting work-stoppage benefits.

# F: Cost-Loss Replay of Exceedance Probability Early Warning

A1 original paired tables with 2022 training / 2023 testing, replay decisions only on workstation CPU without recomputing forecasts. For each threshold/lead time/scale, the identical set of observations and forecasts available to all methods was used; probability thresholds were not tuned for 2023.
P_multi is the equal-weighted average of probabilities from four sources (GraphCast, Pangu, FourCastNet v2, GFS); all four sources are initialized from GFS with correlated shared errors, so surrogate ensembles are not truly independent ensembles. P_stack is a logistic stacking of four probabilities fitted using 2022 data only; tiers with fewer than 30 positives/negatives in 2022 are not fitted, marked in metrics.json. Individual single-source probabilities are listed separately.
Static C/L: C is the cost of stopping work and taking protection, L is the loss when work is not stopped and an event occurs, with loss normalized to 1; E_clim=min(C/L, 2023 event frequency of the same sample), E_perfect=(C/L)×event frequency, V=(E_clim−E_forecast)/(E_clim−E_perfect). The 2023 climatological frequency is used only for score normalization and not for training decisions; V can be negative. For probability, use p≥C/L; for deterministic, use forecast quantity ≥ candidate threshold; for persistence, use initialization observation ≥ threshold. Full curve C/L=0.01..0.99 at intervals of 0.01; [0.05,0.50] is the hypothetical interval of the frozen criterion, not measured construction costs.

## Figures and Limitations

Figures: value_curves_wind_24h_instant.png, value_curves_wind_24h_daily.png, value_curves_wind_48h_instant.png, value_curves_wind_48h_daily.png, value_curves_gust_24h_instant.png, value_curves_gust_24h_daily.png, value_curves_gust_48h_instant.png, value_curves_gust_48h_daily.png. Full 99 points, V of all schemes and point-by-point bootstrap 95% intervals are in metrics.json.
Sustained wind observations are ASOS METAR 2 min; gusts are the maximum gust in a 1 h window centered on the verification time constructed from 3-station IEM 1 min data; persistence gust uses the same-station gust available at initialization time, and pairs are excluded if missing. GFS raw has no corresponding product for gusts; this replay compares raw_speed (sustained wind) with gust thresholds merely as a crude proxy; corrected GFS and GraphCast gusts use A1's pred_gust.
Verification times are only at 00/12 UTC (local morning and evening), without verifying operational window noon, all-day continuous exceedance, or whether stopping work in advance is operable. ASOS measurement heights have not been verified station by station; station surface wind does not equal crane boom tip wind, and thresholds are candidate tiers rather than verified specific crane operation thresholds. The cost/loss interval and taking the maximum of two daily times are both assumptions; actual work-stoppage and loss surveys are required before converting into monetary benefits.
A1 2022 was trained only around 00/12 UTC for the first 15 days of each month, with probabilities regressed per station/lead time; extreme threshold training and 2023 events are scarce. No spatial extrapolation / operational update verification; homologous GFS initial values and post-processing are correlated, and cannot be regarded as four independent members.

projects.digest:
# Wind-Sensitive Operations and Structural Warning (Shelved)

This sub-project (Node F) evaluated whether exceedance probabilities from multi-model AI and numerical weather forecasts provide actionable economic value over deterministic thresholds for wind-sensitive operations such as crane lifting and bridge closures. Combining a standards audit with a 2023 Oklahoma City (12 ASOS stations) cost-loss hindcast using calibrated probabilities from GraphCast, Pangu-Weather, FourCastNet v2, and GFS, the team found that the frozen primary criterion (10 m/s sustained wind at 24 h lead over cost-loss ratios 0.05–0.50) missed statistical significance because its 95% confidence interval crossed zero. Furthermore, a three-reviewer audit confirmed that the economic value gain stemmed from applying probabilistic decision rules rather than multi-model AI skill, leading the AI Weather Models Lead to shelve the sub-project.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-14**: Sub-project launched under Node A to evaluate probabilistic warnings for wind-sensitive operations reusing the 2023 Oklahoma City 12-station paired forecast dataset (2022 training / 2023 testing, GFS-initialized GraphCast, Pangu, FourCastNet v2, and GFS at 24 and 48 h leads).
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead selected crane lifting as the primary operation, dispatched two reviewers to audit international crane and bridge shutdown clauses, and tasked the literature agent to verify cost-loss relative economic value formulas (Murphy 1977, Richardson 2000, Zhu et al. 2002).
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead froze the primary criterion: at 10 m/s sustained wind and 24 h lead across cost-loss ratios C/L = 0.05text–0.50, the four-source mean probability must exceed the best deterministic forecast in mean relative economic value V by ge 0.05 with a daily-block bootstrap 95% CI not crossing zero.
- **2026-10-14**: The research assistant completed the 2023 Oklahoma City hindcast (7,917 station-epochs, 135 exceedances ge 10 m/s at 24 h): the four-source mean probability achieved mean V = 0.266 versus 0.156 for the best deterministic forecast (calibrated GFS, diff +0.111 ge 0.05), but the 95% bootstrap CI was [-0.006, 0.179], crossing zero and failing the primary gate.
- **2026-10-14**: Across all 12 threshold (8, 10, 12 m/s) × lead (24, 48 h) × metric (sustained, gust) combinations, point differences of multi-source probability minus best deterministic were positive (+0.085 to +0.223), with non-zero-crossing 95% CIs at 8 m/s sustained wind and 10 m/s gust, while persistence had negative value everywhere.
- **2026-10-14**: An addendum at 6 m/s sustained wind (approximating 10 m mean wind equivalent of mobile crane 3 s boom-tip gust limits, 1,500/7,917 exceedances) yielded mean V = 0.492 versus 0.320 for best deterministic at 24 h (+0.171, 95% CI [0.119, 0.214]; +0.175 at 48 h), leaving the frozen 10 m/s failure unchanged.
- **2026-10-14**: Two reviewers verified crane wind limits: EN 13001-2 / EN 13000 / EN 14439 define in-service limits (9.8, 14.0, and 20.0 m/s) as 3 s boom-tip gusts (7.0, 10.0, and 14.3 m/s 10 min mean at 10 m height); UK CPA advises taking tower cranes out of service at 16.5 m/s and mobile cranes le 14 m/s (7 m/s for man-riding baskets per BS 7121-1); US OSHA 29 CFR 1926.1417 defers to load charts and sets 20 mph (8.94 m/s, 1926.1431) only for personnel platforms; and Chinese standards (secondary transcripts) specify >9.0 m/s for erection/dismantling (GB 55034-2022) and ge 12.0 m/s for tower crane operation (JGJ 196-2010).
- **2026-10-14**: The audit also documented bridge closure rules—expected gusts on the UK M48 Severn Bridge (30/35/40/70 kt, full closure at 40 kt), sustained winds on the US Mackinac Bridge (20/35/50/65 mph), 50 mph gusts on the Forth Bridges, and 60/75 km/h 10 min mean winds in Hong Kong—with no published empirical cost-loss ratios found for construction shutdowns.
- **2026-10-14**: Three reviewers supported shelving with reservations, noting that (1) UK HS2 Align (2021–2023) already used global NWP plus local LSTM post-processing for viaduct crane lifting; (2) omitting raw GFS in the low-C/L (0.01text–0.10) test inflated the probabilistic gain from +0.210 to +0.40; and (3) at C/L = 0.01text–0.10, single-source GFS probability (V = 0.598) matched four-source mean probability (V = 0.599) and had the highest 24 h ge 10 m/s ROC AUC (0.953 vs. Pangu 0.950, FCNv2 0.942, GraphCast 0.930), whereas the +0.108 gap over GFS in C/L = 0.05text–0.50 came from small-sample logistic tail bias at C/L > 0.2 and averaging (+0.024 over Pangu alone).
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead incorporated all reviewer corrections and placed the sub-project in Shelved status.

## Where it stands

This sub-project is Shelved. The frozen 10 m/s primary criterion failed statistical significance, industry projects such as HS2 and the Severn Bridge already operate forecast-driven shutdown protocols, and the hindcast economic value gain comes from replacing fixed wind-speed cutoffs with probabilistic decision rules rather than multi-model AI skill. Restarting would require real contractor cost-loss schedules or end-user demand, daytime operational verification hours beyond 00/12 UTC, and true ensemble forecasts.

# B Typhoon/hurricane wind fields (primary direction, tier-1 node)

## Objective
Liang Hu's primary research direction. Liang Hu has spent many years developing 3D boundary-layer typhoon wind field models: parametric models for wind-resistant design wind speeds and fast computation, and WRF-class downscaling for single-typhoon forecasting/hindcasting, extending to ensemble forecasting and resilience/performance assessment. This node evaluates where along this pipeline connecting AI weather/climate foundation models is worth investing in, advancing via sub-nodes organized by sub-direction.

## Sub-directions (Set by Liang Hu on 10-14)
| # | Direction | Status | Node |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1+B4 | AI track/intensity (including ensembles) → parametric boundary-layer wind field (using literature models until Liang Hu's model is ready) → station peak winds vs. ASOS, benchmarked against NHC; plus AI ensembles to examine spread | Shelved (10-14); v2 preparation paused: after enforcing strict station type and anemometer height filters (8–12 m), only 13 events × ≥3 stations remain; recount after Liang Hu's model arrives or the 2026 season is ingested | |
| B2 | Design wind speeds and long-term risk: synthetic typhoons (including AI-generated synthetic typhoons) + 3D boundary-layer models | Shelved (10-14 22:30); attribution finalized on 10-15: severely underestimated nearshore Cat3+ passage rate is the root cause, which switching wind field models cannot rescue | |
| B3 | Single-typhoon WRF forecast/hindcast driven by AI large-scale fields (typhoons only; see K for thunderstorms) | Not started (~early-to-mid November) | 10-14 reply: can commit, queued after the first Wister pair and Node K; K will first establish the "AI fields → WPS intermediate format → WRF" pipeline for B3 to reuse; division of labor: the Lab provides AI/GFS fields, WRF bot runs WPS/real/WRF; recommends 9/3 km two-way nesting; a single run costs tens to over a hundred SU → run on CRC (exceeds the Lab's ≤50 SU per-job cap on TACC); select events from the B1+B4 event list. **Pre-launch gate (set by Root Lead on 10-15)**: (1) first ask whether reusable typhoon/hurricane WRF cases or configurations exist; (2) estimate SU (single-node CRC runs are also accounted in SU; multi-node runs go to TACC); if a single job exceeds 50 SU or reaches production scale (>24 h or ≥200 SU), it requires a promotion proposal or handoff to the WRF line, to be confirmed with Liang Hu by Root Lead. Given the estimate of tens to over a hundred SU per run, it will **very likely exceed 50 SU → expected to go through a promotion proposal / handoff to the WRF line**. All supercomputer jobs require a resource request + registration, pre-check and submission separated into two commands, and `ssh -n`. **Must be included at kickoff handoff**: the HRD dropsonde 10–300 m typhoon profile dataset (backed up on CRC) can serve as a WRF boundary-layer profile verification set (over-ocean / inner-core, not overland) |
| B5 | Resilience and performance (Liang Hu: do not lower priority; feasible and publishable, though of slightly lower intrinsic scientific value—unverifiable and low reliability) | Not started | Start after B1/B4 wind field ensembles and Node I (loss database) yield results |

## Current Status
10-14 evening: B1+B4 v1 failed the 48 h gate and was shelved (6/6 support)—cannot conclude whether AI tracks are better or worse: both pipelines underestimated 48 h winds by 35–38%, primarily due to pre-registered size/pressure input assumptions (Δp0 scaling, frozen RMW), while track effects had inconsistent signs. Verified by Node B Lead. Because the core question remained unanswered, B1+B4 was dispatched to run a v2 feasibility check (R1 operationally available size inputs, R2 ≥15 events; output files only without gate evaluation) before deciding whether to launch v2. B2 Grok quick search returned (used as leads only, unverified): existing design wind speed studies all rely on hybrid methods, as free-running AI weather/climate models produce overly weak typhoons; accordingly, Node B2 was launched: pass RAFT (40,000 synthetic typhoons with ML intensity, CC BY 4.0, Zenodo verified by Node B Lead) and STORM through the same H08 wind field model to compare 50-/700-year return period wind speeds at coastal stations against ASCE 7-22. B3 is scheduled for ~early-to-mid November. No rush on Liang Hu's model; use literature models first.

## Finalized Decisions
- 2026-10-14 Accepted shelving of B2 (failed Gate 1 with RAFT at 30.95%); dispatched a pre-restart diagnostic comparing inputs against observations only, without generating new ASCE comparisons → 
- 2026-10-14 Accepted shelving of B1+B4 v1; dispatched v2 feasibility check; dispatched Grok quick search for B2 first → 
- 2026-10-14 Combined B1 and B4 into a single sub-node (sharing the same events, wind field model, observations, and scripts; split B4 out later if ensemble size grows) → 

## Trials and Results

# B Typhoon/Hurricane Node Establishment: B1 and B4 Jointly Open a Sub-node (2026-10-14)

Decision I made: B1 (AI track/intensity → parametric boundary layer wind field → station peak wind) and B4 (AI ensemble → wind speed dispersion) jointly open a sub-node "B1+B4 Landfalling Hurricanes: AI Track and Ensemble to Station Peak Wind", executing bot ideas; B2, B3, and B5 are recorded on the Node B page, to be split when work begins.

Why: In step 1 both use the same batch of landfalling hurricanes, the same wind field model, and the same set of ASOS observations and pairing scripts; B4 merely adds ensemble members onto B1's deterministic chain; splitting into two nodes would duplicate data fetching and pairing, and violate "one sub-topic, one node". If B4 needs to run GenCast-type ensembles itself and scales up, Node B will open a peer Level-2 node (starting 10-14, no Level-3 nodes are opened under Level-2).

Cost of being wrong: If B4 is held up by B1's progress, it will be delayed by a few days; at that point, splitting into an independent node is sufficient, and sharing the event list and scripts incurs no loss.

Others:
- Step 1 sets up three chains for comparison (best track / NHC official / AI track + NHC intensity), using the best track chain to separate "wind field model error" from "AI track error"; criteria are written in the task statement, enter the sub-node page before running, and must not be relaxed post hoc. Basis: DeMaria 2025 AIES (AI track comparable to operational, intensity biased weak)—no wiki card, pending litwiki card creation to verify page numbers; remainder has no literature basis, based on experimental design.
- Do not wait for the Liang Hu model (Desktop D drive PBWE), use literature models first (index).
- B3 has already asked: whether there are off-the-shelf hurricane WRF cases, whether they can be invested, and whether AI-driven WRF is already being done.
- Prior check: No lines in PETW have hurricane wind field implementations or hurricane ASOS data to borrow; no duplication.

projects.digest:
# B Typhoon and Hurricane Wind Fields (Exploring)

This parent node evaluates AI-driven tropical cyclone tracks, synthetic catalogs, and mesoscale simulations for coastal hurricane wind hazard and design speeds across sub-projects B1+B4 (landfalling hurricane AI tracks to station peak winds), B2 (AI synthetic typhoons to coastal design wind speeds), B3 (AI fields driving WRF typhoon simulations), and B5 (resilience). Sub-project B1+B4 was Shelved after missing its event-level non-inferiority gate (5/9 vs. ge 6/9) and the 15-storm sample gate (13 storms with ge 3 height-verified ASOS stations). Sub-project B2 tested the 40,000-year RAFT AI catalog against STORM and ASCE 7-22 coastal design wind speeds (V700) across 19 US stations and was Shelved (6/6 reviewers supporting) after STORM passed Gate 0 (-8.87\% bias) while RAFT underestimated V700 by 30.95% due to a deficit of nearshore Category 3+ passages. Sub-project B3 is scheduled for mid-November with pre-launch compute and promotion gates recorded.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead audited the B2 pre-registration (`v1` freezing 19 coastal stations; `v2` upgrading the baseline from STORM v2 to deduplicated STORM v4 before viewing results) and verified that CLIMADA `H08` computes winds from central pressure, environmental pressure (1010 hPa), radius of maximum wind (RMW), and translation speed—not maximum wind speed (Vmax)—using a 1.07 conversion from 1-minute marine wind to 3-second open-terrain gust.
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead directed B2 (`v3` pre-registration) to replace the assumed RAFT annual storm rate of 14.5 storms/yr (copied from STORM) with the observed 1979–2018 HURDAT2 North Atlantic rate of 12.075 storms/yr as the primary setting so frequency biases would not be masked.
- **2026-10-14**: The research assistant retrieved ASCE 7-22 V700 values for all 19/19 stations, caught a pre-evaluation unit bug in B2 where RMW was passed to CLIMADA in meters instead of nautical miles (voiding and recomputing the first 6 batches), and verified that B1+B4 best-track inputs were natively in nautical miles.
- **2026-10-14**: For B1+B4 `v2` restart feasibility, initial screening found only 7 candidate hurricanes with 1-minute ASOS data and 14 potential storms with hourly data (which cannot be pooled); AI Weather Models Lead kept B1+B4 Shelved and dispatched a zero-compute check on hourly station counts and GFS environmental fields.
- **2026-10-14**: B2 completed Round 1 (~8.7 Colab CU) and Shelved with 6/6 reviewers supporting: STORM passed Gate 0 (-8.87\% median V700 bias vs. ASCE 7-22 across 19 stations), but RAFT failed Gate 1 with a 30.95% median absolute deviation at the 12.075/yr HURDAT2 rate (30.40% at 14.5/yr, V50 ~29% low), and four reviewers confirmed no CLIMADA code bug.
- **2026-10-14**: Because CLIMADA `H08` does not read Vmax directly, AI Weather Models Lead noted that B2 tested RAFT's empirical pressure–wind and RMW closures rather than its neural intensity model alone, and dispatched a zero-compute input attribution diagnostic against HURDAT2/EBTRK observations.
- **2026-10-14**: B1+B4 `v2H08`'s Holland B formula could not be fit to wind radii; B1+B4 remained Shelved.
- **2026-10-15**: The B2 input attribution diagnostic finished (0 SU): swapping RAFT's pressure–wind formula changed station peak winds by 0% median (+1.8\% for Category 4–5) and swapping RMW changed them by +4\%, ruling out both closures; instead, Category 3+ passages within 100 km of stations per 1,000 storms were severely deficient in RAFT versus STORM and HURDAT2—Texas 0.09 vs. 1.04 vs. 3.45, Louisiana–Florida Panhandle 0.17 vs. 1.45 vs. 4.14, Carolina 0.42 vs. 2.66 vs. 3.45, and Florida Peninsula 1.97 vs. 2.55 vs. 2.07.
- **2026-10-15**: AI Weather Models Lead concluded B2 and kept it Shelved without launching a Vmax-driven Holland (2010) rerun because RAFT's near-coast extreme intensity tail itself is deficient; the nearshore Category 3+ passage-rate table was retained as a zero-compute screening gate for future AI catalogs.
- **2026-10-15**: Under Liang Hu's workstation policy, ~790 MB of raw RAFT/STORM files were deleted locally and ~500 MB of intermediate B2 files were archived to supercomputer storage (leaving 88 MB in B2 and 44 MB in B1+B4), and pre-launch gates for B3 (mid-November, requiring promotion or WRF-line handoff if >50 SU per job) were recorded.

## Where it stands

This parent node remains Exploring with no active compute tasks. Both B1+B4 and B2 are Shelved: B1+B4 requires a wind solver assimilating operational Vmax and wind radii plus post-2025 storms to reach ge 15 multi-station events, while B2 requires a new AI catalog passing the nearshore Category 3+ passage-rate screen. Sub-project B3 awaits completion of the thunderstorm WRF pipeline in mid-November and will likely require formal promotion or handoff to the WRF line due to per-run costs exceeding 50 SU.
