# B1+B4 landfalling hurricanes: AI tracks and ensembles to station peak winds

## Objective
When AI global model tracks (+ NHC official intensity) drive an open parametric hurricane boundary-layer wind field model, can station peak winds reach the level of NHC official forecasts driving the same model; and after adding AI ensembles, can the spread cover ASOS observations? Determine whether it is worth continuing (replacing the wind field model once Liang Hu's 3D boundary-layer model is ready and expanding the number of events). Task brief.

## Criteria (Written before launching runs on 10-14; must not be relaxed ex post)
- Primary metric: median absolute error and median bias of the forecast-to-observed ratio of peak gust (or 1 min sustained wind) per station per event; all stations within ±150 km of the landfall point.
- Three chains: (a) best track (HURDAT2 / Extended Best Track including RMW); (b) NHC official forecast track + intensity; (c) AI track (AIWP) + NHC official intensity. Same wind field model, lead times of 24/48/72 h (referenced to landfall time). Chains (b) and (c) use only operationally available information; since OFCL does not report Pc/POCI/RMW, post-event b-decks must not be used (added during 10-14 review as input compliance without altering the criteria); supplementary chain (c′) WeatherNext Cyclones is reported only and not included in the criteria.
- **B1 worth continuing**: Median absolute error of (c) at 48 h ≤ 1.1 × (b), and (c) is no worse than (b) on ≥ 2/3 of events; **simultaneously**, the median bias of (a) is within ±20% (otherwise the problem lies in the wind field model rather than AI, and the conclusion should state "wind field model unqualified" without evaluating AI).
- **B4 worth continuing**: Coverage of station observations by the ensemble 10–90% interval is within 60–95%. B4 is executed only after B1 passes the gate.
- If not met, clearly state where it falls short without relaxing the criteria.

## Boundaries (Effective 10-15, tightened by Liang Hu on 10-14)
- Workstation does not run computations or store compute data: wind field calculations, station pairing, and large-file downloads of AIWP/GFS/HURDAT2 must all be executed and stored in Colab sessions or TACC /work (CRC group space is at ~95%, so large data prioritizes TACC); the workstation only holds scripts, small results <200 MB per item, figures, and reports; if temporary storage >1 GB is truly needed, report to Node B first.
- Supercomputer usage still goes through ComputeOps resource request + registration, with pre-check and submission separated into two commands; CRC defaults to a single node.
- Current status (verified 10-15 02:00): No computations running on the workstation for this node; total is 44 MB, with no files >200 MB. The live GDEX reads in v2c were decoded in memory at the time and not written to disk. Upon restart, the task brief must be written in accordance with this section.

## Current Status
**Shelved (10-14, supported by all 6 reviewers).** Under the refrozen s2b protocol, B1 did not pass the gate: across 9 homogeneous events and 22 stations at 48 h, the Pangu/OFCL median absolute error ratio is 1.021 (satisfying ≤1.1), but only 5/9 events are no worse than OFCL (requiring ≥6/9); using 10 events as the denominator gives 5/10. In accordance with the sequence, B4 is not pursued. This result cannot claim that AI tracks are overall better or worse.

**Why it failed**
- Both chains underestimate by 35–38% at 48 h. This stems from the pre-registered input assumptions: the initial pressure deficit Δp0 is extrapolated by scaling with OFCL intensity (H08 only uses pressure deficit, not Vmax directly), RMW is frozen at the initialization time (Nicole 200 nmi, Milton 5 nmi), and OFCL intensity itself is biased low. The individual contribution of each factor has not been disentangled.
- Track indeed affects station winds, but the direction is inconsistent: Pangu has a closer track on only 4/9 events (median 91 km vs. OFCL 105 km).
- Each event has only 1–4 qualified stations, and 34/67 stations dropped out during high-wind periods, biasing the sample toward outer-periphery stations.

**What conditions are missing and when to restart**: See verdict R1–R4—operationally available size and pressure inputs, or Liang Hu's model; ≥15 evaluable events with ≥3 stations per event; a censoring treatment scheme; switching the primary chain must be pre-registered in advance. Any restart constitutes a new protocol version and does not overturn the current gate verdict.

**Assets left for Node B**: , v1 wind field and ASOS pairing, 850 hPa tracker and AIWP remote reading, and three-chain results.

## Finalized Decisions
- 2026-10-14 v2 preparation stops here: only 13 cases remain after strict station-type and height filtering; do not freeze or run (a), wait for restart triggers → 
- 2026-10-14 after v2b verification returned: complete prerequisites and produce a finalized pre-registration candidate, still without running the gate evaluation → 
- 2026-10-14 after v2 feasibility returned, do not open the v2 gate; dispatch a targeted verification of the hourly homogeneous pool → 
- 2026-10-14 B1 failed to pass the gate, node shelved, B4 not pursued; retract the "track signal swamped" attribution; rewrite restart conditions as R1–R4 → 
- 2026-10-14 Colab policy correction (Node B Lead, following Liang Hu's exact words): no single-experiment cap, report first if projected >100 CU; must stop upon completion, and dispatch only one executor per round
- 2026-10-14 Phase 2 protocol revision s2b: OFCL 12 h interpolation, homogeneous sample (Nicholas 48 h non-evaluable), primary (c) uses Pangu, (c′) does not use Liang Hu's credentials; criteria unchanged → 
- 2026-10-14 Chain (a) v1 passed the ±20% gate; accept the ~2 min ASOS proxy definition; dispatch Phase 2 → 
- 2026-10-14 Literature review verdict: OFCL lacks Pc/POCI/RMW, so (b) and (c) must not use post-event b-decks; check CIRA/Weather Lab first for AI tracks, and use 850 hPa circulation for self-tracking; add (c′) WN-C; narrow incremental contribution scope to "AI tracks + classical parametric boundary layer → US ASOS three-chain comparison, not found within searched scope" → 
- 2026-10-14 Hierarchy rule (set by Root Lead): this node is Level 2 and does not open Level 3 sub-projects; if B4 needs to be independent, report to the Lab Lead for Node B to open a peer-level node; tool bots must not re-delegate
- 2026-10-14 B1 and B4 opened jointly (set by parent node) → 
- 2026-10-14 Phase 1 minimal model (+50.7%) judged as an incomplete implementation; dispatch Phase 1b to retest the same gate with the full model under pre-registration → 
- 2026-10-14 Step 1 split into two phases: first "data access feasibility + event list + wind field model implementation + chain (a)", then proceed to (b) and (c) only after chain (a) passes the ±20% gate →

projects.brief:
# Task Brief: H2 Leave-One-Station-Out Reconstruction for Landfalling Hurricanes (2026-10-14); Execute under Established Authorization without Seeking Mid-Course Approval.

## Objective
Conclusion from the benign-wind phase (r1/r2): pure interpolation suffices for dense station networks, while ERA5 + residual kriging is ~13% better where stations are sparse. H2 asks: during landfalling hurricanes (when background fields are poorest and station dropouts are frequent), can "parametric typhoon wind field + residual kriging" reconstruct station winds—especially each station's event peak—substantially more accurately than pure interpolation and ERA5 backgrounds? This is the scenario needed by Node I (loss–wind speed library) of the Lab.

## Events and Data (Read-only reuse of Node B resources without modifying Node B files; copy needed scripts to this directory before editing)
- Events (revised on 10-14 per parent instructions): the same v1 batch of 10 events from Node B  (Delta, Zeta, Ida, Nicholas, Ian, Nicole, Idalia, Debby, Helene, Milton) + BERYL 2024 listed separately as an addition; events with <8 valid stations are listed only and excluded from criteria evaluation.
- Parametric wind field: reuse Node B  (CLIMADA 6.1.0 Holland 2008 + directional sea/land roughness + averaging-time conversion; pre-registration , errata), without tuning its coefficients in this experiment.
- Observations: METAR hourly sustained winds and gusts from all ASOS/AWOS stations within ±12 h of landfall and within 300 km of the track (IEM, same retrieval convention as r1 ); ERA5 10 m wind (ARCO-ERA5, same as r1).
- Dropouts: stations with missing observations within the peak window are listed separately and excluded from the primary score (Node B found that roughly half of stations drop out during hurricanes), with their counts reported.

## Methods
IDW, ordinary kriging, direct ERA5 interpolation, ERA5 + residual kriging, direct Holland interpolation, and Holland + residual kriging; one "weighted Holland and ERA5" variant may be added, provided the weights are fixed in advance and not tuned to the results. Machine learning methods are excluded (inferior to residual kriging in r2). Leave-one-station-out cross-validation.

## Metrics and Criteria (Written in Advance)
- Primary metrics: RMSE and bias of the event peak per station (maximum hourly sustained wind within the window); secondary metrics: hourly RMSE and peak gust error (gusts compared only against gusts).
- Criteria: best "background + residual" method achieves ≥20% lower peak RMSE than the best pure interpolation method and outperforms it at ≥2/3 of stations → blending is worthwhile for hurricane scenarios; 10–20% improvement or only one condition met → conditional; <10% → pure interpolation suffices. Report each event individually, followed by the aggregate.
- Additional reporting: peak errors stratified by distance to the storm center (<1×, 1–3×, >3× RMW).

## Boundaries
Workstation local CPU, 0 CU; write only in ; all timestamps in UTC; do not mix mean winds and gusts; record assumed parameters in the parameter source table and must not present them as literature values; log new external data in PUBLIC_CITATIONS.md.

## Deliverables
 (per-event and aggregate method comparison tables, one-sentence criteria conclusion, dropout station list, stratification by distance, and parameter source table), one predicted vs. observed peak scatter plot (with data sources labeled), and scripts. Report back only conclusions and numbers.

# B1+B4 Kickoff and Phasing (10-14)

- Decision: Step 1 is divided into two phases. Phase 1: AIWP remote slicing feasibility, event list, wind field model implementation, (a) best track chain against ASOS; Phase 2 (done only if (a) median bias is within ±20%): (b) NHC official and (c) AI track chains. B4 ensemble after B1 passes the gate.
- Why: The criterion requires (a) to qualify first, otherwise comparing (b)/(c) is meaningless; verifying the wind field model and observation pairing first is the most cost-effective.
- Cost of being wrong: If (a) easily passes the gate, there is an extra round of task dispatch, delaying by about half a day.
- Basis: Task statement criteria; wind field model Vickery 2009 card (page numbers to be added when ideas cites).
- Criteria were written into the project page before running, and must not be relaxed.

# B1+B4 段 1：可复核数据入口（10-14，美东）

1. 最佳路径：NHC HURDAT2 Atlantic [2026-09-23 版](https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/hurdat/hurdat2-1851-2025-092326.txt)，逐风暴 `L,HUbALnnYYYY.dat.gz` 中 BEST 的第 19 栏是 RMW（海里），第 17 栏 POCI（hPa）；在主样本逐风暴读回，6 小时线性插值，若缺就剔除，不能以常数填补。CIRA [EBTRK](https://rammb2.cira.colostate.edu/research/tropical-cyclones/tc_extended_best_track_dataset/) 的公开 v3.0.2 实际仅更新到 2021，不能拿它声称有 2022–24 的 RMW；其 [README](https://rammb2.cira.colostate.edu/wp-) 亦说明 RMW 并非全时期正式最佳路径字段。本次 pilot 用 NHC b-deck；HURDAT 中非整 6h 登陆位置需另外保留。
2. 官方链 (b)：相同目录 `aALnnYYYY.dat.gz` 的 `OFCL` 是官方路径和强度（ 等）。实测 GET 返回 200，内有 Milton 的 OFCL 行；按起报时刻与实际登陆时刻选预先定义的 24/48/72 h lead，既不可用事后 BEST 替代官方强度，也不能暗中调整 AI 路径时效。NHC [ATCF 格式说明](https://ftp.nhc.noaa.gov/atcf/docs/NRL_doc_ATCFdatabase.html)。段 2 未计算官方链。
3. AI 链 (c)：CIRA/DeMaria (2025) 研究确实使用自身的 TC tracker；本轮检索 CIRA 页面及论文，尚未找到对全部 2020–24 风暴公开可批量下载的逐预报轨迹档。实测 Milton 2024 的官方 a-deck（279 种 aid）无 PANG/GRCS/FCN2/PGWX 同名记录；这不排除另处 CIRA 内部或公开文件，故仅记“现成统一轨迹未核实可下载”。原始 [AIWP S3 README](https://noaa-) 给出模型/时间/变量； 的 108 个具体对象逐一用 S3 list-prefix 核验，95 个存在、0 次请求错误；Pangu 2024 Francine 的 72 h 对象缺一个。最晚 00/12 UTC 起报时间与确切 lead 另有列，不可把 24 h 标签等同恰为 24 h。
4. 原始 AIWP 四维 netCDF 每个约 7–9 GB；试了 Milton 对应 FOUR 文件的 HEAD（7,472,991,383 B），HTTP `Range: bytes=0-1023` 返回 、HDF5 签名。说明对象支持字节范围，不等于“按空间时间切片已成功”。Colab 会话先用 `h5py`/fsspec 缓存 Range 或远程读取做单文件单时次的经纬度/海平面气压与 10 m u/v 小块读取测量请求字节数；若 netCDF 压缩 chunk 跨全球时次，字节/请求失控就停止，不下载整文件。随后围 NHC 预报先验半径搜 MSLP 局地低值、用 850 hPa 环流复核并记录断链（DeMaria 2025 第 3 节建议环流追踪）；不能只凭一帧全域最低压。当前没有运行 Colab，也没有测得切片实际数据量/时长，不能给虚构数字。论文：https://doi.org/10.1175/AIES-D-24-0085.1；Radford 2025：https://doi.org/10.1175/BAMS-D-24-0057.1。
5. ASOS：IEM [1-minute 页面](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/asos/1min.phtml) 的 [backend](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/request/asos1min.py?help) 用 `station=SRQ&vars=sknt,gust_sknt&sts=2024-10-09T12:30Z&ets=2024-10-10T12:30Z&what=download&tz=UTC`。`sknt` 是档案的逐分钟持续风读数（按 ASOS 传感器解释近似运行 2 min 平均，不是验证过的独立 1 min 平均），`gust_sknthttps://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/request/asos.py?help=` 有 `gust`, `peak_wind_gust`, `sknt`，但低频/不同定义不可混到主指标。IEM 自述 raw 存档有限 QC；本次甚至出现 Ian PIE 最大持续风 82 kt、5s gust 最大仅 18 kt，判疑剔除，不可把此源当已质控真值。
6. 中断/缺测：见 每站 24h 应 1440 条的实有数。Idalia TLH/GNV/AAF 仅 207/151/233，且都在登陆前停止；Helene TLH 0，Milton TPA/BKV 0，Ian APF 0。0 行不等于已证实物理设备故障，可能是档案缺源；另有 Milton PIE 827、GIF 858，Ian FMY 433，均会偏低估实测峰值。主展示需每站完整性与 QC 标志；不可对缺测做零风填充。没有下载任何 AIWP 原始 7–9 GB 文件到 工作站。

本段费用：本地 HTTP/NHC/IEM/S3 目录查询和 CPU 脚本；Colab 未启动，耗费 0 CU。若后续先单模型、单预报切片，预算上限每试验 ≤20 CU，实测花费再报。图和 CSV 仅是公开站点数据的摘要，不保存/发布逐分钟原始序列。

items.text:
# B1+B4 (a) Best Track Trial Calculation (10-14, US Eastern)

Status: Small-sample preliminary check, not a formal pass/fail conclusion on criteria. Inputs: NHC HURDAT2 landfall location/track/1 min maximum wind/central pressure + b-deck RMW/POCI; IEM/NCEI ASOS 1-minute archives, all from public web pages; original paths see ; algorithm see , . Airports within a 150 km radius of the landfall point for each event marked with 1min archives; simultaneous window 12 h before and after landfall, model takes peaks at 15min, stations take peaks from minute-by-minute readings, no missing data imputation. Specific 28 rows per station and data URLs see ; event location sources and coverage see . Figure `chain_a_ratio_pilot5.png.svg`, green interval pre-fixed as predicted/observed 0.8–1.2, caption data sources: NHC HURDAT2 + NHC ATCF b-deck + Iowa Environmental Mesonet/NCEI ASOS one-minute archive.

Quality control: Among 28 candidate stations, only 18 stations had ≥720/1440 non-missing sustained wind minutes; Ian PIE's observed maximum sustained wind was 82 kt but maximum 5-second gust was only 18 kt, failing physical consistency; after excluding it, there are 17 pairs, 4 events in total. For the fifth event Idalia, all three stations stopped reporting before landfall (151–233 min), contributing 0 qualified stations, so it cannot be claimed that five events passed testing. retains all exclusion reasons; original did not perform PIE QC, and its 18-station count is not used for primary conclusions.

Metric definitions: e = predicted/observed − 1; median absolute error = median(|e|), median bias = median(e). 17 pairs after quality control: median absolute error 50.69%, median bias +50.69%, not within the pre-specified ±20%. More strictly including only stations with ≥1296/1440 min, 6 pairs: both metrics 44.745%, still not within ±20%; however, the latter covers only 3 events and has strong airport exposure selection. By event:

| Event | Available / Candidate Stations | Median Absolute Ratio Error | Median Signed Bias | Special Notes on Missing Data |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Ian 2022 | 5/8 | 25.62% | +25.62% | PIE excluded for physical inconsistency; FMY stopped reporting almost before landfall |
| Idalia 2023 | 0/3 | Incalculable | Incalculable | AAF/GNV/TLH stopped before landfall, only 151–233 minutes |
| Francine 2024 | 4/5 | 54.95% | +54.95% | BTR has no rows in 1min archive |
| Helene 2024 | 2/3 | 24.665% | +24.665% | TLH has no rows in 1min archive; records of the other two stations incomplete |
| Milton 2024 | 6/9 | 73.195% | +73.195% | TPA/BKV have no rows, FMY 304 min; PIE/GIF/SPG partially stopped reporting |

Very important: What is compared here is the sustained wind reading reported every minute by ASOS (commonly a 2 min running average) against a minimal Holland / constant 0.85 output without a well-defined averaging duration. It does not achieve pairing of "1 min sustained wind of the same physical definition" or gusts. There is no land-sea roughness correction, storm translation, or azimuthal asymmetry; missing data for the largest peaks is non-random, and the observed denominator may be biased low. One cannot attribute +50.69% to AI track, much less declare scientific direction failure based on a trial run. According to the frozen gate, conclusions on the merits of (b)(c) must not be advanced; complete wind field near-surface conversion, exposure/averaging duration, and IEM missing-data QC should be fixed first, retesting the same unchanged ±20% criterion. If it still exceeds boundaries after fixing, close out according to the project page's "wind field model disqualified". The current simplified implementation itself fails as a proxy screening.

This time there were only local CPU/HTTP requests, no Colab session, no HPC, Colab cost 0 CU. Did not download or publish raw minute-by-minute full time series and large AIWP files; figures and tables are station-level peak summaries.

items.title: Wind-field screening implementation and scope of applicability (10-14)
items.text:
# Wind Field Screening Implementation and Scope of Applicability (10-14)

Implementation: , local standard library; what was executed this time is a minimal screening of "best track + Holland (1980) axisymmetric gradient wind + constant 0.85 reduction", not Vickery et al. (2009) 2D slab + height-resolved profiles, much less 3D boundary layer or topographic corrections. The reason for selection is that inputs (track, Pc, Vmax, RMW, POCI) can be obtained directly from NHC, formulas and code are verifiable, facilitating early discovery of unusable observations and structural parameters. Vickery 2009's model is a more suitable subsequent implementation; its slab, land-sea roughness transition, and dropsonde profiles cannot be replaced by a 0.85 constant. Card , PDF pp. 1, 12, 15, 22–24 (journal pp. 381, 392, 395, 402–404), its 0.85 coefficient is a simple control tuned against the same batch of observations, not a verified universal overland factor.

Hourly set center latitude φ / longitude λ, best track Vmax [kt], Pc [hPa], b-deck RMW [nmi], POCI [hPa]. Linearly interpolate 6h data and preserve non-hourly landfalls from HURDAT2; station-to-center spatial distance uses haversine. Let Δp=100(POCI−Pc) Pa, ρ=1.15 kg/m³ (assumed), f=2Ωsinφ, Ω=7.292115×10^-5 s^-1, R=1852 RMW (m), r=max(3000 m, station-center distance), x=(R/r)^B. Define Vg,max=(0.514444 Vmax)/0.85, back-calculate B=ρ e (Vg,max²+f R Vg,max)/Δp; retain only 0.5≤B≤4, 8≤RMW≤200 nmi, 500≤Δp≤15000 Pa. Gradient wind Vg(r)=sqrt[(B Δp/ρ) x exp(−x)+(rf/2)²]−rf/2. Wind field velocity V10(r)=0.85 Vg(r), taking the maximum on a 15min time grid 12h before and after landfall for each station. Gradient wind pressure formula see Wang et al. (2020) PDF p. 5 Eq. (7) (originally Holland 1980); Vmax → gradient conversion, ρ, RMW interpolation, minimum radius, and B truncation are hypotheses of this experiment and must not be written as literature values. Function `modelinterp` can be recalculated item by item. The radial formula has no storm translation asymmetry, background wind, local decay, or terrain acceleration; in particular, applying 0.85 for offshore to inland airports simultaneously inevitably carries systematic risks.

Physical inconsistency of time/peak: NHC Vmax is the maximum 1 min sustained wind; the near-surface coefficient of this simplified model is not endowed with a stable time-averaging definition; IEM `sknt` is the ASOS sustained wind output every minute, typically approximating a 2 min running average, unconfirmed as 1 min. Ratios in the same figure serve only as proxy screening, not the final qualification verification of "peak gust or 1 min sustained wind" required by the task criteria. `gust_sknt` is 5 s gust; card ZR7S3SEJ (candidate, PDF pp. 2–3, 5–6) separates different sampling durations and exposures; 2KXRIJJB (candidate, PDF pp. 2–4) comparison of approx. 2 s vs 10 min cannot be directly used as a universal 5 s / 2 min multiplier. This station did not perform gust factor and 1→2 min conversions, and therefore does not forcibly pair unforecast gusts with observed gusts. Both cards are pending independence and are not treated as approved design values.

Terrain/exposure: Station coordinates were only screened for 150 km, without using airport directional obstacles or land-cover; land z0=0.03 m, sea z0=0.0013 m are only Vickery examples (card WTPZS77N, PDF pp. 12, 15, 22), not entered into the code. It cannot be claimed that terrain correction has been done. To pass the gate, one must first implement directional/land-sea transition boundary layer conversions, and check original texts / author code / cards before selecting values; any subsequent parameter tuning will be distinguished as a new model from the currently frozen ±20% gate, and coefficients must not be adjusted a posteriori on this sample to fit the gate. The parameter source table has been filled on the project page. Reasonable sensitivities to be done: ρ 1.10–1.25, near-surface coefficient 0.65–0.90, representative sea/land roughness values and directional variations, RMW ±20%; these are range suggestions rather than executed verifications.

# B1+B4 Phase 1 Results and Phase 1b (10-14)
- Results: Minimal Holland + constant 0.85, (a) best track chain 4 events 17 stations (after QC) median bias +50.7%, did not enter ±20%.
- Decision: Do not conclude "wind field model disqualified" based on this; dispatch Phase 1b to use a full parametric model (Vickery 2009 slab + roughness transition, or TCRM/CLIMADA), pre-registering the model, constants, duration conversions, and station inclusion rules first (PREREG_v1.md) before comparing against observations, retesting the same ±20% gate; if v1 still exceeds boundaries, close out without further parameter tuning.
- Why: Phase 1 model lacks overland roughness, duration definitions, and translational asymmetry; the high bias direction is consistent with these omissions; 0.85 is Vickery 2009's offshore control baseline (card WTPZS77N, PDF pp. 23–24, cited via ideas windfield_model.md, Lead has not checked page by page), not an overland conversion factor. Criteria remain unchanged.
- Cost of being wrong: If the full model is likewise disqualified, spend about an extra half day, 0–3 CU.

items.title: Verdict: review of the three B1+B4 literature conclusions (10-14)
items.text:
# Verdict: Review of Three Literature Conclusions for B1+B4 (10-14)
Reviewers: E·Gemini, A·GPT-6, D·GLM (3/3 valid, all "supported with reservations"). Evidence: Grok report b99be0, project page.

## Personal Verification by the Lead
- NHC OFCL does not report Pc/POCI/RMW: The Lead downloaded aal142024 (Milton); for OFCL τ≥12 h there are 383 rows in total, with 0 rows of non-zero mslp/poci/rmw, and 161 rows of non-zero 34 kt wind radii. Confirmed.
- WeatherNext Cyclones public tracks: developers.google.com/weathernext/guides/weatherlab has been reviewed—CSV/ATCF, including ensemble member tracks and paired observations, approx. 2023 to present, historical data under CC BY 4.0; whether registration is required is not stated. Confirmed.
- DeMaria 2025 tracking uses 850 hPa circulation, not MSLP: litwiki card points to Appendix (PDF pp. 2–3, 14–15); both E and A independently stated the same, adopted (the Lead did not re-read the appendix page by page).
- Vickery 2009 was verified on 258 peak gusts across 24 US landfalling hurricanes, RMW/B parameters were fitted through subjective iterative fitting using HWind + station time series, and observations were first standardized to open terrain 10 m 3 s: E and A stated the same, pointing to local Zotero original journal pp. 397–404, consistent with card WTPZS77N, adopted.

## Must Change
1. **Wind field input for chains (b)(c)** (E-1): OFCL only has track, Vmax, and 34/50/64 kt wind radii. Chains (b)(c) must not use post-event b-deck RMW/POCI/Pc. Changed to: Use RMW and POCI at the cycle initiation time (τ=0, operationally available CARQ/BEST τ=0) as initial values, extrapolate during the forecast period according to the pre-registered method (persistence or literature statistical RMW model), determine Pc from Vmax using a literature wind-pressure relationship, or directly fit a Holland profile using OFCL wind radii (similar practice to the NHC wind speed probability model). Specific scheme enters Stage 2 pre-registration; chain (a) can still use b-deck.
2. **AI track tracking method** (E-2, A-1): Retract "tracking from MSLP/10 m wind using TempestExtremes". Order changed to: First check whether CIRA RAMMB public AIWP tracks (NPNG/NGRP/NFOR etc., https://rammb-data.cira.colostate.edu/tc_realtime/about.asp) can be downloaded at the file level; if not, track using 850 hPa circulation per DeMaria 2025 Appendix (using NHC forecast initialization position as initial guess), with MSLP used only as auxiliary. "AIWP has no off-the-shelf track files" rephrased to "NOAA S3 archives contain no track files; the downloadability of CIRA products has not been verified".
3. **Incorporate WeatherNext Cyclones** (E-3, D-1): The Lead's original note "requires login, unverified" was wrong, corrected. Add supplementary chain (c′): WN-C track + intensity + wind radii (from 2023 onward, covering 6 events: Idalia, Beryl, Debby, Francine, Helene, Milton), serving as B4's preferred off-the-shelf AI ensemble source; (c′) is for reporting only and will not enter B1 criteria (criteria remain based on (c), neither relaxed nor replaced). Conclusion (1) is restricted to "FCN/Pangu/GraphCast in the AIWP archive without intensity post-processing (DeMaria 2025 sample)", not generalized to "all AI intensities are inadequate" (Alet 2026 Nature 10.1038/s41586-026-10953-2 is a counterexample).
4. **Narrow incremental scope** (E-5, A-2, D-1): Do not write "no one has done AI forecast to station winds". Write as "Within the retrieved scope, none observed: three-chain comparison of AI forecast track + classical parameterized boundary layer wind field → US ASOS station peak winds", listing adjacent precedents side by side: NHC wind speed probabilities DeMaria 2009 (10.1175/2009WAF2222286.1)/2013; Alet 2026 (explicitly stating station-by-station wind verification is left for the future); Vickery 2009 station verification; Lai et al. (Pangu/AIFS driving UWIN-CM, Hong Kong); Wu et al. 2026 ACDF (arXiv 2603.12828, Zhejiang stations). These precedents can serve as literature basis only after cards are created in litwiki.
5. **Different conditions between chain (a) and Vickery 2009** (E-4, A-3): Vickery's RMW/B were fitted to station time series, whereas we use raw b-deck values without fitting; therefore, the ±20% gate of this node is stricter than Vickery's verification, which must be clearly stated when interpreting results. Criteria remain unchanged (the gate set by Liang Hu / Node B is not relaxed).
6. **Supplement repository table** with SimCenter (Snaiki–Wu 2017 C++ implementation, R2D Hurricane Wind Simulation Tool) (A-4) and stormwindmodel (Willoughby, US gridded peak winds/gusts, CRAN) (D-NOTE); retract "no open-source implementation of Snaiki & Wu found".

## For Reference Only
- A: When comparing (b)/(c), distinguish the operationally available time of early/late guidance; Stage 2 pre-registration should state whether late (available post-hoc) or early is used, and clarify that they are not equivalent operational conditions.
- D: Pangu systematically overestimates RMW (arXiv 2511.21792 abstract)—note this if (c) uses size information from AI fields; this node's (c) does not use AI size.
- D: B4 coverage criteria can be benchmarked against NHC wind speed probabilities, stating that the increment comes from a physical/AI ensemble rather than error climatology.
- D: Current status of HWind has not been verified; check independently before citing.
- D pointed out that the Lead's note "CLIPER is a paraphrase" was redundant: Accepted; CLIPER/TCLP is indeed the paper's baseline name.

## Objections Not Adopted
- E claimed that GenCast plus an empirical wind-pressure relationship can "substantially eliminate intensity underestimation without borrowing NHC intensity": Does not alter the design of (c)—the problem definition for this node is specifically "AI track + official intensity", and this correction in Alet 2026 was targeted at GenCast, not the three AIWP models; (c′) already covers the comparison with "AI native intensity".
- E claimed that WN-C "comprehensively outperforms HAFS/HWRF": Original paper numbers unverified, treated only as a clue, not included in conclusions.

## Literature Basis
DeMaria 2025 card; Vickery 2009 card (journal pp. 397–404, quoted by reviewers); remaining precedents have no cards yet, pending creation.

# B1+B4 Chain (a) v1 Pre-registration (Frozen; Prior to Observation Comparison)

Time: 10-14 15:19 EDT. This document was written prior to computing this round's v1 results; since the previous round pilot's +50.7% has been made public, it is impossible to claim a completely blind state; the following constants do not use station ratios to tune parameters. This document/rules will not be modified hereafter; if changes are needed, a separate v2 will be created.

## Model and Data
CLIMADA v6.1.0 `trop_cyclone` H08 (tag commit bb9595944fcf673152ea53e61efbafeb0b1e4406, GPL-3.0) is selected. It is chosen over the Vickery 2009 slab because the latter has no off-the-shelf, fully open implementation that can be directly verified; nor will the previous round's 0.85 Holland be falsely claimed as full Vickery. CLIMADA's `_compute_windfields` explicitly defines 10 m, 1-min wind, and incorporates vector translational asymmetry according to storm translation speed and radial decay (source code v6.1.0 lines 1131–1257; H08 uses Holland 2008 B, default gradient-to-surface 0.9, source code lines 61–69). The original functions of this software version are used without manual intensity tuning. HURDAT2 center, 1-min maximum wind, and central pressure; ATCF b-deck BEST columns 17/19 for POCI/RMW; linearly interpolated to 15 min between raw time points within ±12 h; if one side is missing or the gap exceeds 7 h, do not extrapolate; nodes with RMW<=0 or POCI<=Pc are removed. Raw HURDAT landfall special points are retained; only longitude/latitude/intensity/pressure are linearly interpolated, without adjusting the storm based on ASOS. Stations are from the IEM ASOS network with HAS1MIN=1, archive covering the event time, and within 150 km of the HURDAT landfall center. Model peak is taken as the maximum within landfall ±12 h.

## Exposure and Averaging Periods (Pre-fixed)
CLIMADA's raw 10 m 1-min H08 field is an oceanic baseline; station wind directions come from model u/v, querying the Natural Earth 10m land polygon (public surface category) at 2/5/10 km along the upstream inflow direction. If >=2 of the three points are land, it is classified as overland; otherwise, water surface; whether the station is located within the polygon is also logged. Near-surface roughness over sea z0=0.0013 m, open land z0=0.03 m, per Vickery et al. 2009 PDF pp. 12, 15, 22; overland factor F=[ln(10/.03)/ln(500/.03)]/[ln(10/.0013)/ln(500/.0013)], water surface F=1; roughness switches hourly when the sampled category changes. The 500 m neutral constant-flux logarithmic layer and single open land z0 are explicit assumptions, not CLIMADA's or Vickery's full land-sea transition; reference height range 200–1000 m, land z0 0.02–0.07 m affect metrics, provided solely as sensitivity notes and not used to tune gates. Topographic elevation is not separately corrected. If Natural Earth data cannot be read, do not silently switch to another exposure definition; mark v1 as failed to execute.

Model 1-min sustained wind is converted to ASOS IEM `sknt` approx. 2-min running average by multiplying by 0.97; this is a conservative assumption (range 0.95–1.00), not an exact measured literature value. The 5-s gust reported by `gust_sknt` is obtained from the model 1-min field multiplied by 1.30 (land) and 1.20 (sea); this is a tentative interpolation assumption based on roughness/3–5s and minute-wind definitions described in Powell et al. 2005 "Hurricane Gust Factors Revisited" PDF pp. 2–3, 5–6, not a universal 1min→5s factor directly provided by that paper; range: land 1.15–1.45, sea 1.10–1.35; the approx. 2s/10min factor of Krayer–Marshall 1992 cannot be directly applied (2KXRIJJB PDF pp. 2–4). Both averaging periods are frozen in advance and peak values are computed separately.

## Station Screening and Statistics
For each station, centered on the model 2-min peak time t* within ±6 h (if exceeding the landfall ±12 h observation window, expand retrieval to the edge of that window), require valid `sknt` independent minutes >=90% of actual minutes in the 12 h (>=648/720), with first valid <=t* and last valid >=t*; failure to meet this results in truncation and exclusion from the two primary metrics. Physical QC: sustained/gust must not be negative; records with gust<sknt when both have values in the same minute are treated as inconsistent, and the entire station is removed; stations where overall maximum gust is less than maximum sustained wind are also removed (two peaks at different times, but still clearly an abnormal proxy). Gusts separately require >=1 valid report, both model/observation >0, without assuming gusts must be reported every minute; stations lacking gusts do not enter gust metrics but sustained wind can be retained. Deduplicate minutes, do not fill missing with 0; count request failures and no-records separately. This QC is a conservative pre-filter and does not imply raw IEM archives are fully quality-controlled.

For each event and station, peak prediction / observation - 1; median(abs(e)) and median(e) are aggregated across eligible stations; reported row by row by event, additionally reporting number of events, number of stations, and number of truncated stations. The primary gate is strictly whether chain (a) sustained wind median bias is within ±20%; gust serves as parallel diagnosis, not replacing the frozen primary gate; if still out of bounds, report the wind field model as failing truthfully without tuning parameters. Events without eligible stations remain in the denominator notes but do not contribute to station metrics. Stations will not be reselected based on the old pilot, nor will constants be modified based on results. Sources: NHC HURDAT2, ATCF b-deck, IEM/NCEI 1min, Natural Earth 10m land; detailed URLs see previous round. Following pre-registration, if software or data is unavailable, clearly report as incomplete; do not provide fabricated numbers.

# B1+B4 Best Track Chain v1: Pre-registered Retest

Frozen document: (10-14 15:19 EDT; prior to observation comparison in this round v1); software CLIMADA 6.1.0 H08 commit lines 1131–1257.

By station e=peak prediction/peak observation−1, median(|e|) / median(e). Inputs: NHC HURDAT2+ATCF b-deck, IEM/NCEI ASOS 1min, Natural Earth 10m land polygon; figures and tables all indicate sources.

Sustained wind (approx. 2min sknt, n=29): median absolute error 21.02%; median bias +9.89%. ±20% bias gate: Passed; but absolute error 21.02% >20%, should not falsely claim overall error is entirely within ±20%.
5s gust (gust_sknt, n=29): median absolute error 11.20%; median bias -0.87%.
67 candidate stations; 34 truncated stations; 3 stations eliminated by physical QC; 1 station request failed; IDA and IDALIA have no eligible stations. All 12 events were attempted.

## Execution and Boundaries
The first execution removed an event entirely if any single 15-min node lacked RMW/POCI, causing Beryl and Francine to be excluded; erroneous run results are retained as-is in of the v1 root directory and the event-by-event table. The code subsequently only corrected the pre-registration implementation error of "excluding missing nodes rather than excluding the entire event", recomputing in the new directory without changing models, constants, or station rules. The above official v1 numbers are from ; original outputs are never overwritten.
Severe weather reporting outages in raw IEM minute archives are not random; the 90% model peak window rule eliminated 34/67 stations, leaving only 1 station for Milton. Natural surface is only land/sea, without resolving specific land categories and terrain across different directions at airports; 500m log layer reference height, 1min→2min factor, and 1min→5s factor are all frozen assumptions, not author-provided universal conversions. IEM sknt is an approx. 2min proxy, not a strict 1min pairing; although the gust factor has definition/exposure basis from Powell et al. 2005 PDF pp. 2–3, 5–6, its numerical value is an assumption. Therefore, "gate passed" is strictly limited to the pre-registered proxy comparison, and does not imply the physical wind field is universally validated.
Error directions across different stations and event samples are strongly imbalanced; 29 stations come from 10 events, not every one of the 12 events having quality-qualified observations.

AIWP slicing listed separately; Colab CPU sessions have been stopped. For B1 subsequent (b)(c), the Lead should judge whether to accept the above 2min proxy/averaging period assumptions as the primary gate before proceeding.

items.text:
# B1+B4 Stage 1b Passes Gate, Dispatch Stage 2 (10-14)
- Results (numbers taken from , verified by the Lead): CLIMADA 6.1.0 H08 + directional land-sea roughness + pre-registered averaging period conversions, (a) best track chain 10 events 29 stations: sustained wind (ASOS approx. 2 min) median bias +9.9%, median absolute error 21.0%; 5 s gust median bias −0.9%, median absolute error 11.2%. Among 67 candidate stations, 34 stations were truncated; Ida and Idalia have no eligible stations.
- Determination: Gate (a) (median bias within ±20%) passed according to frozen criteria. Criteria strictly evaluate bias; median absolute error 21% is not within the gate, reported truthfully without changing criteria.
- Accept approx. 2 min ASOS proxy as primary gate specification. Rationale: (b)(c) and (a) use the same wind field model, same station set, and same averaging period conversions, so specification errors largely cancel out in inter-chain comparisons; the bias of the independent gust specification is also close to 0. This is not "successful validation of 1 min wind field", and must not be described as such externally.
- Known bias: Truncated stations are mostly those with the highest winds and reporting outages, while eligible stations skew toward peripheral, weaker-wind stations. Conclusions apply only to this category of stations.
- run2 correction was an implementation error (pre-registration specified excluding nodes, but the first run excluded the entire event), no constants were changed, acceptable; results of the first run are retained in the v1 root directory.
- Next step: Stage 2 ((b)(c) three chains + (c′)), input scheme pre-registered first. Cost of error: If the 2 min proxy is substandard, the comparison between (b) and (c) remains valid (same specification), except absolute error cannot be cited as wind field accuracy.
- Basis: No literature basis, based on internal track data; sources for averaging periods and roughness see PREREG_v1 (Vickery 2009 card WTPZS77N, PDF pp. 12/15/22; Vickery & Skerlj 2005 card ZR7S3SEJ, authors corrected).

items.title: B1+B4 segment 2 pre-registration s2 (frozen before comparison with observations)
items.text:
# B1+B4 Stage 2 Pre-registration s2 (Frozen Prior to Observation Comparison)

Time: 10-14 EDT. Observations of (a) v1 and their results are already visible; this round is not double-blind. Once written and fixed, this document will not change based on ASOS ratios from (b)/(c). 12 pre-selected landfalling events; primary comparison uses the 10 events with eligible stations from v1, with 29 reason=eligible stations; IDALIA/IDA without observation stations will not serve as gate-passing events. Report input missingness for all pre-selected events; unavailable chains are recorded as missing and not quietly excluded from the denominator to claim gate passage.

## Common Time, Validation, and Wind Field
1. Landfall time is taken from the HURDAT2 special L record of . Nominal 24/48/72 h initialization chooses the nearest 00/12 UTC strictly earlier than or equal to landfall time minus nominal lead time; all three models share the same initialization. Actual lead times are listed event by event; the 24/48/72 labels do not represent exactly equal lengths. OFCL uses official forecasts issued approx. 3 h after that analysis time (late guidance), which is not strictly equivalent in operational availability to 00/12 UTC AI forecasts; must not be claimed as a strictly fair real-time matchup.
2. Forecast 6 h cycles are linearly interpolated to 15 min, with a window of landfall ±12 h, without out-of-bounds extrapolation, allowing a maximum gap of 7 h between adjacent valid nodes. Intensity NHC OFCL Vmax is interpolated by time and shared between (b) and (c); (c) uses this intensity, not the AI grid's own intensity. (a) directly follows v1 without recomputation.
3. Common CLIMADA 6.1.0 H08 original functions, translation vectors, 10m 1-min, majority vote at 2/5/10 km upstream along opposite inflow direction on Natural Earth 10m, sea z0=.0013m / land z0=.03m and 500m neutral logarithmic reference, sustained ×.97, gust land ×1.30 / sea ×1.20, all completely follow v1 PREREG and ; do not adjust with observations. Model peak is the maximum within ±12h. Fix sustained wind and peak gust observations recorded when each station was eligible in v1, ensuring the three chains share identical stations and observations; separately report whether v1 12h observation completeness at the new model peak time still satisfies the original ≥648 minutes window rule; if the full window cannot be obtained, do not re-select samples on a station basis, but only note in sensitivity. Error e = model peak / fixed observed peak − 1, reporting all-station median(|e|), median(e), and within-event station median(|e|) separately. Event not worse means within-event (c) median(|e|) ≤ (b). Primary criterion: 48 h (c) Pangu all-station median(|e|) ≤ 1.1×(b), and at least 7 of the 10 events with observations are not worse (≥2/3 rounded up); simultaneously, (a) v1 sustained wind bias ±20% has passed. 24/72 h are for reporting only and do not enter the gate. Both wind variables must be reported, but sustained wind serves as the frozen primary metric and gust as parallel diagnosis, without picking the best post-hoc.
4. BEST b-deck is used solely to verify forecast center locations and chain (a), not entering the starting point, intensity, pressure, or size of (b)(c). Track error is calculated in km against the HURDAT2 BEST center via linear interpolation of 6h positions at landfall time, and average track error across ±12h nodes is separately reported; if track breaks, do not fabricate.

## Operational Input Freezing
5. Retrieve τ≥0 tracks and Vmax from NHC a-deck by storm / cycle / OFCL. CARQ τ=0 is preferred as initial center, RMW/POCI/Pc (fields 19, 17, 9, 0-based). Missing RMW/POCI will only then use the same cycle's OFCL τ=0; if the latter is still missing, wind fields for both chains in that cycle are missing, never supplemented from future or b-deck. Physical filtering: RMW 0<r≤200 nmi, POCI>Pc, Pc 0<...<POCI. Future RMW and POCI are held constant via persistence, without using AI fields to estimate size; treat the persistence assumption as a physical limitation.
6. Pc: Starting with CARQ τ=0 Pc, pressure deficit Δp0=POCI−Pc0, future Δp(t)=Δp0 [V_OFCL(t)/V_OFCL(0)]^(1/0.644), Pc(t)=POCI−Δp(t). The power exponent is borrowed from Atkinson–Holliday 1977 V=6.7(1010−Pc)^0.644 (original Western Pacific relationship, not directly adapted to the Atlantic); anchoring to the current cycle's CARQ measured pressure with constant environmental pressure is an assumption of this experiment, not confirmed by that paper. If CARQ τ=0 Pc is missing but RMW/POCI exist, use Pc0=POCI−(V0/6.7)^(1/0.644) hPa, explicitly noting as an assumption; if initial V0≤0 or calculated Pc is unphysical, mark as missing. Identical pressure and intensity are provided to (b) and (c), comparing track effect only, without fitting against BEST. Parameter sources: Atkinson & Holliday 1977, MWR 105:421–427, formulas verified from DTIC abstract and Knaff–Zehr 2007 original restatement, references: https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/html/tr/ADA064518/; https://ramsdis.cira.colostate.edu/rammb/resources/docs/Knaff_preswind.v4.pdf; these cannot serve as evidence of Atlantic accuracy.

## AI Track Freezing
7. First retrieve file-level historically downloadable ATCF of NPNG/NGRP/NFOR provided by CIRA RAMMB, used when verifiable for the same storm/cycle; if only images are seen / corresponding files cannot be directly obtained, then track from NOAA AIWP S3 `PANG_v100_GFS`, `FOUR_v200_GFS`, `GRAP_v100_GFS` 850 hPa u/v fields cycle by cycle. Primary (c) is Pangu; FOUR and GRAP are secondary and cannot substitute as primary gate-passers. Seeded with CARQ τ=0 center, not taking future BEST for the first 6h. Spatial 0.25° grid; 850 hPa Northern Hemisphere relative vorticity ζ=∂v/∂x−∂u/∂y, grid differencing and 5×5 grid smoothing; every 6h find the grid point with maximum positive 200-km radius average ζ (must be >0) within 350 km of the previous center, requiring average tangential circulation within 100–400 km of that grid point to be cyclonic (>0), with MSLP local low serving as a flag rather than an optimization objective. If discrete position jumps >350 km in 6h, lacks positive vorticity, or lacks cyclonic circulation, mark immediately as track break, without bypassing nodes / without resetting to BEST; 15-min linear interpolation for continuous 6h series. When size/rotation speed cannot be computed reliably on slices, mark as unavailable, do not switch to MSLP minimum. Tasks read remote HDF5 Range slices with minimal bandwidth, without pulling raw 7GB files to workstation. 850 hPa circulation tracking in DeMaria et al. 2025 PDF pp. 2–3, 14–15 serves as methodological direction; specific thresholds are all pre-set assumptions, not falsely claimed to be given by the paper.
8. (c′) takes Google Weather Lab historical WeatherNext Cyclones tracks, native intensity/wind radii for the same storm/cycle; if files are actually obtained with available fields, report that chain separately. When files are absent, record as not obtained, do not substitute with approximations. It does not enter (c) criteria. Sources from approx. 2023 onward, verified against actual downloads / member coverage for each event, do not extrapolate full coverage.

## Additional Report: Lower Bound for Truncated Stations
9. For the 34 stations with `reason=truncated` in v1 and other outage stations, fix the maximum `skntgust_sknt` within the retrieved window of that station in v1 as the true peak lower bound. List by event, chain, and lead time the number of stations with positive observation lower bounds, and the number/proportion of model peaks below this lower bound; stations with 0 valid observations are only listed as undecidable. The model adopts the same wind direction exposure and averaging period factors; (a) reads v1 predicted values. Truncation information is for diagnosis only and does not enter the primary gate.

## Missingness and Costs
10. Missing cycles, CARQ, or tracking failures for single models are recorded item by item; pairing of the three chains requires the same 29 stations and same observations; missing any target event disqualifies declaring passage of the full-sample gate. CPU Colab, single experiment ≤20 CU, stop upon task completion; record network bytes, duration, and billing changes (not attributed during concurrent consumption). Must not overwrite v1 results. If initialization selection causes OFCL to exclude terminal nodes within landfall ±12h, mark uncovered window portions as missing, do not stitch together forecasts from future cycles.

# Verification of AI Track Sources (10-14, started before preregistration)

CIRA RAMMB product description https://rammb-data.cira.colostate.edu/tc_realtime/about.asp explicitly lists NPNG (Pangu/GFS), NGRP (GraphCast/GFS), NFOR (FourCastNet v2/GFS), and additionally EPNG/EGRP/EFOR with IFS initial conditions; the product page emphasizes that historical products may not exist. Opening 2024 Milton's `storm.asp?storm_identifier=al142024` and `storm_experimental.asp?storm_identifier=al142024aal142024.dat.gz`, the counts for all three aids are 0, so CIRA graphic illustrations cannot be equated with existing tracks in the NHC a-deck. Therefore, the preregistered 850 hPa self-tracking was executed, rather than using the previous MSLP minimum demonstration. It has not yet been definitively confirmed that CIRA's internal historical data interface does not exist; we can only state that storm-by-storm/cycle-by-cycle files were not obtained this time.

Google Weather Lab official documentation https://developers.google.com/weathernext/guides/weatherlab (updated 2026-09-03): experimental WeatherNext Cyclones track CSVs or ATCFs can be downloaded, containing forecasted positions, intensities, timestamps, ensemble member tracks, and paired observations; historical data spans roughly 2023 to present, with history ≥1 h licensed under CC BY 4.0. In practice, opening https://deepmind.google.com/science/weatherlab in this browser redirects to Google login; the credential store contains no saved login for this site, so entering the download UI or verifying the member count/event-by-event coverage was not possible this time. The documentation does not explicitly state that registration is required, nor does it provide a fixed API/total member count; we can only say that login is required for this visit, and cannot assert that any arbitrary user without an account cannot download it. According to this project's list, the 2023+ candidate events are Idalia, Beryl, Debby, Francine, Helene, Milton; whether initialization files and member counts exist for each was not individually retrieved in practice. # B1+B4 Stage 2: Execution Report (10-14 16:42 EDT)

Status: The originally pre-registered 48 h B1 gate could not be completed as specified, so a formal scientific verdict of "pass / fail" cannot be issued. Missing entries are not counted as failures, nor are the original ±20% / 1.1× / ≥2/3 criteria on the project page altered.

## Completed Work and Methodological Compliance
- Migrated the v1 1.4 GB Python environment to WSL while retaining the lightweight environment (112 packages) in the Lab; verified actual imports of `climada` wind-field functions and `numpy`. Left v1 outputs untouched.
- Wrote and froze the evaluation script prior to running the (b)/(c) observation pairing. Chains (b) and (c) read only same-cycle NHC a-deck `CARQ` τ=0 `RMW`/`POCI`/`Pc` and `OFCL` track/`Vmax`; future storm size is held frozen and `Pc` is extrapolated via the pre-specified exponential decay, while `BEST` is used solely for track verification. Chain (a) is carried over directly from v1. Self-tracked chain (c) reads Pangu 850 hPa `u`/`v` directly rather than substituting a toy MSLP-minimum tracker.
- Flaw in original pre-registration: the protocol assumed `OFCL` provides 6 h nodes across all lead times and hard-coded a 7 h maximum interpolation gap, whereas longer lead times actually step at 12 h intervals. Under the strict original rule, zero complete 97-node (15 min) windows exist at 24, 48, or 72 h. Because the original rule cannot evaluate (b) or (c), the raw output is preserved as-is; upon discovering this issue and prior to inspecting any station error summaries, we documented the deviation and defined an exploratory protocol revision `s2a` that relaxes only the allowed `OFCL` interpolation gap to 12 h while keeping all other settings frozen. `s2a` is explicitly reported as an exploratory protocol revision rather than masquerading as the original pre-registered result.
- `s2a` official chain (b) at 24 h: 12/12 event windows complete, covering 29 stations across the 10 events with qualified stations; sustained wind median absolute error is 29.28% (median bias −5.10%), gust median absolute error is 23.44% (median bias −18.55%), and median landfall track error is 66.9 km (12 events). At 48 h: 11/12 windows complete, but the Nicholas `2021-09-12 00 UTC` cycle has no `OFCL` forecast points in the a-deck, leaving 9 events / 22 stations paired out of the 10 events with qualified stations; sustained wind median absolute error is 41.05% (bias −37.89%), gust is 45.53% (bias −43.87%), and median landfall track error is 103.1 km (11 events). At 72 h: 0/12 windows complete, so no aggregate station or track errors are reported. Missing windows are not treated as zero error, and partial 72 h nodes must not be substituted for full windows.
- Pangu 48 h single-event tracking test on Milton: 12 six-hourly points cover the full observation window; fetched 946,339,840 bytes via HTTP Range across 3,610 requests in 468.65 s without downloading raw multi-gigabyte files to the workstation. Landfall center error is 48.87 km vs 64.91 km for contemporaneous `OFCL`. At the sole qualified station (`PGD`), Pangu track + `OFCL` intensity yielded a sustained wind absolute error of 45.29% vs 57.92% for `OFCL` (single-event ratio 0.782), and gust errors of 49.72% vs 61.33%. This demonstrates code and bandwidth feasibility on a single event and single station, not an overall 48 h (c)/(b) ratio, non-inferiority event count, or B1 gate clearance. The tracker implements the pre-registered simplified 850 hPa circulation algorithm rather than a full reproduction of DeMaria Table A2. Remaining Pangu/FourCastNet/GraphCast cases were not completed; missing runs are neither padded with zeros nor swapped for other models.
- Across the 34 pre-identified dropout/right-censored stations: 19 have positive observed lower bounds and 15 lack usable bounds; model peaks fell below the observed lower bound at 2/19 (sustained) and 4/19 (gust) for (a), 11/19 and 13/19 for `s2a` (b) at 48 h, and 4/5 each for (c) on Milton at 48 h.
- The CIRA archive lists `NPNG`/`NGRP`/`NFOR` but provides no file-level ATCF for Milton, and all three aids have 0 entries in the NHC Milton a-deck, so no off-the-shelf historical AI tracks were obtained there. While Weather Lab documentation promises CSV/ATCF and ensemble member tracks from ~2023 onward, accessing the site redirects to Google sign-in with no saved session available, preventing verification of member counts or coverage across the 6 events; thus chain (c′) was not computed.

## Criteria and Cost
Original `s2` 48 h (c)/(b) median absolute error ratio: not computable; non-inferiority event count: not computable; formal gate verdict: undecided. This is because the pre-registered interpolation gap conflicted with actual 12 h `OFCL` nodes, Nicholas lacks 48 h `OFCL` in the fixed sample under `s2a`, and chain (c) completed only the Milton single-event test. A 1/1 single-event result must not be treated as ≥2/3, nor may Nicholas be silently dropped to alter the denominator. In v1, chain (a) sustained wind bias (+9.89%) remains within ±20%, which by itself does not constitute passing Gate B1.

This task used workstation CPU + public HTTP requests, opening zero Colab sessions and zero cluster jobs (0 CU). Network volume and wall time for the Milton AIWP file are reported above; traffic for other public dataset queries was not metered uniformly and is not claimed as 0 bytes. Figures explicitly credit NOAA NHC `OFCL`/`BEST` sources and plot only available official chains.

## Independent Decisions Needed Next
To complete a formal gate evaluation, the Lead must first confirm a new protocol version after publicly logging the invalidation of original `s2`: permitting 12 h `OFCL` interpolation and deciding how to handle Nicholas lacking a 48 h official forecast (retain as ungradable or revise the cohort years?), while keeping the original 29 stations, ±20%, 1.1×, and ≥2/3 thresholds strictly unchanged. Batch remote tracking should proceed only after the revised protocol is frozen. No criteria were altered on behalf of the Lead or Liang Hu here.

1. Adopt s2a's interpolation modification: linear interpolation is allowed when the interval between adjacent OFCL nodes is ≤12 h; the 24 h interval of 72 h spanning 72→96 h is for reporting only, allowing ≤24 h interpolation, labeled "coarse interpolation", not entering the gate; no out-of-bounds extrapolation.
2. The gate is calculated only on homogeneous events where both (b)(c) chains have inputs and have v1 qualified stations. Nicholas 48 h is recorded as "no official forecast, unevaluable", not calculated in either chain, and initialization time is not changed. Expected 9 events, 22 stations; simultaneously reported against the denominator of 10 events with qualified stations for comparison. The original 29-station set, the criteria that 48 h Pangu sustained wind all-station median absolute error ≤1.1×(b) and ≥2/3 evaluable events are not worse than (b) remain unchanged; an event not worse than is defined as within-event station |e| median ≤(b). Gusts are reported in parallel rather than selected post hoc.
3. Primary (c) = Pangu: run all events for 24 and 48 h. FourCastNet v2 and GraphCast are secondary results for 48 h only, not replacing primary gate judgment. s2's 850 hPa tracker is frozen: CARQ τ=0 seed, 850 hPa relative vorticity 5×5 smoothing, 200 km disk average, maximum positive vorticity within 350 km of previous step's center and 100–400 km cyclonic average tangential wind >0; if any 6 h point lacks positive vorticity/cyclonic circulation or jumps >350 km, the track is broken, without skipping missing points to continue, without reseeding to BEST, and without switching to MSLP minimum. Each step moves only according to already tracked points, without using future BEST.
4. (c′) Weather Lab attempts only once via public pathways requiring no login (direct download links in documentation or public storage); if login is required, record as "not obtained" and stop, without using Liang Hu's Google credentials.
5. Truncated lower bound test for the three chains (a)(b)(c) is executed per s2 frozen definition: maximum sustained/gust before reporting dropout of truncated stations serves as true peak lower bound, counting the number/proportion of stations where model peak is below lower bound; for reporting only, not entering the gate.
6. Complete this document before new (c) observation pairings; retain s2 original and s2a output. Wind field, station QC, duration conversion, pressure and scale extrapolations all follow , strictly never tuning parameters based on errors. OFCL and AI use the same initialization time and OFCL intensity; BEST is used only for post hoc track error verification, not for constructing the two forecast chains. HTTP Range limits reading of AIWP, not saving raw full files to disk.

## Additional Reporting (Supplement 7, not entering gate)
Sustained wind and gusts across the three chains (a)(b)(c) are normalized by the closest distance from station to each chain's own track and each chain's own RMW at the closest point time, categorized into <1×RMW, 1–3×RMW, >3×RMW; and binned into <50, 50–100, >100 km. Each bin reports station count, median bias, median absolute error; deliver . Boundary values are assigned to the subsequent bin; based on the shortest distance from each station to the track point of the paired window where the model peak occurs within ±12 h of landfall; if track breaks and is unavailable, it does not enter that chain's stratification. This is diagnostic, and the gate judgment will strictly never be altered based on stratification. Basis: Lead decision document lines 21–22.

Cost: Local CPU only or single-run ≤20 CU Colab CPU; stop after use. Each model/lead time reports failure/missing observation by event, strictly never treated as zero error. Code and numerical outputs are written only to s2b/ new files.

items.text:
# B1+B4 Stage 2 Protocol Modification s2b (10-14, Lead Decision)
## Situation
Stage 2 was unable to evaluate the 48 h gate, neither passing nor failing:
- The original PREREG_s2 assumed OFCL had a node every 6 h with an interpolation interval upper limit of 7 h, but OFCL longer lead times have nodes every 12 h; under the original rules, no window could be fully assembled. This point was discovered and publicly disclosed before reading any station errors (PROTOCOL_DEVIATION.md).
- Nicholas 2021-09-12 00 UTC initialization had no OFCL in the a-deck.
- Pangu only completed one case, Milton.
## Decision (Criteria unchanged: 29 stations; at 48 h, (c) median absolute error ≤ 1.1 × (b), and ≥ 2/3 events not worse than (b))
1. **Adopt s2a's interpolation modification**: Linear interpolation is allowed when adjacent OFCL nodes have intervals ≤ 12 h. This belongs to input implementation and does not involve criteria. For 72 h windows spanning into the 72→96 h 24-h interval, 72 h is for reporting only, allowing ≤ 24 h interpolation labeled "coarse interpolation", not entering the gate.
2. **Homogeneous sample**: The gate is calculated only on events where both (b)(c) chains have inputs and have qualified stations (this is standard practice for NHC/DeMaria forecast verification; cards, PDF pp. 2–5). Nicholas 48 h is recorded as "no official forecast, unevaluable", not calculated in either chain, without changing initialization time. Denominator reported truthfully: expected 9 events, 22 stations.
3. **Primary (c) remains Pangu**: Run all events for 24 and 48 h. FourCastNet v2 and GraphCast run only 48 h as secondary, each reporting one set, without picking the best to enter the gate. The tracker uses the simplified 850 hPa circulation version already written in s2, frozen without changes. Criteria for broken tracks and jumps are written into PREREG_s2b and not changed thereafter.
4. **(c′)**: Weather Lab attempts only once via public pathways requiring no login (direct download links in documentation or public storage). If login is required, record as "not obtained" and stop, **without using Liang Hu's Google credentials**.
5. **Truncated lower bound test**: Conducted for all three chains, reporting only.
6. ideas Before any new (c) observation pairing, first write the above items as-is into , with timestamps. Original s2 and s2a outputs are retained, not overwritten.
## Why
Interpolation and homogeneous samples only handle "how inputs are obtained", touching neither thresholds nor station sets. Changing initialization times or deleting events to alter the denominator are post hoc operations, so they are not done.
## Cost of Being Wrong
If the homogeneous sample is deemed to have relaxed the criteria: the denominator is only reduced from 10 events to 9, and passing the gate still requires ≥ 2/3. All results are reported truthfully, allowing re-examination against the 10-event denominator.
## Observations (Not Drawing Conclusions)
s2a's (b) 48 h sustained wind bias is −37.9% (9 events, 22 stations), much lower than (a)'s +9.9%. Among truncated stations, (b) has 11/19 stations with model peaks below the observed lower bound before reporting dropout. The reason may be track error (landfall position error median 103 km) deflecting the wind swath away from stations, or the scale persistence assumption. Basis: No literature basis, based on internal track data.

## Supplement 7 (10-14 Lab Lead requirement; report only, not entering gate)
Report bias stratified by station distance from track: conduct for all three chains (a)(b)(c), one set each for sustained wind and gusts. Distance is taken as the closest distance from the station to each chain's own track, normalized by the RMW used by each chain itself at that time, divided into three bins: <1×RMW, 1–3×RMW, >3×RMW. In addition, divide into three bins by km (<50, 50–100, >100) for comparison. Each bin reports station count, median bias, median absolute error. Basis: Node H H2 observed a v1 H08 peak bias of +2.41 m/s across 794 stations ( line 92, verified by Lead), suggesting outer wind profile or post-landfall decay is overly broad or overly strong. Written into the "Additional Reporting" section of PREREG_s2b, delivered .

## Supplement 8 (10-14 Node B Lead corrected Colab policy, per Liang Hu's original words "use Colab more at this stage, no CU limit")
The "Colab single experiment ≤20 CU" written during task dispatch is voided, no single experiment upper limit is set; if a single experiment is expected to exceed >100 CU, pause first and report to B1+B4 Lead. Must run `colab stop` when finished, no idle sessions, and dispatch only one executor per round. Sections already completed under the old limit in chunks will not be rerun; reopening sessions for merging is also unnecessary.

Pangu 24/48 h 12 events each, and FOUR 48 h 12 events all completed 850 hPa tracking and can be scored on events with OFCL; GRAP 48 h obtained 8/12 files, with the remaining 4 object requests returning 404 (including 2 primary sample cases). All were read via original code's cycle-by-cycle HTTP Range, without saving entire HDF5 files to disk. 44 successful objects cumulatively read 40,269,774,848 bytes (approx. 40.27 GB decimal), with total elapsed read time of 13,918.84 s (four-way concurrency, not wall-clock time); details , , and logs. Workstation CPU, no Colab/supercomputers, Colab cost 0 CU; USD bills for remote network were not obtained, and $0 is not claimed.

(c′) Weather Lab official documentation does not list historical direct links that can be requested anonymously; the landing page redirects to Google login. Attempted only once, stopped, and recorded as not obtained, details see . Did not use any of Liang Hu's credentials.

Model limitations: AI tracks are frozen 850 hPa simplified circulation tracking, intensity for both chains shares OFCL, future RMW/POCI are held constant, pressure is extrapolated anchored on assumptions; therefore, this only tests the effect of track swapping under shared intensity/scale and fixed H08 wind field conditions, not an end-to-end comprehensive comparison between AI and NHC operational products. OFCL is issued approx. 3 h after initialization, whereas AI corresponds to analysis time, which are not strictly identical availability times. ASOS reporting dropouts left strong wind segments unobserved; censoring tests show that the risk of underestimation cannot be generalized from qualified station scores to all nearshore stations.

Original sources: NOAA NHC HURDAT2 BEST/ATCF a-deck (. Root directory etc. are code previews during the Delta single-case period, not formal results; explanation .

One-sentence verdict: 48 h Pangu's station median absolute error ratio conforms to 1.1x, but only 5/9 events were not worse than official, failing the predetermined dual gates; under this simplified homogeneous protocol, B1 should not be converted into a conclusion that AI is superior to NHC.

## Gate Judgment: Primary (c) Pangu, 48 h
First frozen (10-14 17:25 EDT), then batch tracked/re-paired; s2 original, s2a files, and previous Milton trial calculations were not overwritten. Fixed v1's 29 qualified stations; Nicholas 48 h same-initialization lacked OFCL, judged unevaluable per Lead decision, with 9 events and 22 stations constituting the (b)/(c) homogeneous denominator. Error is model peak / fixed ASOS peak − 1, approximately a 2-minute sustained wind proxy rather than strict 1-minute wind.

| 48 h Sustained Wind | (b) OFCL | (c) Pangu |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Homogeneous sample median | e | | 41.05% | 41.91% |
| Median bias | −37.89% | −34.80% |
| (c)/(b) median | e | ratio | — | 1.0209 |
| Within-event median | e | not worse than OFCL | — | 5/9: Beryl, Helene, Ian, Milton, Nicole |

Ratio 1.0209 ≤ 1.1, satisfying the first condition; event condition requires at least 6/9, whereas 5/9 was actually obtained, so B1's 48 h dual gates were not passed. Under the original denominator of 10 events with qualified stations, it is 5/10 (falling short of 7/10); Nicholas remains unevaluable rather than a forged failure. 48 h gust: OFCL median |e| 45.53%, bias −43.87%; Pangu 42.52%, −42.52% (parallel diagnostic, not replacing primary metric).

Event-by-event sustained wind median |e| (%):

| Event (Station) | OFCL | Pangu | FOUR | GRAP |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Beryl (2) | 61.39 | 35.38 | 37.40 | 52.76 |
| Debby (3) | 42.49 | 57.40 | 55.28 | 57.69 |
| Delta (3) | 43.73 | 76.35 | 87.73 | Missing raw file |
| Francine (4) | 32.91 | 42.75 | 50.85 | 31.52 |
| Helene (1) | 46.27 | 38.23 | 50.04 | 37.25 |
| Ian (4) | 29.94 | 6.62 | 22.19 | 13.60 |
| Milton (1) | 57.92 | 45.29 | 47.46 | 33.14 |
| Nicole (2) | 19.13 | 11.65 | 21.72 | 22.23 |
| Zeta (2) | 39.85 | 65.22 | 58.02 | Missing raw file |

Secondary chain FOUR 48 h in the homogeneous 9 events / 22 stations has median |e| 49.85%, a ratio of 1.2143 relative to contemporary OFCL, with events not worse than OFCL at 3/9. GRAP encountered HTTP 404 on 2020 Delta/Zeta and 2021 Ida/Nicholas objects, obtaining only 8 full windows at 48 h, of which 7 had qualified stations / 17 stations; in its own homogeneous subsample, median |e| is 27.94%, contemporary OFCL is 41.21%, ratio 0.6779, events 5/7. GRAP lacks two primary sample cases, cannot replace Pangu for gate judgment, and its superior subsample values must not be claimed as 9-event results.

## Track and Lead Time
48 h landfall-time center absolute error median (relative to HURDAT2 BEST, km): in the primary homogeneous 9 events, OFCL 105.05, Pangu 90.90, FOUR 59.04; GRAP 58.83 across the 8 available cases (its subset of 7 with qualified stations see ). Pangu 24 h 12-event median 58.77 km, OFCL 48 h 11-event (including events without qualified stations) median 103.12 km. Station-by-point coordinates and distance to BEST for each event track are in (including (a) BEST itself, error by definition 0), per-event status in ; BEST was not used as AI or OFCL forecast input.

24 h all 29 qualified stations: Pangu sustained wind median |e| 24.87%, bias −18.04%; contemporary OFCL 29.28%, −5.10%; Pangu gust 32.63%, −31.88%, OFCL 23.44%, −18.55%. 24 h does not enter the gate.

72 h was attempted only with official OFCL using ≤24 h coarse interpolation; across 12 events, 8 had full windows, of which 6 had qualified stations / 13 stations: sustained wind median |e| 50.95%, bias −50.95%; gust 59.89%, −59.89%; 8-event landfall track error median 177.67 km. Nicole, Debby, Francine lacked full windows, Nicholas lacked initial usable input. This result is for reporting only and cannot be conflated with 48 h gate judgment; the task did not require AI 72 h.

## Truncated Lower Bound and Distance Diagnostics
v1 has 34 truncated stations in total, of which 19 stations have positive observed lower bounds. 48 h forecasts below the pre-dropout peak lower bound: sustained wind (a) 2/19, (b) 11/19, Pangu (c) 10/19; gust (a) 4/19, (b) 13/19, Pangu 12/19. FOUR 8/19, 11/19; GRAP 6/16, 8/16 (only for events with retrieved files); details for each event and 24 h see and , ; diagnostics are not used to reselect thresholds or stations.

## Availability, Cost, and Limitations
Pangu 24/48 h 12 events each, and FOUR 48 h 12 events all completed 850 hPa tracking and can be scored on events with OFCL; GRAP 48 h obtained 8/12 files, with the remaining 4 object requests returning 404 (including 2 primary sample cases). All were read via original code's cycle-by-cycle HTTP Range, without saving entire HDF5 files to disk. 44 successful objects cumulatively read 40,269,774,848 bytes (approx. 40.27 GB decimal), with total elapsed read time of 13,918.84 s (four-way concurrency, not wall-clock time); details , , and logs. Workstation CPU, no Colab/supercomputers, Colab cost 0 CU; USD bills for remote network were not obtained, and $0 is not claimed.

(c′) Weather Lab official documentation does not list historical direct links that can be requested anonymously; the landing page redirects to Google login. Attempted only once, stopped, and recorded as not obtained, details see . Did not use any of Liang Hu's credentials.

Model limitations: AI tracks are frozen 850 hPa simplified circulation tracking, intensity for both chains shares OFCL, future RMW/POCI are held constant, pressure is extrapolated anchored on assumptions; therefore, this only tests the effect of track swapping under shared intensity/scale and fixed H08 wind field conditions, not an end-to-end comprehensive comparison between AI and NHC operational products. OFCL is issued approx. 3 h after initialization, whereas AI corresponds to analysis time, which are not strictly identical availability times. ASOS reporting dropouts left strong wind segments unobserved; censoring tests show that the risk of underestimation cannot be generalized from qualified station scores to all nearshore stations.

Original sources: NOAA NHC HURDAT2 BEST/ATCF a-deck (. Root directory etc. are code previews during the Delta single-case period, not formal results; explanation .

One-sentence verdict: 48 h Pangu's station median absolute error ratio conforms to 1.1x, but only 5/9 events were not worse than official, failing the predetermined dual gates; under this simplified homogeneous protocol, B1 should not be converted into a conclusion that AI is superior to NHC.
