items.title: Verdict and shelving: B1+B4 did not pass the gate (6/6 valid, all "support with reservations" shelving)
items.text:
# Verdict and Shelving: B1+B4 Failed Gate (6/6 Valid, All "Support with Reservations" Shelving)
Reviewers: E Gemini, A GPT-6, D GLM, C DeepSeek, B Kimi, F Grok. No substitutions, no vacancies. Evidence see review cards; draft conclusions (retained as-is, subject to this document).

## Verdict (Final)
Per the publicly revised and refrozen s2b protocol, B1 did not pass the gate: 48 h homogeneous 9 events, 22 stations, Pangu/OFCL median absolute error ratio 1.021 (satisfies ≤1.1), events not worse than OFCL 5/9 (requires ≥6/9); under the original s2 10-event denominator it is 5/10 (requires ≥7/10), with Nicholas recorded as unevaluable, not counted as a failure. Both denominators fail the gate, and failure was not caused by denominator revision. B1+B4 node **Shelved**, B4 is not conducted per sequence. It cannot be stated from this that AI tracks are overall superior or inferior to NHC.

## Lead Personal Verification
- Primary gate numbers: Previously recalculated using station-by-station tables, consistent with the 6 reviewers (1.0209, 5/9, FCN2 1.214 and 3/9, GraphCast 0.678 and 5/7).
- Track error: Homogeneous 9 events, center error median at observed landfall time OFCL 105.0 km, Pangu 90.9 km (F, E correct; D, B stated 90.9 is the 11-event value, incorrect); event-by-event Pangu was closer in only 4/9 events; ±12 h average track error median OFCL 96.9, Pangu 85.7 km. Nominal 48 h actual lead time is 48.5–59 h.
- Inputs: Debby at initialization POCI−Pc = 2 hPa, RMW 75 nmi; Nicole RMW 200 nmi; Milton RMW 5 nmi (a-deck CARQ τ=0). CLIMADA H08 computes wind speed from pressure deficit (`_compute_angular_windspeeds_h08`, `_bs_holland_2008`), not using input Vmax, consistent with E's statement.

## Must Change (Implemented in this document and project page)
1. **Withdraw "Track differences are overwhelmed by small sample size and common bias"** (E-1, A-2, F-1, C). Actual situation: medians are close, but event-by-event differences are large (|Pangu−OFCL| median approx. 68 km), with Pangu closer in only 4/9 events; the lost cases Debby, Delta, Zeta all had worse Pangu tracks, whereas the won cases Helene, Nicole had worse Pangu tracks and only won because errors cancelled each other out. Thus track indeed affects station winds, but not in a consistent direction. The cause has not been isolated.
2. **Mechanism of common underestimation of −35% to −38%** (E-2; A, B requested not concluding a single cause): Candidate mechanisms include (i) Δp extrapolated from initialization Δp0 scaled by OFCL Vmax; events where storms were still weak at initialization (Debby Δp0 = 2 hPa, Francine 6 hPa) severely depress Δp at landfall; whereas H08 only uses Δp, so OFCL Vmax did not actually enter the wind field directly; (ii) RMW frozen at initialization time (Nicole 200 nmi is a giant false eye, Milton 5 nmi is a micro eye); (iii) OFCL intensity itself is underestimated (landfall Vmax median bias calculated by E is −14.9%, Lead did not recalculate); (iv) 850 hPa tracking center and near-surface wind center may have an offset (D). The relative contributions were not disentangled, **insufficient evidence**. These are all caused by input assumptions specified in s2 preregistration, not AI itself.
3. **Supplementary reporting of three items required by preregistration** (E-3, A-3, F): ±12 h average track error (see above) and actual lead times (48.5–59 h, 24 h tier actually 24.5–35.75 h) have been added. Whether the new model peak time still falls within the v1 observation window (≥648 minutes) **was not delivered**; E estimates that (b) 9/22 and (c) 7/22 station peak times fell outside v1's ±6 h window. Per protocol, stations cannot be reselected based on this, and it is written truthfully only as an interpretive limitation.
4. **Faithful representation of protocol modification** (A-1, D, F): Original s2 was unevaluable; s2a was an exploratory modification; s2b was refrozen after seeing (b) results and Milton single case (unblinded). The homogeneous denominator slightly relaxed the threshold from 7/10 to 6/9, which has been disclosed; both denominators fail the gate. What I originally wrote, "only handles inputs, does not alter denominator", was inaccurate and is corrected. Landfall error implementation used fixed landfall points from the event list rather than BEST interpolation (B), which only affects diagnostics.
5. **Limitations of distance stratification** (E-4, B, C, F): (a) distant stations +35% only has n=3, with same-tier gust at −4.8%; (c)(a) used 6 h nodes to calculate nearest distance, whereas (b) used 15 min, creating inconsistent standards that might misclassify stations. H2's +2.41 m/s is full-sample bias (794 event×station peaks, from hourly METAR, 300 km range), not distant-station stratification, and is not used for mutual corroboration.
6. **Rewriting of restart conditions** (all reviewers): GraphCast's AIWP archive only begins in 2022 and originally did not exist for 2020–21; "completing" this item is non-executable and deleted. Any of the following modifications requires **establishing a new protocol and refreezing**, and cannot overturn this gate verdict. Changing wind field models or station sets requires re-passing the (a) ±20% gate first.

## Restart Conditions (Final; open new version once satisfied, not overturning this round)
- R1 Scale and pressure inputs: replace "Δp0 scaling + RMW freeze" with operationally available methods, such as fitting Holland profiles with OFCL 34/50/64 kt wind radii, or deriving Δp from Vmax using wind-pressure relationships; or when Liang Hu's 3D boundary layer model is in place. Re-pass the (a) gate.
- R2 Event count: what failed was the event-by-event condition. The new version must have ≥15 evaluable events, with ≥3 qualified stations per event (quantitative thresholds to be determined in the new protocol). May add 2025 events, or connect to H2's multi-source station network, but observation standards must be unified.
- R3 Censoring / Truncation: there must be a solution for the issue of reporting dropouts during strong winds (34/67 stations truncated), such as multi-source station networks or designing lower bound tests to enter primary metrics.
- R4 Primary chain selection: switching to GraphCast (2022+) or using AI consensus as the primary chain must be preregistered in advance; WeatherNext Cyclones end-to-end chain (AI with its own intensity and wind radii) is a separate issue, not a restart of B1, and data must be obtainable without login.
- Availability timestamp: OFCL is issued approx. 3 h later than AI; the new version must specify whether to correct for this.

## For Reference Only
- D, B: 24 h is reported only without entering the gate; Pangu 0.85 but events 4/10; in 22 station pairings Pangu won 12 stations (sign test p ≈ 0.83)—the two chains have no substantive difference across stations.
- C: Landfall errors for FCN2 and GraphCast are both approx. 59 km, yet station errors differ by nearly a factor of two, indicating that error at landfall time alone cannot explain station winds.
- A: In code, the interpolation upper limit is 13/25 h, and distance bin boundary assignments differ subtly from protocol text, with insufficient evidence of impact.
- B: The draft wrote "35–38%", which is actually −34.8%/−37.9%.

## Unadopted Objections
- E recalculated using BEST intensity plus both chain tracks (Pangu ratio 1.188, 3/9): this is a new standard, not in the protocol, not used as criteria, and serves only as collateral evidence that "track indeed has an impact" (Lead did not recalculate).
- No reviewer advocated against shelving; "run supplementary runs before deciding" was not adopted—both F and E pointed out that there is no test within the protocol that could overturn the primary gate, and supplementary runs require a new protocol.

## Literature Basis
Nearby precedent cards see project page (DeMaria 2009/2013, Alet 2026, Lai 2025, Wu 2026). This conclusion has no literature basis, based on internal track data.
## Cost of Being Wrong
Shelving deletes nothing: scripts, trackers, event lists, pairing code are all kept; opening a new version per R1/R2 is estimated at 1–2 days and a few Colab CUs.

# Post-Shelving of B1+B4: Dispatch v2 Feasibility Check; Node B to First Launch Grok Quick Search (2026-10-14)

## Facts (Verified by Node B Lead)
48 h homogeneous 9 events 22 stations: Pangu/OFCL median absolute error ratio 1.0209 (≤1.1 pass), events 5/9 (requires 6/9) → did not pass gate; median bias of both chains −34.8% / −37.9%. Review (6/6) supports shelving; restart conditions R1–R4 see .

## Decision I made
1. Accept shelving; this round's gate verdict is not overturned.
2. Dispatch B1+B4 to conduct v2 feasibility check (produce documents only, do not run new pairings, do not judge gates): whether R2 can assemble ≥15 evaluable events with ≥3 stations per event; select an operationally available scale/pressure input for R1 and first pass the (a) gate; draft unfrozen PREREG_v2.
 - Why: v1 did not answer "is the AI track chain useful"—both chains were depressed by 35–38% by preregistered input assumptions, obscuring the impact of track; B is Liang Hu's primary research direction, and the check only requires a few CUs and 1–2 days. Basis: No literature basis, based on internal track data.
 - Cost of being wrong: If the check indicates not enough events can be gathered or R1 has no feasible method, 1–2 days of bot time are wasted; v1 conclusions are unaffected (new version requires a new event set and newly frozen protocol, and must not overturn this round).
3. For B2, Node B will first launch a Grok quick search (AI-generated synthetic typhoons and design wind speeds); open node only after having a clear direction; Deep Research quota exhausted, step two temporarily deferred.
 - Why: B1 already has results, and per node page agreement B2 can get started; only incurs subscription quota. Cost of being wrong: One quick search.

items.text:
# B1 v2 Protocol Draft — Unfrozen

Time: 10-14 20:31 EDT. This document is merely a project initiation feasibility plan, and running new (b)(c) station pairings or announcing a gate verdict based on it is prohibited. The original s2b verdict text is unaffected. Refer to the event-by-event inventory of , the original , the project page, and the review verdict.

## Prerequisite Go/No-Go (Finalized by Lead Prior to Official v2)

R1: Prove that each input is operationally available at decision time and capable of providing ΔP/RMW/B required by H08; fix the environmental GFS product release time, KZ07's V500/Penv annulus calculation, OFCL wind radii applicability levels, and missing wind radii rules; determine weights/ranges independently, without fitting to station errors. R2: Approve homogeneous observation station classes and confirm event-by-event at least 15 evaluable events with at least 3 stations per event; currently there are only 7 pre-screened 1-min candidates, with a potential 14 in the hourly pool, and hourly verification for Eta has not yet been conducted. R3: The censoring scheme must be registered in advance and executable. R4: The primary chain defaults to the Pangu 850 hPa circulation track; if changed to GraphCast or AI consensus, pre-registration must be revised prior to any new pairing and explain the 2020–21 gap; do not modify the primary chain based on having seen the results.

## Units, Samples, and Homogeneous Denominator

Landfall event definitions follow the feasibility table; for multiple landfalls, freeze the primary landfall point/UTC time first, and switching to secondary landfalls after seeing errors is prohibited. Fix the 150 km radius from the center and the landfall ±12 h target window, and provide in advance the actual initialization lead time and object list for each event. Separately register station proximity, platform/land, sensor 10m height, HAS1MIN, presence of valid minutes/hours, observation averaging interval, and wind direction exposure. The primary analysis is recommended to use only complete 1-minute ASOS (`sknt` ~2-min sustained wind, `gust_sknt` 5-s reported peak); if R2 requires H2 hourly stations due to insufficient sample size, an "hourly homogeneous primary analysis" must first be separately frozen, synchronously downsampling v1 1-minute data and re-evaluating (a); the two densities cannot be pooled together to calculate a single median. ERA5 cannot be treated as independent station observations. The denominator is the event intersection where both Pangu and OFCL exist for the same initialization, the same batch of observations is qualified for both chains, and peak window checks are completed; the ex-ante list and all missing measurement reasons and station counts per category must be fully listed; events lacking official forecasts, such as Nicholas, must not be treated as forecast failures, nor should cycles be swapped to make up for them. Report both the intention-to-evaluate full event set denominator and the homogeneous evaluable denominator—provide both, and do not cherry-pick the denominator that favors the conclusion.

## Models and Operational Timing

(a) BEST center and intensity, using archived BEST wind radii as the post-hoc physical upper-bound chain, following the exact same pressure/scale solver and station exposure and averaging interval as (b)(c); missing values must not inversely draw on (b) intelligence. Freeze the model, error windows, and parameters first, and then run only (a): sustained wind ratio error median bias  must be within ±20%, reporting both absolute error and gusts, with station-by-station auditing; if disqualified, stop (b)(c). Passing the gate under the old (a) cannot replace passing the gate under new inputs.

(b) NHC official OFCL track and intensity, and wind radii issued at that time; (c) Pangu 850 hPa positive vorticity + tangential circulation tracking track, **sharing (b)'s official intensity and identical pressure/scale inputs**, strictly never reading post-hoc b-decks. First constrain symmetric outer scale using OFCL 34/50/64 kt wind radii, with Knaff et al. 2007 North Atlantic climatological RMW as a prior rather than case-by-case ground truth; Knaff–Zehr 2007 ΔP formula must use large-scale S/V500/Penv from GFS that was already available at the time, and wind radii must not be disguised as S. When wind radii are only 34 kt, Penv or V500 is missing, or H08 RMW/B cannot be fitted, halt the chain for that event/node according to the frozen missing-data scheme or use a pre-specified climatological value labeled "assumption", without back-deriving from station errors. Card PDF 3–4, 6 / Journal 783–784, 786;  PDF 4–5, 10 / Journal 74–75, 80. If H08/land-sea conversion and ~2-min/5-s factors follow v1, retaining them remains an assumption; if modified, the new parameter table must first state the source, range, and sensitivity.

OFCL is typically publicly released about 3 h after the corresponding AIWP 00/12 initialization, and cannot be treated as available at the same moment as the AI initialization. At the frozen common decision time T = actual public release date/time of OFCL for that cycle, compare (b) and (c) both using the latest official intensity and wind radii available before T, and AI using the 00/12 initialization already available before T along with its release time; for each event, record AIWP model initialization, object release time, OFCL release, decision T, and remaining hours until actual landfall. Historical actual release time cannot be presumed from archive filenames. Report actual lead times paired with the same cycle initialization and an "AI available earlier" sensitivity analysis, neither allowing AI to surreptitiously use initializations after decision time nor claiming that both chains share the same release timestamp. Track errors at ±12 h and track error at landfall time are reported independently; BEST is used only for post-hoc scoring.

## Station Peaks, Censoring, and Scoring

Pre-specify station observation completeness thresholds and physical QC (following v1 if applicable: at least 90% valid minutes within model peak t* ± 6 h, with valid records at start and end; for hourly stations, separately specify coverage and boundary conditions), and define uniform window expansion rules if the model peak shifts outside the original download window. All three chains use the same intersection of qualified stations; if t* positions differ across the three chains, record t*, window inclusion, and censoring reasons chain-by-chain; the comparison window must be the same pre-defined event window, rather than cherry-picking observed peaks favorable to each. Incomplete observations are assigned a lower bound `obs_true_peak≥obs_observed_peak`: report primary estimates for complete stations alongside interval/lower-bound sensitivities for censored stations; when right-censoring does not provide a physical upper bound, calculating a fictitious finite median is not permitted. Completeness rates are stratified by event, distance to eye, and forecast peak time difference, clarifying that missingness is not random. Gusts and sustained winds are reported separately; do not treat 5-s gusts as 2-min winds.

The primary criterion follows the project page, unchanged: 48 h homogeneous stations (c)/(b) ≤ 1.1, and in at least 2/3 of homogeneous evaluable events, the within-event station absolute error median has (c) ≤ (b); on the premise of (a) bias ±20%. 24/72 h, gusts, track errors, three-chain censoring lower bounds, and full event set denominator are reported only and not cherry-picked into the primary gate. If the Lead considers adjusting 1.1 or 2/3, this constitutes another scientific criterion and must be decided prior to freezing by the Lead/Liang Hu according to established authority; this draft does not alter it arbitrarily. If fewer than 15 events each with ≥3 stations, do not evaluate the v2 gate, and only report the feasibility gap.

## Fields That Must Be Completed in the Official Pre-registration First

1. Event list/primary landfall, event-by-event 48 h AIWP and OFCL specific initialization + release times, intensity/wind radii valid nodes, GFS operational products at the time and historical availability timestamps.
2. Actual optimization objectives, weights, constraints, missing-threshold fallbacks, and sensitivity ranges from OFCL wind radii to H08 RMW/B; identical algorithm for BEST wind radii and rules for events without radii, with parameter source table noting paper page numbers or "assumption" item by item.
3. Homogeneous observation station table and 10m height, 2-min/5-s averaging intervals, exposure and hourly sampling consistency; reports by event and station for three-chain censoring and "whether new model peak t* falls within complete observation window".
4. Actual lead time, ±12 h track error, landfall center error, observed lower bound violation rate; both denominators for all events and homogeneous intersection, tracking all failures/missing data.

Cost: This round is document design only, local CPU; Colab 0 CU. Prior to official batch processing, estimate CU based on sample size/HTTP Range request volume, and stop Colab after use; do not download raw complete AIWP files to the  workstation.

# B1 v2 可行性核查（只数事件和观测可用性，不做新预报站点配对）

时间：10-14 20:31 EDT。依据：；原 s2b 失败判词保留，不能以本核查翻案。可复核原始元数据：同目录，对应生成脚本 与。无新 (a)/(b)/(c) 观测配对。

## R2：样本可得性与定义

从 NHC 2026-09-23 版 HURDAT2 中筛 2020-10 后美国本土首次显著登陆：登陆标志 L、登陆时 HU 或强 TS（预筛定义 Vmax≥50 kt）；同一事件多次登陆只计一次，以主美国本土登陆为锚。原来的 12 个事件加 7 个新候选，共 19 个；2025 本土 Chantal 为 45 kt，故在本预筛定义下没有新增符合的 2025 个例。这个 ≥50 kt 是本次候选界定，不是重新冻结的科学判据；若 Lead 希望包括较弱 TS，应另列敏感集合。2020-10 之前事件不在 AIWP 覆盖范围内。来源：NHC HURDAT2 上述版本及原。

| Harold (2023) | 是 / 否 | 5/9 | 未建 H2 事件 | 缺同起报 OFCL，排除主对比 |
| Idalia (2023) | 是 / 是 | 0 | 10 | 仅小时池可候选 |
| Ophelia (2023) | 是 / 否 | 6/7 | 未建 H2 事件 | 缺同起报 OFCL，排除主对比 |
| Beryl (2024) | 是 / 是 | 2 | 12 | 仅小时池可候选 |
| Debby (2024) | 是 / 是 | 3 | 12 | 严格 1min 可候选 |
| Francine (2024) | 是 / 是 | 4 | 5 | 严格 1min 可候选 |
| Helene (2024) | 是 / 是 | 1 | 8 | 仅小时池可候选 |
| Milton (2024) | 是 / 是 | 1 | 6 | 仅小时池可候选 |

分母解读：旧事件 1min 列是 v1 的模型峰窗口 ±6 h 完整性和物理 QC 后正式站数（并非纯观测可用性）；新事件只是登陆锚点 ±6h、有效持续风独立分钟数 ≥648 的观测可用性代理，尚未做峰值落窗及物理 QC。不同定义不可当作同等级的“合格站”相加。按更严的旧正式站数 + 新可用性代理，有 OFCL/Pangu 同起报且至少 3 站的候选是旧 4（Delta/Ian/Debby/Francine；Nicholas 虽 7 站但无同起报 OFCL）、新 3，共 **7 个预筛候选**；不是 7 个已确认 v2 可评事件。新候选全部要求在冻结后按新模型峰时补齐观测窗。

H2 与 用原有小时 METAR、有效小时≥75% 且原 H08 模型峰±2h 有报的幸存站；逐站与 H2 站表交集，再筛原登陆点 150 km，得到旧 12 个全都有≥3 小时站，但 Nicholas 无 OFCL，故仅 **11 个**可作新口径候选。与新事件 Elsa/Fred/Henri 三例 1min 预筛相加，宽松潜在集合 14 个；Eta 有 OFCL/Pangu，但本次 1min 站 0/8，须另外以 H2 小时网证实才能使候选数触到 15。不能把未做的 Eta 小时核查当作已可评，也不能把 300 km 的 H2 汇总 794 站当作 150 km 的同质站网。即使 15 个潜在候选成立，重过 (a) 和逐站同质 QC 后还可能减少。当前 **未证明达到 R2 的 ≥15 个可评事件且每事件≥3 合格站**。

H2 并非另一种独立风速传感器网络：H2 主要是 IEM 小时 ASOS/METAR 的更广站点池和 ERA5 背景，ERA5 是再分析/模型而非独立站点真值，WorldCover 是地表类。1min ASOS 的 `sknt` 是约 2min 持续风，`gust_sknt` 是 5s 峰；小时 METAR `sknt` 是报时前约 2min 平均、`gust` 是报时前窗口内约 5s 峰值报告而非连续逐分钟峰。均需同站高度/传感器、站点海陆与风向暴露、时距一致，并以站元数据核查 10m 基准；不能把小时 METAR 峰值与分钟峰值不经抽样校正混合。H2 的小时入选率不是 v1 分钟截尾的替代；同一分钟资料降采样成小时，测量时距可相同但极值采样密度不同。建议只设分层主分析（同一时间采样/站类）和分别报告的副分析，不混成一个站点绝对误差中位数。小时池的独立性/ASOS 与 AWOS 身份、真 10 m 高度须逐站核。

## R1：输入路线选择与未闭合项

选“业务 OFCL 风圈 + 强度 + 大尺度环境场”的组合，而不是事后 BEST RMW/POCI，也不把西北太平洋 AH77 的幂指数搬来大西洋：

1. 对 (b)(c) 同起报、同核算时间使用已发布 OFCL Vmax、位置、平移速度、34/50/64 kt 四象限半径；先以 Knaff et al. 2007 的北大西洋气候 RMW 初值 `r_mc=36.1000−0.0492 Vmax+0.5740(lat−25)` 海里，以及 `x_c=0.1147+0.0055 Vmax−0.0010(lat−25)`。Vmax 单位 kt；这是气候先验，不是逐案观测 RMW。再用非零 OFCL 风圈约束对称外侧尺度（以四象限残差留痕，只有 34 kt 的 Fred 不可声称完整识别 RMW）。Rankine x 不能直接当 Holland B。出处：卡，PDF 第 3–4、6 页/期刊第 783–784、786 页。
2. ΔP 候选用 Knaff–Zehr 2007 式 7：`Vsrm=Vmax−1.5 c^0.63`； hPa。Vmax、c 为 kt，V500 为 400–600 km 环带切向风，Penv 为 800–1000 km 环带平均 MSLP。**S 不是 OFCL 风圈，不能设成 R34/RMW**。气压中心，PDF 第 4–5、10、14 页/期刊第 74–75、80、84 页，原文独立样本气压 MAE 5.30 hPa（不保证本站风误差）。
3. 把 RMW 初值与 ΔP、OFCL 风圈带入已选 H08 的前向风速方程，针对可用阈值半径做有界目标拟合 RMW 与 Holland B，强度作约束，优先保留物理可解释的 RMW/B 范围。**此 Holland 逆问题及目标权重/上下界尚无文献给出的通用常数；这一步是拟议的工程假设，不是 Knaff 原法**。必须在接触 v2 的 (a) 站点误差前，从独立的 BEST 强度/风圈资料或文献给定范围预定目标函数、惩罚与缺失风圈规则，给敏感区间；风圈不全则标识不可识别或切回预注册的气候 RMW 先验。不得从站点风调参。

参数来源表：Vmax/轨迹/风圈来自同起报 OFCL a-deck（新事件）；要换须另开 v2 前冻结。

## (a) 重过闸与截尾

先单独冻结 v2 输入/风场/观测定义：BEST 事后轨迹作为 (a) 的中心和强度，BEST 当时风圈或扩展最佳路径风圈同一拟合器和缺测规则，绝不拿预报链独有的未来信息反灌；不可用的 BEST 风圈要保留缺测，缺失机制对齐。锁定同一站点高度、观测时距、海陆暴露和新峰值窗，先只跑 (a)；持续风站点 必须在 ±20%，同时报中位绝对误差、分事件结果和阵风副指标；未过就停止，不跑 (b)(c)。v1 曾通过的 (a) 不能自动继承到换输入/站池的 v2。

截尾按预测峰时刻与观测窗口完整性预先定义可比较站；若在强风段断报，不以已观测最大值当真峰，标右截尾/下限 `true_peak≥observed_max`，主估计可采用预注册区间型损失并给最乐观/最悲观边界，另报完全观测子集；未知上界不得凭空当有限区间。模型峰 t* 超出已取观测窗，按事前统一扩展窗口取数或记不可评，不能按哪条链的成绩来选站。多链使用同一交集、逐事件截尾数、真实峰下限和两链峰时错位表均必报。

## 结论与花费

**不值得现在启动 v2 正式判闸**：严格 1min 仅 7 个预筛候选；宽松 H2 小时站已有 14 个潜在候选，Eta 尚可能补至 15 但没核实，且小时峰与分钟峰不可无校准混算；R1 的环境场业务可得性和 Holland 拟合闭合也待冻结。值得仅做定向的 Eta 小时站完整性、GFS 归档发布时间和 (a) 前向公式审计，满足 R1–R3 后再决定正式 v2。预计后续元数据核查为本地 CPU 小任务；正式 AIWP 路径链的网络/CPU 工作量可参照 s2b 读取 40.27 GB，具体 CU 在协议和候选站固定后估算，不预支。本次仅本地 CPU 与 HTTP 元数据/1min 下载，没有 Colab 会话，0 CU；网络美元费用未计量。

引用：NHC HURDAT2 https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/hurdat/hurdat2-1851-2025-092326.txt；ATCF https://ftp.nhc.noaa.gov/atcf/archive/；AIWP https://noaa-oar-mlwp-data.s3.amazonaws.com/；IEM https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/asos/1min.phtml。外部来源在 已登记，新用的 Knaff et al. 2007 风圈文献已追加。

# After B1+B4 v2 Feasibility Report: Do Not Open v2 Gate Evaluation, Dispatch Hourly Homogeneous Pool Targeted Verification (2026-10-14)

## Facts (Verified)
- 19 CONUS landfalls ≥50 kt after 2020-10 (HURDAT2 2026-09-23 edition, including the 12 old ones); all have Pangu 48 h objects; Mindy/Nicholas/Harold/Ophelia lack same-cycle OFCL.
- Minute ASOS (≥3 stations): 7 pre-screened candidates (4 old + 3 new). Hourly stations 150 km: all 12 old have ≥3 stations, removing Nicholas leaves 11; adding 3 new yields a potential 14, Eta unverified. Sampling densities for hourly and minute peaks differ and cannot be pooled.
- R1: OFCL wind radii + Knaff 2007 RMW prior (Card ZPYAUTZG, PDF pp. 3–4, 6) + Knaff–Zehr 2007 ΔP Eq. 7 (Card D8NBE3ZE, PDF pp. 4–5), requiring V500 and Penv from GFS operational fields; wind radii → Holland RMW/B inverse fitting lacks a universal method in the literature and is an engineering assumption.

## Decision I made
1. Do not open v2 gate evaluation, keep node Shelved;  is not frozen.
 - Why: R2 (≥15 events × ≥3 stations, set by review ) not satisfied; R1 environmental field availability unproven.
2. Dispatch ideas to conduct 0 CU targeted verification: single hourly sampling standard, recalculate 150 km station counts using the same script (11 old + Eta/Elsa/Fred/Henri + 2026 season operational best track landfalls), and actually read GFS archives to verify V500/Penv are computable.
 - Why: The hourly standard is the only path that might gather 15 and remain homogeneous; the 2026 season (not yet in HURDAT2) may supplement events. Basis: No literature basis, based on data from this line.
 - Cost of being wrong: One or two hours of bot time, 0 CU; if still <15, node remains Shelved, and a restart condition is added: "recount after 2026 season HURDAT2 is released".
3. Criteria unchanged (1.1, 2/3, ±20%, ≥15×≥3); if switching to hourly standard as primary analysis, official v2 must re-evaluate the gate for (a) using the same hourly standard.

All 15 candidate events for 2020–24 have at least 3 stations, along with same-cycle Pangu objects and OFCL; totaling 170 station-events passing the hourly completeness proxy. This reaches R2's "15 events × ≥3 stations" quantity pre-screening threshold, but these are not 15 final evaluable events that have passed new model peak windows, ASOS/AWOS identity, height, and physical QC; the official denominator remains unlocked. Isaias has 8 stations, but the S3 exact prefix KeyCount=0 for Pangu's corresponding 2026-10-08 00 UTC object; hence it cannot be added to the primary chain to make 16.  saves exact keys, initializations, and GFS index verifications event by event; 2026 same-cycle OFCL f048 indeed has records in the current NHC aid_public a-deck.

For the 2026 season, checking NHC operational b-decks listed at the time from `bal01`–: Chantal landfall was 45 kt, adding no cases ≥50 kt. To avoid mixing in weak-wind landfalls, the task specification's "Vmax ≥ 50 kt at landfall" is adopted, not lifetime peak ≥50 kt.

R1: The three 48 h GFS f048 environmental field variables for Fred and Milton have been actually read via Range and V500/Penv computed (see ); among the 15 candidates, AWS `.idx` exists for 12, while the three 2020 cases Delta/Zeta/Eta have AWS paths returning 404, covered by NCAR GDEX metadata but not actually read in this round, nor were actual operational release times verified case by case. The original definition of Knaff–Zehr 2007 is found in Card D8NBE3ZE PDF pp. 5, 10 / Journal pp. 75, 80. 15 is just barely reaching the quantitative pre-screening, and if any single one is disqualified due to station class, height, new peak window, physical QC, or historical environmental field timestamp, it will fall below 15, so opening (b)(c) gate evaluation prematurely is not permitted.

Decision: Worth continuing "official v2 prerequisite verification", but not worth directly opening v2 gate evaluation now. Complete the credential-less access for the three 2020 GDEX cycles, operational time availability evidence, and instrument station class/height first, then lock homogeneous stations, peak windows, and model constants, and redo the (a) ±20% gate; if the gate does not pass, do not run (b)(c). # B1+B4 v2b: Hourly Homogeneous Pool Exactly 15 Cases, Finalize Pre-registration After Completing Prerequisites (2026-10-14)

## Facts (Verified)
- Single hourly METAR standard (150 km, landfall ±12 h ≥75% valid hours): all 15 events for 2020–24 have ≥3 stations, same-cycle Pangu and OFCL both present; margin is 0. Station classes (ASOS/AWOS) and anemometer heights unverified.
- In the 2026 season, only Isaias is a US landfall ≥50 kt, but AIWP lacks the corresponding Pangu object.
- GFS f048: 12 cases accessible for 2021–24, Fred/Milton actually read to compute V500/Penv; the three 2020 cases are AWS 404. V500 used 10 m wind; Card D8NBE3ZE only states "400–600 km annulus mean tangential wind" without specifying vertical level, needing to verify original text (no literature basis confirming level, pending investigation).

## Decision I made
1. Still do not evaluate the gate, do not run (a). Dispatch ideas  (0 CU) to complete 2020 environmental fields, V500 level, unified operational timing rules (following NCEP release schedule, without checking timestamps case by case), station-by-station station class and height QC, Isaias , and produce freezable ; after freezing, run only the ±20% gate of (a) first.
 - Why: Quantity just barely met the standard; any single case disqualified fails R2; all rules and denominators must be fixed before seeing any errors.
 - Cost of being wrong: Half a day of bot time, 0 CU; if fewer than 15 cases remain after QC, write "do not evaluate gate" according to pre-registration, node remains Shelved, recount after 2026 season enters HURDAT2 and AIWP is completed.
2. Lock down in advance: do not evaluate the gate if fewer than 15 events × ≥3 stations remain after QC; criteria 1.1, 2/3, ±20%, ≥15×≥3 remain untouched.

items.title: B1 v2 pre-registration final-draft candidate — not frozen by the Lead; running is prohibited
items.text:
# B1 v2 Pre-registration Finalization Candidate — Not Frozen by Lead, Execution Prohibited

Time: 10-14 22:17 (EDT). Stipulates only the next round of experiments; the published failed-gate results of s2b remain unchanged. No new station wind field pairings were performed in this round. The current R2 station pool for this candidate is not yet closed and cannot serve as an approved official pre-registration. Decision authority rests with the Lead.

## Fixed Gates and Sequence of Execution

The primary pool uses only hourly METAR, IEM `report_type=3` (no mixing with 1-minute data); 15 US landfall events with at least 3 evaluable qualified stations per event, otherwise do not evaluate the v2 gate. Run BEST (a) first using the identical wind field and identical hourly standard, with the median bias of predicted/observed peak ratio minus one at each station within ±20% as a prerequisite; stop if failed, without running (b)(c). Only after passing is the 48 h comparison conducted: ratio of homogeneous station median absolute errors for Pangu (c)/OFCL (b) ≤ 1.1, and in ≥2/3 of homogeneous evaluable events, (c) is no worse than (b) individually; both conditions must be satisfied. B4 is performed only after B1 passes the gate. 24/72 h, gusts, and track errors are diagnostic only. Denominators for both the full intention-to-evaluate set and evaluable intersection are reported, without cherry-picking favorable subsets. Original project page  lines 15–20.

## Events, Timing, and Leakage Defenses

Intended events and landfall points/times follow the 15 cases of 2020–24 from v2b; primary station candidates are those in that table with `hourly_75pct=Trueinit+3h`, but actual archived bulletin release times must be verified by the Lead prior to freezing; actual lead time relative to real landfall is reported separately. **Post-hoc RMW, Pc, POCI, and wind radii from b-deck BEST must not be provided to (b)(c)**; BEST is used only for (a) and post-hoc verification. (b) and (c) share the same-cycle official Vmax/wind radii, pressure deficit/scale, using OFCL/Pangu 850 hPa circulation tracking respectively only for tracks; tracking algorithms follow s2b, without cherry-picking optimal post-hoc tracks. If a valid node in OFFICIAL lacks necessary intensity or cannot obtain GFS fields, that node is treated as missing, without filling gaps using post-hoc data; if any critical node in the peak window is missing, the event is marked as input un-evaluable. OFCL 12 h nodes are linearly interpolated following s2b, without endpoint extrapolation; each node maintains an input availability timestamp.

GFS: NCEP/NCO provides a rolling 30-day average: 00/12 UTC GFS 48 h products are released approximately 03:51 after initialization, 06 UTC at approximately 09:49, and 18 UTC at approximately 21:51; these are not the actual release times on each historical day. Pre-emptively assume conservatively that **the moment when all required GFS forecast lead-time fields are fully public = initialization + 4 h 15 min** (allowing approximately 24 min extra beyond the statistical average; daily anomalous delays require separate review of historical records and cannot be claimed as truly released). Prior to decision T, select the most recent cycle that has already reached +4h15 by T; in cases where T = 3 h after 00/12 initialization, uniformly fall back to the preceding 18/06 UTC cycle, with the forecast lead time for the corresponding valid time being +6 h relative to the original cycle; the 48 h point becomes f054.  lists event-by-event cycles. Retrieve lead times/fields node by node anew according to the same rules, without using newer cycles released in the future. GDEX d084001 2020 0.25° and AWS GFS 2021–24 0.5° differ in grid resolution (non-homogeneous inputs) and require dual-resolution sensitivity checks; the three 2020 cases have now been actually read anonymously, but their 2020 historical release times have not been audited case by case. Current GDEX file times cannot be taken as historical public release times. The NCEP page serves as the basis for published rules rather than historical real-time auditing.

## Scale and Pressure Deficit (Strictly Never Back-Calibrated from Stations)

Knaff–Zehr (2007), Card , PDF pp. 4–5, 10 / Journal pp. 74–75, 80: Vmax=10m/1min kt, translation c kt, Vsrm=Vmax−1.5 c^0.63; Penv is mean sea level pressure in the 800–1000 km annulus around the center in hPa; V500 is 400–600 km annulus mean tangential wind in kt, S=V500/V500c; V500c=Vmax(Rmax/500)^x, x=0.1147+0.0055Vmax−0.001(φ−25), Rmax=66.785−0.09102Vmax+1.0619(φ−25) km. Eq. (7): Pc=Penv+23.286−0.483Vsrm−(Vsrm/24.254)^2−12.587S−0.483φ; ΔP=Penv−Pc. **V500 wind level**: KZ07 original text PDF p. 5 only specifies "400–600-km-annulus-mean tangential wind from the NCEP analyses", and the main text does not explicitly specify 850 hPa; one cannot falsely claim it wrote 850. The abstract/methodology of related Knaff et al. (2014) original text writes 850 hPa V500, citing the precedent of Knaff–Zehr (2007), https://doi.org/10.1175/JCLI-D-13-00096.1; this experiment is operationally fixed to GFS 850 hPa U/V, clarified as a reasonable layer selection following the same series of methods, not a direct specification in the original KZ07 text. v2b mistakenly used 10m wind, and v2c has been verified against actual GRIB at 850 hPa. Wind field four quadrants cannot be directly taken as S; KZ climatological Rmax is not case-by-case observed RMW. When encountering Vmax < 15 kt or V500c ≤ 0, ΔP ≤ 0, or corrupted fields, nodes are treated as missing data, without trimming into "seemingly reasonable" pressure deficits. The two grid resolutions of large-scale S serve as diagnostics; relative winds are calculated against the frozen identical official center, without using BEST center in the operational chain.

RMW prior comes from Knaff et al. (2007) Card , PDF pp. 3–4, 6 / Journal pp. 783–784, 786: North Atlantic rmc=36.1000−0.0492Vmax+0.5740(φ−25) nmi. Rankine x and Holland B in this paper **are not the same number**. H08 and roughness/averaging interval follow v1 CLIMADA 6.1.0 fixed commit bb9595, Natural Earth 10m land, z0 sea 0.0013m/land 0.03m/reference 500m, sustained × 0.97, gusts land × 1.30/sea × 1.20; these remain assumptions, with ranges and grounds see  lines 5–11.

**Proposed frozen engineering assumption for wind radii → H08 scale fitting (still requiring unit testing without observations)**: CLIMADA v6.1.0 H08 `_bs_holland_2008` computes `hol_b` based on pressure deficit, pressure rate of change, latitude, and translational velocity; `_v_max_s_holland_2008` then recomputes based on that B and pressure deficit `vmaxΣ_k w_k / N_k × Σ_q(log(r_pred,k/r_obs,kq))² + 0.25(log(r/rmc))²`, w_34/50/64=1/2/3 (engineering assumption), where N_k is the number of valid quadrants for that threshold; do not sneakily adjust H08 B for "asymmetric radii". Prune nodes with r ≤ 0, threshold ≥ operational Vmax, requiring at least two different thresholds each having ≥2 quadrants, ΔP > 0, rmc ∈ [5, 200] nmi; remaining nodes are missing, with no implicit fallbacks. Proposed sensitivities: r lower bound 3–10, upper bound 150–250 nmi, prior coefficient 0.1–1, equal threshold weighting vs 1/2/3; report only, strictly never cherry-picking based on station errors. **Numerical identity between CLIMADA H08's actual radial function and this offline fitter must still be verified**, which is stricter than syntax checking; unverified experiments cannot be frozen as executable. (a) BEST also uses the same RMW fitting rules and independent BEST wind radii/center/intensity, without borrowing OFCL to fill holes.

## Primary Observations, Censoring, and Scoring

Candidate station equipment prerequisite rules: include only stations explicitly verified as ASOS on the event date with anemometer height verifiable at 8–12 m during the event (8–12 m is an engineering assumption for "close to 10m", with a range of 9–11 m for sensitivity; stations where identity/height cannot be found or having only 2025 snapshots without historical lineage do not enter the **confirmed** sample). AWOS is not included in this edition's primary pool even if height is 10m, to avoid differing equipment standards; listing separate alternative sensitivities requires a new protocol and cannot be added post-hoc to make up numbers. Sources prioritize NCEI HOMR event date ; 2025 snapshot heights in  cannot prove heights for 2020–24. Under this strict rule, 15×3 is currently not confirmed, and **gate evaluation is prohibited**.

Observations follow IEM hourly `report_type=3`, deduplicated to UTC hourly grid, `sknt≥0e=pred_peak/obs_peak−1`; take station then event median, with the primary statistic being the whole-pool median of |e| across stations, and event win/loss compared by within-event median of station-level |e|. Sustained wind serves as the primary gate; gusts are reported alongside and do not substitute. Best track (a) is recalculated using these exact same observation rules and candidate stations, and passing the gate in old 1-minute v1 must never be carried over.

## Unclosed Pre-freeze Verifications

1. Station-by-station HOMR historical heights are currently **incomplete**, and existing 2025 NWS equipment snapshots are insufficient; the conservative confirmed count is 0 (this indicates "evidence not yet confirmed" rather than asserting all stations are unqualified), with conditional snapshots yielding ≥3 stations for only 13 events, falling short for Delta and Milton. The Lead needs to decide whether to supplement historical metadata, legitimately expand homogeneous station types in advance, or halt; R2 15×3 cannot be altered without Liang Hu.
2. The original s2b `init+3h` is merely an assumed uniform public bulletin release time, not verified case by case against historical bulletins; NCEP rolling averages do not guarantee that every GFS field in 2020–24 was actually released prior to T. If unverifiable, be sure to label as "conservative operational timing proxy", and do not write that it has been verified case by case.
3. The coupling between the currently proposed fitter and CLIMADA H08's B calculation needs source code/unit test verification; whether events and nodes lacking complete wind radii lead to <15×3 remains unverified.  is only candidate fitter and pre-validation scripts; running (a) is prohibited after syntax checking.

# B1 v2c Pre-check (10-14 22:20 EDT)

No new (a)(b)(c) model wind–station pairings were executed, nor were gates evaluated. Conclusion: **Currently, v2 preregistration cannot be frozen as an executable version**; the 2020 three-case GFS fields can be read, but neither strict historical equipment height QC nor H08 parameter adaptation has been closed yet.

1. 2020 three-case operational environmental fields: GDEX d084001 anonymous HTTPS full GRIB2 decoded in memory (no large files retained); Delta 20201007 06Z f054: 850 hPa V500 22.315 kt, Penv 1013.311 hPa; Zeta 20201026 06Z f054: 14.366 kt, 1012.218 hPa; Eta 20201106 18Z f054: 31.168 kt, 1013.363 hPa. The center uses the then-current OFCL f048 position, sampling GFS U/V 850 hPa and MSLP only at the forecast valid time. Actual transfer was 1,023,692,184 bytes, taking 13.93/23.28/22.89 seconds for the three cases respectively. The GRIB fields have their respective levels, times, and message offsets, see etc.; this proves the archive is readable, but does not prove it was released on that day in 2020 according to the current product schedule. The 10m V500 calculation from v2b cannot be used for this version. The Knaff–Zehr 2007 card D8NBE3ZE PDF page 5 / journal page 75 only mentions NCEP analysis tangential winds in the 400–600 km annular band, **the original text does not explicitly state 850 hPa**; adopting the 850 layer has an explicit source in the subsequent literature Knaff et al. (2014) https://doi.org/10.1175/JCLI-D-13-00096.1, rather than backfilling it into 2007. KZ07 wind-pressure relation PDF page 10 / journal page 80.

2. Operational timeline: The rolling 30-day average 48h GFS product publicly available from NCEP NCO is approximately 3h50 after the 00/12 cycles, and approximately 3h50 after the 06/18 cycles; uniformly adding a conservative margin, assuming full public availability at initialization + 4h15. Relative to the OFCL public advisory T = AIWP same-cycle initialization + 3 h, selecting the latest fully released cycle before T uniformly rolls back to the preceding 18/06Z, with 48h valid time GFS f054; individual initializations for the 15 events are at . **This is a preregistration operational timeline proxy, not a proof of historical case-by-case release**. If the Lead requires strict historical availability rather than a conservative proxy, this item remains unclosed; the preceding cycle `.idx` for 2021–24 has not been checked case by case (v2b checked the same-cycle f048, which cannot be repurposed as evidence of availability for this cycle).

3. 170 station–event identities and heights: The Wind Tower Height worksheet from the NWS 2025 equipment inventory was matched station ID by station ID with the Legacy ASOS In Service Dates table; among the 170 station–events, 80 in the 2025 inventory have ASOS entries and heights, and 90 are not in this ASOS inventory (which does not equate to having proven they are AWOS; other historical station tables must be checked one by one). Using a **conditional 2025 snapshot** with commissioning date ≤ event year and height 8–12 m as a proxy, 61 station–events and 13 events each have ≥3 stations; Delta and Milton have only 1 station each, while the other 13 cases have 3–17 stations. The 2025 inventory cannot retrospectively verify the instrument model/height back in 2020–24; the NCEI HOMR station-by-station historical verification on event dates has not been completed, so the count of strictly confirmed "historically verified identity and height" is currently 0; **this must not be mislabeled as 0 qualified stations**. Row-by-row original values / sources / conditional conclusions are in , and event counts are in . Under this candidate's rule of "ASOS and historically verified height", 15×3 cannot currently be confirmed; if the 2025 inventory indeed exhausts historical ASOS, the conditional upper bound is also only 13, but that exhaustiveness has not been verified, so it cannot be asserted that there are only 13 in the end. The remaining METAR stations may be AWOS and must not be sneakily added as ASOS.

4. Isaias: The AIWP S3 anonymous listing shows zero objects; 2026/1007 has `2026100700`, and 2026/1009, 1010, 1011, 1012, 1013, 1014 all have date prefixes. The missing 10-08 cycle is not a simple lag where "the entire bucket is only updated through 10-07", but rather a date/cycle void; the target same-initialization 2026100800 has still not been backfilled, and we cannot swap in the 10-07 cycle to cobble together 16 cases. Anonymous bucket: https://noaa-oar-mlwp-data.s3.amazonaws.com/?list-type=2&prefix=PANG_v100_GFS/2026/1008/.

5. Has passed Python syntax compilation checks, including strict `--lead-frozen` and historical 15×3/adapter guards, but **no observational pairings have been run, nor is it an independently executable frozen pipeline**; it still lacks validated input adaptation from upstream BEST wind radii to H08. (a) cannot be launched before the Lead freezes it. The criteria of ±20%, 1.1, 2/3, ≥15×≥3 remain unchanged.

Costs: Local CPU / anonymous HTTP, Colab 0 CU, HPC no jobs; this round consumed ~1.024 GB real read from GDEX + ~1.17 MB from NWS tables, USD bandwidth costs unmetered. If official v2 still runs locally, expected 0 Colab CU; Pangu path alone linearly extrapolated from s2b's 40.27 GB / 9 events to 15 events is ~67.12 GB (rough estimate, not costs and not full newly added GFS / observation traffic). Given the current evidentiary gate of fewer than 15 cases, **investing this official cost is not recommended**.

External sources: NWS 2025 ASOS equipment inventory https://www.weather.gov/asos/asosequip.html; HOMR historical API https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/homr/api; NCAR GDEX 10.5065/D65D8PWK; the aforementioned NCEP NCO release page; AIWP public bucket; Knaff–Zehr (2007) D8NBE3ZE, Knaff et al. (2007) ZPYAUTZG PDF pp. 3–4, 6 / journal pp. 783–784, 786. The use of these sources has been supplementally recorded in .

# B1+B4 v2 Preparation Paused: Only 13 Cases After Strict Station Class and Height (2026-10-14 22:3x)

## Facts (Verified)
- Among the 170 station–events, 80 have anemometer heights in the NWS 2025 ASOS equipment inventory (61 at 33 ft, 18 at 26 ft, 1 at 19 ft), and 90 are not in the inventory. According to the conditional snapshot of "commissioning year prior to the event, height 8–12 m": 13 events have ≥3 stations, while Delta and Milton each have only 1 station. Not a single station's historical height (HOMR) has been verified.
- The 2020 three-case GFS environmental fields can be obtained from NCAR GDEX; V500 uses 850 hPa (based on Knaff et al. 2014, doi 10.1175/JCLI-D-13-00096.1; KZ07 card D8NBE3ZE PDF p. 5 does not specify the level). The operational timeline is uniformly rolled back by one cycle according to the NCEP release schedule (proxy).
- The 2026-10-08 00Z Pangu cycle for Isaias is a data void and cannot be backfilled.
- Holland B in CLIMADA H08 is calculated endogenously from pressure deficit; wind radii can only fit RMW; the adapter from BEST wind radii → H08 has not been written or validated yet.

## Decision I made
1. v2 preparation stops here: do not freeze, do not run (a), keep the node Shelved.
 - Why: Under strict station class and height, R2 (≥15 events × ≥3 stations) only reaches 13; cobbling together 15 would require taking 7.9 m stations for height correction, which still leaves zero margin, and would additionally require HOMR historical verification and H08 adapter development/validation—investing further in an experiment with zero margin and very weak statistical power based on event-count gating (2/3) is not worthwhile. The scientific increment is also limited: the AI track being comparable to the operational track has already been shown by DeMaria 2025 (card NR_demaria_2025, PDF pp. 5–8).
 - Cost of being wrong: If it was actually worth doing, it is delayed by a few months; all materials (preregistration candidates, station tables, environmental field scripts, (a) chain scripts) remain in , and can be picked up from here upon restart without redoing them.
2. Restart triggers (either): ① Liang Hu's 3D boundary layer model is in place (replacing H08 while bypassing the B adaptation issue); ② The 2026 season enters HURDAT2, AIWP is filled, and after HOMR historical height verification it satisfies ≥15×≥3. Whether to include 26 ft stations for height correction must be written into the preregistration before inspecting any errors.
3. Criteria remain unchanged. The main effort of Node B shifts to B2 (running).

reviews.title: Verdict: review of the three B1+B4 literature conclusions (10-14)
reviews.text:
# Verdict: Review of Three Literature Conclusions for B1+B4 (10-14)
Reviewers: E·Gemini, A·GPT-6, D·GLM (3/3 valid, all "supported with reservations"). Evidence: Grok report b99be0, project page.

## Personal Verification by the Lead
- NHC OFCL does not report Pc/POCI/RMW: The Lead downloaded aal142024 (Milton); for OFCL τ≥12 h there are 383 rows in total, with 0 rows of non-zero mslp/poci/rmw, and 161 rows of non-zero 34 kt wind radii. Confirmed.
- WeatherNext Cyclones public tracks: developers.google.com/weathernext/guides/weatherlab has been reviewed—CSV/ATCF, including ensemble member tracks and paired observations, approx. 2023 to present, historical data under CC BY 4.0; whether registration is required is not stated. Confirmed.
- DeMaria 2025 tracking uses 850 hPa circulation, not MSLP: litwiki card points to Appendix (PDF pp. 2–3, 14–15); both E and A independently stated the same, adopted (the Lead did not re-read the appendix page by page).
- Vickery 2009 was verified on 258 peak gusts across 24 US landfalling hurricanes, RMW/B parameters were fitted through subjective iterative fitting using HWind + station time series, and observations were first standardized to open terrain 10 m 3 s: E and A stated the same, pointing to local Zotero original journal pp. 397–404, consistent with card WTPZS77N, adopted.

## Must Change
1. **Wind field input for chains (b)(c)** (E-1): OFCL only has track, Vmax, and 34/50/64 kt wind radii. Chains (b)(c) must not use post-event b-deck RMW/POCI/Pc. Changed to: Use RMW and POCI at the cycle initiation time (τ=0, operationally available CARQ/BEST τ=0) as initial values, extrapolate during the forecast period according to the pre-registered method (persistence or literature statistical RMW model), determine Pc from Vmax using a literature wind-pressure relationship, or directly fit a Holland profile using OFCL wind radii (similar practice to the NHC wind speed probability model). Specific scheme enters Stage 2 pre-registration; chain (a) can still use b-deck.
2. **AI track tracking method** (E-2, A-1): Retract "tracking from MSLP/10 m wind using TempestExtremes". Order changed to: First check whether CIRA RAMMB public AIWP tracks (NPNG/NGRP/NFOR etc., https://rammb-data.cira.colostate.edu/tc_realtime/about.asp) can be downloaded at the file level; if not, track using 850 hPa circulation per DeMaria 2025 Appendix (using NHC forecast initialization position as initial guess), with MSLP used only as auxiliary. "AIWP has no off-the-shelf track files" rephrased to "NOAA S3 archives contain no track files; the downloadability of CIRA products has not been verified".
3. **Incorporate WeatherNext Cyclones** (E-3, D-1): The Lead's original note "requires login, unverified" was wrong, corrected. Add supplementary chain (c′): WN-C track + intensity + wind radii (from 2023 onward, covering 6 events: Idalia, Beryl, Debby, Francine, Helene, Milton), serving as B4's preferred off-the-shelf AI ensemble source; (c′) is for reporting only and will not enter B1 criteria (criteria remain based on (c), neither relaxed nor replaced). Conclusion (1) is restricted to "FCN/Pangu/GraphCast in the AIWP archive without intensity post-processing (DeMaria 2025 sample)", not generalized to "all AI intensities are inadequate" (Alet 2026 Nature 10.1038/s41586-026-10953-2 is a counterexample).
4. **Narrow incremental scope** (E-5, A-2, D-1): Do not write "no one has done AI forecast to station winds". Write as "Within the retrieved scope, none observed: three-chain comparison of AI forecast track + classical parameterized boundary layer wind field → US ASOS station peak winds", listing adjacent precedents side by side: NHC wind speed probabilities DeMaria 2009 (10.1175/2009WAF2222286.1)/2013; Alet 2026 (explicitly stating station-by-station wind verification is left for the future); Vickery 2009 station verification; Lai et al. (Pangu/AIFS driving UWIN-CM, Hong Kong); Wu et al. 2026 ACDF (arXiv 2603.12828, Zhejiang stations). These precedents can serve as literature basis only after cards are created in litwiki.
5. **Different conditions between chain (a) and Vickery 2009** (E-4, A-3): Vickery's RMW/B were fitted to station time series, whereas we use raw b-deck values without fitting; therefore, the ±20% gate of this node is stricter than Vickery's verification, which must be clearly stated when interpreting results. Criteria remain unchanged (the gate set by Liang Hu / Node B is not relaxed).
6. **Supplement repository table** with SimCenter (Snaiki–Wu 2017 C++ implementation, R2D Hurricane Wind Simulation Tool) (A-4) and stormwindmodel (Willoughby, US gridded peak winds/gusts, CRAN) (D-NOTE); retract "no open-source implementation of Snaiki & Wu found".

## For Reference Only
- A: When comparing (b)/(c), distinguish the operationally available time of early/late guidance; Stage 2 pre-registration should state whether late (available post-hoc) or early is used, and clarify that they are not equivalent operational conditions.
- D: Pangu systematically overestimates RMW (arXiv 2511.21792 abstract)—note this if (c) uses size information from AI fields; this node's (c) does not use AI size.
- D: B4 coverage criteria can be benchmarked against NHC wind speed probabilities, stating that the increment comes from a physical/AI ensemble rather than error climatology.
- D: Current status of HWind has not been verified; check independently before citing.
- D pointed out that the Lead's note "CLIPER is a paraphrase" was redundant: Accepted; CLIPER/TCLP is indeed the paper's baseline name.

## Objections Not Adopted
- E claimed that GenCast plus an empirical wind-pressure relationship can "substantially eliminate intensity underestimation without borrowing NHC intensity": Does not alter the design of (c)—the problem definition for this node is specifically "AI track + official intensity", and this correction in Alet 2026 was targeted at GenCast, not the three AIWP models; (c′) already covers the comparison with "AI native intensity".
- E claimed that WN-C "comprehensively outperforms HAFS/HWRF": Original paper numbers unverified, treated only as a clue, not included in conclusions.

## Literature Basis
DeMaria 2025 card; Vickery 2009 card (journal pp. 397–404, quoted by reviewers); remaining precedents have no cards yet, pending creation.

reviews.title: Verdict and shelving: B1+B4 did not pass the gate (6/6 valid, all "support with reservations" shelving)
reviews.text:
# Verdict and Shelving: B1+B4 Failed Gate (6/6 Valid, All "Support with Reservations" Shelving)
Reviewers: E Gemini, A GPT-6, D GLM, C DeepSeek, B Kimi, F Grok. No substitutions, no vacancies. Evidence see review cards; draft conclusions (retained as-is, subject to this document).

## Verdict (Final)
Per the publicly revised and refrozen s2b protocol, B1 did not pass the gate: 48 h homogeneous 9 events, 22 stations, Pangu/OFCL median absolute error ratio 1.021 (satisfies ≤1.1), events not worse than OFCL 5/9 (requires ≥6/9); under the original s2 10-event denominator it is 5/10 (requires ≥7/10), with Nicholas recorded as unevaluable, not counted as a failure. Both denominators fail the gate, and failure was not caused by denominator revision. B1+B4 node **Shelved**, B4 is not conducted per sequence. It cannot be stated from this that AI tracks are overall superior or inferior to NHC.

## Lead Personal Verification
- Primary gate numbers: Previously recalculated using station-by-station tables, consistent with the 6 reviewers (1.0209, 5/9, FCN2 1.214 and 3/9, GraphCast 0.678 and 5/7).
- Track error: Homogeneous 9 events, center error median at observed landfall time OFCL 105.0 km, Pangu 90.9 km (F, E correct; D, B stated 90.9 is the 11-event value, incorrect); event-by-event Pangu was closer in only 4/9 events; ±12 h average track error median OFCL 96.9, Pangu 85.7 km. Nominal 48 h actual lead time is 48.5–59 h.
- Inputs: Debby at initialization POCI−Pc = 2 hPa, RMW 75 nmi; Nicole RMW 200 nmi; Milton RMW 5 nmi (a-deck CARQ τ=0). CLIMADA H08 computes wind speed from pressure deficit (`_compute_angular_windspeeds_h08`, `_bs_holland_2008`), not using input Vmax, consistent with E's statement.

## Must Change (Implemented in this document and project page)
1. **Withdraw "Track differences are overwhelmed by small sample size and common bias"** (E-1, A-2, F-1, C). Actual situation: medians are close, but event-by-event differences are large (|Pangu−OFCL| median approx. 68 km), with Pangu closer in only 4/9 events; the lost cases Debby, Delta, Zeta all had worse Pangu tracks, whereas the won cases Helene, Nicole had worse Pangu tracks and only won because errors cancelled each other out. Thus track indeed affects station winds, but not in a consistent direction. The cause has not been isolated.
2. **Mechanism of common underestimation of −35% to −38%** (E-2; A, B requested not concluding a single cause): Candidate mechanisms include (i) Δp extrapolated from initialization Δp0 scaled by OFCL Vmax; events where storms were still weak at initialization (Debby Δp0 = 2 hPa, Francine 6 hPa) severely depress Δp at landfall; whereas H08 only uses Δp, so OFCL Vmax did not actually enter the wind field directly; (ii) RMW frozen at initialization time (Nicole 200 nmi is a giant false eye, Milton 5 nmi is a micro eye); (iii) OFCL intensity itself is underestimated (landfall Vmax median bias calculated by E is −14.9%, Lead did not recalculate); (iv) 850 hPa tracking center and near-surface wind center may have an offset (D). The relative contributions were not disentangled, **insufficient evidence**. These are all caused by input assumptions specified in s2 preregistration, not AI itself.
3. **Supplementary reporting of three items required by preregistration** (E-3, A-3, F): ±12 h average track error (see above) and actual lead times (48.5–59 h, 24 h tier actually 24.5–35.75 h) have been added. Whether the new model peak time still falls within the v1 observation window (≥648 minutes) **was not delivered**; E estimates that (b) 9/22 and (c) 7/22 station peak times fell outside v1's ±6 h window. Per protocol, stations cannot be reselected based on this, and it is written truthfully only as an interpretive limitation.
4. **Faithful representation of protocol modification** (A-1, D, F): Original s2 was unevaluable; s2a was an exploratory modification; s2b was refrozen after seeing (b) results and Milton single case (unblinded). The homogeneous denominator slightly relaxed the threshold from 7/10 to 6/9, which has been disclosed; both denominators fail the gate. What I originally wrote, "only handles inputs, does not alter denominator", was inaccurate and is corrected. Landfall error implementation used fixed landfall points from the event list rather than BEST interpolation (B), which only affects diagnostics.
5. **Limitations of distance stratification** (E-4, B, C, F): (a) distant stations +35% only has n=3, with same-tier gust at −4.8%; (c)(a) used 6 h nodes to calculate nearest distance, whereas (b) used 15 min, creating inconsistent standards that might misclassify stations. H2's +2.41 m/s is full-sample bias (794 event×station peaks, from hourly METAR, 300 km range), not distant-station stratification, and is not used for mutual corroboration.
6. **Rewriting of restart conditions** (all reviewers): GraphCast's AIWP archive only begins in 2022 and originally did not exist for 2020–21; "completing" this item is non-executable and deleted. Any of the following modifications requires **establishing a new protocol and refreezing**, and cannot overturn this gate verdict. Changing wind field models or station sets requires re-passing the (a) ±20% gate first.

## Restart Conditions (Final; open new version once satisfied, not overturning this round)
- R1 Scale and pressure inputs: replace "Δp0 scaling + RMW freeze" with operationally available methods, such as fitting Holland profiles with OFCL 34/50/64 kt wind radii, or deriving Δp from Vmax using wind-pressure relationships; or when Liang Hu's 3D boundary layer model is in place. Re-pass the (a) gate.
- R2 Event count: what failed was the event-by-event condition. The new version must have ≥15 evaluable events, with ≥3 qualified stations per event (quantitative thresholds to be determined in the new protocol). May add 2025 events, or connect to H2's multi-source station network, but observation standards must be unified.
- R3 Censoring / Truncation: there must be a solution for the issue of reporting dropouts during strong winds (34/67 stations truncated), such as multi-source station networks or designing lower bound tests to enter primary metrics.
- R4 Primary chain selection: switching to GraphCast (2022+) or using AI consensus as the primary chain must be preregistered in advance; WeatherNext Cyclones end-to-end chain (AI with its own intensity and wind radii) is a separate issue, not a restart of B1, and data must be obtainable without login.
- Availability timestamp: OFCL is issued approx. 3 h later than AI; the new version must specify whether to correct for this.

## For Reference Only
- D, B: 24 h is reported only without entering the gate; Pangu 0.85 but events 4/10; in 22 station pairings Pangu won 12 stations (sign test p ≈ 0.83)—the two chains have no substantive difference across stations.
- C: Landfall errors for FCN2 and GraphCast are both approx. 59 km, yet station errors differ by nearly a factor of two, indicating that error at landfall time alone cannot explain station winds.
- A: In code, the interpolation upper limit is 13/25 h, and distance bin boundary assignments differ subtly from protocol text, with insufficient evidence of impact.
- B: The draft wrote "35–38%", which is actually −34.8%/−37.9%.

## Unadopted Objections
- E recalculated using BEST intensity plus both chain tracks (Pangu ratio 1.188, 3/9): this is a new standard, not in the protocol, not used as criteria, and serves only as collateral evidence that "track indeed has an impact" (Lead did not recalculate).
- No reviewer advocated against shelving; "run supplementary runs before deciding" was not adopted—both F and E pointed out that there is no test within the protocol that could overturn the primary gate, and supplementary runs require a new protocol.

## Literature Basis
Nearby precedent cards see project page (DeMaria 2009/2013, Alet 2026, Lai 2025, Wu 2026). This conclusion has no literature basis, based on internal track data.
## Cost of Being Wrong
Shelving deletes nothing: scripts, trackers, event lists, pairing code are all kept; opening a new version per R1/R2 is estimated at 1–2 days and a few Colab CUs.

results.title: B1+B4 segment 1: verifiable data entry points (10-14, US Eastern)
results.text:
# B1+B4 段 1：可复核数据入口（10-14，美东）

1. 最佳路径：NHC HURDAT2 Atlantic [2026-09-23 版](https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/hurdat/hurdat2-1851-2025-092326.txt)，逐风暴 `L,HUbALnnYYYY.dat.gz` 中 BEST 的第 19 栏是 RMW（海里），第 17 栏 POCI（hPa）；在主样本逐风暴读回，6 小时线性插值，若缺就剔除，不能以常数填补。CIRA [EBTRK](https://rammb2.cira.colostate.edu/research/tropical-cyclones/tc_extended_best_track_dataset/) 的公开 v3.0.2 实际仅更新到 2021，不能拿它声称有 2022–24 的 RMW；其 [README](https://rammb2.cira.colostate.edu/wp-) 亦说明 RMW 并非全时期正式最佳路径字段。本次 pilot 用 NHC b-deck；HURDAT 中非整 6h 登陆位置需另外保留。
2. 官方链 (b)：相同目录 `aALnnYYYY.dat.gz` 的 `OFCL` 是官方路径和强度（ 等）。实测 GET 返回 200，内有 Milton 的 OFCL 行；按起报时刻与实际登陆时刻选预先定义的 24/48/72 h lead，既不可用事后 BEST 替代官方强度，也不能暗中调整 AI 路径时效。NHC [ATCF 格式说明](https://ftp.nhc.noaa.gov/atcf/docs/NRL_doc_ATCFdatabase.html)。段 2 未计算官方链。
3. AI 链 (c)：CIRA/DeMaria (2025) 研究确实使用自身的 TC tracker；本轮检索 CIRA 页面及论文，尚未找到对全部 2020–24 风暴公开可批量下载的逐预报轨迹档。实测 Milton 2024 的官方 a-deck（279 种 aid）无 PANG/GRCS/FCN2/PGWX 同名记录；这不排除另处 CIRA 内部或公开文件，故仅记“现成统一轨迹未核实可下载”。原始 [AIWP S3 README](https://noaa-) 给出模型/时间/变量； 的 108 个具体对象逐一用 S3 list-prefix 核验，95 个存在、0 次请求错误；Pangu 2024 Francine 的 72 h 对象缺一个。最晚 00/12 UTC 起报时间与确切 lead 另有列，不可把 24 h 标签等同恰为 24 h。
4. 原始 AIWP 四维 netCDF 每个约 7–9 GB；试了 Milton 对应 FOUR 文件的 HEAD（7,472,991,383 B），HTTP `Range: bytes=0-1023` 返回 、HDF5 签名。说明对象支持字节范围，不等于“按空间时间切片已成功”。Colab 会话先用 `h5py`/fsspec 缓存 Range 或远程读取做单文件单时次的经纬度/海平面气压与 10 m u/v 小块读取测量请求字节数；若 netCDF 压缩 chunk 跨全球时次，字节/请求失控就停止，不下载整文件。随后围 NHC 预报先验半径搜 MSLP 局地低值、用 850 hPa 环流复核并记录断链（DeMaria 2025 第 3 节建议环流追踪）；不能只凭一帧全域最低压。当前没有运行 Colab，也没有测得切片实际数据量/时长，不能给虚构数字。论文：https://doi.org/10.1175/AIES-D-24-0085.1；Radford 2025：https://doi.org/10.1175/BAMS-D-24-0057.1。
5. ASOS：IEM [1-minute 页面](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/asos/1min.phtml) 的 [backend](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/request/asos1min.py?help) 用 `station=SRQ&vars=sknt,gust_sknt&sts=2024-10-09T12:30Z&ets=2024-10-10T12:30Z&what=download&tz=UTC`。`sknt` 是档案的逐分钟持续风读数（按 ASOS 传感器解释近似运行 2 min 平均，不是验证过的独立 1 min 平均），`gust_sknthttps://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/request/asos.py?help=` 有 `gust`, `peak_wind_gust`, `sknt`，但低频/不同定义不可混到主指标。IEM 自述 raw 存档有限 QC；本次甚至出现 Ian PIE 最大持续风 82 kt、5s gust 最大仅 18 kt，判疑剔除，不可把此源当已质控真值。
6. 中断/缺测：见 每站 24h 应 1440 条的实有数。Idalia TLH/GNV/AAF 仅 207/151/233，且都在登陆前停止；Helene TLH 0，Milton TPA/BKV 0，Ian APF 0。0 行不等于已证实物理设备故障，可能是档案缺源；另有 Milton PIE 827、GIF 858，Ian FMY 433，均会偏低估实测峰值。主展示需每站完整性与 QC 标志；不可对缺测做零风填充。没有下载任何 AIWP 原始 7–9 GB 文件到 工作站。

本段费用：本地 HTTP/NHC/IEM/S3 目录查询和 CPU 脚本；Colab 未启动，耗费 0 CU。若后续先单模型、单预报切片，预算上限每试验 ≤20 CU，实测花费再报。图和 CSV 仅是公开站点数据的摘要，不保存/发布逐分钟原始序列。

results.text:
# B1+B4 (a) Best Track Trial Calculation (10-14, US Eastern)

Status: Small-sample preliminary check, not a formal pass/fail conclusion on criteria. Inputs: NHC HURDAT2 landfall location/track/1 min maximum wind/central pressure + b-deck RMW/POCI; IEM/NCEI ASOS 1-minute archives, all from public web pages; original paths see ; algorithm see , . Airports within a 150 km radius of the landfall point for each event marked with 1min archives; simultaneous window 12 h before and after landfall, model takes peaks at 15min, stations take peaks from minute-by-minute readings, no missing data imputation. Specific 28 rows per station and data URLs see ; event location sources and coverage see . Figure `chain_a_ratio_pilot5.png.svg`, green interval pre-fixed as predicted/observed 0.8–1.2, caption data sources: NHC HURDAT2 + NHC ATCF b-deck + Iowa Environmental Mesonet/NCEI ASOS one-minute archive.

Quality control: Among 28 candidate stations, only 18 stations had ≥720/1440 non-missing sustained wind minutes; Ian PIE's observed maximum sustained wind was 82 kt but maximum 5-second gust was only 18 kt, failing physical consistency; after excluding it, there are 17 pairs, 4 events in total. For the fifth event Idalia, all three stations stopped reporting before landfall (151–233 min), contributing 0 qualified stations, so it cannot be claimed that five events passed testing. retains all exclusion reasons; original did not perform PIE QC, and its 18-station count is not used for primary conclusions.

Metric definitions: e = predicted/observed − 1; median absolute error = median(|e|), median bias = median(e). 17 pairs after quality control: median absolute error 50.69%, median bias +50.69%, not within the pre-specified ±20%. More strictly including only stations with ≥1296/1440 min, 6 pairs: both metrics 44.745%, still not within ±20%; however, the latter covers only 3 events and has strong airport exposure selection. By event:

| Event | Available / Candidate Stations | Median Absolute Ratio Error | Median Signed Bias | Special Notes on Missing Data |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Ian 2022 | 5/8 | 25.62% | +25.62% | PIE excluded for physical inconsistency; FMY stopped reporting almost before landfall |
| Idalia 2023 | 0/3 | Incalculable | Incalculable | AAF/GNV/TLH stopped before landfall, only 151–233 minutes |
| Francine 2024 | 4/5 | 54.95% | +54.95% | BTR has no rows in 1min archive |
| Helene 2024 | 2/3 | 24.665% | +24.665% | TLH has no rows in 1min archive; records of the other two stations incomplete |
| Milton 2024 | 6/9 | 73.195% | +73.195% | TPA/BKV have no rows, FMY 304 min; PIE/GIF/SPG partially stopped reporting |

Very important: What is compared here is the sustained wind reading reported every minute by ASOS (commonly a 2 min running average) against a minimal Holland / constant 0.85 output without a well-defined averaging duration. It does not achieve pairing of "1 min sustained wind of the same physical definition" or gusts. There is no land-sea roughness correction, storm translation, or azimuthal asymmetry; missing data for the largest peaks is non-random, and the observed denominator may be biased low. One cannot attribute +50.69% to AI track, much less declare scientific direction failure based on a trial run. According to the frozen gate, conclusions on the merits of (b)(c) must not be advanced; complete wind field near-surface conversion, exposure/averaging duration, and IEM missing-data QC should be fixed first, retesting the same unchanged ±20% criterion. If it still exceeds boundaries after fixing, close out according to the project page's "wind field model disqualified". The current simplified implementation itself fails as a proxy screening.

This time there were only local CPU/HTTP requests, no Colab session, no HPC, Colab cost 0 CU. Did not download or publish raw minute-by-minute full time series and large AIWP files; figures and tables are station-level peak summaries.

results.title: Wind-field screening implementation and scope of applicability (10-14)
results.text:
# Wind Field Screening Implementation and Scope of Applicability (10-14)

Implementation: , local standard library; what was executed this time is a minimal screening of "best track + Holland (1980) axisymmetric gradient wind + constant 0.85 reduction", not Vickery et al. (2009) 2D slab + height-resolved profiles, much less 3D boundary layer or topographic corrections. The reason for selection is that inputs (track, Pc, Vmax, RMW, POCI) can be obtained directly from NHC, formulas and code are verifiable, facilitating early discovery of unusable observations and structural parameters. Vickery 2009's model is a more suitable subsequent implementation; its slab, land-sea roughness transition, and dropsonde profiles cannot be replaced by a 0.85 constant. Card , PDF pp. 1, 12, 15, 22–24 (journal pp. 381, 392, 395, 402–404), its 0.85 coefficient is a simple control tuned against the same batch of observations, not a verified universal overland factor.

Hourly set center latitude φ / longitude λ, best track Vmax [kt], Pc [hPa], b-deck RMW [nmi], POCI [hPa]. Linearly interpolate 6h data and preserve non-hourly landfalls from HURDAT2; station-to-center spatial distance uses haversine. Let Δp=100(POCI−Pc) Pa, ρ=1.15 kg/m³ (assumed), f=2Ωsinφ, Ω=7.292115×10^-5 s^-1, R=1852 RMW (m), r=max(3000 m, station-center distance), x=(R/r)^B. Define Vg,max=(0.514444 Vmax)/0.85, back-calculate B=ρ e (Vg,max²+f R Vg,max)/Δp; retain only 0.5≤B≤4, 8≤RMW≤200 nmi, 500≤Δp≤15000 Pa. Gradient wind Vg(r)=sqrt[(B Δp/ρ) x exp(−x)+(rf/2)²]−rf/2. Wind field velocity V10(r)=0.85 Vg(r), taking the maximum on a 15min time grid 12h before and after landfall for each station. Gradient wind pressure formula see Wang et al. (2020) PDF p. 5 Eq. (7) (originally Holland 1980); Vmax → gradient conversion, ρ, RMW interpolation, minimum radius, and B truncation are hypotheses of this experiment and must not be written as literature values. Function `modelinterp` can be recalculated item by item. The radial formula has no storm translation asymmetry, background wind, local decay, or terrain acceleration; in particular, applying 0.85 for offshore to inland airports simultaneously inevitably carries systematic risks.

Physical inconsistency of time/peak: NHC Vmax is the maximum 1 min sustained wind; the near-surface coefficient of this simplified model is not endowed with a stable time-averaging definition; IEM `sknt` is the ASOS sustained wind output every minute, typically approximating a 2 min running average, unconfirmed as 1 min. Ratios in the same figure serve only as proxy screening, not the final qualification verification of "peak gust or 1 min sustained wind" required by the task criteria. `gust_sknt` is 5 s gust; card ZR7S3SEJ (candidate, PDF pp. 2–3, 5–6) separates different sampling durations and exposures; 2KXRIJJB (candidate, PDF pp. 2–4) comparison of approx. 2 s vs 10 min cannot be directly used as a universal 5 s / 2 min multiplier. This station did not perform gust factor and 1→2 min conversions, and therefore does not forcibly pair unforecast gusts with observed gusts. Both cards are pending independence and are not treated as approved design values.

Terrain/exposure: Station coordinates were only screened for 150 km, without using airport directional obstacles or land-cover; land z0=0.03 m, sea z0=0.0013 m are only Vickery examples (card WTPZS77N, PDF pp. 12, 15, 22), not entered into the code. It cannot be claimed that terrain correction has been done. To pass the gate, one must first implement directional/land-sea transition boundary layer conversions, and check original texts / author code / cards before selecting values; any subsequent parameter tuning will be distinguished as a new model from the currently frozen ±20% gate, and coefficients must not be adjusted a posteriori on this sample to fit the gate. The parameter source table has been filled on the project page. Reasonable sensitivities to be done: ρ 1.10–1.25, near-surface coefficient 0.65–0.90, representative sea/land roughness values and directional variations, RMW ±20%; these are range suggestions rather than executed verifications.

results.text:
# B1+B4 Chain (a) v1 Pre-registration (Frozen; Prior to Observation Comparison)

Time: 10-14 15:19 EDT. This document was written prior to computing this round's v1 results; since the previous round pilot's +50.7% has been made public, it is impossible to claim a completely blind state; the following constants do not use station ratios to tune parameters. This document/rules will not be modified hereafter; if changes are needed, a separate v2 will be created.

## Model and Data
CLIMADA v6.1.0 `trop_cyclone` H08 (tag commit bb9595944fcf673152ea53e61efbafeb0b1e4406, GPL-3.0) is selected. It is chosen over the Vickery 2009 slab because the latter has no off-the-shelf, fully open implementation that can be directly verified; nor will the previous round's 0.85 Holland be falsely claimed as full Vickery. CLIMADA's `_compute_windfields` explicitly defines 10 m, 1-min wind, and incorporates vector translational asymmetry according to storm translation speed and radial decay (source code v6.1.0 lines 1131–1257; H08 uses Holland 2008 B, default gradient-to-surface 0.9, source code lines 61–69). The original functions of this software version are used without manual intensity tuning. HURDAT2 center, 1-min maximum wind, and central pressure; ATCF b-deck BEST columns 17/19 for POCI/RMW; linearly interpolated to 15 min between raw time points within ±12 h; if one side is missing or the gap exceeds 7 h, do not extrapolate; nodes with RMW<=0 or POCI<=Pc are removed. Raw HURDAT landfall special points are retained; only longitude/latitude/intensity/pressure are linearly interpolated, without adjusting the storm based on ASOS. Stations are from the IEM ASOS network with HAS1MIN=1, archive covering the event time, and within 150 km of the HURDAT landfall center. Model peak is taken as the maximum within landfall ±12 h.

## Exposure and Averaging Periods (Pre-fixed)
CLIMADA's raw 10 m 1-min H08 field is an oceanic baseline; station wind directions come from model u/v, querying the Natural Earth 10m land polygon (public surface category) at 2/5/10 km along the upstream inflow direction. If >=2 of the three points are land, it is classified as overland; otherwise, water surface; whether the station is located within the polygon is also logged. Near-surface roughness over sea z0=0.0013 m, open land z0=0.03 m, per Vickery et al. 2009 PDF pp. 12, 15, 22; overland factor F=[ln(10/.03)/ln(500/.03)]/[ln(10/.0013)/ln(500/.0013)], water surface F=1; roughness switches hourly when the sampled category changes. The 500 m neutral constant-flux logarithmic layer and single open land z0 are explicit assumptions, not CLIMADA's or Vickery's full land-sea transition; reference height range 200–1000 m, land z0 0.02–0.07 m affect metrics, provided solely as sensitivity notes and not used to tune gates. Topographic elevation is not separately corrected. If Natural Earth data cannot be read, do not silently switch to another exposure definition; mark v1 as failed to execute.

Model 1-min sustained wind is converted to ASOS IEM `sknt` approx. 2-min running average by multiplying by 0.97; this is a conservative assumption (range 0.95–1.00), not an exact measured literature value. The 5-s gust reported by `gust_sknt` is obtained from the model 1-min field multiplied by 1.30 (land) and 1.20 (sea); this is a tentative interpolation assumption based on roughness/3–5s and minute-wind definitions described in Powell et al. 2005 "Hurricane Gust Factors Revisited" PDF pp. 2–3, 5–6, not a universal 1min→5s factor directly provided by that paper; range: land 1.15–1.45, sea 1.10–1.35; the approx. 2s/10min factor of Krayer–Marshall 1992 cannot be directly applied (2KXRIJJB PDF pp. 2–4). Both averaging periods are frozen in advance and peak values are computed separately.

## Station Screening and Statistics
For each station, centered on the model 2-min peak time t* within ±6 h (if exceeding the landfall ±12 h observation window, expand retrieval to the edge of that window), require valid `sknt` independent minutes >=90% of actual minutes in the 12 h (>=648/720), with first valid <=t* and last valid >=t*; failure to meet this results in truncation and exclusion from the two primary metrics. Physical QC: sustained/gust must not be negative; records with gust<sknt when both have values in the same minute are treated as inconsistent, and the entire station is removed; stations where overall maximum gust is less than maximum sustained wind are also removed (two peaks at different times, but still clearly an abnormal proxy). Gusts separately require >=1 valid report, both model/observation >0, without assuming gusts must be reported every minute; stations lacking gusts do not enter gust metrics but sustained wind can be retained. Deduplicate minutes, do not fill missing with 0; count request failures and no-records separately. This QC is a conservative pre-filter and does not imply raw IEM archives are fully quality-controlled.

For each event and station, peak prediction / observation - 1; median(abs(e)) and median(e) are aggregated across eligible stations; reported row by row by event, additionally reporting number of events, number of stations, and number of truncated stations. The primary gate is strictly whether chain (a) sustained wind median bias is within ±20%; gust serves as parallel diagnosis, not replacing the frozen primary gate; if still out of bounds, report the wind field model as failing truthfully without tuning parameters. Events without eligible stations remain in the denominator notes but do not contribute to station metrics. Stations will not be reselected based on the old pilot, nor will constants be modified based on results. Sources: NHC HURDAT2, ATCF b-deck, IEM/NCEI 1min, Natural Earth 10m land; detailed URLs see previous round. Following pre-registration, if software or data is unavailable, clearly report as incomplete; do not provide fabricated numbers.
