results.text:
# B1+B4 Best Track Chain v1: Pre-registered Retest

Frozen document: (10-14 15:19 EDT; prior to observation comparison in this round v1); software CLIMADA 6.1.0 H08 commit lines 1131–1257.

By station e=peak prediction/peak observation−1, median(|e|) / median(e). Inputs: NHC HURDAT2+ATCF b-deck, IEM/NCEI ASOS 1min, Natural Earth 10m land polygon; figures and tables all indicate sources.

Sustained wind (approx. 2min sknt, n=29): median absolute error 21.02%; median bias +9.89%. ±20% bias gate: Passed; but absolute error 21.02% >20%, should not falsely claim overall error is entirely within ±20%.

## Execution and Boundaries
The first execution removed an event entirely if any single 15-min node lacked RMW/POCI, causing Beryl and Francine to be excluded; erroneous run results are retained as-is in of the v1 root directory and the event-by-event table. The code subsequently only corrected the pre-registration implementation error of "excluding missing nodes rather than excluding the entire event", recomputing in the new directory without changing models, constants, or station rules. Severe weather reporting outages in raw IEM minute archives are not random; the 90% model peak window rule eliminated 34/67 stations, leaving only 1 station for Milton. Natural surface is only land/sea, without resolving specific land categories and terrain across different directions at airports; 500m log layer reference height, 1min→2min factor, and 1min→5s factor are all frozen assumptions, not author-provided universal conversions. IEM sknt is an approx. 2min proxy, not a strict 1min pairing; although the gust factor has definition/exposure basis from Powell et al. 2005 PDF pp. 2–3, 5–6, its numerical value is an assumption. Error directions across different stations and event samples are strongly imbalanced; 29 stations come from 10 events, not every one of the 12 events having quality-qualified observations.

results.text:
# B1+B4 Stage 2 Pre-registration s2 (Frozen Prior to Observation Comparison)

Time: 10-14 EDT. Observations of (a) v1 and their results are already visible; this round is not double-blind. Once written and fixed, this document will not change based on ASOS ratios from (b)/(c). 12 pre-selected landfalling events; primary comparison uses the 10 events with eligible stations from v1, with 29 reason=eligible stations; IDALIA/IDA without observation stations will not serve as gate-passing events. Report input missingness for all pre-selected events; unavailable chains are recorded as missing and not quietly excluded from the denominator to claim gate passage.

## Common Time, Validation, and Wind Field
1. Landfall time is taken from the HURDAT2 special L record of . Nominal 24/48/72 h initialization chooses the nearest 00/12 UTC strictly earlier than or equal to landfall time minus nominal lead time; all three models share the same initialization. Actual lead times are listed event by event; the 24/48/72 labels do not represent exactly equal lengths. OFCL uses official forecasts issued approx. 3 h after that analysis time (late guidance), which is not strictly equivalent in operational availability to 00/12 UTC AI forecasts; must not be claimed as a strictly fair real-time matchup.
2. Forecast 6 h cycles are linearly interpolated to 15 min, with a window of landfall ±12 h, without out-of-bounds extrapolation, allowing a maximum gap of 7 h between adjacent valid nodes. Intensity NHC OFCL Vmax is interpolated by time and shared between (b) and (c); (c) uses this intensity, not the AI grid's own intensity. (a) directly follows v1 without recomputation.
3. Common CLIMADA 6.1.0 H08 original functions, translation vectors, 10m 1-min, majority vote at 2/5/10 km upstream along opposite inflow direction on Natural Earth 10m, sea z0=.0013m / land z0=.03m and 500m neutral logarithmic reference, sustained ×.97, gust land ×1.30 / sea ×1.20, all completely follow v1 PREREG and ; do not adjust with observations. Model peak is the maximum within ±12h. Fix sustained wind and peak gust observations recorded when each station was eligible in v1, ensuring the three chains share identical stations and observations; separately report whether v1 12h observation completeness at the new model peak time still satisfies the original ≥648 minutes window rule; if the full window cannot be obtained, do not re-select samples on a station basis, but only note in sensitivity. Error e = model peak / fixed observed peak − 1, reporting all-station median(|e|), median(e), and within-event station median(|e|) separately. Event not worse means within-event (c) median(|e|) ≤ (b). Primary criterion: 48 h (c) Pangu all-station median(|e|) ≤ 1.1×(b), and at least 7 of the 10 events with observations are not worse (≥2/3 rounded up); simultaneously, (a) v1 sustained wind bias ±20% has passed. 24/72 h are for reporting only and do not enter the gate. Both wind variables must be reported, but sustained wind serves as the frozen primary metric and gust as parallel diagnosis, without picking the best post-hoc.
4. BEST b-deck is used solely to verify forecast center locations and chain (a), not entering the starting point, intensity, pressure, or size of (b)(c). Track error is calculated in km against the HURDAT2 BEST center via linear interpolation of 6h positions at landfall time, and average track error across ±12h nodes is separately reported; if track breaks, do not fabricate.

## Operational Input Freezing
5. Retrieve τ≥0 tracks and Vmax from NHC a-deck by storm / cycle / OFCL. CARQ τ=0 is preferred as initial center, RMW/POCI/Pc (fields 19, 17, 9, 0-based). Missing RMW/POCI will only then use the same cycle's OFCL τ=0; if the latter is still missing, wind fields for both chains in that cycle are missing, never supplemented from future or b-deck. Physical filtering: RMW 0<r≤200 nmi, POCI>Pc, Pc 0<...<POCI. Future RMW and POCI are held constant via persistence, without using AI fields to estimate size; treat the persistence assumption as a physical limitation.
6. Pc: Starting with CARQ τ=0 Pc, pressure deficit Δp0=POCI−Pc0, future Δp(t)=Δp0 [V_OFCL(t)/V_OFCL(0)]^(1/0.644), Pc(t)=POCI−Δp(t). The power exponent is borrowed from Atkinson–Holliday 1977 V=6.7(1010−Pc)^0.644 (original Western Pacific relationship, not directly adapted to the Atlantic); anchoring to the current cycle's CARQ measured pressure with constant environmental pressure is an assumption of this experiment, not confirmed by that paper. If CARQ τ=0 Pc is missing but RMW/POCI exist, use Pc0=POCI−(V0/6.7)^(1/0.644) hPa, explicitly noting as an assumption; if initial V0≤0 or calculated Pc is unphysical, mark as missing. Identical pressure and intensity are provided to (b) and (c), comparing track effect only, without fitting against BEST. Parameter sources: Atkinson & Holliday 1977, MWR 105:421–427, formulas verified from DTIC abstract and Knaff–Zehr 2007 original restatement, references: https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/html/tr/ADA064518/; https://ramsdis.cira.colostate.edu/rammb/resources/docs/Knaff_preswind.v4.pdf; these cannot serve as evidence of Atlantic accuracy.

## AI Track Freezing
7. First retrieve file-level historically downloadable ATCF of NPNG/NGRP/NFOR provided by CIRA RAMMB, used when verifiable for the same storm/cycle; if only images are seen / corresponding files cannot be directly obtained, then track from NOAA AIWP S3 `PANG_v100_GFS`, `FOUR_v200_GFS`, `GRAP_v100_GFS` 850 hPa u/v fields cycle by cycle. Primary (c) is Pangu; FOUR and GRAP are secondary and cannot substitute as primary gate-passers. Seeded with CARQ τ=0 center, not taking future BEST for the first 6h. Spatial 0.25° grid; 850 hPa Northern Hemisphere relative vorticity ζ=∂v/∂x−∂u/∂y, grid differencing and 5×5 grid smoothing; every 6h find the grid point with maximum positive 200-km radius average ζ (must be >0) within 350 km of the previous center, requiring average tangential circulation within 100–400 km of that grid point to be cyclonic (>0), with MSLP local low serving as a flag rather than an optimization objective. If discrete position jumps >350 km in 6h, lacks positive vorticity, or lacks cyclonic circulation, mark immediately as track break, without bypassing nodes / without resetting to BEST; 15-min linear interpolation for continuous 6h series. When size/rotation speed cannot be computed reliably on slices, mark as unavailable, do not switch to MSLP minimum. Tasks read remote HDF5 Range slices with minimal bandwidth, without pulling raw 7GB files to workstation. 850 hPa circulation tracking in DeMaria et al. 2025 PDF pp. 2–3, 14–15 serves as methodological direction; specific thresholds are all pre-set assumptions, not falsely claimed to be given by the paper.
8. (c′) takes Google Weather Lab historical WeatherNext Cyclones tracks, native intensity/wind radii for the same storm/cycle; if files are actually obtained with available fields, report that chain separately. When files are absent, record as not obtained, do not substitute with approximations. It does not enter (c) criteria. Sources from approx. 2023 onward, verified against actual downloads / member coverage for each event, do not extrapolate full coverage.

## Additional Report: Lower Bound for Truncated Stations
9. For the 34 stations with `reason=truncated` in v1 and other outage stations, fix the maximum `skntgust_sknt` within the retrieved window of that station in v1 as the true peak lower bound. List by event, chain, and lead time the number of stations with positive observation lower bounds, and the number/proportion of model peaks below this lower bound; stations with 0 valid observations are only listed as undecidable. The model adopts the same wind direction exposure and averaging period factors; (a) reads v1 predicted values. Truncation information is for diagnosis only and does not enter the primary gate.

## Missingness and Costs
10. Missing cycles, CARQ, or tracking failures for single models are recorded item by item; pairing of the three chains requires the same 29 stations and same observations; missing any target event disqualifies declaring passage of the full-sample gate. CPU Colab, single experiment ≤20 CU, stop upon task completion; record network bytes, duration, and billing changes (not attributed during concurrent consumption). Must not overwrite v1 results. If initialization selection causes OFCL to exclude terminal nodes within landfall ±12h, mark uncovered window portions as missing, do not stitch together forecasts from future cycles.

results.text:
# B1+B4 Stage 2: Execution Report (10-14 16:42 EDT)

Status: The originally pre-registered 48 h B1 gate could not be completed as specified, so a formal scientific verdict of "pass / fail" cannot be issued. Missing entries are not counted as failures, nor are the original ±20% / 1.1× / ≥2/3 criteria on the project page altered.

## Completed Work and Methodological Compliance
- Migrated the v1 1.4 GB Python environment to WSL while retaining the lightweight environment (112 packages) in the Lab; verified actual imports of `climada` wind-field functions and `numpy`. Left v1 outputs untouched.
- Wrote and froze the evaluation script prior to running the (b)/(c) observation pairing. Chains (b) and (c) read only same-cycle NHC a-deck `CARQ` τ=0 `RMW`/`POCI`/`Pc` and `OFCL` track/`Vmax`; future storm size is held frozen and `Pc` is extrapolated via the pre-specified exponential decay, while `BEST` is used solely for track verification. Chain (a) is carried over directly from v1. Self-tracked chain (c) reads Pangu 850 hPa `u`/`v` directly rather than substituting a toy MSLP-minimum tracker.
- Flaw in original pre-registration: the protocol assumed `OFCL` provides 6 h nodes across all lead times and hard-coded a 7 h maximum interpolation gap, whereas longer lead times actually step at 12 h intervals. Under the strict original rule, zero complete 97-node (15 min) windows exist at 24, 48, or 72 h. Because the original rule cannot evaluate (b) or (c), the raw output is preserved as-is; upon discovering this issue and prior to inspecting any station error summaries, we documented the deviation and defined an exploratory protocol revision `s2a` that relaxes only the allowed `OFCL` interpolation gap to 12 h while keeping all other settings frozen. `s2a` is explicitly reported as an exploratory protocol revision rather than masquerading as the original pre-registered result.
- `s2a` official chain (b) at 24 h: 12/12 event windows complete, covering 29 stations across the 10 events with qualified stations; sustained wind median absolute error is 29.28% (median bias −5.10%), gust median absolute error is 23.44% (median bias −18.55%), and median landfall track error is 66.9 km (12 events). At 48 h: 11/12 windows complete, but the Nicholas `2021-09-12 00 UTC` cycle has no `OFCL` forecast points in the a-deck, leaving 9 events / 22 stations paired out of the 10 events with qualified stations; sustained wind median absolute error is 41.05% (bias −37.89%), gust is 45.53% (bias −43.87%), and median landfall track error is 103.1 km (11 events). At 72 h: 0/12 windows complete, so no aggregate station or track errors are reported. Missing windows are not treated as zero error, and partial 72 h nodes must not be substituted for full windows.
- Pangu 48 h single-event tracking test on Milton: 12 six-hourly points cover the full observation window; fetched 946,339,840 bytes via HTTP Range across 3,610 requests in 468.65 s without downloading raw multi-gigabyte files to the workstation. Landfall center error is 48.87 km vs 64.91 km for contemporaneous `OFCL`. At the sole qualified station (`PGD`), Pangu track + `OFCL` intensity yielded a sustained wind absolute error of 45.29% vs 57.92% for `OFCL` (single-event ratio 0.782), and gust errors of 49.72% vs 61.33%. This demonstrates code and bandwidth feasibility on a single event and single station, not an overall 48 h (c)/(b) ratio, non-inferiority event count, or B1 gate clearance. The tracker implements the pre-registered simplified 850 hPa circulation algorithm rather than a full reproduction of DeMaria Table A2. Remaining Pangu/FourCastNet/GraphCast cases were not completed; missing runs are neither padded with zeros nor swapped for other models.
- Across the 34 pre-identified dropout/right-censored stations: 19 have positive observed lower bounds and 15 lack usable bounds; model peaks fell below the observed lower bound at 2/19 (sustained) and 4/19 (gust) for (a), 11/19 and 13/19 for `s2a` (b) at 48 h, and 4/5 each for (c) on Milton at 48 h.
- The CIRA archive lists `NPNG`/`NGRP`/`NFOR` but provides no file-level ATCF for Milton, and all three aids have 0 entries in the NHC Milton a-deck, so no off-the-shelf historical AI tracks were obtained there. While Weather Lab documentation promises CSV/ATCF and ensemble member tracks from ~2023 onward, accessing the site redirects to Google sign-in with no saved session available, preventing verification of member counts or coverage across the 6 events; thus chain (c′) was not computed.

## Criteria and Cost
Original `s2` 48 h (c)/(b) median absolute error ratio: not computable; non-inferiority event count: not computable; formal gate verdict: undecided. This is because the pre-registered interpolation gap conflicted with actual 12 h `OFCL` nodes, Nicholas lacks 48 h `OFCL` in the fixed sample under `s2a`, and chain (c) completed only the Milton single-event test. A 1/1 single-event result must not be treated as ≥2/3, nor may Nicholas be silently dropped to alter the denominator. In v1, chain (a) sustained wind bias (+9.89%) remains within ±20%, which by itself does not constitute passing Gate B1.

This task used workstation CPU + public HTTP requests, opening zero Colab sessions and zero cluster jobs (0 CU). Network volume and wall time for the Milton AIWP file are reported above; traffic for other public dataset queries was not metered uniformly and is not claimed as 0 bytes. Figures explicitly credit NOAA NHC `OFCL`/`BEST` sources and plot only available official chains.

## Independent Decisions Needed Next
To complete a formal gate evaluation, the Lead must first confirm a new protocol version after publicly logging the invalidation of original `s2`: permitting 12 h `OFCL` interpolation and deciding how to handle Nicholas lacking a 48 h official forecast (retain as ungradable or revise the cohort years?), while keeping the original 29 stations, ±20%, 1.1×, and ≥2/3 thresholds strictly unchanged. Batch remote tracking should proceed only after the revised protocol is frozen. No criteria were altered on behalf of the Lead or Liang Hu here.

# B1+B4 Stage 2b Preregistration (s2b)

Freeze time: 2026-10-14 17:25 EDT; finalized in writing before any new (c) observation pairing in this version. Original s2, s2a originals and results are not overwritten. Previously, s2a's (b) and the Milton Pangu single case were already visible, so this is not blinded. Basis: Items 1–6 and Supplement 7.

1. Adopt s2a's interpolation modification: linear interpolation is allowed when the interval between adjacent OFCL nodes is ≤12 h; the 24 h interval of 72 h spanning 72→96 h is for reporting only, allowing ≤24 h interpolation, labeled "coarse interpolation", not entering the gate; no out-of-bounds extrapolation.
2. The gate is calculated only on homogeneous events where both (b)(c) chains have inputs and have v1 qualified stations. Nicholas 48 h is recorded as "no official forecast, unevaluable", not calculated in either chain, and initialization time is not changed. Expected 9 events, 22 stations; simultaneously reported against the denominator of 10 events with qualified stations for comparison. The original 29-station set, the criteria that 48 h Pangu sustained wind all-station median absolute error ≤1.1×(b) and ≥2/3 evaluable events are not worse than (b) remain unchanged; an event not worse than is defined as within-event station |e| median ≤(b). Gusts are reported in parallel rather than selected post hoc.
3. Primary (c) = Pangu: run all events for 24 and 48 h. FourCastNet v2 and GraphCast are secondary results for 48 h only, not replacing primary gate judgment. s2's 850 hPa tracker is frozen: CARQ τ=0 seed, 850 hPa relative vorticity 5×5 smoothing, 200 km disk average, maximum positive vorticity within 350 km of previous step's center and 100–400 km cyclonic average tangential wind >0; if any 6 h point lacks positive vorticity/cyclonic circulation or jumps >350 km, the track is broken, without skipping missing points to continue, without reseeding to BEST, and without switching to MSLP minimum. Each step moves only according to already tracked points, without using future BEST.
4. (c′) Weather Lab attempts only once via public pathways requiring no login (direct download links in documentation or public storage); if login is required, record as "not obtained" and stop, without using Liang Hu's Google credentials.
5. Truncated lower bound test for the three chains (a)(b)(c) is executed per s2 frozen definition: maximum sustained/gust before reporting dropout of truncated stations serves as true peak lower bound, counting the number/proportion of stations where model peak is below lower bound; for reporting only, not entering the gate.
6. Complete this document before new (c) observation pairings; retain s2 original and s2a output. Wind field, station QC, duration conversion, pressure and scale extrapolations all follow , strictly never tuning parameters based on errors. OFCL and AI use the same initialization time and OFCL intensity; BEST is used only for post hoc track error verification, not for constructing the two forecast chains. HTTP Range limits reading of AIWP, not saving raw full files to disk.

## Additional Reporting (Supplement 7, not entering gate)
Sustained wind and gusts across the three chains (a)(b)(c) are normalized by the closest distance from station to each chain's own track and each chain's own RMW at the closest point time, categorized into <1×RMW, 1–3×RMW, >3×RMW; and binned into <50, 50–100, >100 km. Each bin reports station count, median bias, median absolute error; deliver . Boundary values are assigned to the subsequent bin; based on the shortest distance from each station to the track point of the paired window where the model peak occurs within ±12 h of landfall; if track breaks and is unavailable, it does not enter that chain's stratification. This is diagnostic, and the gate judgment will strictly never be altered based on stratification. Basis: Lead decision document lines 21–22.

Cost: Local CPU only or single-run ≤20 CU Colab CPU; stop after use. Each model/lead time reports failure/missing observation by event, strictly never treated as zero error. Code and numerical outputs are written only to s2b/ new files.

# B1 v2 Protocol Draft — Unfrozen

Time: 10-14 20:31 EDT. This document is merely a project initiation feasibility plan, and running new (b)(c) station pairings or announcing a gate verdict based on it is prohibited. The original s2b verdict text is unaffected. Refer to the event-by-event inventory of , the original , the project page, and the review verdict.

## Prerequisite Go/No-Go (Finalized by Lead Prior to Official v2)

R1: Prove that each input is operationally available at decision time and capable of providing ΔP/RMW/B required by H08; fix the environmental GFS product release time, KZ07's V500/Penv annulus calculation, OFCL wind radii applicability levels, and missing wind radii rules; determine weights/ranges independently, without fitting to station errors. R2: Approve homogeneous observation station classes and confirm event-by-event at least 15 evaluable events with at least 3 stations per event; currently there are only 7 pre-screened 1-min candidates, with a potential 14 in the hourly pool, and hourly verification for Eta has not yet been conducted. R3: The censoring scheme must be registered in advance and executable. R4: The primary chain defaults to the Pangu 850 hPa circulation track; if changed to GraphCast or AI consensus, pre-registration must be revised prior to any new pairing and explain the 2020–21 gap; do not modify the primary chain based on having seen the results.

## Units, Samples, and Homogeneous Denominator

Landfall event definitions follow the feasibility table; for multiple landfalls, freeze the primary landfall point/UTC time first, and switching to secondary landfalls after seeing errors is prohibited. Fix the 150 km radius from the center and the landfall ±12 h target window, and provide in advance the actual initialization lead time and object list for each event. Separately register station proximity, platform/land, sensor 10m height, HAS1MIN, presence of valid minutes/hours, observation averaging interval, and wind direction exposure. The primary analysis is recommended to use only complete 1-minute ASOS (`sknt` ~2-min sustained wind, `gust_sknt` 5-s reported peak); if R2 requires H2 hourly stations due to insufficient sample size, an "hourly homogeneous primary analysis" must first be separately frozen, synchronously downsampling v1 1-minute data and re-evaluating (a); the two densities cannot be pooled together to calculate a single median. ERA5 cannot be treated as independent station observations. The denominator is the event intersection where both Pangu and OFCL exist for the same initialization, the same batch of observations is qualified for both chains, and peak window checks are completed; the ex-ante list and all missing measurement reasons and station counts per category must be fully listed; events lacking official forecasts, such as Nicholas, must not be treated as forecast failures, nor should cycles be swapped to make up for them. Report both the intention-to-evaluate full event set denominator and the homogeneous evaluable denominator—provide both, and do not cherry-pick the denominator that favors the conclusion.

## Models and Operational Timing

(a) BEST center and intensity, using archived BEST wind radii as the post-hoc physical upper-bound chain, following the exact same pressure/scale solver and station exposure and averaging interval as (b)(c); missing values must not inversely draw on (b) intelligence. Freeze the model, error windows, and parameters first, and then run only (a): sustained wind ratio error median bias  must be within ±20%, reporting both absolute error and gusts, with station-by-station auditing; if disqualified, stop (b)(c). Passing the gate under the old (a) cannot replace passing the gate under new inputs.

(b) NHC official OFCL track and intensity, and wind radii issued at that time; (c) Pangu 850 hPa positive vorticity + tangential circulation tracking track, **sharing (b)'s official intensity and identical pressure/scale inputs**, strictly never reading post-hoc b-decks. First constrain symmetric outer scale using OFCL 34/50/64 kt wind radii, with Knaff et al. 2007 North Atlantic climatological RMW as a prior rather than case-by-case ground truth; Knaff–Zehr 2007 ΔP formula must use large-scale S/V500/Penv from GFS that was already available at the time, and wind radii must not be disguised as S. When wind radii are only 34 kt, Penv or V500 is missing, or H08 RMW/B cannot be fitted, halt the chain for that event/node according to the frozen missing-data scheme or use a pre-specified climatological value labeled "assumption", without back-deriving from station errors. Card PDF 3–4, 6 / Journal 783–784, 786;  PDF 4–5, 10 / Journal 74–75, 80. If H08/land-sea conversion and ~2-min/5-s factors follow v1, retaining them remains an assumption; if modified, the new parameter table must first state the source, range, and sensitivity.

OFCL is typically publicly released about 3 h after the corresponding AIWP 00/12 initialization, and cannot be treated as available at the same moment as the AI initialization. At the frozen common decision time T = actual public release date/time of OFCL for that cycle, compare (b) and (c) both using the latest official intensity and wind radii available before T, and AI using the 00/12 initialization already available before T along with its release time; for each event, record AIWP model initialization, object release time, OFCL release, decision T, and remaining hours until actual landfall. Historical actual release time cannot be presumed from archive filenames. Report actual lead times paired with the same cycle initialization and an "AI available earlier" sensitivity analysis, neither allowing AI to surreptitiously use initializations after decision time nor claiming that both chains share the same release timestamp. Track errors at ±12 h and track error at landfall time are reported independently; BEST is used only for post-hoc scoring.

## Station Peaks, Censoring, and Scoring

Pre-specify station observation completeness thresholds and physical QC (following v1 if applicable: at least 90% valid minutes within model peak t* ± 6 h, with valid records at start and end; for hourly stations, separately specify coverage and boundary conditions), and define uniform window expansion rules if the model peak shifts outside the original download window. All three chains use the same intersection of qualified stations; if t* positions differ across the three chains, record t*, window inclusion, and censoring reasons chain-by-chain; the comparison window must be the same pre-defined event window, rather than cherry-picking observed peaks favorable to each. Incomplete observations are assigned a lower bound `obs_true_peak≥obs_observed_peak`: report primary estimates for complete stations alongside interval/lower-bound sensitivities for censored stations; when right-censoring does not provide a physical upper bound, calculating a fictitious finite median is not permitted. Completeness rates are stratified by event, distance to eye, and forecast peak time difference, clarifying that missingness is not random. Gusts and sustained winds are reported separately; do not treat 5-s gusts as 2-min winds.

The primary criterion follows the project page, unchanged: 48 h homogeneous stations (c)/(b) ≤ 1.1, and in at least 2/3 of homogeneous evaluable events, the within-event station absolute error median has (c) ≤ (b); on the premise of (a) bias ±20%. 24/72 h, gusts, track errors, three-chain censoring lower bounds, and full event set denominator are reported only and not cherry-picked into the primary gate. If the Lead considers adjusting 1.1 or 2/3, this constitutes another scientific criterion and must be decided prior to freezing by the Lead/Liang Hu according to established authority; this draft does not alter it arbitrarily. If fewer than 15 events each with ≥3 stations, do not evaluate the v2 gate, and only report the feasibility gap.

## Fields That Must Be Completed in the Official Pre-registration First

1. Event list/primary landfall, event-by-event 48 h AIWP and OFCL specific initialization + release times, intensity/wind radii valid nodes, GFS operational products at the time and historical availability timestamps.
2. Actual optimization objectives, weights, constraints, missing-threshold fallbacks, and sensitivity ranges from OFCL wind radii to H08 RMW/B; identical algorithm for BEST wind radii and rules for events without radii, with parameter source table noting paper page numbers or "assumption" item by item.
3. Homogeneous observation station table and 10m height, 2-min/5-s averaging intervals, exposure and hourly sampling consistency; reports by event and station for three-chain censoring and "whether new model peak t* falls within complete observation window".
4. Actual lead time, ±12 h track error, landfall center error, observed lower bound violation rate; both denominators for all events and homogeneous intersection, tracking all failures/missing data.

Cost: This round is document design only, local CPU; Colab 0 CU. Prior to official batch processing, estimate CU based on sample size/HTTP Range request volume, and stop Colab after use; do not download raw complete AIWP files to the  workstation.

# B1 v2 可行性核查（只数事件和观测可用性，不做新预报站点配对）

时间：10-14 20:31 EDT。依据：；原 s2b 失败判词保留，不能以本核查翻案。可复核原始元数据：同目录，对应生成脚本 与。无新 (a)/(b)/(c) 观测配对。

## R2：样本可得性与定义

从 NHC 2026-09-23 版 HURDAT2 中筛 2020-10 后美国本土首次显著登陆：登陆标志 L、登陆时 HU 或强 TS（预筛定义 Vmax≥50 kt）；同一事件多次登陆只计一次，以主美国本土登陆为锚。原来的 12 个事件加 7 个新候选，共 19 个；2025 本土 Chantal 为 45 kt，故在本预筛定义下没有新增符合的 2025 个例。这个 ≥50 kt 是本次候选界定，不是重新冻结的科学判据；若 Lead 希望包括较弱 TS，应另列敏感集合。2020-10 之前事件不在 AIWP 覆盖范围内。来源：NHC HURDAT2 上述版本及原。

起报取登陆时刻减 48 h 后最近的先前 00/12 UTC AIWP 周期。新候选逐一用 S3 列表接口核了 PANG_v100_GFS 精确对象，用相同周期 ATCF a-deck 的 OFCL 行核官方预报存在；有行不等于其未来每节点均可插值，后者留给冻结后再核。已核过的旧 12 个 Pangu 48 h 均有对象；旧 Nicholas 官方同起报无预报，沿 s2b 记不可评。

| 事件（年） | Pangu 对象 / 同起报 OFCL | v1 HAS1MIN 150 km：≥90% 登陆±6h 代理站数；旧事件为 v1 正式合格站数 | H2 小时站 150 km 已有通过数 | 此轮判断 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Delta (2020) | 是 / 是 | 3 | 9 | 严格 1min 可候选 |
| Zeta (2020) | 是 / 是 | 2 | 11 | 仅小时池可候选 |
| Eta (2020) | 是 / 是 | 0/8 | 尚未跑 H2 小时事件 | 暂不可评；小时池可能补 |
| Elsa (2021) | 是 / 是 | 3/3 | 未建 H2 事件 | 严格代理可候选 |

分母解读：旧事件 1min 列是 v1 的模型峰窗口 ±6 h 完整性和物理 QC 后正式站数（并非纯观测可用性）；新事件只是登陆锚点 ±6h、有效持续风独立分钟数 ≥648 的观测可用性代理，尚未做峰值落窗及物理 QC。不同定义不可当作同等级的“合格站”相加。按更严的旧正式站数 + 新可用性代理，有 OFCL/Pangu 同起报且至少 3 站的候选是旧 4（Delta/Ian/Debby/Francine；Nicholas 虽 7 站但无同起报 OFCL）、新 3，共 **7 个预筛候选**；不是 7 个已确认 v2 可评事件。新候选全部要求在冻结后按新模型峰时补齐观测窗。

H2 与 用原有小时 METAR、有效小时≥75% 且原 H08 模型峰±2h 有报的幸存站；逐站与 H2 站表交集，再筛原登陆点 150 km，得到旧 12 个全都有≥3 小时站，但 Nicholas 无 OFCL，故仅 **11 个**可作新口径候选。与新事件 Elsa/Fred/Henri 三例 1min 预筛相加，宽松潜在集合 14 个；Eta 有 OFCL/Pangu，但本次 1min 站 0/8，须另外以 H2 小时网证实才能使候选数触到 15。不能把未做的 Eta 小时核查当作已可评，也不能把 300 km 的 H2 汇总 794 站当作 150 km 的同质站网。即使 15 个潜在候选成立，重过 (a) 和逐站同质 QC 后还可能减少。当前 **未证明达到 R2 的 ≥15 个可评事件且每事件≥3 合格站**。

H2 并非另一种独立风速传感器网络：H2 主要是 IEM 小时 ASOS/METAR 的更广站点池和 ERA5 背景，ERA5 是再分析/模型而非独立站点真值，WorldCover 是地表类。1min ASOS 的 `sknt` 是约 2min 持续风，`gust_sknt` 是 5s 峰；小时 METAR `sknt` 是报时前约 2min 平均、`gust` 是报时前窗口内约 5s 峰值报告而非连续逐分钟峰。均需同站高度/传感器、站点海陆与风向暴露、时距一致，并以站元数据核查 10m 基准；不能把小时 METAR 峰值与分钟峰值不经抽样校正混合。H2 的小时入选率不是 v1 分钟截尾的替代；同一分钟资料降采样成小时，测量时距可相同但极值采样密度不同。建议只设分层主分析（同一时间采样/站类）和分别报告的副分析，不混成一个站点绝对误差中位数。小时池的独立性/ASOS 与 AWOS 身份、真 10 m 高度须逐站核。

## R1：输入路线选择与未闭合项

选“业务 OFCL 风圈 + 强度 + 大尺度环境场”的组合，而不是事后 BEST RMW/POCI，也不把西北太平洋 AH77 的幂指数搬来大西洋：

1. 对 (b)(c) 同起报、同核算时间使用已发布 OFCL Vmax、位置、平移速度、34/50/64 kt 四象限半径；先以 Knaff et al. 2007 的北大西洋气候 RMW 初值 `r_mc=36.1000−0.0492 Vmax+0.5740(lat−25)` 海里，以及 `x_c=0.1147+0.0055 Vmax−0.0010(lat−25)`。Vmax 单位 kt；这是气候先验，不是逐案观测 RMW。再用非零 OFCL 风圈约束对称外侧尺度（以四象限残差留痕，只有 34 kt 的 Fred 不可声称完整识别 RMW）。Rankine x 不能直接当 Holland B。出处：卡，PDF 第 3–4、6 页/期刊第 783–784、786 页。
2. ΔP 候选用 Knaff–Zehr 2007 式 7：`Vsrm=Vmax−1.5 c^0.63`； hPa。Vmax、c 为 kt，V500 为 400–600 km 环带切向风，Penv 为 800–1000 km 环带平均 MSLP。**S 不是 OFCL 风圈，不能设成 R34/RMW**。气压中心，PDF 第 4–5、10、14 页/期刊第 74–75、80、84 页，原文独立样本气压 MAE 5.30 hPa（不保证本站风误差）。
3. 把 RMW 初值与 ΔP、OFCL 风圈带入已选 H08 的前向风速方程，针对可用阈值半径做有界目标拟合 RMW 与 Holland B，强度作约束，优先保留物理可解释的 RMW/B 范围。**此 Holland 逆问题及目标权重/上下界尚无文献给出的通用常数；这一步是拟议的工程假设，不是 Knaff 原法**。必须在接触 v2 的 (a) 站点误差前，从独立的 BEST 强度/风圈资料或文献给定范围预定目标函数、惩罚与缺失风圈规则，给敏感区间；风圈不全则标识不可识别或切回预注册的气候 RMW 先验。不得从站点风调参。

参数来源表：Vmax/轨迹/风圈来自同起报 OFCL a-deck（新事件）；要换须另开 v2 前冻结。

## (a) 重过闸与截尾

先单独冻结 v2 输入/风场/观测定义：BEST 事后轨迹作为 (a) 的中心和强度，BEST 当时风圈或扩展最佳路径风圈同一拟合器和缺测规则，绝不拿预报链独有的未来信息反灌；不可用的 BEST 风圈要保留缺测，缺失机制对齐。锁定同一站点高度、观测时距、海陆暴露和新峰值窗，先只跑 (a)；持续风站点 必须在 ±20%，同时报中位绝对误差、分事件结果和阵风副指标；未过就停止，不跑 (b)(c)。v1 曾通过的 (a) 不能自动继承到换输入/站池的 v2。

截尾按预测峰时刻与观测窗口完整性预先定义可比较站；若在强风段断报，不以已观测最大值当真峰，标右截尾/下限 `true_peak≥observed_max`，主估计可采用预注册区间型损失并给最乐观/最悲观边界，另报完全观测子集；未知上界不得凭空当有限区间。模型峰 t* 超出已取观测窗，按事前统一扩展窗口取数或记不可评，不能按哪条链的成绩来选站。多链使用同一交集、逐事件截尾数、真实峰下限和两链峰时错位表均必报。

## 结论与花费

**不值得现在启动 v2 正式判闸**：严格 1min 仅 7 个预筛候选；宽松 H2 小时站已有 14 个潜在候选，Eta 尚可能补至 15 但没核实，且小时峰与分钟峰不可无校准混算；R1 的环境场业务可得性和 Holland 拟合闭合也待冻结。值得仅做定向的 Eta 小时站完整性、GFS 归档发布时间和 (a) 前向公式审计，满足 R1–R3 后再决定正式 v2。预计后续元数据核查为本地 CPU 小任务；正式 AIWP 路径链的网络/CPU 工作量可参照 s2b 读取 40.27 GB，具体 CU 在协议和候选站固定后估算，不预支。本次仅本地 CPU 与 HTTP 元数据/1min 下载，没有 Colab 会话，0 CU；网络美元费用未计量。

引用：NHC HURDAT2 https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/hurdat/hurdat2-1851-2025-092326.txt；ATCF https://ftp.nhc.noaa.gov/atcf/archive/；AIWP https://noaa-oar-mlwp-data.s3.amazonaws.com/；IEM https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/asos/1min.phtml。外部来源在 已登记，新用的 Knaff et al. 2007 风圈文献已追加。

results.title: B1 v2 pre-registration final-draft candidate — not frozen by the Lead; running is prohibited
results.text:
# B1 v2 Pre-registration Finalization Candidate — Not Frozen by Lead, Execution Prohibited

Time: 10-14 22:17 (EDT). Stipulates only the next round of experiments; the published failed-gate results of s2b remain unchanged. No new station wind field pairings were performed in this round. The current R2 station pool for this candidate is not yet closed and cannot serve as an approved official pre-registration. Decision authority rests with the Lead.

## Fixed Gates and Sequence of Execution

The primary pool uses only hourly METAR, IEM `report_type=3` (no mixing with 1-minute data); 15 US landfall events with at least 3 evaluable qualified stations per event, otherwise do not evaluate the v2 gate. Run BEST (a) first using the identical wind field and identical hourly standard, with the median bias of predicted/observed peak ratio minus one at each station within ±20% as a prerequisite; stop if failed, without running (b)(c). Only after passing is the 48 h comparison conducted: ratio of homogeneous station median absolute errors for Pangu (c)/OFCL (b) ≤ 1.1, and in ≥2/3 of homogeneous evaluable events, (c) is no worse than (b) individually; both conditions must be satisfied. B4 is performed only after B1 passes the gate. 24/72 h, gusts, and track errors are diagnostic only. Denominators for both the full intention-to-evaluate set and evaluable intersection are reported, without cherry-picking favorable subsets. Original project page  lines 15–20.

## Events, Timing, and Leakage Defenses

Intended events and landfall points/times follow the 15 cases of 2020–24 from v2b; primary station candidates are those in that table with `hourly_75pct=Trueinit+3h`, but actual archived bulletin release times must be verified by the Lead prior to freezing; actual lead time relative to real landfall is reported separately. **Post-hoc RMW, Pc, POCI, and wind radii from b-deck BEST must not be provided to (b)(c)**; BEST is used only for (a) and post-hoc verification. (b) and (c) share the same-cycle official Vmax/wind radii, pressure deficit/scale, using OFCL/Pangu 850 hPa circulation tracking respectively only for tracks; tracking algorithms follow s2b, without cherry-picking optimal post-hoc tracks. If a valid node in OFFICIAL lacks necessary intensity or cannot obtain GFS fields, that node is treated as missing, without filling gaps using post-hoc data; if any critical node in the peak window is missing, the event is marked as input un-evaluable. OFCL 12 h nodes are linearly interpolated following s2b, without endpoint extrapolation; each node maintains an input availability timestamp.

GFS: NCEP/NCO provides a rolling 30-day average: 00/12 UTC GFS 48 h products are released approximately 03:51 after initialization, 06 UTC at approximately 09:49, and 18 UTC at approximately 21:51; these are not the actual release times on each historical day. Pre-emptively assume conservatively that **the moment when all required GFS forecast lead-time fields are fully public = initialization + 4 h 15 min** (allowing approximately 24 min extra beyond the statistical average; daily anomalous delays require separate review of historical records and cannot be claimed as truly released). Prior to decision T, select the most recent cycle that has already reached +4h15 by T; in cases where T = 3 h after 00/12 initialization, uniformly fall back to the preceding 18/06 UTC cycle, with the forecast lead time for the corresponding valid time being +6 h relative to the original cycle; the 48 h point becomes f054.  lists event-by-event cycles. Retrieve lead times/fields node by node anew according to the same rules, without using newer cycles released in the future. GDEX d084001 2020 0.25° and AWS GFS 2021–24 0.5° differ in grid resolution (non-homogeneous inputs) and require dual-resolution sensitivity checks; the three 2020 cases have now been actually read anonymously, but their 2020 historical release times have not been audited case by case. Current GDEX file times cannot be taken as historical public release times. The NCEP page serves as the basis for published rules rather than historical real-time auditing.

## Scale and Pressure Deficit (Strictly Never Back-Calibrated from Stations)

Knaff–Zehr (2007), Card , PDF pp. 4–5, 10 / Journal pp. 74–75, 80: Vmax=10m/1min kt, translation c kt, Vsrm=Vmax−1.5 c^0.63; Penv is mean sea level pressure in the 800–1000 km annulus around the center in hPa; V500 is 400–600 km annulus mean tangential wind in kt, S=V500/V500c; V500c=Vmax(Rmax/500)^x, x=0.1147+0.0055Vmax−0.001(φ−25), Rmax=66.785−0.09102Vmax+1.0619(φ−25) km. Eq. (7): Pc=Penv+23.286−0.483Vsrm−(Vsrm/24.254)^2−12.587S−0.483φ; ΔP=Penv−Pc. **V500 wind level**: KZ07 original text PDF p. 5 only specifies "400–600-km-annulus-mean tangential wind from the NCEP analyses", and the main text does not explicitly specify 850 hPa; one cannot falsely claim it wrote 850. The abstract/methodology of related Knaff et al. (2014) original text writes 850 hPa V500, citing the precedent of Knaff–Zehr (2007), https://doi.org/10.1175/JCLI-D-13-00096.1; this experiment is operationally fixed to GFS 850 hPa U/V, clarified as a reasonable layer selection following the same series of methods, not a direct specification in the original KZ07 text. v2b mistakenly used 10m wind, and v2c has been verified against actual GRIB at 850 hPa. Wind field four quadrants cannot be directly taken as S; KZ climatological Rmax is not case-by-case observed RMW. When encountering Vmax < 15 kt or V500c ≤ 0, ΔP ≤ 0, or corrupted fields, nodes are treated as missing data, without trimming into "seemingly reasonable" pressure deficits. The two grid resolutions of large-scale S serve as diagnostics; relative winds are calculated against the frozen identical official center, without using BEST center in the operational chain.

RMW prior comes from Knaff et al. (2007) Card , PDF pp. 3–4, 6 / Journal pp. 783–784, 786: North Atlantic rmc=36.1000−0.0492Vmax+0.5740(φ−25) nmi. Rankine x and Holland B in this paper **are not the same number**. H08 and roughness/averaging interval follow v1 CLIMADA 6.1.0 fixed commit bb9595, Natural Earth 10m land, z0 sea 0.0013m/land 0.03m/reference 500m, sustained × 0.97, gusts land × 1.30/sea × 1.20; these remain assumptions, with ranges and grounds see  lines 5–11.

**Proposed frozen engineering assumption for wind radii → H08 scale fitting (still requiring unit testing without observations)**: CLIMADA v6.1.0 H08 `_bs_holland_2008` computes `hol_b` based on pressure deficit, pressure rate of change, latitude, and translational velocity; `_v_max_s_holland_2008` then recomputes based on that B and pressure deficit `vmaxΣ_k w_k / N_k × Σ_q(log(r_pred,k/r_obs,kq))² + 0.25(log(r/rmc))²`, w_34/50/64=1/2/3 (engineering assumption), where N_k is the number of valid quadrants for that threshold; do not sneakily adjust H08 B for "asymmetric radii". Prune nodes with r ≤ 0, threshold ≥ operational Vmax, requiring at least two different thresholds each having ≥2 quadrants, ΔP > 0, rmc ∈ [5, 200] nmi; remaining nodes are missing, with no implicit fallbacks. Proposed sensitivities: r lower bound 3–10, upper bound 150–250 nmi, prior coefficient 0.1–1, equal threshold weighting vs 1/2/3; report only, strictly never cherry-picking based on station errors. **Numerical identity between CLIMADA H08's actual radial function and this offline fitter must still be verified**, which is stricter than syntax checking; unverified experiments cannot be frozen as executable. (a) BEST also uses the same RMW fitting rules and independent BEST wind radii/center/intensity, without borrowing OFCL to fill holes.

## Primary Observations, Censoring, and Scoring

Candidate station equipment prerequisite rules: include only stations explicitly verified as ASOS on the event date with anemometer height verifiable at 8–12 m during the event (8–12 m is an engineering assumption for "close to 10m", with a range of 9–11 m for sensitivity; stations where identity/height cannot be found or having only 2025 snapshots without historical lineage do not enter the **confirmed** sample). AWOS is not included in this edition's primary pool even if height is 10m, to avoid differing equipment standards; listing separate alternative sensitivities requires a new protocol and cannot be added post-hoc to make up numbers. Sources prioritize NCEI HOMR event date ; 2025 snapshot heights in  cannot prove heights for 2020–24. Under this strict rule, 15×3 is currently not confirmed, and **gate evaluation is prohibited**.

Observations follow IEM hourly `report_type=3`, deduplicated to UTC hourly grid, `sknt≥0e=pred_peak/obs_peak−1`; take station then event median, with the primary statistic being the whole-pool median of |e| across stations, and event win/loss compared by within-event median of station-level |e|. Sustained wind serves as the primary gate; gusts are reported alongside and do not substitute. Best track (a) is recalculated using these exact same observation rules and candidate stations, and passing the gate in old 1-minute v1 must never be carried over.

## Unclosed Pre-freeze Verifications

1. Station-by-station HOMR historical heights are currently **incomplete**, and existing 2025 NWS equipment snapshots are insufficient; the conservative confirmed count is 0 (this indicates "evidence not yet confirmed" rather than asserting all stations are unqualified), with conditional snapshots yielding ≥3 stations for only 13 events, falling short for Delta and Milton. The Lead needs to decide whether to supplement historical metadata, legitimately expand homogeneous station types in advance, or halt; R2 15×3 cannot be altered without Liang Hu.
2. The original s2b `init+3h` is merely an assumed uniform public bulletin release time, not verified case by case against historical bulletins; NCEP rolling averages do not guarantee that every GFS field in 2020–24 was actually released prior to T. If unverifiable, be sure to label as "conservative operational timing proxy", and do not write that it has been verified case by case.
3. The coupling between the currently proposed fitter and CLIMADA H08's B calculation needs source code/unit test verification; whether events and nodes lacking complete wind radii lead to <15×3 remains unverified.  is only candidate fitter and pre-validation scripts; running (a) is prohibited after syntax checking.

# B1 v2c Pre-check (10-14 22:20 EDT)

No new (a)(b)(c) model wind–station pairings were executed, nor were gates evaluated. Conclusion: **Currently, v2 preregistration cannot be frozen as an executable version**; the 2020 three-case GFS fields can be read, but neither strict historical equipment height QC nor H08 parameter adaptation has been closed yet.

1. 2020 three-case operational environmental fields: GDEX d084001 anonymous HTTPS full GRIB2 decoded in memory (no large files retained); Delta 20201007 06Z f054: 850 hPa V500 22.315 kt, Penv 1013.311 hPa; Zeta 20201026 06Z f054: 14.366 kt, 1012.218 hPa; Eta 20201106 18Z f054: 31.168 kt, 1013.363 hPa. The center uses the then-current OFCL f048 position, sampling GFS U/V 850 hPa and MSLP only at the forecast valid time. Actual transfer was 1,023,692,184 bytes, taking 13.93/23.28/22.89 seconds for the three cases respectively. The GRIB fields have their respective levels, times, and message offsets, see etc.; this proves the archive is readable, but does not prove it was released on that day in 2020 according to the current product schedule. The 10m V500 calculation from v2b cannot be used for this version. The Knaff–Zehr 2007 card D8NBE3ZE PDF page 5 / journal page 75 only mentions NCEP analysis tangential winds in the 400–600 km annular band, **the original text does not explicitly state 850 hPa**; adopting the 850 layer has an explicit source in the subsequent literature Knaff et al. (2014) https://doi.org/10.1175/JCLI-D-13-00096.1, rather than backfilling it into 2007. KZ07 wind-pressure relation PDF page 10 / journal page 80.

2. Operational timeline: The rolling 30-day average 48h GFS product publicly available from NCEP NCO is approximately 3h50 after the 00/12 cycles, and approximately 3h50 after the 06/18 cycles; uniformly adding a conservative margin, assuming full public availability at initialization + 4h15. Relative to the OFCL public advisory T = AIWP same-cycle initialization + 3 h, selecting the latest fully released cycle before T uniformly rolls back to the preceding 18/06Z, with 48h valid time GFS f054; individual initializations for the 15 events are at . **This is a preregistration operational timeline proxy, not a proof of historical case-by-case release**. If the Lead requires strict historical availability rather than a conservative proxy, this item remains unclosed; the preceding cycle `.idx` for 2021–24 has not been checked case by case (v2b checked the same-cycle f048, which cannot be repurposed as evidence of availability for this cycle).

3. 170 station–event identities and heights: The Wind Tower Height worksheet from the NWS 2025 equipment inventory was matched station ID by station ID with the Legacy ASOS In Service Dates table; among the 170 station–events, 80 in the 2025 inventory have ASOS entries and heights, and 90 are not in this ASOS inventory (which does not equate to having proven they are AWOS; other historical station tables must be checked one by one). Using a **conditional 2025 snapshot** with commissioning date ≤ event year and height 8–12 m as a proxy, 61 station–events and 13 events each have ≥3 stations; Delta and Milton have only 1 station each, while the other 13 cases have 3–17 stations. The 2025 inventory cannot retrospectively verify the instrument model/height back in 2020–24; the NCEI HOMR station-by-station historical verification on event dates has not been completed, so the count of strictly confirmed "historically verified identity and height" is currently 0; **this must not be mislabeled as 0 qualified stations**. Row-by-row original values / sources / conditional conclusions are in , and event counts are in . Under this candidate's rule of "ASOS and historically verified height", 15×3 cannot currently be confirmed; if the 2025 inventory indeed exhausts historical ASOS, the conditional upper bound is also only 13, but that exhaustiveness has not been verified, so it cannot be asserted that there are only 13 in the end. The remaining METAR stations may be AWOS and must not be sneakily added as ASOS.

4. Isaias: The AIWP S3 anonymous listing shows zero objects; 2026/1007 has `2026100700`, and 2026/1009, 1010, 1011, 1012, 1013, 1014 all have date prefixes. The missing 10-08 cycle is not a simple lag where "the entire bucket is only updated through 10-07", but rather a date/cycle void; the target same-initialization 2026100800 has still not been backfilled, and we cannot swap in the 10-07 cycle to cobble together 16 cases. Anonymous bucket: https://noaa-oar-mlwp-data.s3.amazonaws.com/?list-type=2&prefix=PANG_v100_GFS/2026/1008/.

5. Has passed Python syntax compilation checks, including strict `--lead-frozen` and historical 15×3/adapter guards, but **no observational pairings have been run, nor is it an independently executable frozen pipeline**; it still lacks validated input adaptation from upstream BEST wind radii to H08. (a) cannot be launched before the Lead freezes it. The criteria of ±20%, 1.1, 2/3, ≥15×≥3 remain unchanged.

Costs: Local CPU / anonymous HTTP, Colab 0 CU, HPC no jobs; this round consumed ~1.024 GB real read from GDEX + ~1.17 MB from NWS tables, USD bandwidth costs unmetered. If official v2 still runs locally, expected 0 Colab CU; Pangu path alone linearly extrapolated from s2b's 40.27 GB / 9 events to 15 events is ~67.12 GB (rough estimate, not costs and not full newly added GFS / observation traffic). Given the current evidentiary gate of fewer than 15 cases, **investing this official cost is not recommended**.

External sources: NWS 2025 ASOS equipment inventory https://www.weather.gov/asos/asosequip.html; HOMR historical API https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/homr/api; NCAR GDEX 10.5065/D65D8PWK; the aforementioned NCEP NCO release page; AIWP public bucket; Knaff–Zehr (2007) D8NBE3ZE, Knaff et al. (2007) ZPYAUTZG PDF pp. 3–4, 6 / journal pp. 783–784, 786. The use of these sources has been supplementally recorded in .

# B1+B4 Landfalling Hurricanes: AI Tracks and Ensembles to Station Peak Winds (Shelved)

This sub-project evaluated whether coupling global AI weather model hurricane tracks (from the NOAA AIWP archive for Pangu-Weather, FourCastNet v2, and GraphCast) with official National Hurricane Center (NHC) intensity forecasts (`OFCL`) and a parametric boundary-layer wind model (CLIMADA `H08`) improves 48-hour US landfall station peak wind predictions over the official NHC chain. After validating the best-track baseline and amending the pre-registered protocol for operational 12-hour `OFCLH08` ignored input maximum wind speeds in favor of pressure-drop scaling and that strict station height filtering left only 13 qualifying storms (below the 15-event gate), so the sub-project is Shelved.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead initiated literature reviews on AI cyclone track skill (2025 evaluations showing competitive tracks but ~40 kt negative intensity bias at 72 h) and dispatched Stage 1 best-track verification (`chain a`) to the research assistant.
- **2026-10-14**: Three reviewers audited the literature premises, noting that CIRA tracks 850 hPa vorticity rather than sea-level pressure, operational NHC `OFCL` advisories omit central pressure (P_c), outer closed isobar (POCI), and radius of maximum wind (RMW), and 2026 AI cyclone models predict both track and intensity.
- **2026-10-14**: A 4-hurricane pilot (17 ASOS stations within 150 km) using raw `H08` output produced a +50.69% median sustained wind bias due to unadjusted coastal roughness and 1-minute versus 2-minute averaging differences.
- **2026-10-14**: In Stage 1b (`v1`), the research assistant pre-registered and ran `H08` with translation asymmetry, directional land/sea roughness, and averaging-time conversion across 10 US landfalling hurricanes (29 eligible stations; 34/67 candidate stations censored due to peak-window dropouts).
- **2026-10-14**: Stage 1b reduced best-track sustained wind median bias to +9.89% (passing ±20%, with 21.02% median absolute error; 5-second gust MAE was 11.20% with −0.87% bias) and verified HTTP Range slicing of AIWP archives (88.34 MB in 38.76 s).
- **2026-10-14**: Initial Stage 2 execution (`s2`) hit a pre-registration mismatch because operational NHC `OFCL` advisories step at 12-hour intervals after 36 h rather than 6-hour intervals, and Hurricane Nicholas lacked a 48 h official forecast.
- **2026-10-14**: Under the amended protocol (`s2b`, 9 homogeneous hurricanes, 22 stations), 48 h sustained wind MAE was 41.91% for the Pangu chain versus 41.05% for `OFCL` (ratio 1.0209, passing ≤1.10), with median biases of −34.80% and −37.89%.
- **2026-10-14**: Because Pangu was non-inferior to `OFCL` on only 5/9 events (below the required 6/9; 5/10 under the 10-event denominator), the primary gate failed; secondary 48 h chains yielded ratios of 1.214 (3/9 events) for FourCastNet v2 and 0.678 (5/7 events, 17 stations) for GraphCast, while 24 h Pangu achieved a 0.85 ratio (24.87% vs. 29.28% MAE, 4/10 events).
- **2026-10-14**: Six reviewers unanimously endorsed shelving `v1` and uncovered why both forecast chains underestimated wind by 35–38%: `H08` ignored input `OFCLOFCL`).
- **2026-10-14**: In Stage 2 feasibility probes (`v2a`, `v2b`, `v2c`, 0 CU) testing restart conditions, hourly METAR station pools initially yielded 15 candidate hurricanes (170 station-events) and verified 2020–2024 GFS archive environmental inputs across all 15 storms.
- **2026-10-14**: Auditing the 170 station-events against the official ASOS equipment inventory (8–12 m anemometer height) reduced the sample to 13 qualifying hurricanes with ≥3 stations (below the 15-event gate), and `H08`'s internal Holland B calculation remained incompatible with wind-radii fitting; AI Weather Models Lead kept the sub-project Shelved.
- **2026-10-15**: Project boundaries were updated to enforce the Lab's zero-local-compute policy.

## Where it stands

This sub-project is Shelved after `v1v2` station audits left only 13 qualifying 2020–2024 US landfalling hurricanes (below the 15-event sample gate). Restarting requires both replacing `H08` with a parametric wind solver that directly assimilates operational Vmax and wind radii, and expanding the station sample (via post-2025 hurricane seasons or coastal mesonets) to reach ≥15 multi-station events.

projects.report:
# B2 AI-hybrid synthetic typhoons to coastal design wind speeds

## Objective
Use an AI/ML-assisted synthetic tropical cyclone catalog (RAFT: statistical tracks + MLP intensity) coupled with the parameterized wind field that passed Gate (a) in B1+B4 (CLIMADA 6.1.0 H08 + roughness) to compute 50- and 700-year return-period wind speeds at US Gulf and Atlantic coastal stations; compare these against the traditional statistical catalog STORM run through the same wind field chain and against ASCE 7-22 design wind speeds. Determine whether "AI synthetic typhoons → design wind speeds" is worth continuing (replacing the wind field model once Liang Hu's model is ready). Task brief.

## Criteria (frozen 10-14 19:25 after both EVA and Design Loads tracks replied; no post-hoc relaxation permitted)
**Unified convention**: Station height 10 m, open terrain (z0 = 0.03 m, corresponding to ASCE Exposure C), 3 s gust, denoted V50 and V700 (MRI 50 and 700 years). Basis: Vickery et al. 2010 give 300/700/1,700-year maps as peak gusts at 10 m in open terrain (z0=0.03 m), where Category II is 700 years (card, PDF pp. 1, 5–8 / journal pp. 613, 617–620; that paper does not explicitly state "3 s"); "3 s" is taken from ASCE 7-22 Chapter 26, where the basic wind speed V in ASCE 7-22 is the nominal 3 s gust at 10 m (33 ft) in Exposure C (close reading line 23, Ch. 26; exact page number mapping Risk Category II to 700 years pending verification against the original text by ideas). All stations are uniformly computed assuming open terrain, without directional station-exposure corrections (the ASCE maps themselves assume uniform Exposure C).

- **Gate 0 (wind field chain qualification)**: Across stations, the median bias of V700 from the STORM chain relative to ASCE 7-22 must be within ±20%. If it fails → record the conclusion as "wind field / conversion chain unqualified" and do not evaluate AI (same logic as Gate (a) in B1+B4).
- **Gate 1 (worth continuing)**: Across stations, the median absolute bias of V700 from the RAFT chain relative to ASCE 7-22 must be ≤ 15%, **and** ≤ 1.1 × the median absolute bias of the STORM chain. If both are satisfied → worth continuing; otherwise shelve and clearly document where the discrepancy lies (catalog intensity/frequency, wind field model, or conversion convention).
- **Report-only, non-gating**: Three-way V50 comparison; breakdown by coastal segment (Texas–Louisiana / Mississippi–Florida Panhandle / Florida Peninsula & Keys / Georgia–North Carolina); sampling uncertainty of return periods (annual-resampling bootstrap); sensitivity to averaging-time / gust conversions and the STORM 10 min→1 min conversion; if a public SPIN or Bose 2023 catalog is found, include it as a third chain for reporting only.
- **Decision rule if ASCE values are unavailable (pre-specified at freeze)**: ASCE 7-22 station values are retrieved strictly from public sources (ATC Hazards by Location, etc., without using Liang Hu's credentials; no reading off code PDF maps to make up numbers). If ≥12 out of 19 stations are obtained → compute and judge Gate 0 and Gate 1 on the obtained stations as usual. If <12 stations are obtained → do not judge Gate 0 / Gate 1; downgrade to a **relative comparison**: if the across-station median absolute difference in V700 of RAFT relative to STORM is ≤15%, and the median difference in each of the four coastal segments is within ±25%, record "RAFT is consistent with the traditional catalog and may continue (untested against code)"; otherwise record "RAFT is inconsistent with the traditional catalog" and specify where the discrepancy lies. Conclusions from a relative comparison must not be stated as equivalent to design wind speeds.
- **Design Loads track materials are read-only** (10-14 reply from Design Loads Lead): May cite the ASCE 7-22 wind interface close reading (needs_review), (PDF page = print page + 61), and the code text itself. Do not modify their calculators; do not cite or use for endorsement the numerical artifacts named "B2/C0" on their track (those belong to their own line, not this node).
- **Stratified reporting (added by parent project on 10-14, report-only, non-gating)**: H08 is known to overestimate across broad outer regions by ~+2.5 m/s (Node H) and underestimate in the inner core <1 RMW. For each station's V50 and V700, report the breakdown of exceedance contributions by storm track distance to the station in bins of <1, 1–3, and >3 × RMW (classified by distance/RMW at the time of peak station wind among storms exceeding that return-period wind speed); additionally, stratify and report station biases by distance to the coast (<10, 10–50, >50 km).
- Constants, stations, and methods must be written into (timestamped) before computing any station wind speeds; no changes afterward—any required modification must be logged as v2 while preserving v1.

## Stations (frozen 10-14 19:25, 19 ASOS airport stations from Texas to North Carolina)
KBRO Brownsville, KCRP Corpus Christi, KGLS Galveston, KLCH Lake Charles, KMSY New Orleans, KGPT Gulfport, KMOB Mobile, KPNS Pensacola, KAAF Apalachicola, KTPA Tampa, KRSW Fort Myers, KEYW Key West, KMIA Miami, KPBI West Palm Beach, KMLB Melbourne, KJAX Jacksonville, KCHS Charleston, KILM Wilmington, KHSE Cape Hatteras.
Only station coordinates are used (IEM station table); ASOS wind observations are not needed. If an ASCE value cannot be retrieved for a station, record it as missing and do not substitute the station.

## Current Status
**10-14 22:30 Shelved** (6/6 in favor; verdict).
- **Result** (primary version v6, RAFT annual rate using HURDAT2 observational proxy of 12.075 storms/yr): Gate 0 passed (STORM V700 median bias vs. ASCE 7-22 is −8.87%, 19/19 stations); Gate 1 failed (RAFT median absolute bias is 30.95%, >15% and >1.1×9.21%). RAFT is biased low across all four coastal segments; V50 is also biased low by −29%, showing an overall distributional low bias rather than tail-sampling noise. Sensitivity tests across annual rates of 10–20, POCI ±5 hPa, and conversion factors of 1.03–1.12 do not alter the verdict.
- **Why it failed**: The shared wind field chain is controlled by STORM passing Gate 0, and units/inputs/plotting were verified against CLIMADA 6.1.0 source code by 4 reviewers, finding no implementation error capable of explaining a 30% discrepancy. Because H08 uses only pressure deficit and does not read catalog vmax, this chain actually tests **the empirical Pc/Rmax formulas supplied by RAFT**, not its AI intensity model per se. Whether the low bias stems from the empirical Pc–vmax relation (intercept 1030 hPa paired with POCI 1010), downward-biased Rmax regression, nearshore decay, or shared assumptions was **not quantitatively separated** in this round; the authors' self-reported biases (Rmax ~19% low, landfall 99th percentile ~8 kt low, card NR_xu_2024_raft PDF pp. 6–7) serve only as directional clues.
- **What is missing**: A wind field model that directly ingests vmax (or a self-consistent Pc–vmax relationship), plus a distributional comparison of RAFT Pc/Rmax/nearshore intensity against HURDAT2/EBTRK.
- **Conditions for restart**: Prerequisite work—either Liang Hu's wind field model becomes available, or a distributional diagnostic of RAFT Pc/Rmax/nearshore intensity against HURDAT2/EBTRK is completed first (initial hypothesis: pairing the linear Pc formula with purely pressure-driven H08 loses ~10–15% at the strong-typhoon end, estimated by reviewer E, not yet recomputed); **Trigger**—write a new pre-registration based on those findings and re-run under the exact same frozen thresholds; restart succeeds only if Gate 0 still passes and Gate 1 passes, without tuning any parameters against this round's ASCE errors. If a new public AI synthetic catalog emerges that natively includes Pc/Rmax (which SPIN currently lacks), it may also be tested under the same protocol.
- **10-15 00:10 B2 wrap-up (status remains Shelved)**: Attribution complete—the primary cause is that the RAFT catalog itself produces almost no Cat3+ passages nearshore (especially in the Gulf of Mexico and the Carolinas), rather than the empirical Pc/RMW formulas or the wind field model. Consequently, switching to a wind field model that directly uses vmax (H10) cannot rescue it, because vmax itself is too weak nearshore. **Revised restart condition**: Only when a new AI synthetic catalog (or a new version of RAFT) becomes available, first run a low-cost screen (0 SU) using this diagnostic's "near-station Cat3+ passage rate vs. HURDAT2" table; only if passage rates across segments are of the same order of magnitude as observations should it enter the design wind speed chain, with a fresh pre-registration under the original frozen thresholds and 19 stations. Local copies of raw public data have been deleted from the workstation (re-fetchable).
- **10-14 23:30 Diagnostic v1 returned**: Neither the empirical Pc formula nor RMW is the primary cause, leaving no pre-registerable correction, so no restart PREREG will be drafted; the remaining discrepancy lies in "intensity × passage frequency of strong near-station storms," and ideas has been dispatched for the final step: near-station strong-storm passage frequency of RAFT/STORM vs. HURDAT2 (artifact) to wrap up B2.
- **10-14 22:45 Pre-restart diagnostic dispatched** (Lab Lead, status remains Shelved): ideas (queued), comparing vmax/Pc/ΔP/Rmax of RAFT/STORM against HURDAT2+EBTRK, swapping Pc and Rmax separately in the same H08 chain to inspect single-storm station peak wind changes, and checking CLIMADA wind field models that directly use vmax; without touching ASCE or recomputing return periods; task brief, artifact. Upon return, decide whether to draft a restart PREREG (report drafting to Node B, report to Lab Lead before running gates).
- Report errata (incorrect source for 14.5 storms/yr, relative comparison is not a gate, two undisclosed verification checks).

Opened 10-14 19:20; both EVA and Design Loads tracks confirmed no overlap and no borrowable station values or catalogs, and criteria and stations were frozen at 19:25 (including relative comparison rules if ASCE values are unavailable). Round 1 dispatched to ideas (data fetching, PREREG, dual-chain calculation, ASCE value retrieval, GitHub repository table). Literature: Grok quick check available (clues only, unreviewed); Deep Research monthly quota exhausted, Step 2 to be supplemented once quota resets, followed by ` litwiki card creation based on its conclusions.

## Established Decisions
- 2026-10-14 22:30 Shelved (review 6/6 in favor) → 
- 2026-10-14 19:25 Both tracks replied, criteria frozen (added relative comparison rules if ASCE values cannot be retrieved, plus read-only and prohibited items for Design Loads track materials) → "Supplement 2"
- 2026-10-14 Parent project added two boundaries: wait for replies from EVA / Design Loads tracks before freezing criteria; add stratified reporting by RMW distance and coastal distance → "Supplement"
- 2026-10-14 B2 kickoff, draft criteria and stations, Gate 0 prerequisite → 
- 2026-10-14 B2 opened (Node B Lead) → 

## Boundaries
- **Workstation does not run computations or store compute data (tightened by Liang Hu on 10-14, recorded 10-15)**: All wind field / catalog diagnostics, batch runs, and large downloads must be executed and stored on Colab (CPU/GPU) or CRC/TACC; the workstation only holds scripts, small results <200 MB per item, figures, and reports; if temporary storage >1 GB is strictly necessary, report to Node B first. Public raw data (large RAFT/STORM/HURDAT2 files, GFS/ERA5 fields) belong in Colab sessions or TACC /work. Supercomputer usage follows ComputeOps resource request + registration, with pre-check and submission separated into two commands; CRC defaults to single-node with group storage at ~95%, so large datasets prioritize TACC. Task briefs upon any restart must follow this rule; "workstation local priority" in older entries below is void.

# Task Brief: B2 Design Wind Speeds—AI Hybrid Synthetic Tropical Cyclone Catalogs → Parametric Wind Field → Coastal Station Return-Period Wind Speeds (10-14)

Parent: Node B Typhoon/Hurricane Wind Fields (page). This node's page.

## Question to Answer
When synthetic tropical cyclone catalogs generated with AI/machine-learning components are coupled to our gate-verified parametric wind field model, how much do the resulting 50- and 700-year return-period wind speeds at US coastal stations differ from those derived from traditional statistical synthetic catalogs and from ASCE 7-22 design wind speeds? Determine whether the "AI synthetic tropical cyclones → design wind speeds" pathway is worth continuing (replacing the wind field model once Liang Hu's model is ready).

## Known Information (Already checked by Node B Lead; do not re-check)
- Grok quick-search report (clues only, literature conclusions not yet finalized):  (citations verified in same-directory citations.md, 8/8 DOIs exist). Key takeaways: all studies producing design wind speeds use hybrid approaches (statistical tracks + machine-learning intensity, or NeuralGCM tracks + dynamical intensity), with no purely generative model found that directly outputs design wind speeds; tropical cyclone intensities in free-running AI weather/climate models are generally biased low.
- **RAFT** (Xu et al. 2024, Scientific Data, 10.1038/s41597-024-02952-7): 40,000 synthetic tropical cyclones in the North Atlantic, with statistical tracks and intensity changes predicted by an MLP neural network (using SHIPS environmental predictors), including 6 h tracks, Vmax, Pmin, and RMW. Zenodo 10392725, CC BY 4.0, main file ~154 MB (verified by Node B Lead via Zenodo API). Equivalent years / annual genesis rate must be checked from the original paper.
- **STORM** (Bloemendaal et al. 2020, Scientific Data): global statistical synthetic catalog, local PDF available (Zotero 3K6K2RM5). Serves as the traditional baseline.
- Other leads: Bose, Pintar & Simiu 2023 AIES (10.1175/AIES-D-22-0060.1, coupled ML track + intensity, NIST); Gao & Xi 2026 GMD SPIN (NeuralGCM tracks + FAST intensity, 10.5194/gmd-19-7303-2026)—check whether a public catalog is downloadable; Snaiki & Wu 2019 JWEIA (knowledge-enhanced deep learning boundary-layer wind field surrogate, local PDF Zotero MEK53ESY).
- Wind field model: retain the CLIMADA 6.1.0 H08 + sea/land roughness model from B1+B4 that already passed the chain (a) ±20% gate.

## Step 1 Actions
1. Select 10–20 US Gulf/Atlantic coastal stations (ASOS airport stations recommended, covering Texas to North Carolina, including Florida) and document them on the page.
2. Run both RAFT and STORM (North Atlantic subset) through the same wind field model, and compute 50-year and 700-year return-period wind speeds at each station in terms of 1-minute sustained wind or 3-second gust (standardize the definition and explicitly state the conversion) based on each catalog's equivalent years.
3. Baseline comparison: corresponding station values from ASCE 7-22 wind speed maps (Risk Category II, 700-year; check publicly accessible sources without using Liang Hu's credentials); if feasible, also include HURDAT2 historical empirical estimates for reference.
4. Write the criteria into the page before launching runs (must not be relaxed ex post); suggested rule: median absolute relative deviation of RAFT-chain 700-year wind speeds against ASCE 7-22 ≤15%, and no worse than the STORM chain (median absolute deviation ≤ 1.1× that of STORM) → worth continuing; otherwise clearly identify the source of discrepancy (catalog intensity, wind field model, or conversion convention). You may refine the details, but they must be frozen beforehand.
5. Literature: for any conclusions adopted from the Grok report, launch the second step (``) once Deep Research quota is restored, and create ` litwiki cards (RAFT, STORM, Bose 2023, SPIN, Snaiki 2019) before citing conclusions with card IDs and page numbers. # B2 Initiation: AI Hybrid Synthetic Tropical Cyclone Catalog → Coastal Station Design Wind Speeds (2026-10-14)

Decision I made: Based on a quick search with Grok, initiate the B2 secondary node. The first step uses RAFT (statistical tracks + MLP intensity for 40,000 North Atlantic synthetic tropical cyclones) and STORM (traditional statistical catalog) through the same CLIMADA H08 wind field, comparing 50/700-year wind speeds at 10–20 US coastal stations against ASCE 7-22; criteria are to be frozen by the sub-node before running.

Why: The Grok report indicates that in the direction of design wind speeds, AI appears only in hybrid forms, and AI free-running tropical cyclone intensity tends to be weak (lead, un); RAFT is an off-the-shelf, publicly available AI hybrid catalog containing RMW (Zenodo 10392725, CC BY 4.0, files and license already verified via API by Node B Lead), which can directly test whether "AI synthetic tropical cyclones → design wind speeds" aligns with traditional results at low cost; furthermore, it directly corresponds to the primary use case of Liang Hu's parametric model (wind-resistant design wind speeds). Basis: No literature basis (Grok conclusions pending Deep Research and passing the (a) chain +9.9% gate).

Cost of being wrong: If ASCE 7 station values cannot be obtained or the equivalent number of years for RAFT is unclear, the first step can only perform a relative comparison between RAFT and STORM, wasting one or two days; the high bias in H08 outer regions will affect both catalogs simultaneously, so the relative comparison remains valid.
