## Cat4/5 眼墙假设的直接复核

观测独立静态眼墙检验：同期近站且 EBTRK RMW 有效的 56 个 ≥114 kt 节点，固定纬度、观测 RMW 和 POCI=1010，用 CLIMADA H08 源码中的 B_s 与 Holland 静态径向风公式在 r=RMW 处分别输入观测 Pc 与 RAFT 线性式 Pc；将气压趋势和移速置零作为**静态受控测试**（源码 [5] 第 364–435、701–747 行）。RAFT 式相对观测 Pc 的中位偏高 3.62 hPa，静态眼墙风中位损失 2.87%，节点损失的 p10–p90 为 −5.77%～12.83%；不是普遍的 10–15%。

实际完整 H08 链的强风暴测试：在 5% 合成样本中以沿轨最大 vmax≥114 kt 标为 Cat4/5，而不是以站点峰值倒推强度。RAFT 有 70 条此类风暴在 19 站产出 317 条基线>5 的站点×事件；只换观测拟合 Pc，配对峰值中位 +1.84%（p10–p90 −1.53%～+3.80%）。限制为基线>25 m/s 时，39 条风暴/75 条站点×事件为 +2.97%（p10–p90 +1.14%～+4.27%）。RMW-only 在 >5 子集的中位 +15.64%，但基线>25 子集仅 +2.46%，又受逐节点抽样跳变影响；STORM 同样替换后的对照在。因而“线性 Pc 式使 Cat4/5 眼墙风普遍损失 10–15%”在此观测拟合与受控链下不成立；它不能解释整条目录的输入尾部差异。此处正负号均定义为替换后相对原始 H08 的变化，不是对工程标准的偏差。[1][3][4][5]

## 直接用 vmax 的 CLIMADA 6.1.0 实现

固定源码 （上游 URL [5]）：`MODEL_VANGmodel_kwargs={'vmax_from_cen': False}`，第 307–308 行调用 `_B_holland_1980`，第 503–508 行该 B 来自目录 vmax 与 ΔP；默认 True 则在第 304–306 行根据 Pc **覆盖**目录 vmax，不能作为“直接用 AI vmax”的候选。转换函数第 1297–1346 行显示 vmax、Pc、RMW 仍均需提供（RMW 输入海里，中心压强不高于环境压强）。H10 非“完全不要 Pc”，但非默认模式确实让目录 vmax 进入剖面；目前仅源码核实与小型 H08 pilot，**没有运行 H10 对观测的资格验证**，不得宣称它会改善结果。[5]

## 参数来源、局限与下一步

| 参数/处理 | 值或规则 | 溯源/性质 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 观测期、强度 | 1988–2018、TS/HU≥35 kt、距冻结站 ≤500 km | 与 EBTRK 重叠，按源文件同一风暴 ID/UTC；诊断抽样条件[3][4] |
| RAFT Pc、RMW | 原式 hPa、nmi；6 h | Xu 2024 PDF 第 4 页式 2–3；卡 NR_xu_2024_raft.md[1] |
| STORM Pc、RMW、vmax | hPa、km、m/s 10-min；3 h；RMW 除 1.852 | Bloemendaal 2020 PDF 第 2、5、8 页；卡 KHFQRECZ[2] |
| POCI、换算 | 1010 hPa、1.07、STORM vmax×1.11 | 旧 PREREG 假设；不从本站观测或工程标准重新求优 |
| Pc 替换 | 观测二次拟合；35–150 kt 外端点裁剪 | 本轮 1,515 节点的经验诊断；外推/曲线族均是假设 |
| RMW 替换 | 条件经验池与逐节点固定随机数 | 本轮假设；时间不连续，不能作生产性修正 |
| 事件入样 | SHA256(event) mod 20<1 | 5% 描述性样本；无随机重复或置信区间，不能推至 V50/V700 |
| 海陆分档 | 合成 Natural Earth 1:10m land；观测 EBTRK signed land distance | 不同参考海岸线；前者只二值海/陆，不报精确 <10/10–50/>50 km |

**可预注册的修正：现在没有。** 观测条件 Pc 替换仅引起有限强风提升，RMW 效应受时间不连续抽样污染，STORM 同样受它显著影响；更上游的强度尾部与目录路径/频率未通过本次单因素替换分离。下一轮如要探索可先另写 PREREG：①保留原闸 0/闸 1 的门槛与冻结 19 站，不得删站、改阈值；②仅用本轮观测输入检验来预先选择一个直接用 vmax 的模型（候选 H10 `vmax_from_cen=False`）并先验证单位、眼墙/外围表现，Pc 与 RMW 采用明确来源、时间连续的观测条件规则；③锁定后才可在新运行根上重跑目录对比，并把是否改进作为待验证问题。绝不可依据任何规范比对值拟合 Pc、RMW 或选择风场模型。当前 B2 状态继续搁置。

文件：（主输入表）、脚本及。原始压缩证据 `diag5_output.zip`；诊断不会替代旧产品。Colab CPU 作业完成且会话已 `stop`；账户有其他活跃会话，不能精确归因共享账户的 CU 变化，本任务自身未见 >5 CU 的迹象。

[2] https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0381-2 — Bloemendaal et al. 2020 STORM

# B2 AI Hybrid Synthetic Typhoons to Coastal Design Wind Speeds (Shelved)

This sub-project evaluated whether the 40,000-event `RAFT` AI hybrid synthetic tropical cyclone catalog coupled with the `CLIMADA` Holland (2008) (`H08`) parametric wind field model can estimate 50-year and 700-year coastal design wind speeds (V50 and V700, 3-second gust at 10 m over open terrain) matching ASCE 7-22 across 19 US coastal stations. In a pre-registered benchmark against the 10,000-year physics-based `STORM v4` catalog (~8.7 CU), `STORM` passed Gate 0 with a median signed V700 bias of -8.87% against ASCE 7-22, whereas `RAFT` failed Gate 1 with a median absolute deviation of 30.95% (underestimating all 19 stations by 19%–42%). Following a six-reviewer audit confirming no implementation bugs and unanimously supporting shelving, two attribution diagnostics against 1979–2018 `HURDAT2` and Extended Best Track (`EBTRK`) observations showed that `RAFT`'s underestimation stems not from its empirical pressure–wind or radius-of-maximum-wind (Rmax) closures, but from a severe deficit of nearshore Category 3+ hurricane passages in the catalog itself, leaving the sub-project Shelved.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead launched Round 1 across 19 frozen US coastal stations (Brownsville, Texas to Cape Hatteras, North Carolina) and compiled literature cards for `RAFT` (Xu et al. 2024), `STORM` (Bloemendaal et al. 2020), `SPIN` (Gao & Xi 2026), Snaiki & Wu (2019), and Vickery et al. (2010), noting that `RAFT` provides 40,000 events without an annual rate while `H08` computes winds from central pressure drop (Delta P) and Rmax rather than Vmax.
- **2026-10-14**: A research assistant retrieved public ASCE 7-22 V700 values for all 19/19 stations (and 18/19 for V50) and fixed a unit bug where Rmax was passed to `CLIMADA` in meters instead of nautical miles, voiding the first 6 batches and recomputing all 40,000 `RAFT` and 107,063 `STORM` tracks (~8.7 CU).
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead verified that sibling hurricane reconstruction work was unaffected by the Rmax bug and set `RAFT`'s primary annual rate to the 1979–2018 `HURDAT2` North Atlantic rate (483 storms / 40 yr = 12.075 storms/yr, 3,312.6 equivalent years) rather than 14.5 storms/yr.
- **2026-10-14**: Round 1 failed Gate 1 under both 14.5/yr (30.40% median absolute deviation) and the primary 12.075/yr `HURDAT2STORM`'s 9.21% = 10.13%), while `STORM` passed Gate 0 (-8.87% median signed bias); `RAFT` underestimated V700 across all four segments (-39.6% Texas–Louisiana, -36.1% Mississippi–Panhandle, -25.9% Florida, -28.3% Georgia–North Carolina) and underestimated 18-station V50 by 29.1%.
- **2026-10-14**: Sensitivity checks across annual rates (10–20 storms/yr: 31.48%–29.12%), environmental pressure (1010pm 5 hPa: mp 6\%), and gust factors (1.03–1.12: 33.0%–27.2%) left the gate failure unchanged, while the exploratory `SPIN` chain (V700 46.5–64.8 m/s) was reported descriptively because public tracks lacked P_c and Rmax.
- **2026-10-14**: All six reviewers (6/6 valid) supported shelving the `RAFT` to `H08` route after auditing the solver code and 51 batch outputs, confirming unit conversions, Weibull plotting positions, and annual-maxima checks, while correcting the North Atlantic `STORMH08` tested `RAFT`'s empirical P_c(Vmax) and Rmax closures rather than its neural intensity model directly; AI Weather Models Lead Shelved the sub-project.
- **2026-10-14**: Lab Lead and AI Weather Models Lead dispatched Diagnostic Step 1 comparing `RAFT`, `STORM`, and 1979–2018 `HURDAT2EBTRK` inputs within 500 km of the 19 stations and swapping empirical closures on a 5% sample (2,351 storms, 44,669 station-storm peaks).
- **2026-10-14**: Diagnostic Step 1 refuted the hypothesis that `RAFT`'s linear P_c formula caused a 10%–15% loss in Category 4–5 winds: static eyewall loss was 2.87% median, and replacing P_c with the observed `HURDAT2STORM`).
- **2026-10-14**: In Diagnostic Step 2 (0 SU), comparing nearshore passage rates within 100 km of the 19 stations revealed a severe deficit of Category 3+ passages per 1,000 basin storms in `RAFT`—0.09 in Texas (vs. 1.04 `STORM`, 3.45 `HURDAT2`), 0.17 in Louisiana–Panhandle (vs. 1.45, 4.14), 0.42 in the Carolinas (vs. 2.66, 3.45), and 1.97 in Florida (vs. 2.55, 2.07)—with only 6.2% of nearshore passages reaching Category 3+ in `RAFT` vs. 11.6% in observations and 16.0% in `STORM`.
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead closed out the sub-project as Shelved without an `H10` rerun, establishing the zero-compute nearshore Category 3+ passage-rate screen for future AI catalogs and purging ~790 MB of raw downloads.

## Where it stands

This sub-project is Shelved with all 19-station return-level benchmarks, six-reviewer audit records, and `HURDAT2EBTRK` attribution diagnostics archived (88 MB locally). Because `RAFT`'s ~30% coastal design wind speed underestimation is driven by a near-coast deficit of Category 3+ storms (20× lower than Gulf observations) rather than pressure–wind or Rmax closures, switching wind solvers cannot rescue the catalog, and future AI catalogs must first pass the nearshore Category 3+ screen.

projects.title: R23.4 Thunderstorms and the convective scale
projects.goal: Judge whether there is a usable AI route to thunderstorm/downburst surface winds: convective-scale AI nowcasting (L, including M for environmental lead time and L2 sounding → CM1 downscaling), and AI large-scale forecasts driving WRF (K). The sub-nodes share event lists, data and literature; K serves as the accuracy yardstick for L.

# 雷暴与对流尺度

## 目标
判断雷暴/下击暴流地面风有没有一条能用的 AI 路线：对流尺度 AI 短临（L，含 M 环境提前量、L2 探空→CM1 降尺度），以及 AI 大尺度预报驱动 WRF（K）。各子节点共用事件清单、数据和文献，K 作为 L 的精度标尺。

## 当前状态
10-14 14:34 本节点开立。L与 已迁入本节点（已核），在跑委托照旧回原。K 已开：WRF Lead 同意投入，首个事件 Akron 2020-06-09，WRF 线最早 10-20 起跑。

## 已知结论（不重做）
- AI 全球模型（Pangu、FuXi，0.25°）给对流背景场只能提前 12–24 h 且不稳定，CAPE 是瓶颈（三个事件，定性）→。
- M（10-14 收口，40 个 2023–24 ASOS ≥50 kt 雷暴大风日，AWS AIWP Pangu/GraphCast，逐参数判据）细化上条：DCAPE、0–1 km 风切 12–120 h 全过；0–6 km 风切 Pangu 全过、GraphCast 到 72 h；MUCAPE/MLCAPE 全不过（逐事件胜 14–25/40）。限制：参照是 ERA5（Pangu 本身用 ERA5 训练，对它有利）、对照只有持续性、没有业务数值预报对照、验证时刻偏离风峰最多 6 h，只检验环境不检验阵风 → 、。

## 已定决定
- 2026-10-14 K 开立 → 
- 2026-10-17 K 搁置→ 
- 2026-10-16 L 本配置扩样搁置→ 、；第三轮先写预注册草案再定
- 2026-10-14 L 第二轮整轮 ≤200 CU（母项目批准，第一段作闸门）→ 、

## 子项目
| 节点 | 页 | 状态 | 一句话 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L 对流尺度 AI 与雷暴短临（含 M、L2） | | 搁置（仅本配置扩样） | 审查 （5/6 有效，Gemini 额度用尽缺席）裁决：StormCast V1/CONUS + 10 m 风×1.6677 阵风代理 + 事后 ERA5，按冻结门槛未达扩样标准；但命中差异不显著（McNemar p 0.22–1.0），改集合最大口径峰值比三档全过，任一成员计数 AI 不少于 HRRR GUST，V1 含 7 例已见样本 → 不得写"对流尺度 AI 不如 HRRR"。第三轮预注册草案已交（：V1 80 事件+80 对照、2 h 主时效、HRRR 式混合层阵风诊断、概率型主判据，约 67% 功效；S0–S2 约 105 CU，全部五段约 570 CU）。10-16 本节点批：定稿送 → 放行 S0+S1（约 9 CU）→ S2 前报母项目放行。10-16 01:52 预注册冻结（定稿）；S0 合格盲事件 V1 301、CONUS 132，抽 V1 120、CONUS 80，对照配对已完成 200/200（无缺对照事件），已派 wx 冻结样本并跑 S1；累计约 1.1 CU。S2 按定稿 120–240 组、约 72–144 CU，S0–S2 约 84–156 CU，S1 过闸后由本节点转母项目放行；第二轮 B3 会话 10-16 00:23 收尾，Colab 已无 L 的会话。第二轮约 212 CU |
| K 雷暴：AI 预报驱动 WRF | | 搁置 | Akron 2020-06-09，Pangu（13 层）驱动 vs GFS 全层驱动同一套 WRF：24/48/72 h 0/3 达到"不差于"；24 h 两组位置误差都 >150 km（GFS 183、Pangu 308 km），"值得继续"不可达。审查 （5/6 有效，GPT-6 通道失败， 修好后补一份核对）。措辞只到"这套配置未达标"：单事件、模型与层数未拆开；48 h Pangu 位置误差反而更小；10 m 风只到实测阵风 43–60%。重启：13 层 GFS 对照（CRC 0 SU）、≥3 事件统计、或全层输出的 AI 模型 →。10-17 已告知 WRF Lead |

## 未决与下一步
- K：10-15 WRF 线要求重出 v2.2（Q2 取最低地上完整气压层比湿，v2.1 偏湿 +0.38～+0.91 g/kg、最大 9.3 g/kg，超 1 g/kg 约定），放 CRC 交付根 v22_final/；metgrid 两组已过，real 边界区 NaN 由 WRF 线修；观测改为 NEXRAD Level-II 垂直最大反射率合成 + KAKO METAR，37.04 m/s 仍以 Childs 2021 Table 2 为锚。v2.2 已交付（CRC v22_final/，作业 1544281 退出码 0，66 文件 SHA256 全过，只改 Q2，其余与 v2.1 逐字节相同），10-15 本节点直接交 WRF Lead；WRF Lead 04:58 复核通过并开跑：real NaN 已绕开（all_ic_times=true），先 G06/P06（约半天，含闸门），过闸后 24/48/72 三对并行（最长约 16–18 h 墙钟），三维只留 03–09Z、<15 GB；数值表回 K，结论由 K 按第 5 节下。
- L：第二轮（阵风换算、10 成员、≥20 事件+无事件对照、GFS 真预报条件、CONUS 版 2025-10 后事件）已派；M 已收口；审查 已裁，第二轮加入 NOAA HRRRCast（MIT 许可，GFS 边界、自带 GUST 诊断）。本节点 10-14 补告两条判读，已落实：窗边比例 AI 18/28、HRRR10 13/28、HRRR GUST 14/28；窄窗三者 ≥50 kt 均 0/28；第二轮主表宽窄窗并列，结论以 HRRR GUST 与 HRRR10×同一阵风系数为基线，持续性只进附录。算力：母项目 10-14 批准 L 第二轮整轮 ≤200 CU（仅本轮；第一段 ≤20 CU 作闸门、每会话 ≤50 CU、判据开跑前冻结、120 CU 时报一次、200 CU 停）→。

## 边界
- 层级（根 Lead 10-14 定，5 层上限）：本节点下的二级节点（L、K）不再开三级子项目，需要细分时在二级节点内用任务，或由本节点开同级二级节点；二级节点往下只剩两跳（二级节点 → bot → 工具），任务书里不得让工具 bot 再委托别人。 子树列表不按父节点分组，以界面项目树为准。
- Colab（母项目 10-14 更正，对齐 Liang Hu 原话"现阶段多用 Colab、不限 CU"）：不设单试验上限；单试验预计 >100 CU 先停下报本节点转母项目，>200 CU 由母项目报根 Lead；用完必须 colab stop，不让会话空转；同一轮只派一个执行方。L 第二轮已批的整轮 ≤200 CU 照旧。原"≤20 CU"作废。
- 工作站 不跑计算、不存计算数据（Liang Hu 10-14 加严；10-15 01:59 C 盘余 46 GB）：求解器、训练、批量算例、大下载一律在 Colab 或 CRC/TACC 跑和存；工作站 只放脚本、单项 <200 MB 的小结果、图和报告，临时 >1 GB 先报本节点；CRC 组空间约 95%，新大数据优先 TACC /work 或 /scratch；CRC 默认单节点。10-15 核查：L 的计算全在 Colab，工作站 只跑会话保活与拉回检查点的轻量脚本，convective_ai 目录共 132 MB、无 >50 MB 单文件；K 在 工作站 无计算；驱动场（1.6 GB）10-14 已生成，工作站 副本已移除，唯一一份在 CRC （10-15 04:48 按校验清单全量核对通过）。

items.text:
# Measured Structure of AWS AIWP Archive (2026-10-14)

Data documentation: https://registry.opendata.aws/aiwp/; Radford et al. (2025), BAMS DOI 10.1175/BAMS-D-24-0057.1, literature card , PDF pages 1, 4–6. Objects measured via anonymous S3 GET/Range.

PANG_v100_GFS: 13 levels 1000/925/850/700/600/500/400/300/250/200/150/100/50 hPa, t/q/u/v/z on the same levels, u10/v10/t2; measured at 7.34 GB, global compressed HDF5 packs all 13 levels for each variable and each timestep into a single chunk; reading only a 3×3 grid around a station still requires remotely reading a complete global timestep variable chunk. Single file with eight variables for one timestep takes ~23 s; do not write large files to Workstation. GRAP_v100_GFS trial read of the same levels and variables actually succeeded for the first two lead times.

FOUR_v100_GFS: The archive is actually not the common 13-level output claimed on the documentation page; measured HDF5 variable dimensions and coordinates of object are: zlevel 1000/850/500/250/50, rhlevel 850/500, tlevel 850/500/250, windlevel 1000/850/500/250 hPa. Lacking complete low-level temperature and humidity profiles, no forced interpolation to 13 levels to calculate the five environmental criteria, so this round only performs parameter-by-parameter validation on Pangu/GraphCast Operational. The registry page does not match the actual data; model availability is subject to the actual data.

Limitations: GFS-initialized AIWP compared against ERA5 ground truth; the two initial conditions differ, which is an archived operational hindcast rather than an isolated model comparison with identical ERA5 initial conditions. 2023/24 falls within the archive range listed on the registry page with no training overlap for GraphCast since 2022; however, this statement only guarantees nominal training separation per the archive, not an independent confirmation of all model training data. 0.25° global model environmental fields do not equate to surface wind gust forecasts.

## Reference Differences Between 13-Level and 37-Level
- MUCAPE: Valid 40/40, median absolute difference of 13 vs 37 levels for regional maximum: 71.70 J/kg.
- MLCAPE: Valid 40/40, median absolute difference of 13 vs 37 levels for regional maximum: 38.46 J/kg.
- DCAPE: Valid 40/40, median absolute difference of 13 vs 37 levels for regional maximum: 45.96 J/kg.
- shear06: Valid 40/40, median absolute difference of 13 vs 37 levels for regional maximum: 0.38 m/s.
- shear01: Valid 40/40, median absolute difference of 13 vs 37 levels for regional maximum: 0.71 m/s.

Notes: Units CAPE/DCAPE J/kg, wind shear m/s; no mixed units. 0.25° grid, station grid cell ± one grid point is an ex-ante implementation assumption when no regional extent was given. Event time is taken as the nearest 00/12 UTC synoptic hour, which may deviate from the peak wind by up to 6 h; evaluates only the environment, not gusts.
ERA5 on the same 13 pressure levels serves as the primary reference; 37-level is attached to each case in the reference_37 field; persistence is ERA5 at 24·ceil(L/24) h prior to the verification time. Parcel definitions follow the three-event trial: MetPy mixed_layer_cape_cin default 100 hPa, most_unstable_cape_cin default 300 hPa, downdraft_cape default mid-level; surface 10 m wind is linearly interpolated to 1/6 km AGL. Sub-surface levels below terrain are masked by ERA5 surface geopotential; FCN v2-small archive actually lacks complete thermal/wind levels and thus did not participate in the five parameters.
Completeness: Missing events for each cell can be queried in summary.json; raw error messages are retained in raw_cases.jsonl; missing values are not imputed with 0.

# Sample and Interpretation Boundaries

This round of events_M.csv was selected from the NOAA NCEI Storm Events 2023/2024 annual details (see `source_2023.url`, `source_2024.url` for annual object URLs): event type Thunderstorm Wind, MAGNITUDE_TYPE=MG (measured), SOURCE strictly ASOS, MAGNITUDE ≥50 kt, BEGIN_LOCATION starting with a 3-character station code in parentheses, latitude 25–49°N, longitude 125–67°W; for each event UTC date, only the single instance with the highest wind value was retained, and then 40 days were sampled in rotation by month. 15 days in 2023, 25 days in 2024, across 19 states, with samples in all 12 months; see for the number of selections per month. This is a geographical/seasonal coverage sampling and does not represent natural occurrence frequency; nor were raw ASOS one-minute observations downloaded independently one-by-one to verify NOAA's MAGNITUDE. For SFO on 2023-01-10, NOAA's MAGNITUDE of 60 kt is inconsistent with its narrative of 60 mph; both are above the 50 kt threshold (60 mph is ~52 kt), but the specific observed value should be verified separately. Convection sometimes originated from cold-season fronts, not all being typical summer downbursts.

Verification time is the nearest 00/12 UTC to the event time, thus deviating by up to ~6 h; the 40 distinct event UTC days share only 39 distinct verification times, as the two cases of 2023-02-26/27 share 2023-02-27 00 UTC, so the count cannot be treated as 40 independent synoptic situations. The analysis evaluates only environmental metrics in the ASOS vicinity, without verifying station gusts themselves, and cannot directly claim a 5-day lead time for actual severe convection forecasts.

Four requested forecast objects returned HTTP 404, re-confirmed via independent HEAD requests, and no fabricated substitute initializations were made: PANG initializations for 2024-10-28 00 and 2024-12-11 12 (72 h each), GRAP initializations for 2024-08-26 00 / 08-28 00 (72 / 24 h respectively); thus, out of 400 model × event × lead-time combinations, 396 succeeded, with 38–40 available per parameter. and ; takes the last record by key and excludes failures. In a few grid cells, model geopotential height profiles were non-monotonic; those cells were skipped, retaining regional maxima from the remaining cells; occurrence details are documented under diagnosis_errors in each record without concealment.

Criteria strictly evaluate both conditions simultaneously—single-parameter event median absolute error and per-event win rate—without mixing J/kg and m/s. Stratified conclusions: both CAPE metrics failed both conditions across 0.5–5 days for both models; DCAPE and 0–1 km wind shear passed across all five tiers; 0–6 km wind shear passed all five tiers for Pangu, and up to 72 h for GraphCast. 5-day shear/downdraft energy is merely an environmental reconstruction advantage relative to diurnal-cycle persistence, insufficient to substitute for the CAPE gate, nor does it indicate that gusts can be accurately forecast at 5 days. This result requires verification by the Lead and independent scientific review before formal extrapolation to Liang Hu.

Reproduction commands: only for brand-new directories (this script uses mode x to protect existing event lists); for an existing list, use (N=0..3, each appending only new shards without overwriting completed successful records); run and only in brand-new summary result directories; already generated results in this directory must not be overwritten. Dependency versions are recorded in `.venv`, model files were read from anonymous S3 Range requests, and no large files were saved.

items.title: M: lead time of AI global models for severe-convective environments (2026-10-14)
items.text:
# M: AI Global Model Severe Convective Environment Lead Time (2026-10-14)
Results: AWS AIWP hindcast (Pangu, GraphCast Operational), 40 ASOS ≥50 kt thunderstorm wind days from 2023–24, parameter-by-parameter criteria (median AE ≤ 0.8 × persistence and per-event win rate ≥ 2/3): DCAPE and 0–1 km wind shear passed across all 12–120 h; 0–6 km wind shear passed all for Pangu, and up to 72 h for GraphCast; MUCAPE and MLCAPE all failed (per-event wins 14–25/40). Evidence.
Decision: Accept; close out M with no additions; L2 hindcasts will extract soundings from HRRR/ERA5 analyses; CAPE is the weak link in forecast mode; hand over to Round 2 to evaluate convective-scale models at short lead times.
Why: Sample expanded from 3 to 40, conclusions consistent with the 10-13 three-event trial (CAPE is the bottleneck); further expanding the sample will not change the judgment.
Cost of being wrong: If dedicated forecast metrics for CAPE are needed, launch a separate small experiment (~1 day).
Basis: Data from this line; AIWP source Radford et al. 2025 BAMS 10.1175/BAMS-D-24-0057.1; Limitations: verification time can deviate from peak wind by up to 6 h; evaluates environment only.

results.text:
# Measured Structure of AWS AIWP Archive (2026-10-14)

Data documentation: https://registry.opendata.aws/aiwp/; Radford et al. (2025), BAMS DOI 10.1175/BAMS-D-24-0057.1, literature card , PDF pages 1, 4–6. Objects measured via anonymous S3 GET/Range.

PANG_v100_GFS: 13 levels 1000/925/850/700/600/500/400/300/250/200/150/100/50 hPa, t/q/u/v/z on the same levels, u10/v10/t2; measured at 7.34 GB, global compressed HDF5 packs all 13 levels for each variable and each timestep into a single chunk; reading only a 3×3 grid around a station still requires remotely reading a complete global timestep variable chunk. Single file with eight variables for one timestep takes ~23 s; do not write large files to Workstation. GRAP_v100_GFS trial read of the same levels and variables actually succeeded for the first two lead times.

FOUR_v100_GFS: The archive is actually not the common 13-level output claimed on the documentation page; measured HDF5 variable dimensions and coordinates of object are: zlevel 1000/850/500/250/50, rhlevel 850/500, tlevel 850/500/250, windlevel 1000/850/500/250 hPa. Lacking complete low-level temperature and humidity profiles, no forced interpolation to 13 levels to calculate the five environmental criteria, so this round only performs parameter-by-parameter validation on Pangu/GraphCast Operational. The registry page does not match the actual data; model availability is subject to the actual data.

Limitations: GFS-initialized AIWP compared against ERA5 ground truth; the two initial conditions differ, which is an archived operational hindcast rather than an isolated model comparison with identical ERA5 initial conditions. 2023/24 falls within the archive range listed on the registry page with no training overlap for GraphCast since 2022; however, this statement only guarantees nominal training separation per the archive, not an independent confirmation of all model training data. 0.25° global model environmental fields do not equate to surface wind gust forecasts.

# Thunderstorms and Convective Scale (Exploring)

This first-level node coordinates three AI pathways for thunderstorm and downburst surface winds: convective-scale AI nowcasting (Node L), environmental lead-time statistics from global AI models (Node M), and global AI forecasts driving WRF (Node K). Task M concluded across 40 thunderstorm wind days that global AI models skillfully predict wind shear and DCAPE 3–5 days ahead but fail on CAPE at all leads. In Node L, StormCast V1 failed its frozen 20-event evaluation (capturing only half as many ≥50 kt events as HRRR gusts), and a 54-group evaluation of StormCast CONUS is nearing completion, while Node K has delivered verified v2.2 forcing files to the WRF line for formal Akron downburst integrations.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-14**: Node opened to oversee Node L (convective-scale AI nowcasting, environmental lead-time task M, and CM1 sounding task L2) and prospective Node K (AI-driven WRF), building on an earlier Shelved finding that global AI convective environments hold for only 12–24 h due to CAPE errors.
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead audited Node L's StormCast setup—noting StormCast CONUS weights trained through September 2025 require post-October 2025 test cases and historical CM1 cases fall inside the training window—and queried the WRF Lead on Node K capacity.
- **2026-10-14**: After the WRF Lead agreed to run the 2020-06-09 Akron downburst (4 km domain, KAKO 37.04 m/s and USDA tower 50.45 m/s) plus optional 2018-08-10 Wister (25.9 m/s), the Lead opened Node K and compiled a shared event table.
- **2026-10-14**: Node L reported Round 1 results for StormCast V1 on 7 ASOS thunderstorm wind events (2023–2024) at 1, 2, 3, and 6 h leads (28 runs): median AI/HRRR 10 m peak wind ratios were 0.85 at 1 h and 0.61 at 2 h (<0.90 gate), with 0/28 runs reaching ≥25.7 m/s because 10 m mean winds reached only 0.3–0.5 of ASOS gusts (vs. 0.75 for HRRR gust); inference took ≤88 s per run, and V1's ~440 hPa top precluded full CM1 soundings.
- **2026-10-14**: Auditing Round 1, the Lead added two Round 2 rules: reporting the fraction of peak winds on the 25 km search boundary (18/28 AI maxima in Round 1) alongside a 10 km window, and replacing initialization persistence (4–11 m/s) with same-lead HRRR gusts.
- **2026-10-14**: Task M concluded on 40 ASOS ≥50 kt thunderstorm wind days (2023–2024) using Pangu and GraphCast Operational at 12–120 h leads against ERA5 (median error ≤0.8× persistence, win rate ≥2/3): DCAPE and 0–1 km shear passed at all leads (12–120 h), 0–6 km shear passed to 120 h for Pangu and 72 h for GraphCast, whereas MUCAPE and MLCAPE failed at all leads (winning 14–25/40 events).
- **2026-10-14**: In Node L Round 2 Segment 1, NOAA HRRRCast (6 km grid) hung during weight loading in Python 3.10 / TensorFlow 2.15 and was deferred in favor of StormCast under a 200-compute-unit cap.
- **2026-10-15**: Node L Round 2 evaluation of StormCast V1 (20 ASOS ≥50 kt events in 2023–2024 plus 10 non-event days, 1/2/3 h leads, 10 members, 10 m winds scaled by a 2022 gust factor) failed frozen criteria: AI/HRRR gust peak ratios were 0.93 (1 h), 0.96 (2 h), and 0.85 (3 h, <0.90), and ≥50 kt hits were 4/20, 5/20, and 4/20 versus 8/20, 8/20, and 6/20 for HRRR gusts (0/10 false alarms); V1 was ruled failed, and a 6-reviewer audit was mandated before shelving Node L if CONUS also fails.
- **2026-10-15**: For Node K, the Lead coordinated v2.2 forcing regeneration setting 2 m specific humidity to the lowest complete pressure level above terrain without interpolation (removing a +0.38 to +0.91 g/kg moist bias near KAKO) and updated observations to NEXRAD Level-II composite reflectivity and KAKO METAR/SPECI reports.
- **2026-10-15**: Node K verified and delivered all 66 v2.2 forcing files (mean 2 m specific humidity change −0.37 to −0.91 g/kg, max 9.28 g/kg), and the WRF Lead launched the 6 h gate runs followed by parallel 24/48/72 h integrations.
- **2026-10-15**: As Node L's StormCast CONUS run (12 post-training 2026 events + 6 control days × 3 leads = 54 groups) averaged ~21 min (~2.3–2.45 compute units) per group and reached 30/54 groups (projecting ~700 compute units per 100 events × 3 leads vs. ~140 for V1), the Lead raised the Round 2 cap to 215 compute units so all 54 groups could finish.

## Where it stands

This parent node remains Exploring. Task M is concluded (shear and DCAPE are skillful to 3–5 days, while CAPE fails), Node L's StormCast V1 failed its frozen criteria while the 54-group StormCast CONUS evaluation is completing its remaining groups (to be followed by a 6-reviewer audit if it also fails), and Node K's v2.2 forcing files are running in WRF on the Akron downburst.

# Uses of AI weather foundation models for nowcasting / short-range forecasting

## Objective
Evaluate whether data-driven weather models (GraphCast/GenCast, Pangu, Aurora, FuXi, etc.) and AI nowcasting models can provide background fields for tornadoes/thunderstorms/typhoons, serve wind power forecasting, offer utility for CFD, and assess the value of reforecasts for our research. Deliver an assessment table, a literature review audit ID, a minimal experiment, and a one-sentence conclusion. Task brief: (approved by Liang Hu on 10-13).

## Current Status
10-13 14:00 **Shelved** (feasibility questions fully answered). Three-event reforecast (Wister, Akron, ALTU): maximum lead time simultaneously satisfying all three pre-specified criteria is 12/12/none for Pangu and 24/none/12 h for FuXi, showing instability; the bottleneck is CAPE (on ALTU, Pangu fails MLCAPE across all five lead times, with errors 1.2–11× that of persistence), whereas wind shear and DCAPE outperform persistence across most combinations. Literature review audit verdict issued. Total compute across both experiment phases is roughly estimated at <11.3 CU (≤20 cap). Figures with source footnotes have been generated: , (previous figures retained).

**Reason for shelving**: Because we focus on historical event hindcasts, using ERA5/HRRR analysis fields directly for the environment is superior; when using AI global models directly as downburst background fields, the thermodynamic environment only holds up to 12–24 h and is unstable, while 0.25° cannot resolve the storm itself; the bottleneck in the CM1 track lies in observational candidates rather than environmental data.
**Missing conditions / Conditions for restart**: (1) Our group pivots toward forecasting tasks (assessing severe convective wind environments several days ahead, or wind power forecasting); (2) The WRF track is willing to test "Pangu-driven WRF vs. GFS-driven WRF" (precedents: Xu 2024 ERL, Liu 2024 JGR:MLC), which is the most promising direction but requires formal project scale; (3) When multi-event statistics are needed, start with existing AWS AIWP reforecasts (from 2022-01 onward, GFS/IFS initial conditions at 00/12 UTC, subject to verifying that pressure-level variables are included); (4) If CAPE is the target, switch to 37-level outputs or a post-processing model (such as the Transformer post-processor in Hua et al., arXiv 2505.11750). Use for restart, ~2–3 CU per event.

## Established Decisions
- 2026-10-13 Literature review audit verdict: GraphCast weights open for commercial use starting 2026-08; NowcastNet–HRRR comparison updated to cite Das 2024; reforecast interpretation restricted to qualified scope → 
- 2026-10-13 Minimal experiment criteria and conventions (13-level ERA5 as primary reference, diurnally aligned persistence baseline, all three criteria satisfied simultaneously) → 
- 2026-10-13 Kickoff plan and minimal experiment direction (multi-initialization reforecasts rather than single-time comparisons) →

| 1 Severe convective environmental background fields (directly using AI global models) | Assess favorable environments days ahead and decide whether to schedule WRF/CM1 runs; not used for CM1 multi-event screening (CM1 Lead) | Our group's reforecasts; Feldmann 2024 arXiv 2406.09474, Hua 2025 GRL 10.1029/2024GL109611 (abstract) | Completed on three events: under our n=3, domain-maximum, diurnally aligned persistence criteria, maximum usable lead time is Pangu 12/12/none, FuXi 24/none/12 h; wind shear and DCAPE beat persistence in most combinations, while MLCAPE/MUCAPE is the bottleneck | <11.3 CU | Low–Medium |

| 1b Convection-allowing AI and nowcasting | 0–12 h thunderstorms and gusts | StormCast arXiv 2408.10958, WoFSCast GRL 10.1029/2024GL112383 (numerical model emulators); FuXi-Nowcast arXiv 2512.08974 (includes gusts); NowcastNet third-party evaluation Das 2024 10.1038/s41612-024-00834-8 (CSI 0.30 vs. HRRR 0.04, >16 mm/h) | Not for now: no CAM training archive or radar training data | — | Medium (Monitor) |
| 1c Typhoons | Track / intensity background fields | DeMaria 2025 AIES 10.1175/AIES-D-24-0085.1 (track comparable to best operational models, intensity systematically biased weak); near-surface wind profiles require coupling with WRF or -style reconstruction (unverified when coupled to AI forecasts) | As needed | — | Medium |
| 2 Wind power | Hub-height wind / power | GenCast Nature 10.1038/s41586-024-08252-9 (97.2%/1320; wind power evaluated via idealized power curve aggregation); Hardy 2025 10.1002/met.70038 (0.18 vs. 0.63 is contemporaneous ERA5 reconstruction; AIFS forecast outperforms IFS after ~Day 3) | Do not pursue (outside our group's main track) | — | Medium–High for wind power itself; Low for our group's main track |
| 3 CFD | Downscaling chain boundary conditions, inflow | FuXi-CFD Nat Commun 10.1038/s41467-026-70562-5 (30 m terrain wind including TKE, validated against met masts; trained on neutral steady RANS); urban microclimate CFM (relative to LES) | Do not pursue | — | Low–Medium (not applicable to transient downburst inflow) |
| 4 Reforecasts / predictability | Lead-time statistics, ensembles around historical events | AWS AIWP (Radford 2025 BAMS 10.1175/BAMS-D-24-0057.1; Pangu/FCNv2 from 2020-10, GraphCast operational from 2022-01, GFS/IFS initial conditions at 00/12 UTC); HENS GMD 18:5575; Vonich arXiv 2504.20238 (initial condition optimization given known future, not forecasting skill) | Candidate: fetch post-2022 multi-event data from AIWP (must first verify archive contains pressure-level variables) | Model-run-free, still requires data retrieval & diagnostics | Medium |

## What Was Tried and Results
| Date | What Was Done | One-Line Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10-13 | Reforecasts with Pangu and FuXi (operational GraphCast training period overlaps the events and the ERA5 version lacks an off-the-shelf wrapper, so FuXi was used instead) for Wister 18 UTC and Akron 06 UTC at lead times of 12/24/48/72/120 h against 13-level ERA5, using diurnally aligned persistence as baseline and three pre-specified criteria | Maximum lead time satisfying all three criteria simultaneously: Wister Pangu 12 h, FuXi 24 h; Akron Pangu 12 h, FuXi none. Parameter by parameter: 0–6 km wind shear error at most lead times is only 0.1–0.6× persistence; CAPE at ≥24–48 h is **worse than persistence** (error ratio 1.5–4). Following the literal wording of the task brief, Criterion 2 averaged across mixed units of J/kg, m/s, and K, so it was effectively dominated by CAPE (a flaw in the task brief's wording, judged strictly as written without post-hoc modification). MLCAPE computed from 13 levels is ~500 J/kg lower than from 37 levels, making vertical resolution itself a major error source. FuXi mirror weights were not verified file-by-file against the original weights |
| 10-13 | Added third event ALTU 2023-07-03 18 UTC (supplied by the CM1 track) under the same criteria; also produced a three-event station grid point + 3×3 parameter table | Pangu failed across all five lead times (rejected on MLCAPE alone at every lead time), while FuXi passed only at 12 h; 13-level MLCAPE is 532 vs. 37-level 797 J/kg; model "surface dewpoint" is a proxy taken from the lowest pressure level |

## Open Items and Next Steps
- 10-13 Intra-track trial rule (10-13 to 10-20): Upon restart, batch pure-QA routine tasks with fixed question banks (abstract initial screening, single-value extraction from papers, table field extraction, initial tag classification) default to ` with 10% audited by Claude to log agreement rate; task types below <90% agreement revert to the original workflow; does not apply to reforecasts, diagnostics, scientific judgment, or review submissions.
- Literature review ( default tier) returns → verify citations → ` → finalize assessment table after verdict.
- ideas has returned (10-13 12:30), and Lead has re-verified the parameter-by-parameter error ratios in `metrics.json`. Finalize Row 1 once the ALTU supplemental run returns.
- CM1 has replied (10-13): not currently working on this; offers limited help for their multi-event validation B and serves only as environmental context; provided ALTU 2023-07-03 and the station parameter list → added into the experiment (queued after , criteria unchanged).

- Experimental design note: Parent project review previously canceled the "single-event same-time AI field vs. ERA5" comparison (since AI models are trained on ERA5, that yields no new information). This experiment instead evaluates the growth of environmental parameter errors across **different lead times**, using persistence (ERA5 at initialization time) as the baseline; additionally, event dates must be checked to ensure they fall outside each model's training period (GraphCast/Pangu training ends in 2017, placing Wister 2018 in the test period, pending verification against the original papers).

## Literature Basis

projects.brief:
# Task Brief: Uses of AI weather foundation models for nowcasting / short-range forecasting — Applications to our research (strong-wind background fields, wind power, CFD) (Lab sub-project, approved for opening by Liang Hu on 10-13)

## Origin
Raised by Liang Hu on 10-13 during the "Uses of in-house / local models" sub-project discussion: if AI weather models can perform forecasting (especially nowcasting / short-range), they could provide background fields for tornadoes, thunderstorms, and typhoons; they may be even more useful for wind power; and do they have reference value for CFD? (220 m global LES, physics-based model, not AI), (generative model for urban microclimate), (physics-constrained network for typhoon near-surface wind profiles), .

## Known (already established in parent project, do not repeat)
- Parent project page "Ancillary Outputs" Row 2b: AI weather models offer little incremental value for **hindcast reconstruction** (ERA5 is better); 0.25° does not resolve downbursts; Feldmann 2024 (arXiv 2406.09474) shows seasonal skill for CAPE/shear comparable to IFS but smoother; Hua 2025 GRL (10.1029/2024GL109611) evaluates Pangu at a one-day lead time. WRF Lead reply: a 0.01 K perturbation causes a ~5× difference in high-wind area, so using AI to generate WRF initial-condition perturbations is not recommended.
- GitHub: earth2studio (NVIDIA, Apache-2.0), ecmwf ai-models (Apache-2.0), GraphCast→weathernext, Pangu, Aurora, geoarches.
- Colab A100 high-mem is available (80 GB / 167 GB / 194 GB disk).

## Questions to Answer
1. Severe convection / tornadoes / typhoons: How far ahead can AI global models (GraphCast, GenCast, Pangu, Aurora, FuXi, etc.) and AI nowcasting models (radar-extrapolation class) forecast, what variables do they provide (environmental parameters, track, intensity, near-surface winds), and how do they compare against IFS/GFS/HRRR; can they serve as background fields or screening tools for WRF/CM1/CFD?
2. Wind power: Hub-height wind speed / power forecasting and ramp events—performance of AI models and existing precedents.
3. CFD: Serving as boundary conditions in a downscaling chain, generative turbulence / inflow fields, or methodological borrowing—what verifiable precedents exist?
4. Value of reforecasts to our research: predictability and low-cost ensembles around historical events.

## Steps and Boundaries
- First run a literature review (default tier or `--gemini`; list GitHub repositories when querying open-source implementations), and process conclusions per protocol 
- Then select one minimal experiment: we recommend using earth2studio/ai-models on Colab to run multi-initialization reforecasts for a known event (such as Wister 2018-08-10 or a US landfalling hurricane) and compare environmental parameters / tracks against ERA5; pre-specify the criteria before running; ≤20 CU, and stop the instance when done. Do not use supercomputers.
- Data from other tracks are read-only; for anything involving the WRF/CM1 tracks, ask the respective Lead beforehand whether they are already working on it.
- Deliverables: project-page assessment table (question / use case / existing data / minimal experiment / cost / recommendation), literature review audit ID, minimal experiment results, and a one-sentence conclusion (worth continuing / Shelved / Pending promotion). For `status`, use only Exploring / Shelved / Pending promotion / Promoted.

items.text:
# AI Weather Models Forecast Applications: Grok Review Verification and Assessment Table Revision Proposal (10-13 13:00)

Report: . 32+ sources are all redirect links, 4 DOIs. Lead verified item-by-item online (mostly abstracts only; read full text for FuXi-Nowcast, Aurora 1.5, GenCast arXiv, NowcastNet PMC).

## I. Verification Table
| # | Report Claim | Verification Result | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | "Xu et al. 2025 npj" (DOI 10.1038/s41612-025-01265-9) Pangu+WRF typhoon intensity error reduced by >32% | **DOI/Author/Content mismatch**: That DOI is Baño-Medina et al. 2025 (stretched-grid regional AI model, Western US 6 km, atmospheric river extreme precipitation, no WRF coupling). The 32% actually comes from Liu, Tan, Wang et al. 2024 JGR:MLC 10.1029/2024JH000207 (Abstract): 2-week average intensity error for 5 typhoons reduced by 32% relative to global numerical models and by 23% relative to ERA5-driven WRF | Switch to Liu 2024 and explicitly state comparison targets |
| 2 | StormCast simulates HRRR, 99 variables, realistic cold pool, competitive reflectivity | True (Pathak et al. 2024 arXiv 2408.10958, abstract only) | Adopt (authors' self-evaluation) |
| 3 | WoFSCast 2 h matches 70–80% of storms, comparable FSS | Journal exists (Flora & Potvin 2025 GRL 10.1029/2024GL112383), already verified in parent project review | Adopt |
| 4 | NowcastNet CSI 0.30 vs HRRR 0.04 | **Partially untrue**: The paper does not compare against HRRR or any numerical model; no CSI values in main text; true that 71% of 62 meteorologists ranked it first (Zhang et al. 2023 Nature, PMC full text) | Delete numbers, retain "radar extrapolation category, compared against other extrapolation methods" |
| 5 | FuXi-Nowcast 1 km gusts 10.8/13.9/17.2 m/s superior to CMA-MESO | True (Chen et al. 2025 arXiv 2512.08974 §2.1/§4.5.1), exception: not superior after 6 h for 17.2 m/s threshold; CMA-MESO gusts estimated from 10 m wind, comparison not completely equivalent; no CSI values | Adopt, with qualifications |
| 6 | Aurora 1.5 ENS Helene 24 h track error 26.3 km vs NHC 110.6 | **Partially untrue**: Single case, mean error along entire track (not 24 h), from Microsoft preprint (Weyn et al. 2026 §4.1) | Downgrade to single-case lead |
| 6b | AI global models have good tracks, systematically weak intensity | True (DeMaria et al. 2025 AIES 10.1175/AIES-D-24-0085.1, abstract: tracks comparable to best operational models, intensity error larger than climatology-persistence, almost always weakens typhoons) | Adopt |
| 7 | AIFS→100 m wind U-Net RMSE 0.18 vs power law 0.63 | True (Hardy & Finney 2025 Met. Appl. 10.1002/met.70038, abstract), but "ground truth" is ERA5, not wind towers | Adopt, noting ground truth is ERA5 |
| 8 | GenCast 97.4% metrics surpass ENS, wind power advantage | True: Nature abstract 97.2% (arXiv 97.4%) / 1320 targets; wind power aggregated over 5,344 wind farms, CRPS ~20% better within 2 days (arXiv §8.2) | Adopt |
| 9 | FuXi-CFD 30 m 3D wind, deduces w and TKE, comparable to CFD | True (Lin et al. 2026 Nat Commun 10.1038/s41467-026-70562-5, abstract); abstract states "turbulence-related features", does not state TKE, no error figures | Adopt as precedent, figures pending reading full text |
| 10 | HENS 7,424 members, 2023 heatwave | True (Mahesh et al. 2025 GMD 18:5575/5605); abstract only states summer 2023 | Adopt |
| 11 | Vonich GraphCast initial condition optimization 10-day error drops 86%, >30 days | True (arXiv 2504.20238 abstract), optimization of "known future", not forecast capability | Use only as a predictability research methodology lead |
| 12 | AWS AIWP hindcast dataset | True (Radford et al. 2025 BAMS 10.1175/BAMS-D-24-0057.1): FourCastNetv2/Pangu from 2020-10, GraphCast from 2022-01, GFS and IFS initial conditions; **excludes 2018, 2020 only after October** | Adopt: Events from 2023 onward can directly use off-the-shelf hindcasts |
| 13 | Pangu→WRF heavy precipitation | True (Xu et al. 2024 ERL 10.1088/1748-9326/ad41f0 abstract): North China heavy rain 400 mm TS=0.1 maintained up to 8.5 days, GFS-driven ~3 days | Adopt |
| 14 | GraphCast weights Apache-2.0, commercially friendly | **Untrue**: Code Apache-2.0, weights CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; Pangu, FuXi mirror weights likewise CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (ideas already checked README) | Correct |
| 15 | Report's "feasibility judgments" ("completely replace synthetic turbulence", "zero-cost thousands-member ensemble breaks compute shackles", "perfect fit for EVA", etc.) | Report extrapolation, unsupported by precedent; "thousands-member ensemble" contradicts our line's WRF data (0.01 K perturbation causes ~5-fold difference in strong wind area; dispersion comes from within the storm, which global models cannot provide) | Do not adopt |
| 16 | Report restating numbers from our line's project brief | Report itself marked as non-literature | Do not use as evidence |

## II. Relationship to Our Group's Minimal Experiment
First round of hindcasts: Pangu/FuXi on Wister, Akron: maximum lead time simultaneously satisfying the three criteria is 12–24 h; parameter-by-parameter, wind shear is better than diurnal-cycle-aligned persistence over several days, while CAPE is worse than persistence after ≥24–48 h; 13-level CAPE is ~500 J/kg lower than 37-level. **Not contradictory** with Feldmann 2024 (arXiv 2406.09474, abstract: CAPE and shear seasonal skill comparable to IFS): the latter is large-sample seasonal statistics compared against IFS; our trial is regional maxima for n=2 cases compared against persistence. Directionally consistent with Hua 2025 (pre-storm surrounding CAPE extrema are underestimated).

## III. Assessment Table Revision Proposal
| Question | Recommendation | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Severe convective environmental background field (Global AI) | Low-Medium | Our group's experiment: thermal environment only up to 12–24 h; dynamical environment can lead by several days; 0.25° cannot resolve downbursts. ERA5 is better for hindcasting |
| 1′ AI results driving WRF/CM1 | Medium (precedent exists, untested) | Xu 2024 ERL, Liu 2024 JGR:MLC: AI large-scale + physical model details, longer validity than driving with GFS alone; but the WRF line opposes using AI to generate initial perturbation ensembles |
| 1b Regional convective-scale AI / nowcasting | Medium (observe) | StormCast, WoFSCast, FuXi-Nowcast (including gust verification) exist, all authors' self-evaluations; we lack radar training data, not testing for now |
| 1c Typhoons | Medium | Good track, weak intensity is multi-party consensus (DeMaria 2025); near-surface wind profile must be coupled with WRF or similar models |
| 2 Wind power | Medium-High (for wind power itself), Low for our group's main line | GenCast wind power CRPS precedent, Hardy 2025 100 m downscaling; ground truth mostly ERA5 / aggregated power, not wind towers |
| 3 CFD | Medium (recent precedent) | FuXi-CFD (30 m terrain 3D wind, Nat Commun 2026), urban microclimate generative models; all at abstract level, no precision figures seen |
| 4 Hindcast / Predictability | Medium | AWS AIWP off-the-shelf hindcasts (from 2020-10) available at zero compute; HENS/GenCast large ensemble precedents; but dispersion of downbursts in our group comes from within the storm |

## IV. One Sentence to Liang Hu (Proposal)
Worth continuing, but not as the primary tool for downburst research: AI global models can provide dynamical environments such as wind shear several days in advance, but CAPE is only reliable within one day; more useful directions are "AI large-scale + WRF downscaling" and background fields for wind power / typhoons. Next steps if pursued: use AWS AIWP off-the-shelf hindcasts (zero compute) to expand to multiple events after 2020-10, or test a Pangu→WRF drive compared against GFS drive (requires WRF line collaboration).

# AI Weather Models Forecast Applications: Work Kickoff Arrangements (2026-10-13)

Decision I made:
1. Send the review query only once on default tier (do not turn on Max). Why: Only ~5 units of platform research quota remain; the knowledge base has almost no cards on this topic; get the core literature list first. Cost of being wrong: Supplement with another normal tier (1 unit) if coverage is insufficient.
2. The direction of the minimal experiment is set as "hindcasting known events across multiple initialization times, observing environmental parameter error growth with lead time, with persistence as baseline", rather than the "same-time AI field vs ERA5" comparison that was canceled in the parent project review. Why: The latter yields no new information (models are trained on ERA5); the former directly answers "how many days in advance favorable environments can be identified". Basis: No literature basis; based on the parent project review verdict and WRF Lead's reply (screening environments on event days is most useful). Cost of being wrong: ≤20 CU.
3. Before assigning work, wait for replies from WRF and CM1 on whether they are already working on it, and on event spatio-temporal definitions.

## Addendum (10-13 12:00)
Decision I made: After WRF Lead confirmed they are not working on it, without waiting for CM1 and the review, dispatch the minimal experiment first (ideas). Events expanded from Wister (primary, pulse type) to two: Wister + Akron (elevated convection), verification times 18 / 06 UTC; primary reference uses ERA5 with the same 13 levels (AI outputs have only ~13 levels, avoiding attributing vertical resolution differences to model error); baseline uses diurnal-cycle-aligned persistence; avoid using GraphCast operational version fine-tuned on 2016–2021 HRES (training period covers both events). Why: Experiment is revocable, cost ≤20 CU; if the review indicates design flaws, revise then. Basis: Event definitions per WRF Lead reply, Akron environment based on card 2DPBW6VX PDF pp.9–11; remainder has no literature basis, based on our line's design. Cost of being wrong: ≤20 CU, half a day.

## Addendum (10-13, after CM1 reply)
Decision I made: Add a third similar event ALTU 2023-07-03 to the experiment along with station grid parameter tables, criteria unchanged; delete "multi-event screening" from Application 1. Why: CM1 Lead explained their bottleneck is in observational candidates rather than environmental data, and they already use HRRR 3 km. Basis: CM1 Lead reply, no literature basis. Cost of being wrong: ~1–2 CU more.

## Addendum (10-13 12:40, first-round hindcast results)
Decision I made: Accept first-round results and render verdicts according to preset criteria (Wister 12/24 h, Akron 12 h), without changing criteria. Criterion 2's "mixed-unit average" was a defect in my task description wording, which was actually dominated by CAPE; I additionally read through it by parameter error ratio (AI/persistence) as an annotation: wind shear error ratio was 0.1–0.6 across most lead times, whereas CAPE was 1.5–4 after ≥24–48 h (worse than persistence). Both readings yield consistent conclusions: dynamical environment in AI global models can lead by several days, while thermal environment (CAPE) is limited to 12–24 h. Basis: ; directionally consistent with Feldmann 2024 (arXiv 2406.09474, CAPE constrained by coarse vertical levels), original text pending card creation. Cost of being wrong: n=2, might change once ALTU returns; do not launch large compute based on this.

## Addendum (10-13, review verdict)
Decision I made: Revise assessment table per the verdict: 1 Low-Medium (scope limited to our group's n=2), 1′ (write WRF only) Medium, 1b Medium (observe), 1c Medium, 2 Low for our group's main line, 3 downgraded to Low-Medium, 4 Medium. Why: Reviewers verified that GraphCast weights were updated to permit commercial use, NowcastNet–HRRR numbers originated from Das 2024 (Lead personally verified both), and FuXi-CFD is applicable only to steady-state terrain wind. Basis: see verdict document DOI item-by-item. Cost of being wrong: Recommendations are priority judgments; row 1 may be adjusted again when ALTU results return.

# Verdict: AI Weather Literature Review Verification and Assessment Table Proposal (10-13)

Reviewers E (Gemini), A (GPT-6), D (GLM), 3/3 valid, all "supported with reservations". Lead personally verified two critical objections: GraphCast weight licensing (weathernext README "August 6, 2026 UPDATE … updated to permit commercial use", verified via WebFetch) and NowcastNet–HRRR (Das et al. 2024 npj Clim Atmos Sci 10.1038/s41612-024-00834-8, PMC11573709 abstract: 30 heavy rain events in TVA region, >16 mm/h grid points, 1–3 h, median CSI 0.30 vs HRRR 0.04, verified).

## Must Change
1. **GraphCast weight licensing** (A): Changed to permit commercial use since 2026-08-06 (code Apache-2.0). Row 14 of verification table and "CC BY-NC-SA non-commercial" in results.md are outdated, correct them; Pangu and FuXi remain treated as non-commercial.
2. **Re-cite rather than delete NowcastNet numbers** (A, D): 0.30 vs 0.04 is true; source is Das 2024 third-party evaluation rather than Zhang 2023; Zhang 2023 itself does not compare with HRRR; 71% ranked first among 62 people remains as before.
3. **Add qualifications to hindcast interpretation, acknowledge counterexamples** (A, D, E): Change "wind shear better than persistence within several days" to "better in most combinations" (counterexamples: Pangu E1 48 h, FuXi E1 120 h, FuXi E2 24 h); limit "CAPE only reliable within one day" to "under criteria of our group's n=2 cases, regional maximum, against diurnal-cycle-aligned persistence"; explicitly state that FuXi failed for Akron across all lead times. Not contradictory with Feldmann (high CAPE/shear areas already present multiple days prior in individual cases): different scopes/definitions (presence of high-value area vs regional maximum error ≤25%).
4. **AWS AIWP sample expansion** (E, A, D): Period restricted to after 2022-01 (GraphCast archive is operational version; Pangu/FCNv2 from 2020-10 onward), initial conditions are GFS/IFS, routine 00/12 UTC initializations, different definitions/scopes from our group's ERA5 initial conditions, 06/18 UTC initializations; change "zero compute" to "no need to run models, still requires data retrieval and diagnostics"; confirm first whether each archive contains 13 pressure levels (D: Pangu archive might only contain surface variables, unverified).
5. **Row 1′ write WRF only** (E): CM1 can only take soundings from AI fields as environments, cannot ingest lateral boundary conditions.
6. **Wind power definitions/scope** (A): Hardy 0.18/0.63 is instantaneous 100 m reconstruction from ERA5 input, not AIFS forecast error (the latter outperforms IFS after ~day 3); GenCast 5,344 wind farms is an aggregation of 10 m winds converted via idealized power curves, not measured power generation. Recommendation level maintained, but clearly stated.
7. **CFD row** (E, A, D): FuXi-CFD output includes u,v,w,k (TKE) and has independent validation from European wind towers (A and D read the full text; Lead did not read full text, recorded according to the two reviewers); training data is neutral steady-state RANS, applicable only to terrain steady-state winds, not to downburst transient inflow. Recommendation level changed to "Low-Medium" (for our group's main line). NRMSE figures for urban microclimate CFM are already in card , reported by authors relative to LES.
8. **Narrow inferences on WRF perturbation sensitivity** (A): 0.01 K → ~5-fold only shows internal storm sensitivity, cannot exclusively rule out large-scale AI ensembles; retain only "global AI ensembles cannot replace storm-internal dispersion".
9. **13 levels vs 37 levels** (A): ~500 J/kg applies only to E1 MLCAPE; MUCAPE difference is ~220–235 J/kg.

## For Reference Only
- In the same paper, Aurora 1.5 also has an aggregated evaluation for 2024–2025 (13–34% improvement relative to original Aurora) (A).
- Hua et al. 2025 preprint arXiv 2505.11750: Pangu outputs post-processed via Transformer to yield 1–8 day severe weather probabilities (A, E)—closer to "medium-range severe convective applications" than raw CAPE extrema, listed as candidate.
- Row 1b: WoFSCast/StormCast are surrogates for convective-scale numerical models, not radar extrapolation; reason for not testing for now changed to "lack of CAM training archives and training compute" (E).
- Criterion 2 is actually dominated by CAPE (E, D), already explained in decision records and project page.
- Typhoon profile network is an observational reconstruction; accuracy after coupling with AI forecasts remains unverified (A).

## Dissenting Opinions Not Adopted
- None. E's request to downgrade CFD to "Low-Medium" was adopted; A argued that recommendations lack uniform scoring criteria—conceded, recommendations are internal priority judgments, not objective rankings, noted in assessment table.

Basis: Literature per item seen in verification table; test numbers seen in .

# AI Weather Models Forecast Applications: Shelved (2026-10-13)

Decision I made: Sub-project status changed to "Shelved".
- What was done: Three-event hindcasts (Wister, Akron, ALTU; Pangu, FuXi; 12–120 h lead times; three preset criteria), literature review verification and review verdict, assessment table finalized.
- Why: Maximum usable lead times under preset criteria were Pangu 12 / 12 / none, FuXi 24 / none / 12 h, unstable; the bottleneck is CAPE, while wind shear and DCAPE were better than persistence in most combinations (, ; no literature basis, based on our line's data; directionally consistent with Hua 2025 GRL 10.1029/2024GL109611 abstract "pre-storm surrounding CAPE extrema are underestimated"). Our group works on hindcasting, where ERA5/HRRR are better; CM1 line's bottleneck is in observational candidates (CM1 Lead 10-13 reply). The most promising "AI-driven WRF" (Xu 2024 ERL 10.1088/1748-9326/ad41f0; Liu 2024 JGR:MLC 10.1029/2024JH000207, both at abstract level) is of formal project scale, requiring the WRF line and Liang Hu to set direction.
- Cost of being wrong: If Liang Hu wants to move in the forecast/wind power direction, restarting a single event costs ~2–3 CU, scripts are off-the-shelf.
- Restart conditions see project page. Shelving a lab idea is handled per the Lab's rules, does not constitute abandoning the research line, and was not separately sent to 6 people.

# AI 天气模型回算两个下击暴流环境：最小试验结果（2026-10-13）

性质：n=2 的回顾性、ERA5 初始化确定性全球模型环境筛查；绝非下击暴流发生时间、阵风或概率的预报验证。空间分辨率 0.25°。原定三个闸门全部保留，没有改阈值。

## 最大满足提前量

- Pangu6 × E1：12 h。
- Pangu6 × E2：12 h。
- FuXi × E1：24 h。
- FuXi × E2：无（所测提前量均不满足）。

## 预定判据表

## 13 层与 37 层参照的差别

同一验证时刻、同一 0.25° 水平网格，37 层只作附注，不用于裁决；下表为区域最大值（37 层减 13 层）。近地地下等压面用 ERA5 固定地形位势遮罩；最底有效气压面不等于地表。

| E1 指标 | ERA5 13 层 | ERA5 37 层 | 差值 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MLCAPE | 1086.11 | 1586.22 | +500.11 |
| MUCAPE | 1537.90 | 1773.23 | +235.33 |
| DCAPE | 1021.38 | 1132.99 | +111.61 |
| shear06 | 6.84 | 6.94 | +0.10 |

E1 13 层的区域最大 MLCAPE 为 1086.1 J kg⁻¹，37 层为 1586.2 J kg⁻¹；层数差异不可忽略。E2 的 13 层最大逆温升温 1.94 K，上端高度约 2409 m AGL；37 层最大值 2.51 K。这个定义是 0–3 km 内相邻高度层最大正温差，不是追踪 Akron 事件约 1.3 km AGL 那个特定逆温层，因此 E2 对高架对流的判读尤其脆弱。E1 次日 00 UTC 13 层 ERA5 的 MLCAPE/MUCAPE/DCAPE/0–6 km 切变区域最大值为 332.5/697.6/1019.6 J kg⁻¹ 与 4.9 m s⁻¹，纯作时次参考，不纳入判据。

## 定义与局限

MetPy 1.7.1：MLCAPE 采用 mixed_layer_cape_cin 默认底部 100 hPa 混合层；MUCAPE 采用 most_unstable_cape_cin 默认底部 300 hPa；DCAPE 采用 downdraft_cape 的 700–500 hPa 最小 θe 起始层；0–1/0–6 km 切变采用 10m 地面风与 MetPy bulk_shear 高度插值，递减率为 2m 到 3 km 的温差/3 km；可降水量采用 MetPy precipitable_water，在最低有效等压面以上积分。露点由 q 推算（FuXi 为 RH 推算），未把地表湿度强行填成等压层；近地湿度和 DCAPE 等指数因此有截断偏差。逆温用 2m 温度和地面以上有效等压层的最大相邻正温差，上端高度随一起输出。参数均逐格计算、区域内最大与 cosφ 加权平均，详见 metrics.json 的 n_valid 与错误计数。两模型都是基于 ERA5 再分析初值的后验 hindcast，不能证明实时业务中 ERA5 的获取时延可行。E2 峰位靠近 150 km 阈值（Pangu 12 h 为 146.6 km），边界/地形/高度定义改变可能翻转。

FuXi 输出 RH 而 Google ARCO Earth2Studio 词典不直接提供 r 层变量：由同层 ERA5 q、T、p 用水面饱和水汽压转换成 RH、限幅 0.1–100%，再喂 FuXi；这一数据适配不是重新训练，对冰相及近零水汽情况有近似误差。Pangu 用原生 ARCO q。没有使用 GraphCast operational；其 2016–2021 HRES 微调跨越两事件，标准 ERA5 37 层版在 Earth2Studio 当时没有同样的即用封装；改用同为 0.25°/13 层的 FuXi。

## 训练期与权重使用条件

Pangu-Weather：原模型训练 ERA5 1979–2017，2018 与 2020 留出（WeatherBench 2 §3.9，https://arxiv.org/html/2308.15560v1；原仓库 https://github.com/198808xc/Pangu-Weather）。本次 Earth2Studio `Pangu6` 经 NickGeneva/earth_ai 镜像取得 ONNX 文件，未独立按哈希比对与论文原始权重，故“此镜像权重与论文完全同一版本”未核。原仓库 README §License：trained parameters 为 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0、禁止商业使用，https://raw.githubusercontent.com/198808xc/Pangu-。

FuXi：论文说明训练 1979–2015、验证 2016–2017、2018 测试，事件日期不在所述训练/验证期（https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.12873；作者仓库 https://github.com/tpys/FuXi）。本次使用 Earth2Studio FuXi wrapper 与 NickGeneva/earth_ai 镜像 short/medium/long 权重；镜像自身的 README 给出“CC BY-NC-SA 4.0”（https://huggingface.co/NickGeneva/earth_ai/resolve/main/fuxi/README.md），因此按非商用处理；与原论文原始权重逐文件哈希、镜像具体训练日期尚未独立核实，不能把论文数据拆分当作镜像权重逐字节证明。原 FuXi 仓库 README 没有单列权重许可文本，商用授权不得据此推断。Earth2Studio 代码自身 Apache-2.0，与权重许可不同。GraphCast 原始权重 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0（https://github.com/google-deepmind/graphcast）；本次未运行。

## 成本、文件与复现

Colab A100-SXM4-40GB，一次会话 `lab-ai-weather-1013`，冷启动 `newcolab stop`，随后 `colab sessions` 返回 `No active sessions found on server`，usage 返回 0.00/hr、0 活动分配。

复现：（需在 Colab 用 、；、 为原始日志（失败也保留，不误写为有效结果）。

一行判读：有探索价值——Wister 的 12–24 h、Akron 的 12 h 有模型在预先固定的三个闸门同时过关；仅 n=2、0.25° 背景场，且 13 层缺低空结构、FuXi 权重来源还需逐权重核验，不能推到下击暴流本身或一般化时效。

# AI Weather Hindcast Supplement: ALTU and Three-Event Station Grid Tables (2026-10-13)

This is an increment to the previous , not overwriting its E1/E2 verdicts. Event E3 ALTU: 2023-07-03 18 UTC, 34.5872°N, 99.3381°W, verification domain 34.1–35.1°N, 99.8–98.8°W. The actual 0.25° grid included is latitude 34.25–35.0°N, longitude 99.75–99.0°W (4×4). Models Pangu6, FuXi; initialization lead times 12, 24, 48, 72, 120 h; both truth and initial conditions are ERA5. The actual storm first reached ≥35 dBZ at 21:08 UTC, and the storm peak was not used as a reference. Wister's pre-convective on-the-hour 19 UTC used 18 UTC due to the AI models' 6-hour time step, and Akron used 06 UTC.

## Original Criteria, Unchanged

Same as E1: ① Regional maximum MLCAPE/DCAPE errors against 13-level ERA5 each ≤25%, 0–6 km shear error ≤5 m/s; ② The simple average of the absolute errors of these three regional maximums is at least 30% smaller than the ERA5 persistence baseline P at the same synoptic time; ③ The most favorable grid point of the model regional MUCAPE is ≤150 km from the station. P(t,L)=ERA5(t−24⌈L/24⌉h). The second item mixes J/kg and m/s, which is a predetermined literal criterion, not to be treated as a dimensionally consistent comprehensive score. E3 was calculated using the MetPy 1.7.1 implementation of the original , with 37-level ERA5 serving only as an explanatory note; thresholds were not adjusted.

| E3 Model | Lead h | ① | ② | ③ (Distance km) | Overall Pass | Error AI / P (mixed units) |

| Pangu6 | 12 | No | No | Yes (55.3) | No | 158.9 / 133.0 |

| FuXi | 72 | No | No | Yes (32.4) | No | 291.1 / 277.7 |
| FuXi | 120 | No | Yes | Yes (46.6) | No | 313.4 / 528.7 |

E3 maximum satisfied lead time: Pangu6 None; FuXi 12 h. Pangu6 failed the individual MLCAPE item across all five lead times; FuXi 12 h regional maximum absolute errors for MLCAPE/DCAPE/shear were 52.1 J/kg, 88.6 J/kg, and 0.33 m/s, respectively. E3 13-level ERA5 regional maximum MLCAPE/DCAPE/shear are 532.25 J/kg, 856.98 J/kg, 8.79 m/s, corresponding to 797.33 J/kg, 948.90 J/kg, 8.95 m/s for 37 levels; the number of vertical levels substantially alters CAPE. The longest lead times of previous results remain unchanged: E1 Pangu6 12 h, FuXi 24 h; E2 Pangu6 12 h, FuXi None. Together with E3, there are n=3 events in total, which is not probabilistic verification or forecast evidence for downbursts themselves.

## Station Grid Points and 3×3 Neighborhood CSV for Three Events

`station_parameters_supp.csvTd_method` and `RH03_lower_limit_m`.

Station grid point ERA5 13-level / 37-level examples: E1 SBCAPE 561.9 / 694.8 J/kg, MUCAPE 561.9 / 694.8; E2 SBCAPE 0 / 0, MUCAPE 191.6 / 193.0; E3 SBCAPE 953.7 / 1006.5, MUCAPE 953.7 / 1006.5. This table contains grid point values and must not be mistaken for the aforementioned regional maximums.

Parcel definitions: SBCAPE/SBCIN use MetPy `surface_based_cape_cin`, MUCAPE uses `most_unstable_cape_cin` default bottom 300 hPa, DCAPE uses `downdraft_cape`; wind shear is anchored by 10m wind and interpolated to target heights via `bulk_shear`; RH is the height-integrated mean from the lowest available pressure level above ground to 3 km, with `RH03_lower_limit_m` recording the truncation height, not RH calculated fully from 0m. ERA5's Td is native 2m dew point. Neither model outputs native 2m Td; CSV `surface_Td_K` is a proxy value calculated from 2m T and available pressure after approximately holding q from the lowest above-ground pressure level (derived from RH for FuXi) down to 2m; the ALTU 2023 date is not within the Pangu/FuXi training periods described in the original papers, but the training lineage per weight of the mirrors remains unverified.

## Costs and Files

Supplementary session `lab-ai-weather-supp-1013supp_progress.jsoncolab stop` and read back `sessions`: No active sessions found on server; usage 0.00/hr, 0 active assignments.

Deliverables: , ten copies of , , and reproduction scripts are still retained.

One-line judgment: Has exploratory value, but the third event directly refutes the generalization that 'all models are useful at 12–24 h lead times'; only FuXi satisfied the three original gates at ALTU with a 12 h lead time, while Pangu did not. It is recommended that the Lead conduct an independent review of FuXi mirror weights, 2m dew point proxies, and 13/37-level differences before making stronger statements.

Data sources: ERA5 (Hersbach et al. 2020, C3S/ARCO); Models: Pangu-Weather, FuXi (earth2studio). See for details; new figure with source corner note is (original retained).

reviews.text:
# Verdict: AI Weather Literature Review Verification and Assessment Table Proposal (10-13)

Reviewers E (Gemini), A (GPT-6), D (GLM), 3/3 valid, all "supported with reservations". Lead personally verified two critical objections: GraphCast weight licensing (weathernext README "August 6, 2026 UPDATE … updated to permit commercial use", verified via WebFetch) and NowcastNet–HRRR (Das et al. 2024 npj Clim Atmos Sci 10.1038/s41612-024-00834-8, PMC11573709 abstract: 30 heavy rain events in TVA region, >16 mm/h grid points, 1–3 h, median CSI 0.30 vs HRRR 0.04, verified).

## Must Change
1. **GraphCast weight licensing** (A): Changed to permit commercial use since 2026-08-06 (code Apache-2.0). Row 14 of verification table and "CC BY-NC-SA non-commercial" in results.md are outdated, correct them; Pangu and FuXi remain treated as non-commercial.
2. **Re-cite rather than delete NowcastNet numbers** (A, D): 0.30 vs 0.04 is true; source is Das 2024 third-party evaluation rather than Zhang 2023; Zhang 2023 itself does not compare with HRRR; 71% ranked first among 62 people remains as before.
3. **Add qualifications to hindcast interpretation, acknowledge counterexamples** (A, D, E): Change "wind shear better than persistence within several days" to "better in most combinations" (counterexamples: Pangu E1 48 h, FuXi E1 120 h, FuXi E2 24 h); limit "CAPE only reliable within one day" to "under criteria of our group's n=2 cases, regional maximum, against diurnal-cycle-aligned persistence"; explicitly state that FuXi failed for Akron across all lead times. Not contradictory with Feldmann (high CAPE/shear areas already present multiple days prior in individual cases): different scopes/definitions (presence of high-value area vs regional maximum error ≤25%).
4. **AWS AIWP sample expansion** (E, A, D): Period restricted to after 2022-01 (GraphCast archive is operational version; Pangu/FCNv2 from 2020-10 onward), initial conditions are GFS/IFS, routine 00/12 UTC initializations, different definitions/scopes from our group's ERA5 initial conditions, 06/18 UTC initializations; change "zero compute" to "no need to run models, still requires data retrieval and diagnostics"; confirm first whether each archive contains 13 pressure levels (D: Pangu archive might only contain surface variables, unverified).
5. **Row 1′ write WRF only** (E): CM1 can only take soundings from AI fields as environments, cannot ingest lateral boundary conditions.
6. **Wind power definitions/scope** (A): Hardy 0.18/0.63 is instantaneous 100 m reconstruction from ERA5 input, not AIFS forecast error (the latter outperforms IFS after ~day 3); GenCast 5,344 wind farms is an aggregation of 10 m winds converted via idealized power curves, not measured power generation. Recommendation level maintained, but clearly stated.
7. **CFD row** (E, A, D): FuXi-CFD output includes u,v,w,k (TKE) and has independent validation from European wind towers (A and D read the full text; Lead did not read full text, recorded according to the two reviewers); training data is neutral steady-state RANS, applicable only to terrain steady-state winds, not to downburst transient inflow. Recommendation level changed to "Low-Medium" (for our group's main line). NRMSE figures for urban microclimate CFM are already in card , reported by authors relative to LES.
8. **Narrow inferences on WRF perturbation sensitivity** (A): 0.01 K → ~5-fold only shows internal storm sensitivity, cannot exclusively rule out large-scale AI ensembles; retain only "global AI ensembles cannot replace storm-internal dispersion".
9. **13 levels vs 37 levels** (A): ~500 J/kg applies only to E1 MLCAPE; MUCAPE difference is ~220–235 J/kg.

## For Reference Only
- In the same paper, Aurora 1.5 also has an aggregated evaluation for 2024–2025 (13–34% improvement relative to original Aurora) (A).
- Hua et al. 2025 preprint arXiv 2505.11750: Pangu outputs post-processed via Transformer to yield 1–8 day severe weather probabilities (A, E)—closer to "medium-range severe convective applications" than raw CAPE extrema, listed as candidate.
- Row 1b: WoFSCast/StormCast are surrogates for convective-scale numerical models, not radar extrapolation; reason for not testing for now changed to "lack of CAM training archives and training compute" (E).
- Criterion 2 is actually dominated by CAPE (E, D), already explained in decision records and project page.
- Typhoon profile network is an observational reconstruction; accuracy after coupling with AI forecasts remains unverified (A).

## Dissenting Opinions Not Adopted
- None. E's request to downgrade CFD to "Low-Medium" was adopted; A argued that recommendations lack uniform scoring criteria—conceded, recommendations are internal priority judgments, not objective rankings, noted in assessment table.

Basis: Literature per item seen in verification table; test numbers seen in .

## 13 层与 37 层参照的差别

同一验证时刻、同一 0.25° 水平网格，37 层只作附注，不用于裁决；下表为区域最大值（37 层减 13 层）。近地地下等压面用 ERA5 固定地形位势遮罩；最底有效气压面不等于地表。

| E1 指标 | ERA5 13 层 | ERA5 37 层 | 差值 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MLCAPE | 1086.11 | 1586.22 | +500.11 |
| MUCAPE | 1537.90 | 1773.23 | +235.33 |
| DCAPE | 1021.38 | 1132.99 | +111.61 |
| shear06 | 6.84 | 6.94 | +0.10 |

| E2 指标 | ERA5 13 层 | ERA5 37 层 | 差值 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MUCAPE | 1579.26 | 1800.65 | +221.40 |
| shear06 | 44.28 | 44.19 | -0.09 |
| inversion_K | 1.94 | 2.51 | +0.57 |

E1 13 层的区域最大 MLCAPE 为 1086.1 J kg⁻¹，37 层为 1586.2 J kg⁻¹；层数差异不可忽略。E2 的 13 层最大逆温升温 1.94 K，上端高度约 2409 m AGL；37 层最大值 2.51 K。这个定义是 0–3 km 内相邻高度层最大正温差，不是追踪 Akron 事件约 1.3 km AGL 那个特定逆温层，因此 E2 对高架对流的判读尤其脆弱。E1 次日 00 UTC 13 层 ERA5 的 MLCAPE/MUCAPE/DCAPE/0–6 km 切变区域最大值为 332.5/697.6/1019.6 J kg⁻¹ 与 4.9 m s⁻¹，纯作时次参考，不纳入判据。

## 定义与局限

MetPy 1.7.1：MLCAPE 采用 mixed_layer_cape_cin 默认底部 100 hPa 混合层；MUCAPE 采用 most_unstable_cape_cin 默认底部 300 hPa；DCAPE 采用 downdraft_cape 的 700–500 hPa 最小 θe 起始层；0–1/0–6 km 切变采用 10m 地面风与 MetPy bulk_shear 高度插值，递减率为 2m 到 3 km 的温差/3 km；可降水量采用 MetPy precipitable_water，在最低有效等压面以上积分。露点由 q 推算（FuXi 为 RH 推算），未把地表湿度强行填成等压层；近地湿度和 DCAPE 等指数因此有截断偏差。逆温用 2m 温度和地面以上有效等压层的最大相邻正温差，上端高度随一起输出。参数均逐格计算、区域内最大与 cosφ 加权平均，详见 metrics.json 的 n_valid 与错误计数。两模型都是基于 ERA5 再分析初值的后验 hindcast，不能证明实时业务中 ERA5 的获取时延可行。E2 峰位靠近 150 km 阈值（Pangu 12 h 为 146.6 km），边界/地形/高度定义改变可能翻转。

FuXi 输出 RH 而 Google ARCO Earth2Studio 词典不直接提供 r 层变量：由同层 ERA5 q、T、p 用水面饱和水汽压转换成 RH、限幅 0.1–100%，再喂 FuXi；这一数据适配不是重新训练，对冰相及近零水汽情况有近似误差。Pangu 用原生 ARCO q。没有使用 GraphCast operational；其 2016–2021 HRES 微调跨越两事件，标准 ERA5 37 层版在 Earth2Studio 当时没有同样的即用封装；改用同为 0.25°/13 层的 FuXi。

## 训练期与权重使用条件

Pangu-Weather：原模型训练 ERA5 1979–2017，2018 与 2020 留出（WeatherBench 2 §3.9，https://arxiv.org/html/2308.15560v1；原仓库 https://github.com/198808xc/Pangu-Weather）。本次 Earth2Studio `Pangu6` 经 NickGeneva/earth_ai 镜像取得 ONNX 文件，未独立按哈希比对与论文原始权重，故“此镜像权重与论文完全同一版本”未核。原仓库 README §License：trained parameters 为 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0、禁止商业使用，https://raw.githubusercontent.com/198808xc/Pangu-。

FuXi：论文说明训练 1979–2015、验证 2016–2017、2018 测试，事件日期不在所述训练/验证期（https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.12873；作者仓库 https://github.com/tpys/FuXi）。本次使用 Earth2Studio FuXi wrapper 与 NickGeneva/earth_ai 镜像 short/medium/long 权重；镜像自身的 README 给出“CC BY-NC-SA 4.0”（https://huggingface.co/NickGeneva/earth_ai/resolve/main/fuxi/README.md），因此按非商用处理；与原论文原始权重逐文件哈希、镜像具体训练日期尚未独立核实，不能把论文数据拆分当作镜像权重逐字节证明。原 FuXi 仓库 README 没有单列权重许可文本，商用授权不得据此推断。Earth2Studio 代码自身 Apache-2.0，与权重许可不同。GraphCast 原始权重 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0（https://github.com/google-deepmind/graphcast）；本次未运行。

## 成本、文件与复现

Colab A100-SXM4-40GB，一次会话 `lab-ai-weather-1013`，冷启动 `newcolab stop`，随后 `colab sessions` 返回 `No active sessions found on server`，usage 返回 0.00/hr、0 活动分配。

复现：（需在 Colab 用 、；、 为原始日志（失败也保留，不误写为有效结果）。

一行判读：有探索价值——Wister 的 12–24 h、Akron 的 12 h 有模型在预先固定的三个闸门同时过关；仅 n=2、0.25° 背景场，且 13 层缺低空结构、FuXi 权重来源还需逐权重核验，不能推到下击暴流本身或一般化时效。

数据来源：ERA5（Hersbach et al. 2020, C3S/ARCO）；模型：Pangu-Weather、FuXi（earth2studio）。详见；带来源角注的新图为 （原 保留）。
