# AI Weather Hindcast Supplement: ALTU and Three-Event Station Grid Tables (2026-10-13)

This is an increment to the previous , not overwriting its E1/E2 verdicts. Event E3 ALTU: 2023-07-03 18 UTC, 34.5872°N, 99.3381°W, verification domain 34.1–35.1°N, 99.8–98.8°W. The actual 0.25° grid included is latitude 34.25–35.0°N, longitude 99.75–99.0°W (4×4). Models Pangu6, FuXi; initialization lead times 12, 24, 48, 72, 120 h; both truth and initial conditions are ERA5. The actual storm first reached ≥35 dBZ at 21:08 UTC, and the storm peak was not used as a reference. Wister's pre-convective on-the-hour 19 UTC used 18 UTC due to the AI models' 6-hour time step, and Akron used 06 UTC.

## Original Criteria, Unchanged

Same as E1: ① Regional maximum MLCAPE/DCAPE errors against 13-level ERA5 each ≤25%, 0–6 km shear error ≤5 m/s; ② The simple average of the absolute errors of these three regional maximums is at least 30% smaller than the ERA5 persistence baseline P at the same synoptic time; ③ The most favorable grid point of the model regional MUCAPE is ≤150 km from the station. P(t,L)=ERA5(t−24⌈L/24⌉h). The second item mixes J/kg and m/s, which is a predetermined literal criterion, not to be treated as a dimensionally consistent comprehensive score. E3 was calculated using the MetPy 1.7.1 implementation of the original , with 37-level ERA5 serving only as an explanatory note; thresholds were not adjusted.

| E3 Model | Lead h | ① | ② | ③ (Distance km) | Overall Pass | Error AI / P (mixed units) |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| Pangu6 | 12 | No | No | Yes (55.3) | No | 158.9 / 133.0 |
| Pangu6 | 24 | No | No | Yes (35.8) | No | 224.2 / 133.0 |
| Pangu6 | 48 | No | No | Yes (19.8) | No | 292.5 / 290.8 |
| Pangu6 | 72 | No | No | Yes (19.8) | No | 347.5 / 277.7 |
| Pangu6 | 120 | No | Yes | Yes (19.8) | No | 315.1 / 528.7 |
| FuXi | 12 | Yes | Yes | Yes (46.6) | Yes | 47.0 / 133.0 |
| FuXi | 24 | No | No | Yes (55.3) | No | 166.8 / 133.0 |
| FuXi | 48 | No | No | Yes (48.7) | No | 212.3 / 290.8 |
| FuXi | 72 | No | No | Yes (32.4) | No | 291.1 / 277.7 |
| FuXi | 120 | No | Yes | Yes (46.6) | No | 313.4 / 528.7 |

E3 maximum satisfied lead time: Pangu6 None; FuXi 12 h. Pangu6 failed the individual MLCAPE item across all five lead times; FuXi 12 h regional maximum absolute errors for MLCAPE/DCAPE/shear were 52.1 J/kg, 88.6 J/kg, and 0.33 m/s, respectively. E3 13-level ERA5 regional maximum MLCAPE/DCAPE/shear are 532.25 J/kg, 856.98 J/kg, 8.79 m/s, corresponding to 797.33 J/kg, 948.90 J/kg, 8.95 m/s for 37 levels; the number of vertical levels substantially alters CAPE. The longest lead times of previous results remain unchanged: E1 Pangu6 12 h, FuXi 24 h; E2 Pangu6 12 h, FuXi None. Together with E3, there are n=3 events in total, which is not probabilistic verification or forecast evidence for downbursts themselves.

## Station Grid Points and 3×3 Neighborhood CSV for Three Events

`station_parameters_supp.csvTd_method` and `RH03_lower_limit_m`.

Station grid point ERA5 13-level / 37-level examples: E1 SBCAPE 561.9 / 694.8 J/kg, MUCAPE 561.9 / 694.8; E2 SBCAPE 0 / 0, MUCAPE 191.6 / 193.0; E3 SBCAPE 953.7 / 1006.5, MUCAPE 953.7 / 1006.5. This table contains grid point values and must not be mistaken for the aforementioned regional maximums.

Parcel definitions: SBCAPE/SBCIN use MetPy `surface_based_cape_cin`, MUCAPE uses `most_unstable_cape_cin` default bottom 300 hPa, DCAPE uses `downdraft_cape`; wind shear is anchored by 10m wind and interpolated to target heights via `bulk_shear`; RH is the height-integrated mean from the lowest available pressure level above ground to 3 km, with `RH03_lower_limit_m` recording the truncation height, not RH calculated fully from 0m. ERA5's Td is native 2m dew point. Neither model outputs native 2m Td; CSV `surface_Td_K` is a proxy value calculated from 2m T and available pressure after approximately holding q from the lowest above-ground pressure level (derived from RH for FuXi) down to 2m; the ALTU 2023 date is not within the Pangu/FuXi training periods described in the original papers, but the training lineage per weight of the mirrors remains unverified.

## Costs and Files

Supplementary session `lab-ai-weather-supp-1013supp_progress.jsoncolab stop` and read back `sessions`: No active sessions found on server; usage 0.00/hr, 0 active assignments.

Deliverables: , ten copies of , , and reproduction scripts are still retained.

One-line judgment: Has exploratory value, but the third event directly refutes the generalization that 'all models are useful at 12–24 h lead times'; only FuXi satisfied the three original gates at ALTU with a 12 h lead time, while Pangu did not. It is recommended that the Lead conduct an independent review of FuXi mirror weights, 2m dew point proxies, and 13/37-level differences before making stronger statements.

Data sources: ERA5 (Hersbach et al. 2020, C3S/ARCO); Models: Pangu-Weather, FuXi (earth2studio). See for details; new figure with source corner note is (original retained).

projects.digest:
# Forecasting Applications of AI Weather Models (Severe Wind Backgrounds, Wind Power, CFD) (Shelved)

This sub-project investigated whether global and regional AI weather models—such as Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, FuXi, GenCast, and StormCast—can supply useful forecast backgrounds for severe convective winds (downbursts and tornadoes), tropical cyclones, wind power, and CFD downscaling. It combined a three-reviewer audited literature synthesis across five directions with a pre-registered multi-lead-time reforecast experiment (12 to 120 h) on Colab A100 across three historical US downburst events evaluated against ERA5. While global AI models captured synoptic 0–6 km vertical wind shear up to five days out, convective available potential energy (CAPE) passed pre-registered criteria only within 12–24 h and failed inconsistently across events. Direct use of global AI weather models for historical downburst backgrounds is therefore Shelved.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-13**: Liang Hu approved spinning off the sub-project, and AI Weather Models Lead launched a literature review alongside coordination checks with the WRF and CM1 lines.
- **2026-10-13**: The WRF line confirmed no overlap with its active ERA5/HRRR runs and provided spatiotemporal windows and diagnostics for Wister (2018-08-10, pulse thunderstorm) and Akron (2020-06-09, elevated convection).
- **2026-10-13**: AI Weather Models Lead pre-registered three pass criteria against 13-level ERA5 (regional peak CAPE within ±25% and 0–6 km shear within 5 m/s; composite error ≥30% below 24 h persistence; peak grid point within 150 km) and assigned the 12–120 h reforecast trial to the research assistant.
- **2026-10-13**: The CM1 line noted that its multi-event bottleneck is station proximity rather than reanalysis grids (as 3 km HRRR covers 2016–2025) and contributed a third case (ALTU, 2023-07-03) plus a station-neighborhood parameter list.
- **2026-10-13**: The research assistant completed Round 1 reforecasts on Colab A100 (<5.3 CU) using Pangu-Weather and FuXi (substituting for GraphCast, whose operational weights covered 2016–2021).
- **2026-10-13**: Maximum lead times passing all three criteria were 12 h (Pangu) and 24 h (FuXi) for Wister, and 12 h (Pangu) and 0 h (FuXi failed all lead times) for Akron.
- **2026-10-13**: Parameter breakdown showed 0–6 km wind shear beat persistence in 16/20 combinations out to 120 h, whereas CAPE errors reached 1.5–4× persistence beyond 24–48 h and 13-level pressure data underestimated 37-level ERA5 MLCAPE by ~500 J/kg.
- **2026-10-13**: AI Weather Models Lead audited the literature draft, fixing 16 issues (including a misattributed DOI for a 2024 AI-driven WRF typhoon study showing 32%/23% intensity error reductions), and sent the judgment table to three reviewers.
- **2026-10-13**: All three reviewers returned "support with reservations", verifying that GraphCast updated its weight license to CC BY 4.0 on 2026-08-06 and that NowcastNet's 0.30 vs. HRRR's 0.04 median CSI for >16 mm/h rainfall came from an independent 2024 evaluation.
- **2026-10-13**: Reviewers also required qualifying FuXi-CFD as steady-state neutral RANS terrain flow and noting that public AI forecast archives initialize from operational GFS/IFS analyses starting in 2020–2022; AI Weather Models Lead incorporated all revisions.
- **2026-10-13**: The research assistant completed the ALTU (2023-07-03) supplement and 324-row station table (total compute <11.3 CU): FuXi passed only at 12 h and Pangu failed at all five lead times (CAPE errors 1.2–11× persistence; 13-level CAPE 532 J/kg vs. 37-level 797 J/kg).
- **2026-10-13**: AI Weather Models Lead added data source citations to all figures and marked the sub-project Shelved.

## Where it stands

This sub-project is Shelved after literature review and three-event reforecast tests showed that global 0.25° AI weather models cannot reliably predict CAPE beyond 12–24 h or replace 3 km HRRR/ERA5 for historical downburst simulations. All scripts, literature cards, and the 324-row station parameter table are preserved, while broader operational AI weather and climate topics were reorganized into a dedicated research program.

projects.report:
# Convection-Allowing AI and Nowcasting (L / M / L2)

## Objective
Determine whether ~3 km convection-allowing AI models (StormCast, WoFSCast, etc.) can directly predict thunderstorms and surface wind gusts, and whether they can perform batch forecasts/hindcasts across tens to hundreds of events—which is the only scalable route for the thunderstorm direction (Liang Hu, 10-14). Step 1 deliverables: a verification table of whether publicly available models can run on Colab A100; a verification table comparing 0–6 h lead-time forecasts against ASOS observations and HRRR across 5–10 downburst/severe thunderstorm events with station measurements; and AI/HRRR soundings vs. observed soundings on the same batch of events (prerequisite gate for L2).

## Current Status
10-16 **Shelved** (5/6 valid, verdict). What is shelved is the sample expansion of the configuration "StormCast V1/CONUS + 10 m wind × 1.6677 gust proxy + retrospective ERA5 conditioning": under the frozen thresholds, neither generation met the sample expansion criteria (V1: 20 events; CONUS: 12 events, 53/54 groups). This is **not** a claim that "convection-allowing AI is inferior to HRRR": hit-rate differences are not statistically significant (McNemar p = 0.22–1.0), Criterion 1 passes across all lead times if switched to the ensemble-maximum definition, any-member ≥25.7 m/s counts for AI are at least as high as HRRR GUST (V1: 9/11/9 vs. 8/8/6), V1 includes 7 previously seen cases, and gusts used only a constant scaling factor. Why not continue: the current experimental design can no longer answer whether scaling up is worthwhile, and further sample expansion would merely spend compute on a non-significant gap (CONUS costs ~700 CU per 100 events). Restart conditions (if any is met, open a new topic and pre-register new criteria rather than directly resuming sample expansion): ① blind sample + thunderstorm wind verification + convective non-severe-wind controls + pre-registered ensemble aggregation and probabilistic criteria + sample size estimation; ② mixed-layer wind profile gust diagnostics replacing the constant factor; ③ availability of a public convection-allowing model with native gust output or out-of-training-period verifiability; ④ changing the target to a batch application that does not require station peak accuracy (change of objective, subject to Liang Hu's decision). Round 2 used ~212 CU in total. M is closed; L2 was not started.

## Round 2 Criteria (Frozen on 10-14; No Post-Hoc Relaxation)
See the "Criteria" section: across each 1–3 h lead time, median peak ratio of AI gust estimates ≥ 0.9× HRRR GUST; for ≥25.7 m/s detection (flagged when ensemble P ≥ 0.3) on combined event + non-event samples, hit rate not lower than HRRR GUST and false alarm rate not exceeding 1.5× HRRR GUST; GFS real-forecast conditioning degradation relative to ERA5 not exceeding 20%. Gust factor fixed at 1.6677 (fitted on 2022). Wide and narrow windows reported side by side, window-edge fraction reported, two HRRR baselines; persistence included only in the appendix.

## Step 1 Criteria (Fixed Before Execution)
- Verification target: for each event, take the station with the peak ASOS observed wind; for the model, take the maximum 10 m wind (and gust variable if available) within ±25 km centered on the station and ±1 h around the observed peak time. Baselines: operational HRRR forecasts at the same lead time (10 m wind and GUST), plus persistence of the HRRR analysis at initialization time.
- Metrics: peak ratio (model peak / observed peak), peak timing and location errors, and whether ≥25.7 m/s (50 kt) is predicted.
- "Worth continuing": across 1–6 h lead times, AI model peak ratio ≥ 90% of HRRR, outperforming persistence on at least 2/3 of events; and single-event single-initialization inference time ≤10 GPU minutes (prerequisite for scaling up). If unmet, document exactly where it falls short without relaxing the criteria.
- Events must lie outside the training period of the weights used: StormCast V1 (trained 2018-07 to 2021-12, Apache-2.0 weights) uses post-2022 events; StormCast-CONUS (trained through 2025-09-30, OpenMDW-1.1 weights) uses post-2025-10 events.

## Path to Scaling Up
Write the Step 1 scripts as an automated batch pipeline ("event list → automatic HRRR initialization retrieval → inference → automatic verification against ASOS"); once past the gate, expand to tens to hundreds of thunderstorm high-wind events with ASOS observations in SPC/Storm Events for hindcast statistics; AIWP statistics from M establish the predictable lead time of the environment, determining whether L2 can perform "forecasts" or only "hindcasts." The CM1 ensemble in L2 runs on the supercomputer, with full-scale production handed over to the CM1 line or promoted to a formal project.

## Boundaries
- Hierarchy (Root Lead 10-14, 5-level cap): This node is a Level-2 node and will not open Level-3 sub-projects; when subdivision is needed, use tasks within this node or report to the parent node Lead (Thunderstorms and Convective Scale) to open a peer Level-2 node.
- Only two hops remain downward: this node → bot (`ideas`) → tool; task briefs must not allow tool bots (`gpu-gemini`, reviewer, `litwiki`, etc.) to further delegate to others.
- Subtree lists are not grouped by parent node; the UI project tree is authoritative for hierarchy.
- Compute and data: Colab prioritized, with no single-experiment cap (aligned by the parent project on 10-14 per Liang Hu's verbatim instruction "use Colab heavily at this stage without CU limits"; the previous "≤20 CU per experiment" cap is rescinded); pause and report to the parent Lead if a single experiment is estimated to exceed 100 CU; must run `colab stop` when finished so sessions never idle; dispatch only one executor per round. Round 2 of L remains under its existing cap: ≤200 CU for the entire round, report to the parent Lead once cumulative usage reaches 120 CU, and stop and report at 200 CU. Supercomputer single jobs ≤50 SU via resource request; L2 CM1 ensembles are run by the CM1 line, while we only deliver profiles in `input_sounding` format.
- Compute and storage locations (tightened by Liang Hu on 10-14): the workstation does not run compute or store compute data (46 GB free on the C drive as of 10-15 01:59). All solvers, inference, training, batch cases, and large downloads must run and be stored on Colab or CRC/TACC; the workstation holds only scripts, small results <200 MB per item, figures, and reports, keeping retrieved checkpoints as small files while leaving large intermediates on Colab or the cluster; if >1 GB must be temporarily placed on the workstation, report to the parent Lead first. CRC group space is ~95% full, so new large datasets should prioritize TACC work or scratch storage; CRC defaults to a single node. Every task brief must explicitly specify where computation runs and where outputs are stored.

## Settled Decisions
- 2026-10-14 Literature review verdict: separate the two StormCast weight versions; reclassify FuXi-Nowcast as a counterexample (inferior to persistence at severe gust thresholds); add HRRRCast as a candidate (public version is 6 km, GUST is a post-processed diagnostic, pressure levels up to 200 hPa, GFS boundaries) and retract "only StormCast is usable"; narrow the framing of the Cook 10% finding; retract the Collins extrapolation; state novelty under a narrow framing →
- 2026-10-14 Opened; Step 1 entirely on Colab and the workstation, consult the CM1 line first on the CM1 portion →

## Trials and Results
| Date | Action Taken | One-Line Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10-16 | Round 2 CONUS segment (B: 46.2 + B2: minimal + B3: 78.1 CU, estimated): 12 events in 2026 + 6 controls, 53/54 groups (missing 1 member in one 3 h control group) | **Failed under frozen criteria**. Wide-window AI/obs at 1/2/3 h: 0.67/0.74/0.68, HRRR GUST: 0.79/0.82/0.81, HRRR10×factor: 0.84/0.94/0.86; AI/HRRR GUST: 0.85/0.90/0.84 → Criterion 1 passes only at 2 h; hits AI 1/1/0 vs. HRRR GUST 4/2/3 (/12) → Criterion 2 fails; false alarms 0 for both. The missing control group affects only false alarms and does not alter the conclusion |
| 10-15 | Round 2 Segment A: full V1+ERA5 sample of 20 events + 10 non-event controls × 1/2/3 h × 10 members (~25.7 CU in this session, burn-rate estimate) | **Failed under frozen criteria**. # Brief: Convective-Scale AI Models Step 1 — Can They Run on Colab and Nowcast Severe Thunderstorm Surface Winds?

## Objective
Answer two questions: (1) Among public ~3 km convective-scale AI models, which ones can actually run on our Colab A100 GPUs? (2) For a model that runs, across 5–10 downburst / severe thunderstorm events at 0–6 h lead times, what fraction of severe surface winds can it capture, and how does it compare against operational HRRR forecasts? Because the ultimate goal is scaled-up hindcasting (dozens to hundreds of events), the scripts must be structured as a batch pipeline: "event list → fetch initial conditions → inference → verify against ASOS".

## Deliverables
1. Candidate model table — StormCast (available in Earth2Studio), WoFSCast, FuXi-Nowcast, CorrDiff-HRRR, etc. (list all found): resolution, domain, lead time, output variables (10 m wind / gust / pressure-level or model-level profiles), training years, initial-condition requirements, public availability of weights and code, license (exact quote), verified ability to run on Colab A100, and single-run inference wall time and VRAM usage.
2. Event table — 5–10 events (location, timestamp, ASOS station, observed peak wind and source, nearest radiosonde station), strictly outside the model's training years and inside the model domain; prioritize thunderstorm wind events in SPC / Storm Events where ASOS recorded ≥50 kt. Document the selection protocol.
3. Evaluation table + figures + raw logs + scripts: per-event, per-lead-time (1/2/3/6 h initialization) results under the criteria below.
4. Profile comparison: for the same events, compare vertical profiles from the AI model (if it outputs profiles) and HRRR at the grid point nearest the radiosonde station against observed RAOB soundings across MUCAPE, DCAPE, and 0–6 km wind shear.
5. One-sentence verdict: worth continuing / not worth continuing, plus the estimated GPU time required to scale up to dozens or hundreds of events.

## Criteria (Fixed Ex Ante, No Post-Hoc Changes)
- For each event, take the ASOS station that recorded the observed peak; for the model, take the maximum 10 m wind (and gust variable, if available) within ±25 km of that station and ±1 h of the observed peak time; also report ±10 km / ±0.5 h as a sensitivity check.
- Baselines: operational HRRR forecast at the same lead time (both 10 m wind and GUST fields), plus persistence of the HRRR analysis at initialization time.
- Metrics: peak ratio (model / observation), peak timing and location offsets, and binary detection of ≥25.7 m/s.
- Threshold to continue: across 1–6 h lead times, the AI peak ratio reaches at least 90% of HRRR's, beats persistence in ≥2/3 of events, and takes ≤10 GPU minutes per event per initialization.

## Boundaries
- Run on Colab A100, uncapped CU at this stage, but pause and report first if usage is projected to exceed 100 CU. Must run `colab stop` after each session and include `colab ls` evidence of zero leftover sessions in the report. Do not use the cluster.
- Use only public data sources (AWS HRRR, AIWP, Iowa Mesonet ASOS, SPC, NOAA Storm Events, UWyo/IGRA soundings); do not store large raw files on the workstation.
- Verify model weight licenses individually and note any non-commercial clauses; add newly used datasets, code, and models to the citations registry, and label data provenance in figure footnotes.
- Look up parameters omitted from papers (in the paper, repo, or config files) before making assumptions, and explicitly label any assumptions.
- If a model fails to run, document the exact blocker and move to the next candidate without stopping to ask; if none of the models can run, that itself is a valid result.
- No further confirmation needed before starting.

# Kickoff of Convective-Scale AI and Nowcasting Sub-project (2026-10-14)
Decision: Open L (incorporating M, L2). First step entirely on Colab A100/workstation: Verifying runnability of open models such as StormCast → 5–10 out-of-training-period downburst/severe thunderstorm events with ASOS observations, 0–6 h initializations vs HRRR operational forecast and persistence; soundings of AI/HRRR vs observed soundings for the same batch of events; M uses AWS AIWP hindcasts to compute environmental lead time statistics. Criteria are written down before running (see project page). Inquire first regarding the CM1 part.
Why: Liang Hu agreed on 10-14 that L is the only scalable route in the thunderstorm direction, and requested that the first step demonstrate how to move toward batch processing.
Cost of being wrong: A few Colab CUs and 1–2 days; if criteria are not met, then Shelved.
Basis: Parent project judgment table row 1b/4; JFT4WRDC PDF p3.

Apache-2.0 is earth2studio code license (GitHub API: 1196 stars, pushed on 10-14), weights are OpenMDW-1.1 | Adopt model card specification; DR's "Apache" applies only to code |
| StormCast paper: reflectivity FSS/RMSE at 1–6 h comparable to HRRR, realistic cold pool morphology and power spectra; **no** verification of ASOS/Mesonet surface winds | Both reports agree | Paper original text not read (arXiv 2408.10958) | Lead; "no surface wind verification" treated as a gap to fill, not as a literature conclusion |
| WoFSCast: modified GraphCast, trained on WoFS (Spring 2019–2021), object verification against MRMS; GitHub NOAA-NSSL/frdd-wofs-cast, Apache-2.0 | DR; Grok said no public repo | GitHub API: repository exists, Apache-2.0, 6 stars, last pushed 2024-12-06; whether weights are public unverified; only covers WoFS daily moving small domain, initial conditions require WoFS analysis (high likelihood of not being publicly archived) | Adopt "code is public"; whether it can be used for hindcasts to be verified by ideas |
| FuXi-Nowcast: East China, ≤12 h, outputs gusts, CSI superior to CMA-MESO; grid verification against HRCLDAS; no weights seen | Both reports | arXiv 2512.08974 abstract: gusts are output, East China domain; verification target not stated in abstract | Not usable for us (domain and weights), serves only as methodological precedent |
| All convective-scale AI models have **not** undergone independent verification against ASOS/Mesonet for ≥50 kt thunderstorm gusts | Both reports agree (assertion of absence) | Both independent reports agree, but still an absence in literature search | Adopt as "not found in either search", not proven non-existent |
| HRRR systematically underestimates strong winds: wind speed bias −13.70, gust −11.32 m/s when >20 m/s | DR attributed to Fovell & Gallagher 2022 (10.1175/WAF-D-21-0176.1) | **Misattributed**: Numbers are from Collins et al. 2024 WAF (WAF-D-23-0036.1, Wyoming/Colorado cold-season downslope winds) PDF page 10 (journal page 714), local Zotero PU6IMCA9; Fovell & Gallagher 2022 exists (Crossref) but content not verified | Adopt numbers, correct citation; qualification: cold-season downslope winds, not thunderstorm severe winds |
| Real-time QC after 2013 erroneously deleted ~10% of convective peak gusts in ASOS | DR ("MDPI no author"); Grok mentioned Cook preprint | Local Zotero DZF9GFUU (2023 preprint engrXiv 10.31224/2992) PDF page 1: "The peak gust is culled in around 10% of these events", 450 stations, isolated thunderstorms and active cold fronts | Adopt (preprint); impact on experiment: observed ASOS peaks may be missing, need cross-check with Mesonet and raw 1-minute data |
| No precedent for "AI output soundings → CM1 ensemble"; precedents exist for "observed/HRRR/ERA5 soundings → CM1" (e.g., Pearson et al. 2023 JTECH 10.1175/JTECH-D-22-0130.1 driving CM1 with Nashville sounding; JFT4WRDC 97 soundings ensemble) | Both reports agree | Pearson 2023 title and authors match Crossref check; JFT4WRDC already in library (PDF p3) | Adopt as absence in search; L2 has novelty if accomplished |
| Generative diffusion models alleviate peak smoothing (power spectra); but no evidence on hit rate for ≥50 kt | DR | Original text not read | Lead |
| 3 km can only barely resolve downbursts (core 1–4 km), peaks are smoothed; two Bolgiani 2020 papers | Grok | DOIs both found; KYSQSJZT already in library, page numbers not checked | Qualitatively adopted |
| GBM hybrid regression predicts cell ≥50 kt within 10 km/90 min | DR, no citation | Source not found | Not adopted |
| DR wrote MetNet-3 as Google DeepMind, FuXi-Nowcast as "Fudan & SAIS", and other institutional details | DR | Not verified | Not adopted |

## II. Impact on Sub-project Judgments and First Step Design
1. The gap in the first step is genuine: Convective-scale AI models lack independent station verification for surface thunderstorm severe winds → our 5–10 event verification has novelty and is also a necessary gate to pass before "scaling up hindcasts".
2. The only practically usable model is StormCast (full CONUS, HRRR initial conditions public, weights commercially usable). WoFSCast code is public but relies on WoFS initial conditions, and FuXi-Nowcast is limited to East China with no weights.
3. The baseline HRRR itself substantially underestimates strong winds (cold-season downslope wind gust bias of −11 m/s), so the criterion threshold of "AI peak ratio ≥ 90% of HRRR" is not high; absolute peak ratios relative to observations should also be reported simultaneously.
4. Observation side: ~10% of convective peaks in ASOS were erroneously deleted by QC → cross-check event selection and verification with Mesonet, and record "ASOS peak missing" separately.
5. L2 has no direct precedent and has novelty; however, the prerequisite is that the comparison between M and soundings shows the environment is sufficiently accurate.

## III. Preliminary Assessment (Submitted for Review)
- Route L: Worth conducting first-step experiments (Medium-High, maintained); literature cannot answer "what percentage can be forecasted", which must rely on our verification.
- Usable models: Primarily StormCast; WoFSCast depending on availability of initial conditions; FuXi-Nowcast is not usable.
- L2: Medium-High, has novelty, ranked after environmental verification.

# Convective-Scale AI Surface Severe Winds: Frozen Experiment Results

Sample: 7 NCEI thunderstorm wind ASOS events, 28 runs (1/2/3/6h per event). Raw run-by-run results; raw Colab logs; input events.

## Criteria and Limitations

ASOS peak values come from MG/ASOS in NOAA Storm Events, cross-checked with gust/PK WND from IEM METAR at the same stations; 1kt=0.514444m/s. Peak times are based on NCEI event times (IEM PK WND is within the same minute or several minutes; IEM "valid report time" in events.csv is not always the physical peak minute). Times are UTC; operating times in responses are US Eastern.
Centered on the ASOS station, predicted grid maximum composite 10m wind: wide window radius 25km, peak ±1h; narrow window radius 10km, peak ±0.5h. Verification centers are selected based on the nearest UTC on-the-hour, with initializations at center minus 1/2/3/6h; wide and narrow windows are applied equally to both the model and baselines. Location error is the distance from the maximum wind grid point to the station, and time error is the difference between that synoptic time and the NCEI peak. Persistence takes the 25km maximum of 10m wind from the HRRR analysis at the same initialization.
Note: ASOS measures short-duration gusts, whereas StormCast outputs 10m horizontal winds, not gusts; model results without gusts cannot be claimed as gust skill. HRRR GUST is listed separately, with HRRR 10m horizontal wind used for like-for-like comparison. The model is initialized with 99 HRRR fields but uses ex post ERA5 conditions (matching model training, not pure operationally available inputs); therefore, these are hindcasts, not operational forecasts. Stochastic diffusion single member did not fix the random noise seed, so peak values may vary upon re-running.

# Convective-Scale AI Step 1 Results and Round 2 (2026-10-14)
Results: StormCast V1, 7 events, 28 sets; did not pass under the preset threshold (AI/HRRR 10 m peak ratio ≥0.9) (1 h 0.85, 2 h 0.61); 0/28 predicted ≥25.7 m/s; superior to persistence on 6/7; speed passed. Evidence .
Decision: Do not scale up, nor shelve; commission a Round 2 re-evaluation under the same specification (gust conversion, 10-member ensemble, ≥20 events + no-event controls, GFS true forecast conditions, StormCast-CONUS testing post-2025-10 events), with criteria finalized before running. The record of Round 1 "did not pass" is retained and will not be retroactively modified.
Why: The comparison quantity in Round 1 was 10 m mean wind against ASOS gust, with AI and HRRR both only reaching 0.3–0.5, so the threshold primarily tested the specification rather than the models; single-member diffusion models have high noise; sample size is 7.
Cost of being wrong: If it still does not pass under the same specification, it will cost roughly 1 more day and several tens of CUs; at that point it will be Shelved.
Basis: Data from this line; for HRRR severe wind underestimation, see Collins et al. 2024 WAF (Zotero PU6IMCA9) PDF page 10.

items.text:
# Sounding Supplement: Gap Between CM1 Pre-Convective Column Extraction Rules and the Existing Seven Cases

This supplement does not overwrite or archived . The old comparison was "the 00/12Z of the RAOB closest to ASOS, model initialized 3 h prior to the sounding, nearest grid point to the sounding station"; it is not a CM1-qualified pre-convective land column. The old seven cases and the two NIP/ALTU cases are not the same event sample. The latter two cases are not included in this current CONUS weights test; the old seven cases actually used StormCast V1 weights (trained up to 2021), which are also not the current CONUS weights.

## Rules (Borrowed only, not claiming the seven cases are completed)

According to CM1 `MultiEvent_B_E5_timing_rule_20261013.md:5–11`, `MultiEvent_B_E5_land_column_20261014.md:3–8`: The time of the first ≥35 dBZ near the station is recorded as T_anchor; HRRR f00 is taken as the latest top of the hour prior to T_anchor−45 minutes. Search for LAND=1 grid points from near to far within ≤50 km around the station; within 20 km of that point, there must be no ≥20 dBZ in both the WSR-88D lowest-elevation volume scan closest to the aforementioned top of the hour and the HRRR simulated composite reflectivity for the same hour. Lack of observational radar coverage/missing data in candidate areas must not be treated as no echo. If there is no qualified column, mark as unevaluated. Both AI and HRRR extract profiles using the same latitude/longitude and the same analysis time; the HRRR f00 native levels and the analysis at the same point and same time serve as the reference, and are not replaced by the column from the nearest sounding station. This specific 45 min/20 km/20 dBZ threshold was fixed in advance by this CM1 line; it is not a universal constant given in the literature.

`cm1_column_rule.pycm1_preconvective_hrrr_analysis_utc` and latitude/longitude are left blank (see audit CSV).

## Time Difference Audit

 calculated using the verified ASOS physical peak minute and archived RAOB time, with the sign being RAOB−ASOS peak; this is not RAOB−pre-convective time: the latter can only be computed once T_anchor is determined. Relative to the ASOS peak, DSM/KOAX 2023-04-20 is −3.933 h, CNK/KTOP −2.400 h, SWO/KLMN −4.350 h, OFK/KOAX +2.150 h, DSM/KOAX 2024-08-01 −1.333 h, ALO/KDVN +3.917 h, LNK/KOAX −0.250 h. Among the first three, DSM and SWO, along with ALO (three cases in total), have peak time differences >3 h, for reference only; OFK and ALO soundings occurred after the ASOS peak and are also not prior observations. The >3 h classification relative to the true pre-convective time remains unknown and cannot be replaced by the peak time difference.

## Subsequent Inputs and Deliverables That Cannot Be Faked

Case-by-case raw radar volume scans and grid projections, HRRR contemporaneous REF/CREF, LAND, and native-level f00 are required before extraction can proceed according to the above rules; AI can rerun inference/extract profiles at the same location and time. Already have `soundings_raw.jsonlinput_sounding`. CM1 already has a read-only format example : first line is surface pressure (hPa), potential temperature (K), water vapor mixing ratio (g/kg); remaining lines are z_AGL (m), potential temperature (K), mixing ratio (g/kg), u/v (m/s); once native levels for the same pre-convective qualified land column are obtained, save separate AI/HRRR files and verify surface 2 m temperature/humidity and surface pressure, and do not mistake specific humidity in kg/kg for g/kg. A format example does not equal existing valid event inputs.

Conclusion: Existing only illustrates the old sounding point 3h comparison and cannot serve as the CM1 co-located, contemporaneous background or L2 handover. The time difference audit and column selection verification have been written to disk, but the actual CM1 columns, initialization HRRR f00 profiles, and usable `input_sounding` for the seven cases have not yet been generated; they are retained as empty rather than faked.

items.title: Observation-side and HRRR baseline supplement (10-14, US Eastern)
items.text:
# 观测端与 HRRR 基线补充（美东 10-14）

本补充不更改既定判据、原始 28 组 、 或图。实测权重是 （训练至 2021），不是 2025 年训练截止的 StormCast-CONUS。旧结果是在事后 ERA5 条件场下得到的回算，不能称严格业务预报。

## ASOS 原始 1 分钟交叉核查

脚本 逐例请求 Iowa Environmental Mesonet 的 NCEI ASOS 1 分钟档案 `gust_sknt`（5 秒阵风，单位 kt），于 NCEI 峰值时刻前后各约 1 h 比较；逐例 URL、记录数、精确时刻数值和窗口最大值见。不是独立仪器，也不是未质控传感器原始序列；与 METAR/Storm Events 同源，无法以二者一致证明不存在 ASOS 站内 QC 删除。已查到的峰值真实事件选择还可能存在条件抽样偏差。

| NCEI ID/站 | 报告峰值 kt / UTC | 1 分钟同分钟 kt | 1 分钟 ±1 h 最大 kt / UTC | 观测状态 |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| 1089702 DSM | 54 / 2023-04-20 03:56 | 54 | 54 / 03:56 | 一致 |
| 1102083 CNK | 52 / 2023-05-08 02:24 | 52 | 52 / 02:24 | 一致 |
| 1114169 SWO | 51 / 2023-06-18 04:21 | 51 | 51 / 04:21 | 一致 |
| 1111438 OFK | 56 / 2023-07-12 09:51 | 缺测 | 53 / 09:56 | 需单列：原始 1 分钟未复核到 56 kt；但 IEM METAR 与 NCEI 56 kt 同值，故并非可断言是假峰值，亦不能断言由 QC 删除 |
| 1203698 DSM | 57 / 2024-08-01 01:20 | 57 | 57 / 01:20 | 一致 |
| 1180878 ALO | 61 / 2024-05-21 08:05 | 61 | 61 / 08:05 | 一致 |
| 1107992 LNK | 52 / 2023-07-05 00:15 | 52 | 52 / 00:15 | 一致 |

六例一分钟记录与已归档 ASOS 峰值同分钟、同数值；OFK 一例缺少同分钟 1 分钟记录，但有 METAR 的 PK WND 独立格式交叉。这不是本轮可推断的“约 10% 删峰比例”：Cook (2023) 的约 10% 是对历史对流事件模拟 QC 的研究结论，不适合直接乘到七例。IEM 1 分钟档个别分钟缺失；要辨识源头删除，需另一仪器/网络（如有站旁 Mesonet）和原始质控标识，不能把本次同源比对说成独立传感器核实。本轮没有获取覆盖各站的独立 Mesonet 观测，因此 OFK 保留疑点，扩样前优先复核。

## 每事件绝对比与阈值

 保留未四舍五入的值，可重算。阈值命中为 AI 0/28 组；HRRR GUST 8/28 组；HRRR 10 m 风 1/28 组。对照本轮 10 m 风与短时阵风的物理定义不同，绝对比不等于无偏的同量精度；HRRR GUST 单列同为阵风诊断量，不能拿 Collins 等冷季怀俄明/科罗拉多复杂地形的约 −11 m/s 偏差对本轮暖季雷暴作数值订正。Collins 等 (2024) 原文摘要的适用域明确为“2016–22 winter months over Wyoming and Colorado”；这仅支持基线不应被当作完美真值。按本轮自身观测，上述绝对比和命中结果才是判据证据。

## WoFSCast 可获取性

截至本次核查，官方 仓库 `master` tree SHA `46a1271ee0a27a5b715b4686cdbfea0cd1f86dcf`，GitHub API 返回 166 条且 `truncated=false`，无可供下载的已训练 `.npz` 权重文件；release API 返回空列表。 明列 与，均是本地绝对路径，不是公开下载 URL。README 只讲装源代码和评估程序，没有发布权重/配套 WoFS 初值。因而目前可证“该仓库未提供可公开直接下载的一套权重 + 初始化/边界数据”，不等于证明互联网上或其他 WoFS 数据档绝不存在；也不能拿 HRRR 直接代 WoFS 成员/边界。代码 Apache-2.0（repo license），不可推断未公开权重的许可证、显存或运行时长。

核查链接：
- https://api.github.com/repos/NOAA-National-Severe-Storms-Laboratory/frdd-wofs-cast/git/trees/master?recursive=1
- https://api.github.com/repos/NOAA-National-Severe-Storms-Laboratory/frdd-wofs-cast/releases
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NOAA-
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NOAA-

文献依据：Cook (2023), *Meteorology* 2:276–294, https://doi.org/10.3390/meteorology2020017 （本地 Zotero DZF9GFUU 预印本 PDF 第 1 页）；Collins 等 (2024), *Weather and Forecasting* 39:705–723, https://doi.org/10.1175/WAF-D-23-0036.1 （委托方指出本地 PDF 第 10 页强风样本偏差；这里未将数值迁移）。观测来源 NOAA NCEI Storm Events 年度 CSV、IEM METAR 与 IEM NCEI ASOS 1 分钟档，详见上述脚本、CSV 和。

结论：补充验证未改变既定失败判定；尤其 OFK 的一分钟缺测提醒，当前 7 例不应被说成观测绝无漏峰。现有 WoFSCast 公共仓库也不足以立即做同标准 A100 回算；要试它，先取得有明确使用条款的权重及匹配 WoFS 初值/边界公开档。其他模型不能因 StormCast V1 结果而被否定。

# Round 2 Supplement: Window-Edge Proportions and Baselines (Round 2 Not Run)

This supplement only adds reporting items; the original three joint criteria and the 100 CU stop-first gate remain unchanged. is the prior pre-check report; this document does not overwrite its content or the Round 1 results. prompted by the platform is 's sparse network fusion task, not this StormCast task; no new run root was created, nor was that task's Colab session resubmitted or reused.

## Read-Only Window-Edge Check of Existing 7 Events (Seen Samples, Not Round 2 Validation)

 reads Round 1 line by line, producing . For each model's 28 sets, having the wide-window maximum at distance ≥0.9×25=22.5 km from the station is recorded as window-edge: StormCast V1 10 m wind 18/28 (64.3%), HRRR 10 m wind 13/28 (46.4%), HRRR GUST 14/28 (50.0%). This is of the same order of magnitude as "approximately 20 sets", but exact counting using recorded rounded distances under the new threshold gives 18 sets. Window-edge is merely a spatial proxy; it cannot alone prove that the maximum is ambient wind.

The CSV has one row per event, lead time, and model, presenting in the same table side-by-side the wind speed, peak ratio relative to observations, and ≥25.7 m/s determination for both the wide window (25 km/±1 h) and narrow window (10 km/±0.5 h), while retaining the distance to station of the maximum grid point for both windows. Round 1 wide-window hit counts: AI 0/28, HRRR10 1/28, HRRR GUST 8/28; for the narrow window, all three are 0/28. These are only the uncorrected 10 m wind results for the existing 7 cases, not gust conversions or ensemble scores. Data sources: NOAA Storm Events, IEM ASOS, AWS HRRR, ERA5/ARCO, NVIDIA StormCast V1; for original links, see Round 1 and .

## Round 2 Pre-Determined Presentation and Fair Baselines

For each initialization × event/no-event × model (V1/CONUS) × conditioning field (ERA5/GFS) × lead time, the main table lists on the same row: the wide/narrow window ensemble median, maximum, and P(≥25.7 m/s) of the AI gust estimate, HRRR GUST wide/narrow windows, and HRRR 10 m wind multiplied by the same gust factor for wide/narrow windows; each accompanied by the proportion of whether its wide-window maximum is located at ≥22.5 km (computed by valid numerator/denominator per combination, without mixing across groups). Events separately list their respective absolute peak ratios relative to ASOS/Mesonet observed gusts; no-event forecasts report whether the threshold was exceeded to compute false alarms. If the fixed factor is a scalar obtained from the 2022 fitting group, both predictions use the same scalar; if it is a function varying with space/time/variable, after applying the same pre-fitted function to the 10 m wind grid-by-grid and hour-by-hour, each should re-extract window extrema, and one must not directly multiply by the window-maximum HRRR GUST/10 m wind ratio at different locations, nor back-calculate factors using the verification-period GUST. Training and testing are strictly segregated.

The main verdict is still governed by the three pre-written conditions: HRRR GUST comparison, event + no-event hits/false alarms, and GFS degradation relative to ERA5; HRRR10 multiplied by the same factor is an additional strong baseline and does not change the established numerical gates. Persistence is placed only in the appendix, not as evidence of skill. Deficiencies are explicitly marked as unevaluated: currently there are no fitted gust factors, Round 2 event observations, 10-member probabilities, or GFS or CONUS inferences, so empirical values for these new columns cannot be generated, nor can Round 2 passing be determined based on the Round 1 table.

The complete Round 2 plan extrapolates to approximately 163.4 CU under independent runs, exceeding the statement of work's "if expected >100 CU, stop and report first"; therefore, no Colab session was launched for this task; for specific budgets and read-only inventory of existing sessions, see , . Other task sessions were not touched.

# L Round 2 Colab Cap Relaxed to 200 CU for the Entire Round (2026-10-14, Parent Project Lead)

- Decision I made: The cap for the entire round of L convective-scale AI and thunderstorm nowcasting Round 2 (StormCast/HRRRCast gust conversion, 10 members, ≥20 events + ≥10 no-event controls, estimated at ~163 CU) is set to 200 CU, overriding the parent project boundary of "≤20 CU per single experiment", limited to this round only.
- Conditions: Run the first stage (≤20 CU) first as a gate—the gust conversion pipeline must run through on the Step 1 seven events under the same specification as ASOS gusts, single-set inference time must match estimates, and the L Node Lead must verify before releasing subsequent stages; subsequent Colab sessions ≤50 CU each, stop upon completion, only one executing party per round; report expenditures and results obtained once cumulative usage reaches 120 CU; criteria are frozen before running and must not be retroactively relaxed; stop and report to parent project if exceeding 200 CU.
- Why: Liang Hu's exact words on 10-14: "The ultimate goal is scaled-up forecasting and hindcasting; at this stage, use Colab extensively, no CU limits"; Round 2 is precisely the step to test scaling up; Step 1 single-set inference was ≤88 s, so estimates have a basis; ≤20 CU per stage only adds session switching and delays without reducing risk, which is controlled by the first-stage gate.
- Cost of being wrong: At worst, ~200 CU (~37 A100 hours) spent in exchange for a "did not pass" conclusion; the first-stage gate controls wasted spend to ~20 CU.
- Not submitted for review: Not a supercomputing job, estimated <200 CU, executed in split sessions; no literature basis, falls under a resource decision.

# L Round 2 Compute: Execute at ≤20 CU per Stage First, Report 200 CU for the Entire Round to Parent Project (2026-10-14, Thunderstorm and Convective-Scale Node Lead)
- What was done: The L node approved 200 CU for Round 2 (estimated at 163 CU), exceeding the parent project's boundary given to this node of "≤20 CU per single experiment on Colab". Changed to executing in four stages (HRRRCast → V1 ERA5 → GFS conditions → CONUS 2026 events) at ≤20 CU each, while simultaneously applying to the Parent Project Lead to relax the cap for the entire round to 200 CU.
- Why: The superior boundary explicitly states "the 'no CU limits' in the original statement of work is subject to this clause", which this node cannot override on its own; however, Liang Hu's exact words on 10-14 were "at this stage, use Colab extensively, no CU limits", and Round 2 is precisely the step to validate scaling up, so relaxation was requested rather than cutting it.
- Cost of being wrong: If the parent project maintains 20 CU, Round 2 will be executed in stages, which is slower with more session switches; if relaxed, what was lost during the staging was merely time.

- 10-14 Update: Parent Project Lead approved 200 CU for the entire round; the ≤20 CU per stage in this entry is retained only on the first-stage gate.

items.title: Round 2 supplement: HRRRCast candidate and ASOS quality-control definitions (10-14, US Eastern)
items.text:
# 第二轮补充：HRRRCast 候选与 ASOS 质控口径（10-14 美东）

此处仅做来源与可下载性核查，不更改判据、不改动第一轮结果。第二轮 100 CU 先停闸门仍有效，未为此启动/复用 Colab、未做 HRRRCast 事件推理。

## HRRRCast-live 可取得什么

- 官方代码 https://github.com/NOAA-GSL/HRRRCast-live，MIT `LICENSE` 原文：“Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy of this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell copies of the Software”。许可文件在仓库根目录；权重未看到单独许可声明，不能仅以代码许可推定模型权重独立再分发条款。
- 仓库完整 master tree（GitHub API 返回 51 条，`truncated=false`）有，Git LFS 指针 `oid sha256:2edef5a5a32cd31f9a6b89ea0b0a54f36d4c528fc20990645debf9446a9315a5`，标示 203112115 字节（约 203 MB）。公开 HEAD 返回 200、Content-Length 203112115；HTTP Range 0–15 返回 206、Content-Range 0-15/203112115，前 16 字节为 ZIP/Keras 格式头。故不是“只有代码无权重”；匿名读取得到真实权重文件的首段，但未下载整文件或核完整 SHA256，也未加载、推理或测 A100。GitHub release v1 无附件不是无权重证据。 同仓库公开。下载使用 Git LFS/media 地址而非只取 134 字节指针；实际运行前仍需全量下载验 SHA256、装载与依赖适配。
- README 给定输入 HRRR 分析/预报与 GFS 边界、6 km（原 HRRR 隔点，530×900）、逐小时滚动与扩散集合；默认输入 6 个气压层变量×20 层，预测动态场通道数依配置。 第 43 行明确层值 `[200,300,350,400,450,500,550,600,650,700,750,800,825,850,875,900,925,950,975,1000]` hPa；最低气压 200 hPa，不含 100 hPa，因此现行默认配置不能直接抽至 100 hPa 的 L2 探空。不能把“20 层”误写成“到 100 hPa”。NOAA 模型页也称未来 3 km/9 年为计划，不是本权重能力：https://gsl.noaa.gov/hrrrcast/。权重对应训练起止年份尚未从模型文件和公开 README 证实；正式盲测前须核对，不能假定第二轮所选 2022–2026 事件全在其训练期外。
- 的 `compute_wind_gust`（第 464 行起）产出 GUST、GUST_FACTOR、GUST_CONV：GUST 是由 10m 风经验因子、低层最大风与垂直速度增强三者取最大所得的后处理诊断，不是明确经短时阵风真值训练的直接网络输出；默认经验因子 1.4（第 464 行），GUST_CONV 是其对流增强候选（第 543 行），与最终 GUST 不等同。比较时须并列保存两字段，并报告模型及 HRRR GUST 对观测的比，不能称“神经网络直接预测阵风”。
- README/ 有未来 GFS 时次或未来 synoptic cycle 的处理；严格“起报时可用”检验必须审每个 GFS cycle 的发布时间和源 GRIB URL，防止把事件后才发行的场混入真预报条件。当前仅检索代码，未验证此条件。

## 第二轮执行状态

若预算闸门允许正式开跑，HRRRCast 已是有公开权重的候选，应以同批且处于其训练期外的事件/对照、相同时间/空间窗和原判据，与 StormCast 分模型并列评估；成员随机种子与初值固定，GUST/GUST_CONV 两字段分列，报告宽窄窗、窗边比例及两条 HRRR 阵风基线。当前缺完整权重校验、训练期证明、运行时测量与合格事件，因此“可下载权重”不等于“Colab 已跑通”，本轮所有比较门槛未评估。早先 StormCast 第二轮名义预算约 163.4 CU，已越过任务书的 >100 CU 先停回报线；增加 HRRRCast 只会增加未量化工作量，不得自行开整批计算。

## Cook 2023 与观测处理

正式版 Cook, N. J. (2023), *Meteorology* 2(2):276–294, DOI https://doi.org/10.3390/meteorology2020017 （Crossref metadata 的页码也是 276–294；委托中 274–291 与出版信息不符）。摘要/§3.2 将 2014 年前 ASOS 数据模拟施加 Test 10：约 10% 的该研究所选对流阵风事件的峰值会被删除；不是所有当代 ASOS 事件普遍缺峰率，更不能对七例直接作漏峰概率订正。该文结论“recovery of erroneously culled observations is not possible”；IEM 的归档一分钟资料仍是站内 QC 后归档数据，不是可恢复的未质控传感器原始时序。对已报道强风事件保留 METAR/分钟分钟戳核对与缺失疑点，但独立 Mesonet 交叉主要用于无事件对照和“模型报强风而 ASOS 无记录”的情况，以免把漏观测算成模型误报。独立资料不全的对照不得默认标成真阴性。

第一轮统一表述为“所选强风事件里邻域 10 m 风幅值、使用事后 ERA5 条件场的回报”；不得推广为真预报雷暴阵风技巧或一切无事件误报能力。

## 核查证据（10-14 美东）

GitHub tree https://api.github.com/repos/NOAA-GSL/HRRRCast-live/git/trees/master?recursive=1；README https://github.com/NOAA-；LICENSE https://github.com/NOAA-GSL/HRRRCast-live/blob/master/LICENSE；层值 https://github.com/NOAA-#L42-L43；阵风 https://github.com/NOAA-#L464-L560；边界 https://github.com/NOAA-；NOAA 模型介绍 https://gsl.noaa.gov/hrrrcast/；Cook https://www.mdpi.com/2674-0494/2/2/17。

items.label: Review verdict
items.title: Verdict: review of convective-scale AI literature conclusions (2026-10-14)
items.text:
# Verdict: Literature Conclusion Review on Convective-Scale AI (2026-10-14)
Reviewers: E (Gemini), A (GPT-6), D (GLM), 3/3 valid, all "supported with reservations". After checking item by item, my verdict is as follows.

## Must Change
1. **Write the two StormCast weights separately** (E). Verified: models.md and HF model cards: V1 Central US 512×640, trained 2018-07-01—2021-12-31, **weights Apache-2.0**; CONUS DiT, full CONUS, trained up to 2025-09-30, weights OpenMDW-1.1. Step 1 actually used V1, and the 2023–24 events are outside its training period, hence valid; "can only use events after 2025-10" holds only for the CONUS version. ALO 2024-05-21 falls into V1's additional evaluation window (2024-05-08—06-15), which is not the training period; retain but note it. Reflectivity skill in the V1 paper does not equal validation of the CONUS version (A, D).
2. **Change FuXi-Nowcast to a counterexample** (E, A). Verified arXiv 2512.08974v2 full text: gusts are evaluated on grid points containing >1300 stations in East China, thresholds 10.8/13.9/17.2 m/s; original text: "FuXi-Nowcast becomes the best-performing model after the first few hours at 10.8 m/s, but Persistence and PySTEPS remain superior at 13.9 and 17.2 m/s"; trained April–September 2019–2023. Therefore, "no station evaluation for surface wind" does not hold, and the gap can only be described under a narrow specification; its underperformance relative to persistence at severe gust thresholds serves as a direct counterexample that "AI struggles to predict extreme severe gusts".
3. **Add HRRRCast and retract "only StormCast is available"** (A; D requested adding a line for CorrDiff). Verified GitHub NOAA-GSL/HRRRCast-live (MIT, 21 stars, pushed on 10-09) README: HRRR initial conditions + **GFS boundaries**, diffusion ensemble, 20 pressure levels with 6 variables, diagnostic quantities include **GUST, GUST_CONV**, CAPE/CIN; cited Abdi et al. arXiv 2507.05658. Weight download instructions are not specified in the README, providing insufficient evidence of availability. Changed to "Among checked candidates, StormCast V1 has been empirically tested and can run; HRRRCast weights pending verification; WoFSCast has no public weights or initial conditions; FuXi-Nowcast has no weights; CorrDiff-ERA5-HRRR has restricted weights, requires 80 GB, and is diagnostic downscaling (models.md already has this line); Jua EPT-2 has no weights found". HRRRCast includes gust diagnostics and 20-level profiles, which are more relevant to both Round 2 and L2; incorporated into Round 2.
4. **Narrow the scope of ASOS QC "approx. 10%" and update to the formal source** (A, E). Formal publication Cook 2023, Meteorology 2(2):276–294, DOI 10.3390/meteorology2020017 (verified via Crossref). "Approx. 10%" is the proportion of peak deletions among erroneously culled events when applying simulated Test 10 to pre-2014 records, not the empirical missing rate across all convective events; deleted observations are irrecoverable, and IEM's ASOS archive cannot be treated as un-quality-controlled raw data. Step 1 selected events based on "ASOS already measured ≥50 kt", so main station peaks are unaffected; Mesonet cross-checks are only needed for spatial/no-event verification and situations where "the model predicts severe wind while ASOS records none".
5. **Retract the deduction that "weak HRRR baseline → 90% threshold is not high"** (A, D). Citation correction for Collins 2024 is valid (all three verified PDF page 10), but it concerns winter down-valley/downslope winds in Wyoming/Colorado and cannot be extrapolated to warm-season thunderstorms. The real reason the threshold is lenient is the specification: 10 m hourly wind against 3 s gust, which depresses both AI and HRRR simultaneously.
6. **Complete criteria definitions and narrow conclusions** (all three). "≥90% of HRRR" is a one-way magnitude condition that does not constrain closeness to observations, does not penalize overforecasting, and omits the denominator field. Round 1 ideas evaluated against HRRR 10 m wind (did not pass), and records are retained unchanged; Round 2 has switched to AI gust estimates against HRRR GUST and "HRRR 10 m × same gust factor", added no-event controls to calculate false alarms, added GFS true forecast conditioning fields (addressing A's information cutoff issue), and 10 members with fixed seeds. Round 1 conclusions are stated strictly as "neighborhood 10 m wind magnitude and threshold-exceedance performance in selected severe wind events, hindcast under post-hoc ERA5 conditioning fields", without claiming station gust accuracy or forecasting skill.
7. **Frame novelty under a narrow specification** (D, A, E). Near-domain precedents: CGsNet (Xiao et al. 2023 GMD 10.5194/gmd-16-3611-2023, radar + deep learning convective gust nowcasting, station-interpolated grid evaluation), Lagerquist et al. 2017 WAF 10.1175/WAF-D-17-0038.1 (GBRT predicting ≥50 kt within 10 km of storm cells for 0–90 min, verified via Crossref; DR's claim of "cannot find citation" refers to this paper, changed to adopting as precedent, numbers pending reading original text), MetNet-3 surface station wind evaluation, FuXi-Nowcast. The gap can only be stated as "Not detected in this round: independent verification of native 3 km CAM emulating AI against US ASOS ≥50 kt thunderstorm gusts", and "AI soundings → CM1" is stated as "no direct precedents detected", without claiming to be the first.

## For Reference Only
- Pearson 2023 JTECH title and authors have been verified by me via Crossref; Bolgiani page numbers still pending verification.
- WoFSCast star count changes over time (4/6), marked with snapshot dates.
- Round 1 persistence baseline degradation over 3–6 h (E) — superior Lead has similarly pointed this out; Round 2 persistence is demoted to an appendix.

## Rejected Dissenting Opinions
- D advocated that "main criterion should be against HRRR 10 m wind, with GUST reported only as an accompaniment". Rejected: observations are 3 s gusts, and both E and A pointed out that using 10 m wind as denominator produces false positives where "both sides miss but it still counts as passing"; Round 2 primarily uses HRRR GUST, with 10 m wind reported alongside in the same table. D's concern about "cherry-picking fields after the fact" is resolved by fixing fields prior to running Round 2.
- E argued that Round 1 does not need Mesonet: partially adopted (see item 4), will not be retroactively done for Round 1.

## Impact on Judgments
L maintains "Exploring", and Step 1 conclusion remains unchanged (did not pass under preset threshold). Round 2 adds HRRRCast candidate to re-evaluate under the same specification; if it still does not pass under the same specification, it will be Shelved.

## 10-14 Evening Postscript (ideas verified HRRRCast)
The public repository does have weights (net-diffusion/model.keras, Git LFS, ~203 MB, anonymously accessible); however, this version is 6 km (HRRR skipping grid 530×900), not 3 km as in NOAA announcements (official site describes 3 km as a plan); pressure levels are 20 levels down to 200 hPa at lowest, unable to extract to 100 hPa; GUST is a post-processing diagnostic (maximum of 10 m wind × 1.4, low-level max wind, and vertical velocity enhancement), not a direct network prediction; weights have no separate license statement; training period unverified. "3 km" and "can extract upper-level soundings" in Item 3 are corrected accordingly. Cook 2023 page numbers follow Crossref: 276–294. Evidence .

# 第二轮预检与预算闸门（未运行推理，不是评分结果）

2026-10-14 18:17 美东检查全账户 Colab：A100 `lab-ace-stochastic-` 与一项 CPU 会话在运行；本任务未创建会话、没有覆盖第一轮文件，也没有运行任何第二轮推理。平台提示的 属于 的 H 稀疏站网 ERA5 融合，并非本任务；本任务目录在，没有发现原有 r2 结果。因此不重提 H、不复用其会话。`colab sessions` 此时记录的上述两个会话并非本任务，不能擅自停止。

## 已完成的只读来源预筛

 读取 NOAA NCEI Storm Events 年度 bulk CSV 的 2022–2026 最新索引，筛选 Thunderstorm Wind、MG、≥50 kt、来源或叙述出现 ASOS、位置含三字母站码，并用 V1 美国中部的保守经纬外框 (34–44°N, 102–91°W) 作预筛。 有 666 条候选：2022 年 123，2023 年 160，2024 年 181，2025 年 141，2026 年 61；298 个不同 UTC 日。2026 候选仅 2–7 月（末项 07-01 UTC），不能说已有完整 2026 暖季。此表是候选，不等于模型真实网格覆盖或已核实 ASOS 原始分钟峰值；NOAA 记录时间仍须和 PK WND 的物理峰值分钟核对；无事件控制须用完整报表与分钟观测核实，不能由本表空白推定。初版 7 事件结果已被看过，若复用须标为已见样本而非盲测。

来源：NOAA NCEI 年度 CSV https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/swdi/stormevents/csvfiles/ （每条候选保存具体 URL）。模型卡 V1 https://huggingface.co/nvidia/stormcast-，CONUS https://huggingface.co/nvidia/stormcast-。后者明确训练到 2025-09-30，现列 2026 候选只能经独立观测核验后作其测试。

## 开跑前冻结的判据（照，不调整）

V1≥20 训练后事件、同区同季≥10 无事件对照；至少 10 个固定随机种子/起报，1/2/3/6 h；≥10 事件的 GFS 条件与 ERA5 条件并列，CONUS≥10 个 2025-10 后事件单列。只以 2022 年拟合事件建立阵风系数 HRRR GUST/HRRR 10m 风，绝不以检验事件或检验期 HRRR GUST 拟合；模型、站与时间严格配对。AI 阵风估计和 HRRR GUST 与观测按站 ±25 km/峰值 ±1h 比，±10 km/±0.5h 敏感性另列。集合成员先固定种子再报最大、中位、P(阵风≥25.7m/s)。三个联合门槛原样执行：1–3h 各档 AI/观测峰值比中位≥HRRR GUST/观测的0.9；P≥0.3 的命中率≥HRRR GUST 且误报率≤其1.5；GFS 条件下第一门槛相对 ERA5 下降≤20%。未计算处一律标为“未评估”，不得记作失败或通过。

## 100 CU 先停报的量化依据

第一轮 28 组实际成功运行耗时合计 1530.7s，均值 54.6679s/单成员/事件/提前量，含数据传输和 HRRR 基线，不等于纯 GPU 前向。当前共享账户用量标示 A100 约 5.38 CU/小时。按逐成员独立串行外推，仅 V1 20 事件+10 对照、四档、10 成员为 1200 组，约 18.22 GPU 墙钟小时/98.04 CU；其中 10 事件另跑 GFS 条件约 32.68 CU；CONUS 10 事件四档 10 成员即使用 V1 同速再约 32.68 CU。名义合计约 163.40 CU，尚未含训练组、CONUS 加载与变慢风险。共享初值/基线和复用缓存可能缩短实际时间，CONUS 大域也可能加长；因此这是粗预算，不是下限或账单。按委托“预计超过100 CU先停下回报”，未启动 GPU。Colab 无本任务待停会话，`colab sessions` 的其他会话保留原状。

## 补充核查（HRRRCast 与观测口径）

官方 HRRRCast-live 仓库的 Git LFS 权重文件匿名可读（HEAD 200，Range 206；尚未全量下载/验哈希），与 WoFSCast“未找到公开权重”不同；默认 20 个气压层最低气压 200 hPa，不到 100 hPa； 是代码诊断量，不是网络直接输出。详见， 已补行；因 100 CU 先停闸门，此次未测试 A100，也未评估同批事件。Cook 2023 的约 10% 仅是特定历史模拟 Test 10 的删峰比例；IEM 归档不可恢复已删观测。Mesonet 交叉重点用于无事件对照和模型报强风而 ASOS 未报的情况。第一轮结论限于所选事件邻域 10 m 风、事后 ERA5 条件场的回报。平台提醒的 与 均是 UrbanTALES 学习曲线任务，目标与目录都不属于本轮对流尺度 AI；未复用或触碰它们的 Colab 会话。

## 未完成项目

 的分钟观测核实、无事件对照、拟合/测试严格隔离、GFS 实际适配、10 成员推理、CONUS A100 80GB high-mem 显存和垂直顶层实测、评分表与图均未完成。不能按现有数据判断第二轮是否值得扩样。V1/CONUS 模型卡都列混合层索引至 hl30（跳过部分中间层）；它们是否实际覆盖 100 hPa 必须用输出的 p_hl30 与地形/时刻范围核实，不由层数猜测。

## 后续执行回报（10-14 20:33 美东）
以上为算力放行前的历史预检状态，部分事项已有 pilot；请以不覆盖原记录的 、 和原始 JSONL 为当前证据。V1 仅两事件完成三档十成员，CONUS 仅一事件 L1 十成员；长批 Colab 被平台以 `pruned` 中断，其余验收未评估。已手动停止第二会话，第一会话被平台终止；现无本任务活跃会话。

# Convective-Scale AI Round 2: Execution Report (Partially Completed, Cannot Render Verdict on the Gate)

10-14 20:33 EDT. Neither Round 1 nor the original covered this; this document records actual execution. Data sources: NOAA NCEI Storm Events annual details, Iowa Environmental Mesonet ASOS/METAR, NOAA AWS HRRR and GFS, Google ARCO-ERA5, NVIDIA Earth2Studio 0.19.0 StormCast V1/CONUS; individual URLs are in the event table, raw JSONL, . Figures also note sources.

## Sample and Pre-locked Criteria

. Cross-checking against the same IEM source cannot recover gusts removed by ASOS quality control; the ~10% from Cook (2023) specific simulation was not treated as a general underreporting rate. From one week prior to the same station/time, 10 candidates were constructed: NOAA Storm Events for that year had no thunderstorm wind/high wind/tornado/hail records within 50 km/±3 h, and the station's METAR maximum gust within ±3 h was <40 kt; these candidates have not yet undergone independent Mesonet cross-checking, so they cannot be regarded as confirmed true negatives, nor can they be used for the final false alarm rate.

Gust proxy option (b) was chosen: . Multiply 10 m wind of AI and HRRR by the same scalar, while listing native HRRR GUST values separately. Do not adjust the coefficient using verification-period HRRR GUST. This coefficient is an empirical proxy rather than a physical diagnostic of StormCast output gusts.

Fixed member seeds 101–110 were used; each member shared the same initialization HRRR initial values and ARCO condition source, but Earth2Studio , listing only combinations confirmed to have 10 members.

## Actual Runs and Numerical Values (Pilot Only, Prohibited from Being Treated as Pass/Fail)

V1: Colab A100 high-mem successfully ran two 2023 cases (AMA, CDS) for 1/2/3 h × 10 members each, totaling 60 members with paired HRRR baselines; the third case CID only ran the first member and was excluded from scoring. The raw incremental checkpoint of the first session was 68 lines, containing 7 lines of HRRR baseline and 61 lines of AI; remaining VM data was not archived. In addition, a 10-member engineering pilot for L2 of the previously seen DSM event was completed and not counted toward new samples.

Wide-window gust proxy medians (m/s) for the two complete V1 cases, compared with HRRR GUST and observed gusts: AMA L1 34.811 / 30.561 / 1.041 (AI/observed), L2 30.130 / 30.704 / 0.901, L3 30.317 / 26.492 / 0.907; CDS L1 25.151 / 26.495 / 0.789, L2 26.336 / 26.540 / 0.826, L3 24.469 / 23.089 / 0.767. Their ensemble P(≥25.7 m/s) was 1/1/1 for AMA, 0.3/0.7/0.4 for CDS; window-edge member proportions were 0.4/0.3/0.3 for AMA, 0.3/0.6/0.5 for CDS. Wide and narrow windows and HRRR10 baselines with the same coefficient see CSV; these are pilot observations from two cases, not an acceptance evaluation of ≥20 cases.

True forecast conditions: ). GFS has only a 6-hour cycle, so 02Z cannot be treated as GFS 02Z co-initialization; conservatively select a cycle at least 6 h earlier, as specific historical release times were not confirmed file-by-file. A single member cannot calculate the degradation of the true forecast version relative to the ERA5 ensemble.

CONUS: Completed 2 steps for the 2026-04-04 OKC instance on A100 80GB high-mem, grid 1024×1792, forward pass 97.42 s, peak GPU allocation 20.62 GB; installation and loading underwent , insufficient to judge the CONUS threshold.

HRRRCast: Public Git LFS weights fully downloaded on Colab, 203112115 bytes, SHA256 `2edef5a5a32cd31f9a6b89ea0b0a54f36d4c528fc20990645debf9446a9315a5`, consistent with repository pointer; official code MIT, but no independent license seen for weights. Default Colab Python 3.13/TensorFlow 2.21 incompatible with legacy Keras archives; isolated Python 3.10/TensorFlow 2.15 can successfully load the 329-input/138-output channel model on CPU, but this isolated environment lacks usable CUDA libraries, and still lacks runnable preprocessing for HRRR 20-level analysis and full GFS boundary fields; therefore there are no event forecasts, and it cannot pose as a side-by-side score alongside StormCast. The training period of Abdi et al. arXiv:2507.05658v1 is 2021-03—2024-03, and the 2023 cases selected for V1 fall within its training period; even if run successfully, it cannot serve as an independent evaluation and must be separately tested on the 2026 intersection.

## Platform Interruptions, Budget, and Incomplete Items

The first session `ideas-convective-r2-1014` automatically had `session_terminated` during a long batch, historical log reason being `pruned` (10-14 19:43 EDT; Item 27), losing subsequent VM progress; sent to Platform Lead , requesting them to clarify auto-reclaim rules, without having them run on our behalf. What was archived locally was the 68 lines downloaded at 19:32; subsequent unarchived lines were not treated as results. The second session `ideas-convective-r2-cont-1014colab stop`; final `colab sessions` does not include the two sessions of this task, other task sessions untouched. Shared account balance went from 1435.14 to 1408.38 CU, total drop of 26.76 CU including other task sessions, which cannot be attributed as the exact consumption of this task and clearly did not reach the 200 CU ceiling of this task.

Did not complete established acceptance: V1 ≥20 events with complete 1/2/3h, ≥10 confirmed non-event controls, ≥10 events GFS/ERA5 paired ensembles, CONUS ≥10 events, and HRRRCast same-batch comparable ensembles; therefore, the three joint thresholds—event peak ratio, hit-and-false-alarm rate, GFS degradation ≤20%—are all marked "Unassessed". One cannot recommend expanding to hundreds of events based on pilots, nor judge any model as not worthwhile. If the platform provides a stable and archivable long-run mechanism, work should continue in slices according to the existing manifest, verifying independent non-event data first, and the stored 68 lines must not be duplicated as new results. Currently is the execution and continuation script, applies only to complete 10-member groups; missing summary tables were not forged this round.

# Convective-Scale AI Round 2, Segment ② V1/ERA5 Capped Continuation Report

10-14 22:39 EDT. Only this segment StormCast V1 + ex-post ARCO-ERA5 conditioning, 1/2/3 h, fixed seeds 101–110; gust proxy follows the frozen 2022 HRRR training set coefficient 1.6677111737. , and previous 68-line checkpoint were reused read-only; completed groups for AMA and CDS were skipped, not recalculated. Platform prompt is another line H pairing mini-test, not overlapping with this segment's objective, directory, or session; did not touch it. GFS, CONUS, HRRRCast were not launched in this segment.

## Storage and Compute

The first session `ideas-convective-r2-v1seg2-1014`, after completing L1 of control C1075354, lost CLI connection on the next attempt; confirmed VM idle, downloaded 79-line checkpoint and stopped. Continuation session `ideas-convective-r2-v1seg2b-1014` uploaded this checkpoint, and remote idempotent script skipped existing lines; `colab-keepalive` executed read-only code and downloaded checkpoints every 4 minutes. The budget guardian took shared account balance as a conservative upper bound and stopped when cumulative balance dropped 18.03 CU (1396.12→1378.09). Due to concurrent billing from other sessions, 18.03 CU cannot be fully attributed to this task; this segment itself did not exceed 18.03 CU, below 20 CU. Final `colab sessions` contained neither of the two sessions of this task; sessions of other tasks were not stopped. After each group was completed, the program immediately appended and fsynced on the VM; due to CLI limitations, downloads occurred every 4 minutes and once before termination, rather than strictly immediately after each group, and no claim was made of satisfying this sub-requirement. C1087366 L2 seed110 being computed at termination was not counted toward complete groups. An operational mistake must be disclosed: the keepalive did not explicitly set `--keep`, and default rotation deleted several timestamped copies previously downloaded by it (violating the requirement that existing results must not be deleted on one's own); the original 68-line checkpoint, locally saved checkpoints along the way, and final 153-line complete results were all preserved, without losing completed lines. Future continuations have written the prohibition of default rotation into the Colab skill; all copies must be retained or separately approved.

Final has 153 lines and all are status=ok. Qualified 10-member + HRRR paired events: 3 cases (AMA, CDS, CID) × three tiers, totaling 9 groups; non-event controls: CDS 3 tiers, CID 1 tier, totaling 4 groups; in addition CID L2 9-member unscored. Total 13 groups; reported "complete events 3, complete controls 1" requires all three lead times of the case to be complete. Controls and events progressed alternately, each case completed in the order of 1/2/3 h, leaving incomplete cases at the budget boundary. items.text:
# Proposed Shelving of Sub-Project L (Convective-Scale AI and Thunderstorm Nowcasting): Evidence Summary (2026-10-16)
Frozen criteria ("Criteria"): 1) At each 1–3 h lead time, median peak ratio of AI gust proxy ≥0.9×HRRR GUST; 2) For ≥25.7 m/s discrimination (reported when ensemble P≥0.3), hits no lower than HRRR GUST and control false-alarm rate ≤1.5×HRRR GUST; 3) Under true GFS forecast conditioning, degradation relative to ERA5 ≤20% (run only if Criteria 1 and 2 pass). Gust proxy = AI 10 m wind × 1.6677 (fitted from 2022 HRRR GUST/10 m wind without using verification events). Wide window: 25 km/±1 h; narrow window: 10 km/±0.5 h. Conditioning fields are a posteriori ERA5 (hindcast, not operational forecast).

## StormCast V1 (Trained 2018-07 to 2021-12), 20 ASOS ≥50 kt Events (2023–24) + 10 Controls
| Lead Time | AI / Obs | HRRR GUST / Obs | HRRR10×Factor / Obs | AI / HRRR GUST | Hits (AI vs HRRR GUST) | False Alarms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 h | 0.68 | 0.73 | 0.90 | 0.93 | 4/20 vs 8/20 | 0/10 vs 0/10 |
| 2 h | 0.68 | 0.71 | 0.75 | 0.96 | 5/20 vs 8/20 | 0 vs 0 |
| 3 h | 0.64 | 0.75 | 0.85 | 0.85 | 4/20 vs 6/20 | 0 vs 0 |
Criterion 1: 1 h and 2 h pass, 3 h fails; Criterion 2: all three lead times fail. Source: verification archive.

## StormCast-CONUS (Trained through 2025-09-30), 12 Events (2026) + 6 Controls, 53/54 Groups (Missing 1 Control 3 h Group, 9/10 Members)
| Lead Time | AI / Obs | HRRR GUST / Obs | HRRR10×Factor / Obs | AI / HRRR GUST | Hits (AI vs HRRR GUST) | False Alarms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 h | 0.67 | 0.79 | 0.84 | 0.85 | 1/12 vs 4/12 | 0/6 vs 0/6 |
| 2 h | 0.74 | 0.82 | 0.94 | 0.90 | 1/12 vs 2/12 | 0/6 vs 0/6 |
| 3 h | 0.68 | 0.81 | 0.86 | 0.84 | 0/12 vs 3/12 | 0/5 vs 0/5 |
Criterion 1: only 2 h passes; Criterion 2: hits at all three lead times are lower than HRRR GUST, failing (the missing control group affects only false alarms and does not alter the hit conclusion). Source: verification archive (`scores.csv`, `summary.json`).

## Additional Findings
- Both models perform worse than the simple baseline of "HRRR 10 m wind × same factor". In the narrow window (10 km), both AI models reach only 0.4–0.5 of observations. In the wide window, maxima frequently fall on the window boundary (133–143 out of 300 member-cases in V1 AI).
- Cost: Each CONUS group (1 event × 1 lead time × 10 members) takes ~14/20/27 minutes (1/2/3 h) on a single A100 GPU; 100 events × 3 lead times require ~100 GPU hours ≈ 700 CU; V1 takes 3–5 minutes per group.
- Other candidates: WoFSCast has no public weights or initial conditions; FuXi-Nowcast is restricted to East China with no public weights; the public HRRRCast release is 6 km, covers a 2021-03 to 2024-03 training period, and hung during GPU loading without running to completion; CorrDiff has restricted weights and is purely diagnostic.
- Literature: No independent verification of convective-scale AI against ASOS ≥50 kt thunderstorm gusts was found; FuXi-Nowcast underperforms persistence at 13.9/17.2 m/s gust thresholds (arXiv 2512.08974v2). Subject to review verdict.
- Data generated by this track without external literature basis: the gust factor and all verification numbers.

## Proposed Shelving Rationale and Restart Conditions (Pending Review)
Rationale: Under a matched gust-proxy definition, the two generations of StormCast achieve only ~1/4 to 2/3 of HRRR GUST's hit rate on ≥50 kt thunderstorm winds, with median peak ratios below 0.9 at multiple lead times; they cannot even beat "HRRR 10 m × factor"; scaling CONUS costs ~700 CU per 100 events.
Restart conditions: (1) Emergence of a convective-scale AI model with native gust output or a validated gust diagnostic; (2) Release of a 3 km HRRRCast version or another open-weight model verifiable outside its training period; (3) Availability of a gust conversion that does not rely on 10 m wind × constant factor (such as a boundary-layer wind-profile diagnostic) that can be re-evaluated on V1; (4) A shift by the research group toward high-volume applications with lower peak-magnitude requirements (such as severe-wind environmental probability).

# L Convective-Scale AI and Thunderstorm Nowcasting: Shelved (2026-10-16)
Decision: Per the review verdict, the status of L is changed to "Shelved", with the shelved scope strictly limited to sample expansion under the configuration "StormCast V1/CONUS + 10 m wind × 1.6677 gust proxy + a posteriori ERA5"; externally, this must not be stated as "convective-scale AI is inferior to HRRR".
Why: Neither generation passed the frozen threshold (under Criterion 2 at P≥0.3, hit rates across all six lead-time bins were below HRRR GUST); however, the review and recalculation showed that the differences are not statistically significant, Criterion 1 is sensitive to ensemble aggregation, and seen samples were included, meaning further sample expansion under this setup cannot answer whether scaling up is worthwhile.
Cost if wrong: If convective-scale AI is actually viable, we delay by one round; restarting requires a fresh pre-registration meeting the four conditions in the verdict (recalculating mixed-layer gust diagnostics on existing events can be done first at ~0.5 CU/group for V1).
