# Thunderstorms: AI Forecast-Driven WRF (Exploring)

This sub-project (Node K) evaluates whether global AI weather forecasts (Pangu-Weather) can drive the regional model WRF to simulate mid-latitude thunderstorm downbursts and surface gusts as accurately as operational GFS forecasts at 1–3 day lead times. In collaboration with the WRF modeling line, the AI Weather Models Lead designed a controlled experiment on the 2020-06-09 Akron, Colorado downburst (observed gusts of 37.04 m/s at KAKO ASOS and 50.45 m/s at the USDA tower) using a single 4 km domain initialized at 6, 24, 48, and 72 h leads. After switching from unavailable 0.5° archives to native 0.25° GFS operational forecasts and updating the 2 m specific humidity diagnostic to v2.2 to remove a low-level moist bias, all eight forcing groups (66 WPS intermediate files) passed independent verification. Formal WRF integrations are now underway starting with the 6 h gate pair, with final evaluation pending the paired convective-object and gust tables.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-14**: Sub-project launched under Liang Hu's brief to test whether global AI forecasts driving WRF can reproduce thunderstorm downbursts and serve as a benchmark for convective-scale AI nowcasting.
- **2026-10-14**: The WRF Lead agreed to run the 2020-06-09 Akron, Colorado downburst (out-of-sample for Pangu) on a published 4 km single-domain setup (748×600×80 grid, 20 s step, Thompson microphysics, MYJ PBL, RRTMG longwave, no cumulus scheme), with 2018-08-10 Wister, Oklahoma (25.9 m/s peak) as an optional test.
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead froze the v1 protocol across 8 runs (Pangu vs. GFS at 6, 24, 48, and 72 h leads, 348 model hours) sharing GFS analysis initial conditions and static/soil fields; the primary metric was set to ≥40 dBZ convective object position and arrival time within 50 km of Akron ("not worse than GFS" defined as position error within GFS + 50 km and timing error within GFS + 1 h in at least 2 of the 24/48/72 h leads, gated by a 6 h run within 150 km).
- **2026-10-14**: A literature survey found 13-level Pangu lateral boundaries matched 33-level GFS for extreme rainfall while 13-level truncated GFS degraded (Deng et al. 2025), and GraphCast-driven WRF matched GFS/ECMWF for downslope windstorms (Brewer et al. 2025), with no prior studies on mid-latitude downbursts.
- **2026-10-14**: Protocol v2 retained full GFS vertical levels as the baseline and adopted six WRF Lead adjustments (14 metgrid levels for Pangu, shared 2 m humidity formula, no surface pressure input, WRF v4.0.3, 10 min 2D output, and 06:10 UTC peak time label).
- **2026-10-14**: Research assistant pre-checks found 2020 NCEI 0.5° GFS multi-lead archives returned HTTP 404, halting generation at 0 compute units rather than substituting resolution without approval.
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead issued v2.1, switching both groups to native 0.25° GFS operational forecasts from NCAR and eliminating horizontal interpolation for Pangu initialization.
- **2026-10-14**: The research assistant generated all 8 mandatory forcing groups (66 WPS intermediate files, 1.71 GB; 31 pressure levels for GFS and 13 for Pangu) and passed checksum verification.
- **2026-10-15**: WRF line preprocessing on the 6 h pair showed v2.1 2 m specific humidity was +0.38 to +0.91 g/kg moister on average (up to 9.3 g/kg maximum difference) than the lowest complete pressure level above terrain within 300 km of KAKO; observations were updated to NEXRAD Level-II composite reflectivity and KAKO METAR/SPECI reports (37.04 m/s gust in Childs 2021).
- **2026-10-15**: The research assistant generated v2.2 forcing files (66 files), setting 2 m specific humidity to the lowest complete pressure level above terrain without interpolation (reducing mean 2 m specific humidity around KAKO by 0.37 to 0.91 g/kg, max 9.28 g/kg, byte-identical to v2.1 elsewhere).
- **2026-10-15**: The WRF Lead verified all 66 v2.2 files, resolved a boundary vertical-interpolation NaN in `real.exe` by enabling `all_ic_times=true` (bit-for-bit neutral on boundary forcing), and launched the 6 h gate pair followed by parallel 24, 48, and 72 h integrations.

## Where it stands

This sub-project is Exploring. All 8 groups of v2.2 forcing files (66 files) have been verified and handed over to the WRF line, where the 6 h gate runs and 24/48/72 h integrations are underway. Once the WRF line returns the paired convective-object and station gust tables, the AI Weather Models Lead will evaluate them against the frozen v2.2 criteria to determine whether Pangu-driven WRF performs no worse than GFS-driven WRF.

AI 气候模拟器/合成天气 → 非对流极端风设计风速；气候变化下设计风速（G）作第二阶段。台风设计风速（B2）归 B。

items.title: R23.5a Non-convective extreme-wind design speeds: AI climate emulators

projects.digest:
# Climate and Design Wind Speed (Exploring)

This sub-project evaluates whether an autoregressive AI climate emulator trained on ERA5 reanalysis (ACE2-ERA5) can generate multi-decade synthetic wind records to estimate non-convective extreme design wind speeds (sub-project C) and future design wind speeds under climate change (sub-project G, gated on C passing grid-level validation). Following a 30-year single-member pilot and a three-reviewer literature audit, the team ran a 10-member ensemble across 14 out-of-sample holdout cold seasons (1996/97–2009/10) on Colab A100 GPUs (~94 compute units). Across the 8 initial Midwest, Northeast, and Texas grid points, median GEV 50-year wind speed bias against native 1° ERA5 was -2.6\% (with 6 of 8 grid points within pm 10\%), but the primary pooled-interval coverage test was ruled inconclusive and auxiliary diagnostics revealed severe non-convective tail compression (-23\% to -29\%) at two Great Plains grid points. A newly pre-registered 10-member ensemble on 8 unseen grid points (~75–90 compute units) is now running to deliver a definitive grid-level verdict.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead launched the parent node overseeing sub-project C (non-convective extreme wind design speeds) and holding sub-project G (climate change design wind speeds) until C passes grid-level validation; exploratory thresholds defined pm 10\% versus ERA5 50-year return speeds as credible and >20\% underestimation as systematic tail compression.
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead enforced the five-layer delegation hierarchy (keeping C flat and staging G as a sibling second-level sub-project) and coordinated with the Events team to share read-only Dallas–Fort Worth and Austin ASOS gust lists.
- **2026-10-14**: The research assistant completed a 30-year single-member ACE2-ERA5 pilot (1979–2009, 1° resolution, 6-hourly 10 m wind, ~2.6 min/simulated year, ~8.5 Colab CU): across 6 Midwest and Northeast grid points, Gumbel 50-year return wind speeds differed from 1.5° interpolated ERA5 by -14\% to +18\% (median -2\%, Detroit -14\%, Albany +18\%), with no grid point underestimating by >20\%.
- **2026-10-14**: Three reviewers audited the literature and novelty claims, narrowing the gap to testing an ERA5-trained AI climate emulator for 100–1,000-year near-surface non-convective wind return levels and revising the primary criterion to whether ERA5 statistics fall inside the multi-member ensemble 90% interval.
- **2026-10-14**: Supplemental 30-year checks near Dallas–Fort Worth and Austin yielded 50-year return values +8\% and +14\% above ERA5, while cold-season-only (October–April) recalculation across all 8 pilot grid points gave a median GEV/POT 50-year bias of -3.8\% (all within pm 20\%); stochastic ACE2 was also checked but used different training data.
- **2026-10-14**: Under Liang Hu's updated Colab policy (report before exceeding 100 CU), AI Weather Models Lead authorized running all 10 ensemble members continuously from 1979 initial conditions through April 2010 (covering 14 holdout cold seasons, 1996/97–2009/10) after member 1 completed 1979–2022 (~13.6 CU).
- **2026-10-15**: All 10 ACE2-ERA5 members completed on Colab A100 (~94 CU total): across the 8 grid points over 14 holdout cold seasons, the 10-member median GEV 50-year bias against native 1° ERA5 was -2.6\% (6 of 8 grid points within pm 10\%), but Des Moines (KDSM) and Omaha (KOMA) underestimated by -29\% and -23\%, while Albany (KALB) overestimated by +23\% in the training period.
- **2026-10-15**: On the primary pre-registered test (native ERA5 inside the pooled member×year bootstrap 90% interval), holdout coverage was 2/8 for seasonal-maximum median, 3/8 for p90, 5/8 for GEV 50-year, and 2/8 for POT 50-year; because the pass count threshold was never pre-specified and the pooled interval omitted single-14-season ERA5 sampling variance, AI Weather Models Lead ruled the primary test inconclusive.
- **2026-10-15**: A zero-compute diagnostic showed that at KDSM (ERA5 GEV 50-year 19.0 m/s vs. 10-member range 12.6–14.1 m/s) and KOMA (17.5 vs. 12.1–15.1 m/s), ERA5 exceeded all 10 members on GEV 50-year, POT 50-year, and seasonal-maximum p90, and none of the top five holdout cold-season peaks were convective (the strongest peak on 1998-11-10 was a documented synoptic winter cyclone).
- **2026-10-15**: Classifying KDSM and KOMA as "emulator tail compression (auxiliary evidence)", AI Weather Models Lead approved a newly pre-registered 10-member run (~75–90 CU) on 8 unseen grid points (Sioux Falls and Fargo to Hartford) using an exact rank test of ERA5 among the 11 values (pass if le 2/8 fall outside the 10-member range; tail compression if ge 3/8 exceed all 10 members).

## Where it stands

This sub-project is Exploring. The initial 8-grid-point 10-member ensemble (~94 CU) was ruled inconclusive on its primary pooled-interval test while providing auxiliary evidence of non-convective tail compression (-23\% to -29\%) at two Great Plains grid points. A newly pre-registered 10-member ensemble on 8 unseen grid points (~75–90 CU) is currently running on Colab to deliver a clean rank-based verdict before any station-level downscaling, and sub-project G remains on hold.

projects.report:
# Non-convective extreme wind design wind speeds: AI climate emulators

## Objective
Use AI climate emulators to generate hundreds to thousands of synthetic years, extract station (or grid-point) annual maximum winds, and estimate long-return-period design wind speeds for non-thunderstorm (extratropical cyclone, cold front) extreme winds, filling the synoptic-scale component of the mixed-climate framework in the EVA track. Step 1 only answers: whether the emulator's annual maximum wind distribution is systematically biased low, and whether statistical downscaling can rescue it. G (design wind speeds under climate change) is Stage 2; once C passes, start with "cold-era training, warm-era validation".

## Validation Protocol (Pre-specified 10-14, Revised After Review)
The event population is unified as "non-convective, non-tropical-cyclone": at the grid level, take cold-season (October–March) maximum winds at grid points unaffected by tropical cyclones; at the station level, exclude thunderstorms and tropical cyclones.
1. **Consistency screening (matched grid specification)**: deterministic ACE2-ERA5 multi-member ensemble (forced over the same period as ERA5, ≥10 members recommended) vs. ERA5 on the identical grid and sampling interval. Criterion: ERA5 seasonal maximum median, 90th percentile, and 50-year return level fall within the emulator ensemble bootstrap 90% interval; relative bias within ±10% serves as an auxiliary reference, and bias lower or higher by >20% is recorded as systematic bias (direction not assumed a priori). Report both GEV and high-threshold POT. A 30-year run serves only as a trial run. Stochastic/generative comparisons use only ERA5-trained models (stochastic NeuralGCM, ArchesWeatherGen); ACE2S/HiRO-ACEv2 are trained on SHiELD/X-SHiELD and are not compared against ERA5.
2. **Station consistency check (not claimed as validating 3 s design gusts)**: ERA5 → station non-convective, non-tropical-cyclone gusts with held-out years for cross-validation; the 8-year Texas event list is insufficient, so longer ASOS series will be retrieved from IEM; explicitly state how quantile mapping handles values exceeding the observed maximum, and label the far tail as "unvalidated".
3. Proceed to Step 2 and trial design-value calculations only if Step 1 passes; if Step 1 fails and neither switching models nor downscaling can rescue it, shelve C and G.
4. Scale-up: once passed, run in batch across "station list × synthetic years" and deliver outputs to the EVA track.
Numerical criterion thresholds are assumptions of this track (no literature basis).

## Primary Criterion Determination (10-15, per parent Lead requirement; no existing result files modified)
1. **Pre-registered threshold: unspecified.** The revised protocol (Item 1 under "Verification Protocol" on this page) only stated that "the ERA5 seasonal maximum median, p90, and 50-year return values fall within the ensemble bootstrap 90% interval," without specifying how many grid points or metrics must fall inside to pass. No threshold is retrofitted post hoc.
2. **Why the interval is narrow.** The interval uses a two-level "member × forcing year" bootstrap estimating the uncertainty of the pooled 10-member × 14-season sample statistic, whereas ERA5 is a single 14-season realization. Because all 10 members share the same forcing and differ only in initial conditions, the pooled interval is naturally narrow and excludes the sampling variability of a single 14-season record itself. Under the current implementation, the primary criterion is therefore overly strict toward ERA5 and cannot be judged as failed solely on coverage counts. An apples-to-apples comparison with ERA5 is the distribution of statistics computed individually from each member's own 14-season record (the single-member range being computed by wx)—**this interval construction was modified after inspecting the results, constituting a post-hoc adjustment rather than a pre-registered rule**, and cannot serve as grounds for passing the pre-registered criterion.
3. **Determination: inconclusive.** Under the pre-registered criterion itself (unspecified threshold and interval construction mismatched to a single ERA5 realization), it is judged neither passed nor failed. Grid-by-grid coverage (held-out 14 seasons, ensemble 90% interval):

GEV50 at the remaining six grid points falls within the member range; other out-of-range cases: KALB POT50 and p90 (ERA5 below all members), DFW p90 and AUS POT50 (above all members). Training-period GEV50 at KDSM and KOMA falls within the member range.
 - Strong-season synoptic type: The strongest held-out season at both KDSM and KOMA is 1998-11-10 (documented by NOAA/NWS as a severe winter storm with record-low pressure, verified by Lead against the NWS Sioux Falls page); the second strongest at KDSM is the 2009-12-09 blizzard (NWS Des Moines); 2008-10-26 is post-cold-front high wind; KOMA 2009-03-23 had a squall line that day but occurring after the peak hour, remaining undetermined; 2000-12-16 and 2010-01-25 lack collocated convective evidence. None of the top five strongest seasons show confirmable convection.
 - Interpretation: Each member's own 14-season estimate inherently carries the sampling variability of a 14-season record, making "ERA5 exceeding all 10 members" a better-matched comparison than the pooled ensemble interval; a single metric corresponds to a one-sided probability of ~1/11, though the two grid points are adjacent, share the same extreme event, and have highly correlated metrics that cannot be treated as independent trials. Under the auxiliary rule (still exceeding all 10 members after excluding convection → emulator tail suppression), the two plains grid points are judged as "emulator tail suppression, auxiliary-evidence level"; the pre-registered determination remains "inconclusive".
4. **Condition for advancing to the station stage**: No pass determination will be made on already-inspected data. Advancing requires writing the revised criterion (using the single-member distribution as reference and convective exclusion rules) and passing threshold (number of grid points and metrics) into a new pre-registration first, then testing on unseen data—such as the 2020/21–2021/22 held-out seasons (already covered by m01) or another set of unseen grid points.

Limitations: it is an event list rather than annual maxima; gust averaging duration varies by sensor (Belfort 5 s / Vaisala 3 s) with no replacement history; QC can erroneously delete peaks (H7ZG33PU p.9); covers only 8 years. → For the station conversion step: use EVA data for DFW/AUS, and have ideas retrieve public ASOS data from IEM for central/northeastern stations; attach conversion errors when delivering results back to EVA, and self-check using their v2.7 checker.
- Literature step 2 Deep Research → write the second task brief after Grok quick check returns

## Literature Basis
- Paciorek & Cooley 2026 BAMS 107(5), DOI 10.1175/BAMS-D-25-0178.1 (abstract): ACE2 10,000-year ensemble for extreme precipitation/temperature; authors call for testing whether emulators are fit for purpose
- T.-C. Chen, Collet, Di Luca 2024 IJOC 44(3):729–747, DOI 10.1002/joc.8339 (abstract): ERA5 North American extratropical cyclone 10 m wind top 5% NMB −10.2%
- Dacre et al. 2026 BAMS 107(1), DOI 10.1175/BAMS-D-25-0129.1 (abstract): 7 ML weather models underestimate cyclone minimum pressure by >5 hPa (at 10 days) and produce weaker peak 10 m winds, whereas IFS has no bias
- ACE2: Watt-Meyer et al. arXiv 2411.11268 (HTML full text Methods, §2.2.3, §2.2.6): 10 m horizontal wind is a prognostic variable; TC maximum 10 m wind is accurately simulated relative to ERA5; individual responses to SST/CO2 are not fully realistic (abstract)
- HiRO-ACEv2: Kwa et al. arXiv 2610.17693 abstract: near-surface wind distribution matches up to the 99.9999th percentile in the X-SHiELD model world (lead)
- : ArchesWeather/Gen 45-year AMIP-style run; deterministic models regress toward the mean while generative models may preserve tails (preprint + WeChat post, full text unread)
- : NeuralGCM (Nature 2024, DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07744-y) abstract states it cannot extrapolate to substantially different future climates
- EVA cards: mixed-climate EVA, thunderstorm/non-thunderstorm separation, 18 m/s threshold (PDF pp. 2–3, 5); `KGS2TG8X` (climate change and extreme storms, designload_step5)

## Liang Hu Notes
- 10-14: Approved C; validate extremes first on Colab; Colab balance is ample at this stage, so CU is unlimited (supercomputers still follow existing rules). [Lead note (10-14 correction): per Liang Hu's exact words, Colab has no single-experiment cap; if a single experiment is expected to exceed 100 CU, pause and report to the parent project first; must run colab stop when finished; dispatch only one executor per round. The previous '≤20 CU' limit is voided]
- 10-14: G serves as Stage 2 of C; "This research can be done, though its scientific value is moderate—it is fine for publishing a paper. Currently there is no evidence proving that climate change will lead to an increase in design wind speeds."
- 10-14 Overall guideline: the ultimate goal is at-scale forecasting and hindcasting.
projects.brief:
# Brief: AI Climate Emulator Availability + Grid-Point Annual Maximum Wind Initial Check (2026-10-14)

## Objective
Determine whether any AI climate emulator can run stably and continuously for multiple decades on a Colab A100 while outputting near-surface (10 m or lowest model level) wind, and perform an initial check on whether its annual maximum wind speeds are systematically lower than ERA5. This is Step 1 of the "Non-Convective Extreme Wind Design Wind Speed" sub-project, aimed at quickly deciding whether the direction is worth pursuing.

## Deliverables
1. Candidate emulator table — model name, paper/DOI, code repository and license, public availability and license of weights, spatial resolution and time step, forcing mode (AMIP SST/sea-ice, etc.), whether output variables include 10 m wind (or lowest model-level wind), whether it runs on Colab A100, and GPU wall time per simulated year. Check at minimum: ACE2 (Ai2, ACE2-ERA5), NeuralGCM (including stochastic version), ArchesWeatherGen, DLESyM, and NVIDIA cBottle, plus any other candidates you find. Provide source links for every entry; write "not found" if unavailable, with no guessing allowed.
2. Select the most suitable candidate (prioritizing: 10 m wind output, generative/stochastic formulation, and long-rollout stability) and actually run it: start with a short run to confirm stability, then run as long as practical (target ≥30 simulated years under post-1979 historical forcing for contemporaneous comparison against ERA5; if official pre-computed long rollouts are publicly downloadable, using them directly with provenance documented is also acceptable). Record cold-start time, wall time per simulated year, and CU consumed.
3. Initial grid-point check + one figure: select 6–10 grid cells across the central and northeastern US (avoiding hurricane-dominated Gulf and southeastern coastal regions; label each grid cell with the nearest ASOS station code for downstream use), and compare the annual maximum wind distributions between the emulator and ERA5 (resampled to the emulator grid at identical sampling intervals): median, 90th percentile, and 50-year return level from GEV or Gumbel fits, reporting relative biases. Pre-specified criterion (working hypothesis of this line): relative bias within ±10% counts as "credible grid-point extremes", whereas underprediction exceeding 20% is recorded as "systematic low bias". Also plot a mean wind-speed distribution comparison to distinguish "overall weak winds" from "tail-only weakness".
4. Place all runner scripts, logs, and provenance records in the same directory; do not store large raw datasets on the workstation.

## Boundaries
- Run strictly on Colab; CU is uncapped at this stage, but every session must end with `colab stop` and the final report must attach `colab ls`. Do not use the cluster.
- Access ERA5 via public channels (e.g., WeatherBench2 / ARCO-ERA5 cloud storage) and document the exact path and version; do not download data of unknown provenance.
- Station downscaling is not required at this step (that belongs to the next step). No need to report back before running; report the findings honestly whether the hypothesis holds or fails.
- Look up parameters omitted from papers (in the paper, repo, or config files) before making assumptions, and explicitly label any assumptions as "assumed".
- Add newly used models, datasets, and code to the citations registry, and note data sources in figure footnotes.

## Return Format
One-sentence conclusion (which model runs, how much its grid-point annual maximum wind deviates from ERA5, and whether the bias is "overall weak" or "tail-only weak") + deliverable summary + CU consumed.

items.text:
# AI Climate Emulators for Non-Convective Extreme Winds: Kick-Off and Verification Protocol (2026-10-14)

Decision I made:
1. Verification is split into two stages: first compare annual maximum 10 m winds between the emulator and ERA5 on grid points under the same specifications (criteria ±10%, underestimation >20% recorded as systematically low), then separately evaluate the scale conversion error from ERA5 to station non-thunderstorm 3 s gusts. Why: A single-step direct comparison against stations would conflate both model smoothing and scale conversion errors, making it impossible to determine which stage to fix. Cost of being wrong: One additional grid-point comparison step, about half a day.
2. Threshold values are assumptions of this track (no literature basis, based on experimental needs), noted accordingly in conclusions.
3. Three tasks in parallel: ideas verifies emulator availability and cost, ask the EVA track if off-the-shelf non-thunderstorm annual maximum winds exist,  quick check with Grok. Why: Mutually independent.
Basis:  (regression to the mean in deterministic models);  (NeuralGCM abstract); 68TKWTZ3 PDF pp. 2–3, 5 (approaches for separating thunderstorm/non-thunderstorm).

# Grok Quick Check Verification: Extreme Winds in AI Climate Emulators (Report 20261014_1423_..._14f267)

| Claim | Verification | Handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ACE2-ERA5: 1°, 8 levels, 6 h, Apache-2.0, weights on HF, 10 m wind is a prognostic variable | arXiv 2411.11268 v1 HTML: Methods states 2D prognostic variables include "10-meter horizontal winds"; §2.2.6 evaluates v10m RMSE; HF page Apache-2.0, pip install fme for inference | Adopt |
| ACE2 accurately simulates TC maximum 10 m winds | §2.2.3 original text: TC intensity uses maximum 10 m winds, "accurately emulated by ACE2-ERA5" (relative to ERA5; ERA5 itself is on the weaker side) | Adopt, qualified as "relative to ERA5" |
| ACE2 has evaluations for extratropical cyclone / non-TC 10 m wind extremes | No dedicated evaluation found in original text | Gap, precisely what this project aims to evaluate |
| ACE2's response to isolated changes in SST and CO2 is "not completely realistic" | Confirmed by abstract | Adopt (Phase G risk) |
| HiRO-ACEv2 near-surface wind tail reaches 99.9999th percentile | arXiv 2610.17693 (Kwa et al., submitted 2026-10-13) abstract confirmed; target is an emulator for the X-SHiELD 3 km storm-resolving model, not ERA5/stations | Lead, only indicates that "generative downscaling can preserve the tail" holds in the model world |
| ML weather models systematically underestimate extratropical cyclone intensity and peak 10 m winds by 1–3 m/s (BAMS 2026) | Journal page 403, unchecked | Lead, key check for DR Step 2 |
| Priestley 2022: HighResMIP underestimates ETC winds, improved by higher resolution | DOI exists, main text 403 unchecked | Lead |
| Repositories, licenses, and resolutions of NeuralGCM, ArchesWeatherGen, DLESyM (outputs ws10m), and cBottle | Not checked item-by-item; handed over to ideas' inventory.md for actual verification | Pending ideas |
| Direct precedent for estimating design wind speeds using AI emulators | Report states none found | Temporarily recorded as "none found", recheck in DR Step 2 |

Conclusion: Directionally supports "ACE2-ERA5 is the primary candidate" (native 10 m wind, 6 h, stable over long durations); non-TC wind extremes have not been evaluated by anyone; the claim that deterministic models underestimate extratropical cyclone winds remains to be verified.

items.text:
# Deep Research Verification and Preliminary Assessment: Non-Thunderstorm Extreme Winds in AI Climate Emulators (2026-10-14)
Report: ; for Grok quick check verification, see .

## Item-by-Item Verification
| # | DR Claim | My Verification | Handling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Dacre et al. 2026 BAMS (10.1175/BAMS-D-25-0129.1): 7 ML weather models underestimate cyclone minimum central pressure by >5 hPa at 10-day lead time; FengWu/Aurora/FuXi by ~10 hPa; peak 10 m wind is weaker by 1 m/s starting at 6 h, and 2–3 m/s later; IFS has no such bias | Crossref abstract confirms: >1000 cyclones, 7 MLWPs, >5 hPa (10 days), peak 10 m wind weaker across all MLWPs, no IFS bias. "10 hPa" and "1–3 m/s" are DR's secondhand paraphrasing, not found in abstract | Adopt qualitative conclusions and >5 hPa; flag 1–3 m/s as "unverified". Note: this is weather forecasting (initialized runs ≤10 days), not long rollouts of climate emulators |
| 2 | Paciorek & Cooley 2026 BAMS (10.1175/BAMS-D-25-0178.1): ACE2 generated a 10,560-year ensemble to estimate 1/1,000- and 1/100,000-year precipitation and temperature extremes; does not include wind | Crossref abstract confirms: ACE2, 10,560 years, precipitation and temperature, peaks-over-threshold, emulator produces extremes outside ERA5 training range, authors call for further research on "applicability" | Adopt. Most direct methodological precedent for this project; wind has not yet been done by anyone (gap) |
| 3 | Chen 2023: ERA5 mean NMB for North American extratropical cyclone 10 m wind is −0.7%, and −10.2% for the most extreme 5% of cyclones | Crossref confirms: **Authors are Ting-Chen Chen, Collet, Di Luca**, Int J Climatol 2024, 44(3):729–747, DOI 10.1002/joc.8339; ~3000 stations, 2005–2019, NMB −10.2% for most extreme 5% winds. DR wrote authors as "Chen, Z." (confused with #4) | Adopt, correct authors and year |
| 4 | Chen Z et al. 2026 AGU Adv (10.1029/2025AV002075): NeuralGCM extratropical cyclone composite field comparable to ESM; overestimates cyclone extent; +3/+4 K unreliable | DOI exists (Grok/DR citation list); content is abstract + secondhand | Lead; read original text when needed in Phase G |
| 5 | Priestley 2022 GRL: CMIP6 underestimates 850 hPa system-relative circulation by ≤2 m/s, concentrated on the cold conveyor belt side, improved with higher resolution | DOI exists; DR self-labels as "secondhand"; main text 403 unread | Lead |
| 6 | ERA5 10 m wind is diagnosed based on z0=0.03 m open terrain | No such statement found in ERA5 data documentation | **Do not adopt** (unverified); ideas to check IFS documentation during station conversion |
| 7 | Maddison et al. 2026 NHESS: GloSea6 ~700-year winter hindcast UNSEEN, annual probability of unprecedented storm impact in Europe is 0.5–1.6% | Crossref search returned no hits | Lead, unverified |
| 8 | ArchesWeatherGen's DOI 10.5194/egusphere-2026-3782 | Not found; official version is Science Advances 10.1126/sciadv.adx2372 (verified to exist) | Discard this DOI |
| 9 | "Generative models must be used; the tail of deterministic models cannot be fixed" | No direct evidence: #1 is weather forecast bias; wind extremes in long rollouts of ACE2 have not been evaluated by anyone;  only provides mechanistic hints | **Do not adopt as conclusion**, change to a hypothesis to be tested in this project (comparison of deterministic ACE2 vs. stochastic ACE2S/generative) |
| 10 | HiRO-ACEv2 near-surface wind reaches 99.9999th percentile, weights on HF | arXiv 2610.17693 abstract confirms (target is X-SHiELD 3 km model world); HF weights unverified | Lead; hand over to ideas to verify availability |

## Relationship to This Project
- Literature gap confirmed: No one has evaluated the annual maximum / tail of **non-tropical cyclone** near-surface winds in AI climate emulators (long rollout), nor has anyone used it to estimate design wind speeds. Paciorek 2026 has already demonstrated the pipeline of "ACE2 10,000-year ensemble + extreme value statistics" for precipitation/temperature; extending it to wind is this project's incremental contribution (publishable value).
- Risks exist on two levels and in the same direction: (a) ML models weaken cyclones (Dacre 2026, in a forecasting context); (b) the target it learns from, ERA5 itself, is already ~10% too low for the strongest 5% of extratropical cyclone winds (T.-C. Chen 2024). Therefore, stage one of this project (emulator vs. ERA5) can only test (a), and (b) must be accounted for in stage two during station conversion.
- Phase G: ACE2's response to isolated SST/CO2 changes is acknowledged by authors as "not completely realistic" (abstract); NeuralGCM abstract states it cannot extrapolate to significantly different climates. Phase G considers only near-term scenarios within +1–2 K (lead level, pending original text).

## Preliminary Assessment (Pending Review)
- C is worth continuing: Precedent chain (Paciorek 2026) + clear gap + open model (ACE2-ERA5 native 10 m wind, Apache-2.0).
- Step one verification protocol remains unchanged, but with one addition: run deterministic ACE2 and stochastic version (ACE2S, if available) concurrently to observe tail differences.
- If Paciorek's 10,560-year ACE2 ensemble has public outputs that include 10 m wind, use them directly to save running them ourselves.
- Biases in both stages already have magnitudes from literature (weak peak winds in forecasts, ERA5 strongest 5% biased by −10%), so the criterion "underestimation >20% recorded as systematically low" remains unchanged.

# AI Climate Emulators for Non-Convective Extreme Winds: Post-Review Protocol Revision (2026-10-14)
Decision I made: Revised verification protocol per review —event population unified as non-convective, non-tropical cyclone (cold season, non-tropical cyclone grid points); criteria changed from point estimate ±10% to "ERA5 statistics fall within the multi-member ensemble bootstrap 90% interval" (±10%/20% as auxiliary, bias direction non-a priori); 30 years demoted to pilot run; stochastic version uses only ERA5-trained models as control; station stage demoted to consistency check, not termed validation of design gusts.
Why: D's Monte Carlo shows that at 30 years, sampling noise alone gives ~18% probability of the 50-year return value exceeding ±10%, which would cause false rejection; all three reviewers pointed out population inconsistency and insufficient station data.
Cost of being wrong: Run a few more members (Colab, sufficient CUs), slower by about half a day.
Basis: Verdict document ; Paciorek & Cooley 2026 BAMS (arXiv 2510.08893, annual maximum GEV is biased, POT recommended); IFS Cy41r2 Part IV §3.10.2.

items.title: Verdict: literature review on non-thunderstorm extreme winds in AI climate emulators (2026-10-14)
items.text:
# Verdict: Literature Review on Non-Thunderstorm Extreme Winds in AI Climate Emulators  (2026-10-14)
Reviewers E (Gemini), A (GPT-6), D (GLM), 3/3 valid, all "supported with reservations". I personally verified: Paciorek repository README (outputs only TMP2m, PRATEsfc; checkpoint ace2_era5; 12×22×40 cyclic forcing), Singh et al. arXiv 2605.29976 §4.6 (850 hPa wind return periods, ArchesWeatherGen closer to ERA5; authors state "return periods are only a proxy for extremes"), Bellinghausen et al. egusphere-2026-523 page (winter storm index of ACE2-driven 10 m wind exceeding ERA5 95th percentile days; authors have withdrawn the manuscript and will not resubmit).

## Must Change (Already Changed)
1. **Narrow literature gap** (E4, A1, D1). Existing work: Singh 2026 (45 years × 5 members 850 hPa wind return periods, generative outperforms deterministic); Kwa 2026 (HiRO-ACEv2, 10-year rollout 10 m wind high percentiles and Bora downslope winds, model world); Bellinghausen 2026 (ACE2 winter 10 m wind threshold exceedance days, withdrawn preprint); LUCIE (arXiv 2405.16297, ERA5-trained, 100 years × 100 members, most variables **overestimate** extreme frequencies, whether wind is near-surface to be verified). New phrasing: **No record found** of anyone using ERA5-trained AI climate emulators for centennial-to-millennial near-surface 10 m non-thunderstorm / extratropical cyclone wind annual maxima or POT return periods, connected to station 3 s gust design wind speeds (search boundary: two DRs + independent searches by three reviewers, non-exhaustive). Tail bias direction is non-a priori (weaker in Dacre forecasts, higher in LUCIE long rollouts).
2. **ERA5 10 m wind roughness** (E2, A2, D2): Adopt conditional formulation—IFS Cy41r2 Part IV §3.10.2 Eqs. 3.91–3.92: diagnosed as 0.03 m open terrain when model roughness >0.03 m, otherwise use model value. Engineering implication: identical specifications to ASOS airports and ASCE 7 Exposure C, **not** a "structural error" as claimed by DR; discrepancy between ERA5 and station gusts arises from spatial and temporal averaging.
3. **Paciorek 2026** (E1, A-NOTE): Output does not contain wind, close "check whether it contains wind"; it is a continuous integration with cyclic forcing using deterministic ACE2-ERA5, not "stochastic replicates"; it produced extremes beyond the ERA5 training range, found annual maximum GEV is biased, and recommended high-threshold POT. Serves only as a statistical workflow precedent.
4. **ArchesWeather DOI** (E3): 10.5194/egusphere-2026-3782 corresponds to multi-decadal paper by Singh et al. (arXiv 2605.29976, authors Singh, Brunstein...Couairon), restored; "deterministic tail is weaker" changed from "mechanistic hint only" to "direct empirical evidence for 850 hPa daily-scale winds, 10 m unmeasured".
5. **Bias statistics specifications** (A3): T.-C. Chen 2024's −10.2% is based on the strongest 5% of time steps selected by observed cyclone **regional mean wind**, limited to east-central North America, not station annual maxima or 50-year values; Dacre is "minimum pressure is high (shallower cyclones)". Neither endorses the 20% criterion; 20% remains this track's assumption.
6. **Stochastic version reference baseline** (E5): The only public ERA5-trained ACE2 is deterministic ACE2-ERA5; ACE2S in ACE2S-SHiELD-plus and HiRO-ACEv2 is trained on SHiELD/X-SHiELD and can only be compared against corresponding model data, not against ERA5 at ±10%. To make an ERA5-trained stochastic/generative comparison, use the NeuralGCM stochastic version or ArchesWeatherGen.
7. **Protocol statistics and population** (A4, A5, D3, E6):
 - Population unification: Grid-point side uses cold season (Oct–Mar) annual (seasonal) maxima excluding grid points/time steps affected by tropical cyclones; station side simultaneously excludes thunderstorms and tropical cyclones; uniformly termed "non-convective, non-tropical cyclone".
 - Sample: 30 simulated years serves only as a pilot run. Formal comparisons use a multi-member ensemble with synchronous ERA5 forcing (1940/1979–2024); criterion changed to "ERA5 annual maximum quantiles and 50-year value fall within the emulator ensemble bootstrap 90% interval", with median/90th percentile ±10% as auxiliary; report both GEV annual maximum and high-threshold POT.
 - Station stage demoted to "consistency check", not termed "validation of 3 s design gusts": Texas 8-year event inventory is insufficient, obtain longer ASOS sequences from IEM separately; behavior of quantile mapping beyond observed maximum must be explicitly documented, far-tail transfer labeled "unvalidated".
8. **Project page wording**: Remove direct deduction "credible grid extremes → design wind speeds can be estimated", change to tiered approach: consistency screening passed → proceed to station conversion and trial calculation of design values.

## For Reference Only
- Maddison 2026 NHESS 26:827–844 (title provided by A): 0.5–1.6% is the proportion of "unprecedented" storm events affecting a country, not annual exceedance probability; precedent for large physical model ensembles.
- D: Paper on ACE extremes by Sun/Hassanzadeh et al. 2025, have ideas investigate in passing.
- Paciorek has full arXiv text 2510.08893.

## Unadopted Objections
- E claims Paciorek's use of "deterministic" ACE2 is confirmed by original text: README gives only checkpoint filename ace2_era5_ckpt.tar, without writing "deterministic"; because public ERA5-trained ACE2 only has a deterministic version, the judgment holds with high probability, but is recorded as "inference".
- E claims "static QM cannot rescue thousand-year design wind speed": accepted as a risk, not as a proven conclusion (untested).

## Conclusion
C continues, status Exploring. No matters require Liang Hu's decision.

items.text:
# Initial Check of 30-Year 10 m Grid Wind Speeds for ACE2-ERA5 (10-14)

Conclusion: An actual run of ACE2-ERA5 on Colab A100 was stepped forward continuously from initialization on 1979-01-01 to 2009-01-01 00:00, totaling 43,832 6 h steps (the last step is not included in the 1979–2008 comparison), exit code 0. For six grid points avoiding lake surfaces/coasts, the relative biases of the Gumbel 50-year values against ERA5 are +1.6%, −5.9%, −10.8%, −14.1%, +11.8%, +17.8%, with an across-point median of −2.1%; no grid point reached "underestimated by more than 20%". The across-point median relative bias of mean wind speed is +2.4% (point-by-point −6.5% to +7.4%), which cannot be generalized as an overall underestimation, nor as a widespread tail underestimation: KOMA/KDSM have non-weak mean winds but weakened tails; KDTW is weak in both mean and tail. Verdict: "conditionally worth continuing", not "grid extremes are credible / usable for design".

## Actual Run and Costs

- Model: Ai2 ACE2-ERA5 (Weyn et al. 2025, doi:10.1038/s41612-025-01090-0); public checkpoint [allenai/ACE2-ERA5](https://huggingface.co/allenai/ACE2-ERA5), repository revision `f25123c52d7faa8f3533816a311cf3353ee83daa`, code is PyPI `fmee3a92eb5f164059b077e96c5363a56d91ba8c61a`, no claim that the source code of this run equals this main commit. The model is not explicit step-by-step stochastic sampling; autoregressive meteorological perturbations can evolve naturally.
- Official 1° Gaussian × eight levels, 6 h; native UGRD10m/VGRD10m. Initialization, historical forcing – (official model repository; SST, sea ice, CO₂, solar radiation, etc.), configured in `historical_config.yamlforward_steps_in_memory=50` from the official default configuration, only changing writer variables to U/V.
- Colab A100 40GB, short run of 40 steps succeeded, total wall clock including load/writeout was 60.36 s; long run took 4,716.23 s = 78.60 min, i.e., 157.21 s/simulation year, approx. 2.62 min/simulation year. Started at 14:25:16, stopped at 16:00:43 EDT (original events were logged in UTC, converted to EDT in this report). Cold start: session was READY seconds after creation; genuine time from long-run log start to the first output window was ~24 s, short run total was 60.36 s; downloading/installing the model and 31 years of forcing took additional time and is not conflated with annual inference time.
- CU: The account had concurrent sessions, and balance changes cannot be attributed solely to this task. The observed A100 rate at the time was approx. 5.30–5.34 CU/h; the model long run converts to approx. 6.94–7.00 CU, and the entire 1.5907 h session for this task converts to approx. 8.43–8.49 CU (including installation, download, ERA5 point extraction, plotting); all are runtime × rate estimates, not an independent bill. After completion, `colab stop` was run on this task `lab-ace2-extreme-20261014`, and private `sessions` no longer contains this task's session; the account's public `sessions` still contains GPUs/CPUs belonging to other work, which were untouched.

## Concurrent ERA5 and Methodology

The ERA5 source is a historical version from the [Google WeatherBench2 Public Data Guide](https://weatherbench2.readthedocs.io/en/latest/data-guide.html); the raw ERA5 comes from ECMWF/C3S (Hersbach et al. 2020, doi:10.1002/qj.3803). The 1.5° version of WeatherBench2 was first area-conservatively resampled from the original grid; in this round, u10/v10 were each bilinearly interpolated to ACE2 grid points, interpolating components first before calculating scalar `sqrt(u²+v²)`. Results after 2001 do not equate to holdout testing: the ACE2 training set covers 1940–1995 and 2011–2019, and most of 1979–2008 compared herein is in the training period; 2001–2008 is part of its holdout test period, but the whole table cannot be called an independent 30-year validation. Matched by identical UTC 6 h timestamps, excluding the first initial timestamp 1979-01-01 00:00 and the extra 2009-01-01 00:00 stepped forward at the end; totaling 43,831 pairs of 6 h samples across 30 complete calendar years (the first year only lacks the first initial timestamp).

The annual maximum 6 h wind speed at each grid point was taken; the median and empirical 90th percentile were calculated for each of the 30 values; SciPy `gumbel_r.fit` maximum likelihood was performed independently on each dataset, taking `ppf(0.98)` as the exploratory 50-year return value. Relative bias is uniformly, positive numbers indicate overestimation. Default baseline preset: absolute bias ≤10% counts as "grid extremes are credible" (only as a numerical threshold, does not mean it has passed physical verification for actual design wind speed); below −20% counts as "systematically underestimated". Fitting 30 years and extrapolating to 50 years is unstable, with no bootstrap intervals yet; there is no weather typing / non-convective event separation, site wind speed or gusts, and no station downscaling. Bilinear interpolation of 1.5° ERA5 to the 1° model grid cannot recover the original 0.25° tail, which may underestimate reference extremes and cause ACE2's negative bias to be underestimated; subsequent sensitivity experiments of conservative regridding from original ERA5 0.25° to the ACE2 grid must be performed.

Grid points were anchored using public ASOS station locations, taking the nearest ACE2 model grid cell; in addition, the nearest ASOS across 16 queried states was calculated from [Iowa Environmental Mesonet State ASOS GeoJSON](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/geojson/network/IL_ASOS.geojson) (code uses IEM station IDs, without adding the K prefix manually). The nearest model grid points corresponding to KORD/KBUF were adjacent to or located over Great Lakes water surfaces; they were initially selected and subsequently removed, retaining six points. Station IDs merely indicate locations; station observations are not treated as ground truth.

| Original Anchor Station; Actual Nearest ASOS (Approx. Dist. km) | ACE2 Grid Latitude, West Longitude | Mean 6h Wind Bias | Annual Max Median Bias | Annual Max p90 Bias | Gumbel 50-Year Bias |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| KMSP; PNM (22.4) | 45.374, 93.5 | −1.4% | −1.0% | −1.0% | +1.6% |
| KDSM; DSM (20.9) | 41.385, 93.5 | +5.0% | −0.8% | −4.9% | −5.9% |
| KOMA; CBF (25.7) | 41.385, 95.5 | +3.1% | −2.5% | −5.5% | −10.8% |
| KDTW; YIP (16.2) | 42.382, 83.5 | −6.5% | −10.9% | −13.9% | −14.1% |
| KPIT; 2G2 (17.2) | 40.388, 80.5 | +1.8% | +4.2% | +8.4% | +11.8% |
| KALB; PSF (18.0) | 42.382, 73.5 | +7.4% | +10.2% | +16.5% | +17.8% |

Raw values (m/s and bias) see ; comparison plots of the three annual maximum metrics, and probability density and mean difference plots for 6 h wind speeds ; corner notes on both figures specify model and ERA5 sources. According to the aforementioned ±10% threshold, only 2 of the 6 grid points passed the Gumbel 50-year value, and 4 failed; no grid point was below −20%. One should not conflate "no systematic underestimation" with "sufficiently reliable": biases of eastern and western grid points have opposite signs, sample sizes are small, and topographic differences/resolution as well as non-convective filtering remain to be verified.

## Files and Reproducibility

- , : Actual run scripts ( points to v2 figures).
- , : Configurations, download manifests, logs, and exit receipts.
- , retained to adhere to not overwriting results; delivered using the layout-corrected .

One-sentence verdict: Worth continuing 0.25° ERA5 grid matching, non-convective filtering, and sensitivity checks for independent periods / multiple initializations; existing 6 grid points cannot confirm extreme value credibility, let alone be used for design wind speeds.

# Supplementary Check for ACE2-ERA5 on Two Texas Grid Points DFW/AUS (10-14)

Supplementary check conclusion: ACE2-ERA5 was rerun in a separate continuous 30-year Colab A100 rollout with identical official checkpoint / 1979 initial conditions / historical forcing, comparing 1979–2008 concurrent ERA5 at the nearest ACE2 grid points to the DFW and AUS stations. DFW's Gumbel 50-year return value bias is +8.15%, AUS is +14.01%; neither was underestimated by more than 20%. DFW 6 h mean wind is biased high at +5.75%, with its tail also biased high; AUS mean wind is biased low at −1.76%, yet its tail is biased high, so neither point supports "overall weak" or "tail weak". According to the preset numerical threshold, DFW is within ±10% while AUS is not; this is not design wind speed validation.

| Station Anchor; Nearest ASOS Beside Grid Point | ACE2 Grid Point (Latitude, West Longitude) | Anchor Station Dist. to Grid Point | Mean Wind Bias | Annual Max Median Bias | Annual Max p90 Bias | Gumbel 50-Year Bias |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DFW; CPT (nearest to grid point approx. 8.8 km) | 32.40983, 97.5 | 69.3 km | +5.75% | +1.32% | +11.64% | +8.15% |
| AUS; EDC (nearest to grid point approx. 6.5 km) | 30.41538, 97.5 | 31.1 km | −1.76% | +0.90% | +6.65% | +14.01% |

Station coordinates for DFW/AUS are from [Iowa Environmental Mesonet TX_ASOS GeoJSON](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/geojson/network/TX_ASOS.geojson): DFW (32.8968, −97.038), AUS (30.183, −97.6799). Grid coordinates were read directly from official ACE2 and verified point-by-point in the output wind fields. CPT and EDC are other stations near the grid points, not observation ground truth used in this round; the DFW model grid point is approx. 69 km from the DFW station location, and subsequent station conversion especially needs to account for representativeness error. HOU was not selected.

Methodology completely follows the first round `results.mdf25123c52d7faa8f3533816a311cf3353ee83daags://weatherbench2/datasets/era5/1959-2022-6h-240x121_equiangular_with_poles_conservative.zarrgumbel_r.fit` maximum likelihood 50-year quantiles; relative bias. Fitting 30 years and extrapolating to 50 years provides no confidence intervals; 1979–1995 lies within the model training period, and while 2001–2008 is part of the holdout period, the entire span is not an independent validation. First reducing ERA5 to 1.5° smooths extremes, does not distinguish non-convective/convective and tropical influences, and performs no station or gust conversions.

The exit code of this separate 30-year rerun was 0, wall clock 4,742.53 s (approx. 2.64 min/simulation year). This session ran approx. 16:03–17:29 EDT; GPU billing converted at approx. 5.38 CU/h yielded approx. 7.09 CU for the model and approx. 7.71 CU for the entire session (estimate; concurrent account balances are affected by other sessions and cannot be taken as an independent bill). Final download checks include time series for the two grid points, two tables, and two figures; this session `lab-ace2-dfw-aus-` has been stopped, and the private `colab sessions` no longer contains this session; remaining account sessions belong to other tasks and were untouched.

New files: for specific values of the two grid points; merged previously saved statistics of the six grid points with the two grid points this time; `points_DFW.npz`, `points_AUS.npz` are lightweight paired series; , are eight-grid comparison figures (data sources in corner notes). , and original are reproducible; , retain sources and completion evidence. The original six-grid outputs are retained without overwriting; the eight-grid figures are stitched from point-level results of two rollouts with identical settings, not extracted simultaneously from eight points of the same global field.

Across the merged eight grid points, the median Gumbel 50-year relative bias is +4.89%; three grid points fall within the ±10% threshold, and none is below −20%; the across-grid median mean wind bias is +2.43%. Verdict: The supplementary check remains worth continuing for 0.25° ERA5 alignment, non-convective weather typing, and station representativeness verification; it cannot be claimed on this basis that climate simulator extremes are usable for design.

items.text:
# ACE2 万年集合、随机版与 ERA5 10 m 风：补充核查

日期 10-14（美东）。这是 的补充，不覆盖既有结果。

## 公开万年集合：查到什么

Paciorek & Cooley (2026), *BAMS* 107 E1053–E1070, DOI https://doi.org/10.1175/BAMS-D-25-0178.1 的 ACE2-ERA5 集合为 12 个初始条件 × 22 年强迫 × 40 次重复，共 10,560 年；论文 2.1 节和 Appendix A 描述训练对象、重循环强迫、算力。数据可用性声明（论文 119–120 行）只公开制作/分析代码及**模型输入**，没有给出完整模拟输出下载地址。作者仓库 https://github.com/paciorek/huge-ensemble-eva 的 至 每一个 `data_writer.names` 仅 `TMP2m`、`PRATEsfc`，未保存 `UGRD10m`、`VGRD10m`、最低层 `eastward_wind_7northward_wind_7`； 又只读取温度与降水。仓库树没有模拟的原始 `.nc.zarr`，处理文档只写本地 12 个约 670 GB 源文件与降水/气温 Rda。因此即便作者保有当时输出，也不能从公开材料取得**该批模拟的风**；不能拿它替代风速长 rollout。来源：论文 https://arxiv.org/html/2510.08893 及 https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paciorek/huge- 和 https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paciorek/huge-。这是一轮所列官方公开渠道的否定结果，不是宣称世界任何地方绝无未索引私有副本。

## 随机模型适用性

- ACE2-ERA5 官方 checkpoint https://huggingface.co/allenai/ACE2-ERA5 是先前 30 年 ERA5 对照的确定性模型。**未发现同一 ERA5 训练目标的公开 ACE2S checkpoint**；不能把 X-SHiELD/SHiELD 训练的随机模型当它的唯一随机开关。
- https://huggingface.co/allenai/ACE2S-SHiELD-plus 是公开的随机 ACE2S（Apache-2.0），以 GFDL SHiELD 为目标，历史 AMIP 文件覆盖 1979–2021；https://huggingface.co/allenai/ACE2-SHiELD 是对应确定性候选，官方指定复用前者的 AMIP 强迫与初始条件。二者虽共用物理模拟器/强迫，但训练数据组合、约束与架构并非唯一的随机性差别（随机款还训练了平衡与随机 CO₂ 等情景）；不宜把差异全归因于随机性。参见 https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07928。
- https://huggingface.co/allenai/HiRO-ACEv2 包含 `ACE2S-X-SHiELD.ckpt`，公开 Apache-2.0，提供 2014–2023 年强迫及两个初始场；其高分辨率 HiROv2 确实输出瞬时 10 m u/v，但模型卡明确说相对 X-SHiELD 而**非观测**，粗模只以 2014–2022 的九年 X-SHiELD 训练，对显著超出九年长度或历史强迫外泛化不保证。不是 ACE2-ERA5 的同目标随机版，也不能据其 99.9999% 分位“匹配”结论推断对 ERA5 的偏差。来源 https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17693 、 https://huggingface.co/allenai/HiRO-ACEv2。

## ERA5 陆地 10 m 风口径

ERA5 数据文档指定对应 IFS CY41R2：https://confluence.ecmwf.int/spaces/CKB/pages/76414402/ERA5+data+documentation。该版 *Part IV Physical Processes* §3.10.2（印刷页 52–53；PDF 物理页 52–53）明确：不是直接取最低模式层，而是为匹配开阔地 SYNOP 观测做 exposure correction。地面动量粗糙度 `z0M > 0.03 m` 时，40 m blending height 的风速按 `z0MWMO=0.03 m` 草地粗糙度及稳定度廓线外推至 10 m；`z0M < 0.03 m` 时用模式粗糙度/最低模式层。此为**假定开阔地**诊断量，不是陆地网格实际地表覆盖下的面积平均风，也不是阵风。文档原文 https://www.ecmwf.int/sites/default/files/elibrary/2016/79697-ifs-documentation-cy41r2-part-iv-physical-processes_1.pdf；较新用户指南 §9.3 https://confluence.ecmwf.int/spaces/FUG/pages/673551686/Section+9.3+Surface+wind 与之相符。粗化 ERA5 至 1.5° 还会进一步平滑极值，故先前相对偏差不能视作测站偏差。

## 实跑补检

Colab A100，独立子目录，配对模型均使用 Ai2 SHiELD+ 官方历史 AMIP 强迫和初始场；脚本 、。40 步烟测已分别完成、退出码均 0；接续 1979–1988 十年配对实验，按 `UGRD10mVGRD10m` 在原八点取六小时瞬时 10 m 风年最大值，对照同时间 WeatherBench2 ERA5 1.5° 重网格化及旧 ACE2-ERA5 的轻量点序列。ERA5 与 SHiELD 训练目标不同，配对仅作探索、不能是同目标消融；十年拟合 50 年重现值尤其不稳定。

两款十年连续推演均完成， 与 的退出码均为 0；（八格 × 四种场，共 32 行）、（角注数据来源）、对应的 32 个小点序列，原始全球场未落本机；本地 `small_results.tar.gz` 备份全部小文件和日志。

四种场相对相同十年 ERA5 参考的八格汇总（跨格中位，括号内最小至最大；百分数）：

| 模型 | 六小时平均风 | 年最大中位数 | Gumbel 50 年值 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ACE2-ERA5（旧三十年模型的前十年） | +1.55（−6.95 至 +6.82） | −3.79（−12.63 至 +13.61） | −4.72（−18.46 至 +12.34） |
| ACE2-SHiELD（确定性） | −4.22（−49.05 至 +18.70） | +7.08（−10.81 至 +22.97） | +16.04（−14.21 至 +46.09） |
| ACE2S-SHiELD+（随机） | −2.63（−49.92 至 +21.34） | +4.95（−14.20 至 +19.71） | +11.53（−20.91 至 +19.86） |

随机款 50 年值相对确定性 SHiELD 八格差异依站分别 KMSP −9.59%、KDSM +3.68%、KOMA +4.71%、KDTW −7.81%、KPIT −20.00%、KALB −9.30%、DFW −14.07%、AUS −0.76%。不呈现“随机化必然加厚尾部”。相对 ERA5，随机款 KDTW 十年 Gumbel 估计 −20.91%，但该点平均风 −22.71%；另一组格点偏高，不构成整体“尾部偏低”证据。更重要的是 **SHiELD 两款训练目标并非 ERA5，而且二者训练方案不同**，上表既不是相同模型随机性控制试验，也不能套原先 ACE2-ERA5 的 ±10% / −20% 有效性闸门来判断其 ERA5 极值。10 年外推 50 年没有置信区间，逐格绝对百分数仅初筛。八格坐标与配对步骤见 和；参照的 ERA5 仍是先保守重网格化至 1.5°、再双线性插至 1° ACE 网格的旧轻量序列。

Colab 本任务 `lab-ace-stochastic-` 已 stop，最终。判词：万年集合无可用风输出；随机模型确实可跑，但现有随机版不构成 ACE2-ERA5 的纯随机配对，十年对比尚不能解释 ERA5 风尾偏差机制；继续需同训练目标消融或先用 SHiELD 基准和更长集合验证。

items.text:
# Protocol Revision Following Review : Cold-Season Recalculation of Existing 30-Year Trajectory (10-14, EDT)

Status: Only the recalculation of the existing single-member ACE2-ERA5 1979–2008 point series has been completed; the formal 10 members, 1979–2024 forcing, and ensemble bootstrap 90% intervals are all **not run / not evaluated**. This round used local CPU only, with 0 new Colab CU; prior GPU usage see and . Did not mix SHiELD/X-SHiELD weights into the comparison of ERA5-trained models.

## Data and Filtering

Following the previous full actual run of , native UGRD10m/VGRD10m of ACE2-ERA5 and concurrent ERA5 6-hour 10 m winds were used. ERA5 was conservatively regridded to 1.5° via WeatherBench2, then bilinearly interpolated by U/V to ACE 1° grid points to compute scalar wind speed; therefore, it cannot replace sensitivity tests of direct conservative regridding from original ERA5 0.25°. The model was initialized on 1979-01-01; complete October–March cold seasons run from 1979/80 to 2007/08, totaling 29 seasons and 21,144 paired 6-hour timestamps per grid point. DFW/AUS are Texas reference points, without taking HOU, and cold seasons still cannot rule out local thunderstorms.

**Scientific scope limitation: cold season ≠ already determined as "non-convective, non-tropical cyclone".** This round has no thunderstorm/tropical cyclone event labeling or objective weather typing, and can only be termed "cold-season grid maximum wind (pre-screened for non-tropical-cyclone location)"; this value must not be treated as separated non-convective extremes, nor as station gusts or design wind speeds. The remaining six points are inland anchor points; representativeness of KDTW adjacent to the Great Lakes requires separate inspection.

One maximum value per season was taken, computing median and empirical p90 respectively; SciPy `genextreme.fit` was used for GEV maximum likelihood fitting, taking the 0.98 quantile as the 50-year seasonal return value; 30 calendar-year maxima were additionally used for annual GEV comparison. POT is a **sensitivity assumption, not a literature-specified parameter**: a fixed threshold was set at empirical p95 of all concurrent ERA5 cold-season 6-hour wind speeds per grid, shared between ACE and ERA; adjacent above-threshold timestamps within ≤72 hours in the same season were clustered taking the cluster maximum, GPD location fixed to zero, fitting exceedances by maximum likelihood, cluster rate = cluster count / 29 seasons, taking the quantile yielding an approximate 1/50 seasonal exceedance probability. Stability of p95/72 h, non-stationarity, or mixture of different weather types were not checked, and 50-year extrapolation is exploratory only. All bias = (ACE/ERA − 1) × 100%; positive indicates simulator overestimation. The script asserted sample counts and season counts item-by-item.

| Grid Point | Cold-Season Max Median Bias | p90 Bias | Seasonal GEV 50-Year Bias | Seasonal POT 50-Year Bias | Annual GEV 50-Year Bias |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| KMSP | −4.74% | −3.10% | −7.07% | −6.66% | −3.25% |
| KDSM | +0.72% | +3.39% | −5.26% | −5.15% | −7.85% |
| KOMA | −1.01% | −1.95% | −9.39% | −7.58% | −13.04% |
| KDTW | −9.74% | −13.44% | −10.32% | −10.12% | −15.89% |
| KPIT | +8.60% | +11.20% | +6.19% | +9.27% | +15.16% |
| KALB | +8.69% | +9.62% | +12.74% | +12.44% | +16.78% |
| DFW | +1.43% | +5.72% | +11.55% | +5.03% | +36.92% |
| AUS | −2.84% | −0.44% | −2.28% | −2.51% | +39.52% |

Across the eight grid points, the median seasonal GEV 50-year bias is −3.77%, ranging from −10.32% to +12.74%; the median seasonal POT across grid points is −3.83%, ranging from −10.12% to +12.44%. Existing single-member cold-season values show no underestimation or overestimation >20%, but passing the preset ensemble gate cannot be claimed on this basis. Annual GEV yields +36.92%/+39.52% at DFW/AUS, whereas older annual Gumbel fits yielded +8.15%/+14.01%, respectively: a 30-year sample, seasonal mixing, free shape parameters, and extrapolation differences are sufficient to alter the verdict, and one cannot cherry-pick a more favorable estimate. A single member lacks a "simulator ensemble bootstrap 90% interval", and whether ERA5 seasonal maximum median, p90, and 50-year values fall into that interval is **entirely unassessed**; ±10% serves only as auxiliary, and cannot independently determine "credibility".

## Model, Methodological Precedents, and ERA5 Wind Definition

- The 10,560-year ensemble run configuration in Paciorek & Cooley (2026), DOI https://doi.org/10.1175/BAMS-D-25-0178.1 saved only TMP2m/PRATEsfc, with no publicly available 10 m wind; will not search for it repeatedly. Code: https://github.com/paciorek/huge-ensemble-eva.
- The deterministic baseline trained on ERA5 is ACE2-ERA5; previously run ACE2S-SHiELD+ and HiRO-ACEv2 targeted SHiELD/X-SHiELD and are not included in this ERA5 comparison. ERA5-trained stochastic/generative NeuralGCM and ArchesWeatherGen AIMIP remain pending candidates, with no claim of completed pairing. Precedent Rucker et al. (2025) arXiv:2511.00274v2, §2.1.2, ran a 37-member ACE2-ERA5 initialized every 10 days in 1980 through 2022, but the study focused on regional heat extremes and drying trends, and cannot be treated as already published 10 m wind validation or calculations for this round. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.00274v2
- ERA5 10 m wind is an open-country exposure diagnostic over land rather than lowest model level wind: IFS Cy41r2 Part IV §3.10.2 Eqs. 3.91–3.92, when surface momentum roughness exceeds 0.03 m, it is brought down from the 40 m blending height to 10 m according to 0.03 m grass roughness and stability profiles; when below 0.03 m, the model roughness path is used. See ECMWF PDF physical pages 52–53 for details, https://www.ecmwf.int/sites/default/files/elibrary/2016/79697-ifs-documentation-cy41r2-part-iv-physical-processes_1.pdf; correspondence between ERA5 and Cy41r2 https://confluence.ecmwf.int/spaces/CKB/pages/76414402/ERA5+data+documentation. This does not equate to observed gusts under ASOS exposure.
- Sun, Hassanzadeh et al. (2025), *PNAS*, DOI https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2420914122 examined forecast extrapolation of **FourCastNet** for 2018–2023 Category 5 cyclones after removing Category 3 to 5 tropical cyclone training samples, finding it could not accurately forecast after global removal; **did not evaluate ACE/ACE2 or land 10 m wind extremes**. Rucker/Baxter/Hassanzadeh et al. (2025) arXiv:2511.00274v2 examined ACE2/NeuralGCM regional heat extremes and drying trends, and also not 10 m wind extremes. The two papers cannot be conflated with each other. https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2420914122; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.00274v2
- LUCIE by Guan et al. (arXiv:2405.16297v3) §4.4, Figure 11 (PDF physical pages 13, 23) indeed evaluates extreme return periods of wind in model prognostics, reporting that extremes of most variables are high relative to ERA5, and that the ensemble uncertainty range for wind can encompass ERA5; but its wind is T30 model-level U/V (Table 1 in text U/V 0.34 σ), **not diagnostic 10 m wind or ASOS station wind**, and the high values cannot be transferred to ACE2 10 m grid points. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.16297v3

## Formal Gate Still Outstanding

Requiring ≥10 members with different initial conditions spanning 1979–2024 (whether public ACE2 forcing/ERA5 sources cover 2024 must first be verified in practice; this round's WB2 1.5° source reaches only 2022), or preferably starting from 1940, retaining 6h point series / seasonal maxima per grid per member alongside forcing/checkpoint versions; constructing bootstrap 90% intervals following dependency structures such as member × cold season, comparing three metrics, GEV, threshold, and declustering sensitivities against ERA5 under identical forcing over the same period. One cannot randomly resample a single deterministic rollout 10 times to masquerade as 10 members. With the previous model throughput of 2.62 minutes/simulation year, a linear estimate for 10 × 46 years of model time is approx. 20.09 hours, or approx. 109.67 CU on a single A100 (based on previous 5.46 CU/h, **estimate only**, excluding staging, ERA5, and export); this exceeds what is suitable for an unattended Colab session, and it was not launched this round, leaving no GPU sessions or ensemble intervals produced.

Deliverables: , ; figure corner notes specify both sources, regridding, and unclassified status. Raw global fields are still not saved to workstation, and existing results were not overwritten.

One-sentence verdict: The two tail methods for the single-member cold season do not point to consistent underestimation or overestimation of wind tails across the eight grid points, but rigorous non-convective event separation and the ≥10-member ensemble gate have not yet been executed; the direction tentatively qualifies as "conditionally worth continuing", rather than a qualified extreme-value verification conclusion.

| KMSP | −3.2% No | −0.8% Yes | 12.0/11.6 −3.7% Yes | −3.5% No |
| KDSM | −2.8% No | −4.6% No | 15.9/13.8 −12.8% No | −5.3% No |
| KOMA | −5.0% No | 0.0% Yes | 13.5/13.7 +1.8% Yes | +0.5% Yes |
| KDTW | −3.6% No | −1.4% Yes | 12.5/12.8 +2.5% Yes | +0.8% Yes |
| KPIT | +4.8% No | +11.5% No | 9.6/11.1 +14.7% No | +15.8% No |
| KALB | +9.4% No | +15.1% No | 9.5/11.6 **+22.6%** No | **+22.9%** No |
| DFW | −5.8% No | −1.9% Yes | 12.4/12.2 −1.2% Yes | −3.5% No |
| AUS | −7.6% No | −8.8% No | 11.5/11.2 −2.8% Yes | −5.5% No |
| Inside Count | 0/8 | 4/8 | 5/8 | 2/8 |

## Interpretation and Protocol Caveats (Lead Judgment, No Literature Basis, Based on Data from This Track)
1. **The two Plains grid cells are systematically underestimated, not a single-member sampling artifact**: In KDSM/KOMA, the holdout-period ERA5 p90 and 50-year return values are much higher than in the training period (KDSM GEV50 rises from 15.9 in training to 19.0 m/s in holdout), whereas the ten-member ensemble remains nearly unchanged across the two periods (13.8 → 13.5). Even the strongest season across the entire ensemble fails to reach the ERA5 holdout tail, meaning not a single emulator member reproduced the strong Plains seasons of 1996–2010 (the heavy tail in ERA5). KDSM was already underestimated by −12.8% in the training period, showing this is not solely a holdout-period issue.
2. **The two Northeast grid cells are overestimated**: KALB/KPIT are +15% to +23% higher in the training period; in the holdout period, GEV falls inside the interval, but POT is overestimated by +6% to +12% and the seasonal max median is higher by +3% to +11%. The direction is opposite to the Plains, indicating there is no uniform global bias.
3. **"Falling inside the 90% interval" is a stringent test**: Because all ten members share identical forcing and differ only in initial conditions, inter-member spread is very small, with bootstrap interval widths mostly around ±0.3 to 0.5 m/s. The interval captures only the emulator's internal variability and excludes the sampling error of the single 14-season ERA5 reference sample itself. Thus, only 2/8 medians falling inside the interval does not mean the medians are wrong—5 out of 8 grid cells are within ±5% relative bias. When making the verdict, it is recommended to use "relative bias ±10% / >20%" as the primary criterion and "inside interval" as secondary, or switch to a two-sided test (bootstrapping the reference as well).
4. The cold-season proxy does not separate non-convective events; whether the heavy tail in the KDSM/KOMA holdout period includes intense cold fronts or low-pressure systems has not yet been checked.
5. The ten-member ensemble intervals are directionally consistent with the `m01` single-member preview (holdout GEV50 median −8.6%, KOMA −25%, KALB +26%): ten members narrow the median bias to −2.6%, but the underestimation at KDSM/KOMA and overestimation at KALB persist.

## One-Sentence Judgment
Median levels and 50-year return values match across more than half of the grid cells (6/8 within ±10%), but the holdout 50-year return values at the two Plains grid cells (KDSM, KOMA) are systematically underestimated by 22–29%, and training-period KALB in the Northeast is overestimated by 23%: the emulator can reproduce "typical" cold-season strong winds, but fails to reproduce ERA5's regional heavy tails. The worthwhile next step is to investigate what events drive the tails at those two cells and why the emulator suppresses them, rather than proceeding directly to station design wind speeds.

## CU
Estimated from the controller logs and progress records: `m01` 13.58 + two accidental stops 4.53 + `m02` ~8.7 + `m03` ~8.5 (these two were stopped manually by `ideas`, with no STOPPED entry in the logs) + `m04`–`m10` 58.30 + this CPU aggregation <0.1 ≈ **94 CU** (estimated, consistent with the controller's pre-`m10` projection of 95.5; shared account, not billed separately).

# C Non-Convective Extreme Winds: Interpretation of Ten-Member Results and Next Steps (2026-10-15)
Results: (ACE2-ERA5 ten members, 8 grid cells, cold season, ~94 CU).
- Holdout period (14 seasons) GEV 50-year return value: median bias −2.6%, with 6/8 grid cells within ±10%; KDSM −28.9% and KOMA −22.5% (underestimated); training period KALB +22.6% and KPIT +14.7% (overestimated). Falling inside the ensemble 90% interval: GEV 5/8, median 2/8, POT 2/8.
- Interpretation: typical cold-season strong winds match well; regional heavy tails disagree, with opposite signs between west/Plains and east. "Falling inside the interval" captures only the emulator's internal variability and excludes the sampling error of the 14-season ERA5 sample, making it overly strict and unsuitable as a standalone criterion. (No literature basis; based on data from this track.)
Decision I made: Continue C, but do not proceed to station conversion; first assign `wx` to perform single-member ranking (whether ERA5 falls outside the range of the 10 individual member estimates) and event identification for the strong holdout seasons at KDSM/KOMA (the cold-season proxy may mix in convective events). Why: the 22–29% underestimation at those two grid cells could reflect tail suppression by the emulator, or it could be driven by a few extreme seasons or even convective events in the reference sample—two possibilities that lead to opposite conclusions. Cost of being wrong: ~5 CU and half a day.
Criterion (10-15 evening correction: this clause was proposed after inspecting the results and serves strictly as auxiliary evidence; see record): if the ERA5 value falls within the single-member range, or if the strong seasons are primarily convective events → supports "not emulator tail suppression," though advancing to the station stage will require a new pre-registration + new data; if ERA5 still exceeds all 10 members after removing convective events → judged as emulator tail suppression, and C will either pivot to "investigating the cause of tail suppression / switching to a generative model" or be Shelved.

items.text:
# ACE2 10-Member Single-Member Ranking and Plains Grid Point ERA5 Strong-Season Event Verification

10-15; computed on Colab CPU `wx-ace-rank-events-1015`; outputs downloaded and session stopped. Inputs are the original project's 10 member summaries, ERA5 summary, fixed thresholds, and 1996–2009 cold-season 6-hourly reference npz files; all read-only. Execution script outputs cover (48 rows = 2 periods × 8 grid points × 3 metrics) and (28 rows = 2 grid points × 14 seasons), with original sources documented. Another 90% model bootstrap interval in the original project is not the single-member range reported here.

Each member independently fits a free-shape GEV to the seasonal maxima over the same 14/15 seasons, taking the .98 quantile for the 50-year return level; POT retains the training-period ERA5 6-hourly p95 fixed threshold, 72 h within-season declustering, and the same GPD/arrival-rate formula; p90 is taken directly from each member's seasonal maximum quantile. Rank is defined as one plus the number of the 10 members below ERA5, where 11 = ERA5 exceeds all members. There are no ties; out-of-range flags follow the operational rule specified by the delegating lead and are not a calibrated significance test or reference sampling confidence interval. Shared forcing and the short sample make the 10 members correlated, so they cannot be treated as 10 independent climate-year realizations.

| Period | Grid | Metric | ERA5 m/s | 10-Member Range m/s | ERA5 Rank/11 | Out of Range |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Holdout 14 seasons | KDSM | GEV50 | 18.98 | 12.63–14.12 | 11 | Yes, high side |
| Holdout 14 seasons | KDSM | POT50 | 16.08 | 12.74–13.83 | 11 | Yes, high side |
| Holdout 14 seasons | KDSM | p90 | 15.31 | 11.83–12.81 | 11 | Yes, high side |
| Holdout 14 seasons | KOMA | GEV50 | 17.51 | 12.14–15.10 | 11 | Yes, high side |
| Holdout 14 seasons | KOMA | POT50 | 16.00 | 11.84–14.30 | 11 | Yes, high side |
| Holdout 14 seasons | KOMA | p90 | 15.17 | 11.60–13.08 | 11 | Yes, high side |
| Training 15 seasons | KDSM | GEV50 | 15.87 | 13.02–16.32 | 9 | No |
| Training 15 seasons | KDSM | POT50 | 14.42 | 12.86–14.50 | 10 | No |
| Training 15 seasons | KDSM | p90 | 13.52 | 12.39–13.09 | 11 | Yes, high side |
| Training 15 seasons | KOMA | GEV50 | 13.47 | 12.61–14.28 | 4 | No |
| Training 15 seasons | KOMA | POT50 | 13.38 | 12.77–14.00 | 6 | No |
| Training 15 seasons | KOMA | p90 | 12.90 | 12.10–13.41 | 8 | No |

See the CSV for the full 8-grid record. Out-of-range in the holdout period: for GEV50, only KDSM/KOMA exceed all members; POT50 also includes KALB below all members and AUS above all members; p90 also includes KALB below all members and DFW above all members. In the training period, GEV50 at both KPIT and KALB is below all 10 members. The low tail of the original ensemble is definitely not caused by a single member with an unusually low estimate; however, a narrow member range does not mean that the bias against the true 14-season ERA5 GEV50 is statistically significant. At KDSM, p90 is already low during the training period, whereas at KOMA the strong underestimation is mainly concentrated in the holdout period.

Top five seasonal maxima in the ERA5 holdout period (UTC; m/s; dates and magnitudes verified directly from `cold_YYYY.npz` in the reference data, matching the seasonal maxima in `reference_summary.json` item by item):

| Grid | Season Start Year | ERA5 Max UTC | m/s | Weather Regime Evidence and Assessment |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| KDSM | 1998 | 1998-11-10 18:00 | 16.08 | NCEI describes an explosively deepening low crossing Iowa with statewide high winds lasting 12–18 h; extratropical cyclone / non-convective dominance is highly credible; thunderstorms also occurred the previous night, so local mixing contributions cannot be ruled out from daily-scale records.[1][2] |
| KDSM | 2009 | 2009-12-09 12:00 | 15.66 | NWS Des Moines reports a blizzard with strong northwesterly winds continuing into the 9th; extratropical winter storm is highly credible.[3] |
| KDSM | 1997 | 1998-03-09 12:00 | 14.49 | Coincides with a widespread Iowa/Nebraska snow and wind storm; winter cyclone/frontal forcing is plausible, but lacking synchronous grid-point dynamic charts, this remains an indirect interpretation.[9] |
| KDSM | 2000 | 2000-12-16 18:00 | 14.32 | No event evidence sufficient to match the grid point and timestamp was found; unclassified. |
| KDSM | 2008 | 2008-10-26 18:00 | 12.95 | NWS documents widespread post-cold-front northwesterly winds and strong gusts across Iowa; post-frontal non-convective regime is highly likely.[4] |
| KOMA | 1998 | 1998-11-10 18:00 | 15.85 | Reached seasonal peak simultaneously with KDSM during the same deep low-pressure system; cyclone/frontal forcing is highly credible, though NCEI descriptions focus mainly on Iowa and should not be equated to synchronous grid-point observations at KOMA.[1][2] |
| KOMA | 2009 | 2010-01-25 18:00 | 15.80 | NWS documents a South Dakota low / cold high pressure system and blizzard; Iowa experienced strong northwesterly winds and blowing snow on the same day; regionally a winter low / pressure-gradient wind regime is plausible, but lacking co-located synchronous data at KOMA, it cannot be confirmed.[7][8] |
| KOMA | 2008 | 2009-03-23 18:00 | 13.72 | NWS documents a subsequent squall line from eastern Nebraska into northwestern Iowa on that day, but its 16:08 CDT radar timestamp is 21:08 UTC, later than the 18 UTC maximum; this maximum cannot be directly labeled as a squall line, and neither convection nor pre-frontal pressure gradients are ruled out.[5] |
| KOMA | 1997 | 1998-03-09 00:00 | 12.91 | Regional snow and wind storm on March 8–9, making a winter low plausible; report time granularity is insufficient to confirm 00 UTC.[9] |
| KOMA | 2004 | 2005-03-10 18:00 | 12.84 | NWS Sioux City documents high northwesterly winds on March 10 (gusts reported at 14:11 CST that day, i.e., 20:11 UTC), supporting regional post-frontal gradient winds, but the KOMA peak occurred earlier than that observation and is not co-located, so attribution remains plausible rather than confirmed.[6] |

Interpretation: The 1998-11-10 strong season shared by the top two plains grid points has independent NOAA evidence of an intense cyclone; the second strongest season at KDSM (2009-12-09) was also a blizzard. Current evidence does not support simply attributing the heavy tail in the plains holdout period to a few convective contamination events; however, the heavy-tail sampling uncertainty of the 14-season sample itself remains unquantified, and the 2009-03-23 KOMA event is inconclusive. At this stage, we can only state that "the 10 model members are systematically lower across these strong ERA5 seasons," and cannot render a verdict on physical tail suppression by the model, ERA5 reference representativeness, or design wind speed reliability based on rank alone; if a verdict is required, we recommend conducting a two-sided year-block bootstrap on ERA5 together with synchronous local ERA5 CAPE/precipitation/SLP checks on peak dates, and comparing ACE2 6-hourly peaks stratified on the 1998-11-10 event.

# C 10-Member Ensemble: Evaluation Under Pre-Registered Primary Criterion (2026-10-15, per supervising AI Weather Models Lead request)
- Pre-registered threshold: Unspecified (the revised protocol did not specify how many grid points or metrics must fall within range to pass), and will not be filled in post hoc.
- Interval construction: The two-level "member × forcing year" bootstrap estimates the uncertainty of the pooled-sample statistic and does not include the sampling variability of a single 14-season ERA5 record, making it overly strict toward ERA5. Switching to the single-member distribution as a reference is a post-hoc convention adjustment, not pre-registered.
- Verdict: Inconclusive. Grid-by-grid inclusion counts: seasonal maximum median 2/8, p90 3/8, GEV50 5/8, POT50 2/8 (see "Primary Criterion Evaluation" on the project page for details).
- Correction to the statement in an earlier decision today that "if ERA5 falls within the single-member range or the strong seasons are primarily convective → judge as passed and proceed to station checks": that criterion was proposed post hoc and can only serve as auxiliary evidence; advancing to the station stage requires writing a new pre-registration (criterion + threshold) first and testing on unseen data (2020/21–2021/22 holdout seasons, or new grid points). The rule "if still higher than all 10 members after removing convective events → judge as emulator tail suppression" is retained.
No literature basis; grounded in data from this research thread.

## Addendum (10-15 evening, after wx report)
- Single-member range: At KDSM and KOMA, holdout-period ERA5 values for GEV50/POT50/p90 all exceed all 10 members; no confirmable convective events were found among the top five strong seasons (1998-11-10 severe winter storm, 2009-12-09 blizzard, etc.; see NOAA/NWS sources). Under the auxiliary rule, the two plains grid points are judged as "emulator tail suppression, auxiliary-evidence level"; because both grid points share the same intense event, they do not count as two independent pieces of evidence. The pre-registered verdict remains inconclusive.
Decision I made: Write a new pre-registration (freezing criteria and grid points), and dispatch wx to re-run the 10-member evaluation on 8 unseen grid points while saving regional fields for future reuse. Why: Data already inspected cannot be used to declare a pass, and whether plains tail suppression is widespread must be answered using new grid points. Cost if wrong: ~75–90 Colab CU and ~1 day.
