Note target specification: The actual training entry point for legacy best is (DataFormatter 640 grid, patch, and raw_cases), not feeding directly into the model; the latter is used to independently verify height channels after topo flipping. Generate bundles of the same kind; if inconsistent with legacy cache on the same case, stop sanity checking. Legacy configuration: R11 anisotropic_kernel_operator_unet, n_c=20, depth=6, input_features=height_sdf_normal, masked_l1_gradient (default gradient weight 0.1), Adam lr=0.0004, batch 16, 1000 epochs, no scheduler, save checkpoint every 50 epochs; SDF/normal feature generation strictly follows legacy train.py, with no new data augmentations during training. Best checkpoint is selected solely by case-by-case median R² of corrected stratified_v1 on internal val55 every 50 epochs, breaking ties by selecting the earlier epoch; do not select models by inspecting holdout. Legacy sanity check uses seed 2 on the original train410/val55/holdout47 split (corrected manifest SHA 1a84b78a31c50f6d4fa3139c1422454cf8332279bf140c505f2a0ccd7b743d55); legacy evaluation total102 median R² must return to approximately 0.75–0.80; otherwise stop and report. The 0.7946 reported in the legacy project is a seed mean that includes identical geometries across wind directions between train and holdout, and cannot be treated as strict generalization.

New split is fixed: training 371/160 geometries, internal validation 34/20, test 100/80; 23 cases unqualified by IoU and 10 lacking wind direction are excluded, without supplementing the test set. Four tiers N=50/100/200/All approx. 371, seeds 17/42/73, sampled hierarchically/nested by geometry group; select total case counts as close to the target as possible without splitting the same group, and actual numbers must be recorded; internal validation and testing do not overlap across groups. Run competence gates first across all three seeds for the "All" tier: for the same model, internal validation median R² ≥ 0.5 and test idealized subset median R² ≥ 0.7; if not passed, close out immediately without running other tiers or baselines. Only after passing the gate run the remaining tiers and B baselines. The new model likewise has 1000 epochs, checkpoints every 50 epochs, selecting the best by internal validation median R² and breaking ties by earlier epoch; selection by test set is strictly prohibited.

B0: Global constant mean field of fluid grid points only in training. B1: Look-up table of means binned by distance to building and upwind building height for training grid points, with empty bins falling back to training global mean; binning boundaries are frozen solely based on training feature quantiles. B2: Handcrafted features of local height, SDF, upwind obstacle height/distance, and wind direction from training data, ridge regression (penalty strength selected only on internal validation); none of the three methods may take test ground truth as input, and all use identical raw grid points and frozen test sets. Scoring should as much as possible undergo recovery via the original's raw domain and valid condition `truth>=0 & finitelu_sdf_640`/Uped target differences and different test sets across legacy splits prevent numbers across rounds/papers from being directly compared side by side.

Original criteria (verbatim): Curve is still declining: error = a·N^(−b)+c, RMSE decline from 200→All exceeds 2 times the inter-seed standard deviation, and extrapolating to N=1600 yields a median R² that is another ≥0.03 higher than N=All; Deep model clearly outperforms classical baselines: at N=All, RMSE is ≥20% lower than the best B baseline, and performs better on ≥2/3 of test geometries; Both satisfied → worth generating data; Only 1 → data is useful, but first investigate why classical methods are so strong; Only 2 → reached a plateau; Neither satisfied → not worth it. If worth it, further estimate required N range for R² 0.85/0.90 and GPU LBM GPU-hours/CU, indicating sources or assumptions. Separately report difference between legacy split vs. grouped full dataset; when not on the same test set, the total difference cannot be entirely attributed to leakage.

First measure the wall-clock time of a single sanity training run and the Colab CU balance observation window; use this to estimate the full suite, and if projected to exceed 100 CU, stop and report. At session end, must stop; parallel balance changes in shared accounts are not treated as independent billing. All of the above training results are simulated UrbanTALES data and do not represent field wind measurement validation.

判据①：N200→371 全测试 pooled RMSE 均值下降 0.014738；2×组内合并 SD 0.007809（两档各自2SD 0.010660／0.002886），首条件小幅通过。拟合误差 a·N^(−b)+c：
ideal: RMSE a=1260.38, b=2.49172, c=0.0485216, SSE=0.00718278；1−中位R²拟合 a=54.7816, b=1.38253, c=0.0764426；全量观测均值R²=0.9060 → N1600推算=0.9215（增量0.0156）。
real: RMSE a=0.281683, b=0.23194, c=0.1155, SSE=0.000336172；受 c≥0 约束的 1−中位R²拟合 a=1.57987, b=0.198829, c=0.0181932；全量观测均值R²=0.5086 → 该约束下 N1600推算=0.6174（增量0.1088）。无约束拟合 a=3.525、b=0.0416、c=−2.255；负渐近误差不具可解释性，说明真实街区渐近值无法由当前四档识别，不把 +0.1088 当作可靠收益预测。
all: RMSE a=0.589349, b=0.563043, c=0.149526, SSE=0.00031853；1−中位R²拟合 a=2.86777, b=0.496823, c=0.205325；全量观测均值R²=0.6546 → N1600推算=0.7213（增量0.0667）。
全测试外推增量超过0.03，故判据①按冻结计算通过；理想化单列增量不足0.03，真实街区约束拟合增量更大但不稳定。表中拟合参数不因审查意见重算或更换。
判据②：最佳方向核实基线 B1 pooled RMSE=0.267738；三种子深度模型均值=0.168769，降低 36.96%；80几何组中 79/80 优于基线（门槛54），案例参照 99/100；通过。
敏感性联合改动 B1（16格/6箱）RMSE=0.268209，深度模型降低37.08%，几何胜79/80；方向与非周期边界假设不变，不能拆分距离与分箱效应。

## 定稿结论（审查 后）

按冻结预注册与 修正口径，四选一机械判定为“值得造数据”，但证据强度弱：只支持真实街区误差在已测 N 范围仍随数据量改善、值得继续增加真实街区数据作验证；不支持承诺加数据有可量化收益或据此直接启动造数。具体口径如下（科学解释依据本线结果与上述审查裁决，非文献的直接数值结论）：

1. 理想化街区近平台：N=200→371 的 pooled RMSE 约 0.0496→0.0500，未下降；约束拟合 N=1600 中位 R² 只比全量提高 0.016（小于 0.03）。全体拟合增量 +0.067 主要由真实街区驱动；全量时真实街区占全测试平方误差约 98%。
2. 真实街区 N=200→371 的 pooled RMSE 实测下降约 0.0165，大于 2×组内合并 SD 约 0.0090；但 1−R² 约束拟合的 N=1600 增量 +0.109 依赖 c≥0。无约束最优 a=3.525、b=0.0416、c=−2.255，渐近值不可识别；每档仅三种子，SD 仅 2 自由度，371→1600 约 4.3 倍外推不可当作实测。
3. 判据②的算术比较成立：全量深度模型比本次最好基线 B1 的 pooled RMSE 低 36.96%，80 个测试几何组中 79 组更好（案例参照 99/100）。但 B0/B1/B2 测试中位 R² 均为负（−0.33／−0.21／−0.18）；B1 上风高度分箱坍缩为 [0,16]，B2 岭惩罚未按像素数归一、raw 流体格点高度特征恒为 0。这仅证明优于这三个实现较弱的基线，不证明优于有竞争力的经典方法；方向已核实，非周期 wrap 敏感性未做，B1/B2 联合参数敏感性不能拆解单因素影响。
4. 预注册“若值得”分支所要求的 R² 0.85／0.90 所需 N 区间及 GPU LBM GPU时／CU 成本：不可估。全体约束拟合渐近 R² 上限约 0.79，按此拟合 0.85／0.90 不可达；真实街区渐近值不可识别，不能据此推 N，也不能据不可信 N 乘造数单价。旧划分 total102 中位 R² 约 0.796 与新分组全量 test100 约 0.655 使用不同测试集合，差值不能全归因于几何泄漏。

局限及执行偏离：B 基线先于闸门完成，两次 Colab 结果丢失并重跑；全量 seed17 的验证逐例 RMSE/n 未保存，测试 RMSE 标 † 按相同测试真值与掩膜重建，非直接测得。第二段累计约 275.672 CU 为会话时长×5.4 的估算、不是独立账单，低于获批 290 CU。文献参照：Lu 2025 UrbanTALES 卡 期刊 p.6／PDF p.7；Lumet 2025 卡 期刊 p.12、p.15／PDF p.13、p.16；指标与数据组成不同，不作数值直接对标。

理想化与真实曲线：、（三种子均值±种子范围与B0/B1/B2水平线）。
第二段累计≈275.672 CU（旧会话累计基数216.50 + hm4分配10-17 14:09:57 至手动停机10-18 01:07:25，共10.9578h×5.4=59.172）；按会话时长估算非独立账单，含两次结果丢失及传输开销，低于母项目290 CU。hm4 已手动 stop，sessions 不含该会话，keepalive 单元已消失。全部运行均串行。N50 seed73 完成1000轮、20 checkpoint、选优450轮，训练与评测3691.45秒；七份文件Colab—p14逐一核 SHA，最佳模型SHA-256 `6add909cc4e412120700253e437d8ff3482163986a2d8558e1953ab30755f71a`，CRC同SHA及大小。既有滚动存档不删除。

# v6 第二段偏离与审查修正记录（2026-10-15 美东）

冻结原件 不改；先前审查裁决，终判审查裁决。第二段上限先为 260 CU，母项目 10-17 决策 提高至 **290 CU**；最终累计约 **275.672 CU**（按会话时长×5.4 的估算、非独立账单，含两次结果丢失与重跑）。所有训练模型、batch16、1000 轮、每 50 轮 checkpoint、内部验证选优均未更改。

1. 执行顺序偏离：B0/B1/B2 在三个全量种子闸门全部完成前由 CPU 跑出，违反预注册第 9 行「过闸才跑基线」。保存原始文件 、；B1/B2 原版 +row 方向经 NetCDF 矢量核实正确，B2 alpha 原下边界 0.01 仍须按审查扩网格，不直接用原版作最终判据。它们未用测试真值选参数。闸门解释冻结为三个全量种子各自验证中位 R²≥0.5、理想化测试中位 R²≥0.7，任一失败止损收口。
2. 审查发现分析实现偏差：旧 把两组均值差计入种子 SD，并按 100 案例而非 80 几何计票、按名义 N 拟合。已修为组内合并 SD（并列两组各自 2SD）、同几何多风向按有效格点池化 RMSE 后计票（54/80）、使用清单逐种子的实际 N。旧版未用于科学判定。
3. 上风方向（已用独立矢量场纠正诊断）：先用组合场尾迹代理 错判 d00 为 +col，临时改动适配器，并跑出了；这些及错误方向的 `sensitivity16` 结果均无效、只留审计，不得进入判据。随后从 CRC 原始 （三例各约 1.2 MB，经既有 socket 安全复制，首例 SHA 两端一致）读出 矢量和坐标：x 对应 axis0=row，y 对应 axis1=col；三例外缘有效流体 uped 均值 0.2386、0.2406、0.2446，vped 均值 −0.0224、−0.0408、+0.0178，确定 d00 为 +row、原 `dy=cos θ,dx=sin θdirection_verified` 重算；不覆盖任何既有结果。
4. 边界：旧 250、288 行为旋转/patch 对齐使用 wrap，但这不能证明物理场横纵周期；原始有限矩形 raw 上风搜索继续采用域外 0（非周期），不得把 formatter 数值 padding 误作物理边界。最终 **wrap/不 wrap 敏感性未做**，非周期边界仍为基线实现假设，不把缺项写成已核验。
5. B2 内部验证 alpha 网格从 0.01 扩到 0.0001、0.001，方向核实版输出 和，不覆盖旧版。B2 验证选择 alpha=0.0001（新网格下边界），仅按验证集选。敏感性版本也已在 CPU 完成，分别存 ：上风16/32格、B1分箱6/8、B2 alpha 网格下探到 1e-6（验证选中 1e-6）。16格/6箱 B1 全测试中位 R² −0.207856、pooled RMSE 0.268209（32格/8箱为 −0.210623、0.267738）；16格 B2 为 −0.180307、pooled RMSE **0.273003**（32格为 −0.181228、0.273592）。多个参数同时变化，不能单独归因距离或箱数；最终判据②与方向核实 B1 的联合敏感性仍为 79/80 几何组更好，但不等同于 B2 或 wrap 的单因素稳健性。
6. 三例 `_d00` 的 raw topo 在首末行、首末列恰均为零，该边缘一致性不能证明周期性。旧 formatter 的 wrap 是 patch 对齐，并非物理周期边界；方向核实版仍不 wrap（ 第 27 行），此为边界假设而非论文参数，最终判据需标敏感性局限。审查第 6 项有效格点数逐例核对**已完成，但有例外**：11 个有逐例 `n` 的深度模型与三基线在固定验证34例、测试100例上逐例一致，三基线总数分别为验证6,607,723、测试20,203,621；全量 seed17 的历史摘要只有逐例 R²、没有原始 的 † 注和。
7. 判据①的检验力有限：N=200 与全量各仅 3 种子，样本 SD 均只有 2 自由度；即便 RMSE 条件过闸，371→1600 约 4.3 倍的幂律外推仍高度依赖拟合假设，不可称为实测。母项目已定短路顺序：三个全量种子各自过闸后跑 N=200 的 17/42/73；若修正后的 RMSE 下降不严格超过 2 倍组内合并 SD，则判据①为假，不跑 N=50/100，图注标明按预注册短路结构提前锁定；否则才跑 N=50/100 各三种子。此顺序为母项目 10-15 补充决定，不改变冻结训练配置。第 1 点已记录 B 基线先于闸门完成。
8. 两次 Colab 结果丢失与防丢修正（10-17 美东；CU 均为会话占用×5.4 粗估，不是独立账单）：第一次 10-16 18:38 全量会话达到自 10-15 18:37:59 分配起约 24 小时上限，被 Colab 回收；N=200 seed42 从 16:52 至 18:39 约 9.63 CU 的不完整训练无可用结果，旧根保留、retry1 从零重跑。第二次 10-17 06:32 seed73 原运行达 S2_DONE 后 keepalive 因完成标记自行退出，未拉取 summary/选优模型/逐例结果；07:30:52–07:37:55 因闲置回收。该次 seed73 从 02:58 启动至回收占用约 24.56–25.19 CU，整次结果须重跑；其中完成后空转约 5.30–5.93 CU。旧第950轮 checkpoint 保留备查、不用于评分或续训。retry1 在 09:30 已开训后，增设不改原训练/评测器的 CPU-only 逐50轮内部验证旁路程序 ：每档输出验证34例逐例 R²/RMSE/n/SSE，严格以内部验证中位 R²、平局取较早轮选择当前最优，把单份最优 checkpoint 与指标同步到；测试只由原 runner 在最后选择后评测一次。 同步按120秒探活/每次检查更新；历史滚动 .pt 依 Lead 告知保留待统一处置，不擅自删除。keepalive 不配置完成自动退出或 stop；正式 summary/逐例、checkpoint_selection、train.log 与选优模型先经 Colab—工作站 SHA，模型再送 CRC 核 SHA，之后才手动 stop。重跑 seed73 和余下六项均已完成并归档，最终报告；归档完成前的待办描述至此关闭。

# Dedicated CFD Surrogate Model for Wind Engineering: Data Scaling Learning Curve (Exploring)

This sub-project investigates how urban pedestrian-level wind surrogate error scales with training sample size (N) on the 538-case PALM 1 m large-eddy simulation dataset UrbanTALES, testing whether neural operators significantly beat classical baselines on strictly unseen urban geometries and whether generating thousands of new GPU LBM cases is justified. Early rounds exposed a cross-wind-direction geometry leakage in a legacy split (32 shared geometries between training and holdout sets) and resolved severe training under-convergence (`v3`) as well as a north–south coordinate flip bug between topography and wind arrays (`v4v5`). In `v6` Stage 1 on Colab A100-80GB, reusing the legacy 640×640 signed-distance-field (SDF) pipeline (`anisotropic_kernel_operator`, 1,000 epochs) reproduced the legacy split median R^2 of 0.796 and passed the pre-registered capability gate on strictly unseen geometry groups (internal validation median R^2 = 0.766 ge 0.50, idealized test subset 0.901 ge 0.70, realistic urban blocks 0.493, overall test 0.655). Stage 2 multi-seed learning curve runs and reviewer-audited baseline comparisons are currently executing serially under a 260 CU budget.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-14**: Literature cards were compiled for UrbanTALES (538 PALM LES cases at 1 m pedestrian-level resolution; benchmark U-Net reporting R^2 approx 0.65 overall and 0.94 on idealized arrays).
- **2026-10-14**: Auditing the legacy project split revealed 32 shared geometries between training and holdout sets across different wind directions, meaning the legacy R^2 approx 0.79 did not measure strictly unseen geometry generalization.
- **2026-10-14**: After relaxing a fluid-fraction filter that dropped 14 high-density cases (0.18 vs. 0.20 threshold) and excluding 10 cases lacking wind-direction metadata, the research assistant ran Round 1 (`v3`, 60 epochs on 160×160 and 320×320 grids); U-Net RMSE at N=400 (0.2421) beat the best classical baseline `B1` (0.2647) by only 8.52% (below the 20% gate).
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead invalidated Round 1 as under-trained and anisotropically distorted, launching Round 2 (`v4`) at native 1 m resolution (192 m patches, early stopping, random-split control, and a capability gate requiring validation median R^2 ge 0.50 and idealized test ge 0.70), which still scored negative median R^2 (−0.095 to −0.043).
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead diagnosed the root cause of the `v3v4` failure: PALM ASCII topography rows run north-to-south while the wind array runs south-to-north, leaving building masks vertically inverted (mask IoU 0.015–0.285 before flipping vs. 0.910–0.941 after vertical flipping).
- **2026-10-14**: In `v5`, re-extracting 505 cases with corrected vertical orientation raised native-patch U-Net median R^2 to 0.271–0.385 on internal validation and 0.450–0.632 on idealized test cases, still below the 0.50/0.70 capability gate.
- **2026-10-14**: With parent-program approval (~80–86 CU budget on Colab A100-80GB because cluster A10 GPUs lacked the required 38.8 GB VRAM), AI Weather Models Lead launched `v6` Stage 1 using the legacy 640×640 SDF pipeline (1,000 epochs).
- **2026-10-15**: `v6` Stage 1 sanity reproduction completed in 7.39 hours (~40 CU), achieving a median R^2 of 0.796 across all 102 legacy test cases (0.800 validation, 0.791 holdout) and matching the legacy 0.79 benchmark.
- **2026-10-15**: `v6` Stage 1 strict geometry-grouped capability gate (`seed 17`, full training set, 1,000 epochs, cumulative ~86 CU) passed: internal validation median R^2 reached 0.766 (ge 0.50) and idealized test reached 0.901 (ge 0.70), while realistic urban blocks scored 0.493 (overall 100-case test median R^2 = 0.655).
- **2026-10-15**: AI Weather Models Lead dispatched `v6B0B1B2`) to the research assistant; after dual-process training triggered a CUDA out-of-memory error (42.5 GiB per process), execution switched to serial runs (~7.5 h / ~41 CU per full-data seed) under an expanded 260 CU cap.
- **2026-10-15**: Three reviewers audited the production release plan, mandating eight analysis and baseline fixes (pooled within-group SD for Criterion 1, 80-geometry-group voting for Criterion 2, inflow-angle checks, and ridge regularization down to 10-4), while initial `B0B1B2` runs scored negative median R^2 (−1.06 to −0.03).

## Where it stands

This sub-project is Exploring in `v6` Stage 2 after passing the Stage 1 capability gate on strictly unseen urban geometries (R^2 = 0.901 idealized, 0.493 realistic, 0.655 overall). Full-data runs (`seed 42` and `seed 73`) and N=200 runs across all three seeds (~155 CU cumulative) are prioritized first on Colab A100-80GB alongside the eight reviewer-mandated baseline fixes to evaluate Criterion 1 early stopping before deciding whether N=50 and N=100 runs are needed.

# I Wind-damage loss–wind-speed database

## Objective
Use large language models to batch-extract NOAA Storm Events narratives (and later post-disaster survey reports) into structured "loss–wind-speed" records, and determine whether this direction is worth pursuing. Liang Hu 10-14: For resilience/performance metrics to be used in design, they must first be validated against real loss data; this is currently difficult, so we are only making an initial start.

## Current Status
**Shelved (10-14 22:4x)**, decision.
- **Why it does not work**: LLM extraction is usable (source classification 66/70, able to separate wind speeds inferred from damage), but data are lacking—thunderstorm station networks cannot capture damage-core winds (nearby station gusts are a median of 37 mph lower than DAT damage-estimated winds, and H4 reconstruction is ineffective); hurricane DAT contains only damaged points with no trend; CRASAR patches that include a denominator cover small areas with a wind-speed span of only 0.3 m/s and lie entirely within storm-surge zones, leaving 0 usable buildings after excluding water damage.
- **What is missing**: Inland building-by-building damage data spanning a wide wind-speed band, excluding water damage, and including undamaged buildings; an independent wind-speed source for thunderstorms.
- **Conditions for restarting**: (1) Wide-area post-disaster aerial imagery + building damage classification, systematic inland sampling surveys, or address-level insurance/FEMA data (requires a data agreement, to be decided by Liang Hu); (2) H6 demonstrates that radar near-surface winds can serve as an independent wind speed for thunderstorms; (3) A specific user needs design wind speed vs. actual damage validation and is willing to invest in manual building-by-building verification. Upon restart, reuse scripts and (intermediate data archived on TACC), and run computations on CRC/TACC/Colab rather than locally on the workstation.

## Hierarchy Rules (Set by Root Lead on 10-14; 5-level cap after migration)
- Do not open third-level sub-projects under this node; if subdivision is needed, use tasks within this node, or report to the parent node to open a peer second-level node.
- Only two hops remain downward: this node → bot → tool; task briefs must not allow tool bots to delegate further.
- Subtree lists are not grouped by parent node; the UI project tree is authoritative.

## Boundaries

# Task Brief · Wind-damage loss–wind-speed database Step 1: Batch Extraction and Accuracy of Storm Events Narratives (10-14)

Node: I Wind-damage loss–wind-speed database, parent node Data, CFD Models, and Observations (50648743). Executor: ideas.

## Objective
Determine whether "using large models to batch-extract structured loss–wind-speed records from NOAA Storm Events narratives" is worth continuing: how accurately each field is extracted, and how many records have wind speeds that are **not** inferred from damage (using damage-inferred wind speeds to validate a loss model is circular reasoning and must be separated).

## Data
- NOAA NCEI Storm Events bulk CSVs (official source, direct download): `StormEvents_details-ftp_v1.0_d<year>_c*.csv.gz` from https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/swdi/stormevents/csvfiles/, covering 2018–2023. Store downloads in a local WSL directory (do not place on the local disk), and write back only the sampled subset CSV (a few hundred rows) and results.
- Read-only borrow from the event track: (Storm Events 546 rows, including noaa_magnitude_type: EG 450, MG 94). In the thunderstorm wind sample, prioritize including 30–50 Texas four-city events that overlap with these event_ids to facilitate future alignment with the event track and Node H.
- Post-disaster reconnaissance reports (NWS DAT, StEER/DesignSafe, NIST) are only checked quickly for availability in this round: whether there is a publicly accessible bulk-download entry point, format, and license, summarized in one paragraph in the results; if unavailable, proceed with Storm Events only.

## Sample (~300 Records, in 3 Batches, ≤100 per Batch)
- Thunderstorm (Thunderstorm Wind) ~120; tropical cyclone (Hurricane/Typhoon, Tropical Storm) ~90; extratropical cyclone / synoptic-scale high wind (High Wind, taken from October–April, optionally excluding obvious downslope winds / dust storms) ~90.
- Select only records where EVENT_NARRATIVE is non-empty and mentions damage (or DAMAGE_PROPERTY>0); use stratified random sampling with a fixed random seed, and document the sampling script clearly.

## Field Table (Set by Lead; May Add to but Do Not Delete)
event_id; hazard (thunderstorm / tropical cyclone / extratropical); date_time_local; location (state, county/town, lat/lon if available); structure_type (e.g., single-family home, mobile home, commercial building, barn, utility pole/line, tree, vehicle, sign; multi-valued allowed); damage_description (verbatim quote from text); damage_severity (none / minor / moderate / major / destroyed, per narrative); wind_speed_value and unit (kt/mph, uniformly converted to m/s in a separate column); wind_speed_kind (gust / sustained); **wind_speed_source** (see below); wind_speed_source_quote (verbatim quote supporting the determination); instrument_or_site (e.g., ASOS station name, mesonet); EF/damage rating if mentioned.
Storm Events structured columns (MAGNITUDE, MAGNITUDE_TYPE, SOURCE, DAMAGE_PROPERTY) are retained alongside as reference columns; the model reads only the narrative and is compared against the structured columns afterward.

## Wind-Speed Source Determination Rules (Finalize Before Generating Prompts)
- Official definitions (NCEI *Storm Data Bulk Data Format*, verified by Lead): magnitude is wind speed (knots); magnitude_type: EG = Wind Estimated Gust, ES = Estimated Sustained Wind, MS = Measured Sustained Wind, MG = Measured Wind Gust. **"Estimated" does not specify the basis of estimation**, so type-E records still require inspecting the narrative.
- You need to look up: the exact wording and page numbers in NWS Directive 10-1605 (Storm Data Preparation) regarding how "estimated wind speeds" for thunderstorm winds / high winds are derived (and whether estimation from damage is permitted), and record them in the parameter source table.
- Categories: `measuredradar` (narrative explicitly states estimated from radar velocity); `damage_inferredobserver_estimate` (visual estimate by observer without mentioning damage basis); `estimated_unspecified` (type E and narrative does not state the basis); `none` (no wind speed).
- Report "share of non-damage-inferred wind speeds" at two tiers: strict = measured + radar; relaxed = plus observer_estimate. List estimated_unspecified separately without merging it into either side.

## Procedure
1. Write field table and determination rules → generate prompts (one JSON output template per record) → ` ≤100 prompts; do not launch batch runs while a review is running; do not use --force; if paused to yield, wait for it to resume.
2. Gold standard: manually annotate 20 records per hazard type (60 total) one by one according to the rules (without looking at Gemini output) as the accuracy benchmark; additionally, have Claude review a random 10% of each batch and record the agreement rate—if agreement for any category is <90%, document it and stop that category. Lead will spot-check the gold standard.
3. Calculate accuracy by field × hazard type; score numeric fields by "exact match / match after unit conversion"; score structure types by set matching (report both exact and partial match).

## Deliverables
- (field table + determination rules + parameter source table: source and page number for each definition); , batch prompts and answers jsonl, gold standard, and scripts
- : field accuracy table (field × hazard type), wind_speed_source confusion matrix, share of non-damage-inferred wind speeds (two tiers, by hazard type), consistency between model extraction and the structured column MAGNITUDE_TYPE, representative failure examples per category (2–3 verbatim texts each), and one paragraph on DAT/StEER availability

## Boundaries

items.text:
# Loss–Wind Speed Database Phase 1 Design (10-14)
Decision: Field table + six-class wind speed source taxonomy (measured / radar / damage_inferred / observer_estimate / estimated_unspecified / none); non-damage-inferred proportions reported in strict (measured+radar) and lenient (+observer) tiers; sample 2018–2023 ~300 records (thunderstorm 120, tropical cyclone 90, extratropical 90), prioritizing events in four Texas cities; gold standard 60 records + 10% Claude review per batch; 3 batches ≤100; 0 CU.
Why: EG/ES only states "estimated" without stating basis (NCEI Bulk Data Format, magnitude_type definition); narrative must be relied upon to distinguish damage-inferred, otherwise validating loss models becomes circular reasoning.
Cost of being wrong: If taxonomy is insufficiently granular, gold standard must be relabeled once (a few hours, 0 CU).

## 10-14 14:50 Supplementary Verdict
- "Do not start batches while reviews are running" refers only to those initiated by the Lab itself; reviews from other lines do not count, backed up by platform yield rules. Why: Reviews from other lines are running almost continuously, and following the literal wording would stall indefinitely. Cost: If crowding reviews from other lines, platform yield rules will pause automatically.
- S1 events are all in 2010–2017, conflicting with 2018–2023 (error in task brief) → Supplementary Batch 4: 40 TX4 thunderstorm records listed separately, not merged into main table. Cost: One additional batch of ~40 items.

items.title: Storm Events loss–wind-speed extraction r1 (10-14 19:05 EDT)
items.text:
# Storm Events Loss–Wind Speed Extraction r1 (10-14 19:05 EDT)

## Scope and Reproducibility

Official NCEI Storm Events details 2018–2023, fixed seed 20261014, initial screening by damage narrative / property damage stratified into 300 entries: Thunderstorm Wind 120, Tropical Cyclone 90, winter High Wind 90. Three batches of 100 entries each, –. Review gates lowest at 90%, 90%, 90% respectively, none below 90%; this is not overall accuracy. Time, location, peril, ID are external CSV fields, not evaluating the model. All scores are only for this stratified sample, not a nationwide overall estimate.

Raw CSV URL/hash see , sampling code , questions –, answers –, scoring code , summary code , machine statistics. Field definitions, interval scoring, and NWSI 10-1605 page numbers see . Wind speed values read narrative only; intervals retain lower and upper bounds, considered correct when falling within the gold standard interval during comparison; unit conversions must be consistent. Severity and type are operational definitions for the experiment, not official NWS damage ratings.

## Field Accuracy: Correct/20 (%), Gold Standard 60 Entries

| Field | Thunderstorm | Tropical | High Wind |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Damaged object exact set | 20/20 (100) | 13/20 (65) | 15/20 (75) |
| Damage severity | 17/20 (85) | 18/20 (90) | 16/20 (80) |
| Narrative wind speed value/range, unit | 20/20 (100) | 17/20 (85) | 19/20 (95) |
| gust/sustained/none | 20/20 (100) | 18/20 (90) | 20/20 (100) |
| Narrative wind speed source six-class | 20/20 (100) | 15/20 (75) | 19/20 (95) |
| Instrument/site exact string | 20/20 (100) | 12/20 (60) | 18/20 (90) |
| EF/damage rating | 20/20 (100) | 20/20 (100) | 20/20 (100) |
| Damage quote is original substring | 20/20 (100) | 20/20 (100) | 17/20 (85) |
| Source quote check | 20/20 (100) | 16/20 (80) | 19/20 (95) |

Object set partial hit (non-empty intersection or both empty) respectively 20/20, 19/20, 19/20; cannot replace exact set. Quote metric is only a verbatim original substring validity check, not semantic completeness or coverage; site metric is exact match of the raw string, which may misjudge “KGED” and “Delaware Coastal Airport (KGED)” as incorrect. For wind speed values, the 20 Thunderstorm gold standard entries had no narrative numerical values, sources were also all none, and EF was essentially null, so these 100% scores are “null values are easy to answer”, and must never be interpreted as positive-case extraction of wind speed or rare source identification capability. Tropical and High Wind gold standards had narrative numerical values in only 11/20 and 7/20 entries respectively; taking values within allowed ranges does not equal speed being exact to a single value.

## Source Confusion Matrix (Narrative-only; Row=Gold Standard, Column=Model; n=60)

| Ground Truth \ Prediction | none | estimated_unspecified | measured | damage_inferred | radar | observer_estimate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| none | 37 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| estimated_unspecified | 3 | 3 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| measured | 1 | 0 | 13 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| damage_inferred | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| radar | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| observer_estimate | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Thunderstorm source score 20/20 was entirely none; the sample had no gold standard positive cases for radar or observer wind estimation. The above matrix evaluates only the model reading narratives; the following proportions combine MAGNITUDE_TYPE under predefined rules, and the two must not be conflated.

## Whether Wind Speed Is Independent of Damage Inference

Strict = measured + radar; lenient adds observer_estimate; estimated_unspecified is not allocated to either side. Narrative speed count is the number of entries where the model extracted an on-site numerical value; structured count is the number of non-empty MAGNITUDE entries; denominator with speed is the union of both. Sources prioritize narrative criteria, and supplement measured according to MG/MS, and supplement estimated_unspecified for EG/ES with non-empty MAGNITUDE; if the narrative clearly indicates damage inference, it is not rewritten by EG. Strict figures are “candidate independent wind speeds under current classification”, not yet individually verified true measurements.

| Peril | Total / With Speed | Narrative Numerical | Structured MAGNITUDE | Strict / All; Strict / With Speed | Lenient / All; Lenient / With Speed | Unspecified Estimation Basis / With Speed | Explicit Damage Inference / With Speed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Thunderstorm | 120/120 | 13/120 (10.8%) | 120/120 (100%) | 3/120 (2.5%); 3/120 (2.5%) | 3/120 (2.5%); 3/120 (2.5%) | 116/120 | 1/120 |
| Tropical | 90/54 | 54/90 (60.0%) | 0/90 (0%) | 28/90 (31.1%); 26/54 (48.1%) | 28/90 (31.1%); 26/54 (48.1%) | 6/54 | 1/54 |
| High Wind | 90/90 | 53/90 (58.9%) | 90/90 (100%) | 48/90 (53.3%); 48/90 (53.3%) | 49/90 (54.4%); 49/90 (54.4%) | 38/90 | 3/90 |

In the full Tropical sample, 28 narratives mentioned instruments or measurements, but only 26 entries concurrently had explicit numerical wind speed; 28/90 cannot be treated as the quantity “usable for damage–numerical wind speed pairing”. Another 21 entries had narrative numerical values but sources were none (e.g., multiple wind speeds / locations not corresponding, extraction contradictions), requiring manual review. Among 117 Thunderstorm EG entries, only 1 had explicitly stated basis in the narrative (damage basis 1), the remaining 116 cannot be directly stated as damage-inferred; among 44 High Wind EG entries, basis could be clarified for 7 entries, of which damage basis was 1. NWSI 10-1605 Appendix A §46.3 A-69 (PDF 86) and §24 A-34 (PDF 51) permit estimating wind by professional judgment based on structural or tree damage, §46.4 Table A7 A-71 (PDF 88) provides a comparison guide, but cannot prove the actual method for each EG entry.

## Comparison with MAGNITUDE_TYPE (Main 300)

Only 210 entries in the main sample have MAGNITUDE_TYPE: Thunderstorm 117 EG / 3 MG; High Wind 44 EG / 43 MG / 2 MS / 1 ES; in Tropical 90 entries this column is empty. Joint classification: EG 153 estimated_unspecified, 2 damage_inferred, 1 observer_estimate, 5 measured; MG 44 measured, 2 damage_inferred; MS 2 measured, ES 1 estimated_unspecified. According to the expected binary broad categories by column (MG/MS measured, EG/ES estimated), 203/210 were consistent; the 7 cross-category entries were not automatic labeling errors: in EG, 5 narratives additionally mentioned instrument measurements; in MG, 2 narratives pointed to damage inference. For example, 70 mph in 997302 and 997286 was “damage representative of around 70 mph”, while the two rows of structured MG 56 kt may refer to another ASOS/AWOS wind speed of around 65 mph; 749604’s EG 50 kt and the airport 48 mph in the narrative were also not the same value, and narrative measurements cannot directly overwrite the structured column. 13/13 Thunderstorm entries with numerical records in both columns had conversion differences between narrative value and MAGNITUDE ≤5 mph, High Wind was 43/53; inconsistent records could also be peak values from different stations/events, and cannot be used to conclude model error. An event-location-time-observation correspondence must be established entry-by-entry before claiming “usable for validation”.

## Reviewable Failure Examples (Original text snippets; 2–3 entries per category)

- Damaged objects: 787020 “some downed trees with and power outages.” mistook power outages as physical damage to poles; 993000 had only “power outages” yet extracted power and damage; supplementary batch 648358 “some damage to the carports” overreported commercial (the apartment building itself was not stated as damaged).
- Severity: 1030387 “blew the metal roof off of an auto sales building” gold standard severe, model moderate; 999192 “Five power poles were completely broken off near the ground” gold standard severe, model destroyed; 1060311 “Power outages were reported” model moderate, but no physical damage, gold standard none.
- Wind speed value/object mismatch: 857631 “Wind gust of 59 knots (68 mph) was measured at Ocean Park. Wind gust of 51 knots (59 mph) was measured at Mesonet Station XCRE Creeds.” Model selected 59 mph, gold standard selected 68 per maximum observation at the event site; 924082 “Winds gusted between 35 and 45 mph ... A gust to 37 mph was recorded at the Thomaston AWOS” model 37, gold standard 45 per upper bound of range, involving different observation targets; 913730 “Based on the proxy observations ... likely reached near hurricane force (71 mph)” model treated inferred proxy value 71 as on-site wind speed, gold standard left blank. The rule for choosing one among multiple sources itself needs clarification.
- Source: 1058660 “highest wind reported ... a gust to 111 mph” had no instrument/estimation basis, gold standard estimated_unspecified, model none; 924057 “Winds gusted between 35 and 50 mph” gold standard estimated_unspecified, model none; 924082 model applied the source of AWOS measured 37 mph in the same paragraph to the 35–45 mph range. Radar used only for estimating timing does not count as a radar wind speed source.
- Quotes and sites: 907683 “at Delaware Coastal Airport (KGED)” gold standard site KGED, model full name (strings differ but semantically acceptable); 1051095 “St. Augustine C-man station SAUF1 ... a mesonet station” model generically termed C-man, dropping station number; 929398 narrative had only Broken Bow ASOS gust record and no damage, model quote was empty, the quote “accuracy” in this table cannot be taken as damage recall.

## NWS DAT / StEER Availability (Quick check only)

NWS DAT has public ArcGIS FeatureServer layers 0 (points), 1 (lines), 2 (polygons), layer REST JSON supports paginated queries, data documentation indicates preliminary survey data rather than Storm Data official statistics; service page nominally indicates single-request maxRecordCount 2000, suitable for paginated trial fetching by space-time/ID for Step 2, ID mapping with Storm Events, licensing details, and long-term stability have not yet been verified: <https://services.dat.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/nws_damageassessmenttoolkit/DamageViewer/FeatureServer>, <https://services.dat.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/nws_damageassessmenttoolkit/DamageViewer/FeatureServer/0?f=pjson>. StEER has public event-based published projects and Download Dataset on DesignSafe (e.g., Hurricane Ian PRJ-3709, DOI 10.17603/ds2-f1p1-ev62), potentially mixing PDFs, photos, tables; DesignSafe documentation indicates Published can be programmatically transferred via TAPIS API, but an unauthenticated unified cross-project batch record interface has not been verified, cannot state “already directly fetchable across the entire database via API”: <https://www.designsafe-ci.org/data/browser/public/designsafe.storage.published/PRJ-3709>, <https://designsafe-ci.org/user-guide/managingdata/datatransfer/>.

## Independent S1 Alignment Supplementary Batch (Not merged into main 300)

Main sample years do not overlap with S1’s 2010–2017. Using , official file SHA256 see , structure type 3/4 (75%) was below the 90% gate, this field did not pass, stopped treating it as a reliable field; remaining examined fields were 4/4, but positive cases were too few. S1 is only for future ID alignment by H-node, not included in gold standard 60 or main sample accuracy.

## One-Sentence Judgment and Step 2

Judgment: Worth continuing targeted Phase II validation, but r1 cannot directly build an “independent wind speed–structural damage” training/validation database; most EG sources are unspecified, Tropical source and damaged object accuracy were only 75%/65%, while Thunderstorm 100% source score mainly came from null-value questions.

Recommended for Phase II to first supplement hard gold standards with wind speed and clear sources / damage inference across three perils (especially Thunderstorm EG, MG), verify entry-by-entry whether narrative–MAGNITUDE are the same site/station/time, and use DAT survey layers as small-scale independent cross-validation; clarify rules for proxy observations, maximum/range selection, object damage vs. power outage only, then evaluate source precision/recall on symmetric positive and negative cases. The 40 S1 entries are only handed over to H-node for alignment, not merged into the main sample. Sources related to the use of public data are listed above; formal literature conclusions still require checking original texts/licenses.

items.text:
# Damage–Wind Speed Dataset r1 Conclusions and Step 2 (10-14 19:2x)
Basis: (line data, no literature basis; NWSI 10-1605 Appendix A §46.3 A-69/PDF 86 allows estimating wind by damage, retrieved via ideas, Lead has not personally verified original text).
Decision: Continue (status Exploring), Step 2 will no longer focus primarily on improving extraction accuracy, but directly test how many “co-located and simultaneous pairings of damage points and independent wind speeds” can be assembled: DAT public damage points × ASOS measurements (hurricanes plus H2 reconstruction). Simultaneously fix scoring unit conversion errors, supplement source positive case gold standards.
Why: r1 shows LLM extraction is not the bottleneck (errors mostly come from ambiguous rules and scoring criteria); the bottleneck is the scarcity of independent wind speeds (Thunderstorm 3/120) and that damage and wind speed in Storm Events are mostly not in the same location; H4 has proven that station reconstruction is essentially ineffective for thunderstorm winds.
Cost of being wrong: If the pairing trial shows too few pairings, this node will be Shelved, costing about half a day of bot time, 0 CU.
Lead check: 857631 being judged wrong was due to scoring not performing unit conversion (59 kt = 68 mph), sent back for fix.

# Storm Events r1b: Wind Speed Unit Conversion and Station Semantic Scoring Corrections

Scope remains the main sample of 300 entries, independent gold standard of 60 entries (20 each for Thunderstorm/Tropical/High Wind), not rerunning Gemini; original r1 report and preserved as-is. Recalculation executed, new machine output, 300/300 ok, 60/60 have scorable answers. Scoring script unifies mph, kt (knots), and m/s into m/s, judging single values by ±0.5 m/s; both ends of the gold standard interval are converted first, then each expanded by ±0.5 m/s. Non-empty speeds with unknown units cannot be judged correct. Station raw string exact tier left unchanged, additionally adding a semantic tier with mutual inclusion after lowercasing and whitespace removal (merely a loose alias approximation, not authoritative station ID resolution).

| Field (Correct/20) | Thunderstorm r1→r1b | Tropical r1→r1b | High Wind r1→r1b |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| gust/sustained/none | 20→20 | 18→18 | 20→20 |
| Source six-class | 20→20 | 15→15 | 19→19 |
| Station raw string exact | 20→20 | 12→12 | 18→18 |

| EF/damage rating | 20→20 | 20→20 | 20→20 |

| Source quote check | 20→20 | 16→16 | 19→19 |

For 857631, model’s 59 kt vs. gold standard’s 68 mph is within tolerance after conversion, now judged correct; no longer listed among failure examples. Other narrative wind speed failure examples from r1, 924082 (AWOS 37 mph vs. another wind speed of 35–45 mph) and 913730 (proxy inferred value), still need to be distinguished. Original r1 failure description for 857631 also stated model output 59 mph, which differed from the saved actual answer / instruction description; subject to and new machine scoring. For Thunderstorm 20 gold standard entries, speeds and sources were almost entirely null values; 20/20 cannot be treated as positive-case capability.

Conclusion: Error correction changes only one question for Tropical wind speed value; Tropical station semantic score increased from 12/20 to 15/20, remaining r1 conclusions unchanged. Source accuracy and co-located simultaneous independent wind speed pairing still await validation with r2 hard gold standards and DAT/IEM measurements.

items.text:
# DAT–IEM Spatiotemporal Candidate Pairing Trial (Part C of r2)

Sources: NWS DAT point layer <https://services.dat.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/nws_damageassessmenttoolkit/DamageViewer/FeatureServer/0>; IEM ASOS/AWOS METAR download <https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/download.phtml>, station metadata. Query URL / raw point attributes see , IEM query URL see , raw non-empty gust observations , point-by-point nearest pairing ; reproduction . No H reconstruction input, all candidates use IEM gust measurements; windspeed in DAT is estimated from damage, never serving as an independent observation. Sample consists of demo days selected based on visible DAT points, not representing a nationwide sample.

Filter DAT `stormdate` UTC window and bbox, hurricanes only `efscale='Tropical'`, thunderstorms only ; thus excluding concurrent EF tornadoes, cannot guarantee that all points for a hurricane were caused by that specific cyclone. Centered on the stormdate recorded for each DAT point, hurricane ±12 h, thunderstorm ±3 h, search for the nearest ASOS/AWOS station within 25 km that has non-empty METAR gust in the time window, unit gust=kt. Distance uses spherical Haversine, thresholds cumulative. Windows are experimental assumptions, not NWS DAT time precision guarantees; IEM low-QC as-is archive, instrument quality and damage mechanism matching have not yet been performed.

| Event / Regional Time Window | DAT Classified Points | DAT Inherent Wind Estimation Non-Empty | ≤5 km | ≤10 km | ≤25 km | DAT 00:00 UTC Timestamp | Actual Gust-Reporting Stations within 25 km |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ian 2022, FL 9/27–10/2 | 9 | 7 | 0 | 7 | 9 | 1 | 3 |
| Ida 2021, LA/MS/AL 8/28–8/31 | 122 | 3 | 10 | 40 | 98 | 38 | 6 |
| Dallas 2025-03-04 | 55 | 55 | 2 | 35 | 55 | 0 | 13 |
| Dallas 2019-06-16 | 37 | 37 | 0 | 34 | 37 | 0 | 10 |
| Houston 2024-05-16 | 20 | 20 | 0 | 2 | 20 | 0 | 8 |

Respective totals: Hurricane 131 points, ≤5/10/25 km candidates 10/47/107; Thunderstorm 112 points, 2/71/112. Treating DAT integer midnight timestamps as “potentially date-only” and excluding them, Ida candidates are 9/35/71 respectively, Ian 0/7/8; this is time sensitivity, not asserting all midnight points are invalid. Thunderstorm days were all non-midnight. The thunderstorm sample can find dozens of points at 10 km, but 112 thunderstorm points map to only a limited number of station-time independent combinations: 6 groups for Dallas 2025, 7 groups for Dallas 2019, 7 groups for Houston; multiple adjacent damage points share the same gust observation, and must never be written as 112 independent wind speed labels. At 5 km there are only 2 points. Hurricane Ida’s 98 candidates represent only 28 groups, Ian’s 9 candidates only 4 groups.

Initial assessment: The 25 km threshold can form dozens to hundreds of “spatially proximate candidates with instrument gusts”, 10 km also has dozens in Dallas thunderstorm / Ida; 5 km is barely sufficient. Wind speeds come from neighboring stations rather than damage points; spatiotemporal proximity does not equal wind speed at the same location and same elevation; mechanisms of damage from tornadoes / storm surge / different facilities must be excluded entry by entry; can only be used for exploration, not confirmed damage–independent wind speed ground-truth pairings. H reconstruction was not invoked in this round (reconstruction paired count 0), not counting reconstruction into the strict independent tier. If invoked subsequently, point-by-point record source, method/background, P1/P2/window, wind speed metric / averaging interval, distance to nearest input station, peril, hurricane RMW tier, and corresponding sample RMSE/bias according to §3 and H extension of , counted separately; thunderstorms do not use reconstruction, hurricane maximum wind selects Holland + residual rather than Kriging time series maximum.

## 10-14 21:26 EDT Supplement: Window Peaks and 2019–2024 Full Scale

Original had only nearest-time gust, now kept unchanged, newly added ; point-by-point results must not use nearest-time values to impersonate window peaks. Among the 37 pairings for Dallas 2019, 15 peaks were higher than nearest-time (maximum 30 kt higher), Dallas 2025 was 10/55 (maximum 39 kt), Houston was 16/20 (maximum 38 kt), Ian was 9/9 (median difference 77 kt, PGD’s 117 kt peak triggered anomaly flag), Ida was 98/98 (median difference 15 kt). Anomalies kept as-is, un-QC’d.

Full scrape of NWS DAT point layer exact efscale='TSTM/Wind' or 'Tropical', stormdate 2019-01-01 to 2025-01-01 UTC, counted by year × peril and sorted by objectid at 1000 entries per page: 18,434 entries, pagination count / uniqueness validation passed for 12 queries; stores raw attributes and query definitions. ; available stations within 25 km of DAT points 12,783 entries, another 5,651 entries with no nearby stations; 625 state–month combinations requiring query split into 636 requests with 15-station cap (individual raw non-empty gust CSVs in ). Among them, 1,533 nearby stations had no gusts within window, 11,250 entries paired with neighboring station gusts. IEM networks in other territories not covered; archive as-is, un-QC’d item by item. For each point, select only the nearest station within 25 km that “indeed had gusts in that window”, saving both nearest-time and window peak for that station; 10/25 km are cumulative thresholds. DAT times that are midnight may be date-level precision only, not yet excluded.

Point-by-point , table ; recorded by group , reproduction .

DAT windspeed is string, sentinel values like `-99`, are not treated as numeric. Layer metadata did not label unit for this field; table below **tentatively assumes** positive numbers are mph (comparable public NWS damage surveys write estimated peak wind as mph), IEM gust=kt multiplied by 1.150779448 converted to mph. DAT estimated wind originates from damage assessment, not independent observation; unit assumption awaits checking official DAT data dictionary, differences must not be used for calibration. Each group first takes the point-by-point median of (DAT mph − maximum METAR gust mph of the same station within that point’s window), then looks at P10 / median / P90 of differences across groups; multiple points sharing a group contribute only one group difference. Single-station windows for each point may differ, not forcibly regarding peak values from different windows in a group as a shared observation.

| Category / Threshold | All Station–Time Groups | DAT Numerically Comparable Groups | Difference P10 / Median / P90 (mph) | Positive Difference Groups |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TSTM/Wind ≤10 km | 667 | 663 | 10.0 / 37.0 / 58.2 | 644 |
| TSTM/Wind ≤25 km | 1,972 | 1,956 | 15.5 / 39.7 / 59.7 | 1,919 |
| Tropical ≤10 km | 35 | 5 | −36.2 / 19.4 / 41.8 | 3 |
| Tropical ≤25 km | 86 | 14 | −6.0 / 33.0 / 47.9 | 12 |

Positive difference is not proof of damage method “overestimation”: damage location and station separated by up to 25 km, peak time windows differ, strong gusts not necessarily reported by METAR, and DAT units unverified. Full scale >100 kt flag has 8 points (all being Ian/PGD’s 117 kt window peak), kept as-is; even fewer after deduplicating by station–time, cannot be called 8 independent anomalies. Strict co-located, simultaneous, and QC’d confirmed pairings remain 0 (not yet verified, does not mean nonexistent).

# Damage–Wind Speed Dataset r2 Full-Scale Conclusions: Thunderstorm Suspended, Hurricane Pilot First (10-14 21:3x)
Basis (line data, no literature basis): 21:26 supplementary section, .
- Narrative extraction: enriched source positive cases 66/70, measured recall 34/37, damage inference precision 16/17 → extraction is not the bottleneck.
- DAT 2019–2024 full scale 18,434 points: Thunderstorm 17,588 points, with neighboring station gusts ≤10 km 3,321 points, but only 667 independent station–time groups (≤25 km 1,972 groups); Tropical 846 points, ≤10 km only 35 groups (≤25 km 86 groups).
- Within thunderstorm groups, DAT damage-estimated wind was a median 37 mph higher than neighboring station window maximum gust (≤10 km, P10–P90 10–58, 644/663 groups positive; DAT units assumed as mph). Consistent with H4 (station reconstruction underestimates thunderstorm gust peaks by ~5 m/s, blending brings no gain): existing station networks typically fail to measure core thunderstorm winds causing damage, neighboring station gusts cannot serve as damage point wind speeds.
Decision: Thunderstorm suspended (not abandoned: preserve data and scripts as negative evidence that “station networks cannot measure damaging winds”); Step 3 conducts hurricane pilot first: DAT (+ available StEER) damage points × H2 Holland + residual reconstruction (annotated per protocol v1.1) × neighboring station measurements, across 2–3 events with many H2 land stations, to see if trends of damage severity with wind speed can be mapped by building type (e.g., FR12 single-family residences).
Why: Hurricanes have H2-usable reconstructed wind fields (strong wind stations 3.45/−0.66 m/s), whereas thunderstorms lack independent wind speeds on both ends.
Cost of being wrong: If hurricane pilot also fails to produce a trend, this node will be Shelved, costing ~half a day of bot time, 0 CU; thunderstorm track can be restarted in the future when high-density station networks (e.g., mesonets, private networks) or radar near-surface wind products become available.

# Loss–Wind Speed Database r3 Hurricane Pilot Conclusions (10-14 21:5x)
Basis (internal track data, no literature basis): , .
Results: All 416 DAT Tropical points for Ida/Idalia/Helene can have Holland+residual P2 reconstructed wind speeds recalculated at point locations according to the H2 method (protocol v1.1 fields complete); 89 FR12 residential points (75 for Ida), DOD and reconstructed gusts show no monotonic trend (Ida DOD1–4 medians 19.7/26.0/24.4/25.9 m/s, Spearman +0.08; DOD2 accounts for 60/75).
Lead interpretation: The lack of trend is primarily a design issue, not an issue with the reconstructed wind speeds—DAT only records damaged points (lacking undamaged buildings as denominators), DOD is concentrated at degree 2, confounded with non-wind mechanisms such as tree fall/water damage, and point timestamps partially only resolve to the date. Therefore, the "DAT + reconstructed wind speed" route cannot sort out the damage–wind speed relationship, and according to the gate set at r2, no further investment will be made in this sub-route.
Decision: Do not immediately shelve the entire node; first conduct a 0 CU data availability check: whether there is public hurricane damage data with coordinates and an "undamaged building" denominator (xBD/xView2 imagery building polygons including no-damage, USACE NSI building inventory, OpenFEMA housing inspections, StEER systematic sampling, NIST, etc.), and whether it can align with existing or calculable H2 reconstructed wind fields. If available → use it in Step 4; if none → node Shelved, with restart condition written as "appearance of public building-by-building damage data with denominators".
Why: Liang Hu designated this direction as a very important future direction on 10-14; before shelving, it should first be confirmed whether the bottleneck is merely the data denominator.
Cost of being wrong: One additional round of half-day bot time, 0 CU.
To be verified: Reconstructed gusts of 72–74 m/s at Idalia FR12 points are on the high side; need to check whether this is near-core extrapolation or truncation artifact.

## 10-14 22:1x Supplement: Step 4 Data Check Conclusions and Step 5
Basis: (Lead has verified CRASAR data card license: cc-by-4.0, 4,636 building labels for Idalia, 2,068 for Ida).
- Found public building-by-building data with undamaged denominators: CRASAR-U-DROIDs (drone imagery, building polygons + no/minor/major/destroyed, CC BY 4.0), overlapping with Ian/Ida/Idalia in H2; a patch in Steinhatchee for Idalia has 608 buildings (473 undamaged). xBD is non-commercial and overlaps have not been verified; NSI/OpenFEMA lack building-by-building damage labels.
- Idalia 72–74 m/s has been clarified: Near-core (1.1–1.2 times RMW) high background + approx. +16 m/s positive residual, not a truncation artifact, but the nearest input station is 25–28 km away, and locally it may be overestimated; not to be taken as ground truth at points.
Decision: Do not shelve the node; Step 5 will perform exploratory binning of "damage probability vs. reconstructed gust" for small CRASAR patches. Lead reminder: Both Steinhatchee and Cocodrie are storm surge disaster coasts, water damage must be excluded first; prioritize finding patches farther inland in CRASAR.
Cost: Approx. half a day of bot time, 0 CU; if the sample size is too small or there is no gradient after excluding water damage, this node is Shelved.

items.text:
# Storm Events Narrative Extraction Rules r1

Source: NOAA NCEI Storm Events 2018–2023 details CSV, yearly files and SHA256 see ; NWSI 10-1605 (2021) https://www.weather.gov/media/directives/010_pdfs/pd01016005curr.pdf. Model input is EVENT_NARRATIVE only (does not expose MAGNITUDE / MAGNITUDE_TYPE / SOURCE / DAMAGE_PROPERTY); location, time, event_id, and hazard are determined by structured columns in the output table, not guessed by the model.

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| event_id, hazard, date_time_local, location | External CSV EVENT_ID, categorized by EVENT_TYPE, BEGIN_DATE_TIME + CZ_TIMEZONE (local standard time, not converted to UTC), STATE/CZ_NAME/BEGIN_LOCATION/BEGIN_LAT/BEGIN_LON; does not evaluate model accuracy on these |
| structure_type | Set of objects explicitly damaged in the narrative; house, mobile_home, commercial, barn, power, tree, vehicle, sign, other; empty if unspecified. power includes pole/lines; power outage is not automatically equated to pole damage |
| damage_description | Excerpted sentence from the original narrative, must be an exact verbatim substring; empty if there is no damage sentence |
| damage_severity | none/minor/moderate/severe/destroyed; based solely on text, not back-inferred from property damage dollar values. If multiple locations, the most severe prevails; damaged but no degree indicated → moderate (operational assumption) |
| wind_speed_value, wind_speed_lower, wind_speed_upper, wind_speed_unit, wind_speed_mps | r1 legacy single-value fields are retained for comparability; r2 additionally adds a `wind_observations` array, with one entry for each on-site value/range in the narrative, listing all rather than taking the maximum, retaining station, timestamp, speed kind, source, and original evidence text. Ranges (e.g. 50–60 mph) retain lower and upper bounds, converted to m/s during scoring, counted as correct if falling within the range expanded by ±0.5 m/s; mph×0.44704, kt×0.514444. Forecasts/thresholds/general storm peak wind speeds are not listed as on-site observations; proxy observations are listed and tagged as proxy, not used for measured loss pairing |
| wind_speed_kind | gust/sustained/unknown/none; assigned only when the original text explicitly indicates gust or sustained |
| wind_speed_source | measured/radar/damage_inferred/observer_estimate/estimated_unspecified/none. Explicit instrument measurement measured; radar estimation radar; explicitly inferred from damage or EF/DI/DOD damage_inferred; visual observation by a person without mentioning damage observer_estimate; merely estimated with no basis estimated_unspecified; no on-site event wind speed or source in narrative none. When multiple sources exist, the source corresponding to the extracted wind speed prevails; when the original text is unclear, co-occurrence of damage and estimation is not automatically judged as damage_inferred |
| wind_speed_source_quote, instrument_or_site, ef_damage_rating | Exact verbatim excerpt supporting the source, instrument/station name, explicit EF/DI/DOD rating; empty if no basis |

r2 boundary: Wind speed from a proxy station/radar or elsewhere, even if measured, cannot be treated as measured at the damage location; if the original text explicitly states a proxy inference rather than a local value, tag `proxy=true` in `wind_observations`, and do not count as strict colocation pairing. When the narrative only has power outages (power outage) without actual physical damage to power lines, poles, transformers, or buildings, the set of damaged objects is empty, and severity=none; power outages cannot be treated as `powerprimary_source` is merely the selected wind speed source compatible with the six-category scoring, and cannot replace the entire table.

Post-processing additionally establishes `source_joined`: when model/human narrative source is none or estimated_unspecified, if MAGNITUDE_TYPE=MG/MS, classify as measured; if EG/ES and the record has structured MAGNITUDE, classify as estimated_unspecified; inference from damage cannot be presumed from EG/ES. In the narrative, explicit damage_inferred takes precedence over EG, but conflicts with MG/MS are flagged for review and not overwritten by default. In EG, count separately the number of cases where the narrative can explicitly confirm a basis (measured/radar/observer_estimate/damage_inferred) and the number of cases where a damage basis can be explicitly confirmed; EG + damage description only does not count. Two numerator tiers for non-damage: strict measured+radar; lenient adds observer_estimate. Denominators are reported both for all samples and for samples with structured or narrative wind speeds; estimated_unspecified is not included in any numerator. Occurrence rates of narrative wind speeds and non-empty rates of structured MAGNITUDE are reported separately by hazard type. The supplementary batch of 40 records from four cities for 2010–2017 S1 is reported independently of the main sample, and is not merged into the accuracy of the main 300.

## H Reconstructed Value Pairing Extension (C; Protocol v1.2 §3–4)

The current DAT–IEM small trial only uses IEM measured gusts and does not invoke H; the following fields are mandatory record-by-record only when H reconstructed values are actually ingested in the future, without using sample means from the protocol to impersonate predicted values at damage points. Reconstructed pairing and measured pairing are placed in separate tables and counted separately; reconstruction is not counted in the strict independent wind speed tier; thunderstorms do not use H reconstruction. Maximum wind for hurricane events uses Holland+residual kriging and must not take the maximum from ordinary kriging time histories; if ordinary kriging is used for hourly time histories, it must be noted that it is not used as an estimate of maximum wind.

| Field | Filling Method and Boundaries |
| --- | --- |
| wind_speed_source | `reconstructed`, must not be filled with `measured`; belongs only to pairing table extensions, does not alter the six-category narrative source label |
| reconstruction_method, background_field | Actual method and background field name; e.g. Holland+residual and the Holland field actually used, not guessing background version from method name |
| peak_definition, peak_window_start_utc, peak_window_end_utc | P1=prediction error at observed peak timestamp (applicable only to validation samples that have an observed peak timestamp); P2=maximum within the shared valid timestamp window, hurricane landfall ±12 h, extratropical regional peak ±12 h, thunderstorm ±3 h; when damage points have no anemometer, P1 peak truth must not be claimed; record specific UTC start/end and definition source |
| wind_quantity, averaging_interval | Sustained wind or gust; note that METAR hourly reports sustained wind is approx. 2 min, gust approx. 5 s; if using other archives where raw definitions have not been verified, mark as `unknown`, must not be mixed for comparison |
| nearest_input_station_km, event_type, hurricane_center_distance_km, hurricane_rmw_km, hurricane_rmw_bin | Record nearest distance to actual input station, event type; for hurricanes additionally record center distance, RMW, and `<11–3>3 RMW`, mark as `unknown` if center distance or RMW is unavailable, do not substitute with peripheral bin |
| validation_subset, sample_rmse_mps, sample_bias_mps | Only cite holdout sample values matching the method, wind quantity, peak definition, event type, and RMW/strong-wind subset; bias=prediction−observation; explicitly note "sample statistics, not point-by-point guarantee"; if not applicable, leave null and explain |
| colocated_independent | Fixed `false`, H reconstruction does not enter the strict independent tier; counted separately from measured neighbor-station candidates as well |
| reconstructed_raw, peak_correction_mps, peak_correction_version, reconstructed_corrected | `reconstructed_rawpeak_correction_mps` records the signed additive correction actually applied, filled with 0 rather than missing if uncorrected; `peak_correction_version` records `v1.2`; `reconstructed_corrected = reconstructed_raw + peak_correction_mps`. Corrected values are tagged as "reconstructed, non-measured, corrected (v1.2)"; zero-correction hurricane values should additionally be explicitly tagged as "no peak correction applied", without implying that additive correction improves accuracy |

Select correction values separately according to event type, wind quantity, method, and peak definition, prohibiting cross-category generalization. Protocol v1.2 §4: Recommended method P2 for synoptic sustained wind is +0.82 m/s (not P1 of §1); extratropical sustained wind OK fit is +1.46 m/s, gust OK fit is +1.38 m/s; thunderstorm sustained wind IDW is +3.25 m/s, gust OK fixed is +5.08 m/s (only four Dallas events, single-event residual bias can reach approx. ±2–3 m/s, rough estimate, and thunderstorm pairing in this trial still does not use reconstruction); hurricane Holland+residual sustained wind and gust are both not corrected ( §0–4; the protocol §1, §4 provide original evidence paths.

## H4/H2 Cross-Node Read-Only Pairing and Spatial Footprint (r2 Supplement)

Added point-by-point `footprint_context`: NOAA JetStream "Thunderstorm Hazards - Damaging Wind" "Microbursts and Macrobursts" (webpage without page numbers) gives microburst outflow diameter <4 km and downburst extent up to 10 km; Romanic, Taszarek, Brooks (2022), *Weather and Climate Extremes* 37:100474, abstract / journal page 1 gives 4 km boundary for horizontal scale of damaging wind between micro/macrobursts. Therefore, station distance to point ≤4 km is only spatially possible; 4–10 km has exceeded the diameter of a single microburst but macrobursts or gust fronts remain possible, and 10–25 km exceeds the typical range of a single downburst, so neighbor station peaks should not replace point peaks. DAT records are not confirmed point-by-point as downbursts: the above are merely scale risk labels, not event mechanism attributions; storm translation, station height/exposure, and time differences need separate verification.

Hurricane station–damage points require center distance and RMW at that timestamp to judge `<11–3>3 RMW`; if there is no RMW corresponding to the point, `rmw_bin=unknown`, and the RMW bin of an H2 neighbor station cannot impersonate the damage point bin. H2 `grid_*colocated_independent=false` (colocation and cotemporality not yet verified); reconstructions are listed separately and never counted in the strict independent tier. Thunderstorms only use H4 one-minute `gust_sknt` (5-second gust) and its pre-stored UTC window, without mixing hourly METAR, nor reconstructing; H2 tropical only reads the land station table, with gusts using IEM cached METAR hourly records, which cannot be directly compared with H4 minute records for peak-capturing capability.

## Parameter Source Table

| Definition | Source and Page Number | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local time | NWSI 10-1605 §2.3, text p.5 (PDF page 5): `Use local standard time in 24-hour clock throughout the year` | Retain CSV CZ_TIMEZONE as-is; do not calculate time zone on our own |
| Loss dollar amount estimate | NWSI §2.7, text p.11 (PDF page 11): may use actual estimates from insurance/qualified personnel, must not treat them as measured wind speeds | Do not use DAMAGE_PROPERTY to determine wind speed source |
| Thunderstorm damage wind estimation | NWSI Appendix A §46.3, A-69 (PDF page 86): `The Storm Data preparer exercises professional judgment to determine the estimated maximum wind value based on observed structural or tree damage.` | Indeed permits damage back-inference, but cannot treat all EG as damage back-inference |
| High wind damage wind estimation | NWSI Appendix A §24, A-34 (PDF page 51): `The Storm Data preparer exercises professional judgment to determine the estimated maximum wind value based on observed structural or tree damage.` | High wind can also be damage-inferred |
| Damage–wind speed reference table | NWSI Appendix A §46.4, A-71 (PDF page 88), Table A7 `Table for Estimating Wind Speed from Damage`; includes precautions on vegetation condition and soil moisture | The table is a guideline, not the actual source for each EG in this dataset |
| MG/MS/EG/ES | NWSI Appendix A §24 A-34–35, §46.3 A-70; NCEI Storm Data Bulk Data Format (verified in task description) | Only measured/estimated and gust/sustained, does not encode basis for estimation |
| DAT `windspeed` unit | FeatureServer point layer field metadata only labels String, providing no unit; Lab Lead sampled 500 points each starting from 2023 on 2026-10-14, EF1 86–110, EF2 97–135, EF3 136–165, consistent with EF mph ranges | **Presumed mph** from internal data consistency, unconfirmed by official dictionary; DAT belongs to damage inference and cannot serve as independent wind measurement. Differences converted to mph in old reports remain descriptive; if the original unit were actually kt, the same positive number would convert to a larger mph, shifting the overall DAT−neighbor station/model difference upward, but without guaranteeing that the sign of every single difference remains unchanged |
| Sampling, severity default grade, structural category, six-source priority | Operational rules (assumptions) of this trial; fixed seed=20261014 | Not given in literature, does not claim official definition; conduct source ambiguity review |
