# Loss–Wind Speed Database Step 2 r2 (10-14 21:06 EDT)

Conclusion: Narrative extraction enriched with positive source examples can continue to serve as a candidate generator, but cannot be directly regarded as strict colocated, cotemporal damage–independent wind speed data. 66/70 sources were correct across 70 hard samples; DAT damage points and neighbor stations with reported gusts at 10–25 km can form dozens to hundreds of candidates, very few at 5 km, and multiple points share a single station–time observation.

## A Scoring Fix (Delivered Early)

Subject to , ; main sample 300 records and original gold standard 60 records were not rerun. 59 kt and 68 mph are correct after conversion, tropical wind speed value score changed from 17/20 to 18/20; tropical station semantic mutual containment is 15/20, strict verbatim match remains 12/20. Thunderstorm gold standard 20 records are almost entirely null wind speed/source; original source 20/20 does not represent positive-example capability. The r1 report serves only as pre-correction comparison.

## B Enriched Hard Gold Standard: Six-Category Narrative Source Classification

70 records were selected from official NCEI Storm Events details outside the main 300 using a fixed seed: 20 thunderstorm EG values, 10 thunderstorm MG, 15 tropical stations, 10 High Wind stations, 15 damage wind estimates. Human annotation was based solely on narratives, not treating MAGNITUDE_TYPE as narrative source ground truth; input , `gemini-3.8-flash-high` output , machine results , passing the batch-by-batch <90% stop gate. Did not restart yielded processes or use `--force`.

| Gold Standard Source | Sample Count | Model Predicted Count | True Positives | Precision | Recall |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| measured | 37 | 34 | 34 | 34/34 = 100% | 34/37 = 91.9% |
| damage_inferred | 16 | 17 | 16 | 16/17 = 94.1% | 16/16 = 100% |
| estimated_unspecified | 15 | 17 | 14 | 14/17 = 82.4% | 14/15 = 93.3% |
| observer_estimate | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2/2 = 100% | 2/2 = 100% |
| radar | 0 | 0 | 0 | Incalculable | Incalculable |
| none | 0 | 0 | 0 | Incalculable | Incalculable |

Overall source 66/70 = 94.3%, applicable only to narrative positive examples intentionally enriched this time, and cannot be extrapolated to source occurrence rates in ordinary Storm Events. Source confusion matrix (rows human, columns model; order measured / damage_inferred / estimated_unspecified / observer_estimate / radar / none):

| Human＼Model | measured | damage_inferred | estimated_unspecified | observer_estimate | radar | none |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| measured | 34 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| damage_inferred | 0 | 16 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| estimated_unspecified | 0 | 1 | 14 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| observer_estimate | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| radar | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| none | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Failure cases (NCEI EVENT_NARRATIVE original text excerpts): 1078836 `A gust of 54 mph was reported at nearby Sacramento International Airport.` Human measured, model estimated_unspecified: although the airport wind report did not directly state measured, it does not equal measured at the damage point; 1015501 `An NWS damage survey found a couple of snapped large branches ... Winds were estimated to be 75 mph and time was estimated by radar.` Human estimated_unspecified, model damage_inferred: damage survey and wind estimation co-occurred, yet it was not explicitly stated to be based on damage; radar was only used for timing. 977217 `Wind gusts averaged between 35 and 50 knots. Wind gust of 45 knots (52 mph) was measured at WAL. Wind gust of 37 knots (43 mph) was measured at Parksley.` Human primary source measured, model primary source estimated_unspecified; however, the model's value-by-value array listed both measured stations alongside the preceding estimated speed range, indicating that a single primary_source obscures correct extraction of multiple values. Another case 1008617 narrative contains `The Broken Bow ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph at 457 pm CST.`, yet the model still marked the primary source as estimated_unspecified.

For multi-station multi-value 's `multi_case_audit`. This is merely sample returned count; human-paired gold standards have not been established value-by-value, and it cannot be claimed that recall for all stations and values has been verified; the model may misalign on range sentences, station aliases, or proxies. Station, timestamp, source, and excerpted sentence for each value must be retained; power outage alone is not recognized as physical damage, see .

## C Feasibility of Pairing DAT Damage Points–IEM Gusts

Read-only sources: NWS DAT FeatureServer point layer <https://services.dat.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/nws_damageassessmenttoolkit/DamageViewer/FeatureServer/0>; IEM ASOS/AWOS METAR query <https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/download.phtml>. Per URL, raw , . Points selected by DAT `efscale=Tropical` or and geographic time window; centered on the point's stormdate, hurricane ±12 h, thunderstorm ±3 h, finding the nearest station with non-empty METAR gust within 25 km, threshold cumulative; without point-by-point instrument QC or mechanism verification. DAT's built-in windspeed is a damage estimate and cannot be counted as an independent wind speed.

| Date/Region | DAT Points | DAT Estimated Wind Non-Empty | Neighbor Station Gust ≤5 km | ≤10 km | ≤25 km |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ian 2022, Florida | 9 | 7 | 0 | 7 | 9 |
| Ida 2021, LA/MS/AL | 122 | 3 | 10 | 40 | 98 |
| Dallas 2025-03-04 | 55 | 55 | 2 | 35 | 55 |
| Dallas 2019-06-16 | 37 | 37 | 0 | 34 | 37 |
| Houston 2024-05-16 | 20 | 20 | 0 | 2 | 20 |
| Hurricane Total | 131 | 10 | 10 | 47 | 107 |
| Thunderstorm Total | 112 | 112 | 2 | 71 | 112 |

38 DAT points for Ida are at 00:00 UTC, possibly having only date precision; after removing midnight timestamps, Ida ≤5/10/25 km candidates are 9/35/71, and Ian is 0/7/8; midnight cannot be uniformly judged as erroneous. The 25 km neighboring candidates for the 112 thunderstorm points correspond to only 6/7/7 station–time combinations for Dallas 2025/2019 and Houston, respectively; Ida's 98 candidates have only 28 groups, and Ian's 9 have only 4 groups. Multiple neighboring damage points sharing a single gust does not represent the same number of independent wind speed labels. Samples are selected DAT point days; time windows and distance thresholds are assumptions of this trial, not representative of the national total; hurricane categories do not guarantee that every point belongs to the specified cyclone, nor have storm surge/off-site facility mechanisms been excluded. The confirmed count of strict "damage point colocated and cotemporal with QC'd independent measurement" in this round is 0 (not verified record-by-record), which does not mean they do not exist.

H reconstruction was not invoked; reconstructed pairings are 0, separated from measured neighbor-station candidates and not entering the strict independent tier. When using H in the future, according to H protocol v1.1 §3, point-by-point recording in the fields listed in must include method, background, P1/P2 and window, wind quantity/averaging interval, distance to nearest input station, event type/RMW, and sample RMSE/bias of matching subsets; thunderstorms do not use reconstruction, and hurricane peak wind uses Holland+residual, not impersonated with the maximum of kriging time histories.

Next steps: Deduplicate by event/station–time among 10 km neighbor-station candidates and conduct human checks on instrument QC, DAT temporal precision, and damage mechanisms; simultaneously create value-by-value, station-by-station human gold standards for multi-station multi-value records (including proxy, radar, and source-less), then evaluate recall and pairing independence. Candidates can now be expanded, but 118 10 km candidates cannot be handed directly to design loads as ground truth.

## C Supplement: Window Peak Gust and Full-Scale Size (10-14 21:26 EDT)

Nearest-timestamp gusts from the original small trial have added , in .

All 18,434 points across both categories for 2019–2024 in the NWS DAT point layer were verified with pagination; IEM ASOS/AWOS (50 states + PR) searched point-by-point for the nearest spatial station within ≤25 km with gusts within ±3 h for thunderstorm and ±12 h for Tropical. Each cell in the table below represents "paired DAT points / station–time groups deduplicated by network, station, and nearest wind reporting UTC timestamp"; see , for full annual, hazard-specific breakdowns and query logs.

| DAT Hazard | Point Layer Total | ≤10 km Points / Groups | ≤25 km Points / Groups |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TSTM/Wind | 17,588 | 3,321 / 667 | 10,824 / 1,972 |
| Tropical | 846 | 156 / 35 | 426 / 86 |

Point-by-point lists nearest-timestamp and window-peak wind speeds (kt), timestamps, and differences; group-by-group . Positive DAT wind speeds are damage estimates, not independent measurements; the field itself is a string without units labeled, currently **presumed mph** from internal data consistency (Lab Lead sampled 500 points each starting from 2023 on 10-14: EF1 86–110, EF2 97–135, EF3 136–165, consistent with EF mph ranges; not an official dictionary); IEM gust is multiplied by 1.150779448 to convert to mph; negative sentinels and N/A are excluded. Within groups, first take the median difference across points of "DAT estimated wind − neighbor station maximum gust in point window", then compile group difference distributions: for TSTM/Wind ≤10 km 663 comparable groups, P10/median/P90 are +10.0/+37.0/+58.2 mph, and for ≤25 km 1,956 groups are +15.5/+39.7/+59.7; Tropical has only 5 / 14 comparable groups, with medians of +19.4 / +33.0 mph, too few to generalize. If actually in kt, DAT estimated wind converted to mph would be larger, leaving the direction of the dominant positive TSTM differences unchanged, but without guaranteeing that the sign of every single difference remains unchanged; official unit dictionary has still not been found. Confounding from spatial distance, windows, and station missing reports renders differences descriptive only, not causal estimates of damage wind estimation bias. Peaks >100 kt are retained and tagged; 8 points come from the same Ian/PGD peak, not 8 independent observations. Strict QC'd colocated and cotemporal truth pairs are still unverified (currently confirmed 0); 667 or 1,972 groups cannot be treated as real independent sample sizes.

New reproduction scripts , ; old r2 data and results are retained, the above is an additional supplement only. Next steps prioritize checking DAT wind speed units, PGD extremes, and DAT midnight temporal precision, performing storm-stratified deduplication and human QC on ≤10 km station–time groups before determining usable scale.

## C Supplement: Read-Only Reuse of H4 Dallas Days and H2 Hurricanes (10-14 21:30 EDT)

Added , ; 2025 DAT raw point pagination files. Existing 2019–2024 full tables and the aforementioned small trial do not cover this, and this subset is not added to the national scale (which would double-count). H4 directly reads the query origins of the five-day , and , no longer downloading one-minute data. In , H2 land scoring stations are 110 for Idalia and 95 for Helene; although Beryl has 109 stations, its corresponding DAT Tropical point query for 2024-07-07 to 07-11 returned 0, so the first two events were chosen, reading only the H2 land station table and cached IEM METAR (not invoking H2 predictions). DAT points for the two H2 events are filtered solely by date and state bounds, with no guarantee that they belong to the specified hurricane.

| Subset / DAT UTC Day | DAT Points (Study Area) | H4/H2 Station List | Measured Neighbor-Station Candidates ≤5 km Points / Station–Time Groups | ≤10 km | ≤25 km | Reconstructed Points |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| H4 2024-05-28 | 0 | 14 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0 |
| H4 2024-06-01 | 0 | 14 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0 |
| H4 2025-03-04 | 83 | 14 | 2/2 | 3/3 | 52/9 | 0 |
| H4 2025-06-09 | 33 | 14 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0 |
| H4 2025-07-09 | 0 | 14 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0 |
| H2 Idalia (2023-08-28 to 09-02) | 18 | 128 | 4/3 | 5/3 | 8/4 | 0 |
| H2 Helene (2024-09-25 to 09-30) | 276 | 145 | 49/3 | 78/5 | 138/9 | 0 |

H4 DAT takes Texas 31.5–34°N, 95.5–98.5°W, UTC day; H4's pre-stored regional peak ±3 h window contains non-empty, 0–150 kt one-minute `gust_sknt`, further requiring DAT point time ±3 h; H2 uses event dates, corresponding state geographic bounds, and H2 land stations with non-empty METAR gust in the original full IEM monthly cache, with DAT point time ±12 h. Each point takes the nearest station within 25 km having wind speed in the window, additionally listing the nearest-timestamp gust, the station window peak, and the difference; grouping key remains station ID + nearest gust valid timestamp. The 83 points for H4 2025-03-04 are more than the 55 points in the earlier Dallas small trial because filtering here is by the H4 study area rather than the earlier Dallas bounding box; 10 km pairings are only 3 points, fewer than the 35 points in earlier hourly METAR, and cannot be conflated as the same support set (one-minute archive missing reports, H4 window limitations, and different station cleaning). DAT being 0 in this box for the two 2024 days does not mean Storm Events had no thunderstorms; 2025-07-09 DAT had 0 TSTM/Wind nationwide on that day. On 2025-06-09 there were 33 points in the box, but 0 pairings within the aforementioned H4 minute window / 25 km. Raw DAT point counts are unique by ID, and output 198 point-station records are unique; counts see JSON.

Footprint scale source: NOAA JetStream "Thunderstorm Hazards - Damaging Wind" "Microbursts and Macrobursts" (webpage without page numbers) gives microburst diameter <4 km, general downburst lateral extent up to 10 km; Romanic, Taszarek, Brooks (2022), *Weather and Climate Extremes* 37:100474, abstract / journal page 1 likewise gives 4 km boundary between micro/macro, DOI https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wace.2022.100474. This is not mechanism certification for DAT points: among the 52 25 km candidates for H4 March, point-by-point tags by distance to station are: ≤4 km 1, 4–10 km 2, 10–25 km 49; more distant neighbor station peaks cannot be converted without error into point-location wind speeds. Hurricane spatial correlation should compare real-time center distance/RMW at that point; `rmw_ratio` on the H2 station grid is not the RMW of the DAT point, so `rmw_bin=unknown` this time, without inventing a peripheral bin. H2 `grid_*` only provides Holland/background at station locations, not at DAT point locations; station reconstructed values were not moved to damage points, nor was point-by-point Holland+residual run, resulting in 0 reconstructed pairings. If separate point-by-point reconstruction is to be performed, strictly record according to H v1.1 §3 the P2/landfall window, method/background, gust 5 s or sustained approx. 2 min, distance to input station, RMW bin, and matching holdout subset RMSE/bias; gusts and sustained winds at strong wind stations must not be mixed. For H v1.1 strong wind station sustained wind P2 Holland+residual, sample RMSE/bias is 3.45/−0.66 m/s; near-core underestimation and single-event bias must both be listed separately; the maximum of ordinary kriging time histories cannot substitute, nor are reconstructions counted as strict independent wind speeds.

This supplement only verifies data reuse and candidate scale: neighbor-station measurements have also not undergone review for instrument quality, colocation and cotemporality, storm attribution, and damage mechanism, with strict independent ground truth confirmations remaining 0. The earlier full 2019–2024 annual by-hazard table remains valid, but belongs to "station–time group candidates N", not an independent statistical sample size; H4 dates include 2025 and must not be merged into this full-volume denominator. Next steps prioritize conducting human spatio-temporal/instrument QC on the three H4 March ≤10 km points and the three Helene ≤5 km groups, before considering truly generating P2 Holland+residual at DAT point locations according to H v1.1, without using H2 station grid values as make-weight.

# Hurricane Pilot r3 Supplement: Helene Prioritization and Near-Station Group Human Check (2026-10-14)

This page is merged into Step 3, following the revised version of , .

## Verification of Helene ≤10 km Neighbor-Station Groups

Filtering H2_HELENE and distance_km≤10 from , then grouping by `(station, nearest_utc)`, and using to verify raw DAT damage and model fields: exactly 78 points belong to the 5 groups in the table below. Distances are ranges within the group; station gusts are raw archive values for that station in that window, without instrument quality control or proof of identical location and identical hour.

| Group (UTC) | DAT Points | Point-to-Station Distance km | Neighbor Station Gust kt | Main Damage Type / Verification |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| GA:AZE 09-27 04:35 | 16 | 5.787–9.766 | 34 | Primarily trees; all 16 points have DAT time 09:00, 04:35 cannot be treated as instantaneous damage wind; model sustained peak RMW bin `<1`. Example ID 4240438 is uprooted hardwood (DOD 3), point model gust 39.185 m/s, peak time 07:00. |
| GA:DNL 09-27 07:31 | 48 | 1.274–7.140 | 40 | Primarily trees; all 48 points have DAT time 09:35. The same station-time is repeatedly matched to 48 points and cannot count as 48 independent observations. ID 4234502 note is "Hardwood trees down on house. Estimated 100+ mph", where the estimate in its `windspeed`/note does not count as independent wind; model peak gust 32.479 m/s (10:00), 18.994 km to nearest input station. |
| GA:HQU 09-27 08:55 | 1 | 9.565 | 52 | ID 4238509: Snapped softwood trunk, note "Estimated 80+ mph"; DAT time 10:15; model peak gust 33.698 m/s (10:00), RMW bin `<1`. |
| GA:SBO 09-27 07:15 | 2 | 2.525–2.536 | 47 | Both points are softwood trees; DAT time 09:30. ID 4240478 DOD 1, model peak gust 38.446 m/s (09:00), nearest model input station 82.564 km, exceeding the verified distance range of the H protocol and cannot be used to calibrate local point values. |
| GA:VDI 09-27 05:55 | 11 | 1.680–9.606 | 44 | Primarily trees; all 11 points have DAT time 09:30. ID 4240473 snapped softwood trunk (DOD 4), model peak gust 40.355 m/s (08:00). |

The concentrated identical timestamps suggest these may be batch survey/entry times; without DAT field definitions and point-by-point raw survey forms, it cannot be confirmed whether these are actual damage occurrence times. None of the 5 groups are colocated and cotemporal ground-truth groups. FR12 for Helene has only 10 points, and the original report's assessment of no apparent monotonic trend still holds; the 78 near-station tree and miscellaneous points cannot be substituted as residential trend samples.

## Dallas 2025-03-04 Three-Point Verification (Old H4 Comparison Only; Thunderstorms No Longer Expanded)

The three ≤10 km records from were compared record-by-record with notes in the cached official DAT : ID 4368928, FR12, DAL 7.435 km, DAT 11:27, nearest-timestamp gust 19 kt, window maximum 68 kt (11:34), note "Shingle damage to a few homes"; ID 4368929, warehouse WHB, DAL 4.228 km, DAT 11:30, nearest 25 kt, maximum 68 kt (11:34), note "Debris from roof blown eastward to Mockingbird Rd. Traffic signals out in area."; ID 4383721, manufactured home single-wide MHSW, TKI 3.203 km, DAT 11:47, nearest 39 kt (11:45), maximum 55 kt, note contains "radar indicated straight line winds around 95 mph ... base velocity of 82 knots at 1000 ft". The last item is radar-inferred rather than measured at a surface station and cannot be conflated into the independent wind speed side. The first two points share the same DAL window maximum observation and do not equal two independent extreme values. Microburst scale background see the NWS `Downbursts` link in the original report (webpage without page numbers); although the three points are spatially close, local gusts are not guaranteed to appear at the observation station.

## Judgment and Follow-up

Helene has the largest number of near-station points and was prioritized for screening, but 78 points correspond to only 5 neighbor-station timestamps, and are primarily trees; Ida's 75 FR12 points are superior to Helene's 10 points, suitable for the next round of building type/mechanism spot checks; Idalia has only 4 FR12 points, used as a supplement. That all 416 points in original r3 can be reconstructed does not equate to 416 independent measured pairs. DAT date/timestamp, station as-is quality, peak time misalignment, RMW near-core, and >80 km input station distances must all be checked point-by-point; undamaged buildings must be added to estimate damage probability. Currently, neither can a reliable FR12 monotonic trend be fitted, nor can reconstructed wind speeds be treated as strict independent measurements. DAT `windspeed` is presumed mph from internal spot checks of consistency by Lead on 10-14, but official field definitions have not been found; mph differences in the original report remain descriptive comparisons only, see for details.

Sources: NWS DAT FeatureServer point layer <https://services.dat.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/nws_damageassessmenttoolkit/DamageViewer/FeatureServer/0>; internal track (official response cache), (IEM and DAT pairing), (DAT fields and H2 point-location reconstruction), methods and limitations see in detail , H station reconstruction protocol v1.1 §3. DAT sources have been listed, and this page contains no new external data sources.

# Loss–Wind Speed Database (I) Shelved (10-14 22:4x)
Basis (track data, no literature basis): , .
## Conclusion
- Large model extraction is usable: all 300 Storm Events narratives succeeded, three batches of 10% review ≥90%; enriched source positive cases 66/70, measured recall 34/37, damage-inferred precision 16/17 — reliably separating wind speeds "inferred from damage".
- Stuck on independent wind speed and denominators, not on large models:
 - Thunderstorms: narratives confirmed measured in only 3/120; for DAT 2019–2024 thunderstorm points ≤10 km neighboring stations, there are only 667 independent station-hour groups; within the groups, DAT damage-estimated wind is a median of 37 mph higher than the neighboring station window maximum gust (97% positive); H4 station reconstruction is powerless for thunderstorm peaks → station networks cannot measure damage core winds.
 - Hurricanes: 416 DAT points can have H2 reconstructed wind speeds recalculated at the points, but DAT only has damaged points, with no trend across 89 FR12 points (Spearman +0.08).
 - CRASAR drone building-by-building labels with denominators (CC BY 4.0) cover small areas (a single area's reconstructed gust span is only 0.3 m/s, smaller than H2 error 3–4.5 m/s) and are all in storm surge zones; after conservatively excluding water damage, 0 buildings are usable; after relaxing, 48 buildings, 4 clusters, no major damage.
## Decision
Shelve this node according to the gate set during r2/r3 (shelve if no gradient or insufficient samples). Why: All three feasible public data routes have been tried; what is missing is building-by-building damage data that "spans wide wind speed bands, excludes water damage, and has denominators" as well as independent wind speeds for thunderstorms, which cannot be remedied by doing more small experiments. Cost of being wrong: Restarting only requires reusing existing scripts and field rules, 0 CU.
## Restart Conditions (Any)
1. Inland building-by-building damage data across wide wind speed bands (including undamaged) with post-event inundation verification: such as large-scale post-disaster aerial photography (NOAA emergency imagery) + building damage classification, systematically sampled StEER/NIST inland surveys, or insurance/FEMA address-level data (data agreement required, must be decided by Liang Hu).
2. Thunderstorms: Node H's H6 proves that radar near-surface wind can serve as an independent wind speed source.
3. Specific users require validation samples of "design wind speed vs. actual damage" and are willing to invest in manual building-by-building verification (promotion scale).
## What is Left Reusable
Field rules and six-category wind speed sources (including H protocol v1.2 fields), Storm Events extraction and review scripts, DAT × IEM full pairing and station-hour deduplication, DAT point H2 recalculation script, CRASAR reading and water damage screening script.

## 10-14 23:0x Correction: Idalia Near-Core Reconstructed Values Are Extrapolation Distortions
Basis: NHC TCR AL102023 Idalia (Cangialosi & Alaka, 2024-02-13), PDF page 5 "The estimated peak intensity at landfall is 100 kt"; PDF page 6 "highest reported wind gust was 74 kt in Perry", RMW 10 n mi (near PDF page 7, surge section). r3 Idalia FR12 three points (3811111/3811125/3811127) reconstructed **sustained winds** of 55.8–57.1 m/s (approx. 108–111 kt, H2 approx. 2 min definition), 1.10–1.20 RMW from the center, higher than the landfall intensity of 100 kt (approx. 51.4 m/s, 1 min definition, 2 min should be lower) → judged as **extrapolation distortion**, not "possible local overestimation"; corresponding gusts of 72.8–74.5 m/s are likewise invalidated. r5 Idalia Jena area sustained winds of 39.4–45.9 m/s (approx. 2.1 RMW, lower than landfall intensity), gusts of 55.9–60.7 m/s much higher than measured maximum gust of 74 kt (approx. 38 m/s) but with no nearby stations, labeled "unverified". Ian Harlem Heights is at 1.02–1.05 RMW, close to the core edge, likewise labeled "near-core, unverified".
Handling: Near-core (<1 RMW and edge-hugging ~1.0–1.2 RMW) bins are individually labeled "unverified" and do not enter the main gradient assessment; main conclusions use only 1–3 RMW and beyond. This node has been shelved; this correction does not change the shelving conclusion, only modifies the presentation of evidence.

# Loss–Wind Speed Database r3: DAT Hurricane Points × H2 Point Reconstructions (2026-10-14)

## One-Sentence Judgment
In this DAT sample where only damaged instances are entered into the database, H2 reconstructed peak winds can be paired to the points, but residential damage degree for FR12 has no discernible monotonic trend with reconstructed gusts; therefore, it is worthy of point-by-point screening/quality control, but insufficient to fit damage–wind speed functions or claim independent measured relationships. Reconstructions are not point measurements, and DAT's built-in estimated winds are not independent wind speeds.

## Reproducible Artifacts and Per-Point Table
 stores per-point records and screening IDs;  summarizes;  is the residential scatter and binning plot; `pilot_hurricane_r3.pydoddod_txtdamage_txt` are all from the original API; original r2 full ID list; H2 source code ,  and existing `grid_*_expanded.csv.gz`, H protocol see §3. H and IEM files were not rewritten.

## Events, Algorithms, and Calibers
Select H2-tested events Ida (2021, priority), Idalia (2023), Helene (2024): screen points by DAT `efscale=Tropical`, dates near the event, and wide bounding boxes, rather than by DAT lines 21–67,  lines 27–67; the 40-station cap is an **assumption** for local residuals and computational load in this run, differing from H2's leave-one-out scoring support set across the entire valid station set.

Sustained winds and gusts come from different residuals / different peak times; sustained winds are compared with METAR ~2-minute mean winds, while gusts are compared according to H2's 5-second assumption; H2's original 500 m reference height, 2-minute/5-second, and land exposure conversions are all assumptions rather than DAT product definitions (H protocol §2). The per-point table provides distance to the nearest valid input station, peak-time distance-to-center/RMW bin, and leave-one-out station P2 sample RMSE/bias (m/s, not a per-point guarantee) for H2 using the same method for each event. For instance, Ida high-wind station / near-eye samples cannot be represented by the near-zero bias across all stations. Predicted peaks carry underestimation risks, especially in strong winds / near the core; station model errors, missing reports, and unverified distant station extrapolations may alter the wind speed axis. DAT `stormdate` date precision is unknown; some midnight records are treated as full-day time without forcing instantaneous interpretation.

The neighboring station measured column is independent of the model reconstructed column: using r2-cached IEM ASOS/AWOS METARs, reporting that station's window peak based on the nearest station within DAT time ±12 h and distance ≤10 km (taking maximum gust if distances are identical); IEM is taken as-is without instrument, peak, reporting time, storm attribution, or colocation audits. DAT `windspeed` is strictly used as a damage description throughout. The NWS FeatureServer field table only gives `String` for this field without specifying units; on 10-14, Lab Lead sampled 500 points each from 2023 onward, finding EF1 86–110, EF2 97–135, EF3 136–165, matching EF mph intervals; thus, the comparison column **presumes mph from data internal consistency** (m/s × 2.2369362921), not confirmed by an official data dictionary, and cannot serve as a quantitative calibration conclusion. If actually in kt, the differences between DAT and model would shift upward overall, and the sign of each difference cannot be guaranteed to remain unchanged. Non-numeric and -99 do not participate in comparisons. <https://services.dat.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/nws_damageassessmenttoolkit/DamageViewer/FeatureServer/0>

| Event | DAT Tropical Points / Reconstructible | FR12 (Numeric DOD Available) | Neighboring Station Gust Candidates ≤10 km | DAT Positive Wind Speeds Comparable (Presumed Unit mph) | Median Difference of DAT Estimated Wind − Reconstructed Gust, Presumed mph | FR12 DOD–Reconstructed Gust Spearman (Descriptive) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ida | 122/122 | 75 | 40 | 3 | +24.00 | +0.083 |
| Idalia | 18/18 | 4 | 5 | 10 | −47.31 | −0.738 (n=4 has no inferential value) |
| Helene | 276/276 | 10 | 78 | 11 | +8.32 | +0.052 |
| Total | 416/416 | 89 | 123 | 24 | Do not pool cross-event differences | Do not pool cross-event correlations |

The above numbers are recalculated from the per-point table by ; when mixing the three events, intensity, housing stock, and survey selection bias differ, so point counts cannot be equated to independent statistical samples. For Ida FR12, DOD 2 accounts for 60/75; its median reconstructed gusts in m/s for DOD 1/2/3/4 are 19.71 / 25.99 / 24.36 / 25.91, respectively, which is non-monotonic. Helene corresponding DOD 1/2/4 are 33.51 / 33.24 / 34.12 (n=10), Idalia DOD 1/2/4 are 74.33 / 38.77 / 72.78 (n=4); these are not damage threshold estimates. All points are already damaged, lacking undamaged buildings as denominators; bubble numbers in the figure are damaged point counts, not damage probabilities; points in the same survey cluster are highly correlated. FR12 DOD is only a rating within a building type and cannot be mixed across different DIs as a single numeric damage scale.

## Limitations, StEER, and Next Steps
DAT does not guarantee hazard attribution purely to wind: tree falls on houses, rain/waves/flooding, and differences in building age and construction have not been audited point by point. 12/75 Ida FR12 points have times of 00:00 UTC, possibly preserving only the date; these must not be forcibly co-registered to specific hours. For Helene FR12, the median distance to the nearest model input station is 61.56 km, and distance errors >80 km in the H protocol are unverified; Idalia FR12 point counts are too small and local extremes are relatively high, so background and survey times should be spot-checked first. Performing regression directly across all damaged points incurs selection bias.

StEER's Ida report and Idalia DesignSafe project web page are publicly available: <https://doi.org/10.17603/ds2-w6km-fe51>, <https://www.designsafe-ci.org/data/browser/public/designsafe.storage.published/PRJ-4123>. In this round, no batch table with building-by-building coordinates + DOD that can be obtained directly without login and with clear fields was verified, so StEER points were not fabricated; only DAT was used. StEER materials cannot automatically be regarded as independent wind speed observations.

The previous thunderstorm step is put on hold. The NWS description of microburst scales is approx. <4 km (NWS `Downbursts` web page, no print page number: <https://www.weather.gov/ohx/downbursts>); this serves as scale context for general mechanisms rather than downburst attribution for any single DAT point. Neighboring station thunderstorm winds at 10–25 km in r2 cannot be equated to core winds; specific storms could also be gust fronts/macrobursts, requiring mechanism verification.

Step four recommendations: First manually spot-check the 75 Ida FR12 points (especially duplicate coordinates, 00:00 UTC, DOD text, and housing/water damage mechanisms), checking stormdate and H2 station peak/near-eye residuals point by point; supplement exposure/undamaged buildings as well as construction era, stratifying by building and survey cluster; then decide whether to add StEER building-by-building public tables or expand to hurricanes with clear storm attribution. Although DAT `windspeed` is presumed to be mph based on internal consistency, an official data dictionary and quality control bounds are still needed to quantitatively interpret the estimated wind − reconstructed wind speed difference. Reconstructed points cannot enter the strict "independent measured" category.

Parameter sources: P2 ±12 h, RMW bins, and scoring criteria are H v1.1 §0/§1/§3 (subsequent v1.2 §4 does not calibrate hurricane Holland + residual); 75 km, 0.08, and H08 original parameters are H2 metadata and  output comes with this verification.

## Correction: Idalia Near-Core Extrapolated Values Invalidated (Historical Numbers Retained Above)
NHC Idalia Tropical Cyclone Report AL102023 page 5 (report body page number; PDF page number may differ) gives a maximum sustained wind estimate at landfall of 100 kt, approx. 51.4 m/s; page 6 gives Perry's measured maximum gust of 74 kt. In the original per-point table, the reconstructed sustained winds for Idalia FR12 DAT objectids 3811111, 3811125, and 3811127 were 55.8–57.1 m/s, unexpectedly exceeding NHC's landfall intensity estimate; the H2 sustained winds and corresponding peak wind speed interpretations for these three near-core points are uniformly designated as **extrapolation distortion, invalidated**, and cannot be used for damage–wind speed trends or physical interpretations of DAT estimated wind differences. The previously mentioned 416/416 pairing count, Idalia FR12 correlations/bins, and aggregate differences merely retain historical calculation traces and are not valid point wind speed evidence; original numbers were not recalculated or overwritten. Perry's 74 kt is a gust from another station and is not directly compared quantity-for-quantity with the sustained winds at the three points. Original report: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/AL102023_Idalia.pdf.

# 损失–风速库 r4：公开逐栋损伤分母数据可得性核查（2026-10-14）

## 判定
找到可直接做下一轮小样本配对的公开数据：CRASAR-U-DROIDs，优先 Ida/Idalia 内陆风损较清楚的局部影像覆盖区；它的 JSON 有建筑多边形 EPSG:4326、`building_id` 和 `no damageminor damagemajor damagedestroyed` 等标签，许可 CC BY 4.0，无需批量下载影像，也无需特殊授权。与 H2 Ida、Idalia、Ian 三场重合；但这是灾后影像覆盖内的“可见无损”分母，不是整个县的建筑存量或地面确认的零损伤；未核风、洪、浪致损的归因。先做小片区去重/机制审核和风速重建，不能直接当总体脆弱性曲线。[1][9]

## 候选数据表（“可用”仅为无特殊授权读取元数据/小文件，不代表能直接拟合）

| xBD/xView2 [2] | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0，非商用 | 老版公开灾害集含飓风案例；本次未核官方逐灾清单和 Ida/Ian 收录，**不主张有重合** | 建筑多边形＋损伤分级、可含无损 | 可用但完整包大且许可限制；先核具体 event 名和坐标，只下标签，不下大影像；不如 CRASAR 直接。[2] |
| Ida-BD [6]、Ian-BD [7] | DesignSafe 公共项目目录；具体文件级再许可/匿名逐文件下载本轮未核实 | Ida、Ian 均 H2 | 影像对，论文提及分类数据；没有本轮验证的 EPSG:4326 逐栋标签样本及无损定义 | 暂作备选，不能把影像对直接说成可用逐栋分母。[6][7] |
| USACE NSI 2022 [5] | USACE 公开点图层/仓库 MIT（仓库许可非原数据全量再许可担保） | 全国建筑存量，地理上可覆盖 H2 多场 | 结构点及占用类型，**无事件损伤标签** | 可作暴露核对/背景分母候选；不可把“DAT 未记录损伤”自动记零损伤，点位也非完整建筑多边形。[5] |
| OpenFEMA IA/住房检查 [3][4] | 开放 API、FEMA 使用与引用条款 | 灾难编号可对应多场 | `HousingAssistanceOwners` 按州县邮编汇总含无损检查数；`ValidRegistrations` 去个人信息，只县/市/邮编 | 无地址/逐栋坐标；申请者选择偏差；不能直接配点位 H2。[3][4] |
| StEER/DesignSafe Ida、Idalia [10][11] | 公开项目目录，文件与复用条款需逐件核 | Ida、Idalia H2 重合 | 报告/调查，未核到可匿名直接取且含无损的系统逐栋坐标表 | 不能视作系统分母；用于个案机制核验。项目网页可查，逐点表未证实。[10][11] |
| NIST 公开灾后数据检索 [8] | 逐项条款；核到的 TraCR 开放 | TraCR 跨灾县域指标，不是 H2 同场逐栋 | 县域韧性，无逐栋无损/轻损标签 | 本轮限定官方公开检索未找到符合条件的 NIST 逐栋 H2 飓风数据；这是检索范围内的未发现，不代表 NIST 不存在。[8] |
| DesignSafe PRJ-5700 Hurricane Ian [12] | 公开项目目录；许可和逐点文件待核 | Ian 重合 | Fort Myers Beach 灾后评估与首层标高，**主要洪水/风暴潮场景** | 可用于识别混淆和排除水损，不先充当风致损概率样本。[12] |

## 真实小样本核验（只读，不下载影像）

直接从 HF 数据仓库 的 revision `c3f5421e1167bb7e88a765e3afa38bebd9898479` 匿名读取 （961224 字节）：608 条记录、608 个不同 `building_id`、608 条都有 EPSG:4326；标签分别是 no damage 473、minor 49、major 23、destroyed 3、un-classified 39、obscured 21。Ida 的 仅 20568 字节，14 条不同建筑，no damage 3、minor 1、major 9、destroyed 1。两份均为真实 JSON 响应的计数，不等于当地所有建筑或独立灾害样本。[1]

数据卡按场列 `building labels`（不是去重独栋数）：Ian 100351（32.67 km²）、Idalia 4636（5.69 km²）、Ida 2068（5.14 km²）。同一 `building_id` 可能在多张正射影像中出现且损伤标注不同；`view_id` 是视图唯一键，必须先限定事后时刻、处理重复和 obscured/un-classified，并做空间范围/事件源核验。影像判据与 DAT 的 FR12/DOD 不同，不能混同。[1]

## Idalia FR12 极高重建阵风核查

只读 H2 的，此次用已有 与 H2 vendor，不改 H2）：

| DAT objectid | 峰时（UTC，原记录） | 阵风重建 m/s | H08 背景 m/s | 残差 m/s | 点–中心 / RMW km | RMW 比 | 最近有效阵风输入站 km |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 3811111 | 2023-08-30 12:00 | 72.779 | 56.538 | +16.240 | 20.29 / 18.52 | 1.095 | 24.94 |
| 3811125 | 2023-08-30 12:00 | 74.203 | 58.200 | +16.003 | 20.94 / 18.52 | 1.131 | 26.59 |
| 3811127 | 2023-08-30 12:00 | 74.451 | 58.691 | +15.759 | 22.17 / 18.52 | 1.197 | 28.39 |
| 3811135 | 2023-08-30 13:00 | 38.768 | 41.837 | −3.068 | 29.55 / 21.61 | 1.368 | 1.96 |

前三点在峰时 RMW 外沿约 1.1–1.2 倍，是**近核高背景 + 正残差**，并非 0 m/s 非负截断伪值；24.9–28.4 km 外站残差插值仍可能高估局部峰，H2 事件留一阵风 RMSE 3.327 m/s 不能作为这些点的误差保证。第四点有近站但低很多，提示空间梯度很大。r3 原表的 `rmw_ratio_at_sustained_peak` 恰与此三点峰时相同，但该列定义是持续风峰时；本次显式在**阵风峰时**重新计算，避免把两个峰时混用。尚未核 DAT 时间精度、波浪/洪水和近眼站点真实性，72–74 m/s 不作点位真值。

## 下一步建议

选择 CRASAR Idalia Steinhatchee 的单个事后 crewed JSON（已确认 473 个无损视图），外加 Ida Cocodrie 作第二个区域；在事后影像覆盖内按建筑 ID 去重、筛海潮/洪水与遮挡、检查类别与 H2 坐标范围，再对每个建筑质心只读重建 P2 阵风，按建筑簇/bootstrap 而不是按视图独立样本计算损伤概率分箱。**优先验证风致损机制与模型峰值偏低/局部高估风险，再决定是否扩 Ian**；不把影像无损当全天候/内部构件完好，也不把 DAT 估风当风速。这个试验可以回答局部影像内是否有描述性梯度，不能单靠它推广全国风脆弱性。

## 开源仓库核验（GitHub REST 仓库元数据 + 默认分支最新 commit API，2026-10-14 查询）

| 仓库 | stars | 最近默认分支提交日期 | 仓库许可证 | 本环境 |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| https://github.com/DIUx-xView/xView2_baseline | 243 | 2020-07-29 | GitHub NOASSERTION（仓库授权文件须单核；不等于 xBD 数据许可） | 可读代码；本次无需训练 |
| https://github.com/USACE-NSI/NSI | 20 | 2022-10-14 | MIT（代码仓库） | 可读 API 说明，不必下载全国点 |
| https://github.com/CRASAR/CRASAR-U-DROIDs-BDA | 0 | 2026-05-07 | 未标许可证（不能默认为开源许可；数据卡 CC BY 4.0 另计） | 可读代码；本轮只解析原始 JSON |
| https://github.com/CRASAR/CRASAR-U-DROIDs-RDA | 0 | 2026-01-07 | 未标许可证 | 可读代码；本轮无需运行 |

上述四个仓库并非项目数据本身；论文对应 xBD 原论文见 [2]、CRASAR 论文见 [9]。最近提交日期为 GitHub 默认分支的日期，不是 `pushed_at`。

## Sources

[1] https://huggingface.co/datasets/CRASAR/CRASAR-
[2] https://xview2.org/dataset
[3] https://www.fema.gov/openfema-data-page/housing-assistance-program-data-owners-v2
[4] https://www.fema.gov/openfema-data-page/individuals-and-households-program-valid-registrations-v2
[5] https://www.arcgis.com
[6] https://arxiv.org/html/2208.02205v2
[7] https://designsafe-ci.org/data/browser/public/designsafe.storage.published/PRJ-5770
[8] https://data.nist.gov/od/id/mds2-3978
[9] https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.17673
[10] https://www.designsafe-ci.org/data/browser/public/designsafe.storage.published/PRJ-3268
[11] https://www.designsafe-ci.org/data/browser/public/designsafe.storage.published/PRJ-4123
[12] https://www.designsafe-ci.org/community/dataset-awards

## 更正：Idalia FR12 近核外推值作废（原分解表留档，不重算）
上文 objectid 3811111、3811125、3811127 的 72–74 m/s 阵风虽不是数值截断造成，却不能再解释为可信点位峰值：其配套 H2 重建持续风 55.8–57.1 m/s 超过 NHC Idalia 登陆最大持续风估计 100 kt（约 51.4 m/s）。判为**近核外推失真，作废**；原表的背景和残差分解只作诊断痕迹，不能据此推损伤阈值或拟合。NHC 同报告给 Perry 最大实测阵风 74 kt，属异地、不同平均时距，不能直接与三个点的持续风比较。出处：NHC Tropical Cyclone Report AL102023，报告正文第 5 页（100 kt）和第 6 页（Perry 74 kt），https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/AL102023_Idalia.pdf。历史数字未覆盖。

# 损失–风速库 r5：CRASAR 逐栋分母 × H2 重建（探索性，2026-10-14）

## 一句话判断
本轮在两个事后正射影像小片区取得 1,024 栋可用标签及点位 H2 风速，但保守水损风险筛选后**没有可用于风致损概率分析的建筑**。含疑似水损的描述性图里，Ian 没有单调梯度；Idalia 的分箱有起伏但非单调。**不宜现在写风致损曲线或转正提案**；先寻找经验证无淹没、跨更宽风速带的内陆调查片区。

## 资料、选区和去重
CRASAR-U-DROIDs 数据卡许可 CC BY 4.0；按固定 revision 、；每个被选视图中 building_id 唯一。

剔除 obscured/un-classified；Idalia 第二张事后视图 20230902a 与首张共有 137 个 ID，其中 10 个标签不同（含 4 个明确 no/minor 冲突），保守地将首视图中的这 10 栋从评分排除，冲突仍在 明列。Ian 无同片区第二张 crewed 视图可检。最后 Ian 912 栋（no/minor/major/destroyed = 428/351/125/8），Idalia 112 栋（99/9/3/1）。这些是影像可见损伤，不等于结构检查或随机抽取的全部暴露建筑。[1]

## 风速和水损风险口径
逐栋多边形顶点均值作为质心近似，H2 在本机只读复算 CLIMADA H08 Holland 背景 + H2 陆地站残差普通克里金（固定 75 km；最多近 40 站），在各事件登陆 ±12 h 的 24 个整点求 P2 峰值；持续风与假设的 5 s 阵风分别求峰。输出 逐栋记录原值、P2 窗口、峰时、背景/残差、最近输入站距离、阵风峰时中心距/RMW 档、事件留一 RMSE/偏差、事件类型及版本。H 协议 v1.2 对飓风 Holland+残差不加校正（校正 0，保留 raw）；**重建非点位实测**，RMSE 是样本统计而非逐栋保证，且风轴可能存在事件/点位偏差。H2 的海陆筛选、源站停报、2 min/5 s 与 500 m 参考高度假设照旧；不能据此归因风损。

3DEP bare-earth DEM 小区域栅格（`r5_3dep_*.tifr5_nhc_*_forecast_inundation.tif`），非观测淹没；官方字典中 class 1 是 0–1 英尺潜在地面积水，非零仅表示潜在风险，P-Surge 的 10% 超越水平并非实际水位。[2][3]
对应归档下载页分别为 Ian [6] 与 Idalia [7]。
NHC 也明确该层不计雨洪和河流流量，0 类不能证明没淹过。[3]
Ian 官方事后报告描述海岸与内河风暴潮和雨洪并存，不能只凭影像类别分出风致损。[5]

预先明示的**保守筛选假设**：NHC 潜在淹没 class>0，或地面高程<3 m，或粗尺度岸线距离<5 km，任一即标“疑似水损/风暴潮风险”，主分析排除；这是高敏感度风险代理，**不是实测水损判定**，可误排真风损。敏感性档仅以高程<2 m 或岸距<3 km 标风险，不用 NHC 潜在淹没，仍非无水真值。阈值是本次探索性假设，无来源声称；分区 500 m 网格作空间簇，随机种子 20261014、600 次簇 bootstrap 仅估条件抽样变异，不包括洪水误分、建筑选择偏差和 H2 系统风速误差。

## 样本流与筛选结果

| 片区 | 原始视图 | 无效/冲突剔除 | 可用独栋 | 有 NHC 潜在淹没 | 保守排风险后 | 放宽地形代理后 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ian Harlem Heights | 975 | 63 | 912 | 912 | **0** | 23（2 空间簇） |
| Idalia Jena | 139 | 27（其中 10 冲突） | 112 | 96 | **0** | 25（2 空间簇） |

原始质心高程范围：Ian 1.32–3.30 m，Idalia −0.98–6.07 m；粗尺度岸距 Ian 2.04–3.30 km、Idalia 1.10–3.66 km。即使 Idalia 有若干潜在淹没图外点，也未同时通过高程/距岸保守门槛。放宽档 Ian 19 no/4 minor，Idalia 24 no/1 minor，均无 ≥major；它们仍可能水损，且只有各 2 个簇。**主结果无可画概率曲线**，不能把下图全样本图当水损排除后的结果。

## 含疑似水损的对照：描述性分箱，不能归因

图 分事件、分阈值展示全部可用建筑的可见损伤比例，误差棒是 500 m 簇 bootstrap 的 2.5–97.5 百分位。图上 `c` 为单个箱涉及的空间簇数；只有一个簇时区间退化，**不表示无不确定性**。两事件风速及损伤构成完全不可混池。

| 片区 | H2 阵风箱 (m/s) | n / 簇 | ≥minor | ≥major |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ian | 73.9–74.0 | 209 / 3 | 119/209 = 56.9% | 43/209 = 20.6% |
| Ian | 74.0–74.1 | 494 / 5 | 262/494 = 53.0% | 55/494 = 11.1% |
| Ian | 74.1–74.2 | 179 / 3 | 94/179 = 52.5% | 35/179 = 19.6% |
| Ian | 74.2–74.3 | 30 / 1 | 9/30 = 30.0% | 0/30 = 0% |
| Idalia | 55–56 | 15 / 2 | 1/15 = 6.7% | 0/15 |
| Idalia | 56–57 | 46 / 5 | 2/46 = 4.3% | 0/46 |
| Idalia | 57–58、58–59 | 0 | 未定义 | 未定义 |
| Idalia | 59–60 | 23 / 7 | 5/23 = 21.7% | 3/23 = 13.0% |
| Idalia | 60–61 | 28 / 3 | 5/28 = 17.9% | 1/28 = 3.6% |

Ian 同片区的重建阵风仅 73.927–74.224 m/s，跨度 0.297 m/s，远小于 H2 的 Ian 事件阵风留一 RMSE 4.475 m/s（Idalia 为 3.327 m/s；仅为站点样本误差，不能移作点位误差界）；而≥minor 在微小风速差内略下降，不是单调递增。Idalia 55.918–60.661 m/s，但 57–59 m/s 两箱为空，分组空间离散且≥minor 在最高箱反降；表观阶跃不能排除潮水/地势/片区差异。含疑似水损版本仅用作反例，不用于风致损概率拟合。放宽地形档总共 48 栋、4 簇、≥major 为零，无区分高损伤概率的统计支撑。

## 限制、复算与下一步
### 补充：阵风峰时按 RMW 档分层（2026-10-14；不覆盖原图）
按 H 协议 v1.2 §3，以**每栋重建阵风 P2 峰时**中心距/RMW（ 的 `rmw_ratio_at_gust_peak`、`rmw_bin_at_gust_peak`）将可用标签拆为 `<1`、`1–3`、`>3`、unknown；分层分箱图另存 （ 只读复算）。分事件、不跨片区合并。注意两处都**只有 `1–3 RMW<1 RMW1–3 RMW` 楼栋点位校正**，Holland+残差本轮不加校正。

| 事件和 RMW 档 | 阵风分箱 m/s | n / 簇 | ≥minor | ≥major | 严格水风险筛除后 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ian，1–3 | 73.9–74.0 / 74.0–74.1 / 74.1–74.2 / 74.2–74.3 | 209/3；494/5；179/3；30/1 | 119/209；262/494；94/179；9/30 | 43/209；55/494；35/179；0/30 | 0 |
| Idalia，1–3 | 55–56 / 56–57 / 57–58 / 58–59 / 59–60 / 60–61 | 15/2；46/5；0/0；0/0；23/7；28/3 | 1/15；2/46；—；—；5/23；5/28 | 0/15；0/46；—；—；3/23；1/28 | 0 |
| 两片区，<1 / >3 / unknown | — | 各 0 | 不可估 | 不可估 | 0 |

这与原结果同一批楼栋，不能当独立复现。水风险排除后无样本，含风险对照仍没有可归因风致损的单调梯度；仅 `1–3 RMW` 有样本意味着 RMW 分层并未扩大风速轴或改善近核外推判定。图的标注含 CRASAR-U-DROIDs (CC BY 4.0)、H2/NHC 最佳路径及“重建、非实测”。

1. NHC 栅格是登陆前潜在淹没，而非事件实测高水痕或逐栋水损；3DEP 2026 服务数据用于旧事件有年代错配；Natural Earth 海岸距漏小河渠。此筛查故意保守，也暴露出 CRASAR 当前两片区无法做可信风损归因。须找实际观测/事后淹没、首层标高及建筑类别才可解开。[3][4]
2. 影像仅见外部可见损伤；未据房屋类型、建年或屋顶形式标准化。两事件 H2 误差与强风存活站偏差可能大于本地风速跨度；区间只计算标签簇变异，不能作脆弱性置信带。
3. 下一轮先在 CRASAR 全部标签元数据或另一公开逐栋调查中找地势更高、经事后淹没核实的同一事件**内陆**片区；预先冻结片区/阈值、确认足够风速跨度和多个独立空间簇，再做风/水损机理审核及不同建筑类型分层。若仍无足够未淹水样本，则暂搁置 CRASAR→风致损概率这一特定路线，而非否定独立风速–损失库方向。无需转正提案。

复现顺序（仅在**新输出目录**运行，勿覆盖现有成果）： → → → →，Python 为，H2 文件只读。生成 （1114 原始单视图模型记录）、（风速和筛查字段）、 也下载了两处额外 Ian 候选的仅标签 JSON 和 3DEP 小裁剪，不下载影像。

## Sources

[1] https://huggingface.co/datasets/CRASAR/CRASAR-
[2] https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/gis/inundation/potential_storm_surge_flooding_downloads_guide.pdf
[3] https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/surge/inundation/?text=
[4] https://elevation.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/3DEPElevation/ImageServer
[5] https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/AL092022_Ian.pdf
[6] https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/gis/archive_inundation_results.php?id=al09&year=22&name=Hurricane%20IAN
[7] https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/gis/archive_inundation_results.php?id=al10&year=23&name=Hurricane%20IDALIA

## 更正／图表注（保留原分箱与原图作为历史描述，不重算）
上文两张分箱表和原图是**含潜在水损风险的描述性存档**，不是有效风致损概率。Ian Harlem Heights 建筑的阵风峰时中心距/RMW 为 1.019–1.046（约 1.02–1.05），处于眼墙邻近；Idalia Jena 的阵风峰时比值为 2.060–2.144，但也没有逐栋点位的观测验证。两片区的重建阵风均标记为“近核／未观测验证”；凡包含这些楼栋的近核分箱均标记**未验证**，不用于主梯度判断。注意原 分类并未改变：这批楼栋都在 `1–3` 档，而不是 `<1<1 RMW` 有样本。主结论只依赖经筛查、且合格的 `1–3 RMW` 或外围建筑；本轮严格水损风险排除后实际合格 **0 栋**，故没有可判断的主梯度。Idalia r3 三个 DAT FR12 点的近核持续风已因超过 NHC Idalia 登陆强度估计而判外推失真、作废（见 末尾更正）；这里的 CRASAR Jena 建筑不是那三个 DAT 点，也同样不能视为已验证风速。

修订图为 、；保留原 和 不覆盖。这两张修订图在原画面下增设更正与来源条：近核分箱未验证、不用于主梯度，数据来自 CRASAR-U-DROIDs（Manzini 等，2024，arXiv:2407.17673，CC BY 4.0）、H2 重建（实验室 H 节点）、NHC 最佳路径及潜在淹没图、USGS 3DEP；本节上述两张历史分箱表也使用同一来源。[1][2][3][4] NHC 潜在淹没图非实测淹没。修订图仅加注，不改变散点、分箱数或统计结果。

results.title: Storm Events loss–wind-speed extraction r1 (10-14 19:05 EDT)
results.text:
# Storm Events Loss–Wind Speed Extraction r1 (10-14 19:05 EDT)

## Scope and Reproducibility

Official NCEI Storm Events details 2018–2023, fixed seed 20261014, initial screening by damage narrative / property damage stratified into 300 entries: Thunderstorm Wind 120, Tropical Cyclone 90, winter High Wind 90. Three batches of 100 entries each, –. Review gates lowest at 90%, 90%, 90% respectively, none below 90%; this is not overall accuracy. Time, location, peril, ID are external CSV fields, not evaluating the model. All scores are only for this stratified sample, not a nationwide overall estimate.

Raw CSV URL/hash see , sampling code , questions –, answers –, scoring code , summary code , machine statistics. Field definitions, interval scoring, and NWSI 10-1605 page numbers see . Wind speed values read narrative only; intervals retain lower and upper bounds, considered correct when falling within the gold standard interval during comparison; unit conversions must be consistent. Severity and type are operational definitions for the experiment, not official NWS damage ratings.

## Field Accuracy: Correct/20 (%), Gold Standard 60 Entries

| Field | Thunderstorm | Tropical | High Wind |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Damaged object exact set | 20/20 (100) | 13/20 (65) | 15/20 (75) |
| Damage severity | 17/20 (85) | 18/20 (90) | 16/20 (80) |
| Narrative wind speed value/range, unit | 20/20 (100) | 17/20 (85) | 19/20 (95) |
| gust/sustained/none | 20/20 (100) | 18/20 (90) | 20/20 (100) |
| Narrative wind speed source six-class | 20/20 (100) | 15/20 (75) | 19/20 (95) |
| Instrument/site exact string | 20/20 (100) | 12/20 (60) | 18/20 (90) |
| EF/damage rating | 20/20 (100) | 20/20 (100) | 20/20 (100) |
| Damage quote is original substring | 20/20 (100) | 20/20 (100) | 17/20 (85) |
| Source quote check | 20/20 (100) | 16/20 (80) | 19/20 (95) |

Object set partial hit (non-empty intersection or both empty) respectively 20/20, 19/20, 19/20; cannot replace exact set. Quote metric is only a verbatim original substring validity check, not semantic completeness or coverage; site metric is exact match of the raw string, which may misjudge “KGED” and “Delaware Coastal Airport (KGED)” as incorrect. For wind speed values, the 20 Thunderstorm gold standard entries had no narrative numerical values, sources were also all none, and EF was essentially null, so these 100% scores are “null values are easy to answer”, and must never be interpreted as positive-case extraction of wind speed or rare source identification capability. Tropical and High Wind gold standards had narrative numerical values in only 11/20 and 7/20 entries respectively; taking values within allowed ranges does not equal speed being exact to a single value.

## Source Confusion Matrix (Narrative-only; Row=Gold Standard, Column=Model; n=60)

| Ground Truth \ Prediction | none | estimated_unspecified | measured | damage_inferred | radar | observer_estimate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| none | 37 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| estimated_unspecified | 3 | 3 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| measured | 1 | 0 | 13 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| damage_inferred | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| radar | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| observer_estimate | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Thunderstorm source score 20/20 was entirely none; the sample had no gold standard positive cases for radar or observer wind estimation. The above matrix evaluates only the model reading narratives; the following proportions combine MAGNITUDE_TYPE under predefined rules, and the two must not be conflated.

## Whether Wind Speed Is Independent of Damage Inference

Strict = measured + radar; lenient adds observer_estimate; estimated_unspecified is not allocated to either side. Narrative speed count is the number of entries where the model extracted an on-site numerical value; structured count is the number of non-empty MAGNITUDE entries; denominator with speed is the union of both. Sources prioritize narrative criteria, and supplement measured according to MG/MS, and supplement estimated_unspecified for EG/ES with non-empty MAGNITUDE; if the narrative clearly indicates damage inference, it is not rewritten by EG. Strict figures are “candidate independent wind speeds under current classification”, not yet individually verified true measurements.

| Peril | Total / With Speed | Narrative Numerical | Structured MAGNITUDE | Strict / All; Strict / With Speed | Lenient / All; Lenient / With Speed | Unspecified Estimation Basis / With Speed | Explicit Damage Inference / With Speed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Thunderstorm | 120/120 | 13/120 (10.8%) | 120/120 (100%) | 3/120 (2.5%); 3/120 (2.5%) | 3/120 (2.5%); 3/120 (2.5%) | 116/120 | 1/120 |
| Tropical | 90/54 | 54/90 (60.0%) | 0/90 (0%) | 28/90 (31.1%); 26/54 (48.1%) | 28/90 (31.1%); 26/54 (48.1%) | 6/54 | 1/54 |
| High Wind | 90/90 | 53/90 (58.9%) | 90/90 (100%) | 48/90 (53.3%); 48/90 (53.3%) | 49/90 (54.4%); 49/90 (54.4%) | 38/90 | 3/90 |

In the full Tropical sample, 28 narratives mentioned instruments or measurements, but only 26 entries concurrently had explicit numerical wind speed; 28/90 cannot be treated as the quantity “usable for damage–numerical wind speed pairing”. Another 21 entries had narrative numerical values but sources were none (e.g., multiple wind speeds / locations not corresponding, extraction contradictions), requiring manual review. Among 117 Thunderstorm EG entries, only 1 had explicitly stated basis in the narrative (damage basis 1), the remaining 116 cannot be directly stated as damage-inferred; among 44 High Wind EG entries, basis could be clarified for 7 entries, of which damage basis was 1. NWSI 10-1605 Appendix A §46.3 A-69 (PDF 86) and §24 A-34 (PDF 51) permit estimating wind by professional judgment based on structural or tree damage, §46.4 Table A7 A-71 (PDF 88) provides a comparison guide, but cannot prove the actual method for each EG entry.

## Comparison with MAGNITUDE_TYPE (Main 300)

Only 210 entries in the main sample have MAGNITUDE_TYPE: Thunderstorm 117 EG / 3 MG; High Wind 44 EG / 43 MG / 2 MS / 1 ES; in Tropical 90 entries this column is empty. Joint classification: EG 153 estimated_unspecified, 2 damage_inferred, 1 observer_estimate, 5 measured; MG 44 measured, 2 damage_inferred; MS 2 measured, ES 1 estimated_unspecified. According to the expected binary broad categories by column (MG/MS measured, EG/ES estimated), 203/210 were consistent; the 7 cross-category entries were not automatic labeling errors: in EG, 5 narratives additionally mentioned instrument measurements; in MG, 2 narratives pointed to damage inference. For example, 70 mph in 997302 and 997286 was “damage representative of around 70 mph”, while the two rows of structured MG 56 kt may refer to another ASOS/AWOS wind speed of around 65 mph; 749604’s EG 50 kt and the airport 48 mph in the narrative were also not the same value, and narrative measurements cannot directly overwrite the structured column. 13/13 Thunderstorm entries with numerical records in both columns had conversion differences between narrative value and MAGNITUDE ≤5 mph, High Wind was 43/53; inconsistent records could also be peak values from different stations/events, and cannot be used to conclude model error. An event-location-time-observation correspondence must be established entry-by-entry before claiming “usable for validation”.

## Reviewable Failure Examples (Original text snippets; 2–3 entries per category)

- Damaged objects: 787020 “some downed trees with and power outages.” mistook power outages as physical damage to poles; 993000 had only “power outages” yet extracted power and damage; supplementary batch 648358 “some damage to the carports” overreported commercial (the apartment building itself was not stated as damaged).
- Severity: 1030387 “blew the metal roof off of an auto sales building” gold standard severe, model moderate; 999192 “Five power poles were completely broken off near the ground” gold standard severe, model destroyed; 1060311 “Power outages were reported” model moderate, but no physical damage, gold standard none.
- Wind speed value/object mismatch: 857631 “Wind gust of 59 knots (68 mph) was measured at Ocean Park. Wind gust of 51 knots (59 mph) was measured at Mesonet Station XCRE Creeds.” Model selected 59 mph, gold standard selected 68 per maximum observation at the event site; 924082 “Winds gusted between 35 and 45 mph ... A gust to 37 mph was recorded at the Thomaston AWOS” model 37, gold standard 45 per upper bound of range, involving different observation targets; 913730 “Based on the proxy observations ... likely reached near hurricane force (71 mph)” model treated inferred proxy value 71 as on-site wind speed, gold standard left blank. The rule for choosing one among multiple sources itself needs clarification.
- Source: 1058660 “highest wind reported ... a gust to 111 mph” had no instrument/estimation basis, gold standard estimated_unspecified, model none; 924057 “Winds gusted between 35 and 50 mph” gold standard estimated_unspecified, model none; 924082 model applied the source of AWOS measured 37 mph in the same paragraph to the 35–45 mph range. Radar used only for estimating timing does not count as a radar wind speed source.
- Quotes and sites: 907683 “at Delaware Coastal Airport (KGED)” gold standard site KGED, model full name (strings differ but semantically acceptable); 1051095 “St. Augustine C-man station SAUF1 ... a mesonet station” model generically termed C-man, dropping station number; 929398 narrative had only Broken Bow ASOS gust record and no damage, model quote was empty, the quote “accuracy” in this table cannot be taken as damage recall.

## NWS DAT / StEER Availability (Quick check only)

NWS DAT has public ArcGIS FeatureServer layers 0 (points), 1 (lines), 2 (polygons), layer REST JSON supports paginated queries, data documentation indicates preliminary survey data rather than Storm Data official statistics; service page nominally indicates single-request maxRecordCount 2000, suitable for paginated trial fetching by space-time/ID for Step 2, ID mapping with Storm Events, licensing details, and long-term stability have not yet been verified: <https://services.dat.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/nws_damageassessmenttoolkit/DamageViewer/FeatureServer>, <https://services.dat.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/nws_damageassessmenttoolkit/DamageViewer/FeatureServer/0?f=pjson>. StEER has public event-based published projects and Download Dataset on DesignSafe (e.g., Hurricane Ian PRJ-3709, DOI 10.17603/ds2-f1p1-ev62), potentially mixing PDFs, photos, tables; DesignSafe documentation indicates Published can be programmatically transferred via TAPIS API, but an unauthenticated unified cross-project batch record interface has not been verified, cannot state “already directly fetchable across the entire database via API”: <https://www.designsafe-ci.org/data/browser/public/designsafe.storage.published/PRJ-3709>, <https://designsafe-ci.org/user-guide/managingdata/datatransfer/>.

## Independent S1 Alignment Supplementary Batch (Not merged into main 300)

Main sample years do not overlap with S1’s 2010–2017. Using , official file SHA256 see , structure type 3/4 (75%) was below the 90% gate, this field did not pass, stopped treating it as a reliable field; remaining examined fields were 4/4, but positive cases were too few. S1 is only for future ID alignment by H-node, not included in gold standard 60 or main sample accuracy.

## One-Sentence Judgment and Step 2

Judgment: Worth continuing targeted Phase II validation, but r1 cannot directly build an “independent wind speed–structural damage” training/validation database; most EG sources are unspecified, Tropical source and damaged object accuracy were only 75%/65%, while Thunderstorm 100% source score mainly came from null-value questions.

Recommended for Phase II to first supplement hard gold standards with wind speed and clear sources / damage inference across three perils (especially Thunderstorm EG, MG), verify entry-by-entry whether narrative–MAGNITUDE are the same site/station/time, and use DAT survey layers as small-scale independent cross-validation; clarify rules for proxy observations, maximum/range selection, object damage vs. power outage only, then evaluate source precision/recall on symmetric positive and negative cases. The 40 S1 entries are only handed over to H-node for alignment, not merged into the main sample. Sources related to the use of public data are listed above; formal literature conclusions still require checking original texts/licenses.

results.title: Storm Events r1b: wind-speed unit conversion and station-semantics scoring correction
results.text:
# Storm Events r1b: Wind Speed Unit Conversion and Station Semantic Scoring Corrections

Scope remains the main sample of 300 entries, independent gold standard of 60 entries (20 each for Thunderstorm/Tropical/High Wind), not rerunning Gemini; original r1 report and preserved as-is. Recalculation executed, new machine output, 300/300 ok, 60/60 have scorable answers. Scoring script unifies mph, kt (knots), and m/s into m/s, judging single values by ±0.5 m/s; both ends of the gold standard interval are converted first, then each expanded by ±0.5 m/s. Non-empty speeds with unknown units cannot be judged correct. Station raw string exact tier left unchanged, additionally adding a semantic tier with mutual inclusion after lowercasing and whitespace removal (merely a loose alias approximation, not authoritative station ID resolution).

| Field (Correct/20) | Thunderstorm r1→r1b | Tropical r1→r1b | High Wind r1→r1b |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Damaged object exact set | 20→20 | 13→13 | 15→15 |
| Damage severity | 17→17 | 18→18 | 16→16 |
| Narrative wind speed value (after unit conversion, interval tolerance) | 20→20 | 17→18 | 19→19 |
| gust/sustained/none | 20→20 | 18→18 | 20→20 |
| Source six-class | 20→20 | 15→15 | 19→19 |
| Station raw string exact | 20→20 | 12→12 | 18→18 |
| Station semantic mutual inclusion (new) | —→20 | —→15 | —→19 |
| EF/damage rating | 20→20 | 20→20 | 20→20 |
| Damage quote original substring | 20→20 | 20→20 | 17→17 |
| Source quote check | 20→20 | 16→16 | 19→19 |

For 857631, model’s 59 kt vs. gold standard’s 68 mph is within tolerance after conversion, now judged correct; no longer listed among failure examples. Other narrative wind speed failure examples from r1, 924082 (AWOS 37 mph vs. another wind speed of 35–45 mph) and 913730 (proxy inferred value), still need to be distinguished. Original r1 failure description for 857631 also stated model output 59 mph, which differed from the saved actual answer / instruction description; subject to and new machine scoring. For Thunderstorm 20 gold standard entries, speeds and sources were almost entirely null values; 20/20 cannot be treated as positive-case capability.

Conclusion: Error correction changes only one question for Tropical wind speed value; Tropical station semantic score increased from 12/20 to 15/20, remaining r1 conclusions unchanged. Source accuracy and co-located simultaneous independent wind speed pairing still await validation with r2 hard gold standards and DAT/IEM measurements.

results.title: DAT–IEM spatiotemporal candidate pairing pilot (part C of r2)
results.text:
# DAT–IEM Spatiotemporal Candidate Pairing Trial (Part C of r2)

Sources: NWS DAT point layer <https://services.dat.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/nws_damageassessmenttoolkit/DamageViewer/FeatureServer/0>; IEM ASOS/AWOS METAR download <https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/download.phtml>, station metadata. Query URL / raw point attributes see , IEM query URL see , raw non-empty gust observations , point-by-point nearest pairing ; reproduction . No H reconstruction input, all candidates use IEM gust measurements; windspeed in DAT is estimated from damage, never serving as an independent observation. Sample consists of demo days selected based on visible DAT points, not representing a nationwide sample.

Filter DAT `stormdate` UTC window and bbox, hurricanes only `efscale='Tropical'`, thunderstorms only ; thus excluding concurrent EF tornadoes, cannot guarantee that all points for a hurricane were caused by that specific cyclone. Centered on the stormdate recorded for each DAT point, hurricane ±12 h, thunderstorm ±3 h, search for the nearest ASOS/AWOS station within 25 km that has non-empty METAR gust in the time window, unit gust=kt. Distance uses spherical Haversine, thresholds cumulative. Windows are experimental assumptions, not NWS DAT time precision guarantees; IEM low-QC as-is archive, instrument quality and damage mechanism matching have not yet been performed.

| Event / Regional Time Window | DAT Classified Points | DAT Inherent Wind Estimation Non-Empty | ≤5 km | ≤10 km | ≤25 km | DAT 00:00 UTC Timestamp | Actual Gust-Reporting Stations within 25 km |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

results.text:
# Storm Events Narrative Extraction Rules r1

Source: NOAA NCEI Storm Events 2018–2023 details CSV, yearly files and SHA256 see ; NWSI 10-1605 (2021) https://www.weather.gov/media/directives/010_pdfs/pd01016005curr.pdf. Model input is EVENT_NARRATIVE only (does not expose MAGNITUDE / MAGNITUDE_TYPE / SOURCE / DAMAGE_PROPERTY); location, time, event_id, and hazard are determined by structured columns in the output table, not guessed by the model.

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| event_id, hazard, date_time_local, location | External CSV EVENT_ID, categorized by EVENT_TYPE, BEGIN_DATE_TIME + CZ_TIMEZONE (local standard time, not converted to UTC), STATE/CZ_NAME/BEGIN_LOCATION/BEGIN_LAT/BEGIN_LON; does not evaluate model accuracy on these |
| structure_type | Set of objects explicitly damaged in the narrative; house, mobile_home, commercial, barn, power, tree, vehicle, sign, other; empty if unspecified. power includes pole/lines; power outage is not automatically equated to pole damage |
| damage_description | Excerpted sentence from the original narrative, must be an exact verbatim substring; empty if there is no damage sentence |
| damage_severity | none/minor/moderate/severe/destroyed; based solely on text, not back-inferred from property damage dollar values. If multiple locations, the most severe prevails; damaged but no degree indicated → moderate (operational assumption) |
| wind_speed_value, wind_speed_lower, wind_speed_upper, wind_speed_unit, wind_speed_mps | r1 legacy single-value fields are retained for comparability; r2 additionally adds a `wind_observations` array, with one entry for each on-site value/range in the narrative, listing all rather than taking the maximum, retaining station, timestamp, speed kind, source, and original evidence text. Ranges (e.g. 50–60 mph) retain lower and upper bounds, converted to m/s during scoring, counted as correct if falling within the range expanded by ±0.5 m/s; mph×0.44704, kt×0.514444. Forecasts/thresholds/general storm peak wind speeds are not listed as on-site observations; proxy observations are listed and tagged as proxy, not used for measured loss pairing |
| wind_speed_kind | gust/sustained/unknown/none; assigned only when the original text explicitly indicates gust or sustained |
| wind_speed_source | measured/radar/damage_inferred/observer_estimate/estimated_unspecified/none. Explicit instrument measurement measured; radar estimation radar; explicitly inferred from damage or EF/DI/DOD damage_inferred; visual observation by a person without mentioning damage observer_estimate; merely estimated with no basis estimated_unspecified; no on-site event wind speed or source in narrative none. When multiple sources exist, the source corresponding to the extracted wind speed prevails; when the original text is unclear, co-occurrence of damage and estimation is not automatically judged as damage_inferred |
| wind_speed_source_quote, instrument_or_site, ef_damage_rating | Exact verbatim excerpt supporting the source, instrument/station name, explicit EF/DI/DOD rating; empty if no basis |

r2 boundary: Wind speed from a proxy station/radar or elsewhere, even if measured, cannot be treated as measured at the damage location; if the original text explicitly states a proxy inference rather than a local value, tag `proxy=true` in `wind_observations`, and do not count as strict colocation pairing. When the narrative only has power outages (power outage) without actual physical damage to power lines, poles, transformers, or buildings, the set of damaged objects is empty, and severity=none; power outages cannot be treated as `powerprimary_source` is merely the selected wind speed source compatible with the six-category scoring, and cannot replace the entire table.

Post-processing additionally establishes `source_joined`: when model/human narrative source is none or estimated_unspecified, if MAGNITUDE_TYPE=MG/MS, classify as measured; if EG/ES and the record has structured MAGNITUDE, classify as estimated_unspecified; inference from damage cannot be presumed from EG/ES. In the narrative, explicit damage_inferred takes precedence over EG, but conflicts with MG/MS are flagged for review and not overwritten by default. In EG, count separately the number of cases where the narrative can explicitly confirm a basis (measured/radar/observer_estimate/damage_inferred) and the number of cases where a damage basis can be explicitly confirmed; EG + damage description only does not count. Two numerator tiers for non-damage: strict measured+radar; lenient adds observer_estimate. Denominators are reported both for all samples and for samples with structured or narrative wind speeds; estimated_unspecified is not included in any numerator. Occurrence rates of narrative wind speeds and non-empty rates of structured MAGNITUDE are reported separately by hazard type. The supplementary batch of 40 records from four cities for 2010–2017 S1 is reported independently of the main sample, and is not merged into the accuracy of the main 300.

## H Reconstructed Value Pairing Extension (C; Protocol v1.2 §3–4)

The current DAT–IEM small trial only uses IEM measured gusts and does not invoke H; the following fields are mandatory record-by-record only when H reconstructed values are actually ingested in the future, without using sample means from the protocol to impersonate predicted values at damage points. Reconstructed pairing and measured pairing are placed in separate tables and counted separately; reconstruction is not counted in the strict independent wind speed tier; thunderstorms do not use H reconstruction. Maximum wind for hurricane events uses Holland+residual kriging and must not take the maximum from ordinary kriging time histories; if ordinary kriging is used for hourly time histories, it must be noted that it is not used as an estimate of maximum wind.

| Field | Filling Method and Boundaries |
| --- | --- |
| wind_speed_source | `reconstructed`, must not be filled with `measured`; belongs only to pairing table extensions, does not alter the six-category narrative source label |
| reconstruction_method, background_field | Actual method and background field name; e.g. Holland+residual and the Holland field actually used, not guessing background version from method name |
| peak_definition, peak_window_start_utc, peak_window_end_utc | P1=prediction error at observed peak timestamp (applicable only to validation samples that have an observed peak timestamp); P2=maximum within the shared valid timestamp window, hurricane landfall ±12 h, extratropical regional peak ±12 h, thunderstorm ±3 h; when damage points have no anemometer, P1 peak truth must not be claimed; record specific UTC start/end and definition source |
| wind_quantity, averaging_interval | Sustained wind or gust; note that METAR hourly reports sustained wind is approx. 2 min, gust approx. 5 s; if using other archives where raw definitions have not been verified, mark as `unknown`, must not be mixed for comparison |
| nearest_input_station_km, event_type, hurricane_center_distance_km, hurricane_rmw_km, hurricane_rmw_bin | Record nearest distance to actual input station, event type; for hurricanes additionally record center distance, RMW, and `<11–3>3 RMW`, mark as `unknown` if center distance or RMW is unavailable, do not substitute with peripheral bin |
| validation_subset, sample_rmse_mps, sample_bias_mps | Only cite holdout sample values matching the method, wind quantity, peak definition, event type, and RMW/strong-wind subset; bias=prediction−observation; explicitly note "sample statistics, not point-by-point guarantee"; if not applicable, leave null and explain |
| colocated_independent | Fixed `false`, H reconstruction does not enter the strict independent tier; counted separately from measured neighbor-station candidates as well |
| reconstructed_raw, peak_correction_mps, peak_correction_version, reconstructed_corrected | `reconstructed_rawpeak_correction_mps` records the signed additive correction actually applied, filled with 0 rather than missing if uncorrected; `peak_correction_version` records `v1.2`; `reconstructed_corrected = reconstructed_raw + peak_correction_mps`. Corrected values are tagged as "reconstructed, non-measured, corrected (v1.2)"; zero-correction hurricane values should additionally be explicitly tagged as "no peak correction applied", without implying that additive correction improves accuracy |

Select correction values separately according to event type, wind quantity, method, and peak definition, prohibiting cross-category generalization. Protocol v1.2 §4: Recommended method P2 for synoptic sustained wind is +0.82 m/s (not P1 of §1); extratropical sustained wind OK fit is +1.46 m/s, gust OK fit is +1.38 m/s; thunderstorm sustained wind IDW is +3.25 m/s, gust OK fixed is +5.08 m/s (only four Dallas events, single-event residual bias can reach approx. ±2–3 m/s, rough estimate, and thunderstorm pairing in this trial still does not use reconstruction); hurricane Holland+residual sustained wind and gust are both not corrected ( §0–4; the protocol §1, §4 provide original evidence paths.

## H4/H2 Cross-Node Read-Only Pairing and Spatial Footprint (r2 Supplement)

Added point-by-point `footprint_context`: NOAA JetStream "Thunderstorm Hazards - Damaging Wind" "Microbursts and Macrobursts" (webpage without page numbers) gives microburst outflow diameter <4 km and downburst extent up to 10 km; Romanic, Taszarek, Brooks (2022), *Weather and Climate Extremes* 37:100474, abstract / journal page 1 gives 4 km boundary for horizontal scale of damaging wind between micro/macrobursts. Therefore, station distance to point ≤4 km is only spatially possible; 4–10 km has exceeded the diameter of a single microburst but macrobursts or gust fronts remain possible, and 10–25 km exceeds the typical range of a single downburst, so neighbor station peaks should not replace point peaks. DAT records are not confirmed point-by-point as downbursts: the above are merely scale risk labels, not event mechanism attributions; storm translation, station height/exposure, and time differences need separate verification.

Hurricane station–damage points require center distance and RMW at that timestamp to judge `<11–3>3 RMW`; if there is no RMW corresponding to the point, `rmw_bin=unknown`, and the RMW bin of an H2 neighbor station cannot impersonate the damage point bin. H2 `grid_*colocated_independent=false` (colocation and cotemporality not yet verified); reconstructions are listed separately and never counted in the strict independent tier. Thunderstorms only use H4 one-minute `gust_sknt` (5-second gust) and its pre-stored UTC window, without mixing hourly METAR, nor reconstructing; H2 tropical only reads the land station table, with gusts using IEM cached METAR hourly records, which cannot be directly compared with H4 minute records for peak-capturing capability.

## Parameter Source Table

| Definition | Source and Page Number | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local time | NWSI 10-1605 §2.3, text p.5 (PDF page 5): `Use local standard time in 24-hour clock throughout the year` | Retain CSV CZ_TIMEZONE as-is; do not calculate time zone on our own |
| Loss dollar amount estimate | NWSI §2.7, text p.11 (PDF page 11): may use actual estimates from insurance/qualified personnel, must not treat them as measured wind speeds | Do not use DAMAGE_PROPERTY to determine wind speed source |
| Thunderstorm damage wind estimation | NWSI Appendix A §46.3, A-69 (PDF page 86): `The Storm Data preparer exercises professional judgment to determine the estimated maximum wind value based on observed structural or tree damage.` | Indeed permits damage back-inference, but cannot treat all EG as damage back-inference |
| High wind damage wind estimation | NWSI Appendix A §24, A-34 (PDF page 51): `The Storm Data preparer exercises professional judgment to determine the estimated maximum wind value based on observed structural or tree damage.` | High wind can also be damage-inferred |
| Damage–wind speed reference table | NWSI Appendix A §46.4, A-71 (PDF page 88), Table A7 `Table for Estimating Wind Speed from Damage`; includes precautions on vegetation condition and soil moisture | The table is a guideline, not the actual source for each EG in this dataset |
| MG/MS/EG/ES | NWSI Appendix A §24 A-34–35, §46.3 A-70; NCEI Storm Data Bulk Data Format (verified in task description) | Only measured/estimated and gust/sustained, does not encode basis for estimation |
| DAT `windspeed` unit | FeatureServer point layer field metadata only labels String, providing no unit; Lab Lead sampled 500 points each starting from 2023 on 2026-10-14, EF1 86–110, EF2 97–135, EF3 136–165, consistent with EF mph ranges | **Presumed mph** from internal data consistency, unconfirmed by official dictionary; DAT belongs to damage inference and cannot serve as independent wind measurement. Differences converted to mph in old reports remain descriptive; if the original unit were actually kt, the same positive number would convert to a larger mph, shifting the overall DAT−neighbor station/model difference upward, but without guaranteeing that the sign of every single difference remains unchanged |
| Sampling, severity default grade, structural category, six-source priority | Operational rules (assumptions) of this trial; fixed seed=20261014 | Not given in literature, does not claim official definition; conduct source ambiguity review |

# Loss–Wind Speed Database Step 2 r2 (10-14 21:06 EDT)

Conclusion: Narrative extraction enriched with positive source examples can continue to serve as a candidate generator, but cannot be directly regarded as strict colocated, cotemporal damage–independent wind speed data. 66/70 sources were correct across 70 hard samples; DAT damage points and neighbor stations with reported gusts at 10–25 km can form dozens to hundreds of candidates, very few at 5 km, and multiple points share a single station–time observation.

## A Scoring Fix (Delivered Early)

Subject to , ; main sample 300 records and original gold standard 60 records were not rerun. 59 kt and 68 mph are correct after conversion, tropical wind speed value score changed from 17/20 to 18/20; tropical station semantic mutual containment is 15/20, strict verbatim match remains 12/20. Thunderstorm gold standard 20 records are almost entirely null wind speed/source; original source 20/20 does not represent positive-example capability. The r1 report serves only as pre-correction comparison.

## B Enriched Hard Gold Standard: Six-Category Narrative Source Classification

70 records were selected from official NCEI Storm Events details outside the main 300 using a fixed seed: 20 thunderstorm EG values, 10 thunderstorm MG, 15 tropical stations, 10 High Wind stations, 15 damage wind estimates. Human annotation was based solely on narratives, not treating MAGNITUDE_TYPE as narrative source ground truth; input , `gemini-3.8-flash-high` output , machine results , passing the batch-by-batch <90% stop gate. Did not restart yielded processes or use `--force`.

| Gold Standard Source | Sample Count | Model Predicted Count | True Positives | Precision | Recall |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| measured | 37 | 34 | 34 | 34/34 = 100% | 34/37 = 91.9% |
| damage_inferred | 16 | 17 | 16 | 16/17 = 94.1% | 16/16 = 100% |
| estimated_unspecified | 15 | 17 | 14 | 14/17 = 82.4% | 14/15 = 93.3% |
| observer_estimate | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2/2 = 100% | 2/2 = 100% |
| radar | 0 | 0 | 0 | Incalculable | Incalculable |
| none | 0 | 0 | 0 | Incalculable | Incalculable |

Overall source 66/70 = 94.3%, applicable only to narrative positive examples intentionally enriched this time, and cannot be extrapolated to source occurrence rates in ordinary Storm Events. Source confusion matrix (rows human, columns model; order measured / damage_inferred / estimated_unspecified / observer_estimate / radar / none):

| Human＼Model | measured | damage_inferred | estimated_unspecified | observer_estimate | radar | none |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| measured | 34 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
