| none | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Failure cases (NCEI EVENT_NARRATIVE original text excerpts): 1078836 `A gust of 54 mph was reported at nearby Sacramento International Airport.` Human measured, model estimated_unspecified: although the airport wind report did not directly state measured, it does not equal measured at the damage point; 1015501 `An NWS damage survey found a couple of snapped large branches ... Winds were estimated to be 75 mph and time was estimated by radar.` Human estimated_unspecified, model damage_inferred: damage survey and wind estimation co-occurred, yet it was not explicitly stated to be based on damage; radar was only used for timing. 977217 `Wind gusts averaged between 35 and 50 knots. Wind gust of 45 knots (52 mph) was measured at WAL. Wind gust of 37 knots (43 mph) was measured at Parksley.` Human primary source measured, model primary source estimated_unspecified; however, the model's value-by-value array listed both measured stations alongside the preceding estimated speed range, indicating that a single primary_source obscures correct extraction of multiple values. Another case 1008617 narrative contains `The Broken Bow ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph at 457 pm CST.`, yet the model still marked the primary source as estimated_unspecified.

For multi-station multi-value 's `multi_case_audit`. This is merely sample returned count; human-paired gold standards have not been established value-by-value, and it cannot be claimed that recall for all stations and values has been verified; the model may misalign on range sentences, station aliases, or proxies. Station, timestamp, source, and excerpted sentence for each value must be retained; power outage alone is not recognized as physical damage, see .

## C Feasibility of Pairing DAT Damage Points–IEM Gusts

Read-only sources: NWS DAT FeatureServer point layer <https://services.dat.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/nws_damageassessmenttoolkit/DamageViewer/FeatureServer/0>; IEM ASOS/AWOS METAR query <https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/download.phtml>. Per URL, raw , . Points selected by DAT `efscale=Tropical` or and geographic time window; centered on the point's stormdate, hurricane ±12 h, thunderstorm ±3 h, finding the nearest station with non-empty METAR gust within 25 km, threshold cumulative; without point-by-point instrument QC or mechanism verification. DAT's built-in windspeed is a damage estimate and cannot be counted as an independent wind speed.

| Date/Region | DAT Points | DAT Estimated Wind Non-Empty | Neighbor Station Gust ≤5 km | ≤10 km | ≤25 km |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ian 2022, Florida | 9 | 7 | 0 | 7 | 9 |
| Ida 2021, LA/MS/AL | 122 | 3 | 10 | 40 | 98 |
| Dallas 2025-03-04 | 55 | 55 | 2 | 35 | 55 |
| Dallas 2019-06-16 | 37 | 37 | 0 | 34 | 37 |
| Houston 2024-05-16 | 20 | 20 | 0 | 2 | 20 |
| Hurricane Total | 131 | 10 | 10 | 47 | 107 |
| Thunderstorm Total | 112 | 112 | 2 | 71 | 112 |

38 DAT points for Ida are at 00:00 UTC, possibly having only date precision; after removing midnight timestamps, Ida ≤5/10/25 km candidates are 9/35/71, and Ian is 0/7/8; midnight cannot be uniformly judged as erroneous. The 25 km neighboring candidates for the 112 thunderstorm points correspond to only 6/7/7 station–time combinations for Dallas 2025/2019 and Houston, respectively; Ida's 98 candidates have only 28 groups, and Ian's 9 have only 4 groups. Multiple neighboring damage points sharing a single gust does not represent the same number of independent wind speed labels. Samples are selected DAT point days; time windows and distance thresholds are assumptions of this trial, not representative of the national total; hurricane categories do not guarantee that every point belongs to the specified cyclone, nor have storm surge/off-site facility mechanisms been excluded. The confirmed count of strict "damage point colocated and cotemporal with QC'd independent measurement" in this round is 0 (not verified record-by-record), which does not mean they do not exist.

H reconstruction was not invoked; reconstructed pairings are 0, separated from measured neighbor-station candidates and not entering the strict independent tier. When using H in the future, according to H protocol v1.1 §3, point-by-point recording in the fields listed in must include method, background, P1/P2 and window, wind quantity/averaging interval, distance to nearest input station, event type/RMW, and sample RMSE/bias of matching subsets; thunderstorms do not use reconstruction, and hurricane peak wind uses Holland+residual, not impersonated with the maximum of kriging time histories.

Next steps: Deduplicate by event/station–time among 10 km neighbor-station candidates and conduct human checks on instrument QC, DAT temporal precision, and damage mechanisms; simultaneously create value-by-value, station-by-station human gold standards for multi-station multi-value records (including proxy, radar, and source-less), then evaluate recall and pairing independence. Candidates can now be expanded, but 118 10 km candidates cannot be handed directly to design loads as ground truth.

## C Supplement: Window Peak Gust and Full-Scale Size (10-14 21:26 EDT)

Nearest-timestamp gusts from the original small trial have added , in .

All 18,434 points across both categories for 2019–2024 in the NWS DAT point layer were verified with pagination; IEM ASOS/AWOS (50 states + PR) searched point-by-point for the nearest spatial station within ≤25 km with gusts within ±3 h for thunderstorm and ±12 h for Tropical. Each cell in the table below represents "paired DAT points / station–time groups deduplicated by network, station, and nearest wind reporting UTC timestamp"; see , for full annual, hazard-specific breakdowns and query logs.

| DAT Hazard | Point Layer Total | ≤10 km Points / Groups | ≤25 km Points / Groups |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TSTM/Wind | 17,588 | 3,321 / 667 | 10,824 / 1,972 |
| Tropical | 846 | 156 / 35 | 426 / 86 |

Point-by-point lists nearest-timestamp and window-peak wind speeds (kt), timestamps, and differences; group-by-group . Positive DAT wind speeds are damage estimates, not independent measurements; the field itself is a string without units labeled, currently **presumed mph** from internal data consistency (Lab Lead sampled 500 points each starting from 2023 on 10-14: EF1 86–110, EF2 97–135, EF3 136–165, consistent with EF mph ranges; not an official dictionary); IEM gust is multiplied by 1.150779448 to convert to mph; negative sentinels and N/A are excluded. Within groups, first take the median difference across points of "DAT estimated wind − neighbor station maximum gust in point window", then compile group difference distributions: for TSTM/Wind ≤10 km 663 comparable groups, P10/median/P90 are +10.0/+37.0/+58.2 mph, and for ≤25 km 1,956 groups are +15.5/+39.7/+59.7; Tropical has only 5 / 14 comparable groups, with medians of +19.4 / +33.0 mph, too few to generalize. If actually in kt, DAT estimated wind converted to mph would be larger, leaving the direction of the dominant positive TSTM differences unchanged, but without guaranteeing that the sign of every single difference remains unchanged; official unit dictionary has still not been found. Confounding from spatial distance, windows, and station missing reports renders differences descriptive only, not causal estimates of damage wind estimation bias. Peaks >100 kt are retained and tagged; 8 points come from the same Ian/PGD peak, not 8 independent observations. Strict QC'd colocated and cotemporal truth pairs are still unverified (currently confirmed 0); 667 or 1,972 groups cannot be treated as real independent sample sizes.

New reproduction scripts , ; old r2 data and results are retained, the above is an additional supplement only. Next steps prioritize checking DAT wind speed units, PGD extremes, and DAT midnight temporal precision, performing storm-stratified deduplication and human QC on ≤10 km station–time groups before determining usable scale.

## C Supplement: Read-Only Reuse of H4 Dallas Days and H2 Hurricanes (10-14 21:30 EDT)

Added , ; 2025 DAT raw point pagination files. Existing 2019–2024 full tables and the aforementioned small trial do not cover this, and this subset is not added to the national scale (which would double-count). H4 directly reads the query origins of the five-day , and , no longer downloading one-minute data. In , H2 land scoring stations are 110 for Idalia and 95 for Helene; although Beryl has 109 stations, its corresponding DAT Tropical point query for 2024-07-07 to 07-11 returned 0, so the first two events were chosen, reading only the H2 land station table and cached IEM METAR (not invoking H2 predictions). DAT points for the two H2 events are filtered solely by date and state bounds, with no guarantee that they belong to the specified hurricane.

| Subset / DAT UTC Day | DAT Points (Study Area) | H4/H2 Station List | Measured Neighbor-Station Candidates ≤5 km Points / Station–Time Groups | ≤10 km | ≤25 km | Reconstructed Points |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| H4 2024-05-28 | 0 | 14 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0 |
| H4 2024-06-01 | 0 | 14 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0 |
| H4 2025-03-04 | 83 | 14 | 2/2 | 3/3 | 52/9 | 0 |
| H4 2025-06-09 | 33 | 14 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0 |
| H4 2025-07-09 | 0 | 14 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0 |
| H2 Idalia (2023-08-28 to 09-02) | 18 | 128 | 4/3 | 5/3 | 8/4 | 0 |
| H2 Helene (2024-09-25 to 09-30) | 276 | 145 | 49/3 | 78/5 | 138/9 | 0 |

H4 DAT takes Texas 31.5–34°N, 95.5–98.5°W, UTC day; H4's pre-stored regional peak ±3 h window contains non-empty, 0–150 kt one-minute `gust_sknt`, further requiring DAT point time ±3 h; H2 uses event dates, corresponding state geographic bounds, and H2 land stations with non-empty METAR gust in the original full IEM monthly cache, with DAT point time ±12 h. Each point takes the nearest station within 25 km having wind speed in the window, additionally listing the nearest-timestamp gust, the station window peak, and the difference; grouping key remains station ID + nearest gust valid timestamp. The 83 points for H4 2025-03-04 are more than the 55 points in the earlier Dallas small trial because filtering here is by the H4 study area rather than the earlier Dallas bounding box; 10 km pairings are only 3 points, fewer than the 35 points in earlier hourly METAR, and cannot be conflated as the same support set (one-minute archive missing reports, H4 window limitations, and different station cleaning). DAT being 0 in this box for the two 2024 days does not mean Storm Events had no thunderstorms; 2025-07-09 DAT had 0 TSTM/Wind nationwide on that day. On 2025-06-09 there were 33 points in the box, but 0 pairings within the aforementioned H4 minute window / 25 km. Raw DAT point counts are unique by ID, and output 198 point-station records are unique; counts see JSON.

Footprint scale source: NOAA JetStream "Thunderstorm Hazards - Damaging Wind" "Microbursts and Macrobursts" (webpage without page numbers) gives microburst diameter <4 km, general downburst lateral extent up to 10 km; Romanic, Taszarek, Brooks (2022), *Weather and Climate Extremes* 37:100474, abstract / journal page 1 likewise gives 4 km boundary between micro/macro, DOI https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wace.2022.100474. This is not mechanism certification for DAT points: among the 52 25 km candidates for H4 March, point-by-point tags by distance to station are: ≤4 km 1, 4–10 km 2, 10–25 km 49; more distant neighbor station peaks cannot be converted without error into point-location wind speeds. Hurricane spatial correlation should compare real-time center distance/RMW at that point; `rmw_ratio` on the H2 station grid is not the RMW of the DAT point, so `rmw_bin=unknown` this time, without inventing a peripheral bin. H2 `grid_*` only provides Holland/background at station locations, not at DAT point locations; station reconstructed values were not moved to damage points, nor was point-by-point Holland+residual run, resulting in 0 reconstructed pairings. If separate point-by-point reconstruction is to be performed, strictly record according to H v1.1 §3 the P2/landfall window, method/background, gust 5 s or sustained approx. 2 min, distance to input station, RMW bin, and matching holdout subset RMSE/bias; gusts and sustained winds at strong wind stations must not be mixed. For H v1.1 strong wind station sustained wind P2 Holland+residual, sample RMSE/bias is 3.45/−0.66 m/s; near-core underestimation and single-event bias must both be listed separately; the maximum of ordinary kriging time histories cannot substitute, nor are reconstructions counted as strict independent wind speeds.

This supplement only verifies data reuse and candidate scale: neighbor-station measurements have also not undergone review for instrument quality, colocation and cotemporality, storm attribution, and damage mechanism, with strict independent ground truth confirmations remaining 0. The earlier full 2019–2024 annual by-hazard table remains valid, but belongs to "station–time group candidates N", not an independent statistical sample size; H4 dates include 2025 and must not be merged into this full-volume denominator. Next steps prioritize conducting human spatio-temporal/instrument QC on the three H4 March ≤10 km points and the three Helene ≤5 km groups, before considering truly generating P2 Holland+residual at DAT point locations according to H v1.1, without using H2 station grid values as make-weight.

# Hurricane Pilot r3 Supplement: Helene Prioritization and Near-Station Group Human Check (2026-10-14)

This page is merged into Step 3, following the revised version of , .

## Verification of Helene ≤10 km Neighbor-Station Groups

Filtering H2_HELENE and distance_km≤10 from , then grouping by `(station, nearest_utc)`, and using to verify raw DAT damage and model fields: exactly 78 points belong to the 5 groups in the table below. Distances are ranges within the group; station gusts are raw archive values for that station in that window, without instrument quality control or proof of identical location and identical hour.

| Group (UTC) | DAT Points | Point-to-Station Distance km | Neighbor Station Gust kt | Main Damage Type / Verification |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| GA:AZE 09-27 04:35 | 16 | 5.787–9.766 | 34 | Primarily trees; all 16 points have DAT time 09:00, 04:35 cannot be treated as instantaneous damage wind; model sustained peak RMW bin `<1`. Example ID 4240438 is uprooted hardwood (DOD 3), point model gust 39.185 m/s, peak time 07:00. |
| GA:DNL 09-27 07:31 | 48 | 1.274–7.140 | 40 | Primarily trees; all 48 points have DAT time 09:35. The same station-time is repeatedly matched to 48 points and cannot count as 48 independent observations. ID 4234502 note is "Hardwood trees down on house. Estimated 100+ mph", where the estimate in its `windspeed`/note does not count as independent wind; model peak gust 32.479 m/s (10:00), 18.994 km to nearest input station. |
| GA:HQU 09-27 08:55 | 1 | 9.565 | 52 | ID 4238509: Snapped softwood trunk, note "Estimated 80+ mph"; DAT time 10:15; model peak gust 33.698 m/s (10:00), RMW bin `<1`. |
| GA:SBO 09-27 07:15 | 2 | 2.525–2.536 | 47 | Both points are softwood trees; DAT time 09:30. ID 4240478 DOD 1, model peak gust 38.446 m/s (09:00), nearest model input station 82.564 km, exceeding the verified distance range of the H protocol and cannot be used to calibrate local point values. |
| GA:VDI 09-27 05:55 | 11 | 1.680–9.606 | 44 | Primarily trees; all 11 points have DAT time 09:30. ID 4240473 snapped softwood trunk (DOD 4), model peak gust 40.355 m/s (08:00). |

The concentrated identical timestamps suggest these may be batch survey/entry times; without DAT field definitions and point-by-point raw survey forms, it cannot be confirmed whether these are actual damage occurrence times. None of the 5 groups are colocated and cotemporal ground-truth groups. FR12 for Helene has only 10 points, and the original report's assessment of no apparent monotonic trend still holds; the 78 near-station tree and miscellaneous points cannot be substituted as residential trend samples.

## Dallas 2025-03-04 Three-Point Verification (Old H4 Comparison Only; Thunderstorms No Longer Expanded)

The three ≤10 km records from were compared record-by-record with notes in the cached official DAT : ID 4368928, FR12, DAL 7.435 km, DAT 11:27, nearest-timestamp gust 19 kt, window maximum 68 kt (11:34), note "Shingle damage to a few homes"; ID 4368929, warehouse WHB, DAL 4.228 km, DAT 11:30, nearest 25 kt, maximum 68 kt (11:34), note "Debris from roof blown eastward to Mockingbird Rd. Traffic signals out in area."; ID 4383721, manufactured home single-wide MHSW, TKI 3.203 km, DAT 11:47, nearest 39 kt (11:45), maximum 55 kt, note contains "radar indicated straight line winds around 95 mph ... base velocity of 82 knots at 1000 ft". The last item is radar-inferred rather than measured at a surface station and cannot be conflated into the independent wind speed side. The first two points share the same DAL window maximum observation and do not equal two independent extreme values. Microburst scale background see the NWS `Downbursts` link in the original report (webpage without page numbers); although the three points are spatially close, local gusts are not guaranteed to appear at the observation station.

## Judgment and Follow-up

Helene has the largest number of near-station points and was prioritized for screening, but 78 points correspond to only 5 neighbor-station timestamps, and are primarily trees; Ida's 75 FR12 points are superior to Helene's 10 points, suitable for the next round of building type/mechanism spot checks; Idalia has only 4 FR12 points, used as a supplement. That all 416 points in original r3 can be reconstructed does not equate to 416 independent measured pairs. DAT date/timestamp, station as-is quality, peak time misalignment, RMW near-core, and >80 km input station distances must all be checked point-by-point; undamaged buildings must be added to estimate damage probability. Currently, neither can a reliable FR12 monotonic trend be fitted, nor can reconstructed wind speeds be treated as strict independent measurements. DAT `windspeed` is presumed mph from internal spot checks of consistency by Lead on 10-14, but official field definitions have not been found; mph differences in the original report remain descriptive comparisons only, see for details.

Sources: NWS DAT FeatureServer point layer <https://services.dat.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/nws_damageassessmenttoolkit/DamageViewer/FeatureServer/0>; internal track (official response cache), (IEM and DAT pairing), (DAT fields and H2 point-location reconstruction), methods and limitations see in detail , H station reconstruction protocol v1.1 §3. DAT sources have been listed, and this page contains no new external data sources.

results.text:
# Loss–Wind Speed Database r3: DAT Hurricane Points × H2 Point Reconstructions (2026-10-14)

## One-Sentence Judgment
In this DAT sample where only damaged instances are entered into the database, H2 reconstructed peak winds can be paired to the points, but residential damage degree for FR12 has no discernible monotonic trend with reconstructed gusts; therefore, it is worthy of point-by-point screening/quality control, but insufficient to fit damage–wind speed functions or claim independent measured relationships. Reconstructions are not point measurements, and DAT's built-in estimated winds are not independent wind speeds.

## Reproducible Artifacts and Per-Point Table
 stores per-point records and screening IDs;  summarizes;  is the residential scatter and binning plot; `pilot_hurricane_r3.pydoddod_txtdamage_txt` are all from the original API; original r2 full ID list; H2 source code ,  and existing `grid_*_expanded.csv.gz`, H protocol see §3. H and IEM files were not rewritten.

## Events, Algorithms, and Calibers
Select H2-tested events Ida (2021, priority), Idalia (2023), Helene (2024): screen points by DAT `efscale=Tropical`, dates near the event, and wide bounding boxes, rather than by DAT lines 21–67,  lines 27–67; the 40-station cap is an **assumption** for local residuals and computational load in this run, differing from H2's leave-one-out scoring support set across the entire valid station set.

Sustained winds and gusts come from different residuals / different peak times; sustained winds are compared with METAR ~2-minute mean winds, while gusts are compared according to H2's 5-second assumption; H2's original 500 m reference height, 2-minute/5-second, and land exposure conversions are all assumptions rather than DAT product definitions (H protocol §2). The per-point table provides distance to the nearest valid input station, peak-time distance-to-center/RMW bin, and leave-one-out station P2 sample RMSE/bias (m/s, not a per-point guarantee) for H2 using the same method for each event. For instance, Ida high-wind station / near-eye samples cannot be represented by the near-zero bias across all stations. Predicted peaks carry underestimation risks, especially in strong winds / near the core; station model errors, missing reports, and unverified distant station extrapolations may alter the wind speed axis. DAT `stormdate` date precision is unknown; some midnight records are treated as full-day time without forcing instantaneous interpretation.

The neighboring station measured column is independent of the model reconstructed column: using r2-cached IEM ASOS/AWOS METARs, reporting that station's window peak based on the nearest station within DAT time ±12 h and distance ≤10 km (taking maximum gust if distances are identical); IEM is taken as-is without instrument, peak, reporting time, storm attribution, or colocation audits. DAT `windspeed` is strictly used as a damage description throughout. The NWS FeatureServer field table only gives `String` for this field without specifying units; on 10-14, Lab Lead sampled 500 points each from 2023 onward, finding EF1 86–110, EF2 97–135, EF3 136–165, matching EF mph intervals; thus, the comparison column **presumes mph from data internal consistency** (m/s × 2.2369362921), not confirmed by an official data dictionary, and cannot serve as a quantitative calibration conclusion. If actually in kt, the differences between DAT and model would shift upward overall, and the sign of each difference cannot be guaranteed to remain unchanged. Non-numeric and -99 do not participate in comparisons. <https://services.dat.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/nws_damageassessmenttoolkit/DamageViewer/FeatureServer/0>

| Event | DAT Tropical Points / Reconstructible | FR12 (Numeric DOD Available) | Neighboring Station Gust Candidates ≤10 km | DAT Positive Wind Speeds Comparable (Presumed Unit mph) | Median Difference of DAT Estimated Wind − Reconstructed Gust, Presumed mph | FR12 DOD–Reconstructed Gust Spearman (Descriptive) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ida | 122/122 | 75 | 40 | 3 | +24.00 | +0.083 |
| Idalia | 18/18 | 4 | 5 | 10 | −47.31 | −0.738 (n=4 has no inferential value) |
| Helene | 276/276 | 10 | 78 | 11 | +8.32 | +0.052 |
| Total | 416/416 | 89 | 123 | 24 | Do not pool cross-event differences | Do not pool cross-event correlations |

The above numbers are recalculated from the per-point table by ; when mixing the three events, intensity, housing stock, and survey selection bias differ, so point counts cannot be equated to independent statistical samples. For Ida FR12, DOD 2 accounts for 60/75; its median reconstructed gusts in m/s for DOD 1/2/3/4 are 19.71 / 25.99 / 24.36 / 25.91, respectively, which is non-monotonic. Helene corresponding DOD 1/2/4 are 33.51 / 33.24 / 34.12 (n=10), Idalia DOD 1/2/4 are 74.33 / 38.77 / 72.78 (n=4); these are not damage threshold estimates. All points are already damaged, lacking undamaged buildings as denominators; bubble numbers in the figure are damaged point counts, not damage probabilities; points in the same survey cluster are highly correlated. FR12 DOD is only a rating within a building type and cannot be mixed across different DIs as a single numeric damage scale.

## Limitations, StEER, and Next Steps
DAT does not guarantee hazard attribution purely to wind: tree falls on houses, rain/waves/flooding, and differences in building age and construction have not been audited point by point. 12/75 Ida FR12 points have times of 00:00 UTC, possibly preserving only the date; these must not be forcibly co-registered to specific hours. For Helene FR12, the median distance to the nearest model input station is 61.56 km, and distance errors >80 km in the H protocol are unverified; Idalia FR12 point counts are too small and local extremes are relatively high, so background and survey times should be spot-checked first. Performing regression directly across all damaged points incurs selection bias.

StEER's Ida report and Idalia DesignSafe project web page are publicly available: <https://doi.org/10.17603/ds2-w6km-fe51>, <https://www.designsafe-ci.org/data/browser/public/designsafe.storage.published/PRJ-4123>. In this round, no batch table with building-by-building coordinates + DOD that can be obtained directly without login and with clear fields was verified, so StEER points were not fabricated; only DAT was used. StEER materials cannot automatically be regarded as independent wind speed observations.

The previous thunderstorm step is put on hold. The NWS description of microburst scales is approx. <4 km (NWS `Downbursts` web page, no print page number: <https://www.weather.gov/ohx/downbursts>); this serves as scale context for general mechanisms rather than downburst attribution for any single DAT point. Neighboring station thunderstorm winds at 10–25 km in r2 cannot be equated to core winds; specific storms could also be gust fronts/macrobursts, requiring mechanism verification.

Step four recommendations: First manually spot-check the 75 Ida FR12 points (especially duplicate coordinates, 00:00 UTC, DOD text, and housing/water damage mechanisms), checking stormdate and H2 station peak/near-eye residuals point by point; supplement exposure/undamaged buildings as well as construction era, stratifying by building and survey cluster; then decide whether to add StEER building-by-building public tables or expand to hurricanes with clear storm attribution. Although DAT `windspeed` is presumed to be mph based on internal consistency, an official data dictionary and quality control bounds are still needed to quantitatively interpret the estimated wind − reconstructed wind speed difference. Reconstructed points cannot enter the strict "independent measured" category.

Parameter sources: P2 ±12 h, RMW bins, and scoring criteria are H v1.1 §0/§1/§3 (subsequent v1.2 §4 does not calibrate hurricane Holland + residual); 75 km, 0.08, and H08 original parameters are H2 metadata and  output comes with this verification.

## Correction: Idalia Near-Core Extrapolated Values Invalidated (Historical Numbers Retained Above)
NHC Idalia Tropical Cyclone Report AL102023 page 5 (report body page number; PDF page number may differ) gives a maximum sustained wind estimate at landfall of 100 kt, approx. 51.4 m/s; page 6 gives Perry's measured maximum gust of 74 kt. In the original per-point table, the reconstructed sustained winds for Idalia FR12 DAT objectids 3811111, 3811125, and 3811127 were 55.8–57.1 m/s, unexpectedly exceeding NHC's landfall intensity estimate; the H2 sustained winds and corresponding peak wind speed interpretations for these three near-core points are uniformly designated as **extrapolation distortion, invalidated**, and cannot be used for damage–wind speed trends or physical interpretations of DAT estimated wind differences. The previously mentioned 416/416 pairing count, Idalia FR12 correlations/bins, and aggregate differences merely retain historical calculation traces and are not valid point wind speed evidence; original numbers were not recalculated or overwritten. Perry's 74 kt is a gust from another station and is not directly compared quantity-for-quantity with the sustained winds at the three points. Original report: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/AL102023_Idalia.pdf.

# 损失–风速库 r4：公开逐栋损伤分母数据可得性核查（2026-10-14）

## 判定
找到可直接做下一轮小样本配对的公开数据：CRASAR-U-DROIDs，优先 Ida/Idalia 内陆风损较清楚的局部影像覆盖区；它的 JSON 有建筑多边形 EPSG:4326、`building_id` 和 `no damageminor damagemajor damagedestroyed` 等标签，许可 CC BY 4.0，无需批量下载影像，也无需特殊授权。与 H2 Ida、Idalia、Ian 三场重合；但这是灾后影像覆盖内的“可见无损”分母，不是整个县的建筑存量或地面确认的零损伤；未核风、洪、浪致损的归因。先做小片区去重/机制审核和风速重建，不能直接当总体脆弱性曲线。[1][9]

| 3811125 | 2023-08-30 12:00 | 74.203 | 58.200 | +16.003 | 20.94 / 18.52 | 1.131 | 26.59 |
| 3811127 | 2023-08-30 12:00 | 74.451 | 58.691 | +15.759 | 22.17 / 18.52 | 1.197 | 28.39 |
| 3811135 | 2023-08-30 13:00 | 38.768 | 41.837 | −3.068 | 29.55 / 21.61 | 1.368 | 1.96 |

前三点在峰时 RMW 外沿约 1.1–1.2 倍，是**近核高背景 + 正残差**，并非 0 m/s 非负截断伪值；24.9–28.4 km 外站残差插值仍可能高估局部峰，H2 事件留一阵风 RMSE 3.327 m/s 不能作为这些点的误差保证。第四点有近站但低很多，提示空间梯度很大。r3 原表的 `rmw_ratio_at_sustained_peak` 恰与此三点峰时相同，但该列定义是持续风峰时；本次显式在**阵风峰时**重新计算，避免把两个峰时混用。尚未核 DAT 时间精度、波浪/洪水和近眼站点真实性，72–74 m/s 不作点位真值。

## 下一步建议

选择 CRASAR Idalia Steinhatchee 的单个事后 crewed JSON（已确认 473 个无损视图），外加 Ida Cocodrie 作第二个区域；在事后影像覆盖内按建筑 ID 去重、筛海潮/洪水与遮挡、检查类别与 H2 坐标范围，再对每个建筑质心只读重建 P2 阵风，按建筑簇/bootstrap 而不是按视图独立样本计算损伤概率分箱。**优先验证风致损机制与模型峰值偏低/局部高估风险，再决定是否扩 Ian**；不把影像无损当全天候/内部构件完好，也不把 DAT 估风当风速。这个试验可以回答局部影像内是否有描述性梯度，不能单靠它推广全国风脆弱性。

## 开源仓库核验（GitHub REST 仓库元数据 + 默认分支最新 commit API，2026-10-14 查询）

| 仓库 | stars | 最近默认分支提交日期 | 仓库许可证 | 本环境 |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| https://github.com/DIUx-xView/xView2_baseline | 243 | 2020-07-29 | GitHub NOASSERTION（仓库授权文件须单核；不等于 xBD 数据许可） | 可读代码；本次无需训练 |
| https://github.com/USACE-NSI/NSI | 20 | 2022-10-14 | MIT（代码仓库） | 可读 API 说明，不必下载全国点 |
| https://github.com/CRASAR/CRASAR-U-DROIDs-BDA | 0 | 2026-05-07 | 未标许可证（不能默认为开源许可；数据卡 CC BY 4.0 另计） | 可读代码；本轮只解析原始 JSON |
| https://github.com/CRASAR/CRASAR-U-DROIDs-RDA | 0 | 2026-01-07 | 未标许可证 | 可读代码；本轮无需运行 |

上述四个仓库并非项目数据本身；论文对应 xBD 原论文见 [2]、CRASAR 论文见 [9]。最近提交日期为 GitHub 默认分支的日期，不是 `pushed_at`。

## Sources

[1] https://huggingface.co/datasets/CRASAR/CRASAR-
[2] https://xview2.org/dataset
[3] https://www.fema.gov/openfema-data-page/housing-assistance-program-data-owners-v2
[4] https://www.fema.gov/openfema-data-page/individuals-and-households-program-valid-registrations-v2
[5] https://www.arcgis.com
[6] https://arxiv.org/html/2208.02205v2
[7] https://designsafe-ci.org/data/browser/public/designsafe.storage.published/PRJ-5770
[8] https://data.nist.gov/od/id/mds2-3978
[9] https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.17673
[10] https://www.designsafe-ci.org/data/browser/public/designsafe.storage.published/PRJ-3268
[11] https://www.designsafe-ci.org/data/browser/public/designsafe.storage.published/PRJ-4123
[12] https://www.designsafe-ci.org/community/dataset-awards

## 更正：Idalia FR12 近核外推值作废（原分解表留档，不重算）
上文 objectid 3811111、3811125、3811127 的 72–74 m/s 阵风虽不是数值截断造成，却不能再解释为可信点位峰值：其配套 H2 重建持续风 55.8–57.1 m/s 超过 NHC Idalia 登陆最大持续风估计 100 kt（约 51.4 m/s）。判为**近核外推失真，作废**；原表的背景和残差分解只作诊断痕迹，不能据此推损伤阈值或拟合。NHC 同报告给 Perry 最大实测阵风 74 kt，属异地、不同平均时距，不能直接与三个点的持续风比较。出处：NHC Tropical Cyclone Report AL102023，报告正文第 5 页（100 kt）和第 6 页（Perry 74 kt），https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/AL102023_Idalia.pdf。历史数字未覆盖。

results.text:
# 损失–风速库 r5：CRASAR 逐栋分母 × H2 重建（探索性，2026-10-14）

## 一句话判断
本轮在两个事后正射影像小片区取得 1,024 栋可用标签及点位 H2 风速，但保守水损风险筛选后**没有可用于风致损概率分析的建筑**。含疑似水损的描述性图里，Ian 没有单调梯度；Idalia 的分箱有起伏但非单调。**不宜现在写风致损曲线或转正提案**；先寻找经验证无淹没、跨更宽风速带的内陆调查片区。

## 资料、选区和去重
CRASAR-U-DROIDs 数据卡许可 CC BY 4.0；按固定 revision 、；每个被选视图中 building_id 唯一。

剔除 obscured/un-classified；Idalia 第二张事后视图 20230902a 与首张共有 137 个 ID，其中 10 个标签不同（含 4 个明确 no/minor 冲突），保守地将首视图中的这 10 栋从评分排除，冲突仍在 明列。Ian 无同片区第二张 crewed 视图可检。最后 Ian 912 栋（no/minor/major/destroyed = 428/351/125/8），Idalia 112 栋（99/9/3/1）。这些是影像可见损伤，不等于结构检查或随机抽取的全部暴露建筑。[1]

## 风速和水损风险口径
逐栋多边形顶点均值作为质心近似，H2 在本机只读复算 CLIMADA H08 Holland 背景 + H2 陆地站残差普通克里金（固定 75 km；最多近 40 站），在各事件登陆 ±12 h 的 24 个整点求 P2 峰值；持续风与假设的 5 s 阵风分别求峰。输出 逐栋记录原值、P2 窗口、峰时、背景/残差、最近输入站距离、阵风峰时中心距/RMW 档、事件留一 RMSE/偏差、事件类型及版本。H 协议 v1.2 对飓风 Holland+残差不加校正（校正 0，保留 raw）；**重建非点位实测**，RMSE 是样本统计而非逐栋保证，且风轴可能存在事件/点位偏差。H2 的海陆筛选、源站停报、2 min/5 s 与 500 m 参考高度假设照旧；不能据此归因风损。

3DEP bare-earth DEM 小区域栅格（`r5_3dep_*.tifr5_nhc_*_forecast_inundation.tif`），非观测淹没；官方字典中 class 1 是 0–1 英尺潜在地面积水，非零仅表示潜在风险，P-Surge 的 10% 超越水平并非实际水位。[2][3]
对应归档下载页分别为 Ian [6] 与 Idalia [7]。
NHC 也明确该层不计雨洪和河流流量，0 类不能证明没淹过。[3]
Ian 官方事后报告描述海岸与内河风暴潮和雨洪并存，不能只凭影像类别分出风致损。[5]

预先明示的**保守筛选假设**：NHC 潜在淹没 class>0，或地面高程<3 m，或粗尺度岸线距离<5 km，任一即标“疑似水损/风暴潮风险”，主分析排除；这是高敏感度风险代理，**不是实测水损判定**，可误排真风损。敏感性档仅以高程<2 m 或岸距<3 km 标风险，不用 NHC 潜在淹没，仍非无水真值。阈值是本次探索性假设，无来源声称；分区 500 m 网格作空间簇，随机种子 20261014、600 次簇 bootstrap 仅估条件抽样变异，不包括洪水误分、建筑选择偏差和 H2 系统风速误差。

## 样本流与筛选结果

| 片区 | 原始视图 | 无效/冲突剔除 | 可用独栋 | 有 NHC 潜在淹没 | 保守排风险后 | 放宽地形代理后 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ian Harlem Heights | 975 | 63 | 912 | 912 | **0** | 23（2 空间簇） |
| Idalia Jena | 139 | 27（其中 10 冲突） | 112 | 96 | **0** | 25（2 空间簇） |

原始质心高程范围：Ian 1.32–3.30 m，Idalia −0.98–6.07 m；粗尺度岸距 Ian 2.04–3.30 km、Idalia 1.10–3.66 km。即使 Idalia 有若干潜在淹没图外点，也未同时通过高程/距岸保守门槛。放宽档 Ian 19 no/4 minor，Idalia 24 no/1 minor，均无 ≥major；它们仍可能水损，且只有各 2 个簇。**主结果无可画概率曲线**，不能把下图全样本图当水损排除后的结果。

## 含疑似水损的对照：描述性分箱，不能归因

图 分事件、分阈值展示全部可用建筑的可见损伤比例，误差棒是 500 m 簇 bootstrap 的 2.5–97.5 百分位。图上 `c` 为单个箱涉及的空间簇数；只有一个簇时区间退化，**不表示无不确定性**。两事件风速及损伤构成完全不可混池。

| 片区 | H2 阵风箱 (m/s) | n / 簇 | ≥minor | ≥major |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ian | 73.9–74.0 | 209 / 3 | 119/209 = 56.9% | 43/209 = 20.6% |
| Ian | 74.0–74.1 | 494 / 5 | 262/494 = 53.0% | 55/494 = 11.1% |
| Ian | 74.1–74.2 | 179 / 3 | 94/179 = 52.5% | 35/179 = 19.6% |
| Ian | 74.2–74.3 | 30 / 1 | 9/30 = 30.0% | 0/30 = 0% |
| Idalia | 55–56 | 15 / 2 | 1/15 = 6.7% | 0/15 |
| Idalia | 56–57 | 46 / 5 | 2/46 = 4.3% | 0/46 |
| Idalia | 57–58、58–59 | 0 | 未定义 | 未定义 |
| Idalia | 59–60 | 23 / 7 | 5/23 = 21.7% | 3/23 = 13.0% |
| Idalia | 60–61 | 28 / 3 | 5/28 = 17.9% | 1/28 = 3.6% |

Ian 同片区的重建阵风仅 73.927–74.224 m/s，跨度 0.297 m/s，远小于 H2 的 Ian 事件阵风留一 RMSE 4.475 m/s（Idalia 为 3.327 m/s；仅为站点样本误差，不能移作点位误差界）；而≥minor 在微小风速差内略下降，不是单调递增。Idalia 55.918–60.661 m/s，但 57–59 m/s 两箱为空，分组空间离散且≥minor 在最高箱反降；表观阶跃不能排除潮水/地势/片区差异。含疑似水损版本仅用作反例，不用于风致损概率拟合。放宽地形档总共 48 栋、4 簇、≥major 为零，无区分高损伤概率的统计支撑。

## 限制、复算与下一步
### 补充：阵风峰时按 RMW 档分层（2026-10-14；不覆盖原图）
按 H 协议 v1.2 §3，以**每栋重建阵风 P2 峰时**中心距/RMW（ 的 `rmw_ratio_at_gust_peak`、`rmw_bin_at_gust_peak`）将可用标签拆为 `<1`、`1–3`、`>3`、unknown；分层分箱图另存 （ 只读复算）。分事件、不跨片区合并。注意两处都**只有 `1–3 RMW<1 RMW1–3 RMW` 楼栋点位校正**，Holland+残差本轮不加校正。

| 事件和 RMW 档 | 阵风分箱 m/s | n / 簇 | ≥minor | ≥major | 严格水风险筛除后 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ian，1–3 | 73.9–74.0 / 74.0–74.1 / 74.1–74.2 / 74.2–74.3 | 209/3；494/5；179/3；30/1 | 119/209；262/494；94/179；9/30 | 43/209；55/494；35/179；0/30 | 0 |
| Idalia，1–3 | 55–56 / 56–57 / 57–58 / 58–59 / 59–60 / 60–61 | 15/2；46/5；0/0；0/0；23/7；28/3 | 1/15；2/46；—；—；5/23；5/28 | 0/15；0/46；—；—；3/23；1/28 | 0 |
| 两片区，<1 / >3 / unknown | — | 各 0 | 不可估 | 不可估 | 0 |

这与原结果同一批楼栋，不能当独立复现。水风险排除后无样本，含风险对照仍没有可归因风致损的单调梯度；仅 `1–3 RMW` 有样本意味着 RMW 分层并未扩大风速轴或改善近核外推判定。图的标注含 CRASAR-U-DROIDs (CC BY 4.0)、H2/NHC 最佳路径及“重建、非实测”。

1. NHC 栅格是登陆前潜在淹没，而非事件实测高水痕或逐栋水损；3DEP 2026 服务数据用于旧事件有年代错配；Natural Earth 海岸距漏小河渠。此筛查故意保守，也暴露出 CRASAR 当前两片区无法做可信风损归因。须找实际观测/事后淹没、首层标高及建筑类别才可解开。[3][4]
2. 影像仅见外部可见损伤；未据房屋类型、建年或屋顶形式标准化。两事件 H2 误差与强风存活站偏差可能大于本地风速跨度；区间只计算标签簇变异，不能作脆弱性置信带。
3. 下一轮先在 CRASAR 全部标签元数据或另一公开逐栋调查中找地势更高、经事后淹没核实的同一事件**内陆**片区；预先冻结片区/阈值、确认足够风速跨度和多个独立空间簇，再做风/水损机理审核及不同建筑类型分层。若仍无足够未淹水样本，则暂搁置 CRASAR→风致损概率这一特定路线，而非否定独立风速–损失库方向。无需转正提案。

复现顺序（仅在**新输出目录**运行，勿覆盖现有成果）： → → → →，Python 为，H2 文件只读。生成 （1114 原始单视图模型记录）、（风速和筛查字段）、 也下载了两处额外 Ian 候选的仅标签 JSON 和 3DEP 小裁剪，不下载影像。

## Sources

[1] https://huggingface.co/datasets/CRASAR/CRASAR-
[2] https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/gis/inundation/potential_storm_surge_flooding_downloads_guide.pdf
[3] https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/surge/inundation/?text=
[4] https://elevation.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/3DEPElevation/ImageServer
[5] https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/AL092022_Ian.pdf
[6] https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/gis/archive_inundation_results.php?id=al09&year=22&name=Hurricane%20IAN
[7] https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/gis/archive_inundation_results.php?id=al10&year=23&name=Hurricane%20IDALIA

## 更正／图表注（保留原分箱与原图作为历史描述，不重算）
上文两张分箱表和原图是**含潜在水损风险的描述性存档**，不是有效风致损概率。Ian Harlem Heights 建筑的阵风峰时中心距/RMW 为 1.019–1.046（约 1.02–1.05），处于眼墙邻近；Idalia Jena 的阵风峰时比值为 2.060–2.144，但也没有逐栋点位的观测验证。两片区的重建阵风均标记为“近核／未观测验证”；凡包含这些楼栋的近核分箱均标记**未验证**，不用于主梯度判断。注意原 分类并未改变：这批楼栋都在 `1–3` 档，而不是 `<1<1 RMW` 有样本。主结论只依赖经筛查、且合格的 `1–3 RMW` 或外围建筑；本轮严格水损风险排除后实际合格 **0 栋**，故没有可判断的主梯度。Idalia r3 三个 DAT FR12 点的近核持续风已因超过 NHC Idalia 登陆强度估计而判外推失真、作废（见 末尾更正）；这里的 CRASAR Jena 建筑不是那三个 DAT 点，也同样不能视为已验证风速。

修订图为 、；保留原 和 不覆盖。这两张修订图在原画面下增设更正与来源条：近核分箱未验证、不用于主梯度，数据来自 CRASAR-U-DROIDs（Manzini 等，2024，arXiv:2407.17673，CC BY 4.0）、H2 重建（实验室 H 节点）、NHC 最佳路径及潜在淹没图、USGS 3DEP；本节上述两张历史分箱表也使用同一来源。[1][2][3][4] NHC 潜在淹没图非实测淹没。修订图仅加注，不改变散点、分箱数或统计结果。

projects.digest:
# Wind Damage Loss and Wind Speed Database (Shelved)

This sub-project tested whether large language models (LLMs) can extract structured wind-damage and wind-speed records from NOAA Storm Events narratives and post-storm surveys while separating independent wind measurements from damage-inferred estimates to avoid circularity when validating engineering loss metrics. Across five rounds at zero compute-unit cost, the team evaluated Gemini 3.8 Flash batch extraction against 10% audits and gold-standard sets, paired 18,434 National Weather Service (NWS) Damage Assessment Toolkit (DAT) survey points against Automated Surface Observing System (ASOS) gusts, coupled 416 hurricane DAT points with sibling Holland-plus-residual (`H2`) wind reconstructions, and analyzed 1,024 drone-labeled building footprints from `CRASAR-U-DROIDs`. Although LLM extraction achieved 94% (66/70) wind-source classification accuracy on hard positive cases, the sub-project was Shelved because public datasets lack independent core wind speeds for thunderstorms and lack surge-free inland building denominators across a wide wind-speed range for hurricanes.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead launched the sub-project under Liang Hu's directive to build an empirical loss-versus-wind-speed baseline, defining a six-way wind-source taxonomy (measured, radar, damage-inferred, visual estimate, estimated unspecified, and none) from NCEI and NWS Directive 10-1605 rules, and dispatching Round 1 on 300 stratified 2018–2023 Storm Events narratives (120 thunderstorm wind, 90 tropical cyclone, 90 high wind) plus a 60-item manually labeled gold standard.
- **2026-10-14**: Adding a 40-item 2010–2017 Texas supplement aligned with sibling station reconstruction work, a research assistant completed all 340 extractions via Gemini 3.8 Flash (0 CU), passing the 90% audit-agreement gate across all three primary batches.
- **2026-10-14**: Round 1 showed that while high-wind narratives contained 53% (48/90) independent (measured/radar) speeds and tropical narratives had 26 measured speeds among 54 citing wind values, only 2.5% (3/120) of thunderstorm narratives had non-damage-inferred measured speeds (116/120 labeled `EG` without stated basis).
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead caught a unit-comparison bug in the scoring script (where 59 kt vs. 68 mph—both ~30.4 m/s—was scored wrong) and dispatched Round 2: fixing unit scoring, evaluating a 70-item hard positive gold set, and testing spatial-temporal pairing of public NWS DAT points against ASOS gusts.
- **2026-10-14**: The research assistant delivered corrected scoring (raising tropical wind-value accuracy to 18/20 and station match to 15/20 tropical, 20/20 thunderstorm, and 19/20 high wind) and incorporated the sibling `Station Wind Reconstruction ProtocolH2`) cuts strong-wind hurricane peak RMSE by ~10%.
- **2026-10-14**: On the 70-item hard positive gold set, Gemini 3.8 Flash achieved 66/70 (94.3%) six-class wind-source accuracy, 34/34 precision and 34/37 recall on measured winds, and 16/17 precision and 16/16 recall on damage-inferred winds, confirming reliable filtering of circular speeds.
- **2026-10-14**: Scaling DAT–ASOS pairing across all 18,434 public 2019–2024 NWS DAT points (17,588 thunderstorm/wind and 846 tropical) showed that within 10 km (25 km), thunderstorm points collapsed to 667 (1,972) station-event groups and tropical points to 35 (86) groups; DAT damage-inferred thunderstorm speeds exceeded nearby (10 km) ASOS gusts by 37 mph median (positive in 97% of groups), and 49/52 Dallas pairs lay at 10–25 km—beyond microburst (<4 km) and downburst (~10 km) footprints.
- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead paused the thunderstorm track and dispatched Round 3: pairing 416 hurricane DAT points across Ida, Idalia, and Helene with `H2` peak wind reconstructions.
- **2026-10-14**: In Round 3, all 416 hurricane DAT points received `H2` winds, but the 89 residential (`FR12xBD`, `NSI`, `OpenFEMA`, `StEER`, and `CRASAR-U-DROIDs`), selecting `CRASAR-U-DROIDs` and verifying from 1,500 EF1–EF3 records that DAT speeds are in mph.
- **2026-10-14**: In Round 5, pairing 1,024 deduplicated `CRASAR` buildings (912 in Harlem Heights for Ian, 112 in Jena for Idalia) with `H2` winds showed gusts varying by 0.3 m/s across the Ian tile, conservative NHC surge filtering left 0 surge-free buildings (relaxed filtering left 48 with 0 major damage), all 1,024 buildings fell into one 1–3 Rmax bin, and three Idalia points with 72–74 m/s gusts exceeded the 100 kt (51.4 m/s) NHC landfall intensity and were invalidated; AI Weather Models Lead Shelved the sub-project.

## Where it stands

This sub-project is Shelved at zero compute-unit cost with a validated LLM narrative extraction pipeline (94% wind-source classification accuracy on hard positive cases) and five rounds of empirical pairing audits archived (33 MB locally). It can be reactivated if wide-swath, surge-verified inland hurricane building datasets with undamaged denominators across multiple Rmax bands become available, or if near-surface radar retrievals resolve thunderstorm core winds.

projects.report:
# H Observation–Simulation Fusion for Wind-Field Reconstruction

## Objective
Correct and reconstruct simulated surface wind fields using experimental and observational data (sparse station observations → continuous wind field). Step 1: literature review + leave-one-station-out benchmark on synoptic non-storm winds (Ordinary Kriging / background field + residual Kriging / machine learning) to quantify how much multi-source fusion beats strong interpolation baselines and whether it is worth continuing. Subsequent phases extend to typhoons/hurricanes, extratropical cyclones, and thunderstorms, providing reconstructed wind fields as an independent wind-speed input to Node I (wind-damage loss vs wind-speed database).

## Current Status
**Wrapped up on 10-14 (Shelved)**. Final deliverable: *Station Wind-Speed Reconstruction Protocol v1.2* (handed over to Node I): on the ASOS station network, `background + residual Kriging` improves over pure Ordinary Kriging by only `3–6%` (~`0%` for thunderstorms), reaching conditional utility only at sparse station spacing (~80 km) or high-wind hurricane stations; for hurricane event peaks, `Holland + residual` eliminates peak low bias, while hazard-stratified additive bias correction removes peak low bias across the remaining hazard classes (coarse estimate for thunderstorms). For thunderstorms, station interpolation underpredicts peaks by `3–5 m/s`, and both low-elevation single-Doppler radar trials (`H6` and `H7`) proved "inconclusive" and were wrapped up under the stop-loss rule as "infeasible under current public data constraints".
**Why Shelved**: Station reconstruction and peak correction across all four hazard classes are complete and delivered to Node I, while two targeted radar pilots on the thunderstorm track yielded no positive signal.
**Restart Conditions**: Node I uncovers a systematic flaw when applying the protocol; near-field surface observations become available to validate low-level radar winds inside thunderstorms; TDWR Level-II Nyquist unfolding is reliably resolved with stations sitting under `<300 m` beams; or official verification clarifies NWS DAT wind-speed units and estimation protocols.

## Compute and Storage Boundaries (Updated 10-15 per Liang Hu's 10-14 Tightening)
- **No compute or compute-data storage on the workstation**: If restarted, all solvers, batch leave-one-out runs, radar decoding, and large downloads must run and reside on CRC/TACC or Colab; the workstation holds only scripts, compact results (<200 MB per item), figures, and reports, with temporary staging >1 GB requiring prior parent-node approval. New large datasets prioritize TACC (CRC group storage is ~95% full), and CRC jobs default to single-node.
- Legacy compute data from this node have been archived to TACC by the root Lead and will be read from TACC if needed for future audits without pulling them back to the workstation. Earlier "0 CU local workstation run" clauses in the `H1–H7` briefs are superseded.
- No per-trial CU cap on Colab; pause and report to the parent node if a single trial is projected to exceed 100 CU; always run `colab stop` upon completion and dispatch only one execution agent per round.
- Cluster jobs require a ComputeOps resource request and registry entry, capped at ≤50 SU per job with separate pre-check and submission commands.

## Hierarchy Rules (Set by Root Lead on 10-14, 5-Layer Cap Post-Migration)
- Do not open Level-3 sub-projects under this Level-2 node; handle subdivisions via tasks inside this node or escalate to the parent node to open a sibling Level-2 node.
- Only two delegation hops remain below this node: `Lead → bot → tool`; briefs must not permit tool bots to re-delegate.
- Subtree listings follow the UI project tree rather than grouping by parent node.

## Decisions Made
- 2026-10-14 Step 1 design and evaluation criteria →
- 2026-10-14 **Wrap-up**: Protocol `v1.2` finalized as final deliverable; near-surface thunderstorm wind reconstruction declared infeasible with current public data →
- 2026-10-14 `H7` final pilot and stop-loss rule →
- 2026-10-14 `H6` thunderstorm radar pilot: inconclusive →
- 2026-10-14 `H5` verdict and protocol upgrade to `v1.2` →
- 2026-10-14 Protocol `v1` review verdict and release of `v1.1` →
- 2026-10-14 Finalize thunderstorm station test, wrap up leave-one-out phase, and submit Protocol `v1` for review →
- 2026-10-14 Finalize extratropical cyclone phase and launch `H4` thunderstorm pilot →
- 2026-10-14 Finalize hurricane phase and advance to extratropical cyclones →
- 2026-10-14 Wrap up synoptic non-storm phase and advance to landfalling hurricanes →
- 2026-10-14 `r1` verdict ("interpolation suffices") and pivot in `r2` to thinned station networks →

## Established Premises (In-Line Data)
- Pure interpolation baselines are strong: in the Lab's TPU wind-tunnel trial, ML beat interpolation on `0/5` strict interpolation splits; in Han 2026, pure Kriging achieved MAE `0.36–0.37 m/s`, outperforming LBM-LES at `0.46 m/s` (digital-twin wind-tunnel card, p. 39 Table 6).
- Generative data assimilation (`GenDA`) has been demonstrated only on 2D steady RANS slices of a single idealized urban block with synthetic sensor nodes and closed data.

## Trials and Results
| Date | What Was Done | One-Line Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-10-14 | Grok quick search + primary source verification by Lead | Verified real-station precedents: `KiloDA` (Shanxi complex terrain, 238 stations held out as a spatial block from 1,340 stations) reduced RMSE by `15.4%` over Kriging with `89.5%` of stations improved; Kiessling 2021 (Sweden) beat Universal Kriging by ~`5%`; synthetic twin-experiment gains (`49%`) excluded from real-station evidence; `S2G` numbers pending check |
| 2026-10-14 | `r1` Synoptic non-storm leave-one-station-out (research assistant; 137 stations, 31,898 station-hours) | OK `1.613`, IDW `1.634`; `ERA5 + residual OK` `1.553` (`−3.8%`, `81/137`); `GBT + residual` `1.524` (`−5.5%`, `87/137`); in the `>50 km` bin, OK `2.142` vs `GBT + residual` `1.625`; peaks broadly underpredicted by ~`1.5 m/s` → interpolation suffices |
| 2026-10-14 | `H7` Final thunderstorm radar pilot (2 Chicago cases, `KLOT` low beam + 108 DAT points; research assistant) | Test A had `0` qualified station events (beam height `385–736 m` over stations); in Test B (assuming DAT in mph), median `|radar − DAT|` was `16.0 m/s` vs `9.7 m/s` for `|nearest station − DAT|` → inconclusive, triggering stop-loss |
| 2026-10-14 | `H6` Thunderstorm radar near-surface feasibility (2 Dallas days, `KFWS` lowest tilt; research assistant) | Across 18 station-events: sustained peak bias shifted from `−3.59` (interpolation) to `−3.28 m/s` (radar) while RMSE worsened from `4.71` to `5.18 m/s`; beam height `258–1,646 m` AGL; `0` DAT thunderstorm points on those two days; TDWR unused → inconclusive |

| 2026-10-14 | `r1` Supplement (`WorldCover` 1 km land-cover stratification) | Urban built-up stations (16): `ERA5 + residual` `1.530` vs OK `1.523` (no improvement, `9/16`); non-built-up (121): `1.556` vs `1.625` (`−4.2%`, `72/121`) |

## Parameter Provenance Table

projects.brief:
# Task Brief: H Leave-One-Out Station Reconstruction for Synoptic Winds (Kriging vs. Background Field + Residual vs. Learning Methods) · 2026-10-14; proceed under standing authorization without seeking mid-course approval.

## Objective
Answer one question: on synoptic (non-convective) high-wind days, when reconstructing a continuous 10 m wind field from sparse surface stations, can "model background field + residual kriging" or a learning method be appreciably more accurate than the best pure interpolation (kriging/IDW)? The sole purpose is to judge whether the line is worth continuing, not to chase polish.

## Data (all public, read-only)
- Observations: ASOS/AWOS hourly METAR wind speed and direction (via the Iowa Environmental Mesonet interface, NCEI DSI 6405 source). Existing data-fetching code may be reused.
- Background fields: ERA5 (ARCO-ERA5 public Zarr, 10 m u/v); HRRR (AWS public bucket, using **f01–f03 forecasts**, not the f00 analysis — f00 already assimilates these stations, which would contaminate leave-one-out). Optionally add URMA/RTMA as an "operational product reference", but since it ingests these stations itself, list it for reference only and exclude it from the criterion.
- Terrain / land-surface covariates (optional): station elevation, NLCD or ESA WorldCover roughness class.
- Region: central and eastern Texas, covering the four cities Dallas–Austin–San Antonio–Houston (aligned with the four Texas cities in the event line), roughly 28–34°N, 94–100°W, targeting ≥60 stations.
- Dates: 10–20 synoptic high-wind days from the 2020–2021 cold season (post-frontal / synoptic-scale high winds). Screening: a substantial fraction of station-hours in the region have wind speed ≥8 m/s; no thunderstorms in the region on that day (no TS/CB in METAR, no Thunderstorm Wind in Storm Events); state the screening rules and selected dates clearly.

## Methods (at least the following; more may be added)
1. Pure interpolation: IDW, ordinary kriging (variogram fitted hourly or daily; state the procedure clearly).
2. Background field interpolated directly to stations: ERA5, HRRR (uncorrected).
3. Background field + residual ordinary kriging: one each for ERA5 and HRRR.
4. Learning methods: gradient-boosted trees or Gaussian processes, with features that may include background fields, elevation, roughness, and latitude/longitude; plus "learning method + residual kriging". Train using only stations other than the held-out station (or grouped by day); using data from the held-out station is strictly prohibited.

## Verification
- Leave-one-station-out (LOO): hold out one station at a time, reconstruct from the remaining stations, and predict the 10 m wind speed at that station for that hour (primary variable); wind direction and u/v serve as secondary metrics.
- Metrics: RMSE, bias, MAE; per-station and overall; 95% intervals via day-block bootstrap. Also report the error in each station's daily maximum hourly wind speed (peak subset).
- **Criterion (written in advance, not altered based on results)**: the best "background field + residual" or learning method achieves an overall RMSE ≥20% lower than the best pure interpolation (whichever is better between IDW and OK) and is better at ≥2/3 of the stations → judged "worth continuing"; 10–20% or only one of the two conditions met → "conditional"; <10% → "interpolation is sufficient".
- Also report the inter-station distance effect: group held-out stations by distance to the nearest station (<25, 25–50, >50 km).

## Boundaries
- Local workstation CPU is sufficient; keep total data volume under 2 GB, checking before use; if Colab is genuinely needed, ≤20 CU, stop when done, and only a single executor per round. Do not use HPC clusters.
- For parameters not specified in papers (variogram model, IDW power, HRRR forecast lead time, etc.), look them up first before making assumptions; label any assumption explicitly as "Assumption" with its rationale, and list it in the parameter-source table of the results file.
- Record newly used external data/code; note data sources on result figures.
- Write only under the designated directory.

## Deliverables
Report (method comparison table, per-station LOO errors, a one-sentence criterion conclusion, parameter-source table, known limitations), one comparison figure, and all scripts. Report back with conclusions and numbers only.

# H Observation–Simulation Fusion Wind Field Reconstruction: Step 1 Design (2026-10-14, Node H Lead)

- What was done: Step 1 is established as "two-step literature review + benign-wind station leave-one-out comparison". Region covers central and eastern Texas (covering the four Texas cities on the event track), 10–20 benign high-wind days during the 2020–2021 cold season; observations are ASOS/AWOS hourly winds, background fields ERA5 and HRRR f01–f03; methods are IDW, ordinary kriging, direct interpolation of background fields, background field + residual kriging, learning methods (GBT/GP) and their + residual kriging; station-by-station leave-one-out.
- Criteria (written in advance): best fusion/learning method has RMSE ≥20% lower than best pure interpolation and is better at ≥2/3 of stations → worthwhile to continue; 10–20% or satisfies only one → conditional; <10% → interpolation is sufficient.
- Why: This track already knows the interpolation baseline is strong (TPU strict interpolation ML 0/5; Han 2026 Kriging outperforms LBM–LES, extrapolated to surface stations without literature basis, based on track data); first quantify the upper bound of fusion gains on the simplest benign winds with the most complete data. HRRR uses forecasts rather than analyses, because analysis fields have already assimilated these stations, making leave-one-out not independent (without literature basis, based on common sense of HRRR assimilating METAR, pending DR verification).
- Cost of being wrong: Workstation  local CPU, 0 CU, several hours of bot work; if regions/dates are inappropriate, simply re-run with a different region.
- Dispatching experiments before literature conclusion review: revocable, near-zero cost.

真值只用 IEM METAR `skntgustsknt` https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/request/asos.py?help=。

# Submission Evidence Package: H Observation–Simulation Fusion Reconstruction of Near-Surface Wind—Literature Conclusions + r1 Interpretation (10-14)

## Conclusions Pending Review (Planned for project page, potentially for citation by Node I and subsequent formal projects)
C1. Under testing against actual measurements at real observations and held-out stations (or whole withheld regions), the RMSE reduction of learning/fusion methods in the verified literature relative to the best pure interpolation (Kriging/IDW/Barnes) is in the single digits to approx. 15%: Kiessling 2021 Sweden approx. 5% (unexplained variance 0.370 vs 0.388, random 5-fold); S2G (Baki 2026) held-out stations against actual measurements only reports "centered RMSE reduction", formal version 8.5% (not personally verified); KiloDA (Zheng 2026, arXiv 2609.11230v1) in Shanxi complex terrain with a whole withheld block of 238/1,340 stations, is −15.4% better than Kriging, with 89.5% of stations improved, with the largest gain in high-relief areas.
C2. The 25–54% reductions commonly seen in the literature come from "non-independent ground truth" designs: WRF twin idealized experiments (KiloDA 49%), or grid field comparisons using RTMA (assimilated from the same set of stations) as ground truth (S2G 25–32%); these cannot be treated as gains against actual measurements.
C3. HRRR f00 assimilates METAR 10 m wind; f01 is still affected by cycling assimilation; RTMA has no network-wide leave-one-out error (only airport withholding in Morris 2020). Therefore, leave-one-out tests using HRRR/RTMA as background are on the optimiztic side.
C4. In this track's r1 (137 ASOS stations in central-eastern Texas, average nearest station distance mostly 25–50 km, 10 well-behaved high-wind days, station-by-station leave-one-out): ERA5+residual Kriging is −3.8% relative to ordinary Kriging (81/137 stations), best GBT+residual is −5.5% (87/137); nearest station >50 km subset is −17% (ERA5+residual) / −24% (GBT+residual). Consistent with C1: gains are small under normal station network density, and large where stations are sparse or terrain is complex. Judged as "interpolation is sufficient" (criteria pre-specified in writing: ≥20% and ≥2/3 of stations to be worth continuing).
C5. Next step is to test only on sparse station networks (r2 thinning to 50/25/10%), same criteria as above, ERA5 background, no HRRR features.

## Evidence
- Item-by-item verification between Grok report and Lead: 
- KiloDA PDF original text verification passage (Fig. 5 paragraph): see above file; arXiv 2609.11230v1
- S2G author preprint:  (Fig. 8 caption, Fig. 12 caption, lines 601–604 of main text)
- r1 results: , Lead review 
- Criteria and design: , 

## Limitations (Self-reported)
Deep Research step two was not conducted due to quota; only 4 real observation comparison papers were verified in the literature, which may miss strong evidence under sparse-station/typhoon scenarios; S2G 8.5% is single-source; whether ERA5 land 10 m wind assimilates surface stations was unverified; r1 covers only 10 days, only mean wind, and Kriging parameters were not tuned.

# H r2: Sparse Network Wind Speed Reconstruction (UTC; Independent New Results)

## Criteria and Conclusions
A priori criteria: For sparse tiers with an average nearest input station distance of ≥50 km, the best ERA5 fusion/learning method must achieve at least a 20% reduction in RMSE relative to the best pure interpolation and improve at ≥2/3 of verification stations to be judged as "worthwhile in sparse areas"; 10–20% is judged as "conditional"; <10% is judged as "interpolation is sufficient". For the sparsest 10% tier: 14 input stations, 122 verification stations/run; average nearest distance 81.82 km, pure interpolation IDW RMSE 1.948, ERA5 + residual OK 1.687 m/s, a reduction of 13.40%, with station-by-station improvement at 126/136 stations aggregated across 20 resamplings. Hence, it is judged as "conditional", rather than "worthwhile in sparse areas". Although the 25% tier also reached 50 km, the gain was only 8.84%, indicating that the conclusion depends on the degree of sparsity; the status of ERA5 station assimilation remains to be verified, and it is not a strictly independent background verification.

## Input and Evaluation Scope
Fully reuse observations_qc2.csv.gz, the 10 selected UTC dates, and the daily ERA5 CSVs from r1; no new data was fetched. After removing BSM, which duplicates AUS, there are 136 stations with actual hourly observations; for each tier, with a fixed seed of 314159, 20 random station resamplings were performed, with 68/34/14 input stations. Each run trains/fits only on observations from input stations; observations from verification stations across all periods never entered fitting or variograms. Valid observation stations each hour vary with reports; average distance is calculated using the valid input stations at the actual station-hour being scored. METAR sustained/average wind speed (ASOS is typically a 2-minute average), not gusts or whole-hour averages; time is aligned to UTC. All methods are scored on the same verification station-hours within the same tier; resampled station-hours are not independent new observations.

## Overall Comparison across Sparse Tiers (m/s)

## Grouping by Underlying Surface around Stations
Reused the 1 km dominant class around stations from r1 ESA WorldCover 2021 v200: 50 = built-up, all others = non-built-up (not an anemometer site exposure rating). After removing BSM, there are 15 built-up stations and 121 non-built-up stations; the number of times stations were verified varies.
| Input Ratio | Group | Stations | Verified Station-Hours | Best Overall Pure Interpolation RMSE | Best Overall Fusion RMSE |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 50% | Built-up | 15 | 37451 | 1.647 | 1.641 |
| 50% | Non-built-up | 121 | 279218 | 1.715 | 1.602 |
| 25% | Built-up | 15 | 56225 | 1.732 | 1.709 |
| 25% | Non-built-up | 121 | 418325 | 1.804 | 1.627 |
| 10% | Built-up | 15 | 64304 | 1.925 | 1.795 |
| 10% | Non-built-up | 121 | 503869 | 1.951 | 1.672 |

## Parameter Sources and Default Assumptions
| Parameter | Value, Source, and Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Wind, dates, ERA5 | Original r1 and ; IEM METAR hourly sustained wind, ARCO-ERA5 10 m u/v station interpolation. The original QC2 >40 kt exclusion rule is an r1 assumption. Whether ERA5 assimilates land surface stations: to be verified. |
| Station thinning | Assumption: 136 stations (removing BSM, keeping AUS), fixed seed 314159, non-stratified random sampling 20 times/tier, round(ratio × stations), each tier tests only non-input stations. |
| IDW | Assumption, inherited from r1 inverse distance squared on spherical distance. |
| OK Fixed | Assumption, inherited from r1 exponential covariance 75 km, relative nugget 0.08, constant unknown mean; uses only input stations for that hour. |
| OK Hourly Fit | Assumption: Bin pairwise half-squared differences of wind speeds at input stations for the current hour by 25 km, up to 300 km; ≥4 pairs/bin, at least 3 bins; empirical semivariogram fitted to sill × (1.08 − exp(−h/r)), sill takes the variance of input stations for that hour, r constrained to 20–300 km, falls back to 75 km if bins are insufficient; nugget fixed at 0.08. All parameters determined by input stations, median range 92.490 km, 146 network-hours fell back. |
| Background + Residual | ERA5 direct interpolation or ERA5 + 75 km residual OK after subtracting ERA5 from input station observations. |
| GBT | Assumption following r1: 80 trees, 12 leaves, learning rate 0.06, L2=5; features ERA5 u/v, elevation (missing values replaced with median of this dataset), latitude/longitude, UTC hour sin/cos; no HRRR. Trained only on input stations across all selected days. |
| GBT + Residual | Assumption: Fixed random 2-fold split of input stations, two models each trained on the other half of stations to form strictly station-held-out cross-fitted residuals for each input station; verification stations are predicted by GBT trained on all input stations, plus 75 km residual OK. |
| Underlying Surface | Reused ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 already retrieved in r1; majority class 50 within 1 km around stations is built-up, the rest non-built-up; representativeness for 2020 has a time lag. |

## Limitations and Reproducibility
Repeated station splits are on the same 10-day meteorological field, not independent tests across years; resampled station-hours were not treated as independent samples to report significance. Some of the 136 stations are only valid for short periods; the station-by-station win counts across 20 evaluations were aggregated using all errors whenever that station was sampled as a verification station. Hourly empirical variograms are unstable with small sample sizes; fixed nugget/sill and range bounds are assumptions rather than literature-derived; topography, airport exposure, and model/station representativeness errors are confounded. The ERA5 assimilation status for surface stations remains to be verified by the Lead and cannot be claimed as independent and uninformed. Pure station thinning does not simulate the spatial correlation choices of network deployment, and extreme stationless areas were not verified against gridded ground truth.
Data sources: Iowa Environmental Mesonet/Iowa State University archived METAR and TX_ASOS metadata; Hersbach et al. (2020) ERA5, DOI 10.1002/qj.3803, via Google Research ARCO-ERA5; ESA WorldCover Consortium (2022), DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7254221. All have been registered in lines 130–133, 148–149; no new external data/code was added in this round. Figure marks the sources of observations and ERA5; scripts , .

## One-Line Criterion
In the 10% input station tier with a nearest distance of 81.82 km, ERA5 + residual OK had a 13.40% lower RMSE than the best pure interpolation, improving at 126/136 stations, judged as "conditional" according to the a priori criteria; the 25% tier only decreased by 8.84%, and it cannot be generalized that sparse areas are worthwhile.

items.title: Verdict: review (H literature conclusions C1–C5 + r1 interpretation + r2 design) · 2026-10-14
items.text:
# Verdict: Review (H Literature Conclusions C1–C5 + r1 Interpretation + r2 Design) · 2026-10-14

Reviewers: E (Gemini), A (GPT-6), D (GLM), 3/3 valid, all "supported with reservations". Only one round of review. The Lead has personally verified the evidence marked "verified" below.

## Must Change
1. **r1 ">50 km −17%/−24%" mainly came from offshore platform station BQX** (E). Verified: BQX = "Brazos 451", 28.49°N 95.72°W, elevation 0 m; Lead self-calculation: after removing BQX from the >50 km subset, ERA5 + residual relative to OK dropped from −16.8% to −8.9% (2,244 station-hours, 34 stations). −24% (GBT) includes HRRR features and in-training residuals, no longer cited. → Update lead_check, r1/r2 decisions, project page; recalculate r2 with the cleaned station list.
2. **Incomplete station cleaning** (E, D, A). Verified: CVB and T89 have identical coordinates (29.3419, −98.8509, "Castroville"); F12 and RFI have identical coordinates. E stated that KT89 reports were actually from Lajitas 470 km away (original reports not personally verified; adopting their handling suggestion, but not adopting their place name assertion as fact). Lead self-calculation on the full sample after removing BQX/T89/BSM: OK 1.577, ERA5 + residual 1.537, −2.5%, conclusion unchanged. → Deduplication changed to station distance threshold (merge and retain one station for <2 km) + exclude offshore platforms and stations with suspicious coordinates; during exclusion, simultaneously remove from input stations, training, and variograms (A, Item 5).
3. **Kiessling 2021's "about 5%" is unexplained variance (MSE dimension), not RMSE** (all three agreed; E based on kiessling_arxiv.pdf Eq. (1), Table 1). Changed to: unexplained variance decreased by 4.6%, equivalent to ~2.3% in RMSE; the optimal FF+RF in Table 1 averaged 0.357, equivalent to ~4.1% in RMSE.
4. **C1 cannot merge three metrics into a single "RMSE reduction range"** (A, D). Changed to writing metrics paper by paper: Kiessling (unexplained variance), S2G (held-out station centered RMSE 8.5%, vs. Barnes; official version verified by D and A; D pointed out that the official version states bias reduction is primary, so total RMSE reduction may be larger), KiloDA (station-by-station RMSE median −15.4%, vs. kriging; whole held-out block selected by ERA5 maximum error cluster; D verified original text: the strongest 5% wind speed tier is slightly worse than ERA5).
5. **C2 overworded** (A): The KiloDA ideal experiment is an "independent test in a simulated world, cannot extrapolate real-observation gains", not "leakage"; S2G Fig. 8 uses "RTMA as input and target", cannot serve as real-observation gains. "Assimilated from the same batch of stations" changed to "may contain information from the same stations, station-by-station records not verified".
6. **C3 correction** (D, A): The RTMA operational system routinely performs 10% random held-out cross-validation (EMC RTMA v2.2 overview, retrieved by D, Lead has not personally verified, marked "single source"); "no network-wide leave-one-out" changed to "no published network-wide leave-one-out error retrieved". Morris 2020's NODA is the background field; "about 1 kt higher" is EXP (analysis excluding airports) relative to NODA. ERA5: Hersbach 2020 lists land 10 m wind as not assimilated (D, A, E agree) → "ERA5 land station assimilation to be verified" changed to "does not directly assimilate land 10 m wind", and the ERA5 background can be considered largely independent of target stations. HRRR should only state "f01 cannot guarantee target station independence", without asserting "used upstream" station by station.
7. **"'Kriging tuning will only make the gains smaller' has no basis, deleted"** (A, E, D). E recalculation: after taking optimal variogram parameters for raw values and residuals respectively, the r1 reduction is 4.34%, still <10%. r2 has already reported "hourly fit" kriging simultaneously and taken the best pure interpolation as the baseline (responding to D); residual kriging still uses fixed 75 km (E pointed out asymmetry) → when recalculating r2, also do a fitted version for residuals, taking the best on both sides.
8. **The wording of r2 criteria is ambiguous and inconsistent with the original criteria** (A, E). The original criteria (Step 1 design) included "10–20% or satisfying only one → conditional"; in my r2 decision I wrote "otherwise Shelved", which was my mistake; the original three-tier criteria shall prevail. The "tier with ≥50 km" hits both the 25% (53 km) and 10% (82 km) tiers: report both tiers separately and evaluate separately. Existing results: 25% tier −8.8% → interpolation is sufficient; 10% tier −13.4% → conditional (E recalculated 7.6% / 13.3% after cleaning, does not change the verdict).
9. **Cannot expand "not meeting threshold" into "interpolation meets Node I requirements"** (A). Advice to I is narrowed to: under well-behaved sustained wind, use ordinary kriging for station distances <50 km, and ERA5 + residual kriging for further distances; gusts, peaks, thunderstorms/tropical cyclones/extratropical cyclones are all unverified, and peak hours generally underestimate by ~2 m/s.

## For Reference Only
- D: Austrian TAWES (EMS2026-549 abstract) 54 permanently held-out stations DL+CERRA 1.46 vs. regression kriging 1.51 m/s (about 3%); arXiv 2610.00728 generative assimilation is only about 2.4 percentage points higher than 3D-Var—consistent with C1 direction, not personally verified, listed only as clues.
- A: Samalot 2019 KF–UK 15% is a forecast post-processing gain, not a counterexample.
- A: S2G preprint station distance is written as 30 km, gusts are 3 s maximum within a 5-minute window (different from F's "27 km" "10 min") → update records according to preprint.
- D verified: r2 criteria timestamp precedes r2 run, "written a priori" holds.

## Objections Not Adopted
- A's "r1 is insufficient to support the Shelved basis of 'interpolation is sufficient'": partially not adopted. r1 is only used for triage of well-behaved wind small experiments in this node; the conclusion is already restricted to "this data, established methods, average sustained wind", not written externally as a general conclusion; nor does it shelve Node H on this basis.
- E's Lajitas place name assertion: original reports not personally verified, not written as fact, only used as one of the reasons for excluding T89 (coordinate overlap with CVB is sufficient).

## Conclusion on Counterexample Question
None of the three found verified literature where fusion/learning was ≥20% lower than the best kriging under real observations, held-out stations, flat terrain, and well-behaved high winds; A emphasized that this is "insufficient evidence", not "non-existent". Phrased accordingly.

items.title: H r1 assessment and round 2 (sparse station network) (2026-10-14, Node H Lead)
items.text:
# H r1 Determination and Round 2 (Sparse Network) (2026-10-14, Node H Lead)

- What was done: Judged r1 as "interpolation is sufficient" according to a priori criteria: across 137 stations and 10 well-behaved high-wind days in central-eastern Texas, the primary criteria group ERA5 + residual kriging had an RMSE 3.8% lower than ordinary kriging (81/137 stations), and the best GBT + residual was −5.5% (87/137), both <10%. For review, see .
- Round 2: Rather than doubling down on the dense network, we asked "how much does fusion help once the network becomes sparse?"—in r1 station-hours where the nearest station was >50 km, GBT + residual was −24% and ERA5 + residual was −17%. Node I's loss points mostly fall between stations, which is precisely the scenario it needs to use. r2 randomly thins the station network on the same data (retaining approximately 50%, 25%, 10% of stations, multiple resamplings), testing only on the removed stations; criteria written a priori: in the tier with an average nearest station distance of ≥50 km, if the best ERA5 background fusion (excluding HRRR features) is ≥20% lower than the best pure interpolation and better at ≥2/3 of verification stations → worth continuing and serving as Node I's wind speed source method; otherwise H is shelved as "interpolation is sufficient". Simultaneously adding: sensitivity of hourly-fitted variograms, removal of duplicate AUS/BSM stations, peak-hour bias, underlying surface grouping.
- Why: r1 conclusion direction is robust (kriging tuning will only make the gains smaller); signals in sparse areas are consistent with verified literature (KiloDA whole held-out block vs. kriging −15.4%, arXiv 2609.11230v1 Fig. 5 paragraph, Lead verified original text; no wiki card, litwiki under construction), and directly serves I.
- Cost of being wrong: Workstation local, 0 CU, a few hours of bot work.

**Correction (10-14, Review verdict)**: In this text, "in r1 station-hours where the nearest station was >50 km, GBT + residual was −24% and ERA5 + residual was −17%" mainly came from offshore platform station BQX; after removal, ERA5 + residual was −8.9%; "otherwise H is shelved as interpolation is sufficient" was written erroneously, and the three-tier criteria from Step 1 design shall prevail (10–20% is "conditional"). See .

# H r1 Lead Review (10-14)
Self-calculated using `predictions_r1_clean.csv.gz` (anaconda python), consistent with results_r1.md: OK 1.613, IDW 1.634, GBT + residual OK 1.524 (−5.5%, 87/137 stations).
- Primary criteria group (using only ERA5 background, excluding HRRR, see WRF Lead reminder): ERA5 + residual OK 1.553, −3.8%, 81/137 stations → interpolation is sufficient. HRRR + residual OK −1.2%, 57/137.
- AUS and BSM are about 1.5 km apart (two codes for the same airport), OK errors 0.44/0.50 are on the lower side; after removing both stations: ERA + residual −3.8% (79/135), GBT + residual −5.5% (86/135), conclusion unchanged.
- Variogram is fixed at 75 km, unfitted: will only make kriging weaker; after improvement, the gain will only be smaller, and the direction of the conclusion remains unchanged.
- Station distance grouping (ERA + residual / GBT + residual vs. OK): <25 km 1.534/1.568 vs. 1.550; 25–50 km 1.530/1.473 vs. 1.569; >50 km (2,459 station-hours, 35 stations) 1.781/1.625 vs. 2.142, i.e., −17% / −24%. Direction is consistent with KiloDA (whole held-out block −15.4%): the gains of fusion are concentrated where stations are sparse.
- All methods underestimate at daily peak hours for each station (GBT + residual bias −1.52 m/s): this is a critical specification issue for I (loss–wind speed library).
- Incomplete: Underlying surface grouping (supplementary message not implemented); GBT used HRRR features.

## Correction (After Review Verdict, 10-14)
- The above ">50 km −17% / −24%" is invalidated: the >50 km subset contains offshore platform BQX (Brazos 451). After removal, ERA5 + residual vs. OK is −8.9% (2,244 station-hours, 34 stations, Lead self-calculation). −24% (GBT) contains HRRR features and in-training residuals, not cited.
- The above statement "'variogram tuning will only make the gains smaller' has no basis, deleted"; E recalculated optimal variogram parameters on both sides to be −4.34%, still <10%.
- Duplicate/suspicious stations are not limited to AUS/BSM: CVB/T89, F12/RFI have identical coordinates. After removing BQX/T89/BSM, full-sample OK is 1.577, ERA5 + residual is 1.537, −2.5% (Lead self-calculation), conclusion unchanged.
