# Grok Quick Check (20261014_1440_…_76a209) Lead Verification Record · 10-14

Report:

| Report Statement | Verification | Conclusion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| KiloDA (Zheng 2026, arXiv 2609.11230v1) ideal experiment IDW 1.83 / Kriging 1.64 / KiloDA 0.84 m/s | Near line 217 of original PDF ("reduced from 1.83 m s⁻¹ for IDW and 1.64 m s⁻¹ for Kriging to 0.84 m s⁻¹") is verified true; but this is a WRF twin ideal experiment (prior and "observations" share the same origin) | Verified true, but not used as real-observation evidence |
| KiloDA real observations "19% lower than ERA5" | Original text: "median WS10 RMSE of 1.26 m s⁻¹ … reductions of 19.2%, 18.2% and 15.4% relative to ERA5, IDW and Kriging"; "lower RMSE than ERA5, IDW and Kriging at 66.4%, 88.2% and 89.5% of the withheld stations". Shanxi Lvliang mountainous area, 238 stations withheld as a whole block out of 1,340 stations, January–March 2025; additionally, 100 randomly withheld stations in complex terrain also dominated | **Adopted**: Under real observations and complex terrain, 15.4% lower than kriging (under 20%), with 89.5% of stations better; maximum gain is in high-relief areas. The report failed to mention this key number of "15.4% vs. kriging" |
| KiloDA no code | Original text Code availability: "available … upon reasonable request during peer review and will be made publicly available … upon publication" | Verified true (no public code at present) |
| Kiessling 2021 (Proc. R. Soc. A, 10.1098/rspa.2021.0236) RFF E=0.370 vs Universal Kriging 0.388 vs IDW 0.407 | PMC full text Table 1 is verified true; verification is hourly random 5-fold cross-validation, not fixed held-out stations; code bitbucket.org/the_eye_of_the_breeze/div-fourier-publication | Adopted: Swedish station network, ML is only about 5% better than universal kriging (in terms of unexplained variance) |
| Baki 2026 S2G (AIES, 10.1175/AIES-D-25-0111.1) U-Net 28–32% lower than Barnes | AMS page 403, unverified | **Unverified, not adopted**, handed over to Deep Research Step 2 |
| "Lee et al. 2022" hurricane XGBoost reconstruction (WAF-D-21-0077.1) | Crossref first author is Yang | Author mistaken, to be verified |
| "Fusion/ML is generally 15–50% lower than pure interpolation" | Synthesis sentence, no single source; upper bound comes from ideal experiments | Not adopted |

**Implications for this node**: In the two verified pieces of real-station evidence, learning methods are 5% (Sweden) to 15% (Shanxi complex terrain, whole held-out block) lower than the best kriging; central-eastern Texas has flat terrain, where gains are expected to be even smaller. Node H r1's ≥20% criterion remains unchanged (written a priori), but this serves as a benchmark when reading results.

## Reviewer F (Grok) Verification Results and Lead Review (10-14)
| Item | F's Conclusion and Excerpts | Lead Review | Adopted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S2G (Baki 2026) held-out stations | Fig. 12 "All results are computed at held-out stations using out-of-fold predictions"; main text "only a modest reduction (from 1.790 to 1.637 m s−1 or 8.5%)" (centered RMSE, vs. Barnes); 32.1%, 17.6% are for all stations against RTMA grids, not held-out stations; target is maximum 3 s gust within 10 min, training target comes from RTMA | AMS full text returned 403 to us, unable to open personally; awaiting independent verification by Reviewer E | Tentatively marked "pending cross-validation"; if E agrees, adopt: held-out station U-Net is only 8.5% better than Barnes (centered RMSE) |
| Whether HRRR f00 assimilates METAR 10 m wind | Benjamin 2016 MWR 144 Table 4 and p. 1674; Dowell 2022 WAF 37 p. 1372 | Local literature Collins et al. 2024 WAF (Zotero PU6IMCA9) PDF page 5 (journal page 709) Figure 2 caption "MADIS sites utilized for the HRRR analysis", direction consistent | Adopted: f00 assimilates surface station wind; f01 remains influenced by cyclic assimilation (r1 already marked "used upstream") |
| RTMA 10 m wind held-out station error | Only Morris 2020 WAF 35 p. 990 Part 139 airport exclusion: CONUS NODA RMSE ≤4 kt, ~1 kt higher after exclusion; no network-wide leave-one-out; URMA not found | Not personally verified | For reference only |
| WAF-D-21-0077.1 authors | Yang, Lee, Tippett, Chavas, Knutson; 7 storms held out, metric MSESS | Consistent with Crossref first author | Adopted (corrects Grok report "Lee et al.") |

Additionally: Local library contains Gunter & Long 2024 (West Texas Mesonet deep convective wind gust climatology, Zotero C9KMEQUR), usable later for thunderstorm phase or independent dense network validation.

## Reviewer E (Gemini) and Lead Review of S2G (10-14)
E downloaded author preprint v3: . Lead personally verified using pdftotext:
- The "held-out stations 29.6% (93 stations) / 25.0% (62 stations)" reported by E comes from Fig. 8 (preprint PDF text near line 920, figure caption): "Performance of deep learning models relative to Barnes interpolation … Colors show improvement in (a) RMSE, (b) PSNR, and (c) SSIM"—this is an image metric of the **entire gridded field against the RTMA target field**, merely removing some stations during inference; the ground truth is RTMA (the training target, itself assimilated from these stations), **not against actual observations at held-out stations**. E describing it as "held-out station verification" is inaccurate.
- The only true "held-out stations against observations" is Fig. 12: caption "Statistical evaluation of interpolation performance at held-out NYSM stations … All results are computed at held-out stations using out-of-fold predictions"; preprint main text (PDF text lines 601–604) only states "reduced centered RMSE compared to Barnes", **with no percentage**. The "from 1.790 to 1.637 m s−1 or 8.5%" cited by F comes from the official AMS version, which the Lead cannot open (403); the preprint lacks this sentence.
- Number of stations and setup are consistent between E and F: 124 used out of 126 stations, average station distance ~27 km (preprint p. 11); 4 groups × 31 stations, 93-station inference with 4 folds where each station is held out exactly once, 62-station inference with 6 folds.

**Adopted standard**: S2G is 25–32% lower than Barnes against the RTMA gridded field (ground truth is not independent); against actual observations at held-out stations, there is only a "reduction in centered RMSE", with the official version giving 8.5% (single source F, not personally verified, marked "to be verified").

## Corrections After Review (10-14)
- Kiessling 2021: 0.370 vs. 0.388 is unexplained variance (MSE dimension), equivalent to ~2.3% in RMSE; optimal FF+RF in Table 1 averages 0.357, equivalent to ~4.1% in RMSE.
- S2G official version "from 1.790 to 1.637 m s−1 or 8.5%" (centered RMSE, held-out stations, vs. Barnes) verified by Reviewers D and A, "to be verified" status revoked; official version states bias reduction is the primary contribution, and total RMSE reduction may be larger. Preprint writes station distance as ~30 km, gusts as 3 s maximum within a 5-minute window (earlier "27 km" "10 min" corrected according to preprint).
- KiloDA: −15.4% is the station-by-station RMSE median; held-out block selected by ERA5 maximum error cluster; strongest 5% wind speed tier is slightly worse than ERA5 (D verified original text). The ideal experiment is an independent test in a simulated world, not leakage.
- ERA5: Hersbach 2020 does not assimilate land 10 m wind (all three reviewers agree).
- RTMA: Operational system has 10% random held-out cross-validation (EMC v2.2 overview, D single source, not personally verified); "no network-wide leave-one-out" changed to "no published network-wide leave-one-out error retrieved". Morris 2020's NODA is the background field.

# H2 Landfalling Hurricane Hourly METAR Station Leave-One-Out Reconstruction

Specifications: BERYL 2024, NICHOLAS 2021, NHC landfall ±12 h, all dates and times in UTC. Inputs are hourly METAR 2-min average sustained wind (sknt) from Iowa Environmental Mesonet (IEM); gust is listed separately and only compared against gust. Holland uses CLIMADA v6.1.0 H08 frozen at Node B + Natural Earth inflow land-sea mask + ~2-min factor of 0.97, without refitting model coefficients; ERA5 is the magnitude of ARCO-ERA5 10 m U/V.

Sources: NHC HURDAT2, ATCF b-deck, IEM TX_ASOS/hourly METAR, Google Research ARCO-ERA5, CLIMADA v6.1.0, Natural Earth; for detailed versions and links, see the H2 entry in , as well as this directory. Node B originals are read-only. Figure captions indicate sources.

## Prior Criteria and Conclusions

Primarily based on the RMSE of the maximum observed hourly sustained wind per station during the event; method predictions are evaluated against the observed maximum over the same hours where observations exist for that station. "Fusion is worthwhile in hurricane scenarios" is judged only if the best background + residual reduces RMSE by at least 20% compared to the better of IDW/OK and reduces peak absolute error for at least 2/3 of stations; 10–20% or meeting only one criterion is "conditional"; <10% is "interpolation is sufficient". All findings from this experiment follow these criteria, with no threshold adjustments based on results.

BERYL: 115 qualified stations, 22 unqualified stations; OK 3.377 → H08 Holland+residual OK 2.773 m/s, reduction of 17.89%, station-by-station improvement 56/115 (48.7%); conditional.
NICHOLAS: 86 qualified stations, 11 unqualified stations; OK 2.874 → H08 Holland+residual OK 1.965 m/s, reduction of 31.63%, station-by-station improvement 49/86 (57.0%); conditional.
COMBINED: 201 qualified stations, 33 unqualified stations; OK 3.172 → H08 Holland+residual OK 2.460 m/s, reduction of 22.44%, station-by-station improvement 105/201 (52.2%); conditional.

## Method Comparison

Both peak and hourly columns are RMSE / bias / MAE, in m/s; peak sample size is by station, and hourly sample size is by observed hours.

| Event | Method | Peak Stations | Peak RMSE | Peak bias | Peak MAE | Hourly Samples | Hourly RMSE | Hourly bias | Hourly MAE |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| BERYL | OK | 115 | 3.377 | -1.242 | 2.273 | 2706 | 2.142 | -0.025 | 1.407 |
| BERYL | ERA5 | 115 | 3.367 | -1.815 | 2.520 | 2706 | 2.184 | +0.434 | 1.587 |

| NICHOLAS | IDW | 86 | 3.664 | -1.841 | 2.232 | 2047 | 2.358 | +0.059 | 1.576 |

| NICHOLAS | ERA5 | 86 | 2.808 | -1.718 | 2.018 | 2047 | 2.445 | +0.000 | 1.670 |
| NICHOLAS | ERA5+residual OK | 86 | 2.086 | -0.917 | 1.461 | 2047 | 1.873 | -0.023 | 1.253 |
| NICHOLAS | H08 Holland | 86 | 2.405 | +0.351 | 1.766 | 2047 | 3.483 | +0.416 | 2.828 |
| NICHOLAS | H08 Holland+residual OK | 86 | 1.965 | -0.454 | 1.402 | 2047 | 2.187 | -0.077 | 1.535 |
| COMBINED | IDW | 201 | 3.825 | -1.973 | 2.520 | 4753 | 2.329 | +0.042 | 1.530 |
| COMBINED | OK | 201 | 3.172 | -1.248 | 2.043 | 4753 | 2.097 | -0.025 | 1.395 |
| COMBINED | ERA5 | 201 | 3.140 | -1.773 | 2.305 | 4753 | 2.300 | +0.247 | 1.623 |
| COMBINED | ERA5+residual OK | 201 | 2.528 | -0.860 | 1.806 | 4753 | 1.844 | -0.006 | 1.289 |
| COMBINED | H08 Holland | 201 | 3.391 | +0.881 | 2.512 | 4753 | 4.129 | +0.257 | 3.398 |
| COMBINED | H08 Holland+residual OK | 201 | 2.460 | -0.421 | 1.804 | 4753 | 2.237 | -0.064 | 1.585 |

Peak error is predicted peak minus observed peak. The station assimilation specifications of ERA5 remain to be verified; the leave-one-out of ERA5+residual cannot be claimed to be completely free of station information. Holland itself did not use METAR from current validation stations for parameter tuning, but NHC post-analysis best track, intensity, and b-deck are post-event data rather than real-time forecasts; results must not be extrapolated as future forecasting skill.

## Peak Gust (Independent Scoring)

ERA5 10 m mean wind is not directly converted to gusts; only IDW, OK, Holland, and their residual methods are listed here. The gust factor for H08 is a frozen assumption from Node B, not a fitted value from gust observations.

| Event | Method | n | RMSE | bias | MAE |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BERYL | gust_idw | 113 | 4.380 | +1.011 | 3.591 |
| BERYL | gust_ok | 113 | 3.986 | +0.254 | 2.994 |

| BERYL | gust_holland_resok | 113 | 3.468 | +0.003 | 2.801 |
| NICHOLAS | gust_idw | 81 | 4.904 | +2.138 | 4.125 |

| NICHOLAS | gust_holland | 81 | 3.151 | -0.921 | 2.424 |
| NICHOLAS | gust_holland_resok | 81 | 2.193 | +0.189 | 1.735 |
| COMBINED | gust_idw | 194 | 4.606 | +1.482 | 3.814 |
| COMBINED | gust_ok | 194 | 3.853 | +0.532 | 2.939 |
| COMBINED | gust_holland | 194 | 3.990 | -0.559 | 3.084 |

## Distance to Center / RMW Grouping

Grouping is based on the distance from the left-out station to the NHC center at the hour corresponding to its observed sustained wind peak, divided by the linearly interpolated b-deck RMW at that hour. The two columns are peak RMSE / bias (m/s) for the best pure interpolation and best fusion for each event; groups with very small sample sizes are only described without drawing conclusions.

| Event | Distance/RMW | Stations | Baseline RMSE / bias | Fusion RMSE / bias |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BERYL | <1R | 5 | 4.484 / -2.500 | 5.127 / -1.409 |
| BERYL | 1–3R | 29 | 5.000 / -1.847 | 2.916 / +0.361 |
| BERYL | >3R | 81 | 2.451 / -0.948 | 2.501 / -0.605 |
| NICHOLAS | <1R | 5 | 6.951 / -4.536 | 3.308 / -2.649 |
| NICHOLAS | 1–3R | 38 | 2.272 / -0.978 | 1.840 / -0.103 |
| NICHOLAS | >3R | 43 | 2.518 / -1.118 | 1.860 / -0.509 |
| COMBINED | <1R | 10 | 5.849 / -3.518 | 4.315 / -2.029 |
| COMBINED | 1–3R | 67 | 3.708 / -1.354 | 2.366 / +0.098 |
| COMBINED | >3R | 124 | 2.474 / -1.007 | 2.299 / -0.572 |

## Missing / Outage Stations

Selected stations are those covered by the TX_ASOS archive during the event and ≤300 km from any node of the ±12h track; "unqualified" does not equate to confirmed outage, but includes cases where the archive covers the event but hourly reports are missing, METAR numerical QC failures, <18/24 sustained wind hours within the time window, or no sustained wind report within ±2h of the station peak time predicted by the frozen H08. To prevent missing reports from obscuring peak values, unqualified stations do not participate in the above primary scoring; the table below provides station-by-station details.

| Event | Station | Valid / Expected Hours | H08 Station Model Peak (UTC) | Reports Near Peak Time |

## Parameter Source Table

| Parameter | Value / Rule | Nature of Source and Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Events and time windows | Beryl 2024 / Nicholas 2021, NHC landfall ±12 h, hours aligned to UTC | Project brief preset; HURDAT2 landfall times from read-only Node B |
| Station network | TX_ASOS, archive date covers event, ≤300 km from any point on NHC track within event window | Project brief preset; HAS1MIN was not enforced, because this time it is hourly METAR |
| Mean wind and gust | IEM `sknt`, `gust` knot × 0.514444 m/s | IEM fields; 2-min average wind only for sustained wind, not replaced by gust, physical conversion constant |
| Hourly deduplication | METAR timestamps rounded to nearest hour, selecting the report closest to the hour; `report_type=3,4` | Followed H r1 script rules; only one report retained per hour |
| Numerical QC | sknt 0–120 kt, gust 0–150 kt; if gust < sknt within the same report, that gust is excluded | Assumption: broad upper bounds only remove obvious outliers, not official NCEI QC thresholds |
| Outage threshold | At least 18 valid sustained wind hours in 24h, and at least one report within ±2h of H08 model peak time | Assumption: avoid obviously truncated peaks; threshold is affected by model peak time errors; stations with no reports are not counted as 0 |
| H08 wind field | Original from Node B; this station does not adjust 0.97, land-sea/gust coefficients; Node B preregistration describes its empirical assumptions and limitations |
| ERA5 | ARCO public Zarr, 10 m U/V interpolated to stations, hourly magnitudes | H r1 background loading code; whether station assimilation is independent remains to be verified |
| IDW | Inverse distance squared, available stations in the same hour, excluding the left-out station | Assumption; followed H r1 fixed power of 2 |
| Ordinary Kriging | Fixed hourly exponential covariance exp(−d/75km), diagonal nugget 0.08, constant unknown mean | Assumption; followed H r1 fixed version. Empirical variogram not fitted for the event; same weights used for sustained wind and its background residuals |
| Peak comparison | Predicted maximum over hours with observations during the event per station vs. observed maximum over that period; hourly only for valid observation hours of that station | Assumption: guarantees common observable window; event peaks genuinely missing due to outages are not verified |
| Grouping | Distance from left-out station to NHC center at observed peak time / b-deck RMW at the same time | Project brief preset; RMW linear interpolation follows Node B code |

## Known Limitations

1. Biased sample of qualified stations around Texas airports across two events; missing data is not random, and true peak values of outage stations in hard-hit areas may be higher. "Conditional" cannot be treated as proven wind field reconstruction capability in the landfall core area.
2. Hourly METAR (one report per station per hour) misses minute-level extremes between two reports; the event peak duration is the "maximum hourly mean wind" within the window, not the true 1-min peak, nor is it a gust.
3. Node B's wind field is post-analysis best track and simplified land-sea exposure, not a real-time forecast; ERA5 is also a post-analysis reanalysis and whether it contains information from held-out stations remains to be verified.
4. The fixed variogram was not fitted on an hourly basis; residuals within the same hour may contain local extremes from neighboring stations, and Holland+residual hourly RMSE is worse than ERA5+residual; peak gains must not be misunderstood as outperforming across all time periods.
5. Storm center distance grouping is defined at the observed peak time, which does not represent that the peak time coincided with NHC landfall, nor does it include stations in other states; single-station leave-one-out can leave stations at the same airport / nearby stations on the training side, and group isolation by airport cluster has not yet been performed.

## Reproducible Files

 completes downloads, Node B wind fields, LOO, JSON, and figures in one go;  generates this report from JSON. `grid_*_h2.csv.gz` contains background, observations, and distances; `predictions_h2.csv.gz` contains hourly station-by-station predictions;  is the original peak evaluation table;  contains station-by-station outage candidates. Figure  sources: IEM / NHC HURDAT2 / ATCF / ARCO-ERA5 / CLIMADA H08.

# H r2-clean: Sparse Network Recalculation After Station Cleaning (UTC)

This report is recalculated according to the review  verdict; all source files are read-only, and results use new r2c filenames rather than overwriting original r2. Observations are sustained wind speeds (typically 2-minute average) from IEM METAR hourly reports, not whole-hour means or gusts; background is ARCO-ERA5 10 m u/v. Uses only the 10 established UTC days from r1, QC2 observations (exclusion of >40 kt is an r1 assumption), and the ERA5 cache.

## Prior Criteria and Results
In each tier with average actual nearest input station distance ≥50 km, if the best ERA5 fusion/learning reduces RMSE by ≥20% relative to the best IDW/OK and ≥2/3 of evaluated stations are better → "worthwhile in sparse areas"; 10–20% or meeting only one threshold → "conditional"; <10% → "interpolation is sufficient" (tiered with reduction prioritized). Pure interpolation and fusion each select the optimum within their own tier; the weaker of the two variogram versions is not taken as the baseline.

| Input Tier | Actual Nearest Input Station Distance That Hour km (station-hour weighted; resampling mean±SD) | Best Pure Interpolation RMSE m/s | Best Fusion RMSE m/s | Reduction | Improved Stations | Verdict |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 50% | 40.27 (40.27±2.43) | 1.659 (OK hourly fitted) | 1.556 (ERA5+residual OK hourly fitted) | 6.22% | 98/134 | Interpolation is sufficient |

Station-hours and repetitions share the same weather and are not treated as independent samples. ## Cleaning Rules and Removal List
First, remove BQX (Brazos 451, offshore platform) and GVW (Galveston 209B, offshore platform), where WorldCover 1 km surrounding the station has dominant class 80 (water body); remove T89, which has identical coordinates to CVB and suspicious coordinates. Then, for all pairs of stations with pairwise spherical distance <2 km, keep only one station: AUS/BSM (1.600 km; identical valid station-hours, keep major airport AUS), F12/RFI (0 km, F12 has no valid observations in this batch, keep RFI), 5R3/RYW (0.446 km, 5R3 has no valid observations in this batch, keep RYW), CVB/T89 (0 km, T89 already removed due to being suspicious, keep CVB). Retained stations recompute all random samplings, input/evaluation, training, and variogram fitting; removed stations were strictly never used as input or for scoring; passed the assertion that the minimum distance between stations after cleaning is ≥2 km.

| Observations, dates, ERA5 | Followed r1 , local QC2/ERA5 files; METAR hourly sampled sustained wind, UTC. ERA5 land 10m wind does not directly assimilate these stations (see review verdict), but this still does not mean all upstream information is completely independent. |

Raw field fallback 128 times, median range 93.1 km; residual fallback 128 times, median range 36.9 km. |
| GBT and cross-fitting | Followed r2 assumptions: 80 iterations, 12 leaves, learning rate .06, L2 = 5, features ERA5 u/v, elevation, latitude/longitude, UTC hour sin/cos; residuals strictly 2-fold cross-fitted on input stations; no HRRR. |

## Limitations and Files
10 selected well-behaved wind days from 2020–21, a single random seed, same stations repeatedly evaluated; "improved stations" are not independent new stations. Empirical variogram range and residual applicability are not literature-recommended values, without nested parameter tuning; station representativeness errors may still exist. Although the ERA5 background does not directly assimilate land 10m wind, it may still be indirectly affected by the assimilation system. Gusts, loss points, or gridded ground truth were not validated.
Sources: IEM METAR, Hersbach et al. 2020 ERA5 DOI 10.1002/qj.3803, ESA WorldCover Consortium 2022 DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7254221, all listed in ; no new external data was added in this round. Scripts , ; Figure .

## Conclusion
25% tier: Interpolation is sufficient; 10% tier: Conditional. Applies only to this cleaned station network and sustained wind leave-one-out station evaluation.

items.title: H well-behaved wind phase wrap-up (r2) and next phase (2026-10-14, Node H Lead)
items.text:
# H Well-Behaved Wind Stage Wrap-Up (r2) and Next Stage (2026-10-14, Node H Lead)

- r2 results (136 Texas stations randomly thinned 20 times/tier, scored only at removed stations):
 - 50% stations (average nearest 41 km): ERA5 + residual kriging was −5.9% compared to best pure interpolation (90/136 stations)
 - 25% stations (53 km): −8.8% (107/136)
 - 10% stations (82 km): −13.4% (126/136). In this tier, direct ERA5 interpolation (1.807) was already better than pure interpolation (1.948), and residual kriging only reduced another 6.6% on top of ERA5.
 - Learning methods (GBT, ERA5 features only) were inferior to ERA5 + residual kriging across all sparse tiers.
 - All methods underestimated by about 1.7–2.2 m/s at daily observed peak hours.
- Verdict: According to prior criteria, "Conditional" (best in ≥50 km tiers was 13.4%, not reaching 20%; 25% tier was 8.8%, below 10%). Criteria will not be changed.
- What was done: Wrapped up the well-behaved wind stage, with conclusion "Interpolation is sufficient for dense station networks; starting from station spacing around 80 km, ERA5 + residual kriging is noticeably better (−13%), and learning methods are unnecessary". My 10-14 note "otherwise Shelved as interpolation is sufficient" applies only to well-behaved wind, **Node H is not Shelved**: Liang Hu set Node H to do well-behaved wind first, followed by typhoons / extratropical cyclones / thunderstorms; the well-behaved wind results happened to provide the comparison methods for the next stage.
- Method recommendations for Node I (Loss–Wind Speed Database): For loss points <50 km from the nearest station, ordinary kriging suffices; for farther distances, use ERA5 + residual kriging; both need separate treatment for peak underestimation (about 2 m/s) and cannot be directly used as peak wind speed at the time of loss.
- Next stage (H2): Landfalling hurricanes (Texas, prioritizing the same batch of events as Node B's B1+B4), using ERA5 and parametric typhoon wind fields (Holland-type, best-track driven) as background fields, comparing errors of pure interpolation / ERA5 + residual / parametric wind field + residual on left-out stations, focusing on peaks. First align events and parametric wind fields with Node B through leadership, avoiding reinventing the wheel.
- Why: In well-behaved wind, the ERA5 background is already good enough, so fusion gains are limited; extreme wind (typhoons, thunderstorms) happens to be the scenario where background fields are at their worst, stations are sparsest, and observations are most frequently lost, which is also what Node I genuinely needs. Evidence: data from our r1/r2 line; KiloDA's full-block held-out area was −15.4% compared to kriging (arXiv 2609.11230v1 Fig. 5 section, Lead verified original paper; litwiki card under construction), consistent in magnitude with the −13.4% of the 82 km tier.
- Cost of being wrong: H2 is a small experiment on  workstation / Colab, ≤20 CU; if events are unsuitable, simply swap events.

**Correction (10-14, review verdict)**: r2 criteria are judged separately according to the original three tiers, 25% tier and 10% tier: 25% (53 km) −8.8% → Interpolation is sufficient; 10% (82 km) −13.4% → Conditional (recalculated as 7.6% / 13.3% after E cleaned the station list, verdict unchanged; ideas r2-clean is recalculating). Recommendations for Node I are limited to well-behaved sustained wind; gusts, peaks, and extreme wind are all unverified, and it cannot be claimed that "interpolation satisfies Node I's needs". "Consistent in magnitude with KiloDA" is retained, but note that KiloDA uses median RMSE across stations, complex terrain, held-out areas selected based on clusters with largest ERA5 error, and is slightly worse than ERA5 in the strongest 5% wind speed tier.

**Final (10-14, r2-clean)**: Cleaned station list (removed BQX, GVW offshore platforms, T89; kept one station for pairs <2 km), residual kriging also fitted hourly, taking the best from both sides: r1 all-station leave-one-out OK 1.577 → ERA5+residual 1.537 (−2.6%, 78/134); r2 50% tier (40 km) −6.2% (98/134) interpolation is sufficient; 25% tier (54 km) −9.4% (106/134) interpolation is sufficient; 10% tier (82 km) −12.5% (124/134) conditional. Learning methods remain inferior to ERA5+residual kriging across all tiers. Peak hour underestimation of about 1.6–1.8 m/s remains unchanged. Conclusions for the well-behaved wind stage are subject to this.

# H2 Recalculation After Station Cleaning (Ten Events + Beryl Listed Separately)

2026-10-14; UTC throughout. Original H2/B node files are read-only, and all results use `_clean_h2d_h2d` as the new version; frozen Holland v1 (a) chain coefficients were not changed. The ten-event combined total does not include Beryl. This cleaning supplement does not modify the prior criteria.

## Cleaning and Scoring Boundaries

Starting from the complete candidate station list of each event, spatial cleaning was performed independently of missing reports and scoring eligibility: normalize state-prefix-free TX station IDs for Beryl/Nicholas; suspect-coordinate TX:T89 was excluded (identical to TX:CVB); for connected neighbors <2 km, each group retains the one with the most valid observation hours across all events (ties broken by station ID lexicographical order). Excluded stations do not exist in inputs, fitting, or testing across all hours. Stations with dominant water class or names indicating offshore platforms were placed in a separate pool, and strictly do not participate in IDW, OK, residual fitting, or evaluation for land stations; stations with no WorldCover returns were conservatively excluded.  gives status and reason for each station, and  gives distance.

The water body pool refers to "WorldCover within 1 km perimeter is predominantly water or name indicates offshore", which does not equate to all stations being genuine offshore platforms: for example, SPG/TPF/EYW are coastal airports, and were also separated from the land pool according to the predefined water body criteria. This grouping is not a certification of instrument exposure conditions.

Sustained wind uses only IEM METAR sknt, and gust uses only gust; 12 h before and after event landfall, hourly nearest top of the hour ±30 min. Retain at least 75% valid hours and at least one valid report within ±2 h of the H08 station model peak; predicted peak and observed peak are restricted to the same observed timestamp. Uncovered true extremes are unverifiable.

## Prior Criteria and Results

Across each evaluable event (uncensored and ≥8 stations) and the ten-event combined total, the best background + residual relative to the best IDW / fixed or fitted OK: peak RMSE lower by ≥20% and ≥2/3 stations having smaller peak absolute error is "Worthwhile"; 10–20% or meeting only one of these is "Conditional"; <10% is "Interpolation sufficient". ## Exclusion and Missing Report List

## Parameter Sources Table
| Parameter | Value/Rule | Nature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Events/Fields | B v1 same-batch ten events + Beryl addition; B `chain_a_v1.pygrid_*` | Task specification / existing B artifact; post-analysis track is not a real-time forecast |
| Water Bodies and Neighbors | Dominant class 80 within ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 1 km circle is water, or IEM station name indicates offshore; distance <2 km deduplication; collocated T89 excluded | WorldCover/IEM attributes; threshold and priority retention hours rules are assumptions, per review |
| Missing Reports and Hours | At least 75% valid hours and report present within ±2h of H08 model peak; nearest top of the hour ±30min; sknt 0–120kt, gust 0–150kt, discard if gust<sknt | Original H2 assumption; not official IEM QC |
| Fixed OK | Exponential covariance 75 km, normalized nugget .08; IDW power 2 | Original H2 assumption |
| Fitted OK | Hourly, each leave-out station training set separately fits observations or corresponding background residuals; 25 km bins up to 300 km, ≥4 pairs/bin, ≥3 bins; sill is training variance, nugget .08, exponential scale 20–300 km, fall back to 75 km if fitting is insufficient | r2c parameterization assumption, not literature constants; target station is completely excluded from fitting |
| H08 Averaging Period / Gust | 1-minute sustained wind → METAR ×0.97; marine gust ×1.20, overland ×1.30 | B explicitly states "assumption"; refer to , not values given in literature |
| Wind Field / Time | ERA5 10m u/v interpolated to stations then magnitude taken; H08 interpolated per B chain time; UTC throughout | ARCO ERA5 / B frozen chain; existing cache |

## Limitations

Station missing reports are not random during strong winds, and the true maximum may occur later than station outages; what is left out is a single station rather than an entire cluster of stations. Fitting variograms uses observations from that hour excluding each leave-out station, without selecting parameters using the leave-out station; however, the final "best method" is selected post-hoc on the evaluation data, so gains carry an optimiztic bias. Dominant water class carries the possibility of misclassifying coastal airports as offshore platforms; here they are isolated according to task rules without claiming that instruments are at sea. Stations with unknown land cover classes are conservatively excluded. NHC post-analysis tracks and b-deck information cannot be regarded as forecast accuracy. Figures and tables are sourced from IEM METAR, Google ARCO ERA5, ESA WorldCover, NHC HURDAT2/ATCF, CLIMADA H08/B v1; new data only re-reads WorldCover and public metadata already used by IEM, for citations see  existing corresponding sources.

Scripts , ; audit , ; predictions `predictions_clean_h2d.csv.gz`, ; figures . Initially  used non-normalized Texas station IDs, which has been deprecated and not overwritten.

# Recalculation after H2 Station Cleaning (Ten Events + Beryl Listed Separately)

2026-10-14; UTC throughout. Original H2/B node files are read-only; all results take `_clean_h2d_h2d` as the new version; frozen Holland v1 (a) chain coefficients were not changed. The ten-event combined total does not include Beryl. This cleaning supplement does not modify prior criteria.

## Cleaning and Scoring Boundaries

Starting from the complete candidate station list per event, spatial cleaning was performed independently of missing reports and scoring eligibility: normalize non-state-prefixed TX station IDs for Beryl/Nicholas; suspect coordinates TX:T89 excluded (identical to TX:CVB); for connected neighbors <2 km, each group retains the station with the most valid observation hours across all events (ties broken alphabetically by station ID). Excluded stations do not exist in inputs, fitting, or testing for any hour. Stations with dominant water class or names indicating offshore platforms were placed in a separate pool and never participate in IDW, OK, residual fitting, or evaluation for land stations; stations with no return from WorldCover were conservatively excluded.  gives status and reason for each station,  gives distance.

The water pool refers to "dominant WorldCover water within 1 km or name indicating offshore", which does not equate to all stations being true offshore platforms: for example, SPG/TPF/EYW are coastal airports, which were also separated from the land pool according to the predefined water conditions. This grouping is not a certification of instrument exposure conditions.

Sustained wind uses only IEM METAR sknt, and gusts use only gust; 12 h before and after event landfall, hours rounded to the nearest clock hour ±30 min. Retain at least 75% valid hours and at least one valid report within ±2 h of the H08 station model peak; predicted peak and observed peak are restricted to the same observed time. Uncovered true extremes are unverifiable.

## Prior Criteria and Results

Across each scorable event (uncensored and ≥8 stations) and the ten-event combined total, the best background + residual relative to the best IDW / fixed or fitted OK: peak RMSE lower by ≥20% and ≥2/3 of stations having smaller peak absolute error is "Worthy"; 10–20% or meeting only one of these is "Conditional"; <10% is "Interpolation Sufficient". If "only meeting the winning station condition but RMSE <10%", it is still categorized as Conditional according to the original criteria. Evaluated only in the land pool, with Beryl listed separately.

## Parameter Source Table
| Parameter | Value/Rule | Nature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Events/Fields | Same batch of ten events as B v1 + Beryl addition; B `chain_a_v1.pygrid_*` | Statement of work / existing B artifacts; post-event track is not real-time forecast |
| Water and Neighbors | Dominant class 80 within 1 km circle of ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 is water, or IEM station name indicates offshore; distance <2 km deduplication; collocated T89 excluded | WorldCover/IEM properties; thresholds and priority rules for retained hours are assumptions, per review |
| Missing Reports and Hours | At least 75% valid hours and report within ±2h of H08 model peak; nearest clock hour ±30min; sknt 0–120kt, gust 0–150kt, gust<sknt discarded | Original H2 assumption; not official IEM QC |
| Fixed OK | Exponential covariance 75 km, normalized nugget .08; IDW power 2 | Original H2 assumption |
| Fitted OK | Fitted observation or corresponding background residuals separately for each hour and each leave-one-out station training set; 25 km binning up to 300 km, ≥4 pairs/bin, ≥3 bins; sill is training variance, nugget .08, exponential scale 20–300 km, fall back to 75 km if underfitted | r2c parameterization assumption, not literature constants; target station never enters fitting |
| H08 Time Averaging / Gust | One-minute sustained wind → METAR ×0.97; marine gust ×1.20, land ×1.30 | B explicitly stated as "assumption"; see , not literature-provided values |
| Wind Field / Time | ERA5 10m u/v interpolated to stations then magnitude taken; H08 temporally interpolated according to B chain; UTC throughout | ARCO ERA5 / B frozen chain; existing cache |

## Limitations

Station missing reports are not random in strong winds; true maximums may occur after reporting stations go offline; what is held out is a single station rather than an entire cluster of stations. The fitted variogram uses current-hour observations excluding each held-out station, without using the held-out station to select parameters; however, the final "best method" is selected ex post on the scored data, which carries an optimiztic bias in the gains. Dominant water class has the possibility of misclassifying coastal airports as offshore platforms; here they are isolated according to task rules without claiming instruments are at sea. Stations with unknown land cover types are conservatively excluded. NHC post-event tracks and b-deck information cannot be regarded as forecast accuracy. Sources for figures and tables: IEM METAR, Google ARCO ERA5, ESA WorldCover, NHC HURDAT2/ATCF, CLIMADA H08/B v1; new data only re-reads WorldCover and public metadata already used by IEM; for citations see  existing corresponding sources.

items.text:
# H2 First Edition (Beryl/Nicholas) Verdict and High-Wind Secondary Criterion Registration (2026-10-14, H Node Lead)

- Results (Lead self-calculated and verified consistent using peaks_h2.csv): For event peak sustained winds across 201 qualified stations (33 stations unassessed due to insufficient coverage), OK 3.17 → Holland + residual OK 2.46 m/s (−22.4%), ERA5 + residual OK 2.53 (−20.3%); however, station-by-station better was only 105/201 and 111/201 → "Conditional" according to the pre-specified criterion. Peak bias: OK −1.25, Holland + residual −0.42 m/s. Peak gust: OK 3.85 → Holland + residual 3.00.
- Unregistered observations (used only as clues): On 49 stations with measured peaks ≥12 m/s, −35%/−32% (31/49, 32/49 stations); on 67 stations 1–3× RMW from the center, −36%. Fusion gains are concentrated in high-wind, near-core areas, exactly where losses occur; distant weak-wind stations are large in number with small gains, dragging down the station-by-station ratio.
- First edition did not perform station cleaning (included AUS/BSM, CVB/T89, RFI; Nicholas included offshore platform BQX).
- What was done: Formulated the "high-wind station subset" into a pre-registered secondary criterion, testing only with Node B v1's remaining uncomputed events (≥20% and ≥2/3 stations on stations with ≥12 m/s); primary criterion remains unchanged. Beryl/Nicholas recalculated after cleaning, labeled "seen data".
- Why: To avoid picking subsets after looking at the data; the remaining 9 events (v1 ten events minus Nicholas) have not yet been computed and can serve as independent tests. Basis: data from this line, no literature basis.
- Cost of being wrong: Workstation local 0 CU; if the secondary criterion fails on new events, wrap up as "Conditional" per the primary criterion.

**Postscript (10-14, ten-event edition results_h2_v1batch.md)**: Primary criterion ten-event combined −15.0% (ERA5 + residual OK, 413/794 stations better) → Conditional; event-by-event: Delta/Zeta/Ida/Nicholas/Milton/Idalia are Conditional, Ian/Nicole/Debby/Helene are Interpolation is sufficient. When frozen v1 Holland is used alone, Ida peak is 7.3 m/s too high, worse than ERA5 in most events; most gains come from the ERA5 background itself. Secondary criterion preview (Lead self-calculated using uncleaned peaks_h2_expanded.csv, 9 new events, 304 stations with measured peak ≥12 m/s): OK 4.54 → ERA5 + residual 3.64 (−19.8%, 185/304=61%), Holland + residual −18.7% → previewed as "Conditional", formal verdict subject to the station-cleaned edition *_h2b*.

**Cleaned Edition (10-14, superseding the uncleaned combined totals above)**: Deduplicated, removed T89, moved water/offshore stations (14 stations, including coastal airports) out of the land pool, required ≥75% valid hours; both sides took the better of the fixed/fitted variograms. Ten events land 745 stations: peak RMSE OK fitted 2.79 → ERA5 + residual 2.70 (−3.2%, 379/745) → **Interpolation is sufficient**; event-by-event, only Delta, Nicholas, Idalia, and Milton are Conditional. Beryl −3.5% Interpolation is sufficient. The −15%/−22% in the uncleaned edition mainly originated from large errors when offshore/coastal stations were interpolated by land stations, and does not represent gains on land stations.
One point that still holds: **Peak bias**—OK fitted −1.18 m/s, Holland + residual −0.04 to −0.10, ERA5 + residual −0.91; peak gust OK 3.67 → Holland + residual 3.47. That is, parametric wind field + residual is on par with interpolation in RMSE, but substantially eliminates systematic underestimation of peaks. 239 stations 1–3 RMW from the center −11%, 56 stations <1 RMW fusion is worse. The offshore pool has fewer than 5 simultaneously assessable stations per event, unassessable.
High-wind station secondary criterion results pending *_h2b* (Supplement 3).

**Postscript (10-14, pointed out by superior Lead, Lead verified lines 127–135 of results_clean_h2e.md)**: For hourly RMSE, OK fitted 2.074 is best; ERA5 + residual 2.113, H08 + residual 2.485–2.519 (about 20% worse than OK). Thus, "favoring Holland + residual" holds only for event peaks. Hurricane recommendations for I are split into two use cases: if only event maximum wind is needed (peak sustained wind, peak gust) → Holland + residual kriging; if hourly time series or non-peak wind speeds are needed → ordinary kriging. Finalization pending high-wind station secondary criterion (h2b).

items.text:
# H2b High-Wind Station Secondary Criterion Pre-Registration

2026-10-14. Frozen prior to executing high-wind subset statistics: continues to use H2d cleaned land stations, coverage conditions, LOO predictions, and peak definitions; does not change the primary criterion. The independent validation set consists of the other nine events in B v1 ten events excluding NICHOLAS (DELTA, ZETA, IDA, IAN, NICOLE, IDALIA, DEBBY, HELENE, MILTON); BERYL also does not enter independent validation. For each event, qualified land stations with measured event peak sustained wind ≥12 m/s constitute the high-wind subset; fewer than 8 stations is listed as unassessable and not merged into assessable event combined totals. In addition, descriptive combined totals for high-wind stations across all nine events are provided to display sample coverage.

For each subset, the best of IDW/OK fixed/OK fitted and the best of ERA5 + residual fixed/fitted, H08 + residual fixed/fitted are selected by peak RMSE respectively, calculating the RMSE reduction 1 − fusion/baseline and the number of winning stations where station-by-station absolute error strictly decreases (ties do not count as wins). Reduction ≥20% and winning stations ≥2/3 is "Fusion worthwhile for high-wind stations"; reduction ≥10% or satisfying only the winning station threshold is "Conditional"; otherwise "Interpolation is sufficient". Re-report the primary criterion following the same logic. Post-hoc selection of the minimum RMSE method within each subset carries optimiztic bias; no hyperparameter tuning based on results. Primary/secondary criteria for Beryl and Nicholas are listed as "seen data, for reference only" and do not participate in independent verdicts.

# H2b High-Wind Station Secondary Criterion: Cleaned Land Stations Ten Events

2026-10-14; UTC. The secondary criterion was written first, followed by re-stratified scoring on the existing H2d station-by-station leave-one-out peak table; no re-running or adjustment of wind fields/models. Model predictions for all ten events in H2d were generated prior to this secondary criterion, so this is an independent event test without tuning parameters on the high-wind subset, rather than a strictly prospective predictive validation. Original results are retained.

## Pre-determined Specifications

Only includes cleaned land pool, stations with original H2d coverage qualification; water bodies/platforms, duplicate, and suspicious-coordinate stations do not participate in input, fitting, or evaluation. Event peak is the maximum predicted by each method across observable hours; high wind is selected by the same station's measured maximum sustained wind ≥12 m/s; gusts do not enter this criterion. For each event, the pure interpolation with the minimum peak RMSE (IDW / OK fixed / OK fitted) is compared against background + residual (ERA5/H08, fixed/fitted OK); a station counts as a win only if its absolute error strictly decreases; at least 8 stations to be assessable. Gain ≥20% and winning stations ≥2/3 is judged as "Fusion worthwhile for high-wind stations", ≥10% or only meeting winning station threshold is judged as "Conditional", otherwise "Interpolation is sufficient". Selecting the best method on the test set carries selection optimizm.

# H3 Pre-Registration (2026-10-14, Pre-Computation)

Events: 2018–2024 US South-Central Plains TX/OK/KS/NE/AR/MO/LA/NM/CO; look for candidates with same-state, same-UTC-day High Wind reports ≥5 and Thunderstorm Wind reports 0 from NOAA Storm Events annual details. On the premise that IEM has ≥60 available stations in that state and adjacent plains states, select up to eight events on distinct days sorted by descending High Wind report count and ascending date, covering TX/OK/KS as much as possible. Report times converted to UTC (using NOAA-specified time zone offsets; DST following actual time zone rules), window centered at the hour with the maximum hourly median wind speed in the observation region ±12 h; this is an observation definition post-event selection and is not used to select methods. If thunderstorms are reported across state borders, candidates are not disqualified based on reports outside a given state within the event; their synoptic non-convective nature still requires METAR TS/CB cross-checking. Candidates failing screening and reasons are logged.

Cleaning: Suspicious station T89 with identical coordinates excluded; for <2 km connected components, retain the station with the most valid hours, breaking ties by station ID; WorldCover 1 km dominant class water bodies and clear offshore/platform pooled separately, conservatively excluded if not found in WorldCover. Excluded stations do not participate in input/fitting. IEM METAR nearest top of the hour ±30 min; sknt is sustained wind (kt converted to m/s), gust is independent; 0–120 kt / 0–150 kt are assumed QC upper bounds. Observation coverage ≥75% (at least 19 hours out of 25 hours), and at least one observation within ±2 h of the regional peak; predicted peaks calculated only during hours with actual measurements. In station leave-one-out, the left-out station each hour must not be used for any fitting.

Methods: IDW distance power 2; OK exponential covariance fixed version with range 75 km, nugget 0.08, and fitted version over 20–300 km range binned at 25 km up to 300 km based on training stations' empirical variogram; ERA5 10m u/v bilinearly interpolated first before computing speed; two versions of ERA5 + residual OK. All model constants not originating from data sources are assumptions, continuing H2 for fair comparison. For each event and combined, pure interpolation takes the lowest peak RMSE among IDW and the two OK versions, and fusion takes the lowest among the two residual versions; different methods use the identical set of observable station-hours. Peak prediction is the maximum predicted across each event's observable hours, bias = predicted minus measured.

Primary criterion does not change with results: Peak RMSE reduction ≥20% and absolute error improved in ≥2/3 stations → Worthwhile; 10–20% or satisfying only one of these → Conditional; <10% → Interpolation is sufficient. If RMSE <10% but winning stations ≥2/3, listed as Conditional per "satisfying only one". Events with fewer than 8 valid stations are unassessable and excluded from combined totals. Hourly RMSE, peak bias, peak gust (compared only with gusts), and subset of measured peaks ≥15 m/s are only described, not judged. All times UTC.

## 结论

严格无 TS/CB 的两事件合计（151 站）ERA5+残差固定 OK 峰值 RMSE 2.518→2.378 m/s，降低 5.53%，81/151 站改善，按预定判据“插值够用”；但合格事件只有 2 场而非要求的 5–8 场，完整 H3 问题尚未完成。

# H2 v1 Same-Batch Ten-Event Station Leave-One-Out (Beryl Appended Separately)

2026-10-14; UTC. Freeze Node B v1's CLIMADA 6.1.0 Holland 2008 + land-sea inflow roughness, averaging time factor; original is read-only, and the duplicate in this directory only modifies relative import paths (neither wind field functions nor constants were modified). The original two-event  is retained; 's COMBINED previously included Beryl, corrected here via a new file to only ten events, without overwriting old results.

## Prior Criteria and Conclusions

Evaluated by event only with ≥8 valid and non-truncated stations; the ten B v1 events are combined and reported separately; Beryl is appended separately and not included in the total. Peak RMSE: a reduction of ≥20% for the best background + residual relative to the best IDW/OK and lower peak absolute error at ≥2/3 of stations is "Worthy"; 10–20% or meeting only one of the criteria is "Conditional"; <10% is "Interpolation sufficient". The peak is the predicted maximum and observed maximum at the same held-out station during observed timestamps; criteria were not revised.

# H2f: Errata on Reuse Criteria for Francine and B v1

This round only adds Francine 2024 (landfall 2024-09-11 22:00 UTC, observation window ±12 h, 25 hourly UTC time points); the prior H2d cleaned land station leave-one-station-out peak table was read-only rescored without overwriting old results. For pure interpolation and blending, each selected the optimum from the candidate pool of fixed 75 km / per-target per-hour fitted OK and IDW based on the peak RMSE of the current evaluation subset, so model selection entails optimizm. The peak is taken as the maximum across hours with observations at that station, without mixing sustained wind and gusts.

## Primary Criterion: Event Peak Sustained Wind

| Event or Total | Qualified Land Stations | Best Pure Interpolation / Blending | Peak RMSE (m/s) | Reduction | Winning Stations | Determination |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| FRANCINE | 44 | okfit / era_resok75 | 2.087 / 1.611 | 22.80% | 25/44 | Conditional |
| Original Ten Events | 745 | okfit / era_resok75 | 2.786 / 2.696 | 3.23% | 379/745 | Interpolation sufficient |
| Ten Events + Francine | 789 | okfit / era_resok75 | 2.751 / 2.647 | 3.79% | 404/789 | Interpolation sufficient |

Primary criterion: A peak RMSE reduction ≥20% and peak absolute error reduction at ≥2/3 of stations is judged as "worthwhile"; 10–20% or meeting only the winning stations threshold is judged as "conditional"; less than 10% is judged as "interpolation sufficient". Although the single Francine event had a reduction exceeding 20%, its winning stations did not surpass 2/3, so it remains "conditional"; the total did not cross tiers.

## High-Wind Secondary Criterion: Observed Peak Sustained Wind ≥12 m/s

| Event or Total | Qualified High-Wind Stations | Best Pure Interpolation / Blending | Peak RMSE (m/s) | Reduction | Winning Stations | Determination |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| FRANCINE | 10 | okfit / holland_resok75 | 3.180 / 1.501 | 52.81% | 8/10 | High-wind stations worth blending |
| Original Independent Nine Events | 273 | okfit / holland_resokfit | 3.889 / 3.500 | 10.00% | 154/273 | Conditional |
| Independent Nine Events + Francine | 283 | okfit / holland_resokfit | 3.866 / 3.450 | 10.78% | 162/283 | Conditional |

The high-wind secondary criterion follows : ≥20% and ≥2/3 winning stations is judged as "high-wind stations worth blending"; 10–20% or meeting only one is judged as "conditional"; <10% is judged as "interpolation sufficient"; fewer than 8 stations is not evaluable. The single Francine event reached "worthwhile", but the independent total remains "conditional", without crossing tiers. Beryl/Nicholas have already seen data and are not included in the independent high-wind total.

## Francine Coverage and Station Pool

76 candidate stations: 55 land, 10 water/platform, 10 WorldCover no valid classification, 1 other excluded; 44 land stations meet ≥75% valid hours and have reports at ±2 h of the H08 model peak time, while the other 11 land stations do not. 6 qualified stations in the independent platform pool, not pooled with land for leave-one-out; unknown coverage does not participate in input or scoring. The newly appeared ANR, ETO, GLX, MKQ, and OYE are platform/water, and MPE is land; none have new nearest neighbors <2 km with the original station table. Cleaning table .

## Relationship with B Event Set, Provenance, and Limitations

The events with qualified stations in B v1/run2 are Delta, Zeta, Nicholas, Ian, Nicole, Beryl, Debby, Francine, Helene, and Milton; the original ten events of H2, based on the self-built 300 km hourly station network, additionally used Ida and Idalia, and listed Beryl separately without including it in the ten-event total. H2f "Ten Events + Francine" still follows the H2 ten-event definition, including Ida/Idalia/Nicholas and excluding Beryl, and cannot be regarded as a replication of the B v1 ten events. B's 150 km/HAS1MIN minute station network and this experiment's 300 km/hourly station network are not the same set.
Line 494 of old  has been corrected to refer only to ; numerical values across H2 versions were obtained from the local IEM/ARCO/Holland prediction grid and local station scoring scripts, and were not taken from B root directory , per-event tables, or station_rows tables.  only borrows `build_trackpredict` from ; Francine similarly borrows the function without executing the aggregation entry point of that pipeline; the scoring of the original ten events rechecked from  is completely identical to .
The B pipeline's 500 m reference height neutral constant-flux logarithmic layer, 1 min → METAR ~2 min factor of ×0.97, and 1 min → 5 s gust factor of marine ×1.20 / land ×1.30 are all pre-run assumptions, not directly measured literature values or universal coefficients; any citation of the Holland pipeline error must carry this qualification. Francine's Holland results are also affected by this. NHC best track / b-deck is post-event data, and the independence of ERA5 surface station assimilation remains to be verified. Stations closer to the storm eye are more prone to missing reports, and qualified samples are skewed toward the periphery, representing survivorship bias; this cannot be extrapolated to true peaks at stations with interrupted reports.

# H2 Hurricane Phase Finalization and Next Phase H3 Extratropical Cyclone (2026-10-14, H Node Lead)

- Basis for finalization:  (cleaned version),  (high-wind secondary criterion, registered in prereg_h2b.md at 17:49).
- Primary criterion (ten events, 745 land stations, event peak sustained wind): OK fit 2.79 → ERA5+residual 2.70, −3.2%, 379/745 → interpolation sufficient.
- Secondary criterion (9 independent events, 273 stations with observed peak ≥12 m/s): OK fit 3.89 → Holland+residual 3.50, −10.0%, 154/273 (56%) → conditional, clinging tightly to the 10% lower bound; for single events, only Zeta passed both thresholds; Ida blending was worse (−11.7%). Nicholas/Beryl had already seen data, used only for comparison (+33% / +6.6%).
- Peak bias: OK −1.18 → Holland+residual approx. −0.04 to −0.10 m/s; gust peak 3.67 → 3.47. Hourly RMSE: OK 2.07 is the best, Holland+residual is worse by approx. 20%.
- Conclusion: For land station reconstruction during hurricane landfall, interpolation is sufficient in terms of accuracy; the value of parametric wind field + residual is eliminating systematic underestimation of event peaks. Recommendations to I (by use case): if only the event maximum wind is needed → Holland+residual kriging; if hourly time series is needed → ordinary kriging; offshore/coastal platforms are not evaluable.
- Next phase (order set by Liang Hu: benign wind → typhoon → extratropical cyclone → thunderstorm): H3 extratropical cyclone high winds, under the same protocol (station cleaning, land pool, leave-one-station-out, two variogram functions, ERA5+residual as primary, event peak + hourly + peak bias), criteria identical to primary criterion and pre-registered. Thunderstorm phase discussed separately: thunderstorm wind footprints are often smaller than station spacing, leave-one-station-out might detect nothing; testing approach to be decided after H3 concludes.
- Why: 0 CU, existing protocol; completes the order set by Liang Hu; extratropical cyclones are a source of "High Wind" category losses for I. Basis: internal line data, no literature basis.
- Cost of being wrong: a few hours of bot work.

**Addendum on Francine (10-14)**: Francine single event primary criterion −22.8% (25/44 stations) conditional; high-wind stations 10 stations −52.8% (8/10) "worthwhile". Ten events + Francine primary criterion −3.8% (404/789) remains interpolation sufficient; independent high-wind total −10.8% (162/283) remains conditional; neither crossed tiers, hurricane finalization unchanged. The H2 event set differs from B (includes additional Ida and Idalia), which has been explicitly stated in the results; line 494 of results_h2_v1batch.md has been corrected to point to b_tc/v1/run2/; ideas re-verification confirmed that values across H2 versions were not taken from results in the b_tc/v1/ root directory.

items.text:
# H3 Extratropical Cyclone Finalization and H4 Thunderstorm Pilot (2026-10-14, H Node Lead)

- H3 results (prereg_h3.md registered at 18:05, prior to data fetching starting at 18:08): 5 non-convective high-wind days in the South-Central Plains (NE×2, KS×2, TX×1), 433 land stations. Event peak RMSE: OK fit 2.32 → ERA5+residual 2.24 (−3.2%, 247/433) → interpolation sufficient; among single events, 4 were interpolation sufficient, TX 2019-11-26 was conditional (only satisfied winning stations 92/138). The TSNO misclassification errata only altered compliance labels, not predictions; prior to the errata, the strict total of −5.5% was likewise interpolation sufficient. ERA5 alone underestimated the peak by 3.2 m/s; all methods still underestimated the peak by approx. 1.2–1.4 m/s.
- Combining the three phases (benign wind, landfalling hurricane, extratropical cyclone): On the ASOS station network in the south-central US and the Gulf Coast, the event peak accuracy gain of "background field + residual" relative to the best kriging is only about 3%; it reaches "conditional" only at station spacings of approx. 80 km (−12.5%) or for hurricane high-wind stations (−10%); it has never crossed "worthwhile". Usable outputs are: ordinary kriging is a strong baseline; using Holland+residual for hurricane event maximum winds can eliminate peak underestimation; peak times across all event types are generally underestimated by 1–2 m/s.
- H4 thunderstorm pilot (the final category in the order set by Liang Hu): Denser station area around Dallas–Fort Worth, Texas, 5 thunderstorm high-wind days (Storm Events Thunderstorm Wind, prioritizing Dallas 2024-06-01 and 2025-07-09 recommended by the events thread), ASOS 1-minute gust and hourly sustained wind; methods IDW, OK, HRRR f01+residual (marked "already used upstream"), ERA5+residual; criteria same as before, registered before calculation. Expectation: thunderstorm wind footprints are often smaller than station spacing, and both interpolation and background may fail—the purpose of the pilot is to quantify "what station reconstruction can achieve for thunderstorm winds", providing I with a clear boundary.
- Why: 0 CU, existing protocol, completes the order set by Liang Hu; thunderstorms are one of the main sources of losses for I. Basis: internal line data; events thread response (footprint is the bottleneck, see project page).
- Cost of being wrong: a few hours of bot work.

**Criteria correction (evening of 10-14, raised by superior Lead, revised after Lead verified raw reports)**:
- What the superior relied on was the deprecated preliminary version : it treated METAR's TSNO ("thunderstorm sensor not operating") as thunderstorm, leaving only 2 "compliant" events. The errata version  has corrected this.
- Lead rescanned raw METARs within the 5 event windows using the correct token rules (isolated TS/VCTS/+TS/-TS and FEW/SCT/BKN/OVCnnnCB): ne_20190128, ne_20210114, ks_20221202, tx_20191126 were all 0; **ks_20180306 had 1 VCTS record** (OK:AVK 2018-03-06 14:15 UTC, "VCTS CLR … LTG DSNT N", within the window and region), missed in the errata version. According to prereg "regional METAR has no TS/CB", ks_20180306 is non-compliant.
- Primary numbers revised to strictly compliant 4 events: 359 stations, peak RMSE OK fit 2.295 → ERA5+residual 2.221 (−3.2%, 207/359) → interpolation sufficient (calculated by Lead using peaks_h3.csv). Reference: 5 events 433 stations −3.2% (247/433); the 2 events 151 stations −5.5% (81/151) stated by the superior. All three definitions yield interpolation sufficient.
- "Conditional" in the tx_20191126 table was solely because winning stations 92/138 barely reached 2/3, with a reduction of only 3.8%.
- Viewing the three phases together revised from "approx. 3%" to "3–6%". With only 4 compliant events in the sample, the conclusion is relatively weak.

# H4 Preregistration (2026-10-14, Prior to Scoring)

Event selection: NOAA Storm Events 2020–2025 Texas Thunderstorm Wind sorted descending by number of reports on the same UTC day in the DFW box 31.5–34°N, 95.5–98.5°W, prioritizing the inclusion of 2024-06-01 and 2025-07-09; for the rest, take at most three different days with the highest number of reports. If a target day has no reports in the same region or too few available stations, state so truthfully, and do not retroactively claim microburst ground truth. Times use NOAA original field time zones converted to UTC; the window is defined by the time of the regional 1-minute gust peak ±3h (avoiding the use of held-out stations to select prediction methods; the peak window definition still entails slight held-out information leakage).

Primary scoring uses only station-minutes with actual observations minute-by-minute, computing event peaks separately for minute sustained wind and gusts on the leave-one-out station, and hourly METAR reports must not be directly mixed with minute gusts; METAR is used for cross-checking and 1-minute missing-data reporting. Coverage threshold: at least 75% of expected minutes within the window have available gust / sustained wind reports; because 1-minute products have structural missing reports, if this threshold leads to being unevaluable, list lower-coverage samples separately as exploratory without using them to assert primary criteria. Single events with <8 qualified land stations are not evaluated; totals include only evaluable events.

Cleaning follows H2/H3: stations with suspicious coordinates are excluded; for connected station pairs <2 km, retain the station with the most valid minutes, breaking ties by station identifier; stations with WorldCover 1 km dominant water class or offshore station names are pooled separately, and those where dominant class cannot be found are conservatively excluded from land scoring. All excluded stations must not enter any input/fitting. Leave-one-out requires at least 4 other stations per minute; timestamps used for station peaks must simultaneously possess both the corresponding target observation and the prediction from that method. Observation numerical QC: 0–120 kt sustained wind, 0–150 kt gust, gust must not be less than sustained wind: all are assumptions of this round.

Methods: IDW power 2; OK exponential covariance fixed at 75 km, nugget 0.08, as well as an empirical variogram fitted version from training stations; ERA5 bilinear interpolation of 10m u/v then magnitude + residual OK in two versions. For gusts, there is no ERA5 gust background, and ERA5 sustained wind is not treated as gust; if gust blending is attempted, it can only serve as exploration under a pre-fixed definition and does not enter the primary criterion. Upstream analysis for HRRR f01 has already assimilated stations; if acquired, it serves only as a contamination-flagged reference and does not participate in criteria.

For each event and the total, independently select the pure interpolation (IDW / fixed OK / fitted OK) and ERA5+residual (fixed / fitted) with the lowest peak RMSE, with sustained wind as the primary comparison; for gusts, ERA5 blending criteria apply only when a background of the same quantity and definition is available; otherwise, report pure interpolation gust errors and label gust blending as unevaluable. Peak RMSE reduction ≥20% and ≥2/3 stations with smaller absolute error → worthwhile; reduction 10–20% or satisfying only one → conditional; <10% and winning stations <2/3 → interpolation sufficient. Bias = predicted − observed. An isolated peak is defined as an observed event peak that is ≥5 m/s higher than all other stations' observed peaks within the same window (not neighbor peaks in the same minute); report definitions and station distance groupings; do not use this to prove microburst ground truth.

一分钟 gust_sknt 为独立 5 秒阵风量；ERA5 10m U/V 是持续风背景，没有相同定义的阵风背景。故阵风只能报 IDW/OK 阵风对阵风，不对“ERA5 阵风融合”套主判据；这项是预设对比未能执行的缺口。孤立峰定义为本站事件内观测持续风峰值高出同事件其他所有可评站峰值至少 5 m/s，不等同同一分钟孤立峰或下击暴流证据。

## 清洗和参数来源

ASOS1MIN 网络在目标框共14站。H2/H3 的站点清洗规则重新应用：WorldCover 2021 v200 站点周边1 km主类，水体或平台另池，未知类保守不入，T89 坐标疑点排除，<2 km 连通对保留五事件累计有效分钟最多者。本次14站均为陆地、未发现<2 km站对，详细见。每事件低于75%双变量覆盖的站不评分，但它已有的分钟值仍可当别站输入；无资料者不参与任何拟合。

| 参数 | 来源/性质 |
| --- | --- |
| 雷暴事件及 UTC 报告 | NOAA NCEI Storm Events details， 精确版本 URL；Texas 按 America/Chicago 时区换 UTC；研究区框和挑选规则来自任务书/本轮预登记 |
| 分钟持续风 sknt、5秒阵风 gust_sknt | IEM ASOS 1-minute，逐事件 URL 文件；kt×0.514444 m/s；不与小时 METAR 混合 |
| 小时 METAR | IEM ASOS archived METAR，仅报告覆盖对照，逐日下载 URL 文件；不是主评分 |
| ERA5 10m 风 | Google Research ARCO ERA5 公共 Zarr，小时 10m u/v 双线性空间插值后线性时间插值至分钟，再求风速；再分析不是独立预报，站点同化情况待核 |
| WorldCover | ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 via Microsoft Planetary Computer 1km 主类，或复用 H2/H3 已有同站类别 |
| IDW/OK | 假设：IDW 幂2；OK 指数协方差75 km、nugget .08；拟合：训练站小时风中位数经验变差函数25 km箱、20–300 km拟合，样本稀缺时回退75 km。逐分钟留一目标站不参与拟合 |
| 覆盖及 QC | 假设：361个分钟至少271分钟同时有有效持续风和阵风；≥4个其他同分钟站才预测；持续风0–120 kt、阵风0–150 kt，阵风≥持续风。详细断报见 metrics_h4v3.json |
| HRRR f01 | 未下载/未评分；上游分析已同化站点，即便f01也不作独立留一证据 |

限制：只有14个具1分钟档案站、四个可评事件共44站事件；2025-03-04 虽有87条 Storm Events 报告，但区域一分钟档案只有5站满足覆盖要求，不能凭小时 METAR 填补分钟峰。雷暴尺度峰位可在站间移动，站点峰不是连续场真值。事件窗口由全站观测定，事件/方法择优会乐观，阵风融合比较缺失；小时 vs 分钟支持集不同，不能套用 H2/H3 数字。此处孤立峰计数为零仅是“高出所有其他站峰值”的严格定义下的结果，不证明没有局地极值。

数据源：NOAA NCEI https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/swdi/stormevents/csvfiles/；IEM https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/asos/1min.phtml 及 https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/request/asos.py?help=；ARCO ERA5 https://github.com/google-research/arco-era5；ESA WorldCover https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7254221。新源均已在 PUBLIC_CITATIONS.md 的既有条目中，未越出 h4 写入范围。

## 结论

四个可评事件合计，持续风事件峰值最佳纯插值 IDW 4.776 m/s，ERA5+固定残差 OK 4.786 m/s（恶化0.19%），26/44站绝对误差改善；峰值 bias −3.245→−3.330 m/s。按开算前判据为“插值够用”。纯插值阵风峰值最佳 OK75 RMSE 6.848 m/s、bias −5.079 m/s；ERA5 阵风融合未能同量比较，不能称“阵风融合插值够用”。

# H4 Thunderstorm Finalization and "Leave-One-Station-Out" Phase Wrap-up (2026-10-14, H Node Lead)

- H4 (prereg_h4.md registered at 18:40, prior to data fetching at 18:42): 4 evaluable thunderstorm high-wind days around Dallas, 44 stations (10–13 ASOS 1-minute stations per event). Peak sustained wind RMSE: IDW 4.776 → ERA5+residual 4.786 (−0.2%, 26/44) → interpolation sufficient. Peak bias −3.2 (interpolation) / −3.3 (blended) m/s, ERA5 alone −8.8; gust best interpolation RMSE 6.85, bias −5.1. Isolated peaks 0. Sample is very small.
- Viewing the four phases together: On the ASOS station network, the event peak gain of "background + residual" relative to kriging is 3–6% (benign, hurricane, extratropical), thunderstorm approx. 0; reaches "conditional" only at station spacings of approx. 80 km (−12.5%) and for hurricane high-wind stations (−10.8%), never "worthwhile". The truly useful outputs are: kriging is a strong baseline; using Holland+residual for hurricane event maximum winds can remove peak underestimation; event peaks across all categories are systematically underestimated, with thunderstorms being the most severe.
- What was done: Wrapped up the "leave-one-station-out" step (H Step 1); do not shelve H node. Consolidated the results into the *Station Wind Speed Reconstruction Protocol v1* for Node I's use, sending it to 3 reviewers for review before handover (the protocol is an interface on which I will directly depend). Candidates for H's next step: (a) calibration of peak underestimation (most needed by I); (b) thunderstorms require radar (WSR-88D/TDWR) + stations to possibly reconstruct footprints—scale exceeds the Lab's small pilot, whether to do it is a directional question, left to Liang Hu.
- Why: All four event types have been tested in the order set by Liang Hu, with consistent criteria and consistent conclusions; continuing to add events will not change the conclusions. Basis: internal line data, no literature basis; literature side see review  verdict (blending gains under real observation held-out stations are mostly single digits to approx. 15%).
- Cost of being wrong: If there are errors in the protocol, I's wind speed column will carry systematic errors; sending for review is precisely for this reason.

# Next Steps After Wrapping Up Four Event Categories in H (2026-10-14 19:xx)

Decision I made: H's next step is to perform "peak underestimation calibration" (existing leave-one-out results across four categories, workstation  local 0 CU, criteria written down before computation, cross-validated by event); thunderstorm "radar + station" blending will not be done in the testbed, recorded as a candidate; after peak calibration, if I is blocked on thunderstorm wind speed, write a promotion proposal to ask Liang Hu.
- Why: Results across four categories (benign −2.6%, hurricane land −3.8%, extratropical cyclone −3.2%, thunderstorm −0.2%) show that blending gains on the ASOS station network are very small, and what I lacks most is wind speed whose peaks are not biased low; thunderstorm footprints are smaller than station spacing and require radar data, workload exceeding a small pilot. Basis: internal line data, no literature basis.
- Correction: Lead previously reported "2 events 151 stations −5.5%" based on the deprecated preliminary version , which has been corrected to I and the parent project as 4 events 359 stations −3.2%.
- Cost of being wrong: If peak calibration is ineffective, it only costs workstation  local time; postponing thunderstorms will leave I temporarily without an independent wind speed source for the thunderstorm peril.

# H5 Peak Calibration Preregistration (UTC)

Written prior to reading H5 stratified scores; optimal calibration is not selected based on scores. Raw station leave-one-out predictions are read-only, without reconstruction or re-downloading.

Input: Benign predictions_r1_clean.csv.gz, first removing BQX/GVW/T89/BSM/F12/5R3 (complete list per r2c), taking maximum values of observation and prediction separately for each station × UTC day over hours with shared observations; benign uses OK for nearest station distance <50 km and ERA5+residual OK for ≥50 km, plus unified OK. Hurricane land pool peaks_clean_h2d.csv + peaks_francine_h2f.csv, uses Holland+residual fixed 75 km, plus unified OKfit; extratropical peaks_h3.csv retains only strictly compliant four events, uses OKfit; thunderstorm peaks_h4v3.csv excludes unevaluable 2025-03-04, uses IDW (the protocol treats IDW/OK as co-equal, IDW selected based on H4 overall RMSE); each category additionally uses unified fixed 75 km OK as control (hurricane and extratropical also show cross-comparison between OKfit protocol recommendation and OK75). Gusts are compared only against gusts; benign has no gust column.

Validation: Leave-one-event-out for each category, leave-one-UTC-day-out for benign; all station-events in the same category undergo only a single evaluation. Additive: training station-events pooled mean(obs−pred); linear: training station-events least squares obs = a + b pred; quantile mapping: training predicted values and observed values sorted separately, linear interpolation of empirical quantile mapping, truncated beyond endpoints to observation endpoints. No parameter tuning per target event, no station distance binning (the latter three categories lack a unified comparable distance field). Physical constraints: predictions are non-negative, all three methods output max(0, pred). All three are reported fixedly, without cherry-picking post-hoc best.

Primary judgment: For each category, each variable, and each calibration method separately, pooled across all held-out predictions to calculate bias = predicted − observed, RMSE. If |bias| ≤ 0.5 m/s and RMSE ≤ uncalibrated RMSE × 1.02, judged as "calibration effective"; otherwise, if |bias| decreases by at least half relative to uncalibrated and initial bias is non-zero, or RMSE increase >2% and ≤10%, judged as "partially effective"; others are "ineffective". If RMSE degrades >10%, judged as "ineffective" regardless of bias, avoiding masquerading poor calibrations as partially effective. Zero initial bias cannot be judged by halving. Report for individual folds and combined separately; combined is not fold-equal-weighted.

80% symmetric prediction interval: Taken solely from the finite-sample empirical quantile ceil(0.8×(n+1))/n of absolute errors of the same method after calibration on training events, interval [max(0, predicted−q), predicted+q]; coverage calculated on held-out events. Only empirical calibration under LOEO conditions, non-exchangeable between events, station-correlated, no claim of strict 80% guarantee. Uncalibrated also uses the same training residuals to calculate intervals.

Cross-category extrapolation: Leaving out an entire category each time, pooling the recommended sustained wind methods of the remaining three categories for training, fitting the same additive / linear / quantile mapping; unified OK75 likewise crosses categories separately. Gusts have values only in hurricane and thunderstorm, cannot be trained with "remaining three categories" gusts, labeled unevaluable, without applying sustained wind parameters to gusts. Extrapolation likewise constructs 80% intervals solely using training category residuals.

Sources / Assumptions: Category and event partition and cleaning follow respective H data files and H Station Wind Speed Reconstruction Protocol v1; the category-recommended Holland averaging interval conversion and 500 m reference height are pre-assumptions of Node B; calibration formulas, pooled station-event equal weighting, ECDF tail truncation, interval quantiles, and 2% tolerance are all prior assumptions of this experiment; none are literature parameters. Method comparison only verifies existing leave-one-out stations, without verifying unstationed loss locations.

The primary test uses existing leave-one-station-out predictions, never using the peak of the current station/event for correction fitting.
