## Sample and Parameter Source Table
| Item | Sources and Qualifications |
| --- | --- |
| Fair-weather | Median of `predictions_r1_clean.csv.gznear_km`, <50 km OK, others ERA5+residual OK; this is the implementation assumption of this protocol, not the r2c sparse resampling prediction. |
| Hurricane | + land pool; Beryl additional event included in LOEO, Francine as a separate event; Holland+residual fixed at 75 km, OK75 as baseline, OKfit added. The Holland chain 2 min/5 s averaging period conversion and 500 m reference height are both Node B preregistration assumptions, not values from literature; survivor bias from lost reports near the eye. |
| Extratropical | ; keep only ne_20190128_wide, ne_20210114_wide, ks_20221202, tx_20191126; ks_20180306 has VCTS non-compliance. Recommended OKfit. |
| Thunderstorm | ; exclude non-evaluable 2025-03-04. Recommend sustained wind IDW, gust OK75; all apply only to event peaks across valid minutes. |
| Correction/Interval | Additive mean, OLS linear, empirical quantile rank mapping (extrapolation truncation), non-negative clipping; 80% intervals use absolute residual quantiles within training folds, all of which are H5 preregistration assumptions without complex modeling or post-hoc parameter tuning. |

## Known Limitations
The number of left-out events is small, and event variability is large; training residuals are used both for fitting and calibrating intervals, so coverage may be optimiztic. Fair-weather data are hourly METAR, while thunderstorm data are 1-minute; hurricane and extratropical use different event station networks. The model's "daily predicted peak" here for fair-weather differs from r2c's "prediction at observed peak time", so the raw bias cannot be directly compared against r2c's approximately −1.7 m/s; r1 all-station leave-one-out is also not r2c's sparse resampling. Recommended methods are fixed according to the protocol, and post-hoc superior corrections from the table are not cherry-picked as the final method. Leave-one-station-out does not prove effectiveness for stationless loss locations, and event peaks may be truncated during reporting outages. All times are UTC; no cross-borrowing of parameters for wind direction, gusts, or sustained winds. External inputs have not been updated, with no newly added external data.

## Conclusions
fair/sustained: Raw bias -0.82, RMSE 1.74 m/s; additive correction effective (bias +0.00, RMSE 1.54); linear correction effective (bias -0.00, RMSE 1.53); quantile correction effective (bias -0.00, RMSE 1.67).
hurricane/sustained: Raw bias -0.08, RMSE 2.74 m/s; additive correction effective (bias -0.01, RMSE 2.74); linear correction effective (bias +0.00, RMSE 2.58); quantile correction effective (bias +0.01, RMSE 2.76).
extratropical/sustained: Raw bias -1.46, RMSE 2.29 m/s; additive correction effective (bias +0.03, RMSE 1.78); linear correction effective (bias +0.13, RMSE 1.80); quantile correction effective (bias -0.11, RMSE 1.90).
thunderstorm/sustained: Raw bias -3.25, RMSE 4.78 m/s; additive correction effective (bias +0.02, RMSE 3.60); linear partially effective (bias +0.74, RMSE 3.93); quantile partially effective (bias -0.09, RMSE 5.09).
hurricane/gust: Raw bias +0.27, RMSE 3.44 m/s; additive correction effective (bias -0.00, RMSE 3.44); linear correction effective (bias +0.01, RMSE 3.36); quantile partially effective (bias +0.01, RMSE 3.56).
extratropical/gust: Raw bias -1.38, RMSE 2.78 m/s; additive correction effective (bias +0.11, RMSE 2.51); linear correction effective (bias +0.42, RMSE 2.58); quantile correction effective (bias +0.04, RMSE 2.54).
thunderstorm/gust: Raw bias -5.08, RMSE 6.85 m/s; additive correction effective (bias +0.05, RMSE 4.78); linear partially effective (bias +1.23, RMSE 5.43); quantile correction effective (bias -0.07, RMSE 5.20).

# H5 Peak Underestimation Correction Assessment and Protocol v1.2 (2026-10-14, Node H Lead)

- Results (registered in prereg_h5.md at 19:10, criteria derived from superiors and the task specification): Under leave-one-event-out, additive correction by event type suppresses pooled bias within ±0.5 m/s across all four sustained wind categories and all three gust categories, with RMSE not deteriorating → according to the criterion, "Correction effective". RMSE: fair-weather −12%, extratropical sustained wind −22%, thunderstorm sustained wind −25%, gust −30%; hurricane Holland+residual itself is already nearly unbiased and needs no correction. Cross-category extrapolation (fitting on three categories, scoring on the fourth) is "ineffective" for extratropical and thunderstorm; categorization is mandatory.
- Lead's interpretation (with qualifications): A pooled bias of ≈0 under leave-one-out is almost inevitable for additive correction, and the criterion is relatively lenient toward it; the key is to look at residual bias across individual events: fair-weather ±0.3, extratropical sustained wind ±0.4, extratropical gust −1.0 to +1.25, thunderstorm −2.2 to +1.3 (sustained wind) / −3.4 to +1.9 (gust). Therefore: fair-weather, extratropical, and hurricane (kriging time series) can be used with confidence; the thunderstorm correction magnitude is merely a rough estimate from 4 events.
- What was done: Protocol upgraded to v1.2, adding Section 4 correction table and qualifications, handed over to Node I via superiors (v1.1 will no longer be distributed). Not separately submitted for review: numbers in Section 4 were taken item-by-item from results_h5.md with no new derivations; if superiors wish to review, it can be re-submitted.
- Why: What Node I needs most is that peaks are not underestimated. Basis: internal line data, no literature basis.
- Cost of being wrong: An inaccurate thunderstorm correction magnitude would introduce event-level wind speed errors of ±2–3 m/s at thunderstorm loss locations, which has been explicitly stated in the protocol.
- Next steps for Node H: Both the station phase and corrections are complete. The only remaining candidate is thunderstorm "radar + station" (already logged on the project page; its scale exceeds the testbed, with the decision left to superiors on whether to write a promotion proposal). This node enters the state of awaiting feedback from Node I; if Node I discovers issues after use, a new round will be opened.

# Verdict: Review ("Station Wind Speed Reconstruction Protocol v1" H→I) · 2026-10-14

Reviewers E (Gemini), A (GPT-6), and D (GLM), 3/3 valid, all "supported with reservations". Only one round of review. Lead personally calculated and verified the numbers labeled "verified" using peaks/prediction files. Conclusion: v1 will not be submitted; v1.1 will be produced according to the following revisions and submitted to Node I.

## Must Change
1. **Mismatch between metrics and methods in the two fair-weather wind rows** (Consensus among all three, verified Lines 55–62): 2.319 is ERA5+residual, not kriging; −2.6%/−9.4%/−12.5% are hourly RMSE reductions, not peak; −9.4% belongs to the 54 km bin; the optimal pure interpolation for the 10% bin peak is IDW. v1.1 will list by bin separately: 40 km bin OK fit 2.485/−1.74 vs ERA5+residual 2.319/−1.62 (−6.7% at peak time); 54 km bin IDW 2.674/−1.93 vs 2.405/−1.73 (−10.1%); 82 km bin IDW 2.882/−2.02 vs 2.503/−1.78 (−13.2%); hourly reductions listed separately. Note that r2/r2c are random thinning resamplings, not leave-one-station-out; data consist of 10 fair-weather days with QC removing >40 kt; move the wording "synoptic gale" to the extratropical row.
2. **Inconsistent "peak" definitions** (Consensus among all three): Fair-weather wind is "prediction error at the observed daily peak time" (not error of predicted daily maximum, Line 54); H2/H3/H4 are "predicted maximum vs observed maximum within mutually valid observation times", with windows being landfall ±12 h, 12 h before and after peak, and regional gust peak ±3 h, respectively. v1.1 will add a definitions section, and require Node I to append peak definitions and windows to every record.
3. **Mixed bias criteria in the extratropical row** (E, A, D): −1.4 is the 5-event value. Lead's own calculation for strictly 4 events across 359 stations: OK fit 2.295/−1.46, ERA5+residual 2.221/−1.30; gust OK fit 2.78/−1.38. v1.1 switches to these.
4. **Hurricane row obscures high-wind areas and single-event bias** (Consensus among all three; verified): Lead's own calculation for independent 9+Francine high-wind stations (≥12 m/s, 283 station-events): OK fit 3.87/−2.59, Holland+residual fit 3.45/−0.66, ERA5+residual 3.59/−1.94; broken down by distance ( Lines 256–258): <1 RMW 56 stations interpolation 3.60/−2.02, fusion 4.25/−2.13 (fusion is worse); 1–3 RMW 239 stations 3.42/−1.68 vs 3.04/−1.03; >3 RMW 450 stations 2.24/−0.80 vs 2.21/−0.69. Single-event biases: Ida +0.82 to +0.99, Nicole +0.65, etc. v1.1 will split rows by high wind / distance, deleting the sweeping claim that "all methods systematically underestimate". Note differing event sets for all-station counts vs high-wind counts.
5. **Hurricane "needs time series" row fills hourly RMSE into the peak column** (E): v1.1 will list separately, and warn: the event maximum error of kriging time series under the peak criterion is 2.79/−1.18 (high-wind stations 3.87/−2.59), and 2.07 must not be taken as the peak error.
6. **Thunderstorm row** (Consensus among all three; verified): 44 is the number of station-events (14-station network, 10–13 stations per event); sustained wind optimal is IDW 4.78/−3.25, fixed OK 4.82/−3.46; gust listed separately as fixed OK 6.85/−5.08; gust did not undergo ERA5 fusion; window is determined by all-station observations and contains left-out station information (optimiztic).
7. **Extrapolation and point-by-point assignment** (A): Sample statistics cannot be taken as guaranteed errors for each loss location; change "errors are larger far from stations" to "unverified", citing only the 82 km bin descriptive statistics. Small sample sizes (10 fair-weather days, 4 extratropical events, 4 thunderstorm events) and the optimizm of cherry-picking based on the scoring set must be included in the qualifications.
8. **HRRR phrasing** (A, D): Change to "f01 cannot guarantee target station independence".

## For Reference Only (Adopted and Incorporated)
- A: The sustained wind averaging period in the IEM 1-minute archive was not verified field-by-field; write "approx. 2-minute running average, H4 field unverified".
- A: Water body pool includes coastal airports, not just offshore platforms; stations with no return from WorldCover have also been excluded.
- D: Hurricane gust has results (Holland+residual 3.47/+0.23, fixed OK 3.67/−0.69); add them in.

## Unadopted Objections
None. The three opinions shared a consistent direction, all verifiable against evidence documents.

## Postscript (10-14)
- Modified: The main table originally labeled ks_20180306 as "compliant", with COMBINED_STRICT at 433 stations −3.24% (reviewers may have read the old main table); now COMBINED_STRICT in both the main table and the method-by-method table reflects strictly compliant 4 events across 359 stations (2.295→2.221, −3.23%, 207/359), and the 433-station row has been renamed "five-event historical basis (including 1 non-compliant event)". Protocol v1 marked as obsolete; extratropical numbers in v1.2 and the project page have been verified and are consistent.

# H3 温带气旋风站点留一：TSNO 勘误后五事件版

按计算前登记的 评分，不修改判据。时间 UTC；持续风与阵风分开。原 误将 METAR 的 TSNO（雷暴资料不可用）识别为雷暴，属于已作废先行版，保留原文件不覆盖；本版重新核对所有已下载候选原始 METAR，剔除 TSNO 假阳性，不重训、不改数值预测。

## 事件筛选

NOAA 2018–2024 年度 details：同州同 UTC 日 High Wind ≥5、Thunderstorm Wind=0；重点 TX/KS/NE，选 5 个符合区域≥60可用站的日子。观测区域小时持续风中位数最大时刻±12 h；区域框 TX 30–36°N/103–95°W、KS 36–40°N/102–94°W、NE 与邻近 KS 39–43°N/104–94°W。METAR 雷暴复核使用独立 token TS(?!NO) 或 CB；TSNO 只表示雷暴资料不可用，不是雷暴。五场窗口内均无 TS/CB token（后经勘误：ks_20180306 有 1 条 VCTS，见文末）；已试取其他候选在，筛选并非随机抽样。

| 事件/UTC 日 | 同州 High Wind | 同州 Thunderstorm Wind | 峰时 UTC | 区域真实 TS/CB 条 | 区域陆地候选→合格站 | 判定资格 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| ne_20190128_wide | 53 | 0 | 2019-01-28T11:00:00+00:00 | 0 | 65→65 | 合规 |
| ne_20210114_wide | 63 | 0 | 2021-01-14T19:00:00+00:00 | 0 | 72→70 | 合规 |
| ks_20221202 | 23 | 0 | 2022-12-02T20:00:00+00:00 | 0 | 91→86 | 合规 |
| ks_20180306 | 38 | 0 | 2018-03-06T18:00:00+00:00 | 0 | 75→74 | 不合规（VCTS，OK:AVK 2018-03-06 14:15 UTC） |
| tx_20191126 | 70 | 0 | 2019-11-26T18:00:00+00:00 | 0 | 143→138 | 合规 |

## 预设判据与每事件结果

# Thunderstorm Independent Wind Speed Gap: Radar Minimum Feasibility Check First (2026-10-14 21:xx)

Decision I made: I r2 confirmed that the existing station network cannot detect thunderstorm damaging winds (DAT damage estimated wind is a median 37 mph higher than the window maximum gust of neighboring stations within ≤25 km, 97% positive), plus H4 station reconstruction is ineffective for thunderstorms. Instead of directly drafting a promotion proposal, I will first task H with H6: 1–2 Dallas thunderstorm days, public NEXRAD Level II, testing whether radar lowest-elevation velocity can yield credible near-surface winds at ASOS stations and DAT damage points, asking Event Line Lead first if there is any reusable pipeline. I will concurrently run a hurricane pilot.
- Why: A promotion proposal requires preliminary evidence and an estimable workload; currently there is only negative evidence that "station network does not work", with zero figures indicating "radar works". No literature basis, based on our line's data.
- Cost of being wrong: One extra small pilot (workstation/Colab CPU, a small amount of time); if radar near-surface conversion itself cannot be credible, thunderstorms will be documented as infeasible under current conditions.

items.text:
# H6 Preregistration (Before Running Radar Scoring)

Events: Dallas 2024-06-01, 2025-07-09; time UTC. Only public low-elevation radar velocity is used, reusing existing scan lists from the event line as much as possible, without taking their research conclusions as near-surface wind ground truth. A: Score 1-min observed sustained wind and 5-s peak gust respectively for H4 same-event, same-station cases with available radar gates; radar takes the maximum dealiased |Vr| of quality-acceptable gates nearest to the station within the window as a lower-bound proxy of radial velocity, without falsely claiming to be 10 m wind. H4 same-station method uses the day's optimal pure interpolation, reporting paired-sample RMSE and bias (radar minus observed). B: On the subset covered on both days with DAT points, compare the point-level median difference between the radar proxy and DAT estimated wind following the original DAT–station gust pairing specification; DAT is damage inference, not instrumented observation. When scans are incomplete, event peaks must not be claimed, and even less directly used as criteria against full-window H4 peaks.

Promising: The absolute value of A's radar peak bias is reduced by at least half compared to H4 interpolation and RMSE is not higher than interpolation; B's radar–DAT median difference is halved compared to the 37 mph of neighboring station maximum gust–DAT. Unviable: A is not superior to interpolation and B's gap is not reduced. The rest is Inconclusive, with explanations on beam height, single radial component, temporal coverage, and sample size. Both A and B require observed pairings and adequate window radar coverage to be executed; missing metrics cannot be used as substitutes. Geometry adopts 4/3 effective Earth radius, Earth radius 6371 km (assumption), prioritizing reporting per-gate height rather than correcting aloft velocities to 10 m; no unverified gust conversion factor is used. Radar dealiasing and quality control must be specified before peak selection; missing data and aliasing must not be filled with larger absolute values. The two-day small sample serves only as a feasibility signal.

items.title: H6 Dallas thunderstorm radar near-surface wind minimal feasibility check
items.text:
# H6 Dallas Thunderstorm Radar Near-Surface Wind Minimum Feasibility Check

Conclusion: **Inconclusive; this round's radar radial velocity cannot be used as credible 10 m wind speed at damage points.** The combined sample for station Test A did not meet the preregistered "dual thresholds"; NWS DAT points were 0 for both days within the specified Dallas bounding box and dates, rendering Test B unscorable. This is neither evidence that fusion is effective, nor evidence that radar technology is generally unviable. See for preregistration; all times in UTC.

## Data and Pairing

Reusing the intersection of eligible land stations from the event line S3's , and , , each event has 9 stations (originally 13 and 10 stations), totaling 18 station-events and 410 valid station–scan records. See for exact URL, filter conditions, and 0 returns of the official DAT layer; Node I's legacy pairing only covers up to 2024, and its 3 points on that day were all on the Texas coast rather than Dallas, which cannot substitute for a new query.

Dealiasing used Py-ART's region-based method and the positive Nyquist given by the volume scan, taking the median of absolute values of valid radial velocities from the 3×3 nearest gates to the station as a single scan sample; requiring at least 4 gates, reflectivity ≥ 10 dBZ, spectrum width ≤ 8 m/s, local median deviation ≤ 5 m/s, and then taking the maximum across the entire period of available scans for that station. Radar measures hydrometeor radial velocity; |Vr| is neither horizontal vector wind nor 10 m mean wind or 5-second gust; in the presence of vertical motion / hydrometeor sedimentation lag, it cannot even strictly be called a "lower bound" of 10 m wind. It was **not** multiplied by an empirical gust factor, fitted/calibrated, or extrapolated to heights without justification. Beam height was estimated based on station ground elevation and 4/3 effective Earth radius; the center of the lowest-elevation gate for the 18 stations ranged 258–1646 m AGL, far above 10 m. The number of quality-available scans per station was 3–53/event; only 11/18 sustained wind peak times and 11/18 gust peak times could find valid radar scans within ±3 min. Thus, the "peak" in the table below is not a fully synchronized, same-height, like-for-like quantity test, especially since station counts were selected by radar echo availability.

## Test A: Same-Station Event Peaks (m/s, Radar − Observed Bias)

H4 per-event optimal leave-one-out pure interpolation: 2024-06-01 OK75, 2025-07-09 IDW; re-pooled and scored on the *same radar-matchable stations*, without directly using H4's original 13/10 station summary. Mean wind and gusts are compared separately; the gust column is merely a cross-quantity diagnostic, not used for wind speed improvement criteria.

| Date | Station-Events | Beam Center AGL Range m | Sustained Wind H4 bias / RMSE | Sustained Wind Radar Radial Proxy bias / RMSE | Gust H4 bias / RMSE | Gust Radial Proxy Cross-Quantity bias / RMSE |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2024-06-01 | 9 | 258–1482 | −3.585 / 4.492 | −2.678 / 3.286 | −4.909 / 6.002 | −6.222 / 6.692 |
| 2025-07-09 | 9 | 258–1646 | −3.587 / 4.923 | −3.889 / 6.542 | −5.105 / 6.699 | −8.348 / 10.245 |
| Total | 18 | 258–1646 | −3.586 / 4.712 | −3.284 / 5.176 | −5.007 / 6.360 | −7.285 / 8.653 |

For the total sustained wind, the absolute value of bias only dropped from 3.586 to 3.284 m/s, failing to achieve "halved"; RMSE increased from 4.712 to 5.176. For the comparable 17 station-events / 352 scans aligned within ±3 min scan-by-scan, radar scan peaks relative to *matched observation minute* peaks had bias −1.015, RMSE 3.337 m/s (gust cross-quantity bias −4.041, RMSE 5.135); this is a conditional sample distinct from the full event peaks and is not used for preregistered criteria. See for per-station gate heights, scan counts, and event peaks; see for all quality-available station–scans.

## Test B: DAT Damage Points

Querying the official DAT point layer with bbox `[−98.5,31.5,−95.5,34]`, for all of 2024-06-01 UTC and the two days 2025-07-08–09 UTC returned **0 and 0 points**, respectively (query not truncated). Without within-event DAT damage estimated wind labels, it is impossible to calculate the radar–DAT median difference, let alone compare it to the 37 mph median difference between neighboring station maximum gust and DAT in Node I's large sample; that 37 mph is also influenced by DAT damage estimated wind unit assumptions, sampling, and time windows, and cannot serve as a measured baseline for these two station cases. The absence of DAT points does not imply that no damage occurred.

## Parameter Sources Table and Limitations

| Quantity/Rule | Source or Nature |
| --- | --- |
| Events/stations and H4 peaks | , `raw_minute_*_h4.csv.gz`; original source IEM ASOS 1-minute, cleaned via H4; sustained wind and 5-second gust unmixed |
| Radar/scans | NOAA NEXRAD Level II KFWS, Unidata public S3 mirror; daily volume scan counts and failures at ; event line provides existing reusable scan package for TDAL/KFWS, only as reading reference |
| Dealiasing | Py-ART 2.2.0 `dealias_region_based`; only KFWS with valid positive Nyquist can be processed; existing TDAL scans decode Nyquist=0 in Py-ART, and this round did not arbitrarily assign folding velocities for processing, so TDWR DAL was available but not incorporated into numerical tests; not a "two-radar synthesis" |
| Station radial estimation/QC | This round's **assumption**: nearest 3×3 gates ≥ 4 valid, reflectivity ≥ 10 dBZ, spectrum width ≤ 8 m/s, local median deviation ≤ 5 m/s; local median |Vr|, then taking the maximum; not optimized against independent labels; |
| Beam geometry | This round's **assumption**: effective Earth radius 4/3 × 6371 km; center AGL calculated using radar elevation, station elevation, measured slant range, and elevation angle; 10 m wind not generated from this assumed value |
| Neighboring minutes | This round's **assumption**: radar volume start time ±3 min matched to nearest station minute (same ~6 min scan interval magnitude); marked missing if no echo/valid gate; not continuous instantaneous peak verification |
| Literature limitations | Wiki card `ASI8UKX6TAK3TUDDUU83NPGE` PDF pp. 8–9 describes low-level wind structure in a different environment. None of the three can provide general factors to directly convert this study's single-station KFWS radial quantities hundreds of meters high into 10 m 5-second gusts; `SBEWXJVU` remains a candidate pending independent review, and its values were not adopted. |

Lowest elevation angle still suffers from beam spreading, refraction, and blockage; even with noise reduction, it may be affected by non-meteorological echoes, dealiasing errors, and echo selection bias. Radar across discrete volume scans differs from continuous 1-minute ASOS sampling; velocity components are sensitive to wind direction, and a single station cannot recover 2D wind direction or 10 m gusts. For next-step assessment, re-verification is required on Dallas/other events that have **DAT points and reliable wind damage timing**, using TDWR/dual-radar with confirmable Nyquist and low-level wind vertical verification, pre-fixing a support set with consistent time/space/averaging intervals, and verifying DAT estimated wind units first. Prior to this, this round's radial quantities will not be handed over to Node I as independent wind speeds at damage points.

Figure: ; Data: NOAA NEXRAD Level II / Unidata S3, IEM ASOS 1 min and H4 LOO; open circles in figure are H4, solid circles are KFWS |Vr|, gust column specifically marked as cross-quantity.

# H6 Thunderstorm Radar Near-Surface Wind Minimum Feasibility: Inconclusive (2026-10-14, Node H Lead)

- Results (prereg_h6.md registered at 21:45, prior to 22:00 run): KFWS lowest elevation (approx. 0.48°) radial velocity, Py-ART dealiasing, all 181 volumes across the two days retrieved, raw files not retained. Lowest elevation beam center 258–1646 m AGL above stations.
 - Test A (18 station-events): Event peak sustained wind bias H4 interpolation −3.59 → radar |Vr| −3.28 (not halved), RMSE 4.71 → 5.18 (worsened) → does not pass criteria. Conditional sample aligned within ±3 min of scans (17 station-events, 352 scans) has bias −1.0, RMSE 3.3, but is not the preregistered specification.
 - Test B: Official DAT layer had 0 points within the Dallas bounding box over these two days at , unscorable.
 - TDWR DAL data available, but Py-ART decoded Nyquist=0; folding velocity was not arbitrarily set, not included.
- Verdict: **Inconclusive**. Missing components: (1) Single radar provides only radial component with beam hundreds of meters above ground, lacking reliable conversion to 10 m / gust (ASI8UKX6 PDF pp. 3–4, TAK3TUDD PDF pp. 83, 106–107 do not give general factors); (2) Zero DAT damage points over the two days; (3) TDWR low beam was not utilized; (4) Sample size of 18 station-events.
- Lead's interpretation: This is not evidence that "radar is unviable", but there is also zero positive signal to support writing a promotion proposal right now. If trying again, the design must change: first select events by DAT thunderstorm damage point density within TDWR / dual-radar coverage, verify TDWR Nyquist, then use low beam (<300 m above ground) or dual-Doppler synthesis, and compare against damage points. The scale of this step remains small, and another run can be done in the test ground (H7), to be decided by superiors.
- Do not hand over this round's radar radial quantities to I.
- Basis: Our line's data; literature cards as above, no general conversion factors.
- Cost of being wrong: If the radar route is actually viable, discovery is delayed by one round; cost is only a few bot hours, 0 CU.

# H7 Preregistration (Before Candidate Retrieval and Scoring)
Date 2026-10-14 (US Eastern); original event times strictly UTC. Only public TSTM/Wind DAT damage points are included; DAT estimated wind is damage inference, not true wind speed; its windspeed unit must first be verified against official sources, otherwise numerical Test B comparison will not be conducted.

Candidate rules: Aggregate from Node I's stored 2019–2024 DAT points and available neighboring station records by UTC date/region, prioritizing points with ≥20 positive DAT estimated wind points and distance to WSR-88D/TDWR low-elevation beam center AGL <300 m; verify TDWR or dual-WSR coverage; prioritize those with ≥8 available ASOS 1-minute stations in the vicinity of the same window. Select 2–3 distinct events in descending order of the number of qualifying damage points, without selecting based on wind speed scores. Failure to meet coverage or sample thresholds will also be recorded faithfully. Historical pairings are only used to filter candidates, not as independent wind labels.

Scheme: If TDWR Nyquist cannot be reliably obtained from decoded metadata, do not guess numbers or dealias; switch to WSR-88D nearest lowest-elevation velocity scans, Py-ART dealiasing, and 3×3 gate medians; |Vr| is strictly the radial component magnitude at radar altitude (neither 10 m horizontal wind nor a strict ground wind lower bound); requiring corresponding reflectivity ≥10 dBZ, spectrum width ≤8 m/s, valid gates ≥4, local MAD ≤5 m/s, beam center AGL <300 m, peak time difference ≤3 min. If there is no publicly supported height and gust conversion, do not convert, and report only low-altitude radial proxy / surface gust ratios. Station training and scoring adhere to H4 station cleaning and station leave-one-out, comparing event peaks only during observation periods without mixing sustained wind and gusts.

Test A: For the same station and same event, radar estimated peak vs. observed peak, using the better of IDW/OK under the H4 protocol as baseline; passes when |radar peak bias| ≤ |interpolation peak bias|/2 and radar RMSE ≤ interpolation RMSE. Test B: For the same batch of DAT points, passes when median |radar wind − DAT estimated wind| ≤ median |nearest station window maximum gust − DAT estimated wind|/2; verify DAT windspeed units first. Judged as "Promising" only if both A and B pass; judged as "Unviable" if either fails when A ≥8 station-events and B ≥20 points; judged as "Inconclusive" if sample size is insufficient. Counts are reported for all quality screenings and no-echo removals, without adjusting thresholds based on posterior scores.

items.text:
# H7 Thunderstorm Radar Near-Surface Wind: Final Small Test with Low Beam and Damage Points

Conclusion: Inconclusive. The two Chicago events have 108 damage points that satisfy 3DEP-verified height <300 m, DAT time ±3 min, and radar quality gates; however, scorable ASOS station events in the same low beam are 0, and Test A cannot be scored. The `windspeed` field in the DAT FeatureServer has no declared units, and single-station radar `|Vr|` is the radial component at beam height rather than a 10 m gust; Test B cannot serve as a pass criterion with verified units and identical physical quantities. Even performing sensitivity calculations based solely on "assuming DAT values are mph", the median absolute difference between radar and DAT is 16.043 m/s, greater than the 9.668 m/s of the nearest station window maximum gust, showing no advantage; this comparison cannot be called a surface wind validation.

The protocol was pre-written; the initial version of the decoding script had gate indexing errors, yielding no valid samples on the first attempt; currently, with 28 volume scans fully processed after the fix, is the only valid metric. The initial round of local diagnostics is retained as , and must not be used for scoring. The entire process used workstation local CPU, 0 CU, and retained no raw radar binary files. All times are UTC.

## Candidate and Event Selection

From the full snapshot of official DAT TSTM/Wind points for 2019–2024 at Node I, coarse filtering was performed by date, distance within 25 km of WSR, and lowest 0.5° radar relative height. The top two are 2024-06-23 and 2024-07-16, both within 25 km of KLOT; Level II archives for TORD can be listed for both days, and TMDW can also be listed for July 16, but its Py-ART decoding shows `nyquist_velocity` of 0 m/s (measured on a single TORD V08), which cannot reliably dealias, so it fell back to KLOT's lowest velocity scan per pre-registration without fabricating TDWR Nyquist. Further dual-WSR do not satisfy the low-beam constraint. At candidacy, there were 11 general ASOS station metadata entries within a 60 km radius, but in reality the ASOS 1-minute archive had only 5 metadata stations/events; the expected Test A sample condition of ≥8 did not hold, which is an observable gap from the selection phase.

| Date (UTC) | KLOT Evaluation Window (UTC) | DAT TSTM/Wind Candidate Points in Window | 1-minute Station Metadata | KLOT Volume Scans | Valid Points with Radar–DAT ±3 min, 3DEP <300 m | 3DEP Beam Center AGL Range (Valid Points) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2024-06-23 | 03:45–05:15 | 90 | 5 | 13 | 52 | 213.6–265.1 m |
| 2024-07-16 | 01:45–03:15 | 67 | 5 | 15 | 56 | 73.5–258.6 m |

Beam height is estimated using Py-ART scan elevation angle, station slant range, radar elevation, and the 4/3 effective Earth radius curvature formula; initially, DAT gate sampling approximated damage point ground elevation with the nearest ASOS station elevation; during scoring, USGS EPQS/3DEP point-by-point elevation was checked, and 108/109 matching points obtained 3DEP elevation and were verified <300 m (the remaining 1 point had no elevation and was excluded). This is not beam bottom height; beam width, building blockage, and data epoch mismatch were not evaluated. For valid B points, 3DEP height P10/median/P90 are 152.7/229.8/252.8 m. Points wrongly excluded by the terrain proxy during initial screening cannot be retrieved ex post.

## Test A: Stations (Compared with Station-by-Station Leave-One-Out IDW)

| Variable | Station Events in Same Window with ≥75% Valid Minutes and Low-Beam Echo | KLOT \ | Vr\ | Bias/RMSE | IDW Leave-One-Out Bias/RMSE | Threshold |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1-minute gust event peak | 0 | Cannot be calculated | Cannot be calculated | At least 8 station events; not met |
| 1-minute sustained wind event peak | 0 | Cannot be calculated | Cannot be calculated | Not met |

There are only 5 1-minute metadata stations per event; the center heights of KLOT's lowest ~0.48° beam at these five stations are ARR 417, DPA 385, MDW 400, ORD 478, and PWK 736 m AGL (calculated from radar elevation and IEM station elevation), all above 300 m. Therefore, under the constraints of <300 m, valid echo, ≥75% minute data, and the same 90 min window, no station satisfies all conditions simultaneously; stations cannot be "cobbled together" by relaxing beam height or misusing higher beams. The original Dallas two-day leave-one-out error from H4 is not for the same stations and same events in Chicago, and cannot be misappropriated as a comparison here. retains the same-window minute-by-minute IDW² leave-one-out calculation logic, but does not output fabricated errors without qualified stations.

## Test B: DAT Points (Descriptive and Conditional Sensitivity Only)

| Metric | 2024-06-23 | 2024-07-16 | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Points with low beam/valid echo/near-time/3DEP height verification and neighboring station window gusts | 52 | 56 | 108 |
| DAT `windspeed` unit explicitly verified via service metadata | No | No | No |
| If assuming DAT numbers are mph: \ | Radar radial component − DAT estimated wind \ | Median | — | — | 16.043 m/s |
| Same batch of points: \ | Nearest station ±3 h window max gust − DAT estimated wind \ | Median (same assumption) | — | — | 9.668 m/s |
| Ratio of the above two medians (conditional description only) | — | — | 1.659 (not reduced by half) |

These are DAT points, not 108 independent weather events or independent measured wind speeds. The median distance from the nearest station to the damage point is 16.84 km; the radar takes the nearest volume scan within DAT time ±3 min, while neighboring stations use the maximum METAR gust within DAT ±3 h, having different temporal supports. The P10/median/P90 of the ratio of radar radial component to neighboring station gust are 0.335/0.704/1.059, which is **not** a generalizable conversion factor from radar wind speed to surface gust. `windspeed` is defined as a string without units in the official FeatureServer; the fact that NWS event text typically uses mph is insufficient to prove the data dictionary unit for each entry in this field, so the conditional mph comparison is not used for formal Test B determination. The right axis of the figure clearly shows unit incompatibility.

## Method and Parameter Sources Table

| Parameter or decision | Value | Source or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Criterion and minimum sample | A ≥8 station events, B ≥20 points; promising only if both A and B pass, otherwise deemed failing if either fails under qualified samples | Before current calculation run, not modified based on results |
| DAT classification, location, time, damage estimated wind | Official FeatureServer/0, 2019–2024 Node I read-only snapshot; |
| 1-minute sustained wind/gust, station location/elevation | IEM `sknt`, reserved query |
| Radar | KLOT V06 lowest ~0.5° scan with velocity, Py-ART dealiasing by radar Nyquist region | NOAA/Unidata Level II https://unidata-nexrad-level2.s3.amazonaws.com/; Helmus & Collis 2016, DOI 10.5334/jors.119 |
| Station/point gate quality filtering | 3×3 gates with at least 4 valid, co-located reflectivity ≥10 dBZ, spectrum width ≤8 m/s, local MAD ≤5 m/s, beam center AGL <300 m, near-time ±3 min | Small-test pre-registered **assumption**, not the 10 m conversion given in literature |
| Radar beam ground elevation | Initial screening with nearest station elevation proxy; scoring verified ground elevation with USGS EPQS 3DEP | Proxy is an **assumption**, 3DEP https://epqs.nationalmap.gov/v1/json and , modern data applied to historical events has temporal mismatch |
| Test A leave-one-out baseline | Minute-by-minute remaining valid stations, IDW inverse distance squared, other stations ±2 min, at least 3 stations; peak of observation period | **Assumption**, replicating H4 prototype concept, cannot falsely claim H4 original location scoring; no scorable stations appeared this time |
| Damage point nearest station gust | Node I DAT ±3 h already paired, same 108 points | Node I; not ground truth at damage points |
| 10 m / gust conversion | Not converted; radial component is not a reliable lower bound for surface horizontal wind | Lacks generalizable conversion verified by this data; literature values not cited as empirical constants |
| DAT unit conditional sensitivity | Only provisionally assuming mph, 1 mph=0.44704 m/s | **Assumption**; `windspeed` field in FeatureServer/0 has no unit label, hence not used for pass determination |

No private data from other lines was used or downloaded; TDWR reading methods from the event line were only used as read-only references ( and ). New data citations have been added; raw Level II responses were decoded only in memory, leaving no local raw radar cache; only stored extracted values. Radar gust physical quantity mismatch and the station network–beam intersection are the primary limitations; damage estimated wind is itself an inference rather than ground truth.

## Conclusion

Inconclusive: The low beam can cover and match 108 DAT damage points, but 0 qualified ASOS station events prevent Test A from being conducted; DAT field units are not yet officially specified, and no conversion from low-altitude radial wind to surface gusts has been established. The conditional mph Test B comparison also showed no advantage. This final small test does not provide an independent near-surface gust estimate that can be delivered to Node I; without adding near-field in-situ observations/reliable multi-radar and height conversions, further scaling up the same method lacks an evidentiary basis.

# Node H Closure: Protocol v1.2 is the Final Deliverable; Thunderstorm Wind Speed is Not Feasible Under Current Public Data Conditions (2026-10-14, Node H Lead)

- H7 (registered in prereg_h7.md at 22:24, prior to execution): Chicago 2024-06-23, 2024-07-16, KLOT 0.5° (Nyquist for TORD/TMDW read as 0, not fabricated, fell back to KLOT per pre-registration), 28 volume scans. 108 DAT thunderstorm damage points satisfy beam center <300 m (3DEP verified elevation) and ±3 min matching; however, beam heights above the 5 nearby ASOS 1-minute stations are 385–736 m, yielding 0 qualified station events → Test A cannot be scored. DAT `windspeed` field has no official units; when merely assuming mph, median |radar radial component − DAT| is 16.0 m/s, greater than median |nearest station gust − DAT| of 9.7 m/s (ratio 1.66), showing no advantage. Determination: Inconclusive.
- Stop-loss per superior's plan: Independent near-surface wind speed for thunderstorm winds is recorded at this node as "**not feasible under current public data conditions**"——station interpolation peak is underestimated by ~3–5 m/s (H4); single-radar low-altitude radial component can neither be validated at stations nor is closer to DAT at damage points than neighboring station gusts (H6, H7), and lacks a reliable conversion to 10 m gusts.
- Node H closes, project page status changed to "Shelved": Final deliverable is "Station Wind Speed Reconstruction Protocol v1.2" (delivered to I).
- Restart conditions: (1) Node I identifies systemic issues after using the protocol; (2) Near-field in-situ observations appear (dense Mesonet/mobile radar/towers) that can validate low-altitude radar winds in thunderstorms; (3) TDWR Level II Nyquist can be reliably read, and stations fall under <300 m beams; (4) DAT wind speed field units and definition are officially confirmed.
- Basis: Data from this line (H4, H6, H7); literature cards ASI8UKX6 (PDF pp. 3–4), TAK3TUDD (PDF pp. 83, 106–107) do not provide a general conversion.
- Cost: If the radar approach is actually feasible, it has been shelved; restart conditions have been clearly stated.

reviews.text:
# Verdict: Review (H Literature Conclusions C1–C5 + r1 Interpretation + r2 Design) · 2026-10-14

Reviewers: E (Gemini), A (GPT-6), D (GLM), 3/3 valid, all "supported with reservations". Only one round of review. The Lead has personally verified the evidence marked "verified" below.

## Must Change
1. **r1 ">50 km −17%/−24%" mainly came from offshore platform station BQX** (E). Verified: BQX = "Brazos 451", 28.49°N 95.72°W, elevation 0 m; Lead self-calculation: after removing BQX from the >50 km subset, ERA5 + residual relative to OK dropped from −16.8% to −8.9% (2,244 station-hours, 34 stations). −24% (GBT) includes HRRR features and in-training residuals, no longer cited. → Update lead_check, r1/r2 decisions, project page; recalculate r2 with the cleaned station list.
2. **Incomplete station cleaning** (E, D, A). Verified: CVB and T89 have identical coordinates (29.3419, −98.8509, "Castroville"); F12 and RFI have identical coordinates. E stated that KT89 reports were actually from Lajitas 470 km away (original reports not personally verified; adopting their handling suggestion, but not adopting their place name assertion as fact). Lead self-calculation on the full sample after removing BQX/T89/BSM: OK 1.577, ERA5 + residual 1.537, −2.5%, conclusion unchanged. → Deduplication changed to station distance threshold (merge and retain one station for <2 km) + exclude offshore platforms and stations with suspicious coordinates; during exclusion, simultaneously remove from input stations, training, and variograms (A, Item 5).
3. **Kiessling 2021's "about 5%" is unexplained variance (MSE dimension), not RMSE** (all three agreed; E based on kiessling_arxiv.pdf Eq. (1), Table 1). Changed to: unexplained variance decreased by 4.6%, equivalent to ~2.3% in RMSE; the optimal FF+RF in Table 1 averaged 0.357, equivalent to ~4.1% in RMSE.
4. **C1 cannot merge three metrics into a single "RMSE reduction range"** (A, D). Changed to writing metrics paper by paper: Kiessling (unexplained variance), S2G (held-out station centered RMSE 8.5%, vs. Barnes; official version verified by D and A; D pointed out that the official version states bias reduction is primary, so total RMSE reduction may be larger), KiloDA (station-by-station RMSE median −15.4%, vs. kriging; whole held-out block selected by ERA5 maximum error cluster; D verified original text: the strongest 5% wind speed tier is slightly worse than ERA5).
5. **C2 overworded** (A): The KiloDA ideal experiment is an "independent test in a simulated world, cannot extrapolate real-observation gains", not "leakage"; S2G Fig. 8 uses "RTMA as input and target", cannot serve as real-observation gains. "Assimilated from the same batch of stations" changed to "may contain information from the same stations, station-by-station records not verified".
6. **C3 correction** (D, A): The RTMA operational system routinely performs 10% random held-out cross-validation (EMC RTMA v2.2 overview, retrieved by D, Lead has not personally verified, marked "single source"); "no network-wide leave-one-out" changed to "no published network-wide leave-one-out error retrieved". Morris 2020's NODA is the background field; "about 1 kt higher" is EXP (analysis excluding airports) relative to NODA. ERA5: Hersbach 2020 lists land 10 m wind as not assimilated (D, A, E agree) → "ERA5 land station assimilation to be verified" changed to "does not directly assimilate land 10 m wind", and the ERA5 background can be considered largely independent of target stations. HRRR should only state "f01 cannot guarantee target station independence", without asserting "used upstream" station by station.
7. **"'Kriging tuning will only make the gains smaller' has no basis, deleted"** (A, E, D). E recalculation: after taking optimal variogram parameters for raw values and residuals respectively, the r1 reduction is 4.34%, still <10%. r2 has already reported "hourly fit" kriging simultaneously and taken the best pure interpolation as the baseline (responding to D); residual kriging still uses fixed 75 km (E pointed out asymmetry) → when recalculating r2, also do a fitted version for residuals, taking the best on both sides.
8. **The wording of r2 criteria is ambiguous and inconsistent with the original criteria** (A, E). The original criteria (Step 1 design) included "10–20% or satisfying only one → conditional"; in my r2 decision I wrote "otherwise Shelved", which was my mistake; the original three-tier criteria shall prevail. The "tier with ≥50 km" hits both the 25% (53 km) and 10% (82 km) tiers: report both tiers separately and evaluate separately. Existing results: 25% tier −8.8% → interpolation is sufficient; 10% tier −13.4% → conditional (E recalculated 7.6% / 13.3% after cleaning, does not change the verdict).
9. **Cannot expand "not meeting threshold" into "interpolation meets Node I requirements"** (A). Advice to I is narrowed to: under well-behaved sustained wind, use ordinary kriging for station distances <50 km, and ERA5 + residual kriging for further distances; gusts, peaks, thunderstorms/tropical cyclones/extratropical cyclones are all unverified, and peak hours generally underestimate by ~2 m/s.

## For Reference Only
- D: Austrian TAWES (EMS2026-549 abstract) 54 permanently held-out stations DL+CERRA 1.46 vs. regression kriging 1.51 m/s (about 3%); arXiv 2610.00728 generative assimilation is only about 2.4 percentage points higher than 3D-Var—consistent with C1 direction, not personally verified, listed only as clues.
- A: Samalot 2019 KF–UK 15% is a forecast post-processing gain, not a counterexample.
- A: S2G preprint station distance is written as 30 km, gusts are 3 s maximum within a 5-minute window (different from F's "27 km" "10 min") → update records according to preprint.
- D verified: r2 criteria timestamp precedes r2 run, "written a priori" holds.

## Objections Not Adopted
- A's "r1 is insufficient to support the Shelved basis of 'interpolation is sufficient'": partially not adopted. r1 is only used for triage of well-behaved wind small experiments in this node; the conclusion is already restricted to "this data, established methods, average sustained wind", not written externally as a general conclusion; nor does it shelve Node H on this basis.
- E's Lajitas place name assertion: original reports not personally verified, not written as fact, only used as one of the reasons for excluding T89 (coordinate overlap with CVB is sufficient).

## Conclusion on Counterexample Question
None of the three found verified literature where fusion/learning was ≥20% lower than the best kriging under real observations, held-out stations, flat terrain, and well-behaved high winds; A emphasized that this is "insufficient evidence", not "non-existent". Phrased accordingly.

# Verdict: Review ("Station Wind Speed Reconstruction Protocol v1" H→I) · 2026-10-14

Reviewers E (Gemini), A (GPT-6), and D (GLM), 3/3 valid, all "supported with reservations". Only one round of review. Lead personally calculated and verified the numbers labeled "verified" using peaks/prediction files. Conclusion: v1 will not be submitted; v1.1 will be produced according to the following revisions and submitted to Node I.

## Must Change
1. **Mismatch between metrics and methods in the two fair-weather wind rows** (Consensus among all three, verified Lines 55–62): 2.319 is ERA5+residual, not kriging; −2.6%/−9.4%/−12.5% are hourly RMSE reductions, not peak; −9.4% belongs to the 54 km bin; the optimal pure interpolation for the 10% bin peak is IDW. v1.1 will list by bin separately: 40 km bin OK fit 2.485/−1.74 vs ERA5+residual 2.319/−1.62 (−6.7% at peak time); 54 km bin IDW 2.674/−1.93 vs 2.405/−1.73 (−10.1%); 82 km bin IDW 2.882/−2.02 vs 2.503/−1.78 (−13.2%); hourly reductions listed separately. Note that r2/r2c are random thinning resamplings, not leave-one-station-out; data consist of 10 fair-weather days with QC removing >40 kt; move the wording "synoptic gale" to the extratropical row.
2. **Inconsistent "peak" definitions** (Consensus among all three): Fair-weather wind is "prediction error at the observed daily peak time" (not error of predicted daily maximum, Line 54); H2/H3/H4 are "predicted maximum vs observed maximum within mutually valid observation times", with windows being landfall ±12 h, 12 h before and after peak, and regional gust peak ±3 h, respectively. v1.1 will add a definitions section, and require Node I to append peak definitions and windows to every record.
3. **Mixed bias criteria in the extratropical row** (E, A, D): −1.4 is the 5-event value. Lead's own calculation for strictly 4 events across 359 stations: OK fit 2.295/−1.46, ERA5+residual 2.221/−1.30; gust OK fit 2.78/−1.38. v1.1 switches to these.
4. **Hurricane row obscures high-wind areas and single-event bias** (Consensus among all three; verified): Lead's own calculation for independent 9+Francine high-wind stations (≥12 m/s, 283 station-events): OK fit 3.87/−2.59, Holland+residual fit 3.45/−0.66, ERA5+residual 3.59/−1.94; broken down by distance ( Lines 256–258): <1 RMW 56 stations interpolation 3.60/−2.02, fusion 4.25/−2.13 (fusion is worse); 1–3 RMW 239 stations 3.42/−1.68 vs 3.04/−1.03; >3 RMW 450 stations 2.24/−0.80 vs 2.21/−0.69. Single-event biases: Ida +0.82 to +0.99, Nicole +0.65, etc. v1.1 will split rows by high wind / distance, deleting the sweeping claim that "all methods systematically underestimate". Note differing event sets for all-station counts vs high-wind counts.
5. **Hurricane "needs time series" row fills hourly RMSE into the peak column** (E): v1.1 will list separately, and warn: the event maximum error of kriging time series under the peak criterion is 2.79/−1.18 (high-wind stations 3.87/−2.59), and 2.07 must not be taken as the peak error.
6. **Thunderstorm row** (Consensus among all three; verified): 44 is the number of station-events (14-station network, 10–13 stations per event); sustained wind optimal is IDW 4.78/−3.25, fixed OK 4.82/−3.46; gust listed separately as fixed OK 6.85/−5.08; gust did not undergo ERA5 fusion; window is determined by all-station observations and contains left-out station information (optimiztic).
7. **Extrapolation and point-by-point assignment** (A): Sample statistics cannot be taken as guaranteed errors for each loss location; change "errors are larger far from stations" to "unverified", citing only the 82 km bin descriptive statistics. Small sample sizes (10 fair-weather days, 4 extratropical events, 4 thunderstorm events) and the optimizm of cherry-picking based on the scoring set must be included in the qualifications.
8. **HRRR phrasing** (A, D): Change to "f01 cannot guarantee target station independence".

## For Reference Only (Adopted and Incorporated)
- A: The sustained wind averaging period in the IEM 1-minute archive was not verified field-by-field; write "approx. 2-minute running average, H4 field unverified".
- A: Water body pool includes coastal airports, not just offshore platforms; stations with no return from WorldCover have also been excluded.
- D: Hurricane gust has results (Holland+residual 3.47/+0.23, fixed OK 3.67/−0.69); add them in.

## Unadopted Objections
None. The three opinions shared a consistent direction, all verifiable against evidence documents.

## Postscript (10-14)
- Modified: The main table originally labeled ks_20180306 as "compliant", with COMBINED_STRICT at 433 stations −3.24% (reviewers may have read the old main table); now COMBINED_STRICT in both the main table and the method-by-method table reflects strictly compliant 4 events across 359 stations (2.295→2.221, −3.23%, 207/359), and the 433-station row has been renamed "five-event historical basis (including 1 non-compliant event)". Protocol v1 marked as obsolete; extratropical numbers in v1.2 and the project page have been verified and are consistent.

# 良态大风日筛选 r1

区域：TX_ASOS 公开站点，经纬度 28–34°N、94–100°W，2020-11-01 前已开始归档，共 145 个候选站；每个 UTC 小时取距整点最近的 METAR（±30 分钟），风速 knots × 0.5144444444444445 m/s。[1]

预定筛选：2020-11-01 至 2021-03-31 的 UTC 日；区域内至少 60 站有有效观测；该日区域全部 METAR 的小时样本中风速 ≥8 m/s 比例 ≥10%；该日区域 METAR 主体（不含 RMK）不得出现 TS、VCTS 或云层 CB；该日 NOAA Storm Events 的整个 TEXAS 州不得有 Thunderstorm Wind 记录（保守排除，日期按 Storm Events 原表地方日期，无 UTC 转换）。满足者正好 10 天，全部纳入；无事后挑日。[1][2]

| 日期 UTC | 有数据站数 | 有效小时样本 | ≥8 m/s 比例 |

# Submission Evidence Package: H Observation–Simulation Fusion Reconstruction of Near-Surface Wind—Literature Conclusions + r1 Interpretation (10-14)

## Conclusions Pending Review (Planned for project page, potentially for citation by Node I and subsequent formal projects)
C1. Under testing against actual measurements at real observations and held-out stations (or whole withheld regions), the RMSE reduction of learning/fusion methods in the verified literature relative to the best pure interpolation (Kriging/IDW/Barnes) is in the single digits to approx. 15%: Kiessling 2021 Sweden approx. 5% (unexplained variance 0.370 vs 0.388, random 5-fold); S2G (Baki 2026) held-out stations against actual measurements only reports "centered RMSE reduction", formal version 8.5% (not personally verified); KiloDA (Zheng 2026, arXiv 2609.11230v1) in Shanxi complex terrain with a whole withheld block of 238/1,340 stations, is −15.4% better than Kriging, with 89.5% of stations improved, with the largest gain in high-relief areas.
C2. The 25–54% reductions commonly seen in the literature come from "non-independent ground truth" designs: WRF twin idealized experiments (KiloDA 49%), or grid field comparisons using RTMA (assimilated from the same set of stations) as ground truth (S2G 25–32%); these cannot be treated as gains against actual measurements.
C3. HRRR f00 assimilates METAR 10 m wind; f01 is still affected by cycling assimilation; RTMA has no network-wide leave-one-out error (only airport withholding in Morris 2020). Therefore, leave-one-out tests using HRRR/RTMA as background are on the optimiztic side.
C4. In this track's r1 (137 ASOS stations in central-eastern Texas, average nearest station distance mostly 25–50 km, 10 well-behaved high-wind days, station-by-station leave-one-out): ERA5+residual Kriging is −3.8% relative to ordinary Kriging (81/137 stations), best GBT+residual is −5.5% (87/137); nearest station >50 km subset is −17% (ERA5+residual) / −24% (GBT+residual). Consistent with C1: gains are small under normal station network density, and large where stations are sparse or terrain is complex. Judged as "interpolation is sufficient" (criteria pre-specified in writing: ≥20% and ≥2/3 of stations to be worth continuing).
C5. Next step is to test only on sparse station networks (r2 thinning to 50/25/10%), same criteria as above, ERA5 background, no HRRR features.

## Evidence
- Item-by-item verification between Grok report and Lead: 
- KiloDA PDF original text verification passage (Fig. 5 paragraph): see above file; arXiv 2609.11230v1
- S2G author preprint:  (Fig. 8 caption, Fig. 12 caption, lines 601–604 of main text)
- r1 results: , Lead review 
- Criteria and design: , 

## Limitations (Self-reported)
Deep Research step two was not conducted due to quota; only 4 real observation comparison papers were verified in the literature, which may miss strong evidence under sparse-station/typhoon scenarios; S2G 8.5% is single-source; whether ERA5 land 10 m wind assimilates surface stations was unverified; r1 covers only 10 days, only mean wind, and Kriging parameters were not tuned.

# H r2: Sparse Network Wind Speed Reconstruction (UTC; Independent New Results)

## Criteria and Conclusions
A priori criteria: For sparse tiers with an average nearest input station distance of ≥50 km, the best ERA5 fusion/learning method must achieve at least a 20% reduction in RMSE relative to the best pure interpolation and improve at ≥2/3 of verification stations to be judged as "worthwhile in sparse areas"; 10–20% is judged as "conditional"; <10% is judged as "interpolation is sufficient". For the sparsest 10% tier: 14 input stations, 122 verification stations/run; average nearest distance 81.82 km, pure interpolation IDW RMSE 1.948, ERA5 + residual OK 1.687 m/s, a reduction of 13.40%, with station-by-station improvement at 126/136 stations aggregated across 20 resamplings. Hence, it is judged as "conditional", rather than "worthwhile in sparse areas". Although the 25% tier also reached 50 km, the gain was only 8.84%, indicating that the conclusion depends on the degree of sparsity; the status of ERA5 station assimilation remains to be verified, and it is not a strictly independent background verification.

## Input and Evaluation Scope
Fully reuse observations_qc2.csv.gz, the 10 selected UTC dates, and the daily ERA5 CSVs from r1; no new data was fetched. After removing BSM, which duplicates AUS, there are 136 stations with actual hourly observations; for each tier, with a fixed seed of 314159, 20 random station resamplings were performed, with 68/34/14 input stations. Each run trains/fits only on observations from input stations; observations from verification stations across all periods never entered fitting or variograms. Valid observation stations each hour vary with reports; average distance is calculated using the valid input stations at the actual station-hour being scored. METAR sustained/average wind speed (ASOS is typically a 2-minute average), not gusts or whole-hour averages; time is aligned to UTC. All methods are scored on the same verification station-hours within the same tier; resampled station-hours are not independent new observations.

## Parameter Sources and Default Assumptions
| Parameter | Value, Source, and Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Wind, dates, ERA5 | Original r1 and ; IEM METAR hourly sustained wind, ARCO-ERA5 10 m u/v station interpolation. The original QC2 >40 kt exclusion rule is an r1 assumption. Whether ERA5 assimilates land surface stations: to be verified. |
| Station thinning | Assumption: 136 stations (removing BSM, keeping AUS), fixed seed 314159, non-stratified random sampling 20 times/tier, round(ratio × stations), each tier tests only non-input stations. |
| IDW | Assumption, inherited from r1 inverse distance squared on spherical distance. |
| OK Fixed | Assumption, inherited from r1 exponential covariance 75 km, relative nugget 0.08, constant unknown mean; uses only input stations for that hour. |
| OK Hourly Fit | Assumption: Bin pairwise half-squared differences of wind speeds at input stations for the current hour by 25 km, up to 300 km; ≥4 pairs/bin, at least 3 bins; empirical semivariogram fitted to sill × (1.08 − exp(−h/r)), sill takes the variance of input stations for that hour, r constrained to 20–300 km, falls back to 75 km if bins are insufficient; nugget fixed at 0.08. All parameters determined by input stations, median range 92.490 km, 146 network-hours fell back. |
| Background + Residual | ERA5 direct interpolation or ERA5 + 75 km residual OK after subtracting ERA5 from input station observations. |
| GBT | Assumption following r1: 80 trees, 12 leaves, learning rate 0.06, L2=5; features ERA5 u/v, elevation (missing values replaced with median of this dataset), latitude/longitude, UTC hour sin/cos; no HRRR. Trained only on input stations across all selected days. |
| GBT + Residual | Assumption: Fixed random 2-fold split of input stations, two models each trained on the other half of stations to form strictly station-held-out cross-fitted residuals for each input station; verification stations are predicted by GBT trained on all input stations, plus 75 km residual OK. |
| Underlying Surface | Reused ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 already retrieved in r1; majority class 50 within 1 km around stations is built-up, the rest non-built-up; representativeness for 2020 has a time lag. |

## Limitations and Reproducibility
Repeated station splits are on the same 10-day meteorological field, not independent tests across years; resampled station-hours were not treated as independent samples to report significance. Some of the 136 stations are only valid for short periods; the station-by-station win counts across 20 evaluations were aggregated using all errors whenever that station was sampled as a verification station. Hourly empirical variograms are unstable with small sample sizes; fixed nugget/sill and range bounds are assumptions rather than literature-derived; topography, airport exposure, and model/station representativeness errors are confounded. The ERA5 assimilation status for surface stations remains to be verified by the Lead and cannot be claimed as independent and uninformed. Pure station thinning does not simulate the spatial correlation choices of network deployment, and extreme stationless areas were not verified against gridded ground truth.
Data sources: Iowa Environmental Mesonet/Iowa State University archived METAR and TX_ASOS metadata; Hersbach et al. (2020) ERA5, DOI 10.1002/qj.3803, via Google Research ARCO-ERA5; ESA WorldCover Consortium (2022), DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7254221. All have been registered in lines 130–133, 148–149; no new external data/code was added in this round. Figure marks the sources of observations and ERA5; scripts , .

## One-Line Criterion
In the 10% input station tier with a nearest distance of 81.82 km, ERA5 + residual OK had a 13.40% lower RMSE than the best pure interpolation, improving at 126/136 stations, judged as "conditional" according to the a priori criteria; the 25% tier only decreased by 8.84%, and it cannot be generalized that sparse areas are worthwhile.

results.title: H r1 Lead verification (10-14)
results.text:
# H r1 Lead Review (10-14)
Self-calculated using `predictions_r1_clean.csv.gz` (anaconda python), consistent with results_r1.md: OK 1.613, IDW 1.634, GBT + residual OK 1.524 (−5.5%, 87/137 stations).
- Primary criteria group (using only ERA5 background, excluding HRRR, see WRF Lead reminder): ERA5 + residual OK 1.553, −3.8%, 81/137 stations → interpolation is sufficient. HRRR + residual OK −1.2%, 57/137.
- AUS and BSM are about 1.5 km apart (two codes for the same airport), OK errors 0.44/0.50 are on the lower side; after removing both stations: ERA + residual −3.8% (79/135), GBT + residual −5.5% (86/135), conclusion unchanged.
- Variogram is fixed at 75 km, unfitted: will only make kriging weaker; after improvement, the gain will only be smaller, and the direction of the conclusion remains unchanged.
- Station distance grouping (ERA + residual / GBT + residual vs. OK): <25 km 1.534/1.568 vs. 1.550; 25–50 km 1.530/1.473 vs. 1.569; >50 km (2,459 station-hours, 35 stations) 1.781/1.625 vs. 2.142, i.e., −17% / −24%. Direction is consistent with KiloDA (whole held-out block −15.4%): the gains of fusion are concentrated where stations are sparse.
- All methods underestimate at daily peak hours for each station (GBT + residual bias −1.52 m/s): this is a critical specification issue for I (loss–wind speed library).
- Incomplete: Underlying surface grouping (supplementary message not implemented); GBT used HRRR features.

## Correction (After Review Verdict, 10-14)
- The above ">50 km −17% / −24%" is invalidated: the >50 km subset contains offshore platform BQX (Brazos 451). After removal, ERA5 + residual vs. OK is −8.9% (2,244 station-hours, 34 stations, Lead self-calculation). −24% (GBT) contains HRRR features and in-training residuals, not cited.
- The above statement "'variogram tuning will only make the gains smaller' has no basis, deleted"; E recalculated optimal variogram parameters on both sides to be −4.34%, still <10%.
- Duplicate/suspicious stations are not limited to AUS/BSM: CVB/T89, F12/RFI have identical coordinates. After removing BQX/T89/BSM, full-sample OK is 1.577, ERA5 + residual is 1.537, −2.5% (Lead self-calculation), conclusion unchanged.

| KiloDA no code | Original text Code availability: "available … upon reasonable request during peer review and will be made publicly available … upon publication" | Verified true (no public code at present) |
| Kiessling 2021 (Proc. R. Soc. A, 10.1098/rspa.2021.0236) RFF E=0.370 vs Universal Kriging 0.388 vs IDW 0.407 | PMC full text Table 1 is verified true; verification is hourly random 5-fold cross-validation, not fixed held-out stations; code bitbucket.org/the_eye_of_the_breeze/div-fourier-publication | Adopted: Swedish station network, ML is only about 5% better than universal kriging (in terms of unexplained variance) |
| Baki 2026 S2G (AIES, 10.1175/AIES-D-25-0111.1) U-Net 28–32% lower than Barnes | AMS page 403, unverified | **Unverified, not adopted**, handed over to Deep Research Step 2 |
| "Lee et al. 2022" hurricane XGBoost reconstruction (WAF-D-21-0077.1) | Crossref first author is Yang | Author mistaken, to be verified |
| "Fusion/ML is generally 15–50% lower than pure interpolation" | Synthesis sentence, no single source; upper bound comes from ideal experiments | Not adopted |

**Implications for this node**: In the two verified pieces of real-station evidence, learning methods are 5% (Sweden) to 15% (Shanxi complex terrain, whole held-out block) lower than the best kriging; central-eastern Texas has flat terrain, where gains are expected to be even smaller. Node H r1's ≥20% criterion remains unchanged (written a priori), but this serves as a benchmark when reading results.

## Reviewer F (Grok) Verification Results and Lead Review (10-14)
| Item | F's Conclusion and Excerpts | Lead Review | Adopted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S2G (Baki 2026) held-out stations | Fig. 12 "All results are computed at held-out stations using out-of-fold predictions"; main text "only a modest reduction (from 1.790 to 1.637 m s−1 or 8.5%)" (centered RMSE, vs. Barnes); 32.1%, 17.6% are for all stations against RTMA grids, not held-out stations; target is maximum 3 s gust within 10 min, training target comes from RTMA | AMS full text returned 403 to us, unable to open personally; awaiting independent verification by Reviewer E | Tentatively marked "pending cross-validation"; if E agrees, adopt: held-out station U-Net is only 8.5% better than Barnes (centered RMSE) |
| Whether HRRR f00 assimilates METAR 10 m wind | Benjamin 2016 MWR 144 Table 4 and p. 1674; Dowell 2022 WAF 37 p. 1372 | Local literature Collins et al. 2024 WAF (Zotero PU6IMCA9) PDF page 5 (journal page 709) Figure 2 caption "MADIS sites utilized for the HRRR analysis", direction consistent | Adopted: f00 assimilates surface station wind; f01 remains influenced by cyclic assimilation (r1 already marked "used upstream") |
| RTMA 10 m wind held-out station error | Only Morris 2020 WAF 35 p. 990 Part 139 airport exclusion: CONUS NODA RMSE ≤4 kt, ~1 kt higher after exclusion; no network-wide leave-one-out; URMA not found | Not personally verified | For reference only |
| WAF-D-21-0077.1 authors | Yang, Lee, Tippett, Chavas, Knutson; 7 storms held out, metric MSESS | Consistent with Crossref first author | Adopted (corrects Grok report "Lee et al.") |

Additionally: Local library contains Gunter & Long 2024 (West Texas Mesonet deep convective wind gust climatology, Zotero C9KMEQUR), usable later for thunderstorm phase or independent dense network validation.

## Reviewer E (Gemini) and Lead Review of S2G (10-14)
E downloaded author preprint v3: . Lead personally verified using pdftotext:
- The "held-out stations 29.6% (93 stations) / 25.0% (62 stations)" reported by E comes from Fig. 8 (preprint PDF text near line 920, figure caption): "Performance of deep learning models relative to Barnes interpolation … Colors show improvement in (a) RMSE, (b) PSNR, and (c) SSIM"—this is an image metric of the **entire gridded field against the RTMA target field**, merely removing some stations during inference; the ground truth is RTMA (the training target, itself assimilated from these stations), **not against actual observations at held-out stations**. E describing it as "held-out station verification" is inaccurate.
- The only true "held-out stations against observations" is Fig. 12: caption "Statistical evaluation of interpolation performance at held-out NYSM stations … All results are computed at held-out stations using out-of-fold predictions"; preprint main text (PDF text lines 601–604) only states "reduced centered RMSE compared to Barnes", **with no percentage**. The "from 1.790 to 1.637 m s−1 or 8.5%" cited by F comes from the official AMS version, which the Lead cannot open (403); the preprint lacks this sentence.
- Number of stations and setup are consistent between E and F: 124 used out of 126 stations, average station distance ~27 km (preprint p. 11); 4 groups × 31 stations, 93-station inference with 4 folds where each station is held out exactly once, 62-station inference with 6 folds.

**Adopted standard**: S2G is 25–32% lower than Barnes against the RTMA gridded field (ground truth is not independent); against actual observations at held-out stations, there is only a "reduction in centered RMSE", with the official version giving 8.5% (single source F, not personally verified, marked "to be verified").

## Corrections After Review (10-14)
- Kiessling 2021: 0.370 vs. 0.388 is unexplained variance (MSE dimension), equivalent to ~2.3% in RMSE; optimal FF+RF in Table 1 averages 0.357, equivalent to ~4.1% in RMSE.
- S2G official version "from 1.790 to 1.637 m s−1 or 8.5%" (centered RMSE, held-out stations, vs. Barnes) verified by Reviewers D and A, "to be verified" status revoked; official version states bias reduction is the primary contribution, and total RMSE reduction may be larger. Preprint writes station distance as ~30 km, gusts as 3 s maximum within a 5-minute window (earlier "27 km" "10 min" corrected according to preprint).
- KiloDA: −15.4% is the station-by-station RMSE median; held-out block selected by ERA5 maximum error cluster; strongest 5% wind speed tier is slightly worse than ERA5 (D verified original text). The ideal experiment is an independent test in a simulated world, not leakage.
- ERA5: Hersbach 2020 does not assimilate land 10 m wind (all three reviewers agree).
- RTMA: Operational system has 10% random held-out cross-validation (EMC v2.2 overview, D single source, not personally verified); "no network-wide leave-one-out" changed to "no published network-wide leave-one-out error retrieved". Morris 2020's NODA is the background field.

# H2 Landfalling Hurricane Hourly METAR Station Leave-One-Out Reconstruction

Specifications: BERYL 2024, NICHOLAS 2021, NHC landfall ±12 h, all dates and times in UTC. Inputs are hourly METAR 2-min average sustained wind (sknt) from Iowa Environmental Mesonet (IEM); gust is listed separately and only compared against gust. Holland uses CLIMADA v6.1.0 H08 frozen at Node B + Natural Earth inflow land-sea mask + ~2-min factor of 0.97, without refitting model coefficients; ERA5 is the magnitude of ARCO-ERA5 10 m U/V.

Sources: NHC HURDAT2, ATCF b-deck, IEM TX_ASOS/hourly METAR, Google Research ARCO-ERA5, CLIMADA v6.1.0, Natural Earth; for detailed versions and links, see the H2 entry in , as well as this directory. Node B originals are read-only. Figure captions indicate sources.

## Prior Criteria and Conclusions

Primarily based on the RMSE of the maximum observed hourly sustained wind per station during the event; method predictions are evaluated against the observed maximum over the same hours where observations exist for that station. "Fusion is worthwhile in hurricane scenarios" is judged only if the best background + residual reduces RMSE by at least 20% compared to the better of IDW/OK and reduces peak absolute error for at least 2/3 of stations; 10–20% or meeting only one criterion is "conditional"; <10% is "interpolation is sufficient". All findings from this experiment follow these criteria, with no threshold adjustments based on results.

BERYL: 115 qualified stations, 22 unqualified stations; OK 3.377 → H08 Holland+residual OK 2.773 m/s, reduction of 17.89%, station-by-station improvement 56/115 (48.7%); conditional.
NICHOLAS: 86 qualified stations, 11 unqualified stations; OK 2.874 → H08 Holland+residual OK 1.965 m/s, reduction of 31.63%, station-by-station improvement 49/86 (57.0%); conditional.
COMBINED: 201 qualified stations, 33 unqualified stations; OK 3.172 → H08 Holland+residual OK 2.460 m/s, reduction of 22.44%, station-by-station improvement 105/201 (52.2%); conditional.

## Method Comparison

Both peak and hourly columns are RMSE / bias / MAE, in m/s; peak sample size is by station, and hourly sample size is by observed hours.

Peak error is predicted peak minus observed peak. The station assimilation specifications of ERA5 remain to be verified; the leave-one-out of ERA5+residual cannot be claimed to be completely free of station information. Holland itself did not use METAR from current validation stations for parameter tuning, but NHC post-analysis best track, intensity, and b-deck are post-event data rather than real-time forecasts; results must not be extrapolated as future forecasting skill.

## Peak Gust (Independent Scoring)

ERA5 10 m mean wind is not directly converted to gusts; only IDW, OK, Holland, and their residual methods are listed here. The gust factor for H08 is a frozen assumption from Node B, not a fitted value from gust observations.

## Distance to Center / RMW Grouping

Grouping is based on the distance from the left-out station to the NHC center at the hour corresponding to its observed sustained wind peak, divided by the linearly interpolated b-deck RMW at that hour. The two columns are peak RMSE / bias (m/s) for the best pure interpolation and best fusion for each event; groups with very small sample sizes are only described without drawing conclusions.

## Missing / Outage Stations

Selected stations are those covered by the TX_ASOS archive during the event and ≤300 km from any node of the ±12h track; "unqualified" does not equate to confirmed outage, but includes cases where the archive covers the event but hourly reports are missing, METAR numerical QC failures, <18/24 sustained wind hours within the time window, or no sustained wind report within ±2h of the station peak time predicted by the frozen H08. To prevent missing reports from obscuring peak values, unqualified stations do not participate in the above primary scoring; the table below provides station-by-station details.

## Parameter Source Table

| Parameter | Value / Rule | Nature of Source and Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Events and time windows | Beryl 2024 / Nicholas 2021, NHC landfall ±12 h, hours aligned to UTC | Project brief preset; HURDAT2 landfall times from read-only Node B |
| Station network | TX_ASOS, archive date covers event, ≤300 km from any point on NHC track within event window | Project brief preset; HAS1MIN was not enforced, because this time it is hourly METAR |
| Mean wind and gust | IEM `sknt`, `gust` knot × 0.514444 m/s | IEM fields; 2-min average wind only for sustained wind, not replaced by gust, physical conversion constant |
| Hourly deduplication | METAR timestamps rounded to nearest hour, selecting the report closest to the hour; `report_type=3,4` | Followed H r1 script rules; only one report retained per hour |
| Numerical QC | sknt 0–120 kt, gust 0–150 kt; if gust < sknt within the same report, that gust is excluded | Assumption: broad upper bounds only remove obvious outliers, not official NCEI QC thresholds |
| Outage threshold | At least 18 valid sustained wind hours in 24h, and at least one report within ±2h of H08 model peak time | Assumption: avoid obviously truncated peaks; threshold is affected by model peak time errors; stations with no reports are not counted as 0 |
| H08 wind field | Original from Node B; this station does not adjust 0.97, land-sea/gust coefficients; Node B preregistration describes its empirical assumptions and limitations |
| ERA5 | ARCO public Zarr, 10 m U/V interpolated to stations, hourly magnitudes | H r1 background loading code; whether station assimilation is independent remains to be verified |
| IDW | Inverse distance squared, available stations in the same hour, excluding the left-out station | Assumption; followed H r1 fixed power of 2 |
| Ordinary Kriging | Fixed hourly exponential covariance exp(−d/75km), diagonal nugget 0.08, constant unknown mean | Assumption; followed H r1 fixed version. Empirical variogram not fitted for the event; same weights used for sustained wind and its background residuals |
| Peak comparison | Predicted maximum over hours with observations during the event per station vs. observed maximum over that period; hourly only for valid observation hours of that station | Assumption: guarantees common observable window; event peaks genuinely missing due to outages are not verified |
| Grouping | Distance from left-out station to NHC center at observed peak time / b-deck RMW at the same time | Project brief preset; RMW linear interpolation follows Node B code |

## Known Limitations

1. Biased sample of qualified stations around Texas airports across two events; missing data is not random, and true peak values of outage stations in hard-hit areas may be higher. "Conditional" cannot be treated as proven wind field reconstruction capability in the landfall core area.
2. Hourly METAR (one report per station per hour) misses minute-level extremes between two reports; the event peak duration is the "maximum hourly mean wind" within the window, not the true 1-min peak, nor is it a gust.
3. Node B's wind field is post-analysis best track and simplified land-sea exposure, not a real-time forecast; ERA5 is also a post-analysis reanalysis and whether it contains information from held-out stations remains to be verified.
4. The fixed variogram was not fitted on an hourly basis; residuals within the same hour may contain local extremes from neighboring stations, and Holland+residual hourly RMSE is worse than ERA5+residual; peak gains must not be misunderstood as outperforming across all time periods.
5. Storm center distance grouping is defined at the observed peak time, which does not represent that the peak time coincided with NHC landfall, nor does it include stations in other states; single-station leave-one-out can leave stations at the same airport / nearby stations on the training side, and group isolation by airport cluster has not yet been performed.

## Reproducible Files

 completes downloads, Node B wind fields, LOO, JSON, and figures in one go;  generates this report from JSON. `grid_*_h2.csv.gz` contains background, observations, and distances; `predictions_h2.csv.gz` contains hourly station-by-station predictions;  is the original peak evaluation table;  contains station-by-station outage candidates. Figure  sources: IEM / NHC HURDAT2 / ATCF / ARCO-ERA5 / CLIMADA H08.
