# H r2-clean: Sparse Network Recalculation After Station Cleaning (UTC)

This report is recalculated according to the review  verdict; all source files are read-only, and results use new r2c filenames rather than overwriting original r2. Observations are sustained wind speeds (typically 2-minute average) from IEM METAR hourly reports, not whole-hour means or gusts; background is ARCO-ERA5 10 m u/v. Uses only the 10 established UTC days from r1, QC2 observations (exclusion of >40 kt is an r1 assumption), and the ERA5 cache.

## Prior Criteria and Results
In each tier with average actual nearest input station distance ≥50 km, if the best ERA5 fusion/learning reduces RMSE by ≥20% relative to the best IDW/OK and ≥2/3 of evaluated stations are better → "worthwhile in sparse areas"; 10–20% or meeting only one threshold → "conditional"; <10% → "interpolation is sufficient" (tiered with reduction prioritized). Pure interpolation and fusion each select the optimum within their own tier; the weaker of the two variogram versions is not taken as the baseline.

| Input Tier | Actual Nearest Input Station Distance That Hour km (station-hour weighted; resampling mean±SD) | Best Pure Interpolation RMSE m/s | Best Fusion RMSE m/s | Reduction | Improved Stations | Verdict |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 50% | 40.27 (40.27±2.43) | 1.659 (OK hourly fitted) | 1.556 (ERA5+residual OK hourly fitted) | 6.22% | 98/134 | Interpolation is sufficient |
| 25% | 54.11 (54.11±3.26) | 1.762 (IDW p=2) | 1.597 (ERA5+residual OK hourly fitted) | 9.36% | 106/134 | Interpolation is sufficient |
| 10% | 82.45 (82.44±7.25) | 1.901 (IDW p=2) | 1.664 (ERA5+residual OK hourly fitted) | 12.47% | 124/134 | Conditional |

The 25% and 10% tiers are judged separately, and the 50% tier is also shown as a reference. Across the 20 resamplings, RMSE is computed by pooling the squared errors of all evaluated station-hours in that tier and taking the square root, rather than the arithmetic mean of 20 RMSEs; each station pools its errors only across repetitions where it was sampled as an evaluation station, and the station-by-station RMSEs of the best methods are then compared, with one vote per station. Station-hours and repetitions share the same weather and are not treated as independent samples. The nearest station distance is calculated for each scoring hour using input stations that actually had observations at that time, rather than the nominal station list.

## r1 All-Station Leave-One-Out Cleaned Version
Compares only the fixed 75 km OK and fixed 75 km ERA5+residual OK from the original r1; for each hour, an augmented ordinary kriging matrix is constructed, and analytical LOO strictly excludes observations from the target station; all anomalous stations are removed before matrix construction.

## Cleaning Rules and Removal List
First, remove BQX (Brazos 451, offshore platform) and GVW (Galveston 209B, offshore platform), where WorldCover 1 km surrounding the station has dominant class 80 (water body); remove T89, which has identical coordinates to CVB and suspicious coordinates. Then, for all pairs of stations with pairwise spherical distance <2 km, keep only one station: AUS/BSM (1.600 km; identical valid station-hours, keep major airport AUS), F12/RFI (0 km, F12 has no valid observations in this batch, keep RFI), 5R3/RYW (0.446 km, 5R3 has no valid observations in this batch, keep RYW), CVB/T89 (0 km, T89 already removed due to being suspicious, keep CVB). Retained stations recompute all random samplings, input/evaluation, training, and variogram fitting; removed stations were strictly never used as input or for scoring; passed the assertion that the minimum distance between stations after cleaning is ≥2 km.

## Parameter Source Table
| Parameter | Source / Nature |
| --- | --- |
| Observations, dates, ERA5 | Followed r1 , local QC2/ERA5 files; METAR hourly sampled sustained wind, UTC. ERA5 land 10m wind does not directly assimilate these stations (see review verdict), but this still does not mean all upstream information is completely independent. |
| Removal rules | Review 2598bcfe verdict: water body dominant class, suspicious identical coordinates, <2 km deduplication; those with more valid observations prioritized, AUS prioritized when tied. |
| Station network | Assumptions followed r2: random seed 314159, 20 runs per tier, no geographic stratification, input ratios 50/25/10%, rounded using Python round. |
| IDW | Assumptions followed r1/r2, inverse square of spherical distance. |
| Fixed OK | Assumptions followed r1/r2: exponential covariance 75 km, relative nugget = 0.08, unknown constant mean. |
| Hourly fitted OK | Assumptions followed r2: pairwise semivariance of input stations in that hour, 25 km distance bins, up to 300 km; ≥4 pairs per bin and ≥3 bins, fixing that hour's input station variance as the sill, fitting exp range 20–300 km, falling back to 75 km if insufficient; pure interpolation fits raw observations, fusion fits residuals of observations minus ERA5. Raw field fallback 128 times, median range 93.1 km; residual fallback 128 times, median range 36.9 km. |
| GBT and cross-fitting | Followed r2 assumptions: 80 iterations, 12 leaves, learning rate .06, L2 = 5, features ERA5 u/v, elevation, latitude/longitude, UTC hour sin/cos; residuals strictly 2-fold cross-fitted on input stations; no HRRR. |
| Underlying surface | Reused r1 ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 1 km dominant class around stations; 50 built-up, remaining non-built-up; 2020 dates not completely contemporaneous with imagery year. |

## Limitations and Files
10 selected well-behaved wind days from 2020–21, a single random seed, same stations repeatedly evaluated; "improved stations" are not independent new stations. Empirical variogram range and residual applicability are not literature-recommended values, without nested parameter tuning; station representativeness errors may still exist. Although the ERA5 background does not directly assimilate land 10m wind, it may still be indirectly affected by the assimilation system. Gusts, loss points, or gridded ground truth were not validated.
Sources: IEM METAR, Hersbach et al. 2020 ERA5 DOI 10.1002/qj.3803, ESA WorldCover Consortium 2022 DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7254221, all listed in ; no new external data was added in this round. Scripts , ; Figure .

## Conclusion
25% tier: Interpolation is sufficient; 10% tier: Conditional. Applies only to this cleaned station network and sustained wind leave-one-out station evaluation.

# H2 Recalculation After Station Cleaning (Ten Events + Beryl Listed Separately)

2026-10-14; UTC throughout. Original H2/B node files are read-only, and all results use `_clean_h2d_h2d` as the new version; frozen Holland v1 (a) chain coefficients were not changed. The ten-event combined total does not include Beryl. This cleaning supplement does not modify the prior criteria.

## Cleaning and Scoring Boundaries

Starting from the complete candidate station list of each event, spatial cleaning was performed independently of missing reports and scoring eligibility: normalize state-prefix-free TX station IDs for Beryl/Nicholas; suspect-coordinate TX:T89 was excluded (identical to TX:CVB); for connected neighbors <2 km, each group retains the one with the most valid observation hours across all events (ties broken by station ID lexicographical order). Excluded stations do not exist in inputs, fitting, or testing across all hours. Stations with dominant water class or names indicating offshore platforms were placed in a separate pool, and strictly do not participate in IDW, OK, residual fitting, or evaluation for land stations; stations with no WorldCover returns were conservatively excluded.  gives status and reason for each station, and  gives distance.

The water body pool refers to "WorldCover within 1 km perimeter is predominantly water or name indicates offshore", which does not equate to all stations being genuine offshore platforms: for example, SPG/TPF/EYW are coastal airports, and were also separated from the land pool according to the predefined water body criteria. This grouping is not a certification of instrument exposure conditions.

Sustained wind uses only IEM METAR sknt, and gust uses only gust; 12 h before and after event landfall, hourly nearest top of the hour ±30 min. Retain at least 75% valid hours and at least one valid report within ±2 h of the H08 station model peak; predicted peak and observed peak are restricted to the same observed timestamp. Uncovered true extremes are unverifiable.

## Prior Criteria and Results

Across each evaluable event (uncensored and ≥8 stations) and the ten-event combined total, the best background + residual relative to the best IDW / fixed or fitted OK: peak RMSE lower by ≥20% and ≥2/3 stations having smaller peak absolute error is "Worthwhile"; 10–20% or meeting only one of these is "Conditional"; <10% is "Interpolation sufficient". If "only meeting the winning station condition but RMSE <10%", it is still listed as conditional per the original criteria. Determined only in the land pool, with Beryl listed separately.

## Exclusion and Missing Report List

## Parameter Sources Table
| Parameter | Value/Rule | Nature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Events/Fields | B v1 same-batch ten events + Beryl addition; B `chain_a_v1.pygrid_*` | Task specification / existing B artifact; post-analysis track is not a real-time forecast |
| Water Bodies and Neighbors | Dominant class 80 within ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 1 km circle is water, or IEM station name indicates offshore; distance <2 km deduplication; collocated T89 excluded | WorldCover/IEM attributes; threshold and priority retention hours rules are assumptions, per review |
| Missing Reports and Hours | At least 75% valid hours and report present within ±2h of H08 model peak; nearest top of the hour ±30min; sknt 0–120kt, gust 0–150kt, discard if gust<sknt | Original H2 assumption; not official IEM QC |
| Fixed OK | Exponential covariance 75 km, normalized nugget .08; IDW power 2 | Original H2 assumption |
| Fitted OK | Hourly, each leave-out station training set separately fits observations or corresponding background residuals; 25 km bins up to 300 km, ≥4 pairs/bin, ≥3 bins; sill is training variance, nugget .08, exponential scale 20–300 km, fall back to 75 km if fitting is insufficient | r2c parameterization assumption, not literature constants; target station is completely excluded from fitting |
| H08 Averaging Period / Gust | 1-minute sustained wind → METAR ×0.97; marine gust ×1.20, overland ×1.30 | B explicitly states "assumption"; refer to , not values given in literature |
| Wind Field / Time | ERA5 10m u/v interpolated to stations then magnitude taken; H08 interpolated per B chain time; UTC throughout | ARCO ERA5 / B frozen chain; existing cache |

## Limitations

Station missing reports are not random during strong winds, and the true maximum may occur later than station outages; what is left out is a single station rather than an entire cluster of stations. Fitting variograms uses observations from that hour excluding each leave-out station, without selecting parameters using the leave-out station; however, the final "best method" is selected post-hoc on the evaluation data, so gains carry an optimiztic bias. Dominant water class carries the possibility of misclassifying coastal airports as offshore platforms; here they are isolated according to task rules without claiming that instruments are at sea. Stations with unknown land cover classes are conservatively excluded. NHC post-analysis tracks and b-deck information cannot be regarded as forecast accuracy. Figures and tables are sourced from IEM METAR, Google ARCO ERA5, ESA WorldCover, NHC HURDAT2/ATCF, CLIMADA H08/B v1; new data only re-reads WorldCover and public metadata already used by IEM, for citations see  existing corresponding sources.

# Recalculation after H2 Station Cleaning (Ten Events + Beryl Listed Separately)

2026-10-14; UTC throughout. Original H2/B node files are read-only; all results take `_clean_h2d_h2d` as the new version; frozen Holland v1 (a) chain coefficients were not changed. The ten-event combined total does not include Beryl. This cleaning supplement does not modify prior criteria.

## Cleaning and Scoring Boundaries

Starting from the complete candidate station list per event, spatial cleaning was performed independently of missing reports and scoring eligibility: normalize non-state-prefixed TX station IDs for Beryl/Nicholas; suspect coordinates TX:T89 excluded (identical to TX:CVB); for connected neighbors <2 km, each group retains the station with the most valid observation hours across all events (ties broken alphabetically by station ID). Excluded stations do not exist in inputs, fitting, or testing for any hour. Stations with dominant water class or names indicating offshore platforms were placed in a separate pool and never participate in IDW, OK, residual fitting, or evaluation for land stations; stations with no return from WorldCover were conservatively excluded.  gives status and reason for each station,  gives distance.

The water pool refers to "dominant WorldCover water within 1 km or name indicating offshore", which does not equate to all stations being true offshore platforms: for example, SPG/TPF/EYW are coastal airports, which were also separated from the land pool according to the predefined water conditions. This grouping is not a certification of instrument exposure conditions.

Sustained wind uses only IEM METAR sknt, and gusts use only gust; 12 h before and after event landfall, hours rounded to the nearest clock hour ±30 min. Retain at least 75% valid hours and at least one valid report within ±2 h of the H08 station model peak; predicted peak and observed peak are restricted to the same observed time. Uncovered true extremes are unverifiable.

## Prior Criteria and Results

Across each scorable event (uncensored and ≥8 stations) and the ten-event combined total, the best background + residual relative to the best IDW / fixed or fitted OK: peak RMSE lower by ≥20% and ≥2/3 of stations having smaller peak absolute error is "Worthy"; 10–20% or meeting only one of these is "Conditional"; <10% is "Interpolation Sufficient". If "only meeting the winning station condition but RMSE <10%", it is still categorized as Conditional according to the original criteria. Evaluated only in the land pool, with Beryl listed separately.

## Limitations

Station missing reports are not random in strong winds; true maximums may occur after reporting stations go offline; what is held out is a single station rather than an entire cluster of stations. The fitted variogram uses current-hour observations excluding each held-out station, without using the held-out station to select parameters; however, the final "best method" is selected ex post on the scored data, which carries an optimiztic bias in the gains. Dominant water class has the possibility of misclassifying coastal airports as offshore platforms; here they are isolated according to task rules without claiming instruments are at sea. Stations with unknown land cover types are conservatively excluded. NHC post-event tracks and b-deck information cannot be regarded as forecast accuracy. # H2b High-Wind Station Secondary Criterion Pre-Registration

2026-10-14. Frozen prior to executing high-wind subset statistics: continues to use H2d cleaned land stations, coverage conditions, LOO predictions, and peak definitions; does not change the primary criterion. The independent validation set consists of the other nine events in B v1 ten events excluding NICHOLAS (DELTA, ZETA, IDA, IAN, NICOLE, IDALIA, DEBBY, HELENE, MILTON); BERYL also does not enter independent validation. For each event, qualified land stations with measured event peak sustained wind ≥12 m/s constitute the high-wind subset; fewer than 8 stations is listed as unassessable and not merged into assessable event combined totals. In addition, descriptive combined totals for high-wind stations across all nine events are provided to display sample coverage.

For each subset, the best of IDW/OK fixed/OK fitted and the best of ERA5 + residual fixed/fitted, H08 + residual fixed/fitted are selected by peak RMSE respectively, calculating the RMSE reduction 1 − fusion/baseline and the number of winning stations where station-by-station absolute error strictly decreases (ties do not count as wins). Reduction ≥20% and winning stations ≥2/3 is "Fusion worthwhile for high-wind stations"; reduction ≥10% or satisfying only the winning station threshold is "Conditional"; otherwise "Interpolation is sufficient". Re-report the primary criterion following the same logic. Post-hoc selection of the minimum RMSE method within each subset carries optimiztic bias; no hyperparameter tuning based on results. Primary/secondary criteria for Beryl and Nicholas are listed as "seen data, for reference only" and do not participate in independent verdicts.

Source: Lab Lead this round Supplement 3; basic data and cleaning, original files read-only; new file suffix for this round `_h2b`.

# H2b High-Wind Station Secondary Criterion: Cleaned Land Stations Ten Events

2026-10-14; UTC. The secondary criterion was written first, followed by re-stratified scoring on the existing H2d station-by-station leave-one-out peak table; no re-running or adjustment of wind fields/models. Model predictions for all ten events in H2d were generated prior to this secondary criterion, so this is an independent event test without tuning parameters on the high-wind subset, rather than a strictly prospective predictive validation. Original results are retained.

## Pre-determined Specifications

Only includes cleaned land pool, stations with original H2d coverage qualification; water bodies/platforms, duplicate, and suspicious-coordinate stations do not participate in input, fitting, or evaluation. Event peak is the maximum predicted by each method across observable hours; high wind is selected by the same station's measured maximum sustained wind ≥12 m/s; gusts do not enter this criterion. For each event, the pure interpolation with the minimum peak RMSE (IDW / OK fixed / OK fitted) is compared against background + residual (ERA5/H08, fixed/fitted OK); a station counts as a win only if its absolute error strictly decreases; at least 8 stations to be assessable. Gain ≥20% and winning stations ≥2/3 is judged as "Fusion worthwhile for high-wind stations", ≥10% or only meeting winning station threshold is judged as "Conditional", otherwise "Interpolation is sufficient". Selecting the best method on the test set carries selection optimizm.

# H3 Pre-Registration (2026-10-14, Pre-Computation)

Events: 2018–2024 US South-Central Plains TX/OK/KS/NE/AR/MO/LA/NM/CO; look for candidates with same-state, same-UTC-day High Wind reports ≥5 and Thunderstorm Wind reports 0 from NOAA Storm Events annual details. On the premise that IEM has ≥60 available stations in that state and adjacent plains states, select up to eight events on distinct days sorted by descending High Wind report count and ascending date, covering TX/OK/KS as much as possible. Report times converted to UTC (using NOAA-specified time zone offsets; DST following actual time zone rules), window centered at the hour with the maximum hourly median wind speed in the observation region ±12 h; this is an observation definition post-event selection and is not used to select methods. If thunderstorms are reported across state borders, candidates are not disqualified based on reports outside a given state within the event; their synoptic non-convective nature still requires METAR TS/CB cross-checking. Candidates failing screening and reasons are logged.

Cleaning: Suspicious station T89 with identical coordinates excluded; for <2 km connected components, retain the station with the most valid hours, breaking ties by station ID; WorldCover 1 km dominant class water bodies and clear offshore/platform pooled separately, conservatively excluded if not found in WorldCover. Excluded stations do not participate in input/fitting. IEM METAR nearest top of the hour ±30 min; sknt is sustained wind (kt converted to m/s), gust is independent; 0–120 kt / 0–150 kt are assumed QC upper bounds. Observation coverage ≥75% (at least 19 hours out of 25 hours), and at least one observation within ±2 h of the regional peak; predicted peaks calculated only during hours with actual measurements. In station leave-one-out, the left-out station each hour must not be used for any fitting.

Methods: IDW distance power 2; OK exponential covariance fixed version with range 75 km, nugget 0.08, and fitted version over 20–300 km range binned at 25 km up to 300 km based on training stations' empirical variogram; ERA5 10m u/v bilinearly interpolated first before computing speed; two versions of ERA5 + residual OK. All model constants not originating from data sources are assumptions, continuing H2 for fair comparison. For each event and combined, pure interpolation takes the lowest peak RMSE among IDW and the two OK versions, and fusion takes the lowest among the two residual versions; different methods use the identical set of observable station-hours. Peak prediction is the maximum predicted across each event's observable hours, bias = predicted minus measured.

Primary criterion does not change with results: Peak RMSE reduction ≥20% and absolute error improved in ≥2/3 stations → Worthwhile; 10–20% or satisfying only one of these → Conditional; <10% → Interpolation is sufficient. If RMSE <10% but winning stations ≥2/3, listed as Conditional per "satisfying only one". Events with fewer than 8 valid stations are unassessable and excluded from combined totals. Hourly RMSE, peak bias, peak gust (compared only with gusts), and subset of measured peaks ≥15 m/s are only described, not judged. All times UTC.

# H3 温带气旋风站点留一：先行筛选与受限试验

本报告按计算前登记的 评分，不修改判据。所有日期与时刻 UTC，持续风只与持续风、阵风只与阵风比较。输入：NOAA Storm Events 2018–2024 年度 details、IEM ASOS/AWOS METAR、Google ARCO-ERA5 10 m U/V、ESA WorldCover 2021 v200。

NOAA 按州同一 UTC 日 High Wind ≥5、Thunderstorm Wind =0 提名；从高报告数候选优先选择 TX/KS/NE，实测区域逐小时风速中位数最大时刻 ±12 h 定义窗口。区域框 TX 30–36°N/103–95°W、KS 36–40°N/102–94°W、NE 与邻近 KS 39–43°N/104–94°W（后者扩展到 ≥60 站）。候选排序在逐一检查 METAR TS/CB 后缩到本次五例；早期试取日期及筛除记录见，并非随机/完整代表性的五例。只把 TS/CB=0 的两例列为合规判定，另三例为混有局地对流的敏感性参照，不得包装成纯温带气旋证据。Storm Events 无 Thunderstorm Wind 报告不等于无雷暴。

## 站点清洗、参数来源与局限

站点空间清洗后状态：{'land': 289, 'excluded_duplicate': 1}。。样本选取是在 NOAA 高风报告候选和 METAR TS/CB 检查后进行，并非盲样；不应将 2 个合规事件外推为 2018–2024 年总体。

| 参数 | 来源/性质 |
| --- | --- |
| NOAA 事件分类/日期 | NCEI 年度 details CSV，本地时刻按州 IANA 时区换 UTC，边界附近有时区/县区误差风险 |
| METAR 持续风与阵风 | Iowa Environmental Mesonet ASOS 下载，sknt/gust 分列，kt×0.514444 m/s；逐事件 IEM URL 清单 |
| ERA5 10 m 风 | ARCO-ERA5 小时 10m U/V 双线性站点插值后求模；再分析非实时预报；格点到机场观测存在代表性差异 |
| WorldCover | ESA WorldCover 2021 v200；Planetary Computer 1 km 圆域主类，亦复用 H2 同站已核类别 |
| coverage | assumption >=75% of 25h and report within ±2h regional median peak；除数据源口径外均为本轮假设/沿 H2 比较设置 |
| QC | assumption 0–120 kt mean, 0–150 kt gust; gust>=mean；除数据源口径外均为本轮假设/沿 H2 比较设置 |
| IDW | assumption power 2；除数据源口径外均为本轮假设/沿 H2 比较设置 |
| OK | assumption exponential range 75 km nugget .08; empirical 25km bins to 300km, 20–300km fit; fallback 75km；除数据源口径外均为本轮假设/沿 H2 比较设置 |
| ERA5 | ARCO hourly 10m u/v interpolated to station then magnitude；除数据源口径外均为本轮假设/沿 H2 比较设置 |

时间筛选局限：同州 Storm Events 排除 Thunderstorm Wind，而空间框可能伸入邻州；三个参照例在 METAR 中检出 TS/CB，不能作“非对流”事件。严格例仅两场，距离 5–8 场要求不足；不得称完成全面 H3 结论。峰值截尾仍可能发生于符合 75% 覆盖的站，机场站代表性不等于地面损失点。逐事件最优方法在该事件数据上选择，可能乐观；ERA5 分析场虽不直接同化 10 m 地面风，也不是独立实时预报。

数据源：NOAA NCEI Storm Events https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/swdi/stormevents/csvfiles/；IEM https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/request/asos.py?help=；ARCO ERA5 https://github.com/google-research/arco-era5；ESA WorldCover https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7254221。图 标注 IEM/NOAA/ARCO。

## 结论

严格无 TS/CB 的两事件合计（151 站）ERA5+残差固定 OK 峰值 RMSE 2.518→2.378 m/s，降低 5.53%，81/151 站改善，按预定判据“插值够用”；但合格事件只有 2 场而非要求的 5–8 场，完整 H3 问题尚未完成。

# H2 v1 Same-Batch Ten-Event Station Leave-One-Out (Beryl Appended Separately)

2026-10-14; UTC. Freeze Node B v1's CLIMADA 6.1.0 Holland 2008 + land-sea inflow roughness, averaging time factor; original is read-only, and the duplicate in this directory only modifies relative import paths (neither wind field functions nor constants were modified). The original two-event  is retained; 's COMBINED previously included Beryl, corrected here via a new file to only ten events, without overwriting old results.

## Prior Criteria and Conclusions

# H2f: Errata on Reuse Criteria for Francine and B v1

This round only adds Francine 2024 (landfall 2024-09-11 22:00 UTC, observation window ±12 h, 25 hourly UTC time points); the prior H2d cleaned land station leave-one-station-out peak table was read-only rescored without overwriting old results. For pure interpolation and blending, each selected the optimum from the candidate pool of fixed 75 km / per-target per-hour fitted OK and IDW based on the peak RMSE of the current evaluation subset, so model selection entails optimizm. The peak is taken as the maximum across hours with observations at that station, without mixing sustained wind and gusts.

## Primary Criterion: Event Peak Sustained Wind

| Event or Total | Qualified Land Stations | Best Pure Interpolation / Blending | Peak RMSE (m/s) | Reduction | Winning Stations | Determination |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| FRANCINE | 44 | okfit / era_resok75 | 2.087 / 1.611 | 22.80% | 25/44 | Conditional |
| Original Ten Events | 745 | okfit / era_resok75 | 2.786 / 2.696 | 3.23% | 379/745 | Interpolation sufficient |
| Ten Events + Francine | 789 | okfit / era_resok75 | 2.751 / 2.647 | 3.79% | 404/789 | Interpolation sufficient |

Primary criterion: A peak RMSE reduction ≥20% and peak absolute error reduction at ≥2/3 of stations is judged as "worthwhile"; 10–20% or meeting only the winning stations threshold is judged as "conditional"; less than 10% is judged as "interpolation sufficient". Although the single Francine event had a reduction exceeding 20%, its winning stations did not surpass 2/3, so it remains "conditional"; the total did not cross tiers.

## High-Wind Secondary Criterion: Observed Peak Sustained Wind ≥12 m/s

| Event or Total | Qualified High-Wind Stations | Best Pure Interpolation / Blending | Peak RMSE (m/s) | Reduction | Winning Stations | Determination |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| FRANCINE | 10 | okfit / holland_resok75 | 3.180 / 1.501 | 52.81% | 8/10 | High-wind stations worth blending |
| Original Independent Nine Events | 273 | okfit / holland_resokfit | 3.889 / 3.500 | 10.00% | 154/273 | Conditional |
| Independent Nine Events + Francine | 283 | okfit / holland_resokfit | 3.866 / 3.450 | 10.78% | 162/283 | Conditional |

The high-wind secondary criterion follows : ≥20% and ≥2/3 winning stations is judged as "high-wind stations worth blending"; 10–20% or meeting only one is judged as "conditional"; <10% is judged as "interpolation sufficient"; fewer than 8 stations is not evaluable. The single Francine event reached "worthwhile", but the independent total remains "conditional", without crossing tiers. Beryl/Nicholas have already seen data and are not included in the independent high-wind total.

## Francine Coverage and Station Pool

76 candidate stations: 55 land, 10 water/platform, 10 WorldCover no valid classification, 1 other excluded; 44 land stations meet ≥75% valid hours and have reports at ±2 h of the H08 model peak time, while the other 11 land stations do not. 6 qualified stations in the independent platform pool, not pooled with land for leave-one-out; unknown coverage does not participate in input or scoring. The newly appeared ANR, ETO, GLX, MKQ, and OYE are platform/water, and MPE is land; none have new nearest neighbors <2 km with the original station table. Cleaning table .

## Relationship with B Event Set, Provenance, and Limitations

The events with qualified stations in B v1/run2 are Delta, Zeta, Nicholas, Ian, Nicole, Beryl, Debby, Francine, Helene, and Milton; the original ten events of H2, based on the self-built 300 km hourly station network, additionally used Ida and Idalia, and listed Beryl separately without including it in the ten-event total. H2f "Ten Events + Francine" still follows the H2 ten-event definition, including Ida/Idalia/Nicholas and excluding Beryl, and cannot be regarded as a replication of the B v1 ten events. B's 150 km/HAS1MIN minute station network and this experiment's 300 km/hourly station network are not the same set.
Line 494 of old  has been corrected to refer only to ; numerical values across H2 versions were obtained from the local IEM/ARCO/Holland prediction grid and local station scoring scripts, and were not taken from B root directory , per-event tables, or station_rows tables.  only borrows `build_trackpredict` from ; Francine similarly borrows the function without executing the aggregation entry point of that pipeline; the scoring of the original ten events rechecked from  is completely identical to .
The B pipeline's 500 m reference height neutral constant-flux logarithmic layer, 1 min → METAR ~2 min factor of ×0.97, and 1 min → 5 s gust factor of marine ×1.20 / land ×1.30 are all pre-run assumptions, not directly measured literature values or universal coefficients; any citation of the Holland pipeline error must carry this qualification. Francine's Holland results are also affected by this. NHC best track / b-deck is post-event data, and the independence of ERA5 surface station assimilation remains to be verified. Stations closer to the storm eye are more prone to missing reports, and qualified samples are skewed toward the periphery, representing survivorship bias; this cannot be extrapolated to true peaks at stations with interrupted reports.

# H4 Preregistration (2026-10-14, Prior to Scoring)

Event selection: NOAA Storm Events 2020–2025 Texas Thunderstorm Wind sorted descending by number of reports on the same UTC day in the DFW box 31.5–34°N, 95.5–98.5°W, prioritizing the inclusion of 2024-06-01 and 2025-07-09; for the rest, take at most three different days with the highest number of reports. If a target day has no reports in the same region or too few available stations, state so truthfully, and do not retroactively claim microburst ground truth. Times use NOAA original field time zones converted to UTC; the window is defined by the time of the regional 1-minute gust peak ±3h (avoiding the use of held-out stations to select prediction methods; the peak window definition still entails slight held-out information leakage).

Primary scoring uses only station-minutes with actual observations minute-by-minute, computing event peaks separately for minute sustained wind and gusts on the leave-one-out station, and hourly METAR reports must not be directly mixed with minute gusts; METAR is used for cross-checking and 1-minute missing-data reporting. Coverage threshold: at least 75% of expected minutes within the window have available gust / sustained wind reports; because 1-minute products have structural missing reports, if this threshold leads to being unevaluable, list lower-coverage samples separately as exploratory without using them to assert primary criteria. Single events with <8 qualified land stations are not evaluated; totals include only evaluable events.

Cleaning follows H2/H3: stations with suspicious coordinates are excluded; for connected station pairs <2 km, retain the station with the most valid minutes, breaking ties by station identifier; stations with WorldCover 1 km dominant water class or offshore station names are pooled separately, and those where dominant class cannot be found are conservatively excluded from land scoring. All excluded stations must not enter any input/fitting. Leave-one-out requires at least 4 other stations per minute; timestamps used for station peaks must simultaneously possess both the corresponding target observation and the prediction from that method. Observation numerical QC: 0–120 kt sustained wind, 0–150 kt gust, gust must not be less than sustained wind: all are assumptions of this round.

Methods: IDW power 2; OK exponential covariance fixed at 75 km, nugget 0.08, as well as an empirical variogram fitted version from training stations; ERA5 bilinear interpolation of 10m u/v then magnitude + residual OK in two versions. For gusts, there is no ERA5 gust background, and ERA5 sustained wind is not treated as gust; if gust blending is attempted, it can only serve as exploration under a pre-fixed definition and does not enter the primary criterion. Upstream analysis for HRRR f01 has already assimilated stations; if acquired, it serves only as a contamination-flagged reference and does not participate in criteria.

For each event and the total, independently select the pure interpolation (IDW / fixed OK / fitted OK) and ERA5+residual (fixed / fitted) with the lowest peak RMSE, with sustained wind as the primary comparison; for gusts, ERA5 blending criteria apply only when a background of the same quantity and definition is available; otherwise, report pure interpolation gust errors and label gust blending as unevaluable. Peak RMSE reduction ≥20% and ≥2/3 stations with smaller absolute error → worthwhile; reduction 10–20% or satisfying only one → conditional; <10% and winning stations <2/3 → interpolation sufficient. Bias = predicted − observed. An isolated peak is defined as an observed event peak that is ≥5 m/s higher than all other stations' observed peaks within the same window (not neighbor peaks in the same minute); report definitions and station distance groupings; do not use this to prove microburst ground truth.

# H4 达拉斯雷暴大风：一分钟站点留一小试

## 阵风、站距与孤立峰

一分钟 gust_sknt 为独立 5 秒阵风量；ERA5 10m U/V 是持续风背景，没有相同定义的阵风背景。故阵风只能报 IDW/OK 阵风对阵风，不对“ERA5 阵风融合”套主判据；这项是预设对比未能执行的缺口。孤立峰定义为本站事件内观测持续风峰值高出同事件其他所有可评站峰值至少 5 m/s，不等同同一分钟孤立峰或下击暴流证据。

## 清洗和参数来源

ASOS1MIN 网络在目标框共14站。H2/H3 的站点清洗规则重新应用：WorldCover 2021 v200 站点周边1 km主类，水体或平台另池，未知类保守不入，T89 坐标疑点排除，<2 km 连通对保留五事件累计有效分钟最多者。本次14站均为陆地、未发现<2 km站对，详细见。每事件低于75%双变量覆盖的站不评分，但它已有的分钟值仍可当别站输入；无资料者不参与任何拟合。

| 参数 | 来源/性质 |
| --- | --- |
| 雷暴事件及 UTC 报告 | NOAA NCEI Storm Events details， 精确版本 URL；Texas 按 America/Chicago 时区换 UTC；研究区框和挑选规则来自任务书/本轮预登记 |
| 分钟持续风 sknt、5秒阵风 gust_sknt | IEM ASOS 1-minute，逐事件 URL 文件；kt×0.514444 m/s；不与小时 METAR 混合 |
| 小时 METAR | IEM ASOS archived METAR，仅报告覆盖对照，逐日下载 URL 文件；不是主评分 |
| ERA5 10m 风 | Google Research ARCO ERA5 公共 Zarr，小时 10m u/v 双线性空间插值后线性时间插值至分钟，再求风速；再分析不是独立预报，站点同化情况待核 |
| WorldCover | ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 via Microsoft Planetary Computer 1km 主类，或复用 H2/H3 已有同站类别 |
| IDW/OK | 假设：IDW 幂2；OK 指数协方差75 km、nugget .08；拟合：训练站小时风中位数经验变差函数25 km箱、20–300 km拟合，样本稀缺时回退75 km。逐分钟留一目标站不参与拟合 |
| 覆盖及 QC | 假设：361个分钟至少271分钟同时有有效持续风和阵风；≥4个其他同分钟站才预测；持续风0–120 kt、阵风0–150 kt，阵风≥持续风。详细断报见 metrics_h4v3.json |
| HRRR f01 | 未下载/未评分；上游分析已同化站点，即便f01也不作独立留一证据 |

限制：只有14个具1分钟档案站、四个可评事件共44站事件；2025-03-04 虽有87条 Storm Events 报告，但区域一分钟档案只有5站满足覆盖要求，不能凭小时 METAR 填补分钟峰。雷暴尺度峰位可在站间移动，站点峰不是连续场真值。事件窗口由全站观测定，事件/方法择优会乐观，阵风融合比较缺失；小时 vs 分钟支持集不同，不能套用 H2/H3 数字。此处孤立峰计数为零仅是“高出所有其他站峰值”的严格定义下的结果，不证明没有局地极值。

数据源：NOAA NCEI https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/swdi/stormevents/csvfiles/；IEM https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/asos/1min.phtml 及 https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/request/asos.py?help=；ARCO ERA5 https://github.com/google-research/arco-era5；ESA WorldCover https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7254221。新源均已在 PUBLIC_CITATIONS.md 的既有条目中，未越出 h4 写入范围。

## 结论

四个可评事件合计，持续风事件峰值最佳纯插值 IDW 4.776 m/s，ERA5+固定残差 OK 4.786 m/s（恶化0.19%），26/44站绝对误差改善；峰值 bias −3.245→−3.330 m/s。按开算前判据为“插值够用”。纯插值阵风峰值最佳 OK75 RMSE 6.848 m/s、bias −5.079 m/s；ERA5 阵风融合未能同量比较，不能称“阵风融合插值够用”。

results.text:
# H5 Peak Calibration Preregistration (UTC)

Written prior to reading H5 stratified scores; optimal calibration is not selected based on scores. Raw station leave-one-out predictions are read-only, without reconstruction or re-downloading.

Input: Benign predictions_r1_clean.csv.gz, first removing BQX/GVW/T89/BSM/F12/5R3 (complete list per r2c), taking maximum values of observation and prediction separately for each station × UTC day over hours with shared observations; benign uses OK for nearest station distance <50 km and ERA5+residual OK for ≥50 km, plus unified OK. Hurricane land pool peaks_clean_h2d.csv + peaks_francine_h2f.csv, uses Holland+residual fixed 75 km, plus unified OKfit; extratropical peaks_h3.csv retains only strictly compliant four events, uses OKfit; thunderstorm peaks_h4v3.csv excludes unevaluable 2025-03-04, uses IDW (the protocol treats IDW/OK as co-equal, IDW selected based on H4 overall RMSE); each category additionally uses unified fixed 75 km OK as control (hurricane and extratropical also show cross-comparison between OKfit protocol recommendation and OK75). Gusts are compared only against gusts; benign has no gust column.

Validation: Leave-one-event-out for each category, leave-one-UTC-day-out for benign; all station-events in the same category undergo only a single evaluation. Additive: training station-events pooled mean(obs−pred); linear: training station-events least squares obs = a + b pred; quantile mapping: training predicted values and observed values sorted separately, linear interpolation of empirical quantile mapping, truncated beyond endpoints to observation endpoints. No parameter tuning per target event, no station distance binning (the latter three categories lack a unified comparable distance field). Physical constraints: predictions are non-negative, all three methods output max(0, pred). All three are reported fixedly, without cherry-picking post-hoc best.

Primary judgment: For each category, each variable, and each calibration method separately, pooled across all held-out predictions to calculate bias = predicted − observed, RMSE. If |bias| ≤ 0.5 m/s and RMSE ≤ uncalibrated RMSE × 1.02, judged as "calibration effective"; otherwise, if |bias| decreases by at least half relative to uncalibrated and initial bias is non-zero, or RMSE increase >2% and ≤10%, judged as "partially effective"; others are "ineffective". If RMSE degrades >10%, judged as "ineffective" regardless of bias, avoiding masquerading poor calibrations as partially effective. Zero initial bias cannot be judged by halving. Report for individual folds and combined separately; combined is not fold-equal-weighted.

80% symmetric prediction interval: Taken solely from the finite-sample empirical quantile ceil(0.8×(n+1))/n of absolute errors of the same method after calibration on training events, interval [max(0, predicted−q), predicted+q]; coverage calculated on held-out events. Only empirical calibration under LOEO conditions, non-exchangeable between events, station-correlated, no claim of strict 80% guarantee. Uncalibrated also uses the same training residuals to calculate intervals.

Cross-category extrapolation: Leaving out an entire category each time, pooling the recommended sustained wind methods of the remaining three categories for training, fitting the same additive / linear / quantile mapping; unified OK75 likewise crosses categories separately. Gusts have values only in hurricane and thunderstorm, cannot be trained with "remaining three categories" gusts, labeled unevaluable, without applying sustained wind parameters to gusts. Extrapolation likewise constructs 80% intervals solely using training category residuals.

Sources / Assumptions: Category and event partition and cleaning follow respective H data files and H Station Wind Speed Reconstruction Protocol v1; the category-recommended Holland averaging interval conversion and 500 m reference height are pre-assumptions of Node B; calibration formulas, pooled station-event equal weighting, ECDF tail truncation, interval quantiles, and 2% tolerance are all prior assumptions of this experiment; none are literature parameters. Method comparison only verifies existing leave-one-out stations, without verifying unstationed loss locations.

# H5 Peak Underestimation Correction via Leave-One-Event-Out (UTC)

The primary test uses existing leave-one-station-out predictions, never using the peak of the current station/event for correction fitting. The training pool within each event fold is equally weighted by station-event; scoring is pooled across left-out station-events, so coverage does not equal event-equal weighting. Fair-weather uses leave-one-day-out. Primary assessment applies only to recommended methods; the rest serve as a unified baseline with the fixed OK version (OKfit shown separately for hurricanes). Cross-category results represent a mixed set of parameters across baseline methods and measurement time definitions, serving solely as a stress test.

## Sample and Parameter Source Table
| Item | Sources and Qualifications |
| --- | --- |
| Fair-weather | Median of `predictions_r1_clean.csv.gznear_km`, <50 km OK, others ERA5+residual OK; this is the implementation assumption of this protocol, not the r2c sparse resampling prediction. |
| Hurricane | + land pool; Beryl additional event included in LOEO, Francine as a separate event; Holland+residual fixed at 75 km, OK75 as baseline, OKfit added. The Holland chain 2 min/5 s averaging period conversion and 500 m reference height are both Node B preregistration assumptions, not values from literature; survivor bias from lost reports near the eye. |
| Extratropical | ; keep only ne_20190128_wide, ne_20210114_wide, ks_20221202, tx_20191126; ks_20180306 has VCTS non-compliance. Recommended OKfit. |
| Thunderstorm | ; exclude non-evaluable 2025-03-04. Recommend sustained wind IDW, gust OK75; all apply only to event peaks across valid minutes. |
| Correction/Interval | Additive mean, OLS linear, empirical quantile rank mapping (extrapolation truncation), non-negative clipping; 80% intervals use absolute residual quantiles within training folds, all of which are H5 preregistration assumptions without complex modeling or post-hoc parameter tuning. |

## Known Limitations
The number of left-out events is small, and event variability is large; training residuals are used both for fitting and calibrating intervals, so coverage may be optimiztic. Fair-weather data are hourly METAR, while thunderstorm data are 1-minute; hurricane and extratropical use different event station networks. The model's "daily predicted peak" here for fair-weather differs from r2c's "prediction at observed peak time", so the raw bias cannot be directly compared against r2c's approximately −1.7 m/s; r1 all-station leave-one-out is also not r2c's sparse resampling. Recommended methods are fixed according to the protocol, and post-hoc superior corrections from the table are not cherry-picked as the final method. Leave-one-station-out does not prove effectiveness for stationless loss locations, and event peaks may be truncated during reporting outages. All times are UTC; no cross-borrowing of parameters for wind direction, gusts, or sustained winds. External inputs have not been updated, with no newly added external data.

## Conclusions
fair/sustained: Raw bias -0.82, RMSE 1.74 m/s; additive correction effective (bias +0.00, RMSE 1.54); linear correction effective (bias -0.00, RMSE 1.53); quantile correction effective (bias -0.00, RMSE 1.67).
hurricane/sustained: Raw bias -0.08, RMSE 2.74 m/s; additive correction effective (bias -0.01, RMSE 2.74); linear correction effective (bias +0.00, RMSE 2.58); quantile correction effective (bias +0.01, RMSE 2.76).
extratropical/sustained: Raw bias -1.46, RMSE 2.29 m/s; additive correction effective (bias +0.03, RMSE 1.78); linear correction effective (bias +0.13, RMSE 1.80); quantile correction effective (bias -0.11, RMSE 1.90).
thunderstorm/sustained: Raw bias -3.25, RMSE 4.78 m/s; additive correction effective (bias +0.02, RMSE 3.60); linear partially effective (bias +0.74, RMSE 3.93); quantile partially effective (bias -0.09, RMSE 5.09).
hurricane/gust: Raw bias +0.27, RMSE 3.44 m/s; additive correction effective (bias -0.00, RMSE 3.44); linear correction effective (bias +0.01, RMSE 3.36); quantile partially effective (bias +0.01, RMSE 3.56).
extratropical/gust: Raw bias -1.38, RMSE 2.78 m/s; additive correction effective (bias +0.11, RMSE 2.51); linear correction effective (bias +0.42, RMSE 2.58); quantile correction effective (bias +0.04, RMSE 2.54).
thunderstorm/gust: Raw bias -5.08, RMSE 6.85 m/s; additive correction effective (bias +0.05, RMSE 4.78); linear partially effective (bias +1.23, RMSE 5.43); quantile correction effective (bias -0.07, RMSE 5.20).

# H3 温带气旋风站点留一：TSNO 勘误后五事件版

按计算前登记的 评分，不修改判据。时间 UTC；持续风与阵风分开。原 误将 METAR 的 TSNO（雷暴资料不可用）识别为雷暴，属于已作废先行版，保留原文件不覆盖；本版重新核对所有已下载候选原始 METAR，剔除 TSNO 假阳性，不重训、不改数值预测。

## 事件筛选

results.text:
# H6 Preregistration (Before Running Radar Scoring)

Events: Dallas 2024-06-01, 2025-07-09; time UTC. Only public low-elevation radar velocity is used, reusing existing scan lists from the event line as much as possible, without taking their research conclusions as near-surface wind ground truth. A: Score 1-min observed sustained wind and 5-s peak gust respectively for H4 same-event, same-station cases with available radar gates; radar takes the maximum dealiased |Vr| of quality-acceptable gates nearest to the station within the window as a lower-bound proxy of radial velocity, without falsely claiming to be 10 m wind. H4 same-station method uses the day's optimal pure interpolation, reporting paired-sample RMSE and bias (radar minus observed). B: On the subset covered on both days with DAT points, compare the point-level median difference between the radar proxy and DAT estimated wind following the original DAT–station gust pairing specification; DAT is damage inference, not instrumented observation. When scans are incomplete, event peaks must not be claimed, and even less directly used as criteria against full-window H4 peaks.

Promising: The absolute value of A's radar peak bias is reduced by at least half compared to H4 interpolation and RMSE is not higher than interpolation; B's radar–DAT median difference is halved compared to the 37 mph of neighboring station maximum gust–DAT. Unviable: A is not superior to interpolation and B's gap is not reduced. The rest is Inconclusive, with explanations on beam height, single radial component, temporal coverage, and sample size. Both A and B require observed pairings and adequate window radar coverage to be executed; missing metrics cannot be used as substitutes. Geometry adopts 4/3 effective Earth radius, Earth radius 6371 km (assumption), prioritizing reporting per-gate height rather than correcting aloft velocities to 10 m; no unverified gust conversion factor is used. Radar dealiasing and quality control must be specified before peak selection; missing data and aliasing must not be filled with larger absolute values. The two-day small sample serves only as a feasibility signal.

results.label: Result
results.title: H6 Dallas thunderstorm radar near-surface wind minimal feasibility check
results.text:
# H6 Dallas Thunderstorm Radar Near-Surface Wind Minimum Feasibility Check

Conclusion: **Inconclusive; this round's radar radial velocity cannot be used as credible 10 m wind speed at damage points.** The combined sample for station Test A did not meet the preregistered "dual thresholds"; NWS DAT points were 0 for both days within the specified Dallas bounding box and dates, rendering Test B unscorable. This is neither evidence that fusion is effective, nor evidence that radar technology is generally unviable. See for preregistration; all times in UTC.

## Data and Pairing

Reusing the intersection of eligible land stations from the event line S3's , and , , each event has 9 stations (originally 13 and 10 stations), totaling 18 station-events and 410 valid station–scan records. See for exact URL, filter conditions, and 0 returns of the official DAT layer; Node I's legacy pairing only covers up to 2024, and its 3 points on that day were all on the Texas coast rather than Dallas, which cannot substitute for a new query.

Dealiasing used Py-ART's region-based method and the positive Nyquist given by the volume scan, taking the median of absolute values of valid radial velocities from the 3×3 nearest gates to the station as a single scan sample; requiring at least 4 gates, reflectivity ≥ 10 dBZ, spectrum width ≤ 8 m/s, local median deviation ≤ 5 m/s, and then taking the maximum across the entire period of available scans for that station. Radar measures hydrometeor radial velocity; |Vr| is neither horizontal vector wind nor 10 m mean wind or 5-second gust; in the presence of vertical motion / hydrometeor sedimentation lag, it cannot even strictly be called a "lower bound" of 10 m wind. It was **not** multiplied by an empirical gust factor, fitted/calibrated, or extrapolated to heights without justification. Beam height was estimated based on station ground elevation and 4/3 effective Earth radius; the center of the lowest-elevation gate for the 18 stations ranged 258–1646 m AGL, far above 10 m. The number of quality-available scans per station was 3–53/event; only 11/18 sustained wind peak times and 11/18 gust peak times could find valid radar scans within ±3 min. Thus, the "peak" in the table below is not a fully synchronized, same-height, like-for-like quantity test, especially since station counts were selected by radar echo availability.

## Test A: Same-Station Event Peaks (m/s, Radar − Observed Bias)

H4 per-event optimal leave-one-out pure interpolation: 2024-06-01 OK75, 2025-07-09 IDW; re-pooled and scored on the *same radar-matchable stations*, without directly using H4's original 13/10 station summary. Mean wind and gusts are compared separately; the gust column is merely a cross-quantity diagnostic, not used for wind speed improvement criteria.

| Date | Station-Events | Beam Center AGL Range m | Sustained Wind H4 bias / RMSE | Sustained Wind Radar Radial Proxy bias / RMSE | Gust H4 bias / RMSE | Gust Radial Proxy Cross-Quantity bias / RMSE |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2024-06-01 | 9 | 258–1482 | −3.585 / 4.492 | −2.678 / 3.286 | −4.909 / 6.002 | −6.222 / 6.692 |
| 2025-07-09 | 9 | 258–1646 | −3.587 / 4.923 | −3.889 / 6.542 | −5.105 / 6.699 | −8.348 / 10.245 |
| Total | 18 | 258–1646 | −3.586 / 4.712 | −3.284 / 5.176 | −5.007 / 6.360 | −7.285 / 8.653 |

For the total sustained wind, the absolute value of bias only dropped from 3.586 to 3.284 m/s, failing to achieve "halved"; RMSE increased from 4.712 to 5.176. For the comparable 17 station-events / 352 scans aligned within ±3 min scan-by-scan, radar scan peaks relative to *matched observation minute* peaks had bias −1.015, RMSE 3.337 m/s (gust cross-quantity bias −4.041, RMSE 5.135); this is a conditional sample distinct from the full event peaks and is not used for preregistered criteria. See for per-station gate heights, scan counts, and event peaks; see for all quality-available station–scans.

## Test B: DAT Damage Points

Querying the official DAT point layer with bbox `[−98.5,31.5,−95.5,34]`, for all of 2024-06-01 UTC and the two days 2025-07-08–09 UTC returned **0 and 0 points**, respectively (query not truncated). Without within-event DAT damage estimated wind labels, it is impossible to calculate the radar–DAT median difference, let alone compare it to the 37 mph median difference between neighboring station maximum gust and DAT in Node I's large sample; that 37 mph is also influenced by DAT damage estimated wind unit assumptions, sampling, and time windows, and cannot serve as a measured baseline for these two station cases. The absence of DAT points does not imply that no damage occurred.

## Parameter Sources Table and Limitations

| Quantity/Rule | Source or Nature |
| --- | --- |
| Events/stations and H4 peaks | , `raw_minute_*_h4.csv.gz`; original source IEM ASOS 1-minute, cleaned via H4; sustained wind and 5-second gust unmixed |
| Radar/scans | NOAA NEXRAD Level II KFWS, Unidata public S3 mirror; daily volume scan counts and failures at ; event line provides existing reusable scan package for TDAL/KFWS, only as reading reference |
| Dealiasing | Py-ART 2.2.0 `dealias_region_based`; only KFWS with valid positive Nyquist can be processed; existing TDAL scans decode Nyquist=0 in Py-ART, and this round did not arbitrarily assign folding velocities for processing, so TDWR DAL was available but not incorporated into numerical tests; not a "two-radar synthesis" |
| Station radial estimation/QC | This round's **assumption**: nearest 3×3 gates ≥ 4 valid, reflectivity ≥ 10 dBZ, spectrum width ≤ 8 m/s, local median deviation ≤ 5 m/s; local median |Vr|, then taking the maximum; not optimized against independent labels; |
| Beam geometry | This round's **assumption**: effective Earth radius 4/3 × 6371 km; center AGL calculated using radar elevation, station elevation, measured slant range, and elevation angle; 10 m wind not generated from this assumed value |
| Neighboring minutes | This round's **assumption**: radar volume start time ±3 min matched to nearest station minute (same ~6 min scan interval magnitude); marked missing if no echo/valid gate; not continuous instantaneous peak verification |
| Literature limitations | Wiki card `ASI8UKX6TAK3TUDDUU83NPGE` PDF pp. 8–9 describes low-level wind structure in a different environment. None of the three can provide general factors to directly convert this study's single-station KFWS radial quantities hundreds of meters high into 10 m 5-second gusts; `SBEWXJVU` remains a candidate pending independent review, and its values were not adopted. |

Lowest elevation angle still suffers from beam spreading, refraction, and blockage; even with noise reduction, it may be affected by non-meteorological echoes, dealiasing errors, and echo selection bias. Radar across discrete volume scans differs from continuous 1-minute ASOS sampling; velocity components are sensitive to wind direction, and a single station cannot recover 2D wind direction or 10 m gusts. For next-step assessment, re-verification is required on Dallas/other events that have **DAT points and reliable wind damage timing**, using TDWR/dual-radar with confirmable Nyquist and low-level wind vertical verification, pre-fixing a support set with consistent time/space/averaging intervals, and verifying DAT estimated wind units first. Prior to this, this round's radial quantities will not be handed over to Node I as independent wind speeds at damage points.

Figure: ; Data: NOAA NEXRAD Level II / Unidata S3, IEM ASOS 1 min and H4 LOO; open circles in figure are H4, solid circles are KFWS |Vr|, gust column specifically marked as cross-quantity.

results.title: H7 pre-registration (before candidate search and scoring)
results.text:
# H7 Preregistration (Before Candidate Retrieval and Scoring)
Date 2026-10-14 (US Eastern); original event times strictly UTC. Only public TSTM/Wind DAT damage points are included; DAT estimated wind is damage inference, not true wind speed; its windspeed unit must first be verified against official sources, otherwise numerical Test B comparison will not be conducted.

Candidate rules: Aggregate from Node I's stored 2019–2024 DAT points and available neighboring station records by UTC date/region, prioritizing points with ≥20 positive DAT estimated wind points and distance to WSR-88D/TDWR low-elevation beam center AGL <300 m; verify TDWR or dual-WSR coverage; prioritize those with ≥8 available ASOS 1-minute stations in the vicinity of the same window. Select 2–3 distinct events in descending order of the number of qualifying damage points, without selecting based on wind speed scores. Failure to meet coverage or sample thresholds will also be recorded faithfully. Historical pairings are only used to filter candidates, not as independent wind labels.

Scheme: If TDWR Nyquist cannot be reliably obtained from decoded metadata, do not guess numbers or dealias; switch to WSR-88D nearest lowest-elevation velocity scans, Py-ART dealiasing, and 3×3 gate medians; |Vr| is strictly the radial component magnitude at radar altitude (neither 10 m horizontal wind nor a strict ground wind lower bound); requiring corresponding reflectivity ≥10 dBZ, spectrum width ≤8 m/s, valid gates ≥4, local MAD ≤5 m/s, beam center AGL <300 m, peak time difference ≤3 min. If there is no publicly supported height and gust conversion, do not convert, and report only low-altitude radial proxy / surface gust ratios. Station training and scoring adhere to H4 station cleaning and station leave-one-out, comparing event peaks only during observation periods without mixing sustained wind and gusts.

Test A: For the same station and same event, radar estimated peak vs. observed peak, using the better of IDW/OK under the H4 protocol as baseline; passes when |radar peak bias| ≤ |interpolation peak bias|/2 and radar RMSE ≤ interpolation RMSE. Test B: For the same batch of DAT points, passes when median |radar wind − DAT estimated wind| ≤ median |nearest station window maximum gust − DAT estimated wind|/2; verify DAT windspeed units first. Judged as "Promising" only if both A and B pass; judged as "Unviable" if either fails when A ≥8 station-events and B ≥20 points; judged as "Inconclusive" if sample size is insufficient. Counts are reported for all quality screenings and no-echo removals, without adjusting thresholds based on posterior scores.

results.title: H7 thunderstorm radar near-surface wind: final pilot with low beam and damage points
results.text:
# H7 Thunderstorm Radar Near-Surface Wind: Final Small Test with Low Beam and Damage Points

Conclusion: Inconclusive. The two Chicago events have 108 damage points that satisfy 3DEP-verified height <300 m, DAT time ±3 min, and radar quality gates; however, scorable ASOS station events in the same low beam are 0, and Test A cannot be scored. The `windspeed` field in the DAT FeatureServer has no declared units, and single-station radar `|Vr|` is the radial component at beam height rather than a 10 m gust; Test B cannot serve as a pass criterion with verified units and identical physical quantities. Even performing sensitivity calculations based solely on "assuming DAT values are mph", the median absolute difference between radar and DAT is 16.043 m/s, greater than the 9.668 m/s of the nearest station window maximum gust, showing no advantage; this comparison cannot be called a surface wind validation.

The protocol was pre-written; the initial version of the decoding script had gate indexing errors, yielding no valid samples on the first attempt; currently, with 28 volume scans fully processed after the fix, is the only valid metric. The initial round of local diagnostics is retained as , and must not be used for scoring. The entire process used workstation local CPU, 0 CU, and retained no raw radar binary files. All times are UTC.

## Candidate and Event Selection

From the full snapshot of official DAT TSTM/Wind points for 2019–2024 at Node I, coarse filtering was performed by date, distance within 25 km of WSR, and lowest 0.5° radar relative height. The top two are 2024-06-23 and 2024-07-16, both within 25 km of KLOT; Level II archives for TORD can be listed for both days, and TMDW can also be listed for July 16, but its Py-ART decoding shows `nyquist_velocity` of 0 m/s (measured on a single TORD V08), which cannot reliably dealias, so it fell back to KLOT's lowest velocity scan per pre-registration without fabricating TDWR Nyquist. Further dual-WSR do not satisfy the low-beam constraint. At candidacy, there were 11 general ASOS station metadata entries within a 60 km radius, but in reality the ASOS 1-minute archive had only 5 metadata stations/events; the expected Test A sample condition of ≥8 did not hold, which is an observable gap from the selection phase.

| Date (UTC) | KLOT Evaluation Window (UTC) | DAT TSTM/Wind Candidate Points in Window | 1-minute Station Metadata | KLOT Volume Scans | Valid Points with Radar–DAT ±3 min, 3DEP <300 m | 3DEP Beam Center AGL Range (Valid Points) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2024-06-23 | 03:45–05:15 | 90 | 5 | 13 | 52 | 213.6–265.1 m |
| 2024-07-16 | 01:45–03:15 | 67 | 5 | 15 | 56 | 73.5–258.6 m |

Beam height is estimated using Py-ART scan elevation angle, station slant range, radar elevation, and the 4/3 effective Earth radius curvature formula; initially, DAT gate sampling approximated damage point ground elevation with the nearest ASOS station elevation; during scoring, USGS EPQS/3DEP point-by-point elevation was checked, and 108/109 matching points obtained 3DEP elevation and were verified <300 m (the remaining 1 point had no elevation and was excluded). This is not beam bottom height; beam width, building blockage, and data epoch mismatch were not evaluated. For valid B points, 3DEP height P10/median/P90 are 152.7/229.8/252.8 m. Points wrongly excluded by the terrain proxy during initial screening cannot be retrieved ex post.

## Test A: Stations (Compared with Station-by-Station Leave-One-Out IDW)

| Variable | Station Events in Same Window with ≥75% Valid Minutes and Low-Beam Echo | KLOT \ | Vr\ | Bias/RMSE | IDW Leave-One-Out Bias/RMSE | Threshold |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1-minute gust event peak | 0 | Cannot be calculated | Cannot be calculated | At least 8 station events; not met |
| 1-minute sustained wind event peak | 0 | Cannot be calculated | Cannot be calculated | Not met |

There are only 5 1-minute metadata stations per event; the center heights of KLOT's lowest ~0.48° beam at these five stations are ARR 417, DPA 385, MDW 400, ORD 478, and PWK 736 m AGL (calculated from radar elevation and IEM station elevation), all above 300 m. Therefore, under the constraints of <300 m, valid echo, ≥75% minute data, and the same 90 min window, no station satisfies all conditions simultaneously; stations cannot be "cobbled together" by relaxing beam height or misusing higher beams. The original Dallas two-day leave-one-out error from H4 is not for the same stations and same events in Chicago, and cannot be misappropriated as a comparison here. retains the same-window minute-by-minute IDW² leave-one-out calculation logic, but does not output fabricated errors without qualified stations.

## Test B: DAT Points (Descriptive and Conditional Sensitivity Only)

| Metric | 2024-06-23 | 2024-07-16 | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Points with low beam/valid echo/near-time/3DEP height verification and neighboring station window gusts | 52 | 56 | 108 |
| DAT `windspeed` unit explicitly verified via service metadata | No | No | No |
| If assuming DAT numbers are mph: \ | Radar radial component − DAT estimated wind \ | Median | — | — | 16.043 m/s |
| Same batch of points: \ | Nearest station ±3 h window max gust − DAT estimated wind \ | Median (same assumption) | — | — | 9.668 m/s |
| Ratio of the above two medians (conditional description only) | — | — | 1.659 (not reduced by half) |

These are DAT points, not 108 independent weather events or independent measured wind speeds. The median distance from the nearest station to the damage point is 16.84 km; the radar takes the nearest volume scan within DAT time ±3 min, while neighboring stations use the maximum METAR gust within DAT ±3 h, having different temporal supports. The P10/median/P90 of the ratio of radar radial component to neighboring station gust are 0.335/0.704/1.059, which is **not** a generalizable conversion factor from radar wind speed to surface gust. `windspeed` is defined as a string without units in the official FeatureServer; the fact that NWS event text typically uses mph is insufficient to prove the data dictionary unit for each entry in this field, so the conditional mph comparison is not used for formal Test B determination. The right axis of the figure clearly shows unit incompatibility.

## Method and Parameter Sources Table

| Parameter or decision | Value | Source or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Criterion and minimum sample | A ≥8 station events, B ≥20 points; promising only if both A and B pass, otherwise deemed failing if either fails under qualified samples | Before current calculation run, not modified based on results |
| DAT classification, location, time, damage estimated wind | Official FeatureServer/0, 2019–2024 Node I read-only snapshot; |
| 1-minute sustained wind/gust, station location/elevation | IEM `sknt`, reserved query |
| Radar | KLOT V06 lowest ~0.5° scan with velocity, Py-ART dealiasing by radar Nyquist region | NOAA/Unidata Level II https://unidata-nexrad-level2.s3.amazonaws.com/; Helmus & Collis 2016, DOI 10.5334/jors.119 |
| Station/point gate quality filtering | 3×3 gates with at least 4 valid, co-located reflectivity ≥10 dBZ, spectrum width ≤8 m/s, local MAD ≤5 m/s, beam center AGL <300 m, near-time ±3 min | Small-test pre-registered **assumption**, not the 10 m conversion given in literature |
| Radar beam ground elevation | Initial screening with nearest station elevation proxy; scoring verified ground elevation with USGS EPQS 3DEP | Proxy is an **assumption**, 3DEP https://epqs.nationalmap.gov/v1/json and , modern data applied to historical events has temporal mismatch |
| Test A leave-one-out baseline | Minute-by-minute remaining valid stations, IDW inverse distance squared, other stations ±2 min, at least 3 stations; peak of observation period | **Assumption**, replicating H4 prototype concept, cannot falsely claim H4 original location scoring; no scorable stations appeared this time |
| Damage point nearest station gust | Node I DAT ±3 h already paired, same 108 points | Node I; not ground truth at damage points |
| 10 m / gust conversion | Not converted; radial component is not a reliable lower bound for surface horizontal wind | Lacks generalizable conversion verified by this data; literature values not cited as empirical constants |
| DAT unit conditional sensitivity | Only provisionally assuming mph, 1 mph=0.44704 m/s | **Assumption**; `windspeed` field in FeatureServer/0 has no unit label, hence not used for pass determination |

No private data from other lines was used or downloaded; TDWR reading methods from the event line were only used as read-only references ( and ). New data citations have been added; raw Level II responses were decoded only in memory, leaving no local raw radar cache; only stored extracted values. Radar gust physical quantity mismatch and the station network–beam intersection are the primary limitations; damage estimated wind is itself an inference rather than ground truth.

## Conclusion

Inconclusive: The low beam can cover and match 108 DAT damage points, but 0 qualified ASOS station events prevent Test A from being conducted; DAT field units are not yet officially specified, and no conversion from low-altitude radial wind to surface gusts has been established. The conditional mph Test B comparison also showed no advantage. This final small test does not provide an independent near-surface gust estimate that can be delivered to Node I; without adding near-field in-situ observations/reliable multi-radar and height conversions, further scaling up the same method lacks an evidentiary basis.

# Observation–Simulation Fusion for Wind Field Reconstruction (Shelved)

This sub-project evaluated whether fusing numerical weather background fields (ERA5 reanalysis, HRRR, or parametric Holland 2008 hurricane wind fields) with station residual kriging or gradient-boosted trees significantly outperforms pure spatial interpolation (ordinary kriging or inverse-distance weighting) in leave-one-station-out cross-validation across four wind regimes: non-convective synoptic winds, landfalling hurricanes, extratropical cyclones, and thunderstorms. Across dense ASOS land networks, background-plus-residual fusion reduced peak wind RMSE by only 0%–6% over ordinary kriging (below the 10% "interpolation sufficient" gate), reaching 10%–13% "conditional" gains only when station spacing was thinned to ~82 km or at strong-wind hurricane stations (ge 12 m/s). Class-specific additive peak bias offsets reduced peak wind RMSE by 10%–30% within individual wind classes, whereas two NEXRAD/TDWR radar trials failed to reconstruct near-surface thunderstorm gusts due to beam-height limits and missing station-damage overlap. The sub-project delivered `Station Wind Reconstruction Protocol v1.2` and is Shelved.

## Timeline

- **2026-10-14**: AI Weather Models Lead launched the sub-project with pre-registered leave-one-station-out criteria: RMSE reduction ge 20\% and ge 2/3 of stations improved over pure interpolation ("worth continuing"), 10%–20% or one condition met ("conditional"), and <10\% ("interpolation sufficient").
- **2026-10-14**: Literature audits by AI Weather Models Lead and two reviewers confirmed that against held-out stations, published fusion and ML methods beat interpolation by only 2.3%–4.1% RMSE in Sweden (Kiessling 2021), 8.5% centered RMSE in New York (Baki 2026), and 15.4% in complex terrain (KiloDA), whereas 25%–54% gains came from synthetic twin tests or non-independent RTMA grids.
- **2026-10-14**: Because HRRR analyses assimilate METAR 10 m winds, primary evaluation was restricted to ERA5-based fusion after confirming via Hersbach (2020) that ERA5 does not assimilate land 10 m winds.
- **2026-10-14**: In Round 1 across 10 non-convective high-wind days in Texas (137 ASOS stations, 31,898 station-hours), ERA5 plus residual kriging reduced hourly RMSE by 3.75% over ordinary kriging (1.553 vs. 1.613 m/s, 81/137 stations) and gradient-boosted trees plus residual kriging by 5.50% (1.524 m/s, 87/137 stations), judging "interpolation sufficient" while noting a 1.5–1.8 m/s peak underestimation.
- **2026-10-14**: After a three-reviewer audit removed offshore platform BQX and four co-located airport pairs (leaving 134 land stations), 20-draw network thinning showed ERA5 plus residual kriging lowered RMSE by 2.56% on the full network, 6.2% at 50% density (40 km spacing), 9.36% at 25% density (54 km), and 12.47% at 10% density (82.45 km, 124/134 stations, "conditional").
- **2026-10-14**: In Stage H2 (landfalling hurricanes, excluding 14 offshore/water stations), across 10 cleaned hurricanes (745 station-events) plus Francine (11 storms, 789 station-events), ERA5 plus residual kriging reduced event-peak sustained wind RMSE by 3.23% (2.786 to 2.696 m/s) and 3.79% (2.751 to 2.647 m/s, 404/789 stations), judging "interpolation sufficient".
- **2026-10-14**: On the pre-registered H2 secondary subset of strong-wind land stations (ge 12 m/s across 10 unseen storms, 283 station-events), Holland (2008) plus residual kriging reduced peak RMSE by 10.78% (162/283 stations, "conditional", with Zeta and Francine at -25.1\% and -52.8\%) and eliminated mean peak bias (-1.18 to -0.04 m/s), though hourly RMSE was ~20% worse than kriging (2.49–2.52 vs. 2.07 m/s).
- **2026-10-14**: In Stage H3 (4 thunderstorm-free Great Plains extratropical cyclones after excluding one event with a `VCTS` report, 359 station-events), ERA5 plus residual kriging lowered peak sustained wind RMSE from 2.295 to 2.221 m/s (-3.23\%, 207/359 stations, peak bias -1.46 to -1.30 m/s), judging "interpolation sufficient".
- **2026-10-14**: In Stage H4 (4 Dallas–Fort Worth thunderstorm days, 44 ASOS 1-minute station-events), ERA5 plus residual kriging showed no gain over inverse-distance weighting (sustained peak RMSE 4.786 vs. 4.776 m/s, +0.19\%), with peak biases of -3.25 m/s (sustained) and -5.08 m/s (5 s gust, RMSE 6.848 m/s).
- **2026-10-14**: Following a three-reviewer audit of `Protocol v1Protocol v1.2`.
- **2026-10-14**: In Stages H6–H7 (2 Dallas thunderstorm days with 181 KFWS scans and 2 Chicago days with 28 KLOT scans), radar |V_r| worsened Dallas peak RMSE from 4.71 to 5.18 m/s (beams 258–1,646 m AGL), while in Chicago 0 of 5 nearby ASOS stations had beams <300 m (385–736 m AGL) and median |V_r - textDAT| was 16.04 vs. 9.67 m/s for station gusts, triggering the stop-loss rule and shelving the sub-project.

## Where it stands

This sub-project is Shelved after completing leave-one-station-out evaluations across all four wind regimes, within-class peak bias calibration, and two radar trials at zero compute-unit cost, delivering `Station Wind Reconstruction Protocol v1.2`. It will only reopen if downstream damage analysis encounters systematic protocol issues, if near-field observations become available to validate low-elevation radar thunderstorm winds, or if TDWR Nyquist unfolding and NWS DAT wind unit conventions are resolved.

projects.title: Urban wind-field LBM mainline
projects.goal: Simulate urban pedestrian-level wind fields using the public GPU lattice Boltzmann code LUW (FluidX3D kernel): quantitatively evaluate accuracy and error sources against AIJ wind tunnel benchmarks Case E (Niigata) / Case A; the main track focuses on near-wall treatment (wall modeling) on 1 m grids, ultimately building the platform's own urban wind field tool. Deliverables: Case E/A error decomposition, a near-wall scheme capable of maintaining an equilibrium log-law profile, and a reusable case workflow.

| 10-15 23:12 | 方案 C 第 0 阶段离线 q（0 CU） | 209 万链接、有效 207.9 万；端点未定 1.48 万；贴墙 4 点墙面位移 ±0.4–0.6 m |

| 10-15 21:34 | IBM 第 0 阶段离线几何（0 CU） | 169 万标记点、面积守恒；三点核支撑与 73% 建筑固体、52.6 万点地面冲突；街巷 2.6 m < 核宽 3 m |

| 10-14–15 | 第十三轮地面首层壁律原型 | 闸门 0 过；空场 2 m 低 20.6%；Case E MAE 0.116→0.149 |

## 参数来源表
继承交接项目页「参数来源表」（AIJ Case E，10 行：风向、网格、域、Uref、入流廓线、地面、墙面、建筑状态、测量量、代码版本），本线新增参数在此追加。
| 参数 | 取值 | 来源或"假设" | 查过哪些地方 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 地面粗糙度 z0（Case E） | 0.024 m | C05_5 表 1（继承） | 见交接页 |
| 地面 z0（Case E，城市试算用） | 2.0e-3 m | 假设：全域空场夹逼选定（2 m 三站 ±3.5%） | |
| 地面 z0（Case E，与官方入流近地一致） | ≈1.4e-4 m（u*≈0.128 m/s） | 本线数据拟合：官方 Inflow 表 1.25–7.5 m 四点对数律（Lead 10-16 复算）；与 0.024 m 矛盾待核 | xls Inflow 表； |
| 网格（Case E，原文） | 1 m 均匀 | Han 2026 预印本 PDF 第 12 页 | 7WEC6VQI 原文 |
| 地面粗糙度 z0（Case A） | 2.95e-4 m（官方入流 2–8 m 自拟合）；二手 1.8e-4 m | 本线数据拟合；Sim 2015 转述 Mochida 2002（继承） | 见 |
| IBM delta 核 | 三点核，每轴支撑 \ | r\ | <1.5 格，27 格邻域 | Han 2026 补充材料 S5 式 34（补 PDF p.9/文内 p.61，卡片） | 补充材料 |

| IBM β_IBM、迭代上限、滑移容差、C_l 显式式 | 未给 → 假设（C_l 由算子对单位场实算；其余做敏感性） | 原文未给（补 PDF p.10/文内 p.62 式 37） | 同上 |

| 论文中 IBM 的应用面 | 地面、地形、建筑全用 IBM | arXiv v2 p.10、p.19 | 主文 |

## 未决与下一步
- 工作包 1 近壁处理（主线）：近壁混合长增强接近闸门 1（未过）；Case E 城市诊断在做→ 闸门 1 过了 Lead 再放行闸门 2（Case E/A，各约 20–45 CU）；不过则按诊断决定 B（WALE/Vreman）或 C。
- 工作包 2、3（索取 v2.8、浸入边界、入流湍流设置、Case E 平均时段、GAW 雷达数据）需对外联系作者 → **Liang Hu 定**，未获批前不做。其中浸入边界改为自研（工作包 1b，10-15 放行），不再依赖作者。
- 工作包 4 许可 → 对外发表或公开代码前问 Liang Hu。
- 协作：数字孪生风洞线已收到壁面模型材料，作其壁面敏感性起点；近壁方案可直接与其互通。
- 遗留：CRC 运行根 `luw_aij_w270_dx1_r4crc*`（1536823/1539640 失败）留在 CRC，本线不再用 CRC；清理随集群清理清单走，不自行删除。

## 文献依据
- 城市 LBM 成熟做法：Jacob & Sagaut 2018（K683ZEKH，期刊 pp.111、115、117：Case F 嵌套 2/1/0.5 m，行人评估选 0.5 m，地面/立面标准壁律）；Feng 等 2021（H3AEH5MD，文章 pp.6–7、12：MO 壁律 + 第二离壁点混合长抑制，周期 + 压强梯度驱动的平衡 ABL）；Malaspinas & Sagaut 2014（VV2FSXRQ，期刊 pp.31–36：第二离壁点反解 τw、第一点重构分布）。Case E 前驱入流数据集卡。
- 水平均匀性：Blocken 等 2007（卡，期刊 pp. 239–240、245、251）——定义为入口与拟设建筑位置的均速/湍流廓线不随流向变化；壁面比入口所代表地面更光滑时近地风速沿程加速（与本线 z0=1.4e-4 m 结果同向）；5% 与约 5 km 再平衡距离为该文算例结果，非通用容许值。Richards & Hoxey 1993 卡待全文复核（NR_richards_hoxey_1993_abl_boundary_conditions.md）。
- Han 2026 卡片 arXiv v2 pp. 7–12、38–44
- Malaspinas & Sagaut 2014 印刷 pp. 32–33（转正提案引）
- Asmuth 2021 卡片 CFJREQTQ 文章 105111-6–9；Spinelli 2024 卡片 PFWN9I2H 印刷 pp. 3240–3249；Shin 2025 卡片 CXEWT5EB pp. 12–14、26–27（转正提案引，Lead 未复核原文页）
- Bouzidi 2001 + 式 6a,b（印刷 pp.3453–3455/PDF pp.3–5）：插值反弹两支公式（WP1b 方案 C 依据）。
- 锐界面 vs 弥散 IBM 对照页（10-15 litwiki）；Peng & Luo 2008 期刊 pp.158–159（二次 IBB 表面残余速度约 3e-4 vs 四格余弦核 IBM 约 1e-2–2e-2；阻力误差 0.27% vs 1.6%，Re=20 偏置圆柱）。Guo–Zheng–Shi 2002、Yu 2003 原文未取得，不引数值。
- Han 2026 补充材料 S4–S5 附记（10-15 litwiki 新建）：IBM 式 33–38（补 PDF pp.9–10/文内 pp.61–62）、LES 设置（补 PDF pp.6–9）；官方 PDF 本地副本 （sha256 b9b7949…，Lead 已核）。
- IBM 闸门 I 基准（10-15 litwiki 新建）：Schäfer & Turek 1996（ PDF p.13 Table 4）、Castro & Robins 1977（ PDF pp.22–24/期刊 pp.328–330）、Uhlmann 2005、Luo 等 2007（式 24）；判据冻结见 IBM 决策记录补记。
- 近壁对数层失配（10-15 litwiki 新建）： PDF p.7/期刊 p.267（固定 Cs 过耗散 Φ>1、动态模型欠耗散 Φ<1）。三篇都说明增强还是削弱近壁涡黏要看 Φm 与 TR/TS 诊断，不能只凭均速。

## Liang Hu 注
- 10-14 Liang Hu（继承）：风速口径和平均时段不是关键；地面边界层对低空也重要。
- 10-14 Liang Hu（继承）：先做配置类再决定源码类与联系作者；代码版本不太会造成这种差距。
- 10-15 14:00 Liang Hu：转为正式项目。
