# LUW Work Package 1: 1 m Flat-Ground Near-Wall Treatment DESIGN v2 (Design Draft; 0 CU)

Time: 10-15 16:29 (ET). Read-only code baseline, HEAD `dd438c1`; read-only handoff from the Lab. This draft has not modified, compiled, or executed the solver; everything below consists of proposed implementations and proposed acceptance checks, not new results. Flat ground only; buildings, roofs, DEM, and edge non-horizontal walls retain the original algorithm. This design draft must not be used to claim reproduction, publishability, or improvements on Case A/E.

## Evidence and Problem Boundaries

The complete handoff diff is the only complete patch for the prototype implementation; `solver_wallmodel_cont5_final.diff`, which omits first-layer index initialization in `setup.cpp`, must not be used. The prototype `kernel.cpp` swaps 9↔16 and 11↔18 after `load_f` so that ground specular reflection replaces bounce-back, and applies local rough log-law stress via Guo forcing at the first fluid cell; lines 44–60 and 66.

Equilibrium log-law empty-fetch run: κ=0.40, z0=0.024 m, U(15.9 m)=3.9286416 m/s, prescribed u*=0.2418545 m/s; core domain 500×200×270 m, Δ=1 m, with an upper sponge layer; 31000 steps, 500 samples over the last 20000 steps. At x=200/300/400 m, the modeled U2/U_inlet2=0.785/0.792/0.804; U5/U_inlet5=1.053/1.069/1.068; the model actual step-by-step wall stress and complete control-volume budget were not output. The u* ratios 0.770/0.787/0.814 back-calculated from the time-averaged first-cell velocity are merely proxies, not the actual mean stress. Physical ground=0, solid cell center=0, first fluid cell center=1 m, and half-way specular effective wall=0.5 m; the physical 2 m point is only 1.5 m from the numerical wall, and the resulting ~6.4% difference is purely geometric sensitivity rather than an observational correction. Based on lines 7–28 and lines 27–30 (handoff copy). The existing second-layer instantaneous test reads the previous-step velocity, giving U2/U_inlet2=0.694/0.753/0.792 (x=200/300/400 m) without filtering, so the second layer cannot be claimed effective yet; based on lines 15–30 and lines 5–12. In Case E, the first-layer prototype 80-point scalar-approximation MAE went from 0.1160→0.1485 with overshoots at open points; see lines 32–43. All of the above are data from this line of work with no literature extrapolation; the urban diagnostic was granted a one-time exception previously and cannot be treated as passing Gate 2 here.

Literature boundaries (card paths all relative to root):
-, printed pp.32–33 §4.2 of the original paper: tangential velocity at the second off-wall node matches the stress, while distribution functions are reconstructed at the first node; the Musker/boundary-layer law and quasi-parallel conditions in the paper are on printed pp.31–32. That paper does not directly prescribe the rough log law and temporal filtering used in this project.
-, within-article p.3 §III, p.4 Eq. (19), p.13 §VI: replacing no-slip with stress; distribution reconstruction and near-wall SGS over-dissipation issues; numerical results from cumulant/AMD cannot be carried over directly to the SRT/Smagorinsky setup in this project.
-, printed pp.3240–3243 Tables 6–7, p.3249: in a fixed channel setup, WALE is more accurate than Vreman/standard Smagorinsky, while Vreman was chosen for computational cost; its MRT/HRR collision operators differ from this project's SRT, so urban performance cannot be guaranteed on this basis.
-, PDF/article pp.12–14 §3, pp.26–27 §5/Fig.16: filtering the sampled velocity and raising the matching height target different sources of mismatch; curvature issues related to displacement height are not solved by stronger filtering. Its d/hwm threshold depends on the conditions of that paper and is not transferred as a layer-selection rule for flat ground.
-, within-article 105111-5–6 §III B Eqs. (27)–(28): iMEM uses a virtual wall velocity on bounce-back links to match the prescribed tangential stress; this is a different candidate from the first-layer distribution reconstruction in p.4 Eq. (19) above, and the two must not be conflated.

Here we only performed targeted verification of the literature cards and handoff records without re-reading every paper in full; specific formula adaptations still require checking the original pages and carrying out discrete derivations during implementation. Aside from the sourced motivations listed above, all new thresholds, filter bounds, and code line counts below are engineering assumptions and must not be presented as numbers given by the papers.

## Recommended Path and Isolated Controls

We recommend executing Option A first: retain the approved local specular reflection + first-cell Guo shear forcing, change the stress sampling to a temporal low-pass filter of the second-cell tangential velocity without changing the location where ground stress is applied, and include "second layer unfiltered" and "first-layer prototype" as controls under the exact same domain, inflow, and averaging window. This draws on Malaspinas's second-cell velocity sampling / first-cell execution architecture and Asmuth's ESG, but this implementation is neither their distribution reconstruction nor iMEM, and carries no accuracy guarantee for this 1 m LUW grid. First keep the original geometry with the physical wall at 0.5 m fixed to reproduce the mismatch, and then conduct height-datum sensitivity separately: if the numerical wall is to be shifted to physical 0 m, an explicit and consistent mapping among ground/fluid-center coordinates, inflow, and sampling must be rebuilt, rather than quietly altering y inside the log law alone or shifting measurement points by 0.5 m post hoc; results from the two configurations must not be mixed in attribution.

Proposed definition for Option A: at the second fluid cell center (1.5Δ relative to the numerical wall) of each flat-ground column, take the horizontal tangential velocity vector q and update `q_f^{n+1}=q_f^n+alpha*(q^n−q_f^n)`; we recommend an independent experimental setup benchmarked against Asmuth's time scale, locking Tf first using the reference mean velocity measured in the baseline run, and never varying Tf cell-by-cell or step-by-step using instantaneous velocity. The vector itself is filtered to compute the stress magnitude and direction, where h_m is the distance from the matching cell center to the actual numerical wall; the first-cell force density is added along the existing Guo path without duplicating tangential specular reflection. Because `rhonu` in the prototype may be written concurrently by `UPDATE_FIELDS` within the same kernel, it must not be read directly inside `stream_collide` and claimed to be the same-step velocity. Sampling and filtering should be performed in an independent kernel / previous-step double buffer indexed by the global fluid column ID, supporting cross-GPU halo exchange or reading only when the synchronized second cell resides in the same subdomain; cross-domain cases must not be identified using local z==2. Initialize q_f with the initial physical velocity of the same second cell, and record q_f, step number, Tf/alpha, and geometry/inflow configuration upon checkpoint/restart; otherwise cold starts and restarts will follow different dynamics. The ground-column mask excludes buildings, roofs, TYPE_E, and corner points; when a cell is missing, do not silently fall back to first-cell sampling—count the occurrence and fail the gate. Mismatches in direction and velocity decay/backflow are diagnosed separately. The prototype local swap is only an approximation for diagonal links (as noted in lines 81–98 of the complete diff), so link-level mass/momentum checks must be retained.

Option B is an independent two-factor sensitivity test and is not tuned jointly in the same batch with Option A: under the exact same boundary condition of the original first layer + specular reflection/Guo forcing, first replace the SUBGRID closure with WALE (with Vreman as an alternative control), and compare profiles, actual stress, effective viscosity, TKE, and numerical stability under the same stress formulation and sampling method. WALE requires computing the velocity gradient and strain / squared-gradient tensors from the macroscopic velocities of the current cell and neighboring fluid cells; near walls, explicit one-sided finite differences, building-boundary rules, and inter-domain halo rules must be used to avoid naively treating solid u=0 as a fluid velocity sample. Vreman likewise requires definitions for gradients and filter width; model coefficients are not back-inferred for LUW from Spinelli's channel ranking—first verify the constants used in that paper against the LUW discrete definitions, and if unavailable, list them as assumptions and perform controlled sensitivity tests. The existing `Q0.76421222*sqrt(Q)` in `kernel.cpp:1723–1737` is not equivalent; one should first define `nu_eff=nu_mol+nu_t` and then compute the relaxation parameter under lattice unit conditions (Δt=Δx=1), with unit tests for clipping and stability, ensuring that the force prefactor tracks the new omega. If B fails on its own while A passes on its own, no combined run is needed; if both fail individually with complementary mechanisms, a combined run serves only as a new configuration and cannot be claimed as a single-factor explanation.

Option C (fallback) is Asmuth-style first-cell distribution reconstruction or iMEM link-stress matching, selecting one of the two first and deriving conservation for each independently. The specific coefficients and even/odd link addresses for reconstructing `f_eq+f_neq` under SRT/D3Q19, FP16C, and Esoteric-Pull must be re-derived; copying cumulant/AMD formulas verbatim from another implementation is prohibited, as is "retaining bounce-back + adding first-cell body force on top." Compared with A and B, this carries the highest engineering risk and will be activated only if actual wall-force and flux diagnostics from A/B pinpoint the stress-application operator as the culprit. Literature basis is CFJREQTQ within-article p.4 Eq. (19) and 105111-5–6 as cited above; the LUW adaptation details have no literature basis and are proposed based on this codebase.

## Exact Modification Points and Scope (Future Implementation Estimates; Not Yet Modified)

| Code Baseline Path (all within repo) | Function / Location and Modification | Estimated Changed Lines |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `defines.hpp` | Compile-time `GROUND_WALL_MODEL` / sampling-layer, filter, and mutually exclusive SGS switches, all disabled by default; existing D3Q19/SRT/FP16C/SUBGRID/VOLUME_FORCE states preserved | 12–25 |
| `setup.cpp` | `main_setup` profile section around lines 5782 and 5936–6078: build true first-fluid-cell indices and column masks from the global physical ground plane, convert SI→lattice for z0, wall distance, and filter time, check geometry and inflow, and echo independent settings | 50–100 |
| `lbm.cpp`, `lbm.hpp` | `LBM_Domain::device_defines` around lines 612–783, domain initialization / step-by-step driver: pass global ground elevation, switches, and alpha to device; Option A adds bottom 2D double buffers and checkpoint/restart metadata; multi-GPU synchronization | A 90–180; B 10–30 |
| `kernel.cpp` | omega computation in `stream_collideu[j[5]]SUBGRID`, gradient kernels, and boundary finite differences | A 100–180; B 140–260 |
| New verification scripts / minimal configs (in future isolated run root only) | Per-link parity verification, switch-off equivalence, checkpointing, conservation, field diagnostics, and gating | A 120–220; B 100–200 |

Option A requires ~250–485 lines in the solver and ~120–220 lines for verification; Option B adds ~150–290 lines in the solver and ~100–200 lines for verification; Option C, if activated, adds another ~250–500 lines in the solver, not double-counted with A/B. Estimates include interfaces, checks, and restart logic rather than raw line diffs. The Esoteric-Pull even/odd addressing in `kernel.cpp:1338–1350` must preserve single-writer semantics and mutually exclusive input/output; arbitrary post-collision swapping or cross-cell writes of compressed distributions are prohibited. `lbm.cpp:711–715defines.hpp:18–24` already enables `FORCE_FIELD`, but it is not a zero-cost reusable storage buffer for temporal filtering; filtering uses a compact 2D buffer over ground columns to avoid allocating a full-domain three-component field. Global offsets and halos in `lbm.cpp:637–651` and the update timing of u in `kernel.cpp:1701–1717` must be verified together. Memory capacity and bandwidth have not yet been proven sufficient to accommodate the new closure and filtering; actual peak memory usage and performance regression on an A100 40GB are listed as Gate 0 engineering checks rather than guarantees.

## Parameter Source Table (Must Be Frozen Before Running)

| Parameter | Value / TBD | Source and Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Δ / Core domain, flat-ground test case | 1 m, 500×200×270 m, 31000 / last 20000 steps | Existing equilibrium empty-fetch setup in this line of work, lines 7–9; not a literature parameter |
| κ, z0(E), U15.9, prescribed u* | 0.40, 0.024 m, 3.9286416 m/s, 0.2418545 m/s | κ=assumption; z0(E) cites AIJ `C05_5.pdf` PDF p.2 Table 1 at line 13 of the handoff, and this draft did not re-verify the official PDF; the rest are equilibrium log-law inflow values constructed in this line of work, not AIJ measurements |
| Wall location and h_m | Prototype numerical wall at physical 0.5 m; second cell h_m=1.5 m | Lines 5–13 of this line of work; changing the physical wall position constitutes a separate sensitivity assumption and must be updated together with the coordinate system |
| Matching layer | Second cell as primary test for Option A, first cell as control; third cell as diagnostic fallback only | Second-cell configuration based on VV2FSXRQ printed pp.32–33 and CFJREQTQ 105111-6–9; third cell has no literature verification, assumption |
| Tf/alpha | Initial test , ; reference mean velocity must be measured and frozen first | Time scale adapted from CFJREQTQ 105111-6–9; exponential recurrence, reference window, and actual LUW numerical values are assumptions; physical seconds, lattice steps, and sensitivity must be reported |
| WALE/Vreman constants, gradient scheme, and clipping | To be verified against original papers before implementation; if not found, mark as "assumption" and pre-specify a finite candidate set rather than fitting to Case E MAE | Spinelli card PFWN9I2H printed pp.3240–3243 only supports method comparison; specific numerical values for LUW implementation have no literature basis and must not be treated as settled |
| Case A ground z0 | Do not use Case E's 0.024 m; official value not yet verified. If testing is necessary, use only the near-ground inflow fit 2.9466×10⁻⁴ m with half/double sensitivity | Lines 9 and 26–28 of this line of work, fitted/secondary value rather than an official AIJ value; mark as "assumption" when used |
| Empty-fetch acceptance thresholds, budget thresholds, CU | See next section | Project-proposed engineering criteria/budget, not acceptance standards from any paper |

When parameters are unavailable, first check the original paper's appendices/figures/tables, authors' public code, foundational method papers, and existing project files before searching online; if still unavailable, retain them as explicit assumptions with range sensitivity, and do not optimize constants post hoc against urban MAE. Where the magnitude of global impact from parameters such as temporal filtering is unknown, we recommend pre-locking unfiltered / baseline / shorter / longer filter times; in the absence of a physical basis for selection, report only the sensitivity rather than claiming an optimum.

## Gates and CU Estimates (Future Plan, 0 CU Consumed)

Gate 0, estimated 2–8 CU (Option A), plus 3–8 CU for Option B: on an isolated source copy, perform pointwise comparisons against a clean HEAD with the model switch turned off for decompressed `fi` distributions, rho/u/flag, and time-step hashes (same device, same compile macros, and same initialization; statistical similarity is not accepted as pointwise identity); auxiliary cross-checks between FP16C and FP32; step-by-step tests covering even/odd t parity, non-uniform distributions, diagonal ground links, single-/multi-subdomain boundaries, zero velocity, backflow, mask contact with buildings, halos, filter initialization, and checkpoint/restart continuation. In a closed double-slip mini-channel, zero-force mass conservation / normal leakage / tangential drag must remain near numerical precision; with forcing active, the discrepancy between actual per-step ΣF and ΔPx relative to the zero-force run must be ≤5% over a pre-declared warm-up window, with the raw startup steps reported separately; tabulate storage, bottom/top/side/inlet/outlet pressure and advection fluxes, viscous/SGS fluxes, specular tangential exchange, Guo forcing, and closure residual over an independent control volume, targeting ≤10%—do not proceed if unmet. Log engineering performance/VRAM usage and checksums. The switch-off control must be an independent clean HEAD build, not a dual compile of the same modified branch. Not yet executed in this design round.

Gate 1, estimated 12–35 CU (Option A: unfiltered, second-cell unfiltered, second-cell baseline filtered plus pre-declared sensitivity runs, and prototype/no-model re-verification), plus 15–40 CU for Option B if A fails and diagnostics support proceeding: maintain the same equilibrium log-law empty-fetch inflow and fixed averaging window; across five spanwise lines at x=200/300/400 m and physical heights z=2/5/10/15.9/20 m, simultaneously report absolute U, U relative to same-height inlet U, mean velocity profiles, actual time-averaged u*, τ vector and filtered q time series, Σ actual forces, and the complete control-volume budget, checking for drift across time blocks. Each of the three stations at 2 m requires U/Uin∈[0.90,1.05]; from 2–20 m, beyond visual "fit," we pre-propose a deviation ≤10% at each sampled height with no systematic opposite-sign bias (e.g., slow at 2 m / fast at 5–20 m); the actual time-averaged u* must deviate by ≤10% relative to the prescribed 0.2418545 m/s, and control-volume closure must be ≤10%. Stability at 15.9 m must also be ≤10%. These are project-assumed thresholds that preserve the commissioning brief's original requirements of 0.90–1.05 at 2 m and u*≤10% without relaxation. The ~6.4% shift from the 0.5 m wall location is treated solely as an independent geometric sensitivity: it must not be used as an excuse to lower the 0.90 lower bound to 0.84; if a unified physical coordinate definition proves the original criterion inapplicable, a new criterion must be frozen first and submitted to the Lead for a verdict before running, with no post-hoc changes. Stress proxies obtained merely by substituting line-averaged or time-averaged velocities into the wall law cannot pass the u* gate. If Gate 1 is not passed, work stops at the empty-fetch stage without falling back to Case E/A tuning.

Gate 2, estimated 20–45 CU (Case E) and 20–45 CU (Case A) only after passing Gate 1, plus 10–19 CU buffer for independent configurations/restarts and statistics; the mechanical sum if all candidate branches above were executed is ~82–200 CU (reduced in practice by branch gating), with each case re-verified against measured A100 wall-clock time and burn rate under a hard cumulative stop line of 200 CU; estimates must not be treated as pre-approved budget to be spent in full. Case E keeps the original 80 points, registration, inflow, and statistical definitions fixed, simultaneously reporting both vector S and scalar-approximation S* MAE, r, mean ratio, near-wall/open grouping, and bias direction; it must not degrade relative to the original baseline and must exhibit an interpretable physical mechanism from empty fetch to the urban canopy, rather than being cleared on a single MAE metric alone. Case A evaluates FAC2, q, r, NRMSE, and centerline profiles after independently verifying the ground z0, inflow, and measurement point definitions; Case E's z0 must not be used as Case A's official value. Even if urban metrics improve, success must not be claimed if empty-fetch mismatch or stress-budget failure persists. All CU figures above are non-binding estimates; this task does not launch Colab/TACC or submit jobs; future background Colab runs must enable keepalive and shut down per `colab-gpu` rules on every launch, and TACC runs require prior ComputeOps resource approval, separation of pre-check and single submission, and post-submission registration. The workstation retains only scripts, figures, and small summary results.

## Recommended Delivery Verdict

Decision I made (design recommendation): proceed first with Option A's second-cell temporal filtering while retaining the original specular reflection / Guo stress application and measuring actual wall forces and control-volume budgets; next, test Option B independently with WALE (Vreman as fallback) under fixed boundary conditions, while deferring Option C's distribution reconstruction / iMEM. Rationale: the existing second-layer test was unfiltered and failed under the old empty-fetch inflow, so simply "switching layers" cannot be treated as the answer; the WALE ranking comes from different collision operators and channel setups and is a pointer rather than a directly transferable conclusion. Cost of being wrong: Option A may only alleviate stochastic stress correlation without eliminating height-datum offset or SGS mismatch, in which case execution halts at Gate 1 and diagnostics determine whether to activate B/C; this is an engineering design pending review and GPU verification, not a scientific conclusion.

# WP1 Option A: Implementation Attempt and Gate Status (Internal, Not a Validation Conclusion)

Time: 10-15 16:43 ET. Read-only baseline clone dd438c1; starting point is the handoff `solver_wallmodel_complete_20261015.diff` (independently copied via the handoff `eqlog_corrected_inputs.tar.gz`; not cont5_final, which omits setup.cpp). All new code resides solely in the isolated copy within this directory. No CRC/TACC/Case E/A runs were performed.

## Actually Executed
- Added the `GROUND_WALL_FILTER` switch (disabled by default) to the isolated source copy, using the previous-step second-cell velocity `uLUW_GROUND_ALPHA`. The first layer retains the original specular reflection and Guo wall forcing. Added an accumulator for actual step-by-step applied force, planned for `t>=11000solver_A_unvalidated.patch`, with the isolated source in the local copy; `A_stage_v2_unvalidated.tar.gz` is an archive of the current copy and the empty-fetch deck, containing no results. This implementation can currently only be called an experimental candidate.
- Source contract tests: 4 tests OK. This only tests source-text hooks and is not a physical gate. On Colab A100 session `luw-wp1-a-1015`, the first `make Linux -j4` failed because the filter method was private; after updating the header, the build in the same session returned 0 (CLI echoed BUILD2 0). A subsequent single-GPU 10-step smoke test on the same empty-fetch grid succeeded: OpenCL C 3.0 compiled cleanly, initial model index 21, alpha=0.2, exit code 0; see the log and `smoke.rc`. This is strictly a compilation/wiring test, not a 31000-step empty-fetch run or Gate 0 physical validation. The alpha=0.2 in this smoke test is used solely for compilation and wiring, not the production alpha from Tf=10Δ / the frozen mean velocity from the preceding group.
- After launching the background smoke test, `colab-keepalive --detach` was started as required; after execution, our session was stopped and both private and global session lists were verified to contain no `luw-wp1-a-1015`; the keepalive unit is stopped (inactive). The total account balance moved from 1089.52→1087.36 CU, but two other active sessions owned by others were running concurrently, so the difference must not be attributed as the exact CU cost of this task; this task used only this single brief A100 session, well below the wall-clock scale of 30 CU. No over-budget runs were performed.

## Gate Verdict and Reason for Stopping
Gate 0 Not Passed: pointwise comparison between a truly clean HEAD and the switch-off branch has not yet been performed; the single-GPU double-slip mini-channel tests for zero-force conservation and ≤5% agreement of ΣF/ΔPx under forcing have not been run; initialization and checkpoint/restart continuation consistency tests are missing. More importantly, the isolated build only maintains in-process previous/next buffers and **has not yet implemented disk checkpoint recovery for filter values, even/odd step parity, and alpha metadata**; consequently, restart consistency currently has no verifiable interface. A smoke test returning 0 cannot substitute for this evidence. Following the Lead's rule to "stop immediately if Gate 0 does not pass," we did not launch the Gate 1 31000-step runs (first-layer re-verification, second-layer unfiltered, and second-layer filtered), did not modify any gate criteria, and did not run Case E/A. With no new numbers for three-station U2/Uin, actual time-averaged u*, or control-volume closure, no claim can be made that Option A improves or fails.

## Remaining Fixes Needed and Assumed Parameters
- To complete Gate 0: implement filter checkpoint write/read with mandatory verification of grid dimensions, step parity, alpha, and wall-index/inflow metadata; pointwise comparison between a truly clean HEAD and the switch-off branch; single-domain FP16C two-wall slip tests covering random DDF even/odd link parity, zero-force mass/momentum conservation, and ≤5% agreement between velocity-dependent force integration and ΔPx over the warm-up window; pointwise comparison of split-restart continuation runs; and invalid ground-column mask counting. Gate 1 must not be entered before actual measurements are obtained. The existing model macros and counter arrays are for the next revision only and should not be used directly in production.
- For Gate 1 if approved in the future: keep the core domain 500×200×270 m, 1 m, 31000/last 20000 steps, κ=.40, z0=.024 m, U15.9=3.9286416 m/s, and prescribed u*=.2418545 m/s; measure the reference mean velocity from the preceding second-layer unfiltered group and freeze it across three independent cases; average only the last 20000 step-by-step actual forces. Prior empty-fetch runs, design notes, and Asmuth card article 105111-6–9 provide the configuration and time scale; the specific reference mean velocity and window for alpha have not yet been measured and are all marked as "assumed / to be frozen." κ=.40, the criteria, and the budget are likewise project assumptions rather than paper parameters. This line is not an execution record.
- The current actual wall-force columns only output the five y-lines at x=200/300/400; full-boundary instantaneous fluxes and a complete closure algorithm across the entire x=100–400 control volume are not yet implemented, so Gate 1 could not be declared passed even if velocities met the criteria. The output path for the actual wall_tau CSV will only exist after a future full run and does not exist in this attempt.

Literature boundaries: Malaspinas & Sagaut card, printed pp.32–33; Asmuth card in the same directory, article 105111-6–9. The above support the candidate configuration and are not acceptance criteria for this GPU smoke test. No new literature conclusions were added in this task.

# WP1 A Follow-up Test: Gate 0 Failed (Stopped, Gate 1 Not Started)

Time: 10-15 17:07 ET. This file appends follow-up test evidence without modifying the original, the handover directory, or the read-only clone. The Colab A100 session `luw-wp1-g0-1015` has been stopped; no CRC/TACC/workstation solvers were used. Neither the three 31000-step empty-fetch runs for Gate 1 nor Case E/A were started.

## Source Code and Configuration

In the isolated source code of this directory, the filter kernel parameter index was fixed: in `stream_collide(fi,rho,u,flags,t,fx,fy,fz,omega_x,omega_y,omega_z,tau_sum,tau_count,q)`, `q` is the 0-based 13th argument; previous code mistakenly set it to 14, and a 10-step smoke test was insufficient to rule out this error. The current diff `solver_A_gate0_failed.patch` is a failed candidate and must not be used as a production patch. The ground still uses local specular reflection and first-layer Guo forcing; the second fluid cell's previous-step velocity uses a 2D float double buffer sampled before collision. The filter parameter `alpha=0.2` in the small gate channel is solely for wiring verification, not the production Tf; this version does not support restart continuation, and checkpoint/restore for filter state, parity, and alpha must be added before continuation is used. Continuation is not required for this brief.

Gate fixture `gate0_fixture.hpp` and runner `run_gate0_colab.pyground_force[n]=applied_ground_fx` along with full-fluid ρu and ρ. The test-specific upper-wall specular reflection is not a production setting. Wall force is the lattice momentum source term without dividing by rho, compared in the same lattice units.

## Measured Gate 0

- Switch-off equivalence: Both head/off builds and runs exited with 0; across 8 sampled steps (0,1,9,39,80,119,199,200), binary SHA-256 hashes of rho/u/flag matched pointwise. Because `fi` was not exported, the pointwise `fi` equivalence required by the brief is **unverified**; rho/u/flag agreement cannot substitute for the full switch-off gate.
- Zero force: From t=39→199, the x-momentum drift in the 0.05 channel is −0.02581977 (about 0.0234% relative to the final value), and in the 0.12 channel is −0.06371996 (about 0.0240%); the latter has a mass drift over the same window of +0.10217 / 2304 (about 4.43×10⁻⁵). Both are measured numerical errors, with no claim of exact conservation; the drift must be accounted for in the error budget.
- With force: Stepwise over t=40…199, ΣFx=−0.97458596 and corresponding ΔPx=−0.13787241 (initial ux 0.05), giving a relative force-momentum discrepancy of 85.85% > 5%; after increasing initial velocity to 0.12, ΣFx=−5.45993299 and ΔPx=−3.66666458, a discrepancy of 32.84% > 5%. Window endpoint values are taken from the full 201-line per-step record; see calculation scripts. The result cannot be attributed to a single mechanism: FP16C quantization, macroscopic momentum definition / half-step source term, and discrete specular reflection action still need to be isolated separately; theoretical ΣF must never be substituted for measured ΔP.
- Invalid columns: The actual flag array in `gate0_force_step0.bin` has 24×12=288 ground columns in total; judged by the filter kernel's first-layer/second-layer fluid and lower-layer solid criteria, 288 are valid and 0 are invalid. This count holds only for the small gate0 channel; the full-scale empty-fetch run was not executed, so it cannot be claimed to be zero there as well.

## Verdict and Budget

Gate 0 clearly failed on the required forced momentum consistency (neither initial velocity met ≤5%), and switch-off pointwise equivalence of `fi` was not checked. Therefore, following the Lead's sequential hard-gate rule, execution stopped immediately without proceeding to Gate 1; across the three empty-fetch groups, U(2 m), actual time-averaged u*, and control-volume budget are all "unmeasured", and no improvement or gate passage may be claimed. Planned thresholds remain unchanged: Gate 1 requires a 2 m three-station ratio of 0.90–1.05, 2–20 m deviations ≤10% at each height with no opposite signs, actual time-averaged u* deviation ≤10%, and control-volume budget residual ≤10%. The latter two must be re-measured over the full time window at full scale; old velocity proxies are unacceptable.

This named A100 session ran for about 20 minutes, plus an earlier round of about 5 minutes; estimated at 5.4 CU/h wall-clock time, the two rounds total about 2.25 CU (for budget estimation only, not attributed by shared-account balance difference), well below the cumulative 30 CU hard cap. After stopping, `colab sessions` showed only two unknown sessions belonging to others, and this session was no longer listed.

Parameter sources: dd438c1 and the handover are the existing numerical and empty-fetch input sources; κ=0.40, z0=0.024 m, U(15.9)=3.9286416 m/s, u*=0.2418545 m/s, core domain 500×200×270 m, Δ=1 m, and 31000 / last 20000 steps belong to the planned original Gate 1 and **were not run in this round**. The small-channel initial velocities of 0.05/0.12, alpha=0.2, 201 steps, and 24×12×10 are all marked as fixture assumptions rather than literature parameters; Tf=10Δ/〈U(hm)〉 awaits determination from the full-scale unfiltered second-cell group before freezing, and currently has no measured value.

The next step must first isolate the ΣF−ΔP mismatch in the small channel and complete the switch-off equivalence check using the actual `fi` array; the empty-fetch runs will not be restarted until the 5% criterion is met. This is an engineering gate failure, not a scientific conclusion on the accuracy merits of Scheme A.

# Work Package 1: Clearing Scheme A (Second-Cell Time-Filtered Wall Law) Implementation and Empty-Fetch Gate (10-15)

**Decision I made**: After reviewing luw's submission, I am clearing Scheme A—retaining local specular reflection + first-layer Guo forcing, while computing wall stress from the temporal low-pass filtered horizontal velocity at the second fluid cell (1.5 m above the numerical wall). This brief covers only implementation, Gate 0 (reduced to a single GPU and single subdomain), and Gate 1 (equilibrium log-law empty-fetch flow, three groups + at most one Tf sensitivity group), with a hard cap of 30 Colab CU; Schemes B (WALE/Vreman) and C (distribution reconstruction / iMEM) are deferred for now; Case E/A will not be run.
- Why: In the Lab's "unfiltered second-layer" test, the 2 m ratio only reached 0.69–0.79, and temporal filtering was never tested; sampling velocity at the second cell + temporal filtering is a direct literature remedy for log-layer mismatch (Malaspinas & Sagaut 2014, card VV2FSXRQ printed pp.32–33: velocity sampled at the second node, force applied at the first node; Asmuth 2021, card CFJREQTQ_asmuth_2021_imem_abl article pp. 105111-6–9: ESG Tf=10Δx/〈u(zel)〉 mitigates mismatch, mean u* of 1.004). The Lead spot-checked both card entries and confirmed they match the design draft citations. Gate criteria (2 m ratio 0.90–1.05, u* ≤10%) follow the standards set on 10-15 without relaxation.
- Known risks: Asmuth notes in the same passage that even after ESG, the first cell remains slightly slow and the second-cell gradient overshoots; in Case E, the first-layer prototype causes overshoot at open points (in-line data), so even if the empty-fetch gate passes, urban cases may degrade—Gate 2 will be judged separately.
- Cost of being wrong: ≤30 CU and about 1–2 days; no existing results are touched.

## Addendum 10-15 16:45 (Decision I made)
Delegated task report: Scheme A is implemented (patch, 356 lines), compiled cleanly on Colab A100, and passed a 10-step trial run on the empty-fetch grid with exit code 0; however, Gate 0 was not run because the bot halted citing "filter disk checkpoint/restore not implemented" as a blocker.
Verdict: Remove restart consistency from Gate 0—both the empty-fetch flow and Case E are single continuous runs (about 20 minutes) without checkpoints; this version is marked "restart continuation unsupported". The control-volume budget is switched to time-averaged cross-sectional fluxes + time-averaged integral of actual wall force. All other gate items and criteria remain unchanged. Dispatched follow-up to complete Gate 0 and proceed directly into Gate 1 (cumulative budget for this brief remains ≤30 CU).
Cost of being wrong: If long-duration restart continuation is needed in the future, checkpointing and restart consistency testing must be added; this has no impact on current empty-fetch conclusions.

## Addendum 10-15 17:15 (Decision I made)
Delegated task report: Gate 0 failed. Switch-off equivalence matched on rho/u/flag hashes, but `fi` was not compared; zero-force drift was about 0.02%; with forcing, the relative discrepancy between ΣFx and ΔPx was 85.9% at ux=0.05 and 32.8% at ux=0.12 (FP16C). Cost was about 2.25 CU.
Lead interpretation: The Lab's 4.0% wall-force closure was obtained under an FP32 test build (handover line 56), whereas forced closure under FP16C was never tested; since the mismatch decreases as force increases, the primary suspect is FP16C quantizing away small per-step wall-force increments. If true, the Lab's empty-fetch conclusion under FP16C (2 m velocity 20.6% low) must also be re-evaluated.
Dispatched: Run a precision matrix on the same fixture across {FP32, FP16S, FP16C} × {first-layer prototype, Scheme A} + complete the `fi` switch-off equivalence check; if confirmed to be a precision issue, switch production to FP32 (empty-fetch takes ~4.4 GB, Case E ~11 GB, which fits on an A100), run Gates 0/1 directly in FP32, and compare FP32 vs. FP16C no-model empty-fetch runs (cumulative ≤30 CU).
Cost of being wrong: If it is not a precision issue, about 1–2 CU extra is spent on diagnostics; FP32 runs at roughly half the speed of FP16C, adding about 1 CU per empty-fetch run. Basis: No literature basis; grounded in in-line data and FluidX3D `defines.hpp` comments (FP16C is 16-bit compressed DDF storage).

items.text:
# RUN_A_precision — FP16 Storage Diagnostics and FP32 Empty-Fetch Gate

Time: 10-15 18:09 ET. Compilation and solving for this task were performed exclusively on Colab A100; the workstation only packaged source code and analyzed small JSON files. The source baseline is read-only dd438c1; the copy in this directory is an isolated replica, with final diff `solver_A_FP32_gate1_failed.patch` (failed candidate, not to be used as verified production code). Case E/A was not run, and the author's files were not touched.

## 1. Gate 0: Single-Domain Double-Specular 24×12×10, Initial ux=0.05, t=40…199

See the raw 201-line/group per-step records and SHA-256 hashes of the eight snapshot steps; see also the two additional zero-force and constant-force groups. Both compilation and execution exited with 0. HEAD/off comparisons were performed on the same A100, with identical macros and initialization; snapshots now additionally include the full raw `fi` storage along with rho/u/flag. For FP32 and FP16C respectively, the entire binary file hashes matched at 8/8 snapshots; because the raw `fi` bytes matched pointwise, the decompressed `fi` values also matched. This comparison is not a cross-precision pointwise comparison.

Precision | Model | ΣFx | ΔPx | |ΔPx−ΣFx|/|ΣFx|
:--|:--|--:|--:|--:
FP32 | First-layer prototype | −1.716509 | −1.655838 | 3.53% (Pass)
FP32 | Second-cell filtered, fixture α=0.2 | −0.967389 | −0.936539 | 3.19% (Pass)
FP16S | First-layer prototype | −1.742669 | −0.191705 | 89.00% (Fail)
FP16S | Second-cell filtered | −0.975613 | −0.039549 | 95.95% (Fail)
FP16C | First-layer prototype | −1.727033 | −0.895287 | 48.16% (Fail)
FP16C | Second-cell filtered | −0.974586 | −0.137872 | 85.85% (Fail)
FP16C | Constant stress τ=5×10⁻⁵ (fixture assumption) | −2.304000 | −1.780062 | 22.74% (Fail)

FP32 zero-force, first-layer specular reflection: from t=39→199, mass change ΔM=0.000000/2304, horizontal momentum change ΔPx=−0.007978 (−7.21×10⁻⁵ relative to Px at t=39), judged to be within numerical error. The ground fixture has 288 columns with 0 invalid (prior-round flag evidence `gate0_force_step0.bin`); note that this cannot replace the full-scale invalid-column check. Double specular reflection with zero force is not equivalent to HEAD solid-wall bounce-back; the latter reference exhibits slip decay, so its ΔP cannot be used as a zero-force conservation criterion. The filtered version does not support checkpoint continuation; all empty-fetch runs in this task were single continuous runs. Conclusion: All three Gate 0 checks pass under FP32; forced momentum closure fails under FP16S/C. Storage quantization is highly suspect, though this matrix alone cannot prove a single microscopic mechanism; FP16C with enhanced constant force still shows a 22.74% mismatch.

## 2. Gate 1: Identical Equilibrium Log-Law Empty-Fetch Flow, Full FP32

Inputs inherited from the handover: core domain 500×200×270 m, Δ=1 m, plus a 200-cell upper sponge layer, 31000 steps, averaged over the last 20000 steps (mean field every 40 steps, wall force every step), κ=0.40, z0=0.024 m, U(15.9)=3.9286416 m/s, u*=0.2418545 m/s; all four groups compiled and solved with exit code 0. On this actual grid, the second fluid cell center lies at physical z=2 m, i.e., 1.5 m above the numerical wall; this was not quietly changed to physical z=1.5 m. Because the filtered scheme fell significantly short at x=200 m, the sensitivity group—marked as "optional" rather than mandatory in the brief—was not added.

Group | x200 U2/U_inlet | x300 | x400 | Actual stepwise stress u*/prescribed (same 3 stations, 5-y average)
:--|--:|--:|--:|:--
FP32 No model | 0.5960 | 0.6421 | 0.6392 | No wall law, N/A
FP32 First layer | 0.7868 | 0.7905 | 0.8038 | 0.8154 / 0.8318 / 0.8504
FP32 Second cell unfiltered | 0.7223 | 0.7646 | 0.8073 | 0.8313 / 0.8747 / 0.9090
FP32 Second cell filtered A | 0.7390 | 0.7825 | 0.8134 | 0.8471 / 0.8890 / 0.9047

Actual wall-force accounting: Across all 15 sampled columns in each group over 20000 steps, actual per-step tau/ρ was accumulated first before taking the time average and computing u*, rather than substituting mean velocity as a proxy. Out of 59598 interior y-columns along x=100–400, 59341 counted as active while the remaining 257 had no wall force applied; this should be checked against the geometry/boundary mask, and zero invalid columns across the entire domain cannot be claimed.

2–20 m deviation (%); each cell ordered as x200 / x300 / x400, with the full meter-by-meter 228 rows in the output file:

Group | 2 m | 5 m | 10 m | 15 m | 20 m | 2–20 m Max Abs Deviation
:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|--:
No model | −40.40/−35.79/−36.08 | +3.23/+3.32/+1.37 | +5.10/+7.56/+7.80 | +4.96/+6.04/+7.11 | +4.87/+5.55/+5.41 | 40.40%
First layer | −21.32/−20.95/−19.62 | +5.39/+6.96/+6.14 | +5.15/+8.10/+9.60 | +4.56/+5.90/+6.89 | +4.48/+5.10/+5.43 | 21.32%
Second cell unfiltered | −27.77/−23.54/−19.27 | +4.09/+5.20/+3.38 | +4.67/+7.63/+8.75 | +4.47/+6.06/+7.00 | +4.43/+5.23/+5.47 | 27.77%
Second cell filtered | −26.10/−21.75/−18.66 | +4.25/+4.77/+4.96 | +4.53/+7.40/+8.53 | +4.09/+5.75/+6.45 | +4.32/+5.00/+5.11 | 26.10%

All groups exhibit a systematic opposite-sign pattern of "slow at 2 m, fast at 5–20 m"; for Second-Cell Filtered A, all three stations at 2 m fall below 0.90, the maximum 2–20 m deviation is 26.10%, and actual u* at 200/300 m is 15.29%/11.10% low respectively, so it clearly **fails Gate 1**. In the Lab's previous FP16C no-model baseline, x200/300/400 = 0.595/0.636/0.655; the present FP32 run gives 0.596/0.642/0.639, a shift of +0.001/+0.006/−0.016, meaning Scheme A's failure cannot be blamed on FP16C errors in the old no-model baseline.

## 3. Boundaries of the Time-Averaged Control-Volume Diagnostic

`precision_gate1_metrics.jsonlbm_ref_u=0.10`, `si_ref_u=3.9286416`, `si_rho=1.225`. The output computes the **incomplete time-averaged proxy residual / |wall force|** as "inlet − outlet − top + ground wall force": first layer 40.43%, second cell unfiltered 40.89%, filtered 35.65%. Components for the filtered group (integrated over discrete 1 m² surface elements): x-cross-section advection difference +12927.93, pressure difference −9374.47, top outflow +2466.44, ground wall force −1689.31, residual −602.29. See the JSON for the other two groups.

The above is not a strict closure rate: it uses only products of time averages rather than 〈ρux²〉 and 〈ρuxuz〉, and omits both lateral y-faces, Reynolds/SGS/viscous terms, pressure fluctuations, and storage. As an order-of-magnitude warning, in the filtered group the difference in 〈ρ〉k between the two x-cross-sections is about 9989 (an unsigned upper-bound proxy for correlated flux), and the total 〈ρ〉k over the top surface area is about 54935, far exceeding the 1689 wall force; one cannot estimate the missing terms to be under 10% on this basis. Hence the ≤10% **complete** budget gate is not accepted, and an incomplete proxy will not be misrepresented as accurate closure; velocity and actual stress have already independently ruled out Scheme A.

## 4. Budget, Parameter Sources, and Verifiable Files

In this round, two personal A100 sessions (`luw-wp1-precision-1015` and `luw-wp1-fp32-full-1015colab-keepalive --detach`) were used, but because a relative `--config` path was passed, systemd status showed `exec_ok=0`; manual CLI polling kept the session alive, and after stopping the session the keepalive unit was stopped and reported to the platform Lead; an absolute config path must be used next time. Data and solver runs resided solely on Colab, while the workstation retained only scripts, patches, JSON, CSV, and this report with individual file sizes under 200 MB.

Parameter sources: Grid, 31000/20000 steps, κ/z0/U15.9/u*, inlet, and VK settings come from the handover (in-line data); FP32 and half-precision switches come from in-line commit dd438c1.

Recomputed raw small-file results and analyzer. Isolated candidate patch `solver_A_FP32_gate1_failed.patch`; source-code changes are in `defines.hpp`, `setup.cpp` (actual wall force and x-segmentation), `lbm.hpplbm.cpp` (filter buffer and kernel call), and `kernel.cpp` (specular reflection + Guo + filter).

## Conclusion

Single-GPU FP32 passed Gate 0, whereas FP16C/FP16S showed severe forced conservation mismatch; after switching to FP32, all four empty-fetch groups ran to completion, but Scheme A (filtered) yielded U2/U_inlet = 0.7390/0.7825/0.8134 and actual stress u*/prescribed = 0.8471/0.8890/0.9047, failing the established Gate 1 criteria, while a complete control-volume budget remains unproven. We do not proceed to Case E/A in this round; the patch is for diagnostics only and is not cleared for production. It is recommended that the Lead review the numerical wall height / sampling height, local ground stress, and missing control-volume terms before making a decision on the next design; Scheme A accuracy improvement must not be claimed as accepted.

# Work Package 1: Scheme A Failed Gate 1; Switching to Near-Wall Stress Budget Diagnostics (10-15 18:20)

## Results (In-line data, ~4.8 CU, cumulative ~7.3 CU)
- Precision: In the 24×12×10 small-channel forced momentum closure test, FP32 achieved 3.5% for the first-layer prototype and 3.2% for Scheme A (Pass); FP16S showed 89–96% and FP16C showed 48–86% (Fail). However, in the full-scale equilibrium log-law empty-fetch flow, the no-model FP32 2 m ratio is 0.596/0.642/0.639, virtually identical to the Lab's FP16C result of 0.595/0.636/0.655—**precision is not the cause of the slow near-wall empty-fetch velocity, and the Lab's conclusion that "the first-layer wall law is ~20% low at 2 m" holds** (FP32 first-layer is 0.787/0.791/0.804, matching FP16C at 0.785/0.792/0.804).
- Gate 1 (full FP32, 2 m U/U_inlet at x=200/300/400 m; actual time-averaged u*/prescribed): No model 0.60/0.64/0.64; first layer 0.79/0.79/0.80, u* 0.82/0.83/0.85; second cell unfiltered 0.72/0.76/0.81, u* 0.83/0.87/0.91; second cell filtered (Scheme A) 0.74/0.78/0.81, u* 0.85/0.89/0.90. All four groups exhibit the pattern "slow at 2 m, 4–10% fast at 5–20 m". **Scheme A failed** (requires 0.90–1.05 and u* deviation ≤10%). The control-volume budget only has an incomplete proxy (missing turbulent fluxes, etc.) and was not accepted.

## Decision I made
1. Stop tuning Scheme A (do not add Tf sensitivity runs): Filtering changes the 2 m ratio by only −0.05 to +0.01 relative to the first-layer prototype, with an unstable direction and far short of 0.90.
2. Pivot to mechanism diagnostics: Wall stress is already 10–18% below the prescribed value while near-wall wind remains too slow, indicating insufficient downward momentum transport within z=2–4 m rather than excessive wall drag. My working hypothesis: on a 1 m grid, the Smagorinsky mixing length CsΔ≈0.17 m is much smaller than κz (about 0.6–0.8 m at z=2 m), and resolved turbulence in the first two or three cells cannot sustain u*², causing an overly steep velocity gradient. I dispatched luw to output vertical profiles of resolved Reynolds stress, subgrid-scale (SGS) stress, and total stress in the same empty-fetch flow; if confirmed, run a single-factor group with "near-wall mixing-length enhancement" (l=max(CsΔ, κ·wall_distance)) + a control group using WALE from Scheme B of the design draft (see delegation on the project page, ≤22 CU, cumulative ≤30 CU).
 - Note: WALE/Vreman has an even smaller near-wall eddy viscosity than Smagorinsky, so if the hypothesis holds, it may act in the opposite direction; it is retained as a control rather than the primary candidate. The Lab's Mason–Thomson damping (which reduces near-wall mixing length) was ineffective, consistent with the direction of this hypothesis.
3. In parallel, delegate litwiki to build literature cards for Brasseur & Wei 2010, Kawai & Larsson 2012, and Porté-Agel et al. 2000 to verify the causes and correction directions for near-wall log-layer mismatch for citation in the next design step.
4. Compile all wall models in FP32 during the development phase (small-force closure fails under FP16; GPU memory is sufficient for both empty-fetch and Case E).
- Basis: In-line data; Shin et al. 2025 card CXEWT5EB PDF pp.12–14 (filtering only mitigates one source of mismatch, namely spurious velocity–friction velocity correlation); the working hypothesis (insufficient mixing length) **currently has no literature basis** and awaits confirmation from the litwiki cards and diagnostic data.
- Cost of being wrong: If diagnostics show total stress is balanced, the near-wall mixing-length enhancement group will not be run, spending only ~2–3 CU on diagnostics; worst case is ~22 CU.

## Addendum 10-15 19:00: Literature Cards Ready, Revising Interpretation Criteria
litwiki built three cards (Brasseur & Wei 2010 PDF pp.9–11 / journal 021303-8–10; Kawai & Larsson 2012 PDF pp.8–10 / journal 015105-7–9; Porté-Agel et al. 2000 PDF p.7 / journal p.267). All three agree: whether to enhance or damp near-wall SGS stress depends on Φm(z)=κz(∂U/∂z)/u* and the resolved-to-subgrid stress ratio, and cannot be judged solely from a slow mean velocity; Brasseur & Wei's classic regime (first-layer SGS dominance with balanced total stress) calls for **damping** SGS stress, opposite to my initial hypothesis.
luw's intermediate data (final report pending): In the first-layer prototype at x=200 m and z=1–2 m, total stress is only about 0.29–0.58 of the prescribed u*², where first-layer SGS dominates but the total magnitude is insufficient—this is a different regime from Brasseur & Wei's "excessive SGS with balanced total stress" and instead supports "insufficient total stress". With mixing-length enhancement (increasing l up to κ·wall_distance within the lowest 10 cells), the 2 m U/U_inlet ratio reaches 0.95–1.00 and the u* ratio reaches 1.05–1.14; with 70% enhancement, 2 m U/U_inlet is 0.92–0.96 and u* is 0.98–1.08 (the 70% factor was obtained by tuning). These are intermediate results, awaiting full y-averaged stress profiles and the formal report before a final verdict. Sent `--note` requiring the report to include Φm and TR/TS and to explicitly label 70% as a tuned parameter.

items.title: RUN stress budget — FP32 Empty-Fetch Stress Profiles and Near-Wall Mixing-Length Single-Factor Comparison
items.text:
# RUN_stress_budget — FP32 Empty-Fetch Stress Profile and Single-Factor Near-Wall Mixing-Length Comparison

Time: 10-15 19:03 ET. Compiled and solved exclusively on Colab A100; the workstation was used only for source packaging, small-result analysis, and SVG generation. The input is an isolated copy of `stage_precision_full` under `A_impl`, keeping the first-layer prototype specular reflection + Guo wall force and FP32 unchanged; all cases share the same 500×200×270 m core domain, 200-cell top buffer, 1 m resolution, and 31000 steps, sampling every 40 steps over the last 20000 steps (500 samples), with specified κ=.40, z0=.024 m, and u*=.2418545 m/s. Neither Case E nor Case A was run, and `A_impl`, the handoff record, and the read-only clone were not modified. Two of the four runs share the exact same physical configuration for the first-layer prototype: the 5-line diagnostic and the subsequent full-y diagnostic; the 2 m ratios from both runs are identical.

## 1. Full-y Stress Diagnostic (First-Layer Prototype)

True omega: after `stream_collide` completes the calculation of the local Smagorinsky relaxation rate w, ν_t=(1/w−1/def_w)/3 is sampled from the same kernel at x=200/300/400, y=1…198, z=1…30, with unit conversion using the median u*/sqrt(tau_lattice) of 57.0388 m/s per LU from the actual wall-force output (rather than 3.9286416/.1 used in the incomplete CV proxy from the previous round). At the same 500 time steps, ux, uz, and uxuz are sampled; we first compute −(〈uw〉−〈u〉〈w〉) across time and y, and then multiply 〈ν_t〉 by the 〈u〉 gradient across adjacent heights; the viscous term is 1.48e−5∂〈u〉/∂z. This definition follows the specified 〈ν_t〉∂〈u〉/∂z rather than a strict instantaneous SGS stress average, using the solver's actual omega rather than back-calculating from the Cs constant. All stresses have dimensions of m²/s² (expressed after dividing by density); scalar u is the x-component. The dataset contains 17820 points with 500 samples per point, alongside a 90-row meter-by-meter summary across the three stations; the numerical wall lies 0.5 m above physical zero height. Ground stress is accumulated from the actual step-by-step applied force across 197 active columns at each x-section (1 column out of 198 interior y-points had no applied force) and averaged over the active columns; fluid stress is averaged across all 198 interior y-points, and this mask discrepancy is noted as a limitation. Piece-wise non-stationarity and top-boundary effects may prevent the total stress from being strictly constant, so this profile does not represent a full control-volume closure rate.

Measured full-y stress (per cell: resolved / SGS / total stress / total stress ÷ measured local wall stress at that station; viscous stress on the order of ~1e−5 is included in total stress):

| x m | z=1 m | z=2 m | z=3 m | z=4 m |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | .0020 / .0177 / .0197 / .462 | .0148 / .0191 / .0339 / .796 | .0238 / .0111 / .0349 / .820 | .0267 / .0049 / .0316 / .742 |
| 300 | .0025 / .0182 / .0207 / .465 | .0210 / .0189 / .0399 / .895 | .0343 / .0111 / .0454 / 1.020 | .0380 / .0062 / .0441 / .990 |
| 400 | .0027 / .0183 / .0210 / .446 | .0241 / .0176 / .0417 / .885 | .0397 / .0097 / .0494 / 1.049 | .0443 / .0055 / .0498 / 1.056 |

Measured τ_wall/ρ: x200/300/400=.04257/.04455/.04712 m²/s²; specified u*²=.058494. At z=1, total stress is only 44.6–46.5% of the local true wall stress, with a resolved contribution of ~.002–.003 and SGS dominating but still insufficient; at z=2, it reaches 79.6–89.5%, with resolved stress already at .015–.024. At z=3–4, stress already approaches the wall stress at x300/400 while remaining low at x200, so the claim that "the entire 2–4 m layer lacks transport" is not confirmed; the lowest near-wall cell indeed lacks transport, meaning the Lead's directional assessment is supported by data but requires height qualification. Relative to the specified u*², the z1 ratios are .336/.354/.359 and the z2 ratios are .580/.682/.713. See visualization `total_stress_fully.svg`, where the red line denotes the specified stress and the short dashed line denotes the measured local wall stress.

The re-verified first-layer 2 m U/U_in=.7868/.7905/.8038 matches the three previous values exactly. The 17820 rows were downloaded and verified alongside the generated profile, without erroneously re-running the solver due to a post-processing path error.

## 2. Single Factor: Near-Wall Mixing-Length Enhancement Only

The first-layer prototype Guo/specular reflection, other LES/inflow settings, and all statistical configurations were kept unchanged. For Smagorinsky in `kernel.cpp`, CsΔ=sqrt(.76421222/(18sqrt(2))) cells; height above the numerical wall is z_w=layer+.5 m. For z_w≤5.5 m, we use `l=CsΔ+a max(κ z_w−CsΔ,0)`, linearly tapering a to 0 across 5.5<z_w<9.5 m, and restoring the original CsΔ above that. One group was tested with `a=1`; after its u* slightly exceeded the threshold, a second group with `a=.70` was tested under the same mode for single-factor amplitude sensitivity. Both the linear taper and .70 are working assumptions rather than literature values; the local mixing length is l≈.2 m in the first cell and up to l≈.6 m in the second cell. The primary implementations (with the single-kernel diff in `mixing07_kernel.diff`) are not intended as production patches.

| Group | U2/U_in at x200/300/400 | 2–20 m Max Abs Deviation (3 stations) | True Step-Wise Time-Mean u*/Specified (3 stations) | U2 Ratio Re-Referenced to 0.5 m Numerical Wall (3 stations, reference only) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Original first-layer | .7868/.7905/.8038 | 21.32/20.95/19.62% | .8154/.8318/.8504 | .8406/.8445/.8587 |
| Mixing length a=1 | .9951/.9866/.9540 | 4.36/4.02/5.32% | 1.1444/1.1107/1.0493 | 1.0631/1.0540/1.0192 |
| Mixing length a=.70 | .9586/.9496/.9172 | 4.46/5.04/8.28% | 1.0762/1.0422/.9836 | 1.0241/1.0146/.9798 |

Both enhanced groups achieve U2 within [.90,1.05] at all three stations, with meter-by-meter absolute deviations ≤10%; for a=1, the true u* at x200 and x300 exceeds the specified value by +14.44% and +11.07%, failing the ≤10% threshold; for a=.70, the three-station u* deviations are +7.62%, +4.22%, and −1.64%, meeting the individual threshold. However, Gate 1 cannot be declared passed on this basis: for a=.70, 2 m is slow by −4.14%/−5.04% at x200/300 while 5, 10, and 20 m all show positive bias; at x400, 2 m is slow by −8.28% while 10 and 20 m are positive, retaining the prohibited "slow at 2 m, fast aloft" sign structure. The a=1 run also retains this sign structure at x200/300, albeit with smaller amplitude. Representative values (x200/300/400) for a=.70: 5 m ratio 1.0244/1.0225/.9989, 10 m 1.0179/1.0305/1.0190, 20 m 1.0442/1.0440/1.0530; complete meter-by-meter results can be recomputed from the three output sets. Re-referencing to the numerical wall is for diagnostic purposes only and does not replace the formal physical-inlet criterion.

WALE was omitted in this round: obtaining the full velocity gradient tensor and neighbor flags at fluid cells under Esoteric-Pull, and then implementing WALE tensor invariants/limiting and missing-neighbor boundary interpolation, is estimated at >150 lines plus an additional off-equivalence/conservation short test; an unverified simplified WALE cannot be compared on equal footing against these two full empty-fetch runs. The original brief explicitly permitted omitting WALE if implementation exceeded roughly 150 lines. The negative assessment here is only a mechanistic clue from the present SGS/resolved stress structure, not an empirical conclusion on WALE.

## 3. Resources, Parameters, and Boundaries

Sessions `luw-stress-1015` (5-line diagnostic + enhanced a=1), `luw-stress-tune-1015` (a=.70), and `luw-stress-fully-1015` (full transverse 198-line completion) have all been stopped and confirmed absent from `colab sessions`; the two A100 instances belonging to others were untouched. Each detached job launched a keepalive with an absolute config, all showing `exec_ok>0`; no long jobs lost connection. Based on session durations of ~22+10+10 minutes at 5.4 CU/h, this task consumed ~3.78 CU; combined with ~7.3 CU previously, the cumulative total is ~11.08 CU, well below the 22 CU task cap and 30 CU work-package cap (attributed by session rather than shared account balance). Neither TACC/CRC nor workstation solving was used.

Parameter sources: grid/steps/window/inlet z0, u*, and κ come from this track's baseline specifications; SGS constants and computed omega come from the `SUBGRID` branch of the isolated build, and molecular viscosity 1.48e−5 m²/s comes from `setup.cpp` in the same build; the actual unit conversion factor 57.0388 is governed by the stress outputs and `total_stress_fully.svg`. The previous round's CV proxy used 39.2864 and omitted fluxes, so this report does not treat it as complete closure evidence.

## Conclusion

Full-y stress decomposition confirms that momentum transport in the bottom-most cell is significantly insufficient and z2 remains low, whereas 3–4 m already approaches equilibrium at downstream stations. Enhancing the near-wall Smagorinsky mixing length raises the empty-fetch U2 ratio from .787–.804 to .917–.995; at a=.70, both the true u* and meter-by-meter amplitudes fall within their prescribed numerical ranges, but the opposite bias signs across heights remain, failing the unmodified Gate 1. Case E/A cannot be cleared, and WALE was not empirically tested. Next steps should investigate first-cell wall-stress transfer and the numerical-wall reference frame under the same FP32/empty-fetch configuration so that near-wall amplitude and profile sign meet the criteria simultaneously; if the Lead wishes to revise the gate criteria, a separate verdict is required rather than relaxing them automatically based on these results.

# Work Package 1: Near-Wall Mixing-Length Enhancement Approaches Gate 1; One-Off Case E Urban Diagnostic Authorized (10-15 19:10)

## Results (Track Data, ~3.8 CU; Work Package 1 Cumulative ~11.1 CU)
- Full-transverse (198-line) stress decomposition, first-layer wall law: at z=1 m, total stress is only 45–47% of the measured local wall stress (resolved 0.002–0.003; SGS 0.018 dominates but is insufficient), 80–90% at z=2 m, and already near equilibrium at z=3–4 m for x=300/400 while remaining low at x=200. → Insufficient momentum transport in the bottom one to two cells is supported by the data; this differs from the "excessive SGS, balanced total stress" overshoot regime of Brasseur & Wei 2010 (card NR_brasseur_wei_2010_law_wall_scaling, PDF pp.9–11 / journal 021303-8–10).
- Near-wall mixing-length enhancement (l=CsΔ+a·max(κz_w−CsΔ,0), z_w≤5.5 m, linear taper across 5.5–9.5 m, assumed values):
 - a=1: 2 m U/U_inlet 0.995/0.987/0.954; u*/specified 1.14/1.11/1.05 (exceeds 10% at x=200, 300).
 - a=0.70 (obtained via tuning): 0.959/0.950/0.917; u* 1.08/1.04/0.98; 2–20 m max deviation 4.5/5.0/8.3%; however, the "slow at 2 m, fast aloft" sign residual persists.
- WALE not implemented (>150 lines to implement; omitted as permitted by the brief).

## Decision I made
1. **Gate 1 is not considered passed, and the criteria remain unchanged.** Amplitude and u* meet the targets, but the sign residual remains; a=0.70 was tuned on the gate itself and cannot serve as independent validation. Note also that the no-model and first-layer baseline runs are 4.5–5.5% fast at 20 m, meaning the upper-layer positive bias may contain domain/inlet components unrelated to the wall model; a baseline-subtracted check has been requested (for reference only).
2. **Authorize a one-off Case E urban diagnostic (not Gate 2)**: FP32, first-layer wall law + mixing-length enhancement with both a=0.70 and a=1.0, matching the Lab's cont5 urban diagnostic configuration; compare against no-model 0.116 and first-layer wall law 0.149 (scalar-approximation MAE). Do not run Case A, and do not tune a/κ/z0 against urban MAE (≤10 CU).
- Why: the Lab already knows that the first-layer wall law alone degrades Case E (overshoot at open points) and that "the ground boundary layer is not the primary error source in Case E." Before spending more CU smoothing out the empty-fetch profile sign, we spend ~5–8 CU to see whether Case E improves, stays unchanged, or degrades once the near-ground treatment is improved as a whole, informing the decision on where Work Package 1 should focus next (continue on ground / pivot to building walls / wrap up).
- Cost of being wrong: ≤10 CU; if the urban results were misread as validation, they would be misleading—the task brief explicitly states "diagnostic only; do not claim improvement or acceptance."
- Basis: data from this track; for literature context see Brasseur & Wei 2010, Kawai & Larsson 2012 (NR_kawai_larsson_2012_wall_modeling PDF pp.8–10 / journal 015105-7–9), and Porté-Agel et al. 2000 (NR_porte_agel_meneveau_parlange_2000_scale_dependent PDF p.7 / journal p.267); the specific functional form and coefficients of the mixing-length enhancement **have no literature basis** and are working assumptions of this track.

# In-House Immersed Boundary Method (IBM): Initiating Design Draft (10-15 19:30)

Liang Hu asked: "Can we handle the immersed boundary ourselves?"

**Assessment: Yes.** Supplementary Material S5 of the paper describes an immersed boundary method based on a "three-point regularized delta kernel + multi-direct forcing" (Eqs. 33–38; audit row 12, supplementary PDF pp.9–10 / internal pp.61–62). This is a standard method in the open literature (Peskin-type delta function, direct forcing, multi-direct forcing), not a proprietary algorithm unique to the authors; implementing it ourselves from the equations does not require the authors' code. Once implemented, what we obtain is an "IBM implemented according to the S5 equations"—which still cannot be called "the paper's version," but is sufficient as our own platform tool.

**Decision I made**:
1. Task `litwiki` with retrieving the official supplementary material PDF (locally we only have the arXiv main text, not `mmc1`) and building a literature card, transcribing S5 Eqs. 33–38 and their parameters equation by equation, and tracing the primary source literature for the method.
2. Task `luw` with producing a 0-CU IBM design draft: the implementation path inside the FluidX3D kernel (whether the existing marker-point interpolation/spreading mechanism in the `PARTICLES` extension can be reused), interfacing with voxel solids and the existing ground wall model, an honest assessment of whether it helps or hurts near-wall probes <1 m from walls, the verification gates (conservation → single-body drag coefficient against literature → Case E/A), and a CU estimate.
3. Defer the decision on whether to implement until both the design draft and the Case E urban diagnostic return; neither consumes GPU resources.
- Why: Work Package 2 originally had to wait for Liang Hu's approval to contact the authors before obtaining the immersed boundary implementation; building it in-house removes our dependency on their reply. The remaining errors in Case E are concentrated at near-wall points, making building-wall treatment the next logical link to tackle.
- Known risks: a three-point kernel smears the wall over roughly ±1.5 grid cells, which may not improve probes located <1 m from the wall on a 1 m grid; on 1 m building resolution, standard IBM merely replaces a "staircase wall" with a "diffuse soft wall." The design draft must address this point head-on.
- Cost of being wrong: 0 CU for the design; if implemented, estimated at 20–40 CU and several days of work. Licensing: any modified code published externally must release its source code, same as the wall model.
- Basis: audit records from this track; primary IBM method literature awaits card creation by `litwiki` (no specific page numbers cited before the card is verified).

items.text:
# RUN_city_diag — Case E West-Wind Authorized Diagnostic, Not Gate 2

Time: 10-15 20:26 ET. Compiled and solved exclusively on Colab A100; the workstation was used only for small-file packaging and 80-point statistics. Gate 1 remains unpassed, and this urban diagnostic does not clear Case E/A. All three runs in this round completed 31000 steps, extracted the 80 points, and exited with code 0; however, an exit code of 0 by no means implies a physically valid field. Raw 80-point outputs, registration checks, analysis scripts, summary metrics, and point-by-point tables have been recorded; large VTK files were not saved to the workstation.

## Configuration and Comparability

Across the three isolated source builds `stage_mix07`, `stage_mix10`, and `stage_mix00`, FP32 (`FP16C` and `FP16S` both disabled) and first-layer local specular reflection + Guo wall force were used. `stage_mix07` uses the SGS mixing length `L=CsΔ+0.70 t(z_w) max(κ z_w−CsΔ,0)`; `stage_mix10` changes only 0.70 to 1.0; the additional FP32 first-layer control `stage_mix00` sets the coefficient to 0. Here t is 1 for z_w≤5.5m and decays linearly to 0 across 5.5–9.5m; z_w is height above the numerical wall, and κ=.40. The enhancement acts on **all fluid cells** satisfying the global near-ground condition, including street-canyon ground columns and fluid near buildings; this is neither a canyon-specific height scaling nor a building-facade wall function, so changes cannot be interpreted solely as upstream flat-fetch conditioning. The parameter a, transition height, and global application are all experimental assumptions of this track with no literature parameter provenance.

Case E West wind 270°, PF 500×500×270m, 1m resolution, base_height=20m, 470 vertical cells total including top sponge, TI=.1621087892, integral length scale L=100m (existing assumption), windward inflow only, 31000 steps, sampling statistics/TKE every 40 steps over the last 20000 steps. Geometry clips the original 9210-triangle STL by x−760/y−750; across all 3 runs, the 10m zero-velocity solid/STL registration achieves IoU=1 (5996/5996) at offset (+1,+1,0)m, with no position tuning against MAE. All 80 points use official After Construction W wind-tunnel probes at physical z=2m; `S=|〈u⃗〉|`, `S*=sqrt(S²+2k):32–43`, referenced against R10a.

## 80-Point Statistics (MAE / Pearson r / Simulated Mean ÷ Wind-Tunnel Mean)

| Group | S Vector Magnitude | S* Scalar Approx | x=25/42m Upwind U2/Uin2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R10a old no-model FP16C | .1401 / .7838 / .8211 | .1160 / .8009 / 1.0565 | .7375 / .5190 |
| cont5 old first-layer FP16C | .1517 / .7836 / .9544 | .1485 / .8122 / 1.1968 | .9448 / .7807 |
| Current first-layer a=0 FP32 | 8.3417 / −.0447 / 20.2725 | 10.8601 / .0579 / 26.0911 | 12.6793 / 12.7735: anomalous / invalid |
| Current first-layer a=.70 FP32 | 1.6443 / −.3329 / 4.7989 | 5.1648 / .2089 / 12.9327 | 2.7490 / 2.7801: anomalous / invalid |
| Current first-layer a=1.0 FP32 | .2062 / .6518 / .5711 | .1721 / .6591 / .6583 | .9764 / .8695: descriptive value, stability unverified |

The first two rows are historical references only, not repeat runs from this round. Although the solver exited with code 0 and mask registration was normal for a=0 and a=.70, the 2m mean velocities near the inlet reached ~12.7× and ~2.75× the inflow velocity, respectively, and resolved k at one probe in a=.70 reached 206.65m²/s², which is clearly unphysical; the MAE/r values in these rows are fault-diagnostic numbers only and **must not be interpreted as measured urban accuracy or tuning effects**. While a=1.0 has a plausible order of magnitude, it contradicts the instability seen in the same-precision first-layer control; without time-series stationarity or mass-conservation diagnostics saved, it cannot be deemed physically valid either, nor can MAE .1721 be used to claim improvement. The exact stochastic turbulence realization and instability mechanism across runs have not yet been isolated. Furthermore, the pre-solve stress-diagnostic `setup.cpp` retained fixed-index stress-probe readout code indexed for the 500×200 flat domain, which does not correspond to the intended locations on the 500×500 urban grid; although unused in the point metrics above, urban-specific code cleanup and off-equivalence regression were not performed in this round and must be audited first.

## Pre-Specified Subsets and Point-by-Point Direction

Each cell below reports S* MAE / r / simulated-to-observed mean ratio; formal near-wall IDs are 50/51/52/54, and open-area IDs are 23/25/37/17 (**not the same subset** as 4/39/44/75 in the old cont5 report, and must not be conflated).

| Group | 4 Near-Wall Points | 4 Open-Area Points | S* Increase/Decrease vs R10a; Abs Error Improved/Degraded Points |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R10a no-model | .3454 / .7514 / .2506 | .3456 / .9825 / 1.4682 | — |
| cont5 first-layer | .2944 / .8676 / .3612 | .3917 / .9641 / 1.5306 | 64/16; 31/49 |
| FP32 a=0 (anomalous) | 9.7570 / .7657 / 22.1730 | 10.6734 / .5657 / 15.4566 | 80/0; 0/80 |
| FP32 a=.70 (anomalous) | 4.7570 / .7660 / 11.3229 | 4.9895 / .6620 / 7.7580 | 80/0; 0/80 |
| FP32 a=1.0 (stability unverified) | .4164 / .8566 / .0963 | .1339 / .9008 / .9694 | 2/78; 24/56 |

Point-by-point S, S*, observations, changes relative to no-model, and 8-corner fluid counts are recorded in the output tables. Run a=1 is lower at near-wall points while closer to observations at the four open-area points; taken together with the two unstable same-precision controls, this shows that urban MAE cannot currently be used to rank a, let alone fit a, κ, or z0 against MAE.

## Baseline Subtraction for Empty-Fetch Sign (Reference Only, Gate Unchanged)

Subtracting the same-height ratios of the FP32 empty-fetch no-model baseline cell-by-cell from those of the enhanced group yields "enhanced bias minus no-model bias." For a=.70 at x=200/300/400m: 2m +36.27/+30.76/+27.79 percentage points; 5m −.79/−1.07/−1.49; 10m −3.31/−4.51/−5.89; 20m −.46/−1.15/−.11. This shows that under the physical-inlet reference, the upper-layer positive bias includes a common domain/inlet component; after subtraction, the sign flips to strongly positive at 2m and weakly negative aloft, which **does not** mean a=.70 passes Gate 1, nor is it an unbiased estimate of true error. Under the original physical-inlet reference, 2m remains −4.14/−5.04/−8.28% and 5–20m remains predominantly positive; per the Lead's verdict, Gate 1 is not passed.

## Cost, Verifiability Boundaries, and Decision

In this round, the private Colab session `luw-citydiag-1015` has ended and `colab sessions` lists only others' sessions. Raw mean-field VTKs and detailed solver logs remained on the terminated ephemeral VM and were not persisted; the small result JSONs and packaged source SHAs remain verifiable, though this limitation prevents reconstructing the exact onset time and details of the instability from surviving data, so one should not speculate on which single factor among FP32, SGS, inflow, or wall force was responsible.

**Determination**: This authorized diagnostic has been executed, but the FP32 same-precision first-layer baseline and a=.70 produced anomalous fields, while a=1 lacks stationarity verification; urban differences cannot serve as a valid test of model accuracy improvement. For the next round, we recommend first freezing an identical stochastic inflow in a new short urban fixture, saving step-by-step domain means/extrema and conservation metrics, and removing flat-fetch fixed-index diagnostics from the prototype source before isolating the unstable operator; we should not tune parameters directly or proceed to Case A / Gate 2. This recommendation is a data-driven diagnostic from this track with no literature basis, and is not an additional pre-approved run.
