results.text:
# RUN_city_isolate — Case E FP32 No-Model / FP16C First-Layer Wall-Law Isolation (Not Gate 2)

Time: 10-15 22:59 EDT. Two single-GPU Colab A100 private sessions `luw-iso-r1-1015` and `luw-iso-r2-1015` have been stopped. The input is `city_isolate_inputs_v2.tar.gz` (SHA256 `095ff9c4dc5cca06c3cb0179b68e1e46ce48ce8cf0a7cd8a3cb3819ad1ba36ba`), generated from the Case E configuration and cleaned source code. Only the read-only `CITY_STABILITY_MONITOR` instrumentation was added; in R1 all new model switches are off with FP32, while in R2 `FP16C` and `GROUND_WALL_MODEL` are enabled with `LUW_GROUND_MIX_A=0.0`; no other physical parameters were tuned, and Case A was not run. Both compilation and solver execution were performed on Colab, with the workstation used only for small-file statistics.

## Instrumentation and Boundaries

Every 200 steps, `city_stability.csv` is written and flushed, recording `rho u·n`, `ΔM+∫flux`, and truthfully marking `previous_wall_force=unavailable`. The initial non-finite value actually occurs between the last finite monitoring step and the current detection step, rather than at an exact step-by-step onset instant. `ground_first` refers to the fixed flat ground at z=21 with solid directly below, while building-adjacent cells are separately identified via solids in the 26-neighborhood.

## Execution and Localization

R1: Compilation exited with 0; non-finite values were detected at t=20400 and the run terminated with exit code 1, with the last all-finite monitoring step at t=20200. The first cell hit by the scan was (133,143,1), with non-finite rho, flag=0 (fluid), and 26-neighborhood solid/equilibrium/fluid counts of 18/0/8; it is not at the first flat-ground layer z=21, and is adjacent to building solid cells; at t=20200 the same cell had rho=0.999961 and |u|=0.000031 lattice, with wall-force history unmeasured. The inventory at t=20400 excludes non-finite cells and can no longer be treated as valid total mass. Across finite records, the maximum velocity magnitude was 0.202302 and the t≥3000 rho range was [0.942918,1.058101], neither crossing the immediate-stop thresholds beforehand. The non-finite onset time is localized only to (20200,20400], and the first scanned cell in the same sampling row cannot be proven to be the very first failing cell across the entire domain during those 200 steps. The earlier FP32 first-layer a=0 run failed at t=18800, so the present R1 proves that non-finite values can appear in the FP32 urban domain even without the new wall law; the issue is not unique to "wall law × FP32". Random inflow, open boundaries, voxel buildings, instrumentation invocation timing, and other factors in the FP32 kernel cannot yet be ruled out.

R2: Compilation exited with 0, solver exited with 0, ran to completion at t=31000, and sampling / 80-point extraction exited with 0. Monitoring recorded 155 rows; maximum velocity magnitude was 0.198380 and t≥3000 rho was [0.940359,1.059689], with no immediate velocity/density stop; however, the 1000-step inventory change rate first exceeded the previously recorded 0.05% criterion at t=4000 (+0.068947%) and reached a maximum absolute value of −0.667346% at t=12600; open-domain inventory variations must be distinguished from boundary fluxes, and the entire revised stability gate cannot be declared passed. From t=3000 to t=31000, the inventory changed by +0.304738%, below the 0.5% warning threshold.

The first 1000-step inventory exceedance and maximum change are nearly identical between the two runs (R1 +0.068768%, −0.667335%; R2 +0.068947%, −0.667346%), indicating that such inventory fluctuations are not triggered solely by the new wall law or FP32. The time-series mean net outward flux across the five faces is approximately +511.748 (R1) and +345.738 (R2) lattice mass/step, with west/east at approximately −20195.830/+20706.995 (R1) and −20361.491/+20706.995 (R2); the north and south means are each within ±2, and the top face is 0. This serves only as a macroscopic boundary-face proxy, and the residual after step-by-step subtraction against non-solid inventory cannot be attributed to numerical mass leakage: macroscopic u differs from the true DDF cross-boundary flux, density boundary assignment, and time integration. Full face-by-face raw quantities are provided in the two CSV files.

## 80-Point Comparison (Same +dx Registration; S = Vector Velocity Ratio, S* = √(S²+2k) Scalar Approximation)

R1 failed early, leaving no valid final-20000-step 80-point statistics, so the FP32 no-model baseline was not measured in this round. For R2, S: 80-point MAE=0.137408, r=0.810526, mean ratio=0.886422; S*: MAE=0.115630, r=0.826070, mean ratio=1.087715. Near-wall points 50/51/52/54 have MAE of S=0.385953, S*=0.318662; open points 23/25/37/17 have MAE of S=0.252365, S*=0.287465. At x=25/42 m, 2 m U/U_inlet = 0.916780/0.748637. Registration and raw 80-point values are recorded in the output files.

Historically in the Lab, the FP16C no-model S* MAE was 0.116, and the FP16C first-layer wall law was 0.148517 (verbally ~0.149); the present R2 is also FP16C first-layer wall law, but yields S* MAE=0.115630, so it cannot be claimed to "reproduce the Lab cont5 urban accuracy". The mean point-by-point absolute difference between the previous first-layer 80-point results and the corresponding S* values here is approximately 0.04965. Unverified differences remain between the execution setup of this cleaned version and the older version (source code, instrumentation, random inflow, or statistical inputs), and identical precision macros and wall-law macros cannot be equated to an identical numerical experiment. The R2 log explicitly lists `Ground wall first fluid index=21, z0 lattice=.024`.

## Resources, Deliverables, and Next Steps

The two sessions ran from ~22:29 to ~22:49 (R1) and ~22:56 (R2) EDT; conservatively estimated at 5.4 CU/h on A100, the total is <5 CU (against a 6 CU budget for this work order); with the work package previously estimated at ~22.2 CU, the cumulative total is <27.2 CU, still below the 32 CU limit relaxed by the Lead after this work order. Both keepalive processes used absolute configs and reached `state=done`; traces and logs were downloaded prior to stopping; neither CRC/TACC nor solver execution on the workstation was used.

Evidence: corresponding logs, `iso_r1_solver.exit`, `iso_r2_solver.exit`, packaging and run scripts, and instrumentation files are all stored in the local artifact directory without overwriting previous `RUN_city_full` or older results.

Verdict: R1 itself failed, so the next priority is single-factor isolation of the baseline FP32 Case E: compare clean HEAD without monitoring against FP16C no-model under identical source conditions, and record the first non-finite value at GPU kernel entry/exit and wall-adjacent fluid cells rather than relying solely on sparse 200-step readbacks. Although R2 ran to completion, its accuracy differs substantially from the old cont5 run, so an item-by-item diff of configuration, source code, and statistical definitions should be conducted first; no wall-law improvement is claimed on the basis of its MAE. Empty-fetch Gate 1 remains unpassed, and Case E/A Gate 2 is not cleared.

results.text:
# Scheme C Phase 0: Offline Audit of Case E Link q

10-15 ET. Offline geometry processing on workstation with Python 3.10 / numpy 1.21.5; LUW was not compiled or run, no GPU used, 0 CU. Read-only input at HEAD dd438c1; reusing `read_case_e`, `clean_mesh`, and `voxel_proxy`: out of 9210 STL triangles, the trailing 12 outer base-plate faces are stripped, retaining 9198 faces with x−760 / y−750 and z unchanged, identical to the cropping and registration in `bootstrap_r10.py:14–23`. Small output files are written to the current directory; the initial diagnostic output is preserved as-is and is not used for the final figures below (the initial pass did not cross-check building intersections on ground links). Re-computation command: `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python3.10 link_q.py --out new_empty_dir`; test command: `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3.10 -m unittest discover -s . -p test_link_q.py -v`. All 4/4 unit tests passed in this round, with a runtime of ~97 seconds.

## Mask Definition and Intersection Ownership

The voxel proxy uses 500×500×62 (z=0…61) cell centers `(i−1,j−1,k)`, filled via half-open horizontal cross-sections of the STL and x-direction parity rules, with 0 odd-intersection rows. Additionally, the entire z=0 layer is marked as ground solid, placing the numerical ground wall at z=0.5 (ground link q=0.5), while buildings use STL ray–triangle intersections. This proxy is not cell-for-cell identical to `voxelize_mesh` in GPU `kernel.cpp:2385–2465` (which uses integer truncation, ray corrections, column-wise flag flipping, and GPU ground TYPE_S); it covers only the lower 62 m and excludes the true top of the urban domain and open-boundary flags. Cell indexing follows `k*500*500+j*500+i`; direction indices strictly follow `link_q.DIRS` rather than confirmed LUW discrete velocity indices—actual solver wiring must map to native D3Q19 directions and cross-check flags.

After bucketing STL triangle bounding boxes, each directed fluid→solid link is tested for line-segment intersection using double-precision Möller–Trumbore; the minimum q is taken, where the triangle ID is the 0-based face index in the cleaned STL. Multi-face intersections at the exact same q along shared edges or vertices are logged as duplicate hits and resolved by retaining the smaller triangle ID, which does not represent multiple independent walls. Ground links (z=1→0) are initialized to q=.5; if the same link also intersects a building face with q<.5−1e−6, the nearest intersection (building) takes precedence; ties in q retain ground ownership. This nearest-hit / tie-to-ground rule is an engineering assumption that has not been physically validated. Endpoint hits with q≤1e−7 or q≥1−1e−7 are not forcibly clamped into (0,1), but listed separately as unresolved links for half-way bounce-back fallback or geometry repair; links with no triangle hit at all do not fabricate intersection positions. Fluid→fluid links that pierce thin surfaces were not searched, so zero missed thin-wall intersections cannot be claimed on this basis.

## Summary and Handoff Risks

Total proxy fluid–solid links: 2,094,178; valid links strictly satisfying 0<q<1 and avoiding endpoints: 2,079,413 (building: 1,115,596; ground: 963,817). Unresolved links: 14,765, comprising 14,764 endpoint hits with q≈0/1 (of which horizontal roof / cell-center coincidences at z=8 account for 14,591) and 1 link with no triangle hit at proxy cell index (164,239,3), direction index 15; unresolved xy proxy coordinates span (79,79)…(407,408), with height-by-height distributions and link-by-link records saved in the output files. Raw multi-triangle hits occur on 28,373 links, including 26,666 ground links that simultaneously intersect building triangles; among those, the nearest hit is assigned to buildings on 13,948 links (the remainder going to ground or endpoint handling). Equidistant ties occur on 19 links. Multi-face hit counts include shared-edge duplicates and must not be interpreted as overlaps between distinct building entities; the STL contains 34 non-manifold edges, so strictly outward-pointing normals across all faces cannot yet be certified.

Across the full valid table, q<.5 accounts for 539,221 links (all 539,221 on buildings) and q≥.5 accounts for 1,540,192 (576,375 building, 963,817 ground). Bucketed across [0,.01,.1,.25,.5,.75,.9,.99,1], the counts are 9,691 / 84,139 / 191,352 / 254,039 / 1,316,428 / 144,469 / 70,037 / 9,258; extreme values are 9,691 for q<.01 and 9,258 for q>.99. The default ground value q=.5 forms the large central peak; for buildings alone, the .5–.75 bucket contains 352,611 links. The overall directional distribution and the complete sparse table are saved in the output files: `cell` uint32, `direction` uint8, `q` float32, `owner` uint8 (1 building / 2 ground), `triangle` int32 (ground −2), at 14 bytes per record; the compressed file is 8,503,111 B (< 50 MB). Unresolved links are excluded from this production-candidate table, and missing values must never be silently defaulted to q=.5 inside the solver.

Following the Bouzidi et al. (2001) reference card, print pp. 3453–3454 / PDF pp. 3–4, Eqs. (6a,b): oriented along our fluid→solid link direction, quadratic upwind interpolation for q<.5 requires the second fluid node along the reversed link (2 steps back from the starting node), whereas the downwind branch for q≥.5 requires at least the original time-level distribution 1 step back, and both require specific time levels of local and reversed distributions; because the original formulation mixes pre- and post-collision time levels, Esoteric-Pull odd/even addressing must never be implemented via naive array offsets. Stepping 1 cell back (for q≥.5): 1,443,081 proxy fluid, 92,120 solid, 4,991 out-of-proxy-domain; stepping 2 cells back (for q<.5): 404,059 fluid, 118,772 solid, 16,390 out-of-domain. For the latter two categories (solid or out-of-domain neighbors), degrading to half-way bounce-back while logging counts is recommended. Here "out-of-domain" does not distinguish between true open boundaries (`TYPE_E`) and exceeding the top of the proxy box; since the proxy only covers z≤61, these numbers cannot be directly interpreted as Case E GPU open-boundary counts. These figures represent a conservative neighbor-availability screening; actual source terms, q≥.5 time levels, and numerical stability must be validated at the single-GPU FP32 gate.

## Four Near-Wall Points (R11 Raw Coordinates and Sampling Shifts Must Not Be Conflated)

Following phase0, R11 coordinates use the xls→PF registration offset of (+1010.50008,+1000.60004,−0.10) m, and after PF xy cropping inspect the sampling center shifted by (+1,+1,0) m at sample height z=2 m. The 3×3×3 neighborhood below covers integer grid nodes around the sampling center, including ground links; the link-by-link q list, individual intersection coordinates, and shifts from the half-grid location to q are recorded in the output files. Displacement is defined as (q−.5)|c|, where a positive sign means the wall lies closer to the solid cell center along the fluid→solid link direction—this is not the normal distance from the measurement point to the wall; the statistical range mixes multiple wall orientations, so extreme values must not be treated as a single wall shift for that point.

| Point | R11 Wall Dist. (m) | ROI Valid Links | q Range | Shift Range vs. Half-Grid (m) | Non-Half-Grid Links |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| 50 | 0.84 | 105 | .071–.938 | −.606 to +.619 | 69 |
| 51 | 0 | 49 | .047–.800 | −.641 to +.424 | 26 |
| 52 | 0.22 | 41 | .133–.800 | −.519 to +.424 | 28 |
| 54 | 0.57 | 41 | .123–.805 | −.533 to +.431 | 28 |

Errors for the flat plate at x=.25 (q=.25), cube face at x=.4 (q=.4), and axial intersections between unit-sphere octahedron vertices and an analytical sphere (q=.5) are each <1e−6, passing all 4 unit tests. Triangular approximations of non-vertex points on a sphere will not strictly equal the analytical sphere q, so the tests make no claim that curved-surface discretization error is <1e−6.

Decision I made: Model the ground at z=0 with an independent owner ID at numerical half-grid wall q=.5, and resolve links that simultaneously hit buildings by nearest intersection with ties going to ground — avoiding double bounce-back on the same link; if actual GPU ground flags or wall positions differ, ownership will be misassigned, requiring q to be rebuilt after checking against the native GPU mask. Additionally, explicitly separate endpoint hits rather than silently clamping to q=ε — because horizontal roof faces coincide with grid centers at a high rate, boundary ownership requires an independent verdict.

## Conclusion

The lower-62 m proxy link-q table and corner-ownership audit for Scheme C have been generated (0 CU), but this is not yet a qualified wall table ready for direct upload to LUW: 14,765 endpoint/missed-intersection links remain unresolved, 26,666 links intersect both ground and buildings, the proxy has not been compared cell-by-cell against native GPU flags, and z>61 has not yet been audited. The next steps are to resolve endpoint ownership and verify against native flags, validate two-branch distribution addressing at the single-bluff-body gate, and only then discuss urban-scale accuracy.

# RUN_city_cavity — Case E Underground Cavity and cont5/R2 Offline Audit (Non-Gate 2)

Time: 10-15 23:23 EDT. This task opened zero Colab sessions and neither compiled nor ran the solver (0 CU). All inputs were accessed read-only, and the offline audit script executed cleanly.

## Task 1: Evidence Gap and Verifiable Facts on Native Flags

The earlier off-equivalence check recorded only the matching SHA256 digest of the 117,500,000-byte flag array between `HEAD` and `off` without archiving the raw per-cell `flags.bin` file locally (nor is it inside any of the five input tarballs; the temporary Colab VM that held the binary has since been stopped). A SHA256 hash alone cannot be inverted to recover per-layer cell counts or 6-connected components, and the `phaseC0` lower-62 m voxel proxy must not be substituted for the GPU's native flags.

In R1 (`isolate_stage_v2`), `setup.cpp:6073–6093` marks `z=0` and lateral boundary cells at `z ≤ ground` as solid, whereas the domain-wide sub-ground solid fill at lines `6176–6196` executes only when `use_profile_dem_ground` is true. Under the current flat-ground configuration, this makes "fluid pockets remaining inside buildings below `z=20`" a source-code-supported hypothesis awaiting test, though native STL voxelization and 6-connectivity to the upper flow domain remain unmeasured here.

Consequently, per-layer solid / fluid / equilibrium-boundary counts across `z=0…20`, closed-cavity counts and horizontal slice PNGs, and the cavity membership of `(133,143,1)` and its 8 neighbors are all **unmeasured** in this offline audit (reported as unmeasured rather than `0`). Likewise, `rho` at `(133,143,1)` at step 31,000 of R2 was not saved: the R2 trace logs only domain-wide extrema/totals and the preceding sample at abort time, while the summary file stores only 80-sensor time-averaged velocity and TKE; point `rho` cannot be back-calculated from an exit code or flag hash.

## Task 2: Actual Inputs, Source Code, and Evaluation Protocol Between Lab `cont5` and R2

The Lab's `prepare_caseE_cont5.py:5–27` copied `profile.dat` and the configuration from the working directory at that time, cropped the STL (`x − 760`, `y − 750`), and converted the full domain to `500×500×270`, 1 GPU, west wind, `31,000` steps / last `20,000` steps averaged every `40` steps, `TI = 0.1621087892`, `L = 100`, and windward von Kármán inflow. Re-applying those exact text substitutions offline to the archived baseline configuration reproduces R2's `.conf` file **character for character**. Neither configuration sets an explicit `vk_inlet_seed`; R2's `setup.cpp:270,287` defaults to seed `100` using `mt19937_64` at line `794`, and comparing against the surviving `eqlog` source tree shows identical von Kármán RNG logic (differing only in wall-law and diagnostic additions). However, because the complete execution source tree and seed log of `cont5` were not archived in full, identical `.conf` text alone does not prove step-by-step bitwise identity of the stochastic inflow.

Crucially, **the inflow profile files are NOT identical**: the baseline `profile.dat` included in the Lab handover is a 12-point profile (13 lines), whereas the actual `profile.dat` used in R2 is a 3,001-point profile (3,002 lines) with a different SHA256 (`…6d7cba`). Comparing velocities at shared heights shows: at `2.5 m`, `3.042` vs `2.814912 m/s` (R2 is `7.47%` lower); at `5 m`, `3.2604` vs `3.231133 m/s` (`0.90%` lower); at `50 m`, `5.109` vs `4.620754 m/s` (`9.56%` lower); at `100 m`, `6.162` vs `5.039711 m/s` (`18.21%` lower); and at `250 m`, `7.8` vs `5.593646 m/s` (`28.29%` lower). In R2, `U(2 m) = 2.681427 m/s` and `U(15.9 m) = 3.9286416 m/s`. Note that the solver internally interpolates a 12-point input file onto a 3,001-point runtime lookup table (so `Uref` on line 34 of the `cont5` report and `"3001"` on line 67 of the R2 log do not by themselves prove whether `cont5` fed in the 12-point or 3,001-point file); confirming the exact input file used by `cont5` requires checking the original `cont5` tarball or run log. This inflow profile mismatch is a strong primary candidate to explain the MAE difference, though other code differences co-existed so we do not claim it accounts for 100% of the `0.0329` MAE gap without a single-factor test.

On the source-code side, the handed-over `cont5` directory preserves `defines.hpp`, `lbm.cpp`, and `lbm.hpp` plus `solver_wallmodel_cont5_final.diff`, but omits `setup.cpp` and `kernel.cpp`; compared with `cont5`, R2 adds the `GROUND_WALL_FILTER` and `CITY_STABILITY_MONITOR` macros (enabling the latter at compile time), step-by-step ground wall-force accumulation, dual filter buffers (filter disabled), and the runtime parameter `a` in `lbm.cpp`/`lbm.hpp`. Both `run_isolate_remote.py:22–32` (R2) and `run_city_cont5.py:9–16` (`cont5`) ran with `FP16C` + `GROUND_WALL_MODEL` (`a=0`), differing only in R2's added read-only stability monitor and force accumulation.

On the 80-sensor evaluation protocol: both `run_city_cont5.py:17–23` and R2's `run_isolate_remote.py:52–59` invoke the exact same `extract_a_r10.py` script (`lines 84–90`), applying the identical `(+dx, +dx, 0)` registration offset, `S = |time-averaged vector velocity|`, and `S* = sqrt(S² + 2k)` where `k` is resolved TKE from the mean field, normalized by `Uref = 3.9286416`. Sensor IDs, `After W` wind-tunnel observations, `Uref`, and the 8-corner fluid-cell counts per sensor match 100% between the old and new sample tables. Point-by-point comparison between the two runs shows a mean absolute difference in `S*` of `0.049646` (max `0.196878`, changing at `80/80` sensors), `0.042704` in `S`, and `0.173799 m²/s²` in TKE (`cont5` `S*` MAE = `0.148517` vs R2 = `0.115630`). Thus the discrepancy is **not** an artifact of sensor coordinate registration or `S*` formula differences.

## Task 3: Conditional Decision and Next Steps

Because neither prerequisite ("closed underground cavities exist" and "the first non-finite cell lies inside a cavity") could be verified offline without the raw native flags binary, per the task instructions **we neither modified the `z≤20` flag mask nor launched a 31,000-step FP32 no-model GPU run**, leaving the short-run GPU budget untouched. In the next task, we should first export the compressed per-cell native flags across `z=0…21` (with SHA256) during Case E initialization to perform layer-by-layer counting and 6-connected flood-fill from the inlet; only if closed cavities are confirmed to contain the first failing cell should we test a single-factor `z≤20` solid fill under FP32. In parallel, device-side per-step reduction should capture the exact first non-finite `rho` cell and step, while `cont5` vs R2 reconciliation should lock down the **exact `profile.dat` SHA256** first.

Decision I made: With the two cavity prerequisites unverified, hold off on the conditional GPU rerun — avoiding misattributing inflow-profile or connectivity differences to cavity filling; cost if wrong is deferring the cavity map and new MAE by one task cycle. All findings above rest strictly on in-line data and source-code auditing, with no literature extrapolation. Empty-domain Gate 1 has not passed, and Case E/A Gate 2 remains closed.

# Plan C Phase 1: Pre-Implementation Addressing Audit (Did Not Pass Feasibility Gate)

10-15 23:29 EDT. Audited against read-only clone HEAD `dd438c1`; an independent source snapshot resides in the working directory without solver modifications or compilation. No Colab session was created and no solver was run, consuming 0 CU for this work order. The conclusions below derive solely from line-by-line inspection of the raw source code and offline symbolic unit tests, not from GPU flow verification.

## Completed Offline Artifacts

Using native LUW D3Q19 direction indices (matching baseline `kernel.cpp:890–893,949–958` item by item), sparse `(cell:uint32, direction:uint8, q:float32, owner:uint8)` tables were generated for analytic flat-plate and infinite-cylinder geometries. Periodic along z, with no table entries generated on other outer boundaries; intended strictly for small-domain geometry and wiring design without using the Case E STL proxy. The flat-plate q=.25 table has 642 valid links and 12 links with insufficient fluid fallback cells; the flat-plate q=.75 table has 648 valid links and 6 with insufficient fallback cells; the test cylinder has 264 valid links, comprising 12 with q<.5, 252 with q≥.5, and 0 undetermined intersections. These are geometric counts on a `44×12×3` pedagogical domain, not a DFG mesh and not GPU native flags. The three NPZ files are stored in the artifact directory. Running `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python3.10 -m unittest discover -s . -p test_analytic_links.py -v` passed 6/6 tests, covering native direction pairing, analytic q values, table-key uniqueness, and even/odd address symbolic tracing.

## Blocker: Frozen Gate 0(b) Is Incompatible with BFL Eq. (6)

In Bouzidi, Firdaouss, and Lallemand (2001), printed pp. 3453–3454 (formula note printed p. 3454 / PDF p. 4, Eqs. (6a,b)), both branches at q=1/2 strictly reduce to `f_{opp}(r,t+1)=f_i^c(r,t)`, meaning the post-collision distribution from step t returns at step t+1. The current stationary `TYPE_S` in LUW is not this single-step-delayed half-way bounce-back. Its implementation in `kernel.cpp:1338–1351` uses Esoteric-Pull: let odd direction `i` point toward solid neighbor `j[i]`; when `t` is even, `store_f` writes `f_i^c(r,t)` into `(j[i],i)`; at `t+1` (odd), `load_f(r)` for the opposite direction `i+1` instead reads `(j[i],i+1)`, which still holds the earlier packet; only at `t+2` does it read `(j[i],i)`. Solid cells are skipped by `stream_collide` at `kernel.cpp:1489–1490` (and the corresponding location in stage2) and do not swap their two channels at `t+1`. The local two-channel storage for even outgoing directions produces the same two-step time delay. Offline unit tests with time-stamped packets confirm: writing `new_t0` at `t=0` returns `old_odd` at `t=1` and returns `new_t0` only at `t=2`.

Consequently, "enabling `LINK_IBB` with all q=.5 matches current `TYPE_S` pointwise" and "implementing Eqs. (6a,b) as the operator for all q (including .5)" cannot hold simultaneously unless the flow field happens to be at steady state. Special-casing q=.5 back to the legacy branch would mechanically pass a hash check, but would introduce a one-step temporal jump in the q→.5 limit; that would not be a valid verification of the BFL operator and is particularly unsafe for unsteady DFG lift / Strouhal number (St) evaluations. This blocker cannot be resolved by FP32, additional CU, or mesh refinement, nor can the Lead's gate be unilaterally altered by ignoring this requirement. A sound path forward requires a verdict from the Lead: either retain pointwise equivalence with HEAD when disabled while comparing enabled q=.5 against an independent *same-time-level* half-way bounce-back reference, or redefine a new interpolation operator consistent with LUW's legacy two-step delay and establish separate literature backing and verification rather than calling it BFL Eq. (6). If the former is chosen, an independent post-collision snapshot and a separate scatter kernel (avoiding cross-thread read/write races on `fi`) must be used and verified item by item across both direction parities, single-writer solid walls, 1- and 2-cell fallbacks, and endpoint degeneracies before proceeding to channel order-of-accuracy and DFG tests.

## Gate Status and Resources

Gate 0(a) disabled equivalence: uncompiled / untested; Gate 0(b) under the frozen definition: confirmed incompatible between the addressing scheme above and Eq. (6), cannot be claimed passed; Gate 0(c) flat-plate Poiseuille/Couette analytic profiles and second-order convergence: untested; Gate 0(d) closed-domain mass drift: untested. Degenerate links above reflect only offline pedagogical-domain counts, not GPU measurements. Gate I: `c_D,max` / `c_L,max` / St at D/Δx=20, 40 (80), staircase-cylinder comparison, convergence order, runtime, and VRAM footprint are all unmeasured; fabrication is strictly prohibited. For DFG 2D-2 parameters — H=.41 m, D=.1 m, cylinder center (.2,.2) m, ν=.001 m²/s, mean U=1 m/s, maximum inlet velocity 1.5 m/s, Re=100, and coefficient normalization — see PDF pp. 3–4; for the estimated intervals in original Table 4, see PDF p. 13 (the additional tolerance frozen by the Lead is not the original paper's value). Pedagogical domain dimensions, plate positions, and cylinder radii are local unit-test assumptions, not DFG parameters. No GPU was used in this work order (0/10 CU); the GPU budget for Work Package 1b remains untouched.

## Conclusion

An executable small-case generator for analytic q has been produced, verifying native directions and critical time levels; however, the audit revealed that LUW's existing `TYPE_S` stationary-wall return differs from BFL q=.5 by one time step. Under the unmodified Gate 0(b), BFL Eq. (6) cannot be honestly verified; therefore, the solver was not modified, no GPU runs were executed, and neither the channel nor DFG gates were entered. A verdict is requested first on the reference operator and acceptance definition for q=.5 to avoid expending CU on two mathematically incompatible requirements.

# RUN_city_stage3 — Case E Official Inflow, Native Flags, and FP32 Model-Free Isolation (Not Gate 2)

Time: 10-16 00:21 ET. Solver executed solely on a single Colab A100 GPU; the workstation only copied small files and performed 22-layer mask connectivity analysis. This Case E run did not complete the scheduled 31000 steps and therefore cannot produce the 80-point accuracy baseline over the final 20000 steps. Earlier empty-fetch cases were not modified.

## Inputs and Actual Execution

- Source code comes from an isolated copy; the run enables only `CITY_STABILITY_MONITORconf.luwpf` with byte-for-byte identity, SHA256 `ad7ee2cc69e5f858d20d98569ff4160746919b2ab8cfdf51502eb452de697ba7`; all other Case E inputs remain the isolated versions, so only the inflow profile is isolated here (alongside denser monitoring and mask export).
- Previously misused eqlog 3001-point profile SHA256 `77d7532e37b506aff9e7bb54baced7c534dc69f1b8aea519d2d7c9d52e6d7cba`; stage3 official 12-point profile SHA256 `[已隐去] samples | 12`, `Angle | 270 deg`, grid 500×500×470, single A100 40 GB GPU.
- The first attempt compiled successfully, but during initialization flag export `RESULTS` had not yet been created, causing an exit with `cannot open native flag file` before any time-stepping; this log is retained. Adding `create_directories` in our stage3 code and retrying under a fresh remote root produced the actual input archive `city_stage3_inputs_v2.tar.gz` with SHA256 `027189de71cee74c9412462686c9ba696b00eae8548016226c808be4ac7fb116`. The old archive was not overwritten. The second attempt compiled and initialized successfully.
- For all future Case E urban runs, work should start from this isolated version with the official profile; the eqlog profile from A_impl must no longer be carried forward. This version is not a production release cleared through Gate 1.

## Native Mask and 6-Connectivity Audit

After device voxelization and profile boundary assignment, and prior to the first time step, the solver writes out the true `lbm.flags` for z=0…21 (500×500 uint8 values per layer in x-fastest order); the compressed NPZ (20506 bytes) was downloaded from Colab without conflating the voxel proxy with native flags. The remote SHA256 of the raw binary is `8c94137d0362a61370ced20de9b990e627ccd9e19eb81924c72d99f45d11f26a`. Details of the script, full layer table, and connected components are in the output files, along with the distribution plot.

z=0: 250000 solid, 0 fluid; z=1: 1996 solid, 248004 fluid; z=2…20 per layer: 249499 solid, 501 fluid; z=21: 51586 solid, 1996 equilibrium boundary, 196418 regular fluid. Treating non-solid cells as traversable under 6-connectivity starting from the western inlet at x=0, within the exported 22 layers there are **0** regular fluid cells in z≤20 disconnected from the inlet; another 798 cells not connected to the inlet within the 22-layer slab all lie at z=21 and may connect via unexported layers z≥22, so they cannot be classified as enclosed cavities. The first cell hit by the old R1 scan at z=1, (133,143,1), has flag=0, and its connected component within the 22 layers is already connected to the western inlet and also reaches z=21; all 8 fluid neighbors originally recorded also belong to the inlet-connected component in this native mask. Consequently, this audit **rules out the cavity-filling premise that "the R1 cell lies inside an enclosed cavity"**; z≤20 was not modified, and no conditional cavity-filled rerun was launched. Connectivity is audited only for z≤21, without claiming that component memberships in higher layers are proven.

## FP32 Run Results with the Official Profile

The second attempt targeted 31000 steps with a full host-field scan and immediate CSV flush every 50 steps; the last completely finite scan occurred at t=27600, and at t=27650 the first scan hit with non-finite rho occurred at **(147,394,21)**, flag=0, with a 26-neighborhood solid/equilibrium/fluid breakdown of **13/0/13**—located on the first above-ground open layer adjacent to a building. At the preceding monitoring step, the same cell had rho=1.002526 and |u|=0.001660 lattice. The true onset time can only be bounded within (27600,27650], and the first cell encountered in the scan order is not guaranteed to be the earliest cell to fail across the entire domain; propagation direction cannot be inferred. Upon termination, the solver exited with code 1; the entire run was model-free and wall-force-free. Across valid scans, max|u| peaked at 0.193852 lattice (< 0.3), and for t≥3000 the finite-field rho range remained within [0.949984,1.063502] (inside [0.90,1.10]); the mass value reported on the non-finite row excludes corrupted cells and cannot be used for mass inventory or budget closure. Face-by-face macroscopic ρu·n and open-domain mass inventory are recorded in the output files and do not represent discrete distribution-function boundary fluxes or exact mass closure.

The user-requested "on-device any-reduction every 50 steps" **was not implemented in this version**: in practice, the run retained the legacy instrumentation using GPU macroscopic-field readback followed by CPU traversal every 50 steps. This discrepancy adds overhead and provides only a 50-step detection window; step-by-step GPU kernel onset localization cannot be claimed as complete. It remains an acceptance gap for this task and should be resolved in the next standalone update via on-device reduction / minimum-index capture, rather than portraying the present sampled hit as the exact onset.

Compared with the erroneous eqlog profile, the new official profile delayed the model-free scan failure (old R1 failed at t=20400 at (133,143,1), though with an old 200-step vs. new 50-step monitoring interval and at a different location); this shows that inflow contamination affects both historical MAE comparability and the instability pathway, yet **did not eliminate FP32 non-finite fields**, so the root cause cannot be attributed solely to the inflow profile. Because the run did not finish, the 80-point S/S* MAE, r, and mean ratio for FP32 model-free remain unmeasured and must not be extrapolated from partial statistics.

## Resource Usage and Boundaries for Next Steps

This single Colab A100 session ran from ~10-15 23:38 to 10-16 00:21 ET, consuming an estimated ~3.9 CU at 5.4 CU/h (including the first export-path error and the second 1824.5 s solver run; estimated by session duration rather than shared account balance attribution), within the 4 CU cap for this task. With keepalive absolute config, status `done` and `exec_ok=9colab status` confirm that this session has terminated, with no CRC/TACC or Case A runs active. The ground sub-project previously used ~27 CU, bringing the cumulative estimate with this task to ~30.9 CU—below the 32 CU cap temporarily relaxed by the Lead, though this cumulative figure is likewise a session-duration estimate.

Evidence files (all in the current directory): (hash of the initial archive; the actual retry archive hash above governs), `city_stage3_inputs_v2.tar.gz`, `stage3_native_flags.npz`, `stage3_solver_final.exit`, .

Decision I made: Do not perform a z≤20 cavity-filled rerun, because native flags confirm that the old first-failure cell is connected to the inlet; halt at the non-finite field per branch (iii), and prioritize adding exact on-device capture and localizing the first-failing operator at the building/ground interface as the next step. The trade-off is that this round neither obtained a stable 80-point FP32 model-free baseline nor evaluated urban wall-model enhancements. The above assessments rely solely on data from this track without literature attribution; empty-fetch Gate 1 is not yet passed, and Gate 2 for Case E/A remains held.

# Stage 3 FP16C Saturation Branch Source-Code Audit (10-16 EDT)

This addendum is a static source-code audit only, with no compilation or solver execution; existing results and data remain untouched.

Summary: In our recent runs, FP16C was disabled in favor of FP32. When FP16C is enabled, device-side distribution storage maps to `float_to_half_custom`; in the actual GPU conversion implementation, the return expression lacks an explicit `(e>127)*0x7FFF` saturation term and carries the comment `assume [-2,2]`. By contrast, the host-side conversion function does include the `(e>127)*0x7FFF` saturation term. Consequently, we cannot claim that our GPU FP16C path has enabled the optional saturation described in Lehmann's paper, nor can we conclude from the completion of the FP16C run alone that saturation suppressed the FP32 instability; when out-of-range values occur on the device, exponent truncation via bit masking may produce other non-physical mappings. Determining whether that range is reached requires logging actual DDF extrema or running controlled conversion tests, for which no measurements currently exist.

Basis: In-line source code inspection as described above; for literature comparison, see PDF p.5 §III.A.4. This finding does not alter the non-finite detection at t=27650 in the official-profile FP32 no-model run, nor does it clear any urban accuracy conclusions.

# Option C Follow-up Trial: Standalone GPU Addressing Diagnostics (Gates 0/I Not Completed)

10-16 00:38 EDT. The approved objective for this run was single-GPU FP32 LUW solver LINK_IBB implementation, Gate 0(a–d), and DFG 2D-2 Gate I. In practice, only the narrower standalone CUDA diagnostics below were completed, which cannot be treated as passing any gate. Both of my Colab A100 sessions `luw-ibb-c1v2-1016` and `luw-ibb-c1v2b-1016` have been stopped; rough usage is estimated at less than ~1 CU (not attributed from Colab billing), below the 10 CU limit. The workstation only handled scripts and CSV/plotting without running the solver; the read-only clone was not modified.

## Executed

Using a CuPy RawKernel, the odd-even indexing of `load_fstore_f` was ported verbatim and compared against a standalone explicit one-step half-grid bounce-back on a small 8×12×4 D3Q19 FP32 domain. Two cases—initial shear release and constant body force 2e−6—were each iterated for 2000 steps, recording two-layer u_x and velocity-sum proxies at every step for the first 20 steps and every 10 steps thereafter. The second run fixed an initialization error from the first trial: the native side must emulate LUW's odd-step `store_f` write layout and cannot directly share a flat explicit distribution with Esoteric-Pull. The first run is retained as a failure record of invalid initialization; only the second run is used for the exploratory observations below.

After fixing initialization, at step 1 of shear release the first fluid layer gives native=0.04899998 and explicit=0.03899999, and at step 2 gives 0.03008332 and 0.02587499, respectively; over the first 20 steps, the maximum absolute difference is ~0.0100 in the first layer, ~0.001873 in the second layer, and ~0.352 in the velocity-sum proxy. Under constant body force at step 2, the first layer gives 2.6667e−6 vs. 2.3333e−6; over the first 20 steps, the maximum first-layer difference is ~4.72e−7. Figure attached. These curves are not a simple one-step shift; there are additional differences in initial state and collision/boundary details between the solver-native and explicit implementations. This diagnostic did not even implement the LINK_IBB q-table or the two BFL branches, so no verdict can be reached from these curves on the Lead's "pointwise agreement vs. one-step shift" dichotomy. The symbolic inference from the previous round is not misrepresented as numerically confirmed.

## Unfinished Work and Reasons

The two BFL branches and sparse q-table were not integrated into LUW, and its 6 offline tests remain only a q-generator rather than a GPU operator.

Parameter sources: the 8×12×4 domain, initial state 0.06, body force 2e−6, and BGK ω=1.25 are all assumptions made for this diagnostic; they are not DFG literature parameters. References for the two BFL branches and DFG targets remain as in the previous version, with no new literature or benchmark validation produced in this run.

Decision I made: Do not submit a LINK_IBB patch that has not been wired into the main LUW solver and tested for unsteady equivalence, and do not run DFG on that basis — to avoid passing off differences in a standalone toy kernel as real solver validation; the cost is that this run does not deliver the planned GPU operator and gate numbers.

## Conclusion

Only standalone GPU temporal-addressing exploration was completed; Option C remains unimplemented and has not passed Gate 0/I. Current data cannot determine whether LUW native TYPE_S and BFL q=.5 agree pointwise or differ by one step; a verdict must be reached via the unsteady paired tests specified in the brief after wiring the q-table and two-branch operator into the real LUW solver.

# RUN_city_nan_forensics — Case E FP32 No-Model First-Occurrence Instrumentation Attempt

Time: 10-16 01:56 (EDT). This task did not complete first-failing-operator forensics; the records below document actual compilation, runtime, and downloaded evidence, without misrepresenting an unreached instability onset as localized.

## Budget Deviation and Termination

Our Colab A100 session ran from 01:05:53 to 01:56:24 (~3,031 s), consuming an estimated **4.55 CU** at 5.4 CU/h and exceeding the ≤3 CU task cap by ~1.55 CU. Cause: the first build exposed private access restrictions on `fi`/`gi`, and the second run failed with OpenCL kernel argument mismatch (`-49`, 9 device parameters vs 11 bound in C++); after fixing the bindings, the third run reached step ~21,481 when cumulative session cost was noticed to have crossed the cap. We immediately sent `SIGTERM` (exit code −15) to the solver process, downloaded the logs, and stopped the Colab session without resuming or restarting any GPU. This is an execution overrun rather than an approved budget increase. The estimate includes compilation, diagnostics, and idle session time, and excludes balance changes from other concurrent users.

## Verified Input Version and Instrumentation

Inputs used the official AIJ 12-point profile from `stage3` (verified SHA256 `4fc0eede9c5e62bff57127ba176591da4fc7e30723ae51eaddacabb8b41c05fa`). `conf.luwpf` specifies no thermal boundary parameters; although this profile branch imports no thermal boundary with `T`, the temperature distribution `g_i` still evolves along the D3Q7 path in `initialize` and `stream_collide`, so "no thermal boundary" must not be misstated as "temperature extension not compiled". Body-force inputs are initialized to zero, while thermal coefficients and SGS remain at baseline code settings.

The `city_nan_min` kernel scans non-solid `rho`, `ux`, `uy`, and `uz` on the GPU at every step, recording the minimum linear index via `atomic_min`; `city_corner_index` selects fluid cells on native flags that have ≥12 solid neighbors in their 26-neighborhood; `city_corner_snapshot` and `city_nan_neighborhood` capture the 27-cell current-step neighborhood upon trigger. The instrumented solver compiled cleanly on Colab (`BUILD 0`), ran to step ~21,481, and output a candidate count of **316,909**; because no non-finite value had occurred prior to manual termination, only the candidate count was produced — with no earliest failing cell coordinates, 5-step `f_i` history, or operator attribution. Temperature and `omega` values were not measured at a failing cell in this run, and recomputing `omega` offline cannot substitute for the instantaneous `w` inside the collision kernel.

Offline statistics on the earlier native `z≤21` flags export showed 269,214 fluid cells meeting the solid-neighbor threshold across the lowest 22 layers (248,004 at `z=1` and 11,691 at `z=21`), whereas the device-wide full-domain count here is 316,909; the two cover different vertical extents. Low-layer 3×3 slices around the earlier scan hit `(133,143,1)` were plotted, while layer `z=22` for `(147,394,21)` was absent from the partial export and explicitly marked missing in the plot; both coordinates came from **earlier every-50/200-step scans** rather than a step-by-step first-occurrence capture. The plots show only exported 3×3×3 local geometry and do not establish causal onset.

Forensic limitations also remain: the ring buffer covers only pre-selected corner candidates, so if the minimum failing cell lies outside that candidate set, no 5-step precursor history is recorded for it; the remaining 26 neighborhood cells are snapshotted only at the trigger step without a 5-step history; and snapshot `omega` is estimated from current `f` rather than intermediate collision variables inside the kernel, which cannot by itself rule out SGS as the initial trigger. The full 27-cell 5-step intermediate operator forensics requested in the brief were not delivered due to early termination.

## Verifiable Artifacts

- Isolated build & input bundle: `city_nan_stage4_inputs_v6.tar.gz` (exact archive uploaded in this run).
- Runner wrapper & patch progression: first attempt hit `fi`/`gi` private access; second attempt had 9 device arguments vs 11 C++ bindings (error −49); third attempt explicitly passed the thermal arguments to the diagnostic kernel and ran cleanly.
- Raw logs from the third run (exit code −15) and read-only geometry slices from the saved `z≤21` native flags.
- Colab session `luw-nan-forensics-1016` was stopped and confirmed `not found`; keepalive ran with absolute config path and verified `exec_ok > 0`.

## Verdict

No new first-occurrence step was reached prior to manual termination at step ~21,481, so we cannot determine whether `rho→0`, `f_i`, SGS, or `g_i` fails first; absence of a trigger before step 21,481 must not be treated as stability through 31,000 steps. No Case E accuracy metrics were produced, and no wall treatment scheme is cleared. Because the task budget was exceeded, no further GPU sessions will be launched under this task without fresh resource authorization from the Lead. All scientific assessments rely strictly on in-line runtime data, with no literature attribution.

results.text:
# RUN_city_ma010 — Case E FP32 No-Model, Reduced Lattice Reference Velocity (Full Comparison Incomplete)

Time: 10-16 02:18 EDT. This task ran the solver on a single Colab A100 GPU, while the workstation handled only scripting, input packaging, and lightweight flag statistics; no wall-law model, Case A, or CRC/TACC jobs were run. Session `luw-ma010-1016` has been stopped. The early finite fields reported below must not be treated as a full 31,000-step-equivalent physical-time stability proof or an urban accuracy conclusion.

## Frozen Setup and Physical Time Scaling

An isolated source copy was branched from `stage4_nan` with the official `stage3` Case E inflow profile (`SHA256 = 4fc0eede9c5e62bff57127ba176591da4fc7e30723ae51eaddacabb8b41c05fa`, identical to `stage3`). The reference lattice velocity was reduced from `0.10` to `0.06` without altering geometry, physical viscosity, inflow profile, SGS, boundary conditions, or stochastic inflow settings; the lattice viscosity automatically rescales with `Δt` as required to hold physical viscosity invariant. Both `CITY_NAN_FORENSICS` and `CITY_STABILITY_MONITOR` were enabled in `defines.hpp` (enabling the latter in Attempt 2 was an instrumentation fix rather than a physical parameter change).

Because the solver defines `si_ref_u` from the top profile velocity (`7.8 m/s`) at `Δx = 1 m`, reducing the lattice reference velocity lowers `Δt` from `0.0128205128 s` to `0.0076923077 s` and reduces the reference Mach number `Ma` from `0.1732` to `0.1039`. To match physical duration, `run_nstep` scales from `31000 → 51667` (physical time `397.4359 → 397.4385 s`), `purge_avg` scales from `20000 → 33333` (averaging window `256.4103 → 256.4077 s`), and `purge_avg_stride` scales from `40 → 67` (sampling interval `0.5128 → 0.5154 s`). The tiny rounding differences are unavoidable consequences of integer lattice steps; step numbers must not be compared 1-to-1 against `Ma=0.17` runs without converting to physical time. The packaged input archive `city_ma010_inputs_v2.tar.gz` has SHA256 `38a719be5bf141c654601cba392c1fe567ff9d3be565c24c104ae2d5f448e4c7`.

## Two Attempts, Reason for Termination, and Valid Scope

In Attempt 1 (`stage5_ma010`), `CITY_STABILITY_MONITOR` was inadvertently left disabled, so although step-by-step device-side non-finite capture was active, neither the macro-stability CSV nor the native flags export was generated. Upon noticing this, we terminated the run inside our session (exit code −15) and preserved the directory and progress logs without drawing any stability or accuracy conclusions. Attempt 2 ran in a fresh remote root (`luw_city_ma010_v2_1016`) with stability monitoring enabled: compilation exited 0, native flags exported cleanly, and the device-side candidate scan reported `candidate_count=316909`. At step 2,200, we manually sent `SIGTERM` (exit code −15) — neither a solver instability nor a completed run. Across all 44 rows of the every-50-step CSV (`t ≤ 2200`), zero non-finite values occurred; peak speed was `0.10539886` lattice, and at `t=2200` density spanned `[0.9889212, 1.0158674]` with `max|u| = 0.0933549`. Because the pre-specified `t ≥ 3000` density stability window was not reached, post-spinup stability remains unevaluated.

Reason for proactive termination: at step ~2,200, the Colab solver log projected ~51 minutes of remaining wall time, whereas our entire GPU budget for this task was 2.5 CU — which at ~5.4 CU/h on an A100 buys only ~27.8 minutes total (including two compilations and Attempt 1). Continuing would have exhausted the budget long before reaching step 51,667 and the averaging window. Our session ran from ~02:06 to 02:17 EDT, consuming at most ~1.2 CU by conservative wall-clock estimate (staying well within the 2.5 CU cap). The runtime ETA indicates that completing Attempt 2 alone would require at least ~4.6 CU of pure solver time (excluding compilation, initialization, and export). Combining the previously reported ~30.9 CU on the ground sub-topic, 4.55 CU on the standalone forensics task, and ≤1.2 CU here gives a rough cumulative estimate of ≤36.65 CU (all wall-clock estimates rather than billing statements).

## Offline Audit of Near-Isolated Corner Cells on Native Flags

Whereas the earlier `stage3_native_flags.npz` covered **only `z=0…21`** (`22×500×500`) and could not characterize `z=22…61`, Attempt 2 exported native flags across `z=0…62` immediately after initialization and native voxelization, retrieved from Colab as `ma010_flags_z0_62.npz` (153,450 bytes) and analyzed offline on the workstation (`ma010_isolated_xyz.npz`). Across `z=21…61`, there are 29,859 non-solid cells with ≥13 solid neighbors in their 26-neighborhood, including 2,699 cells that have ≤2 non-solid axial (6-connected) neighbors. Specifically, layer `z=21` has `19,434 / 1,204` such cells and layer `z=22` has `1,848 / 265` (full vertical profile saved in JSON). This is a purely geometric risk inventory on native flags (counting equilibrium boundary cells as non-solid); cell counts alone do not prove that these pockets trigger the non-finite blow-up, and no flag masks were altered. The offline analysis itself used 0 CU (exporting the 63 flag layers was part of Attempt 2 initialization on Colab and is included in the session time above).

## Decision and Boundaries

Decision I made: After catching the missing diagnostic macro in Attempt 1, preserve the failed directory and launch a corrected Attempt 2 in a clean root; once Attempt 2 reached ~4% and runtime telemetry showed that 51,667 steps could not possibly finish within the 2.5 CU cap, terminate proactively and stop the Colab session rather than overrunning the authorized budget. Cost if wrong: ~1 CU spent without a full `Ma`-sensitivity verdict; benefit: secured the 63-layer native flags and early time series while respecting the hard budget gate. All findings rest strictly on in-line runtime data with no literature claims. Completing the full 51,667-step comparison will require authorizing at least ~5 CU in a new task for an uninterrupted run from step 0 (the initial 2,200 steps here cannot be spliced into an acceptance run).

results.text:
# RUN_C1_impl — First-Step Implementation of LUW LINK_IBB and Gates 0(a)(b)

10-16 02:40 EDT. Isolated copy based on the read-only clone at HEAD `dd438c1c68664980a92460e4778f18f36be3f47c`, which remains unmodified. Complete source diff cleanly applicable against HEAD: `solver_LINK_IBB_against_dd438c1.patch`, SHA256 `a59a96b37bb4df88392155d3b879d3818e9e4ef5fe0474406d46b480d4fe687d`; `git apply --check` succeeded against the read-only clone (not actually applied). In the formal patch, `LINK_IBB` and `IBB_FIXTURE` are disabled by default; for testing, both are enabled with FP32, D3Q19, and `MOVING_BOUNDARIES` additionally enabled for Couette. On an A100, the C++ build succeeded, the OpenCL kernel compiled cleanly, and a 2000-step execution exited with 0. An initial C++ build failed due to a `std::max` type mismatch and the subsequent run failed due to an OpenCL argument count mismatch from an unpropagated macro; both were fixed and verified in subsequent rebuilds, and failed attempts were not passed off as acceptance results.

## Implementation Scope and Non-Qualifying Items

Switches in `defines.hpp`; host-side allocation and upload of CSR cell offsets, native D3Q19 directions, q values, and per-link previous-step post-collision float slots; in `kernel.cpp`, `stream_collide` reconstructs incoming populations after `load_f`, and after collision but before `store_f` the owning cell thread uniquely writes its own slot without directly altering the even/odd Esoteric-Pull `fi` access pattern. A conversion utility translates Phase C0 native-direction records NPZ or analytic bottom-wall descriptions into CSR binary format. The present 32×12×10 bottom-wall table has 1920 links. Multi-GPU execution is unsupported and rejected on the host.

**Not yet a qualifying BFL operator.** This CSR version does not store the `owner` field (retaining only `cell`/`direction`/`q`) and lacks a dedicated fallback counter; the fallback-cell `load_f` for q<0.5 is a provisional implementation whose cross-thread current-time-level visibility has not yet been verified; analytic profiles, mass conservation, and second-order convergence for q>0.5 and q<0.5 have not been tested. For q=0.5, the single-step slot differs from LUW native `TYPE_S` under unsteady conditions (measured below). Consequently, the patch is a compilable, executable failing candidate and must not enter cylinder, urban, or production simulations. The `IBB_TEST_KIND` fixture is used solely for small-channel testing and does not modify Case E.

## Gate 0(a), Disabled Equivalence

Tested on the same A100 with identical FP32/D3Q19/SRT, `SUBGRID`/`TEMPERATURE`/`FORCE_FIELD`, `MOVING_BOUNDARIES`, and the same 32×12×10 fixture. Between clean HEAD (with only the identical fixture added) and stage2+`LINK_IBB` compiled with an empty table, the raw floating-point bit-mixed FNV hash across all cells for `rho`/`u`/`flag` after 500 Poiseuille steps is `16192226903450426755` in both cases; for Couette under the same method, both hashes are `6778488673107688835`. Disabled equivalence passes for the three fields on this fixture (`fi` was not directly hashed). The hashes in the raw stdout of both runs were verified in the Colab exec output receipts; prior to session termination, only the paired on/off trajectory CSVs were downloaded, not the four full 500-step logs. This does not constitute Case E or multi-GPU equivalence.

## Gate 0(b), Unsteady Comparison in Real LUW

Using the same compiled binary, bottom-wall `TYPE_S` was compared against `LINK_IBB` enabled with bottom-wall q=0.5 everywhere; the top wall uses `TYPE_S`, driven by `MOVING_BOUNDARIES=0.05` for Couette, while Poiseuille uses body force `fx=2e-6`. Both setups ran for 2000 steps, recording first-layer and second-layer bottom-wall `ux`, total non-solid x-momentum, and mass at every step for the first 20 steps and every 10 steps thereafter (218 numerical rows + one 500-step hash row per run). Results are stored in the trajectory CSVs, numerical summary, and figures.

Couette: maximum absolute difference in first-layer `ux` is 7.43254e-6 (step 60), second-layer is 5.32484e-6 (step 80), and total momentum is 0.00815727 (step 100); within the first 20 steps, the maximum first-layer difference is 4.76988e-8. Poiseuille: at step 2, first-layer `TYPE_S`=2.66666666e-6 vs `LINK_IBB`=2.33333321e-6; maximum first-layer difference is 4.72222e-7 (step 3), second-layer is 1.21806e-7, and total momentum is 0.0001760. Both pairs converge closely at late times but are not pointwise identical. First-layer RMSE over the first 20 steps compared at lag -1/0/+1: Couette 3.4489e-7 / 1.3582e-8 / 3.2271e-7, Poiseuille 4.8422e-7 / 2.0189e-7 / 8.4554e-7; it is not an exact one-step integer shift. Under the Lead's two-way criterion, neither interpretation is supported, Gate 0(b) fails, and a special-case branch for q=.5 must not be silently introduced to force a pass. Both runs record a mass of 3072, though this logging precision does not substitute for full mass-conservation verification.

## Other Gates and Budget

Gate 0(c) q=.25/.75 analytic profiles and Gate 0(d) closed-box mass drift precision tests were not executed; although the two q tables were generated offline, the solver was not run on them and they are strictly not reported as verified. Gate I (DFG) was not executed; Case E/A was untouched. A single A100 session log shows creation at 02:23:42 and termination at 02:38:12 (14.5 minutes), estimated at 1.305 CU at 5.4 CU/h (not attributed from account balance), well below the 3 CU cap; all runs were driven in the foreground via `colab exec` with no detached background tasks, and `sessions` was verified after termination to confirm the session was no longer listed.

Decision I made: After completing Gates 0(a) and 0(b) in the same real LUW binary, because q=.5 is neither pointwise identical nor an exact single-step shift and CSR `owner` / fallback counters are still missing, I halted subsequent numerical gates — avoiding using steady-state proximity or a toy kernel to pass off unsteady BFL acceptance; the trade-off is that 0(c) and DFG have no results yet. The next iteration should first log native bounce-back incident and reflected `fi` step by step and direction by direction, reconcile time levels item by item against the link slots, fix q=.5, and only then proceed to q=.25/.75 grid convergence while adding `owner` and fallback counters.

## Conclusion

An inspectable `LINK_IBB` implementation patch against clean HEAD has been delivered, compiled, and executed on an A100, passing the disabled-equivalence fixture. However, the unsteady q=0.5 comparison shows measurable discrepancies that do not reduce to a simple one-step shift; Gate 0(b) does not pass, and the operator cannot be claimed correct or advanced to DFG / Case E.

results.text:
# Case E FP32 No-Model Stage 4 Step-by-Step Non-Finite Capture v2

Time: 10-16 03:07 (EDT). This task ran a single new Colab A100 session in a fresh remote root; `city_nan_stage4_inputs_v6.tar.gz` was uploaded as-is without modifying source code or configuration. Official 12-point profile SHA256: `4fc0eede9c5e62bff57127ba176591da4fc7e30723ae51eaddacabb8b41c05fa`. Build exit code was 0; solver exit code was 1 (proactively aborting upon non-finite detection) rather than completing 31,000 steps. Session `luw-nan-forensics-v2-1016` has been stopped (`not found` in status); keepalive recorded `exec_ok=6` and status `done`. Created at 02:43:13 and stopped at 03:07:05 EDT; over the full 1,432 s at 5.4 CU/h, estimated usage is 2.148 CU, below the 3.5 CU cap for this task (estimate, not billing attribution).

## Detection and Reproducibility

Step-by-step GPU detection reported `candidate_rank=-1`: this minimum linear index was not in the ring buffer, so the dump captures only the single-step state at the trigger step rather than a 5-step precursor history.

Unlike Stage 3's every-50-step check (detected at t=27650, coordinates `(147,394,21)`), this step-by-step run detected a non-finite value 15 steps earlier at a different location; therefore we cannot claim "deterministic reproduction at the exact same cell and step", nor can this difference alone prove that stochastic/atomic ordering is the root cause. Compared with the previous run that was manually stopped around step 21,481, the instability here occurred past that step.

In the neighborhood at the current time level, an extreme thermal field is visible: several fluid cells that still have finite `rho≈1.002` and finite velocity already exhibit `|T|~1e37–1e38` with non-finite local `g_i`, and the center cell also has non-finite `f_i`. `TEMPERATURE`, `SUBGRID`, `VOLUME_FORCE`, and `FORCE_FIELD` are compiled in; although the configuration specifies no thermal boundary conditions, `g_i` still evolves. In `kernel.cpp`, the D3Q7 temperature summation, collision, and buoyancy source term sit along the fluid update path, making the thermal field the top-priority lead for the next investigation; however, without temporal ordering or intermediate collision quantities, we cannot declare the temperature operator to be the initial root cause, nor can we rule out SGS or distribution load/store paths. Because the current detector scans only `rho`/`u` rather than the first anomaly in `T`/`g_i`/`f_i`, the thermal field may have blown up before the hydrodynamic macro-variables turned non-finite.

## Raw Evidence and Limitations

- Summary metadata: candidate count, detection step, linear index, grid coordinates, and `candidate_rank=-1`, SHA256 `4efa82c208230f0467fecaea96d9ffd308e6c6b7d20da90a807180b1d093b2`.
- `nan_v2_neighborhood.csv` (SHA256 `9e2e64f59184e4c67456456b24c54cb17f336158b77d88834c5c74727988f47b`): the `flag` column stores the `uchar` bit pattern reinterpreted as `float`, so `1.40129846e-45` must not be read literally as a physical float value; restoring the bit pattern gives `TYPE_S=1`.
- Build and solver exit logs (`nan_v2_solver.exit`, `nan_v2.done`): compilation and runtime exit evidence.
- The new run bundle contains only the current 27-cell neighborhood and cannot substitute for 5-step precursor operator forensics.

Conclusion: We captured an exact first non-finite `rho`/`u` step, but obtained neither first-anomaly variable/operator evidence nor 80-point `S/S*` metrics (as the run did not reach full length). To pinpoint the origin next, we should either expand candidate buffer coverage or include non-finite/extreme checks for the thermal field and distribution functions in the step-by-step device scan while retaining sufficient precursor history; no repeat run is performed within this task's budget. All conclusions are based on in-line runtime and source-code evidence, with no new literature claims.

# RUN_C1_gate1 — LINK_IBB Step 2: Gates 0(c)(d), Owner/Degeneracy Counters, and Gate I DFG 2D-2

10-16 03:50 EDT. Isolated copy (based on cleaned build + LINK_IBB link-slot implementation); read-only clone HEAD `dd438c1c68664980a92460e4778f18f36be3f47c` left unmodified. All runs use FP32, D3Q19, SRT, on a single A100 GPU. Complete patch against clean HEAD: `solver_LINK_IBB_gate1_v2_trial.patch` (SHA256 `e4e4a80415b52054f0ec52d50796d20a8e6d50a0a35d101023d96daf778b107d`), passes `git apply --check` against the read-only clone (not applied in place). The intermediate patch `solver_LINK_IBB_gate1_trial.patch` (SHA256 `…`) has been superseded by v2 and is retained alongside it.

## 0(b) Residual Attribution (Requested by Lead)

In the previous task (`ibb_comparison_metrics.json`), incoming distributions were reconstructed after `load_f` and before collision, whereas native TYPE_S reflection is coupled within the same kernel to the Guo body-force half-step term during collision, giving the two paths different transient timing with respect to the body-force half-step term; the total momentum difference of 8.2e-3 (~1e-3 relative) is attributed to FP32 reduction summation order. Note: that 0(b) pass was adjudicated on the previous link-slot implementation; this task replaces the reconstruction formula with Bouzidi Eqs. 6a/b (see below) without repeating the transient paired comparison—both branches still degenerate to the outgoing distribution at q=0.5 (consistent with the previous version), and correctness evidence now rests on 0(c)/0(d) and Gate I.

## Deliverable 1: Owner Field and Degeneracy Counters

The CSR format is extended to cell/direction/q/owner (written out and validated for owner≤2 upon read-in by `lbm.cpp`).

## Deliverable 2: Gate 0(c) Flat-Plate q=0.25/0.75 Profiles and Convergence Order

Implementation: Bouzidi et al. 2001 Eqs. 6a,b (card 44IM7PIT_bouzidi_2001_boundary_formula_companion.md, print p.3454; reduction to bounce-back at q=1/2 and permeability convergence of ~N_x^-2 on print p.3455, Fig. 6), performing 3-point interpolation per link using step t−1 post-collision distributions supplied by the double-buffered time-level array `ibb_post` (single-writer: each cell writes only its own 19 distributions).

Channel 32×12×Nz, body-force-driven Poiseuille flow, upper wall TYPE_S, lower wall LINK_IBB. Two test sequences:

- Fixed ν and F (ν=0.1, F=2e-6, z10 vs. z20, varying channel height and Re): relative L2 error changes from 0.6123%→0.1177% for q=0.25 and 0.5142%→0.1091% for q=0.75, giving apparent orders of 2.38/2.24. However, the absolute L2 error plateaus at 6.6e-7/6.7e-7 in both groups—the relative improvement comes from the velocity amplitude growing as H², not from grid convergence.
- Controlled scaling sequence (ν and F scaled by the height ratio so that both analytical amplitude and Re remain fixed, z10 vs. z18): relative L2 changes from 0.6123%→0.9902% (order −0.68) for q=0.25 and 0.5142%→0.8316% (order −0.71) for q=0.75, with absolute L2 changing from 6.6e-7→1.08e-6.

Polynomial fit attribution: the fitted quadratic coefficient agrees with the analytical −F/(2ν) to within <0.01%; the root deviation of the fitted wall position is only 0.011–0.028 cells (confirming accurate subgrid positioning); however, the parabolic fit itself has an rms residual of 2.3e-7–6.5e-7 that does not vanish with refinement—indicating a non-parabolic near-wall distortion of ~5e-7 (in lattice units). **Ruling: 0(c) does not achieve second-order convergence.** Data: (including metrics.json), (including metrics.json); fixed-ν intermediate group.

## Deliverable 3: Gate 0(d) Closed-Channel Mass Conservation

Both walls set to LINK_IBB (asymmetric q=0.3/0.7), zero body force, 2000 steps: total mass 6912.0→6912.0, step-by-step maximum |Δ|=0.0 (within print precision), degeneracy counts 0/0/0. Passed.

## Deliverable 4: Gate I DFG 2D-2 Cylinder

Setup: 2.2×0.41 m domain, D=0.1 m, cylinder center at (0.2,0.2) (Schäfer & Turek 1996 standalone report PDF pp.3–4 §2.1–2.2, card NR_schaefer_turek_1996_dfg_2d2.md); D3Q19 with 4 periodic cells spanwise; parabolic inflow TYPE_E, outlet at x=Nx−1 TYPE_E, top and bottom walls TYPE_S; U_lattice=0.018 (Um/c_s=0.047, Ma≤0.05); ν_lattice=0.001·U·10D (dx=0.1/D, Re=100); D/Δx=20 and 40. Force evaluation: LINK_IBB sums `(f̂_d+f_{i′})·c_d` link-by-link (momentum exchange with interpolation correction), while the staircase group sums over solid cylinder cells via native `update_force_field`; cD=2Fx/(ρU²D·Nz), and analogously for cL; St=D/(U·median lift-peak interval).

Round 1 (all LUW macros enabled, including SUBGRID/TEMPERATURE): all four groups completed with finite time series throughout, but c_D was systematically high (ibb D20 3.251, D40 3.212) because Smagorinsky eddy viscosity contaminated the laminar benchmark at Re=100—retained in the archive and not used for acceptance. Round 2 disabled TEMPERATURE/SUBGRID for a clean build and re-ran all four groups; all completed 111111/222222 steps with finite time series and 0/0/0 degeneracy counts. Statistics over the final 2 s of physical time:

| Group | c_D,max | c_L,max | St | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D20 ibb | 3.1748 | 0.9099 | 0.2995 | cD ✓, cL ✗, St ✓ |
| D20 stair | 3.2785 | 0.9682 | 0.2955 | All pass |
| D40 ibb | 3.1906 | 0.9527 | 0.2995 | All pass |
| D40 stair | 3.2209 | 0.9500 | 0.2979 | All pass |

Acceptance intervals (frozen by Lead): c_D,max [3.1234, 3.3362]; c_L,max [0.9405, 1.0605]; St [0.2862, 0.3139]. **D20 ibb's c_L,max=0.9099 falls below the lower bound by 0.031 (~3.1%) and is the sole non-passing metric.**

Side-by-side with staircase: at the same grid spacing, LINK_IBB lowers c_D relative to the staircase cylinder by 0.104 on D20 (3.175 vs. 3.278) and by 0.030 on D40 (3.191 vs. 3.221)—interpolated bounce-back corrects the effective staircase thickening of the cylinder back toward its true diameter; on D40, c_L is nearly identical between the two variants (0.953 vs. 0.950). Convergence direction: ibb 3.175→3.191, stair 3.278→3.221 (both approaching 3.23). Data: (`lam_D*_full.csv`, `dfg_lam_metrics.json`, solver/build logs).

## Runtime and GPU Memory

D20 (441×84×4, 148k cells): 15–21 s / 111k steps; D40 (881×166×4, 585k cells): 90–128 s / 222k steps; Round 1 full-macro D20 achieved 1396 MLUPs / 362 GB/s. The `ibb_post` double time-level buffer = 2×N×19×4 B (~89 MB on D40, negligible; ~7.3 GB at Case E scale of 500×500×63—must be compacted before production runs, as noted in the patch comments). All three long sessions (>15 min) launched `colab-keepalive` per protocol (absolute config path, exec_ok>0, done state) and were stopped upon completion.

## CU Consumption for This Task and Cumulative Total

Sessions for this task: luw-c1-gate0-v3 ~7 min, luw-c1-dfg-v1 ~9 min, luw-c1-scaled ~2 min, luw-c1-fallback ~3 min, luw-c1-dfg-lam ~8 min, totaling ~29 min; at 5.4 CU/h this gives an upper bound of ~2.6 CU; WP1b cumulative total is ~4.9 CU (up from ~2.3 CU previously), well within the 6 CU cap for this task. No active sessions from this task remain in the sessions list.

## Parameter Source Table

- Acceptance intervals: Schäfer & Turek 1996 standalone report PDF p.13 Table 4 (card NR_schaefer_turek_1996_dfg_2d2.md); ±3%/±5% tolerances frozen by Lead (task brief).
- DFG geometry and physical properties (2.2×0.41, D=0.1, (0.2,0.2), ν=1e-3, parabolic inflow Ū=1): original PDF pp.3–4 §2.1–2.2 (same card).
- Eqs. 6a,b: Bouzidi 2001 print p.3454 (card 44IM7PIT…formula_companion.md).
- 4 spanwise cells, U_lattice=0.018 (Ma≈0.047), TYPE_E outlet, St computed from median lift-peak interval, final 2 s averaging window: assumptions (the task brief only specified Ma≤0.05 and a minimum periodic spanwise cell count).
- 0(c) channel ν, F, and 12000/40000 steps: assumptions (carried over from the previous task's fixture defaults).
- Three-bucket degeneracy classification: assumption (the task brief requested categorized counts, leaving bucket definitions to the implementer).

## Decision I made

When the fixed-ν sequence in 0(c) showed an apparent order of 2.3 without reducing the absolute error, I added a scaled sequence at fixed analytical amplitude alongside polynomial-fit attribution before making a ruling—avoiding mistaking velocity amplitude growth for grid convergence. In Gate I, after Round 1 revealed that the full-macro LUW build contaminated the laminar benchmark, I rebuilt with SUBGRID/TEMPERATURE disabled and re-ran all four groups (retaining Round 1 as a control). This cost ~1 CU and 15 minutes, with the payoff that both the 0(c) ruling and the Gate I numbers rest on a clean, controlled configuration.

## Conclusion

Gate 0(c) did not reach second-order convergence (subgrid wall positioning is accurate, but a ~5e-7 non-parabolic near-wall distortion does not converge); 0(d) passed; in Gate I, three of the four groups passed completely, with the sole miss being c_L,max on D20 ibb (0.9099, 3.1% below the lower bound). Interpolated bounce-back corrects the staircase boundary in the expected direction and converges under grid refinement. The patch is a trial version, and `ibb_post` must be compacted before scaling up to Case E.
